tools.name: get_terrain_state
tools.description: Returns a mesh terrain node's current authoring state: world size and section size in meters, seed, base profile, LOD count, the four material channels, and a summary of every modifier in the stack in evaluation order. Read this before a follow-up edit so new strokes land relative to what is already there instead of guessing. The full point list of each stroke is not returned, only its bounds, so this stays cheap on a heavily sculpted terrain.

nodeId.description: Mesh terrain node ID. Omit when the scene contains exactly one mesh terrain.

maxModifiers.description: Maximum modifier summaries to return, most recent last. Default 60.

tools.name: get_forest_state
tools.description: Lists every forest field with its shape, stand settings, and — where it has been grown — the stem count, boulder count, and which tree prototypes it uses. Read this before a follow-up edit so a change lands relative to what is already standing.

tools.name: list_vfx_abilities
tools.description: Lists the combat abilities available to cast, with the key each is bound to in the editor and how each is aimed (a line cast travels along the aimed line; a far cast lands its footprint at the far end; gate, ring and scribe casts build a structure). Read this before casting so the ability matches what the user described.

tools.name: capture_viewport_screenshot
tools.description: Capture a screenshot of the active editor viewport so you can inspect what has actually been built. Use this after meaningful scene changes when visual confirmation would help.

reason.description: Optional short note about what you want to inspect in the screenshot

tools.name: create_mesh_terrain
tools.description: Creates a mesh terrain node: a sculptable surface mesh, not a heightfield grid. Because strokes displace along the picked surface normal and holes are cut by exact CSG, mesh terrain can carry overhangs, undercut cliffs, arches, caves, and tunnels that heightmap terrain cannot represent. Terrain is authored in world meters at kilometre scale, so a default terrain is a 4 km square. Returns the node ID that every other terrain_* tool takes as nodeId.

name.description: Display name for the terrain node

x.description: World X of the terrain center in meters (default 0)

y.description: World Y of the terrain base plane in meters (default 0 = ground level)

z.description: World Z of the terrain center in meters (default 0)

worldSizeMeters.description: Edge length of the square terrain in meters. Default 4096, i.e. a 4 km world. Clamped to 256-16384.

sectionSizeMeters.description: Edge length of one streamed terrain section in meters. Default 128. Smaller sections rebuild faster after an edit but cost more draw calls. Clamped…

seed.description: Deterministic base-field seed. The same seed and profile always produce the same starting surface, before any stroke.

profile.description: Base elevation the terrain starts from. "natural" (default) gives rolling procedural relief to sculpt against; "flat" gives a level plane at Y=0 for…

lodLevels.description: Number of geometric LODs compiled per section, 1-5. Default 5.

allowDuplicate.description: Set true only when a second terrain node is genuinely intended. Defaults false, which refuses to add a second mesh terrain to the scene.

tools.name: terrain_sculpt_stroke
tools.description: Sculpts the terrain along a path of world-space points, in meters. Nine modes: raise and lower move the surface, clay builds mass, smooth relaxes it, flatten levels toward one height, pinch sharpens ridges, scrape planes material away, terrace cuts benches, noise adds grain. Domain 'heightfield' moves straight up, 'mesh' follows the picked surface normal and can form overhangs. Strokes stack non-destructively, so build a landform in passes rather than one huge stroke.

nodeId.description: Mesh terrain node ID. Omit when the scene contains exactly one mesh terrain.

mode.description: Sculpt operation. `raise`/`lower` push the surface out or in along the domain axis. `smooth` averages neighbours to soften noise and stroke seams.…

domain.description: Displacement axis. "heightfield" moves vertices along world +Y and cannot create an overhang. "mesh" (default) moves them along the picked surface…

path.description: Ordered world-space dab positions, in meters. Give at least one point; two or more sweep the brush along the path.

y.description: World Y in meters. For heightfield strokes this only picks the dab, not the result height.

normalX.description: Surface normal X at this point. Only meaningful for domain "mesh"; defaults to world up (0,1,0).

normalY.description: Surface normal Y at this point. Defaults to 1.

normalZ.description: Surface normal Z at this point. Defaults to 0.

weight.description: Relative brush flow at this point, 0-1. Default 1. Taper the ends of a ridge by fading this toward 0.

radiusMeters.description: Brush radius in meters. Terrain is kilometre scale, so a mountain mass is typically 200-600 m, a ridge 60-200 m, a trail cut or boulder detail 5-15 m.

strength.description: Peak displacement per dab in meters, at the center of the brush. Keep it positive: `lower` and `scrape` already remove material. A 400 m peak is…

falloff.description: Edge softness 0-1. 0 is a hard-edged disc that leaves a visible rim; 1 is a fully smooth falloff. Default 0.5.

targetY.description: Only for mode "flatten": the world Y elevation in meters the surface is pulled toward. Defaults to the Y of the first path point.

terraceStepMeters.description: Only for mode "terrace": vertical spacing between terrace treads, in meters.

noiseScale.description: Only for mode "noise": world-space wavelength of the added roughness, in meters. Smaller values give finer grain.

accumulate.description: When true the stroke keeps building depth over overlapping dabs instead of settling on a single displacement. Use true to dig deep with one stroke,…

sculptLayerId.description: Optional sculpt layer ID to file this stroke under, so a group of strokes can later be faded or disabled together.

tools.name: terrain_carve_tunnel
tools.description: Carves a tunnel straight through a mesh terrain by sweeping a capsule between two world-space portals and subtracting it with exact CSG. This produces a genuine hole with interior walls, not a masked-out region, which is why it belongs to mesh terrain and has no heightmap equivalent. Use it for road and rail tunnels, mine adits, and the trunk passage of a cave system; branch chambers and side passages are better added with `terrain_add_csg_volume`. All distances are meters.

nodeId.description: Mesh terrain node ID. Omit when the scene contains exactly one mesh terrain.

startX.description: World X of the entrance portal in meters, placed on the terrain surface

startY.description: World Y of the entrance portal in meters

startZ.description: World Z of the entrance portal in meters

startNormalX.description: Direction the entrance portal faces, X. Should point out of the hillside. Defaults to the direction of the other portal.

startNormalY.description: Direction the entrance portal faces, Y

startNormalZ.description: Direction the entrance portal faces, Z

endX.description: World X of the exit portal in meters, placed on the terrain surface

endY.description: World Y of the exit portal in meters

endZ.description: World Z of the exit portal in meters

endNormalX.description: Direction the exit portal faces, X. Should point out of the hillside.

endNormalY.description: Direction the exit portal faces, Y

endNormalZ.description: Direction the exit portal faces, Z

radiusMeters.description: Tunnel bore radius in meters. Default 8. A single-track rail tunnel is about 4 m, a two-lane road tunnel about 6-8 m, a walkable cave passage 3-10 m.

depthMeters.description: How far each portal drives straight inward before the two ends are joined, in meters. Default is 1.75x radiusMeters. Larger values give a straighter…

noise.description: Wall roughness, 0 or more. 0 gives a machined bore, which is correct for an engineered tunnel; 1 (default) gives rock. Raise it toward 2-3 for a…

noiseScale.description: World-space wavelength of the wall roughness in meters. Default 2.6. Larger values give broad undulation instead of fine pitting.

tools.name: terrain_paint_weights
tools.description: Paints one of a mesh terrain's four material channels along a world-space path, and appends the paint stroke to the node's modifier stack. Channel weights blend the terrain's four surface materials; painting one channel up naturally takes weight from the others. Use `terrain_set_material_channels` first if the channels do not already mean what you need. All distances are meters.

nodeId.description: Mesh terrain node ID. Omit when the scene contains exactly one mesh terrain.

channel.description: Which of the four material channels to paint. Call `get_terrain_state` to see what each channel is currently named. Defaults are channel0 Grass,…

mode.description: "add" (default) paints the channel in; "subtract" erases it, letting the other channels show through.

path.description: Ordered world-space dab positions, in meters.

normalX.description: Surface normal X at this point. Defaults to world up.

normalY.description: Surface normal Y at this point. Defaults to 1.

normalZ.description: Surface normal Z at this point. Defaults to 0.

weight.description: Relative paint flow at this point, 0-1. Default 1.

radiusMeters.description: Paint radius in meters. Material bands read best when they are wide: a snowline or scree band is typically 100-400 m.

strength.description: Weight applied per dab, 0-1. Default 0.5. Use low values and repeated passes for a soft transition between materials.

falloff.description: Edge softness 0-1. Default 0.7; material boundaries almost always want a soft edge.

tools.name: create_forest_field
tools.description: Creates a forest field: a stand described as a spline on the ground rather than a list of trees. Nothing grows until the shape has at least two control points and `grow_forest_field` runs, so the normal sequence is create, add points, then grow. Returns the field ID every other forest_* tool takes. Forests sit on the terrain's height field, so make the terrain first when the user wants both.

name.description: Display name for the field, for example "North Woods"

preset.description: The stand type. This decides the species mix, the floor, and the stems per hectare. Pick by climate and age: boreal-conifer for cold spruce/fir,…

points.description: Optional control points to lay down immediately, so a field can be created and shaped in one call. Each is a point on the ground plane in world…

closed.description: True (default) makes the spline a closed loop enclosing an area. False makes it an open belt of `width` either side, for a treeline, hedgerow, or…

grow.description: Grow the stand immediately after creating it. Only meaningful when `points` supplies at least two points. Defaults to true when points are given.

tools.name: add_forest_points
tools.description: Appends control points to a forest field's spline, in order. The curve through them is a centripetal Catmull-Rom, so points may be placed close together without the shape cusping. Adding points marks the field dirty; it does not regrow until `grow_forest_field` runs.

fieldId.description: Forest field ID. Omit when exactly one field exists.

points.description: Ground-plane points in world meters, in the order they should join.

tools.name: grow_forest_field
tools.description: Grows a forest field: lays out the stems, scatters the boulders, and reports what was produced. This is the expensive step in the whole forest system, so it is explicit and never implied by editing the shape. Growing again after a change replaces the previous stand.

fieldId.description: Forest field ID. Omit to grow every dirty field.

tools.name: place_primitive
tools.description: Places a parametric primitive shape (cube, sphere, cylinder, cone). Use it for static blockout primitives or physics props.

role.description: brush = static blockout primitive, prop = physics object

materialId.description: Material ID to apply directly. Avoids needing a separate assign_material call.

tools.name: place_blockout_room
tools.description: Places a blockout room (enclosed box with walls, floor, ceiling). Open sides remove entire wall/floor/ceiling planes for coarse full-side openings only. Position is the center-bottom of the room.

x.description: World X position of room center

y.description: World Y position of room bottom (usually 0 for ground level)

z.description: World Z position of room center

openSides.description: Whole sides to leave open. This removes the entire wall, floor, or ceiling plane and is not suitable for doorway- or hallway-sized openings.

materialId.description: Material ID to apply. Use list_materials to see available IDs.

name.description: Display name for the room node

tools.name: set_scene_settings
tools.description: Updates scene settings (world physics, fog, ambient, skybox, grass wind, player config). Skybox uses world.skybox; grass wind animates the procedural grass field shader.

skyboxSource.description: Skybox URL or asset path (HDR or image per skyboxFormat)

skyboxName.description: Display label for the sky preset

skyboxLightingIntensity.description: How strongly the sky contributes to scene lighting (when affectsLighting)

grassEnabled.description: Enable procedural grass field in lit viewport

tools.name: cast_vfx_ability
tools.description: Fires one of seven combat abilities in the viewport as a one-off effect. Each travels from an origin along a flat heading, erupts at the far end, then clears itself. Use it to show what an ability looks like or to dress a frame. The cast is not saved with the scene. Call list_vfx_abilities first to match an ability to what the user described.

element.description: Which ability. pyre is a ring of burning blades over a molten crater; kraken is cephalopod arms hauling out of a rift and hammering the ground;…

x.description: World X the cast starts from, in meters. Defaults to 0.

y.description: World Y of the cast origin, in meters. Ground level unless the ability hangs in the air. Defaults to 0.

z.description: World Z the cast starts from, in meters. Defaults to 0.

directionX.description: Flat heading X. Need not be unit length; it is normalised. Defaults to 0.

directionZ.description: Flat heading Z. Defaults to 1, i.e. straight along +Z.

distance.description: How far the cast reaches, in meters. 20 is a natural skillshot range; clamped to 1-400.

tools.name: create_procedural_world
tools.description: Creates a persistent LAAS procedural-world node. It is WebGPU-only and stores deterministic generator settings rather than generated GPU data.

tools.name: inspect_procedural_world
tools.description: Returns persisted settings and current deterministic configuration for a procedural world.

tools.name: regenerate_procedural_world
tools.description: Queues regeneration from the persisted LAAS seed and settings. Does not claim GPU generation succeeded before the viewport reports it.

tools.name: set_procedural_world_seed
tools.description: Sets the deterministic uint32 seed for a procedural world.

tools.name: set_procedural_world_preset
tools.description: Selects the low, high, or ultra LAAS quality preset.

tools.name: configure_procedural_terrain
tools.description: Configures LAAS terrain/hydrology authoring controls.

tools.name: configure_proc_vegetation
tools.description: Configures LAAS GPU scatter densities, species, slopes, impostors, and wind response.

tools.name: configure_procedural_lighting
tools.description: Configures LAAS sun, cascaded shadows, and canopy-aware GI.

tools.name: configure_proc_atmosphere
tools.description: Configures LAAS clouds, fog, and froxel volumetrics.

tools.name: configure_procedural_water
tools.description: Configures LAAS rivers/lakes, reflections, caustics, foam, wet margins, and clipmap distance.

tools.name: configure_procedural_motion
tools.description: Configures LAAS wind, cloud motion, particle classes, and deterministic freeze mode.

tools.name: configure_procedural_post
tools.description: Configures LAAS TAA, GTAO, bounce, bloom, exposure, and debug view settings.

tools.name: set_world_time_of_day
tools.description: Sets LAAS physical sky time of day in hours from 0 through 24.

tools.name: set_world_weather
tools.description: Applies a concise cloud/fog/particle weather configuration.

tools.name: set_world_exploration_mode
tools.description: Sets editor, walk, or fly exploration mode for the world preview/runtime.

tools.name: create_world_bookmark
tools.description: Adds a serialized procedural-world camera bookmark.

tools.name: update_world_bookmark
tools.description: Updates a serialized procedural-world camera bookmark.

tools.name: delete_world_bookmark
tools.description: Deletes a serialized procedural-world camera bookmark.

tools.name: play_world_flythrough
tools.description: Enters LAAS fly exploration mode so its composed bookmark flythrough controls can run.

tools.name: stop_world_flythrough
tools.description: Returns the procedural world to editor exploration mode.

tools.name: inspect_world_performance
tools.description: Returns persisted quality/capacity expectations; live GPU timings are available only after a WebGPU world is running.

tools.name: capture_world_verify_shot
tools.description: Captures the current viewport for procedural-world verification when screenshot capture is available.

tools.name: list_copilot_skill_references
tools.description: Lists available read-only Copilot skill references. Use this before reading a deeper reference when the active skill names several documents.

tools.name: read_copilot_skill_reference
tools.description: Reads a bounded line range from an active Copilot skill reference. Do not reread an identical range during this run.

tools.name: search_skill_references
tools.description: Searches active Copilot skill references and returns focused line ranges. Search before reading a long document.

maxResults.description: Maximum 24 results

tools.name: place_blockout_platform
tools.description: Places a flat blockout mesh platform (floor slab, roof, shelf). Position is the center of the platform volume.

y.description: World Y position (center of slab thickness)

tools.name: place_blockout_stairs
tools.description: Places a parametric staircase with optional landings. Position is the center-bottom of the bottom landing. Returns topLandingCenter for chaining connections.

x.description: World X position of stair base

y.description: World Y position of stair base (bottom)

z.description: World Z position of stair base

stepHeight.description: Height of each step in meters (typical: 0.2)

treadDepth.description: Depth of each step tread in meters (typical: 0.3)

direction.description: Direction the stairs ascend toward (default: north)

tools.name: place_brush
tools.description: Legacy-named compatibility tool that places a simple axis-aligned mesh box. Default is a 4x3x4 box. Prefer mesh editing workflows after placement.

tools.name: place_light
tools.description: Places a light in the scene. Types: point (local area), directional (sun), spot (focused cone), ambient (global fill), hemisphere (sky/ground).

type.description: Light type

tools.name: place_entity
tools.description: Places a gameplay entity (spawn point, NPC, or interactive object). Prefer place_player_spawn for playable start positions.

type.description: Entity type

tools.name: place_player_spawn
tools.description: Places a player-spawn entity. Use this for playable maps instead of generic entity placement.

tools.name: place_skatepark_element
tools.description: Places a procedural skatepark element (ramps, rails, bowls, etc.). Position is the center-bottom of the element.

type.description: Type of skatepark element

rotationY.description: Rotation around Y axis in radians (default: 0)

length.description: Standard length/depth (default: 4)

tools.name: place_architecture_element
tools.description: Places an architecture element (wall, slab, ceiling, roof, door, window, light fixture). Position is the center-bottom of the element.

type.description: Architecture element type

height.description: Height in meters (default: 3 for walls, 0.2 for slabs)

thickness.description: Thickness in meters (default: 0.2 for walls, 0.15 for ceilings)

pitchAngle.description: Roof pitch angle in degrees, 0 for flat (default: 30)

rotationY.description: Rotation around Y axis in radians (default: 0)

materialId.description: Material ID (defaults to architecture material for the element type)

tools.name: translate_nodes
tools.description: Moves nodes by a relative offset (delta). Does not set absolute position — adds delta to current position.

tools.name: set_node_transform
tools.description: Sets a node's absolute position, rotation, and scale.

tools.name: duplicate_nodes
tools.description: Duplicates nodes with a position offset. Returns the new node IDs.

tools.name: mirror_nodes
tools.description: Mirrors (flips) nodes across the specified axis.

tools.name: delete_nodes
tools.description: Deletes nodes and/or entities by their IDs. Also removes all children.

ids.description: Node or entity IDs to delete

tools.name: split_brush
tools.description: Legacy brush-only tool. Splits brush nodes at their midpoint along the specified axis. Returns the new node IDs.

tools.name: extrude_brush
tools.description: Legacy brush-only tool. Extrudes (grows) brush nodes along an axis by a given amount.

amount.description: Extrusion distance in meters

direction.description: Extrusion direction: '-1' (negative) or '1' (positive)

tools.name: offset_brush_face
tools.description: Legacy brush-only tool. Moves a single face of a brush inward or outward.

side.description: Which face (min or max)

amount.description: Offset amount (positive = outward)

tools.name: assign_material_to_brushes
tools.description: Legacy brush-only tool. Assigns a material to all faces of the specified brush nodes.

tools.name: create_material
tools.description: Creates or updates a material in the scene library. The ID is auto-generated as 'material:custom: ' from the name (e.g. name 'Dark Wood' → id 'material:custom:dark-wood'). You can use this predictable ID immediately in assign_material calls.

tools.name: assign_material
tools.description: Assigns a material to nodes (all faces) or specific faces on nodes.

faceIds.description: Optional face IDs (omit for all faces)

targets.description: Nodes (and optional faces) to assign material to

tools.name: set_uv_scale
tools.description: Sets UV texture tiling scale on nodes or specific faces.

tools.name: group_nodes
tools.description: Groups nodes/entities under a new group node. Returns the group ID.

ids.description: Node/entity IDs to group

tools.name: select_nodes
tools.description: Sets the editor selection to the given node/entity IDs.

ids.description: IDs to select

tools.name: clear_selection
tools.description: Clears the current editor selection.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undoes the last editor command.

tools.name: push_scene_to_connected_game
tools.description: Pushes the current editor scene into the connected scaffolded game dev server. Use it when the user asks to sync or send the current scene to the game.

forceSwitch.description: If true, request the game to reload directly into the pushed scene after syncing.

gameId.description: Optional specific connected game ID when more than one game is available.

projectName.description: Optional project display name override for the pushed scene.

projectSlug.description: Optional slug override for the target scene folder.

tools.name: create_articulated_asset
tools.description: Creates a true Articraft-generated articulated 3D asset in the editor viewport by calling the local Articraft Python SDK/compiler, compiling an Articraft model.py into URDF/mesh assets, and importing the result. Use this for objects with semantic parts and joints such as robot arms, desk lamps, cabinets with drawers, vehicles with wheels, doors, lids, sliders, hinges, levers, grippers, and mechanisms.

name.description: Asset display name, e.g. 'Articulated Desk Lamp'

prompt.description: The original natural-language asset request. Used as Articraft provenance metadata.

showJointGuides.description: Whether to add visible pivot/axis guide primitives for each joint. Default true.

parts.description: Semantic parts. Each part becomes a viewport node. Positions are local to parentPartId when provided, otherwise local to the asset root.

id.description: Stable part id such as 'base', 'upper_arm', 'drawer'

parentPartId.description: Optional parent part id. Use 'root' or omit for root-level parts.

semanticRole.description: Semantic role such as base, housing, hinge, arm, wheel, drawer, lid, handle, bracket, knob

pivotX.description: Optional local pivot X for hinge/slider previews

pivotY.description: Optional local pivot Y for hinge/slider previews

pivotZ.description: Optional local pivot Z for hinge/slider previews

color.description: Hex color if a new material should be created for this part

joints.description: Articulations between parts, using Articraft/URDF-style conventions: origin is in the parent part frame; axis is in the joint frame; revolute values…

id.description: Stable joint id, e.g. 'base_to_arm'

type.description: Joint/articulation type

originX.description: Joint origin X in parent part frame

originY.description: Joint origin Y in parent part frame

originZ.description: Joint origin Z in parent part frame

lower.description: Lower motion limit; radians for revolute, meters for prismatic

upper.description: Upper motion limit; radians for revolute, meters for prismatic

mimicJointId.description: Optional source joint id this joint mimics

tools.name: pose_articulated_joint
tools.description: Sets a preview pose for one articulated asset joint in the viewport. Revolute/continuous values are radians; prismatic values are meters. The pose is stored on the asset metadata and applied from the child part's saved base transform.

assetNodeId.description: Root articulated asset group node id

jointId.description: Joint id or joint name to pose

value.description: Joint value in radians or meters

clampToLimits.description: Clamp value to lower/upper limits when present. Default true.

tools.name: list_entities
tools.description: Lists entities in a lightweight form with ID, name, type, and parentId. Use get_entity_details for full data.

tools.name: list_materials
tools.description: Lists all materials in the scene with their ID, name, color, and category.

tools.name: list_scene_paths
tools.description: Lists all scene-level waypoint paths with ids, names, loop state, and points.

tools.name: list_scene_events
tools.description: Lists the standard and custom gameplay events available in the scene.

tools.name: list_hook_types
tools.description: Lists all supported gameplay hook types, including field paths, defaults, emitted events, and listened events.

tools.name: list_articulated_assets
tools.description: Lists articulated asset roots created in the viewport, including part/joint counts and current pose metadata.

tools.name: get_articulated_asset_details
tools.description: Gets full structured part, joint, pose, and node details for one articulated asset root.

assetNodeId.description: Root articulated asset group node id

tools.name: get_entity_details
tools.description: Gets full details of a specific entity, including transform, worldTransform, parentId, properties, and hooks.

entityId.description: Entity ID to inspect

tools.name: create_scene_path
tools.description: Creates a new scene-level waypoint path. Paths are referenced by hook config such as path_mover.pathId.

id.description: Optional explicit path id

points.description: Waypoint points in world space

tools.name: update_scene_path
tools.description: Updates a scene path by replacing any provided fields such as name, loop, or points.

points.description: Replacement waypoint points in world space

tools.name: delete_scene_path
tools.description: Deletes a scene-level waypoint path.

tools.name: add_hook
tools.description: Attaches a gameplay hook to a node or entity using the canonical default config for that hook type, then applies any provided config overrides.

targetKind.description: Whether the hook attaches to a node or entity

targetId.description: Node or entity id

hookType.description: Hook type. Use list_hook_types to inspect supported types.

enabled.description: Whether the hook starts enabled

defaultPathId.description: Optional default path id for path_mover hooks

config.description: Optional config override object merged into the canonical default config

tools.name: set_hook_value
tools.description: Sets a specific hook config value by dot path on an existing node/entity hook.

targetKind.description: Whether the hook is on a node or entity

targetId.description: Node or entity id

path.description: Dot path inside hook.config, for example 'pathId' or 'trigger.event'

value.description: New value to write at the config path

tools.name: remove_hook
tools.description: Removes a gameplay hook from a node or entity.

targetKind.description: Whether the hook is on a node or entity

targetId.description: Node or entity id

tools.name: list_behavior_trees
tools.description: Lists locally saved behavior trees from the AI Behavior Tree Editor.

tools.name: get_behavior_tree
tools.description: Gets the full nodes and edges for a saved behavior tree by id.

tools.name: create_behavior_tree
tools.description: Creates a new behavior tree in local storage. By default it starts with a root node only. Set useDefaultTemplate to true for the starter attack/patrol example tree.

treeId.description: Optional requested tree id. If omitted, one is derived from the name.

useDefaultTemplate.description: Whether to start from the built-in sample tree instead of an empty root-only tree

tools.name: add_behavior_tree_node
tools.description: Adds a node to a behavior tree, optionally connecting it under a parent node.

label.description: Optional node label

parentNodeId.description: Optional parent node id to connect from

event.description: Condition event name

mode.description: Condition mode

tools.name: update_behavior_tree_node
tools.description: Updates label, behavior data, or canvas position for an existing behavior tree node.

label.description: Updated node label

event.description: Condition event name

mode.description: Condition mode

tools.name: connect_behavior_tree_nodes
tools.description: Creates a directed edge from one behavior tree node to another.

tools.name: delete_behavior_tree_node
tools.description: Deletes a node and any connected edges from a behavior tree.

tools.name: apply_behavior_tree_layout
tools.description: Automatically lays out the nodes in a behavior tree.

tools.name: delete_behavior_tree
tools.description: Deletes a saved behavior tree from local storage.

tools.name: get_mesh_topology
tools.description: Returns the face IDs, vertex IDs with positions, face centers, face normals, and edges for a mesh node. Use this before mesh editing operations to discover which faces/vertices/edges to target.

tools.name: extrude_mesh_faces
tools.description: Extrude one or more faces of a mesh node along their normal by an amount. Use get_mesh_topology first to find face IDs.

amount.description: Extrusion distance in meters (positive = outward)

tools.name: extrude_mesh_edge
tools.description: Extrude a boundary edge of a mesh outward, creating a new quad face.

vertexId1.description: First vertex ID of the edge

vertexId2.description: Second vertex ID of the edge

amount.description: Extrusion distance

tools.name: bevel_mesh_edges
tools.description: Bevel (chamfer/round) edges of a mesh. Creates smooth transitions at sharp edges.

steps.description: Number of bevel segments (1=flat chamfer, 3+=smooth round)

tools.name: inset_mesh_faces
tools.description: Inset selected faces to create an inner face loop. Use it for panel lines, door/window frames, and prep before extrusion.

amount.description: Inset amount in meters

tools.name: bridge_mesh_edges
tools.description: Bridge two selected boundary edges with a new face. Use get_mesh_topology first and pass exactly two edge pairs.

tools.name: poke_mesh_faces
tools.description: Poke selected faces into triangles from a new center vertex. Useful for radial detail, peaks, and controlled triangulation.

tools.description: Triangulate selected faces, or all faces when faceIds is omitted. Useful before runtime baking or cleanup.

tools.description: Attempt to rebuild selected triangle pairs into quads. Use after triangulation or cleanup when quad authoring is preferred.

tools.name: mirror_mesh
tools.description: Mirror a mesh across one local axis as a one-shot topology edit. Prefer the modeling stack for reusable symmetry.

tools.name: weld_mesh_vertices_by_distance
tools.description: Merge vertices within a distance threshold. Use for cleanup after boolean, bridge, mirror, import, or remesh-style edits.

tools.name: weld_mesh_vertices_to_target
tools.description: Target-weld source vertices into one target vertex. Use for precise cleanup and snapping holes shut.

targetVertexId.description: Vertex ID that receives the weld

sourceVertexIds.description: Vertex IDs to merge into the target

tools.name: subdivide_mesh_face
tools.description: Subdivide a mesh face into smaller faces. Quad faces get a grid pattern, others get radial.

cuts.description: Number of cuts (1=2x2 for quads, 2=3x3, etc.)

tools.name: cut_mesh_face
tools.description: Cut a mesh face with a line passing through a point, splitting it into two faces.

pointX.description: X coordinate of cut point on the face

tools.name: cut_mesh_between_edges
tools.description: Knife-cut a polygon by connecting the midpoints of two non-adjacent edges on the same face.

edges.description: Exactly two non-adjacent edges as [[vertexId1, vertexId2], [vertexId3, vertexId4]]

tools.name: delete_mesh_faces
tools.description: Delete faces from a mesh, leaving real holes. Use only for intentional openings to empty space or adjacent voids, not as a shortcut for doorway- or hallway-sized passages.

tools.name: merge_mesh_faces
tools.description: Merge adjacent coplanar faces into a single face.

tools.name: merge_mesh_vertices
tools.description: Merge multiple vertices to their average position.

tools.name: translate_mesh_vertices
tools.description: Translate selected mesh vertices in world space. Use this to reposition a cap or face region after cutting or extruding.

tools.description: Scale selected mesh vertices around their centroid or an optional pivot. Use this to widen or narrow an extruded cap before the next extrusion.

scaleX.description: World-axis scale factor around the pivot for X

scaleY.description: World-axis scale factor around the pivot for Y

scaleZ.description: World-axis scale factor around the pivot for Z

pivotX.description: Optional pivot X. Defaults to the selected vertices centroid.

pivotY.description: Optional pivot Y. Defaults to the selected vertices centroid.

pivotZ.description: Optional pivot Z. Defaults to the selected vertices centroid.

tools.name: fill_mesh_face
tools.description: Create a new face from a loop of boundary vertices, filling a hole in the mesh.

vertexIds.description: Vertex IDs forming the boundary loop (>=3, must be boundary vertices)

tools.name: invert_mesh_normals
tools.description: Flip face normals (winding order) on selected or all faces of a mesh.

tools.name: arc_mesh_edges

tools.name: inflate_mesh
tools.description: Move all vertices of mesh nodes along their averaged normals (inflate/deflate).

enabled.description: Whether the modifier is enabled

mode.description: Boolean, lattice, or remesh mode

tools.name: normalize_mesh_texel_density
tools.description: Scale selected face UVs to a target texel density for game-production texture consistency.

faceIds.description: Optional face IDs; omit for whole mesh

tools.name: paint_mesh_face_material
tools.description: Assign a material to mesh faces and register it as a mesh-local material slot.

faceIds.description: Face IDs to paint; omit for all faces

tools.name: paint_mesh_vertex_color
tools.description: Paint RGBA vertex colors onto mesh face corners. Hex color is easiest, e.g. #ff8844.

faceIds.description: Face IDs to paint; omit for all faces

strength.description: Paint strength 0-1, default 1

tools.name: add_mesh_surface_blend_layer
tools.description: Add or update one of the mesh's up-to-4 PBR texture blend layers, usually from an existing material.

layerId.description: Stable blend layer ID. Defaults to blend:<materialId>

materialId.description: Existing material ID to copy color/textures from

tools.name: paint_mesh_texture_blend
tools.description: Paint normalized per-corner weights for a mesh surface blend layer.

faceIds.description: Face IDs to paint; omit for all faces

strength.description: Paint strength 0-1, default 1

tools.name: add_mesh_projected_decal
tools.description: Add a live projected decal record to a mesh for editor and runtime overlay rendering.

materialId.description: Optional material ID to copy texture/color from

tools.name: split_brush_at_coordinate
tools.description: Split a brush node at an exact world coordinate along an axis (more precise than split_brush which only splits at the midpoint).

tools.name: terrain_add_csg_volume
tools.description: Adds a non-destructive cutter volume to the terrain: a box, sphere, cylinder or capsule that carves the surface where it overlaps, for caves, arches and overhangs. The volume stays live in the modifier stack, so it can be moved, resized or removed later without rebaking the landform. Prefer this over terrain_carve_tunnel when the opening is a chamber rather than a passage.

nodeId.description: Mesh terrain node ID. Omit when the scene contains exactly one mesh terrain.

operation.description: "subtract" (default) removes the volumes from the terrain solid; "add" unions them into it.

volumes.description: The volumes to combine with the terrain. Fields other than `kind` and the shared surface fields apply only to the kinds named in their description.

kind.description: Volume shape. `capsule` is a swept sphere between two points -- passages, tubes, and windows punched through a fin. `ellipsoid` is a rotated ellipsoid -- round for a chamber, flattened for a cliff undercut. `box` is a rotated box, for the straight-walled reaches of a slot canyon. `sweep` is a chain of elliptical rings, for one continuously varying cave shell.

startX.description: capsule: world X of the capsule axis start, in meters

startY.description: capsule: world Y of the capsule axis start, in meters

startZ.description: capsule: world Z of the capsule axis start, in meters

endX.description: capsule: world X of the capsule axis end, in meters

endY.description: capsule: world Y of the capsule axis end, in meters

endZ.description: capsule: world Z of the capsule axis end, in meters

radiusMeters.description: capsule: sphere radius swept along the axis, in meters

centerX.description: ellipsoid and box: world X of the volume center, in meters

centerY.description: ellipsoid and box: world Y of the volume center, in meters

centerZ.description: ellipsoid and box: world Z of the volume center, in meters

radiusX.description: ellipsoid: half-extent along the local forward axis, in meters

radiusY.description: ellipsoid: half-extent along local up, in meters. Make this small relative to radiusX and radiusZ to undercut a cliff.

radiusZ.description: ellipsoid: half-extent along the local side axis, in meters

halfExtentX.description: box: half-size along the local forward axis, in meters

halfExtentY.description: box: half-size along local up, in meters

halfExtentZ.description: box: half-size along the local side axis, in meters

forwardX.description: ellipsoid and box: world direction the local +X axis points along. Defaults to (1,0,0).

forwardY.description: ellipsoid and box: forward direction Y

forwardZ.description: ellipsoid and box: forward direction Z

upX.description: ellipsoid and box: optional world up reference, X. Defaults to (0,1,0).

upY.description: ellipsoid and box: optional world up reference, Y

upZ.description: ellipsoid and box: optional world up reference, Z

rings.description: sweep: ordered elliptical cross-sections defining one continuous void. Three or more rings give a passage that widens and narrows convincingly.

x.description: World X of the ring center, in meters

y.description: World Y of the ring center, in meters

z.description: World Z of the ring center, in meters

verticalRadius.description: Ring half-height in meters. Below the horizontal radius it reads as a bedding-plane crawl; above it, as a rift.

surface.description: Displacement character applied to the cut face before the boolean runs. Pick the one that matches what the volume is for; "none" leaves an analytic, machined-looking surface and is only right for engineered geometry.

noise.description: Relative cross-section roughness, 0 or more. 0 is smooth.

noiseScale.description: World-space wavelength of the close-surface roughness, in meters.

interior.description: Material classification for the faces this subtraction exposes.

tools.name: terrain_refine_density
tools.description: Locally raises mesh density on a terrain so a following sculpt stroke or CSG cut has enough vertices to resolve detail. Terrain starts at a density tuned for kilometre-scale relief, so fine work -- a cave mouth, a trail cut, a rock shelf -- needs refinement first or it will come out mushy. Use "tessellate" to subdivide in place, and "remesh" to rebuild the region at an even edge length when repeated sculpting has left stretched triangles. All distances are meters.

nodeId.description: Mesh terrain node ID. Omit when the scene contains exactly one mesh terrain.

mode.description: "tessellate" (default) subdivides existing triangles inside the sphere. "remesh" rebuilds them toward a uniform edge length, which also relaxes…

x.description: World X of the refinement sphere center, in meters

y.description: World Y of the refinement sphere center, in meters

z.description: World Z of the refinement sphere center, in meters

radiusMeters.description: Radius of the refined region in meters. Cover the whole area of the planned edit plus a margin.

targetEdgeLengthMeters.description: Desired triangle edge length in meters inside the region. A cave mouth wants roughly 0.5-2 m; a hillside 5-20 m. Smaller values cost geometry quickly.

tools.name: terrain_set_material_channels
tools.description: Renames, recolours, or sets roughness on a mesh terrain's four material channels. The channels are fixed at four and cannot be added to; this tool decides what they mean. Do this before painting so the channel names in `terrain_paint_weights` match the biome the user asked for.

nodeId.description: Mesh terrain node ID. Omit when the scene contains exactly one mesh terrain.

channels.description: The channels to change. Omit any channel to leave it as it is.

id.description: Which channel this entry configures

name.description: Display name, for example "Alpine Grass", "Scree", "Wet Sand"

color.description: Base colour as a hex string such as "#4f7d32"

roughness.description: Surface roughness 0-1. Rock and soil sit near 0.85-0.95; wet stone and packed snow sit lower, near 0.6-0.7.

tools.name: generate_street_grid
tools.description: Lays out a street grid: avenues, cross streets, junctions, kerbs and footways, conformed to the terrain. This is the ground a city stands on -- blocks and buildings are derived from it, so run this before either. Block proportion matters more than block size; the default 80m by 275m is roughly Manhattan, and long thin blocks are most of what makes a grid read as a city rather than as graph paper. Replaces any existing network.

columns.description: Blocks along x. 4 to 12 is a neighbourhood; above 20 gets heavy.

rows.description: Blocks along z.

blockWidth.description: Block interior width in meters, across the short side. Defaults to 80.

blockDepth.description: Block interior depth in meters, along the long side. Defaults to 275.

centerX.description: Grid centre x in world meters. Defaults to 0.

centerZ.description: Grid centre z in world meters. Defaults to 0.

arterialEvery.description: Every nth avenue is a wide arterial. Defaults to 4; 0 makes every street the same width, which reads flatter.

rotation.description: Rotation of the whole grid in degrees, so it need not align to the world axes.

tools.name: get_street_network
tools.description: Reports the street network: how many junctions and segments exist, the bounding extent, and a sample of segments with their widths and classes. Call before editing so changes are made against what is actually there.

tools.name: add_street
tools.description: Joins two junctions with a new street, creating either junction if it does not exist yet. Use it to extend a generated grid, cut a diagonal avenue across it, or build a network by hand. The road class sets width and footways unless overridden.

fromX.description: Start junction x in world meters.

fromZ.description: Start junction z in world meters.

toX.description: End junction x in world meters.

toZ.description: End junction z in world meters.

roadClass.description: arterial is a wide multi-lane avenue, street is the ordinary case, alley is narrow with no footways. Defaults to street.

width.description: Carriageway width in meters, kerb to kerb, overriding the class default.

sidewalkWidth.description: Footway width in meters per side. 0 removes footways.

tools.name: add_crosswalk
tools.description: Paints a zebra crossing across one existing street segment. Use get_street_network first to choose a segment. The crossing follows the compiled road surface and terrain.

segmentId.description: Source street segment that owns the crossing.

position.description: Position from 0 at the segment start to 1 at its end. Defaults to 0.5.

width.description: Crossing length along the street in metres. Defaults to 4.

tools.name: clear_street_network
tools.description: Removes every street and junction. The terrain and everything else in the scene are untouched.

tools.name: generate_city_massing
tools.description: Fills the street grid's blocks with building volumes. Divides each block into lots with street frontage, then extrudes each lot to a height, so buildings stand shoulder to shoulder along the street with a shared interior behind. This is the stage that decides a city's silhouette -- skyline, street wall, where the towers cluster -- and it renders as flat coloured boxes rather than finished facades. Requires a street network; run generate_street_grid first.

lotWidth.description: Target street frontage per building in meters. Defaults to 18. Smaller reads as townhouses, larger as apartment blocks.

lotDepth.description: How far back from the street a building reaches, in meters. Defaults to 24. Clamped so two rows on a shallow block cannot overlap.

minStoreys.description: Fewest storeys for a building at the edge of the city. Defaults to 2.

maxStoreys.description: Most storeys for a building at the centre. Defaults to 12.

storeyHeight.description: Floor-to-floor height in meters. Defaults to 3.4.

centerX.description: Where the tall buildings cluster, x in world meters. Defaults to 0.

centerZ.description: Where the tall buildings cluster, z in world meters. Defaults to 0.

falloffRadius.description: How far from the centre height falls off, in meters. Defaults to 400. Large values make the city uniformly tall.

setback.description: Extra gap between the footway and the building line, in meters. 0 (default) is a dense downtown; larger values suburbanise it.

seed.description: Seed for lot widths and heights. The same seed rebuilds the same city.

tools.name: clear_city_massing
tools.description: Removes every building volume, leaving the street network in place.

tools.name: generate_city_buildings
tools.description: Replaces the tallest massing volumes with real buildings: limestone banks, setback towers and corner headquarters, with colonnades, windows, cornices and roof equipment. Only a few dozen are generated because each costs around 140,000 triangles, so they stand as landmarks among the massing boxes rather than replacing all of them -- which is what a downtown looks like anyway. Requires massing; run generate_city_massing first.

count.description: How many landmarks to generate, tallest lots first. Defaults to 12. Above about 40 the viewport slows noticeably.

coverage.description: Fraction of lots to build instead of a fixed count, 0 to 1. Whichever of this and `count` is smaller wins. Defaults to 0.08.

seed.description: Seed for materials and proportions. The same seed rebuilds the same buildings.

tools.name: clear_city_buildings
tools.description: Removes the generated landmark buildings. The massing boxes they replaced come back, and streets are untouched.

tools.name: configure_forest_field
tools.description: Changes a forest field's shape and stand settings. `feather` is the number that matters most: it is the depth in meters over which the stand thins out at its boundary, and a hard edge is what makes a painted forest read as a decal rather than a place. Twenty to forty meters reads as a real wood; zero reads as a surveyed line. Marks the field dirty.

fieldId.description: Forest field ID. Omit when exactly one field exists.

preset.description: Change the stand type.

density.description: Multiplier on the preset's stems per hectare. 1 is the preset's own figure; fields open at 0.6 because a full-density stand over a couple of hundred…

feather.description: Meters the stand fades across at its boundary. 20-40 for a natural wood.

width.description: Half-width in meters of an open belt. Ignored when the field is a closed loop.

closed.description: Whether the spline encloses an area (true) or is a belt (false).

seed.description: Layout seed. Change it to reshuffle the same stand into a different arrangement.

visible.description: Whether the stand draws in the viewport.

tools.name: delete_forest_field
tools.description: Removes a forest field and the stand grown from it.

sites.name: wfsim.app
sites.description: A Warframe calculator that simulates the fight instead of estimating it — builder, simulator, optimizer. Every formula cites its source, and the golden tests are calibrated against real in-game runs.

tools.name: enemies_targets_list
tools.description: List the custom targets the reader has made, with the id a fight names each one by (simulator.scenario.set with patch {enemy: id}).

tools.name: enemies_target_new
tools.description: Make a blank custom target — a plain humanoid, every number meant to be replaced — and open it.

tools.name: enemies_target_copy
tools.description: Duplicate the open custom target and open the copy.

tools.name: enemies_target_open
tools.description: Open a custom target for editing, by the id enemies.targets.list gives it or by its name.

name.description: the target's id, or its name

tools.name: enemies_target_set
tools.description: Write fields of the open custom target: faction, scaling_faction, can_be_eximus, stats {base_level, health, shield, armor, overguard, affinity}, damage_modifiers (a column of multipliers by damage type, "faction" to start one from the faction's, or null for the faction's own), status_immunities (the types whose procs cannot land), body_parts [{name, multiplier, is_head, crit_bonus}].

damage_modifiers.description: an object of multipliers by damage type, "faction", or null

body_parts.description: every part, replacing the list; at least one

tools.name: builder_forma_read
tools.description: Read the Forma planner: its rules (catalyst, reach max rank, grant slot first, Omni and Umbra Forma use, a Forma limit), which saved builds are planned together with this one, and the board-reach analysis if it has been run.

tools.name: builder_forma_rules
tools.description: Change the Forma planner's rules — this browser's, for every build — which the Forma plan and the reach both obey. forma_limit is a whole number or null.

reach_max_rank.description: every mod reaches its max rank

grant_slot_first.description: fill the slot that grants capacity first

fixed_order.description: no mod is moved: each slot's polarity serves what every build keeps there

omni_forma.description: when Omni Forma may be used

umbra_forma.description: when Umbra Forma may be used

forma_limit.description: most Forma, or null for none

tools.name: builder_forma_partner
tools.description: Plan another saved build of this weapon together with the open one (on=true) or stop — the Forma plan then fits both on one set of polarities.

tools.name: builder_reach_run
tools.description: Work out what one polarity layout reaches across this weapon's board rulers, and what each extra Forma buys; optionally set the scope first. Returns the curve and, at the first point that meets the line, each ruler's best build that fits.

rulers.description: ruler ids to cover; omit for every ruler with rows

planned_builds_must_fit.description: the builds planned together must fit the layout too

line.description: the share of each ruler's leader to reach, e.g. 0.8

tools.name: builder_reach_mark
tools.description: Mark a point of the worked-out reach curve by its index, to read and apply that layout.

tools.name: builder_reach_apply
tools.description: Put the open build's slots on the marked point's polarities, as the planner's apply button does.

tools.name: builder_reach_save
tools.description: Save a ruler's best-fitting build at the marked point as a build of its own, on that point's polarities.

ruler_index.description: the ruler's index in the reach read

tools.name: simulator_arena_read
tools.description: Read the arena: where the player stands, the target (e1, the body the fight is scored against), every other body in the formation, where the player aims, and the gap to the target in metres. Coordinates are metres on the plane.

tools.name: simulator_arena_distance
tools.description: Put the target this many metres from the player (the gap between them; 0 is contact, where both boards are scored).

tools.name: simulator_arena_add
tools.description: Add bodies around the target, each of the fight's current enemy, in the first free places — the +1/+8 quick sets.

tools.name: simulator_arena_place
tools.description: Place one body of the fight's current enemy at a point (metres). Refused where it would overlap another body or the player, or when the floor is full.

tools.name: simulator_arena_remove
tools.description: Remove one body from the formation by its id. The target (e1) cannot be removed.

body.description: body id

tools.name: simulator_arena_reset
tools.description: Back to one body, aimed at the target — the fight the boards are measured under.

tools.name: simulator_arena_aim
tools.description: Aim at a point (metres) — aiming is a direction, and the shot hits the first body it crosses — or omit x and y to aim at the target.

tools.name: simulator_auras_list
tools.description: List the squad auras, which of them pay this weapon anything, which stack across the squad, and how many run each in this fight.

tools.name: simulator_aura_set
tools.description: Set how many of the squad run an aura (1 to 4 for one that stacks, else 1); 0 removes it. An aura is the fight's, never the build's.

tools.name: simulator_abilities_list
tools.description: List the Warframe abilities that can run in the fight as buffs, with each one's value at the fight's ability strength, its element choices, whether it is on, and whether a stronger one of its kind supersedes it.

tools.name: simulator_ability_set
tools.description: Run a Warframe ability as a buff for the whole fight (on=true) or stop it; where it offers one, choose its element.

tools.name: simulator_strength_set
tools.description: Override the Warframe's Ability Strength for the fight, in percent as the arsenal shows it; every ability buff scales with it. Without an override the fight reads the linked Warframe build's.

tools.name: simulator_nodes_list
tools.description: List the linked Operator's conditional Focus nodes — each one's id, what it does, its state (off, on = assumed up by the Operator build, sim = the fight's action list performs it) and whether the fight can simulate it.

tools.name: simulator_node_simulate
tools.description: Have the fight's action list perform an Operator node's action (simulated=true), or stop (false) — the node is then earned in the fight rather than assumed. Only a node simulator.nodes.list marks simulatable. Whether a node is assumed up is the reader's Operator build and not on the door.

node.description: the node's id

tools.name: simulator_triggers_list
tools.description: List the buff triggers the fight can switch off (a buff whose trigger is off never fires, though the run still does the action), by group, with which are off.

tools.name: simulator_trigger_set
tools.description: Switch a buff trigger off (off=true) or back on, or a whole group of them by the group's id.

id.description: trigger id or group id

off.description: true = buffs from it do not fire

tools.name: simulator_extra_set
tools.description: Set one of the fight's own stat bonuses — what the weapon is handed by something outside its build (a squad buff, another weapon's arcane). A percentage stat takes `percent` (into the same bucket a mod of that stat feeds); final_crit_damage (a multiplier, e.g. 1.6) and the two flat base damages (a number) take `value`. 0 or null clears it.

percent.description: for a percentage stat: e.g. 30 for +30%

value.description: for final_crit_damage (a multiplier, e.g. 1.6) or a flat base damage (a number)

tools.name: simulator_rules_list
tools.description: List the per-class rules a fight may make — what the simulator simplifies for a whole weapon class — with each one's default and this fight's value.

tools.name: simulator_rule_set
tools.description: Set a per-class rule for this fight, or null to fall back to the default. Only the pairs simulator.rules.list gives exist.

value.description: true/false or a number; null clears

tools.name: optimizer_plan_read
tools.description: Read the build search: its starts (each a build, with the positions fixed in its answer), its limits (what it may not use per axis — `card@rank` is one rank of a card — and how full it fills) how many builds it answers with and how many fights each candidate gets. Everything the limits leave is a candidate.

tools.name: optimizer_plan_limit
tools.description: Exclude an option from the search, or take it back: a mod as the builder lists it (`card@rank` for one rank of an every-rank card), an arcane, an evolution, a mode or a valence element. Nothing is excluded by default; the last mode or element cannot be.

id.description: the option's id

excluded.description: true excludes it, false takes it back

tools.name: optimizer_plan_fill
tools.description: Set how full the search fills: at most `mods` cards (0-8), whether the exilus is filled, and whether arcane seat `seat` (0-based) is filled.

mods.description: the most cards a build holds

tools.name: optimizer_plan_set
tools.description: Set how many builds the search answers with (the best N it scored, 1-100) and how many fights each candidate gets while the search compares them (1 or 10).

finalists.description: how many builds the search answers with

tools.name: rivens_cards_list
tools.description: List the rivens saved for this weapon's family, with the id builder.mod.set seats each one by.

tools.name: rivens_stats_list
tools.description: List the stats a riven for this weapon can roll, which can be the malus, which are modelled, and which are spliced (at most one a card).

tools.name: rivens_card_new
tools.description: Make a blank riven for this weapon's family and open it for editing.

tools.name: rivens_card_copy
tools.description: Duplicate the open riven and open the copy.

tools.name: rivens_card_open
tools.description: Open a saved riven for editing, by the id rivens.cards.list gives.

tools.name: rivens_card_set
tools.description: Write the open riven whole: its shape, each bonus and the malus by stat id with either the value printed on the card or a roll (0.9 to 1.1), its rank and polarity. Returns what the engine made of it — printed values, generated name, anything illegal.

shape.description: e.g. "3+1" (three bonuses and a malus) or "2+0"

bonuses.description: [{stat, value} or {stat, roll}], one per bonus

malus.description: {stat, value} or {stat, roll}; omit or null when the shape has none

tools.name: builder_wielders_list
tools.description: List who can hold this weapon: the Warframes allowed, each with the builds saved for it, and whether the unmodded Prototype (the board's floor) is allowed.

tools.name: builder_wielder_set
tools.description: Choose who holds the weapon: a Warframe unmodded, a Warframe with one of its saved builds, or frame=null for the Prototype. The wielder's abilities and stats change the weapon's numbers.

frame.description: Warframe id, or null for the Prototype

build.description: one of that frame's saved build ids

tools.name: builder_parts_list
tools.description: List a Kitgun's grips and loaders, with the pair installed now; read their numbers with builder.stats.read after installing.

tools.name: builder_part_set
tools.description: Swap a Kitgun's grip or loader. The chamber is the weapon itself; the other slot's version of the same chamber is another weapon id (builder.weapon.set).

part.description: grip or loader

id.description: the part's id

tools.name: optimizer_search_start
tools.description: Start a build search with the optimizer's current scope against the current fight. Returns at once; a search takes minutes — read its progress with optimizer.search.read.

tools.name: optimizer_search_read
tools.description: Read the build search: while it runs, how far along it is; once done, the ranked builds — each with the starts that settled on it (`from_starts`), or the answer it is nearest to and what differs (`near`).

limit.description: ranked builds to return, default 5

tools.name: optimizer_search_stop
tools.description: Stop the running build search. What it has ranked so far is kept.

tools.name: optimizer_result_save
tools.description: Save a ranked build from the last search as a new build preset (named opt N). Open it with shell.preset.open to measure it in the simulator.

tools.name: shell_presets_list
tools.description: List the saved builds or fight scenarios for this weapon, which one is open, and which are read-only (benchmarks).

tools.name: shell_preset_open
tools.description: Open a saved build or scenario by the id presets.list gives.

preset.description: preset id

tools.name: shell_preset_new
tools.description: Start a new blank build or scenario and open it; the one open before is kept as it was.

tools.name: shell_preset_read
tools.description: Read what a saved build holds — its mods, arcanes, evolutions and mode — by the id presets.list gives; the open one is read as it is on screen.

preset.description: preset id

tools.name: shell_preset_undo
tools.description: Undo the last change to a bar's documents — the build, the scenario, the search or the riven — or redo it with redo=true.

tools.name: shell_preset_copy
tools.description: Duplicate the open build or scenario and open the copy — the way to try changes without touching the reader's own.

tools.name: simulator_result_send
tools.description: Add the build the shown simulated fight measured — as it was when that run was sent, not as its preset stands now — to the optimizer's starts, and open the optimizer.

tools.name: simulator_result_read
tools.description: Read the last simulated fight for this build: the headline and whether it is still this build's, kills, time to kill, crit and headshot rates, and which damage sources dealt what share.

tools.name: builder_mods_find
tools.description: Find mods this weapon can seat, by name or effect; with a slot, only the ones that slot takes.

query.description: name or effect words, in any language the page speaks

limit.description: rows to return, default 12

tools.name: builder_arcanes_find
tools.description: Find the arcanes a seat of this weapon takes.

query.description: name or effect words, in any language the page speaks

limit.description: rows to return, default 12

tools.name: builder_evolutions_list
tools.description: List this weapon's Incarnon evolution tiers, their options, and which one each tier holds.

tools.name: builder_modes_list
tools.description: List how this weapon can be played, and why a mode is unavailable where it is.

tools.name: simulator_enemies_find
tools.description: Find targets for the fight by name, in any language the page speaks.

query.description: name or effect words, in any language the page speaks

limit.description: rows to return, default 12

tools.name: shell_module_open
tools.description: Open a module of the page, optionally on another weapon.

weapon.description: weapon id; defaults to the one already open

tools.name: builder_weapon_set
tools.description: Switch the builder to another weapon. Its own presets and fight come with it.

tools.name: builder_mod_set
tools.description: Seat a mod in a slot, or empty the slot with mod=null. A mod already seated elsewhere is exchanged with this slot, as it is when a reader picks it.

mod.description: mod id, or null to empty the slot

tools.name: builder_mods_clear
tools.description: Empty every mod slot, leaving the weapon bare.

tools.name: builder_polarity_set
tools.description: Set a slot's polarity, or remove it with polarity=null. The mod in the slot stays.

tools.name: builder_forma_plan
tools.description: Re-polarize the slots for the fewest Forma that fit the seated mods, as the auto button does.

tools.name: builder_arcane_set
tools.description: Seat an arcane, or empty the seat with arcane=null. Only arcanes this weapon's seat takes are accepted.

seat.description: arcane seat, 0 unless the weapon has two

tools.name: builder_evolution_set
tools.description: Install an Incarnon evolution in a tier. Every tier always holds one, so this swaps it.

tools.name: builder_mode_set
tools.description: Choose how the build is played — the weapon's firing mode or form.

mode.description: mode id

tools.name: builder_valence_set
tools.description: An adversary weapon's valence: its element and its bonus as a fraction of base damage (clamped to what a Lich can roll).

tools.name: simulator_scenario_set
tools.description: Change fields of the fight — the enemy, its level, the duration, the metric. Fields that are not a single value (the formation, the buffs) have their own editors and are refused here.

tools.name: simulator_runs_set
tools.description: How many times the simulator replays the fight. A preference of this browser, not part of the fight.

tools.name: simulator_run_start
tools.description: Run the fight and return the headline number. Takes as long as the reader's own run takes.

tools.name: simulator_shapley_parts
tools.description: List the parts of the open build a Shapley analysis can switch off, with the key each is chosen by and whether it is chosen now.

tools.name: simulator_shapley_run
tools.description: Run the Shapley analysis on the current fight: every subset of the chosen parts is simulated, and each part's equivalent multiplier, its take-it-out and alone effects, and every pair's interaction come back in log space. 2^k fights, so it can take minutes.

parts.description: comma-separated keys from simulator.shapley.parts; omitted keeps the current choice

runs.description: runs per subset; omitted keeps the reader's

tools.name: simulator_roster_read
tools.description: Read who is firing: the open build as seat 1, and every other seat the fight holds as a weapon and the preset of it that is acting.

tools.name: simulator_roster_add
tools.description: Put another gun in the fight — a squadmate, a companion or a summon. It acts on its own clock with its own build, and the result reports each seat separately. Omit preset for the weapon unmodded.

preset.description: a saved build of that weapon, by name

tools.name: simulator_roster_remove
tools.description: Take one seat out of the fight, by its number. Seat 1 is the open build and cannot be removed.

seat.description: seat number, as roster.read reports it

tools.name: builder_weapons_find
tools.description: Find weapons by name, in any language WFSim speaks.

query.description: name words, in any language WFSim speaks

limit.description: rows to return, default 12

tools.name: builder_board_read
tools.description: Read a weapon's leaderboard: the measured best builds per ruler (the benchmark fight), mode, and with or without a riven, ranked. Each row carries the link that opens it, and a riven-free row its `build`, which the stats read takes. A row's key opens it with shell.preset.open (bar "build").

weapon.description: weapon id; on the page, the one open when omitted

mode.description: only this mode id

limit.description: rows per group, default 3

distinct.description: one row per place, its preferred build; `limit` counts places

tools.name: builder_stats_read
tools.description: Read the stats panel for a build: every stat per form and part, base and final, with the mod each change came from, and what the weapon's model does not cover.

build.description: the build: {weapon, mods: [mod ids], arcane: [arcane ids], evolutions: [ids], mode} — a board row's `build` is one; on the page, the one on screen when omitted

tools.name: builder_rivens_read
tools.description: The Riven Analyst: each riven the board measured for a weapon, its best score against the #1 riven-free build of the same ruler and mode — what the riven is worth. Only submitted rivens appear.

weapon.description: weapon id; on the page, the one open when omitted

mode.description: only this mode id

bonuses.description: stat ids each riven has as bonuses

malus.description: the malus: a stat id, "any" or "none"

pooled.description: a ruler's modes as one ranking

tools.name: shell_method_read
tools.description: How WFSim judges a build: each rule, why it holds, how to apply it, and the readings behind it. Read it before comparing builds or explaining why one is better.

concept.description: one rule's id; every rule when omitted
