sites.name: flow-studio-app.netlify.app
sites.description: Use the Godot Engine editor directly in your web browser, without having to install anything.

tools.name: godot_get_session_status
tools.description: Returns live diagnostics for Godot WebEditor runtime, WebMCP native discovery, session revision, and WebGL health

tools.name: godot_restore_project_session
tools.description: Restores the persisted authoritative project into a fresh Godot Editor process after a page reload without changing scene revision or undo history

tools.name: godot_list_saved_projects
tools.description: Lists the projects kept in this browser, newest first. Every acknowledged persist writes a row keyed by project name, so a project you stopped working on can be returned to instead of being overwritten by the next one. Reports name, main scene, revision, file count, and when it was last saved.

tools.name: godot_open_saved_project
tools.description: Opens a project kept in this browser by name, replacing the editor with it. The current project is persisted to the library first, so switching away never loses it. Restores that project's files, main scene, and revision; undo history is session state and does not travel with the library row.

tools.name: godot_import_asset
tools.description: Imports a binary asset - image, font, audio (.wav/.ogg/.mp3), or model (.glb/.gltf) - into the RUNNING Godot editor and makes it loadable, without restarting. Supply the bytes as content_base64, or a public http(s) url to fetch (the server fetches it, because this page is cross-origin isolated and cannot; the URL must end in an importable extension and must not resolve to a private address). The asset becomes a real project file: it survives editor restarts and is included in godot_export_zip. Place an imported model into a scene with godot_node_instance. Reports what Godot confirmed - that it sees the file, its size on disk, and whether it imported into a loadable resource - rather than assuming the write succeeded.

path.description: Project-relative or res:// path, for example sfx/pickup.wav. Omit it when passing a url and the file name from the url is used.

content_base64.description: Base64 of the raw file bytes. Give this or url, not both.

url.description: http(s) URL of an asset to fetch and import. Fetched by the server, not the browser, and only from a public address; the URL must end in an importable extension.

reimport.description: Ask Godot to import it into a loadable resource

tools.name: godot_get_user_focus
tools.description: Reports what the human is currently pointed at in the editor: which nodes they have selected, which workspace they are in, which script is open and at what line, and which scene is being edited. Use it to resolve a pronoun - "make this taller", "rename that" - instead of asking which node was meant. Reports selection_count 0 rather than guessing when nothing is selected, and is read-only: it never changes the selection or the workspace.

tools.name: godot_adopt_open_project
tools.description: Adopts the project Godot currently has open into this browser's project library, without restarting the editor. Use it when the editor is holding a project the bridge did not create - one made through Godot's own project manager - which otherwise cannot be listed, reopened, or persisted. Reads the open project's text files back out of the editor filesystem and publishes them as the active project. Binary assets are named in skipped_files rather than carried, because the bridge's project model is text; the WebMCP addon itself is never adopted.

project_name.description: Overrides the name; defaults to the project's own application/config/name

tools.name: godot_get_operation_status
tools.description: Returns status and final results for long-running authoring operations that outlive a browser tool-call deadline

operation_id.description: Specific operation ID; omit to inspect the active and recent operations

after_sequence.description: Return immediately if operation sequence is newer than this value

wait_ms.description: Max ms to wait for a change before returning

tools.name: godot_author_3d_runner
tools.description: Transactionally authors the complete Neon Skyrail 3D runner with chase camera, elevated skyrail, 8 coral hazards, 11 energy pulses, and Dawn Gate

idempotency_key.description: Unique mutation key

tools.name: godot_synthesize_audio_suite
tools.description: Procedurally synthesizes a 6-piece 16-bit PCM sound suite in the browser, with duration, loudness and MIT licence metadata. By default this only returns previews: pass import_into_project to write them into the project as ordinary .wav files, imported by Godot like any other asset, plus an sfx_library.gd convenience wrapper. They appear in the FileSystem dock, load() returns an AudioStreamWAV, and they can be assigned to an AudioStreamPlayer in the Inspector. Reports per-file what Godot confirmed - that it imported and is loadable - rather than what was written.

import_into_project.description: Also write the suite into the running editor and import it

directory.description: Project-relative folder for the imported files

tools.name: godot_semantic_playtest_step
tools.description: Executes a semantic playtest action (steer_left, steer_right, jump, boost, observe_state, restart_playtest) and returns structured telemetry

tools.name: godot_get_game_telemetry
tools.description: Reads project-owned runtime telemetry emitted as godot-game-telemetry events; never substitutes simulated state for custom games

tools.name: godot_export_zip
tools.description: Packages the active project and an explicit per-file provenance manifest into a standard downloadable ZIP archive

provenance.description: Optional map of project paths to source/license/author/url metadata

tools.name: godot_begin_project_upload
tools.description: Begins a transport-safe staged custom-project upload; send each file through bounded sequential chunks before committing

tools.name: godot_upload_project_file_chunk
tools.description: Appends one bounded UTF-8 or base64 chunk to a staged project file using an exact decoded-byte offset

tools.name: godot_upload_project_chunk_batch
tools.description: Atomically appends up to four transport-safe project chunks in one call, with a 2 MiB decoded batch limit

tools.name: godot_get_project_upload_status
tools.description: Inspects staged project upload progress without returning uploaded contents

tools.name: godot_abort_project_upload
tools.description: Removes one staged project upload and all of its persisted chunks without changing the active Godot project

tools.name: godot_commit_project_upload
tools.description: Validates and transactionally boots a completed staged project through the same acknowledged custom-project authoring path

tools.name: godot_create_project
tools.description: Creates a Godot project from a built-in template or an explicit file set, and REPLACES the running editor to open it. Because that takes several seconds it may return {status: 'pending', operation_id} instead of a result - poll godot_get_operation_status until it reports succeeded before calling any other tool, or the next call will be refused while the editor is being torn down. Audio is never staged into a project: add it afterwards with godot_synthesize_audio_suite, and other assets with godot_import_asset.

template.description: orbital_garden is a 3D sanctuary with a CharacterBody3D player and camera; neon_skyrail_3d is a 3D endless runner; arcade_2d is a side-on 2D scene with a CharacterBody2D runner, ground and camera; custom requires files.

files.description: Custom dictionary of file paths to source strings/buffers to write into res://

tools.name: godot_inspect_project_files
tools.description: Inspects the authoritative in-memory project manifest and optionally returns selected text source files for revision-safe editing

tools.name: godot_inspect_scene_graph
tools.description: Returns the durable authored Godot scene graph so collaborators can verify which visible objects are editable in the 3D editor, rather than runtime-only script output

tools.name: godot_apply_file_transaction
tools.description: Revision-checked atomic project edit. Eligible GDScript-only writes use the running editor hot channel; deletes and other project-file edits replace the editor. It commits only after the applicable acknowledgement and records an undo snapshot.

tools.name: godot_apply_script_patch
tools.description: Revision-checked GDScript creation or exact-patch editing applied to the RUNNING Godot editor without replacing it. Copies candidate bytes into the live editor filesystem, has Godot refresh and recompile the script on a deferred editor frame, and publishes only after Godot acknowledges the path, source hash, and compilation. A compile failure restores the previous bytes and leaves the revision untouched. It never launches the game or restarts the editor. With workspace follow enabled it opens the Script workspace at the changed lines; with follow disabled it preserves the current workspace and only reveals the file in the FileSystem dock. Reports changed line ranges, before/after hashes, compilation result, diagnostics, persistence, navigation, and preview freshness as independent facts.

path.description: res:// path of the .gd script to create or edit.

content.description: Complete script source. Use for creation or full replacement; mutually exclusive with patches.

patches.description: Exact search/replace patches applied to the existing script source.

attach_to_node_path.description: Optional scene-relative node path to attach the script to through the editor UndoRedo stack.

attach_scene_path.description: Scene whose authoritative .tscn source records the attachment. Defaults to the main scene.

tools.name: godot_apply_text_patch
tools.description: Applies exact revision-checked search/replace patches to project text files, then delegates to the same acknowledged editor/runtime transaction and undo path

tools.name: godot_undo_transaction
tools.description: Restores the exact project snapshot captured by the most recent acknowledged authoring transaction. Hot GDScript transactions undo through the running editor without a restart; transactions that changed other project files may replace the editor.

tools.name: godot_select_node_live
tools.description: Selects a node in the live Godot Editor scene dock through the WebMCP editor command channel. Fails explicitly when the channel is unavailable; never fabricates selection success.

tools.name: godot_transform_node_live
tools.description: Transforms a node in the live Godot Editor through the editor command channel and its UndoRedo stack. Viewport-only: it does not rewrite the .tscn text — use godot_node_transform for a transform that persists to source.

tools.name: godot_connect_signal_live
tools.description: Connects a signal on the live scene - Area3D body_entered to a handler, Timer timeout to a callback - through Godot's own undo stack, and records it in the scene source as a [connection] entry. The target method must already exist on the receiving node's script: a connection to a missing method is refused by name here, because Godot would accept it and then only warn at load. Applied without restarting the editor.

to_node.description: Node whose script has the handler (defaults to the scene root)

method.description: Method on to_node to call

tools.name: godot_inspect_property_live
tools.description: Reads a live Inspector property from the edited scene through the editor command channel. Omit `property` to list the editable property names of the node.

tools.name: godot_generate_audio_fx
tools.description: Synthesizes procedural 16-bit WAV sound effects (laser, explosion, pickup) and writes them to res:// .wav

tools.name: godot_switch_mode
tools.description: Switches the visible Godot main-screen workspace. Reports which workspace the editor is actually showing afterwards, read back from the visible editor control, rather than echoing the request - a switch that did not take says so.

mode.description: Which main-screen editor to show

tools.name: godot_open_scene
tools.description: Opens a res:// scene in the live Godot Editor through the editor command channel. This changes the edited scene only; use godot_apply_file_transaction to change project.godot run/main_scene.

tools.name: godot_node_set_property
tools.description: Sets one property on a node in the edited scene - light energy, camera fov, a body's mass, gravity_scale, visible - through Godot's own undo stack, and reads the value back from the node afterwards. Primitives, Vector2/Vector3 and Color only: a property that holds a resource is refused by name, because setting one blind is how a scene ends up looking right and being wrong. Use godot_node_material for materials and godot_node_transform for position, rotation and scale. This edits the EDITOR scene; it does not reach into a running game.

node_path.description: Path or name of the node

property.description: Property name as Godot spells it, for example light_energy

value.description: Number, boolean, string, [x, y], [x, y, z], or a #rrggbb colour

tools.name: godot_run_game
tools.description: Runs the project in the WebGL Game viewport

tools.name: godot_stop_game
tools.description: Stops the running game and returns to the editor

tools.name: godot_send_input
tools.description: Dispatches a keyboard event to the game canvas and reports any subsequent project-owned telemetry without claiming unverified gameplay acknowledgement

key.description: DOM KeyboardEvent name, used as both `key` and `code`: ArrowUp, ArrowDown, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Space, Enter, KeyW, KeyA, KeyS, KeyD. Godot's default ui_* actions are the arrow keys and Space.

target.description: Which Godot canvas to address. 'auto' follows the visible tab.

tools.name: godot_send_input_sequence
tools.description: Schedules a bounded timeline of keyboard down/up edges in one call for chords, diagonals, jumps, dodges, and other coordinated controls

key.description: DOM KeyboardEvent name, used as both `key` and `code`: ArrowUp, ArrowDown, ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Space, Enter, KeyW, KeyA, KeyS, KeyD. Godot's default ui_* actions are the arrow keys and Space.

target.description: Which Godot canvas to address. 'auto' follows the visible tab.

tools.name: godot_get_input_sequence_status
tools.description: Returns planned and actual dispatch timing for one coordinated keyboard sequence, or recent sequences when no ID is supplied

tools.name: godot_capture_viewport
tools.description: Captures the pixel buffer of the editor viewport or the running playtest canvas as a base64 PNG data URL

target.description: Which Godot canvas to address. 'auto' follows the visible tab.

tools.name: godot_send_pointer
tools.description: Dispatches mouse/pointer input at Godot canvas coordinates and reports dispatch geometry without claiming unverified gameplay acknowledgement

target.description: Which Godot canvas to address. 'auto' follows the visible tab.

tools.name: godot_start_recording
tools.description: Starts a real MediaRecorder capture of the visible Godot game canvas; optionally auto-stops and persists after a bounded duration

mime_type.description: Optional MediaRecorder MIME override, for example video/webm or video/webm;codecs=vp8,opus

duration_ms.description: Optional in-page auto-stop duration for precise persistence without a second Browser round trip

tools.name: godot_stop_recording
tools.description: Stops the active canvas recording, persists the WebM blob in IndexedDB, and exposes a durable download link in the viewport

tools.name: godot_list_recordings
tools.description: Lists recordings persisted for this deployed origin and restores a visible download link for the newest artifact

tools.name: godot_get_logs
tools.description: Retrieves engine logs and stdout telemetry

tools.name: godot_diagnose_session
tools.description: Diagnoses current-generation Godot logs and recovery state into structured platform, project-source, persistence, lifecycle, and fatal-engine issues. Reports ownership, impact, evidence, and only remedies the agent can safely perform; read-only and never mutates the project.

since_ms.description: Optional lookback window in milliseconds. Omit to inspect the full current editor generation.

tools.name: godot_camera_focus
tools.description: Transient viewport-only framing: selects a node, dispatches Godot's own spatial_editor/focus_selection so the editor camera eases to it, and anchors the on-page focus reticle to the node's projected screen position. Reports what it measured, not what it attempted: status is 'framed' only when the viewport pose actually changed, 'dispatched_unconfirmed' when the shortcut was delivered but the camera did not move (Godot only advances camera interpolation while rendering, so a backgrounded tab reports this), 'overlay_only' without the editor plugin, or 'yielded' during the 750 ms cooldown after user input. target_reached additionally requires the node to project inside the frame. Never mutates scene JSON, advances scene_revision, creates an undo entry, triggers autosave, or survives a project reload. Yields to the user for 750 ms after any pointer, wheel, or key input on the viewport.

node_path.description: Node name or scene-relative path to frame

tools.name: godot_camera_follow
tools.description: Enables or disables automatic camera follow for this browser session. When enabled, a geometry change (node added, moved, or deleted) queues exactly one coalesced framing move; material-only changes never move the camera. The preference is stored in sessionStorage and is also exposed as the Auto follow control in the page rail.

enabled.description: Omit to read the current preference without changing it

tools.name: godot_workspace_follow
tools.description: Enables or disables visible workspace following for this browser tab, and chooses how strongly a script edit follows. In mode 'file' (the default) a script edit never takes the screen: the changed file is revealed in the FileSystem dock and the current workspace is preserved. In mode 'script' a script edit also opens the Script workspace at the changed lines. 3D node changes switch to the 3D workspace and select the edited node in both modes. The state is persisted in sessionStorage and mirrored by the Follow agent control.

enabled.description: Omit to read the current preference without changing it

mode.description: 'file' reveals the edited script in the FileSystem dock and leaves the workspace alone; 'script' opens the code at the changed lines

tools.name: godot_node_spawn
tools.description: Adds a 3D mesh node with position, rotation, scale, and material to the live scene. This is visual geometry only: it has no collision, so nothing stands on it and nothing collides with it. Use godot_node_body for floors, walls, solid props and trigger volumes, and godot_node_instance to place an imported model. Applied through the editor command channel without restarting the engine when the WebMCP editor plugin is present; otherwise falls back to a full editor restart. Reports the measured elapsed time and which channel was used.

size.description: Vector3 dimensions [x, y, z] for box/prism

position.description: 3D position coordinates [X, Y, Z]

tools.name: godot_node_spawn_2d
tools.description: Adds a 2D node to the live scene: a coloured rect, a label, a polygon, a line, or a sprite from an imported texture. Positions are in pixels with +Y downward, which is Godot's 2D convention and the opposite of the 3D tools. Use godot_node_body_2d for anything that needs collision. Applied through the editor command channel without restarting the engine. Requires a 2D scene open - create one with the arcade_2d template or godot_open_scene.

position.description: Pixel position [x, y], +Y downward

color.description: Hex colour, for rect / polygon / line

text.description: Text, for label

points.description: Points [[x, y], ...] for polygon and line

texture.description: res:// path of an imported texture, for sprite

tools.name: godot_node_body_2d
tools.description: Adds a 2D physics body with a collision shape - and by default a matching coloured rect - to the live scene. Static for level geometry, rigid for something that falls, character for something a script drives, area for a trigger. Positions are in pixels with +Y downward. The body, its collider and its rect are created in one undo action. Applied through the editor command channel without restarting the engine.

name.description: Unique name of the body node

size.description: Pixel size [w, h], for a rect shape

radius.description: Radius in pixels, for circle and capsule

visible_rect.description: Set false for an invisible collider or trigger

position.description: Pixel position [x, y], +Y downward

tools.name: godot_node_body
tools.description: Adds a physics body with a collision shape - and, by default, a matching visible mesh - to the live 3D scene. This is what a floor, a wall, a solid prop or a pickup trigger needs: godot_node_spawn creates visual geometry only, so nothing stands on it and nothing collides with it. Choose static for level geometry, rigid for something that falls and is pushed, character for something a script drives, area for a trigger volume that detects overlap without blocking. The body, its collider and its mesh are created in one undo action and move together as one node. Applied through the editor command channel without restarting the engine when the plugin is present.

name.description: Unique name of the body node

body_type.description: static = immovable level geometry; rigid = simulated, falls and is pushed; character = script-driven; area = trigger volume that detects overlap without blocking

mesh_type.description: Shape of both the collider and the visible mesh. prism and torus are not offered: they have no analytic collision shape.

size.description: Vector3 dimensions [x, y, z] for box; [width, depth] for plane

thickness.description: Slab thickness for a plane floor. A zero-thickness floor lets fast bodies tunnel through it.

visible_mesh.description: Set false for an invisible collider or trigger volume

position.description: 3D position coordinates [X, Y, Z]

tools.name: godot_node_instance
tools.description: Places an imported model or saved scene into the live 3D scene as a child node: a .glb or .gltf imported with godot_import_asset, or a .tscn already in the project. Use this for anything that came from an asset file - godot_node_spawn only builds Godot's own primitive meshes and cannot place a model. The instantiated node moves, rotates and scales like any other node via godot_node_transform, and its own sub-nodes belong to the imported scene, so they are reported rather than editable from here. Applied through the editor command channel without restarting the engine when the plugin is present.

name.description: Unique name for the new node in this scene

scene_path.description: res:// path of the model or scene to instantiate, for example res://models/crystal.glb

position.description: 3D position coordinates [X, Y, Z]

tools.name: godot_node_transform
tools.description: Translates, rotates, or scales a 3D node in the live editor scene. Applied through the editor command channel without restarting the engine when the WebMCP editor plugin is present; otherwise falls back to a full editor restart.

node_path.description: Path or name of the node in the scene tree

position.description: New position coordinates [X, Y, Z]

rotation.description: New rotation angles in degrees [Pitch, Yaw, Roll]

relative.description: If true, offsets existing transform instead of setting absolute values

tools.name: godot_node_material
tools.description: Updates the albedo, metallic, roughness, and emissive properties of a 3D node material. Applied through the editor command channel without restarting the engine when the WebMCP editor plugin is present; otherwise falls back to a full editor restart. Material changes never move the camera.

node_path.description: Path or name of the node

tools.name: godot_node_delete
tools.description: Removes a 3D node from the live scene tree. Applied through the editor command channel without restarting the engine when the WebMCP editor plugin is present; otherwise falls back to a full editor restart.

node_path.description: Path or name of the node to remove

sites.name: seqcraft.onrender.com
sites.description: Inspect plasmids, simulate PCR and restriction digests, compare constructs, and prepare cloning proposals in one exact, private workspace.

tools.name: seqcraft_get_capabilities
tools.description: Discover SeqCraft scientific workflows, coordinate conventions (1-based closed [start1, end1]), privacy boundaries, approval rules, and suggested agent task sequences. Use this when planning a multi-step interaction or deciding which SeqCraft tools to call.

tools.name: seqcraft_get_workspace_context
tools.description: Read the current SeqCraft workspace state, including the active molecule, current selection, selected feature, pending transaction state, active view, and registered tool count. Preferred bootstrap tool for any task involving SeqCraft.

includeDocumentList.description: Whether to include a list of all open document names, IDs, lengths, and topologies in the workspace.

tools.name: seqcraft_get_selected_context
tools.description: Read the currently selected nucleotide sequence slice and overlapping biological features in 1-based closed coordinates. Use this to inspect what the human user or current selection is highlighting without retrieving the entire molecule.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses the currently selected or active construct.

tools.name: seqcraft_get_document_revision
tools.description: Query the current revision number and canonical SHA-256 sequence hash of a document. Essential for revision-locking proposals, avoiding race conditions, and verifying mutation commits.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, checks the active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_get_transaction_status
tools.description: Check the lifecycle state (awaiting_approval, applied, rejected, or stale) and provenance of a staged sequence transaction. Call this after staging an edit with seqcraft_edit_sequence or candidate staging tools to check if the human approved the change.

transactionId.description: Identifier of the staged transaction to inspect. If omitted, inspects the current pending transaction.

tools.name: seqcraft_get_pending_transaction
tools.description: Check the lifecycle state (awaiting_approval, applied, rejected, or stale) and provenance of a staged sequence transaction. Call this after staging an edit with seqcraft_edit_sequence or candidate staging tools to check if the human approved the change.

transactionId.description: Identifier of the staged transaction to inspect. If omitted, inspects the current pending transaction.

tools.name: seqcraft_set_active_document
tools.description: Switch the active document tab in the SeqCraft workspace. Use this when you want to view, inspect, or edit a different open construct.

documentId.description: ID of the open document to activate.

tools.name: seqcraft_set_active_view
tools.description: Switch the primary workspace visualization view tab. Available views: map (plasmid/linear map), sequence (base-level nucleotide editor), features (annotation table), primers (primer design panel), enzymes (restriction digests), history (revision log), compare (sequence comparison/diff).

view.description: The target workspace representation view.

tools.name: seqcraft_select_range
tools.description: Select a continuous range of nucleotides on the active or specified molecule using 1-based closed coordinates [start1, end1]. Updates the visible editor selection for human and agent context sharing.

documentId.description: Target document ID. If omitted, uses the active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_select_sequence_range
tools.description: Select a continuous range of nucleotides on the active or specified molecule using 1-based closed coordinates [start1, end1]. Updates the visible editor selection for human and agent context sharing.

documentId.description: Target document ID. If omitted, uses the active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_select_feature
tools.description: Select an existing biological feature/annotation on the active or specified document by its unique feature ID. Highlights the feature in the viewer and opens its properties in the inspector.

documentId.description: Document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_clear_selection
tools.description: Clear the active range selection and unselect any highlighted features or primers in the SeqCraft workspace.

tools.name: seqcraft_focus_region
tools.description: Navigate, scroll, and center the editor view around a specific nucleotide region using 1-based closed coordinates [start1, end1]. Optionally selects the region or switches representation.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

preferredView.description: Optional preferred editor view (e.g. sequence or map).

tools.name: seqcraft_list_documents
tools.description: List all sequence constructs/documents currently loaded in the SeqCraft workspace with their IDs, names, topologies, lengths in base pairs, and revision numbers.

tools.name: seqcraft_get_active_document
tools.description: Retrieve summary details, topological properties, annotations count, primers count, and revision metadata for the active or specified document.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, returns active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_create_document
tools.description: Create a new sequence document in the SeqCraft workspace from a nucleotide string. Validates sequence alphabet (DNA/RNA IUPAC).

sequence.description: Nucleotide sequence (5′→3′). Supports IUPAC degenerate bases.

tools.name: seqcraft_duplicate_document
tools.description: Create an independent, isolated working copy of an existing document. Useful for safe experimentation, staging edits without altering the original construct, and testing modifications.

documentId.description: Document to duplicate. If omitted, duplicates the active document.

newName.description: Optional name for the new copy. Defaults to "<Original Name> (Copy)".

tools.name: seqcraft_update_document_metadata
tools.description: Update metadata for a document, such as renaming it or changing its topology (linear circular).

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, updates the active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_delete_document
tools.description: Remove a document from the SeqCraft workspace. To prevent accidental deletion during exploration, you must explicitly set confirmDelete: true.

documentId.description: Identifier of the document to remove.

confirmDelete.description: Must be explicitly set to true to confirm deletion.

tools.name: seqcraft_edit_sequence
tools.description: Stage an insertion, deletion, or replacement on a DNA/RNA molecule using 1-based closed coordinates. Evaluates biological consequences (CDS frames, amino acid translations, restriction sites) and stages a revision-locked transaction for human review. Does NOT modify the molecule until the human clicks Apply. Follow up with seqcraft_get_transaction_status.

documentId.description: Target document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

operation.description: Structured sequence edit operation (insert, delete, or replace).

type.description: Edit operation type.

start1.description: 1-based start coordinate (for delete or replace operation).

end1.description: 1-based end coordinate (for delete or replace operation).

range1.description: Alternative legacy shorthand for replacement [start1, end1].

sequence.description: Alternative legacy shorthand for replacement sequence.

rationale.description: Biological rationale for the edit.

tools.name: seqcraft_reverse_complement_region
tools.description: Stage an in-place reverse complement of a sequence region [start1, end1] on the target molecule. Creates a revision-locked transaction for human review.

documentId.description: Target document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_rotate_origin
tools.description: Stage setting a new circular origin (position 1) on a circular plasmid. Re-indexes nucleotide coordinates and feature locations. Requires a circular topology and human review.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

newOrigin1.description: 1-based nucleotide position to become the new origin (position 1).

rationale.description: Biological rationale for the edit.

tools.name: seqcraft_list_features
tools.description: List all annotated biological features (CDS, promoters, genes, origins, resistance markers, tags) on the target construct with their coordinates [start1, end1], strand (+/-), type, and qualifiers.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, lists features for active document.

type.description: Optional filter by feature type (e.g. CDS, promoter, gene, origin).

tools.name: seqcraft_show_feature
tools.description: Highlight and focus a specific feature on the canvas / editor view and reveal its properties in the inspector panel.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

featureId.description: Unique identifier of the feature to display.

tools.name: seqcraft_mutate_feature
tools.description: Create, update, delete, or batch-create biological annotations on the active or specified construct using 1-based closed coordinates [start1, end1]. Immediately updates document annotations and records revision provenance.

documentId.description: Target document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

action.description: Annotation mutation action to perform.

feature.description: Single feature input for create or update action.

id.description: Feature ID (required for update).

type.description: Biological feature type.

strand.description: Strand orientation (+ for forward 5'->3', - for reverse complement).

qualifiers.description: Additional GenBank qualifiers (e.g. note, gene, product).

features.description: Array of feature inputs for batch_create action.

featureId.description: Feature ID to delete (for delete action).

tools.name: seqcraft_detect_known_features
tools.description: Scan the active or specified sequence against SeqCraft built-in curated biological feature library (promoters, origins, antibiotic resistance markers, reporters, tags). Returns identified matches with positions and confidence.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_propose_annotation
tools.description: Automatically detect and apply a known annotation match from the built-in database to the molecule.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

matchIndex.description: 0-based index of the detected feature match to apply.

tools.name: seqcraft_list_primers
tools.description: List all custom oligonucleotides and primers configured for the target molecule, including their sequences, lengths, and binding positions.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_mutate_primer
tools.description: Create, auto-bind, update, or delete primers on the construct. Action "add_from_sequence" automatically validates the primer, finds binding loci on the template molecule, and attaches the primer to the document.

documentId.description: Target document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

action.description: Primer mutation action.

sequence.description: 5'->3' primer nucleotide sequence (for create or add_from_sequence).

primerId.description: Existing primer ID (for update or delete).

tools.name: seqcraft_analyze_primer
tools.description: Compute melting temperature, GC content, molecular weight, and exact IUPAC-compatible binding loci on the template construct.

documentId.description: Template document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_simulate_pcr
tools.description: Simulate exact-match in silico PCR on a linear or circular template. Returns predicted amplicon coordinates, lengths, GC content, and primer-pair melting temperatures.

documentId.description: Template document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_analyze_restriction_sites
tools.description: Search for recognition and cut sites of standard restriction enzymes (Type II and Type IIS, e.g. EcoRI, BamHI, BsaI, BsmBI, NotI, HindIII) on the target molecule. Returns 1-based coordinates [start1, end1], forwardCut1, reverseCut1, and overhang types.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_show_restriction_site
tools.description: Highlight a restriction enzyme cut site on the map and editor view.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

view.description: Target editor view mode.

tools.name: seqcraft_simulate_digest
tools.description: Simulate single or multi-enzyme restriction digestion on a circular plasmid or linear DNA. Returns predicted fragment sizes, fragment sequences, and terminal overhang types.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

enzymeNames.description: Enzyme names for single or double digest.

tools.name: seqcraft_simulate_golden_gate
tools.description: Simulate Golden Gate multi-fragment assembly using Type IIS restriction enzymes (e.g. BsaI, BsmBI, AarI). Validates compatible overhang pairs, checks junction fidelity, and returns the assembled construct.

documentIds.description: List of document IDs participating in the assembly in order.

enzymeName.description: Type IIS enzyme driving the assembly (default: BsaI).

tools.name: seqcraft_domesticate_sequence
tools.description: Scan a sequence for internal Type IIS or standard restriction sites and return revision-bound synonymous mutation candidates to eliminate internal cut sites without altering protein translation. Follow up with seqcraft_stage_domestication_candidate to stage a proposal for human review.

documentId.description: Target document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_plan_domestication
tools.description: Scan a sequence for internal Type IIS or standard restriction sites and return revision-bound synonymous mutation candidates to eliminate internal cut sites without altering protein translation. Follow up with seqcraft_stage_domestication_candidate to stage a proposal for human review.

documentId.description: Target document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_stage_domestication_candidate
tools.description: Stage an exact synonymous mutation candidate returned by seqcraft_domesticate_sequence. Checks revision locking to ensure the molecule was not modified since analysis, then creates a revision-locked transaction for human review.

candidateId.description: The candidateId returned by seqcraft_domesticate_sequence.

documentId.description: Optional target document ID.

tools.name: seqcraft_stage_sequence_transaction
tools.description: Stage an exact synonymous mutation candidate returned by seqcraft_domesticate_sequence. Checks revision locking to ensure the molecule was not modified since analysis, then creates a revision-locked transaction for human review.

candidateId.description: The candidateId returned by seqcraft_domesticate_sequence.

documentId.description: Optional target document ID.

tools.name: seqcraft_prepare_restriction_clone
tools.description: Simulate restriction cloning between an insert construct and a destination vector using compatible restriction enzyme sticky ends.

tools.name: seqcraft_compare_documents
tools.description: Perform pairwise biological sequence comparison and alignment between two documents in the workspace. Returns identity percentage, nucleotide differences (substitutions, insertions, deletions), and feature discrepancies.

tools.name: seqcraft_find_orfs
tools.description: Search for open reading frames across all six reading frames using NCBI genetic code table 1 and a configurable minimum codon count.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

minCodons.description: Minimum ORF length in codons (default: 30 codons = 90 bp).

tools.name: seqcraft_find_crispr_targets
tools.description: Scan sequence for CRISPR-Cas guide RNA target sites and protospacers across multiple Cas effectors (SpCas9, SaCas9, Cas12a/Cpf1, Cas12e/CasX). Computes on-target quality scores, GC balance, Pol III termination penalties, and MMEJ frameshift predictions.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

nuclease.description: CRISPR Cas nuclease system (default: SpCas9). SpCas9 (3' NGG), SaCas9 (3' NNGRRT), Cas12a (5' TTTV), Cas12e (5' TTCN).

maxResults.description: Maximum number of target sites returned (default: 20).

tools.name: seqcraft_screen_biosecurity
tools.description: Run automated biosecurity reference pre-screening against diagnostic signature motifs of regulated Select Agents and Controlled Biological Toxins (Filoviruses, Poxviruses, Henipaviruses, Anthrax, Tularemia, Plague, BoNT, Ricin). Informational diagnostic screening only.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_copy_region_between_documents
tools.description: Extract a nucleotide region [sourceStart1, sourceEnd1] from a source construct and stage its insertion into a target construct at targetPosition1. Stages a revision-locked transaction on the target construct.

sourceStart1.description: 1-based inclusive start position on source document.

sourceEnd1.description: 1-based inclusive end position on source document.

orientation.description: Orientation of the copied fragment (default: forward).

tools.name: seqcraft_create_document_from_region
tools.description: Extract a nucleotide sub-region [start1, end1] from a construct and create a new independent construct in the workspace.

sourceDocumentId.description: Source document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

topology.description: Topology of the new document (default: linear).

tools.name: seqcraft_get_history
tools.description: Retrieve the change history log and undo/redo availability for the active or specified construct.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_undo
tools.description: Undo the most recent sequence edit on the active or specified construct in SeqCraft history.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_redo
tools.description: Redo the previously undone sequence edit on the active or specified construct in SeqCraft history.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, uses active document.

tools.name: seqcraft_restore_revision
tools.description: Stage restoration of a document to a historical snapshot in the undo stack. Stages a revision-locked transaction.

documentId.description: Target document ID.

historySnapshotIndex.description: 0-based index in the document undo stack to restore.

tools.name: seqcraft_import_sequence_text
tools.description: Import DNA/RNA sequence data into SeqCraft from FASTA, GenBank flat file, or raw sequence text. Creates and opens the construct(s) in the workspace.

content.description: Sequence file content (FASTA, GenBank flat file, or raw sequence text).

name.description: Optional override name for raw sequence inputs.

tools.name: seqcraft_export_document
tools.description: Export the active or specified construct to standard bioinformatic formats: GenBank flat file (including all features and annotations), FASTA, or SeqCraft JSON format. Returns generated text, filename, revision, and sequence hash.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, exports the active document.

format.description: Export format (default: genbank).

tools.name: seqcraft_export_sequence
tools.description: Export the active or specified construct to standard bioinformatic formats: GenBank flat file (including all features and annotations), FASTA, or SeqCraft JSON format. Returns generated text, filename, revision, and sequence hash.

documentId.description: Document identifier. If omitted, exports the active document.

format.description: Export format (default: genbank).

tools.name: seqcraft_search_sequence_database
tools.description: Search public biological sequence databases (NCBI Nucleotide / GenBank, RefSeq, ENA / EMBL-EBI, Addgene) for accession IDs, plasmid constructs, genes, or genomes matching a query. Returns compact candidate records with accession, title, organism, length in bp, and molecule type.

provider.description: Target database provider: 'ncbi' (GenBank/RefSeq), 'ena' (EMBL-EBI), or 'addgene'. Defaults to 'ncbi'.

query.description: Search term, organism, plasmid name, gene symbol, or keyword (e.g. 'pBR322', 'eGFP', 'lambda phage', 'cas9').

limit.description: Maximum number of candidate records to return (1-20). Defaults to 5.

tools.name: seqcraft_import_from_database
tools.description: Fetch and import an authoritative biological sequence from a public repository (NCBI Nucleotide / GenBank, RefSeq, ENA, Addgene) by accession ID into the SeqCraft workspace. Use this tool whenever the user references a known public accession (e.g. J01749.1, NC_001416.1, OQ870305.1) or asks SeqCraft to obtain a biological sequence from a public repository. Preserves sequence topology, GenBank annotations, and origin metadata.

provider.description: Target database provider: 'ncbi' (default), 'ena', or 'addgene'.

format.description: Format preference: 'genbank' (default, preserves annotations and features) or 'fasta'.

openAfterImport.description: Whether to activate and open the imported document in the workspace immediately. Defaults to true.

tools.name: seqcraft_generate_opentrons_protocol
tools.description: Compile a production-ready Python protocol for automated liquid handling on Opentrons OT-2 or Flex robots. Supports PCR master mix distribution and restriction digestion setups.

mode.description: Protocol type to generate (pcr or digest).

documentId.description: Target document ID. If omitted, uses active document.

ampliconLengthBp.description: Expected PCR amplicon length in base pairs.

enzymeNames.description: Restriction enzymes for digestion (for digest mode).

incubationTempC.description: Incubation temperature in Celsius for digest (default: 37).

tools.name: seqcraft_execute_actions
tools.description: Execute a batch of SeqCraft tool actions in sequential order. Rejects recursion. If any action stages a sequence mutation (status: awaiting_approval) or errors in stop_on_error mode, execution halts immediately without executing subsequent actions.

tool.description: Name of the tool to invoke.

actions.description: Ordered list of tool calls to execute.

mode.description: Execution mode (default: stop_on_error).

sites.name: estro-webmcp.vercel.app
sites.description: A photo editor that does not assume you know what saturation means. Describe what you want and an agent moves the real controls, then tells you which ones and what they do. Everything stays in your…

tools.name: get_capabilities
tools.description: Report what Estro can actually do in this browser right now, with import, decode, proxy, preview, video encode, audio encode, mux, worker, durable storage, and fallback support reported separately. Never changes a project.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the Estro projects in this browser, newest first, with the id every other tool needs. Start here: nearly every tool takes a projectId, and there is no other way to discover one. Reports whether each project holds an image document, sequences, or media, and whether it has an unsaved draft to recover, so a caller can pick the right one without opening each in turn. Never changes anything.

limit.description: How many projects to return.

query.description: Case-insensitive match against the project name.

kind.description: Only projects of this kind.

tools.name: inspect_project
tools.description: Inspect one local Estro project, its durable revision, recovery state, snapshots, media, sequences, and a bounded transaction history. This never mutates the project.

tools.name: manage_project
tools.description: Create, rename, duplicate, save, Save As, snapshot, or request deletion of a local Estro project. Deletion always pauses for visible user confirmation. Use create_sample when the user has no media of their own: a browser cannot open a file without a user gesture, so create_sample builds a photo project from a bundled photograph and returns its ids, giving you something real to edit in one call. Pass `sample` to choose which photograph; omit it for the first. Each was picked for a different problem, so choose the one whose difficulty matches what the user wants to learn to change.

sample.description: sindhudurg — Greens and a blue sky. Good for saturation and for seeing what temperature does. city — A blue cast over a busy street. The one to practise white balance on. deer — Mist, low contrast, almost no colour. Good for exposure and for shadows. quarry — Flat grey overcast with fine detail. Good for contrast and for sharpening.

expectedRevisionId.description: Refuse the command if the project has moved past this revision. Accepted by every operation except create.

tools.name: propose_transaction
tools.description: Validate and normalize an ordered Estro project transaction without mutating the project. The proposal expires and is bound to its source revision.

tools.name: apply_transaction
tools.description: Atomically apply one reviewed Estro proposal if its source revision is still current. A stale or invalid proposal changes nothing.

tools.name: inspect_transaction
tools.description: Explain one Estro transaction, including actor, intent, operations, warnings, source revision, resulting revision, and Undo identity.

tools.name: list_presets
tools.description: List reusable presets and project templates available here, with the attributes each carries, its version, and whether it ships with Estro. Never changes anything.

tools.name: save_preset
tools.description: Save a named, reusable bundle of attributes, either from an existing object or from explicit parameters. Re-saving an existing preset raises its version rather than replacing it silently. Presets that ship with Estro cannot be overwritten.

projectId.description: Set to keep the preset inside one project; omit to make it available everywhere.

presetId.description: Update this preset instead of creating a new one.

fromTargetId.description: Read the attributes from this object.

attributes.description: Which attribute names to take from the object.

parameters.description: Explicit attribute values, instead of reading an object.

expectedRevisionId.description: With fromTargetId: refuse if the project has moved past this revision, so the copied attributes are the ones you inspected.

tools.name: apply_batch
tools.description: Apply one bundle of attributes to many objects at once, from a preset or from explicit parameters. Plans by default: every target is costed and the result says which would change, which would not, and why. Set apply to true to commit, as a single transaction and a single Undo step. The failure policy decides whether a batch that cannot reach every target proceeds at all.

parameters.description: Explicit attribute values, instead of a preset.

tools.name: inspect_history
tools.description: Read a project's history: every transaction with its actor, intent, summary, affected objects, warnings, and revision pair, plus its named snapshots and which entries can be reverted on their own. Never changes anything.

tools.name: revert_transaction
tools.description: Revert one past change that need not be the most recent. Plans by default and reports whether the revert is safe, which later changes block it, and over which objects; set apply to true to commit it. The reversal is recorded as a new transaction, so history is never rewritten.

tools.name: undo_transaction
tools.description: Undo the latest safe Estro transaction by immutable transaction ID, or return a structured dependency conflict without changing the project.

expectedRevisionId.description: Refuse the undo if the project has moved past this revision.

tools.name: inspect_document
tools.description: Inspect the current image document, exact dimensions, resolution, background, stable ID, and project revision without changing project or workspace state.

tools.name: apply_document_operation
tools.description: Create one empty non-destructive image document in a photo or unassigned project through Estro's shared revision and Undo engine.

expectedRevisionId.description: Optional. Refuse if the project has moved past this revision.

tools.name: resize_document
tools.description: Resize the canvas frame or resample the whole image, with an explicit anchor, resampling algorithm, and aspect lock. Returns the normalized size, the algorithm actually used, the resampling job IDs it started, and any content that now falls outside the frame. A canvas resize reports no algorithm because it resamples nothing.

tools.name: inspect_workspace
tools.description: Inspect viewport, panels, overlays, tool, selection, preview quality, active sequence, monitor context, media view, comparison, and timeline view state. Never changes the project.

tools.name: set_workspace
tools.description: Set viewport, panels, dock, tool, overlays, guides, distraction-free mode, solo, isolate, preview quality, active sequence, monitor, source marks, media view, comparison, or timeline view. These are view changes and never create a project revision.

tools.name: inspect_selection
tools.description: Inspect the current selection, including multiple selected layers or clips, without changing it.

tools.name: set_selection
tools.description: Select the canvas, the document, one or more layers, clips, tracks, assets, sequences, or an output. Validated against what actually exists, and never changes project content.

tools.name: focus_ui
tools.description: Reveal and focus one stable semantic editor control so the user can see what an operation affected. Navigation only; it never changes project or workspace data.

tools.name: search_commands
tools.description: Search every manual editor command by name, category, shortcut, or keyword, with the semantic target each one acts on. Never changes state.

tools.name: inspect_assets
tools.description: Search the project's media with structured filters over kind, format, availability, editability, proxy state, duration, pixels, and bin. Returns stable IDs, technical metadata, and which fields matched. Never decodes media and never changes state.

tools.name: inspect_asset
tools.description: Inspect one asset by stable ID: detected container and streams, dimensions, duration, content hash, source revision, durability, editability, derivatives, and every layer, clip, and subclip that uses it.

tools.name: manage_asset
tools.description: Update tags, remove an asset through the shared Undo engine, re-check availability, or start a thumbnail, proxy, or waveform job. Importing and relinking files need the visible interface, because a browser only grants file access from a user gesture; those operations focus the right control and explain what to do.

candidates.description: For plan_relink: the files available to relink from, each {key, name, byteSize, contentHash}. A key is anything that identifies the file to you; Estro only matches on it.

expectedRevisionId.description: For remove: refuse if the project has moved past this revision.

tools.name: preview_revision
tools.description: Render a bounded preview of one asset at a named quality and return it with the exact project revision, source revision, and the derivative's real dimensions. This is a read: it never changes project state.

tools.name: inspect_organization
tools.description: Inspect bins, bin membership, storyboard positions, subclips, and source markers with stable IDs. Organization is project state, so it is versioned and undoable, but this call never changes it.

tools.name: manage_organization
tools.description: Create, rename, move, or delete bins; move items between bins; set storyboard positions; reorder items; create, rename, or delete subclips; and manage source markers. Each is one reversible project mutation that never changes where media lives.

tools.name: inspect_job
tools.description: Inspect one job or list a project's recent jobs, with monotonic status, stage, real progress when measurable, priority, warnings, failure codes, retry eligibility, derivative and output IDs, and whether it ran off the interface thread.

jobId.description: Inspect this one job.

projectId.description: List this project's recent jobs instead.

limit.description: With projectId: how many to list.

tools.name: manage_job
tools.description: Cancel a running job or retry one that failed, was cancelled, or was interrupted by a reload. Cancellation reaches the worker rather than only updating a record, and is idempotent.

tools.name: inspect_layers
tools.description: Inspect the document's layer stack: stable IDs, kind, nesting, visibility, lock, opacity, transform, crop, and active colour adjustments. Never returns pixels.

tools.name: apply_layer_operation
tools.description: Every edit to a photo layer, chosen with the operation field. Structure: add, remove, duplicate, reorder, group, ungroup, move between groups, rename, show, hide, lock. Placement: transform, crop, crop ratio, reset, quarter-turn, fit, fill, straighten, flip, align, distribute, free transform, perspective, warp, lens correction. Appearance: opacity, blend mode, clip to the layer below, masks, and an effect container holding exposure, levels, curves, vibrance, colour balance, selective colour, black and white, gradient map, photo filter, 3D LUT, shadows and highlights, replace colour, posterize, threshold, invert, equalize. Content: text, shapes, fills, adjustment layers, layer styles, brush and retouch strokes, keyframes. Everything is stored as settings and re-run at export size, so any of it can be changed or removed later. Each operation reads only the fields it needs; the rest are ignored. Alignment and grouping act only on the layers named.

content.description: Text content for add_text or a whole-block replacement.

range.description: Character range: start and end.

layout.description: Point text, or a paragraph box with a width and height.

shape.description: Rectangle, ellipse, polygon, or path commands.

paint.description: Fill paint for a fill layer: solid, gradient, or a swatch.

style.description: A layer style: kind is one of stroke, drop_shadow, inner_shadow, glow, overlay, plus that kind's own settings.

corners.description: Four corners in reading order — topLeft, topRight, bottomRight, bottomLeft — each {x,y} in document pixels. Null clears the correction.

sliders.description: Perspective as angles instead of corners: verticalDeg, horizontalDeg, rotationDeg, scale.

columns.description: Warp grid width.

rows.description: Warp grid height.

point.description: Moves one warp control point: column, row, and an offset {x,y} in fractions of the layer's size.

correction.description: Lens correction: distortion, distortionFine, chromaticAberration, vignette, each -1 to 1.

brush.description: Brush settings: kind (brush, pencil, eraser, clone, dodge, burn, sponge, blur, sharpen, smudge, red_eye), sizePx, hardness, flow, opacity, spacing, roundness, angleDeg, scatter. Only what is given changes.

cloneOffset.description: For a clone stamp: {x,y}, the distance from where it paints to where it reads. Required for clone.

strength.description: How strongly a retouching brush works. Not opacity: these change what is already there. Defaults to 0.5.

dynamics.description: What the pen drives: pressureToSize, pressureToOpacity, pressureToFlow, tiltToRoundness, rotationToAngle, velocityToSize, each 0 to 1.

points.description: Pointer samples: x, y, and optionally pressure, tiltDeg, rotationDeg, velocity. Pressure defaults to full, so a mouse draws at the brush's stated size.

selectionId.description: A saved selection the stroke or fill is confined to.

simplifyPx.description: Thins the points to the ones that describe the shape. 0 keeps every sample.

propertyPath.description: An animatable property, such as transform.x or opacity.

time.description: A rational time: numerator and denominator.

handles.description: Bezier control handles, for custom easing.

mask.description: Mask source, feather, density, inverted, and enabled.

parameters.description: Adjustment values for an effect or an adjustment layer.

profile.description: A camera profile or a creative look: id, name, kind ('camera' or 'creative'), and an ordered list of colour operations. Applied before everything else, so later edits are edits away from it. Its operations are copied onto the layer, so editing the profile later does not change photographs already developed with it.

remove.description: For apply_profile: removes the profile of that kind.

colourOperation.description: One tone or colour operator for an effect. `kind` is one of exposure, levels, curves, vibrance, colour_balance, selective_colour, black_and_white, channel_mixer, gradient_map, photo_filter, lut, shadows_highlights, replace_colour, posterize, threshold, invert, equalize, plus that kind's own settings. Replaces the operator whole on an update, because a curve and a lookup table share no fields.

tools.name: inspect_color_state
tools.description: Report every colour adjustment on a layer with its current value, documented range, unit, and a plain-language description. This never changes the project.

tools.name: apply_color_adjustment
tools.description: Set one colour adjustment on a layer using its documented range. Values outside the range are clamped and the clamp is reported rather than applied silently.

tools.name: inspect_histogram
tools.description: Measure the current visible composite and return binned tone distribution per channel with clipping diagnostics and a plain-language exposure reading. Returns summaries, never pixels.

tools.name: compare_revisions
tools.description: Resolve a before-and-after comparison to a real revision pair, either from a transaction or from a chosen baseline, and optionally set the interface's comparison mode. Returns identifiers, never pixels.

tools.name: explain_edit
tools.description: Explain a transaction, layer, clip, sequence, or colour parameter: what it does, its current value, the visible consequence, whether it can be undone, and where its control lives. This is a read and never changes the project.

tools.name: guided_step
tools.description: Return one step of a guided walkthrough with the real control to reveal and how to verify it. Teaching never performs the edit; the person stays in control, and every step points at a control the interface actually has.

tools.name: export_image
tools.description: Encode the current photo composite at a chosen format, quality, size, and resampling algorithm, and store it as a durable output. The reported size is measured by encoding, never estimated, and a substituted format is stated.

maxEdgePx.description: Longest edge in pixels, or null for full size.

expectedRevisionId.description: Refuse the export if the project has moved past this revision, so the file is of the picture you inspected.

tools.name: inspect_outputs
tools.description: List the project's finished deliveries with their kind, scope, source revision, preset, real format and settings, size, warnings, substitutions, job linkage, and whether their bytes are still stored.

tools.name: manage_output
tools.description: Reveal a finished output in the interface so the user can download it, or delete one permanently. Deleting an output removes its stored file and cannot be undone through project history, because outputs are deliveries rather than project state.

tools.name: select_region
tools.description: Choose the part of the image the next edit applies to. Tools: a rectangular or elliptical marquee, a freehand or polygonal lasso, a magic wand that spreads from one point by colour, a colour range or brightness range across the whole image, a layer's own transparency, or everything. Every tool supports replace, add, subtract, and intersect, so selections are built up rather than restarted. A selection is where the next edit lands, not an edit itself, so it does not appear in Undo; save it by name to keep it.

mode.description: How this combines with what is already selected. Defaults to replace.

source.description: Which tool, and its parameters. One of: {kind:'marquee',shape:'rectangle'|'ellipse',x,y,width,height,featherPx}, {kind:'lasso',points:[{x,y},…]}, {kind:'wand',x,y,tolerance,contiguous}, {kind:'colour_range',colour:'#rrggbb',tolerance}, {kind:'luminance_range',low,high,softness}, {kind:'layer_alpha',layerId}, {kind:'all'}.

tools.name: refine_selection
tools.description: Adjust the current selection: grow it, shrink it, soften its edge, smooth a ragged boundary, keep only a band along the edge, move it, or invert it. Also runs the whole refinement workspace in one pass when given smoothPx, featherPx, contrast, and shiftEdge together, which is how a difficult edge is cut without degrading the selection through repeated rounding.

operation.description: One of: {kind:'feather',radiusPx}, {kind:'expand',amountPx}, {kind:'contract',amountPx}, {kind:'smooth',radiusPx}, {kind:'border',widthPx}, {kind:'move',dx,dy}, {kind:'invert'}. Leave out to use the workspace sliders instead.

contrast.description: Positive hardens the edge, negative softens it, without moving it.

shiftEdge.description: Slides a soft boundary in or out without changing how soft it is. A hard edge has no band to slide; use expand for that.

tools.name: manage_selections
tools.description: Keep, reload, list, or discard named selections. A saved selection survives a reload and can be brought back on its own or combined with whatever is selected now; loading one into a differently sized image is refused rather than silently misplaced. Use inspect to see what is selected right now without changing it.

name.description: For save. Saving over an existing name replaces it.

mode.description: For load. Defaults to replace.

tools.name: manage_channels
tools.description: Look at the document one colour channel at a time, hide channels, or list the stored greyscale ones. An alpha channel here is the same thing as a saved selection, so anything kept in one panel appears in the other and can be loaded from either. Which channels are shown is a way of looking at the document, not an edit, so it never appears in Undo.

channel.description: For isolate. Pass null to stop isolating.

visible.description: For set_visible. At least one.

tools.name: exchange_svg
tools.description: Reads an SVG into editable shape layers, or writes the document's shapes back out as SVG. Importing keeps each object as its own layer rather than flattening the file into a picture of itself, and anything Estro cannot draw is named in the warnings rather than dropped in silence. Exporting resolves swatch fills to the colours they currently hold, because an SVG has nowhere to keep a reference.

tools.name: manage_swatches
tools.description: Add, rename, recolour, remove, and list the document's named colours and gradients. A swatch is shared: changing it changes every shape, stroke, and fill pointing at it in one edit rather than in forty. Removing one leaves anything using it unpainted and says so, rather than quietly baking in the colour it had.

tools.name: match_photos
tools.description: Copy one photograph's settings onto photographs in other projects. Plans by default: every target is checked before anything is written, so a strict batch can refuse rather than leave half a set synchronised. Each project gets its own Undo step, because each project keeps its own history and there is nowhere a single one could live.

targets.description: Each {projectId, layerId}: the photograph in each project to bring into line.

attributes.description: Which attributes to copy. All of the source layer's if left out.

apply.description: False (the default) plans without writing anything.

tools.name: batch_export
tools.description: Export many photographs at once, in one or more sizes and formats. Plans by default and says how many files that is, which projects cannot take part, and why — three sizes of a hundred photographs is three hundred encodes, so it runs as a job with progress and a cancel rather than blocking. Set apply to true to queue it; poll inspect_job for progress.

projectId.description: The project the job belongs to, for progress and cancellation.

variants.description: Each {name, mediaType, quality, maxEdgePx, resampleAlgorithm}. The name goes into the file name, so a set of three sizes stays tellable apart.

onFailure.description: continue (the default) keeps going past a photograph that fails; stop refuses to begin unless every one can take part.

tools.name: resolve_phrase
tools.description: Read a phrase like “make it a bit warmer” or “black and white” into the exact command Estro would run, without running it. Says what it understood, what it did not, and which words meant nothing here. This is a lookup rather than a language model: a phrase it does not know is refused by name instead of being approximated, and the command it returns is an ordinary one that goes through the same history as any other edit. Call list_phrases to see everything it knows.

tools.name: list_phrases
tools.description: Every phrase resolve_phrase understands, with what each one means. Making people guess at a vocabulary is worse than showing them. Never changes anything.

tools.name: mark_media
tools.description: Rate, label, favourite, tag, or note media. Many items at once, as one transaction and one press of Undo, because that is how selects are actually made. A rating of zero means unrated rather than bad, so “show me everything nobody has looked at” stays answerable. Tags are added and removed rather than replaced, so marking fifteen shots “wide” does not strip whatever else each was tagged.

rating.description: 0 clears it; 0 means unrated, not bad.

tools.name: manage_collections
tools.description: Saved questions about the media, as against places to file it. A collection is not a bin: nothing is moved into it, and an item that stops matching leaves on its own — so a collection is always current and never has to be maintained. List, run, add, change, or remove one; browse with the same rules without saving them.

rules.description: Each {field, comparison, value}. Fields: rating, label, favourite, tag, name, kind, duration, used.

tag.description: For browse.

tools.name: manage_package
tools.description: Plan moving a project between machines. This tool reads and reasons; it does not write or open a package, because a browser cannot hand a file to another machine without a user gesture. estimate says how large a package would be under each media policy — “everything” on a long project is very large. offline_state says what this copy would be missing if it were opened elsewhere. inspect and plan_open take the contents of a package you already have and say whether this copy is behind, ahead, diverged, or unrelated, because those four need different things done. Writing the file itself is a user action through the interface.

projectId.description: For estimate and offline_state.

mediaPolicy.description: used_only by default. none needs the media to already be on the machine that opens it.

writtenBy.description: Names the machine, so two packages can be told apart.

tools.name: manage_review
tools.description: People on a project, comments anchored to an object, a timecode, or a region of the frame, version stacks, claims, and shares. None of it is enforcement and every answer says so: a role decides what Estro offers rather than what it prevents, and a claim is a note to whoever else opens the project. Comments are resolved rather than deleted, so the thread that explains a decision survives, and each records which version it was written against.

body.description: For comment and reply.

anchor.description: Where a comment points: {kind:'project'} | {kind:'object',objectType,objectId} | {kind:'time',sequenceId,time,duration} | {kind:'region',sequenceId,time,x,y,width,height}.

tools.name: inspect_accessibility
tools.description: How the interface presents itself, and how to operate it without a mouse. Reports the resolved motion and contrast modes, every status indicator with the shape and word that carry its meaning without colour, and the keyboard route to each action. Colour is never the only signal here, and no status is described by naming its colour — “red” tells nobody anything they can act on.

sites.name: freenet.free
sites.description: Design how to build a product on Cloudflare or Vercel, watch requests flow and get billed, and let your browser's agent drive the canvas through WebMCP.

tools.name: get_diagram
tools.description: Read the current architecture as DSL plus a structured summary (nodes, groups, edges, provider, plan, parse errors). Call this before editing.

tools.name: set_diagram
tools.description: Replace the whole architecture with new DSL. Grammar: `id [kind: , label: "...", attr: value]` for nodes, `group "Label" { ... }` for groups, `a > b: "label" [ops: 2]` for edges (`ops` = calls per request), `direction right|down`, `title "..."`, `provider cloudflare|vercel`. Kinds: client, edge-cache, waf, bot-shield, rate-limit, static, ssr, compute, kv, sql, blob, queue, actor, workflow, vector, llm, ai-gateway, search, cron, realtime, hyperdrive, images, stream, browser, turnstile, email, load-balancer, zaraz, analytics, access, container, flags, sandbox, middleware, external. Prefer patch_diagram for small edits.

tools.name: patch_diagram
tools.description: Apply small edits to the architecture: add/remove/set nodes, groups and edges, or set direction/title/provider. Node attrs that matter to the simulator: hit (cache 0..1), cpuMs, bytesKb, rowsRead, writeShare, limitRps, neurons, ops on edges. Third-party services: kind external with attrs { service: "openai.gpt55_chat" } (ids from list_services).

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: List starting-point architectures (id, name, tagline, lesson). Load one with load_template.

tools.name: load_template
tools.description: Load a template architecture by id onto the canvas, replacing the current diagram.

tools.name: list_products
tools.description: List the generic product kinds and what each maps to on Cloudflare and Vercel, including gaps where a provider has no first-party product.

tools.name: explain_product
tools.description: Explain one product kind on both providers: what it is, when to use it, limits, recommended stack, billing meters, and the counterpart gap.

tools.name: set_provider
tools.description: Switch the whole architecture between Cloudflare and Vercel. Nodes are re-labelled and re-priced; the diagram itself does not change.

tools.name: set_plan
tools.description: Choose which plan to price against: free (Cloudflare Free / Vercel Hobby) or paid (Workers Paid / Vercel Pro).

tools.name: set_traffic_mix
tools.description: Set requests per day and the share of each request class (human, googlebot, ai-crawler, scraper, botnet). Shares are normalised. Omitted fields keep their value.

tools.name: set_protection
tools.description: Set a gate node's protection mode. Modes: off, bots (block scrapers + botnets), bots+ai (also block AI crawlers), all-bots (also block search crawlers, which hurts SEO). Works on bot-shield, waf and rate-limit nodes.

tools.name: get_snapshot
tools.description: Current simulation state: offered traffic by class, what was blocked/dropped, and per-node arrivals. Use it to explain where requests go.

tools.name: get_bill
tools.description: Projected monthly bill for the current architecture and traffic, priced from the official pricing pages (with source URLs). Optionally for a different provider or plan.

tools.name: compare_providers
tools.description: Price the same architecture on Cloudflare and Vercel, free and paid, side by side, with the gaps each provider has for the kinds in use.

tools.name: explain_charge
tools.description: Explain what drives a meter: which nodes contribute, how much, and which request classes are behind it. Without a meter, explains the top five by monthly volume.

tools.name: analyze_product
tools.description: Analyse a product from its URL or a description: what it is, the core loop vs polish features, which platform primitives it needs, and a build verdict. Follow with propose_architecture.

tools.name: propose_architecture
tools.description: Generate an architecture from the last analyze_product result (or from explicit needs flags) and put it on the canvas. Needs: auth, sql, kv, blob, queue, realtime, llm, vector, search, cron, payments, email, ssr.

tools.name: export_config
tools.description: Generate deployable configuration for the current architecture: wrangler.jsonc and a Worker entry for Cloudflare, or vercel.json and a setup guide for Vercel, plus the recommended stack.

tools.name: describe_studio
tools.description: Start here. What freenet.free is and how it thinks (request classes, gates, caches, free-tier quotas), a map of the UI, which tool to use for what, common workflows, and the current state: provider, plan, traffic, clock position, view, selection, open blueprint.

tools.name: get_layers
tools.description: The layer view: every node with the meters it drives, projected monthly volume against the plan's allowance (percent used, over or not), unit cost and what happens past the quota. This is what the timeline tracks and the Inspect overview show.

tools.name: set_simulation_period
tools.description: Choose what the timeline simulates: a day (hours), a month (30 days) or a year (12 months with monthly quota resets). Restarts the clock and starts playing; the whole period plays in about 90 real seconds.

tools.name: control_timeline
tools.description: Drive the timeline: play, pause, reset to the start, or seek to a position given as a fraction of the period (0 = start, 1 = end; seeking pauses). Returns the clock readout. Use seek 1 to jump to the end-of-period totals.

tools.name: set_view
tools.description: Arrange the canvas: layout snake (rows that wrap, the default), vertical or horizontal; edge style curved, step or straight; relayout true re-runs auto layout and discards manual nudges.

tools.name: focus_node

tools.name: open_panel

tools.name: list_alternatives
