tools.description: Choose which take actually plays for this shot in the cut — the ⬆ timeline source override. Any take works: a still, a restyle, a motion clip or a frozen one. Presses ⬆ on the take, and the Film Editor immediately shows the new pick. Pass clear:true to drop the override and fall back to the shot's default (keeper, or the newest motion). Defaults to the selected take. Run cut_film afterwards to see it in a rendered cut.

shot.description: The shot: a sid (B10-S2), its number in the cut, a beat, or a description.

take.description: Which take plays. A path, or: "latest", "newest still", "newest motion", "keeper", "plays", "selected", "third still". Defaults to the selection.

clear.description: True removes the override so the shot falls back to its default source.

tools.name: set_shot_timing
tools.description: Retime a shot in the cut: how many seconds it holds, how far its voice-over slides against the picture, and whether the VO is muted. Opens the Film Editor, selects the shot and edits its quick panel, so the strip re-widths in front of the director. Positive vo_offset delays the line, negative pulls it earlier. Anything you leave out is left alone. Takes effect on the next cut_film. Returns the resulting override.

shot.description: The shot: a sid (B10-S2), its number in the cut, a beat, or a description.

seconds.description: How long the shot holds in the cut, in seconds. Overrides the scripted duration.

vo_offset.description: Seconds to slide the voice-over: positive delays the line, negative pulls it earlier.

mute_vo.description: True silences this shot's voice-over in the cut; false restores it.

tools.name: synthesize_vo
tools.description: Record a voice-over line for a shot. Opens the shot's Audio tab, fills the line, voice and treatment, and presses ▶ synthesize. Defaults to the line the script already gives the shot — its narration or first piece of dialogue — so you usually only pass the shot. `treatment` is what the line is heard through: none (default), radio, phone, megaphone or hall. ElevenLabs v3 tags pass through. Paid voice backends require confirm_cost. Returns job and take.

shot.description: The shot: a sid (B10-S2), its number in the cut, a beat, or a description.

text.description: The line to speak. Omit to use the shot's own narration or first dialogue line as written.

voice.description: Voice id on the VO backend. Omit for the project's default voice.

treatment.description: What the line is heard through: none (default), radio, phone, megaphone or hall.

backend.description: Force a specific VO backend id instead of the project's lane default.

confirm_cost.description: Set true to approve a paid voice backend. Required whenever the VO lane bills money.

tools.name: direct_shot
tools.description: Compile a plain-English direction into Genga Studio's own edit plan and show it on screen as a preview — "hold his pose for the rest of the line", "restyle this warmer", "make it two seconds longer". Types the instruction into the shot's Direct box and compiles it; the deterministic grammar goes first and reads the real voice-over duration. Clips play in full unless the direction asks for a freeze. NOTHING RUNS: it only returns the plan. Show it, then call apply_plan.

shot.description: The shot: a sid (B10-S2), its number in the cut, a beat, or a description.

instruction.description: The direction in plain English, exactly as the director said it.

tools.name: apply_plan
tools.description: Run an edit plan that direct_shot compiled, after the director has approved it. Presses ▶ apply on the plan preview, so the same ops a human would run execute in order: freezes, trims, generations and state changes. Pass the plan object direct_shot returned, unchanged. Returns the jobs it submitted and how each op landed. Only call this once the human has said yes to the preview.

shot.description: The shot the plan belongs to: a sid, its number in the cut, or a description.

plan.description: The plan object direct_shot returned, unchanged: { ops: [...], note }.

ops.description: The ops to run, in order.

note.description: The plan's note.

tools.name: cut_film
tools.description: Assemble the film as it currently stands into a watchable cut: every shot's chosen source, its duration, its voice-over and offsets, in film order. Sets the scope (the whole film or a single act) and the resolution on the Film Editor, then presses 🎞 cut the film. Use it after a run of picks or retimes so the director can watch the change in context. 720 is the preview, 1080 the final. Returns the job and, when it renders fast, the cut's path and duration.

scope.description: What to assemble: the whole film, or one act. Default full.

res.description: Resolution: "720" for a preview (default) or "1080" for the final.

tools.name: get_jobs
tools.description: Check on generation jobs without waiting: their status, what they produced and, for anything that failed, the tail of the log with the reason. Pass the job ids a generation tool returned, or call it with no arguments for the project's most recent jobs. Use it when the director asks "is it done yet?" or after a tool came back with jobs still running. Returns immediately — call wait_for_jobs instead when you want to block until they finish.

jobs.description: Job ids to check (up to 8). Omit for this project's most recent jobs.

tools.name: wait_for_jobs
tools.description: Wait for generation jobs to finish, up to 60 seconds, then report what landed. Progress stays visible in the topbar and the Jobs page while you wait. Use it after a generation tool returns jobs that are still running, so the next thing you say to the director is the actual result rather than a promise. Anything still running when the timeout expires comes back as "running" — call again or check with get_jobs. Returns each job's status and the takes it produced.

jobs.description: The job ids to wait for (up to 8), as returned by a generation tool (ids, or the job objects a previous wait returned).

timeout_s.description: How long to wait, in seconds. Capped at 60.

tools.name: generate_music
tools.description: Compose a music cue for the film and lay it on the audio bed. Opens a shot's Audio tab, fills the Music console, presses ▶ music, then places the finished piece as a cue — at that shot's start, at a time you name, or at the head of the film. Describe the music the way a director would (instrument, tempo, feeling). Gain is decibels: -8 is a bed under narration, 0 is a hero cue. Paid backends require confirm_cost. Set place false to audition it without touching the cut.

prompt.description: The music, in plain words: instruments, tempo, mood — e.g. 'slow upright bass and brushed snare, elegiac'.

seconds.description: How long the piece runs. The ElevenLabs music model's floor is 10s; shorter asks are raised to it.

instrumental.description: True forbids vocals — the right default for anything sitting under dialogue.

shot.description: Place the cue at this shot's start: a sid (B10-S2), its number in the cut, a beat, or a description.

start.description: Place the cue at this many seconds into the film instead. Ignored when shot is given.

gain.description: Cue level in dB. 0 is unity, negative is quieter. Defaults to -8, a bed under the voice-over.

fade_in.description: Fade the cue up over this many seconds.

fade_out.description: Fade the cue down over this many seconds at its end.

place.description: False generates the take but leaves the cut alone — audition first, place later with place_cue.

backend.description: Force a music backend id instead of the project's lane default.

confirm_cost.description: Set true to approve a paid music backend. Required whenever the music lane bills money.

tools.name: generate_sfx
tools.description: Make a sound effect for one shot and pin it there. Opens that shot's Audio tab, fills the SFX console, presses ▶ sfx, then places the result as a cue at the shot's start plus any offset you give — so it follows the shot when the timing changes. Describe the sound, not the feeling: 'a heavy wooden door slamming in a stone hall'. Gain is decibels; -4 is an accent, -18 is a bed. Paid backends require confirm_cost.

shot.description: The shot: a sid (B10-S2), its number in the cut, a beat, or a description.

prompt.description: The sound itself — source, material and space, e.g. 'chalk scraping on brick, close, dry room'.

seconds.description: How long the effect runs. Keep it tight; the backend's ceiling is 30s.

offset.description: Seconds after the shot's first frame to trigger it. Defaults to 0, right on the cut.

gain.description: Cue level in dB. 0 is unity, negative is quieter. Defaults to -4, an accent over the bed.

prompt_influence.description: How literally the model follows the words. Higher is obedient, lower is inventive.

place.description: False generates the take but leaves the cut alone — audition first, place later with place_cue.

backend.description: Force an SFX backend id instead of the project's lane default.

confirm_cost.description: Set true to approve a paid SFX backend. Required whenever the SFX lane bills money.

tools.name: place_cue
tools.description: Lay an existing audio file on the film's music or SFX track. Give it a take path and either a shot (the cue rides that shot's start and moves with it) or a start time in film seconds. Opens the Film Editor's cue strip so the placement is visible. Gain is decibels — 0 unity, -8 a bed. Use it to re-place a take you generated with place false, or to move a piece of music you already have. Returns the cue with its id.

kind.description: Which track the cue rides. Inferred from the path (audio/music/… or audio/sfx/…) when omitted.

take.description: The audio file, project-relative — e.g. audio/music/theme.mp3. A generate_music or generate_sfx take path.

path.description: Alias for take. The project-relative audio file to place.

shot.description: Anchor the cue to this shot's start: a sid, its number in the cut, a beat, or a description.

start.description: Anchor the cue this many seconds into the film instead. Ignored when shot is given.

offset.description: Seconds added to whichever anchor won. Use it to sit a hit just after the cut.

duration.description: Trim the cue to this many seconds. Required when loop is true.

gain.description: Cue level in dB. 0 is unity, negative is quieter. Defaults to -8 for music, -4 for SFX.

fade_in.description: Fade the cue up over this many seconds.

fade_out.description: Fade the cue down over this many seconds at its end.

loop.description: Repeat the file until duration is filled — for room tone and ambience beds.

label.description: A short note shown on the cue strip, e.g. 'main theme' or 'door slam'.

tools.name: list_cues
tools.description: Read the film's cue sheet — every music and SFX cue with the time it fires, the shot it rides, its level in dB and its length. Use it before scoring to see what is already there, after placing to confirm, and to get the cue ids that remove one. A cue whose file is missing is flagged; a cue anchored outside the current scope shows no time.

kind.description: Only this track. Omit for both.

scope.description: Resolve times against a single act (act1..act4) instead of the whole film.

tools.name: add_cel_layer
tools.description: Animate one region of a shot as a cel layer over a background that stays put — the ink-first grammar: name only what moves ("only the hand turns the key"), and the rest of the frame never boils. Draws the region on the cel workbench, fills the motion prompt and submits. Creates the comp from the keeper plate (or `background`, which may be a clip) when the shot has none. Regions are background pixels, snapped to /32. Paid backends need confirm_cost.

shot.description: The shot: a sid (B10-S2), its number in the cut, a beat, or a description.

region.description: [left, top, right, bottom] on the background, in its own pixels — or fractions 0-1. Snapped to /32.

prompt.description: Motion prompt for this cel. Name ONLY what moves; the rest of the frame is the background's job.

frames.description: Cel length in frames at 24fps. Default 49 (about two seconds).

comp.description: Which comp to add to. Default: the shot's newest, or a new one staged on the keeper.

background.description: Only when creating the comp: "keeper", "newest motion", "plays", or a take path. A clip gives a moving background.

confirm_cost.description: True approves a paid motion backend. Required when the motion lane costs money.

tools.name: reroll_layer
tools.description: Generate another take of one cel layer, leaving the background and every other layer untouched — the comparison take. Same prompt and a fresh seed by default; pass prompt, seed, backend or model to direct it. Every take a layer has ever had stays in its variants strip, so nothing is overwritten. Opens the workbench, selects the layer and presses reroll. Paid backends need confirm_cost. If a cel ignores its plate, switch model and rerun.

shot.description: The shot: a sid (B10-S2), its number in the cut, a beat, or a description.

layer.description: Which layer: its id (L1, L2…), "newest" for the last one added, or "selected".

prompt.description: A new motion prompt for this cel. Default: keep the layer's own prompt.

seed.description: Fix the seed to reproduce a take. Default: a fresh random seed.

backend.description: Motion backend id, e.g. "mock" or "fal". Default: the project's motion lane.

model.description: Model id on that backend. Default: the backend's own default.

comp.description: Which comp the layer belongs to. Default: the shot's newest comp.

confirm_cost.description: True approves a paid motion backend. Required when the motion lane costs money.

tools.name: restyle_background
tools.description: Change the comp's background plate while every cel layer stays exactly where it is. mode "edit" keeps this plate and follows guidance (strength 0.55 holds the staged geometry, 0.85+ redesigns); mode "regen" paints a brand-new plate from a full image prompt. Every previous plate stays toggleable in the comp's background history. Still plates only — a clip background is footage, so animate a new clip and set_background instead.

shot.description: The shot: a sid (B10-S2), its number in the cut, a beat, or a description.

prompt.description: Edit guidance ("warmer, dusk light") for mode edit, or the full image prompt for mode regen.

mode.description: "edit" keeps this plate and guides it; "regen" paints a new one. Default edit.

strength.description: Edit mode only: how much may change. 0.55 keeps the staging, 0.85+ redesigns. Default 0.55.

comp.description: Which comp to restyle. Default: the shot's newest comp.

confirm_cost.description: True approves a paid image backend. Required when the still or i2i lane costs money.

tools.name: set_background
tools.description: Point a comp at a different background — any take, still or clip. A still is the classic cel plate that never shimmers; a clip gives a MOVING background under the cel layers, which is how a comp holds camera motion without the figures boiling. Every layer keeps its region and its takes, the old background stays toggleable in the history, and the composite re-renders. Accepts a path or "newest motion", "keeper", "plays".

shot.description: The shot: a sid (B10-S2), its number in the cut, a beat, or a description.

take.description: The new background: a take path, or "keeper", "newest still", "newest motion", "plays".

comp.description: Which comp to repoint. Default: the shot's newest comp.

tools.name: set_layer
tools.description: Adjust one cel layer in place: opacity, stacking order ("front", "back" or an explicit z), matte mode ("window" is a feathered rectangle, "figure" cuts a per-frame anime matte so only the figure lands on the plate) and its region. Everything you pass is written in ONE edit, so the composite re-renders once rather than once per field. The cel itself is not regenerated — use reroll_layer for that.

shot.description: The shot: a sid (B10-S2), its number in the cut, a beat, or a description.

layer.description: Which layer: its id (L1, L2…), "newest" for the last one added, or "selected".

opacity.description: How strongly the cel reads over the background. 1 is solid, 0.5 is a ghost.

z.description: Stacking: "front", "back", or a number. Higher z draws over lower z.

matte.description: "window" = feathered rectangle; "figure" = per-frame anime matte, only the figure lands.

region.description: Move or resize the cel. [left, top, right, bottom] on the background, in its own pixels — or fractions 0-1. Snapped to /32.

comp.description: Which comp the layer belongs to. Default: the shot's newest comp.

tools.name: remove_layer
tools.description: Take one cel layer out of a comp. The background and the other layers are untouched, and the composite re-renders without it. The layer's generated clips stay on disk as takes, so this is a composition decision, not a delete — restage it with add_cel_layer if you change your mind. Defaults to the newest layer when none is named.

shot.description: The shot: a sid (B10-S2), its number in the cut, a beat, or a description.

layer.description: Which layer: its id (L1, L2…), "newest" for the last one added, or "selected".

comp.description: Which comp the layer belongs to. Default: the shot's newest comp.

tools.name: render_comp
tools.description: Render the comp into one clip: the background (a still plate, or a clip playing under everything) with every cel layer merged through its matte, at the comp's duration. Runs on the CPU pool and costs nothing. Pass promote:true to also make the finished composite what this shot plays in the cut, which is the usual last step of a cel build. Returns the job and, when it lands quickly, the rendered take.

shot.description: The shot: a sid (B10-S2), its number in the cut, a beat, or a description.

comp.description: Which comp to render. Default: the shot's newest comp.

promote.description: True also sets the finished composite as the shot's timeline source (the ⬆ button).

tools.name: list_layers
tools.description: Read a shot's compositions without changing anything: each comp's background (and whether it is a still plate or a moving clip), its duration, how many alternative plates are stored, and every cel layer with its region, prompt, z order, opacity, matte mode and how many takes it has. Call it before reroll_layer or set_layer so you name a layer that exists, or to answer "what is in this comp?".

shot.description: The shot: a sid (B10-S2), its number in the cut, a beat, or a description.

comp.description: Only this comp. Default: every comp on the shot.

tools.name: list_backends
tools.description: Report every generation backend this server knows: its id and adapter type, which lanes it can serve (still, i2i, motion, vo, music, sfx, direction), whether it is enabled, whether a key is stored, and whether it costs money per job. Nothing is probed, so it is instant and never bills. Call it before naming a backend in generate_takes or set_lane_default, or to answer "what can this machine actually run?". Also lists the motion and image models with their price and what each is good at.

tools.name: set_lane_default
tools.description: Point one generation lane at a backend (and optionally a model) for this project, so every later generate that leaves the console blank runs there — the "(project default)" the model picker shows. Lanes are still, i2i, motion, vo, music, sfx and direction. Opens the Settings lane table and changes the row on screen. Hosted demos allow this to the admin only; the server's refusal is relayed verbatim.

lane.description: Which lane: still, i2i, motion, vo, music, sfx or direction.

backend.description: The backend id to make default, e.g. "mock", "fal", "elevenlabs". Use list_backends to see them.

model.description: Model (or voice) id on that backend. Omit to leave the backend's own default.

tools.name: export_timeline
tools.description: Hand the cut to another program. "otio" is OpenTimelineIO JSON, which opens natively in Resolve, Nuke Studio and Kdenlive and carries each clip's Genga Studio lineage in its metadata; "edl" is a CMX3600 edit decision list, the universal conform format. Nothing is rendered and nothing changes — this compiles the current film and returns a download URL plus the first lines, so you can check the cut before opening it downstream.

format.description: "otio" for OpenTimelineIO JSON (default), "edl" for a CMX3600 edit decision list.

tools.name: render_timeline
tools.description: Render the compiled timeline through the lifted FreeCut engine — the clip model with real source in/out points, not the shot-slot assembler that cut_film uses. Optionally scope it to the first N seconds so a check is quick. Returns the job. The engine is an optional dependency: when it is not configured — and on the hosted studio it never is — this answers "engine offline" cleanly rather than failing, and cut_film remains the way to see the film.

scope_sec.description: Render only the first N seconds. Omit for the whole film.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Start a new, empty film in Genga Studio and open its Film Editor. Give it a title; the id is a slug derived from that unless you pass one. The new project inherits this instance's lane defaults and a style register — the house anime look, applied to every still, so shot prompts never carry style words. Hosted demos cap how many films one visitor may start per day. Follow it with write_script to fill the film with shots.

title.description: What the film is called, e.g. "The Bread Riot". Shown on the project card.

id.description: URL slug for the project. Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Derived from the title when omitted.

fps.description: Frames per second for the cut. Default 24; leave it alone unless the director asks.

style.description: The film's look: anime-cel (default), anime-noir, anime-pastel, or a custom prefix sentence. Change it later with set_style.

tools.name: write_script
tools.description: Write a film's whole shot list in one call — the list IS the cut, in order. Each image_prompt describes setting, subject, framing and light. Do not add style words (hand-painted, caricature, cartoon, watercolour) and never ask for text in frame; the project's style register is applied to every still automatically. Narration under 25 words, dialogue under 12. Up to 40 shots, 2-20 seconds each, 300 seconds total. Use replace to throw out the old script.

sid.description: Shot id like B01-S3 (beat, then shot within it). Omit and they are numbered for you.

act.description: Which act this shot belongs to, 1-4. Shots with no beat get one beat per act.

beat.description: Beat id like B02 — a scene inside an act. Optional; the act supplies one.

type.description: STILL for a plain shot, HERO for the one the eye lands on. Default STILL.

seconds.description: How long the shot holds, 2 to 20 seconds. Default 6. The whole film must stay under 300.

register.description: The colour and light register of this run of shots, e.g. "R2 (warm lamplight, the bakery)".

image_prompt.description: Setting, then "Subject: …", then framing and light. No style words: the project's style register supplies the look.

negative.description: Extra bans for this shot only. The project's style register already bans text, lettering and photorealism everywhere.

motion_prompt.description: The one thing that moves, if anything: "only the wig trembles". Leave it out for a held still.

narration.description: Narration over the shot. Twenty-five words at most — it has to fit the hold.

dialogue.description: Lines spoken in the shot, in order. Twelve words each at most.

line.description: What they say. Twelve words at most.

sfx.description: One sound effect, in words: "a distant crowd, one cart wheel".

ambient.description: The bed under the shot: "street noise, rain on stone".

cut.description: How this shot leaves: "hard", "freeze then cut".

render_notes.description: A rule for whoever renders it: "no visible faces anywhere in the film".

shots.description: The shots, in the order they play. Each needs an image_prompt; everything else has a sensible default.

project.description: Project id to write into. Defaults to the film that is open.

replace.description: True deletes every shot this script does not name — a rewrite, not an edit. Default false.

tools.name: set_project_cast
tools.description: Register who is in the film so shots can be found by character later: "the Margot close-up" resolves because the cast index knows Margot is the baker. Each entry is a name plus a short descriptor of the role, and aliases are derived from both. Write it right after write_script, using the same names the prompts use. Replaces the whole cast each time, so send everyone at once.

characters.description: Everyone in the film. Send them all: this replaces the cast rather than adding to it.

name.description: The character's name as the prompts write it, e.g. "Margot".

descriptor.description: The role in a few words: "the baker who starts it". Becomes searchable aliases.

id.description: Stable id. Derived from the name when omitted.

aliases.description: Extra ways the director might say this character: "the baker", "her".

project.description: Project id. Defaults to the film that is open.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List every film on this server: its id, its title, how many shots it holds and whether it is paused. Use it to find out whether the film the director means already exists before starting another one, and to get the project id the other tools take. Reads only; nothing is opened and nothing changes.

tools.name: play_cut
tools.description: Play an assembled cut full screen in the screening room, from anywhere in it. Picks the cut (newest by default, or a file name or an index from newest), opens the Film Editor, opens the room over it and starts playing. `from` takes seconds, "1:05", a shot sid, "act2", "start"/"end", or a description like "the lighthouses". The room shows the cut's shot list as a chapter strip. Returns the shot now on screen. Use stop_playback to close it.

project.description: Project id. Defaults to the film that is open.

cut.description: Which cut: "latest" (default), a file name, or an index from newest where 1 is newest.

from.description: Where to start: seconds (65), "1:05", a shot sid ("B03-S2"), "act2", "start", "end", or a description of the shot.

to.description: Stop and hold at this many seconds. Leave it out to play to the end.

muted.description: Start muted. Browsers allow a muted clip to autoplay when a normal one is refused.

tools.name: play_take
tools.description: Put a single take on the big screen: full-viewport playback of one shot's clip, or a still held for the shot's duration with a progress bar. `take` accepts a path or the usual words: "latest", "newest motion", "newest still", "keeper", "plays" (what is in the cut). Use it when the director wants to look hard at one shot rather than the whole film. stop_playback closes it.

shot.description: The shot: a sid (B10-S2), its number in the cut, a beat, or a description.

take.description: Which take: a path, or "latest", "newest motion", "newest still", "keeper", "plays". Defaults to what plays.

from.description: Start this many seconds in, or "0:02". Defaults to the head of the take.

tools.name: stop_playback
tools.description: Stop whatever is playing and close the full-screen screening room, putting the director back on the page underneath with nothing lost. Also clears the ?screen and ?t deep-link parameters. Safe to call when nothing is playing.

tools.name: preview_timeline
tools.description: Play the Timeline's live preview: the film compiled straight from the clip model, with no render step, so it reflects edits the instant they are made. Seeks to `from` (seconds, "1:05", a shot sid, "act2", or a description) and presses play. Picture and sound both: the VO, music and SFX clips play with it. A browser that has seen no click yet may hold the sound back — the page says so under the monitor, and ▶ there releases it.

project.description: Project id. Defaults to the film that is open.

from.description: Where to start: seconds (65), "1:05", a shot sid ("B03-S2"), "act2", "start", "end", or a description of the shot.

play.description: Start playing (default true). False seeks and holds on the frame.

scope_sec.description: Set the render-scope dropdown to this many seconds, for a following render_timeline.

tools.name: plan_motion
tools.description: Plan how to spend a dollar budget on animating this film. Ranks every shot by how much movement would buy it — HERO shots, shots with a motion prompt, the longest holds, later acts as climaxes, shots that already have a clip pushed down — then fits the budget, picking a model per shot from the registry of cost and use cases. Reads only. Faithfulness problems are usually the model, not the prompt: switch to the fallback and rerun.

project.description: Project id. Defaults to the project on screen.

budget_usd.description: Dollars to spend on motion, e.g. 4. The plan stops when the next clip would pass it.

seconds_per_clip.description: Clip length in seconds. Defaults to the backend's own default and is clamped to what it supports.

prefer.description: Criteria to weight double: hero, motion_prompt, longest, climax.

max_shots.description: Cap the plan at this many shots even if the budget allows more.

backend.description: Price the plan against a specific backend id instead of the project's motion default.

tools.name: apply_motion_plan
tools.description: Spend a motion budget: animate each shot of a plan_motion plan in order, on screen, one clip per shot, stopping the moment the next clip would pass the budget. Pass the plan back verbatim, or the same arguments to re-plan and run in one turn. Paid backends need confirm_cost. Returns the jobs and takes per shot with the running total; clips play in full at the backend's clip length.

project.description: Project id. Defaults to the project on screen.

plan.description: The items from plan_motion, in order. Omit to re-plan from budget_usd.

shot.description: The shot sid.

source.description: Which still to animate: a take path, or "selected". Defaults to the shot's keeper.

seconds.description: Clip length in seconds.

why.description: Why this shot earned a clip.

budget_usd.description: Dollars to spend. Required when no plan is passed; also the hard stop while running.

seconds_per_clip.description: Clip length in seconds. Defaults to the backend's own default.

prefer.description: Criteria to weight double: hero, motion_prompt, longest, climax.

max_shots.description: Cap the run at this many shots.

backend.description: Force a backend id instead of the project's motion default.

confirm_cost.description: Set true to approve a paid backend. Required whenever the motion lane bills money.

tools.name: set_style
tools.description: Set the style register — the look the server puts on every still and restyle in this film, so no shot prompt has to carry style words. Pick a named preset (anime-cel, anime-noir, anime-pastel) or write a custom prefix sentence of your own. `avoid` is the negative sent with every generation, and it also strips those words out of prompts that already carry them. Shots generated before the change keep the look they were made with; regenerate to bring them over.

preset.description: A named house look: anime-cel (default), anime-noir for night, anime-pastel for daylight.

prefix.description: Custom look, as one sentence put in front of every prompt: "Cinematic anime film still, 1970s rotoscope …".

avoid.description: Comma-separated negative applied to every still: "text, lettering, photorealistic, western cartoon".

refs.description: Style-reference frames the model matches, as paths. Empty array turns reference conditioning off.

project.description: Project id whose look this is. Defaults to the film that is open.

tools.name: attach_reference
tools.description: Attach a reference image to a shot so every still and restyle generated for it is sent that picture with the prompt. Say what it is for: character (match the face and costume), prop (match the object), setting (match the room), style (match line and palette only). The image can be a take path, words like "keeper of B02-S2", or an http(s) link, which is downloaded into the project. Four per shot. Shows in the Generate tab's References strip. Backends that take no image input skip them.

shot.description: The shot the reference belongs to: a sid (B10-S2), its number in the cut, a beat, or a description.

image.description: A take path, an http(s) image url, or words: "keeper of B02-S2", "newest still of B04-S2", "plays", "latest".

role.description: What to match: character (face, costume), prop (object), setting (place), style (line and palette only). Default character.

note.description: Optional reminder of why this picture is attached, e.g. "her coat is grey, not black".

tools.name: remove_reference
tools.description: Take a reference image off a shot, so later generations stop being conditioned on it. Name the image (a path or file name), or a role (character, prop, setting, style) to drop every reference in that role, or pass image:"all" to clear them. The picture itself stays in the project's takes — only the attachment goes.

shot.description: The shot: a sid (B10-S2), its number in the cut, a beat, or a description.

image.description: Which reference to drop: a path or file name, a role name, or "all" for every one on the shot.

role.description: Drop every reference in this role instead of naming a file.

tools.name: list_references
tools.description: Read the reference images attached to a shot and what each one is for, without changing anything. Use it before generating to see whether a face, a prop or a room is already pinned to a picture, and before attaching a fourth (four is the limit).

shot.description: The shot: a sid (B10-S2), its number in the cut, a beat, or a description.

tools.name: move_audio
tools.description: Slide one piece of audio along the film — a shot's voice-over, or a music or SFX cue — the way dragging it on the Timeline does. `at` puts it that many seconds into the film; `delta` slides it from where it sits (negative pulls it earlier). Use it to lift a cue off a line it is stepping on: the result says where it landed and what it still overlaps. A shot's lines share one offset, so they travel together.

target.description: What to move: a shot id for its VO, a cue id from list_cues, or part of the file name.

at.description: Put it this many seconds into the film. Wins over delta.

delta.description: Slide it this many seconds from where it is now; negative pulls it earlier.

snap.description: Let it land on a cut or the playhead when it is close (default true).

project.description: Project id. Defaults to the film that is open.

sites.name: terraforming-planet.github.io
sites.description: ForgeMCP combines evidence-first Terra satellite research, deterministic Cube Chess testing, and a human-gated 3D product lab through WebMCP.

tools.name: get_forgemcp_status
tools.description: Return local runtime status.

tools.name: list_capabilities
tools.description: List bounded capabilities.

tools.name: get_integration_status
tools.description: Report browser integration boundaries without probing hidden services.

tools.name: search_location
tools.description: Resolve a place with public OpenStreetMap Nominatim.

tools.name: set_area_of_interest
tools.description: Validate and bound a WGS84 AOI.

tools.name: create_research_station
tools.description: Create a browser-run research station.

tools.name: set_station_timespan
tools.description: Set an ISO date range.

tools.name: find_observations
tools.description: Query real NASA EONET events near an AOI.

tools.name: compare_dates
tools.description: Compare supplied observation counts without inferring cause.

tools.name: get_elevation_profile
tools.description: Fetch public Copernicus DEM samples via Open-Meteo.

tools.name: plan_hazard_investigation
tools.description: Validate a user-selected region, multi-year period and hazard classes, then return the real agent/tool plan without claiming that retrieval already ran.

tools.name: analyze_multiyear_imagery
tools.description: Ask the public Terra evidence Worker to visually inspect representative official/public NASA, USGS and Copernicus imagery for a selected AOI and period.

tools.name: retrieve_multiyear_imagery
tools.description: Retrieve one explicit official Landsat browse or labelled NASA GIBS fallback slot per requested year; returned gallery images are not falsely reported as model-inspected.

tools.name: rank_causal_hypotheses
tools.description: Create competing causal hypotheses and the measurements needed to test them; never convert an analogue or visual pattern into local causal proof.

tools.name: draft_preliminary_risk_alert
tools.description: Draft, but never send, a preliminary environmental risk alert that preserves uncertainty and requires human approval.

tools.name: propose_recovery_options
tools.description: Return conditional monitoring, repair and regeneration options with engineering, authority and permit gates.

tools.name: record_ground_verification
tools.description: Evaluate a precisely scoped field verification record. VERIFIED_FINDING requires independent measurements, a public source, a responsible expert and literal human approval.

tools.name: run_hazard_investigation
tools.description: Run the complete user-selected multi-agent environmental investigation: geocoding, multi-year official imagery, visual analysis, DEM/events, analogues, causal hypotheses, an unsent alert draft, recovery options and verification gates.

tools.name: inspect_test_001_evidence
tools.description: Retrieve and validate the recorded public TEST 001 pond measurement and separate author field report without claiming a fresh EO run.

tools.name: resolve_reference_dataset
tools.description: Resolve candidate records for a named reference such as Toruń without silently selecting an incompatible dataset.

tools.name: find_global_water_analogues
tools.description: Search the live public validated hydrology catalogues and return deterministic context-only analogues.

tools.name: inspect_local_hydrology_context
tools.description: Return curated, source-linked Lake Kuchnia connectivity references without claiming live page/PDF revalidation or current flow.

tools.name: run_labmcp_test_001
tools.description: Run the bounded TEST 001 LabMCP workflow over real recorded evidence, the Toruń resolver, documentary connectivity context and global analogue catalogues.

tools.name: inspect_hazard_signals
tools.description: Inspect TEST 001 competing hazard hypotheses while keeping recorded anomaly, current risk and causation separate.

tools.name: verify_evidence
tools.description: Apply deterministic provenance/sufficiency checks.

tools.name: generate_research_report
tools.description: Package supplied evidence without inventing findings.

tools.name: create_ai_candidate
tools.description: Create a deterministic capture-policy candidate.

tools.name: start_selfplay
tools.description: Execute one legal deterministic Cube game.

tools.name: run_ai_tournament
tools.description: Execute paired seeded candidate-v-baseline games.

tools.name: inspect_game
tools.description: Inspect a replay record.

tools.name: analyze_blunders
tools.description: Report deterministic material-loss proxy.

tools.name: evaluate_candidate
tools.description: Evaluate explicit tournament gates.

tools.name: promote_ai_candidate
tools.description: Promote only after gates and explicit approval.

tools.name: rollback_ai_candidate
tools.description: Reversibly restore prior policy with approval.

tools.name: analyze_visual_readability
tools.description: Analyze current visual configuration.

tools.name: propose_visual_change
tools.description: Create a reversible preview diff.

tools.name: preview_visual_change
tools.description: Return before/after without live mutation.

tools.name: run_visual_qa
tools.description: Run deterministic configuration QA.

tools.name: approve_visual_change
tools.description: Record approval; never mutate upstream.

tools.name: reject_visual_change
tools.description: Reject and discard preview.

tools.name: list_asset_station_presets
tools.description: List the four versioned Terra station concepts available as Game Studio material systems.

tools.name: configure_3d_asset
tools.description: Create a deterministic, versioned asset specification. This does not generate a mesh or texture archive.

tools.name: generate_procedural_asset_preview
tools.description: Return the bounded browser preview contract for an asset concept; never claim that a GLB, STL or manufacturing file was generated.

tools.name: generate_procedural_asset_files
tools.description: Generate low-poly glTF model data and deterministic PNG bytes in memory, then return the bounded QA/download manifest. The UI performs explicit file downloads; nothing is persisted by this tool.

tools.name: run_asset_qa
tools.description: Run deterministic configuration QA and disclose missing mesh, UV, PBR, printability and physical tests.

tools.name: prepare_codex_asset_prompt
tools.description: Prepare an explicit Codex agent handoff from a human asset prompt without claiming that external generation ran.

tools.name: prepare_shopify_product_draft
tools.description: Prepare an unpublished local product brief for later Shopify field mapping. No ProductCreateInput, store write, variant or checkout is created.

tools.name: create_shopify_test_cart
tools.description: Guarded Shopify cart boundary. It cannot return a fake checkout and remains NOT_CONNECTED until a real store variant is authorized.

tools.name: prepare_b2b_rfq
tools.description: Prepare an unsent manufacturing request from the asset specification; Shopify is not represented as a supplier search engine.

tools.name: submit_b2b_rfq
tools.description: Guarded supplier-send boundary. No request is sent until a real recipient is verified and separately authorized.

sites.name: autolab.run
sites.description: Super intelligence for car lovers. A WebMCP vehicle configurator, an agentic owner's guide with a live digital twin, and the 3D creation engine that measures the model instead of looking at it.

tools.name: list_autolab_experiences
tools.description: Return the three AutoLab experiences with their navigation labels, Build (configure), Learn (garage) and Create (engine), plus their URLs, roles, WebMCP tool counts, summaries and source repositories. The garage entry carries the direct link to the Tesla Roadster's Play run.

tools.name: get_autolab_overview
tools.description: Return what AutoLab by AutoMoto is, how to run it with an agent, the repositories, and the independence disclaimer. Read this before opening an experience.

tools.name: open_autolab_experience
tools.description: Navigate this tab to Build, the Configurator ('configure'); Learn, the Owner's Guide ('garage'), which opens on the Tesla Roadster; or Create, the 3D Creation Engine ('engine'). Each destination publishes its own WebMCP tools once loaded. To fly the Tesla Roadster, open 'garage' and call start_run there; garage/?vehicle=roadster&play=1 starts the same run as a link.

experience.description: Which experience to open: configure (Build), garage (Learn) or engine (Create).

tools.name: get_vehicle_configuration
tools.description: Read the current vehicle build, buyer context, price, range, delivery status, revision, transaction status, presentation state, and which vehicle body is on screen. Check renderedBody before describing what the person is looking at: representsConfiguredVehicle is false when the viewport is showing a licensed stand-in of a different car rather than the vehicle being configured. Call this before making a change so expectedRevision is current.

tools.name: list_vehicle_configuration_options
tools.description: List real options for one configuration group or all groups, including the current selection and whether each candidate resolves into a valid build.

tools.name: simulate_vehicle_configuration_change
tools.description: Preview an atomic option change without altering the build. Returns exact price, range, delivery, validity, and compatible-alternative consequences at expectedRevision.

tools.name: apply_vehicle_configuration_transaction
tools.description: Apply one to four validated configuration stages through the live mutation service. Each visible stage is revision-safe, interruptible, and captured in one undoable receipt.

tools.name: interrupt_vehicle_configuration_transaction
tools.description: Stop any currently active agent configuration transaction after its latest committed stage. Completed stages remain visible and may be undone from the returned current revision.

tools.name: undo_vehicle_configuration_transaction
tools.description: Undo the latest eligible agent configuration transaction atomically. Requires the current expectedRevision and never undoes a human change.

tools.name: present_vehicle_configuration
tools.description: Move the CONFIGURE canvas to showroom or blueprint mode, choose an angle/profile/wheel/interior view, optionally focus a truthful vehicle hotspot, and open or close the body. This changes presentation only, never the selected build — and it only affects the Configure surface, so if the page is showing the Garage nothing visible happens. Use set_autolab_workspace first, or set_vehicle_twin_view to move the twin's camera instead.

bodyOpen.description: Swing the doors, frunk and liftgate open. Refused, and reported back under `unapplied`, in blueprint mode or on a body with no openable panels — see renderedBody.canOpen from get_vehicle_configuration.

tools.name: set_vehicle_buyer_context
tools.description: Set only buyer facts the person has actually provided—EV experience, state, utility, charging access, use cases, priorities, financing, and cross-shopped vehicles—so configuration guidance and incentive results can adapt without guessing.

tools.name: estimate_vehicle_ownership_cost
tools.description: Estimate monthly payment, sales tax, loan principal, energy, maintenance, and a multi-year ownership total for the current build. Read-only, so several financing scenarios can be priced without changing the build. Every assumption is optional and falls back to a catalog-derived default; the response names which defaults were used. Conditional credits and deductions are never netted into the payment.

aprPct.description: Annual percentage rate, expressed in percent (6.5 = 6.5%).

downPayment.description: Cash down in USD. Cannot exceed the vehicle total.

homeKwhRate.description: Home electricity price in USD per kWh.

publicKwhRate.description: Public charging price in USD per kWh.

homeChargingShare.description: Fraction of charging done at home. 0.8 means 80%.

horizonYears.description: Ownership horizon used for the running total.

tools.name: compare_vehicle_configurations
tools.description: Compare the current build against up to three alternatives side by side on price, range, power, 0-60, matched savings, and delivery. Each alternative is a patch applied to the current build. Read-only: nothing is applied. Invalid alternatives are still returned, marked invalid with their violations, so a trade-off can be explained rather than hidden.

includeCurrent.description: Include the current build as the first column. Defaults to true.

tools.name: get_vehicle_twin_state
tools.description: Read the AutoLab Garage camera, active motions, selected component, available views, and the configuration revision synchronized from the configurator. Read-only and does not move the vehicle.

tools.name: list_vehicle_parts
tools.description: List the RX2 digital twin's named components. Filter by shell, chassis, running gear, or interior; request detail for measured world-space bounds in metres.

tools.name: inspect_vehicle_part
tools.description: Open AutoLab Garage, find one named component, reveal it through the body when necessary, frame it with the camera, and highlight it with an authored technical leader. Part ids come from list_vehicle_parts — call it first rather than guessing. This switches the page to Garage; set_autolab_workspace switches it back.

revealUnderBody.description: Dissolve the shell for chassis and interior components. Defaults to true.

tools.name: set_vehicle_twin_view
tools.description: Open AutoLab Garage and move the synchronized vehicle to an authored ISO, three-quarter, side, front, or top view. Side, front, and top are true orthographic elevations.

tools.name: set_vehicle_twin_motion
tools.description: Open AutoLab Garage and turn one vehicle demonstration on or off. The values do not all read the way they look: run = idle telemetry and wheel spin; drive = rolling road with steering; lights = headlamp and tail-lamp beams; panels = DISSOLVE the body shell to reveal the chassis (it does not show panels); explode = separate every component along its assembly axis; open = swing the hood, liftgate, four doors and charge-port door. run and drive are coupled — turning drive on turns run on, turning run off turns drive off — so the reply reports all six. Omit `on` to toggle. This switches the page to Garage; set_autolab_workspace switches it back.

tools.name: measure_vehicle_parts
tools.description: Measure the centre-to-centre distance and per-axis separation between two named digital-twin components in metres. Read-only and does not move the vehicle.

tools.name: set_autolab_workspace
tools.description: Show either the Configure surface (build, pricing, paint, wheels, interior) or the Garage digital twin (components, motion, measurement). Inspecting a part, setting a twin view or running a twin motion switches to Garage on its own; this is how you come back. Presentation tools such as present_vehicle_configuration only affect the Configure canvas, so switch back before using them. Read the current surface from get_vehicle_configuration. On screen the switch is labelled Shop (configure) and My Car (garage).

tools.name: tour_vehicle_twin
tools.description: Open AutoLab Garage and start (or stop) the twin's guided tour: nine stops over about thirty seconds, each a tool call on the drawing, with a caption card. The tour shows the overview, the headlamps lit, the side elevation with dimensions, the structural battery with the shell dissolved, the front drive unit, everything open, the exploded assembly, drive with lights, and the reset. A scene-changing twin tool call, or a click or key on the drawing, stops it where it is. Read-only calls and configurator context sync do not interrupt it. Pass from to start at a later stop.

from.description: Stop to start at, 1-based. Only with action start.

tools.name: get_engine_fit_report
tools.description: Return the AutoLab engine's measurement of the vehicle model against its published specification, as taken when this site was assembled: per-dimension deviation in millimetres with tolerances, the part that owns each extreme, and the self-test gate. Includes the model commit and the assembly time.

tools.name: list_engine_instruments
tools.description: Return every command the AutoLab 3D Creation Engine offers and the question each one answers.

tools.name: get_aperture_report
tools.description: Return the engine's aperture gate for the model: for each door, hood, liftgate and lid opening, whether any fixed geometry sits at the skin and well inside the opening at four open fractions, naming the part, how far inside the opening (mm) and how deep behind the skin (mm), plus the parts that merely touch the opening's edge. Read out/apertures.json as assembled by build.sh; PASS, FAIL or INFO per opening.

tools.name: start_tour
tools.description: Start the current vehicle's 30-second tour, nine stops: an overview, its lamps lit, the side dimensions, details under or behind the skin, its opening panels, the exploded assembly, a drive with lights, then reset. get_vehicles gives each vehicle's stops. from is a 1-based step. Any other call except get_state/start_tour/stop_tour interrupts the tour; stop_tour stops it explicitly. Any call that moves the scene (views, motions, camera, framing, highlighting, annotations, reset), and any click or key on the drawing, stops it where it is; reads and the host's context sync do not.

tools.name: stop_tour
tools.description: Stop the tour at its current step without restoring the scene. The tour shows views, lights, dimensions, details under the skin, open panels, explode and drive. Any other call except get_state/start_tour/stop_tour also interrupts it. Reads never stop the tour; only this, a scene-moving call, or a person's click or key does.

tools.name: get_state
tools.description: Which vehicle is on the sheet, the current view preset, camera pose, which motions are running, and what is selected. Call this first to orient.

tools.name: get_vehicles
tools.description: The vehicles this Garage can show and which one is on the sheet now, each with its views, motions, tour length and whether it has a run mode (the tray's PLAY). Every other tool works on the current vehicle; set_vehicle switches.

tools.name: set_vehicle
tools.description: Put another vehicle on the sheet: rx2 is the Hudian RX2, roadster the Tesla Roadster. Its sheet text, key, callouts, camera presets and tour come with it, and the scene goes back to how it opens (ISO view, run only, shell on, nothing selected). Stops a running tour. The first switch to a vehicle loads its model, so that reply can take a moment. Returns the new state, as get_state does.

tools.name: set_vehicle_context
tools.description: Synchronize the vehicle identity and selected build supplied by the AutoLab configurator. This does not change engineering geometry; it lets the owner guide and agent verify that both lifecycle surfaces refer to the same revision.

tools.name: set_view
tools.description: Move the camera to one of the drawing's standard views. side, front and top are true orthographic elevations; iso, q34f and q34r are perspective.

tools.name: set_motion
tools.description: Turn one of the sheet's motions on or off. run = idle telemetry and wheel spin; drive = rolling road with steering; lights = headlamp and tail-lamp beams; panels = dissolve the body shell to reveal the chassis; explode = separate every component along its assembly axis; open = swing every opening panel of the current vehicle (the RX2's hood, liftgate, four doors and charge-port door; the Roadster's two gull-wing doors; the reply's opens names them). run and drive are coupled: turning drive on turns run on, and turning run off turns drive off. The reply reports every motion, not just the one asked about, so the coupling is visible.

tools.name: set_camera
tools.description: Place the camera by absolute pose. azimuth 0 looks at the driver side in profile and increases clockwise seen from above; elevation 0 is eye level, 90 is directly overhead. Omitted angles and distance keep their current value, but any call here leaves the named view preset (the reply's preset becomes null), recentres the orbit target on the vehicle, and stops the ISO drift — so a pose set here is reproducible, which the drifting default view is not. To go back to an authored framing, call set_view.

orthographic.description: True for a flat technical projection with no convergence.

tools.name: orbit_camera
tools.description: Nudge the camera relative to where it is now. Use this to walk around the vehicle a few degrees at a time rather than guessing an absolute pose. Keeps whatever frame_part centred on, but leaves the named view preset and stops the ISO drift, so the resulting pose is reproducible. Distance is clamped to 1.2-22 m, so a zoom past either end returns the clamped distance rather than the one requested — read distance_m back from the reply.

zoom.description: Positive multiplier on distance; 0.8 moves closer, 1.25 pulls back.

tools.name: list_parts
tools.description: Every named component in the current vehicle (the reply's vehicle says which). category is one of shell (body panels and glass), chassis (the structure under the skin: the RX2's battery, subframes and drive units, the Roadster's floor, fans and thrusters), running (the wheels) or interior. The brakes ride on the wheel hubs: a chassis part on the RX2, a running part on the Roadster. Pass detail:true for bounding boxes in metres.

tools.name: get_part
tools.description: Full record for one component: its engineering description, its bounding box in metres in the vehicle frame, and where EXPLODE sends it. Accepts either the id from list_parts or the label shown on the sheet.

tools.name: frame_part
tools.description: Point the camera at one component and zoom so it fills the sheet. The best way to inspect a specific piece of the vehicle.

margin.description: Fraction of slack around the part, default 0.6.

tools.name: highlight_part
tools.description: Select a component: it is picked out of the drawing and a numbered leader runs to it, the same as hovering its row in the key. Call with no argument to clear.

part.description: Omit to clear the selection.

tools.name: set_annotations
tools.description: Show or hide the callout cards, dimension lines and title block, leaving the vehicle alone. Hide them for a clean look at the geometry.

tools.name: get_specification
tools.description: The published dimensions the current vehicle's model is built to (an independent reconstruction fitted to its maker's published figures; basis says which). Every value in dimensions_m is a length in metres; a mass, where the model carries one, comes separately as mass_kg. Also returns the model's own derived coordinates (NOSE, TAIL, XF, XR: the x positions of the bumpers and axles), which is what part bounds and measurements are expressed against. The body is an independent reconstruction fitted to published dimensions and photographs, not manufacturer CAD.

tools.name: measure
tools.description: Distance in metres between the bounding-box CENTRES of two components, plus the per-axis separation. This is not a clearance: two parts that interpenetrate and two parts 200 mm apart can return the same distance. For clearance, read both parts' bounds_m from get_part and compare the facing faces. Axes: x forward (+x is the nose), y up (0 is the ground), z lateral (+z is the passenger side).

tools.name: list_visible_parts
tools.description: What the camera can see right now: a grid of rays through the sheet, first surface hit per ray, tallied by component. Returns each visible component with the percentage of the sheet it covers, where its visible area sits on the sheet (0..1 from the left and from the top) and its nearest distance; plus how much of the sheet the vehicle fills. Use it to know what a person is looking at before explaining it, or to confirm a frame_part landed. Reads the sheet's own part-id buffer, so it honours the dissolved shell and open panels.

columns.description: Ray grid width; rows follow the sheet aspect. Default 40.

tools.name: clearance
tools.description: Nearest surface-to-surface gap in metres between two components as they are posed right now (open panels and explode change it), with the two closest points in the vehicle frame. Unlike measure, which uses bounding-box centres, this is the real gap: use it for packaging questions such as how close the battery pack sits to the floor or a tyre to its arch. Zero means the surfaces touch or intersect.

tools.name: frame_point
tools.description: Point the camera at a coordinate in the vehicle frame (metres: x forward from the wheelbase midpoint, y up from the ground, z to the right) and look at it from a chosen bearing and distance. For inspecting a place rather than a part: an engine finding at x/y/z, a gap between two components, a spot on the skin. Omitted azimuth and elevation keep the current bearing; distance defaults to 1.6 m. Things under the shell need set_motion {motion:"panels", on:true} first.

distance_m.description: Camera distance from the point; 1.2 m is the floor (the near plane is 0.5 m).

tools.name: reset
tools.description: Return the sheet to how it opens: no run, ISO view, shell on, nothing exploded or open, nothing selected. The ISO view drifts slowly by design, so the camera pose it returns to is not fixed.

tools.name: start_run
tools.description: Start the run mode, as the tray's PLAY does: the Tesla Roadster at the start line at the foot of the wall-ride ramp, 8 m before the curl, which turns vertical 9 m up and runs on upside down to an overhang 21.6 m up (the hop autopilot starts 30 m back), in drive mode with a chase camera. A real-time simulation decides whether the car makes the wall ride or falls off it, and whether a hop lands. Switches the Garage to the Roadster first if another vehicle is on the sheet. Without autopilot the car waits for set_drive_inputs or a person's keys; autopilot "wallride" drives the reveal's wall ride (fans on, about 20 ft/s up the wall, a hang upside down on the overhang, then off the tip on the jets) and "hop" the thruster hop (8.5 m up on the corner jets and down again); any input takes over from the autopilot (set_drive_inputs with only fans or wing leaves it driving). A run already on starts again from its start line. The tools that move the drawing's own views, camera or motions (set_view, set_motion, set_camera, orbit_camera, frame_part, highlight_part, frame_point) end the run first, as stop_run does. Returns get_run_state.

tools.name: stop_run
tools.description: End the run, as STOP or Esc does: the ramp goes, the car is parked back at the garage origin and the sheet returns to its ISO view. Returns how the run ended (last), or nothing when no run was on.

tools.name: set_drive_inputs
tools.description: Set what the driver holds in a run; each value stays until changed, and omitted ones keep theirs. throttle -1..1 (negative reverses), brake 0..1, steer -1..1 (+ is right), boost (the four rear cold-gas nozzles), hop (the corner jets: lift off, hover, and once let go a landing burn), yawL / yawR (the nose side jets: nose left / right), fans (the downforce fans, about 4,800 kgf once spooled; they hold the car on the wall) and wing (road, lowDrag, highDownforce). The thrust gas is one 250 kg tank whose pressure falls as it empties. Takes over from an autopilot, except a call that sets only fans and/or wing: the autopilot keeps driving with the car set up that way (start_run with autopilot "wallride", then fans: false, is the same wall ride without its fans). Needs a run (start_run). Returns the inputs the next physics step will use and get_run_state.

tools.name: get_run_state
tools.description: The run as its telemetry shows it: active, outcome (running, summit, fell, crashed or stopped) and its message in words ("Held the overhang", "Fell off at 108 deg", "Crashed", "Out of gas"), speed km/h, pitch deg (past 90 up the wall, about 170 upside down on the overhang), altitude ft, downforce kg, g, tank psi and gas kg, fans %, wing, the car's position in metres (x along the run-in, the ramp's foot at x = 0; y up), the inputs in use, whether an autopilot drives, and the camera. With no run on: active false and how the last run ended.

sites.name: gentropic.org
sites.description: @gcu/weir

tools.name: weir_queryItems
tools.description: Search/list weir feed items, newest first. Filters: q (substring over title/excerpt/text), feed (a source by id OR name, e.g. "Saved Links"), category (folder name; "" = ungrouped), type (article|video|release|paper|status|track|podcast|commit|issue|note|doc), view (inbox|saved|archived), unread (bool), saved (bool), limit (default 30, max 100). PROVENANCE filters (the agent footprint): addedBy = items the agent ADDED (true = any agent, or an identity string like "claude:librarian"); taggedBy = items the agent TAGGED. Filters combine. Paginated: returns { count, total, hasMore, items, nextCursor }; page by passing nextCursor back with the SAME filters. Items are compact (id, title, url, feed, published, tags, added_by, excerpt). Use weir_listSources first to see feed/folder names.

feed.description: Scope to one source — its feed id or display name (e.g. "Saved Links")

category.description: Scope to one folder by name ("" = ungrouped)

type.description: Item type filter

view.description: Which view to scope to

addedBy.description: Items the agent ADDED — true (any agent) or an identity string (e.g. "claude:librarian")

taggedBy.description: Items the agent TAGGED — true (any agent) or an identity string

limit.description: Max items per page (default 30, cap 100)

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous call’s nextCursor — reuse the same filters

tools.name: weir_listSources
tools.description: Source overview (compact — safe on a 400+ feed corpus). DEFAULT returns { feedCount, folders:[{category,feeds,inbox}], health:{failing,stale,…}, troubled:[…] } — folder summaries + a health tally + ONLY the non-healthy feeds (state/lastPolled/fails/lastError), so you can spot prune candidates without dumping everything. Pass `q` to FIND a feed by name/URL/id across ALL folders (the way to locate a specific feed) → { query, count, feeds:[…incl url] }. Pass `category` for the FULL per-feed list of one folder. Pair with weir_updateFeed / weir_removeFeed to curate, weir_queryItems({feed}) to drill in.

q.description: Find feeds whose name/URL/id contains this (across all folders)

category.description: Full per-feed detail for one folder ("" = ungrouped)

tools.name: weir_addFeed
tools.description: Subscribe to a feed by URL — adapter auto-detected (RSS/Atom/JSON Feed, YouTube channel, GitHub repo); an initial poll fires in the app. Optional `name` + `category` (folder). When YOU (Claude) add it, it is stamped source:agent + your identity and lands in weir_reviewQueue as a `feed` proposal for the user to ratify — pass `rationale` so they see WHY. Returns the created feed.

url.description: Feed or page URL to subscribe to

name.description: Display name (default: derived from the URL/adapter)

rationale.description: Why you are proposing this feed — shown in the review queue at ratify time

tools.name: weir_updateFeed
tools.description: Curate a feed: ARCHIVE/unarchive it (retire a dead/dormant feed off the health warning — items kept, poller skips it, fully reversible — the never-delete alternative to removing), change its URL (e.g. fix a moved/404 feed — items stay, validators reset, it re-polls now), rename, recategorize (folder), set retention ("forever" or a day count), poll interval (minutes), image policy, or full-text auto-fetch. Identify it by `id` (from weir_listSources). Not destructive. Returns the applied patch (+ `repoll` result when the URL changed).

id.description: Feed id (from weir_listSources)

archived.description: true = retire the feed (off the failing/stale warning, poller skips it, items kept); false = restore + re-poll. Reversible, never deletes.

url.description: New feed URL (fixes a moved/dead feed; re-polls immediately)

retention.description: "forever", or a number of days to keep before archiving

images_allowed.description: Always load images for this feed

tools.name: weir_removeFeed
tools.description: Unsubscribe and DELETE a feed and its items — for pruning dead/moved sources (DNS-gone, TLS-dead, 404) during a curation sweep. Destructive + NOT reversible (no trash, unlike the stacks). Gated behind a user setting; if disabled, errors and points to the UI. Confirm with the user before calling. Returns { removed, name, items }.

id.description: Feed id (from weir_listSources)

tools.name: weir_renameFeed
tools.description: Re-key a feed's ID (not its display name — use weir_updateFeed for the name). A feed id is load-bearing: the adapter mints item ids as ` : ` every poll, and content files, tombstones, and catalog cards are addressed by it. This migrates ALL of that in lockstep (relocating content; nothing is data-deleted) and preserves read/saved/tags. Use it to clean up an id that was auto-derived from a bad name — e.g. a feed that landed on the generic host slug `bsky-app`. The newId is slugified; a collision with an existing id is rejected. Returns { renamed, from, items, tombstones }.

id.description: Current feed id (from weir_listSources)

newId.description: Desired feed id (will be slugified, e.g. "arne-androidarts")

tools.name: weir_repoll
tools.description: Force a fresh poll of one feed right now, bypassing conditional-GET so the full body re-parses even if nothing changed — re-derives titles, picks up edits. The clean way to refresh a feed (does NOT reset validators or schedule, unlike changing the URL). Use it to heal a microblog feed reading as "(untitled)", or to pull a feed immediately. Returns { id, inserted, updated, skipped } or { error }.

id.description: Feed id (from weir_listSources)

tools.name: weir_recover
tools.description: Recover a dead/truncated feed's lost history from the Internet Archive (Wayback Machine): finds old snapshots of the feed URL, re-parses their items, and stores them — archived history preserved, nothing deleted. Default QUEUES feed(s) into a gentle background drip (one IA request every few minutes, resumes across restarts) — the right tool for a batch of dead feeds; `now:true` recovers a single feed immediately as a throttled burst and returns counts (good for proving one feed before queuing many). Scope by id, ids[], or category. Returns recovery counts (now) or drip status (queued). Pairs with never-delete: recover the data, keep the feed, don't prune.

id.description: A single feed id (from weir_listSources)

ids.description: Multiple feed ids to queue into the drip

category.description: Queue every feed in this folder

now.description: Recover the single `id` immediately (foreground burst) instead of queuing the background drip

tools.name: weir_resolveLinks
tools.description: Kick the background resolver to process pending saved links now — resolve share.google/shortener URLs to their real destination and fetch thumbnail/title/excerpt metadata, gently over time (a couple every ~15s, so it never burst-hits the shortener). Returns { kicked, pending, running }. Imported links resolve on their own; use this to nudge it.

tools.name: weir_resolverLog
tools.description: Read the background link-resolver run log — { pending, running, resolved, parked, reasons, recent, startedAt, updatedAt }. `resolved` = links fully resolved+enriched; `parked` = gave up after retries; `reasons` tallies every failed try (http-429 = share.google throttling, no-redirect, network); `recent` = the last few parked links (host + reason). Use it to review an overnight run.

tools.name: weir_reEnrich
tools.description: Rework saved links: clear their enriched flag so the background resolver re-fetches + re-applies metadata (title/thumbnail/excerpt). `weakTitles:true` re-does only links with a weak title (e.g. "Source: Hackaday" → real og:title); `all:true` re-does every saved link. Already-resolved urls are re-fetched directly (fast, no share.google throttle). Returns { queued, pending }.

weakTitles.description: Only links whose title is weak

tools.name: weir_getItem
tools.description: Get one weir item by id: glass facets + description (if cataloged), the card's `card` authorship block (cataloger=provider:model, reviewer human|agent, by=identity, needs_review), item provenance (`added_by`, plus `tag_src`/`tag_by` = who applied each tag), and its knowledge-graph edges — `links` (what its body links to via [[ref]], resolved to {ref,id,title}) and `backlinks` (items whose body links to it). Pass content:true to include the extracted article/note text (capped 8k).

id.description: Item id (from weir_queryItems)

content.description: Include the extracted body text

tools.name: weir_getItems
tools.description: BATCH weir_getItem — fetch many items at once (reference work fans out: one search → pull a dozen cards). Pass `ids` (from weir_search / weir_queryItems / weir_queryCatalog). Returns { count, items:[…same shape as weir_getItem], missing?:[ids not found], omitted? }. With content:true each body is capped at 8k so the batch is capped tighter (~25 vs ~60). Saves a round-trip storm vs. calling weir_getItem N times.

ids.description: Item ids to fetch

content.description: Include each item's extracted body text (capped 8k each)

tools.name: weir_search
tools.description: RANKED full-text search (the librarian BM25 index) — relevance-ordered, better than weir_queryItems's substring `q` for "most relevant about X" on a large corpus. CURATION-AWARE by default: results are reranked so the curated minority (books, notes, repo `doc` items, saved links) outranks the auto-ingested feed/video firehose, with a bonus when the query matches an item's facet terms — for a reference query the curated layer is the signal (pass rerank:false for raw BM25, or curated:true to hard-scope to the curated tier only). Each hit carries its `tier` (curated|neutral|firehose) when reranked. VOCAB-SYNONYM EXPANSION is also on by default: a query term that is a controlled-vocabulary prefLabel/altLabel also matches its synonyms (the seeded cross-lingual pairs like kriging↔krigagem bridge lexically, no embeddings) — the response carries `expanded:{term→[synonyms]}` when it fires; pass expand:false for the literal query. SEES THE ARCHIVE by default (the standing corpus, never-delete) — hits carry `archived:true` when archived; pass includeArchived:false to limit to active. Optional scope filters (feed/type/category/view/unread/saved) narrow it like queryItems. Returns { ranked, reranked?, count, items:[…,score,tier?,archived?] } (ranked:false = index not ready, fell back to substring). Use queryItems to LIST a whole feed/folder; use search to FIND by relevance; use weir_queryCatalog to search WITHIN a facet set.

feed.description: Scope to a source (id or display name)

type.description: Scope to an item type (e.g. "doc" for repo/project docs)

view.description: Scope to a view

curated.description: Hard-scope to the curated tier only (books/notes/repo docs/saved links) — excludes the feed firehose

rerank.description: Curation-aware reranking (default true); pass false for raw BM25 relevance

expand.description: Vocab-synonym query expansion (default true): a query term that is a controlled-vocabulary prefLabel/altLabel also matches its synonyms — bridges curated + cross-lingual pairs (kriging↔krigagem) lexically. Pass false for the literal query. When it fires, the response carries `expanded:{term→[synonyms]}`.

weights.description: PER-CALL rerank weight override (ephemeral — for tuning; defaults are curated 2.5 / neutral 1.0 / firehose 0.6 / facet 0.2). Clamped 0–10. Sweep these against the eval queries, then report the winning set to bake as the default.

explain.description: Surface the raw lexical `lex` score per hit + the `weights` used, so you can SEE why each item ranked where it did while tuning

includeArchived.description: Include archived items (default TRUE — the reference desk sees the whole archive; pass false to limit to active)

limit.description: Max hits (default 20, cap 100)

tools.name: weir_setState
tools.description: Set read / saved / archived (each a boolean; pass only the ones to change) — on ONE item (`id`), a LIST of specific items (`ids`: an array — applied in one atomic pass, the right way to flip many known items at once), or every item matching a query (pass q/feed/category/type/view/unread/saved — e.g. archive a dead feed, mark a folder read). A query bulk call REQUIRES a scoping filter (no accidental whole-corpus change). All reversible — archive never deletes (weir_unarchiveAll reverses a sweep). Returns the item (id mode) or { matched, patch, missing? } (ids/query mode).

id.description: A single item id; omit to bulk over `ids` or a query

ids.description: An explicit list of item ids — flip them all in one atomic write (preferred over many single-id calls). Unknown ids come back in `missing`.

feed.description: Bulk scope: a source by id or name

type.description: Bulk scope: item type

view.description: Bulk scope: a view (use view:"saved" to scope to saved items)

tools.name: weir_tag
tools.description: Add and/or remove tags — on ONE item (pass `id`) or on EVERY item matching a query (pass any of q/feed/category/type/view/unread/saved — the "tag all these results" verb). Tags are stamped source:'llm' (the UI shows them apart from your 'human' tags), are immediately searchable/queryable, and feed the glass `entity` facet on the next catalog. Returns the updated item (id mode) or { matched, changed } (query mode). Use weir_queryItems first to preview a bulk scope.

id.description: Tag a single item by id (from weir_queryItems); omit to bulk-tag a query

feed.description: Bulk scope: a source by id or display name

category.description: Bulk scope: a folder name ("" = ungrouped)

type.description: Bulk scope: item type (article|video|paper|note|…)

view.description: Bulk scope: a view

tools.name: weir_unarchiveAll
tools.description: Bring EVERY archived item back to active and clear its expiry (so retention won't re-shelve it) — the one-shot "I keep everything" restore that reverses an over-eager auto-archive sweep. Reversible; nothing is deleted. Returns { unarchived }.

tools.name: weir_provenanceMigrate
tools.description: One-shot cleanup: normalize the agent's historical authorship stamps to the unified `source:agent` tier — tags previously marked 'llm' and relation edges marked 'claude' (both meant Claude) become 'agent'. Pass `backfillBooks` (an identity string, e.g. "claude:librarian") to ALSO repair agent-proposed book holdings whose `added_by` was stripped by the pre-fix makeItem bug — identified by their `web-proposed` tag — so they re-enter the review queue. Idempotent and safe to re-run; nothing is deleted. Returns { migrated: { tags, edges, books } }.

backfillBooks.description: Identity to stamp on web-proposed books missing added_by (e.g. "claude:librarian"); omit to skip the book backfill

tools.name: weir_addBook
tools.description: Add OR update owned/physical books in the holdings (the "Books" library) — e.g. cataloging a real shelf, or stamping series/seq onto books already there. Each book: title (required), author, isbn (→ Open Library fills cover/date/publisher), series + seq (the volume number — series+seq keep a numbered set TOGETHER and in volume order on the shelf; without seq a series scatters by year), date, tags (yours), ddc/lcc (display codes). To UPDATE an existing holding in place, pass its `id` (e.g. "book:269049145", from the shelf list / weir_queryItems) — read/saved/tags and the catalog card are preserved, and `structured` is MERGED, so you only pass the fields you are changing (existing isbn/ddc/lcc/series/seq are kept; a plain LibraryThing re-import will not wipe a stamped series). Without an id a new book is created (keyed by isbn||title). Batch with `books:[…]` (preferred) or pass ONE book inline. A NEW book YOU add is stamped source:agent and surfaces in weir_reviewQueue as a `book` proposal (tag it `to-buy` for a wishlist item you don't own yet); pass `rationale` so the user sees why. Returns { inserted, updated, books }.

id.description: Existing holding id to UPDATE in place (e.g. "book:269049145"); omit to create a new book
