title.description: Book title (required for a NEW book; omit when updating an existing holding by id, e.g. a shelved-status write)

author.description: Author ("Surname, Given" or "Given Surname")

series.description: Series title for a numbered set (e.g. "YKK")

tags.description: Your tags (stamped as human; only applied when creating)

shelved.description: Physical-shelf status — round-trips with the shelf-list export’s "shelved" JSON; preloads the sheet checkboxes

rationale.description: Why you are proposing this book (e.g. a to-buy suggestion) — shown in the review queue; tag it "to-buy" for a wishlist item you don't own yet

id.description: Shortcut: update a single existing holding by id

title.description: Shortcut: add/update a single book by its title (with the same sibling fields)

tools.name: weir_addLink
tools.description: Save a link into weir's "Saved Links" — the same source the Telegram bot feeds, so you can save a URL directly (not only via Telegram). Pass `url` (one link) or `links:[{ url, title?, tags?, date? }]`. The background resolver follows wrapped/shortened URLs and fetches title/excerpt/thumbnail over time; it then catalogs like any item. Idempotent (keyed by URL hash) — re-saving updates in place and never resets read/saved/tags. A NEW save is stamped source:agent + your identity (its tags too); a re-import of an existing link is not relabeled. Returns { inserted, updated, links }.

url.description: A single link URL to save

title.description: Optional title (else derived from the host; the resolver may improve it)

tags.description: Optional tags to apply (stamped as yours-via-agent)

links.description: Batch: [{ url, title?, tags?, date? }] (preferred over a single url for many)

tools.name: weir_ingestRepo
tools.description: Ingest a code repo’s own DOCS as a first-class source (SPEC-repos-as-source) — so the GCU constellation becomes a queryable subgraph in weir. weir never runs git; YOU (with the files + git) decide WHAT to ingest. `repo` = the repo name/path (e.g. "auditable"). `anchor` = the commit SHA these docs are from. TWO ways to supply content: (a) **`paths`** = [path strings, or { path, title?, url? }] — weir reads each NAMED file from the read-only repos folder you mounted in Settings (no full text through this call; the way to ingest at fidelity without a verbatim conduit); (b) **`docs`** = [{ path, title?, markdown, url?, date? }] — you pass the body inline (use for a gitignored/untracked file like CLAUDE.md, or when no folder is mounted). Mix both. README/SPEC/docs/CLAUDE.md — docs, NOT code. First call CREATES the source as a proposal (→ weir_reviewQueue, ratify like a feed); later calls REFRESH it (and can fix the name/category/rationale in place). REFRESH recipe: read the stored anchor from weir_listSources, run `git diff --name-only HEAD -- ` (+ `--diff-filter=D` for deletions) locally, then call this with only the changed `paths`/`docs` + the new HEAD as `anchor` + deleted paths in `removed`. Idempotent (stable ids; never resets read/saved/tags); `removed` archives (never deletes). Docs become `doc` items — searchable, quotable, relatable; relate your dive-map (a stacks note) to them with weir_relate. Returns { ok, source, inserted, updated, removed, anchor, bodyless?, bodylessReason? } — `bodyless` lists paths that landed with NO body (they can't be cataloged — no text to read), and `bodylessReason` maps each to WHY (not-found | read-error: | empty | no-path) so you can self-diagnose. Paths are repo-relative (weir prepends the repo slug → ` / / `); keep them repo-relative so re-ingest updates the same items in place.

repo.description: The repo name or path (e.g. "auditable" or "../auditable") — the source key + mounted-folder dir is its basename

name.description: Display name for the source (default: "<repo> (repo)"); updatable on refresh

anchor.description: The commit SHA these docs are from — the dive-ledger anchor; advanced on each refresh

paths.description: Doc paths to READ from the mounted repos folder: ["README.md", …] or [{ path, title?, url? }]. No verbatim conduit — weir reads the named files itself.

docs.description: Docs with inline bodies: [{ path, title?, markdown, url?, date? }] — for gitignored/untracked files or when no folder is mounted

removed.description: Doc paths deleted since the anchor — archived (never deleted)

category.description: Folder to group the source under (default "repos"); updatable on refresh

rationale.description: Why you are adding this source — shown in the review queue; updatable on refresh (capped to a short blurb)

annotations.title: Ingest a repo as a source

tools.name: weir_ingestDocument
tools.description: Ingest PDF document(s) you have DROPPED under the read-only repos folder Arthur mounted in weir (Settings → Courier) — the way to add binary documents at fidelity without a verbatim conduit or a bridge fetch. YOU (free to download from anywhere) save the PDFs under the mounted GitHub folder, then pass their `paths` (relative to the mount root, e.g. ["weir-desk/documents/ccg/declustering.pdf"], optionally [{ path, title?, author?, url? }]). weir reads each file, extracts its text (+ a per-page offset map for page-anchored weir_quote), and stores it as a first-class, content-addressed `document` item: full-text searchable, quotable, catalogable, relatable. Idempotent (same bytes → same id, updates in place). Ingested LIVE + attributed (source:agent + your identity) — NOT gated in the review queue (a corpus the user asked for shouldn't flood it; see your footprint via weir_listMine). NOTE: extraction is currently naive reading order (v0) — fine for single-column; two-column docs (CCG guidebooks) shuffle until the reconstruction pass ships, after which the corpus is re-extracted in place (the binary is the source of truth). Returns { added, items:[{id,path,title,pages,chars}], failed?:{path:reason} }.

paths.description: PDF paths relative to the mounted folder root: ["weir-desk/documents/x.pdf", …] or [{ path, title?, author?, url? }]. weir reads the named files itself (no bytes through this call).

path.description: Convenience: a single path (use `paths` for batches)

tools.name: weir_catalogItem
tools.description: Catalog one item with the configured LLM right now (fills its glass facets + description) — best for items with real body text. Returns glass_id, facets, description. On a metadata-only item (too little text to read, e.g. a book with no body/abstract) it ABSTAINS rather than fabricate: returns ok:false + skipped + a note, leaving it needs_review — author it yourself via weir_reviewItem({ id, description, facets }). Needs the cataloger configured and reachable (Lemonade via the bridge).

id.description: Item id (from weir_queryItems)

tools.name: weir_listModels
tools.description: List the catalog provider's available models (so you can pick one). Optional `provider` overrides the configured one (lemonade|ollama|nanogpt|groq|custom). Returns { provider, count, models }.

provider.description: Override the configured provider

tools.name: weir_setCatalog
tools.description: Set cataloger config — provider, model, baseUrl, paceMs (delay between calls; 0 = fastest, good for cloud), maxBodyChars (doc text sent; cost/context). NOT the API key (set that in the UI). Takes effect on the next cataloged item; a running batch picks it up. Returns the new config.

provider.description: lemonade | ollama | nanogpt | groq | custom

paceMs.description: Delay between catalog calls in ms (0 = no pause)

maxBodyChars.description: Max doc chars sent to the LLM (500–20000)

mailto.description: Contact email for the Crossref/OpenAlex polite pool (biblio enrich); sent only to those scholarly APIs

tools.name: weir_catalogControl
tools.description: Start / stop / clear / inspect the catalog batch. action:"start" catalogs un-cataloged non-archived items (paced, runs in the page) — optionally SCOPED to one feed/folder/type via feed|category|type (omit all → whole corpus); "stop" cancels; "clear" discards ALL cards + un-files every item (items/content/reading state untouched; reversible by re-cataloging) for a clean restart; "status" (default) reports running state, progress {total,done,failed}, and cataloged/total counts. start returns {running, todo, deferred}.

action.description: Default: status

feed.description: start scope: a source by id OR display name (e.g. "Saved Links")

category.description: start scope: a folder name ("" = ungrouped)

type.description: start scope: item type (article|video|paper|…)

recatalog.description: with action:start + a scope: discard that scope's cataloger-generated cards and re-catalog from scratch (re-do a batch cataloged under an old rule). SAFE-BY-DEFAULT: hand-authored / human-reviewed cards (a `reviewer` stamp) are PRESERVED — only regenerable cataloger cards are redone — so it can't silently destroy authored curation (the cataloger abstains on thin/metadata-only items like book holdings, which would have nothing to regenerate them). Returns `preserved` (count kept).

includeAuthored.description: with recatalog: ALSO redo hand-authored / human-reviewed cards in scope (default false → they're preserved). Use only when you want authored cards re-derived — e.g. body text has since arrived and the body-fed cards beat the hand facets.

tools.name: weir_reviewQueue
tools.description: The UNIFIED review queue — everything awaiting human attention, tagged by `kind`: "catalog" = cataloger cards flagged low-confidence/unparseable (carry facets + confidence); "feed"/"relation"/"book" = things the agent ADDED (source:agent) not yet ratified — a feed, a relation edge, or a book holding (e.g. a to-buy suggestion). Each item carries the proposer `by` identity, a `rationale` (why), and `ratifyWith` — the tool to act on it: catalog → weir_reviewItem (confirm/correct), feed/relation/book → weir_ratify (bless or dismiss). Returns { counts:{catalog,feed,relation,book,total}, count, items }. Optional `kind` filters to one. This is the decides-vs-proposes gate: the agent proposes, you ratify here.

kind.description: Filter to one kind (default: all)

limit.description: Max items (default 30, cap 100)

tools.name: weir_listMine
tools.description: Your footprint on the corpus — every contribution stamped by an agent identity, across kinds, with its ratification status. The provenance LENS for self-audit, the propose-vs-ratify ledger, and cross-channel coordination; pairs with weir_reviewQueue (which shows only the pending tray). Defaults to the CALLING channel's identity; pass identity:"*" for any agent (the cross-channel view), or a specific identity string. `kinds` filters to a subset of tag|note|edge|feed|book|catalog; `status` filters to one (pending|ratified|applied|authored|dismissed). Returns { identity, counts:{total, byKind, byStatus}, contributions:[{ kind, id, label, identity, status, … }] }. IMPORTANT: this is a CURRENT-STATE lens, not a history — contributions later undone or corrected by a human are NOT shown (weir's stamps are attribution; the undo paths erase them). It is the ground truth to reconcile your MEMORY against (memory says you added X but it is not here → your memory is stale). Read-only.

identity.description: Scope to an identity (default: the calling channel); "*" = any agent

kinds.description: Limit to these contribution kinds

status.description: Filter to one status: pending | ratified | applied | authored | dismissed

limit.description: Max contributions (default 100, cap 500)

tools.name: weir_ratify
tools.description: Ratify or dismiss an agent STRUCTURAL proposal from the review queue (decides-vs-proposes §2.1) — a feed the agent added, a relation edge it proposed, or a book holding it suggested. `action:"ratify"` blesses it (it stays, marked ratified, and leaves the queue); `action:"dismiss"` undoes it (feed → remove it + its just-polled items; relation → unrelate; book → archive it, non-destructive). For kind "feed" pass `feedId`; "book" pass `bookId`; "relation" pass `from` + `to` (+ optional `type`). Catalog cards are confirmed via weir_reviewItem instead, not here. Returns the action taken.

kind.description: What kind of proposal

action.description: ratify = keep + bless; dismiss = undo (default ratify)

feedId.description: kind "feed": the proposed feed id (from weir_reviewQueue)

bookId.description: kind "book": the proposed book holding id

from.description: kind "relation": the source item id or glass_id

to.description: kind "relation": the target item id or glass_id

type.description: kind "relation": optionally scope to one edge type

tools.name: weir_reviewItem
tools.description: Confirm, correct, or AUTHOR a catalog card. Facets-only on an existing card = confirm (clears needs_review). Pass a `description` (a precise one-sentence summary) to set the card's blurb by hand — and if the item has no card yet, this CREATES one (a deliberate "I know this item" add, e.g. a metadata-only book the cataloger can only hallucinate). Authored over MCP, the card is stamped source:agent + your identity. `facets` is an object of facet→string[] overwriting only the given facets (e.g. {"entity":["minecraft"],"scale":[]}). Pairs with weir_addBook → weir_reviewItem to land a pointed add fully formed.

id.description: Item id (from weir_reviewQueue / weir_queryItems)

description.description: A precise one-sentence card summary to set by hand (creates the card if none exists)

facets.description: Optional facet corrections, e.g. {"scale":[],"entity":["minecraft"]} — overwrites only the given facets

tools.name: weir_mergeFacetTerm
tools.description: Thesaurus normalization: rewrite a facet term across the WHOLE catalog (from → to within one facet, de-duped) so facet-browsing stops splitting one concept across spelling/synonym variants — e.g. spatial usa→united states, entity ai→artificial intelligence. Also RECORDS the merge in the controlled vocabulary: the from-term becomes a skos:altLabel (synonym) of the target, so the decision is remembered (inspect via weir_vocab), not just applied. An empty/omitted `to` DROPS the term (records nothing). Use weir_listFacets to spot variants first. Pass one {facet, from, to} or a {merges:[…]} batch (one atomic flush). Pure card edit — items/reading state untouched, reversible. Returns each merge's card-change count.

from.description: Existing term to rewrite

to.description: Replacement term (empty/omitted = drop the from-term)

merges.description: Batch of {facet, from, to} merges applied atomically

tools.name: weir_vocab
tools.description: Inspect the controlled vocabulary / thesaurus (SKOS-shaped, GLASS §7). No args → per-facet concept-count overview. `facet` → that facet's concepts. `facet`+`term` → one concept (prefLabel + altLabels/synonyms + broader/narrower/related). `export:true` → SKOS JSON-LD (optionally for one `facet`). The vocabulary GROWS from curation: weir_mergeFacetTerm records the merged term as a synonym (altLabel); weir_relateTerm declares BT/NT/RT.

term.description: With facet: return just this term's concept

tools.name: weir_relateTerm
tools.description: Declare typed thesaurus relations (SKOS, GLASS §7) on a term: broader (BT), narrower (NT), related (RT), or alt (a synonym/altLabel that redirects to this term). Inverses are maintained automatically (declare broader → the target gains narrower). Each value is a string or list of terms. This is the ratified way to grow hierarchy — a similarity signal may propose, but a relation exists only once you declare it here (decides-vs-proposes). Use weir_vocab to inspect.

term.description: The preferred term to relate

alt.description: Synonym(s) that redirect to this term — string or array (altLabel/UF)

tools.name: weir_buildGazetteer
tools.description: Bulk-populate SPATIAL containment from the vendored gazetteer (GLASS §7 thesaurus): the CC0 CIA World Factbook backbone (country→continent, capital→country) + a curated supplement (US states, major cities). Declares the broader/narrower edges so the faceted browser + weir_queryCatalog roll up — selecting a parent (e.g. japan) catches its subtree (tokyo, osaka). Deterministic + idempotent (re-running links only what is new). Inspect with weir_vocab({facet:"spatial"}). Returns { linked, total }.

tools.name: weir_works
tools.description: Inspect (and optionally rebuild) FRBR work-grouping (GLASS §4.1): items that are the same Work across manifestations — wire-syndication, re-uploads, cross-posts. `regroup:true` runs the deterministic grouping pass (identical canonical URL + SimHash near-duplicate; NOT an LLM call) then reports; default reports current grouping. Returns { stats:{items,works,manifestations,biggest}, works:[{work_id,size,members:[{title,feed}]}] } biggest-first — to eyeball precision. De-dup as GROUPING not discarding: nothing is deleted, work_id is a reversible overlay.

regroup.description: Recompute the grouping before reporting (run this first — the corpus has no work_ids until you do)

maxHamming.description: SimHash near-dup threshold in bits (default 3; higher = looser grouping)

limit.description: Max example clusters to return (default 20, cap 100)

tools.name: weir_relatedTo
tools.description: The knowledge graph around an item OR stacks note (GLASS §10): its ratified `related` edges — outgoing + backlinks — PLUS on-demand SUGGESTIONS (set suggest:false to skip) from facet co-occurrence, each carrying the shared facet terms (the "why") and a score, PLUS the soft `wikilinks` layer (resolved [[name]] cross-references + who annotates this, navigable without ratification). Pass an item id (from weir_queryItems), a glass_id, or a stacks PATH (e.g. "gcu/README.md"). An uncataloged note has no ratified edges yet but still shows its wikilinks. Suggestions/wikilinks are NOT edges until ratified via weir_relate.

id.description: Item id, glass_id, or stacks path

limit.description: Max suggestions (default 8, cap 25)

tools.name: weir_relate
tools.description: Propose a typed `related` edge between two items or stacks notes — decides-vs-proposes (GLASS §2.1): a facet-overlap suggestion becomes a real edge ONLY when declared here. `from`/`to` are item ids, glass_ids, OR stacks paths (e.g. "gcu/README.md"); an uncataloged endpoint (e.g. a fresh note) is auto-carded at Stage-0 so it can join the graph — no manual catalog step needed. `type` ∈ related | same-topic | extends | contradicts | responds-to | same-work (default "related"). Pass `rationale` (why these relate) — it shows in weir_reviewQueue as a `relation` proposal until the user ratifies. Pass remove:true to delete the edge (optionally just one type). Stored on the from-item, stamped source:agent + your identity; reversible (weir never deletes the items).

from.description: Source item id / glass_id / stacks path

to.description: Target item id / glass_id / stacks path

type.description: related | same-topic | extends | contradicts | responds-to | same-work

rationale.description: Why these relate — shown in the review queue at ratify time

remove.description: Remove the edge instead of creating it

tools.name: weir_listFacets
tools.description: Glass catalog facets across the non-archived corpus: each facet → { total, terms:[{term,count}], omitted }, top terms by count (entity alone can be thousands). Facets: domain, entity, process, method, scale, spatial, temporal, form, provenance. Cataloged items contribute LLM facets; the rest contribute deterministic Stage-0 facets. Use facet+limit to drill into one.

limit.description: Top terms per facet by count (default 25, max 200)

minCount.description: Only terms appearing at least this many times

tools.name: weir_queryCatalog
tools.description: Faceted INTERSECTION query over the catalog — the Ranganathan move: find interdisciplinary material by intersecting facets instead of one shelf or keyword. Pass `facets`, a map of facet → term(s): within a facet the terms UNION, across facets they INTERSECT — e.g. { domain:["geostatistics"], entity:["kriging","itabirite"], process:["estimation"] } = (geostatistics) AND (kriging OR itabirite) AND (estimation). Facets: domain, entity, process, method, scale, spatial, stance, form, provenance, temporal (weir_listFacets shows live terms). Terms resolve against the controlled vocabulary (a synonym → its preferred term); unknown or zero-hit terms come back in `vocabularyNotes` instead of silently missing. Optional `q` ANDs a ranked full-text constraint (composes with weir_search). Finds what excerpt/substring search cannot — e.g. entity:"itabirite" hits a cataloged item even when the word is not in its title. Read-only. Returns { count, total, items:[{ …, glass_id?, facets, matchedTerms }], vocabularyNotes? }.

facets.description: Map of facet name → term or [terms]. e.g. { domain: ["geostatistics"], entity: ["kriging","itabirite"] }. Union within a facet, intersect across facets.

q.description: Optional free-text to AND a ranked-search constraint (weir_search) onto the intersection

includeArchived.description: Include archived items (default TRUE — sees the whole archive; pass false to limit to active)

limit.description: Max items (default 20, cap 100)

tools.name: weir_quote
tools.description: Verify a citation against a source — strict-grounding's self-check. Given an item `id` and a candidate `quote`, confirm the text actually appears in that source and get a stable locator + surrounding context (so you can cite it precisely, or REFUSE if it is not there). Whitespace is normalized before matching (HTML/wrapping ignored), with a case-insensitive fallback. Returns { found:true, locator:" #start-end", quote (the source's verbatim span), before, after, match } when present, or { found:false, note } when the quote is NOT in the source — in which case do not assert it as grounded. Read-only. Pair with weir_getItem (the body + citation chain) and weir_search/weir_queryCatalog (to find the id).

id.description: The item id to verify against (from weir_search / weir_queryItems / weir_queryCatalog)

quote.description: The candidate quote/claim text to locate in the source

context.description: Chars of surrounding context to return on each side (default 240, max 1000)

tools.name: weir_cite
tools.description: Render a canonical, stable citation for an item — the companion to weir_quote (quote VERIFIES a span; cite RENDERS the reference). Pass `id` for one item, or `ids` for a batch. SINGLE mode: pass `quote` to fold verification in — you get `cited:true` + the verified verbatim span + a `glass_id#start-end` locator embedded in the reference, or `cited:false` (and NO reference) if the quote is not in the source, so a fabricated claim cannot get a citation. (Or pass a `locator` you already got from weir_quote to splice it without re-verifying.) Each citation comes in every form: `inline` "(Author year)", `reference` (a full reference-list line with a durable weir handle that survives a dead URL), `footnote` (markdown [^key]: …), `wikilink` ([[handle]] — a LIVE graph backlink once written into a stacks note), and `csl` (CSL-JSON for machine reuse), plus `missing` (essentials absent — cite what is known, never fabricate). BATCH mode (`ids`): returns per-item `entries`, a `keys` map (stable BibTeX-style cite-keys), and an assembled `bibliography` (markdown footnotes by default; `style:"numbered"|"plain"`). Read-only; pure render over metadata weir already holds.

id.description: One item id / glass_id to cite

ids.description: Batch: item ids → entries + a deduped bibliography with cite-keys

quote.description: Single mode: a candidate quote to VERIFY + embed (refuses with cited:false if not in the source)

locator.description: Single mode: a weir_quote locator (glass_id#start-end) to splice in without re-verifying

style.description: Batch bibliography format: footnotes (default) | numbered | plain

tools.name: weir_stacksList
tools.description: List the STACKS — weir’s notes/files vault (authored markdown notes + dropped files, living as real files under /stacks/). Optional `path` scopes to a folder (recursively). Returns { count, folders:[…], entries:[{ id, path, uid, type:note|file, title, tags, missing, glass_id }] }. The `id` is a normal item id (stacks: ) — pass it to weir_getItem/weir_catalogItem/weir_setState. Stacks entries are also queryable via weir_queryItems({ feed: "Stacks" }).

path.description: Scope to a folder (recursive), e.g. "specs/weir"

limit.description: Max entries (default 200, cap 500)

tools.name: weir_stacksRead
tools.description: Read one stacks entry by `path` (from weir_stacksList). For a note: returns its markdown body (capped 16k) + tags + metadata. For a file: metadata only (mime, no bytes). Returns { id, path, uid, type, title, tags, glass_id, markdown? , mime? }.

path.description: Entry path, e.g. "inbox/huffman.md"

tools.name: weir_stacksWrite
tools.description: Create OR update a stacks NOTE — "draft a note straight into the stacks". If `path` names an existing note, its body is updated (uid/created preserved); otherwise a new note is created. Address it with `path` (e.g. "specs/weir/idea.md") OR `folder`+`name`. If you give NO folder (bare name / bare path), the note is filed to inbox/ as triage and the result says so (routedToInbox:true) — pass `folder` (or a path that includes a folder) to file it directly. `markdown` is the body (required); `title` and `tags` optional (tags stamped as yours-via-Claude). Link other notes/holdings with [[uid]] or [[name]] (resolved by weir_relatedTo). For a one-line change, prefer weir_stacksEdit (find/replace/append) over rewriting the whole note here. Returns { ok, id, path, uid, title, tags, folder, routedToInbox? }. Files are dropped via Telegram or the app, not here.

path.description: Target path, e.g. "specs/weir/idea.md" (folder + filename)

folder.description: Folder (alternative to a full path); defaults to "inbox"

title.description: Note title (defaults to the first heading / filename)

markdown.description: The note body (markdown)

tags.description: Tags to set

tools.name: weir_stacksEdit
tools.description: Partial edit of a stacks NOTE — change one part without rewriting the whole note (the way the agent Edit tool works). Address it by `path`. Either replace text: `find` (the exact string to locate) + `replace` (its replacement; omit/empty to delete the text) — `find` must be UNIQUE unless you pass replaceAll:true. OR append: `append` (a block added to the end of the note). Exact-string match; errors are explicit (find-not-found / find-not-unique), never silent. Identity (uid/created) and source-stamp are preserved. Notes only (not files). Returns { ok, id, path, uid, title, tags, markdown }.

path.description: Entry path, e.g. "gcu/README.md"

find.description: Exact text to locate (must be unique unless replaceAll)

replace.description: Replacement for `find` (omit or empty string to delete it)

replaceAll.description: Replace every occurrence of `find` (default false → must be unique)

append.description: A block to append to the end of the note (alternative to find/replace)

tools.name: weir_stacksMove
tools.description: Move/refile a stacks entry to another folder. Identity (uid) is preserved, so its tags, read-state, catalog card and inbound [[uid]] links ride along. Returns { ok, movedFrom, id, path, uid, title }.

path.description: Current entry path

tools.name: weir_stacksTag
tools.description: Add/remove tags on a stacks entry by `path`. Tags are stamped source:'llm' and mirrored into the note’s frontmatter / the file’s .meta.json sidecar (portable, Obsidian-readable). Returns the updated entry.

path.description: Entry path

tools.name: weir_stacksTrash
tools.description: Delete a stacks entry by `path` — but weir never really deletes: the file (+ sidecar) is moved into /stacks/.trash/ (a hidden folder the scanner ignores), so it disappears from weir while the bytes survive on disk, recoverable. Drops the index entry. Returns { ok, trashed, dest }.

path.description: Entry path to delete

tools.name: weir_mcpDiag
tools.description: Diagnostics for weir's numen fs channels (transport debugging — for tracking down why a channel won't connect). No input. Per known channel returns: connection state + clientId, whether a token is set, the folder-handle NAME it points at, what weir reads from that folder's bridge.live (present? session, ageMs, fresh under 90s?), and the folder's top-level entries. Reading: bridgeLive absent or stale while the bridge insists it is announcing ⇒ FOLDER MISMATCH (weir and the bridge are on different directories); bridgeLive fresh but clientId null ⇒ STALE HANDSHAKE (re-dial / token). If a channel shows hasHandle:false, open weir Settings → Connections once to cache the handle, then re-run.

sites.name: promptflow-webmcp.netlify.app
sites.description: PromptFlow.ai

tools.name: architect_system
tools.description: PRIMARY PromptFlow Agent OS tool. Turn an arbitrary product/system brief into a complete live architecture in one round-trip. For best semantic fidelity, the AI agent should provide its inferred components and connections; PromptFlow validates, applies, scales, structurally repairs, lays out, and verifies the graph atomically. If components are omitted, PromptFlow falls back to its fast local intent compiler.

request.description: The user's complete product/system brief. Preserve important domain, scale, realtime, security, data, AI, media, and integration constraints.

targetUsers.description: Optional explicit user-scale target. Omit when the brief contains no meaningful scale requirement.

replaceCurrent.description: Replace the current canvas before building. Defaults to true. Set false only when ids are guaranteed not to conflict with existing nodes.

autoFix.description: Automatically repair deterministic structural findings after the initial build. Defaults to true.

id.description: Stable unique component id using lowercase kebab-case when possible.

label.description: Human-readable software component name.

components.description: Optional agent-authored architecture plan. For arbitrary briefs, provide the components you infer semantically so PromptFlow can apply the whole plan in one tool call. Omit to use PromptFlow's local intent compiler fallback.

connections.description: Relationships between the optional agent-authored components.

tools.name: analyze_architecture
tools.description: Read the live PromptFlow graph and return structural audit, architecture metrics, represented capabilities, and graph counts without mutating the canvas.

tools.name: recommend_architecture
tools.description: Act like a senior architecture reviewer. Return prioritized structural, scale, security-boundary, and observability recommendations. Recommendations are explicit and do not mutate the graph.

targetUsers.description: Optional future scale target used to include capacity recommendations.

tools.name: simulate_architecture_scale
tools.description: Run a non-destructive what-if simulation for a target scale. Return the exact projected operations plus before/after metrics and audits so the agent can reason before changing the live architecture.

tools.name: apply_architecture_recommendations
tools.description: Apply deterministic structural fixes and/or a requested scale plan in one agent round-trip, then auto-layout and verify the resulting architecture.

fixStructural.description: Apply deterministic fixes for the latest structural findings. Defaults to true.

targetUsers.description: Optional target scale. When supplied, apply PromptFlow's deterministic scaling patterns in the same transaction flow.

tools.name: explain_architecture
tools.description: Explain the whole architecture or one component using the live graph as source of truth, including upstream/downstream dependencies and represented capabilities.

nodeId.description: Optional component id. Omit for a whole-system explanation.

tools.name: generate_implementation_plan
tools.description: Convert the live architecture into an ordered implementation plan with foundation, core services, delivery, integrations, and recommended first code targets. This is planning metadata; it does not fabricate source code.

tools.name: assess_architecture_intelligence
tools.description: Run the full architecture-intelligence review across reliability, scalability, performance, security, resilience, observability, stress readiness, findings, recommendations, and Architecture DNA. This is a deterministic heuristic preflight, not a security certification or capacity guarantee.

targetUsers.description: Optional target user scale for the stress-readiness assessment.

tools.name: stress_test_architecture
tools.description: Run a non-destructive heuristic scale and failure-pressure simulation for a concrete target population. Returns modelled RPS pressure, bottlenecks, failure modes, and projected intelligence.

targetUsers.description: Projected user population for the heuristic stress scenario.

tools.name: get_architecture_dna
tools.description: Return the architecture's deterministic DNA: archetype, structural fingerprint, traits, strengths, and likely bottlenecks.

tools.name: apply_intelligence_recommendations
tools.description: Apply selected safe architecture-intelligence recommendations as a validated batch, then re-assess the live graph. Review-only recommendations intentionally produce no mutation.

targetUsers.description: Optional scale target used when selecting scale recommendations.

tools.name: run_digital_twin
tools.description: Run a non-destructive multi-scenario digital-twin simulation against the live architecture. Model load spikes, component failures, dependency failures, and regional outages, including failure propagation, survivability, recovery strategy, and critical paths.

targetUsers.description: Optional user scale for the load scenario.

tools.name: simulate_failure
tools.description: Inject a named failure into the architecture model without changing the live canvas. Return affected components, propagation depth, failure modes, survivability, and recovery strategy.

tools.name: simulate_load
tools.description: Model a production traffic spike for a target population without mutating the architecture. Return estimated sustained/burst RPS, bottlenecks, survivability, and hardening priorities.

tools.name: apply_digital_twin_hardening
tools.description: Apply safe, deterministic hardening derived from the digital-twin model: scale patterns, observability, and cache where appropriate. Validate the batch, re-layout, then return the post-hardening simulation and audit.

tools.name: assess_implementation_readiness
tools.description: Review the live architecture as an implementation lead. Return a deterministic readiness score, component work map, risks, missing code artifacts, and production-oriented test targets. This is planning intelligence, not generated source code.

tools.name: generate_project_blueprint
tools.description: Translate the live architecture into a concrete implementation blueprint: project structure, ordered delivery phases, component files, environment contract, risks, tests, and recommended first files. Does not mutate the canvas or pretend to generate source code.

includeTests.description: Whether to include the generated test strategy. Defaults to true.

includeEnvironment.description: Whether to include environment and secret requirements. Defaults to true.

tools.name: generate_implementation_contracts
tools.description: Map every represented architecture relationship into an implementation contract with boundary kind, inputs, outputs, and reliability requirements. Use this before writing service-to-service, event, data, or external integration code.

tools.name: generate_project_code
tools.description: Generate a bounded, inspectable project scaffold from the live architecture: manifest, runtime configuration, source boundaries, tests, contracts documentation, and architecture documentation. This mutates only the generated artifact workspace, not the architecture graph.

includeTests.description: Include executable test scaffolds. Defaults to true.

tools.name: validate_generated_project
tools.description: Validate the current generated project artifact set for manifest, executable source, tests, path integrity, and execution readiness without changing files or the canvas.

tools.name: run_project_execution_preflight
tools.description: Evaluate whether the generated project is ready for install, test, build, and local execution. This is a static browser-side preflight; it does not execute arbitrary generated code.

tools.name: review_generated_project
tools.description: Run a deterministic production-code review over generated artifacts for secrets, unfinished markers, missing contracts, tests, manifests, and entrypoints. This is a heuristic review, not a security certification.

tools.name: prepare_build_workspace
tools.description: Materialize the current generated artifacts as an inspectable browser-side build workspace with a manifest and execution preflight. No arbitrary code is executed.

tools.name: export_project_artifacts
tools.description: Export the current generated project and PromptFlow workspace manifest as a standards-compatible ZIP directly from the browser. No server upload is performed.

tools.name: run_project_execution_loop
tools.description: Execute the generated Node.js/React project inside an isolated browser-native WebContainer: mount artifacts, install dependencies, run tests, run the production build, diagnose failures, and apply a bounded deterministic self-healing patch before retrying. Host-page code is never executed.

tools.name: diagnose_execution_failure
tools.description: Classify the latest execution failure into a bounded diagnostic category with evidence and confidence. This tool never mutates the project.

tools.name: run_final_hackathon_demo
tools.description: Run the deterministic end-to-end showcase over the current architecture: structural audit, architecture intelligence, load simulation, severe traffic digital twin, implementation intelligence, project generation, execution preflight, and Architecture DNA. Results are stored without mutating the architecture.

tools.name: create_architecture_version
tools.description: Create an immutable architecture checkpoint containing the full graph, fingerprint, audit score, and Architecture DNA. Version history stays local to the current browser session.

message.description: Short reason or release note for this architecture checkpoint.

tools.name: list_architecture_versions
tools.description: Return the local architecture release history with version number, fingerprint, graph size, audit score, and release message.

tools.name: compare_architecture_versions
tools.description: Diff two immutable architecture checkpoints by component identity and dependency topology. Classify breaking, significant, and non-breaking changes without mutating the canvas.

tools.name: plan_architecture_migration
tools.description: Turn a version diff into an ordered production migration plan covering database compatibility, data backfills, API contracts, infrastructure rollout, application cutover, preflight checks, and rollback.

tools.name: restore_architecture_version
tools.description: Restore a previous immutable architecture checkpoint into the live canvas. All downstream audit, intelligence, simulation, implementation, code, workspace, and execution artifacts are invalidated.

tools.name: clear_version_analysis
tools.description: Clear the currently displayed version diff and migration plan while preserving immutable architecture history.

tools.name: run_production_qa
tools.description: Run the final deterministic release gate across architecture integrity, generated artifacts, security boundaries, performance budgets, WebMCP coverage, real execution, code review, and architecture version integrity.

tools.name: run_judge_mode
tools.description: Run PromptFlow's cinematic end-to-end hackathon flow: reason about the live architecture, break it with load and compute failure, diagnose the impact, apply bounded hardening, re-test, generate and execute the project, then run the production release gate and return a judge-facing before/after scorecard.

tools.name: get_promptflow_capabilities
tools.description: Read the recommended WebMCP operating contract for PromptFlow. Use this when an agent needs to understand how humans, ChatGPT, WebMCP, PromptFlow's deterministic engine, WebContainer execution, and Judge Mode fit together. No external model API is required inside PromptFlow: the calling AI agent supplies semantic reasoning and PromptFlow supplies validated execution.

tools.name: build_and_verify_system
tools.description: RECOMMENDED ONE-CALL WebMCP workflow. Turn an arbitrary human software brief into a live architecture and a verified generated project. The calling AI agent should infer semantic components/connections when needed; PromptFlow validates and applies the plan, performs deterministic structural repair and scaling, then runs the full Judge Mode pipeline: architecture intelligence, digital-twin failure injection, hardening, re-test, code generation, real WebContainer install/test/build/runtime verification, production QA, and final verdict. Use this instead of chaining many tools when the user asks to create and prove a complete system.

request.description: The user's complete product/system brief. Preserve important domain, scale, realtime, security, data, AI, media, and integration constraints.

targetUsers.description: Optional explicit user-scale target. Omit when the brief contains no meaningful scale requirement.

replaceCurrent.description: Replace the current canvas before building. Defaults to true. Set false only when ids are guaranteed not to conflict with existing nodes.

autoFix.description: Automatically repair deterministic structural findings after the initial build. Defaults to true.

id.description: Stable unique component id using lowercase kebab-case when possible.

label.description: Human-readable software component name.

components.description: Optional agent-authored architecture plan. For arbitrary briefs, provide the components you infer semantically so PromptFlow can apply the whole plan in one tool call. Omit to use PromptFlow's local intent compiler fallback.

connections.description: Relationships between the optional agent-authored components.

tools.name: add_architecture_node
tools.description: Atomic tool: add one software architecture component to the live PromptFlow canvas. For a complete product brief, prefer architect_system; for model-planned batches, prefer transform_architecture.

id.description: Stable unique node id.

label.description: Human-readable architecture component name.

description.description: Short explanation of the component's responsibility.

x.description: Optional canvas X coordinate. Omit to let PromptFlow place the node automatically.

y.description: Optional canvas Y coordinate. Omit to let PromptFlow place the node automatically.

tools.name: connect_architecture_nodes
tools.description: Atomic tool: create one directed relationship between existing architecture nodes. Prefer architect_system for complete briefs or transform_architecture for multi-step changes.

targetId.description: Id of the target node.

label.description: Optional relationship label.

tools.name: update_architecture_node
tools.description: Atomic tool: update one architecture component. Prefer architect_system for complete briefs or transform_architecture for multi-step changes.

nodeId.description: Id of the node to update.

label.description: Optional replacement component name.

tools.name: remove_architecture_node
tools.description: Remove one architecture component and its relationships. For multi-step changes, prefer transform_architecture.

nodeId.description: Id of the node to remove.

tools.name: clear_architecture_canvas
tools.description: Remove every node and connection from the PromptFlow architecture canvas.

tools.name: generate_node_boilerplate
tools.description: Attach generated implementation code to an existing architecture node so it can be inspected in PromptFlow.

nodeId.description: Id of the architecture node receiving the code.

tools.name: get_architecture_snapshot
tools.description: Read the current architecture graph, including components, relationships, positions, and attached code metadata.

tools.name: audit_architecture
tools.description: Run a structural preflight audit of the current architecture and expose the findings in the PromptFlow canvas.

tools.name: auto_layout_architecture
tools.description: Arrange all architecture components into a clean deterministic grid and refocus the canvas.

tools.name: transform_architecture
tools.description: Apply a model-planned batch of atomic architecture changes. Inspect the current graph first and prefer this tool for multi-step changes to minimize agent round-trips.

reason.description: Why the architecture should be transformed. Prefer this batched tool for multi-step architecture changes instead of many individual mutations.

tools.name: scale_architecture
tools.description: Apply deterministic production scaling patterns for the requested user scale. Use the current graph as the source of truth.

targetUsers.description: Expected peak active users or equivalent scale target.

reason.description: Why the system needs to scale.

tools.name: fix_architecture
tools.description: Address fixable findings from the latest structural audit without changing unrelated components.

findingIds.description: Optional audit finding ids to address. Omit to address all fixable findings.

sites.name: victorious-sea-029fc1400.6.azurestaticapps.net
sites.description: A Jupyter-inspired Python notebook rebuilt with Microsoft Fluent UI.

tools.name: get_notebook_state
tools.description: Read the visible notebook cells (source, outputs, table and chart summaries, status), Python kernel status, selected cell, and current theme.

tools.name: add_python_cell
tools.description: Append a new editable Python code cell to the notebook. This does not execute the code. Cells accept Jupyter-style %pip install and !pip install lines; do not use micropip directly.

code.description: Python source code for the new cell.

tools.name: add_markdown_cell
tools.description: Append a Markdown cell for headings, explanations, notes, or conclusions.

markdown.description: Markdown content for the new cell.

tools.name: insert_cell
tools.description: Insert a new code or Markdown cell directly above or below an existing cell, so content can be placed in the middle of the notebook.

cellId.description: Existing cell used as the anchor.

position.description: Where to insert relative to the anchor cell (default below).

tools.name: update_cell_source
tools.description: Replace the source of an existing code or Markdown cell after reviewing or debugging it. This does not execute the cell. Cells accept Jupyter-style %pip install and !pip install lines; do not use micropip directly.

tools.name: delete_cell
tools.description: Remove a cell from the notebook. The user can undo the deletion from the notebook.

tools.name: move_cell
tools.description: Move a cell one position up or down in the notebook.

tools.name: run_python_cell
tools.description: Execute one existing Python cell in the in-browser kernel and return its text output, table summary, or error.

cellId.description: The numeric ID of the code cell to run.

tools.name: run_all_cells
tools.description: Execute every Python code cell of the open notebook from top to bottom in the shared in-browser kernel, exactly like the Run all toolbar button: execution continues after a failing cell so one error does not hide the rest. Use it after adding or editing several cells, or after restart_kernel, instead of calling run_python_cell in a loop. Returns how many cells ran, every failure with its cell id and traceback tail, and the total duration.

tools.name: comment_on_cell
tools.description: Attach a visible review, explanation, or debugging comment to an existing notebook cell.

tools.name: read_cells_for_summary
tools.description: When the user asks for a summary of each cell: read every cell (source, kind, status, output preview), write a one- or two-line summary per cell in your own words, then submit them with set_cell_summaries so they appear under the cells.

cellIds.description: Limit to specific cells; omit for every cell.

tools.name: set_cell_summaries
tools.description: Display the summaries you wrote under the matching notebook cells (1-2 lines each). Pass an empty summary to clear one. Summaries also appear in the Outline panel.

tools.name: summarize_notebook
tools.description: Return a concise structural summary of the notebook, including sections, code imports, execution state, and outputs.

tools.name: suggest_python_completion
tools.description: Return context-aware Python code completions for the cursor in a notebook cell, including notebook symbols and pandas, NumPy, matplotlib, and DataFrame members.

tools.name: find_file_bugs
tools.description: Statically analyze any project file and list problems with line numbers: Python syntax errors, undefined names, unused imports, unreachable code, risky patterns (pyflakes-powered), CSV column mismatches, invalid JSON, Markdown and requirements issues. Notebooks are checked cell by cell. Results also appear in the Problems panel.

fileName.description: File name or path from Explorer; omit for the open file.

tools.name: get_problems
tools.description: List the problems currently shown in the Problems panel, including runtime errors captured from executed cells and files.

tools.name: find_cell_errors
tools.description: List every notebook cell whose latest execution failed, including its source and captured traceback.

tools.name: diagnose_cell_error
tools.description: Inspect a failed cell and return a focused debugging suggestion based on its latest traceback.

tools.name: list_kernel_variables
tools.description: List the variables defined in the Python kernel with their type, shape or length, and a short preview.

tools.name: modify_chart
tools.description: Change an existing chart type, title, color, axes, labels, or data values in a notebook cell.

tools.name: explain_chart
tools.description: Explain the variables, range, average, extrema, and trend in an interactive notebook chart.

tools.name: list_project_files
tools.description: List the Explorer folders, their colors, and files with their paths.

tools.name: read_project_file
tools.description: Return the full text of any project file (Python, Markdown, CSV, text, JSON) or the cells of a notebook.

fileName.description: File name or path such as data/iris.csv.

tools.name: edit_project_file
tools.description: Edit any non-notebook project file: replace its whole content, or find and replace an exact snippet (optionally every occurrence). The file opens in the editor so the user can review the change.

content.description: New full content of the file.

tools.name: preview_project_file
tools.description: Open a project file in the editor. Supports notebooks, CSV, Markdown, text, JSON, and Python files listed in Explorer.

fileName.description: File name or path from Explorer.

tools.name: create_project_file
tools.description: Create a new editable Python, Markdown, text, CSV, or JSON file in an Explorer folder.

tools.name: get_file_path
tools.description: Return the relative and project-rooted path of a file so it can be copied or referenced in code.

tools.name: set_project_folder_color
tools.description: Assign a color to a folder in Explorer.

tools.name: rename_project_file
tools.description: Rename a file, notebook, or folder in Explorer with the same rules as the Explorer rename dialog. Pass the path shown by list_project_files or get_file_path (a bare file name works when it is unique) and the new name including its extension. Open tabs, the editor header, and Problems entries follow the new name. Protected folders, duplicate names in the same folder, empty names, and names containing a slash are rejected. Returns the old and the new path.

path.description: Current path or name of the file, notebook, or folder.

newName.description: New name without slashes, including the file extension.

tools.name: delete_project_file
tools.description: Delete a file, notebook, or folder from Explorer, closing its editor tab and clearing its Problems entries. Deleting a folder also deletes the files inside it. Only the PROJECT folder itself is protected. Confirm with the user before calling this: nothing is restored afterwards.

path.description: Path or name of the file, notebook, or folder to delete.

tools.name: move_project_file
tools.description: Move a file or notebook into another Explorer folder, which changes the relative path that Python code must use to open it. Pass folderPath as the folder path from list_project_files, or "" (or "/") for the PROJECT root. Duplicate names in the target folder, protected folders, and moving a folder into itself or its own subfolder are rejected. Returns the old and the new path.

path.description: Path or name of the file, notebook, or folder to move.

folderPath.description: Destination folder path; "" or "/" means the PROJECT root.

tools.name: import_notebook_from_url
tools.description: Import a public Jupyter notebook from a GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or Kaggle-hosted HTTPS .ipynb link. Replaces the current notebook after validating nbformat 4 JSON.

url.description: Public HTTPS notebook URL.

tools.name: import_notebook_from_json
tools.description: Create and open a new notebook from raw .ipynb JSON text that you fetched yourself. Use this whenever import_notebook_from_url cannot reach a notebook because the browser blocks the page from fetching it (CORS) or the host is not GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or Kaggle: read the .ipynb yourself and pass its exact JSON here. Unlike import_notebook_from_url this keeps the current notebook and opens the imported one in a new tab. Returns the new notebook path and its cell count.

content.description: Raw nbformat 4 .ipynb JSON text.

name.description: Optional notebook name; ".ipynb" is appended when missing.

tools.name: get_notebook_ipynb
tools.description: Serialize a notebook to Jupyter nbformat 4 JSON, identical to what the Export .ipynb button downloads, including every cell source, captured output, and execution count. Use it to hand the notebook to another tool, to keep a copy before a risky edit, or to diff it against an earlier version. Defaults to the notebook in the active tab.

fileName.description: Optional notebook name or path; defaults to the active notebook.

tools.name: profile_csv_file
tools.description: Inspect a CSV file from Explorer and return its dimensions, missing values, inferred column types, distinct counts, and a small sample.

fileName.description: CSV file name or path from Explorer.

tools.name: clean_csv_file
tools.description: Clean a CSV file in Explorer by dropping empty rows, removing duplicate rows, or both. The updated CSV remains editable in the project.

fileName.description: CSV file name or path from Explorer.

tools.name: open_data_wrangler
tools.description: Open the Data Wrangler drawer for a CSV file, for the DataFrame output of a cell, or for a DataFrame variable in the kernel.

cellId.description: Cell whose output table to open.

tools.name: get_cell_table
tools.description: Return the columns, dtypes, and rows (up to 1000) of the DataFrame shown under a cell.

tools.name: run_python_terminal_command
tools.description: Execute Python, pip install, pip list, or browser environment commands in the docked terminal using the shared in-browser kernel.

tools.name: read_terminal_output
tools.description: Read the visible terminal transcript, active browser environment, and available environments before choosing the next command.

tools.name: create_python_environment
tools.description: Create and activate a named conda-style browser environment, restarting the shared notebook kernel with isolated variables.

tools.name: install_python_packages
tools.description: Install one or more Pyodide-compatible Python packages with pip in the active or selected browser environment and show the result in the terminal.

tools.name: run_project_python_file
tools.description: Open and run a Python file from Explorer in the shared browser kernel. Text output is sent to the terminal and generated charts are opened in the visualization drawer.

fileName.description: .py file name or path from Explorer.

tools.name: restart_kernel
tools.description: Restart the shared in-browser Pyodide kernel like the Restart toolbar button: every variable, import, and execution count is dropped and all cell outputs and statuses are cleared. Use it when kernel state is inconsistent, after installing a package that shadows an import, or before a clean run_all_cells. It waits for a busy kernel to finish first and returns once the kernel is ready again, or reports the kernel state if the wait times out.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for a busy or starting kernel before giving up (default 20000).

tools.name: set_terminal_visibility
tools.description: Open or close the docked terminal / problems panel, optionally choosing which tab to show.

tools.name: get_current_user
tools.description: Return who is signed in to Fluent Notebook (name, provider, user id) when the Azure host provides authentication, or report that the workspace is anonymous.

tools.name: save_workspace_to_cloud
tools.description: Save every project file, folder, notebook cell, and environment name to the signed-in user's private Azure Blob Storage workspace. Requires the user to be signed in.

tools.name: load_workspace_from_cloud
tools.description: Replace the current project with the signed-in user's workspace saved in Azure Blob Storage. Requires the user to be signed in.

tools.name: set_notebook_theme
tools.description: Switch the Fluent Notebook appearance between light and dark theme.

sites.name: acoustom.vercel.app
sites.description: Acoustom

tools.name: get_acoustom_overview
tools.description: Returns what Acoustom is, what the agent can do here, what the platform deliberately does not do, the page map, and the capability-to-tool mapping. The first call for any new session.

tools.name: list_acoustom_skills
tools.description: Returns every skill available to the agent in this session: a one-line description, when to load it, and the tool names it expects the agent to call. Use get_acoustom_skill to read the full instructions for a single skill.

tools.name: get_acoustom_skill
tools.description: Returns the full instructions for a single Acoustom skill by name. Load a specialised skill before running a workflow it owns; load acoustom-guided-discovery for broad or combined requests.

tools.name: list_webmcp_tools
tools.description: Returns every tool this WebMCP host has registered, grouped by capability. Use get_webmcp_tool_contract to inspect a single tool’s full input and response schema before calling it.

tools.name: get_webmcp_tool_contract
tools.description: Returns the input schema and response schema for a registered Acoustom WebMCP tool. Backend response schemas reference the live FastAPI OpenAPI document.

tools.name: get_user_context
tools.description: Returns the live state of the user’s view: the visible page, the comparison selection, the listening lab’s selected speaker, room and current simulation, the active custom build, music preferences, and the bag. Read this first when returning to a session or before a handoff.

tools.name: get_acoustom_workflow
tools.description: Returns the four objective-aligned agent workflows (recommend, compare, custom build, integrated guided discovery), their tool order, purpose, and the output fields to carry to each next step, plus same-view navigation rules. An agent without prior context should call this after get_acoustom_overview.

tools.name: get_navigation_context
tools.description: Returns the current visible Acoustom page, selected product where applicable, supported destinations, the user-facing sections that can be focused, the full navigation schema, and the navigation policy. Use before navigating when the current page is unknown.

tools.name: navigate_acoustom
tools.description: Moves the visible Acoustom app to a supported in-app destination and can carry the relevant context in the same call: productNames fills the comparison matrix, speakerName selects the listening-lab speaker, buildId opens a saved build in the custom builder, trackId loads a reference track. Use only when showing the page materially helps collaboration. This cannot navigate to arbitrary URLs, checkout, payment, or purchase.

destination.description: A supported visible Acoustom destination. Never infer or construct URLs.

productName.description: Required when destination is product_detail. Must be a catalog product name.

sectionId.description: Optional visible section to focus after navigation when that section exists on the destination. Use get_navigation_context to discover valid sections for the current destination.

productNames.description: Optional comparison selection to load in the same call. catalogProductNames and customBuildIds are kept in their respective slots.

buildId.description: Local build id to open in the custom design builder (destination must be custom_design).

speakerName.description: Speaker to select in the listening lab (destination must be listening_lab). Use the catalog name or "custom-reference" for the active custom build.

trackId.description: Reference track to load in the listening lab (destination listening_lab).

tools.name: recommend_speakers
tools.description: Ranks catalog speakers for room size and listening preference, with optional format, budget (USD per pair), and feedback. Returns transparent matching reasons; use get_product and simulation to inspect recommendations. Room size and sound profile are required so an empty request cannot be mistaken for a meaningful recommendation.

feedback.description: Optional user feedback that the chatbot should consider when explaining or refining the recommendation.

tools.name: list_products
tools.description: Returns the current Acoustom catalog: name, type, price, tone, and category.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Returns complete current-page details and specifications for one catalog speaker.

productName.description: Exact or case-insensitive Acoustom product name.

tools.name: compare_speakers
tools.description: Returns a column-per-speaker comparison for two to five catalog speakers and/or local custom builds. Prices are USD per pair; a custom build’s price is the configured component total from validation. Pass includeSimulation:true to run every column through the current live listening-lab room and return the complete simulation result: simulation id, impulse-response URLs, RT60, early decay time, C80 clarity, D50 definition, frequency response, and speaker performance. The result depends on the room the user is currently simulating in, so call apply_agent_room_estimate or get_current_room_spec first when the room is unknown.

customBuildIds.description: Optional local custom build ids from list_local_builds. Builds that have not been validated carry empty specifications until they are revalidated.

includeSimulation.description: When true, simulate every column in the current live listening-lab room and return the complete simulation data alongside the specifications.

tools.name: set_comparison_selection
tools.description: Loads up to five catalog speakers and/or local custom builds into the comparison matrix without changing the visible page. Use navigate_acoustom(destination: compare, productNames) to do the same and also land on the comparison page.

tools.name: get_room_simulation_presets
tools.description: Returns the room-acoustic presets accepted by simulate_speaker_in_room.

tools.name: list_reference_tracks
tools.description: Returns the reference tracks the listening lab can audition. Use set_reference_track to load one.

tools.name: set_reference_track
tools.description: Loads a reference track into the listening lab without moving the page. The track is identified by id from list_reference_tracks. The user still needs to press play in the lab; this only chooses the track.

tools.name: upload_reference_audio
tools.description: Loads agent-provided reference audio into the listening lab. Pass a data URL containing an audio file; the audio remains in this browser and is not uploaded to Acoustom servers.

dataUrl.description: A data URL such as data:audio/wav;base64,...

tools.name: set_music_preferences
tools.description: Stores a short summary of the user’s listening habits so the reasoning, recommendations, and visible page share the same context. Acoustom has no Spotify or playlist integration; this tool only records what the agent already knows.

source.description: Where the agent obtained this, e.g. "spotify_playlist" or "conversation".

tools.name: get_room_estimate_contract
tools.description: Returns the schema and collaboration guidance for translating a user-provided room image into editable simulation inputs. This tool does not analyse images itself.

tools.name: attach_room_reference_images
tools.description: Pushes image URLs the agent already holds into the listening-lab room reference panel so the user can see them. Acoustom has no built-in image understanding; the estimate is the agent’s.

guidance.description: Optional one-line note shown alongside the images in the lab.

tools.name: get_room_reference_images
tools.description: Returns temporary, user-approved room-image URLs uploaded in Listening Lab. Inspect every returned image before inferring an editable room estimate. If no references are returned, the user can attach images directly to the agent conversation or call attach_room_reference_images with image URLs you already hold.

tools.name: apply_agent_room_estimate
tools.description: Applies an agent’s best-effort image-based room estimate to the live browser simulation controls. speakerPositions and listener are optional; when only dimensions and a preset are known, Acoustom fills a sensible default stereo layout. The estimate is collaborative, editable, and intentionally not a hard confirmation gate.

directivity.description: Optional source directivity. Omit for omni.

input_schema.description: Best-effort room estimate derived collaboratively from a user-provided image. speakerPositions and listener are optional when only dimensions are known; Acoustom fills sensible defaults.

tools.name: get_current_room_spec
tools.description: Returns the room dimensions, acoustic preset, stereo speaker positions, and listener position currently used by the listening lab. Use after a room-image estimate is applied or a user edits the room, before explaining or explicitly overriding a simulation.

tools.name: set_listening_lab_speaker
tools.description: Selects the speaker the listening lab will simulate. Pass a catalog product name, or "custom-reference" to simulate the most recently validated custom build. Use navigate_acoustom(destination: listening_lab, speakerName) to do the same and also move the page.

tools.name: refresh_room_simulation
tools.description: Forces the listening lab to re-run the simulation against its current room and selected speaker. The lab usually re-runs automatically; use this when the user changed controls outside the lab or you want a guaranteed fresh result.

tools.name: get_live_simulation_result
tools.description: Returns the simulation result the listening lab is currently displaying, including the profile provenance. Use this instead of re-running a simulation through the API when the user has not changed the room or speaker since the last run.

tools.name: get_shared_simulated_audio
tools.description: Returns the playable URL for the latest browser-rendered WAV that the user explicitly shared with the agent. The URL expires automatically.

tools.name: get_custom_speaker_builder_options
tools.description: Returns server-owned custom-speaker platforms. All other accepted builder values are enumerated by validate_custom_speaker_build.

tools.name: fill_custom_builder_form
tools.description: Fills the visible custom-design builder form on the user's screen with the supplied choices, exactly as if the user had clicked them. Use for the choices you gathered from conversation or a recommendation. If the user is not on the custom-design page, call navigate_acoustom(destination: "custom_design") first. The user sees and can change every value.

fields.description: Builder choices to apply. Only the fields you pass are changed.

preferences.description: Optional brief-question answers shown on the builder's first step. Stored as user preferences, separate from the custom-speaker configuration spec.

focusStep.description: Optional builder step to open so the user sees the filled fields: 0 brief, 1 format, 2 platform, 3 bass, 4 cabinet, 5 finish, 6 personalisation, 7 review.

tools.name: validate_custom_speaker_build
tools.description: Validates and derives a curated build. Returns the validated build plus the USD component pricing breakdown and total used by the custom builder. Treat pricing as an estimate; the backend remains authoritative for engineering values.

tools.name: generate_custom_build_sheet
tools.description: Validates a custom configuration and renders a downloadable two-angle catalog build-sheet PNG. Returns the validated build, the USD pricing estimate, and imageDataUrl, which an agent can present as an image attachment. The custom builder must be open in this browser so its 3D renderer is available.

tools.name: list_saved_custom_configurations
tools.description: Lists the signed-in user’s durable custom speaker designs. Use an id from this result to load or edit a shared configuration.

tools.name: get_saved_custom_configuration
tools.description: Loads one saved custom-speaker configuration, its current revision, and the same USD pricing estimate shown by the custom builder.

tools.name: save_custom_configuration
tools.description: Creates or updates a saved custom-speaker design and returns the same USD pricing estimate shown by the custom builder. For an update, pass the id and current revision returned by get_saved_custom_configuration; changes are recorded as an agent revision.

tools.name: simulate_speaker_in_room
tools.description: Runs a speaker-specific stereo room simulation for one catalog speaker. Returns its profile provenance, in-room frequency response, impulse-response URLs, and RT60. Detailed room surfaces and cardioid sources are optional.

productName.description: Exact or case-insensitive Acoustom product name.

length.description: Metres.

surfaceAbsorption.description: Optional absorption coefficients (0 reflective to 1 absorbent) by room surface. Omit to use roomPreset.

directivity.description: Optional source directivity. Omit for omni.

speakerPositions.description: Optional exact left/right speaker positions in metres. When omitted, Acoustom uses its default stereo layout.

listener.description: Optional listening position in metres. Provide with speakerPositions for a custom layout.

tools.name: simulate_custom_speaker_in_room
tools.description: Runs a validated custom build in the current live listening-lab room by default. Pass the returned build unchanged. Omit room fields to use the browser room dimensions, preset, stereo positions, and listener position, including a user-edited or image-derived room estimate. Supply room fields only to intentionally override those live values.

length.description: Metres.

surfaceAbsorption.description: Optional absorption coefficients (0 reflective to 1 absorbent) by room surface. Omit to use roomPreset.

directivity.description: Optional source directivity. Omit for omni.

speakerPositions.description: Optional exact left/right speaker positions in metres. When omitted, Acoustom uses its default stereo layout.

listener.description: Optional listening position in metres. Provide with speakerPositions for a custom layout.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Returns current shopping-bag items and total item count.

tools.name: get_wishlist
tools.description: Returns names of catalog speakers currently saved in the wishlist.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Adds one to ten pairs of a catalog speaker to the current shopping bag. The bag is browser-local; it is not a checkout or purchase.

productName.description: Exact or case-insensitive Acoustom product name.

tools.name: update_cart_quantity
tools.description: Sets a speaker quantity in the current bag; use zero to remove it. The bag is browser-local.

productName.description: Exact or case-insensitive Acoustom product name.

tools.name: remove_from_cart
tools.description: Removes a catalog speaker completely from the current shopping bag. The bag is browser-local.

productName.description: Exact or case-insensitive Acoustom product name.

tools.name: toggle_wishlist
tools.description: Saves a catalog speaker to the wishlist, or removes it if already saved. The wishlist is browser-local.

productName.description: Exact or case-insensitive Acoustom product name.

tools.name: delete_saved_custom_configuration
tools.description: Permanently deletes a saved custom-speaker configuration from the signed-in user's account. Use a configurationId from list_saved_custom_configurations.

tools.name: list_local_builds
tools.description: Lists custom speaker builds saved in this browser's local storage. Available without signing in. Each build stores the full spec data and the validated engineering profile so it can be simulated and compared.

tools.name: save_local_build
tools.description: Creates or updates a custom speaker build in this browser's local storage without requiring sign-in. Validates the configuration against the server and persists the derived engineering profile so the build can be simulated and compared. If buildId is provided, updates that build; otherwise creates a new one. The configuration follows the same schema as validate_custom_speaker_build.

buildId.description: Existing build ID to update. Omit to create a new build.

setAsActive.description: When true (default), mark the build as active so the listening lab uses it. The build is also written to session storage as the live custom-reference profile.

tools.name: delete_local_build
tools.description: Deletes a custom speaker build from this browser's local storage. Does not require sign-in. If the build has been synced to an account, it remains on the server.

tools.name: rename_local_build
tools.description: Renames a custom speaker build in this browser's local storage without requiring sign-in.

sites.name: codesplitter.notryanquinn.workers.dev
sites.description: Every line is its own record, so people and agents edit the same file at once without stepping on each other.

tools.name: current_page
tools.description: What the page shows now: its view (home, r repo, f file, l level, c cut, s share, u profile, search…), the repo, file or level, the selected lines, what you may do there, and who is signed in.

tools.name: agent_guide
tools.description: The prompt a person hands their own agent for steering this site: the CLI, MCP and WebMCP routes (CLI first), and the rules to follow.

tools.name: open_page
tools.description: Go to a page by its hash: #/ home, #/r/owner/repo[/dir], #/f/owner/repo/path/to/file, #/l/level-slug[/path], #/u/handle, #/m/owner/repo (agents and branches, for a phone), #/b/owner/repo/branch (a branch's merge page, a card per conflict), #/search/query, #/about. Answers with the new page.

hash.description: like #/f/owner/repo/src/app.ts

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: A repo folder's files and folders. Defaults to the repo and folder on screen.

path.description: folder, "" for the root

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: A file's lines, numbered, each with who last wrote it. Defaults to the file on screen.

tools.name: list_scenes
tools.description: The scenes play_scene can play (the tour's chapters): each one's id, name and steps, with the steps that are a person's to press marked in `you`. A scene can be just some steps: "id:2-3" is the chapter's 2nd and 3rd, "id:2" its 2nd.

tools.name: play_scene
tools.description: Start a scene on screen, the way the tour does: a card and a fake cursor, and scene_step does each step's real action. `scene` is an id from list_scenes, or "id:2-3" for just those steps; `queue` lists scenes to play after it. Scenes with steps on a repo's file page open that repo's page themselves when given `owner`/`repo` (or when one is on screen). Answers with the first step.

scene.description: an id from list_scenes, or id:from-to for some of its steps

tools.name: scene_step
tools.description: Do the shown step of the scene playing: the cursor glides to it and its real action runs, then the scene moves on. Signing in, running an agent, merging and deploying are a person's to press, so on those it answers `held` and does nothing; `skip: true` moves past a step without doing it. Answers with what it did and the next step.

tools.name: list_conflicts
tools.description: On a branch's merge page (#/b/owner/repo/branch; the repo page's Branches links to it), its merge conflicts as their cards show them: branch, path, line, base, main, branch_text, the picks it takes, the suggestion if any, and how it's settled so far.

tools.name: settle_conflict
tools.description: Settle one conflict card on a branch's merge page, as clicking would: pick main, branch, both, both:branch-first, suggestion, or text (with `text`, the lines that replace it). Nothing lands until the branch's Merge button is pressed.

line.description: the conflict's line, as list_conflicts says

text.description: with pick text: the settled lines

tools.name: select_lines
tools.description: Select lines on the file on screen, as clicking their numbers would, so the line commands (share, cut, make private) act on them. Give `from` and `to` for one run, or `ranges` for several. `mode` says what to do with the current pick: replace it (the default), add to it, remove from it, or toggle. Answers with the pick as runs.

tools.name: deselect_lines
tools.description: Drop the picked lines on the file on screen, as Esc does. With `from`/`to`, drop just those and keep the rest.

tools.name: select_all_lines
tools.description: Pick every line of the file on screen, as Cmd+A does.

tools.name: invert_selection
tools.description: Pick the lines that aren't picked and drop the ones that are, on the file on screen.

tools.name: expand_selection
tools.description: Grow the pick one level of structure: to the lines around it at the same depth, then to the block that holds them (header to closing brace), out to the whole file. Call it again to go wider.

tools.name: select_matching
tools.description: Pick the lines of the file on screen that hold `match` (any case), or match it when written /regex/flags. `mode` as select_lines: replace (the default), add, remove or toggle. Answers with the pick as runs.

tools.name: select_lines_by
tools.description: Pick the lines of the file on screen that `who` last wrote (a handle, or an agent's name as read_file shows it in `by`). Mode as select_matching.

tools.name: selected_lines
tools.description: The lines picked on the file on screen: the runs ([from, to], 1-based) and each line's text and author.
