sites.name: dashboard.orderly.network
sites.description: Orderly dashboard

tools.name: get_site_overview
tools.description: START HERE. Returns a map of this site: what it is, its areas, which tools back each area, common multi-step flows, parameter conventions, and suggested first queries. Call this once to get oriented before using the other tools. This is a read-only analytics dashboard for the Orderly Network perpetual-futures DEX; it does not place trades.

tools.name: get_dashboard_main
tools.description: Daily platform totals for Orderly: taker/cumulative volume, revenue (fees), TVL, deposits/withdrawals, new accounts/addresses, and active builders, as a historical time series. For a live snapshot use get_market_summary; for weekly/monthly user aggregates use get_metrics_overview. Returns rows newest-last over the trailing `days` window.

days.description: Trailing days (default 90, max 730).

tools.name: get_tvl_by_chain
tools.description: Total Value Locked broken down by chain, plus a total row. Drives the TVL By Chain widget. Returns newest snapshot rows.

tools.name: get_tvl_by_token
tools.description: TVL and token balance held per collateral token over a trailing window. Drives the TVL By Token widget.

days.description: Trailing days (default 30, max 730).

tools.name: get_weekly_symbol_volume
tools.description: Weekly per-symbol volume and listed-markets count from the analytics API. For the live market list (prices, 24h change, open interest) use get_markets.

tools.name: get_funding_rates
tools.description: 8-hour funding rates for every perpetual symbol, from a trailing start date. For cross-exchange funding comparisons use get_funding_comparison.

days.description: Trailing days for the start date (default 30).

tools.name: get_daily_liquidations_by_symbol
tools.description: Daily liquidation notional aggregated per perpetual symbol across all markets. For individual recent liquidation events of one symbol use get_recent_liquidations.

tools.name: get_staking_daily
tools.description: Daily $ORDER staking metrics: staked/unstaked/net amounts, cumulative staker addresses, buybacks, and burned ORDER. Drives the Staking Daily widget.

tools.name: get_builder_daily
tools.description: Per-builder daily metrics: taker/maker/total volume, active users, broker fees, and net flow. Drives the Builder Volume, Builder Active Traders, Builder Revenue, and Net Flow By Builder widgets.

days.description: Trailing days (default 30, max 730).

tools.name: get_fund_flows_by_broker
tools.description: Daily deposits, withdrawals, and net fund flow per broker. Drives the Net Flow By Builder widget (fund-flow variant).

days.description: Trailing days (default 30, max 730).

tools.name: get_fund_flows_by_chain
tools.description: Daily deposits, withdrawals, and net fund flow per chain. Drives the Fund Flows By Chain widget.

tools.name: get_dex_users
tools.description: Per-builder user activity snapshot: DAU/WAU/MAU with day/week/month-over-month deltas and new-user counts. Drives the DEX Users widget.

tools.name: get_metrics_overview
tools.description: Weekly and monthly aggregates for new users, active users, trading volume, and Orderly revenue. For daily historical totals use get_dashboard_main.

tools.name: get_volume_segments
tools.description: Weekly trading volume split by market-maker vs retail segment. Drives the Volume Segments widget.

tools.name: get_stake_users
tools.description: Weekly average active stakers. Drives the Stake Users widget.

tools.name: get_stake_vs_supply
tools.description: Weekly ORDER staked vs circulating supply and staking ratio. Drives the Stake vs Supply widget.

tools.name: get_omnivault_tvl
tools.description: Weekly average TVL per OmniVault (USD millions). Drives the OmniVault TVL widget.

tools.name: get_distributor_stats
tools.description: Referral distributor statistics: invitee counts, graduated invitees, revenue share, and fee tier. Drives the Distributors widget. Returns an array of distributor rows.

tools.name: get_distributor_invitees
tools.description: Per-invitee detail for referral distributors: invite date, DEX, status, and 30D volume/revenue share. Returns an array of invitee rows.

tools.name: get_market_share
tools.description: Orderly's DEX perpetuals market share vs. other on-chain perp venues, computed from CoinGecko 24h derivatives volume and DefiLlama open interest. Drives the Market Share widget. Returns ranked protocols with volume, open interest, and share %.

tools.name: get_markets
tools.description: Snapshot of all active perpetual markets: the futures market list, 24h price changes, and per-symbol open interest. Drives the Markets page. Returns an object { markets, priceChanges, openInterest }. Optional search (a case-insensitive substring on the symbol), sort_by (24h_volume | 24h_change | open_interest | symbol), limit (max 200), and desc (default true) filter and rank the markets and trim the priceChanges / openInterest arrays to the same symbol set. Defaults to 50 markets in API order; pass limit: 200 for the full set.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring on the symbol (e.g. "btc", "sol", "perp_btc").

sort_by.description: Rank markets by this metric (default: API order).

limit.description: Max markets to return after filter/sort (default 50; max 200).

tools.name: get_market_detail
tools.description: Composite single-symbol bundle for the market detail page. Returns only the requested sections (default: all of market info, top-50 orderbook levels, recent trades, funding history, and OHLCV candles). Requesting fewer sections keeps the payload small. Drives the Price Chart, Orderbook, Recent Trades, and Funding Chart.

symbol.description: Perp symbol. Accepts a base tick (BTC) or full form (PERP_BTC_USDC).

include.description: Sections to return; omit for all.

tools.name: get_symbol_info
tools.description: Full configuration for a single perpetual symbol: leverage limits (1/base_imr), tick/lot sizes, price precision, and status flags. Returns the symbol info object.

symbol.description: Perp symbol: base tick (ETH) or full form.

tools.name: get_market_summary
tools.description: Live platform-wide market snapshot: 24h volume, open interest, trader counts, and fee totals across all symbols. For historical daily time series use get_dashboard_main; for weekly/monthly user aggregates use get_metrics_overview.

tools.name: get_funding_comparison
tools.description: Cross-exchange funding rate comparison: last value plus 1d/7d/30d averages per symbol across venues (Orderly vs. Binance, Bybit, etc.). Omit symbol for all symbols. For per-symbol 8h funding history use get_funding_rates.

symbol.description: Perp symbol: base tick (BTC) or full form; omit for all.

tools.name: get_recent_liquidations
tools.description: Recent individual liquidation events for one symbol: side, size, notional, mark/liquidation price, and the liquidated account. For daily liquidation totals aggregated across all symbols use get_daily_liquidations_by_symbol.

symbol.description: Perp symbol: base tick (BTC) or full form (PERP_BTC_USDC).

limit.description: Max events (default 50, max 500).

tools.name: get_top_traders
tools.description: Top addresses ranked by a chosen metric (notional, volume, PnL, or trade count) for a symbol or platform-wide. Paginated via cursor. Drives the Top Traders panel and Whale Leaderboard.

symbol.description: Perp symbol: base tick (BTC) or full form; omit for platform-wide.

sort_by.description: Ranking metric (default notional).

limit.description: Page size (default 50, max 200).

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response — pass it back unchanged.

tools.name: get_whale_context
tools.description: Whale research bundle for a single address: account state (collateral, PnL), open positions, and recent trades. Requires an address; optionally scope to a broker or account_id. Drives the Whale Detail modal.

address.description: Wallet address (EVM 0x…).

tools.name: get_platform_positions
tools.description: Platform-wide open positions for a symbol (large-position liquidation-heatmap data). Returns up to 1000 positions filtered by minimum notional. Drives the Liquidation Heatmap.

symbol.description: Perp symbol: base tick (BTC) or full form.

tools.name: get_insurance_fund
tools.description: Orderly insurance fund balance, holdings, and status. Drives the Insurance Fund widget.

tools.name: get_leaderboard
tools.description: Daily trading leaderboard: realized PnL and perp volume per trader over a date range (YYYY-MM-DD). Supports pagination, broker/address filters, sort, and aggregation by address, account, or date. Drives the Leaderboard (trading) tab.

page.description: 1-based page (default 1).

sort.description: Default descending_realized_pnl.

address.description: Filter to a wallet address.

tools.name: get_positions
tools.description: Open-positions leaderboard: largest open positions by notional, optionally filtered by account, broker, or symbol. Drives the Leaderboard (positions) tab.

symbol.description: Perp symbol: base tick (BTC) or full form (PERP_BTC_USDC).

offset.description: Pagination offset (default 0).

limit.description: Page size (default 50, max 500).

tools.name: resolve_address
tools.description: Resolve a wallet address or account ID into its Orderly broker/account pairs. Accepts an EVM address (0x + 40 hex), a Solana address (43-44 base58 chars), or an account ID (0x + 64 hex). Returns an array of {broker_id, account_id, …} pairs for the identity. For address queries (not account IDs) each account is enriched with 90-day perp_volume and realized_pnl, sorted by volume descending — matching the Search results page. First step of the Explorer/address flow.

address.description: EVM address, Solana address, or Orderly account ID.

tools.name: get_events
tools.description: Historical trading events for an account: trades, settlements, liquidations, ADLs, and margin transfers (versioned v1/v2/v3 already flattened to a uniform shape). Time range is capped at 31 days; omit both times for the most recent page. Drives the address Events tab. Returns { events, nextCursor, pageSizeLimit, tradesCount }; pass the nextCursor back as the cursor param to fetch the next page.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor (the nextCursor value from a prior response). Do not construct this object yourself — only pass back the cursor you received.

tools.name: get_account_state
tools.description: Account snapshot for an address: collateral, margin ratios, 24h PnL, and all OPEN positions (qty, notional, entry/mark price, leverage, est. liquidation price). Drives the address Positions tab.

address.description: Wallet address (EVM 0x…).

tools.name: get_portfolio
tools.description: Daily account-value time series with cumulative PnL (equity curve) for an address, up to 365 days. Drives the Portfolio Chart on the address page.

address.description: Wallet address (EVM 0x…).

limit.description: Max snapshots (default 90, max 365).

tools.name: get_brokers
tools.description: Directory of all Orderly brokers (broker_id → human-readable broker_name), sorted by name. Use to label broker_id values returned by other tools.

tools.name: get_all_symbols
tools.description: Every known perp symbol (including delisted) as a hash→name map: {symbol, symbol_hash}. Use to resolve keccak256 symbol hashes in event/position data to display names. Active symbols are also available via get_markets.

tools.name: get_all_tokens
tools.description: Every known settlement/collateral token as a hash→name map: {token, token_hash}. Use to resolve keccak256 token hashes in settlement/fee fields to display names.

tools.name: open_market
tools.description: Navigate the user to a market detail page. Pass a base tick (BTC), the full form (PERP_BTC_USDC), or a broker-suffixed variant (PERP_AAPL_USDC_mythos). The page renders a graceful "Market Not Found" for unknown symbols, so no pre-validation is performed — the user lands on the right place regardless.

tools.name: open_address
tools.description: Navigate the user to an address / account detail page. Accepts an EVM address (0x + 40 hex), an Orderly account_id (0x + 64 hex), or a Solana base58 address. Solana addresses are url-safe-base64 encoded to match in-app AddressLink links.

address.description: EVM address, Solana address, or Orderly account_id.

tools.name: focus_widget
tools.description: Scroll a dashboard widget into the user's view and highlight it briefly. Only widgets present on the current page can be focused (widgets render on specific pages, not everywhere). Use get_site_overview to learn which widgets live where.

tools.name: share_widget
tools.description: Open the share dialog for a dashboard widget, presenting the user with the widget's embed/share link. Only works when the widget and its share button are rendered on the current page (share buttons are hidden on embeds).

tools.name: get_current_view
tools.description: Read-only snapshot of what the user is currently looking at: the current route/URL, the page area, the active market symbol (base tick) when on a market page, and the list of widget ids currently rendered on screen (valid inputs for focus_widget / share_widget / get_widget_url). Call this to ground yourself in the user's current view before navigating or pointing at a widget. After open_market or open_address, call this to confirm the destination rendered — the result includes a status (loading | ready | not-found | error) and, when available, a short summary.

tools.name: get_widget_url
tools.description: Return the embeddable share URL for a dashboard widget — the same link the Share dialog produces — without opening any UI. Use this to give the user a link to a widget. Market widgets (market-*) take an optional symbol.

widget_id.description: Widget id to get a link for.

symbol.description: Symbol for market widgets (e.g. BTC). Ignored for non-market widgets.

sites.name: fin-esse-beta.vercel.app
sites.description: A WebMCP-powered financial planning workspace where you and an AI agent reason across your loans, portfolio, budget and goals together.

tools.name: loan_list
tools.description: List every loan in the user's profile with its EMI, outstanding balance, months remaining and interest still to be paid. Call this first whenever a question involves debt, and before calling any other loan_* tool, so you know which loan ids exist.

tools.name: loan_add
tools.description: Add a new loan to the user's profile. Use this when the user describes a debt they hold. Returns the computed EMI and the new loan's id.

name.description: Human label, e.g. "Home loan - Sector 62 flat".

annualRatePct.description: Nominal annual interest rate as a percentage, e.g. 8.6.

kind.description: Category of loan.

monthsPaid.description: How many EMIs have already been paid. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: loan_remove
tools.description: Remove a loan from the profile by its id. Use when a loan was entered by mistake or has been closed.

tools.name: loan_emi_calculator
tools.description: Compute the EMI, total interest and total repayment for hypothetical loan terms, without touching the user's profile. Use for 'what would the EMI be if...' questions.

annualRatePct.description: Annual interest rate as a percentage.

tools.name: loan_amortisation
tools.description: Show the month-by-month interest/principal split for a loan already in the profile. Use to explain where the money is actually going.

months.description: How many months to show. Defaults to 12, maximum 60.

fromMonth.description: Offset from today in months. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: loan_simulate_prepayment
tools.description: Simulate paying a lump sum and/or a permanent extra monthly amount into a loan, holding the EMI constant. Returns months saved and interest saved. This only simulates -- it does not change anything. To actually apply it, call loan_propose_prepayment.

lumpSum.description: One-off amount paid now. Defaults to 0.

extraMonthly.description: Permanent monthly top-up on top of the EMI. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: loan_propose_prepayment
tools.description: Propose actually applying a prepayment to the user's profile. This does NOT take effect immediately: it creates a proposal card the human must approve or reject in the app. Use this after loan_simulate_prepayment when the user agrees they want to go ahead.

lumpSum.description: One-off amount to pay against the principal.

reason.description: One sentence explaining why this is the right move, shown to the human on the approval card.

tools.name: loan_compare_offers
tools.description: Compare two or more loan offers on total cost including processing fees, and identify the cheapest. Use when the user is shopping for a loan or considering a refinance.

label.description: Name of the lender or offer.

annualRatePct.description: Annual interest rate as a percentage.

offers.description: Two or more offers to compare.

tools.name: portfolio_list
tools.description: List every investment holding with its units, price, current value and asset class. Call this before any other portfolio_* tool so you know which holding ids exist.

tools.name: portfolio_add_holding
tools.description: Add an investment holding to the portfolio. Use when the user tells you about something they own, so allocation and risk maths include it.

assetClass.description: Which asset class this belongs to.

price.description: Current price per unit.

tools.name: portfolio_remove_holding
tools.description: Remove a holding from the portfolio by id or ticker symbol. Use when the user has sold a position or entered it in error.

tools.name: portfolio_allocation
tools.description: Break the portfolio down by asset class, with the weight of each, the blended expected return, the volatility and a 0-100 risk score. Use this to answer 'how is my portfolio positioned' or before recommending a rebalance.

tools.name: portfolio_plan_rebalance
tools.description: Compute the buys and sells needed to move the portfolio to a target allocation by asset class. Targets are normalised, so they need not sum to 100. This only plans -- call portfolio_propose_rebalance to actually apply it.

tools.name: portfolio_propose_rebalance
tools.description: Propose actually rebalancing the portfolio to a target allocation. This does NOT take effect immediately: it creates a proposal card the human must approve or reject. Use after portfolio_plan_rebalance when the user agrees.

reason.description: One sentence explaining the rationale, shown to the human on the approval card.

tools.name: portfolio_simulate_market_event
tools.description: Simulate a named market event (equity crash, rate spike, crypto winter, broad risk-off, gold rally) against the portfolio and report the damage per holding. Read-only.

event.description: Which market event to simulate.

tools.name: portfolio_add_real_asset
tools.description: Record a non-investable asset such as a self-occupied home. It counts towards net worth but is deliberately excluded from allocation, rebalancing and concentration risk, because you cannot sell a third of the house you live in. Use this when the user mentions property they own.

value.description: Current market value.

tools.name: portfolio_update_price
tools.description: Update the current price of a holding, for example to reflect a live quote the user gives you.

price.description: New price per unit.

tools.name: budget_summary
tools.description: Show monthly income, essential and discretionary spending, total EMI outflow, the resulting surplus, the savings rate and how many months of emergency runway the cash reserve buys. Call this for any question about affordability, spare cash or monthly capacity.

tools.name: budget_set_income
tools.description: Set the user's monthly take-home income. Everything downstream -- surplus, savings rate, debt-service ratio and goal feasibility -- is derived from this, so set it before giving cashflow advice.

tools.name: budget_set_cash_reserve
tools.description: Set the liquid cash the user holds outside their investments. This is what funds prepayments and emergencies.

tools.name: budget_add_expense
tools.description: Add a recurring monthly expense. Mark it essential if it cannot be cut in a crisis.

amount.description: Monthly amount.

essential.description: True if this cannot be cut during an income shock. Defaults to true.

tools.name: budget_remove_expense
tools.description: Remove a recurring expense by id or name. Use when the user stops paying for something, which frees up monthly surplus.

tools.name: budget_add_goal
tools.description: Add a savings goal with a target amount and a deadline in months.

targetMonths.description: Months from now by which it is needed.

savedSoFar.description: Already set aside for this goal. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: budget_remove_goal
tools.description: Remove a savings goal by id or name. Use when a goal has been met, abandoned, or was entered in error.

tools.name: budget_goal_feasibility
tools.description: Assess whether the user's savings goals are actually reachable given their current monthly surplus, and flag which ones collide. Use when the user asks whether they can afford a goal, or before recommending they commit spare cash elsewhere.

tools.name: budget_set_expected_return
tools.description: Set the assumed long-run annual portfolio return used by goal and prepay-vs-invest maths. Use when the user wants to test a more or less optimistic assumption.

expectedReturnPct.description: Assumed nominal annual return as a percentage, e.g. 11.

tools.name: advisor_net_position
tools.description: Give the whole balance sheet at once: investable portfolio, non-investable real assets such as a home, cash, total debt, net worth, debt-to-assets, monthly EMI and monthly surplus. The fastest way to orient yourself before answering any cross-domain question.

tools.name: advisor_prepay_vs_invest
tools.description: THE cross-domain question: should a given amount of spare cash go towards prepaying a loan or into the portfolio? Compares every active loan against the assumed portfolio return by simulating both paths month by month with identical cash outflow, and ranks them. Call this whenever the user asks what to do with spare money, a bonus, or a windfall.

amount.description: The spare cash to deploy.

horizonMonths.description: How far ahead to compare, in months. Defaults to 60.

tools.name: advisor_risk_exposure
tools.description: Score the user's overall financial fragility out of 100 by combining debt service burden, leverage, emergency runway, portfolio risk and savings rate. Reads loans, portfolio and budget together. Use when asked 'how exposed am I' or 'is my position safe'.

tools.name: advisor_stress_test
tools.description: Stress-test the entire financial picture against a combined shock: months without income, a named market event, and/or an interest rate rise, all at once. Reports whether the plan breaks and at what point. Use for 'what if I lose my job' or 'what if the market crashes' questions.

jobLossMonths.description: Months with no income. Defaults to 0.

marketShock.description: A simultaneous market event, if any.

rateHikeBps.description: Interest rate rise in basis points applied to every loan, e.g. 200 for +2%.

tools.name: advisor_recommendations
tools.description: Generate a prioritised action list synthesised across loans, portfolio and budget, each item citing which tools produced its evidence and what the impact would be. Use to answer 'what should I do' or to close out an advisory conversation.

tools.name: advisor_assumptions
tools.description: List every planning assumption the app uses -- expected returns and volatility per asset class, and the user's assumed portfolio return. Call this when the user asks why a number is what it is, or before presenting any recommendation as fact.

tools.name: advisor_begin_whatif
tools.description: Open a sandboxed what-if branch. While a branch is open, every write tool changes only the sandbox, never the user's real profile, so you can explore freely -- apply prepayments, rebalance, reprice holdings -- and then discard it. Always pair with advisor_end_whatif. Use this before exploring a hypothetical the user has not committed to.

name.description: What you are exploring, e.g. "Clear the credit card first".

tools.name: advisor_save_scenario
tools.description: Snapshot the current financial picture under a name so it can be compared against others later. Use to capture a branch worth remembering before discarding it.

note.description: One line on what makes this scenario different.

tools.name: advisor_explain_number
tools.description: Explain how a specific headline figure was derived, showing the inputs and the formula. Supported figures: net_worth, surplus, emi_burden, risk_score, emergency_runway. Use when the user challenges or asks about a number you quoted.

tools.name: advisor_horizon_projection
tools.description: Project net worth forward over a horizon, showing how debt runs down and investments compound under current behaviour. Use to make a recommendation concrete.

horizonMonths.description: Months to project forward. Defaults to 60, maximum 360.

tools.name: advisor_create_handoff_link
tools.description: Package the user's entire financial position into a shareable link so another person's AI agent can pick it up and continue the analysis in their own browser session. Use when the user wants a second opinion from a partner, a friend or a financial advisor. The position travels inside the URL fragment, so it is never sent to any server. Give the user the returned URL verbatim.

from.description: Who is sharing, e.g. "Nikunj". Shown to whoever opens the link.

note.description: A short message to the receiving agent explaining what you want them to look at.

tools.name: advisor_load_handoff_link
tools.description: Load a financial position that someone else shared with you as a handoff link. Paste the whole URL. This replaces the profile currently on screen with theirs, so you can analyse their numbers instead of your own.

url.description: The full handoff URL that was shared with you.

tools.name: advisor_second_opinion
tools.description: Run the same decision through two deliberately different advisors -- a growth stance assuming 13% returns and a capital-preservation stance assuming 7% -- and report where they agree, where they diverge, and the exact assumption the disagreement turns on. Use when the user asks what the counter-argument is, wants a second opinion, or when you want to be honest that a recommendation depends on assumptions rather than arithmetic.

amount.description: The spare cash the decision is about.

horizonMonths.description: Comparison horizon in months. Defaults to 60.

tools.name: advisor_argue_as
tools.description: Get the strongest honest case one specific stance would make, so you can voice that side of a debate. Stances are 'growth' (assumes 13% returns, treats cheap debt as leverage) and 'preservation' (assumes 7%, prices certainty above expectation). Use to role-play a disagreement between two advisors, or to steelman the option the user is leaning against.

amount.description: The spare cash the decision is about.

horizonMonths.description: Comparison horizon in months. Defaults to 60.

tools.name: advisor_list_stances
tools.description: List the advisor stances available for a second opinion and the assumptions each one holds. Call this if you need to know what positions can be argued before staging a debate.

tools.name: advisor_shared_position_info
tools.description: Report whether the position currently loaded came from someone else's handoff link, who shared it and what note they attached. Call this at the start of a session so you know whose finances you are actually looking at.

tools.name: market_research_brief
tools.description: Get a research brief telling you exactly what market news to go and look up for THIS user's holdings, ranked by how much each exposure actually matters to them. The page holds no market data and fetches nothing — use your own web search to find the news, then bring what you found back through market_apply_conditions. Call this first whenever the user asks about market conditions, the news, or how current events affect them.

tools.name: market_apply_conditions
tools.description: Take what you found in your research and work out what it means for this specific person — every aspect of it. Give one entry per asset class with the percentage move you observed and a short note on why. Returns the impact on portfolio value, each holding, allocation, risk, volatility, expected return, net worth, goals, and whether the prepay-versus-invest recommendation flips. It deliberately also reports what did NOT move. This is a what-if: it changes nothing in the app.

assetClass.description: Which asset class this observation is about.

changePct.description: The move you observed, as a percentage. Negative for a fall, e.g. -12.5.

note.description: One line on what you read and why it moved.

source.description: Where you read it.

conditions.description: One entry per asset class you researched.

tools.name: market_last_read
tools.description: Report the market conditions most recently applied in this session, if any — what was observed, when, and the resulting move. Use it to avoid re-researching something you already looked up a few minutes ago.

tools.name: describe_scene

detail.description: Default "summary".

id.description: Object id or name.

tools.name: get_bounds

ids.description: Object ids or names. Omit for the whole scene.

tools.name: capture_view
tools.description: Quick snapshot of the live viewport exactly as the user sees it, including grid and selection. For a polished image use render.

tools.name: create_primitive
tools.description: Add a primitive solid. Types: box, rounded_box, sphere, cylinder, cone, torus, torus_knot, plane, capsule, icosahedron, dodecahedron, octahedron, tetrahedron, ring, prism. Each type has its own params (see list_presets); omitted params use defaults. Primitives are centered on their origin, so a box of height 1 spans y -0.5 to 0.5 before on_ground lifts it.

type.description: Primitive type.

params.description: Type-specific dimensions, e.g. {"width":1,"height":2,"depth":0.5} for box or {"radius":0.4} for sphere.

name.description: Display name. Names are unique; a numeric suffix is added on collision.

parent.description: Id or name of a parent object (usually a group). Position and rotation are then relative to it.

on_ground.description: Lift the object so its lowest point sits on the ground plane. Defaults to true when position is omitted (except for tube and mesh, whose coordinates are absolute), false otherwise.

visible.description: Default true.

tools.name: create_lathe
tools.description: Revolve a 2D profile around the Y axis. points are [radius, height] pairs from bottom to top; radius must be >= 0. Ideal for vases, bottles, bowls, chess pieces, knobs, and anything round. Use phi_length < 360 for a partial sweep (set the material double_sided).

points.description: Profile as [[radius, y], ...], at least 2 points, ordered bottom to top. Start and end at radius 0 for a closed solid.

segments.description: Radial segments around the axis. Default 64.

path.description: [[x, y, z], ...] with at least 2 points.

closed.description: Join the end back to the start. Default false.

tools.name: create_gear

outer_radius.description: Radius to the tooth tips. Default 0.5.

hole_radius.description: Center bore radius, 0 for none. Default 0.1.

tooth_depth.description: Radial tooth height. Default is proportional to the pitch.

tools.name: create_mesh
tools.description: Add raw triangle geometry: a flat positions array [x,y,z, x,y,z, ...] and optional indices (triples of vertex indices, counter-clockwise when seen from outside). Use this for shapes the other tools cannot make. Keep it under about 20k vertices.

positions.description: Flat vertex list, length a multiple of 3.

indices.description: Optional triangle index list, length a multiple of 3. Omit for unindexed triangles taken three vertices at a time.

smooth.description: Merge shared vertices and smooth normals. Default true. Set false for hard-edged shapes.

visible.description: Default true.

tools.name: create_group
tools.description: Create an empty group, optionally moving existing objects into it (their world placement is preserved). Groups can be moved, rotated, scaled, and duplicated as one unit.

children.description: Objects to move into the group.

position.description: Group origin. Default [0, 0, 0].

scale.description: Uniform number or [x, y, z]. Default 1.

tools.name: update_object
tools.description: Set properties of an object: name, absolute transform, geometry params (merged into the existing ones), material, visibility, shadows. For relative moves use transform_object.

id.description: Object id or name.

params.description: Geometry parameters to change, merged with the current ones, e.g. {"radius": 0.8}.

scale.description: Uniform number or [x, y, z]. Default 1.

material.description: Material id or name, or a preset name such as plastic, metal, gold, chrome, glass, wood, clay. See list_presets.

color.description: Hex color like "#D9A441". Combined with a preset it makes a tinted copy; alone it makes a plastic of that color.

on_ground.description: After other changes, drop the object onto the ground plane.

tools.name: transform_object
tools.description: Move, rotate, or scale an object relative to its current state (in parent space).

id.description: Object id or name.

tools.name: duplicate_object
tools.description: Copy an object (with its children) one or more times, offsetting and rotating each successive copy. Makes linear arrays: count 5 with offset [1.2, 0, 0] gives a row.

id.description: Object id or name.

offset.description: Added to the position for each successive copy. Default [0, 0, 0].

rotate_step.description: Degrees added for each successive copy.

tools.name: array_radial
tools.description: Arrange copies of an object evenly around an axis (bolt circles, spokes, petals, chair legs). The original stays; count minus one copies are added.

id.description: Object id or name.

center.description: Center of the circle in parent space. Default [0, 0, 0].

rotate_copies.description: Also rotate each copy to face outward. Default true.

tools.name: mirror_object
tools.description: Mirror an object across a plane through the given coordinate (default the origin) perpendicular to axis. Keeps the original unless keep_original is false.

id.description: Object id or name.

axis.description: Axis perpendicular to the mirror plane.

at.description: Coordinate of the mirror plane along axis. Default 0.

tools.name: drop_to_ground
tools.description: Move objects straight down (or up) so their lowest point touches the ground plane. Omit ids to drop every top-level object.

ids.description: Object ids or names.

tools.name: place_on
tools.description: Stack one object on top of another: its bottom lands on the target's top, centered over the target (plus an optional x/z offset).

id.description: Object to move.

target.description: Object to rest on.

offset.description: [dx, dz] offset from the target center. Default [0, 0].

tools.name: align_objects
tools.description: Line objects up along one axis by their bounding boxes: align their min, center, or max to a world coordinate, or to the first object when "to" is omitted.

ids.description: Two or more objects (or one object with an explicit "to").

mode.description: Which edge of each box to align. Default "center".

to.description: World coordinate to align to. Default: the first object's value.

tools.name: set_parent
tools.description: Move an object under another object (or to the top level with parent null). World placement is preserved.

id.description: Object id or name.

parent.description: Parent id/name, or null for top level.

tools.name: delete_objects
tools.description: Delete objects and their children.

ids.description: Object ids or names.

tools.name: boolean
tools.description: Combine solids: union merges the target with the tools, subtract cuts the tools out of the target (holes, slots, pockets), intersect keeps only the overlap. The target becomes a baked mesh; the tool objects are removed unless keep_tools is true. Overlap the shapes slightly to avoid coplanar faces.

target.description: Object that receives the result.

tools.description: One or more objects used as cutters or additions.

keep_tools.description: Keep the tool objects (hidden) instead of deleting them. Default false.

tools.name: select_objects
tools.description: Highlight objects in the user's viewport and inspector. Purely visual; use it to point at something you are discussing.

ids.description: Object ids or names. Empty to clear the selection.

tools.name: create_material
tools.description: Create a physically based material. Start from a preset (plastic, glossy_plastic, matte, clay, rubber, ceramic, metal, brushed_metal, chrome, steel, gold, copper, brass, glass, tinted_glass, frosted_glass, wood, velvet, emissive, wireframe) and override any property.

preset.description: Starting point.

opacity.description: 0 to 1. Below 1 turns on alpha blending.

transmission.description: 0 to 1. Physically based glass; keep opacity at 1 and set roughness low.

ior.description: Index of refraction, 1 to 2.333. Glass is 1.5.

thickness.description: Volume thickness for transmission refraction, in scene units.

clearcoat.description: 0 to 1. Lacquer layer on top of the base.

double_sided.description: Render back faces too (needed for open shapes like planes and lathes with partial sweep).

tools.name: update_material
tools.description: Change properties of an existing material. Every object using it updates.

id.description: Material id or name.

transmission.description: 0 to 1. Physically based glass; keep opacity at 1 and set roughness low.

ior.description: Index of refraction, 1 to 2.333. Glass is 1.5.

thickness.description: Volume thickness for transmission refraction, in scene units.

clearcoat.description: 0 to 1. Lacquer layer on top of the base.

double_sided.description: Render back faces too (needed for open shapes like planes and lathes with partial sweep).

tools.description: Apply a material (existing id/name, or a preset optionally tinted with color) to one or more objects. Applies to every solid inside a group.

ids.description: Object ids or names.

material.description: Material id or name, or a preset name such as plastic, metal, gold, chrome, glass, wood, clay. See list_presets.

color.description: Hex color like "#D9A441". Combined with a preset it makes a tinted copy; alone it makes a plastic of that color.

tools.name: list_materials
tools.description: List materials in the scene with their properties and which objects use them.

tools.name: delete_material
tools.description: Delete a material. Objects using it fall back to the default material.

id.description: Material id or name.

tools.name: set_lighting
tools.description: Replace all lights with a preset rig: studio (three-point studio rig with soft shadows. good default for product renders); soft (environment light only, with one faint shadow-casting sun. flat and forgiving); sun (hard warm sunlight with a cool sky fill. outdoor look); dramatic (one strong key from the side, deep shadows, little fill); none (no lights. only the environment map lights the scene). Tweak individual lights afterwards with update_light.

env_intensity.description: Override the environment (image based) light strength, 0 to 3.

tools.name: add_light
tools.description: Add a light. directional: parallel sunlight (intensity 1 to 5). point: bulb (intensity 20 to 300). spot: cone (intensity 50 to 400, angle in degrees). ambient and hemisphere: flat fill (0.2 to 2).

intensity.description: Directional lights: 1 to 5. Point and spot lights use candela-like values: 50 to 300 is typical at a few units away.

target.description: Point the light aims at (directional and spot).

cast_shadow.description: Shadows cost performance; keep to one or two lights.

angle.description: Spot cone half-angle in degrees.

ground_color.description: Hemisphere light color from below, hex.

tools.name: update_light
tools.description: Change a light's color, intensity, position, target, shadows, or spot cone.

id.description: Light id or name.

intensity.description: Directional lights: 1 to 5. Point and spot lights use candela-like values: 50 to 300 is typical at a few units away.

target.description: Point the light aims at (directional and spot).

cast_shadow.description: Shadows cost performance; keep to one or two lights.

angle.description: Spot cone half-angle in degrees.

ground_color.description: Hemisphere light color from below, hex.

tools.name: delete_light
tools.description: Remove a light.

id.description: Light id or name.

tools.name: set_environment
tools.description: Set the backdrop and ground for renders: background (gradient, solid color, or transparent), ground plane (invisible shadow catcher, solid plane, or a curved cyclorama backdrop), exposure, environment light strength, and shadows.

type.description: "shadow" shows only shadows on an invisible plane; "cyclorama" is a seamless studio sweep.

opacity.description: Shadow darkness for type "shadow", 0 to 1. Default 0.35.

exposure.description: Tone mapping exposure. Default 1; 0.7 darker, 1.4 brighter.

tools.name: set_camera
tools.description: Move the camera. Use view (perspective, front, back, left, right, top, bottom, iso, three_quarter, low, high) and frame to fit the whole scene or specific objects, or set position/target/fov directly. Frame is applied first, then explicit values override.

view.description: Named viewing direction.

frame.description: "all", an object id/name, or a list of them: fit these in view.

padding.description: Framing margin multiplier. Default 1.2; smaller is tighter.

position.description: Camera position.

target.description: Point the camera looks at.

fov.description: Vertical field of view in degrees. Default 38; 20 to 30 looks like a product shot.

tools.name: render
tools.description: Render a polished image of the scene with shadows, environment lighting, and antialiasing. Optionally frame objects and pick a view first. Returns the image. The camera stays where the render was taken unless restore_camera is true. Keep width at or below 1600 for quick turnaround.

view.description: Viewing direction for this render.

frame.description: "all", an object id/name, or a list: fit these before rendering.

format.description: Default png. jpeg is smaller.

supersample.description: 1 or 2. Default 2 (renders at double size and downsamples).

restore_camera.description: Put the camera back afterwards. Default false.

tools.name: render_turntable
tools.description: Render several views evenly spaced around the scene or given objects, at one elevation. Good for checking a model from all sides. Restores the camera afterwards.

elevation.description: Camera elevation in degrees above the horizon. Default 22.

frame.description: "all" or object ids/names.

format.description: Default jpeg.

tools.name: export_model
tools.description: Export the scene (or selected objects) as a file the user downloads: glb (with materials, best for sharing), stl (for 3D printing), obj, or json (this studio's own format, reloadable with load_scene). format.description: Default glb.

ids.description: Only these objects (world placement baked in). Omit for everything visible.

filename.description: Without extension. Default is the scene name.

download.description: Trigger a browser download for the user. Default true.

include_content.description: For json: return the document text in the result. Default false.

tools.name: load_scene
tools.description: Replace the current scene with a studio JSON document (from export_model format json). The previous scene stays in undo history.

scene.description: The document as a JSON object or string.

tools.name: new_scene
tools.description: Clear everything and start a fresh scene with the default studio lighting. The old scene stays in undo history.

tools.name: set_scene_name
tools.description: Rename the scene (used for export filenames).

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo the last change(s).

steps.description: Default 1.

tools.name: redo
tools.description: Redo the last undone change(s).

steps.description: Default 1.

tools.name: get_history
tools.description: List recent changes, newest last.

limit.description: Default 30.

tools.description: Scan every on the current page for C2PA Content Credentials (content provenance metadata) and return a per-image summary: whether a manifest is present, the claim generator (the tool that produced or edited the image), the title, and the signer name. limit.description: Maximum number of images to fetch and scan (default 25, max 100).

tools.name: inspect_image_c2pa
tools.description: Fetch a single image (by CSS selector or URL) and return its fully decoded C2PA manifest store: every manifest's claim, assertions (e.g. c2pa.actions edit history, schema.org authorship), and the COSE signature details (algorithm and signing-certificate identity). Provide exactly one of `selector` or `url`. Note: the signature is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

selector.description: CSS selector for an element on the page.

url.description: Image URL (absolute, or relative to the current page) to fetch and inspect.

tools.name: ilan_ara
tools.description: BirMakine'de ikinci el ve yeni iş makinesi, endüstriyel ekipman, endüstriyel mutfak ve ağır vasıta ilanı arar. Anahtar kelime, kategori, fiyat aralığı ve şehir ile filtreler. JSON sonuç döndürür.

q.description: Anahtar kelime, ör. ekskavatör, matkap, fritöz

sort.description: Sıralama

after.description: Keyset imleci — derin sayfalama için önceki yanıtın sonraki_imlec değeri (10000+ ilan için)

tools.name: ilan_detay
tools.description: Bir BirMakine ilanının detayını döndürür: ad, fiyat, açıklama, kategori, satıcı, şehir, teknik bilgiler. İlan slug'ı (URL son parçası) ile çağrılır.

tools.name: kategori_gez
tools.description: BirMakine'deki tüm ilan kategorilerini (89) ilan sayılarıyla listeler. ilan_ara için kategori slug almak amacıyla kullanılır.

tools.name: marka_listele
tools.description: BirMakine'deki üretici markalarını (Makita, Bosch, Stihl, Öztiryakiler vb.) ilan sayılarıyla listeler. Opsiyonel q ile marka adına göre arar.

tools.name: satici_profil
tools.description: Bir BirMakine satıcısının/firmasının profilini döndürür: ad, şehir, aktif ilan sayısı, üyelik yılı. Satıcı slug'ı ile çağrılır.

tools.name: benzer_ilan
tools.description: Bir ilana benzer (aynı kategori) ilanları getirir.

tools.name: pazar_istatistik
tools.description: Pazar istatistiği: toplam aktif ilan, fiyat aralığı (min/ort/max TL) ve en çok ilanlı kategoriler.

tools.name: populer_kategori
tools.description: En çok ilanlı kategorileri (popüler) döndürür.

tools.name: en_yeni_ilan
tools.description: En yeni eklenen ilanları getirir (opsiyonel kategori).

tools.name: konum_ilanlari
tools.description: Belirli bir şehirdeki (plaka id) ilanları getirir.

tools.name: satici_ilanlari
tools.description: Bir satıcının ilanlarını getirir (satıcı slug).

tools.name: marka_ilanlari
tools.description: Bir üretici markasının (Makita, Bosch…) ilanlarını getirir (marka slug).

tools.name: blog_ara
tools.description: BirMakine blog/rehber yazılarını arar.

tools.name: blog_getir
tools.description: Bir blog yazısının içeriğini getirir (slug).

tools.name: sss_getir
tools.description: BirMakine sık sorulan soruları ve cevaplarını döndürür.

tools.name: yazar_getir
tools.description: Bir blog yazarının uzmanlık, deneyim ve bilgilerini döndürür (slug).

tools.name: ilan_filtrele
tools.description: İlanları kategori, marka, fiyat ve şehir facet'leriyle filtreler (ilan_ara ile aynı, filtre odaklı).

tools.name: site_ara
tools.description: BirMakine genel araması (ilan).

tools.name: marka_modelleri
tools.description: Bir üretici markasının ilan başlıklarından çıkarılan model kodlarını (ör. HMK 140, GBH 2-26) ilan sayılarıyla döndürür (tahmini/heuristik). Marka slug ile.

tools.name: fiyat_gecmisi
tools.description: Bir kategorinin medyan/ortalama fiyat zaman-serisini (günlük snapshot) döndürür + dönem medyan değişim yüzdesi. Fiyat trendi/enflasyon soruları için. Kategori slug ile.

tools.name: sozluk_terim
tools.description: Sektör terimleri sözlüğünü döndürür. Terim verilmezse tüm terimleri; terim verilince o terimin tanımını + ilgili aramayı. Makine/ekipman terimlerini (ekskavatör, motosaat, CE belgesi, TCO…) açıklamak için.

tools.name: finansman_karsilastir
tools.description: Bir tutar için 12/24/36/48/60 ay vadelerinde taksit karşılaştırma matrisi döndürür (aylık taksit, toplam geri ödeme, toplam faiz). Sunucu-taraflı, birden çok vade tek çağrıda.

tools.name: stok_durumu
tools.description: Bir ilanın güncel durumunu döndürür: aktif/preorder/discontinued + son güncelleme tarihi. İlan slug ile.

tools.name: trend_kategoriler
tools.description: Son 30 günün trend aramalarını (en çok aranan terimler) ve popüler kategorileri döndürür. "Şu an ne aranıyor / gündemde ne var" için.

tools.name: fiyat_dagilimi
tools.description: Bir kategorinin fiyat dağılımını döndürür: histogram (fiyat aralıkları + adet) + özet (min/P10/P25/medyan/P75/P90/max/ortalama TL). "X ne kadar, fiyatlar nasıl dağılıyor" soruları için. Kategori slug ile.

tools.name: benzer_fiyatli
tools.description: Verilen bütçeye en yakın ilanları bir kategoride bulur (gauss yakınlık). Kategori slug + fiyat (TL) ile; opsiyonel adet. "500.000 TL bütçeyle hangi ekskavatörler" gibi.

tools.name: satici_kategorileri
tools.description: Bir satıcının hangi kategorilerde kaç aktif ilanı olduğunu döndürür (satıcının uzmanlık alanı). Satıcı slug ile.

tools.name: kategori_agaci
tools.description: Tüm ilan kategorilerini TAM hiyerarşik ağaç olarak (üst kategori → alt kategoriler) ilan sayılarıyla tek çağrıda döndürür. Her düğümde dogrudan_ilan + toplam_ilan (alt-ağaç rollup). Kategori yapısını keşfetmek için kategori_gez'e göre daha zengindir.

tools.name: kategori_ozet
tools.description: Bir kategorinin pazar özetini döndürür: toplam ilan, satıcı sayısı, fiyat bandı (min/ortalama/max TL) ve popüler üretici markaları. "Forklift pazarı nasıl?" gibi sorular için. Kategori slug ile çağrılır.

tools.name: finansman_hesapla
tools.description: Makine alımı için basit leasing/taksit hesaplar. Yerel hesap, PII gerektirmez.

tools.name: talep_durumu
tools.description: Write-tool ile oluşturulan talebin (fiyat_alarmi/arama/mesaj/teklif) durumunu döndürür — kullanıcı e-posta onayı verdi mi (aktif/iletildi) yoksa bekliyor mu. token = write yanıtındaki undo_token.

tools.name: kategoriler
tools.description: Tüm kategoriler + ilan sayısı.

tools.name: markalar
tools.description: Üretici markaları.

tools.name: fiyat_alarmi_kur
tools.description: Kullanıcının e-postasına fiyat/kategori alarmı kurar. Uygun ilan (kategori + hedef fiyat) çıktığında e-posta gönderilir. ÇİFT-OPT-IN: kullanıcı e-postadaki linki onaylamadan alarm aktifleşmez; onay için kullanıcının açık isteği/e-postası gerekir.

email.description: Kullanıcının e-posta adresi (onay linki buraya gider)

tools.name: mesaj_gonder
tools.description: Alıcı adına bir ilanın satıcısına mesaj iletir. ALICI ONAYI ŞART: mesaj önce beklemede kalır, alıcı e-postasındaki linki onaylayınca satıcıya iletilir (spam önlenir). Kullanıcının açık isteği + geçerli e-postası gerekir.

tools.name: arama_kaydet
tools.description: Kullanıcının aramasını (metin/kategori/fiyat) kaydeder; uygun yeni ilan çıktığında e-posta bildirir. ÇİFT-OPT-IN: e-posta onayı şart. Kullanıcının açık isteği + e-postası gerekir.

tools.name: teklif_gonder
tools.description: Alıcı adına satıcıya bir ilan için yapılandırılmış TEKLİF (fiyat + mesaj) iletir. ALICI ONAYI ŞART: teklif önce beklemede, alıcı e-postasını onaylayınca satıcıya iletilir.

tools.name: karsilastirma_listesi
tools.description: Geçici karşılaştırma listesi (2-4 ilan). token vermezseniz yeni liste açılır ve token döner; aynı token ile ekle/çıkar/oku. Yanıt ilanların fiyat/marka/konum/özelliklerini karşılaştırmalı döndürür. Ephemeral (24 saat), e-posta/hesap gerektirmez.

token.description: Var olan liste token'ı (ilk çağrıda boş bırakın)

tools.name: favori_ekle
tools.description: Kullanıcının favori/kaydedilenler listesine ilan ekler (token-tabanlı, 30 gün saklanır, hesap gerektirmez). token vermezsen yeni liste + token döner; aynı token ile ekle/çıkar/oku (max 50).

token.description: Var olan favori listesi token'ı (ilk çağrıda boş)

tools.name: get_listing_details
tools.description: Su an goruntulenen ilanin adini, fiyatini, kategorisini, saticisini ve URL'sini dondurur.

tools.name: open_seller_product_page
tools.description: Bu ilanin saticisinin orijinal urun sayfasini yeni sekmede acar.

tools.name: get_palette_context

tools.name: get_current_phase

tools.name: navigate_to_phase

tools.name: get_references

tools.name: get_selected_references

tools.name: get_directions

tools.name: get_design_decisions

sites.name: pixel-art-tutor.thomasjvu.com
sites.description: Pixel Art Tutor — a WebMCP-powered pixel art studio where AI agents and humans co-create sprites, characters, animations and tilemaps together.

tools.name: get_project_state
tools.description: Overview of the whole pixel art project: palette with indices, all sprites (ids, names, sizes, kinds, frame counts), which sprite/frame is on the human's screen, and tilemap info. Call this first to ground yourself.

tools.name: read_sprite
tools.description: Read one frame of a sprite as ASCII art rows plus a color legend, so you can see exactly what the human is drawing. '.' = transparent; other characters use the 64-symbol palette alphabet returned in the legend.

spriteId.description: Sprite id. Defaults to the active sprite.

layerId.description: Layer id. Defaults to the first layer.

tools.name: set_pixels
tools.description: Paint specific pixels on a sprite frame. Each valid requested pixel is applied in order, one cell at a time on the page. Use fill_region or flood_fill for bulk areas.

pixels.description: List of pixel changes, applied one cell at a time, e.g. [{"x":3,"y":4,"color":"#38b764"}]

color.description: Color to paint. Use a palette index (number), a hex string like '#38b764' (auto-added to the palette), 'transparent', or null to erase.

allFrames.description: Apply the same change to every frame.

layerId.description: Layer id. Defaults to the first layer.

tools.name: fill_region
tools.description: Fill a rectangular region of a sprite frame with one color. Great for blocking in base shapes quickly.

color.description: Color to paint. Use a palette index (number), a hex string like '#38b764' (auto-added to the palette), 'transparent', or null to erase.

tools.name: flood_fill
tools.description: Bucket-fill: starting at x,y, replace all connected pixels of the same color with the new color (transparent counts as a color). Fails clearly if the start pixel is out of bounds.

color.description: Color to paint. Use a palette index (number), a hex string like '#38b764' (auto-added to the palette), 'transparent', or null to erase.

tools.name: clear_frame
tools.description: Erase every pixel of one sprite frame, making it fully transparent.

tools.name: transform_sprite
tools.description: Apply a geometric transform to a sprite. Ops: flip_h, flip_v, rotate_90 (clockwise), rotate (RotSprite-style nearest-neighbor angle in degrees), shift (wrap-around move by dx/dy), outline (adds outlineColor around silhouettes). Applies to all frames unless frameIndices given.

angle.description: rotate only: clockwise angle in degrees; keeps the sprite dimensions

color.description: outline only: outline color (defaults to palette index 0)

tools.name: replace_color
tools.description: Swap every occurrence of one palette color for another across a sprite (or the whole project if no spriteId). Accepts palette indices or hex strings.

from.description: Color to replace.

to.description: Replacement color ('transparent'/null erases).

spriteId.description: Scope to one sprite; omit for all sprites.

layerId.description: Scope to one layer; omit for all layers.

tools.name: add_palette_color
tools.description: Add a new hex color to the shared project palette and get its index back.

tools.name: set_palette_alpha
tools.description: Set the selected palette entry's opacity from 0 to 1 without changing its color index.

tools.name: move_palette_color
tools.description: Reorder a palette entry while remapping all pixel indices so the artwork keeps its appearance.

tools.name: set_active_sprite
tools.description: Switch the human's editor view to a given sprite (and optionally frame). Use this to show them something you made or want them to review.

tools.name: add_frame
tools.description: Add a new animation frame to a character sprite, copying an existing frame by default so it can be nudged into the next pose.

copyFrameIndex.description: Frame to duplicate. Defaults to the last frame.

layerId.description: Layer id. Defaults to the selected layer.

tools.name: delete_frame
tools.description: Delete one animation frame from a sprite. Requires confirm:true. Refuses to delete a sprite's last remaining frame.

layerId.description: Layer id. Defaults to the selected layer.

confirm.description: Must be true to perform the deletion

tools.name: link_frame
tools.description: Link two cels on one layer so future pixel edits stay synchronized across both frames.

targetIndex.description: Zero-based cel to link it with

layerId.description: Layer id. Defaults to the selected layer.

tools.name: unlink_frame
tools.description: Detach one cel from its linked group so it can be edited independently.

layerId.description: Layer id. Defaults to the selected layer.

tools.name: add_layer
tools.description: Create an empty animation layer above the selected layer. It starts with matching cels so it can be painted immediately.

spriteId.description: Sprite id; defaults to the active sprite.

aboveLayerId.description: Insert above this layer; defaults to the top.

tools.name: duplicate_layer
tools.description: Copy a layer, including every cel, and place the copy directly above it.

tools.name: delete_layer
tools.description: Delete a layer after explicit confirmation. A sprite must keep at least one layer.

tools.name: move_layer
tools.description: Move a layer one slot up or down in the stack. Direction 1 moves toward the top.

tools.name: set_layer_properties
tools.description: Update a layer name, visibility, lock, opacity, or blend mode.

tools.name: set_animation_preview
tools.description: Control playback mode, tagged range, speed, and onion-skin display without changing sprite pixels.

tools.name: set_canvas_options
tools.description: Set zoom, grid, pixel-perfect stroke, shading ink, tiled preview, and dither brush options. The default canvas is a 256x256 logical grid displayed at 1px per cell; zoom in for detailed editing.

tools.name: add_frame_tag
tools.description: Create a named animation section over a range of frames, such as idle or walk.

tools.name: delete_frame_tag
tools.description: Delete a named animation section after explicit confirmation.

tools.name: rename_sprite
tools.description: Rename an existing sprite (e.g. after giving an untitled sprite an identity).

tools.name: add_sprite
tools.description: Create a new empty sprite (character, item, or tile for the tileset). It becomes the active sprite so the human sees it immediately. Character sprites default to 4 empty animation frames and items/tiles default to 1; pass frameCount to choose another count. Optionally copy dimensions/content from an existing sprite.

kind.description: 'tile' adds it to the tileset for map painting.

copyFromId.description: Clone pixels from this sprite id if sizes match.

frameCount.description: Animation frame count. Defaults to 4 for characters and 1 for items/tiles.

tools.name: get_tilemap
tools.description: Read the tilemap grid as ASCII rows where each token maps to a tileset sprite via the returned legend. Maps with more than 64 tiles use two-character tokens and return tokenWidth: 2.

tools.name: ensure_tilemap
tools.description: Create the project tilemap (or resize it, preserving overlapping cells) so tiles can be placed. Cols/rows are clamped to 2-64; default to 12x9 when unsure. No-ops with ok:true if the map already has these dimensions.

rows.description: Map height in tiles (2-64)

tools.name: place_tile
tools.description: Put one tileset sprite at a map coordinate. Pass tileId=null or 'empty' to clear the cell.

tools.name: fill_tiles
tools.description: Fill a rectangular region of the tilemap with one tileset sprite. Pass tileId=null or 'empty' to clear the area.

tools.name: critique_artwork
tools.description: Run the built-in pixel-art tutor analysis on a sprite: color discipline, value contrast, outline strength, noise, centering, symmetry, animation readiness. Returns a score, stats and findings with concrete tips. Use it to give the human structured feedback before/after you edit.

tools.name: export_project
tools.description: Serialize the entire project (palette, sprites, frames, tilemap) as JSON that can be re-imported via the import_project tool, the Sprites > Project file > Import button, or a share permalink.

tools.name: import_project
tools.description: Replace the current project with one previously exported via export_project (or a project file). The JSON is sanitized and validated; the human sees the imported project immediately.

tools.name: new_canvas
tools.description: Replace the current project with a fresh blank 256x256 logical canvas (one empty character sprite, default palette, no tilemap). Defaults to 4 empty animation frames; pass frameCount to choose another count. Requires confirm:true. The human sees the blank canvas immediately; use this to start a new drawing together.

confirm.description: Must be true to clear the current project

frameCount.description: Optional animation frame count; defaults to 4.

tools.name: start_tutorial
tools.description: Open the step-by-step guided tour overlay (shared with the room, so following humans see the same step) and jump to a step. Use it to walk the human through the whole app, then guide them to a first project together with your drawing tools.

step.description: Zero-based step index. Defaults to 0 (the beginning).

tools.name: tutorial_goto
tools.description: Jump the shared guided-tour overlay to a given step (0-based). Pair each step with a live demo using your drawing tools.

tools.name: end_tutorial
tools.description: Close the shared guided-tour overlay on this window (following humans keep their own copy until they close it). Call it when the tour is done so it never pops back up.

tools.name: rename_project
tools.description: Rename the current project (e.g. 'guided-tutorial-01' when starting a tutorial piece). The human sees the new title immediately.

tools.name: save_project
tools.description: Save the current project into the on-device library under a name (defaults to the project name), so it can be reopened later with open_project. Saved names are listed in get_project_state.

name.description: Slot name, e.g. 'guided-tutorial-01'. Defaults to the project name.

tools.name: open_project
tools.description: Replace the current project with a saved one from the on-device library. Requires confirm:true. The human sees the opened project immediately.

confirm.description: Must be true to replace the current project

tools.name: save_palette
tools.description: Save the current shared palette into the on-device library under a name, so it can be merged into any project later with apply_palette. Saved names are listed in get_project_state.

tools.name: apply_palette
tools.description: Merge a saved palette into the current project: missing colors are appended (up to 64), existing indices never move so artwork is untouched. Reports how many colors were added.

sites.name: remap-xi.vercel.app
sites.description: Your keyboard's best friend

tools.name: get_keyboard_state
tools.description: Get the currently connected keyboard: its name, protocol version, layer count, active layer, and layout options. Call this first to see what keyboard (if any) is connected before using other keymap tools.

tools.name: get_keymap
tools.description: Get the keycodes assigned to every key position (as human-readable QMK keycode strings like "KC_A") for one layer, or all layers if none is given. Each entry's array index is the "keyIndex" used by remap_key and propose_remap.

layer.description: Layer index to read; omit to read every layer.

tools.name: remap_key
tools.description: Assign a QMK keycode (e.g. "KC_A", "KC_LSFT", "MO(1)") to one key position on a layer. keyIndex is the position in the array returned by get_keymap. Switches the active layer first if it differs from the requested one, so the change is visible on screen. For changing several keys together as one reviewable set, use propose_remap instead.

layer.description: Target layer index.

tools.name: set_active_layer
tools.description: Switch the keyboard configurator UI to show a different layer.

tools.name: list_available_keycodes
tools.description: List QMK keycodes supported by the connected keyboard, for use with remap_key and propose_remap. Use "search" to filter (e.g. "shift", "KC_F") since the full list can be large.

search.description: Substring filter, optional.

limit.description: Max results to return, default 60.

tools.name: save_keymap_snapshot
tools.description: Export the full keymap (every layer) and macros as a JSON snapshot the agent can hand back to the user or restore later with load_keymap_snapshot.

tools.name: load_keymap_snapshot
tools.description: Overwrite the entire keymap (all layers) and macros from a JSON snapshot produced by save_keymap_snapshot. This replaces every key on the keyboard, so it requires user confirmation.

tools.name: get_lighting_state
tools.description: Read the current RGB/backlight state of the connected keyboard: raw values for v2 keyboards, or the list of controllable lighting/custom options (with current values) for v3+ keyboards.

tools.name: set_lighting_value
tools.description: Set a raw backlight/RGB value on a v2-protocol keyboard. "command" is a LightingValue name such as "BACKLIGHT_BRIGHTNESS", "BACKLIGHT_EFFECT", "QMK_RGBLIGHT_COLOR", or "BACKLIGHT_COLOR_1". "values" is the raw byte payload (e.g. [hue, saturation] for a color, [level] for brightness/effect). Use get_lighting_state first to see supported commands. Only works on v2 keyboards -- use set_custom_menu_option for v3.

tools.name: set_custom_menu_option
tools.description: Set a keyboard-defined "custom menu" option on a v3+ keyboard, identified by the "id" returned from get_lighting_state (covers RGB and other firmware-defined settings). "value" is the logical value within the option's [min, max] range.

tools.name: get_macro_capabilities
tools.description: Check whether this keyboard supports macros at all, how many slots it has, the buffer size in bytes, and whether explicit delays are supported in macro expressions. Call this before authoring a long or delay-using macro.

tools.name: list_macros
tools.description: List every macro slot and its current expression text (empty string means unassigned).

tools.name: set_macro
tools.description: Set the expression for one macro slot, e.g. "KC_H,KC_I,KC_LSFT(KC_1)". Use list_macros to see available slot indices and the expression syntax already in use.

tools.name: clear_macro
tools.description: Clear one macro slot back to empty.

tools.name: get_layout_options
tools.description: Get the physical layout option labels and their currently selected values (e.g. index 0 of a "Bottom Row" option meaning ANSI vs ISO).

tools.name: set_layout_option
tools.description: Set one physical layout option to a new value, from the list returned by get_layout_options.

tools.name: remap_encoder
tools.description: Assign a QMK keycode to a rotary encoder's clockwise or counter-clockwise rotation on a given layer.

tools.name: navigate_to_pane
tools.description: Switch the app's top-level view. Available panes: default, test, design, console, settings, debug, errors.

tools.name: switch_configure_tab
tools.description: Switch the sub-tab within the Configure pane (Keymap/Lighting/Macros/Layouts/Save + Load). Navigates to the Configure pane first if needed. Not every tab is available on every keyboard.

tools.name: reset_eeprom
tools.description: Erase the keyboard's saved settings (keymap, macros, lighting) back to firmware defaults. Irreversible -- requires user confirmation.

tools.name: jump_to_bootloader
tools.description: Reboot the keyboard into its firmware bootloader for reflashing. The keyboard will disconnect. Requires user confirmation.

tools.name: propose_remap
tools.description: Propose a set of key changes for a person to review, across one or more keys. This writes nothing to the keyboard. It returns a proposal_id, the exact before and after for every key, and any collisions found against what is already bound. Every change needs its own reason in plain language, because that reason is what the person reviewing it is actually evaluating. Use this for anything touching more than one key; for a single key, use remap_key directly instead.

rationale.description: One or two sentences on what this set of changes is for, as a whole.

reason.description: Why this specific key moves.

tools.name: get_proposal
tools.description: Check what happened to a proposal from propose_remap: still waiting, approved, rejected, written, or reverted.

tools.name: list_connected_devices
tools.description: List every keyboard this browser currently has WebHID access to: which one is active, which are connected but not selected, and which were seen but could not be used (no definition found, or an unsupported protocol). Pairing a new device is not possible from a tool -- the human has to click "Authorize device" -- but this tells an agent what is already available.

tools.name: select_device
tools.description: Make a different already-connected keyboard the active one, by path from list_connected_devices. All other tools (keymap, lighting, macros, ...) act on whichever device is active.

tools.name: list_custom_controls
tools.description: List every keyboard-defined custom setting (toggle, dropdown, button, color, range, or keycode) with its type, label, options, and current value. Covers whatever the keyboard's own firmware definition exposes beyond the keymap -- often lighting, but also anything else the maker defined. Use "id" from here with set_custom_control.

tools.name: set_custom_control
tools.description: Set one keyboard-defined custom control, by "id" from list_custom_controls. The shape of "value" depends on the control's type: toggle wants a boolean, dropdown wants the option's label (string) or explicit value (number), button wants no value at all, color wants {hue, sat} (each 0-255), range and keycode want a single number or keycode string respectively -- list_custom_controls tells you which.

tools.name: get_per_key_rgb
tools.description: Read the individual RGB color (hue, saturation, each 0-255) of every key that has its own addressable LED. Only meaningful on v3+ keyboards with per-key lighting; returns an empty list otherwise.

tools.name: set_per_key_rgb
tools.description: Set the RGB color of one key with its own addressable LED, by keyIndex from get_keymap. hue and sat are each 0-255. Only works on v3+ keyboards with per-key lighting.

tools.name: get_custom_colors
tools.description: Read the v2-protocol custom color palette (the small set of saved colors some boards offer, indexed 0..N) as a list of {index, hue, sat}.

tools.name: set_custom_color
tools.description: Set one entry in the v2-protocol custom color palette, by index. hue and sat are each 0-255.

tools.name: get_app_settings
tools.description: Read the configurator app's own display preferences: theme (light/dark), theme name, keyboard render mode (2D/3D), and macro editor behavior. This is about the app, not the connected keyboard.

tools.name: set_theme_mode
tools.description: Switch the app between light and dark mode.

tools.name: set_render_mode
tools.description: Switch the on-screen keyboard between a 2D and 3D render. Falls back to 2D automatically if this browser doesn't support WebGL.

tools.name: get_app_errors
tools.description: Read the app's internal error log -- failed HID commands, device-loading retries, and similar. Useful for diagnosing "why didn't that work" without asking the person to open DevTools.

tools.name: clear_app_errors
tools.description: Clear the app's internal error log.

tools.name: get_activity_log
tools.description: Read this agent's own recent tool calls -- name, input, result or error, and timing -- the same feed shown in the Agent Dock's Activity tab. Lets an agent check what it already did instead of relying on conversation memory, e.g. after a page reload mid-task.

limit.description: Max entries to return, newest first. Default 20.

tools.name: get_host_keyboard_layout
tools.description: Read the OS keyboard layout the app assumes when showing keycodes (e.g. "keymap_us"). This affects display only, not what's written to the device.

tools.name: set_host_keyboard_layout
tools.description: Set the OS keyboard layout the app assumes for display purposes (e.g. "keymap_us", "keymap_uk", "keymap_dvorak"). Does not change anything on the device itself.

tools.name: set_test_keyboard_sound
tools.description: Configure the app's own audio feedback for the Key Tester (a synthesized tone per keypress, played by the browser -- not the physical keyboard). Omit any field to leave it unchanged.

tools.name: get_definition
tools.description: Get the physical layout of every key: its position/size in key units (x, y, w, h, rotation), its firmware matrix position (row, col), and the keycode currently bound to it on the given layer. Use this instead of get_keymap when the request is spatial (e.g. "the key left of spacebar") rather than by keyIndex.

layer.description: Layer to resolve keycodes against. Default 0.

tools.name: diagnose_matrix
tools.description: Read the live physical switch matrix from the device -- which row/col positions are electrically closed right now. Real-time, not related to what keycodes are assigned; use it to check for a stuck key or a wiring problem, not to read the keymap.

tools.name: get_device_info
tools.description: Read device identity and health: QMK firmware version, VIA keycodes protocol version (both cached from connection time), and live uptime in milliseconds (a fresh read).
