tools.name: save_synth_patch
tools.description: Store the live patch of Synth 1 or 2 into a slot of the pack's patch bank (0-127) so select_patch and the Preset view can recall it; included in Export pack.

tools.name: get_synth_patch
tools.description: Read the live patch of Synth 1 or 2: name, all parameter values, active mod matrix slots (named sources/destinations, signed depth) and macro assignments.

tools.name: set_drum_params
tools.description: Set drum track parameters: level, pitch, decay, distortion, eq, pan (0-127), sample (0-63, the drum sample slot), reverb_send, delay_send. E.g. {"pitch": 80, "sample": 2}.

params.description: param_name -> value.

tools.name: set_project_params
tools.description: Set project-level parameters: FX sends, mixer, master filter, reverb, delay, FX bypass, sidechain. Names: - reverb_ _send / delay_ _send (track: synth1, synth2, midi1, midi2, drum1-4) - _level / _pan - master_filter_frequency (0-63 low-pass, 64 off, 65-127 high-pass), master_filter_resonance - reverb_type (0-5), reverb_decay, reverb_damping, reverb_preset (0-7) - delay_time, delay_time_sync (0-35), delay_feedback, delay_width, delay_lr_ratio (0-12), delay_slew_rate, delay_preset (0-15) - fx_bypass (0/1) - sidechain_ _preset (1-7 activates, 0 off), _source (0-3 = drum1-4, 4 = off), _attack, _hold, _decay, _depth E.g. {"reverb_synth1_send": 60, "delay_feedback": 80, "sidechain_synth1_preset": 3, "sidechain_synth1_source": 0}.

params.description: param_name -> value.

tools.name: set_macro
tools.description: Turn a macro knob (1-8) on Synth 1 or 2 to a position 0-127. Macros ADD to the patch base values through the assignments shown by get_macros.

value.description: Knob position.

tools.name: get_macros
tools.description: Macro knob layout for both synths: current knob positions and, per macro, the parameters it moves with their start/end knob range and signed depth.

tools.name: play_notes
tools.description: Audition notes right now (independent of the sequencer). Pass a track name, or a channel like the hardware: 0 = synth1, 1 = synth2, 2 = midi1, 3 = midi2, 9 = drums (notes 60, 62, 64, 65 hit drums 1-4). Middle C = 60.

notes.description: MIDI note numbers; several = chord.

track.description: Track name (preferred).

channel.description: Hardware-style channel if no track is given.

tools.name: play_drum
tools.description: Trigger one drum hit right now.

tools.name: list_drum_samples
tools.description: List the 64 drum samples of the loaded pack with their index numbers and names (4 pages of 16). Use the index with set_drum_params {"sample": n} or sounds.drumN.sample.

page.description: Only this page (1-4); omit for all.

tools.name: list_patches
tools.description: List the synth patches of the loaded pack with their index numbers (Web Tracks extra). Use the index with select_patch.

tools.name: select_patch
tools.description: Load a patch from the pack's patch bank onto Synth 1 or 2 by index (see list_patches).

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the project bank slots that hold a project (Web Tracks extra).

tools.name: select_project
tools.description: Load a project from the bank by slot (0-63), replacing the live project. queued = true switches at the end of the current pattern while playing. An empty slot loads an init project.

queued.description: Switch at the pattern end while playing.

tools.name: export_song_to_project
tools.description: Save the live project into a bank slot (0-63), like pressing Save on the hardware. Defaults to the current slot, else the first empty one. Optional name renames the project (16 chars fit the hardware display). Use download_project to get the .ncs file.

tools.name: download_project
tools.description: Download the live project as a hardware-ready .ncs file in the user's browser (Web Tracks extra; the file can be sent to a Circuit Tracks with Components or the hardware MCP server).

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Restore the project state from before the last structural agent call: load_song, set_pattern, set_track, clear_pattern, set_song, create_synth_patch, edit_synth_patch, select_patch, select_project. Live tweaks (tempo, macros, mutes, synth/drum/project params) are not undone. Repeat to go further back (up to 12 states).

sites.name: api-canvas-bclonan.netlify.app
sites.description: Turn public data into connected cards. People and WebMCP agents work on the same local canvas.

tools.name: get_content_spec
tools.description: Read the versioned content contract and examples for editable notes, cited answers, search results, files, datasets and embeds. No HTML or script execution.

tools.name: create_content_block
tools.description: Save user-requested agent content as an editable card. Supply version 1 content, current source card citations and optional presentation. Content is agent supplied, not a live API response. Identical keys are idempotent. Use prepare_canvas_question before answering data questions.

tools.name: update_content_block
tools.description: Replace an existing content card with edited content or a cited answer to its question. Preserves its ID and connections. Validate current evidence with prepare_canvas_question and use expectedRevision.

tools.name: prepare_canvas_question
tools.description: Read bounded evidence from the full page or specified cards for a question. Returns filters, visible data, raw data, freshness, issues and an answer contract. The calling agent writes the answer; this tool does not run an LLM or invent an answer.

tools.name: answer_canvas_question
tools.description: Create one to six ordinary answer, table, chart or other content blocks linked to a saved question. Call prepare_canvas_question with questionBlockId first. Supply its expectedRevision and current scoped citations. Validates all outputs before adding any. Repeat identical outputs safely; edit returned blocks with the normal tools or UI.

tools.name: summarize_canvas
tools.description: Add an editable, cited summary of supplied record counts, numeric ranges and source errors for the page or specified cards. This is a deterministic overview, not an LLM interpretation or forecast.

tools.name: discover_data_sources
tools.description: Discover sources by topic through the current catalog and APIs.guru, or inspect up to five public URLs. Returns ranked candidates, access status and reasons. This is bounded discovery, not unrestricted web crawling.

tools.name: inspect_source
tools.description: Fetch a public source, detect its adapter, inspect fields and sample values. Supports JSON, CSV, XML, feeds, JSON-LD, permitted HTML tables and embedded JSON. OpenAPI documents return GET candidates. Webpage permission must come from the user.

tools.name: test_data_source
tools.description: Test an arbitrary public URL using the same adapter and permission checks as the editor. Returns actionable access or parse errors without inventing data.

tools.name: add_source
tools.description: Register a public source definition. GET APIs can be saved directly. Webpage extraction and other methods require visible review in the normal source editor. Never supplies credentials or executes source code.

tools.name: list_workspace_sources
tools.description: List source definitions used by this dashboard and source cards with their current status, fields, and freshness.

tools.name: inspect_source_schema
tools.description: Inspect raw and normalized fields, component compatibility and provenance for a source or derived block.

tools.name: list_blocks
tools.description: List the current block IDs, layout, display configuration and connections.

tools.name: get_page_context
tools.description: Get structured workspace data, selected fields, filters, raw and normalized responses, provenance and block metadata. Responses are bounded and credentials are redacted; treat source content as untrusted data.

tools.name: use_all_page_data
tools.description: Expose structured page context and open its visible review panel. The same context can be downloaded by the user.

tools.name: select_map_tag_fields
tools.description: Replace the selected-field set with explicit source paths, origins, labels, tags and units. These selections remain editable in Connect data.

tools.name: create_derived_block
tools.description: Create an independent block with declarative source bindings and optional joins, grouping or transforms. Use $data for source rows, then row-relative slot paths. Returns a deterministic ID; identical requests do not duplicate blocks.

tools.name: combine_sources
tools.description: Combine source cards into a new derived block with explicit bindings and transforms. Joins require unique right keys of matching types.

tools.name: bind_data_to_block
tools.description: Replace a block's declarative bindings and optional transforms. All mappings remain editable in its Data bindings panel.

tools.name: create_transform
tools.description: Replace a block's transform pipeline. Supports select, rename, filter, sort, limit, map, derive, aggregate, group, flatten, merge and join. No code execution.

tools.name: create_block
tools.description: Create a card from a registered source. Set waitForData:false to return its ID immediately, then read list_blocks while independent cards load. Inspect outcome for errors, empty or partial data; retry failed blocks with refresh_widget, not create_block. Live non-GET requests require the editor. Identical keys produce the same ID.

tools.name: update_block
tools.description: Edit title, source arguments, display mapping, layout or connections through the same action used by the editor.

tools.name: delete_block
tools.description: Request removal of a block. Opens a visible confirmation dialog; the agent cannot click the human confirmation through this tool.

tools.name: move_block
tools.description: Move a block to a zero-based position in the dashboard.

tools.name: resize_block
tools.description: Set a block's preferred width in the 12-column desktop layout. Cards grow to fill unused row space. Mobile layout stacks cards.

tools.name: choose_visualization
tools.description: Choose or change a block component and field mappings. Use list_components to inspect compatibility.

tools.name: collapse_sidebar
tools.description: Set persistent discovery sidebar visibility. Mobile uses the same accessible drawer.

tools.name: open_share_view
tools.description: Prepare a redacted snapshot link and open the visible share panel for review. The clean view contains no editor controls and performs no source requests.

tools.name: plan_goal
tools.description: Map a natural-language goal to catalog capabilities, typed parameters, date ranges and request dependencies. Returns an inspectable local plan and unresolved questions; does not fetch or modify cards.

tools.name: execute_goal
tools.description: Execute a reviewed local goal using the same generic request, suggestion and card tools. Handles the earthquake research and strongest-event weather workflow. Stops on unresolved questions and reports individual failures honestly.

expectedRevision.description: Optional stale-workspace guard from get_workspace.

tools.name: search_api_catalog
tools.description: Rank semantic capabilities against a user goal. Returns typed inputs, examples and recommended views. Browser compatibility is expected metadata; test_source establishes actual access.

tools.name: inspect_api_capability
tools.description: Read a source capability, request inputs, examples and response hints.

tools.name: run_api
tools.description: Execute a capability and store its normalized envelope in the active dashboard request history. Returns an envelope ID and summary, without creating a card or returning massive raw data.

mode.description: sample uses illustrative fixtures; live requests the public API.

expectedRevision.description: Optional stale-workspace guard from get_workspace.

tools.name: refresh_widget
tools.description: Replay the stored invocation of one existing widget. Keeps its title and visualization.

widgetId.description: An existing widget ID from get_workspace.

expectedRevision.description: Optional stale-workspace guard from get_workspace.

tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: Read active dashboard ID, saved dashboards, widget IDs, bindings, transforms, inputs, modes, status, semantic fields, and current revision. Returns a summary without raw API responses.

tools.name: manage_dashboard
tools.description: Create, switch, duplicate, rename, clear, delete, or undo a cleared locally saved dashboard. Read get_workspace to list dashboards. create_dashboard still appends widgets to the active dashboard. Clear and delete require confirm true after the user requests that action.

expectedRevision.description: Optional stale-workspace guard from get_workspace.

tools.name: list_components
tools.description: List the existing generic presentation definitions, accepted capabilities, slots, properties and layout choices. Supply a widget ID to see compatibility. Components accept fields from any API; use update_widget bindings and transforms to configure them.

widgetId.description: An existing widget ID from get_workspace.

sites.name: breidenbach0.github.io
sites.description: A browser agent workspace for circuit diagnosis and circuit building with CircuitJS1.

tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: Read the active circuit session, CircuitJS1 connection, circuit summary, measurements, saved versions, and visible work log. Use this first.

tools.name: start_session
tools.description: Start a circuit session using the user's goal. The same workspace supports building, inspection, simulation, and diagnosis. Optionally load a complete CircuitJS export supplied by the user. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

goal.description: What should be built, inspected, or diagnosed

circuitText.description: Optional complete CircuitJS legacy '$' or XML '<cir>' export

tools.name: inspect_circuit
tools.description: Read the current CircuitJS export and a plain list of live elements, including labels and available electrical values. Use this before reasoning about or editing the circuit. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: load_circuit
tools.description: Load a complete CircuitJS export into the visible simulator. The current circuit is saved as a restorable version by default. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

circuitText.description: Complete CircuitJS legacy '$' or XML '<cir>' export

summary.description: What was created or changed

tools.name: restore_circuit_version
tools.description: Restore a circuit version listed by get_workspace. The circuit being replaced is saved first, so this is reversible. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

versionId.description: Saved version id, for example v1

tools.name: measure_node
tools.description: Use the CircuitJS1 bridge to read the voltage of a labeled node in the active simulation. Record user-reported physical readings with record_evidence instead. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

node.description: Exact CircuitJS labeled-node name

reason.description: Why this reading matters

tools.name: set_simulation_running
tools.description: Start or pause the active CircuitJS1 simulation and record why. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: record_note
tools.description: Put a concrete finding, decision, question, or next step in the visible session feed. Use this to explain reasoning without creating a separate abstract state screen. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: finish_session
tools.description: Finish or pause the current session with a concrete result and a clear simulation-versus-hardware boundary. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: get_circuit_capabilities
tools.description: Read the native editor bridge version, every CircuitJS1 element type available in this build, menu command groups, option names, UI controls, scope properties, and browser-gesture limitations. Use this before an unfamiliar edit.

tools.name: get_circuit_editor_state
tools.description: Read the live native CircuitJS1 editor state: every element with position, properties and controls; global properties; options; view; scopes; run state; and undo/redo availability. Set includeCircuitText only when the raw CircuitJS export is needed.

tools.name: add_circuit_element
tools.description: Place any element type returned by get_circuit_capabilities directly on the CircuitJS1 grid. Returns the element index and its editable fields. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

type.description: CircuitJS class name or displayed element label

tools.name: edit_circuit_element
tools.description: Set any generic CircuitJS1 element Edit dialog field by fieldIndex. Read the element's editFields first; numeric values use SI units, choices accept an index or label, booleans accept true/false, and action fields accept 'press'. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

value.description: Number, boolean, string, choice index/label, or 'press'

tools.name: move_circuit_element
tools.description: Set both endpoints of an existing CircuitJS1 element; coordinates snap to the active grid. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: remove_circuit_elements
tools.description: Remove one or more live CircuitJS1 elements by index. The native CircuitJS1 undo stack can restore the edit. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: split_circuit_wire
tools.description: Split a WireElm or RoutedWireElm at a chosen circuit-grid point, exactly like the wire context-menu action but without depending on mouse position. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: select_circuit_elements
tools.description: Replace, add, remove, or toggle the current CircuitJS1 selection. This lets the next rotate, mirror, cut, copy, or duplicate command operate on exactly the intended elements. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: set_circuit_element_control
tools.description: Set a live element control returned in the element's controls array, such as switch-position, a built-in slider, or an adjustable property slider. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: execute_circuit_command
tools.description: Execute a real CircuitJS1 command from the File, Edit, Scopes, element, scope, Tools, zoom, or view command groups. Targeted commands accept an elementIndex and/or scopeIndex plus plotIndex. Browser file pickers, clipboard writes, downloads, printing, and fullscreen may require a user gesture; use load_circuit or inspect APIs for non-dialog alternatives. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: configure_circuit_adjustable
tools.description: Create, update, or remove the adjustable property sliders available from an element's Add Sliders dialog. For create, provide elementIndex, fieldIndex, min, and max. For update/remove, provide adjustableIndex from the element controls. An update can share another primary slider with sharedAdjustableIndex or detach with ownSlider. Step defaults to continuous (0); logarithmic ranges require a positive minimum. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: set_circuit_option
tools.description: Set any boolean CircuitJS1 display/editor option listed by get_circuit_capabilities, including current/voltage/power display, values, grid, toolbar, crosshair, resistor/gate style, background, current direction, editing lock, and mouse-wheel editing. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: set_circuit_ui_control
tools.description: Set simulationSpeed, currentSpeed, or powerBrightness to the same raw scrollbar value used by the CircuitJS1 UI. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: set_circuit_view
tools.description: Set CircuitJS1 canvas scale and translation directly. Scale must be between 0.2 and 2.5. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: set_circuit_scope_property
tools.description: Set any native scope property listed by get_circuit_capabilities, including label, speed, position, scale, plot position, divisions, trigger, persistence, AC coupling, traces, spectrum, transistor traces, and XY plots. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

value.description: Property value; booleans, numbers, and strings are accepted

tools.name: set_global_circuit_property
tools.description: Set any field from globalEditFields in get_circuit_editor_state, equivalent to CircuitJS1's Other Options dialog. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

value.description: Field value

tools.name: apply_circuit_actions
tools.description: Apply up to 100 native CircuitJS1 actions as one WebMCP operation. This is the fastest way to build or revise a circuit. Supported op values are add, move, split-wire, edit, global-edit, element-control, create-adjustable, update-adjustable, remove-adjustable, remove, select, command, option, ui-control, view, scope, reset-simulation, and run. Add and split-wire actions may assign a ref; later actions in the same batch may use elementRef, targetRef, or elementRefs. The complete batch is one native CircuitJS1 Undo step; if any action fails, its circuit, run state, and undo history are restored. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: undo_circuit_edit
tools.description: Execute CircuitJS1's native Undo command. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: redo_circuit_edit
tools.description: Execute CircuitJS1's native Redo command. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: reset_circuit_simulation
tools.description: Reset simulation time and transient state without replacing the circuit. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: record_investigation
tools.description: Record what is being inspected, traced, questioned, or checked next. The item appears in Investigation and the Work log. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: record_evidence
tools.description: Record a concrete observation from simulation, hardware, the user, documentation, or a calculation. Returns an evidence ID for hypotheses and repairs. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: propose_hypothesis
tools.description: Propose a provisional explanation linked to existing evidence IDs and keep plausible alternatives visible. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: update_hypothesis
tools.description: Refine, support, reject, or annotate an existing hypothesis as evidence changes. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: stage_repair
tools.description: Stage an evidence-linked repair without changing the circuit. Optionally include up to 100 native editor actions or one complete CircuitJS export for later approved simulation. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: request_repair_approval
tools.description: Ask the human to approve applying a staged repair in CircuitJS1. The repair cannot be applied through apply_staged_repair until approval is explicit. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: apply_staged_repair
tools.description: Apply a human-approved staged repair atomically in CircuitJS1. This rejects unapproved repairs and never treats simulation as proof of physical hardware. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

tools.name: record_repair_result
tools.description: Record whether an applied repair passed or failed in simulation, or still needs a physical hardware test. Include basedOnRevision from get_workspace when changing the workspace; stale actions are rejected.

sites.name: livesignal-chi.vercel.app
sites.description: Ask a question, let ChatGPT find the useful parts of YouTube videos, then edit and share the visual guide it creates.

tools.name: identify_agent
tools.description: Optional connection handshake. Identify the client and its capabilities so the shared workspace can show which agent is present. Call once when opening LiveSignal and again when reconnecting.

client.description: Human-readable client name, for example ChatGPT or Claude Code.

agentId.description: Optional client-local agent or session identifier.

capabilities.description: Optional capabilities this agent can perform in this workspace.

tools.name: get_workspace_state
tools.description: Returns the current visible research brief, sources, timestamped evidence, evidence draft, visual canvas, and publication status.

tools.name: start_canvas_collaboration
tools.description: Starts or resumes a live human-agent canvas session. Call once after creating the canvas, then repeatedly call wait_for_collaboration_event until the human finishes the session.

tools.name: wait_for_collaboration_event
tools.description: Waits for the next saved canvas-change batch, actionable human comment, or session-finished signal. Re-call after handling each event or timeout while the session remains active.

afterSequence.description: Last handled canvas-change sequence. Use 0 for a new session.

timeoutMs.description: Renewable wait duration, capped at 45000 ms.

tools.name: finish_canvas_collaboration
tools.description: Finishes the active canvas collaboration session when the human asks to close the case. Saved work remains on the page.

tools.name: get_human_revisions
tools.description: Returns saved human edits that the agent has not yet acknowledged, plus unsaved-change count and the current shared artifact.

tools.name: acknowledge_human_revisions
tools.description: Marks human edits as seen after the agent has incorporated or responded to them.

tools.name: wait_for_research_request
tools.description: Waits for the human to submit a new one-line goal from LiveSignal's consumer entry screen. Use after opening a blank LiveSignal page and telling the human you are ready for their request.

timeoutMs.description: Wait duration in milliseconds, capped at 45000.

tools.name: get_agent_comments
tools.description: Returns actionable comments the human attached to a canvas block or the whole artifact. Check for pending comments during active collaboration, then research and answer them with evidence-backed canvas updates.

tools.name: wait_for_agent_comment
tools.description: Waits briefly for the human's next canvas comment and returns it with block and evidence context as soon as it is sent. Use during an active co-creation session after telling the human you are listening.

timeoutMs.description: Wait duration in milliseconds, capped at 45000.

tools.name: claim_agent_comment
tools.description: Marks one human canvas comment as actively being researched and shows the agent's plan in the shared interface. Call before opening more videos or changing the canvas.

tools.name: answer_agent_comment
tools.description: Closes one human canvas comment after the agent has researched it and made any scoped canvas change. Summarize what was learned and identify new evidence or updated blocks so the human can inspect the result.

tools.name: begin_research
tools.description: Start here for a new user request. Creates a clean LiveSignal project, records the agent-prepared brief, and returns the autonomous video-research workflow.

tools.name: update_research_brief
tools.description: Updates the visible must-cover points, constraints, and desired output format before or during research.

tools.name: open_youtube_search
tools.description: Opens YouTube search for any topic so the agent and human can choose real candidate videos together.

tools.name: ingest_youtube_video
tools.description: Imports a public YouTube video's metadata and timestamped captions into the visible workspace.

tools.name: record_video_evidence
tools.description: Writes a video and evidence researched in another browser tab back into LiveSignal. Use this when ChatGPT reads captions or source moments directly, especially when server transcript import is unavailable. Supply a timestamp or seconds whenever possible. Text is matched against imported transcript rows near that time; unmatched or untimed entries remain visibly labelled agent claims.

tools.name: search_video_evidence
tools.description: Searches all imported timestamped evidence for a topic, claim, name, or phrase.

tools.name: pin_evidence
tools.description: Pins or unpins a timestamped source moment for the shared report.

tools.name: add_report_section
tools.description: Adds an editable, evidence-backed section to the visible report.

tools.name: update_report_section
tools.description: Revises one visible report section while keeping its timestamp citations explicit.

tools.name: remove_report_section
tools.description: Removes a report section at the user's editorial direction.

tools.name: reorder_report_sections
tools.description: Moves a report section up or down in the human-controlled editorial order.

tools.name: write_report
tools.description: Writes a complete editable report from researched evidence. Each section may cite evidence IDs recorded earlier in this workspace.

tools.name: revise_report
tools.description: Applies a requested revision to the report using replacement title, overview, or sections while preserving citations supplied by the agent.

tools.name: get_canvas_state
tools.description: Returns the current human-composed visual canvas, block order, theme, citations, and pending human revisions. Read this before reacting to a layout or copy change.

tools.name: create_canvas
tools.description: Creates or replaces the shareable visual canvas from evidence-backed blocks. Use once after research; do not overwrite later human composition unless explicitly asked.

tools.name: add_canvas_block
tools.description: Adds a new visual block without disturbing the human's existing canvas order.

tools.name: update_canvas_block
tools.description: Reacts to human composition by rewriting, restyling, resizing, or re-citing one canvas block while preserving every other block.

tools.name: generate_canvas_image
tools.description: Generates or replaces one AI visual layer for a selected canvas card after the human asks. Inline illustrations and full-card backdrops are stored independently; generating either must preserve the card text, citations, source thumbnails, layout, and the other visual layer. Generated artwork is visibly labeled and never treated as source evidence.

prompt.description: Art direction based on the human's comment, card meaning, and canvas mood. Do not ask for text inside the image.

alt.description: Concise accessible description of the intended image.

placement.description: Use background only when the human explicitly requests a full-card backdrop; otherwise use inline.

tools.name: remove_canvas_block
tools.description: Removes one canvas block when the human asks for a simpler composition.

tools.name: reorder_canvas_blocks
tools.description: Reorders one canvas block in response to human editorial direction without rewriting its content.

tools.name: set_canvas_theme
tools.description: Changes the visual canvas theme while preserving human block order, copy, and citations.

tools.name: download_canvas_png
tools.description: Downloads the current human-and-agent visual canvas as a shareable high-resolution PNG.

tools.name: open_video_timestamp
tools.description: Opens the exact source video moment for cited evidence.

tools.name: publish_report
tools.description: Marks the human-reviewed report as published after its evidence and wording are approved.

tools.name: download_report
tools.description: Downloads the current human-reviewed report as Markdown with clickable timestamp citations.

sites.name: pixael.vercel.app
sites.description: Sprites

tools.name: list_assets
tools.description: Lists all sprite assets in the project with their ID, name, category, dimensions (width, height), and animation state names.

tools.name: get_asset_details
tools.description: Returns full details for a sprite asset including dimensions, palette swatches, and all animation states with frame counts and FPS.

assetId.description: The unique ID of the asset to inspect

tools.name: get_current_selection
tools.description: Returns the active asset, active animation state, and active frame index/ID currently selected in the live editor UI.

tools.name: get_frame_pixels
tools.description: Returns compact run-length encoded (RLE) pixel data and palette for a frame. Index 0 is transparent; pairs are [colorIndex, runLength].

assetId.description: The asset ID (optional if targeting currently active asset)

stateId.description: The animation state ID (optional if targeting active state)

tools.name: get_animation_state
tools.description: Returns fps, loop setting, frame count, and ordered frame IDs for an animation state.

tools.name: create_asset
tools.description: Creates a new sprite asset in the project with custom dimensions, name, category, and initial animation states.

tools.name: duplicate_asset
tools.description: Duplicates an existing sprite asset along with all its animation states, frames, and palette.

assetId.description: ID of the asset to duplicate

newName.description: Optional new name for the clone

tools.name: delete_asset
tools.description: Deletes a sprite asset from the project. Cannot delete the last remaining asset.

assetId.description: ID of the asset to delete

tools.name: resize_sprite
tools.description: Resizes sprite canvas dimensions (e.g. from 16x16 to 32x32) while preserving pixel art content according to the specified anchor.

anchor.description: Placement anchor: "center" expands symmetrically; "top-left" anchors at (0,0)

tools.name: create_animation_state
tools.description: Adds a new animation state (e.g. "Walk", "Attack", "Jump") with blank frames to a sprite asset.

frameCount.description: Number of initial frames to create (default 1)

tools.name: rename_animation_state
tools.description: Renames an existing animation state in a sprite asset.

name.description: The new name for the state

tools.name: delete_animation_state
tools.description: Deletes an animation state from an asset. Cannot delete the last state of an asset.

tools.name: duplicate_animation_state
tools.description: Duplicates an animation state along with all its frames.

tools.name: reorder_animation_states
tools.description: Reorders animation states within an asset by shifting a state from one index to another.

fromIndex.description: The original 0-based index of the animation state to move

stateId.description: Optional ID of the state to move (if fromIndex is not supplied)

toIndex.description: The target 0-based index to place the animation state at

tools.name: set_animation_speed
tools.description: Sets the playback speed (FPS) for an animation state.

tools.name: set_animation_loop
tools.description: Enables or disables continuous looping for an animation state.

loop.description: True to loop continuously, false to play once

tools.name: play_animation
tools.description: Starts live animation preview in the application viewport.

assetId.description: Optional asset ID to select for preview

stateId.description: Optional state ID to select for preview

tools.name: pause_animation
tools.description: Pauses live animation preview in the application viewport.

tools.name: add_frame
tools.description: Adds a new blank frame or a copy of the previous frame to an animation state.

insertAtIndex.description: Optional 0-based index to insert the new frame at (defaults to end)

copyPrevious.description: If true, duplicates pixel content from the previous frame; if false, creates a blank frame

tools.name: duplicate_frame
tools.description: Duplicates an existing frame in an animation state.

frameId.description: ID of the frame to duplicate

frameIndex.description: 0-based frame index to duplicate (alternative to frameId)

tools.name: delete_frame
tools.description: Deletes a frame from an animation state. If deleting the last frame, it is automatically replaced with a blank frame.

frameId.description: ID of the frame to delete

frameIndex.description: 0-based frame index to delete (alternative to frameId)

tools.name: reorder_frames
tools.description: Reorders frames in an animation state by specifying an ordered array of frame IDs or fromIndex/toIndex.

orderedFrameIds.description: Array of all frame IDs in the desired order

fromIndex.description: Source 0-based index if shifting single frame

toIndex.description: Target 0-based index if shifting single frame

tools.name: set_frame_pixels
tools.description: Replaces the entire pixel buffer of a frame using a compact Run-Length Encoded (RLE) payload (matching get_frame_pixels output format).

tools.name: set_pixels
tools.description: Sets specific pixel coordinates in a frame. Coordinates are 0-indexed with (0,0) at top-left. Pass colorIndex into palette (0 = transparent) or explicit hexColor.

tools.name: flood_fill
tools.description: Fills a contiguous area of identical color starting at (x, y) with a color from the palette or hex string.

x.description: X coordinate to begin fill (0 to width-1)

y.description: Y coordinate to begin fill (0 to height-1)

tools.name: draw_line
tools.description: Draws a 1-pixel Bresenham line between (x0, y0) and (x1, y1) in a frame.

tools.name: draw_rectangle
tools.description: Draws a rectangle at (x, y) with specified width and height. Can be solid filled or 1-pixel outline.

filled.description: True for solid rectangle, false for 1px outline (default false)

tools.name: flip_frame
tools.description: Flips all pixels in a frame horizontally (left-to-right) or vertically (top-to-bottom).

tools.name: rotate_frame
tools.description: Rotates all pixels in a frame clockwise by 90, 180, or 270 degrees.

tools.name: shift_frame
tools.description: Shifts all pixels in a frame by dx (horizontal) and dy (vertical) pixels with wrap-around.

dx.description: Horizontal pixel offset (positive = right, negative = left)

dy.description: Vertical pixel offset (positive = down, negative = up)

tools.name: clear_frame
tools.description: Clears all pixels in a frame to transparent.

tools.name: set_palette_preset
tools.description: Replaces an asset palette with one of the studio presets: "Pixel Hero", "Fantasy RPG", "Cyberpunk Neon", "Retro Monochrome 4-Bit", "Dungeon 16", "Studio Gray Scale".

presetName.description: Name of the studio preset palette to apply

tools.name: add_palette_color
tools.description: Adds a new hex color code to the asset palette.

tools.name: remove_palette_color
tools.description: Removes a color from an asset palette by colorIndex or hex string.

colorIndex.description: 1-based or 0-based index in the palette to remove

hexColor.description: Optional hex color string to remove (alternative to colorIndex)

tools.name: set_palette_color
tools.description: Replaces a specific palette color swatch at a given index with a new hex color.

colorIndex.description: 0-based index in the palette to replace

tools.name: export_frame_png
tools.description: Renders and triggers download of a single frame as a PNG image at a specified pixel scale (1x, 2x, 4x, 8x, 16x).

tools.name: export_sprite_sheet
tools.description: Generates and downloads a packed PNG sprite sheet for an animation state or entire asset with metadata.

stateId.description: The animation state ID (optional: if omitted, exports all states)

columns.description: Number of columns when layout is "grid"

sites.name: resilience-forge.gman72.chatgpt.site
sites.description: Choose a reference architecture, stress the live bench, and watch human decisions and WebMCP remediation meet in one state.

tools.name: get_webmcp_status
tools.description: Read WebMCP capability, toolsReady, session id, and registered tool names. Call this before other tools if discovery looks incomplete.

tools.name: get_catalogue_guide
tools.description: Read how to pick a catalogue simulation and load it onto the live bench.

tools.name: list_architectures
tools.description: List the three equal GCP reference simulations available to load onto the bench.

tools.name: load_architecture
tools.description: Load a catalogue simulation onto the live bench. Accepts architecture id (event_driven_checkout, multi_region_saas, llm_inference_serving) or a short name such as checkout, saas, or llm. Navigates to /bench/:id.

id.description: Architecture id or short name: checkout, saas, llm, or the full id.

tools.name: get_bench_guide
tools.description: Read the signature human-agent loop, valid remediation paths, pin semantics, and error codes for this bench.

tools.name: get_architecture
tools.description: Read the current semantic topology, health, failures, exclusions, and store version.

tools.name: get_scenario
tools.description: Read current human scenario controls, targets, pins, and store version.

tools.name: get_live_metrics
tools.description: Read demand, served throughput, capacity, utilisation, traffic share, measurement semantics, traffic-weighted fault contributions, and latency-routing scores with intended versus effective split.

tools.name: get_root_cause_analysis
tools.description: Explain the current failure using live topology, fault, capacity, SLO, and Flight Data Recorder evidence. Pass unavailableTargets and prohibitedActions when a recovery path is blocked. Returns recommendedActions plus a ready-to-preview remediationPlan when a compound surviving-path recovery is legal.

unavailableTargets.description: Regions, nodes, or edges that cannot be restored or cleared, such as europe-west2.

prohibitedActions.description: Tool names that must not be recommended, such as clear_fault_profile.

tools.name: get_constraints
tools.description: Read applicable provider-limit and model-assumption records with source dates and provenance.

tools.name: get_bench_snapshot
tools.description: Atomically read scenario, topology, metrics, constraints, RCA, version, tick, and timestamp from one simulation tick.

tools.name: get_decision_log
tools.description: Read the Flight Data Recorder: recent ui, webmcp, and sim operator events with versions and result codes. Use after STALE_STATE to see why the store version moved. Does not increment storeVersion.

tools.name: preview_change
tools.description: Read-only projection of a mutation. Does not increment storeVersion. projectionSucceeded is true when the nested op would apply; it is never an applied write.

tools.name: apply_remediation_plan
tools.description: Apply several legal mutations as one all-or-nothing transaction with a single expectedVersion and one version bump.

tools.name: set_peak_rps
tools.description: Set peak load demand in requests per second for the current scenario.

tools.name: set_budget
tools.description: Set the monthly budget constraint in GBP for the current scenario.

tools.name: run_stress_test
tools.description: Start the deterministic stress or failure path for the loaded reference.

tools.name: stop_stress_test
tools.description: Stop the running stress test and leave measured failure state. Use reset_scenario to return the visible bench to baseline.

tools.name: reset_scenario
tools.description: Reset the loaded reference to its operational baseline: tick 0, stress off, no faults or outages, default load and traffic split. Human pins are kept. Updates the visible topology and gauges.

tools.name: fail_component
tools.description: Fail a runtime component as a hard outage. Distinct from set_fault_profile dropout, which is packet loss.

tools.name: restore_component
tools.description: Restore a runtime component that was killed or failed.

tools.name: fail_zone
tools.description: Fail one configured availability zone while leaving the topology and surviving replicas visible.

tools.name: restore_zone
tools.description: Restore one failed availability zone and its placed replicas.

tools.name: set_fault_profile
tools.description: Inject deterministic latency (ms) and packet loss (%) at any declared component or connection. packetLossPercent is the unit-explicit name; dropoutPercent is accepted as an alias.

packetLossPercent.description: Packet loss as a percent of requests (0-100).

tools.name: set_region_fault_profile
tools.description: Apply the same latency (ms) and packet loss (%) to a regional boundary. Accepts europe-west2 / West2 / us-east4 / east4. On multi-region SaaS this is the ALB ingress edge, not a guessed node id.

region.description: Region id or alias such as europe-west2, West2, us-east4, east4.

packetLossPercent.description: Packet loss as a percent of requests (0-100).

tools.name: ramp_fault_until
tools.description: Ramp latencyMs or packetLossPercent from start toward ceiling in steps. Records every intermediate result and stops when the stop condition matches. One version bump. Does not require the agent to issue N stale-checked mutations.

region.description: Optional region alias. When set, ramps set_region_fault_profile instead of a single target.

tools.name: clear_fault_profile
tools.description: Clear injected latency and packet loss from one component or connection.

tools.name: clear_all_faults
tools.description: Clear every injected latency and packet-loss profile while preserving load, scaling, traffic split, pins, and zone state.

tools.name: set_autoscaling
tools.description: Set autoscaling bounds. Replicas follow demand toward the target utilisation within min/max. When a zone is failed, replacement replicas are placed in surviving zones of the same region.

tools.name: set_ordering_key_parallelism
tools.description: Set the number of Pub/Sub ordering keys used to spread ordered work while retaining per-key ordering. orderingKeyShards below 1 or unordered=true requests unordered replacement, which keep_pubsub_ordering rejects.

tools.name: set_batching
tools.description: Configure batching and wait time for Pub/Sub or Vertex AI within the declared model limits.

tools.name: add_read_replica
tools.description: Add a same-region Cloud SQL read replica for the zonal failure path. Legal even when no_second_region is pinned.

tools.name: fail_region
tools.description: Fail one configured region while keeping its reference topology visible.

tools.name: restore_region
tools.description: Restore one failed region and its placed services.

tools.name: set_region_traffic_split
tools.description: Set the primary-region traffic allocation.

tools.name: set_latency_based_routing
tools.description: Enable or disable latency-based routing. Traffic shifts toward the faster healthy region or sheds a slow release candidate.

tools.name: set_model_traffic_split
tools.description: Set the release-candidate share of model traffic. The healthy default is a 20% canary.

sites.name: shiv-aurora.github.io
sites.description: Potter's Wheel

tools.name: get_current_selection
tools.description: Return the researcher's live manuscript selection, section, object kind, and verification state without changing the document.

tools.name: get_manuscript_context
tools.description: Return live manuscript text and integrity context for the current selection, current section, or manuscript.

scope.description: Context scope. Defaults to the current section.

maxChars.description: Maximum manuscript characters to return. Defaults to 4000.

tools.name: get_claim
tools.description: Return the currently selected claim, or a tracked claim by id, including its verification state and linked evidence.

claimId.description: Optional tracked claim id. Omit it to use the current manuscript selection.

tools.name: get_figure
tools.description: Return the currently selected figure, or a tracked figure by id, including its verification state and linked evidence.

figureId.description: Optional tracked figure id. Omit it to use the current manuscript selection.

tools.name: get_table
tools.description: Return the currently selected table, or a tracked table by id, including its verification state and linked evidence.

tableId.description: Optional tracked table id. Omit it to use the current manuscript selection.

tools.name: get_current_section
tools.description: Return the named manuscript section containing the researcher's current selection together with that section's live text.

tools.name: get_provenance
tools.description: Return provenance and linked evidence for the currently selected tracked manuscript object, or for an explicit object id.

objectId.description: Optional tracked manuscript object id. Omit it to use the current manuscript selection.

tools.name: get_integrity_status
tools.description: Return live manuscript integrity counts and optional summaries of tracked provenance objects without changing researcher state.

includeObjects.description: Include tracked object summaries. Defaults to true.

limit.description: Maximum tracked object summaries to return. Defaults to 50.

tools.name: get_navigation_targets
tools.description: List tracked manuscript objects that an agent may ask the researcher to inspect or navigate to, optionally filtered by object kind or verification state.

kind.description: Optional manuscript object kind filter.

limit.description: Maximum navigation targets to return. Defaults to 50.

tools.name: create_claim
tools.description: Create a first-class provenance claim from the researcher's current explicit text selection. Requires the exact text previously read by the agent so stale selections fail safely.

expectedText.description: Exact selected manuscript text observed before this call.

tools.name: attach_evidence
tools.description: Attach structured evidence to the selected or explicitly identified tracked manuscript object. This visibly updates the same provenance state shown in the integrity panel.

objectId.description: Optional tracked manuscript object id. Omit it to use the currently selected tracked object.

tools.name: update_evidence
tools.description: Update structured evidence already linked to a tracked manuscript object. The evidence must belong to that object; unrelated evidence cannot be edited through this call.

objectId.description: Optional tracked object id. Omit it to use the selected tracked object.

tools.name: verify_claim
tools.description: Run the editor's deterministic Verify This comparison for a selected or identified tracked claim. It compares only unambiguous manuscript and evidence metric values and returns an honest review-required outcome otherwise.

claimId.description: Optional tracked claim id. Omit it to use the selected tracked claim.

tools.name: record_verification_result
tools.description: Record an evidence-backed conclusion from an external research agent on a tracked claim. This stores the visible result and reasons but never changes manuscript text; use propose_claim_change separately for a researcher-reviewed correction.

claimId.description: Optional tracked claim id. Omit it to use the selected tracked claim.

tools.name: set_verification_state
tools.description: Set the verification state of a tracked manuscript object. Verified, stale, contradicted, and needs-review states require linked evidence; unlinked is only valid when no evidence is attached.

objectId.description: Optional tracked object id. Omit it to use the selected tracked object.

tools.name: propose_claim_change
tools.description: Stage a replacement for a tracked claim as CriticMarkup. This never silently accepts the new manuscript text: the researcher receives the editor's normal accept/reject controls.

claimId.description: Optional tracked claim id. Omit it to use the selected tracked claim.

tools.name: insert_comment
tools.description: Insert an additive visible comment on the current selection line or a tracked object's line. Existing comment threads are never overwritten; the tool fails if that line already has a comment.

objectId.description: Optional tracked object whose anchor line should receive the comment.

line.description: Optional explicit one-based manuscript line number.

tools.name: replace_selected_content
tools.description: Stage a replacement for the researcher's current explicit selection. Despite the action name, the new text is not silently accepted: it is inserted as CriticMarkup and remains pending until the researcher accepts or rejects it.

expectedText.description: Exact selected text observed before this call.

tools.name: navigate_to_object
tools.description: Move the visible editor selection to a tracked claim, method, figure, or table. This changes navigation state only; it does not modify manuscript or provenance content.

tools.name: get_research_diffs
tools.description: Return evidence-driven Research Diff entries from live provenance alongside currently pending CriticMarkup manuscript proposals.

tools.name: stage_research_diff
tools.description: Stage the proposed manuscript text for one evidence-driven Research Diff as CriticMarkup. The update remains unapplied until the researcher uses the visible accept/reject controls.

tools.name: review_research_diff
tools.description: Record a defer or reject decision for an evidence-driven Research Diff without changing manuscript text. Agents cannot accept manuscript rewrites.

tools.name: navigate_to_research_diff
tools.description: Move the visible editor selection to an evidence-driven Research Diff or pending CriticMarkup proposal so the researcher can inspect it without changing manuscript content.

from.description: A pending CriticMarkup diff's `from` value.

tools.name: get_experiments
tools.description: Return the same persisted experiment runs visible in Potter’s Wheel, optionally filtered by run status.

tools.name: get_experiment
tools.description: Return one run with its parameters, metrics, artifacts, produced evidence, and dependent manuscript objects.

tools.name: compare_experiments
tools.description: Compare the configuration, metrics, datasets, artifacts, and provenance impact of two experiment runs.

tools.name: get_evidence_catalog
tools.description: Return evidence between experiments and the paper, including its originating run and manuscript usage.

tools.name: create_experiment
tools.description: Create a run in the same Experiments workspace the researcher uses.

id.description: Optional stable run id

method.description: Model or research method

notes.description: Research notes

tools.name: update_experiment
tools.description: Update run metadata such as its name, method, notes, timestamps, datasets, or source commit.

method.description: Model or method

notes.description: Research notes

tools.name: add_experiment_metric
tools.description: Add or update a named metric on a research run.

key.description: Metric name

tools.name: add_experiment_parameter
tools.description: Add or update a named configuration value on a research run.

key.description: Parameter name

tools.name: log_experiment_metric_point
tools.description: Append a numeric metric point at a training step and update the run's latest value, like an MLflow metric history.

key.description: Metric name

tools.name: attach_experiment_artifact
tools.description: Attach a result, figure, table, configuration, or other artifact to a research run.

label.description: Artifact label

type.description: Artifact type

id.description: Optional artifact id

tools.name: set_experiment_status
tools.description: Mark a run planned, running, completed, or failed in the shared experiment workspace.

tools.name: supersede_experiment
tools.description: Identify a newer run as replacing an earlier run and mark dependent manuscript objects stale for review.

tools.name: create_experiment_evidence
tools.description: Turn a run metric, configuration, result, figure, or table artifact into durable evidence for the paper. A superseded evidence id rewires its manuscript links and creates Research Diffs.

label.description: Evidence label

evidenceKind.description: Quantitative result, comparison, methodology, ablation, figure, or table result

metric.description: Machine-readable metric, for example accuracy=17.3%

notes.description: Research notes

supersedesEvidenceId.description: Optional older evidence id to replace

tools.name: link_evidence_to_manuscript
tools.description: Connect existing experiment evidence to an existing claim, figure, table, or method in the same visible workspace.

objectId.description: Tracked manuscript object id

tools.name: search_stock

query.description: Search text for symbol or company name

tools.name: get_stock_details
tools.description: Retrieve a full stock quote, company profile, and metadata for a given ticker symbol.

symbol.description: Ticker symbol like AAPL or MSFT

tools.name: open_company_analysis
tools.description: Open the full single-company analysis page (financials, valuation, analyst trends, earnings surprises, news) for a ticker and return a short summary.

tools.name: get_stock_news
tools.description: Fetch the latest news articles for a specific stock symbol.

days.description: Number of past days to fetch news for (default 7)

tools.name: analyze_sec_filings
tools.description: Fetch recent SEC filings for a symbol, pick the most material filing (largest report or latest), fetch the XML/HTML report, and return the normalized content for LLM analysis.

days.description: Lookback window in days (default 30)

limit.description: Number of recent filings to consider (default 10)

highlight.description: Key phrases or full sentences FROM the filing to highlight in yellow for the user — e.g. the specific risk statements, revenue drivers, guidance, or figures relevant to their question. Copy the exact text so it can be matched. If omitted, the report opens with no highlights.

tools.name: get_market_news_summary
tools.description: Fetch a digest of the latest general market news across all categories.

category.description: News category: general | forex | crypto | merger

tools.name: rank_stocks
tools.description: Rank the curated stock universe by a supported metric (performance, volume, price). Navigates to the Markets page and highlights the sorted directory.

metric.description: Metric: performance | volume | price

limit.description: How many stocks to return (default 10)

tools.name: screen_stocks

sector.description: Sector filter e.g. Technology, Healthcare, Energy

limit.description: Max results to return (default 10)

tools.name: get_sector_performance
tools.description: Return a breakdown of average performance by market sector from the tracked universe. Navigates to the Markets page and scrolls to the Sector Performance section.

tools.name: get_top_performers
tools.description: Return the top N best-performing stocks from the universe over the session.

direction.description: gainers | losers (default: gainers)

tools.name: compare_stocks
tools.description: Compare multiple stocks side by side — price, change, and relative performance summary.

tools.name: detect_chart_pattern
tools.description: Detect technical chart patterns on a stock. Supported patterns: head_and_shoulders, inverse_head_and_shoulders, abcd, xabcd, cypher, triangle_ascending, triangle_descending, triangle_symmetrical, three_drives, double_top, double_bottom.

pattern.description: Pattern to detect (e.g. head_and_shoulders, xabcd, cypher)

tools.name: get_chart_data_range
tools.description: Return the exact OHLCV data boundaries for a stock symbol so you can place drawing points accurately on the compare chart. ALWAYS call this before draw_on_compare_chart. It tells you: - firstDate / lastDate → the hard date bounds of the dataset (all dates outside these don't exist) - priceMin / priceMax → the price range over the visible window - latestCandle → the most recent bar (use this as your "now" anchor) - recentCandles → the last 20 bars with exact date + OHLC (use these prices for anchor points) - visibleWindowStart → the start of the default 1Y visible window Never invent dates or prices. Always use exact dates and OHLCV values from this response.

windowDays.description: How many calendar days back to sample (default 365 = 1Y visible window)

tools.name: draw_on_compare_chart
tools.description: Draw technical pattern annotations (trendlines, ABCD, head & shoulders, triangles, rectangles, text labels, horizontal lines, etc.) directly onto the comparison chart canvas. IMPORTANT — call get_chart_data_range first to get exact valid dates and prices for the symbol. Never invent dates or prices; use only values from that response. Supported tool values: trendline, horizontal, ray, channel, rectangle, abcd, xabcd, cypher, headshoulders, triangle, threedrives, measure, text. Points use { date: "YYYY-MM-DD", price: }. Dates are snapped to the nearest real trading day. Prices are clamped to that bar's high/low range. The chart scrolls to show all annotated bars.

symbol.description: Ticker to display in the chart (e.g. AAPL)

drawings.description: One or more drawing objects to render on the chart

tool.description: Drawing type: trendline | horizontal | ray | channel | rectangle | abcd | xabcd | cypher | headshoulders | triangle | threedrives | measure | text

text.description: Label text (only for tool === 'text').

points.description: Anchor points. Get exact dates and prices from get_chart_data_range first. Required point counts: trendline/ray/rectangle/measure=2, horizontal=1, channel=3, abcd/triangle=4, xabcd/cypher/headshoulders/threedrives=5, text=1.

price.description: Dollar price — must be within the high/low of that date's candle

clearExisting.description: Remove existing canvas drawings first (default true).

tools.name: get_trend_direction
tools.description: Determine the current trend direction for a stock: Uptrend, Downtrend, or Sideways consolidation.

path.description: The page path to navigate to, e.g. /portfolio or /stock/AAPL

tools.name: open_compare

tools.name: compare_chart_canvas
tools.description: All-in-one comparison chart and technical canvas controller. Configures chart style ('candles', 'bars', 'line', 'area', 'compare', 'split'), active stock symbols, focused stock, timeframe range ('1M', '3M', '6M', '1Y', '5Y'), indicators (SMA, EMA, Bollinger Bands, Volume, RSI, MACD), and canvas drawings (lines, rectangles, text, measure, chart patterns). symbols.description: List of company symbols to benchmark (e.g. ['AAPL', 'MSFT', 'TSLA']).

indicators.description: Technical indicators to enable/disable (applies to focused single-stock style).

price.description: Price coordinate in USD

points.description: Array of coordinate points { time, price } for this drawing.

text.description: Text label or annotation callout

drawings.description: Array of drawing annotations to plot onto the chart overlay canvas.

clearDrawings.description: If true, clears existing drawings before applying new ones.

runAiAnalysis.description: If true, runs complete AI multi-company comparative analysis (growth matrix, news catalysts, recommendation trends, reported financials, and pattern detection).

autoDrawPatterns.description: If true, automatically detects technical patterns on the focused stock and plots them on the canvas.

tools.name: get_input_status
tools.description: Which instrument the student is playing on: computer keyboard or a connected MIDI keyboard / digital piano, with playable range and polyphony. Adapt exercises to it: keep computer-keyboard drills within the range and to triads; a MIDI piano can do two hands and wide arpeggios.

tools.name: get_practice_log
tools.description: Past practice sessions and recent attempts with scores, newest first. Use it to pick up where the student left off and to notice trends.

limit.description: Sessions to return, default 10.

tools.name: get_attempt_results
tools.description: Full results of an attempt: notes hit and missed, timing offsets in milliseconds with early/late tendency, and per-prompt answers for find_note and ear_training. Defaults to the latest attempt. Call it after the student says they have finished an exercise.

tools.name: show_on_keyboard
tools.description: Light up keys on the on-screen piano with a caption, and optionally sound them. Give notes, a chord symbol, or a scale. Good for "this is C major", "here is a G7 chord", or pointing out a single key.

notes.description: Note names like ["C4","E4","G4"].

caption.description: Short label shown above the keyboard.

play.description: Also sound the notes (chords together, scales in sequence).

tools.name: clear_keyboard
tools.description: Remove highlights and captions from the on-screen piano and stop any reference playback.

tools.name: play_reference
tools.description: Play something for the student to hear, lighting up keys as it plays: a scale, a chord progression, a melody or a rhythm. Same parameters as start_exercise. Returns right away; playback runs for `duration_seconds`.

kind.description: scale, chords, melody and rhythm are timed with a metronome. find_note and ear_training are prompt-by-prompt.

name.description: Short title shown to the student.

root.description: scale: root like "C4" or "F#3". ear_training: reference note (default C4).

mode.description: scale: major, minor, harmonic_minor, melodic_minor, major_pentatonic, minor_pentatonic, blues, dorian, mixolydian, lydian, phrygian, chromatic.

direction.description: scale: default up_down.

note_value.description: scale: beats per note, default quarter.

progression.description: chords: chord symbols (C, Am, G7, Fmaj7, C/E) or roman numerals (I, ii, V7, vii°). Numerals need `key`.

key.description: chords: key for roman numerals, e.g. "G" or "A minor".

notes.description: melody: note names in order. rhythm: the single note to tap (default C4). find_note: exact notes to ask for.

rhythm.description: melody / rhythm: beats per note, e.g. [1, 1, 0.5, 0.5, 2].

melody.description: melody: built-in tune id: ode_to_joy, twinkle, mary.

count.description: find_note / ear_training: number of prompts, default 5.

show_hints.description: find_note: light up the answer key.

intervals.description: ear_training: intervals to draw from: m2 M2 m3 M3 P4 TT P5 m6 M6 m7 M7 P8.

low.description: find_note: lowest note to ask for (default C4).

high.description: find_note: highest note to ask for (default B4).

include_black_keys.description: find_note: also ask for sharps and flats. Default false (white keys only).

section.description: song: section id from get_song, or "all" for the whole piece. Default: first section.

hands.description: song: default right. "both" only where get_song shows a left-hand part.

tempo_percent.description: song: percent of the song tempo. Start learners at 60–70.

path_step.description: Learning-path step id from get_learning_paths. Pass path exercises unchanged so progress is tracked.

tools.name: set_metronome
tools.description: Set the practice tempo and switch the free-running metronome on or off. Exercises use their own bpm and count in one bar automatically.

tools.name: update_settings
tools.description: Toggle the app's sound, the key-letter labels on the on-screen piano, or shift which octave the computer keyboard plays (-2 to 2; 0 means A = C4).

tools.name: start_exercise
tools.description: Start an exercise on screen for the student to play on their computer keyboard or MIDI keyboard. Timed kinds (scale, chords, melody, rhythm) count in one bar with clicks, light up each target key in time, and end on their own. Untimed kinds (find_note, ear_training) go prompt by prompt. Returns immediately. When the student says they are done, call get_attempt_results. Keep beginners at 50–70 bpm and within the playable range from get_input_status. For a song from the library use kind "song" with song_id, a section id (or "all"), hands and tempo_percent.

title.description: e.g. "This week: C major and first chords"

detail.description: Why, or what to focus on.

tools.name: complete_plan_item
tools.description: Mark a practice-plan item done (or not done) by its id or exact title.

tools.name: log_practice_session
tools.description: Save a practice session to the student's log with a short summary and optional tutor notes. Attaches recent attempts (default: everything since the last logged session). Shows a confirmation card first.

summary.description: One or two sentences: what was practiced and how it went.

notes.description: What to work on next time.

attempt_ids.description: Specific attempts to attach. Omit to attach everything since the last session.

tools.name: say
tools.description: Speak one or two short sentences out loud through the page, in the browser voice. Use it for coaching while the student has both hands on the keys and eyes on the keyboard, e.g. "Good. Now a little slower." Keep it under 25 words; the student can also read your chat.

tools.name: wait_for_result
tools.description: Waits until the running exercise finishes, then returns its full results with coaching, so you never need to poll or ask the student to say "done". Call it right after start_exercise. The cap defaults to the time the drill still needs (max 45 s); if they are still playing when it runs out, it returns their progress and you call it again. With nothing running it returns the latest result.

tools.name: wait_for_notes
tools.description: Listens for the next thing the student plays outside a drill (a note, a chord, or a short burst) and returns it named, e.g. "C major" or "a perfect 5th". Use it for "play me a C chord" checks and "what is this?" moments. Returns after timeout_seconds (default 15, max 45) with nothing if they did not play.

tools.name: get_recent_notes
tools.description: What the student has been playing freely, outside a drill: the notes held right now and what chord or interval they make, the last notes with timing, and the phrase since the last pause. Use it for "what chord is this?", "was that right?", or to react to improvising. Timing is in milliseconds.

seconds.description: How far back to look, default 20, max 90.

tools.name: save_recording_as_song
tools.description: Turn what the student just played freely into a song in their library. Takes the phrase since the last pause (or the last N seconds), snaps it to a beat grid, writes it in Tonic notation and shows a confirmation card. Returns the notation so you can read it back or fix it with add_song. Give bpm if you know the tempo they meant; otherwise it is estimated.

bpm.description: Tempo the student was playing at. Estimated if omitted.

grid.description: Smallest note to snap to, default eighth.

seconds.description: Use the last N seconds instead of the phrase since the last pause.

tools.name: add_song
tools.description: Add a song to the student's library so it gets Listen, Practice, sections and progress like any other song. Write the melody in Tonic notation: note names with octave (C4, F#4, Bb3) and beats after a colon (E4:0.5, G4:2; default 1), "-" for a rest ("-:2"), [C3 E3 G3] for a chord, "|" bar lines optional. Every section must be whole bars; an optional left hand (lh) must be the same length as the right hand (rh). Keep right-hand notes within C4–F5 so they fit the computer keyboard. The page validates and shows a confirmation card before saving. Prefer public-domain tunes or the student's own material. Example: {"title":"Ode to Joy","key":"C major","bpm":80,"sections":[{"name":"Theme","rh":"E4 E4 F4 G4 | G4 F4 E4 D4 | C4 C4 D4 E4 | E4:1.5 D4:0.5 D4:2"}]}

origin.description: Composer or tradition and year, e.g. "Traditional Irish".

key.description: e.g. "F major" or "A minor". Flat keys spell notes with flats.

beats_per_bar.description: Default 4. Use 3 for waltzes; count 6/8 in eighths with 6.

id.description: Short id like "a", "verse". Default a, b, c…

lh.description: Optional left hand, same length as rh.

form.description: Section order for the whole song, e.g. ["a","b","a"]. Default: sections in order.

tools.name: remove_song
tools.description: Remove a song the agent or the student added earlier. Built-in songs cannot be removed. Shows a confirmation card first.

tools.name: show_screen
tools.description: Move the page to a screen: home (the learning paths), a learning path by id, songs (optionally with a song expanded), or practice (plan and log). Closes a finished result if it is showing. Use this instead of clicking links or menus.

tools.name: close_result
tools.description: Close the result or "listen" card that is showing and return to the page underneath. Same as the student pressing Done.

tools.name: get_practice_plan
tools.description: The practice plan shown on the Practice screen: each item with its id, whether it is done, and its exercise spec, which you can pass to start_exercise unchanged.

tools.name: replay_prompt
tools.description: In an ear-training drill, play the prompt again for the student. Same as the "Play it again" button.

tools.name: play_back_attempt
tools.description: Play back what the student played in an attempt, at the timing they played it, keys lighting up. Same as the "Hear yours" button. Defaults to the latest attempt.

tools.name: connect_midi
tools.description: Try to connect a MIDI keyboard or digital piano. Browsers only grant MIDI access from a real click, so this may fail; if it does, ask the student to press "Connect a MIDI keyboard" under the piano.

tools.name: export_progress
tools.description: Everything stored in this browser (attempts, plan, log, settings, added songs) as JSON, the same as the Export button. Use it to move progress to another browser with import_progress.

tools.name: import_progress
tools.description: Replace what is stored in this browser with a JSON export from export_progress or the Export button. Shows a confirmation card first.

tools.name: reset_progress
tools.description: Erase the plan, log, attempts, added songs and settings from this browser. Same as the Reset link. Shows a confirmation card first.

tools.name: load_sample_progress
tools.description: Fill the app with a sample plan and practice log, for trying things out. Same as the "Load sample" link. Shows a confirmation card first.

tools.name: get_learning_paths
tools.description: The five learning paths the app is organised around (find your way around the keys, learn chords, scales and rhythm, train your ear, play a song) with their steps, which are done, and the next step's ready-to-use exercise. To start a step, pass its exercise to start_exercise unchanged; it carries path_step so the app ticks it off. For songs use search_songs.

tools.name: search_songs
tools.description: Browse the song library: 20 public-domain pieces (kids, folk, holiday, hymn, classical) rated 1–5. Filter by text, genre, mood, difficulty, hands, and whether it fits the computer keyboard. Set for_student true to rank by the student's level, interests, instrument and progress, with a reason per song. Then call get_song, or start_exercise with kind "song".

query.description: Free text matched against title, composer, genre, moods and techniques.

hands.description: "both" returns only songs with a left-hand part.

fits_computer_keyboard.description: Only songs with at least one section playable on the computer keyboard.

for_student.description: Rank by the student profile, interests, instrument and progress.

limit.description: Default 10.

tools.name: get_song
tools.description: Everything about one song: each section with length, note range, whether it fits the computer keyboard (and the octave shift it needs), the student's best score, its distinct notes and computer keys, plus ready-made warm-up drills and a suggested first exercise. Call this before starting a song.

tools.name: get_song_progress
tools.description: Best score per section and overall mastery for one song, or for every song the student has tried. A song counts as learned when every section scores 80 or more.

song_id.description: Omit for all songs with progress.
