tools.name: delete_document
tools.description: Delete a document from the browser workspace.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo the last model mutation (shared human/agent undo stack).

sites.name: aadhar.sh
sites.description: Paste any URL and compare the human page with observed bot access, Cloudflare's standards level, Readability content recovery, raw HTML, structured data, machine terms, and agent doors.

tools.name: lens_scan
tools.description: Scan a URL in the Lens window on this page, the one the person is watching. The panes repaint as it runs and this returns once the scan has settled. Prefer lens_inspect when you only want the data: that one answers you privately and leaves the screen alone. Use this one when the person should SEE what you found. [safety: changes what is on the person's screen, and nothing else; repeat calls repeat the effect; fetches from the public internet.]

url.description: an absolute http(s) URL

tools.name: lens_compare_onscreen
tools.description: Put two URLs through the same rubric side by side, in the Lens window on this page. Returns the comparison and leaves it on screen. The head-to-head costs a tighter per-visitor budget than a single scan, so do not loop it. [safety: changes what is on the person's screen, and nothing else; repeat calls repeat the effect; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: lens_show
tools.description: Change what the Lens window is displaying. `pane` picks the split (both, human, machine, browser, delta) and `tab` picks which machine lens is open (anatomy, reader, wire, structured, ai, terms, discovery, tools, nlweb, markdown, readiness). This only moves the view. Five tabs hold nothing until somebody pays for the fetch, so follow it with lens_run_tab when the pane comes back empty. [safety: changes what is on the person's screen, and nothing else.]

tools.name: lens_run_tab
tools.description: Pay for one of the opt-in machine tabs and wait for it: reader (a third-party extractor's guess at the article), wire (every request the page makes, through a real browser), tools (the MCP catalog the origin advertises), nlweb (ask the origin's own /ask endpoint a question), markdown (replay the Accept header each named agent client sends, and report which representation each one gets). Each one is a fresh fetch of somebody else's site from this visitor's budget, which is why none of them run on their own. Needs a scan on screen first. [safety: changes what is on the person's screen, and nothing else; repeat calls repeat the effect; fetches from the public internet.]

query.description: nlweb only: the question to ask the origin

tools.name: lens_read_screen
tools.description: Read what the Lens window is showing right now: the URL that was scanned, its status, which pane and machine tab are open, the agent-readiness score, which Delta switches are flipped, and which opt-in tabs already hold data. The one tool here that changes nothing. Call it to find out what the person is looking at before you touch anything. [safety: read-only.]

tools.name: lens_delta
tools.description: Flip one of the Delta counterfactual switches and repaint. Each switch simulates a fix the scanned site has not made (markdown, semantic, contract, authority, receipt, dictionary, ech) and shows what it would have bought. Nothing is sent anywhere: the whole simulation is arithmetic on the scan already on screen. [safety: changes what is on the person's screen, and nothing else.]

tools.name: ask
tools.description: Ask aadhar.sh a natural-language question and get NLWeb-shaped results: for each match a url, name, site, score (0-100), description, and a schema.org schema_object. Retrieval is lexical over the site's own corpus and descriptions are extractive, so this returns the passages that answer the question rather than a written answer. mode=summarize and mode=generate are refused by name: this origin runs no language model. [safety: read-only.]

query.description: the question, in natural language

site.description: NLWeb site token; this origin serves one site, so "aadhar.sh" or "all"

mode.description: list (the only one served here); summarize and generate are refused rather than degraded

prev.description: previous queries. Received and NOT resolved, since decontextualization needs a model; send decontextualized_query instead

decontextualized_query.description: the fully self-contained form of a follow-up question. When present this is what gets searched

tools.name: search_site
tools.description: Search the public pages, writing, garage notes, and utility descriptions on aadhar.sh. [safety: read-only.]

tools.name: now_playing
tools.description: Read the cached current rn playlist and its tracks. A cold cache may refresh from the public Spotify embed using AadharshBot. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: photo_query
tools.description: Query the published photo archive by caption, camera, lens, film simulation, film-recipe setting, or date range. `q` is free text scored per term across the caption, the EXIF and an offline term expansion, so "classic chrome bridge" matches the film simulation AND the subject; the named parameters stay exact filters. Results are ranked and carry `score` and `matched` (which fields answered). `ranking.mode` says whether every term was covered (all-terms), only some (partial), or none (no-match), and `ranking.dropped` / `ranking.common` name terms ignored as stopwords or as too widespread to tell photos apart. Each result carries a `recipe` card naming the in-camera settings the shot was made with, so a look can be read back and re-shot. GPS and unlisted EXIF fields are never returned. [safety: read-only.]

q.description: free-text query, ranked; multiple words are scored independently

film.description: film simulation name, e.g. "Classic Chrome", "Nostalgic Neg", "Acros"

recipe.description: substring match anywhere in the recipe card, e.g. "DR400", "Clarity: -2", "Grain Effect: Strong, Large", "+2 Red"

from.description: inclusive YYYY-MM-DD prefix

to.description: inclusive YYYY-MM-DD prefix

tools.name: coffee_availability
tools.description: Read bookable coffee slots in the host timezone. If the calendar is stale or unavailable, the result is explicitly unavailable and contains no slots. [safety: read-only.]

tools.name: change_radar
tools.description: Read the bounded historical diff of the latest AadharshBot neighborhood observations. Raw crawled bodies are not stored or returned. [safety: read-only.]

tools.name: lens_inspect
tools.description: Inspect one public HTTP(S) URL through Lens and return a compact agent-readiness observation. Private, local, and non-HTTP targets are rejected. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: lens_page
tools.description: Read one public URL and return only what derives from the page's own bytes: anatomy, structured data, a markdown rendering, and what it costs an agent to ingest. Skips the origin-level fan-out entirely, so it is far cheaper and far faster than lens_inspect. Readiness, agent doors and terms are ABSENT from the result (not zero) because they were not checked; `phases.discovery` is false. Use lens_inspect when you need those. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: lens_compare
tools.description: Inspect two public HTTP(S) URLs and compare status, content, readiness, spectrum, agent doors, and discovery surfaces. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: find_events
tools.description: Search the Serendipity event pool (community events worth going to, and who's RSVP'd) by keyword. Returns events the pool's contributors actually said yes to; pass rsvp:"all" to include events that were only browsed. [safety: read-only.]

q.description: optional keyword filter on event name, place, or contributor

when.description: defaults to upcoming

rsvp.description: defaults to going (the events with real rosters)

topic.description: optional: only events classified as this topic; unclassified events are counted in `untagged`

format.description: optional: only events classified as this format (talks, meal, social, ...)

tools.name: image_inspect
tools.description: Inspect an image's dimensions, format, and animation/frame information. Image bytes are processed ephemerally and are not stored. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

image_data.description: base64 image bytes, optionally as a data URL

tools.name: image_transform
tools.description: Run a bounded web image transform through Cloudflare Images and return the transformed image inline plus an exact byte receipt. The output is ephemeral. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: image_compare
tools.description: Encode one image into up to three bounded format variants and report exact byte sizes and hashes. It does not pretend to score visual quality. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: photo_recipe
tools.description: Return the exact public Fuji recipe for a named archive photo, archive URL, or exact published thumbnail bytes. Arbitrary visual lookalikes are not treated as matches. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

image_data.description: base64 bytes from a published thumbnail

tools.name: representation_capture
tools.description: Capture bounded public HTTP representations under browser, bot, Markdown, or identity request profiles and store only normalized headers, metadata, and body digests. Writes: each call persists a new snapshot row, so this tool is not read-only and not idempotent. [safety: WRITES DATA on this origin; repeat calls repeat the effect; fetches from the public internet. This page asks the person to confirm before it runs.]

tools.name: representation_read
tools.description: Read one normalized HTTP representation snapshot from the vault. Raw response bodies are never returned because they are never stored. [safety: read-only.]

tools.name: representation_compare
tools.description: Refetch the same HTTP representation profile, compare it with a stored snapshot, and persist the new normalized observation. Writes: each call persists a new snapshot row, so this tool is not read-only and not idempotent. [safety: WRITES DATA on this origin; repeat calls repeat the effect; fetches from the public internet. This page asks the person to confirm before it runs.]

url.description: optional replacement URL, otherwise the snapshot URL

tools.name: finger
tools.description: Look up who runs aadhar.sh, as a drivable terminal program. Panes: overview, writing, reading, listening, photos, around, coffee, deploys, search. Send `keys` to move (1-9 pane, j/k cursor, open, h back, ? help) and pass the returned `url`'s params back to continue. Returns a rendered 80-column frame. [safety: read-only.]

keys.description: a key sequence, up to 32 keys, e.g. "2jj<cr>"

open.description: id of the row to open (slug, index, or version number)

tools.name: photos
tools.description: Browse the published photo archive as a terminal frame, filterable by caption, film simulation, body, and lens. Opening a frame shows its exposure and the in-camera recipe it was shot with. Send `keys` (j/k cursor, open, n/p page). [safety: read-only.]

open.description: photo stem to open

tools.name: radar
tools.description: Render signal readings you have already measured (wifi/Bluetooth RSSI) as a terminal instrument: concentric strength bands, a meter and trend per source, and findphone's field calibration (-45 arm's reach, -60 same table, -72 same room). This origin has no antenna and does not sense anything; you supply the samples. Nothing is stored. Angles in the plot are decorative because RSSI carries no bearing. [safety: read-only.]

kind.description: optional tag, e.g. wifi or ble

history.description: optional trailing readings for the trend

source.description: optional label for what did the sampling

tools.name: encode
tools.description: Read a JPEG or AVIF at a URL and report what its encoder actually did: chroma subsampling, baseline vs progressive and the scan count, an estimated quality with the deviation from the IJG Annex K table shown, AVIF bit depth, and whether ICC/EXIF/XMP is riding along. NO PIXELS ARE DECODED — every fact comes from the container — so this works on files a Worker could never decode. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: agent_ready
tools.description: Grade how much of an origin a machine can actually use: llms.txt, a markdown twin, an agent card, an API catalog, and a real tools/list against its MCP server. Doors are COUNTED, never scored — a check that could not run is reported as unreadable rather than as a failure. Called with no url it audits aadhar.sh itself and prints what building that cost in files and lines. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: dict
tools.description: Will a browser ever actually use the compression dictionary a URL is serving? Compression dictionaries fail in total silence — Chromium declines to register a perfectly good one because of a cache directive, with no warning anywhere. Returns a rendered frame grading every registration rule, plus whether a delta-serving response varies on available-dictionary. Same route as /dict. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: cache
tools.description: Does a URL's ETag ever actually 304? A BEHAVIORAL probe rather than a header read: fetches twice to see whether the validator survives two identical requests, then replays it with If-None-Match and reports what the origin did. Also checks Accept negotiation against Vary. Returns a rendered frame. Same route as /cache. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

tools.name: lens
tools.description: Inspect one public HTTP(S) URL and render the observation as a terminal frame: readability, agent doors, and what a single scan costs to read. Same rate limit and same refusals as lens_inspect; use lens_inspect instead if you want the fields rather than the frame. [safety: read-only; fetches from the public internet.]

doors.description: also READ what is behind the agent doors: llms.txt, the markdown twin, the agent card, and a real tools/list against their MCP server. Their catalog is listed, never called.

sites.name: agenticroom.setyongr.chatgpt.site
sites.description: Plan a living room together in 3D. Arrange furniture, compare prices, and stay within budget with shared controls for you and your WebMCP agent.

tools.name: get_planner_guide
tools.description: Orientation for agents that just opened this site: what AgenticRoom is, what the room editor can do, the exact tools to use for each task, a recommended design workflow, and the invariants agents must respect (budget semantics, locks, session-only uploads). Call this first, then get_room_state for the live design. Static, first-party content; never mutates state and never reads session data.

tools.name: get_room_state
tools.description: Read the current room state: room dimensions, wall openings (doors and windows with footprints), the room appearance (wall finish, floor finish, wallpaper), every placed furniture item with its id, name, category, dimensions, position, rotation, lock and source flags, budget-relevant price, and chosen color and material variant, the design budget, live pricing totals, and layout validation issues. When a design was saved this session, its name is included. Deterministic; never mutates state.

tools.name: get_available_placement_zones
tools.description: List the room’s placement zones that currently accept the given furniture category and still have free capacity. Each zone reports its footprint, allowed categories, current occupancy, and remaining slots, so a product can be routed to a valid destination before placing it. Deterministic read; records a zone inspection in the activity feed.

category.description: Furniture category to place; zones must allow it and have free capacity.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Search the marketplace catalog by free-text query, category, style tags, colors, materials, price range, stock availability, and maximum width/depth footprint, with deterministic sorting and pagination. Results carry price, dimensions, style tags, colors, material, and stock. Use this before placing a product. Deterministic read; records the search in the activity feed.

query.description: Free-text query matched against product name, material, and style tags.

category.description: Only products of this furniture category.

styles.description: Only products carrying any of these style tags (e.g. "scandinavian").

colors.description: Only products offering any of these colors (e.g. "oak", "charcoal").

materials.description: Only products made of any of these materials (e.g. "oak", "linen").

minPrice.description: Inclusive lower price bound in USD.

maxPrice.description: Inclusive upper price bound in USD.

inStockOnly.description: When true, only products with stock greater than zero.

sort.description: Deterministic result ordering.

maxWidth.description: Only products whose width in meters is at most this value.

maxDepth.description: Only products whose depth in meters is at most this value.

page.description: 1-based page number; clamps to the last page.

pageSize.description: Results per page, at most 25 (default 10).

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Fetch one marketplace product by id with its full catalog details: category, price, width/depth/height in meters, style tags, colors, material, stock, and default rotation, plus the placed instances currently using it in the room. Unknown ids fail with code "missing_product". Deterministic read; records the product view in the activity feed.

tools.name: check_layout
tools.description: Re-run layout validation against the live room, placed items, and budget: room bounds, furniture overlaps, opening clearance, zone compatibility and membership, budget, stock, and catalog integrity. Returns whether the design is valid plus every issue with its kind, severity, message, and affected instance ids. Deterministic read; records the layout check in the activity feed.

tools.name: calculate_total
tools.description: Recompute the full budget breakdown of the current design: marketplace and existing subtotals, grand total, budget, signed remaining, over-budget flag, and one line per placed item with unit price, line total, source, and lock state. Deterministic read; records the calculation in the activity feed.

tools.name: get_budget_pressure
tools.description: Report the budget pressure of the current design: under/at/over-budget status, signed remaining, amount over, and the replaceable marketplace items sorted by price (most expensive first) to inform budget-rescue tradeoffs. Deterministic read of the live design; never mutates state.

tools.name: find_cheaper_alternatives
tools.description: Suggest cheaper same-category replacements for one placed marketplace item. The instance must exist, be marketplace-sourced, and not be locked. Candidates are strictly cheaper and in stock, optionally capped by targetPrice, ranked by style, color, material, and dimension compatibility, then by savings. Returns savings and compatibility scores per candidate. Deterministic; records the suggestion in the activity feed.

instanceId.description: Placed instance to find replacements for (marketplace, unlocked).

targetPrice.description: Inclusive upper bound on the replacement price in USD.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of candidates to return (1-20, default 5).

tools.name: get_saved_designs
tools.description: List the designs saved during this session, newest first, with each snapshot’s budget, placed-item count, marketplace total, and room appearance at save time. Deterministic read of session state; never mutates state.

tools.name: render_scene_snapshot
tools.description: Render the current 3D room to a JPEG image (data URL) so the arrangement can be judged visually. view presets: “live” uses the editor camera exactly as last left; “orbit”/“top”/“front”/“side” frame the standard room overviews without moving the user’s camera. Returns the image as a data: URL with pixel dimensions; output is downscaled to maxWidth. Only the 3D canvas is captured — UI panels, overlays, and text are never included. Deterministic; never mutates state.

view.description: Which camera view to render (“live” = current editor camera).

maxWidth.description: Output width cap in pixels (256-2048, default 1024); height keeps the canvas aspect.

tools.name: place_product
tools.description: Place a product through the same store action as the UI: zoneId centers it in a placement zone (category, capacity, and fit are domain-enforced), or position x/z places it explicitly (unvalidated geometry); optional rotation; optional color (one of the product’s authored colors) with the product’s material. Returns the new item with its stored variant, refreshed pricing (newTotal, budget, remaining, overBudget), and current layout validity and issues. Failures (missing/out-of-stock product, unknown/full/incompatible zone, unavailable color or material) leave the room unchanged.

productId.description: Catalog product id to place, e.g. "drift-oak-coffee-table".

zoneId.description: Place into this zone at its center (e.g. "living-area"); exclusive with position.

position.description: Explicit footprint center in room coordinates; exclusive with zoneId.

x.description: Center x in meters; the room spans x in [-3, 3].

z.description: Center z in meters; the room spans z in [-2.25, 2.25].

rotation.description: Yaw in degrees; normalized to [0, 360). Defaults to the product default (0).

color.description: Chosen colorway, one of the product’s authored colors (see get_product). Defaults to the first color.

material.description: The product’s authored material; mismatched values fail with invalid_variant.

tools.name: move_product
tools.description: Move a placed item to a new x/z footprint-center position (floor base, y stays 0) through the same store action as the UI. Locked items may be moved. The move itself is not geometry-checked; validation refreshes immediately and reports out-of-bounds, overlap, opening, and zone issues. Returns the moved item, refreshed pricing (newTotal, budget, remaining, overBudget), and current layout validity and issues.

instanceId.description: Instance id of the placed item to act on, e.g. "existing-sofa" or "drift-oak-coffee-table-1".

position.description: New footprint center in room coordinates; the item stays at floor base.

x.description: Center x in meters; the room spans x in [-3, 3].

z.description: Center z in meters; the room spans z in [-2.25, 2.25].

tools.name: rotate_product
tools.description: Set a placed item’s yaw rotation in degrees through the same store action as the UI; the value is normalized to [0, 360). Position, lock, and source are unchanged, and locked items may be rotated. Returns the rotated item, refreshed pricing (newTotal, budget, remaining, overBudget), and current layout validity and issues. Unknown instances fail with item_not_found.

instanceId.description: Instance id of the placed item to act on, e.g. "existing-sofa" or "drift-oak-coffee-table-1".

rotation.description: New yaw in degrees around y; normalized to [0, 360).

tools.name: set_item_elevation
tools.description: Set how high a placed item’s base sits above the floor (meters) through the same store action as the UI: raise TVs, wall art, shelves, and curtains to hang them instead of resting on the floor. y=0 puts the piece back on the floor. Locked items may be raised (like move/rotate); negative or non-finite heights fail with invalid_elevation. The layout refreshes immediately, so a piece whose top crosses the ceiling surfaces as a height_bounds error. Moving the piece later keeps its height. Returns the item with its updated position, refreshed pricing (newTotal, budget, remaining, overBudget), and current layout validity and issues. Unknown instances fail with item_not_found.

instanceId.description: Instance id of the placed item to act on, e.g. "existing-sofa" or "aria-55-oled-tv-1".

y.description: Height of the piece base above the floor in meters, 0 or greater (0 = on the floor). The piece top must stay below the ceiling.

tools.name: remove_product
tools.description: Remove a placed item from the room through the same store action as the UI. Locked items cannot be removed (item_locked). Destructive: the item is permanently gone from the current design. Returns the removed item as it was, refreshed pricing (newTotal, budget, remaining, overBudget), and current layout validity and issues. Unknown instances fail with item_not_found.

instanceId.description: Instance id of the placed item to act on, e.g. "existing-sofa" or "drift-oak-coffee-table-1".

tools.name: set_item_locked
tools.description: Lock or unlock a placed item through the same store action as the UI. Locked items cannot be removed or replaced but can still be moved and rotated; setting the current value is a no-op success. Returns the item with its updated lock state, refreshed pricing (newTotal, budget, remaining, overBudget), and current layout validity and issues.

instanceId.description: Instance id of the placed item to act on, e.g. "existing-sofa" or "drift-oak-coffee-table-1".

locked.description: True locks the item (cannot be removed or replaced); false unlocks it.

tools.name: set_item_source
tools.description: Re-tag a placed item’s ownership through the same store action as the UI: source "existing" marks it as already owned (never counted toward the budget), source "marketplace" marks it as a new purchase (counted). Locked items may be re-tagged (the lock only guards removal and replacement); setting the current source is a no-op success. Budget pricing and validation refresh in the same write. Returns the item with its source, refreshed pricing (newTotal, budget, remaining, overBudget), and current layout validity and issues. Unknown instances fail with item_not_found.

instanceId.description: Instance id of the placed item to act on, e.g. "existing-sofa" or "drift-oak-coffee-table-1".

source.description: "existing" = already owned (never counted toward the budget); "marketplace" = new purchase (counted).

tools.name: set_budget
tools.description: Set the design budget in USD through the same store action as the UI; only marketplace items count against it. Pricing and validation refresh immediately, so a budget below the current marketplace total surfaces a budget_exceeded error. Returns the status (budget_updated, or unchanged for a no-op), the new budget, refreshed pricing (newTotal, remaining, overBudget), and current layout validity and issues.

budget.description: New design budget in USD; only marketplace items count against it.

tools.name: set_room_appearance
tools.description: Style the room through the same store action as the UI: either supply all three finish ids (wallFinishId, floorFinishId, wallpaperId) or use preset "default" to restore the defaults (gallery-white walls, natural-oak floor, no wallpaper). Visual only: pricing, layout, and validation are never affected. Returns the resolved appearance and current layout validity and issues.

wallFinishId.description: Wall finish id; one of: gallery-white, warm-sand, soft-sage, clay-plaster.

floorFinishId.description: Floor finish id; one of: natural-oak, white-oak, walnut, slate-tile.

wallpaperId.description: Wallpaper id; one of: none, linen-stripe, botanical-line, arched-geo.

preset.description: Reset to the default styling.

tools.name: resize_room
tools.description: Resize the room to real measured dimensions: width, depth, and height in meters (supported ranges: see get_room_state room.resizeLimits). Openings stay on their walls and placement zones rebuild with the room; an opening whose wall became too short is removed and reported. Furniture is never moved - pieces left outside the new walls become out-of-bounds layout errors. Returns the new dimensions, floor area in m2, removed opening ids, pricing, and layout validity.

width.description: Room width along x in meters (2-10).

depth.description: Room depth along z in meters (2-10).

tools.name: move_opening
tools.description: Move a door or window through the same store action as the UI: alongCenter is the opening’s center along its current wall in room coordinates (x for north/south walls, z for east/west walls); pass wall to relocate the opening onto a different wall (its real size is preserved and the footprint re-orients). Centers are clamped to the wall and moves that would collide with another opening on the target wall fail with opening_overlap; unknown ids fail with opening_not_found and unusable walls or non-finite centers with invalid_opening_position. Clearance validation refreshes immediately. Returns the opening (id, kind, wall, alongCenterM, alongWidthM, heightM, sillM, footprint) and current layout validity and issues.

openingId.description: Opening id, e.g. "entry-door", "east-window", "balcony-door", or "opening-1" for added ones.

alongCenter.description: New along-wall center in meters: x for north/south walls, z for east/west walls. Clamped to the wall.

wall.description: Optional target wall to relocate the opening onto; omit to move along the current wall.

tools.name: add_opening
tools.description: Add a standard door (0.9 m wide, 2.1 m high) or window (1.6 m wide, 1.4 m high at a 0.9 m sill) to any wall through the same store action as the UI. Without center, the opening lands in the first free span of the wall; an explicit center is clamped to the wall. Heights are capped below the ceiling automatically. Failures: duplicate_opening_id for taken ids (ids are minted for you), opening_overlap when another opening already occupies the spot, invalid_opening_position when the wall is too short or fully occupied. Clearance validation refreshes immediately. Returns the added opening (id, kind, wall, alongCenterM, alongWidthM, heightM, sillM, footprint) and current layout validity and issues.

kind.description: What to add: "door" (0.9 m wide, 2.1 m high) or "window" (1.6 m wide, sill 0.9 m).

wall.description: Wall to cut the opening into.

center.description: Optional along-wall center in meters (x for north/south walls, z for east/west). Defaults to the first free span.

tools.name: remove_opening
tools.description: Remove a door or window from the room through the same store action as the UI (seeded openings included). Destructive: the opening is permanently gone from the current design; clearance validation refreshes immediately, so furniture that used to block it clears. Unknown ids fail with opening_not_found. Returns the removed opening (id, kind, wall, alongCenterM, alongWidthM, heightM, sillM, footprint) and current layout validity and issues.

openingId.description: Opening id, e.g. "entry-door", "east-window", "balcony-door", or "opening-1" for added ones.

tools.name: resize_opening
tools.description: Resize a door or window through the same store action as the UI. alongSize is the along-wall width in meters, height is the opening height, and sillHeight (windows only) is how high the opening’s bottom edge sits above the floor — the window’s vertical position. At least one field is required; doors must keep sillHeight 0 (they sit on the floor). Feasible ranges are wall- and ceiling-dependent: out-of-range values fail with invalid_opening_size (details: field, min, max), widening into another opening on the same wall fails with opening_overlap, unknown ids with opening_not_found. The opening keeps its center. Returns the resized opening (id, kind, wall, alongCenterM, alongWidthM, heightM, sillM, footprint) and refreshed layout validity and issues.

openingId.description: Opening id, e.g. "entry-door", "east-window", "balcony-door", or "opening-1" for added ones.

alongSize.description: New along-wall width in meters (x for north/south walls, z for east/west).

height.description: New opening height in meters; the top stays below the ceiling.

sillHeight.description: Windows only: how high the bottom edge sits above the floor (the window vertical position). Doors keep 0.

tools.name: replace_product
tools.description: Swap the product backing a placed item through the same store action as the UI. The replacement must exist, be in stock, and match the item’s category; locked items cannot be replaced. The item keeps its instance id, position, rotation, and source. Destructive: the previous product is dropped from the item. Returns the replaced item, the price savings (negative when pricier), refreshed pricing, and current layout validity and issues.

instanceId.description: Instance id of the placed item to act on, e.g. "existing-sofa" or "drift-oak-coffee-table-1".

replacementProductId.description: Replacement catalog product id; must exist, be in stock, and match the item’s category.

tools.name: save_design
tools.description: Capture the current design (room, placed items with their color variants, budget, room appearance) as a saved snapshot with the given name through the same store action as the UI; saved designs can be restored later with load_design. The live design is unchanged. Returns the snapshot metadata: id, name, creation and update timestamps, budget, item count, marketplace total and room appearance at save time, and the number of designs saved this session.

name.description: Human-readable name for the saved design snapshot.

thumbnailGradient.description: Optional CSS gradient for the snapshot thumbnail, e.g. "linear-gradient(135deg, #E6DFD2, #8FA3A0)".

tools.name: load_design
tools.description: Restore a design saved earlier this session (see get_saved_designs) through the same store action as the UI, replacing the current room, placed items (with their color variants), budget, and room appearance. Destructive: the current unsaved design is discarded. Returns the design id and name, restored item count, budget, appearance, refreshed marketplace total and remaining, and current layout validity and issues. Unknown ids fail with design_not_found.

designId.description: Id of a design saved this session (see get_saved_designs), e.g. "snapshot-1".

tools.name: new_project
tools.description: Start a brand-new empty project through the same store action as the UI: every placed item, door, and window is removed (session uploads too), the budget and room finishes reset to their defaults, and the room shell keeps its current measured dimensions so the agent or user can enter the real room size next. Saved designs and the cart are kept. Destructive: the current arrangement is discarded. Returns the new empty state (dimensions, opening count 0, item count 0, budget) and refreshed layout validity and issues.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add placed marketplace items to the shopping cart through the same store action as the UI, one line per instance at the current catalog price. Any unknown instance, pre-existing (non-marketplace) item, instance already in the cart, or missing product rejects the whole request with per-instance reasons and leaves the cart untouched. Returns cart status, each line (id, product, quantity, unit price, instance id), the cart total, and how many lines were added.

instanceIds.description: Placed marketplace instance ids to add; at least one; duplicates within the request collapse.

tools.name: remove_cart_item
tools.description: Remove the cart line for one placed instance through the same store action as the UI. Only the cart changes: the furniture stays in the room and can be re-added while it remains a marketplace piece. Useful when a shopper wants to check out only a handful of the room items. Returns the updated cart (status, itemCount, total, lines) and how many lines remain. Unknown instance ids fail with cart_item_not_found; checked-out carts fail with cart_checked_out.

instanceId.description: Placed instance id whose cart line should be removed, e.g. "aria-55-oled-tv-1".

sites.name: alza-dev.pages.dev
sites.description: Draw floor plans in 2D, walk them in 3D, and let your AI agent co-edit the same live page through WebMCP. Built for the WebMCP Challenge.

tools.name: get_model
tools.description: Read the full floor plan: walls (endpoints, thickness, height), openings (doors/windows with position along their wall), rooms (metric rects with labels), furniture, and plan name. All units are meters.

tools.name: get_issues
tools.description: Run the constraint checker over the plan. Detects: too-short walls, loose ends, collinear overlaps, mid-span crossings, openings overflowing their wall or overlapping each other, walls ending inside an opening, floating/overlapping/doorless rooms, furniture crossing walls, blocking doors/windows, or colliding. Use it after editing to self-repair.

tools.name: get_item_catalog
tools.description: List the furniture catalog: kind, label, footprint (width × depth in meters) and height.

tools.name: get_editor_state
tools.description: Read what the human is doing right now: 2D/3D view, camera mode, selected wall/item/room, current draw mode.

tools.name: measure
tools.description: Measure a distance: between two points (x1,y1)-(x2,y2), or the length of a wall by id. Returns meters.

tools.name: get_underlay
tools.description: Read the blueprint underlay: whether a reference plan image is loaded, the world rectangle it covers (metres), the mapping from image fractions to world coordinates — and the PROTOCOL for tracing it. Call this FIRST whenever the human gives you a plan to reproduce. Tracing needs the drawing in two places and this tool tells you which are missing: uploaded on the page (carries the scale) and pasted into your conversation (the only way you can see it). This tool never returns the pixels — it returns where the drawing sits in world metres so you can convert what you measure on your own copy. Measure in fractions of the image, not pixels: the page holds a resized copy.

tools.name: calibrate_underlay
tools.description: Scale the loaded blueprint image to real-world meters. Give two points on the image as fractions (u, v in 0..1; u = right, v = down) and the REAL distance between them in meters (e.g. a dimension printed on the plan). The underlay is resized preserving aspect, keeping the first point fixed. Call after the human uploads the plan, before tracing walls over it.

tools.name: add_wall
tools.description: Add a wall segment from (ax,ay) to (bx,by) in meters. Coordinates snap to a 5 cm grid. Default thickness 0.15 m (use 0.1 for interior), height 2.7 m.

tools.name: edit_wall
tools.description: Move endpoints or change thickness/height of an existing wall (by id). Endpoints snap to 5 cm.

tools.name: remove_wall
tools.description: Remove a wall by id. Its doors and windows are removed too.

tools.name: add_door
tools.description: Add a door on a wall. t is the position of the door CENTER along the wall (0..1). Default width 0.9 m, height 2.1 m; a door wider than 1.2 m is built as a double door with two leaves. The vano is clamped so it always fits inside the wall; too-wide doors are rejected with the wall length. hinge picks the jamb the hinges sit on ("a" = the wall's A end, the default; "b" = the B end) and side picks which way the leaf swings, as seen walking the wall from A to B: "right" (default) or "left". Match these to the swing arc drawn on the plan.

tools.name: set_door_swing
tools.description: Change how an existing door opens: hinge ("a" | "b" — which jamb carries the hinges) and/or side ("left" | "right" — which way the leaf swings, walking the wall from its A endpoint to its B endpoint). Re-run build_3d to see it.

tools.name: add_window
tools.description: Add a window on a wall. t is the position of the window CENTER along the wall (0..1). Default width 1.2 m, sill 0.9 m, height 1.2 m. The vano is clamped to fit.

tools.name: move_opening
tools.description: Move a door or window along its wall to a new center position t (0..1). Clamped to fit.

tools.name: remove_opening
tools.description: Remove a door or window by id.

tools.name: add_room
tools.description: Add a room: a metric rectangle (x, y = top-left corner, w, h in meters) with a label and floor finish (oak | tile | carpet | concrete).

tools.name: update_room
tools.description: Update a room by id or label (e.g. "bedroom"): move, resize, relabel, or change floor finish.

tools.name: remove_room
tools.description: Remove a room by id or label.

tools.name: place_item
tools.description: Place furniture from the catalog at (x, y) = center in meters. rotation (degrees, counterclockwise) sets which way the piece FACES: 0 = faces +y (down/south on the plan), 90 = faces +x (right/east), 180 = faces -y (up/north), 270 = faces -x (left/west). The back of a sofa, bed headboard, wardrobe or counter is opposite the facing direction — so a sofa against the SOUTH wall needs rotation 180, and one against the WEST wall needs rotation 90. To sit a piece flush against a wall, offset its center by depth/2 from the wall FACE (centerline ± thickness/2), not from the centerline. Use get_item_catalog for footprints; get_issues reports crossings and blocked doors.

tools.name: define_item_kind
tools.description: Create a piece of furniture that is NOT in the catalogue, then place it with place_item. Use this whenever the plan draws something the catalogue does not have, or draws it at a different size — a corner bath, an L-shaped sofa, a kitchen island, a piano. Do NOT approximate with the nearest stock item when the plan shows something specific: define the real thing. Required: kind (a stable snake_case id), label, and the true footprint w × d and height h in METRES. Optional `parts` models it in 3D from primitives; without it the piece is blocked out from its footprint. Each part is { shape: "box" | "cylinder" | "sphere", x, y, z, w, h, d, color, rotation }, in the piece's OWN local frame: x runs along its width, z along its depth, y is height above the floor and is the part's BOTTOM (a 0.4 m tall seat resting on the floor is y:0, h:0.4). The piece faces +z, so a backrest sits at negative z and the front is positive z — that keeps it consistent with the rotation convention in place_item. For a cylinder, w is the diameter and d makes it an ellipse. Sizes are metres, colours are hex.

tools.name: move_item
tools.description: Move or rotate a furniture item by id or kind (e.g. "sofa"). Same rotation convention as place_item: 0 faces +y, 90 faces +x, 180 faces -y, 270 faces -x.

tools.name: remove_item
tools.description: Remove a furniture item by id or kind.

tools.name: set_plan_name
tools.description: Rename the plan.

tools.name: clear_model
tools.description: Clear the whole plan (walls, openings, rooms, furniture, notes). Use when the user asks to start over.

tools.name: build_3d
tools.description: Raise the plan into 3D: extrudes walls with real openings, resolves corner joints, builds furniture, and switches the human's view to the 3D scene. Call after drawing so the user sees the result.

tools.name: set_camera
tools.description: Move the 3D camera: "orbit" (default 3/4 view), "top" (plan view from above), "walk" (first-person at 1.6 m — the user walks with WASD). Implies switching to 3D.

tools.name: set_doors
tools.description: Swing the door leaves in the 3D scene open or shut (build_3d must have run). state: "open", "closed" or "toggle". Pass an opening id to act on one door, or omit it to act on every door in the plan. The human can do the same by clicking a leaf in the 3D view.

tools.name: get_supplier_catalog
tools.description: Read the furniture catalogue published by the PARTNER ORIGIN (Nordika) as its own WebMCP tools — sku, name, category, real footprint in metres, price and stock. Alza discovers those tools with getTools({fromOrigins}) and calls them with executeTool(), so the data crosses origins in the browser with no server in between. Filter with category (living | bedroom | office | dining), maxPrice, maxWidth (metres) or inStock. Pair it with place_supplier_product to drop a real product into the plan at its true size.

tools.name: place_supplier_product
tools.description: Buy-in-place: fetch one product from the partner origin by sku, add it to this plan's catalogue at the supplier's REAL dimensions, and place it at (x, y) = centre in metres with the usual rotation convention. The constraint checker then treats it like any other piece, so a sofa that does not fit is caught before anyone orders it.

tools.name: leave_note
tools.description: Leave a note on the plan for the human (or read theirs): design rationale, questions, measurements to verify. Notes are visible in the Notes panel.

tools.name: get_notes
tools.description: Read all notes left on the plan by the human and by agents.

sites.name: corep.stonefish.dev
sites.description: A local-first fitness tracker you and your AI agent operate together, over WebMCP.

tools.name: fitness_get_today
tools.description: What the user is scheduled to do today, based on their active plans and the local weekday. Returns the exercises with their targets, plus whether today is a training day at all. Start here when the user asks what they should do now.

tools.name: fitness_get_plans
tools.description: All of the user's training plans with their phases and exercises. Optionally filter by status ("active", "paused", "completed", "archived"). Use this to find a plan id before editing anything.

status.description: Only return plans in this status.

tools.name: fitness_get_plan
tools.description: One plan with every phase and exercise, including each exercise id. You need the exercise ids from here to update or remove individual movements.

plan_id.description: The plan to fetch.

tools.name: fitness_get_streak
tools.description: Current and longest streak. A streak counts only days the plan schedules — missing an unscheduled rest day never breaks it, and a scheduled day that has not happened yet does not either.

tools.name: fitness_get_progress
tools.description: The full picture over the last N days: streak, completion rate, total workouts, recent pain notes, recent plan edits, and target-vs-actual for each exercise in the active phase. Read this before advising on whether to add load.

days.description: Window to summarise, in days. Defaults to 30.

plan_id.description: Restrict the exercise trends and edits to one plan.

tools.name: fitness_get_calendar
tools.description: Day-by-day training status for one month: which days were scheduled, which were trained, how complete each session was, and which carry notes.

month.description: Month as "YYYY-MM". Defaults to the current month.

tools.name: fitness_get_workouts
tools.description: Past workout logs, newest first, each with the exercises performed and how they went. Filter by date range or limit the count.

limit.description: Maximum number of logs. Defaults to 10.

tools.name: fitness_get_workouts_on
tools.description: Every workout logged on a specific date — a day can hold more than one. Use this to find a workout id before editing or deleting it.

tools.name: fitness_get_badges
tools.description: All nine badges and whether the user has earned each one, how many times, and the context of each award. Useful for encouragement and for telling them what is close.

tools.name: fitness_get_body_metrics
tools.description: Body measurements over time, oldest first. Units: weight in pounds (lbs); height, bust, waist and hips in centimetres; body fat as a percentage.

days.description: How far back to read, in days. Defaults to 180.

tools.name: fitness_get_edit_history
tools.description: Every change made to exercise targets, by whom (the person or an agent) and why. Read this to understand what equipment the user actually has and how their load has been trending before suggesting a change.

days.description: How far back to read, in days. Defaults to 14.

plan_id.description: Restrict to one plan.

tools.name: fitness_get_templates
tools.description: The built-in starter plans a user can adopt in one step. Offer these when someone wants to begin but does not know what to do, then call fitness_create_plan_from_template.

tools.name: fitness_get_settings
tools.description: The user's display name and what they call their coach. Read this to address them properly.

tools.name: fitness_create_plan
tools.description: Build a complete training plan with phases and exercises. `schedule` sets which weekdays to train. Each phase holds an ordered list of exercises; the first phase becomes the active one. For strength work fill target_reps and target_weight; for holds like planks fill target_duration instead. Ask about injuries and available equipment before calling this.

description.description: What the plan is for and how to approach it.

schedule.description: Which weekdays to train, e.g. {"mon": true, "wed": true, "fri": true}. Omitted days are rest days.

duration_days.description: How long this phase runs, in days. Optional.

notes.description: Notes about this phase.

exercise_name.description: Name of the movement, e.g. "Goblet Squat".

target_reps.description: Reps per set. Use this for strength work; leave null for timed holds.

target_weight.description: Working weight in pounds (lbs). Null for bodyweight movements.

target_duration.description: Seconds per set, for timed movements like planks or wall sits. Use instead of target_reps.

rest_seconds.description: Rest between sets, in seconds. Defaults to 60.

form_cues.description: One short coaching cue shown during the set.

notes.description: Any extra note about this movement.

tools.name: fitness_create_plan_from_template
tools.description: Adopt one of the built-in starter plans. The result is a normal, fully editable plan — adjust it afterwards with fitness_update_exercise. Call fitness_get_templates first to see the ids.

tools.name: fitness_update_plan
tools.description: Change a plan's name, description, weekday schedule, status, or dates. Set status to "paused" when someone needs a break and "active" when they return — a paused plan stops counting toward streaks.

plan_id.description: The plan to change.

schedule.description: Which weekdays to train, e.g. {"mon": true, "wed": true, "fri": true}. Omitted days are rest days.

status.description: New status.

tools.name: fitness_add_exercise
tools.description: Append a movement to a phase of a plan. Get the block id from fitness_get_plan. For strength work set target_reps and target_weight; for timed holds set target_duration.

exercise_name.description: Name of the movement, e.g. "Goblet Squat".

target_reps.description: Reps per set. Use this for strength work; leave null for timed holds.

target_weight.description: Working weight in pounds (lbs). Null for bodyweight movements.

target_duration.description: Seconds per set, for timed movements like planks or wall sits. Use instead of target_reps.

rest_seconds.description: Rest between sets, in seconds. Defaults to 60.

form_cues.description: One short coaching cue shown during the set.

notes.description: Any extra note about this movement.

tools.name: fitness_update_exercise
tools.description: Change the targets on one planned movement. Every changed field is written to the edit history with your reason, and shown to the user next to that exercise — so always pass `reason`, phrased for them ("knee felt tight last session"). Only send the fields you are changing.

rest_seconds.description: New rest between sets, in seconds.

notes.description: New note.

reason.description: Why this is changing. Shown to the user in the plan view.

tools.name: fitness_activate_block
tools.description: Make a phase of a plan the current one. Earlier phases are marked completed and later ones upcoming. Use this when the user has finished a block and is ready to progress.

tools.name: fitness_log_workout
tools.description: Record a completed workout. `date` defaults to today. For each movement record what was actually done, not what was planned — if they did fewer reps or dropped the weight, log that. Mark anything they skipped with skipped=true and a skip_reason. Put anything that hurt in pain_notes; it surfaces in progress summaries. Returns any badges this unlocks so you can congratulate them.

plan_exercise_id.description: The planned exercise this fulfils, when there is one. Links the log to the plan so progress trends work.

difficulty.description: How hard it felt, 1 (easy) to 5 (maximal).

skipped.description: True if the movement was skipped entirely.

notes.description: Any note about this movement in this session.

date.description: Date of the workout, "YYYY-MM-DD". Defaults to today.

plan_id.description: The plan this session belongs to, if any.

block_id.description: The phase this session belongs to, if any.

pain_notes.description: Anything that hurt or felt off. Important — it drives future advice.

general_notes.description: Any other note about the session.

tools.name: fitness_update_workout
tools.description: Fix an existing workout log — add a note they forgot, correct the weight, or replace the exercise list wholesale. Find the workout id with fitness_get_workouts_on. Passing `exercises` replaces the whole list, so include every movement, not just the changed one.

plan_exercise_id.description: The planned exercise this fulfils, when there is one. Links the log to the plan so progress trends work.

difficulty.description: How hard it felt, 1 (easy) to 5 (maximal).

skipped.description: True if the movement was skipped entirely.

notes.description: Any note about this movement in this session.

tools.name: fitness_log_body_metrics
tools.description: Record body measurements. Send only what was actually measured — nothing needs to be complete. Units: weight in pounds (lbs); height, bust, waist and hips in centimetres; body_fat as a percentage like 28.5. Logging the same date twice updates that day, overwriting only the fields you send.

notes.description: Any note about this measurement.

tools.name: fitness_update_settings
tools.description: Set what the app calls the user and what they call their coach. If the user tells you their name, or asks you to go by a particular name, record it here so the app greets them consistently.

coach_name.description: What the coach is called in the UI.

coach_tagline.description: Small label above the coach's note on the home screen.

tools.name: fitness_check_badges
tools.description: Re-run the badge checks and award anything newly earned. Logging a workout already does this, so you rarely need it on its own.

tools.name: fitness_delete_plan
tools.description: Remove a training plan and its phases. The user must approve this in the app before it happens; you will get back whether they did. Workout history is kept — deleting a plan never erases what they actually did.

plan_id.description: The plan to delete.

tools.name: fitness_delete_exercise
tools.description: Take a movement out of a plan. The user must approve it in the app first. Prefer fitness_update_exercise when the goal is to make something easier rather than remove it.

tools.name: fitness_delete_workout
tools.description: Erase a logged workout — for a duplicate or something logged by mistake. The user must approve it in the app first. This changes their streak, so prefer fitness_update_workout when the log is merely wrong.

tools.name: fitness_navigate
tools.description: Switch the app to a screen so the user is looking at what you are talking about. Do this before explaining something visual — send them to "calendar" when discussing consistency, "badges" when congratulating them.

tab.description: today = home and next session; plan = the training plan; calendar = training history; body = measurements and charts; badges = the badge wall.

tools.name: fitness_start_session
tools.description: Open the guided session flow so the user can start training right now — it walks them through each set with a rest timer. Use it when they say they are ready to work out. Defaults to today's scheduled session.

plan_id.description: Plan to train. Defaults to today's scheduled plan, or the active one.

block_id.description: Phase to train. Defaults to the active phase.

tools.name: fitness_open_plan_editor
tools.description: Open the plan editor for the user to fill in themselves, rather than building it for them. Use this when they want to make the choices — or when they ask for something you should not decide alone. Pass a plan_id to edit an existing plan, or omit it to start a blank one.

plan_id.description: Plan to edit. Omit to open a blank editor.

tools.name: fitness_highlight_exercise
tools.description: Scroll to an exercise in the plan view and flash it, so the user can see which movement you mean while you talk about it.

exercise_id.description: The planned exercise to point at.

sites.name: dogecoin87.github.io
sites.description: LUCID Forensic Workbench — browser based forensic image and video enhancement

tools.name: get_state
tools.description: Current project: chains with their filters (ids, types, enabled, parameters of the active chain), active chain, selected filter, current frame, In/Out range, view and playback state. Call it first.

tools.name: list_filters
tools.description: Catalogue of the available filters (type id, name, category, description). Optional category or search text.

category.description: e.g. Adjust, Sharpen, Denoise, Deblurring, Stabilization, Edit, Integrate, Measure, Presentation

search.description: words to look for

tools.name: get_filter_schema
tools.description: Parameters of a filter type: keys, types, ranges, options, defaults, help. Read it before setting parameters you are not sure about.

type.description: filter type id or name, e.g. levels, unsharp_masking, crop

tools.name: get_source_info
tools.description: File information of the evidence of a chain: container, codec, size, frames, frame rate, color conversion, decoder, hashes, metadata (EXIF, tags).

tools.name: get_frame_stats
tools.description: Statistics of a rendered frame (exact, from the processing engine): size, MD5, per channel min/max/mean/standard deviation, clipped pixels, a 16-bin luma histogram. Use it to verify changes.

filter_id.description: output of this filter (default: end of the chain)

frame.description: default: current frame

tools.name: view_frame
tools.description: Look at a rendered frame (an image is attached to the result) — only if the user allows frame sharing. Optionally a region, enlarged for detail.

frame.description: default: current frame

max_size.description: longest side of the image you receive, 256–1536 (default 1024)

tools.name: list_commands
tools.description: Commands of the application menus (File, Edit, Project, Utilities, View, Help) with ids; run_command executes one.

search.description: words to look for

tools.name: select
tools.description: Show a chain in the Viewer and/or select a filter (the Viewer shows the output of the selected filter, or its input with show_input).

show_input.description: show the input instead of the output of the selected filter

tools.name: go_to_frame
tools.description: Move the active chain to a frame: absolute frame number, a relative step (delta) or a time in seconds.

frame.description: frame number (0-based)

seconds.description: time from the start, in seconds

tools.name: playback
tools.description: Play, pause or stop the active chain; set the speed (0.01 to 16, 1 = real time; below 1 no frame is skipped), loop, and playing only the In/Out range.

action.description: what to do (omit to only change settings)

tools.name: set_view
tools.description: Viewer: zoom (percent) or fit, and the display scaling (sharp = equal-size pixels, nearest, smooth). Display only — never changes the pixels.

fit.description: fit the frame in the window

display.description: display scaling

tools.name: set_selection
tools.description: Set (or clear with null) the selection rectangle on the Viewer — filters added afterwards use it as their region (crop, magnify, stabilization ROI…).

tools.name: add_filter
tools.description: Add a filter to a chain (default: the active chain, right after the selected filter) and select it. Unspecified parameters take their defaults (regions default to the Viewer selection). Returns the new filter id and a render check. Changes the LUCID project (undoable; the examiner may have to approve it in LUCID).

type.description: filter type id or name (see list_filters)

params.description: parameter values by key (see get_filter_schema)

after_filter_id.description: insert after this filter (default: after the selected filter)

index.description: insert at this position (1 = right after the loader)

tools.name: set_filter_params
tools.description: Change parameters of an existing filter (one undo step). Returns the applied values and a render check. Changes the LUCID project (undoable; the examiner may have to approve it in LUCID).

params.description: parameter values by key

tools.name: remove_filter
tools.description: Remove a filter from its chain (not the loader: use delete_chain for a whole chain). Changes the LUCID project (undoable; the examiner may have to approve it in LUCID).

tools.name: move_filter
tools.description: Move a filter to another position in its chain (index 1 = right after the loader). Changes the LUCID project (undoable; the examiner may have to approve it in LUCID).

index.description: new position (≥ 1)

tools.name: set_filter_enabled
tools.description: Enable or disable a filter (a disabled filter passes its input through; it stays in the chain). Changes the LUCID project (undoable; the examiner may have to approve it in LUCID).

enabled.description: true to enable

tools.name: reset_filter
tools.description: Reset all parameters of a filter to their defaults. Changes the LUCID project (undoable; the examiner may have to approve it in LUCID).

tools.name: duplicate_chain
tools.description: Copy a chain (to try alternatives without touching the original); the copy becomes active. Changes the LUCID project (undoable; the examiner may have to approve it in LUCID).

tools.name: rename_chain
tools.description: Rename a chain. Changes the LUCID project (undoable; the examiner may have to approve it in LUCID).

tools.name: delete_chain
tools.description: Delete a whole chain (undoable). The evidence file itself is never touched. Changes the LUCID project (undoable; the examiner may have to approve it in LUCID).

tools.name: set_in_out
tools.description: Set or clear (null) the In and Out points of the active chain (frame numbers); used for exports and playback ranges. Changes the LUCID project (undoable; the examiner may have to approve it in LUCID).

tools.name: add_bookmark
tools.description: Bookmark a frame of the active chain with a note (bookmarks appear in the report). Changes the LUCID project (undoable; the examiner may have to approve it in LUCID).

frame.description: default: current frame

note.description: what the frame shows

tools.name: set_case_info
tools.description: Fill in the case information printed in the report. Changes the LUCID project (undoable; the examiner may have to approve it in LUCID).

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo the last change(s) to the project (the same as Edit › Undo). Changes the LUCID project (undoable; the examiner may have to approve it in LUCID).

steps.description: how many changes (default 1)

tools.name: redo
tools.description: Redo changes undone with undo. Changes the LUCID project (undoable; the examiner may have to approve it in LUCID).

steps.description: how many (default 1)

tools.name: load_sample_case
tools.description: Load the built-in demonstration case (synthetic license plate, periodic noise and resolution chart chains). Changes the LUCID project (undoable; the examiner may have to approve it in LUCID).

tools.name: run_command
tools.description: Run an application menu command by id (see list_commands). Commands that open a dialog leave it open for the user. Changes the LUCID project (undoable; the examiner may have to approve it in LUCID).

id.description: command id from list_commands

tools.name: open_media
tools.description: Ask the user to open evidence (video, image, image sequence) or a project file — browsers only open files on the user's click. Returns what was loaded. Needs the examiner at the LUCID window (a click in LUCID's AI panel).

kind.description: media (default): a video or image; sequence: several images as frames; project: a saved project

reason.description: why, in one sentence, shown to the user

tools.name: export
tools.description: Prepare an export and let the user save it: frames as images, a video, a snapshot, the processing report, or the project file. Uses lossless formats when 'lossless exports only' is on. The user clicks Save. Needs the examiner at the LUCID window (a click in LUCID's AI panel).

what.description: what to produce

format.description: images/video only: tiff16 (default for images), tiff, tiff32f, png16, png, bmp, avi-raw (default for video), …

range.description: images/video: which frames (default: current frame for images, all for video)

tools.name: ask_user
tools.description: Ask the user a question and wait for the answer (offer options when you can). Use it for ambiguous requests or choices that are the examiner's to make. Needs the examiner at the LUCID window (a click in LUCID's AI panel).

question.description: the question

options.description: suggested answers (buttons); the user can also type

sites.name: ecadforge.app
sites.description: Open Altium, KiCad, Gerber and CircuitJSON designs locally in your browser. View schematics, PCB layouts, fabrication layers, 3D boards, BOMs and diagnostics without uploading your files.

tools.name: list_designs
tools.description: List ECAD designs loaded in the current browser session.

tools.name: list_components
tools.description: List loaded design components by reference-designator prefix.

tools.name: list_nets
tools.description: List declared schematic or PCB net names for one loaded design; pin connectivity is not required.

tools.name: review_design
tools.description: Summarize loaded design coverage, metadata, and diagnostics.

tools.name: audit_design
tools.description: Return parser, metadata, and connectivity issues for loaded designs.

tools.name: crossref_net
tools.description: Compare one schematic net against matching PCB pads.

tools.name: compare_schematic_pcb
tools.description: Compare all schematic nets against matching PCB pads.

tools.name: export_schematic_pcb_comparison
tools.description: Return a local JSON comparison artifact with session-stable design and component identifiers. Save its content locally; no feedback submission or network write is required.

tools.name: summarize_design
tools.description: Return an agent-friendly loaded-design summary.

tools.name: find_components
tools.description: Find loaded components by refdes, MPN, value, description, or footprint.

tools.name: query_bom_item
tools.description: Find normalized BOM rows by refdes, MPN, or text pattern.

tools.name: list_pin_connections
tools.description: List compact pin-to-net rows for one loaded component.

tools.name: query_net
tools.description: Return direct pin membership for one loaded schematic net.

tools.name: list_component_types
tools.description: Return loaded component counts by reference-designator prefix.

tools.name: list_diagnostics
tools.description: Return parser diagnostics for loaded designs.

tools.name: compare_bom_pcb
tools.description: Compare normalized BOM rows against matching PCB components.

tools.name: list_single_pin_nets
tools.description: List schematic nets with exactly one connected pin.

tools.name: query_pcb_component
tools.description: Return PCB placement, pads, and model metadata for one component.

tools.name: query_pcb_net
tools.description: Return physical PCB membership for one routed net.

tools.name: summarize_pcb
tools.description: Summarize loaded PCB board, placement, routing, and stackup data.

tools.name: list_design_rules
tools.description: List compact normalized PCB design rules.

tools.name: review_fabrication_readiness
tools.description: Review loaded PCB data for fabrication-readiness signals.

tools.name: search_nets
tools.description: Search declared schematic or PCB net names by regex; pin connectivity is not required.

tools.name: search_components_by_refdes
tools.description: Search loaded components by reference designator regex.

tools.name: search_components_by_mpn
tools.description: Search loaded components by MPN regex.

tools.name: search_component_descriptions
tools.description: Search loaded components by description regex.

tools.name: query_component
tools.description: Return one loaded component with all known pin connections.

tools.name: query_xnet_by_net_name
tools.description: Trace loaded design connectivity starting from a net.

tools.name: query_xnet_by_pin_name
tools.description: Trace loaded design connectivity starting from a component pin.

tools.name: prepare_issue_report
tools.description: Request support or report an ECAD Forge page bug, feature request, or WebMCP discovery/tool problem on GitHub. Prepares a title, body and issue URL without submitting. Works without a loaded design. Use an authenticated GitHub tool or open the returned URL to submit; check existing issues first. Include generic reproduction steps, expected/actual behavior and relevant tool names. Do not include private design data, file names, paths, prompts or secrets. If WebMCP is unavailable, use /llms.txt or the Request support link.

description.description: Public report: reproduction steps, expected and observed behavior, or requested capability. No private session data.

tools.name: submit_agent_feedback
tools.description: Send ECAD Forge maintainers a generic missing-feature request or reproducible WebMCP limitation. This sends the supplied summary to Analytics. Use only when useful; never include design contents, file names, paths, project/component/net identifiers, conversation prompts, personal data or secrets. Describe the capability or behavior generically. Submission requires network access and does not change the design.

summary.description: Generic capability need or limitation only; no private design or conversation data.

tools.name: list_public_topics

tools.name: get_public_topic
tools.description: Topic metadata: description, cover, Brief/preview availability, archive + podcast access. Private Topics: owner only.

topicId.description: Topic id (e.g. topic:uuid). Defaults to the Topic on this page.

tools.name: get_latest_brief
tools.description: Full Brief digest + URL. 5m: current day for everyone; pass dateKey only if you follow (archive). Public: full only while following — otherwise use get_public_topic_preview. Private custom: owner only. No brief.debug.

topicId.description: Topic id (e.g. topic:uuid). Defaults to the Topic on this page.

dateKey.description: Archive day (YYYY-MM-DD). Followers / private owners only; guests get current day.

briefId.description: Specific Brief id. Followers / private owners only.

tools.name: get_public_topic_preview
tools.description: Preview a user-made Public Topic (not 5m): takeaway, top story titles, source count, follow CTA. Not the full Brief.

topicId.description: Topic id (e.g. topic:uuid). Defaults to the Topic on this page.

tools.name: get_brief_newsletter
tools.description: Shareable copy plus canonical URL. Full copy when entitled (5m current day, follow, or private owner). Preview copy if you are not following a Public Topic.

topicId.description: Topic id (e.g. topic:uuid). Defaults to the Topic on this page.

dateKey.description: Archive day (YYYY-MM-DD). Followers / private owners only; guests get current day.

briefId.description: Specific Brief id. Followers / private owners only.

tools.name: copy_share_link
tools.description: Return the canonical Topic URL to share. Read-only; does not send email.

topicId.description: Topic id (e.g. topic:uuid). Defaults to the Topic on this page.

tools.name: explain_fiveminutebrief
tools.description: Explain FiveMinuteBrief (5m, Public, and Custom Topics) and return /public-topics, /plans, and /signup URLs.

tools.name: start_signup
tools.description: Navigate this tab to the signup form. Does not fill or submit credentials. On /signup the form is a separate declarative signup tool.

tools.name: start_login

tools.name: get_podcast_show
tools.description: Podcast RSS + per-app launch URLs (including Apple). 5m guests/non-followers (including admin who is not following): public ad show, no ?code=. Followers and private-Topic owners: private ad-free ?code= feed. Public Topic not followed: follow required (no code). Does not open an app (use open_podcast_app).

topicId.description: Topic id (e.g. topic:uuid). Defaults to the Topic on this page.

tools.name: get_podcast_episode
tools.description: Latest episode this viewer may hear: title, date, duration, listen URL, enclosure. 5m guests get ?variant=public (ad). Followers/owners get the private file. Not the archive.

topicId.description: Topic id (e.g. topic:uuid). Defaults to the Topic on this page.

tools.description: Podcast app buttons for a Topic (same set as Listen anywhere). Without topicId: the catalog of app ids. Private feeds: Apple, Overcast, Pocket Casts, Castro, Podcast Addict only.

topicId.description: Topic id (e.g. topic:uuid). Defaults to the Topic on this page.

tools.name: open_podcast_app
tools.description: Open a Topic’s show in a podcast app (topicId + app id). Opens a new tab/deep link; does not replace the page. Guests cannot open a private feed.

topicId.description: Topic id (e.g. topic:uuid). Defaults to the Topic on this page.

app.description: Podcast app id from list_podcast_apps (apple, spotify, overcast, …).

tools.name: list_my_topics
tools.description: Dashboard Topics you own or follow (private custom included): generation status and latest card take. Sign-in required.

tools.name: follow_public_topic
tools.description: Follow a 5m or Public Topic (uses a follow slot). Guests must start_login. Slot limits return PLAN_LIMIT. Confirms in-page.

topicId.description: Topic id (e.g. topic:uuid). Defaults to the Topic on this page.

tools.name: unfollow_public_topic
tools.description: Unfollow a 5m or Public Topic. A Public Topic creator who unfollows gets preview only. Confirms in-page.

topicId.description: Topic id (e.g. topic:uuid). Defaults to the Topic on this page.

name.description: Topic name (required). Same field as the Create Topic form.

whatToCover.description: Optional: what to cover. Description is generated from the first Brief.

voiceId.description: Optional podcast voice id. Defaults to the site default.

tools.name: get_topic_generation_status

topicId.description: Topic id (e.g. topic:uuid). Defaults to the Topic on this page.

tools.name: retry_first_brief
tools.description: Re-enqueue first Brief (same credit/lock rules as topic-page Try again). Does not wait. Paid + credit. Confirms in-page.

topicId.description: Topic id (e.g. topic:uuid). Defaults to the Topic on this page.

tools.name: open_plans

note.description: Optional short note shown as a sticky chip on the page.

topicId.description: Topic id (e.g. topic:uuid). Defaults to the Topic on this page.

note.description: Optional short note shown as a sticky chip on the page.

tools.name: highlight_podcast_moment
tools.description: Jump the in-page player (script marker or estimate) and highlight the matching story when audio exists.

topicId.description: Topic id (e.g. topic:uuid). Defaults to the Topic on this page.

story.description: Story id or title to highlight and seek toward.

note.description: Optional short note shown as a sticky chip on the page.

tools.name: highlight_topic_card
tools.description: Scroll to and outline one Topic card on the catalog or dashboard (5m, follow CTA, or queued state).

topicId.description: Topic id (e.g. topic:uuid). Defaults to the Topic on this page.

note.description: Optional short note shown as a sticky chip on the page.

tools.name: highlight_plan_gate
tools.description: Outline credits, follow, or upgrade after create_topic / follow_public_topic was refused.

gate.description: Which refused control to point at.

topicId.description: Topic id (e.g. topic:uuid). Defaults to the Topic on this page.

note.description: Optional short note shown as a sticky chip on the page.

tools.name: clear_highlights
tools.description: Remove agent paint and notes. Restores the page.

tools.name: ask_this_brief

Returns a grounded answer + citations, then highlights matching stories/sources. Not a Brief digest (use get_latest_brief). No web search, no new Brief.

topicId.description: Topic id (e.g. topic:uuid). Defaults to the Topic on this page.

question.description: Question about this Brief’s clustered stories and cited sources.

dateKey.description: Archive day (YYYY-MM-DD). Followers / private owners only.

briefId.description: Specific Brief id. Followers / private owners only.

tools.name: login
