denseStars.description: Show the dense background star field

deepSky.description: Show Messier objects, planets and the Moon

nightMode.description: Red-light mode for night-time instrument use

daylightMode.description: Use real daylight or remove daylight for simulation

showHiddenStars.description: Show stars that are present but hidden

tools.name: save_observation_results
tools.description: Saves only observation statuses explicitly reported by the user for every target in a Mission. It does not invent or infer observations, and it preserves the Mission creation-time prediction snapshot. Overwriting a Mission that already has saved results requires confirm:true. A successful save returns an undoToken valid for 5 minutes; pass it back as { "undoToken": "..." } to restore the previous record (or remove a newly created one).

results.description: Exactly one user-reported result per Mission target

status.description: The user's observation status

confirm.description: Required as true when the Mission already has saved results and this call would overwrite them

undoToken.description: Token returned by an earlier save: restores the previous record instead of saving new results

tools.name: open_observation_results
tools.description: Selects a saved observation result and opens the human-facing Results screen. Without a missionId, uses the selected record or newest completed record. This tool does not recompute or modify results.

tools.name: capture_sky_snapshot
tools.description: Captures the currently rendered Sky canvas as a PNG, stores it in the app's snapshot storage, and returns its metadata. An optional missionId links the image to an existing Mission. The tool does not return a large base64 image; use the returned browser download URL or the Snapshots screen.

missionId.description: Optional existing Mission ID to associate

download.description: Trigger a browser download in addition to saving; defaults to true

tools.name: list_sky_snapshots
tools.description: Lists saved Sky snapshot metadata in newest-first order. PNG blobs are not included.

limit.description: Maximum metadata records to return

tools.name: get_sky_snapshot_metadata
tools.description: Returns one saved Sky snapshot's observation conditions and storage metadata without returning the PNG blob.

tools.name: propose_plan
tools.description: Stages a ghost plan proposal for human review without creating a Mission. The proposal lists one item per star; the human accepts or rejects items on the Plan screen, and commit_proposal materializes the accepted subset into a real Mission. Proposing again replaces the pending proposal.

dateTime.description: ISO 8601 observation date and time; a value without an offset is interpreted in the site's timeZone

starIds.description: One to five star IDs, e.g. returned by predict_visible_stars

tools.name: commit_proposal
tools.description: Materializes the pending proposal's accepted items into a real Mission via the normal creation path (immutable from then on). Pass acceptedStarIds to commit a subset, or omit to commit the items currently marked accepted.

acceptedStarIds.description: Subset of the proposal's star IDs to commit (defaults to the accepted items)

tools.name: plan_stale
tools.description: Reports whether the pending proposal's assumptions still hold: it compares the site and observation dateTime the proposal was computed against with the current ones. A stale proposal's per-star predictions may no longer be accurate.

tools.name: get_sky_conditions
tools.description: Fetches live cloud cover (total and per layer) and visibility for the current observation site from Open-Meteo, plus a 0-100 stargazing score. Advisory only: weather is not part of the geometric visibility prediction and the tool fails cleanly when the service is unreachable.

tools.name: compare_dark_sky_sites
tools.description: Fetches Open-Meteo cloud cover and visibility for the current site plus reference dark-sky sites (or a caller-provided list of 2-8 sites), scores each for stargazing, and reports the clearest one. Sites that fail are reported individually instead of failing the whole comparison.

sites.description: Optional site list; defaults to the current site plus reference dark-sky locations

tools.name: generate_observation_guide
tools.description: Prepares a print-ready Observation Guide using the Mission creation-time site, date, and fixed star predictions. It includes a deterministic Mission Sky Snapshot as inline SVG and generates a PDF directly in the browser. The tool does not return the PDF binary to the Agent; it starts a browser download, while the Guide screen also offers Print / Save as PDF.

timeZone.description: Optional IANA time zone for printed time

sites.name: jobbbler.com
sites.description: Find explainable technology roles, monitor the right opportunities, and apply with human-controlled agent assistance.

tools.name: plan_job_workflow
tools.description: Pass one required goal: complete_job_hunt, find_roles, compare_roles, save_search, monitor_search, manage_saved_search, prepare_application, withdraw_application_consent, enable_recovery, or recover_workspace. Search, compare, and prepare default to headless; use follow only when asked to open them. Jobbbler-managed email updates use monitor_search, not a client-side scheduler. Returns route-aware decision steps. Advisory only; grants nothing.

goal.description: The outcome to plan for.

tools.name: get_search_filters
tools.description: Read Jobbbler's exact search vocabulary: accepted categories, work models, seniorities, salary options, and sort orders. Use when an enum is unclear, not before every search; search_jobs already documents common values.

tools.name: search_jobs
tools.description: Search Jobbbler's source-backed catalog directly. Do not use external job sources when the person asks for this site's tools. Pass only the criteria the person stated; leave categories, employmentTypes and unknownPolicy unset so nothing is narrowed silently. For ‘Berlin or remote’, pass locations=['Berlin'] with remoteOrLocations=true. Default headless keeps the page unchanged; use follow only when asked to watch. Results include IDs, salary, seniority, evidence, and a cursor.

query.description: Technology role, skill, or outcome to search for.

categories.description: Technology job functions to include.

employmentTypes.description: Employment arrangements that matching roles must use.

locations.description: Cities, countries, or regions to include. Do not use Remote as a place; use remoteOrLocations for requests such as ‘Berlin or remote’.

remoteOrLocations.description: Match listed locations OR remote roles anywhere. Requires a location; for remote-only, use workModels=['remote'].

skills.description: Technology skills to prefer in match ranking.

excludeKeywords.description: Keywords that must not appear in a matching role.

salary.description: Annual, monthly, or hourly compensation constraint.

postedWithinDays.description: Maximum age of a posting in days.

sort.description: Result ordering.

tools.name: open_job_details
tools.description: Navigate to a role returned by search_jobs while preserving the current criteria. Every Jobbbler tool stays registered across the navigation.

jobId.description: A job ID returned by search_jobs.

tools.name: prepare_application
tools.description: Use one job ID the person selected to create or reopen its private application and return the application ID, URL, and next tool. Default headless keeps the current page; use presentation=follow only when the person asks to open it. This grants no preparation authority, shares no candidate data, and submits nothing.

jobId.description: A job ID returned by search_jobs or get_job_details.

presentation.description: headless keeps the current page unchanged; follow opens the application workspace.

tools.name: get_applications
tools.description: Use optional limit and offset with a current or recovered owner session to return application and job IDs, each application's page href, role details, status, update time, receipt availability, and nextOffset without returning answers, contact data, or credentials.

limit.description: Number of applications to return, from 1 to 20. Defaults to 10.

offset.description: Zero-based offset into applications sorted newest first. Defaults to 0.

tools.name: open_jobbbler_page
tools.description: Use a supported page name plus exact job or application IDs when required to open Search, Saved searches, Applications, the WebMCP guide, a comparison, or one application, and return the opened page and URL without changing stored data.

tools.name: enable_workspace_recovery
tools.description: Use the current owner session and the person's exact email to start, then its challengeId and the six-digit code the person supplies to finish, returning only the phase and next tools; this is not data consent, not submission approval, and not email-update permission.

email.description: Email explicitly supplied by the person for optional recovery.

challengeId.description: Exact challengeId returned by this tool's start action.

code.description: Six-digit code explicitly supplied by the person in the agent client.

tools.name: recover_jobbbler_workspace
tools.description: Use the verified email the person supplies to start, then its exact recoveryId and six-digit code to finish, returning only the phase and next tools without exposing the email, code, owner, or session credential.

email.description: Verified email explicitly supplied by the person in the agent client.

recoveryId.description: Exact recoveryId returned by this tool's start action.

code.description: Six-digit code explicitly supplied by the person in the agent client.

detail.description: summary for display; exact for criteria reusable by save_job_search or request_search_alert.

tools.name: get_job_details
tools.description: Read one technology role's full description, requirements, provenance, compensation, known unknowns, and fit evidence. Pass the exact Jobbbler role ID in jobId. It works from any page and changes nothing.

jobId.description: A Jobbbler job ID returned by search_jobs or another Jobbbler tool.

tools.name: compare_jobs

Default headless keeps the current page; use presentation=follow only when the person asks to open the comparison. Never call it with one role; search or ask for the missing target first.

jobIds.description: Two or three distinct job IDs returned by Jobbbler tools.

items.description: A Jobbbler job ID returned by search_jobs or another Jobbbler tool.

presentation.description: headless keeps the current page unchanged; follow opens the visible comparison.

tools.name: get_comparison
tools.description: Read the current one-to-three-role comparison, including fit evidence, compensation, provenance, and unknowns. Use when the user asks about the comparison already open. If the person asks which role is best, which to keep, or which to remove without giving a ranking preference, ask for the person's ranking criteria instead of asking them to choose a role ID.

tools.name: remove_job_from_comparison

tools.name: add_job_to_comparison

jobId.description: A job ID from search_jobs or get_job_details to add to this comparison.

offset.description: How many saved searches to skip, starting with the newest. If omitted, skip none.

tools.name: get_application_readiness
tools.description: Pass the application ID returned by prepare_application as draftId. Read safe completion counts, missing field keys and labels, receipt state, and the next useful action without returning private answers.

draftId.description: An application ID returned by prepare_application.

tools.name: request_application_assistance
tools.description: Pass the application ID returned by prepare_application as draftId. The person's request to apply is the authority: assistance is granted at once, without a question, and propose_application_updates is the next step. Nothing is sent to an employer until the person approves the exact completed application.

draftId.description: An application ID returned by prepare_application.

tools.name: decide_application_assistance
tools.description: Assistance is granted automatically; call this only when the person asks to stop the agent's help. Pass draftId, the requestId from request_application_assistance, and withdraw (or declined) to revoke active assistance bound to it; it never shares data or submits.

draftId.description: An application ID returned by prepare_application.

requestId.description: The server-issued assistance request ID.

decision.description: The person's explicit decision in the agent client.

tools.name: propose_application_updates
tools.description: Pass draftId for the application and update up to 24 distinct fields from known facts in one call. For cover_letter, use the full role and local CV context but send only the finished letter. Ask once, in a single message, for every fact readiness reports as missing; skip optional fields the person never mentioned.

draftId.description: An application ID returned by prepare_application.

patches.description: Answers from known facts only. For cover_letter, use get_job_details and local CV facts; send only the letter. Ask; never invent missing facts.

fieldKey.description: A field key reported by get_application_readiness.

value.description: A truthful answer written from supplied facts. A cover_letter should be complete and role-specific, not a generic motivation sentence.

tools.name: request_submission_review
tools.description: Pass draftId for the completed application. Freeze its exact field values and return them to the already-authorized agent client. Present every value before asking for one final decision. The review link is an optional browser fallback; this submits nothing.

draftId.description: An application ID returned by prepare_application.

tools.name: decide_application_submission
tools.description: Pass draftId for the same application, the exact requestId and draftVersion returned by request_submission_review, and the person's explicit decision. Never approve on the person's behalf. On approval, store disclosure consent, seal the unchanged payload, submit once, and return a receipt; on decline, share and submit nothing.

draftId.description: An application ID returned by prepare_application.

requestId.description: The review request ID returned by request_submission_review.

draftVersion.description: The exact draft version returned with the review request.

decision.description: The person's explicit decision in the agent client.

tools.name: withdraw_application_consent
tools.description: Pass draftId for the owner-accessible application to immediately withdraw every live consent-based permission tied to it. This stops future processing under that consent; it does not erase the application or retract a submission already sent.

draftId.description: An application ID returned by prepare_application.

sites.name: merge-queue-eta.vercel.app
sites.description: Merge Queue safely combines concurrent human and agent edits with a semantic three-way merge.

tools.name: get_workspace_summary
tools.description: Read the live project board, its revision, people, tasks, active agent branch, and the valid next actions. Use this before proposing changes.

includeArchived.description: Include archived tasks. Defaults to false.

tools.name: begin_agent_branch
tools.description: Open an isolated agent branch from the current workspace revision. Staged work will not mutate the human's live board until a reviewed merge is committed.

tools.description: Stage up to 12 bounded task updates on the active agent branch. These are proposals only and do not change the live human workspace.

tools.name: stage_new_task
tools.description: Stage one new task on the active agent branch without changing the live human workspace.

tools.name: get_branch_diff
tools.description: Read the active branch's staged operations and summarize human changes made since the branch began.

tools.name: preview_merge
tools.description: Run a deterministic three-way merge between the branch base, the human's current board, and the agent proposal. Opens the visible review drawer and never commits changes.

tools.name: get_merge_conflicts
tools.description: Read unresolved semantic conflicts from the current merge preview. This does not resolve conflicts; those decisions belong to the human in the page.

tools.name: request_merge
tools.description: Open the merge review UI and request explicit human approval. This tool never commits on its own; the human must resolve conflicts and click Commit merge in the page.

tools.name: get_branch_status
tools.description: Read whether the branch is open, conflicted, awaiting approval, merged, or aborted.

tools.name: abort_branch
tools.description: Discard the active agent branch without changing the human's live workspace.

tools.name: revert_last_merge
tools.description: Revert the latest committed merge as a new workspace revision. Use only after the human explicitly asks to undo the merge.

tools.name: get_seating_plan
tools.description: Read the live wedding floor plan, table capacities, meal needs, locked placements, revision, and active agent branch. Use before proposing changes.

tools.name: begin_seating_branch
tools.description: Open an isolated seating branch. Guest moves remain proposals while the human continues editing the live floor plan.

tools.name: stage_guest_changes
tools.description: Stage bounded table, meal, accessibility, lock, or note changes for up to 20 guests. Never changes the live floor plan.

tools.name: preview_seating_merge
tools.description: Three-way merge the original seating plan, current human placements, and agent proposal. Opens a visible human review and never commits.

tools.name: get_seating_conflicts
tools.description: Read unresolved seating or meal conflicts without deciding them for the human.

tools.name: request_seating_merge
tools.description: Open the seating review and request human approval. The human alone resolves conflicts and commits in the page.

tools.name: get_seating_branch_status
tools.description: Read whether the seating branch is open, conflicted, awaiting approval, merged, or aborted.

tools.name: abort_seating_branch
tools.description: Discard the proposed seating branch without changing the live floor plan.

tools.name: revert_seating_merge
tools.description: Revert the latest seating merge after the human explicitly asks to undo it.

tools.name: get_catalog
tools.description: Read the live merchant catalog, prices, inventory, publication state, collections, price locks, revision, and active branch. Use before proposing changes.

tools.name: begin_merchandising_branch
tools.description: Open an isolated merchandising branch while the merchant keeps editing the live catalog.

tools.name: stage_product_changes
tools.description: Stage bounded price, inventory, collection, feature, protection, or publication changes for up to 20 products. Never changes the live catalog.

tools.name: preview_catalog_merge
tools.description: Three-way merge the branch base, current merchant edits, and agent proposal. Opens a visible review and never publishes.

tools.name: get_catalog_conflicts
tools.description: Read unresolved price, inventory, or publication conflicts without deciding them for the merchant.

tools.name: request_catalog_merge
tools.description: Open the catalog review and request human approval. The merchant alone resolves conflicts and publishes in the page.

tools.name: get_merchandising_branch_status
tools.description: Read whether the merchandising branch is open, conflicted, awaiting approval, merged, or aborted.

tools.name: abort_merchandising_branch
tools.description: Discard the merchandising branch without changing the live catalog.

tools.name: revert_catalog_merge
tools.description: Revert the latest catalog merge after the merchant explicitly asks to undo it.

sites.description: A little space, reimagined. Arrange furniture, explore layouts, and make a room your own with RoomDex.

tools.name: inspect_room
tools.description: Inspect room dimensions, derived floor area, architecture, circulation, shared view, revision, and a bounded furniture page with geometry, finish, mounting, support, and art intent.

inventoryOffset.description: Zero-based inventory offset. Follow nextInventoryOffset until hasMore is false.

inventoryLimit.description: Maximum inventory entries requested. The response may return fewer to stay within its output budget.

tools.description: Return up to five newest committed room changes retained locally, with actor, revision, timestamp, and bounded summary, newest first.

tools.description: List RoomDex's curated furniture catalog with real-world dimensions, placement type, and support-surface capability.

tools.name: analyze_layout
tools.description: Analyze the current room for furniture collisions, room-boundary errors, tight clearances, blocked wall openings, and circulation obstructions in the walkway or entry landing.

tools.name: compare_layouts
tools.description: Simulate every built-in room arrangement without changing the room. Compare fit, moved catalog pieces, issue counts, chair-to-window distance, chair-to-lamp clearance, and sofa-to-chair clearance before applying one.

tools.name: measure_clearance
tools.description: Measure horizontal edge-to-edge clearance in feet between two uniquely named room items.

tools.description: Inspect one named item's exact geometry, finish, mounting, support, and artwork direction at the current revision. Does not select or change it.

target.description: Unique visible furniture name, such as Floor lamp.

tools.name: preview_furniture_move
tools.description: Simulate moving one named item and its supported objects without changing the room or selection. Returns whether the move can apply and the resulting layout issue counts. A valid move may still have clearance or collision concerns; inspect the analysis before committing.

target.description: Unique visible furniture name, such as Floor lamp.

x.description: Center position across the room in feet.

y.description: Base elevation above the floor in feet.

z.description: Center position from back to front in feet.

anchor.description: Unique visible name of the anchor item.

side.description: Preferred side when relation is beside.

wall.description: Wall to place the item against.

offset.description: Position along the selected wall, measured from its center.

elevation.description: Bottom elevation above the floor for a wall-mounted item.

tools.description: Select one named item in the shared canvas and inspector, or use null to clear the selection. Does not alter furniture, create an undo step, or advance the room revision.

anyOf.description: Unique visible furniture name, such as Floor lamp.

expectedRevision.description: Optional room revision from a prior read. The write is rejected if the room changed.

tools.description: Translate up to twelve named floor pieces together by an offset in feet. Attached surface objects follow automatically. Commits one undoable change or rejects the entire move if affected items overlap, leave the room, block openings, or obstruct circulation.

items.description: Unique visible furniture name, such as Floor lamp.

targets.description: One to twelve distinct, uniquely named room items.

offsetX.description: Horizontal group offset in feet; defaults to zero.

The rest of the street stays managed. Use detachClone for a single object and convertStreetToShapes for the whole street. Name the generator by the segment entity and the component name on it; segments list their generators as 'street-generated-*' components in the scene state.

Name the clone by the segment entity, the generator component on it and the clone slot index (0-based creation order from the start of the segment; a slot already detached has no clone, and the generator's skip array lists the detached placements as 'x z' keys), or omit all three to detach the currently selected clone. Optional position/rotation place the detached entity.

segmentId.description: ID of the street-segment entity carrying the generator

tools.name: managedStreetCreate
tools.description: Create a new managed street from a cross-section (array of segments, listed from one edge to the other). If the scene has geographic context (setLatLon / Google 3D Tiles), the tiles already supply the surroundings: do NOT add boundary segments, buildings or other land-use models unless the user explicitly asks for synthetic surroundings — the cross-section should normally begin and end with sidewalks. For each segment, omit surface/color/elevation/direction/generated to receive the type's preset — the same content a user gets by picking that type in the sidebar (e.g. bike-lane → green asphalt, bike-arrow stencils, cyclists; bus-lane → BUS ONLY stencil, buses; sidewalk → pedestrians). Call listSegmentPresets to see them. Only supply `generated` to override a preset. Returns entityId, width, presetsApplied, warnings and a readBack of what actually mounted.

length.description: Length of the street in meters (default: 60)

position.description: Position as space-separated x y z values (e.g., "0 0 0")

segments.description: Array of segment definitions for the street

items.description: Segment definition

type.description: Type of segment. Valid values: "drive-lane", "bike-lane", "sidewalk", "parking-lane", "divider", "grass", "rail", "bus-lane", "boundary". "boundary" is SYNTHETIC flanking land use (buildings, waterfront, fences) for scenes without geographic context — it renders outside the travelled way at the street edge and auto-tiles models edge-to-edge (`variant` + `side`, no `generated` needed). Do not add boundaries when the scene has a location: the Google 3D Tiles already show the real surroundings and synthetic buildings would overlap them.

surface.description: Surface material (e.g., "asphalt", "concrete", "grass", "sidewalk", "gravel", "sand", "planting-strip", "none", "solid"). Optional for building segments — the variant supplies a sensible default. For hatched dividers use `generated.striping` with `striping: "hatched"` instead of a surface.

elevation.description: Vertical offset in meters (0 = road level, 0.15 = curb/sidewalk height). Negative values are not supported.

direction.description: Traffic direction ("none", "inbound", "outbound")

variant.description: Variant preset for `type: "boundary"` segments. Valid values: "brownstone" (urban mixed-use SM3D blocks), "suburban" (detached single-family houses), "arcade" (arched street-front buildings), "water" (seawall), "grass" (fenced grass strip), "parking" (fenced parking lot), "sp-mixeduse" (StreetPlan mixed-use), "sp-residential" (StreetPlan single-family/townhouse), "sp-big-box" (StreetPlan big-box stores), "custom" (preserve existing settings). Setting variant on a boundary segment auto-fits the model array; do NOT pass `generated.clones` for boundaries unless you want full control. Only meaningful when `type: "boundary"`, and only for scenes without geographic context (see `type`).

side.description: Side of the street the segment sits on. Required for `type: "boundary"` (controls placement outside the travelled way edge and which direction the models face). Valid values: "left", "right". Frame of reference is the street's own cross-section, not the camera: "left" is the inbound side and "right" the outbound side (right-hand-drive convention; swap for left-hand-drive countries). segments[0] sits at the first edge; getGeoContext reports the compass bearing of each edge.

generated.description: Optional generated content — omit to receive the type preset. Two different systems: `clones` places 3D models (vehicles, cyclists, trees, lamps, furniture — any listMixins id with generator "clones"); `stencil` paints flat road markings (arrows, sharrows, words like BUS ONLY — only ids with generator "stencil"). Never put a vehicle in `stencil` or a marking in `clones`.

mode.description: Clone mode ("random", "fixed", "single")

modelsArray.description: Comma-separated 3D model ids from listMixins (generator "clones"), e.g. "sedan-rig, box-truck-rig" or "bus". Unknown ids are rejected.

spacing.description: Distance between models in meters

modelsArray.description: Comma-separated painted-marking ids (generator "stencil"), e.g. "bike-arrow", "sharrow", "word-bus, word-only". Unknown ids are rejected — use listMixins.

spacing.description: Distance between stencils

direction.description: Stencil orientation

side.description: Side of segment ("left", "right")

type.description: Type of segment. Valid values: "drive-lane", "bike-lane", "sidewalk", "parking-lane", "divider", "grass", "rail", "bus-lane", "boundary". tools.name: takeSnapshot
tools.description: Render a snapshot of the scene and return it as a JPEG image (max 1280 px wide) plus `metadata.camera` (tilt, isTopDown, isNorthUp, screenUpBearingDeg, lat/lon). To VERIFY placement or alignment use type "plan": top-down, north-up, whole scene — the only view with absolute orientation. One plan snapshot beats several angled ones; do not take multiple perspective shots to check position. In a geospatial scene "plan" is the default when type is omitted.

caption.description: Optional caption to display with the snapshot

focusEntityId.description: Optional entity ID to focus on before taking the snapshot

type.description: View to render. "plan": top-down, north-up, whole scene — use this to judge orientation and alignment (default in geospatial scenes). "focus": current view, or framed on focusEntityId (default otherwise). "birdseye", "straightOn", "closeup": presentation shots of the first managed street — not orientation references; use them only when the user asks for a picture, not to verify.

zoomOut.description: Plan view only: altitude multiplier applied after the top-down fit. 1 = street fills the frame; 2 (default in geospatial scenes) shows about twice the ground extent so the real roads around the street are visible; use 3-4 for a wider context check. The result reports `metadata.groundExtent` (visible metres across the viewport).

tools.name: setLatLon
tools.description: Set the latitude and longitude for the scene, which triggers elevation lookup and activates the Google 3D Tiles map layer. Signed-in users can set any location; signed-out sessions are limited to locations within California (demo).

tools.name: getScene
tools.description: Return the full 3DStreet scene as Format-1 JSON (the same data the Save button writes), plus the currently selected entity id and scene id.

tools.name: getEntity
tools.description: Return one entity serialized as Format-1 JSON.

entityId.description: The DOM id of the entity to read

tools.name: getSelectedEntity
tools.description: Return the entity the user has selected in the scene graph (or null).

tools.name: selectEntity
tools.description: Programmatically select an entity (mirrors clicking it in the scene graph). Pass an empty entityId to clear selection.

entityId.description: The DOM id to select; pass empty string to clear selection.

tools.name: listMixins
tools.description: List available A-Frame mixins (model assets) grouped by category. Optional category arg filters to one category.

tools.name: listSegmentPresets
tools.description: List the per-type segment presets (surface, color, elevation, default direction, and the generated stencils/clones/pedestrians) that managedStreetCreate and managedStreetUpdate apply when a segment omits those fields — identical to picking the type in the editor sidebar. Read this before composing a cross-section so you only override what you need.

tools.name: getSessionInfo
tools.description: Return the running build version, signed-in user, current scene id/url/title, whether edits are being persisted (`saved`: cloud scene exists and the user is its author, so autosave is on — otherwise call saveScene), and viewport size.

tools.name: getManagedStreet
tools.description: Return one managed-street entity as Format-2 segment-list JSON (reverse of the parser, reads live DOM so it includes per-segment edits).

entityId.description: The DOM id of a managed-street entity

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Step the editor history back by one command.

tools.name: redo
tools.description: Step the editor history forward by one command.

tools.name: getGeoContext
tools.description: Return the exact relationship between scene coordinates and geographic coordinates: the lat/lon at the scene origin, the compass bearing of the scene axes, the camera pose (tilt, north-up state, lat/lon), and optionally one entity converted to lat/lon + compass heading (for a managed street: centerline bearing and both endpoint coordinates), and/or a lat/lon converted to a scene world position. Conversions use the live Google 3D Tiles WGS84 frame, so they match where the map renders. Errors with a reason when the geo layer is off or still loading — call setLatLon or retry.

entityId.description: Optional entity to describe geographically (position → lat/lon, heading → compass bearing; managed streets also get endpoint coordinates).

latitude.description: Optional latitude to convert to a scene world position (pair with longitude).

longitude.description: Optional longitude to convert to a scene world position (pair with latitude).

tools.name: orientPlanView
tools.description: Move the editor camera to a top-down, north-up plan view using the same compass action a user clicks (perspective camera, framing the whole scene), optionally pulled back by `zoomOut`. Returns the resulting camera state (tilt, needle angle, isTopDown, isNorthUp, lat/lon, groundExtent in metres). Use before takeSnapshot when judging alignment or orientation; focusCamera reframes around one entity and is NOT a reliable orientation reference. takeSnapshot type "plan" does this for you.

zoomOut.description: Altitude multiplier after the fit: 1 = scene fills the frame, 2 = twice the ground extent (see surrounding real roads), 3-4 = wide context.

tools.name: focusCamera
tools.description: Frame an entity in the viewport (same effect as double-clicking it in the scene graph). This reframes and rotates the view around that entity, so the result is NOT a north-up or alignment reference — use orientPlanView + takeSnapshot for that.

entityId.description: The DOM id to focus on

tools.name: saveScene
tools.description: Persist the current scene to the signed-in user's cloud account. Edits are NOT saved until this is called once; afterwards autosave persists every further edit in this tab. Returns sceneId and sceneUrl — always give the user the sceneUrl (or remember the sceneId) so the work can be reopened in a later session with loadScene. Signed out: opens the sign-in modal and errors; ask the user to sign in, then retry. If the open scene belongs to someone else, saves a copy.

title.description: Optional scene title to set before saving (e.g. "Geary Blvd BRT").

tools.name: loadScene

tools.name: list_page_tables

Use a returned tableKey with the other table tools. tools.name: get_form_schema
tools.description: Read the schema of a form open on the user's screen: fields with labels, kinds, current values, validation errors, and selectable options (option tokens). A form is open ONLY when it is listed as a `form` surface in the current page context (the page_capabilities hint sent with the message, or get_current_page_context). If no `form` surface is listed, no form is open — there is nothing to read, so do not call this. Call it before filling a listed form. Omit form_id only for initial discovery when exactly one form is open and no intended form_id is already known. Keep using the intended form_id after failures; never omit or replace it to recover from a closed-form error.

form_id.description: The open form to target, from get_current_page_context form capabilities. Optional only for initial discovery when exactly one form is open and no intended form_id is already known. Keep using the intended form_id once known; never omit or replace it to recover from a closed-form error.

tools.name: set_form_fields
tools.description: Fill fields on a form open on the user's screen. Only usable when a `form` surface is listed in the current page context; read it first with get_form_schema. Values must match the field kind from get_form_schema; select fields take an option token and multiselect fields take an array of option tokens. Returns validation errors so you can self-correct. Changed fields are highlighted for the user and can be undone. Never claim to submit the form — ask the user to review the highlighted fields and submit.

form_id.description: The open form to target, from get_current_page_context form capabilities. Optional only for initial discovery when exactly one form is open and no intended form_id is already known. tools.name: set_skill_editor_fields
tools.description: Edit the skill editor open on the user's screen. Sets the name (when is_skill_name_editable), description, and/or replaces the document body markdown in the live editor WITHOUT saving. Content replaces require the editor_revision from a fresh get_skill_editor_state read and are rejected if the user edited in between. Never claim to have saved — ask the user to review the editor and save.

skill_name.description: New name for the skill or agent being edited. Only accepted when get_skill_editor_state reports is_skill_name_editable, and expected whenever it reports a skill_name_hint. For editor_kind ask_ramp_skill this is only settable while creating a new skill and must be lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens as separators; for editor_kind procurement_agent it is the free-text agent title.

content_markdown.description: Replacement markdown for the full document body. Replaces the entire live document, so include unchanged parts. Do not open it with the skill or agent name as an H1: the name is a separate field set with skill_name, and a leading H1 is moved into that field. Requires expected_editor_revision.

expected_editor_revision.description: The editor_revision returned by get_skill_editor_state that this update was computed from. Required with content_markdown; the update is rejected if the user has edited the draft since that read.

tools.name: get_procurement_report_editor
tools.description: Read the procurement report open in the fullscreen editor, including unsaved changes, section stable IDs, and editor_revision. Read before editing. The execution_id comes from the procurement_agent_report_editor page capability. This is the report, not the agent instructions or request fields.

tools.name: edit_procurement_report
tools.description: Edit sections of the live procurement report draft WITHOUT saving. Requires execution_id and expected_editor_revision from get_procurement_report_editor. Apply at most 20 edits per call; read again before each additional batch. Update only the requested sections; omitted header/body fields and all other sections are preserved. Preserve source citations and links. Put section headings in header, not body_markdown. Insert after a stable ID, or at the start with after_stable_id=null. Remove deletes only that section. Edits apply atomically and fail if the user changed the draft since your read. Read again after a conflict. Never claim changes are saved; the user reviews the editor and clicks Save.

tools.name: get_spend_program_editor_state
tools.description: Read the live state of the spend program editor open on the user's screen: program shape, every settings section in the shape set_spend_program_settings accepts, the names and available choices behind referenced ids (policies, merchant categories, accounting coding), approval and change request workflow pointers, custom request form questions (intake) and change order form questions (change_request_intake, purchase order programs only) with their ids, and editor_revision. Includes unsaved edits. Call this before the first write and again after a revision conflict.

tools.name: prepare_spend_program_workflow_edit
tools.description: Save current questions as a draft before using them in Blank Canvas workflow conditions. Requires expected_editor_revision from a fresh get_spend_program_editor_state read. Use form="request" for approval workflows and form="change_request" for dedicated change request workflows. Change request preparation saves the request form first. Await success, then pass the returned template_id and custom_form_collection_log_entry_uuid to GetBlankCanvasConditionFields and ApplyBlankCanvasWorkflowEdits. The template_id is resolved after preparation; use it instead of earlier editor or autosave pointers. Prepare again after question edits; discard cached condition fields when the returned revision changes. On failure, reread the editor and prepare again rather than falling back to published questions. Does not save or publish the program or edit the workflow.

expected_editor_revision.description: The editor_revision returned by get_spend_program_editor_state that this update was computed from. The update is rejected if the editor changed since that read.

tools.name: set_spend_program_settings
tools.description: Edit settings of the spend program editor open on the user's screen WITHOUT saving. Send one or more complete sections as read from get_spend_program_editor_state with your changes applied; fields left out keep their current value. Requires the editor_revision from a fresh read and is rejected if the editor changed since. Returns applied fields, fields that could not be applied for this program shape, and the form's validation errors so you can self-correct. Never claim to have saved.

tools.name: set_spend_program_intake_questions
tools.description: Create, name, rename, or remove request form sections and add, update, or remove custom questions in the spend program editor open on the user's screen WITHOUT saving. Requesting programs only. form selects the target: request (default) edits the request form and takes ids from intake.sections; change_request edits the change order form requesters fill in when changing an approved request and takes ids from change_request_intake.sections, which only purchase order programs have. Read the target form from get_spend_program_editor_state first: it lists every question with its id, and built-in fields you must not duplicate. Section operations are only supported for form=request. add_section names the sole untitled section if present, preserving its questions, or appends a new section. update_section names or renames an existing section by section_id while preserving its id, questions, and conditions. remove_section deletes the section and all its questions and clears dependent visibility or required-when rules, including change order rules. A section containing a protected question cannot be removed. Removing the last section leaves a fresh empty untitled section. Create sections first, then use created_section_ids from the result as section_id when adding questions. If the request form uses sections, every section must have a meaningful, nonblank title and at least one question before saving or publishing. When organizing a form into sections, use update_section to name any existing unnamed sections. A sole section with title=null is the default unsectioned form and may remain unnamed and empty, including after removing the last section. Leave new question descriptions blank unless the user explicitly requests them; do not repeat the question title. Only add question types listed in that form's available_question_types; other types are rejected for this program. Select choices carry ids: when replacing a question's choices, pass { id, label } for every choice you kee…

operations.description: Applied in order. Create sections first, then use their returned ids to add questions. Add a controlling question in one call and reference its returned id before adding dependent questions.

Use the returned created_section_ids to add questions in a subsequent call. Every section needs at least one question before saving or publishing.

question_id.description: id from the target form (intake.sections or change_request_intake.sections) in get_spend_program_editor_state.

choices.description: Replacement choices, in order. Pass { id, label } with an id from the target form's sections to keep or rename an existing choice so visibility and required-when rules that depend on it keep working; pass a bare string to add a new choice. Existing choices left out are removed; removal is rejected when another question's or section's rule depends on the choice. The type cannot change.

id.description: Choice id from the target form (intake.sections or change_request_intake.sections) in get_spend_program_editor_state. Ids change when the user saves, so read them from the same editor_revision you write against.

visible_when.description: Replace the visibility rule; null always shows the question.

anyOf.description: Show this question only when an earlier answer matches.

question_id.description: id of an EARLIER question of type BOOLEAN, TEXT_SINGLE_SELECT, or TEXT_MULTI_SELECT that controls whether this question is shown.

equals.description: For a BOOLEAN controlling question: show when the answer equals this value.

is_one_of.description: For a select controlling question: show when the answer is one of these choice labels.

question_id.description: id from the target form (intake.sections or change_request_intake.sections) in get_spend_program_editor_state.

expected_editor_revision.description: The editor_revision returned by get_spend_program_editor_state that this update was computed from. The update is rejected if the editor changed since that read.

tools.name: set_spend_program_change_request_selection
tools.description: Set how change requests to approved requests are approved in the spend program editor open on the user's screen: reuse the approval workflow ("same-as-spend-request") or point at a dedicated Blank Canvas change request workflow ("custom") after a server tool created it. Requires the editor_revision from a fresh get_spend_program_editor_state read and is rejected if the editor changed since. Applies to the live editor WITHOUT saving.

selection.description: same-as-spend-request: change requests reuse the approval workflow of the original request. custom: change requests use their own Blank Canvas workflow.

workflow_id.description: Required for custom: Blank Canvas workflow id of the change request workflow, as returned by the server tool that created it. The workflow must exist and approve change requests (protected_workflow_identifier SPEND_REQUEST_CHANGE_ORDER_APPROVALS); other ids are rejected.

draft_template_id.description: For custom: draft template id of that workflow when it has unsaved draft edits. Omitting it leaves the current draft pointer unchanged when workflow_id matches the workflow already selected; when workflow_id selects a different workflow, omitting it points at that workflow with no draft.

expected_editor_revision.description: The editor_revision returned by get_spend_program_editor_state that this update was computed from. The update is rejected if the editor changed since that read.

sites.name: atlas-preview.ohdsi.org
sites.description: Home

tools.name: add_criterion
tools.description: Propose adding one criterion to the cohort. The user sees a confirmation card and accepts or rejects.

domain.description: OMOP domain

operator.description: Measurement value operator (only for Measurement domain)

value.description: Threshold value (only for Measurement domain)

tools.name: add_criteria
tools.description: Propose adding multiple criteria to the cohort with AND/OR logic. ALWAYS provide a `name` describing the rule (e.g. "On metformin or sulfonylurea", "Excludes pregnancy"); never omit it. Prefer add_inclusion_rule when cardinality or temporal constraints are needed.

name.description: Short, human-readable label for this group (REQUIRED). E.g. 'Confirmatory T2DM treatment', 'Exclude Type 1 DM'.

domain.description: OMOP domain

operator.description: Measurement value operator (only for Measurement domain)

value.description: Threshold value (only for Measurement domain)

tools.name: add_qualifying_criterion
tools.description: Restrict the ENTRY EVENT itself rather than the person — the editor's "Restrict initial events". Use when the qualifying event must coincide with something, e.g. an inpatient visit, a diagnosis recorded on the same admission. Distinct from add_criterion, which qualifies the person over a window.

isExcluded.description: Optional exclusion flag for concept-set items

tools.name: set_censor_window
tools.description: Bound the study period with fixed dates (YYYY-MM-DD): nobody is followed before startDate or after endDate, whatever their observation. Use when the user names a study window ('2015 to 2019') — without it the cohort spans the whole database and the counts answer a different question.

startDate.description: Earliest date to include, YYYY-MM-DD.

endDate.description: Latest date to include, YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.name: set_era_collapse
tools.description: Gap in days below which two stretches of cohort membership are merged into one era (the editor's era collapse). Default 0 — a person who leaves and re-enters counts as two episodes. Raise it when brief gaps should not split a person's follow-up.

gapDays.description: Merge stretches separated by fewer than this many days.

tools.name: set_event_limits
tools.description: Choose which qualifying events count, per person. 'first' is the new-user / first-diagnosis design — one row per person at their earliest qualifying event; 'all' (the default) puts a person in the cohort once per qualifying event, so counts mean episodes rather than people. Set this deliberately whenever the design is about new users or incident disease; phenotype_patterns reports what accepted definitions of the condition use.

entryEvents.description: Which entry events qualify a person ('Cohort entry on' in the editor).

qualifyingEvents.description: Which qualifying events the inclusion rules apply to ('Apply rules to').

inclusionRuleEvents.description: Which events remain after the inclusion rules are applied.

tools.name: add_demographic_criterion
tools.description: Restrict the cohort by age or sex — the criteria that have no concept set. Use for "adults", "age 18 and over", "women aged 40 to 70": pass minAge / maxAge in years and/or sex. Without this a cohort NAMED for adults contains children, because nothing in the definition says otherwise. Added as an inclusion rule, which is where CIRCE keeps demographic criteria.

minAge.description: Lowest age in years, inclusive. 18 for adults.

sex.description: Restrict to one sex. Omit for any.

name.description: Rule name shown in the editor. Defaults to a label like "Age 18+".

tools.name: use_concept_set
tools.description: Use an EXISTING saved concept set in the cohort being built, by its id from search_existing_concept_sets. Prefer this over rebuilding the same set concept by concept: it reuses the definition the user already curated, and stays in step with it. The host reads the saved set's concepts and adds the criterion. Use group 'entry' for a qualifying event, 'inclusion' to require it, 'exclusion' to require its absence.

conceptSetId.description: Id of the saved concept set (from search_existing_concept_sets).

group.description: Where the criterion goes. Defaults to 'inclusion'.

name.description: Rule name to show in the editor. Defaults to the concept set name.

tools.name: remove_inclusion_rule
tools.description: Remove an inclusion rule from the cohort being edited, by its name (as shown in the editor) or its id. Use this when the user asks to drop, delete or undo a rule you added — do not rebuild the cohort to get rid of one rule.

name.description: Exact rule name as it appears in the cohort.

id.description: Rule id, if you have it.

tools.name: remove_entry_event
tools.description: Remove one entry event from the cohort being edited, identified by the concept it was built from. Use when the cohort qualifies on several entry events and the user wants one dropped. To replace the entry event entirely, call set_entry_event instead.

conceptId.description: Concept id of the entry event to remove.

conceptName.description: Concept name, if the id is not to hand.

tools.name: set_entry_event
tools.description: Set the cohort's primary qualifying entry event. Replaces any existing entry event.

isExcluded.description: Optional exclusion flag for concept-set items

tools.name: set_observation_window
tools.description: Set the prior + post observation window (in days) around the entry event. priorDays = days of continuous observation required BEFORE entry; postDays = days of continuous observation required AFTER entry.

tools.name: add_exit_criterion
tools.description: Define how a patient exits the cohort. Strategy: end_of_observation = end of continuous observation period; fixed_duration = N days after entry; continuous_drug = persistence-window-driven exit.

offset.description: Days offset (for fixed_duration and continuous_drug)

persistenceWindow.description: Gap days between exposures for continuous_drug

surveillanceWindow.description: Trailing days after final exposure for continuous_drug

isExcluded.description: Optional exclusion flag for concept-set items

concept.description: Drug concept whose exposure eras define the exit (for continuous_drug)

tools.name: set_censor_event
tools.description: Add a censoring criterion that ends a patient's time-at-risk when the event occurs.

isExcluded.description: Optional exclusion flag for concept-set items

tools.name: create_standalone_concept_set
tools.description: Create a NEW reusable concept set on the server via WebAPI, saved globally and usable across cohorts. This is NOT the default: criteria capabilities (set_entry_event, add_criterion, add_criteria, add_inclusion_rule) already build the concept set they need inside the cohort definition, which is what most phenotypes want. Reach for this only when the set is meant to be reused — the user asked for a standalone concept set, or the same set is needed by several cohorts or analyses. The host persists it, then attaches it to the open cohort if there is one, otherwise navigates to the concept-set editor. Use a clinical, descriptive name (e.g. 'Statins', 'Inhaled corticosteroids', 'Type 2 Diabetes diagnoses').

name.description: Concept set name (REQUIRED). Clinical and descriptive.

isExcluded.description: Optional exclusion flag for concept-set items

tools.name: navigate_to
tools.description: Suggest moving the user to a different view in ATLAS. The user sees a 5s undo toast after the navigation is applied (no approval card). Always include a one-sentence `reason` so the toast is self-explanatory. Each `view` accepts a specific set of params — see the route manifest.

view.description: Route name from the Atlas3 route manifest (resources/routes.manifest.json — generated by Atlas3/scripts/emit-route-manifest.mjs). Edit the manifest to add a new view.

reason.description: One short sentence; surfaced in the undo toast.

tools.name: add_inclusion_rule
tools.description: Add an inclusion rule: a named group of criteria with AND/OR logic and optional cardinality (AT_LEAST/AT_MOST count) or temporal window. Prefer this over add_criteria when the model needs cardinality or temporal constraints.

temporalWindow.description: Optional temporal window for the criteria, relative to the index (cohort entry) start date.

startDays.description: Window start in days vs index start: negative = before index, 0 = at index, null = all time prior.

endDays.description: Window end in days vs index start: positive = after index, null = all time after. Default 0 (index date).

domain.description: OMOP domain

operator.description: Measurement value operator (only for Measurement domain)

value.description: Threshold value (only for Measurement domain)

tools.name: create_feature_analysis
tools.description: Persist a NEW feature analysis (covariate definition) on the server. The user sees an approval card; on accept, ATLAS navigates to the editor. `type` controls the design shape: PRESET (built-in OHDSI preset id as a string), CRITERIA_SET (JSON object with conceptSets + criteria), or CUSTOM_FE (raw SQL string). Pass `design` accordingly.

type.description: PRESET for built-in feature library entries; CRITERIA_SET for custom criteria sets; CUSTOM_FE for raw SQL.

design.description: Type-dependent: string for PRESET/CUSTOM_FE; object for CRITERIA_SET.

tools.name: create_characterization
tools.description: Persist a NEW cohort characterization on the server. REQUIRES at least one cohort and at least one feature analysis attached. Before calling this you MUST have called search_existing_cohorts and search_existing_feature_analyses to find the IDs. If neither result has matches, do NOT call this — instead, propose creating the missing prerequisite (cohort first, then feature analysis) and emit a navigate_to(view='cohort-new' or 'feature-analysis-new').

cohorts.description: REQUIRED. One or more cohorts to characterize. Each item is {id, name} pulled from search_existing_cohorts results.

featureAnalyses.description: REQUIRED. One or more feature analyses to apply. Each item is {id, name} pulled from search_existing_feature_analyses results.

tools.name: create_pathway
tools.description: Persist a NEW pathway analysis on the server. Only `name` is required; sensible OHDSI defaults are applied for the rest (combinationWindow=30, minCellCount=5, maxDepth=5, allowRepeats=false). Pass target/event cohort references when the user has named them.

allowRepeats.description: Whether the same event can repeat in a pathway (default false)

tools.name: generate_analysis
tools.description: Run a SAVED analysis against a data source, the same as clicking Generate in the editor. Use after the analysis exists (create_pathway / create_characterization / create_incidence_rate returned an id). Results appear in the editor when the job finishes. Omit sourceKey to use the source the user is currently working against.

analysisType.description: Which kind of analysis to run. REQUIRED.

sourceKey.description: CDM source key, e.g. EUNOMIA. Defaults to the current source.

tools.name: update_concept_set
tools.description: Apply a partial edit to an existing standalone concept set: rename, change description, append items, or replace items. Mutates the open editor; user clicks Save to persist. Use itemsToAdd to append (skips duplicate conceptIds), items to fully replace.

id.description: Concept set id (REQUIRED).

isExcluded.description: Optional exclusion flag for concept-set items

items.description: Full replace — overwrites the existing items array.

isExcluded.description: Optional exclusion flag for concept-set items

itemsToAdd.description: Append-only — skips items whose conceptId already exists.

tools.name: update_feature_analysis
tools.description: Apply a partial edit to an existing feature analysis: rename, change description, change type/domain/statType, or replace the design payload. Mutates the open editor; user clicks Save to persist.

id.description: Feature analysis id (REQUIRED).

design.description: Type-dependent: string for PRESET/CUSTOM_FE; object for CRITERIA_SET. Replaces the existing design entirely.

tools.name: update_characterization
tools.description: Apply a partial edit to an existing characterization: rename, change description, replace or extend cohorts/featureAnalyses. Each cohort and feature-analysis ref is {id, name} from search_existing_* results.

id.description: Characterization id (REQUIRED).

tools.name: update_pathway
tools.description: Apply a partial edit to an existing pathway analysis: rename, change description, replace or extend target/event cohorts, tweak combinationWindow / minCellCount / maxDepth / allowRepeats.

id.description: Pathway id (REQUIRED).

tools.name: update_incidence_rate
tools.description: Apply a partial edit to an existing incidence-rate analysis: rename, change description, replace or extend target/outcome cohort ids, tweak timeAtRisk or studyWindow.

id.description: Incidence-rate id (REQUIRED).

tools.name: create_incidence_rate
tools.description: Persist a NEW incidence-rate analysis on the server. Only `name` is required; the time-at-risk window defaults to {start: StartDate +0, end: EndDate +0} which means 'from cohort start to cohort end'. Provide a custom timeAtRisk when the user describes a specific risk window (e.g., '365 days after exposure' → start: StartDate +0, end: StartDate +365).

startDate.description: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD

endDate.description: ISO date YYYY-MM-DD

tools.name: save_cohort
tools.description: Persist the CURRENTLY OPEN cohort to the WebAPI so it gets a stable id. Call this AFTER the user has accepted the cohort's entry event + criteria, and BEFORE creating any analysis (incidence rate / pathway / characterization) that must reference this cohort by id — analyses can only target SAVED cohorts. Returns the saved cohort id. Optional name/description override the open cohort's current values.

name.description: Optional clinical name to save under (defaults to the open cohort's name).

sites.name: deskmate-cc.vercel.app
sites.description: Deskmate

tools.name: get_desktop_state
tools.description: Return which apps and folders exist on this desktop, which windows are open, and which one has focus, plus what this browser lets the page do. Call it first: what the user is looking at decides whether they are writing, filming or editing, and a note about the timeline is useless to someone standing in front of a camera.

tools.name: list_scripts
tools.description: Return every script saved on this desktop with its title, how many lines it has and its estimated spoken runtime. A line is one spoken beat plus an optional shot direction, and it is the unit the teleprompter advances through. Returns titles and lengths, not the words; call get_script for those.

tools.name: get_script
tools.description: Return one saved script in full: every line with what is said out loud, its shot direction, and how long that line takes to say. Read it before suggesting anything about the take or the edit, because the shot directions say what the footage is meant to show.

tools.name: get_open_script
tools.description: Return the script the writer has open in front of them right now, taken from the live fields rather than the saved record, so a line they are still typing is included. Says which line and which field their caret is in and what they have selected. Use this before answering anything phrased as 'this line', 'what I just wrote', or 'this bit'.

tools.name: get_prompter_state
tools.description: Return what the teleprompter is showing at this instant: the line the speaker is on, its shot direction, how far through the script they are, and whether it is scrolling or paused. Only meaningful while the prompter is up. If it is running, the person is mid-performance: keep any answer to one short sentence, or say nothing.

tools.name: get_recorder_state
tools.description: Return what the Camera is doing right now: idle, armed with a live preview, or recording, how many seconds into the take it is, and the teleprompter script loaded into it with the exact line they are on. Check this before suggesting anything. Someone mid-take cannot read a paragraph of advice, and you cannot start or stop a recording yourself.

tools.name: list_clips
tools.description: Return the clip library: everything recorded or imported on this desktop, oldest first, including sound files, which have kind "audio". Each clip says which of the person's own library folders it is in, if any. Clips are held in this browser and have never been uploaded anywhere, so this is the only place they can be listed.

kind.description: Optional. Restrict to one kind of clip. Sound files are "audio".

tools.name: get_timeline
tools.description: Return the cut as it stands: every segment in order with its in and out points, look, speed and where it starts in the finished piece. This is the working edit, not the clip library. Use list_clips for what is available to add.

tools.name: get_selection
tools.description: Return the segment the user currently has selected in the Editor. Use this before answering anything phrased as 'this clip', 'this bit', or 'tighten this'. Nothing outside this tab knows what is selected.

tools.name: get_playhead
tools.description: Return where the playhead is in the Editor preview and which segment sits under it. Use it to talk about the moment the user is actually looking at.

tools.name: get_graphics
tools.description: Return the motion graphics on this cut, both the ones you have proposed and the ones the editor has accepted, with their timings and settings. Call it before proposing, so you build on what is there instead of stacking a second title card on top of the first.

tools.name: propose_graphic
tools.description: Propose a motion graphic over the cut. It appears immediately on the timeline as a dashed, unconfirmed overlay the editor can watch and then accept or reject; it is not in the video until they accept it. Choose a type from: lower_third: A name and a role sliding in at the lower left. For introducing a person or a place. title_card: A full-frame headline over a wash. For a chapter break or the opening line. caption_pop: Words appearing one at a time along the bottom, in time with speech. For a line worth landing. callout_arrow: An arrow and a label pointing at a spot in the frame. For a screen recording, or anything you need someone to look at. stat_badge: A number that counts up, with a label under it. For a figure you say out loud. progress_bar: A bar filling across the bottom over its own duration. For a walkthrough with steps. Call get_timeline first so the timing lands on the right moment, and get_selection if they asked for it over "this bit".

text.description: The words that appear on screen. Not a description of them. Short: this is a graphic, not a paragraph.

subtext.description: Optional second line: a role, a source, a label under a number.

start.description: Seconds from the start of the finished cut, from get_timeline.

palette_role.description: A role, not a colour. The theme decides what it looks like, so this works in light and dark.

point.description: callout_arrow only. Where to aim, as fractions of the frame: {x: 0.5, y: 0.5} is the middle.

reason.description: One sentence, shown to the editor on the card. Why this, here.

tools.name: propose_graphic_change
tools.description: Propose a change to a graphic that is already on the cut: retime it, move it, reword it, recolour it. The original stays exactly as it is until the editor accepts the change, so rejecting costs them nothing. Send only the fields you are changing.

tools.name: propose_script_line
tools.description: Write a line into the draft the person has open: a new beat, or a rewrite of one that is already there. It appears in their Draft view, at the line you aimed it at, as a dashed suggestion they accept or discard; it is not in their script until they do. This is where writing and researching happen, so it is where suggestions belong. Call get_open_script first, so you write from their research and their current draft rather than from memory, and so you do not repeat a line already waiting for them. One line per call: a beat is one thing said to camera, not a paragraph. Several lines is several calls, in order.

text.description: The words they say out loud. Their voice, not yours, and short enough to say in one breath.

note.description: Optional shot direction for this beat: camera, b-roll, tone, what is on screen.

index.description: Which line this concerns, from get_open_script. With mode 'insert' the line lands before this one, so 0 is a new opening and the line count appends at the end.

mode.description: 'insert' adds a beat, 'replace' offers a rewrite of the line at index. Default insert.

reason.description: One sentence shown under the suggestion. Why this line, here.

tools.name: offer_folder
tools.description: Tell this page about a folder you have access to, so it can offer to import it. Send the folder's name and a list of what is in it; the page draws it on the desktop as a ghost folder the person can accept or ignore. For text files (.txt, .md, .srt, .vtt) you may include the contents and they land immediately as scripts. Do not try to send video: it will not fit, and the page asks the person to point the browser at the folder instead. This does not read anything from their machine and does not import anything by itself.

name.description: The folder's name as they would recognise it.

files.description: What is in the folder. Names only, unless it is a text file you can include.

size.description: Bytes, if you know. Shown to them, never used to decide anything.

text.description: Text files only. The contents, which become a script with one line per paragraph. Omit for video.

reason.description: One sentence, shown when they hover it. Why this folder is worth importing.

tools.name: get_offered_folders
tools.description: Return the folders you have offered this page and whether the person accepted them. Check it before offering again, so you do not offer the same folder twice, and to find out whether the files you expected are actually in their library now.

tools.name: list_ai_skills
tools.description: Return the skills this workstation offers you: name, when to use it, and how long it is. These are instructions the person put here for you, about how they want this kind of work done. Call this early, once, and remember what is on the list. It returns descriptions only, so it is cheap; when one of them matches what you have been asked to do, call load_ai_skill to get it.

tools.name: load_ai_skill
tools.description: Return the full text of one skill from list_ai_skills, so you can follow it. Load a skill when its 'use_when' matches the task in front of you, not speculatively. Once loaded, treat it as the person's instruction for this kind of work and apply it for the rest of the session; they can see which skills you have taken.

tools.name: get_composition
tools.description: Return the motion graphics, sound and format layered over the cut, with every timing in both seconds and frames. Call it before proposing anything so you build on what is there instead of stacking a second title card on the first, and so you know the format: a graphic laid out for 16:9 reads differently once the same composition is reframed to 9:16.

tools.name: get_transcript
tools.description: Return what is said in the cut, word by word, with the second each word lands on. The timing comes from the teleprompter: the Camera recorded which script line was on screen at which second of the take, so this is derived from what they actually performed, not guessed from the page. Times are positions in the finished edit, already adjusted for every trim, reorder and speed change, so a time from here can be handed straight to propose_layer or propose_cut. Pass `quote` to locate a specific phrase.

quote.description: Optional. Words to find, as they were said. Case and punctuation are ignored. Returns every occurrence with exact start and end seconds, which is how you turn 'the bit where I talk about the stack' into a range.

include_words.description: Optional. Include the full word-by-word array. Default false, which returns the text and the beats and is usually enough; ask for words when you need to time a caption to individual words.

tools.name: get_composition_code
tools.description: Return the composition as the TSX file it compiles to: one Sequence per graphic, with the exact frame it starts on and how many frames it runs for. Read it when you need to reason about the composition as a whole rather than one layer at a time, or to quote a specific line back to the person you are helping.

tools.name: propose_layer
tools.description: Propose a motion graphic over the cut. It appears at once on the timeline as a dashed, unconfirmed layer that previews live, and it is not in the video until the editor accepts it. Choose from: title_card: A full-frame headline over a dimmed wash, with an optional line under it. For an opening or a chapter break. lower_third: A name and a role on a panel at the lower left. For introducing a person, a place or a tool. caption_pop: Words appearing one at a time along the bottom, in time with speech. Pass word timings from the transcript and each word lands on the frame it is said. bullet_list: A titled list whose rows arrive one at a time. For anything you say as 'three things' or 'first, second, third'. comparison_cards: Two or three bordered cards side by side, each with a heading and a line. For 'before and after', 'this versus that', or a set of options. process_flow: Numbered steps joined by a line, revealed one at a time. For a process, a pipeline, or anything you narrate as a sequence. stat_badge: A number that counts up from zero, with a label under it. For a figure you say out loud and want to land. callout_arrow: A label with an arrow pointing at a spot in the frame. For a screen recording, or anything you need someone to look at. progress_bar: A bar filling across the bottom over its own duration, with an optional label. For a walkthrough with steps, or a chapter you want a sense of the length of. code_card: Monospaced lines on a dark panel, arriving one at a time. For a command, a snippet, a file tree, or a stack you are listing out. quote_card: An oversized quote mark, the line, and who said it. For something worth attributing, or your own sentence worth repeating on screen. text: Free text you control completely: typeface, size, colour, alignment, tracking, a plate behind it, an outline, and how it enters and leaves. Use this when none of the preset graphics fit, or when the styling is the point. shape: A rectangle, ellipse, pill, triangle, line, arrow,…

text.description: title_card, lower_third, caption_pop, bullet_list, comparison_cards, process_flow, stat_badge, callout_arrow, progress_bar, code_card, quote_card, text only. The figure, with its furniture: '40%', '$1.2M', '3×'. The number inside is what counts up.

subtext.description: title_card, lower_third, stat_badge, quote_card only. The role, the title, the one-line description.

eyebrow.description: title_card only. A small tracked label above it: a chapter number, a section name.

timings.description: caption_pop only. Optional. One frame number per word, from get_transcript, relative to this layer's start. Without it the words are spread evenly, which is close but never exact.

items.description: bullet_list, comparison_cards, process_flow, code_card only. One entry per card. Write each as 'Heading: the line under it'; a colon, en dash, or pipe splits them.

point.description: callout_arrow, text, shape only. Free placement as fractions of the frame: {x: 0.5, y: 0.5} is the middle. Leave it out to use `position` instead.

size.description: text only. Type size in points of a 1080-tall frame, 12 to 220. It scales with the format, so one number is right in every aspect ratio.

align.description: text only. left, center or right. Also decides which way the block grows from its anchor.

tracking.description: text only. Letter spacing as a fraction of the size, -0.05 to 0.4. Small caps labels want about 0.07.

line_height.description: text only. Multiple of the size, 0.8 to 2.4. Defaults to 1.18.

backdrop.description: text only. none, box, or scrim. A box is a plate behind the words; a scrim dims the whole frame so text over busy footage stays readable.

outline.description: text only. Outline thickness in points of a 1080 frame, 0 to 12. Reads on any background, which a plate does not.

opacity.description: text, shape only. 0 to 1. Below 1 the words are see-through, for a watermark or a caption you do not want to fight the picture.

animation.description: text, shape, effect only. How it enters and leaves: fade, rise, drop, slide_left, slide_right, pop, grow, none.

shape.description: shape only. rect, ellipse, pill, triangle, line, arrow, ring or star.

width.description: shape only. As a fraction of the frame width, 0.01 to 1.5.

height.description: shape only. As a fraction of the frame height, 0.01 to 1.5.

fill.description: shape only. A hex like "#F54E00", a palette role, or "none" for an outline only.

stroke.description: shape only. Outline colour: a hex, a palette role, or "none".

stroke_width.description: shape only. Outline thickness in points of a 1080 frame, 0 to 40.

radius.description: shape only. Corner rounding for a rect, in points of a 1080 frame.

effect.description: effect only. dip, flash, vignette, grain, scanlines, glitch, letterbox or wash. `dip` fades to the colour and back out, which is the transition you put over a cut.

strength.description: effect only. 0 to 1. Half is usually plenty; grain above 0.4 is a stylistic choice rather than an accident.

tag.description: effect only. An internal label. The editor uses it to find the transition it put on a clip; leave it out.

at_seconds.description: Seconds from the start of the finished cut. From get_timeline or get_transcript.

duration_seconds.description: Seconds on screen. Leave it out for the component's own sensible default.

position.description: A named anchor. For `text` and `shape` you can send `point` instead and place it anywhere.

palette_role.description: A palette role, or a hex like "#F54E00". Roles resolve against the live theme, so one spec is legible in light and dark; send a hex when the exact colour is the point. Roles: accent, warm, cool, positive, plain, invert.

reason.description: One sentence, shown to the editor on the card. Why this, here.

tools.name: propose_blank_clip
tools.description: Propose a blank clip on the timeline: a solid colour that takes up time, for building motion graphics on when there is no footage to put them over. Stage this first when they ask for a title sequence, an animated card or a graphics-only piece, then propose layers over it with propose_layer. It appears as a dashed block on the base track and is not part of the cut until the editor accepts it.

seconds.description: How long it lasts. Five is a sensible title card.

colour.description: The ground, as a hex like "#101018". Leave it out for the theme's own dark ground, which is the safe choice.

reason.description: One sentence, shown to the editor. Why this, here.

tools.name: propose_layer_change
tools.description: Propose a change to a layer that is already on the cut: retime it, move it, reword it, recolour it. The original stays exactly as it is until the editor accepts the change, so rejecting costs them nothing. Send only the fields you are changing; everything else is kept.

component.description: Change what kind of graphic it is. The fields it takes change with it.
