tools.name: propose_sound
tools.description: Propose sound: a one-shot effect on a moment, or a music bed under a stretch of the cut. Effects are synthesised in the browser, so there is nothing to load and nothing to license; pick one of: hit (A short, low, percussive thump. For a title card landing.) pop (A bright click. For a list row or a caption word arriving.) whoosh (Filtered noise sweeping up. For anything sliding in from an edge.) riser (A pitch climbing to a stop. For building into a reveal.) tick (A dry tick. For a step in a process, or a counter.) chime (Two soft tones. For a result, a total, or a positive stat.) A music bed takes an existing clip from the library and ducks itself under speech automatically, using the transcript's word boundaries, so you do not need to shape the volume yourself.

kind.description: 'sfx' for a one-shot on a moment, 'music' for a bed under a stretch.

preset.description: sfx only. Which effect.

clip_id.description: music only. The clip to take the bed from, from list_clips.

at_seconds.description: Seconds from the start of the cut. For an effect under a graphic, use that graphic's at_seconds so they land together.

duration_seconds.description: music only. Leave it out to run to the end of the cut.

gain.description: 0 to 1. A bed under speech wants 0.1 to 0.25; above 0.4 it competes with the voice. An effect wants 0.4 to 0.8.

duck.description: music only. Duck under speech. Default true, and leaving it true is almost always right.

tools.name: propose_format
tools.description: Propose reframing the whole composition to a different aspect ratio. Every graphic is laid out as fractions of the frame, so this moves nothing and rewrites nothing: the same composition simply becomes 16:9, 9:16 or 1:1, with the safe margins that format needs. Use it when they mention shorts, reels, vertical or a square post.

format.description: landscape is 16:9, vertical is 9:16, square is 1:1

tools.name: propose_cut
tools.description: Propose removing a stretch of the cut. Give it a quote and it finds the words in the transcript and stages a cut over exactly them, which is how 'take out the bit where I stumble over the second point' becomes a precise range. It appears as a marked region on the timeline and nothing is removed until the editor accepts it. Removing footage is the most destructive thing in this app, so it is also the one most firmly behind a click.

quote.description: The words to cut, as they were said. Preferred over raw seconds: it is checked against the transcript, so it cannot land in the wrong place.

start_seconds.description: Use only when there is no transcript. Seconds into the finished cut.

end_seconds.description: Use only when there is no transcript.

reason.description: One sentence shown on the marker. Why this should go.

tools.name: propose_tidy
tools.description: Find every hesitation and every silence in the cut and stage a cut over each one, in a single call. Only mechanical things: 'um' and 'uh' and holes in the audio longer than about a second. It never proposes cutting a sentence for being weak, because that is a judgement and this is a list. Each one is marked separately on the timeline so they can be taken or left one at a time.

min_silence_seconds.description: How long a gap has to be before it counts as dead air. Default 1.1. Below about 0.8 you start cutting breaths, which makes the edit sound rushed.

sites.name: living-evidence.doralemon.chatgpt.site
sites.description: A Living Evidence document: a meta-analysis of the Pygmalion effect that you — and your AI agent — can cross-examine, re-run, and extend, right on this page.

tools.name: get_document_overview
tools.description: Orientation for agents: what this living document claims, the current state of its evidence base, which analyses its tools can run, and the rules of engagement. Call this first.

tools.name: list_claims
tools.description: List addressable claims, their document-registered rules, and canonical rule outcomes (not_run / passed / failed / inconclusive). Legacy status codes remain for compatibility. A rule outcome reports document-registered rule outcome only — not an independent judgment of truth, validity, risk of bias, or evidence quality.

tools.name: get_data_manifest
tools.description: Return the citeable scientific-state manifest: dataset identity, record and experiment counts, estimand definition, unit note, claim rules, provenance-completeness counts, risk-of-bias coverage, and SHA-256 state id. Records are omitted by default to protect context; set include_records=true for the full evidence table.

include_records.description: include every effect-size record with provenance and risk-of-bias fields (default false)

tools.name: get_studies
tools.description: Return the full effect-size evidence table with record and experiment counts, experiment cluster ids, yi/vi, moderators, sample sizes, source locator/DOI/derivation/verification provenance, and structured risk-of-bias state. Set include_pending=true to include proposals.

tools.name: run_meta_analysis
tools.description: Fit a meta-analytic model to the current evidence base and RENDER A FOREST PLOT into the document. method: REML or DL random-effects, or FE common-effect (FE assumes one common effect; tau2 is null by model assumption, not estimated as zero). p is a two-sided test of the pooled effect against zero. Optionally exclude specific study ids (e.g. to test sensitivity to one study). Returns pooled estimate, 95% CI, p, tau^2, I^2, and heterogeneity Q.

method.description: model / tau^2 estimator: REML or DL random-effects, FE common-effect (default REML)

tools.name: leave_one_out
tools.description: Leave-one-record-out sensitivity analysis: re-fit the random-effects model omitting each effect-size record in turn, and RENDER the plot into the document. Shows whether any single record drives the pooled result (min/max estimates, significance flips). It reports estimate changes and p<.05-status flips only — not stability of magnitude, dependence, moderators, heterogeneity, or bias diagnostics.

tools.name: subgroup_analysis
tools.description: Split the studies into subgroups, fit each subgroup separately, test the between-group difference, and RENDER a subgroup forest plot. For weeks, omit split_at to use 1 or provide another threshold; split_at is rejected for setting/tester (categorical fields split by value, so a threshold would be silently meaningless).

split_at.description: threshold for the numeric field weeks (group A: value <= split_at; default 1). Rejected for setting/tester.

tools.name: meta_regression
tools.description: Mixed-effects meta-regression of effect size on a numeric moderator (REML), RENDERING a bubble plot with the fitted line. cap truncates the moderator (cap=3 replicates the published Raudenbush model min(weeks,3)); it must be > 0 and is only accepted for moderator "weeks" — capping any other field is rejected rather than silently fitted. Returns slope, p, and R^2 (a boundary-clipped proportional reduction in estimated tau^2, with no uncertainty interval).

cap.description: optional truncation: x = min(field, cap). Must be > 0, and only accepted for moderator "weeks".

tools.name: funnel_check
tools.description: Small-study asymmetry diagnostics: render a funnel plot and run Egger's regression test. Asymmetry can have causes other than publication bias, and a non-significant result (especially at k≈19) is not evidence of absence of bias. Returns the intercept, p-value and an interpretation.

tools.name: cumulative_meta
tools.description: Retrospective cumulative meta-analysis in publication-year order: prefixes of the CURRENT corpus. It does not reconstruct which evidence was actually available or discoverable at each historical date. RENDERS the step plot.

tools.name: evaluate_claim
tools.description: Run one claim's document-registered rule. The analysis renders into the document and the badge reports passed / failed / inconclusive. It is not a truth, validity, bias, or evidence-quality rating. Legacy verdict codes remain in the response. Scope: document-registered rule outcome only — not an independent judgment of truth, validity, risk of bias, or evidence quality.

tools.name: propose_study
tools.description: Propose one independent SMD record. Source locator, quote, derivation, design, outcome/timepoint, experiment id, SMD variant/direction, collection frame and explicit risk-of-bias status are required. An assessed RoB label additionally requires instrument, assessor, date, source, and domain rationales; otherwise use not_assessed. DOI remains optional when none exists. Dependent records and incompatible estimands are rejected because this v1 package runtime does not model their covariance. Human approval accepts an extraction into the local evidence base; it does not independently verify it.

yi.description: standardized mean difference, coded in effect_direction

tester.description: whether the tester knew the expectancy assignment (aware|blind)

source.description: citation or URL for provenance

quote.description: short verbatim excerpt the extracted numbers were read from (required)

derivation.description: how yi and vi were derived, including the metafor measure or source cells used

source_url.description: resolvable source URL when available; the page does not fetch or verify it

source_locator.description: page, table, figure, row, cell, or supplement locator

doi.description: DOI when one exists; omit rather than inventing one

study_design.description: design relevant to interpreting this effect-size record

outcome.description: outcome represented by yi

timepoint.description: measurement time point represented by yi

experiment_id.description: unique experiment id; v1 rejects a second record with the same id because dependent effects are unsupported

record_role.description: what this row represents within its experiment

smd_variant_detail.description: required description when smd_variant is other

effect_direction.description: what a positive yi means, including contrast direction

collection_frame.description: eligibility/search frame defining what this evidence base attempted to collect

risk_of_bias_status.description: overall status; an assessed label requires all assessment metadata and remains author-supplied/unverified

risk_of_bias_assessor.description: person or team responsible for the assessment

risk_of_bias_source.description: citation, file, registry or record locating the assessment

risk_of_bias_overall_rationale.description: rationale for the overall judgment; stored verbatim and not checked against an instrument-specific algorithm

risk_of_bias_domains.description: instrument-specific domain judgments with a rationale

tools.name: get_audit_log
tools.description: Return the reload-persistent, append-ordered audit ledger. Every entry carries SHA-256 result_digest, previous_entry_hash and entry_hash. The chain detects edits and reordering; it does not prove author identity or provide a trusted timestamp. Use create_reproducibility_receipt to sign a state with the current browser-session key.

tools.name: get_reproducibility_status
tools.description: Return SHA-256 scientific-state identity, audit-chain verification, persistence scope and the latest signed receipt. Runtime/artifact hashes are signed claims but are not self-verified in-page; use the detached receipt verifier for exact artifact bytes. This distinguishes content integrity from authorship, peer review, primary-source correctness and preservation.

tools.name: create_reproducibility_receipt
tools.description: Create and visibly render an ECDSA P-256 signed receipt for the current scientific-state SHA-256 and audit-chain head. The signing key is generated for this browser session; pin its fingerprint externally before treating the signature as authorship evidence.

tools.name: set_hypothesis
tools.description: Set the hypothesis this workspace examines (1–500 characters). Shown at the top of the page and carried into the exported document.

text.description: the hypothesis, as one sentence (1–500 characters, not blank after trimming)

tools.name: add_claim
tools.description: Register a new addressable claim with its deterministic machine check. `test` is the declarative rule AST: {analysis, args?, focus?, verdicts:[{when:[{path,op,value}], verdict, reason}, …, {default:true, verdict, reason}]}. Ops: lt, le, gt, ge, eq, ne, abs_lt, abs_ge. Copy an existing claim's machine_check from list_claims as a template. Only the SHAPE is validated here — a claim is registered because it is well-formed, not because it currently passes. Use evaluate_claim afterwards to get a canonical passed / failed / inconclusive rule outcome.

id.description: optional claim id; auto-assigned (wc01, wc02, …) when omitted

statement.description: the claim in plain language, as a reader would argue about it

rule.description: human-readable description of the check ("Supported iff …")

test.description: the machine-check AST; mirrors what list_claims returns as machine_check

analysis.description: which page analysis produces the result the conditions read

args.description: arguments passed to that analysis, e.g. {"method":"REML"} or {"moderator":"weeks","cap":3}

focus.description: optional: pick one element of a result collection and expose it as ctx.f (e.g. one subgroup)

collection.description: array field of the result, e.g. "groups"

match_field.description: field of each element to match on, e.g. "group"

match_substring.description: substring that identifies the element, e.g. "≤ 1"

verdicts.description: walked in order; the LAST entry must be {default:true} and carries no conditions

when.description: all conditions must hold for this entry to match

path.description: dotted path into the analysis result, e.g. "moderator.p"

value.description: comparison value; numeric for every op except eq/ne

default.description: true on the final fallthrough entry only

reason.description: template rendered against the result, e.g. "pooled SMD {estimate}, p = {p}"

tools.name: export_document
tools.description: Write a self-contained single-file Living Evidence document with evidence provenance, registered rules, runtime, WebMCP tools and an embedded ECDSA-signed scientific-state receipt. Returns an exact artifact_sha256 plus a detached receipt that must be saved and checked externally for byte-level artifact verification; HTML is included only when requested.

include_html.description: return the full HTML in the response (large); default false

tools.name: atlas_overview
tools.description: Orientation for agents: what this evidence map is, how big the graph is, the one estimand cell’s current synthesis, the honesty labels that constrain what the map may claim, and which tool to reach for. Call this first.

tools.name: get_cell
tools.description: Everything hanging off the one estimand cell: its canonical definition, the live synthesis (spec + result), heterogeneity, the claims attached to it and the record counts per band of prior teacher–pupil contact.

cell_id.description: optional, and only this value: the map holds exactly one estimand cell (cell:teacher-expectancy-iq)

tools.name: list_claims
tools.description: The claims asserted about this cell, each with its human-readable rule, declarative machine-check AST and current registered-rule outcome. An outcome reports document-registered rule outcome only — not an independent judgment of truth, validity, risk of bias, or evidence quality. Legacy verdict codes remain for compatibility.

tools.name: evaluate_claim
tools.description: Run the deterministic machine check behind one claim against the full record set. It does not inherit synthesize exclusions. The node gets a registered-rule glyph (✓ passed / ✗ failed / △ inconclusive); this is document-registered rule outcome only — not an independent judgment of truth, validity, risk of bias, or evidence quality. Legacy verdict codes remain in the response.

claim_id.description: claim id from list_claims, e.g. c-textbook (the node form claim:c-textbook is accepted too)

tools.name: get_gaps
tools.description: The three typed gaps this map computes from the records themselves: a coverage gap along the weeks-of-prior-contact dimension, a replication gap and a verification gap. Each carries its collection frame — computed absence is not the same as "not searched".

tools.name: get_study_brief
tools.description: Compile a gap into a prospective study-design brief: the design inputs the Atlas can supply, filled in and labelled for what they are, plus the ones it cannot, named. It computes NO sample size — the inputs that would justify one are not present in this Atlas or its corpus, and a pooled τ² is not an outcome variance. Gaps without a brief return {available: false, reason}, not an error. Renders the brief as a card in the detail panel; ledgered.

gap_id.description: gap id from get_gaps; only gaps whose get_gaps entry has brief_available:true compile — currently gap:coverage-weeks

tools.name: focus_node
tools.description: Select a node on the map the human is looking at and open it in the detail panel, returning that node’s full detail object. This is the shared surface: your exploration is visible on their screen. Changes only which node is selected — no record, edge or claim is touched. Ledgered as navigation.

node_id.description: node id or bare id — rec:s10 or s10, claim:c-window or c-window, gap:coverage-weeks or coverage-weeks (see list_nodes)

tools.name: synthesize
tools.description: Re-fit the cell under a named spec: method REML or DL random-effects, or FE common-effect (FE assumes one common effect; tau2 is null by model assumption, not estimated as zero). p is a two-sided test of the pooled effect against zero. Optional record exclusions. Changes only the displayed synthesis (cell node + panel) — the record set is untouched and evaluate_claim does not inherit the exclusions; ledgered. Excluding down to fewer than 2 records is an error, not a silent empty fit.

method.description: tau^2 estimator / model: REML or DL random-effects, FE common-effect (default REML)

exclude.description: record ids to leave out, bare or node form, e.g. ["s04"] or ["rec:s04"]

tools.name: list_nodes
tools.description: Every addressable node on the map, grouped by type, with its label — the id directory for focus_node. Record entries carry {record_id, node_id, author, year, weeks, yi, vi} so a record can be picked without a second call. Pure read: not ledgered, nothing on the human’s screen changes.

tools.name: get_audit_log
tools.description: Return this page’s append-only audit ledger: every claim verdict, synthesis, brief and navigation in this session, in order. Each entry is {run, time, actor (human|agent|system), kind, tool, inputs, summary, evidence_version, result_digest}. result_digest is a non-cryptographic FNV-1a checksum for detecting accidental payload changes, not tamper evidence. The ledger is session-local: it lives in this page for this visit and is not published, synced or shared.

sites.name: next.builder.run
sites.description: Home

tools.name: get_space
tools.description: Inspect the active space: apps, actors, backend, and exposed_types. Types with expose: true live on the account space and every app here shares those records — use that for data two apps both need (clients, organisations). App-only types do not appear here. Example: get_space({}).

tools.name: get_spec
tools.description: Return the live spec, including generated default views, forms, and pages, and types the space exposes (those have expose: true — shared across apps). App-local types omit expose. Use get_space for the space-level exposed_types list. Use export_spec for the portable authored spec (defaults omitted).

tools.name: get_widgets
tools.description: Discover page widgets and their configuration contract. Call without widget to list or search widgets. Pass a widget key for its inputs. Also pass view for exact compatible field options before calling upsert_page.

view.description: Optional View key used to resolve compatible field inputs

query.description: Optional text search when listing widgets

category.description: Optional category filter when listing widgets

tools.name: get_automation_primitives
tools.description: Discover the canonical structured-workflow grammar, registered conditions and effects, and this runtime's capability profile. Call with a condition or effect key for its parameter contract before authoring a workflow.

tools.name: export_spec
tools.description: Export the portable authored spec as YAML or JSON. Generated default views, forms, and pages are omitted; they are recreated from types on import. Use get_spec to inspect the live spec including defaults.

tools.name: query_view
tools.description: Run a named view and return its rows. Views can filter, sort, limit, and derive live grouped measures — list_records returns every source record (list_ in typed mode). Discover view keys via get_spec. Example: query_view({ view: "active_projects" }).

view.description: View key from get_spec

expose.description: Runtime values for the view's expose filters, e.g. { status: "active" }

record_id.description: Current record id when the view filters on $record.id

tools.name: apply_spec
tools.description: Replace the entire active app spec with a YAML or JSON document. Not a merge: types, views, forms, workflows, and pages missing from the document are deleted. Generated defaults are recreated from types. Requires confirm: true. A document with no types is refused unless wipe: true — { key: "foo" } is not a full spec. Example: apply_spec({ spec: " ", confirm: true }).

spec.description: Full YAML or JSON document for the app spec

confirm.description: Must be true. apply_spec replaces the entire spec.

wipe.description: Required with confirm if the document has no types and the app already has some.

tools.name: upsert_type
tools.description: Create or update a type and its fields. Use a singular key and label for one record; optional collection_label overrides the automatically pluralized list name. Providing fields replaces the type's field list; omitting fields leaves existing fields unchanged. Field type is canonical; compatible format, presentation, validation, and conditional behavior are optional. lifecycle turns one enum field into a validated state machine. Add or change one field with upsert_field. expose: true stores the type on the account space so every app shares its records. Example: upsert_type({ key: "task", fields: [{ key: "status", type: "enum", values: ["draft", "done"] }], lifecycle: { field: "status", initial: "draft", terminal: ["done"], transitions: [{ key: "complete", from: ["draft"], to: "done" }] } }).

collection_label.description: Optional plural label for lists and navigation. Omit it to infer an English plural from label; pass an empty string to clear an existing override.

expose.description: If true, the type lives on the account space and all apps share its records. If false or omitted, the type belongs only to this app.

anyOf.description: Optional state machine attached to one enum field

field.description: Enum field containing the current state

initial.description: State assigned to every new record

lifecycle.description: State machine definition, or null to remove the existing lifecycle

fields.description: Fields to create with the type. Array of field objects, or a map of field key → field (or shorthand type string).

target.description: Referenced type key (reference fields)

anyOf.description: Shorthand field type, e.g. text

target.description: Referenced type key (reference fields)

tools.name: rename_type
tools.description: Rename a technical type key while preserving its stable identity, records, and direct spec references. Explicit view, form, page, and workflow keys remain unchanged.

tools.name: upsert_field
tools.description: Add or update one field without replacing the type's other fields. type identifies the record type; kind is the field kind. Formats, presentations, and validation must be compatible with that kind. Enum fields need values, reference fields need target, currency fields need currency, and rating fields use max from 2 to 10. Example: upsert_field({ type: "submission", key: "stage", kind: "enum", values: ["submitted", "winner", "rejected"], presentation: "badge", value_semantics: { submitted: "neutral", winner: "success", rejected: "danger" } }).

type.description: Type key (not the field kind)

kind.description: Field kind

target.description: Referenced type key (reference fields)

tools.name: rename_field
tools.description: Rename a field key while keeping its identity and stored values.

tools.name: delete_field
tools.description: Remove a field from a type and drop its SQLite column.

tools.name: upsert_view
tools.description: Create or update a named view (a stored query: filter, sort, limit, columns, or live grouped measures). For a normal view, include fields in the order people should see them, such as fields: ["name", "status", "client.name"]. If fields is omitted while creating a normal view, builder.run chooses up to six useful source fields automatically; an empty fields array is invalid. Omitting fields while updating preserves the existing selection. For a grouped view, omit fields to derive them from group_by and measure aliases. group_by accepts one source field. measures supports count, sum, avg, min, and max; avg accepts field or fields. Sort aggregate aliases with order_by. Run it with query_view. Example: upsert_view({ key: "scores", source: "review", group_by: "submission", measures: { review_count: { op: "count" }, overall_score: { op: "avg", fields: ["quality", "impact"] } }, order_by: { overall_score: "desc" } }).

fields.description: Ordered visible columns for a normal view. Reference labels may use paths such as client.name. Omit on creation to infer useful defaults; omit on update to preserve existing columns; omit for grouped views to derive aggregate columns.

measures.description: Named live aggregates for a grouped view

tools.name: upsert_form
tools.description: Create or update a record-backed or standalone form. Record forms use type plus ordered field keys. Standalone forms own reusable field definitions under inputs and emit form.submitted with {form, values}. submit.success optionally customizes the standalone confirmation; workflow behavior belongs in a workflow listening for form.submitted. Example: upsert_form({ key: "contact_us", mode: "standalone", inputs: { name: { type: "text", required: true }, email: { type: "text", format: "email" } }, submit: { success: { title: "Thanks" } } }).

inputs.description: Named field definitions for a standalone form.

target.description: Referenced type key (reference fields)

tools.name: upsert_workflow
tools.description: Create or update a structured workflow. Call get_automation_primitives first. Use registered effects and {$ref:"vars.name"} bindings. Gates contain pass/fail steps; loops and parallel branches contain their own steps. expose: ["agent"] registers invoke_ . Example: upsert_workflow({ key: "mark_paid", expose: ["agent"], input: { invoice: { record: "invoice" } }, steps: [{ effect: { key: "records.set", params: { record: {$ref:"vars.invoice"}, values: {status:"paid"} } } }] }).

input.description: Named inputs. Each value is {record:"type_key"} or {value:"text|number|boolean|date|object|array"}.

trigger.description: Optional {key, config?}. Omit for a callable workflow.

steps.description: Canonical nested steps returned by get_automation_primitives.

tools.name: upsert_page
tools.description: Create or update a page of grids and widgets. Call get_widgets first to discover widget keys, required values, and compatible fields. Widget values are validated against that contract. Optional folder groups it in the app menu. Optional icon is one of: page, dashboard, table, chart, line, donut, board, calendar, list, inbox, people, money, time. If icon is omitted when creating a page, a one-time default is inferred from its widgets; later edits do not change it. A group nests children in a blocks array even when there is only one widget. columns is how many widgets sit side by side; unused columns stay empty. Example: upsert_page({ key: "board", icon: "board", path: "/board", blocks: [{ kind: "group", columns: 1, blocks: [{ kind: "widget", widget: "table", values: { view: "active_projects" } }] }] }).

blocks.description: Page layout. A group nests children in a blocks array — always an array, even for one widget.

columns.description: Widgets side by side in this group (1–4). Unused cells stay empty.

tools.name: create_app
tools.description: Create an app in the active space and switch to it. The new app can use types the space already exposes (see get_space.exposed_types) — do not recreate those types in the app. Example: create_app({ name: "Invoicing" }).

tools.name: delete_app
tools.description: Delete an app created from this account space. Shared records stay.

tools.name: switch_app
tools.description: Switch the active app by id. Space-exposed types stay available; app-local types change with the app.

tools.name: create_space
tools.description: Create a new account space with its own apps. After switching to it, upsert_type({ expose: true }) creates types every app in this space shares — e.g. a customer type used by both a CRM and invoicing. Example: create_space({ name: "Studio" }).

tools.name: list_samples
tools.description: List gallery sample applications that can be loaded as an app.

tools.name: describe_type
tools.description: Inspect one record type on demand, including field constraints and lifecycle transitions. Pass a record id to also see its current state and available transitions. Call this before creating or updating unfamiliar records.

type.description: Type key from get_spec

id.description: Optional record id

tools.name: list_records
tools.description: List every record of one type, unfiltered. Use query_view when you need filtering, sorting, limits, or aggregates.

type.description: Type key from get_spec or describe_type

tools.name: get_record
tools.description: Get one record by type and id.

type.description: Type key from get_spec or describe_type

id.description: Record id

tools.name: create_record
tools.description: Create a record of one type. Call describe_type first for fields and constraints; lifecycle state and audit fields are system-managed.

type.description: Type key from get_spec or describe_type

values.description: Field values accepted by the selected type. Use describe_type for the contract.

tools.name: update_record
tools.description: Update fields on one record. Call describe_type first; use transition_record for lifecycle state changes.

type.description: Type key from get_spec or describe_type

id.description: Record id

values.description: Field values accepted by the selected type. Use describe_type for the contract.

tools.name: delete_record
tools.description: Delete one record by type and id.

type.description: Type key from get_spec or describe_type

id.description: Record id

tools.name: transition_record
tools.description: Apply a named lifecycle transition to a record. Use describe_type with the record id to discover transitions currently available.

type.description: Type key from get_spec or describe_type

id.description: Record id

sites.name: open-architect.vercel.app
sites.description: OpenArchitect — describe a home. An agent asks follow-ups, then draws a schematic floor plan on a live canvas. The same tools are exposed to browser agents via WebMCP.

tools.name: get_brief
tools.description: Read the current project brief: description, plot size, bedroom/bathroom counts, notes, and answers already collected.

tools.name: get_design_rules
tools.description: Return the house-making standards this studio enforces: NBC-aligned room sizes, doors, windows, and adjacency rules for living, dining, bedrooms, kitchen, bathrooms, and hallways.

tools.name: get_standards_check
tools.description: Return only the current standards-check issues (errors and warnings): room size minima, overlaps, openings, adjacency, missing porch/stairs/street, etc. Prefer this over get_floor_plan when you only need to know what is failing.

tools.name: update_brief
tools.description: Patch the project brief. Use this to store requirements from the conversation. If plotWidthM and plotHeightM are set, the canvas plot is resized to match.

tools.name: ask_user
tools.description: Ask the human one to six structured follow-up questions before drawing. Opens a modal on the OpenArchitect page and WAITS until they click Send answers. The questions are also in this tool's arguments for ChatGPT to display. When it returns, answers are already saved in the brief — continue with set_plot / apply_layout. Do not call apply_layout before this tool returns.

tools.name: get_floor_plan
tools.description: Return the full floor plan JSON plus validation issues (overlaps, NBC size minima, missing exterior windows, awkward adjacencies).

tools.name: set_plot
tools.description: Set the overall rectangular plot size in meters. Origin is the top-left (northwest) corner. x increases east, y increases south.

tools.name: apply_layout
tools.description: Replace rooms, openings, furniture, and the frontage street in one shot. Prefer this for the first draft. Include an entrance porch, a stairs area, and street.edge on the same side as the main door unless the user declined them. Room ids must be stable slugs (kitchen, bed-1, porch, stairs). Coordinates are meters on a 0.5 m grid.

edge.description: Plot edge the street runs along — the same side as the main entrance

id.description: Stable id, e.g. kitchen or bed-1

name.description: Human label shown on the canvas

x.description: Meters from the plot's left (west) edge

y.description: Meters from the plot's top (north) edge

roomId.description: Id of the room this opening belongs to

edge.description: Wall: north is top of the canvas

offset.description: Meters along the edge from its start (west for N/S, north for E/W)

kind.description: bed, sofa, table, counter, toilet, sink, stove, wardrobe, desk, other

x.description: Meters from the room's left edge

y.description: Meters from the room's top edge

tools.name: add_room
tools.description: Add a single axis-aligned room rectangle. Coordinates are meters from the plot origin (top-left).

id.description: Stable id, e.g. kitchen or bed-1

name.description: Human label shown on the canvas

x.description: Meters from the plot's left (west) edge

y.description: Meters from the plot's top (north) edge

tools.name: update_room
tools.description: Move or resize one room by id. Does not push shared walls into neighbors — use resize_wall for that.

tools.name: remove_room
tools.description: Remove a room and any openings or furniture attached to it.

tools.name: add_opening
tools.description: Add a door or window on a room edge. offset is meters from the start of that edge (west end for north/south, north end for east/west).

roomId.description: Id of the room this opening belongs to

edge.description: Wall: north is top of the canvas

offset.description: Meters along the edge from its start (west for N/S, north for E/W)

tools.name: remove_opening
tools.description: Remove a door or window by id.

tools.name: add_furniture
tools.description: Add a labeled furniture block inside a room. x/y are relative to the room origin, not the plot.

kind.description: bed, sofa, table, counter, toilet, sink, stove, wardrobe, desk, other

x.description: Meters from the room's left edge

y.description: Meters from the room's top edge

tools.name: remove_furniture
tools.description: Remove a furniture item by id.

tools.name: resize_wall
tools.description: Move one wall of a room. Neighbors that share that wall move with it. Prefer this over update_room when stretching a room against another. Provide position (plot meters) or delta (positive = east/south).

roomId.description: Room whose wall to move

edge.description: Which wall: north is the top of the canvas, east is the right

position.description: New plot coordinate of that wall in meters (x for east/west, y for north/south)

delta.description: Meters to shift the wall from where it is now. Positive moves east or south.

tools.name: replace_furniture
tools.description: Swap an existing furniture piece for a catalog object (bed, sofa, table, desk, wardrobe, counter, stove, sink, fridge, toilet, chair). Keeps the same id and recenters in place.

id.description: Furniture id from get_floor_plan

kind.description: Catalog kind: bed, sofa, table, desk, wardrobe, counter, stove, sink, fridge, toilet, chair

tools.name: move_furniture
tools.description: Move furniture inside its room. x/y are meters from the room's top-left, not the plot.

x.description: Meters from the room's left (west) edge

y.description: Meters from the room's top (north) edge

tools.name: resize_furniture
tools.description: Change a furniture block's width and height in meters.

tools.name: replace_opening
tools.description: Change an existing opening between door and window without moving it.

id.description: Door or window id from get_floor_plan

kind.description: door or window

tools.name: move_opening
tools.description: Slide a door or window along its wall, or onto another wall of the same room. offset is meters from the start of that edge (west for N/S, north for E/W).

id.description: Door or window id from get_floor_plan

offset.description: Meters along the edge from its start (west for N/S, north for E/W)

edge.description: Move onto another wall of the same room. Omit to stay on the current wall.

tools.name: resize_opening
tools.description: Change a door or window width in meters along the wall.

id.description: Door or window id from get_floor_plan

width.description: New opening width in meters along the wall

tools.name: export_png
tools.description: Download the current floor plan as a PNG image in the user's browser. Optional filename (extension added automatically).

filename.description: Download name without path, e.g. 3bhk-ground-floor. Extension is added.

tools.name: export_pdf
tools.description: Download the current floor plan as a PDF in the user's browser. Optional filename (extension added automatically).

filename.description: Download name without path, e.g. 3bhk-ground-floor. Extension is added.

tools.name: export_project
tools.description: Download the current brief + floor plan as an OpenArchitect JSON project file the user can re-import later. Optional filename.

filename.description: Download name without path, e.g. 3bhk-ground-floor. Extension is added.

tools.name: import_project
tools.description: Replace the canvas with a project JSON payload (plan required; brief optional). Accepts OpenArchitect exports or a bare plan object.

name.description: Human label shown on the canvas

x.description: Meters from the plot's left (west) edge

y.description: Meters from the plot's top (north) edge

roomId.description: Id of the room this opening belongs to

edge.description: Wall: north is top of the canvas

offset.description: Meters along the edge from its start (west for N/S, north for E/W)

kind.description: bed, sofa, table, counter, toilet, sink, stove, wardrobe, desk, other

x.description: Meters from the room's left edge

y.description: Meters from the room's top edge

tools.name: set_display_layers
tools.description: Toggle canvas display layers: roomColors (fill colors), doors (door openings), and objects (furniture/fixtures). Pass only the layers you want to change. Does not modify the floor plan data.

roomColors.description: Show or hide room fill colors on the 2D/3D canvas.

doors.description: Show or hide doors on walls (windows stay visible).

objects.description: Show or hide furniture and fixture blocks.

tools.name: generate_3d
tools.description: Build an interactive 3D dollhouse from the current floor plan (extruded rooms, walls, doors, windows, furniture). Opens the 3D viewer so the user can orbit it and download a GLB. Optional filename for the GLB. Call this when the user asks to see the house in 3D, generate 3D, or export a 3D model.

filename.description: Download name without path, e.g. 3bhk-ground-floor. Extension is added.

sites.name: sentinental.vercel.app
sites.description: SENTINEL reads your dependency tree, triages every advisory against the versions you actually ship, works out how risky each fix is, prepares the patch — and stops to ask a human before the pull…

tools.name: get_project_status
tools.description: Report what this deployment can actually do: whether a model key, a Daytona sandbox key, a GitHub token and a TrueForge harness are configured, and whether remote writes are permitted. Returns booleans and names only — never a key.

tools.name: scan_dependencies
tools.description: Parse a package.json plus an optional lockfile into a flat dependency list with the versions that are actually installed. Pure computation; no network.

lockfile.description: Optional lockfile contents (package-lock.json v2/v3, yarn.lock or pnpm-lock.yaml).

lockfileName.description: Name of the lockfile that was supplied, for warnings.

tools.name: fetch_repository_manifest
tools.description: Read package.json (and the lockfile if present) straight out of a public GitHub repository, so a scan needs no local checkout. Accepts 'owner/repo' or a github.com URL.

branch.description: Optional branch; defaults to the repository default branch.

tools.name: lookup_advisories
tools.description: Query the GitHub Advisory Database for one package@version and keep only the advisories whose affected range actually contains that version. Falls back to OSV. This is the triage step that separates a real exposure from a page of noise.

tools.name: assess_blast_radius
tools.description: Classify an upgrade from installed to target version as patch/minor/major and say how risky it is to apply automatically.

targetVersion.description: Version the fix would move to.

dependents.description: How many places import the package, if known.

tools.name: summarise_triage
tools.description: Collapse advisory matches into one safe target version per package — the highest fix version, so no advisory is left open — ordered worst first.

matches.description: Advisory matches as returned by lookup_advisories.

tools.name: propose_patch
tools.description: Generate the patched package.json for a plan, preserving the project's existing range operators (^, ~, exact). Returns the new file content and a unified diff. Writes nothing anywhere.

plan.description: Plan entries as returned by summarise_triage.

tools.name: list_tool_catalog
tools.description: Return every tool this site exposes to agents, with its JSON Schema and safety annotations, plus how to reach the same tools over remote MCP.

group.description: Optional filter: 'sentinel', 'labs' or 'site'.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search SENTINEL's documentation corpus (landing sections, docs pages, the tool contract) and return matching passages with a pointer you can hand to fetch_docs.

query.description: Words to look for.

limit.description: Maximum hits, 1–20 (default 6).

tools.name: fetch_docs
tools.description: Fetch one documentation passage by id, as returned by search_docs.

id.description: Passage id, e.g. 'docs:approval'.

tools.name: navigate_console
tools.description: Move the human's view to a station in this site's console (deck, scan, agent, labs, keys, bridge). In-page only — registered when a real tab is present, so an agent driving the page can show its work.

tools.name: breachlab_analyze_cve_ast
tools.description: Deep static AST analysis for code and dependency manifests. Identifies zero-days, RCE sinks, credential theft, prototype pollution, and computes blast radius.

tools.name: breachlab_detonate_sandbox
tools.description: Detonate suspicious code in an isolated simulated client-side sandbox container. Intercepts outbound network, eval, and subprocess commands.

tools.name: breachlab_trace_taint_flow
tools.description: Trace tainted data propagation from untrusted source inputs (e.g. req.query) to dangerous execution sinks.

tools.name: breachlab_generate_hotpatch
tools.description: Synthesize automated cryptographic hot-patch diffs that replace dangerous sinks with safe, parameterized equivalents.

tools.name: biosynth_load_pdb_structure
tools.description: Load and parse 3D Protein Data Bank (PDB) atomic coordinates into structured 3D atom graph and sequence.

tools.name: biosynth_mutate_residue
tools.description: Simulate in-silico point mutation (CRISPR / protein engineering) and predict stability change (ΔΔG) and steric clashes.

tools.name: biosynth_highlight_binding_pockets
tools.description: Scan 3D atomic structure to discover druggable active catalytic cavities and binding pockets.

tools.name: chrono_load_media_streams
tools.description: Retrieve multi-angle spatial and acoustic sensor streams (CCTV, bodycam, drone) for forensic reconstruction.

tools.name: chrono_sync_flash_audio_markers
tools.description: Cross-correlate optical flash peaks and acoustic transients across video streams to compute millisecond time offsets.

tools.name: chrono_triangulate_acoustic_source
tools.description: Triangulate 3D physical coordinates of an acoustic blast or gunshot origin using Time-Difference-Of-Arrival (TDOA).

tools.name: chrono_generate_forensic_dossier
tools.description: Assemble unified cryptographic forensic report with synchronized timeline sequence and SHA-256 evidence hash.

tools.name: metaloop_inspect_trace_tree

tools.name: ui_list
tools.description: List the agent-operable UI elements on the page. Call it first: it gives each element's id, state, and the tools that act on it — pass that id as target, except an action_ tool, which names its element. Pass target to list an element's children — the recovery when one reports childrenOmitted. A cut listing, or any you window with offset or limit, reports window — walk by advancing offset by window.returned. A listed state is current; ui_read gives detail the digest omits.

target.description: An element id: given, the tool lists that element's children instead of the whole page. Use it on an element that reports childrenOmitted.

offset.description: Index of the first element to return. Defaults to 0.

limit.description: How many elements to return. Defaults to as many as fit.

tools.name: ui_read
tools.description: Read the current semantic state of one UI element by id; use ui_list first for valid ids. Actions already return the element's post-change state, so this is for detail an action result windowed away and for elements you did not just act on. Pass offset or limit and the reply always reports window — field, offset, returned, true total — so returned equal to total means that is every entry the element holds. The budget windows a long list unasked. Walk by advancing offset by window.returned.

target.description: The id of the UI element to act on, as returned by ui_list.

offset.description: Index of the first entry to return from this element's largest list. Defaults to 0.

limit.description: How many entries of that list to return. Defaults to as many as fit; the output budget may clamp it, and window.returned reports what actually returned.

tools.name: button_press
tools.description: Press a button, exactly as a person clicking it would. The button's own name — the text a person reads on it, like "Send Invitation" — is its label in ui_list. Pressing may submit a form, open a dialog, navigate, or trigger whatever the button is wired to. The result carries the element's full state after the change, so a follow-up ui_read on the same element is unnecessary; when the result reports window, walk the rest with ui_read by advancing offset by window.returned.

target.description: The id of the UI element to act on, as returned by ui_list.

tools.name: dialog_open
tools.description: Open a dialog element. The result carries the element's full state after the change, so a follow-up ui_read on the same element is unnecessary; when the result reports window, walk the rest with ui_read by advancing offset by window.returned.

target.description: The id of the UI element to act on, as returned by ui_list.

tools.name: dialog_close
tools.description: Close a dialog element. The result carries the element's full state after the change, so a follow-up ui_read on the same element is unnecessary; when the result reports window, walk the rest with ui_read by advancing offset by window.returned.

target.description: The id of the UI element to act on, as returned by ui_list.

tools.name: ui_fill
tools.description: Fill several elements in one call — a form's fields, say. values maps an element id to its new value: a string for an input, select or tabs, a boolean for a checkbox, an array for a multi-select. Fillable kinds: tabs, select, multi-select, checkbox, input, slider, date. Each value travels through that element's own action, so the page reacts as it does to that tool. Every id is checked first, so one bad id changes nothing. Submitting is a separate press.

values.description: An object mapping element ids to their new values. Call ui_list for valid ids and kinds.

tools.description: Get every manual adjustment, non-destructive geometry value, independently selected filter, and revision for the active image. Manual values are applied on top of the filter.

tools.name: get_edit_history
tools.description: Get concise ordered edit history and redo entries. Returns command summaries and sources without pixel data.

tools.name: get_image_preview
tools.description: Return an original or edited image preview as a bounded data URL. maxDimension is 64–2048 pixels and quality is 1–100.

variant.description: Whether to render the untouched source or current edit.

tools.name: open_image_from_url

url.description: Required HTTPS image URL.

filename.description: Optional safe display filename.

tools.name: open_image_from_data_url
tools.description: Open a JPEG, PNG, or WebP data URL up to 12 MiB encoded length. Set replace true only to discard unexported edits.

filename.description: Optional safe display filename.

tools.name: set_exposure
tools.description: Set the manual exposure layer to an absolute value from -5 through 5. It is applied on top of the selected filter and creates one undoable edit.

value.description: Absolute exposure value.

tools.name: set_brightness

tools.name: set_tint
