Supply unfamiliar names as constraints.storeNames or verified official domains as storeDomains. Named stores are hard restrictions: resolve their official domain through resolve_store before research. Use Rove search_shop_catalog for built-in anonymous Shop HTTP discovery (https://shop.com/skill.md and /shop.md); no local CLI, plugin or login is required. Use per-need store restrictions for mixed-retailer requests. Follow returned next steps, inspect Shop messages, and compare exact returned options before enrichment or adding to Your Thread. Only prepare merchant carts/checkouts on request; never complete payment.

quantity.description: How many distinct products must fulfill this need. Defaults to 1.

budgetCad.description: Maximum combined CAD subtotal for products selected for this need.

retailerIds.description: Hard store restriction for this need only. Use an empty array for an unrestricted need.

referenceImage.description: A photo the person shared as the style guide: base64 bytes, not a URL. Large images are resized in the browser.

data.description: Base64-encoded image bytes.

inspirationId.description: Use an image already on the inspiration board as the style guide.

visualCues.description: What you see in the reference photo. Rove ranks with these and adds them to Shop’s relevance hint.

palette.description: Garment colours, e.g. white, tan, denim.

descriptors.description: Silhouette, fabric and style, e.g. relaxed linen, cropped, crochet.

overallBudgetCad.description: Maximum CAD subtotal for the proposed products across all required needs.

storeDomains.description: Verified official storefront domains for named stores outside the retailer registry. Rove applies a hard Shop shops filter and validates returned sellers.

storeNames.description: Unresolved store names; resolve_store must verify each official domain before research.

tools.name: claim_search_targets
tools.description: Claim a bounded batch of queued research targets, dynamically reprioritized around required mission needs that are still unfulfilled. Shop catalogue targets (sourceType "catalog") come first: call Rove search_shop_catalog for each requestIndex; the built-in anonymous HTTP connection needs no agent installation. Inspect real results and publish with shop provenance. Zero matches are no-results; actual connection failures are failed with the returned reason. Do not infer unavailability from missing agent tools. For retailer and discovery targets, open the returned need-specific search URLs and publish listing-page candidates. Resolve each target before claiming more.

limit.description: Batch size from 1 to 4. Defaults to 3.

workerId.description: Optional stable browser worker label for traceability.

tools.name: search_shop_catalog
tools.description: Run one exact planned Shop catalogue request directly from this browser. Works anonymously without a Shop plugin, CLI, account or local setup. First read the official Shop guide at https://shop.com/skill.md. Requires a claimed catalogue target; requestIndex defaults to zero. Returns original Shop evidence and every message; inspect sellers, exact options and currency before publishing. An empty result means no matches, not a disconnected Shop. On an actual error, use the retailer fallback with the returned reason. Never substitutes or broadens filters.

tools.name: inspect_shop_product
tools.description: Read exact options, price and stock of a Shop product already published in this mission, through anonymous browser HTTP. Pass requestedOptions using exact returned names and labels. Inspect the effective response for substitutions before enrich_product. Does not add to a cart or purchase.

tools.name: resolve_store
tools.description: Before claiming research, resolve an unfamiliar store named in the brief to its verified official storefront domain. Visit the official site to establish the domain; do not invent it, pass a marketplace listing, or broaden the request to other merchants. If it cannot be verified, tell the person. Rove regenerates Shop requests with a hard shops filter.

tools.name: publish_candidates
tools.description: Publish multiple products observed on a claimed retailer listing, or returned by Shop search_catalog for a claimed Shop catalogue target. For Shop results, set url to the featured variant url exactly as returned, image to its first media url, and copy product/variant/seller IDs into shop and product.options into shop.options so every size and colour is recorded; Rove converts shop.price minor units to a decimal price itself, but never converts currency: a non-CAD shop.price is rejected unless priceCad is a CAD price the seller actually shows. Every candidate must include its canonical product page URL, name, and a direct HTTP(S) product image URL so recommendations are never published without imagery. Rove derives canonical identity, retailer, source, and timestamp, then enforces target-domain, mission, department, category, retailer, budget, and CAD rules.

retailer.description: Used only for unknown retailers found through discovery; known identity is derived from the domain.

priceCad.description: Required for non-CAD listings and budget-constrained missions.

image.description: Required direct HTTP(S) URL for the product image observed on the retailer page. Do not use the product page URL, a search result, or a placeholder.

needIds.description: Mission need IDs this observed product can fulfill. IDs must be present on the claimed target.

sizes.description: Retailer listings: every size label the product page or listing offers, exactly as shown. Shop candidates use shop.options instead.

colors.description: Retailer listings: every colour label offered, exactly as shown.

shop.description: Required for Shop catalogue targets and rejected elsewhere. Copy values unchanged from the search_catalog product and its featured variant.

checkoutUrl.description: Copy the exact featured variant checkout_url, when returned. Never construct it.

variantId.description: Featured variant id, e.g. gid://shopify/ProductVariant/….

sellerDomain.description: variant.seller.domain (the myshopify domain Shop uses for carts).

price.description: variant.price unchanged: integer minor units plus ISO currency.

available.description: variant.availability.available.

options.description: product.options names and value labels (with available/exists when returned), e.g. [{"name":"Size","values":[{"label":"S"},{"label":"M"}]}]. Records every size and colour the person can choose.

tools.name: enrich_product
tools.description: Hydrate one candidate after detailed inspection or user interest. Use the canonical product page to add variants, availability, material, description, tags, and any price details needed before cart selection. For Shop, send shopProductId, requestedOptions (the exact requested name/label pairs), and one exact returned variant with options, availability, price and checkoutUrl when returned. Compare the effective selection: a dropped option, changed volume, or substitute body wash is a mismatch, not a valid perfume. Rove rejects mismatches. Search results may verify the featured selection without another lookup; use get_product only for unresolved facts or different options. Never infer combinations from size lists. Strip HTML from descriptions.

shopProductId.description: Copy the returned Shop product ID. A different product is rejected.

requestedOptions.description: Exact options sent to Shop, including Size, Color, Width, Finish, volume or accessory size. Omit only to verify the previously published selection. Returned options must match exactly; never silently relax them.

variants.description: Shop catalogue products only: exact variants copied unchanged from Shop.

id.description: gid://shopify/ProductVariant/…

url.description: The complete returned variant URL, unchanged.

checkoutUrl.description: Exact checkout_url returned for this variant; never construct one.

tools.name: complete_search_target
tools.description: Resolve one claimed retailer as complete, no-results, or failed. Complete requires an accepted product; no-results and failed require a reason. When the mission ends with products, Rove starts a timed recommendation review before saving the result.

tools.name: get_search_status
tools.description: Read the persisted mission, full visible collection, fulfillment, retailer coverage, timed recommendation review, and next action. During selective replacement, collection shows which products remain preserved and which IDs are being replaced. Expired reviews are accepted and saved locally.

tools.name: get_products
tools.description: Page through the full visible mission edit, including products preserved during selective replacement plus fresh candidates. Supports cursor or offset, up to 100 records, plus retailer, category, and sort filters; returned IDs are valid for enrichment and cart actions.

tools.name: review_recommendations
tools.description: Resolve the pending recommendation review after research finishes. Accept everything, replace selected product IDs, or replace the entire set. Selective replacement removes only those IDs, keeps every other accepted item visible in the current edit, and excludes every previously shown product link from fresh research.

rejectedProductIds.description: Required only for replace-selected. Use exact IDs returned in recommendationReview.productIds.

tools.name: research_again
tools.description: Start another research pass from an accepted mission. Omit productIds to refresh the whole set, or provide presented product IDs to replace only those items while preserving every other accepted product in the visible edit. Previously shown product families are excluded.

tools.name: get_research_history
tools.description: Read locally saved completed mission prompts and their final accepted product collections, plus compact style cues and the count of product families excluded from future research. Replacement chains are saved as one merged root mission, not disconnected partial missions.

tools.name: cancel_search
tools.description: Stop or explicitly abandon the active retailer pass, cancel every unresolved target, and preserve products already accepted for human review.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Read the exact shared cross-store cart visible to the human, including selected variants, CAD subtotal, unpriced count, and canonical retailer checkout links.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add an enriched mission product to the shared browser-local cart. Provide a size or colour only when that product exposes the corresponding choices. Shop products require a verified exact combination; use variantId and selectedOptions for all choices including fragrance volume, belt size, width and finish. Missing or sold-out combinations are rejected. Non-Shop products retain their existing size/colour flow. Exact product-and-variant duplicates are prevented.

productId.description: Exact Rove product ID returned by a product tool.

size.description: Available size when the product exposes size choices; otherwise omit.

variantId.description: Exact verified Shop variant ID. Use with selectedOptions for merchant-specific choices.

color.description: Available colour when the product exposes colour choices; otherwise omit.

tools.name: remove_from_cart
tools.description: Remove one exact cart entry by its collision-safe item ID. Read get_cart first when the item ID is unknown. The visible human cart updates immediately.

itemId.description: Exact cart item ID returned by get_cart.

tools.name: get_checkout_plan
tools.description: Read Your Thread grouped by seller. Shop-backed groups list exact variant IDs and quantities for one Shop cart or checkout per seller; a line without variantId carries a ready get_product request that resolves it. Create Shop carts or checkouts only when the user asks to save a cart or check out, then call attach_merchant_cart with the returned continue_url. Other stores keep their retailer links. Rove never completes a purchase.

tools.name: attach_merchant_cart
tools.description: After creating a Shop cart or checkout for one get_checkout_plan seller group, store its continue_url unchanged so the human can continue to that merchant. Include the merchant-returned total and every warning or disclosure message. This records a handoff only; it does not place an order.

groupKey.description: Exact key of a Shop-backed group from get_checkout_plan.

continueUrl.description: The complete continue_url returned by Shop, unchanged.

total.description: Merchant-returned total in integer minor units.

messages.description: Every returned warning and disclosure, verbatim.

tools.name: add_inspiration
tools.description: Add one Pinterest pin to the shared inspiration board the human sees. Use the pin’s direct HTTPS image URL and its pin URL. While working a claimed Pinterest target, pass searchId and targetId so the pin counts toward that target. Pins become visual "Shop this look" searches through find_similar.

imageUrl.description: Direct HTTPS image URL of the pin.

note.description: A short description of the look, used as a text fallback.

targetId.description: The claimed discovery:pinterest target.

tools.name: get_inspiration
tools.description: Read the shared inspiration board. Uploaded photos include a ready Shop `like` image entry; pins include their image URL, whose bytes you fetch for a Shop `like` search.

tools.name: find_similar
tools.description: Search for pieces like one product ("More like this") or one inspiration image ("Shop this look"). During an active mission this adds a Shop similarity target; otherwise it starts a focused follow-up mission. Then claim targets as usual. Shop products search by product ID; images search by bytes.

tools.name: record_purchases
tools.description: Tell Rove what the user bought so it stops recommending owned items and learns favourite brands. Use source "checkout" only after Shop returns status completed with an order; Rove then marks that seller’s handoff as Ordered. Use "order-history" for items from Shop search_orders. Send only seller domain, product link, brand, and order link: never addresses, emails, payment details, or prices.

tools.name: cart_proposed_basket
tools.description: After the person accepts the proposed basket (or it auto-accepts), add every piece to Your Thread in their saved sizes. Pieces that still need a stock check or a size choice come back in needsAction with exact Shop, browser, or person steps; run them, then call this again. It never checks out.

sites.name: webmcp-visual-yard.ashmangamer0406.workers.dev
sites.description: Visual Graph Lab

tools.name: inspect_graph
tools.description: Read the live patch: every operator node with its id, operator, name, enabled/bypass state, changed parameters, what is wired into each input, which signal operator drives which parameter, and whether it is actually executing this frame. Also lists the compiler issue list and which nodes are idle because no output needs them. Start here before changing anything. Pass nodeId to get full detail for one node (every parameter, its value, range, and whether a signal can drive it). Use get_media_topology instead when the question is about cameras and outputs.

nodeId.description: Optional. A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates. Focuses the report on that one node.

tools.name: list_operators
tools.description: Browse the operator catalog — the set of things this application can do. Grouped by category (sources, generators, filters, warp, composite, control, audio, outputs) with operator id, label, a one-line description, the TouchDesigner equivalent, input ports, and which parameters a signal can drive. Filter with query (free text over labels, descriptions, keywords and TD names) or category. Narrow results get the detailed form; broad results get a compact one — call describe_operator for a single operator in full.

query.description: Optional free text, e.g. "blur", "feedback", "audio", "Movie File In TOP".

category.description: Optional category filter. One of: source, generator, filter, warp, composite, control, audio, output.

tools.name: describe_operator
tools.description: Full reference for one operator: what it does, its TouchDesigner equivalent, every input and output port with its type (including delayed feedback ports), and every parameter with kind, range, unit, default, menu options, help text, and whether a signal operator can drive it. Call this before set_parameter on an operator you have not used yet.

operator.description: Operator id ("glitch") or label ("Glitch"). See list_operators.

tools.name: get_media_topology
tools.description: The end-to-end signal path, from external sources to outputs: cameras, video files, screen capture and remote phone streams with their live status and resolution; the generators feeding the texture graph; and every output with the chain that reaches it, whether it currently has a live signal, and where the picture is going (program monitor or a /output projector link). Use this to answer "is anything on screen?" and "where does the stream output come from?".

tools.name: inspect_source
tools.description: Detail on one input source (camera, video file, image, screen capture, remote phone stream or text layer): live media status and resolution, the device or URL it is using, everything downstream of it, and any problem stopping it from producing frames. Use get_media_topology first if you do not know which sources exist.

node.description: The source node. A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates.

tools.name: inspect_output
tools.description: Detail on one output: whether it currently has a live signal, the whole chain feeding it, the display grade parameters applied to it, and where the picture is going (program monitor, or a /output link for a projector). Use this when someone says a screen is black.

node.description: The output node. A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates.

tools.name: trace_dependencies
tools.description: Everything that contributes to a node and everything it affects, nearest first, with each link marked as a texture link or a signal (parameter) link, and delayed feedback links called out. Use this before deleting or rewiring something, to see what you would break.

node.description: The node to trace. A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates.

tools.name: get_system_health
tools.description: The diagnostic tool: call it whenever something looks wrong. GPU adapter, engine state, fps and frame time, texture and pipeline counts, shader compile errors with the node they belong to, audio input state with live level and detected BPM, MIDI state and devices, remote session state and connected publishers, and the full compiler issue list for the patch.

tools.name: get_recent_changes
tools.description: The change log, newest first: who changed what and when, with the nodes each change touched. Human edits and agent edits are both recorded, so use this to see what a collaborator just did before you change the same thing, or to check what you yourself changed before calling revert_agent_changes.

sinceSeconds.description: Optional. Only changes newer than this many seconds ago.

limit.description: Optional maximum number of entries to return (default 25).

tools.name: read_signals
tools.description: The current numeric value of every signal (CHOP) operator, plus what each one drives and the live audio analysis behind it. Call this before wiring audio reactivity, to see whether the music is actually reaching the app and which band is moving.

tools.name: list_sketches
tools.description: Lists all creative preloaded sketches available in Signal Yard, showcasing different aspects like audio reactivity, hand tracking gestures, recursive feedback loops, fluid simulation, and retro shaders.

tools.name: create_node
tools.description: Place a new operator on the canvas. Optionally name it, position it, set parameters, and connect it immediately. The operator id must come from list_operators; on a miss the error suggests the closest matches. Use insert_effect instead when you want the new operator spliced into an existing link, and route_source_to_output when you want a whole chain built.

name.description: Optional display name. Defaults to the operator label.

position.description: Canvas position in graph units. Omit to have the editor find a free slot.

params.description: Optional parameter values, keyed by parameter key or label. Menu parameters accept the option name ("Screen") or its index (4). Values are clamped to the parameter range and the result is reported back.

connectTo.description: Optional immediate connection. Give `to` to feed another node, and/or `from` to feed the new node. Within `to`, use toInput for a texture input or toParameter to drive a parameter.

to.description: Node the new operator should feed. A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates.

toInput.description: Input port id, label, or index on that node. Omit to pick the first free one.

toParameter.description: Parameter on that node to drive instead of an input. Parameter key ("amount") or inspector label ("Amount"), case-insensitive. Call describe_operator or inspect_graph with a nodeId to see the list.

from.description: Node that should feed the new operator. A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates.

tools.name: connect_nodes
tools.description: Wire one operator into another. Texture outputs go to texture inputs; a signal (CHOP) output goes either to a numeric input or, with toParameter, to a modulatable parameter so it animates every frame. If toInput and toParameter are both omitted, the first free input of the matching type is used and the response says which one. Refusals quote the editor's own reason (occupied input, type mismatch, feedback loop).

from.description: Source node. A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates.

to.description: Destination node. A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates.

toInput.description: Optional input port id ("in-0"), label ("Texture 1"), or index ("0").

toParameter.description: Optional parameter to drive instead of an input. Parameter key ("amount") or inspector label ("Amount"), case-insensitive. Call describe_operator or inspect_graph with a nodeId to see the list.

tools.name: disconnect
tools.description: Remove a link. Identify it by edgeId, or by the from/to pair (every link between them is removed), or by to plus toParameter to stop a signal driving that parameter. Do this before set_parameter on a parameter that is currently animated.

edgeId.description: Optional exact link id, as shown by inspect_graph.

from.description: Optional source node. A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates.

to.description: Optional destination node. A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates.

toParameter.description: Optional parameter on `to` whose signal link should be cut. Parameter key ("amount") or inspector label ("Amount"), case-insensitive. Call describe_operator or inspect_graph with a nodeId to see the list.

tools.name: set_parameter
tools.description: Change one parameter on one node, live. Menu parameters accept the option name or its index; numbers are clamped to the parameter range; the response reports the value that actually landed. Refuses when the parameter is currently driven by a signal operator, because the signal would overwrite it next frame. Use set_parameters for several at once.

nodeId.description: The node to change. A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates.

parameter.description: Parameter key ("amount") or inspector label ("Amount"), case-insensitive. Call describe_operator or inspect_graph with a nodeId to see the list.

value.description: New value. Number for float/int, true/false for bool, option name or index for menu, string for text, "#rrggbb" or [r,g,b,a] (0..1) for colour.

tools.name: set_parameters
tools.description: Change several parameters on one node in a single call — the right tool for an instruction like "make it more aggressive". Every parameter name is validated before anything is written, so a typo changes nothing.

nodeId.description: The node to change. A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates.

params.description: Parameter key or label → new value. Same value rules as set_parameter.

tools.name: delete_node
tools.description: Delete one operator and every link touching it. Call trace_dependencies first if you are unsure what it feeds — deleting a node in the middle of a chain leaves the downstream operator unwired.

node.description: The node to delete. A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates.

tools.name: delete_nodes
tools.description: Delete several operators and all their links in one call, recorded as a single history entry.

nodes.description: Node ids or names to delete. A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates.

tools.name: insert_effect
tools.description: Splice an operator into an existing texture link, so "add a VHS look to camera 1" needs no rewiring: the upstream link is broken, the new operator is placed between the two nodes, and both links are remade. Identify the link with after (the node the effect goes below), before (the node it goes above), both, or an exact edgeId.

operator.description: Effect operator id from list_operators, e.g. "glitch", "bloom", "rgb-shift".

after.description: Optional. Insert directly downstream of this node. A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates.

before.description: Optional. Insert directly upstream of this node. A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates.

edgeId.description: Optional exact link id from inspect_graph.

tools.name: bypass_node
tools.description: Bypass or un-bypass an operator. A bypassed filter passes its first input straight through, which is the safe way to A/B an effect without deleting it or losing its parameters.

node.description: The node to bypass. A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates.

bypass.description: true to bypass (default), false to bring the operator back into the chain.

tools.name: enable_node
tools.description: Enable or disable an operator. A disabled operator outputs nothing at all, so everything downstream of it goes black — prefer bypass_node when you only want to skip an effect.

node.description: The node to change. A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates.

enabled.description: true to enable (default), false to disable.

tools.name: route_source_to_output
tools.description: Build or repair a whole video chain in one call: source → optional effects → output. Any operator that does not exist yet is created (so source="camera" makes a Camera node if there is none), links that point somewhere else are replaced, and links that are already correct are left alone. This is the tool for "send the clean camera to the stream output" or "put a glitch and a bloom between the camera and the program out".

source.description: The start of the chain: an existing node (A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates.) or an operator id such as "camera", "remote-in", "video", "noise-top".

output.description: The end of the chain: an existing output node, or an operator id ("out" for the program monitor, "remote-out" for a projector/stream link). Defaults to "out".

effects.description: Optional operators to pass through, in order. An operator id creates a new node ("glitch"); an existing node id reuses that node ("glitch-1").

tools.name: make_parameter_reactive
tools.description: Animate a parameter from the music (or from an oscillator, or from hand tracking) in one call. Creates the right signal operator — Audio Band for bass/mid/treble, Audio In for level, Beat for onsets, LFO for a steady sweep, Hand In for palms, pinches, two-hand distance, or individual fingertips — places it near the target, wires it to the parameter, and shapes its output range so the movement is actually visible. Add a Range operator when the parameter does not live in 0..1. Use amount, or explicit low/high, to control how far it swings.

nodeId.description: The node whose parameter should move. A node id ("glitch-1") or a node name ("Glitch"). Names are matched case-insensitively; if a name is ambiguous the error lists the candidates.

parameter.description: The parameter to animate. Parameter key ("amount") or inspector label ("Amount"), case-insensitive. Call describe_operator or inspect_graph with a nodeId to see the list. It must be modulatable.

source.description: What drives it: "bass", "mid", "treble" (frequency bands), "level" (overall loudness), "beat" (onset envelope), "lfo" (steady oscillator), or hand tracking: "hand-x", "hand-y", "pinch", "openness", "hand-distance".

amount.description: Optional 0..1, default 0.75: the fraction of the parameter's full range the movement covers. Ignored when low and high are given.

low.description: Optional. Exact value the parameter takes when the signal is at its minimum.

high.description: Optional. Exact value the parameter takes when the signal peaks.

replace.description: Optional. Set true to replace a signal that already drives this parameter. Defaults to false, which refuses rather than silently rewiring.

tools.name: load_sketch
tools.description: Loads one of the creative preloaded sketches onto the canvas, replacing the current patch (undoable). Use list_sketches to see available sketches and what aspects they showcase.

sketchId.description: The id of the sketch to load: "cyberpunk-glitch", "hand-tracking-puppet", "infinite-feedback-tunnel", "liquid-oil-slick", "kinetic-typography", "retro-arcade-cmyk", "cosmic-polar-wormhole", "camera-kaleidoscope".

tools.name: revert_agent_changes
tools.description: Undo everything the agent changed recently, leaving edits made by the human operator in place. Use this when the user says "put it back how it was" after you have made several changes; use undo for a single step regardless of who made it.

sinceSeconds.description: How far back to reverse, in seconds. Default 120.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo the most recent change, whoever made it. Prefer revert_agent_changes when you specifically want to take back your own edits.

tools.name: redo
tools.description: Redo the change that was most recently undone.

sites.name: aisle-three.vercel.app
sites.description: A wedding seating chart that you and your AI agent arrange together, live on the same canvas. Built on WebMCP.

tools.name: share_plan
tools.description: Tell the human what you are about to do, before you start a multi-step change — one or two plain-language sentences, e.g. "I'll seat both families first, then sort out the two feuds." It appears as a speech bubble on your cursor and in the shared activity feed. Use it at the start of a task and again whenever the plan changes; it makes your work much easier to follow.

plan.description: What you are about to do, in one or two short sentences

tools.name: ask_human
tools.description: Ask the human a question and WAIT for their answer. The question appears as a card on the chart with your suggested options as buttons (and, unless you say otherwise, a box for a reply in their own words); their answer comes back in this tool's result. Use it when a seating decision is theirs to make — which side Grandma sits on, whether the kids get their own table, which of two trade-offs they prefer — rather than guessing. One short question at a time, with 2–4 concrete options. Waits up to ~90 seconds; if they have not answered by then the reply says so and the card stays up.

question.description: The question, in one or two plain sentences

options.description: Suggested answers shown as buttons — 2 to 4 is ideal

allow_free_text.description: Also offer a box for an answer in their own words (default true)

tools.name: point_at
tools.description: Direct the human's eye without changing anything: your cursor flies to each named guest, table, or amenity in turn and hovers there, with your note in its speech bubble; each one glows for a moment. Use it while explaining — "this is the table under the speakers", "these two are the exes". Up to three targets per call.

targets.description: Guest names, table names, or amenities (entrance, dance_floor, band, bathroom, photo_booth, bar, buffet, cake_table, gift_table)

note.description: What to say while pointing — one short sentence

tools.name: get_recent_activity
tools.description: What has happened on the chart lately — the shared activity feed, newest first, each entry marked "human" (done by hand) or "agent" (done by you). Call it at the start of a turn to learn what the human did since you last looked: dragged someone, added a rule, pinned a seat, answered a question. Filter to their actions with who "human".

limit.description: How many entries to return (default 12)

since_seconds.description: Only entries from the last N seconds

tools.name: update_venue
tools.description: Configure the shared venue floor plan. Show, hide, place, resize, and rotate the entrance, dance floor, band & speakers, restrooms, photo booth, bar, buffet & catering, cake table, or gifts & cards table. Prefer the real-world *_ft fields, measured from the room’s top-left; legacy x/y/width/height floor-plan units remain supported. The reply warns if the amenity now overlaps a table or another amenity. The human sees the same saved layout and can adjust it afterward.

enabled.description: Whether this amenity is present and visible

location.description: Named part of the room

x_ft.description: Amenity left edge in feet from the room’s left wall (preferred)

y_ft.description: Amenity top edge in feet from the room’s top wall (preferred)

x.description: Legacy horizontal floor-plan position from the room’s left edge

y.description: Legacy vertical floor-plan position from the room’s top edge

width.description: Legacy amenity width in floor-plan units

height.description: Legacy amenity height in floor-plan units

tools.name: update_venue_dimensions
tools.description: Set the real-world venue room width and length in feet, plus the movement snap grid. The floor plan is drawn to a fixed scale, so growing the room adds floor space around the existing furniture (which stays put); shrinking it nudges anything stranded outside back inside the walls.

snap_ft.description: Grid spacing in feet; use 0 to turn grid snapping off

tools.name: get_seating_chart
tools.description: Read the full current state of the wedding seating chart: every table with its occupants, unseated guests, all constraints with their status, current violations, and the drama score. Call this before making changes so you are working from the latest state — the human may have dragged guests around since your last call.

tools.name: list_guests
tools.description: List guests on the wedding guest list with their group, RSVP status, dietary needs, notes, and where they are seated. Optionally filter to only unseated guests, a specific group/party, or an RSVP status.

filter.description: Optional filter

group.description: Only guests in this group/party, e.g. "College friends"

tools.name: explain_seating
tools.description: Explain one guest’s seating in full: where they sit and with whom, every rule involving them with its live status (including how near or far their table actually is from the dance floor, band, or entrance), their group context, dietary needs, and notes. For an unseated guest: what to honor when choosing their seat, where their group sits, and which tables have space. Use it before moving someone — or when the human asks "why is she there?"

tools.name: add_guest

tools.description: Update a guest's details: name, group, dietary needs, RSVP status, or notes. Identify the guest by name (fuzzy match is fine). Setting RSVP to "no" frees up their seat.

group.description: New group/party

notes.description: Replacement note

tools.name: remove_guest
tools.description: Remove a guest from the wedding entirely. Their seat is freed and any constraints involving them are dropped.

tools.name: import_guests
tools.description: Bulk-import guests from pasted text. Rows copied out of a spreadsheet work as-is — CSV, TSV, or semicolon-separated, with or without a header row; a header (Name / Group or Side / RSVP / Dietary / Notes, in any order, and First + Last name as separate columns) is read and its columns mapped. So does one guest per line with fields separated by " — ", " | " or tabs: name, then group, dietary needs, RSVP (yes/no/pending) — e.g. "Nora Flynn — Childhood friends — vegetarian". A JSON array of {name, group, dietary, rsvp, notes} objects also works. Duplicate names are skipped. (To load an .xlsx file, ask the human to use "Import a Spreadsheet…" under Guests, or paste its rows here.)

text.description: The pasted guest list

default_group.description: Group to assign when a line does not specify one

tools.name: add_table
tools.description: Add one or more tables to the room. Choose a seat count (2–16), shape (round or rect), and optionally count to add a whole row at once — "ten rounds of eight" is one call, and one thing for the human to undo. A single table can be given a name and a position in real-world feet from the room’s top-left, plus a rotation; extras are auto-numbered and each lands in its own open spot. The reply warns if a placement overlaps other furniture.

name.description: Name for the table, e.g. "Head table"; auto-numbered if omitted, and ignored when count is above 1

count.description: How many identical tables to add (default 1)

x_ft.description: Table center in feet from the room’s left wall; single table only

y_ft.description: Table center in feet from the room’s top wall; single table only

tools.name: add_group
tools.description: Create a guest group (a party or side, e.g. "Sailing club") before anyone is in it — useful when you are about to import or add several guests and want the group to exist first. Adding a guest with a new group name creates it too, so only reach for this when you want the empty group itself. Returns the existing name if one already matches, case-insensitively.

tools.name: remove_group
tools.description: Remove an empty group from the guest list. Groups with guests in them are kept — move or remove those guests first (update_guest changes someone’s group).

tools.name: add_constraint
tools.description: Add a seating rule. Pair rules: must_sit_together / must_sit_apart between guest_a and guest_b (same table vs. different tables). Zone rules for a single guest: near_dance_floor, far_from_dance_floor, near_band, far_from_band, near_entrance, far_from_entrance — "near" means one of the closest tables to that spot, "far" one of the farthest. Rules are enforced by auto_arrange and any breach shows up as a violation on the chart.

type.description: Kind of rule

guest_a.description: First guest (pair rules) or the guest (zone rules)

note.description: Why this rule exists, e.g. "recently divorced"

tools.name: remove_constraint
tools.description: Remove a seating rule by its id (see list_constraints or get_seating_chart), or remove every rule involving a named guest.

guest.description: Alternatively: remove all rules involving this guest

tools.name: list_constraints
tools.description: List every seating rule with its id and current status: ok, violated, or pending (someone involved is not seated yet).

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Step the whole chart back one change — the same Undo the human has in the header (⌘Z), and it undoes their edits as well as yours. Use it to take back something you just did that the human did not like; the reply names the change that was undone. For a bigger jump back, save_checkpoint / restore_checkpoint are the better tools. Note: undoing while one of your proposals is on screen counts as rejecting it.

steps.description: How many changes to step back (default 1)

tools.name: redo
tools.description: Put back a change that undo took away — the same Redo the human has in the header. Only available until the next edit, which clears the redo history.

steps.description: How many changes to step forward (default 1)

tools.name: reset_chart
tools.description: Clear the whole chart back to an empty room — every guest, table, and rule, exactly as the human’s Reset button does. This throws away their work, so only call it when the human has asked for it in as many words, and pass confirm true to say that they did. It is a single undo away, and save_checkpoint first if you want a way back.

confirm.description: Must be true. Set it only when the human has explicitly asked to clear the chart.

tools.name: save_checkpoint
tools.description: Save a named snapshot of the entire chart — guests, tables, seating, rules, venue — that restore_checkpoint can return to. Session-only (it does not survive a page reload). Use it before trying something bold: checkpoint, propose a daring layout, and if the human hates it, restore. Saving an existing name overwrites it.

tools.name: restore_checkpoint
tools.description: Restore the chart to a previously saved checkpoint — everything comes back: guests, tables, seating, rules, venue. The restore itself is undoable, and the checkpoint stays saved so you can return again. With no name given and exactly one checkpoint saved, that one is restored.

tools.name: load_sample_wedding
tools.description: Replace the current chart with the built-in sample wedding: 72 named guests in 8 groups, 10 tables, and 17 seating rules including divorced relatives, exes, and a grandmother who hates loud speakers. Great for a demo. Everyone starts unseated; the previous chart can be restored with undo.

tools.name: wrap_up
tools.description: Call once you have finished the human's request. Give a one-or-two-sentence closing summary of what changed, e.g. "Everyone is seated and both feuds are resolved." Your cursor announces it and steps off the canvas until the next request. Optional — the cursor also retires on its own after a quiet minute — but it gives the session a clean ending.

tools.description: Reveal the visible click-through Cognistration science guide for the current machine direction. It explains the two-channel signal, FFR, descriptive frequency bands, evidence limits, and safe listening; it never starts audio or saves a user record, and its PDF export is a static technical snapshot without diary content.

toneId.description: Optional ID from the public tone catalog.

tools.name: cognistration_search_tone_packs
tools.description: Public finished tone-pack browsing for relaxation, sleep preparation, journaling, focus, or creative work. Results include metadata and preview tracks without starting audio.

query.description: Optional pack search or intention text.

tools.name: cognistration_preview_tone_pack
tools.description: Start one public tone-pack preview in the current browser after the user or agent explicitly confirms audio should begin. Search for a pack first and use one of its listed tracks.

confirmed.description: Must be true to start pack audio.

tools.name: cognistration_get_policy_info
tools.description: Canonical policy lookup for Cognistration safety, terms, privacy, cookies, AI use, pricing, or account creation, with a source-grounded summary and page link.

tools.name: cognistration_get_account_options
tools.description: Account and access overview for questions about a free trial, account, platform access, or cost. It explains the free public preview and one-time private workspace without collecting credentials or submitting payment.

tools.name: cognistration_begin_preview
tools.description: Start the visible browser audio preview after the user or agent explicitly confirms they want audio to begin.

confirmed.description: Must be true to start browser audio.

tools.name: cognistration_stop_preview
tools.description: Stop local browser audio in the visible machine without changing the selected controls. This is safe to repeat.

tools.name: cognistration_open_fullscreen
tools.description: Request the visible machine in the host’s larger display mode without changing its controls or audio.

tools.name: cognistration_open_account_signup
tools.description: Navigate the current browser to the semantic Cognistration account-creation form. The user must review and submit it.

tools.name: cognistration_set_session_controls
tools.description: Set the visible carrier, rhythm, and volume controls in the current Cognistration browser session.

tools.name: cognistration_begin_preview
tools.description: Start the local Cognistration audio preview after the listener explicitly confirms playback.

tools.name: cognistration_set_session_direction
tools.description: Select one published Cognistration listening direction in the visible machine without pausing existing audio.

sites.name: edgewright.vercel.app
sites.description: Edgewright turns your Netlify, Vercel and Cloudflare redirect rules into a live console an AI agent drives through WebMCP: test any URL, catch the rule that shadows another, fix the order, export a…

tools.name: test_url
tools.description: Test what a request path does against the current rules: which rule wins, the final status, the destination, and whether it hits a redirect loop. Read-only.

url.description: The request path to test, e.g. /docs/getting-started (query string allowed).

country.description: Optional 2-letter country to simulate Country conditions.

language.description: Optional language to simulate Language conditions.

role.description: Optional role to simulate Role conditions.

cookies.description: Optional cookie name/value map to simulate Cookie/has/missing conditions.

tools.name: audit_rules
tools.description: Scan every rule for problems: rules shadowed by a broader rule above them, rules made unreachable by a catch-all, redirect loops, and lines the platform silently ignores. Read-only.

tools.name: export_config
tools.description: Return the current rules serialized in the active platform native format, ready to paste into your project. Read-only.

tools.name: add_rule
tools.description: Add a redirect or rewrite rule to the end of the list. Use status 200 for a rewrite/SPA fallback, 301/302/307/308 for a redirect.

source.description: Source pattern, e.g. /old/* or /blog/:slug

destination.description: Destination, e.g. /new/:splat or https://example.com

status.description: HTTP status. 200 = rewrite, 301/302/307/308 = redirect. Defaults to the platform default.

tools.name: edit_rule
tools.description: Change the source, destination, or status of the rule at a given position (1-based, as shown in the list).

position.description: 1-based position of the rule to edit.

tools.name: remove_rule
tools.description: Delete the rule at a given position (1-based).

position.description: 1-based position of the rule to remove.

tools.name: reorder_rule
tools.description: Move the rule at one position to another. Order matters: the first matching rule wins, so this is how you fix a rule shadowed by a broader one above it.

from.description: 1-based current position.

to.description: 1-based target position.

tools.name: import_config
tools.description: Replace all rules by importing a config in the active platform format (Netlify _redirects text, a vercel.json string, or Cloudflare _redirects text).

text.description: The raw config text to import.

tools.name: translate
tools.description: Translate the current rules to another platform (netlify, vercel, cloudflare, nextjs) and return the config in that format, with notes on anything that could not carry across. Read-only.

tools.name: bulk_test
tools.description: Test many request paths at once and report each outcome, failures first. Accepts a list of paths and/or a sitemap.xml body. Read-only.

sitemap.description: A sitemap.xml body; its <loc> paths are tested too.

tools.name: test_path
tools.description: Compile a single source pattern and report whether it matches a URL and what it captures, without touching the rule list. Read-only.

tools.name: explain_rule
tools.description: Explain the rule at a given position (1-based) in plain English. Read-only.

tools.name: list_platforms
tools.description: List the platforms Edgewright can parse, test, translate and export. Read-only.

tools.name: set_platform
tools.description: Switch the working platform and translate the current rules into it. Constructs the target does not support are dropped and reported.

tools.name: audit_headers
tools.description: Audit response headers for a path against a headers config (Netlify _headers, or Vercel/Next.js headers). Flags missing security headers and weak CSP. Read-only.

tools.name: load_config
tools.description: Load a redirect config into Preflight. Optionally set the platform (netlify, vercel, cloudflare, nextjs).

tools.name: set_expectations
tools.description: Set the routes that must work: a list of { path, destination?, status? }. These are what the gate checks.

tools.name: run_gate
tools.description: Run the preflight gate: resolve every expected route, audit the rules and return a single pass or fail with the failing detail. Read-only.

tools.name: explain_failure
tools.description: Explain why the last gate failed, route by route. Read-only.

tools.name: export_report
tools.description: Export the last gate result as a PR-comment markdown block or a JSON artifact. Read-only.

tools.name: load_source
tools.description: Load the source config to migrate. Optionally set the source platform (netlify, vercel, cloudflare, nextjs).

tools.name: set_target
tools.description: Set the platform to migrate the config to.

tools.name: migrate
tools.description: Translate the source config to the target platform and return it, with notes on anything that could not carry across.

tools.name: verify_migration
tools.description: Replay every source URL through both the source and migrated configs and report whether they resolve identically. Read-only.

tools.name: audit_source
tools.description: Audit the source config for shadowed rules, unreachable rules and loops. Read-only.

tools.name: export_report
tools.description: Export the migration as a markdown report or the target config text. Read-only.

sites.name: fieldwork-beat-machine.openai.chatgpt.site
sites.description: A tactile 12-voice beat machine with classic drum-machine grooves, deep synths, keyboard and touch pads, WebMCP controls, and stereo WAV export.

tools.name: get_state
tools.description: Read the current beat-machine preset, tempo, transport, musical key and scale, 24-sound library, six editable instrument slots and their complete sound-design parameters, selected pad bank, all 12 playable pads, plus the 12 by 16 velocity and MIDI-note patterns.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Read the complete portable Fieldwork project document, including its name, pattern, notes, mix, musical key, and six instrument patches. Use it for backup or as input to load_project.

tools.name: load_project
tools.description: Validate and atomically replace the current local project with a Fieldwork project document. Stops playback and recording, preserves an undo step, and autosaves locally. Invalid documents leave the current project unchanged.

tools.name: export_project
tools.description: Create a portable JSON backup of the current project and optionally download it. This does not render audio; use export_track for WAV audio.

tools.name: undo_edit
tools.description: Undo the most recent local project edit. Returns changed=false when no undo history remains.

tools.name: redo_edit
tools.description: Restore the most recently undone local project edit. Returns changed=false when no redo history remains.

tools.name: set_tempo
tools.description: Set the beat-machine tempo in BPM (45 to 220).

tools.name: set_swing
tools.description: Set sixteenth-note swing. Use a fraction from 0 to 0.45 or a percentage from 0 to 45.

tools.name: set_controls
tools.description: Adjust the beat-machine mix and timing controls: tempo, swing, tone, space, master volume, humanize, and default export bars. Omitted controls stay unchanged.

tools.name: select_kit
tools.description: Load one of the nine instrument and groove presets: 808-night, 909-warehouse, linn-pop, sp-dust, mpc-swing, acid-cell, electro-break, dub-orbit, or minimal-12.

tools.name: select_instrument
tools.description: Map the performance pads to all voices, a 12-pad drum bank, or one of six playable instrument slots using the selected key and scale. Slots are laid out U I O / J K L; instruments can be lead, chord, pluck, bass, sub, or tuned fx.

tools.name: configure_instrument
tools.description: Load one of 24 categorized sound presets into a U I O / J K L instrument slot, or target a base voice. Sounds cover neon leads, pads, brass, strings, keys, bells, acid, reese, 808 and sub basses, noise, radio, and atmospheric FX.

tools.name: configure_instruments
tools.description: Atomically load sounds into 1 to 6 distinct U I O / J K L instrument slots. Results preserve input order; duplicate slots or any invalid item reject the whole batch without changing the current configuration.

tools.name: set_instrument_params
tools.description: Dial in an instrument slot with attack, decay, sustain, release, cutoff, resonance, drive, motion, stereo width, octave, and waveform. Omitted sound-design controls stay unchanged and changes apply to live playback and WAV export.

tools.name: reset_instrument
tools.description: Restore a U I O / J K L instrument slot's current sound preset to its original ADSR, filter, drive, motion, width, octave, and waveform settings.

tools.name: randomize_instrument
tools.description: Create a playable sound-design variation for a U I O / J K L instrument slot. An optional seed makes the ADSR, filter, motion, waveform, and timbre result repeatable.

tools.name: set_key
tools.description: Choose the musical root and scale used by all twelve melodic pads. Root accepts note names such as C, F#, Bb, or a pitch class from 0 to 11; scales are minor, major, dorian, pentatonic, and chromatic.

tools.name: set_step
tools.description: Write or clear a single sequencer step, optionally setting a MIDI note for a melodic lane. Steps are numbered 1 to 16; voices include kick, snare, clap, hatClosed, hatOpen, perc, sub, bass, chord, lead, pluck, and fx.

tools.name: set_pattern
tools.description: Replace any number of voice lanes in the 16-step sequencer. Supply velocity lanes and, optionally, matching MIDI-note lanes to lay complete melodic tracks in one action; omitted lanes stay unchanged.

tools.name: clear_pattern
tools.description: Clear all 12 sequencer lanes, leaving a silent 16-step grid ready for an agent or performer to lay a new track.

tools.name: set_voice_mute
tools.description: Mute or unmute one instrument lane without deleting its sequencer steps.

tools.name: set_recording
tools.description: Arm or disarm on-tempo grid recording. When armed, performance pads and trigger-pad actions can print at the playhead.

tools.name: mutate_pattern
tools.description: Create a musical variation or fill while keeping the core kick and sub pocket intact.

tools.name: transport
tools.description: Start, stop, or toggle the beat-machine transport.

tools.name: trigger_pad
tools.description: Audition a voice or one of the 12 currently mapped performance pads and optionally place it onto the current sequencer step. Melodic pads automatically print their note; an explicit MIDI note can override it.

tools.name: export_track
tools.description: Render the current beat and synth arrangement to a stereo 48 kHz WAV file, make it available for preview, and optionally download it.

sites.name: hanifasepthi.github.io
sites.description: ITS Maps memantau peta, kamera lalu lintas, status Raspberry Pi, dan object detection RF-DETR secara realtime.

tools.name: list_its_maps_device_ids
tools.description: List all ITS Maps Raspberry Pi device IDs and their online/offline status from Firebase RTDB.

tools.name: research_with_its_maps_assistant
tools.description: Ask the evidence-grounded ITS Maps AI assistant about Indonesian maps, realtime devices, traffic, CCTV availability, scientific sources, calculations, or public technical documentation. The assistant reports uncertainty and source limitations instead of inventing map or camera data.

question.title: Question for ITS Maps Assistant
question.description: A complete question or task for the ITS Maps research and map assistant.

tools.name: get_its_maps_device_status
tools.description: Get realtime ITS Maps Raspberry Pi status: online/offline, last heartbeat, road, traffic light color/duration, vehicle counts, RF-DETR object data, camera status, and update state from Firebase RTDB.

deviceId.description: Optional device ID, for example 'raspberry-its'. Omit to list every device.

tools.name: get_its_maps_camera_health
tools.description: Check whether the ITS Maps Raspberry Pi camera tunnel is healthy, including local camera, public camera, stream state, note, and heartbeat.

tools.name: get_its_maps_camera_snapshot
tools.description: Get the latest ITS Maps Raspberry Pi camera snapshot image when RTDB stores a base64 data URL, together with the current object detection count.

tools.name: get_its_maps_latest_ai_detections
tools.description: Get metadata about the latest ITS Maps AI/camera snapshot pair captured by Raspberry Pi from Firebase RTDB snapshotHistory.

tools.name: get_its_maps_realtime_map_summary
tools.description: Return a realtime ITS Maps summary for AI agents: generated time, device count, online count, and per-device traffic/camera/object status.

tools.name: get_its_maps_windows_app_status
tools.description: Check whether the verified ITS Maps Microsoft Store package is installed on this Windows device. The browser may request the Apps on device permission.

tools.name: get_its_maps_microsoft_store_public_status
tools.description: Read the verified public Microsoft Store rating, acquisition count, and recent reviews snapshot for ITS Maps. Missing values are returned as unavailable and are never estimated.

tools.name: search_its_maps_traffic_location
tools.description: Search ITS Maps RTDB traffic devices by location, road name, device ID, or Raspberry label.

location.description: Location text, road name, or device ID, for example 'Gang Gotong Royong' or 'raspberry-its'.

tools.name: close_its_modal
tools.description: Close the topmost visible ITS Maps modal, detail panel, or AI history sheet.

tools.name: analyze_its_modal
tools.description: Read and summarize the open ITS Maps modal, including active tab, AI history, metrics, text, and scroll state.

tools.name: scroll_its_modal
tools.description: Scroll the open ITS Maps modal to the top, bottom, or both directions.

tools.name: go_its_raspberry_home
tools.description: Close the blocking modal and center ITS Maps on the primary Raspberry Pi device.

tools.name: get_its_creator_profile
tools.description: Return the locally verified ITS Maps creator profile, photo, education, skills, and source links. No external search API is used.

tools.name: list_its_ai_skills
tools.description: List the client-side AI skills and models available in ITS Maps.

tools.name: research_its_public_knowledge
tools.description: Plan and run one evidence-grounded ITS Maps research pipeline. It searches public metadata, reads only accessible HTML/PDF blocks, synthesizes with a local model, validates citations, and lists only sources actually cited.

question.description: Complete user question or follow-up.

tools.name: plan_its_public_research
tools.description: Use the same local planner as ITS chat and return its validated research/realtime/tool plan without starting retrieval.

tools.name: read_its_public_url
tools.description: Read and explain one public URL through the single ITS ResearchOrchestrator. CORS, authentication, robots, or paywall restrictions are reported as blocked; page content is never invented.

url.description: Public HTTP or HTTPS URL.

question.description: Optional question about the page.

tools.name: get_its_live_research_activity
tools.description: Return the current event-sourced research playback with actual search, source, block, PDF, evidence, writing, and validation events.

tools.name: get_its_research_diagnostics
tools.description: Return local model selections and timing diagnostics. Model details are exposed here rather than inserted into user answers.

tools.name: get_its_last_research_context
tools.description: Return the latest client-side research memory for grounded follow-up questions.

tools.name: clear_its_research_context
tools.description: Clear current client-side research memory and cancel the active research worker.

tools.name: open_its_maps_resource
tools.description: Open a public ITS Maps resource such as documentation, privacy policy, licence, PDF preview, llms.txt, or the realtime map.

tools.name: search_its_maps_site
tools.description: Search public ITS Maps documentation and route the user to the documentation page with the requested query.

tools.name: get_its_maps_public_context
tools.description: Return public ITS Maps AI-agent context from llms.txt or llms-full.txt.

sites.name: planner.kitchen.hotelos.ai
sites.description: Design commercial kitchens online with dimensioned 2D floor plans, interactive 3D walkthroughs, configurable equipment, and service-flow simulation.

tools.name: get_workspace_guide
tools.description: Read compact workspace conventions when the task needs coordinate, revision, workflow, or safety guidance. Request full detail only for operation schemas, recovery codes, tool descriptions, and complete limitations.

detail.description: Defaults to compact. Use full for operation schemas, error recovery, and tool descriptions.

input_schema.description: Returns the coordinate system, workflow, and conventions agents must follow.

tools.name: get_component_catalog
tools.description: Search catalog components for add_component operations. Returns a compact, paginated list by default; request full detail only for shortlisted entries. Filter by free text, category, or capability.

query.description: Optional free-text search over catalog names, synonyms, and tags.

category.description: Optional category filter such as cooking, cold, prep, washing, landing, storage, hood.

capability.description: Optional station capability filter such as range-cook or dish-wash.

detail.description: Defaults to compact. Full includes clearances, placement rules, presets, skins, and footprint.

offset.description: Zero-based result offset; defaults to 0.

limit.description: Maximum entries to return; defaults to 5.

tools.name: get_layout
tools.description: Read the current plan in exact millimetres — the spatial model agents work with instead of screenshots. Views: summary (room, per-component rects and rotations), architecture (polygon, openings, pillars, zones), components (full equipment records), full (everything incl. scenarios and settings). Defaults to the active variant.

view.description: Detail level; defaults to summary.

variantId.description: Optional layout variant ID; defaults to the active variant.

componentIds.description: Optional component ID filter for the components view.

tools.name: analyze_layout
tools.description: Structured diagnostics for a layout revision: outside-room, equipment-overlap, pillar-overlap, and clearance-obstructed findings with severity, affected component IDs, and remediation. Advisory only — not regulatory certification.

variantId.description: Optional layout variant ID; defaults to the active variant.

tools.name: suggest_component_placement
tools.description: Ask the workspace for a collision-free anchor position for a catalog component, optionally near a preferred millimetre point. Useful before add_component when you do not care to compute free space yourself.

variantId.description: Optional layout variant ID; defaults to the active variant.

xMm.description: Millimetres from the room origin along +x.

yMm.description: Millimetres from the room origin along +y.

preferredPoint.description: Optional preferred millimetre point to place near.

tools.name: get_simulation_guide
tools.description: Read the service-simulation contract: scenario list with parameters, editable fields with constraints, staff roles, and the meaning of each result metric. Scenario edits are applied as update_scenario operations through preview_layout_changes; runs execute with run_simulation.

tools.name: get_app_state
tools.description: Read the current visible workflow stage, plan/3D and simulation views, 3D scene controls, overlays, panels, open dialogs, source reference visibility, active layout and scenario, component selection, simulation-result availability, and undo/redo availability. This does not change the workspace.

tools.name: set_app_view
tools.description: Navigate the visible app by setting its workflow stage, plan/3D or simulation view, 3D scene controls, overlay, panels, or source reference visibility. Omitted fields remain unchanged; pass overlay null to close an overlay. Open dialogs are reported but cannot be controlled by agents. This does not change the document revision.

stage.description: Optional workflow stage to display.

view.description: Optional workspace view to display.

overlay.description: Optional workspace overlay. Pass null to close the active overlay.

walkMode.description: Enter or exit kitchen walk mode.

walkView.description: Set the kitchen walk camera to first-person or third-person.

showClearances.description: Show or hide equipment and opening clearance overlays in the 3D scene.

wallsTransparent.description: Render the 3D room walls as transparent or opaque.

showLabels.description: Show or hide labels in the 3D scene.

simulationView.description: Set the simulation result view to 2D operations, 3D overview, or first-person walk mode.

catalog.description: Show or hide the component catalog.

essentials.description: Show or hide operational essentials in the inspector.

revisions.description: Show or hide revision history in the inspector.

panels.description: Patch one or more panel visibility flags. Omitted flags remain unchanged.

showReference.description: Show or hide the source reference overlay in the plan.

input_schema.description: Provide at least one field. Omitted fields keep their current values.

tools.name: select_components
tools.description: Replace, add to, toggle, or clear the current component selection using IDs from the active layout. Optionally reveal the result in the plan, 3D scene, or split view. Selection does not change the document revision.

componentIds.description: Component IDs in the active layout. Required and non-empty except when mode is clear.

mode.description: Selection operation. Defaults to replace.

reveal.description: Optionally switch to the equipment stage and reveal the selection in plan, 3D, or split view.

tools.name: focus_camera
tools.description: Move the visible 3D camera to fit the room, frame a component, or inspect an exact millimetre point. Optionally switches between perspective and top view without changing the project revision.

target.description: Camera target type.

componentId.description: Required component ID when target is component.

xMm.description: Horizontal millimetres from the room origin.

yMm.description: Vertical millimetres from the room origin.

point.description: Required exact plan point when target is point.

tools.name: check_operational_essentials
tools.description: Check scenario-based operational readiness for a layout: required stations, service flows, staffing, capacities, circulation, clearances, and professional-review reminders. Advisory planning guidance only, not regulatory certification.

variantId.description: Optional layout variant ID; defaults to the active variant.

scenarioId.description: Optional scenario ID; defaults to the active scenario.

tools.name: preview_layout_changes
tools.description: Validate an operation batch and return a single-use token, changes, warnings, and diagnostics.

tools.name: apply_layout_changes
tools.description: Commit live workspace: previewToken or expectedRevision + operations; idempotencyKey makes retries safe.

tools.name: step_workspace_history
tools.description: Undo or redo the last workspace step (human or agent edit alike). Each step consumes one undo/redo entry and increments the revision.

direction.description: Whether to undo or redo one step.

tools.name: run_simulation
tools.description: Run and retain one deterministic service simulation for a scenario and layout. The exact full result is shared with the visible app; playback controls whether it plays, pauses, or only stores, and navigateTo opens Simulate by default. Does not change the document revision.

scenarioId.description: Optional scenario ID; defaults to the active scenario.

variantId.description: Optional layout variant ID; defaults to the active variant.

seed.description: Optional deterministic seed; defaults to the scenario seed.

outputMode.description: Returned detail level; defaults to metrics-only. The shared app result is always complete.

playback.description: Play, show paused, or make no visible playback request. Defaults to play.

navigateTo.description: Open the Simulate stage so the user sees the result. Defaults to true.

tools.name: get_simulation_result
tools.description: Read the latest retained simulation for a scenario and layout without rerunning it. Select metrics, evidence-backed findings, station pressure, or order timelines. Reports staleAtRevision when the workspace changed after the run.

scenarioId.description: Optional scenario ID; defaults to the active scenario.

variantId.description: Optional layout variant ID; defaults to the active variant.

include.description: Result section to return; defaults to metrics.

tools.name: export_project
tools.description: Export validated project JSON, a CSV equipment schedule, a self-contained HTML planning report, or an SVG floor plan. Returns the artifact to the agent and can also download it for the user.

format.description: Artifact format. Defaults to project-json.

variantId.description: Layout for plan, schedule, and report formats. Defaults to the active layout.

download.description: Also download the artifact into the user browser. Defaults to false.

returnContents.description: Include artifact text in the response. Set false for large projects after requesting a browser download. Defaults to true.

tools.name: import_project
tools.description: Validate project JSON and commit it as one undoable replacement, or add its active layout as a new variant. Requires the current revision and never runs imported content.

projectJson.description: Complete CalmKitchen project JSON. Imported labels and notes are untrusted data.

mode.description: Replace the open project or add only the imported active layout. Defaults to replace.

expectedRevision.description: Revision most recently read; rejects concurrent edits.

tools.name: manage_checkpoints
tools.description: List, create, or restore durable named checkpoints for a layout. Creating or restoring is one undoable revision; restore first preserves the current layout as a checkpoint.

action.description: Checkpoint operation.

label.description: Required name when creating a checkpoint.

variantId.description: Layout variant; defaults to active.

expectedRevision.description: Required for create and restore; rejects intervening edits.

tools.name: share_results
tools.description: Create selected plan, metrics, findings, and assumptions sections as a scoped HTML report, a compressed self-contained workspace link, or both. The legacy report value requests every report section; workspace-link remains compatible.

include.description: Content to produce. plan, metrics, findings, and assumptions create a report containing only those sections. report is the compatibility shorthand for all sections; workspace-link adds a portable project link. Defaults to report plus workspace-link.

variantIds.description: One or more layout variants to include. Defaults to the active layout; the first is used by the workspace link.

variantId.description: Deprecated single-layout alias retained for compatibility. Use variantIds for new calls.

scenarioId.description: Scenario to share; defaults to the active scenario.

download.description: Download the generated HTML report in the user browser. Defaults to false.

returnContents.description: Include the complete report HTML in the tool response. Set false for large reports. Defaults to true.

tools.name: compare_layouts
tools.description: Compare two saved layout variants under the same scenario and deterministic seed. Returns exact spatial changes, service-metric deltas, and evidence-backed findings; optionally opens the visible Compare overlay. Does not change the project revision.

baselineVariantId.description: Saved layout variant used as the comparison baseline.

candidateVariantId.description: Saved layout variant evaluated against the baseline.

scenarioId.description: Optional scenario ID; defaults to the active scenario.

openOverlay.description: Open the visible Compare overlay after a successful comparison. Defaults to false.

tools.name: run_auto_layout
tools.description: Use only when the user explicitly requests an automated multi-candidate search; do not use for routine improvements that a focused preview/apply edit can solve. Starts a computationally expensive, deterministic, revision-bound search without changing the project. Poll get_auto_layout_run, then adopt only a user-chosen confirmed finalist.

variantId.description: Optional baseline variant ID; defaults to the active variant.

scenarioId.description: Optional scenario ID; defaults to the active scenario.

objective.description: Optimization priority; defaults to balanced.

seed.description: Deterministic non-negative integer seed. Defaults to a normalized form of the scenario seed.

maxDurationMs.description: Time budget in milliseconds, 100–120000. Defaults to 30000.

targetP90WaitSeconds.description: Optional target P90 order wait in seconds.

minimumAisleMm.description: Optional minimum aisle rule in millimetres; defaults to the layout constraint.

openOverlay.description: Open manual Auto-layout controls. Agent-run progress is returned by get_auto_layout_run; defaults to false.

tools.name: get_auto_layout_run
tools.description: Read status, progress, and compact confirmed-finalist and candidate summaries from a run started by run_auto_layout. Page candidates with offset and limit; pass a confirmed finalist resultId to retrieve its complete layout. Reports when its source project revision has become stale; never changes or adopts a layout.

runId.description: Run ID returned by run_auto_layout.

resultId.description: Optional confirmed finalist ID. When present, finalist contains its complete saved-layout candidate.

offset.description: Zero-based candidate-summary offset. Defaults to 0.

limit.description: Maximum candidate summaries to return. Defaults to 20.

tools.name: cancel_auto_layout_run
tools.description: Cancel one active auto-layout run by ID. This affects transient optimizer work only and never changes the project revision.

runId.description: Active run ID returned by run_auto_layout.

tools.name: adopt_auto_layout_candidate
tools.description: Save one confirmed finalist from a completed auto-layout run as a new child layout. Requires the unchanged source revision and commits through the same atomic adoption operation as the human Auto-layout workspace.

runId.description: Completed run ID returned by run_auto_layout.
