tools.name: scan_images_c2pa
tools.description: Scan every on the current page for C2PA Content Credentials (content provenance metadata) and return a per-image summary: whether a manifest is present, the claim generator (the tool that produced or edited the image), the title, and the signer name. Use this to find which images on a page carry provenance data. Note: provenance is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

limit.description: Maximum number of images to fetch and scan (default 25, max 100).

tools.name: inspect_image_c2pa
tools.description: Fetch a single image (by CSS selector or URL) and return its fully decoded C2PA manifest store: every manifest's claim, assertions (e.g. c2pa.actions edit history, schema.org authorship), and the COSE signature details (algorithm and signing-certificate identity). Provide exactly one of `selector` or `url`. Note: the signature is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

selector.description: CSS selector for an element on the page.

url.description: Same-origin image URL (absolute same-origin, or relative to the current page) to fetch and inspect. Cross-origin URLs are rejected.

tools.name: search_pokemon_cards
tools.description: Search for Pokemon TCG cards across multiple Shopify stores in real time. Returns products with title, price, currency, vendor (store), availability, and link. Use this when the user wants to find a specific card by name, set, or keyword. For deep catalog queries against the local database (rarity, HP, type), use browse_card_database instead.

query.description: Card name, set code, or keyword (e.g. 'charizard'). Required.

country.description: Two-letter ISO country code (e.g. 'GB', 'US', 'JP'). Default 'GB'. Use 'ALL' for global.

max_price.description: Maximum price in the country's major currency unit.

mode.description: 'cards' (default) returns only cards; 'merch' returns merch; 'all' returns everything.

limit.description: 1–50. Default 20.

tools.name: browse_card_database
tools.description: Browse the offline Pokemon TCG card database (~20k cards) with structured filters. Returns card metadata only — no prices or stores. Pair with get_card_details to find where to buy.

type.description: Pokemon type, e.g. 'Fire', 'Water'.

language.description: Card language. Default 'en'.

sort.description: Sort order. Default 'date-desc'.

limit.description: Results per page, 1–60. Default 24.

offset.description: Pagination offset. Default 0.

tools.name: get_card_details
tools.description: Get full product details for a single card listing — title, price, vendor/store, availability, shipping to the requested country, and a buy link. Use the product_id from search_pokemon_cards results.

product_id.description: Product ID from search results (e.g. 'gid://shopify/Product/12345'). Required.

country.description: Two-letter ISO country code. Default 'GB'.

tools.name: list_sets
tools.description: List all Pokemon TCG sets in the database with codes, names, release dates, and card counts.

tools.name: find_cards_in_set
tools.description: List cards within a specific Pokemon TCG set, optionally filtered by rarity or supertype. Use this for set-completion workflows, e.g. 'show me all holo rares in sv3'.

limit.description: Results per page, 1–60. Default 60.

offset.description: Pagination offset. Default 0.

tools.name: get_filter_taxonomy
tools.description: Return the available values for every filter dimension used by search_pokemon_cards and browse_card_database: rarities, supertypes, types, subtypes, series, languages, and sets. Call this BEFORE searching if the user gives a domain-specific term (rarity, supertype, set, etc.) and you need to map it to the canonical value the search tool accepts.

tools.name: get_featured_cards
tools.description: Return ~24 curated popular Pokemon cards (Charizard, Pikachu, Mewtwo, etc.) WITHOUT requiring a search query. Use this when an agent needs to show the user something useful before the user has typed anything — landing page, 'what's popular', or to seed a cold-start UI. Always returns real products (never an empty page) so agents see content immediately. Returns prices already normalized to the requested country's currency.

country.description: Two-letter ISO country code. Default 'GB'. Use 'ALL' for a global mix (USD-priced).

tools.name: analyze_card_image
tools.description: Analyze a Pokemon card image for authenticity signals using Workers AI vision (Llama 3.2 11B Vision). Returns centering estimate, holo pattern, print sharpness, surface condition, and any visible authenticity marks (1st Edition stamp, Shadowless border, error-card indicators). Optionally cross-checks against an expected card name. image_url must be a public HTTPS URL the server can fetch. ~5–15 sec per call. Unavailable in EU regions.

image_url.description: Public HTTPS URL of the card image. Must be fetchable by the server. Required. Max ~5 MB.

expected_card.description: Optional. The name of the card you expect (e.g. 'Charizard Base Set Holo'). If provided and the visible card does not match, the analysis will flag the mismatch.

tools.name: compare_prices
tools.description: Compare prices for a specific card across every connected Shopify store, with all prices normalized into the requested currency. Returns the cheapest listing plus the full normalized listings (sorted low→high). Use this when the user asks 'where's the cheapest place to buy this card in [currency]?' or 'show me all the listings for [card] sorted by price'.

query.description: Card name or keyword. Required.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO currency to normalize into (e.g. 'GBP', 'USD', 'EUR'). Default 'GBP'.

limit.description: Max stores to compare. Default 30, max 50.

tools.name: identify_card_image
tools.description: Identify a Pokemon TCG product from a photo (card, tin, box, pack, ETB, bundle, deck). Returns the product type, name, set, number, year, confidence, and a clean search term you can pass straight to search_pokemon_cards. Accepts the image as either an HTTPS URL or a base64 data URI. Powered by Workers AI Llama 3.2 11B Vision — ~5–15 sec per call. Unavailable in EU regions.

image_url.description: Public HTTPS URL of the image. Server fetches it. Use this OR image_base64, not both. Max ~5 MB.

image_base64.description: Base64-encoded image bytes (no data URI prefix). Combined with image_content_type to form the data URI sent to the server. Use this when the image is already in memory (e.g. user just picked a file) and forwarding the URL would require an extra fetch. Mutually exclusive with image_url.

image_content_type.description: MIME type for image_base64 (e.g. 'image/jpeg', 'image/png'). Required when image_base64 is set, ignored otherwise. Default 'image/jpeg' when omitted.

mode.description: How the server should read the image. Default 'url' when image_url is set; Default 'data_uri' when image_base64 is set. Normally you can omit this — the tool picks based on which input was provided.

tools.name: add_to_basket
tools.description: Add a card to the user's basket by its UCP product_id (from search_pokemon_cards results). type.description: Pokemon type (e.g. 'Fire').

series.description: Series (e.g. 'Scarlet & Violet').

price_max.description: Maximum price in user's currency.

sort.description: Sort order.

tools.name: highlight_card

tools.name: update_graph

Before the first edit, call get_agent_instructions and inspect_document. This appends to the one pending human-reviewed draft and never applies changes automatically.

expectedRevision.description: Revision returned by inspect_document. Required for every write.

expectedShape.description: The complete current canonical shape returned by inspect_document. Used as a freshness guard.

targetId.description: Use "CANVAS" on a whiteboard document together with absolute x/y.

tools.name: insert_graph3d
tools.description: Insert a 3D figure (graph3dShape) from a preset and typed Graph3D fields. Coordinates are z-up (zUp) right-handed; object rotation is in radians (pi/2 = 90 degrees) while camera.fov is in degrees, and w/h are px. Expressions are evaluation expressions, not TeX. Use insert_graph for 2D function graphs, coordinate planes and number lines. Before the first edit, call get_agent_instructions and inspect_document. This appends to the one pending human-reviewed draft and never applies changes automatically.

expectedRevision.description: Revision returned by inspect_document. Required for every write.

targetId.description: Use "CANVAS" on a whiteboard document together with absolute x/y.

preset.description: Starting point: revolution (solid of revolution with a section), surface (surface with contours), tricylinder (common part of three cylinders), sphereTetrahedron (sphere and tetrahedron), blank (axes and grid only).

spec.description: A whole Graph3DSpec, minus version and cuts. Individual fields below override it.

objects.description: Solids, surfaces, curves, points and planes. Replaces the whole list (it does not append). Expressions are evaluation expressions, not TeX; rotation/translation/scale are expression strings and rotation is in radians (pi/2 = 90 degrees).

regions.description: Parts two or more objects have in common, drawn in their own colour. Nothing is cut away.

annotations.description: labelTex is TeX. Labels are never baked into the picture; they stay a vector layer.

camera.description: Shallow-merged onto the current camera. fov is in degrees (the one degree-valued field).

view.description: Shallow-merged onto the current view settings. Coordinates are z-up (zUp) right-handed.

tools.name: update_graph3d
tools.description: Partially update an existing 3D figure in place. The shape ID, position, anchor and every unspecified field are preserved; supplied arrays replace the whole list while camera and view are shallow-merged. Never rebuild a figure with delete_shapes plus insert_graph3d — that loses its position, size and camera. Before the first edit, call get_agent_instructions and inspect_document. This appends to the one pending human-reviewed draft and never applies changes automatically.

tools.name: list_comments
tools.description: List the comment threads on the document: where each is pinned, who wrote it, and whether it is resolved. Call this before commenting so you do not repeat a point that is already raised.

includeResolved.description: Include threads a person already marked resolved.

targetId.description: Only threads pinned to this body block or overlay shape.

tools.name: add_comment
tools.description: Pin a new comment thread to any place in the document: a whole block, an exact phrase inside it, one inline formula, or one or more figures. State who you are in author so the reader sees which AI wrote it. The target must exist in the document as it stands; content that only exists inside the pending edit draft cannot be commented on until a person applies it. Comments annotate the document without changing any content, so they apply immediately and never occupy the pending edit draft.

author.description: Who is writing. Required: the person reading the document must be able to see which AI left the comment.

name.description: Display name on the comment, for example ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini.

vendor.description: Which company's model is writing. This chooses the logo drawn on the comment avatar; use other when none of these fit.

model.description: Optional exact model name shown next to the display name.

target.description: Where the comment is pinned. Pass shapeIds for a figure, blockId plus mathInlineId for one formula, blockId plus text for a phrase, or blockId alone for the whole block.

blockId.description: Body or problem-area block ID from inspect_document.

text.description: Exact phrase inside that block to underline. Must appear verbatim.

occurrence.description: Which occurrence of text to use when it appears more than once.

mathInlineId.description: Inline math ID inside that block.

text.description: Comment body. $...$ becomes math and **bold** / *italic* are honoured.

tools.name: reply_comment
tools.description: Reply inside an existing comment thread. Use this to answer a person's question or to follow up on your own comment instead of pinning a second thread to the same place. Comments annotate the document without changing any content, so they apply immediately and never occupy the pending edit draft.

author.description: Who is writing. Required: the person reading the document must be able to see which AI left the comment.

name.description: Display name on the comment, for example ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini.

vendor.description: Which company's model is writing. This chooses the logo drawn on the comment avatar; use other when none of these fit.

model.description: Optional exact model name shown next to the display name.

threadId.description: Thread ID from list_comments or add_comment.

tools.name: resolve_comment
tools.description: Mark a comment thread resolved, or reopen one. Resolve only threads whose point is actually settled. Comments annotate the document without changing any content, so they apply immediately and never occupy the pending edit draft.

sites.name: ventouris.github.io
sites.description: A 2D room layout planner. Place furniture, check clearances, and let an AI agent read and edit the exact same geometry through WebMCP.

tools.name: get_room
tools.description: Get the room dimensions in centimetres. Coordinates start at the top-left corner of the room.

tools.name: get_openings
tools.description: List the doors and windows, with the wall each sits on, its offset along that wall, and its width in centimetres.

tools.name: get_objects
tools.description: List every furniture object with its position, footprint, rotation and locked flag.

tools.name: get_object
tools.description: Get one furniture object by id.

objectId.description: Id of a furniture object, e.g. "desk-1".

tools.name: get_constraints
tools.description: List the layout constraints, each with a human-readable description and whether it is currently satisfied.

tools.name: get_collisions
tools.description: List overlapping furniture, objects outside the room bounds, and objects blocking a door clearance zone.

tools.name: get_distances
tools.description: Distances for one object: to each wall, to every other object (nearest first), to each opening, and to the nearest window.

objectId.description: Id of a furniture object, e.g. "desk-1".

tools.name: validate_layout
tools.description: Check the whole layout: returns valid plus the current collisions and constraint violations.

tools.name: set_room_dimensions
tools.description: Resize the room. Furniture keeps its coordinates, so shrinking a room can push objects out of bounds.

tools.name: add_object
tools.description: Add a piece of furniture. Known types (bed, desk, chair, sofa, table, wardrobe, bookshelf, nightstand) fill in default dimensions when width and depth are omitted. Position defaults to a free-ish spot near the top-left.

type.description: bed | desk | chair | sofa | table | wardrobe | bookshelf | nightstand | custom

tools.name: move_object
tools.description: Move an object to an absolute position (top-left corner, in centimetres) and re-validate the layout.

objectId.description: Id of a furniture object, e.g. "desk-1".

tools.name: rotate_object
tools.description: Rotate an object to 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees. At 90 and 270 its width and depth swap.

objectId.description: Id of a furniture object, e.g. "desk-1".

tools.name: resize_object
tools.description: Change an object width and/or depth in centimetres.

objectId.description: Id of a furniture object, e.g. "desk-1".

tools.name: rename_object
tools.description: Rename an object. The label is what the person sees on the canvas.

objectId.description: Id of a furniture object, e.g. "desk-1".

tools.name: remove_object
tools.description: Remove an object from the room. Constraints that referenced it are removed too.

objectId.description: Id of a furniture object, e.g. "desk-1".

tools.name: duplicate_object
tools.description: Duplicate an object, offset 20 cm down and right, and return the copy.

objectId.description: Id of a furniture object, e.g. "desk-1".

tools.name: lock_object
tools.description: Lock or unlock an object. A locked object cannot be moved, rotated or resized — by the agent or by dragging.

objectId.description: Id of a furniture object, e.g. "desk-1".

tools.name: add_opening
tools.description: Add a door or a window to one of the four walls. offsetCm is measured from the top or left end of that wall.

tools.name: update_opening
tools.description: Move or resize a door or window.

tools.name: remove_opening
tools.description: Remove a door or window, along with any keep-clear constraint attached to it.

tools.name: add_constraint
tools.description: Add a layout rule. min_distance needs objectAId, objectBId and distanceCm; near_window needs objectId and maxDistanceCm; against_wall needs objectId; keep_clear needs openingId and clearanceCm; clearance_zone needs objectId, side and clearanceCm — a functional clearance on one side of a piece of furniture (wardrobe door swing, desk chair pull-out, drawer access) rather than a door; max_distance needs objectAId, objectBId and maxDistanceCm — keeps two objects near each other, e.g. a nightstand near a bed; facing needs objectAId and objectBId — objectA's front (derived from its rotation: 0°=bottom, 90°=left, 180°=top, 270°=right) must point toward objectB, e.g. a chair facing a desk; centered_on_wall needs objectId, wall and toleranceCm — the object must touch that wall and sit centred along it.

side.description: Which side of the object the clearance_zone extends from.

wall.description: Which wall the object should be centered on.

toleranceCm.description: Allowed off-centre slack for centered_on_wall, in centimetres.

tools.name: update_constraint
tools.description: Change the values on an existing constraint.

tools.name: remove_constraint
tools.description: Remove a layout constraint.

tools.name: highlight_objects
tools.description: Draw attention to objects or openings on the canvas and show the person a short message explaining why.

message.description: Shown above the room, e.g. "These three items drive the layout."

tools.name: clear_highlights
tools.description: Clear the highlight banner and outlines.

tools.name: capture_floorplan
tools.description: Render the floor plan on its own — no app chrome — as a PNG or a standalone SVG, and return it as a data URL the caller can save to a file. Pass download:true to have the browser save it instead, which keeps the (large) data URL out of the reply.

format.description: Default png.

background.description: Default paper.

download.description: Save via the browser instead of returning the image data.

sites.name: voyagehacks.com
sites.description: Expert travel destination guides with tips on when to visit, cheapest flights, top hotels and money-saving advice. Plan your perfect trip with VoyageHacks.

tools.name: scan_images_c2pa
tools.description: Scan every on the current page for C2PA Content Credentials (content provenance metadata) and return a per-image summary: whether a manifest is present, the claim generator (the tool that produced or edited the image), the title, and the signer name. Use this to find which images on a page carry provenance data. Note: provenance is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

limit.description: Maximum number of images to fetch and scan (default 25, max 100).

tools.name: inspect_image_c2pa
tools.description: Fetch a single image (by CSS selector or URL) and return its fully decoded C2PA manifest store: every manifest's claim, assertions (e.g. c2pa.actions edit history, schema.org authorship), and the COSE signature details (algorithm and signing-certificate identity). Provide exactly one of `selector` or `url`. Note: the signature is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

selector.description: CSS selector for an element on the page.

url.description: Same-origin image URL (absolute same-origin, or relative to the current page) to fetch and inspect. Cross-origin URLs are rejected.

tools.name: search_articles
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Full-text search across the VoyageHacks travel guides, about 680 published pages per language, covering flights, airline reviews, hotels, destinations, car rental, trains, airport transfers, eSIM, travel VPN, travel credit cards, travel gear and month-by-month "where to go" guides. Returns ranked matches with the title, canonical URL, section and a matching excerpt for each. Useful when a travel question needs published prices, comparisons, best-time-to-visit advice or step-by-step detail that can be attributed to a source URL. It searches VoyageHacks content only: not the wider web, not live fares or hotel availability, and it returns no booking or product links.

query.description: Search terms, e.g. "cheap hotels rome" or "esim japan". Matched against titles, keywords, tags and article text.

lang.description: Language of the VoyageHacks guides returned. One of: en, de, fr, es, it, pl, cs, ja, nl, pt, zh. Defaults to "en".

section.description: Restrict results to one site section. Omit to search every section.

limit.description: Maximum results to return. Defaults to 5.

tools.name: get_article
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Fetch one VoyageHacks page by URL or site path (for example "/en/hotels/best-budget-hotels-in-rome/") and return its body as Markdown, together with the title, canonical URL, language, section, publication date and last-updated date read from the page itself. Useful when the full text of a guide is needed to quote figures accurately, and when a source needs to be cited with a real date. Only HTML pages on voyagehacks.com can be read: the tool cannot fetch other websites, data files or images, and very long pages are truncated with a marker at the cut.

url.description: Page URL or site path on voyagehacks.com, e.g. https://voyagehacks.com/de/esim/esim-japan/ or /de/esim/esim-japan/.

tools.name: search_travel_gear
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Search the VoyageHacks travel gear catalog: about 320 products that appear as picks in roughly 50 published buying guides, including carry-on backpacks, packing cubes and compression bags, universal travel adapters, GaN chargers, airline-compliant power banks, luggage trackers, neck pillows, earplugs and eye masks, toiletry and makeup bags, travel-size bottles, travel routers, translation earbuds and camping and outdoor gear. Each result returns the product name, its category, the published reason it was picked, its Amazon ASIN and a link to the product on the VoyageHacks buying guide that reviews it, where it can be bought on Amazon. Useful when a user asks which travel product to buy, or what to pack for a trip and names a category or a destination. This is the VoyageHacks editorial catalog, not a search of all of Amazon: products outside the published guides are not findable here, and prices, star ratings, review counts and stock are not available and are never returned. The guides carry Amazon affiliate links: VoyageHacks may earn a commission from qualifying purchases at no additional cost to the buyer, which should be disclosed when the products are presented.

query.description: What the traveler needs, e.g. "power bank for a long flight", "packing cubes", "adapter for Japan".

lang.description: Language of the VoyageHacks guides returned. One of: en, de, fr, es, it, pl, cs, ja, nl, pt, zh. Defaults to "en".

limit.description: Maximum products to return. Defaults to 6.

tools.name: recommend_travel_gear
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Turn a trip description into a packing and gear kit drawn from the VoyageHacks travel gear catalog: one product per category, each with the published reason it was picked, its Amazon ASIN and a link to the product on the VoyageHacks guide that reviews it, where it can be bought on Amazon. Takes a plain-language trip summary ("10 days in Japan in October, carry-on only, long-haul red-eye, working remotely") plus optional structured hints (destination, trip length in days, season, activities, luggage constraint, traveler type, budget), all of which are used to weight which categories make the kit. Answers questions of the form "what should I pack for X", "what gear do I need for Y" and "I only have carry-on, what should I bring". It draws on the VoyageHacks editorial catalog, not a search of all of Amazon, and returns published picks only: prices, star ratings, review counts and stock are not available and are never returned, and it produces no clothing sizes and no itinerary. The guides carry Amazon affiliate links: VoyageHacks may earn a commission from qualifying purchases at no additional cost to the buyer, which should be disclosed when the products are presented.

trip.description: Free-text trip description: destination, length, style, flight type, season, gadgets needed.

destination.description: Optional country, region or city, e.g. Japan, Iceland, Thailand.

season.description: Optional season or climate at the destination.

luggage.description: Optional luggage constraint. carry_on_only and personal_item_only weight the packing and compression categories.

budget.description: Optional budget level. Recorded in the response; the catalog carries no prices, so it does not filter products.

lang.description: Language of the VoyageHacks guides returned. One of: en, de, fr, es, it, pl, cs, ja, nl, pt, zh. Defaults to "en".

limit.description: Maximum items in the kit. Defaults to 6.

tools.name: get_flight_links
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Build a flight search link on Booking.com Flights for a route and optional dates, and return up to four VoyageHacks guides on fares, budget airlines and baggage rules for that trip. Pass origin and destination as IATA codes for a prefilled route search; without both, the link opens the general flight search page. Also returns a delayed or cancelled flight compensation link (AirHelp), a Vueling link for short-haul Europe, and, when the route touches their hubs, direct links for Air Serbia (Belgrade) and Air India. The Booking.com link is regionalized to the traveler's country. Useful when a trip involves air travel and the user wants somewhere to compare fares. It returns search links only: no live fares, seat availability or schedules, no booking and no airport transfers. Affiliate links: VoyageHacks may earn a commission at no additional cost to the traveler, which should be disclosed when the links are presented.

origin.description: Origin IATA city or airport code, e.g. LON, NYC, BER.

destination.description: Destination IATA city or airport code, e.g. HKT, TYO, ROM.

depart_date.description: Outbound date, YYYY-MM-DD. Omitted dates default to about a month ahead.

return_date.description: Return date, YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for a one-way search.

passengers.description: Number of adult passengers. Defaults to 1.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country the traveler is booking from, e.g. US, DE, GB. Selects the regional Booking.com programme. Defaults to the caller's geolocation, then to the language default.

lang.description: Language of the VoyageHacks guides returned. One of: en, de, fr, es, it, pl, cs, ja, nl, pt, zh. Defaults to "en".

tools.name: get_hotel_links
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Build a Booking.com search link for a city or property, with optional check-in and check-out dates, guest count and room count, the same search on Expedia, Vrbo (apartments and holiday homes) and Agoda, plus an IHG brand search link (Holiday Inn, InterContinental, Crowne Plaza) and up to four VoyageHacks guides on the best areas and best-value stays there. The Booking.com link is regionalized to the traveler's country. Useful when a user asks where to stay, or about hotels, hostels or apartments in a place. It returns search links only: no live room rates, no availability check, no reviews and no reservation. Affiliate links: VoyageHacks may earn a commission at no additional cost to the traveler, which should be disclosed when the links are presented.

city.description: City, region or property name to search, e.g. Rome, Phuket, Hotel Kossak.

checkin.description: Check-in date, YYYY-MM-DD. Used only when checkout is also given.

checkout.description: Check-out date, YYYY-MM-DD.

adults.description: Number of adults. Defaults to 2.

children.description: Number of children. Defaults to 0.

rooms.description: Number of rooms. Defaults to 1.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country the traveler is booking from, e.g. US, DE, GB. Selects the regional Booking.com programme. Defaults to the caller's geolocation, then to the language default.

lang.description: Language of the VoyageHacks guides returned. One of: en, de, fr, es, it, pl, cs, ja, nl, pt, zh. Defaults to "en".

tools.name: get_car_rental_links
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Return car and scooter rental comparison links for a destination: EconomyBookings and QEEQ for worldwide comparison, Localrent and GetRentacar for local suppliers with lower deposits in southern Europe, Georgia, the Balkans and Asia, BikesBooking for scooters and motorbikes, and Booking.com Cars, plus up to four VoyageHacks car-rental guides for that country covering real prices, insurance excess and one-way fees. Useful when a user mentions renting a car, a road trip, driving abroad, or an island or countryside trip that needs a vehicle. These are comparison landing pages: dates and the pickup point are entered on the provider site, so pickup_date and dropoff_date are echoed in the response for context rather than embedded in the links. No live quotes, no vehicle availability and no reservation. Affiliate links: VoyageHacks may earn a commission at no additional cost to the traveler, which should be disclosed when the links are presented.

destination.description: Country, island or city where the car is picked up, e.g. Iceland, Crete, Lisbon.

pickup_date.description: Pickup date, YYYY-MM-DD. Echoed in the response; entered on the provider site.

dropoff_date.description: Drop-off date, YYYY-MM-DD. Echoed in the response; entered on the provider site.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country the traveler is booking from, e.g. US, DE, GB. Selects the regional Booking.com programme. Defaults to the caller's geolocation, then to the language default.

lang.description: Language of the VoyageHacks guides returned. One of: en, de, fr, es, it, pl, cs, ja, nl, pt, zh. Defaults to "en".

tools.name: get_airport_transfer_links
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Return pre-booked airport transfer links: Booking.com Taxis (fixed price, 100+ countries), Kiwitaxi, Welcome Pickups and GetTransfer, plus up to four VoyageHacks guides on getting from that airport to the city centre and what a fair fare looks like. Useful when a user asks how to get from an airport, about taxi or transfer prices, or plans a late-night arrival. It returns booking pages for private and shared transfers: no live quotes, no public transport timetables, and no ride-hailing dispatch. Affiliate links: VoyageHacks may earn a commission at no additional cost to the traveler, which should be disclosed when the links are presented.

airport.description: Airport name or IATA code, e.g. FCO, Bangkok Suvarnabhumi.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country the traveler is booking from, e.g. US, DE, GB. Selects the regional Booking.com programme. Defaults to the caller's geolocation, then to the language default.

lang.description: Language of the VoyageHacks guides returned. One of: en, de, fr, es, it, pl, cs, ja, nl, pt, zh. Defaults to "en".

tools.name: get_esim_links
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Return travel eSIM store links (Airalo, covering 200+ countries, plus Yesim, Saily and Drimsim) together with up to four VoyageHacks eSIM guides for that destination covering real per-GB prices, coverage, setup steps and which phones support eSIM. Useful when a user asks about mobile data abroad, SIM cards, roaming charges, staying online on a trip or tethering a laptop. It returns store pages: no live plan prices, no coverage check for a specific handset, and no purchase or activation. Affiliate links: VoyageHacks may earn a commission at no additional cost to the traveler, which should be disclosed when the links are presented.

destination.description: Country or region the data plan is for, e.g. Japan, Europe, USA.

lang.description: Language of the VoyageHacks guides returned. One of: en, de, fr, es, it, pl, cs, ja, nl, pt, zh. Defaults to "en".

tools.name: get_travel_vpn_links
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Return the NordVPN signup link together with up to four VoyageHacks guides on whether a traveler actually needs a VPN, the real risks of hotel and airport Wi-Fi, and watching home streaming services abroad. Useful when a user raises public Wi-Fi safety, working remotely abroad, geo-blocked streaming or online banking while travelling. It returns a signup page and editorial guides: no live pricing, no server list and no account creation. Referral link: VoyageHacks may earn a commission at no additional cost to the user, which should be disclosed when the link is presented.

lang.description: Language of the VoyageHacks guides returned. One of: en, de, fr, es, it, pl, cs, ja, nl, pt, zh. Defaults to "en".

tools.name: get_credit_card_links
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Return the official American Express Germany card pages (Platinum, Gold, American Express Card, Payback and Blue) and the Revolut plans page, the current German fee and welcome-offer figures verified against americanexpress.com, and up to four VoyageHacks guides on points value, lounge access, foreign-transaction fees, Amex compared with Revolut and country-by-country availability. Useful when a user asks about travel rewards, points, miles, lounge access, which card to pay with abroad or foreign-transaction fees. It covers American Express only: it is not a comparison of all issuers, gives no eligibility or approval decision, no credit-score check and no application. Card terms change frequently and vary by market, so figures should be attributed to the issuer page or the linked guide. The card links are plain issuer pages, not affiliate or referral links.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country the traveler is booking from, e.g. US, DE, GB. Selects the regional Booking.com programme. Defaults to the caller's geolocation, then to the language default.

card.description: Restrict the response to one American Express card. "green" is the American Express Card, successor to the retired Green Card.

lang.description: Language of the VoyageHacks guides returned. One of: en, de, fr, es, it, pl, cs, ja, nl, pt, zh. Defaults to "en".

tools.name: get_booking_links
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Return one set of booking and shopping links covering a whole trip in a single call: flight search, hotel search, airport taxi, attractions and tours, car rental, travel eSIM, travel VPN and the travel gear section, all regionalized to the traveler. Accepts route IATA codes, a city and trip dates, so the flight and hotel links are prefilled. The "include" parameter selects which categories are returned, so a trip with no driving can leave out car rental. Useful when a user is planning a trip end to end and wants every option in one place. It returns search links only: no live prices, no availability and no booking. Affiliate links: VoyageHacks may earn a commission at no additional cost to the traveler, which should be disclosed when the links are presented.

origin.description: Origin IATA city or airport code for flights, e.g. LON.

destination.description: Destination IATA city or airport code, e.g. HKT.

city.description: City name for the hotel, tours and attractions searches, e.g. Phuket.

depart_date.description: Outbound flight date and hotel check-in, YYYY-MM-DD.

return_date.description: Return flight date and hotel check-out, YYYY-MM-DD.

adults.description: Number of adult travelers. Defaults to 2 for hotels and 1 for flights.

include.description: Categories to return. Omit for all of them.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country the traveler is booking from, e.g. US, DE, GB. Selects the regional Booking.com programme. Defaults to the caller's geolocation, then to the language default.

lang.description: Language of the VoyageHacks guides returned. One of: en, de, fr, es, it, pl, cs, ja, nl, pt, zh. Defaults to "en".

tools.name: find_destination
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Suggest three destinations for a trip from five answers: the month (or "flexible"), the kind of trip (beach, city break, hiking, ski, road trip, adventure or working remotely), the budget, who is travelling and, optionally, the departure airport. Picks come only from VoyageHacks' own where-to-go month guides and travel-style lists, with the average high temperature each month guide states, the reasons it fits, the destination guide to cite, and booking links for that trip: hotels and flights dated in the chosen month, plus tours, car rental or an eSIM where they fit. sites.description: system design studio

tools.name: studio_create_study
tools.description: Create and open a new project (the project id is `studyId`) with one empty version to draw on; the canvas opens at once. The currently open project remains saved and can be reopened with studio_open_study. Order of work: read studio_get_catalog, draw components then links with studio_apply_architecture_patch, set-workflow for the highest-risk flow, then set the yardstick with studio_update_study (workload, targets, faults, invariants naming the collections you drew), seal with studio_import_architecture { fromCandidateId }, then evaluate. Pass the evidenced arrival as workload here or set it with studio_update_study before the first run: the Studio's placeholder workload is refused by the runners.

tools.name: studio_update_study
tools.description: Set the project's shared yardstick: workload, SLOs, business goals, invariants, faults and exploration bounds. Every version is judged against these. Set it AFTER the workflow exists and BEFORE sealing or running: rules name collections, and collections exist only once set-workflow has run. Invariants may be written as { template, args } using studio_get_catalog.invariantTemplates, or as a full Invariant. A project with no invariants fails the correctness gate rather than passing it. Replace the placeholder workload here before the first run. Refused once any evaluation exists or a version is promoted.

tools.name: studio_list_studies
tools.description: List saved projects.

tools.name: studio_open_study
tools.description: Open a saved project by studyId. Replaces what is open; nothing is deleted.

tools.name: studio_import_architecture
tools.description: Import the current as-is architecture of a repository revision. Atomically links the repository and creates an immutable baseline with a source inventory and code, config, runtime, documentation or user evidence. Use observed only for facts directly supported by the cited source; mark deductions inferred and unknown production behaviour assumed. Code/config citations carry a SHA-256 hash of the normalized cited slice. Documentation may orient the scan but never qualifies as grounding evidence. Mark numeric measurements aspect=performance; code proving that a call exists is architecture evidence, not timing calibration. Every component timing and link network.propagationLatency must be positive; every link must set semantics and fanoutFactor (1 for one-to-one). Async links require a queue/event channel and maxHops. Missing inventory, evidence, workflow or source-state details seal the baseline as PROVISIONAL: it can be evaluated, but cannot be approved or handed off until the grounding report is clear. Two ways in: pass the complete design in one call, or pass fromCandidateId to seal an experiment you drew step by step on the canvas (the version studio_create_study opened, patched with studio_apply_architecture_patch per component and link). Either way this is what makes the drawing the immutable as-is baseline, shown to the person as CURRENT.

intent.default: As-is architecture reconstructed from repository evidence.

tools.name: studio_get_study
tools.description: Read the current project: problem, workload, SLOs, business goals, invariants, bounds, and its versions (candidates) with their revisions. Workload, SLOs, invariants and bounds are project-level; a version cannot change them. Contains user-authored text.

tools.name: studio_get_architecture
tools.description: Read the active or named architecture as a repository-linked model: role, ancestry, revision, full design, topology validation issues, bounded distributed-semantics report, and per-node/per-link evidence. Use this before proposing or patching an experiment. Contains repository paths and user- or agent-authored claims.

tools.name: studio_get_catalog
tools.description: Read the modelling vocabulary: component kinds, workflow operations and which are indivisible, the shipped patterns, injectable faults, invariant templates and the Invariant shape, layout rules, and network-profile placeholders. Read this before drawing. The operations are a closed set, and the indivisible ones are what make a design safe.

tools.name: studio_get_candidate
tools.description: Read one version: its design, workflow, revision and stated intent. The revision is required by studio_replace_candidate_draft. Contains user-authored text.

candidateId.description: Version id (`candidateId`), from studio_get_study.

tools.name: studio_apply_architecture_patch
tools.description: Apply a small atomic graph delta to an experiment instead of resending the whole design. Operations can add, update or remove nodes and links, replace the workflow, or rename the design. Every accepted patch is drawn on the canvas immediately, so drawing an architecture one component or link per call lets a person watch it form; coordinates communicate the topology (callers to dependencies left-to-right, parallel branches on separate rows, shared dependencies centered): either choose x/y per node from studio_get_catalog.layoutGuide, or include an auto-layout operation and the studio computes that layout from the links. Overlapping nodes and missing coordinates are otherwise refused, never silently repositioned. Agent-authored servers must set fanout explicitly; agent-authored service components must set positive timing fields explicitly, and links must include explicit synchronous/asynchronous semantics, a network profile with positive one-way propagationLatency plus fanoutFactor (1 for one-to-one; asynchronous queue/event links also require maxHops). Requires the revision read from studio_get_architecture or returned by the previous call, and refuses baselines, promoted versions, stale revisions, missing targets and results with errors (a link to a node that does not exist yet, for example).

node.description: Complete node. x and y are required and should follow studio_get_catalog.layoutGuide (x by dependency depth, parallel branches on separate y rows), unless the same patch contains an auto-layout operation, which places every node.

patch.description: Shallow node field patch. Cannot contain id or kind.
Shallow link field patch. Cannot contain id.

anyOf.description: Move every node to a layered layout computed from the links: callers in the leftmost column, one column per dependency depth, each node level with the middle of its callers, no overlaps. Applied after the other operations in the patch, so nodes added in the same patch may omit x and y. Use it when hand-placed coordinates would be guesswork, or after a newly found dependency changes the shape of the graph.

operations.description: Atomic graph changes, applied in order and committed only if the final design validates.

tools.name: studio_attach_code_evidence
tools.description: Append evidence to nodes, links, collections, handlers or operations without replacing the architecture. Requires the current version revision and refuses duplicate ids or missing targets. Evidence is append-only through WebMCP so an agent cannot silently erase the basis for an as-is claim.

tools.name: studio_upsert_source_inventory
tools.description: Add or replace audited source-inventory items on a repository baseline. The update is deterministic by item id and revision-guarded. Every runtime boundary must be modeled, excluded with a reason, or left visibly unresolved.

tools.name: studio_get_grounding_report
tools.description: Read the computed grounding status, coverage, source inventory and exact gaps for a repository baseline. This tool cannot set the status; it is derived from the current snapshot, model, evidence and receipt.

tools.name: studio_upsert_issue
tools.description: Propose an evidence-linked design issue. Repeated identical analysis updates the same deterministic row rather than creating duplicates. If an existing row changes, pass its current expectedRevision. This tool cannot verify, dismiss, accept risk, or approve anything; those decisions remain with trusted checks or people.

tools.name: studio_get_issues
tools.description: Read current-baseline issues with computed states. States come from snapshot-pinned evidence and trusted receipts; they are not agent-authored fields. Pass status=historical to inspect findings from prior source snapshots.

tools.name: studio_validate_draft
tools.description: Check a design without storing it. Returns schema, topology and workflow errors naming the field and what is wrong, plus warnings. Call this before creating or replacing a version. A valid result changes nothing on the page; pass the same design to studio_import_architecture or studio_create_candidate to render it.

design.description: A design document to check without storing it.

tools.name: studio_create_candidate
tools.description: Create a new version: isolated, marked agent-authored, revision 0. Omit the design to copy the active version, which is what you want when changing one aspect of it. Called right after studio_create_study, while the blank drawing it opened is still empty, this adopts that drawing (relabelled, filled with the design if one is given) instead of adding a second empty version. The version is drawn on the page at once. Never modifies a version somebody has worked on.

label.description: Short human-readable name.

tools.name: studio_propose_alternatives
tools.description: Create two to eight isolated alternatives together. Each repository-fix alternative must name registered issues and preserve its own hypothesis, trade-offs, verification plan and expected architecture impact. The alternatives are proposals only: this tool cannot verify issues or approve a version.

label.description: Short human-readable name.

tools.name: studio_replace_candidate_draft
tools.description: Replace a version's design with a complete, validated document. Requires the revision you read, and is refused if the version changed since, so two editors cannot silently overwrite each other. Refused for the promoted version and for the as-is baseline; create a new version before redesigning code-derived architecture.

expectedRevision.description: The revision you believe you are replacing, from studio_get_candidate. The call is refused if the version has moved on.

tools.name: studio_run_evaluation
tools.description: Run the bounded correctness search and/or the replicated performance measurement for one version. Refused while the project's workload is still the Studio placeholder, because the first result locks the yardstick for every version. Performance defaults off and is refused for a repository model until every component and link has observed runtime or user performance evidence. Verdicts: VIOLATED, NO_VIOLATION_WITHIN_BOUNDS, INCONCLUSIVE_BOUND_REACHED, INVALID_MODEL. NO_VIOLATION_WITHIN_BOUNDS is not proof of safety, and INCONCLUSIVE_BOUND_REACHED establishes nothing either way. Fetch the counterexample with studio_get_evaluation.

tools.name: studio_run_production_scenarios
tools.description: Run the standard production suite for one version: bounded concurrent requests and retries, a 3x 30-second traffic spike with recovery, a load ramp to the project SLO boundary, and 30% degradation of a high-impact dependency. Returns measured evidence and a specific recommendation for every probe. For a repository model this is refused until every component and link has observed runtime or user performance evidence. An inconclusive result names the missing workflow, invariant, SLO, dependency or bound; never treat it as a pass.

candidateId.description: Version id (`candidateId`), from studio_get_study.

tools.name: studio_get_evaluation
tools.description: Read a version's cached evaluation, including the full counterexample trace when an invariant was violated: actor lanes, operation order, state changes and the faults injected. Null when the version has not been evaluated at the current design, seeds and bounds.

candidateId.description: Version id (`candidateId`), from studio_get_study.

tools.name: studio_compare_candidates
tools.description: Compare versions. Returns each eligibility decision with the reason every gate opened or did not, and the Pareto frontier among the ELIGIBLE ones. Eligible means the correctness search ran to exhaustion without a violation, every required issue is verified or has a human disposition, no critical regression is open, repository performance inputs are calibrated, AND the conservative end of the performance interval meets every SLO and goal. The frontier is Pareto-optimal among the versions tested: not globally best, and not ranked. Differences within the measured intervals are ties, not wins.

tools.name: studio_get_implementation_handoff
tools.description: Read the exact revision-pinned architecture change a person approved for implementation: repository source state, before/after component and workflow values, issue-to-change-to-verification mappings, source evidence, acceptance criteria, and unresolved production findings. A new repository import invalidates old issue verification. Returns a blocker until a repository-backed experiment has been approved in the interface. This tool does not approve, edit repository files, run tests, deploy, or mark the visual model synchronized.

tools.name: studio_annotate
tools.description: Pin a short note to a component, link, counterexample step or version so the person sees your reasoning on the canvas (for example: which component the race happens at, what a proposed version trades off). Notes are session-only narration: they are not part of the project, are never saved or exported, and cannot change any result.

targetKind.description: What the note is pinned to (candidate = a whole version). A step is a 0-based index into that version's counterexample.

targetId.description: Node id, edge id, step index as a string, or version id.

text.description: The note, one or two sentences. Say what, and cite where when you can.

tools.name: studio_focus
tools.description: Point the person at something: select and pan the canvas to a component or link, or scrub the active version's counterexample to a step (0-based) so the sprites and state chips show that moment. Changes only what is on screen.

kind.description: Select a node or edge, or scrub to a counterexample step.

sites.name: groundwork-delta-murex.vercel.app
sites.description: A floor-plan drawing tool where you and an AI agent work on the same canvas. Walls, doors and furniture that understand clearance, circulation and what actually fits.

tools.name: describe_scene
tools.description: Read the whole floor plan: rooms with sizes, areas and compass-mapped walls, what each contains, which rooms connect through which doors, free space, and any problems. Call this first, and whenever you need to re-orient.

detail.description: 'summary' omits contents and free space; 'full' is the default.

tools.name: list_symbols
tools.description: Browse or search the symbol library. Call with no arguments for an overview of every category and what is in it; with a category to list that group; or with a query to search. Queries understand what things are called ('couch', 'loo', 'fridge') and what they are for ('sit', 'sleep', 'wash', 'cook').

query.description: Search terms, e.g. 'queen bed' or 'somewhere to sit'.

category.description: List one category instead of searching.

measured_only.description: Only symbols whose real size was measured rather than estimated. Use when clearances matter.

limit.description: Maximum results (default 25).

tools.name: get_element
tools.description: Everything known about one element, room or node, as structured data. Walls come back with their endpoints, length, the openings they hold and the runs still free — which is what you need before adding a door. Node ids (n1, n7) resolve too.

ref.description: Element id (W15, D2, F7), node id (n11), room id or name.

tools.name: find_free_space
tools.description: Where something would fit in a room, accounting for furniture, walls, door swings and door approaches. Pass 'symbol' rather than width/height wherever you can: the answer then already accounts for the rotation that 'against' implies, and the position it returns is one place_furniture will accept. Raw width/height are read as world axes, before any rotation.

room.description: Room name or id.

width.description: Width in mm, along the world x axis.

height.description: Depth in mm, along the world y axis.

rotation.description: Rotation the object will be placed at. Ignored when 'against' is given.

clearance.description: Extra clear space to leave all round, in mm.

tools.name: measure
tools.description: Distance between two points, or the size of an element.

from.description: Start point.

to.description: End point.

ref.description: Element to measure instead of two points.

tools.name: draw_walls
tools.description: Draw a connected run of walls through a list of points, in mm. Set closed:true to form a loop, which creates a room. Walls automatically share junctions and split where they cross.

points.description: Points in order, at least two.

items.description: A point in mm.

closed.description: Join the last point back to the first.

tools.name: draw_room_rect
tools.description: Draw a rectangular SHELL — the outer envelope of a building or a floor. Use this once per building, then divide it with subdivide_room. Do NOT call it repeatedly to make individual rooms: separate rectangles share no walls, so they come out as free-floating boxes with gaps between them rather than a floor plan. x,y is the top-left corner in mm; north is negative y.

tools.name: move_node
tools.description: Move a wall junction. Every wall meeting at it follows.

node.description: Node id, e.g. n3.

to.description: New position in mm.

tools.name: set_wall_thickness
tools.description: Change the thickness of one or more walls.

items.description: A wall id.

tools.name: add_opening
tools.description: Add doors or windows. Identify each wall by id, or by a room plus a compass side — 'the south wall of Bedroom 1'. Pass 'openings' with an array to add several at once, which is one call and one undo step instead of a dozen. Position with centre (mm along the wall), or leave it to centre automatically. Check a wall's freeRuns first to see where there is space.

wall.description: Wall id, if you know it.

room.description: Room name, used with 'side' to find the wall.

side.description: Which wall of that room.

type.description: Kind of opening.

width.description: Width in mm. Defaults to the standard for the type.

centre.description: Distance in mm along the wall to the opening's centre.

swing.description: Which jamb a door is hinged on.

outward.description: Swing away from the room instead of into it.

openings.description: Several openings at once. Each entry takes the same fields as above.

wall.description: Wall id.

room.description: Room name, used with 'side'.

side.description: Which wall of that room.

type.description: Kind of opening.

centre.description: Distance along the wall to the centre.

tools.name: place_furniture
tools.description: Place a symbol. Prefer describing intent — a room and a side to sit against — over raw coordinates; the position is then computed from real geometry and clearances. Rejections come back with positions that would work.

room.description: Room to place it in.

against.description: Put it against this side of the room. The object is turned to face inward automatically — a sofa against the north wall faces south.

clearance.description: Extra clear space to leave around it, in mm.

x.description: Explicit x in mm. Only when 'room' will not do.

rotation.description: Rotation in degrees, snapped to 15. At 0 an object faces north; each 90 turns it clockwise. Usually better to give 'against' and let it be worked out.

tools.name: move_element
tools.description: Move an element to a point, or by an offset. Doors slide along their wall; walls carry their junctions.

ref.description: Element id or name.

to.description: Target position in mm.

tools.name: rotate_element
tools.description: Rotate an element, in degrees, snapped to 15.

ref.description: Element id or name.

tools.name: delete_elements
tools.description: Delete elements. Deleting a wall also deletes the doors and windows it hosts.

items.description: An id or name.

tools.name: subdivide_room
tools.description: THE PRIMARY WAY TO MAKE ROOMS. Cut an existing space into a row of smaller ones — a shell into zones, a zone into offices. The dividing walls tee into the shell properly, so the result is real connected rooms sharing walls, which is what a floor plan is. Call it repeatedly, and on its own results, to build up a plan: shell -> zones -> rooms. Fifteen manager offices means subdividing a zone into fifteen, not drawing one enormous room called 'manager offices'.

room.description: Room name or id to divide.

axis.description: Which way the dividing walls run.

count.description: How many cells to end up with.

sizes.description: Explicit cell sizes in mm, instead of count.

items.description: A size in mm.

names.description: Names for the resulting cells, in position order along the axis. Safer than naming afterwards, since ids do not run in that order.

items.description: A room name.

doors.description: Put a door in each dividing wall so the cells are reachable.

tools.name: arrange_room
tools.description: Fill a room with a grid of one symbol — desks, dining tables, seating rows. Each position is checked individually, so anything that would block a door or overlap is skipped, and the response says how many actually fitted. Use this rather than calling place_furniture repeatedly.

room.description: Room name or id.

count.description: How many to place. Omit to fill the room.

spacing.description: Gap between items in mm. Defaults to the symbol's own clearance.

rotation.description: Rotation for every item, in degrees.

margin.description: Clear space to leave at the room edge, in mm.

tools.name: apply_layout
tools.description: Lay out a whole room in one call, describing items by their RELATIONSHIP to each other rather than by coordinates. Name an item with 'as', then refer to it from later items with '$name'. Strongly preferred over repeated place_furniture: it is one undo step, it validates the finished arrangement rather than each half-built stage, and relations like 'around' and 'beside' are computed exactly.

room.description: Room name or id.

dry_run.description: Resolve the layout and report where everything would land and what it would clash with, WITHOUT changing the drawing. Use this to check an arrangement before committing it, rather than placing, inspecting and deleting.

items.description: Items in order. Each may refer to any earlier one.

as.description: Name this item so later items can refer to it as '$name'.

against.description: Put it against this side of the room, facing inward.

beside.description: Place it beside this item, e.g. '$bed'.

side.description: Which side of that item, from that item's own point of view.

align.description: How to line the two up along the shared edge (default back).

around.description: Ring this item, e.g. '$table'. Each copy turns to face it.

items.description: An item reference.

group.description: Items sharing a group are treated as one arrangement — no clearance or overlap complaints between them. 'around' groups automatically.

facing.description: Turn to face this item, overriding the relation's own rotation.

at.description: Explicit position, when no relation fits.

gap.description: Gap to the related item, in mm.

tools.name: set_sheet
tools.description: Change the paper size and drawing scale. Do this BEFORE drawing anything large: the sheet decides how much building fits on the page, and a plan drawn far outside it cannot be printed or read. An A2 at 1:50 covers about 620 m²; at 1:200 about 10,000 m².

name.description: Sheet name, e.g. 'A-101 Ground Floor Plan'. Also names the plan if it is still untitled.

fit.description: Pick the smallest paper and scale that fits what is drawn. Ignored if you give paper or scale yourself.

tools.name: annotate
tools.description: Add a dimension line between two points, or a text note.

kind.description: What to add.

from.description: Dimension start.

to.description: Dimension end.

offset.description: How far the dimension line stands off, in mm.

text.description: Text content.

tools.name: set_style
tools.description: Recolour elements. Targets ids, or everything in a room.

items.description: An id or name.

room.description: Recolour everything in this room instead.

stroke.description: Outline colour as hex, or 'default' to clear.

fill.description: Fill colour as hex, or 'default' to clear.

tools.name: name_room
tools.description: Name a room, so it can be referred to by name afterwards.

room.description: Room id, or its current name.

tools.name: set_program
tools.description: Record the design brief BEFORE drawing: the rooms wanted, how many people each is for, minimum areas, which must adjoin which, orientation, and required fixtures. Giving 'occupants' and 'use' is what makes validate_program a real check — it sizes each space against actual area-per-person figures, so an oversized or under-divided room fails.

key.description: Short identifier, e.g. 'bedroom-1'.

name.description: Room name to match against the drawing.

adjacent_to.description: Keys of rooms this must connect to.

items.description: A key.
A symbol id or keyword.

occupants.description: How many people this space is for. Checked against real area-per-person figures.

use.description: What kind of space, which sets the area each person needs.

tools.name: validate_program
tools.description: Check the drawing against the brief: areas, adjacencies, orientation and required fixtures.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Undo recent changes, yours or the user's.

steps.description: How many steps (default 1).

tools.name: focus_view
tools.description: Pan and zoom the user's view to an element or room, so they can see what you changed.

ref.description: Element id, room name, or omit to fit everything.

sites.name: labmcp.vercel.app
sites.description: A virtual chemistry lab shared by a human and an AI agent. The human has hands, the agent has WebMCP tools, both act on the same experiment.

tools.name: get_lab_state
tools.description: Returns the full current bench state: every container and instrument, the shelf, indicators, and the last few observations. This never reports pH, moles, or the concentration of a container's contents; use measure_ph, calculate_moles, or inspect_contents for those. Call this first when planning, and call it again after any OBJECT_NOT_FOUND error, because a human may have changed the bench since your last call.

tools.name: list_reagents
tools.description: Lists every reagent stocked on the shelf: id, kind (solution or solid), formula, role (acid, base, salt, weak_acid, weak_base, carbonate), default and max concentration for liquids, and molar mass plus a solubility note for solids. Also lists the available indicators and their color ranges. Unknown samples from a challenge scenario are never listed here; use get_lab_state to see what is on the bench.

tools.name: list_equipment
tools.description: Lists every equipment type LabMCP supports (with capacity and purpose) and every object currently on the bench (id, type, and, for instruments, what it's attached to). Use add_container to place more.

tools.name: check_objective
tools.description: Returns the active scenario's goal: which steps are done, whether it is complete, and a short status line (e.g. current pH vs target, or current molarity vs target). Call this before planning so you know what is left; get_lab_state's `objective` field carries the same information.

tools.name: measure_ph
tools.description: Measures the pH of a container's contents using a pH meter. If a pH meter is already on the bench but attached elsewhere, it is moved to this container automatically. If no pH meter exists on the bench at all, this fails with INSTRUMENT_MISSING; call add_container with type 'ph_meter' first. Prefer this over inspect_contents, which is blocked on unidentified samples until a challenge is revealed. The reading is logged to the notebook.

container_id.description: Container id exactly as returned by get_lab_state, e.g. "c_1". Type names are not ids.

tools.name: measure_temperature
tools.description: Measures the temperature (°C) of a container's contents using a thermometer. A thermometer already on the bench is moved to this container automatically; if none exists, this fails with INSTRUMENT_MISSING, so call add_container with type 'thermometer' first. Also reports whether the container is currently heating, cooling, or idle.

container_id.description: Container id exactly as returned by get_lab_state, e.g. "c_1". Type names are not ids.

tools.name: measure_volume
tools.description: Reads the current liquid volume (mL) in a container, its capacity, and the fraction of capacity filled (0 to 1).

container_id.description: Container id exactly as returned by get_lab_state, e.g. "c_1". Type names are not ids.

tools.name: get_titration_data
tools.description: Returns the recorded titration curve: burette and flask ids, the titrant, the analyte's initial volume, and every dispensed point (titrant mL, pH if a meter was attached at the time, clock time). Empty outside the titration scenario. pH points are null until a pH meter has been attached to the flask via measure_ph.

tools.name: get_notebook
tools.description: Returns the lab notebook: an append-only, timestamped log with one entry per action, each tagged with the actor (human or agent) that caused it, containers named by label rather than id. Undo does not remove entries, it adds one. Optionally limit to the last N entries (1 to 200, default all).

last_n.description: Only return the most recent N entries.

tools.name: inspect_contents
tools.description: Reads the exact dissolved species, moles, and molarity in a container, plus any solids and which reactions have occurred there. Blocked with PERMISSION_DENIED on a container tainted by an unidentified sample until the challenge is revealed (via submit_conclusion); use measure_ph or add a test reagent and watch for a precipitate or color change instead. Always allowed on ordinary sandbox containers.

container_id.description: Container id exactly as returned by get_lab_state, e.g. "c_1". Type names are not ids.

tools.name: predict_supported_reactions
tools.description: Predicts which reactions could fire in a container right now (based on which ions are already present) and which new reactions would become possible if each shelf reagent were added. On a hidden challenge container this returns only the general reaction registry (evaluated: false), since the actual ions can't be read.

container_id.description: Container id exactly as returned by get_lab_state, e.g. "c_1". Type names are not ids.

tools.name: calculate_moles
tools.description: Computes moles, millimoles, and molarity of one species in a container. Blocked with PERMISSION_DENIED on a hidden challenge container, except in the titration scenario where the titrant species OH- and Na+ remain computable (needed to work the titration by material balance). Use get_titration_data plus this tool instead of guessing.

container_id.description: Container id exactly as returned by get_lab_state, e.g. "c_1". Type names are not ids.

tools.name: add_container
tools.description: Places a new piece of equipment on the bench: glassware (beaker, flask, test_tube, graduated_cylinder, burette) or an instrument (ph_meter, thermometer, hotplate). Uses the free bench slot nearest the existing objects when position is omitted. Fails with OUT_OF_RANGE if the bench is full or the slot is occupied.

type.description: Equipment type. beaker 250 mL, flask 250 mL (Erlenmeyer), test_tube 20 mL, graduated_cylinder 100 mL, burette 50 mL, ph_meter, thermometer, hotplate.

position.description: Bench grid slot. Omit to use the next free slot.

label.description: Optional custom label, shown instead of the default type name.

tools.name: add_reagent
tools.description: Adds a stock reagent (or water) to a container. Water dilutes without changing species. Overflow fails with nothing added; check capacity with measure_volume first if unsure. Mixing may trigger a supported reaction, reported in the observation and in `reaction`. Liquids use volume_ml; solid reagents (see list_reagents) use mass_g instead and dissolve up to their solubility limit. Use add_indicator for indicators and transfer to move existing liquid between containers instead of re-adding stock.

container_id.description: Container id exactly as returned by get_lab_state, e.g. "c_1". Type names are not ids.

reagent_id.description: Shelf reagent id from get_lab_state.shelf, e.g. "hcl", "naoh", "water", or a challenge's "unknown_acid". See list_reagents.

volume_ml.description: Volume in mL for a liquid reagent, greater than 0. Omit for a solid reagent; use mass_g instead.

mass_g.description: Mass in grams for a solid reagent (see list_reagents for which ids are solid). Omit volume_ml when using mass_g.

concentration_m.description: Concentration in mol/L (0 < x ≤ 2) for a liquid reagent. Omit to use the reagent's default concentration.

tools.name: transfer
tools.description: Pours liquid from one container to another, moving species proportionally to the fraction of the source's volume moved. Solids stay behind in the source. Use dispense instead when the source is a burette (for controlled, incremental titration additions).

source_id.description: Container id exactly as returned by get_lab_state, e.g. "c_1". Type names are not ids.

destination_id.description: Container id exactly as returned by get_lab_state, e.g. "c_1". Type names are not ids.

tools.name: dispense
tools.description: Dispenses liquid from a burette into a destination container; the titration action. Use coarse increments (1 to 5 mL) far from the endpoint and fine increments (0.1 to 0.5 mL) once color or pH starts moving quickly. pH is recorded on the titration curve only when a pH meter is attached to the destination; call measure_ph on it first if you need pH tracked.

burette_id.description: Container id exactly as returned by get_lab_state, e.g. "c_1". Type names are not ids.

destination_id.description: Container id exactly as returned by get_lab_state, e.g. "c_1". Type names are not ids.

volume_ml.description: Volume to dispense in mL, greater than 0, up to 50.

tools.name: stir
tools.description: Stirs a container for the given duration (0.5 to 30 s, default 3 s), keeping any solids suspended while stirring and speeding settling once it stops.

container_id.description: Container id exactly as returned by get_lab_state, e.g. "c_1". Type names are not ids.

tools.name: heat
tools.description: Sets a container heating toward a target temperature (0 to 100 °C). Requires a hotplate on the bench; fails with INSTRUMENT_MISSING otherwise.

container_id.description: Container id exactly as returned by get_lab_state, e.g. "c_1". Type names are not ids.

tools.name: cool
tools.description: Sets a container cooling toward a target temperature (0 to 100 °C), or toward ambient if omitted. Requires a hotplate on the bench; fails with INSTRUMENT_MISSING otherwise.

container_id.description: Container id exactly as returned by get_lab_state, e.g. "c_1". Type names are not ids.

tools.name: add_indicator
tools.description: Adds drops of a color indicator to a container. phenolphthalein: colorless below pH ~8.2, pink above. universal: red/orange/yellow/green/blue/purple across pH 1 to 14. litmus: red below pH 7, blue at or above. 1 to 10 drops, default 2.

container_id.description: Container id exactly as returned by get_lab_state, e.g. "c_1". Type names are not ids.

tools.name: remove_container
tools.description: Removes a container or instrument from the bench entirely, disposing of any liquid it held. This cannot be undone.

object_id.description: Object id exactly as returned by get_lab_state, e.g. "c_1" for glassware or "i_3" for an instrument.

tools.name: undo_last_action
tools.description: Reverts the single most recent action in the history (yours or the human's) and restores the lab to its exact prior state. There is no redo, so use this only when you are sure. Fails with NOTHING_TO_UNDO if history is empty.

tools.name: reset_experiment
tools.description: Reloads the current scenario with its original seed, discarding every change. Destructive: requires confirm: true.

confirm.description: Must be exactly true to acknowledge this discards all changes.

tools.name: load_scenario
tools.description: Loads a scenario onto a fresh bench. 'sandbox': Sandbox. 'titration': Titration. 'unknown_id': Reaction mystery. 'precipitation': Precipitation. 'neutralize': Neutralize to pH 7. 'dilution': Dilution. 'solubility': Solubility. Uses the fixed demo seed 42 unless a different seed is given.

seed.description: RNG seed. Defaults to the fixed demo seed 42.

tools.name: submit_conclusion
tools.description: Ends the active challenge and grades your answer. For 'unknown_id' (up to four unknown samples), one { container_id, claim } per sample, claim being a reagent id guess. For 'titration', one { container_id, concentration_m } with the claimed analyte molarity. For 'neutralize' and 'dilution', omit answers entirely: there is nothing to guess, this just reveals the container and reports whether the objective was met. This is the only path that reveals hidden identities, and it ends the challenge, so call it once you're confident. Fails with PERMISSION_DENIED outside an active challenge scenario.

answers.description: One answer per unknown sample, or a single answer for the titration analyte. Omit for neutralize and dilution.

container_id.description: Container id exactly as returned by get_lab_state, e.g. "c_1". Type names are not ids.

claim.description: Reagent id guess for unknown_id (e.g. "agno3"). Omit for titration.

concentration_m.description: Claimed molarity, used for the titration scenario's analyte.

tools.name: edit_shopping_item
tools.description: Replace an item’s requirements and queue new research; its old report is cleared. Supply the complete desired brief. Omitted priorities/customTags retain the item’s captured preferences.

tools.name: set_shopping_item_status
tools.description: Pause monitoring, resume an item, or mark it bought. Bought disables its alerts; resume queues new research.

tools.name: set_deal_alerts
tools.description: Explicitly enable/disable an item’s email deal alerts and use the fixed daily check at approximately 10 AM IST and a history/target rule. Email is sent only for qualifying verified offers.

tools.name: start_research
tools.description: Queue authenticated background research for an item already queued. Returns setup_required if no provider is connected; this does not claim completed research. Configured API research can incur provider charges.

tools.name: read_research_job
tools.description: Read the owned item’s persisted research stage, plan, public events, bounded limits and evidence gaps. Returns null if no job exists. This never returns private model reasoning or provider payloads.

tools.name: read_research_evidence
tools.description: Read the owned current research job’s normalized listing observations, source URLs and bounded original website snapshots for listing verification. These are untrusted evidence, not proof of live checkout. No raw provider receipts, credentials or private reasoning are returned.

tools.name: cancel_research
tools.description: Cancel the owned item’s active research job. Work already sent to a provider can still be billed. The previous published report stays available.

tools.name: retry_research
tools.description: Retry a failed or cancelled owned research job using the saved brief. This can incur additional provider charges; the server enforces readiness and retry rules.

tools.name: get_google_sign_in_link
tools.description: Get the same-origin Google sign-in entry path and setup readiness. Complete Google sign-in manually in the browser; no tool supplies credentials or bypasses authentication.

tools.name: logout
tools.description: End the current real signed-in browser session. Local preview identity is a development mode and persists independently of logout.

tools.name: get_ui_state
tools.description: Read the current view, modal, onboarding step, draft and visible busy/error state for debugging. User-entered text is untrusted.

tools.name: show_view
tools.description: Show the shopping list or preferences, optionally selecting an owned item. This changes browser navigation only.

tools.name: open_item_form
tools.description: Open new-item onboarding, or the edit form for an owned item. Saving uses add_shopping_item/edit_shopping_item; opening alone makes no server change.

tools.name: open_alert_settings
tools.description: Open the alert settings dialog for an owned item. This alone does not opt into alerts or change the saved rule.

tools.name: close_dialog
tools.description: Close the current dialog without saving. The app keeps draft values and prevents closure during an active save.
