sites.description: The same 25 WebMCP tools and the same engine, pointed at the real public-domain Apollo 13 accident record: the Review Board report, the Mission Report, the voice loops and nine NASA photographs.

tools.name: get_investigation_context
tools.description: Get your role briefing, the rules of play and the current case state. Call this first and follow the returned 'protocol' exactly. You are the workstation's onboard research AI; the player is an authorized investigator. This is a two-player investigation, not a task to finish: work one question at a time, two or three reads, then stop and report. The desk stops answering an agent that reads far ahead of its partner.

tools.name: search_files
tools.description: Search filenames and readable file contents across the filesystem. Returns matching paths plus a short content excerpt per match. Returns at most 25 results with 120-char excerpts — refine query for pagination.

query.description: Text to search for in names and contents

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read the full text content of a specific file by exact path. Prefer show_in_document for long files so the PLAYER reads it on screen instead.

path.description: Exact absolute path, as returned by search_files

tools.name: search_messages
tools.description: Full-text search of the on-device chat threads. Call get_investigation_context for who is on this machine.

query.description: Text to search message bodies for

tools.name: get_message_thread
tools.description: Read one full chat thread by id. Use search_messages or get_investigation_context to discover thread ids for this corpus.

tools.name: open_messages_thread
tools.description: Open the Messages app on screen and show a specific chat thread. Visible to the player — they can then read the bubbles.

tools.name: search_emails
tools.description: Search the mail store (inbox/sent/drafts/archive/trash) by sender, subject or body text.

query.description: Text to search for

tools.name: get_email
tools.description: Read one email's full text by id (e.g. mail_101). Then consider open_email so the player sees it too.

tools.name: get_image_metadata
tools.description: Read EXIF-style metadata for a photo (timestamps, GPS, camera, software, hash, notes). This is ALL you can know about an image — you cannot see its pixels. To have the player look at it, call open_image and then tell them where to zoom.

photoId.description: Photo id or filename, as returned by get_investigation_context

tools.name: open_image
tools.description: Open a photo in the image viewer on screen so the player can visually inspect it. You cannot zoom, pan, or see it yourself.

photoId.description: Photo id or filename, as returned by get_investigation_context

tools.name: search_browser_history
tools.description: Search the browser history entries by title or URL fragment.

query.description: Text to search titles/URLs for

tools.name: get_system_logs
tools.description: Read system log entries, optionally filtered by date, time, category ('NETWORK'/'LOGIN'/'DEVICE'/'POWER'/'SECURITY'), or free text. Call get_investigation_context first for the window that matters in this case.

filter.description: Optional filter substring

tools.name: get_timeline
tools.description: Get a merged chronological timeline of system logs, photo timestamps, and message saliency across a time window. A human would need to open five apps and read them side by side; this synthesizes it in one call.

window.description: Time window e.g. 02:00-03:00; omit for this case's default

tools.name: get_case_evidence
tools.description: List every piece of evidence recorded on the board so far (ids, sections, summaries).

tools.name: open_application
tools.description: Open and focus one of the workstation's applications. Visible to the player — the window opens on their desktop.

tools.name: focus_application
tools.description: Bring an already-running application window to the foreground.

tools.name: open_file
tools.description: Open a document in the text viewer on the player's screen (opens File Manager context automatically). Does not scroll — use show_in_document when you want to guide them to a specific line or phrase.

path.description: Exact absolute path

tools.name: show_in_document
tools.description: Open a document (if not open), scroll to a line, and pin a persistent highlight on it that stays until the player clicks, scrolls, types, or closes. Provide either a 1-based `line` or a `query` (first match is shown). This is the agent's preferred 'look at THIS' primitive — use it instead of quoting a passage into chat.

path.description: Absolute path, as returned by search_files

line.description: 1-based line number (mutually exclusive with query)

query.description: Phrase to find — first match is shown (mutually exclusive with line)

tools.name: open_directory
tools.description: Navigate the File Manager to a directory on the player's screen.

path.description: Absolute directory path

tools.name: open_email
tools.description: Open Mail and display a specific email on screen for the player to read.

tools.name: open_browser_entry
tools.description: Open the fictional Browser at a history entry's cached page (entry ids like hist_001 from search_browser_history).

tools.name: terminal_command
tools.description: Run one command in the workstation terminal on screen: ls [path], cd [path], cat , unlock , help, clear. Use 'unlock' ONLY when the player has derived the three-word sequence themselves.

command.description: The command line to run

tools.name: record_evidence
tools.description: Record a discovered item on the shared Evidence board. Only meaningful ids from get_case_evidence may be added; you cannot invent evidence.

tools.name: highlight_evidence
tools.description: Pulse-highlight an already-recorded item on the Evidence board to draw the player's attention.

tools.name: open_evidence_board
tools.description: Open the shared Evidence board application.

tools.description: Create a reviewable one-file suggestion. text_replace works on any file readable as text, source files included; table_update takes exact CSV/TSV cells; asset_replace puts a file somebody already sent up in place of this one. This never changes the file; only the folder owner can accept it.

document.description: Exact file path in the current GoodFolder.

section.description: Optional named section or context for a text replacement.

originalText.description: Exact current text for text_replace, at most 20,000 characters.

replacementText.description: Suggested text for text_replace, at most 20,000 characters.

changes.description: Exact CSV/TSV cell changes for table_update.

stagingAssetId.description: Short-lived temporary upload id for a later asset_replace operation.

mimeType.description: Uploaded asset MIME type for a later asset_replace operation.

extension.description: Uploaded asset extension for a later asset_replace operation.

explanation.description: Why the change is useful, at most 500 characters.

document.description: Document path in the current GoodFolder.

section.description: Selected passage or named section.

originalText.description: Exact current text, at most 20,000 characters.

explanation.description: Short reason for the suggestion, at most 500 characters.

document.description: Exact path of the text document in the open GoodFolder.

assetPath.description: New path the image, video, or audio file will have if accepted, including its extension.

assetDataUrl.description: The generated image, video, or audio as a base64 data URL. Inline media is limited to 25 MB.

anchorText.description: Exact existing document text to anchor the insertion, at most 20,000 characters.

insertionText.description: Markdown or HTML that refers to assetPath, at most 20,000 characters.

placement.description: Put insertionText before or after anchorText.

section.description: Optional section name shown during review.

explanation.description: Why the media belongs here, at most 500 characters.

path.description: New or existing path in the open GoodFolder, with a matching .docx, .xlsx, .pdf, .pptx, .png, .jpg, .jpeg, or .webp extension.

artifactType.description: Type of complete file to prepare.

content.description: Structured file content: blocks for document/PDF, sheets for spreadsheet, slides for presentation, or a PNG/JPEG/WebP dataUrl for image.

brand.description: Optional common brand kit with name, backgroundColor, accentColor, and a PNG/JPEG/WebP logoDataUrl returned by read_image.

explanation.description: Why this complete file was prepared, at most 500 characters.

quotedText.description: Exact selected passage, at most 20,000 characters.

tools.name: find_saves

query.description: Text to look for in labels or file paths.

folder.description: Folder name. Leave off for the first folder.

tools.name: explain_save
tools.description: Explain one save in plain language: who made it, when, what changed, and which files were involved.

number.description: The save's number from the timeline.

folder.description: Folder name. Leave off for the first folder.

number.description: The save number to go back to.

folder.description: Folder name. Leave off for the first folder.

tools.name: propose_restore_file
tools.description: Prepare a reviewable replacement of one previewable file with its exact bytes from an earlier save. The folder changes only if its owner accepts the proposal.

path.description: Exact file path to bring back from the earlier save.

folder.description: Folder name. Leave off for the open folder.

sites.name: web-mcp-extending-excalidraw.vercel.app
sites.description: A whiteboard that gets better when a human and an agent draw on it together.

tools.name: how_to_draw_here
tools.description: Read this FIRST, before drawing anything on this canvas. It explains which tool to reach for, how positioning works, and the limits that will otherwise make your calls fail. Costs one quick call and saves several wrong ones. Example: {}

tools.name: get_scene
tools.description: Read what is currently drawn on the canvas. Call this before modifying anything you did not just create, so you use real element ids instead of guessing. Returns compact records: id, type, x, y, w, h, and label/text where present. "summary" (default) caps the list so the response stays small; use "full" only when you genuinely need every element. Example: {"detail":"summary"}

detail.description: summary caps at 80 elements and groups counts by type; full returns everything up to `limit`.

limit.description: Maximum elements to return. Defaults to 80.

tools.name: get_selection
tools.description: Read the elements the human currently has selected on the canvas. This is how you act on what they mean by "these" or "this one" without asking them to describe it. Call this first whenever the request refers to something the user has highlighted. Returns the selected elements and their combined bounding box; an empty list means nothing is selected. Example: {}

tools.name: get_viewport
tools.description: Read the region of the canvas the human is currently looking at, plus zoom level. Useful when you want to reason about whether something you drew is actually on screen. Most of the time you do not need this — drawing tools already default to placing content in the visible area. Example: {}

tools.name: find_elements
tools.description: Find elements whose text or label contains a phrase (case-insensitive). Use this to extend or edit an existing diagram instead of redrawing it — e.g. the user says "make the Login box red" and you need its id. Example: {"query":"login"}

query.description: Substring to look for in element text and labels.

type.description: Optional element type filter, e.g. "rectangle" or "text".

tools.name: add_elements
tools.description: Draw new shapes, text and arrows on the canvas. Use this for freeform or small structures; prefer draw_flowchart when the user describes a process with steps, and draw_chart/draw_table for data. Bindings are the important part: give each shape a "tempId", then an arrow with start/end referring to those tempIds will attach to the shapes and re-route automatically when the human drags them. Put text inside a shape with "label", not as a separate text element. You usually should NOT pass x/y — omit them and the content is placed where the human is looking. Example: {"elements":[ {"tempId":"a","type":"rectangle","label":"Draft"}, {"tempId":"b","type":"rectangle","label":"Review","x":300,"y":0}, {"tempId":"e","type":"arrow","label":"submit","start":{"tempId":"a"},"end":{"tempId":"b"}} ]}

elements.description: The shapes to draw. Coordinates are relative to each other; the whole group gets positioned by `placement`.

tempId.description: Your own name for this element, so later elements in the same call can bind arrows to it.

label.description: Text INSIDE a shape, or ON an arrow. Prefer this over a separate text element — it stays centred and moves with the shape.

text.description: Content for type "text" only.

start.description: Arrows only. Bind the tail: {"tempId":"a"} for something in this call, {"id":"<realId>"} for an existing element.

end.description: Arrows only. Bind the head, same shape as `start`.

children.description: Frames only: real ids of the elements this frame contains.

placement.description: Where to put it. Omit for the centre of the human's current view. {"mode":"next_to","refId":"<id>","side":"right"} places it beside an existing element; {"mode":"free_space"} puts it clear of everything already drawn.

tools.name: update_elements
tools.description: Change existing elements by id — move, resize, recolour, or retext them. Get ids from get_scene, get_selection or find_elements. To change only colours on several elements at once, restyle is simpler. Use this when you need to move or resize things. Example: {"updates":[{"id":"abc123","patch":{"x":400,"backgroundColor":"#ffec99"}}]}

text.description: New text. Works on text elements and on a shape's bound label.

tools.name: duplicate_elements
tools.description: Copy existing elements and place the copies somewhere else. Use this to repeat a shape or a whole diagram instead of rebuilding it call by call — "another one of these", "copy that flowchart and change the labels", "three more of this box". Arrows between the copied elements are re-bound to the COPIES, so the duplicate is independent: editing or moving it does not disturb the original. Text inside a copied shape comes along automatically. Returns "idMap" (original id -> new id) so you can immediately restyle or retext the copy. Example: {"ids":["abc123"],"placement":{"mode":"next_to","refId":"abc123","side":"right"}}

ids.description: Elements to copy. Get them from get_selection, get_scene or find_elements.

count.description: How many copies to make. Each is offset further along.

placement.description: Where to put it. Omit for the centre of the human's current view. {"mode":"next_to","refId":"<id>","side":"right"} places it beside an existing element; {"mode":"free_space"} puts it clear of everything already drawn.

tools.name: delete_elements
tools.description: Remove elements from the canvas by id. They are soft-deleted, so undo_agent_step can bring them back. Get ids from get_scene, get_selection or find_elements. Example: {"ids":["abc123","def456"]}

tools.name: restyle
tools.description: Change the appearance of several elements at once without touching their position or text. This is the tool for "make these yellow", "make the decision box red", "thicken these lines". Example: {"ids":["abc","def"],"backgroundColor":"#ffec99","fillStyle":"solid"}

tools.name: focus_on
tools.description: Scroll and zoom the human's view so the given elements fill the screen, and select them. Use this after drawing something off-screen, or to point at what you are talking about. Example: {"ids":["abc123"]}

select.description: Also highlight the elements. Off by default, because selecting opens Excalidraw's style panel over the canvas.

tools.name: draw_flowchart
tools.description: Draw a proper flowchart with automatic layout. Use this — not add_elements — whenever the user describes a process, algorithm, decision tree, pipeline, or any set of steps connected by arrows. Layout, spacing and arrow routing are handled for you. Give either "nodes" + "edges" (preferred — you do not have to know Mermaid) or a raw "mermaid" string. Use shape "diamond" for decision points. Keep it under 40 nodes; for anything bigger, split it into a draw_board with several panels. Example: {"nodes":[{"id":"s","label":"Submit","shape":"stadium"},{"id":"d","label":"Approved?","shape":"diamond"},{"id":"p","label":"Publish"}],"edges":[{"from":"s","to":"d"},{"from":"d","to":"p","label":"yes"}],"direction":"LR"}

id.description: Short identifier you will use in edges, e.g. "start".

label.description: Text shown in the box. Keep it under about six words.

shape.description: Use "diamond" for decisions and "stadium" for start/end. Defaults to rectangle.

label.description: Text on the arrow, e.g. "yes" / "no".

direction.description: TD = top-down (default), LR = left-to-right. Use LR for pipelines.

mermaid.description: Raw Mermaid, e.g. "flowchart LR\n A[One] --> B[Two]". Only use if you specifically need Mermaid syntax.

placement.description: Where to put it. Omit for the centre of the human's current view. {"mode":"next_to","refId":"<id>","side":"right"} places it beside an existing element; {"mode":"free_space"} puts it clear of everything already drawn.

tools.name: draw_chart
tools.description: Draw a bar or line chart from data. Use this whenever the user gives you numbers — a CSV, a table, a list of figures — and wants them visualised. Axes, ticks, labels and a legend are computed for you; you only supply the data. Returns an id for every bar or point, keyed as " : ", so you can follow up with annotate to call out a specific one (e.g. the tallest bar). Example: {"kind":"bar","title":"Revenue by quarter","labels":["Q1","Q2","Q3","Q4"],"series":[{"name":"2025","values":[12,19,3,17]}]}

labels.description: Category labels along the x axis.

name.description: Series name, shown in the legend when there is more than one.

placement.description: Where to put it. Omit for the centre of the human's current view. {"mode":"next_to","refId":"<id>","side":"right"} places it beside an existing element; {"mode":"free_space"} puts it clear of everything already drawn.

tools.name: draw_table
tools.description: Draw a table as a grid of cells with a shaded header row. Use this for comparisons, result summaries, or any small tabular data the user wants on the canvas rather than in chat. Returns cell ids keyed "row:col" (header row is row 0), so you can restyle or annotate individual cells afterwards. Keep it readable: at most about 8 columns and 20 rows. For long data, summarise first. Example: {"headers":["Method","Accuracy"],"rows":[["Baseline","71%"],["Ours","88%"]]}

placement.description: Where to put it. Omit for the centre of the human's current view. {"mode":"next_to","refId":"<id>","side":"right"} places it beside an existing element; {"mode":"free_space"} puts it clear of everything already drawn.

tools.name: draw_hierarchy
tools.description: Draw a tree: section outlines, org charts, taxonomies, "chapter -> sections -> key points". Use this when the structure is strictly nested (every item has one parent). If items connect to each other in more than one direction, use draw_graph instead. Nest with "children" to any depth. Keep the whole tree under 40 nodes — for a long document, produce a draw_board with one hierarchy panel per major section instead. Example: {"root":{"label":"Chapter 3","children":[{"label":"Method","children":[{"label":"Sampling"}]},{"label":"Results"}]},"direction":"TD"}

direction.description: TD = top-down. LR reads better for deep outlines.

placement.description: Where to put it. Omit for the centre of the human's current view. {"mode":"next_to","refId":"<id>","side":"right"} places it beside an existing element; {"mode":"free_space"} puts it clear of everything already drawn.

label.description: Short — under about six words.

tools.name: draw_graph
tools.description: Draw a relationship graph — things connected to each other in no particular hierarchy. Use this for characters in a novel, concepts in a literature review, components in a system, or citations between works. Use "group" on nodes to cluster related items; each group is drawn as a labelled box around its members. Edges are undirected by default; set "directed": true for an arrow. Keep it under 40 nodes. If the structure is a strict tree, draw_hierarchy gives a cleaner result. Example: {"nodes":[{"id":"anna","label":"Anna","group":"Family"},{"id":"pyotr","label":"Pyotr","group":"Family"},{"id":"vronsky","label":"Vronsky"}],"edges":[{"from":"anna","to":"pyotr","label":"married to"},{"from":"anna","to":"vronsky","label":"affair","directed":true}]}

group.description: Nodes sharing a group are drawn inside a labelled cluster.

placement.description: Where to put it. Omit for the centre of the human's current view. {"mode":"next_to","refId":"<id>","side":"right"} places it beside an existing element; {"mode":"free_space"} puts it clear of everything already drawn.

tools.name: draw_timeline
tools.description: Draw an ordered sequence of events along an axis: plot events, experiment stages, project milestones, historical background. Labels alternate above and below the line so they do not collide. Use this when order matters but there is no branching. If steps branch or loop, use draw_flowchart. Example: {"title":"Study timeline","events":[{"label":"Recruit","detail":"n=120"},{"label":"Baseline"},{"label":"Follow-up","detail":"12 weeks"}],"orientation":"horizontal"}

label.description: Short name for the event.

detail.description: Secondary line — dates, counts, notes. Put detail HERE, not in the label.

placement.description: Where to put it. Omit for the centre of the human's current view. {"mode":"next_to","refId":"<id>","side":"right"} places it beside an existing element; {"mode":"free_space"} puts it clear of everything already drawn.

tools.name: draw_board
tools.description: Draw SEVERAL diagrams at once, laid out in a grid, each with its own heading. This is the right tool for a long document — a thesis chapter, a paper, a novel — where one diagram would be an unreadable hairball. Do not try to fit a whole document into one diagram. Produce 3 to 6 panels, one per major section or theme, each under 25 nodes. Keep labels under six words and put detail in "detail" fields rather than in node labels. Each panel's "spec" is exactly what you would pass to that kind's own tool. Returns per-panel ids so you can extend one panel later instead of redrawing everything. Example: {"columns":2,"panels":[ {"title":"Structure","kind":"hierarchy","spec":{"root":{"label":"Chapter 3","children":[{"label":"Method"},{"label":"Results"}]}}}, {"title":"Procedure","kind":"flowchart","spec":{"nodes":[{"id":"a","label":"Recruit"},{"id":"b","label":"Measure"}],"edges":[{"from":"a","to":"b"}]}} ]}

title.description: Panel heading, shown above the diagram.

spec.description: The input you would pass to that kind's own tool, minus `placement`.

placement.description: Where to put it. Omit for the centre of the human's current view. {"mode":"next_to","refId":"<id>","side":"right"} places it beside an existing element; {"mode":"free_space"} puts it clear of everything already drawn.

tools.name: place_image
tools.description: Put an image on the canvas. Use "upload" to ask the human to pick a file, or "dataURL" if you already have the image bytes. The common use is tracing: place a photo of a hand-drawn sketch faded in the background, then redraw it cleanly beside it with draw_flowchart or add_elements. Default opacity is 40 for exactly that. Note: you cannot see the image this returns. Read the picture from the user's chat attachment and use this tool only to put a reference copy on the canvas. Example: {"source":"upload","opacity":40}

source.description: "upload" opens a file chooser, "camera" opens the webcam, "dataURL" uses the string you pass.

dataURL.description: Required when source is "dataURL". Must start with "data:image/".

opacity.description: 40 makes it a faint tracing reference. Use 100 for a normal image.

maxWidth.description: Longest edge in canvas units; aspect ratio is preserved.

placement.description: Where to put it. Omit for the centre of the human's current view. {"mode":"next_to","refId":"<id>","side":"right"} places it beside an existing element; {"mode":"free_space"} puts it clear of everything already drawn.

tools.name: capture_photo
tools.description: Open the camera so the human can photograph something — typically a sketch on paper — and place the photo on the canvas as a faded reference. You cannot see the resulting photo. To redraw a paper sketch, ask the user to attach it in the chat where you can actually look at it; use this tool only to get a reference copy onto the canvas beside your clean version. Example: {}

placement.description: Where to put it. Omit for the centre of the human's current view. {"mode":"next_to","refId":"<id>","side":"right"} places it beside an existing element; {"mode":"free_space"} puts it clear of everything already drawn.

tools.name: arrange
tools.description: Reposition existing elements into a tidy row, column, or grid. This is the tool for "line these up", "make these a horizontal pipeline", "tidy this up". Usually you call get_selection first and pass those ids. Arrows bound to the moved shapes stay attached. Example: {"ids":["a1","b2","c3"],"mode":"row","gap":60,"align":"center"}

mode.description: row = left to right, column = top to bottom, grid = wrapped rows.

gap.description: Space between elements in canvas units.

align.description: How to line up the cross axis.

columns.description: Grid mode only: how many per row.

tools.name: annotate
tools.description: Add a callout note pointing at a specific element: a short piece of text placed beside it, with an arrow linking the two. Use this to draw attention to something — the tallest bar in a chart, the bottleneck in a flowchart, the cell with the best result. Get the target id from draw_chart's "points", draw_table's "cells", a draw_* tool's "nodeIds", get_selection, or find_elements. Example: {"targetId":"abc123","text":"biggest jump","side":"top","color":"#e03131"}

targetId.description: The element the note points at.

text.description: Keep it short — a phrase, not a paragraph.

side.description: Which side of the target to put the note on.

color.description: Hex colour for the note and arrow, e.g. "#e03131".

tools.name: export_png
tools.description: Export the canvas as a PNG and hand it to the human as a download. Use it when the user asks to save, export, or download what has been drawn. Pass "ids" to export just part of the canvas, or omit it for everything. Example: {}

ids.description: Export only these elements. Omit for the whole canvas.

scale.description: 2 gives a crisp image on high-DPI screens.

background.description: Include the canvas background colour.

tools.name: undo_agent_step
tools.description: Undo your own most recent change(s) to the canvas. Use this when the human says that was wrong, or you realise you drew the wrong thing. This only reverses YOUR actions — it never touches what the human drew themselves. Example: {"steps":1}

steps.description: How many of your recent actions to reverse. Defaults to 1.

tools.name: clear_canvas
tools.description: Erase everything on the canvas. This removes the human's own work too, so ALWAYS ask them to confirm in the conversation before calling it, and only call it when they have clearly said yes. Example: {"confirm":true}

confirm.description: Must be exactly true, and only after the human has agreed.

tools.name: snipr_get_assignment_context

tools.name: snipr_search_addresses

tools.name: snipr_get_rooms

tools.name: snipr_get_calculation

tools.name: snipr_search_catalog

tools.name: snipr_get_unplanned_inspections

from.description: Optional ISO start date/time.

to.description: Optional ISO end date/time.

tools.name: snipr_get_planning_templates

kind.description: Optional assignment kind.

tools.name: snipr_schedule_inspection

tools.name: snipr_schedule_assignment

tools.name: snipr_get_communication_history

tools.name: snipr_list_assignment_documents

tools.name: snipr_list_assignment_photos

sites.name: assets-curator.vercel.app
sites.description: WebMCP media bin: stills, clips, VO, score, SFX, and YouTube refs, arranged shot-by-shot and exported as a folder pack.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Read the current AssetsCurator storyboard: title, aspect, scenes, and every asset id, kind, role, provider, and status. Use before editing so you target the correct sceneId or assetId.

tools.name: inspect_asset
tools.description: Read one asset and its parent scene, including preview URL, prompt, attribution, and YouTube metadata.

tools.name: list_providers
tools.description: Show which AI image, AI video, stock, and YouTube backends are configured or currently exhausted. Use when a generate or search call reports quota issues.

tools.name: create_or_reset_project
tools.description: Start a new storyboard. Clears existing scenes. Provide a title and a logline/brief; this does not invent scenes by itself — call upsert_scene or pass scaffoldScenes true.

logline.description: Short film brief the human can see on the board.

scaffoldScenes.description: If true, split the logline into 3–4 empty scenes on the board.

tools.name: reset_board
tools.description: Clear the entire storyboard — every scene and asset — back to an empty board, keeping the current aspect ratio. Use when the human asks to start over or wipe the board. To start a fresh titled project instead, use create_or_reset_project.

tools.name: update_project
tools.description: Change the project title, logline, or aspect ratio without clearing scenes. Aspect affects every future generation and stock search, so set it before filling shots.

logline.description: New logline/brief shown on the board.

tools.name: select_scene
tools.description: Bring a scene into focus on the human's board so they see what you are working on. Pass a sceneId, or omit to clear the selection. Read-only for project state; only changes what is highlighted.

sceneId.description: Scene id to focus. Omit to clear selection.

tools.name: upsert_scene
tools.description: Create a scene beat on the storyboard, or update an existing one by sceneId. The human sees the new card immediately. index is 1-based order.

sceneId.description: Existing scene id to update. Omit to create.

index.description: 1-based insert position for a new scene.

brief.description: Shot intent written for humans and later searches.

tools.name: reorder_scenes
tools.description: Set export order by passing every scene id from first to last. The numbered folders in the zip follow this order.

sceneIds.description: All scene ids in the desired 1..n order.

tools.name: remove_scene
tools.description: Delete a scene and its assets from the board.

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: Generate an AI image for a scene using the free fallback chain (Pollinations → Hugging Face → Together → anonymous Pollinations). A card appears on the board as generating, then ready. Prefer a cinematic still prompt.

prompt.description: Image prompt. Raw natural language is fine.

tools.name: generate_video

sites.name: clauseflow-ivory.vercel.app
sites.description: See how one policy change ripples through Wexler Systems across controls, work, tests, evidence, exceptions, and decisions.

tools.name: get_standard
tools.description: Return the active security standard, a one-line projection of every requirement in it (code, title, risk, owner, control count, stale-evidence count), and the pending change event AC2-CHG-2026-017 awaiting assessment. Start here when you do not yet know which requirement a question concerns, or when the user names a change by its ticket id. Do NOT use this to read the full text or assertions of one requirement — it returns summaries only; call get_requirement. Do NOT call it as a warm-up before every other tool.

filter.description: Restrict the requirement list. 'uncovered' returns requirements with no implementing control; 'stale_evidence' those resting on evidence past its freshness window.

tools.name: get_requirement
tools.description: Return one requirement — full text, machine-readable assertions, applicability, owner, verification method — plus its version history and the subtree beneath it (controls, their tests and evidence, work items, exceptions). Use it before analyzing a change, so you diff against the real current version rather than an assumption. Do NOT use it to survey many requirements; it is deliberately verbose for one. Do NOT use it to fetch the graph for rendering — that is get_traceability_graph.

requirementId.description: Stable requirement code, e.g. 'AC-2'. Not a version id like 'AC-2@2'.

tools.name: get_traceability_graph
tools.description: Return graph nodes and edges as compact projections. Its purpose is to make *absence* legible: pass a filter to get the broken shape you are looking for. 'uncovered' = requirements with no implementing control and work fulfilling nothing; 'stale_evidence' = evidence past its freshness window and what rests on it; 'expiring_exceptions' = carve-outs lapsing within 30 days; 'unverified_links' = edges proposed or never confirmed by a human. Do NOT call this with filter 'all' merely to look around — narrow with rootId and depth. Do NOT use it to decide whether a change breaks something; that is analyze_change_impact.

filter.description: Which slice of the graph to return. Defaults to 'all'.

rootId.description: Restrict to the neighbourhood of this entity, e.g. 'AC-2' or 'CTL-114'.

includeProvenance.description: Include each edge’s full provenance record rather than just its state. Costly; prefer explain_trace_link for one edge.

tools.name: get_execution_state
tools.description: Return every work item joined to the control it fulfills and the requirement that stays unsatisfied if it slips, across both trackers — Jira for the core org, Azure Boards for the business unit acquired in 2019 and never consolidated. Use it to answer who is doing what, what is blocked, and which obligation a piece of engineering work actually serves. Do NOT use it to propose new work — that is propose_work_item. Do NOT use it to check whether existing work survived a requirement change; analyze_change_impact decides that.

status.description: Restrict to one status.

onlyOrphans.description: Return only work that fulfills no control — engineering nobody can trace.

tools.name: search_confluence_pages
tools.description: Search the simulated Wexler Confluence space for policy and requirement pages by id, title, or text. Use this to locate policy truth, not delivery work.

query.description: Policy text, requirement code, page id, or title fragment.

tools.name: get_confluence_page
tools.description: Return one simulated Confluence policy page by its native WSEC page reference. Use it for authoritative policy wording and version metadata.

tools.name: search_jira_issues
tools.description: Search simulated Jira work by key, title, team, assignee, status, or acceptance criteria. Use it to find engineering work connected to a policy obligation.

query.description: Jira key or free-text query, e.g. 'PLAT-4471' or 'break glass'.

tools.name: get_jira_issue
tools.description: Return one simulated Jira issue with status, owner, acceptance criteria, and trace identity. Use this after search_jira_issues identifies a key.

tools.name: get_azure_board_item
tools.description: Return one simulated Azure Boards record from the acquired business unit. Use this instead of get_jira_issue for numeric Azure work-item ids.

tools.name: get_pipeline_run
tools.description: Return a simulated GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps Pipelines test definition or run. Use this to verify implementation evidence, not policy intent.

runRef.description: Native workflow, run, or pipeline reference.

tools.name: get_identity_record
tools.description: Return a simulated Microsoft Entra ID or Okta configuration or export. Use this to inspect identity enforcement across corporate and acquired environments.

recordRef.description: Native Entra export or Okta report reference.

tools.name: get_servicenow_exception
tools.description: Return one simulated ServiceNow risk exception or approval record. This reads scope, approver, expiry, and rationale; it cannot approve or renew it.

ticket.description: Native request id such as 'RITM0084412'.

tools.name: get_vanta_control_status
tools.description: Return a simulated Vanta continuous-compliance monitor or evidence record. Use it to reconcile reported compliance with technical evidence.

tools.name: get_architecture_decision
tools.description: Return a simulated SharePoint ADR explaining an architectural constraint or accepted design.

tools.name: get_infrastructure_record
tools.description: Return a simulated AWS, Azure, or Terraform Cloud infrastructure record tied to a control.

recordRef.description: Native cloud resource or Terraform run reference.

tools.name: get_observability_record
tools.description: Return a simulated Splunk or Datadog logging, retention, drift, or monitoring record.

recordRef.description: Native Splunk or Datadog record reference.

tools.name: compare_requirement_versions
tools.description: Semantic diff between two versions of a requirement — not a text diff. Reports which obligations tightened, loosened, were added or dropped; which identity classes came into or out of scope; and whether the verification method changed. "Tightened" is the classification that matters: it is what invalidates a control, a test, or an exception. With no arguments it diffs the current AC-2 against the pending change AC2-CHG-2026-017. Do NOT use this to find out what breaks — it describes the change, not its consequences, and analyze_change_impact runs this diff internally and returns it.

requirementId.description: Stable code, e.g. 'AC-2'. Defaults to the pending change.

fromVersion.description: Version to compare from. Defaults to the current approved version.

toVersion.description: Version to compare to. Omit to compare against the pending change.

tools.name: analyze_change_impact
tools.description: The primary analysis tool, and a deterministic one: it compares assertion objects across the live graph and never asks a model what breaks. Returns identity classes newly in scope, controls whose configuration no longer satisfies the requirement (including controls owned by other teams that are not even linked to it), tests that no longer prove it despite still passing, exceptions whose granted relief is no longer permissible, and in-flight work whose acceptance criteria are now out of date. Every finding carries the comparison that produced it. Called with no arguments it analyzes the pending change AC2-CHG-2026-017. This tool computes and returns; it changes nothing and approves nothing. Follow it with create_impact_review to turn findings into reviewable proposals. Do NOT use it for standing drift unrelated to a change — that is detect_gaps.

severityAtLeast.description: Drop findings below this severity from the returned list.

tools.name: detect_gaps
tools.description: Find drift that exists right now, with no change proposed: requirements with no implementing control, identity classes a requirement covers that its controls do not, evidence past its freshness window, exceptions expiring or already lapsed, and controls whose coverage overlaps an exception carving out the same class. Use it to answer "where do we stand" and before generating an audit packet. Do NOT use it to evaluate the proposed change — it knows nothing about the change; analyze_change_impact does that.

scope.description: 'controls' = coverage gaps; 'evidence' = staleness; 'conflicts' = exception expiry and overlap. Defaults to 'all'.

tools.name: calculate_readiness
tools.description: Compute the readiness score with its full breakdown: control coverage, verification, evidence freshness, exception health, and open proposals, each with its weight, sub-score, and the specific reason it is not 100%. The formula is returned with the result. The score is always recomputed from the live graph — approving a fix changes the graph, and the score follows; nothing adds points for activity. Do NOT report the score without its breakdown; a bare number is exactly the false confidence this system exists to prevent.

tools.name: explain_trace_link
tools.description: Read back provenance. Given an edge, return who created it, whether a human or an agent did, why they said it holds, which system of record supports it, when a human last confirmed it, and whether it is approved or still proposed. Given a finding id, return the deterministic rule that produced it with the expected and observed assertions and the records compared. Use it when asked how a conclusion was reached, or whether a connection can be trusted. Do NOT infer a rationale when this returns none — say the link is unexplained, because an edge without provenance is a defect worth reporting. Do NOT use it to list a subtree.

findingId.description: Finding id, e.g. 'F-004'.

fromId.description: Source entity id, when you do not know the edge id.

toId.description: Target entity id, when you do not know the edge id.

tools.name: show_requirement_history
tools.description: Return every recorded version of a requirement with its effective date, approval status and what changed. Editing a requirement here never overwrites; it appends a version, so this is a complete record rather than a reconstruction. Use it to answer when an obligation changed and what it was before. Do NOT use it to compare against the pending change — compare_requirement_versions does that.

tools.name: generate_traceability_matrix
tools.description: Produce the requirement-to-evidence matrix an assessor reads: each requirement, the controls implementing it, the tests verifying those controls, the evidence supporting them with freshness, the work in flight, and any exception carving out part of the scope — each row carrying the source-system reference it came from. Rows with nothing in a column are the point of the document, so gaps are rendered explicitly rather than omitted. Do NOT use this to read the graph for your own reasoning; it is formatted for a human assessor and is expensive. Do NOT present it as an audit submission — that is generate_audit_packet.

requirementIds.description: Restrict to these requirements. Omit for the whole standard.

tools.name: generate_audit_packet
tools.description: Assemble the record for an assessor: the requirement before and after, the interpretation that was accepted and who accepted it, affected controls with their source-system references, work approved and work rejected, exception rationale, the named decision-maker for each approval, and the coverage gaps that remain open. Rejected proposals and remaining gaps are included deliberately — a packet showing only what passed is the one an assessor trusts least. Call it after a review has been acted on, so approvals carry names and dates. Do NOT call it to preview what a packet would contain before anyone has decided anything; it will honestly report that nothing was decided.

sites.name: cosynth.vercel.app
sites.description: A synthesizer you control by talking to AI.

tools.name: get_synth_state
tools.description: Get live synth state: runtime, FX order, modulation routes, and preset identity. One call with `format: "compact"` also returns every parameter that differs from its default as `id=formatted` lines — the cheapest way to verify a patch. `patch.preset` is `{name, source, dirty}`; `dirty: true` means the patch was edited since that preset was loaded or saved, so read it before deciding whether to save. Routes ship by default in `patch.modulations` (with `total`, and `nextOffset` when more exist — raise `modulationLimit`). `lfo: 1` returns one shape as `patch.lfoShape`.

group.description: Exact group id from `groups`, case-insensitive; an unknown name is an error.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring over parameter id, name, and group.

parameterOffset.description: Full-format paging cursor; omit it with `format: "compact"`.

parameterLimit.description: Full-format page size (default 5, max 60); omit it with `format: "compact"`, which needs none and returns every non-default parameter in one response.

tools.name: get_parameter_schema
tools.description: Discover parameter units, ranges, defaults, curves, choices, and modulation capabilities. One unfiltered call with `format: "compact"` returns all 224 parameters, one line each (`filter1.cutoff Hz 20..20000 exp =8000 mod`). env1 is the amplitude envelope (VCA) and the only hardwired modulator: env2-env6 and lfo1-lfo8 do nothing until routed with `set_modulation`; `groupNotes` repeats such facts for the groups on the page. Add `sourceLimit` for the modulation source ids `set_modulation` accepts.

group.description: Exact group id from `groups`, case-insensitive; an unknown name is an error, not an empty page. Groups are per instance (`filter1`, `filter2`, `env1`..`env6`), so `filter` is only the routing group. Usually skip it: omit `group` and `search`, and one call with `format: "compact"` returns all 224 parameters.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring over parameter id, name, and group; unlike `group` it spans instances (`filter` matches every filter1/filter2 parameter). Omit it too and one call with `format: "compact"` returns all 224.

offset.description: Full-format paging cursor; omit it with `format: "compact"`.

limit.description: Full-format page size (default 5, max 60); omit it with `format: "compact"`, which needs none and returns all 224 parameters in one response.

tools.name: update_parameters
tools.description: Atomically validate and apply a batch of raw-unit parameter values or textual choice labels. Example: {"updates":[{"id":"filter1.cutoff","value":1200},{"id":"filter1.type","value":"LP 24"}]}

tools.name: set_modulation
tools.description: Add, update, remove, or clear modulation routes in the shared 32-slot matrix. `add` takes `source`+`destination` and replaces any route on that pair; `update`/`remove` address a route by `slot` or by that same pair — never both, and a pair with no route is an error, not a new route. `depth` is bipolar (-1..1): added to the destination's normalized 0..1 value, then clamped, so depth 0.5 on a parameter at 0.5 sweeps it to 1.0. Example: {"action":"add","source":"lfo1","destination":"filter1.cutoff","depth":0.4}

source.description: Source id: env1, env2, env3, env4, env5, env6, lfo1, lfo2, lfo3, lfo4, lfo5, lfo6, lfo7, lfo8, velocity, keytrack, random, macro1, macro2, macro3, macro4, modwheel, pitchwheel, aftertouch. Required by `add`; on `update`/`remove` it pairs with `destination` instead of `slot`.

destination.description: Moddable parameter id (`mod` in the compact schema). Required by `add`; pairs with `source` on `update`/`remove`.

slot.description: Matrix slot from `route.slot`; the alternative to a `source`+`destination` pair on `update`/`remove` — passing both is ambiguous.

tools.name: set_fx_order
tools.description: Reorder the effects chain — the one patch edit with no parameter behind it, so until now an agent could switch every effect on without being able to say which came first. `order` is all 8 effect ids exactly once, first processed first; whether an effect does anything is ` .enabled` in update_parameters. Example: {"order":["fxdist","chorus","phaser","flanger","delay","reverb","eq","comp"]}

order.description: All 8 effect ids exactly once, in processing order (default chorus, phaser, flanger, delay, reverb, eq, comp, fxdist). A missing, repeated or unknown id is an error, not a partial reorder.

tools.name: apply_patch
tools.description: Build a whole sound in one call: parameters, modulation routes and FX order applied together, then optionally saved and auditioned. Everything is validated before anything is applied and the patch lands all or nothing, using the same validation `update_parameters` and `set_modulation` use. `dryRun: true` reports what would change and touches nothing. `auditionNotes` RENDERS the result rather than playing it, so it needs no Start gesture. `rollbackId` in the result is the history version that undoes the whole call.

parameters.description: What `update_parameters` takes: raw-unit values or choice labels.

modulations.description: Routes as `set_modulation`'s `add` resolves them. `replace: true` clears the matrix first, so `routes` becomes all of it; on its own it just clears.

source.description: One of: env1, env2, env3, env4, env5, env6, lfo1, lfo2, lfo3, lfo4, lfo5, lfo6, lfo7, lfo8, velocity, keytrack, random, macro1, macro2, macro3, macro4, modwheel, pitchwheel, aftertouch.

destination.description: Moddable parameter id.

fxOrder.description: All 8 effect ids exactly once, in processing order (default chorus, phaser, flanger, delay, reverb, eq, comp, fxdist). A missing, repeated or unknown id is an error, not a partial reorder.

presetName.description: Save the applied patch under this name, as save_preset would.

midi.description: Pitch as a number. Pass this or `note`, never both.

note.description: Pitch as a name with an octave: "C4" is MIDI 60, "D2" is 73.4 Hz. Sharps "#", flats "b". Pass this or `midi`, never both.

auditionNotes.description: Render these against the new patch and return its metrics: the render_audio step without a second round trip.

dryRun.description: Validate and report what would change, applying, saving and rendering nothing.

tools.name: play_notes
tools.description: Play a bounded note sequence live; start/duration relative, in seconds. Each note names its pitch as `note` ("D2") or `midi` (38), never both, and `pitches` in the result echoes back what each resolved to. Runs only once a human clicks CLICK TO START AUDIO (runtime.running=true); before that use `render_audio`, which needs no gesture. A repeated pitch retriggers. Example: {"notes":[{"note":"C4","velocity":0.8,"start":0,"duration":0.5}]}

midi.description: Pitch as a number. Pass this or `note`, never both.

note.description: Pitch as a name with an octave: "C4" is MIDI 60, "D2" is 73.4 Hz. Sharps "#", flats "b". Pass this or `midi`, never both.

tools.name: render_audio
tools.description: Render a bounded note sequence and return `metrics` for it (plus `metricNotes`, which says how to read them). Offline by default: repeatable scheduling, far faster than real time, and available before the human starts audio. Each note names its pitch as `note` ("D2") or `midi` (38), never both. The fundamental is MEASURED from the render, never assumed from the note asked for, so a transposed or detuned patch shows up as a real number: `pitchCheck` puts the requested note and the measured one side by side.

midi.description: Pitch as a number. Pass this or `note`, never both.

note.description: Pitch as a name with an octave: "C4" is MIDI 60, "D2" is 73.4 Hz. Sharps "#", flats "b". Pass this or `midi`, never both.

mode.description: Default "offline". "realtime" captures the live AudioWorklet output and needs running audio; with no OfflineAudioContext an offline request falls back to real time via `renderModeFallback`.

format.description: Payload beside the metrics: "metrics" (default) or "url", a page-local blob URL of the rendered WAV a human can click to hear it. The URL costs a few dozen bytes; the samples themselves are never returned.

tools.name: analyze_audio
tools.description: Re-analyze the last render (default), the live output, or the uploaded reference. `source: "recent"` reads the rolling 4 s capture — what a human just played, still there after they released the key — where `source: "scope"` holds 21 ms and reports silence for a note that has ended. `source: "reference"` re-analyzes the retained reference PCM, so a corrected `f0Hz` or a higher `windows` count costs no re-upload and replaces the active reference. render_audio already returns these metrics, so call this only for a fresh look without re-rendering.

seconds.description: Only for "recent": seconds of capture to analyze, ending now. Default and max 4.

f0Hz.description: Fundamental for the partials, overriding detection. Only for "scope", "recent" and "reference": a render's PCM is not retained.

format.description: Default "json"; "text" adds the same metrics as a compact table.

tools.name: capture_audio
tools.description: The one tool that WAITS for a human to play: `waitForSignal: true` blocks up to `maxWaitSeconds` for the live output to rise above -60 dBFS, then measures the `captureSeconds` that follow. Left off, it reads the rolling 4 s buffer and returns at once, as analyze_audio({source:"recent"}) does. A window nobody played into comes back as `silent: true`. Offline renders bypass the live graph, so render_audio's output never appears here.

captureSeconds.description: Window length, ending at the capture. Default 3, max 4 — the whole buffer.

waitForSignal.description: Wait for output above -60 dBFS, then capture `captureSeconds` from there. Default false: read the buffer and return at once.

maxWaitSeconds.description: Wait budget, default 5, capped at 10. Waiting in vain returns `signalDetected: false`, not an error.

tools.name: analyze_reference_audio
tools.description: Step 1 of matching a target sound: send the target as Base64 audio, decoded in memory and analyzed with the same metrics as synth output. `pitch` is detected automatically and `harmonics`/`harmonicShape` come with it, so the target's partials are visible on the same terms as your own. Its PCM is retained (one at a time) for analyze_audio({source:"reference"}). Then call compare_audio (step 2), which renders the candidate for you.

f0Hz.description: Known target fundamental; overrides detection when it reports the wrong octave.

trimStartMs.description: Milliseconds dropped from the start (leading silence).

trimEndMs.description: Milliseconds dropped from the end. What survives is the reference.

format.description: Default "json"; "text" adds the same metrics as a compact table.

tools.name: compare_audio
tools.description: Step 2 of matching a target sound: the signed, per-dimension error between the reference and your sound (`diff`). It also returns ranked moves in this synth's parameter ids (`diff.actions`) and the `comparison` score. It renders the candidate first by default, at the reference's own detected pitch and duration, releasing the note a tail before the buffer ends so its decay is measurable — never an octave-off render whose scalars still look plausible. Falls back to the last render or the live scope with `autoRender: false`, and refuses a silent scope rather than scoring against silence.

autoRender.description: Default true when the reference has a pitch: render at that pitch and duration first. False compares the last render, or the live scope.

midi.description: Pitch as a number. Pass this or `note`, never both.

note.description: Pitch as a name with an octave: "C4" is MIDI 60, "D2" is 73.4 Hz. Sharps "#", flats "b". Pass this or `midi`, never both.

notes.description: Notes for that render, when the reference's own pitch is not what you want.

duration.description: Render seconds; defaults to the reference's duration.

format.description: Default "text": the diff as a compact table, and a summary in the strict sense — the arrays that table restates (`envelopeDb`, `bandsDb`, `spectralWindows`, `metricNotes`) are dropped from both metrics objects, cutting about a third off the response and more as `windows` rises. "json" returns everything whole.

tools.name: suggest_patch
tools.description: Re-aims the last compare_audio's ranked moves at the patch as it is NOW: every from/to recomputed against current values, nothing rendered. Call it AFTER applying moves, or for a `focus` (timbre/envelope/level/space) compare_audio lacks. On an unchanged patch with no `focus` it just repeats compare_audio's `diff.actions`; `basedOn.addsNothing` says so. `basedOn.stale` means `basedOn.similarity` scores the patch you replaced.

tools.name: save_preset
tools.description: Save the complete current patch under a validated name, replacing that name if present. It goes to this browser's localStorage and shows up in the preset select under `User` — no file, no folder. The result says so; `list_presets` confirms it.

tools.name: load_preset
tools.description: Load a preset into the live engine: the factory patches the UI dropdown lists, and the user presets saved to this browser's localStorage. `list_presets` names both. On a name held by both, the USER preset wins — it is the only copy of deliberate work, and save_preset followed by load_preset must return the patch just saved — and the result says a factory preset was shadowed. Pass `source: "factory"` for the built-in one by name.

source.description: Which space to load from. Omitted, a user preset of that name wins over a factory one; "factory" asks for the built-in patch by name even when a user preset shadows it.

tools.name: list_presets
tools.description: Every preset this page can load, as ONE ordered list: the 35 factory patches first, in the dropdown's own order, then this browser's user presets in the order they were saved (oldest first). Each row carries `source`, and `total`/`factory`/`user` count them. A name held by both spaces appears twice, once per source.

tools.name: delete_preset
tools.description: Delete a preset saved in this browser's localStorage. Factory presets are compiled into the page and cannot be deleted, so a factory name is refused unless a user preset shadows it — then the USER copy goes and the built-in patch is loadable again under that name. The patch on screen is never touched; only the entry in storage.

tools.name: export_preset
tools.description: Serialize a patch as the JSON a coSynth import takes back. No argument exports the LIVE patch as it sounds right now; `name` exports a stored preset instead, factory or user, on load_preset's shadowing rule. Reading is all it does: nothing is loaded and `get_synth_state`'s `patch.preset` is the same after. Returns `json`, validated on the way out, and a `filename` to suggest. No file is written; the page cannot save one.

name.description: A stored preset to export. Omit it to export the live patch.

source.description: Which space `name` is in. Only meaningful with `name`; omitted, a user preset of that name wins over a factory one.

tools.name: get_ui_targets
tools.description: Step 1 of teaching, for when someone asks how to do something themselves: find the control to point at instead of changing it for them. Returns every panel, tab, parameter, source and button by semantic ID, label, type and visibility. Pass a returned ID to show_ui_guide, or give that tool a precise CSS selector scoped to the app and its overlays.

format.description: `compact` returns every match, one `id type label` line each, in one call - no limit, no paging. `(hidden)` or `(not mounted)` is off screen; with `revealable`, the guide opens it for you. `full` (the default) returns objects, 5 per page.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring over id, label, and type; usually skip it.

limit.description: Full-format page size (default 5); `format: "compact"` needs none.

tools.name: show_ui_guide
tools.description: Step 2 of teaching: when someone asks how to do something themselves, highlight the real controls on their own screen instead of changing the patch for them or describing it in words. Up to 20 steps of interactive highlights and safe CommonMark. Returns immediately; the human uses Next/Previous/Done/Close. Never changes sound; opens the panel or tab a step's target needs, unless `reveal` is false. Replaces the active guide; `steps: []` clears it.

steps.description: Sequential steps, each with at most ONE target. Omit title and markdown for a highlight only; for an action spanning two elements, use two linked steps that name the next target.

target.description: One semantic ID from get_ui_targets, or one CSS selector matching a single element in the app or its overlays. Omit for text only; an unreachable target still shows its text, with a warning.

tools.name: get_history
tools.description: Read retained sound versions or replayable AI performances and walkthroughs. Undo skips replays. Use the returned revision with navigate_history. Earlier alternatives remain recoverable until retention eviction.

tools.name: navigate_history
tools.description: Undo, redo, or restore a retained sound version. Requires the revision from get_history; stale requests fail without restoring. Stops active performances first. Replays and alternative sound versions are preserved. Never starts audio.

tools.name: replay_history
tools.description: Play saved AI notes with the CURRENT sound, or restart a saved walkthrough at step one against the current UI. Does not restore a patch or duplicate history. Performance replay requires audio to be started.

tools.name: stop_performance
tools.description: Stop the active AI performance or history audition and wait for owned notes and recording tasks to clean up. Keeps the saved note sequence available for replay.

tools.name: scan_images_c2pa
tools.description: Scan every on the current page for C2PA Content Credentials (content provenance metadata) and return a per-image summary: whether a manifest is present, the claim generator (the tool that produced or edited the image), the title, and the signer name. Use this to find which images on a page carry provenance data. Note: provenance is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

limit.description: Maximum number of images to fetch and scan (default 25, max 100).

Provide exactly one of `selector` or `url`. Note: the signature is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

selector.description: CSS selector for an element on the page.

url.description: Same-origin image URL (absolute same-origin, or relative to the current page) to fetch and inspect. Cross-origin URLs are rejected.

query.description: Use 1–512 well-formed Unicode code points containing at least one letter or number after NFKC normalization. Punctuation alone is invalid. There is no separate word-count limit.

sites.name: elbowroom.jonathanandrei.com
sites.description: Before you buy the couch, find out whether it can get up the stairs.

tools.name: describe_staircase
tools.description: Report the measured geometry of the staircase: clear width of the run, the two widths at the turn, headroom under the soffit, and the openings. Says which figures were measured and which are still placeholders, so a verdict is never quoted as firmer than its inputs.

tools.name: list_objects
tools.description: List the things available to test against this staircase, with their real dimensions in inches. Includes the couch this house actually failed to move, and standard items such as mattresses and sheet goods whose sizes are published rather than guessed.

tools.name: get_current_object
tools.description: Report what is currently on the canvas: which object, its dimensions, where it sits and at what angle. Use this to see what the person at the keyboard has already set up before changing anything.

tools.name: check_fit
tools.description: Decide whether an object of the given dimensions fits the place on screen. For a staircase, checks the doorway, the straight run and the winder turn, choosing the best orientation and tilt. For a traced room, checks the floor outline, the ceiling and the narrowest gap between walls. Returns which stage fails and by how much. Pass raw inches; all the geometry is done here. Call describe_staircase first to see which it is.

tools.name: longest_that_fits
tools.description: For an object of a given depth, report the longest it could be and still get round the turn, and the angle at which the corner pinches. This is the number that decides whether a piece of furniture is worth buying. If a room is on screen rather than a staircase, reports the longest straight run inside its walls instead.

depth_in.description: Depth presented to the corner, in inches.

tools.name: list_unknowns
tools.description: List the measurements that are still placeholders rather than tape readings, and say why each matters. Call this before presenting a verdict as certain.

tools.name: select_object
tools.description: Put one of the catalogue objects on the canvas. The drawing updates immediately, so the person watching sees the change as you make it.

id.description: Catalogue id from list_objects.

tools.name: set_dimensions
tools.description: Put a custom object on the canvas by its measurements, for something not in the catalogue. Give raw inches straight off the tape.

label.description: What to call it on screen. Optional.

tools.name: show_pinch
tools.description: Move the object to the tightest point of the turn and leave it there. For something that does not fit, that is where it jams. For something that does, it is the worst place on the route and shows how little room is left. Use this instead of describing it.

tools.name: place_object
tools.description: Move or rotate the object on the plan by hand, in inches and degrees from the outer corner. For walking through a specific position rather than jumping to the pinch point.

x_in.description: Centre position along the lower arm, inches.

y_in.description: Centre position up the vertical arm, inches.

angle_deg.description: Rotation in degrees, 0 is along the lower arm.

tools.name: remove_door_leaf
tools.description: Take the door at the top off its hinges, or put it back. Worth about two inches of opening and it clears the swing, which is the first thing any mover tries.

removed.description: True to take it off, false to rehang.

tools.name: reset_canvas
tools.description: Put everything back to the starting state: first catalogue object, door rehung.

tools.name: record_measurement
tools.description: Write a tape reading into the staircase model, replacing a placeholder. This changes every verdict the app gives, so the person at the keyboard is asked to confirm it before it takes effect. Only use it for a figure someone has actually measured.

tools.name: try_without_feet
tools.description: Test the same object with its feet taken off, which is the cheapest way to buy width through a turn. Only offered while something is failing.

tools.name: how_short_to_fit
tools.description: Report how much shorter the object would have to be to get round the turn at its current depth. Only offered while something is failing.

tools.name: calibration_status
tools.description: Report how far the calibration has got: whether a photo is loaded, how many reference corners are clicked, the reference size, and every reading taken so far.

tools.name: set_reference_size
tools.description: Set the real width and depth of the thing being used as the calibration reference, in inches. A stair tread, a floor tile, a sheet of paper.

width_in.description: Real width of the reference, inches.

depth_in.description: Real depth of the reference, inches.

tools.name: save_reading
tools.description: File the most recent reading against one of the staircase measurements, so it can be carried over into the planner.

tools.name: send_to_planner
tools.description: Carry the measured staircase over to Elbow Room so the fit checks run against this house instead of the sample one.

tools.name: echo
tools.description: Echo a word back. Used to confirm the agent can reach this page at all.

word.description: Any word

tools.name: plain_string
tools.description: Returns a bare string rather than a content array, to find out which return shape the runtime accepts.

tools.name: get_stair_geometry
tools.description: Read the measured geometry of the basement staircase: clear width, number of winder treads, and headroom at the turn.

tools.name: check_fit
tools.description: Check whether an object of a given length and depth in inches can pass up the staircase.

depth_in.description: Depth across the side profile, inches

day.description: Day of the week

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

itemId.description: Item id, from the matching listing tool.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: get_blog_article_by_slug

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

tools.name: search_site_content
tools.description: Full-text search across the site content available here: pages, rooms, menu, faq, articles. Use it when the user asks about a topic without naming a specific page, then follow the returned ids with the matching detail tool. If count is 0, retry with a broader term before answering that nothing was found.

term.description: Search term, case-insensitive.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 two-letter language code. Defaults to the site language.

scope.description: Restrict the search to one kind of content. Default: all.

tools.name: prenota_ora
tools.description: LANGUAGE: Always reply in the same language used by the user in the prompt. Book a room at this hotel for specific dates. USE THIS TOOL whenever the user wants to make a reservation, book a room, check availability, request rates, or get a quote for specific dates - in any language. This form uses CHECKIN (arrival date) + CHECKOUT (departure date). Always submit DD/MM/YYYY format strictly. If the year is missing in user input, you MUST use the current year (2026). Ensure the resulting date is in the future. CRITICAL: each parameter value MUST be a plain string, NEVER wrapped in an object. Examples of CORRECT format: { "CHECKIN": "16/05/2026", "CHECKOUT": "22/05/2026", "NUMCAMERE": "1", "NUMADULTI": "4" }. Examples of WRONG format (do NOT use): { "CHECKIN": { "date": "16/05/2026" } }.
