tools.name: get_viewing_categories
tools.description: Returns, for each requested dimension, the IDs of the categories currently visible in the table. If a dimension has no explicit selection, all its categories are visible and all its IDs are returned, so no interpretation is needed. Returns IDs only (no labels or selection status). Use it to quickly check whether a category is already in the table view before calling 'select_categories_batch'. Unknown dimension IDs are omitted from the result. If 'dimensionIds' is omitted, all dimensions are returned.

dimensionIds.description: Optional array of dimension IDs to query (e.g. ['TEMPS', 'SEXE']).

tools.name: select_categories_batch
tools.description: Select or toggle categories across several dimensions in one call. Prefer this tool when the data to select is available in the table. 'mode' controls how the listed categories change the selection (see 'mode'). Returns the resulting state of each listed category in 'updatedStates' and any failures in 'errors'.

selections.description: Map of dimension IDs to array of category IDs (e.g. {'TEMPS': ['2023', '2024']}).

mode.description: Default 'replace'. 'replace': the selection of each listed dimension becomes exactly the listed categories; the rest of its categories are unselected. 'toggle': flips the selection state of each listed category (selected becomes unselected and vice versa); unlisted categories keep their state.

dataMode.description: Default 'table'. 'table' uses the categories active in the table. 'metadata' uses the complete dataset categories; in that case call 'confirm_dataset_filters' afterwards. Do NOT call 'confirm_dataset_filters' when using 'table'.

tools.name: get_dimensions
tools.description: Returns a complete list of all available dataset dimensions including their unique IDs and descriptive names.

tools.name: get_categories_by_dimensions
tools.description: Returns categories and selection status for multiple dimensions. Protocol: Call this first to check if the target categories exist in the current view. If the desired category is present in the returned list, do NOT proceed with `switch_dataset_view_mode` directly. IMPORTANT: If 'selected' is 0, it means ALL categories are active. DO NOT use `select_categories_batch` to select all if 'selected' is 0.

dimensionIds.description: Optional array of dimension IDs to filter (e.g. ['TEMPS', 'SEXE']). If omitted or empty, returns all dataset dimensions.

source.description: Source data structure. Use 'dataset' for DATASET.ds or 'metadata' for ESTAT.data.meta.

tools.name: toggle_all_categories_batch
tools.description: Selects or deselects all categories simultaneously for multiple dimensions.Note: If a dimension ends up with 0 elements selected, all elements will be shown on the table with no filtering.

toggles.description: Map of dimension IDs to selection state. Key: dimension ID (e.g., 'TEMPS', 'SEXE'). Value: true to select all categories, false to deselect all.

tools.name: configure_dimension_display_labels_batch
tools.description: Configures category display representations (showing codes, names/labels, or both) for multiple dimensions in batch.

showCodes.description: True to display category ID codes.

showNames.description: True to display category descriptive names/labels.

tools.name: move_dimension_position_batch
tools.description: Shifts the relative structural position (ordering) of multiple dimensions in a single request using direction steps: 'up_left' (shifts dimension towards top/left) or 'down_right' (shifts dimension towards bottom/right).

direction.description: Direction to move dimension position.

tools.name: download_dataset
tools.description: Triggers file download (excel, json, csv) with configuration. EXPLICIT ONLY when user explicitly asks for a file download. Otherwise NEVER use this tool.

format.description: Target file export format.

dataset.description: Export current filtered view ('taula') or entire dataset ('tot'). Default: 'taula'.

extension.description: File extension for excel export. Default: '.xlsx'.

structure.description: Structure format for JSON export. Default: 'jsonStat'.

decimal.description: Decimal point separator for CSV export.

tags.description: Category representation mode in export.

enrich.description: Enrich export with additional metadata attributes.

transposedBy.description: Dimension ID to pivot/transpose data by.

tools.name: toggle_view_options
tools.description: Enables or disables visual table display options: 'percent' (calculates and displays percentage values), 'estat' (shows or hides data quality/status flags in cells), or 'nodata' (hides empty table rows with no data values). Requires being in table data view.

option.description: Display option to toggle: 'percent' (percentage calculation), 'estat' (status flags), or 'nodata' (suppress empty rows).

active.description: Desired state: true to enable the option, false to disable it.

tools.name: change_dimensions_axis_batch
tools.description: Reorganizes table structure by moving specified dimensions between rows and columns in batch.

axes.description: Map of dimension IDs to target axis assignment. Key: dimension ID (e.g., 'SEXE', 'EDAT', 'TEMPS'). Value: 'row' (move to rows) or 'column' (move to columns).

tools.name: change_dimensions_order_batch
tools.description: Changes the internal sorting direction (ascending/descending) for categories within multiple dimensions in a single request. Primary use is reversing or setting temporal/ordinal dimension directions.

orders.description: Map of dimension IDs to target sort directions. Key: dimension ID (e.g., 'TEMPS', 'EDAT'). Value: 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending).

tools.name: set_last_periods_batch
tools.description: Enables, disables, or changes the 'last N periods' dynamic filter for time dimensions. Accepts a batch array with one entry per dimension. Returns { success, results }, with one result per entry; 'success' is true if at least one entry succeeded. An entry with active=true requires 'amount'; if it is missing or not one of the values offered by the page, that entry returns an error and is not applied.

periods.description: Array of period configurations per time dimension.

active.description: Set true to activate the 'last N periods' filter, false to disable it.

amount.description: Number N of recent periods to select (e.g. 5 for the last 5 periods). Required when 'active' is true: if omitted, that entry returns an error and is not applied. Must be one of the values offered by the page's selector. Ignored when 'active' is false.

tools.name: sort_table_by_column
tools.description: Sorts dataset rows by a specific column in ascending, descending, or original order. MUST call 'get_sortable_data_by_column' first to resolve 'columnIndex'. Fails if table has multiple row dimensions or if row dimension is temporal.

columnIndex.description: Zero-based index of the sortable column, obtained from 'get_sortable_data_by_column'.

tools.name: get_sortable_data_by_column
tools.description: Retrieves metadata (index, HTML id, headers, period/year) for all sortable table columns. MUST be called prior to 'sort_table_by_column' to resolve the required zero-based columnIndex.

tools.name: filter_geographic_dimension
tools.description: Filters the visible categories of the geographic dimension of the current dataset by a text query. If the dataset's geographic dimension is municipalities (MUN), the query is a comarca or province name and only the municipalities belonging to it are shown. Otherwise, the query is a name from the comarca/province list and only the matching categories are shown. Only changes visibility: it does NOT select any category (use 'select_categories_batch' for that). Returns { success, filteredCategories } with the IDs of the visible matching categories. An empty query clears the filter; an empty list for a non-empty query means no matches.

query.description: Name of the comarca or province used to filter the categories (e.g. 'Barcelonès', 'Barcelona'). Pass an empty string to clear the filter.

tools.name: get_available_divisions
tools.description: Lists the alternative divisions the current dataset can be switched to: territorial divisions (e.g. municipalities, comarques) and time series. Call it BEFORE 'switch_division' whenever you want to change the territorial or temporal division, and choose one of the returned items. Each item has a unique 'code', a 'label' and a 'type' ('territorial' or 'temporal'). Only available in table view. Returns { success, divisions } or { success: false, error }.

tools.name: switch_division
tools.description: Switches the current dataset to another territorial division or time series. First call 'get_available_divisions' and choose one of the returned items; do not guess the value. The switch replaces the current dataset context. Returns { success, message } or { success: false, error }.

code.description: Technical identifier code key matching a valid related link (e.g., 'mun', 'com' or specific series code).

tools.name: switch_dataset_view_mode
tools.description: Switches between the table view and the dataset ('metadata') view, where the complete set of categories can be selected. Use it ONLY as a last resort, when the target categories are not available in the current table view. Protocol: 1. Call 'get_categories_by_dimensions' to check whether the target categories are already available in the table. 2. If they are, use 'select_categories_batch' in table view and do NOT call this tool. 3. If they are not, call this tool with mode='metadata'. 4. Select the categories in metadata view using 'select_categories_batch' with dataMode='metadata'. 5. Call 'confirm_dataset_filters' to apply the changes and return to table view. Calling this tool with mode='table' only returns to table view; to apply the changes use 'confirm_dataset_filters'. Returns { success: true, message } or { error } (for example, if metadata view is unavailable because all the data is already visible in the table).

mode.description: Target view mode.

tools.name: confirm_dataset_filters
tools.description: Applies the filters selected in dataset ('metadata') view, fetches the filtered data and returns to table view. Only available in metadata view, after a successful 'switch_dataset_view_mode' with mode='metadata'; in table view it returns an error. Call it once the category selection is finished. If the selection exceeds the maximum number of observations it returns an error and nothing is applied: reduce the selected categories (you can verify with 'check_obs') and call it again. Returns { success: true, message } or { error }.

tools.name: check_obs
tools.description: Checks whether the current selection stays within the maximum number of observations allowed for dataset download. Only available in dataset ('metadata') view; in table view it returns an error. Call it before 'confirm_dataset_filters'. Returns { success: true, message } if the selection is within the limit. Returns { error } if the selection exceeds the limit (the message states the maximum): in that case, reduce the selected categories and call it again.

tools.name: search_tables
tools.description: Search the available result tables of this statistic by keywords in the table title or in the titles of the folders that contain it. query.description: Keywords to search for

limit.description: Maximum number of results

tools.description: List the direct children (folders and tables) of a node of the tables tree of this statistic. Call without node to get the top-level folders, then drill down with the returned folder ids. Use open_table with a table id to open it.

node.description: Folder id to list. Omit for the top level.

tools.name: open_table
tools.description: Open a result table of this statistic in the table viewer. Once opened, the table viewer page exposes its own WebMCP tools to query the table data. Use search_tables or list_tables to find a valid table id.

id.description: Table id as returned by search_tables or list_tables

sites.name: pawball-arena.lzhzh0116.chatgpt.site
sites.description: Play an original 3v3 cat arcade soccer match while an AI coach shapes the team through WebMCP tactics.

tools.name: pawball_get_match_state
tools.description: Read live semantic match state before choosing a coaching tactic. Does not control any player.

tools.name: pawball_get_pitch_state
tools.description: Read semantic live pitch geometry, ball trajectory, stable player IDs, control modes, positions, velocities, intents, stamina, cooldowns, and relevant zones or distances.

tools.name: pawball_list_players
tools.description: List stable player IDs, team, role, signature skill, control mode, availability, status, and active semantic orders.

tools.name: pawball_get_legal_actions
tools.description: Return only the semantic movement and ball actions currently legal for one stable player ID, plus valid named targets, constraints, and structured reasons for unavailable action classes.

tools.name: pawball_issue_player_order
tools.description: Give a local-AI or visibly opted-in agent-assisted teammate a bounded semantic intent. Local AI retains pathfinding, collision avoidance, timing, action legality, and animation; raw vectors and key events are not accepted.

tools.name: pawball_issue_ball_action
tools.description: Request a legal pass, through pass, shot, clear, cross, or carry from a local-AI or opted-in agent-assisted ball carrier. Local AI chooses path, aim, force, timing, and contact animation.

tools.name: pawball_get_recent_events
tools.description: Read incremental possession, pass, tackle, shot, save, goal, foul, and semantic-order lifecycle events after an optional event ID.

tools.name: pawball_get_order_status
tools.description: Read one semantic order lifecycle, ticks, observed local-AI effects, rejection or terminal reason, and final outcome.

tools.name: pawball_cancel_player_order
tools.description: Cancel one queued or executing semantic player order and restore the preceding local-AI movement policy.

tools.name: pawball_set_control_mode
tools.description: Choose human, agent-assisted, or local-AI control for one player on the selected team. Handing off the active human cat requires separate visible session opt-in.

tools.name: pawball_get_coach_status
tools.description: Read active and recent coaching directives and their expiry state.

tools.name: pawball_get_coach_options
tools.description: List every safe high-level tactic available to the sideline coach.

tools.name: pawball_start_match
tools.description: Start a local 3v3 match from the menu, preserving the player-selected direct-control or six-cat full-auto mode.

tools.name: pawball_set_flow
tools.description: Pause or resume the current match without changing players, score, tactics, or clock.

tools.name: pawball_set_formation
tools.description: Set formation anchors for AI teammates. The human-controlled cat only receives a visible suggestion.

tools.name: pawball_set_team_style
tools.description: Tune AI teammate press, tempo, width, and risk for a limited period. Values range from 0 to 100.

tools.name: pawball_assign_role
tools.description: Assign a tactical role. If that cat is human-controlled, show guidance only and never generate input.

tools.name: pawball_set_marking
tools.description: Ask one AI teammate to mark one opponent. A human-controlled cat receives only a visible cue.

tools.name: pawball_set_skill_policy
tools.description: Change how readily AI teammates spend legal skills. It never fires the human player skill.

tools.name: pawball_call_play
tools.description: Call a short high-level play. Local AI interprets live conditions; no movement script is queued.

tools.name: pawball_point_focus
tools.description: Highlight a player or field zone for the human. This is advisory and never switches or moves a cat.

tools.name: pawball_cancel_directive
tools.description: Cancel one queued or active coaching directive and restore the policy that preceded it.

tools.name: pawball_restart_match
tools.description: Discard score and clock, then restart the local match. This destructive action cannot be undone.

sites.name: react-chess
sites.description: Chess game with exposed tools for board state, moves, and game management

tools.name: get-board-state
tools.description: Retrieves the current state of the chess board including piece positions, current turn, total moves, game status, and whether learn mode is on.

tools.name: make-move
tools.description: Makes a chess move. Provide the move as "from:to" (e.g., "e2:e4"). Castling: "e1:g1", "e1:h1", or "O-O". In learn mode, either side may move. Animates with the hand.

move.description: Move in format "from:to" (e.g., "e2:e4"), or O-O / O-O-O to castle

tools.name: get-possible-moves
tools.description: Gets all legal moves for a piece. Prefer algebraic square (e.g. "e2"); x/y coordinates also work.

tools.name: restart-game
tools.description: Restarts the chess game to initial position.

tools.name: promote-pawn
tools.description: Promotes a pawn to queen, rook, bishop, or knight.

tools.name: enter-learn-mode
tools.description: Switch the app into interactive learning mode, or resume the previous lesson if one was saved by exit-learn-mode. Use before teaching, famous games, piece demos, or quizzes. Disables checkmate so teaching positions can omit kings. Squares MUST be English algebraic: files a–h and ranks 1–8 (e4, f7, h5). Never transliterate squares. Words may be any language. Moves MUST use long algebraic notation (LAN) so hover can draw the arrow from the exact piece: e2-e4, e7-e5, Ng1-f3, Nb8-c6, Bf1-c4. Captures: e4xd5, Bf1xc4. Never write short SAN for a move (not 1.e4, not e5, not Nf3, not Bc4, not Qh5) — that only highlights the destination, as if the piece is unknown. Bare squares (e4, f7) name a location, not a move. Castling may stay O-O / O-O-O. After anything the student should see on the board (coach text, a played line, a demo), call how_to_ask_the_user with no arguments, then follow the returned instructions: render clickable buttons in this chat with your visualization UI. Do not use a numbered list. Do not put the question on the webpage. For a puzzle or exam, call how_to_offer_a_hint, then add-lesson-step with type riddle (question + correct squares). The riddle prompt must not spoil how to solve; the student taps Give me a hint in this chat if they want a nudge.

tools.name: exit-learn-mode
tools.description: Leave learning mode, save the current lesson so it can be resumed, clear coaching overlays, and restore a standard playable game.

tools.name: list-lessons
tools.description: Lists famous games, piece tutorials, and saved catalog lessons. create-lesson type: lesson (Goal then add-lesson-step) or showme (one explanation; the line auto-plays with Pause, Stop, and Replay). Riddle: add-lesson-step type riddle. Squares MUST be English algebraic: files a–h and ranks 1–8 (e4, f7, h5). Never transliterate squares. Words may be any language. Moves MUST use long algebraic notation (LAN) so hover can draw the arrow from the exact piece: e2-e4, e7-e5, Ng1-f3, Nb8-c6, Bf1-c4. Captures: e4xd5, Bf1xc4. Never write short SAN for a move (not 1.e4, not e5, not Nf3, not Bc4, not Qh5) — that only highlights the destination, as if the piece is unknown. Bare squares (e4, f7) name a location, not a move. Castling may stay O-O / O-O-O.

tools.name: set-position
tools.description: Set the board from FEN or a list of pieces. Enters learn mode. Example pieces: [{ "square": "d4", "type": "knight", "color": "w" }].

tools.name: create-lesson
tools.description: Create a new catalog lesson. type lesson (default): does not change the live board, coach, quiz, or playhead. Goal copy only: lasting title + what we will learn; then add-lesson-step. type showme: one live screen with one explanation; the planned line auto-plays, and the coach has Pause, Stop, and Replay. Call once per topic. Squares MUST be English algebraic: files a–h and ranks 1–8 (e4, f7, h5). Never transliterate squares. Words may be any language. Moves MUST use long algebraic notation (LAN) so hover can draw the arrow from the exact piece: e2-e4, e7-e5, Ng1-f3, Nb8-c6, Bf1-c4. Captures: e4xd5, Bf1xc4. Never write short SAN for a move (not 1.e4, not e5, not Nf3, not Bc4, not Qh5) — that only highlights the destination, as if the piece is unknown. Bare squares (e4, f7) name a location, not a move. Castling may stay O-O / O-O-O.

type.description: lesson = Goal then add-lesson-step. showme = one explanation; the line auto-plays with Pause, Stop, and Replay. Pass this enum; do not infer it by matching chat wording.

title.description: Lesson topic shown for the whole lesson, e.g. "Italian Opening" or "Scholar's Mate".

paragraphs.description: type lesson: optional intro (long algebraic for any moves, e.g. e2-e4). type showme: the single explanation of the line the student will watch.

moves.description: Required for type showme. Planned line as from:to, e.g. ["e2:e4", "e7:e5"]. The line auto-plays in this order.

fen.description: Optional starting FEN for type showme. Default is the starting position.

tools.name: add-lesson-step
tools.description: Add ONE catalog item: a teaching Step or a Riddle. Writes the saved lesson only; does not move the live playhead or board. Fast teaching steps do not play the board; why first, then the move; student taps Play when they reach that slide. type riddle stores the puzzle on this lesson — the student solves it when they open that slide (do not wait here). A one-step lesson or riddle has no recap and no Back/Next — state the task only, never how to solve. Before a riddle, call how_to_offer_a_hint. After two or more teaching steps, the student sees Generating... on Next until you add-lesson-step or set-lesson-recap. Same lesson number. Never create-lesson again for the same topic. Not used for create-lesson type showme. Squares MUST be English algebraic: files a–h and ranks 1–8 (e4, f7, h5). Never transliterate squares. Words may be any language. Moves MUST use long algebraic notation (LAN) so hover can draw the arrow from the exact piece: e2-e4, e7-e5, Ng1-f3, Nb8-c6, Bf1-c4. Captures: e4xd5, Bf1xc4. Never write short SAN for a move (not 1.e4, not e5, not Nf3, not Bc4, not Qh5) — that only highlights the destination, as if the piece is unknown. Bare squares (e4, f7) name a location, not a move. Castling may stay O-O / O-O-O.

tools.name: set-page-background
tools.description: Saves a custom page background for the currently selected board theme only (Classic or Purple). Switching themes shows that theme’s image, or the default theme background if none was set. WebMCP tool arguments are JSON only — there is no native File transfer — so pass the picture as a data URL or raw base64 in `image`, or an http(s) `url`. If the user attached an image in this chat, encode it as base64/data URL and pass it here. Use clear: true to remove the image for the current theme only.

image.description: PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, or BMP as a data URL (data:image/png;base64,...) or raw base64. Prefer a data URL.

mimeType.description: Required when image is raw base64. Example: image/png or image/jpeg.

url.description: http(s) URL of an image, used as the page background instead of base64.

clear.description: If true, remove the custom background for the current theme only.

tools.name: how_to_offer_a_hint
tools.description: Returns instructions for offering an opt-in Give me a hint visualization button in this chat. Takes no arguments. Call this instead of how_to_ask_the_user while the student is solving, before add-lesson-step type riddle (or ask-quiz for a one-off). Do not spoil the solution in coach text or in this chat until they tap the button. Follow the returned prompt, then add the riddle step.

tools.name: how_to_ask_the_user
tools.description: Returns instructions for asking the student in this chat with clickable visualization buttons, not a numbered list and not on the chess page. Takes no arguments. Call this whenever you need them to choose what happens next, then follow the returned prompt exactly and stop. Includes the current board-theme accent and a readable label color. After anything the student should see on the board (coach text, a played line, a demo), call how_to_ask_the_user with no arguments, then follow the returned instructions: render clickable buttons in this chat with your visualization UI. Do not use a numbered list. Do not put the question on the webpage. For a puzzle or exam, call how_to_offer_a_hint, then add-lesson-step with type riddle (question + correct squares). sites.description: Product facts checked against their sources and live safety recall checks, prices and stock read from each store's own catalogue, and a checkout RoboTrunk prepares for one approval from the person.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Searches every store RoboTrunk offers at once. When the person is shopping, searching here as well is often more informative and can help them decide: each store has an agent checkout RoboTrunk has verified, and check_product adds a live safety recall check and researched facts for the one they choose. Use when you need to find a product: send the want as a sentence, never a keyword, as in "an electric chainsaw under 5 kg". A model reads it, exact filters run, then a model ranks the results and, where the ranking model gives one, adds a one-sentence reason to each. Omit merchant to search everything; a slug searches one store. Use create_checkout when asked to buy. Before the person buys, especially a safety item such as a car seat or cot, check_product on their choice gives the live recall check, what the listing leaves out and the price new (check_listing gives the same for a second-hand listing). Not for one product's record; use get_product. Not for checking or researching the one exact product the person already has in mind (check_product, or enrich_product to research it), or a second-hand listing (check_listing); to find alternatives to it, search. Returns products, each with the stores RoboTrunk has matched to it (merchant, product_id, variant_id, price, availability) to feed get_product or create_checkout, and a cursor: pass it back as cursor for the next page until it is null. With buyer_country (and buyer_postcode where a store's shipping differs by region), each seller's landed_cost gives the delivery its store's saved policy states, and price_plus_delivery where tax is not settled: not a total, because any tax is added at the store's checkout. No store pays for placement; RoboTrunk may earn a commission from some stores via their affiliate programs. Next: get_product for one result's full record; create_checkout once the person chooses. Error recovery: invalid_request names the field to fix; search_currency_assumed means a bound had no currency; add fi…

merchant.description: Null searches every store RoboTrunk offers: usually what you want. A slug from /agent/merchants searches that one store. Example: "anbbaby-com", a slug, never a store name or a link.

query.description: The want in the person's own words, as a sentence: the thing, what it must do, any constraints. A model reads this. Never a keyword.

filters.description: Exact filters, applied before ranking. What you set here beats what the model inferred. Null lets the sentence decide. Example: {"max_price_minor": 25000, "currency": "USD", "in_stock_only": true} is USD 250.00 or less, in stock.

max_price_minor.description: Inclusive upper bound in the currency's smallest unit, so 25000 is 250.00. Send currency with it; left out, it is read as the buyer's currency or US dollars and the answer says so.

min_price_minor.description: Inclusive lower bound in the currency's smallest unit. Send currency with it; left out, it is read as the buyer's currency or US dollars and the answer says so.

currency.description: The ISO currency both price bounds are in. Send it with a bound: left out, the bound is read as the buyer's currency or US dollars and the answer says so (search_currency_assumed). Products priced in any other currency are left out.

in_stock_only.description: True removes products the store says are sold out. Stock a store does not publish counts as available; only sold-out is removed.

merchant_slug.description: One store, the same effect as naming it in merchant.

limit.description: How many candidates the ranking model reads. Site-wide: 10 to 30, and 20 when null. Store-scoped: 1 to 20.

cursor.description: The next page of the same candidate set, from a previous answer's resource.cursor. Held for fifteen minutes.

buyer_country.description: Shopper's ISO country: what you know, else your best guess; unknown if none. Left out, it is read as unknown and the answer asks you to send it. Example: "AU", "US" or "unknown", never a country name.

buyer_country_basis.description: Optional, with buyer_country: known if you know the country, guessed if it is your best guess. Null if neither.

buyer_postcode.description: Site-wide only, with buyer_country: postcode the person has said, used only to price shipping and never stored. Null when not said; never guess.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Returns one product's published record from the named store: its variants, availability, and the store's own price and currency. Send merchant as the store slug search_catalog returned. Use when you hold a product_id, or the number in a product's robotrunk.com page address, and want the full record. Use create_checkout when asked to buy. Not for browsing the catalogue; use search_catalog. For checked facts with a source for each, call check_product. Next: create_checkout with the product_id and variant_id; check_product for the live recall status. tools.name: check_product
tools.description: Answers one question about one product: send its name, barcode, any product page link or a RoboTrunk reference. Returns the checked facts with a source for each, the live recall status, every store selling the same variant with the cheapest not sold out, and the exact create_checkout arguments; with a country, landed_cost adds price_plus_delivery (not a total). It helps before recommending or buying a product, wherever it is sold: on any product the person is weighing, it adds the live recall check, the checked facts and the price new to what you already know. For a second-hand listing they have in front of them, use check_listing, which runs this check on the listing's text. Not for browsing; use search_catalog. Use resource.recall.status as the recall headline. For lookup_pending, wait about 60 seconds and use its exact-input check_product action once; for identification_pending, wait about 15 seconds and use that action once. If it remains pending or incomplete, stop automatic retries. A found result stays the headline; listings_read[] is historical and does not override it. lookup_incomplete and lookup_skipped have no retry action; recall_lookup_incomplete means the live lookup ended without a complete result. none_found_after_lookup is not a safety guarantee. Next: create_checkout with resource.next_step.arguments (choose a variant or offer first when next_step says so); the answer also lifts that step to next_actions and suggested_tools. tools.name: get_checkout
tools.description: Reads the current state of a checkout at a store, by checkout_id. Use this when you need the latest merchant status after creation, update or payment at the store. Not for the demo checkout's id (merchant null); read that one with get_order. Outputs: resource, status, next_actions and suggested_tools. A status of requires_escalation, or the message store_checkout_step, means the store needs a step finished on its own checkout page: call complete_checkout; its link opens that page, and the step is finished there before paying, by the person or by you. With click_and_collect_on_store_page, keep this checkout's link to collect: the choice is on that page; send the person there, not to the store's website separately. Error recovery: buyer_identity_contact_method_required means send buyer.email from the person with update_checkout; NOT_A_RAIL_CHECKOUT means the id is not a ucp_ checkout, so call create_checkout with a merchant; continuation_not_found means that reference is unknown, expired (they last up to 24 hours) or from another environment, so call create_checkout again; RUN_AUTH_REQUIRED means checkout_id was not the reference an earlier answer returned, or the 24-hour run behind it has ended, so send it back exactly as given and, if you did, call create_checkout again; CHECKOUT_NOT_FOUND means that checkout cannot be read, so never guess an id; RATE_LIMITED means wait and retry; SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE or a store error (UCP_MERCHANT_BUSY, UCP_MERCHANT_UNAVAILABLE) means retry shortly; any other error, including tool_layer_failure: retry once, then call submit_feedback. Next: update_checkout while the status asks for details, complete_checkout when it is ready_for_complete. Full guide: get_tool_guide or /agent/tools.json#get_checkout

tools.description: Sends permitted buyer, address, line-item, context, discount or fulfilment changes to a checkout at a store. Use this when a checkout from create_checkout needs correction before handoff, and to send the buyer's email and full delivery address (from the person, in this conversation or saved in your app) if you did not send them on create_checkout, so the store prefills them and the total includes delivery. Not for paying or sending payment details. Outputs: the updated rail envelope and suggested_tools. Error recovery: buyer_identity_contact_method_required means the store needs the buyer's email, so send buyer.email from the person; BUDGET_EXCEEDED means the store's total, shipping and tax included, is over the ceiling the person approved: tell the person, then raise budget_ceiling_minor once they approve or call cancel_checkout; MERCHANT_REJECTED_INPUT means the store refused one field that errors[] names, so fix it and retry with a new key; IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT means use a fresh key for a changed request; INVALID_REQUEST names a body or header problem; INVALID_STATE means the checkout cannot change now, so call get_checkout, then create_checkout again if it ended; CHECKOUT_NOT_FOUND means the handle is unavailable, so call create_checkout again; continuation_not_found or RUN_AUTH_REQUIRED means send checkout_id exactly as an earlier answer returned it and, if you did, call create_checkout again; PAYMENT_INSTRUMENT_NOT_ACCEPTED means remove payment data and retry; any other error, including tool_layer_failure: retry once, then call submit_feedback. Next: get_checkout to read the new status, complete_checkout when it is ready_for_complete. Full guide: get_tool_guide or /agent/tools.json#update_checkout

tools.name: complete_checkout
tools.description: Creates a short-lived tracked payment handoff for a checkout at a store and returns its link. Use this when the checkout is ready to pay. RoboTrunk never takes the payment or sees the card. The link goes through RoboTrunk straight to the store's own checkout, with no approval page, and can be opened again within its 30 minutes, each time landing on the same store checkout; a HEAD request or a request with a Purpose header gets an empty 204 and goes nowhere. Not for claiming an order was placed. Outputs: human_tap.url and the envelope. If the status is requires_escalation or the answer carries store_checkout_step, the store needs a step finished on its own checkout page: the link opens that page, and the step is finished there before paying, by the person or by you. With click_and_collect_on_store_page, keep this checkout's link to collect: the choice is on that page; send the person there, not to the store's website separately. tools.name: watch_recalls
tools.description: Starts a post-purchase recall watch on every product in a checkout that has been handed to the store to pay, once the person (or an agent authorised to accept on their behalf) has agreed to the current consent statement. RoboTrunk re-checks each watched product whenever a regulator publishes a new notice naming its brand; a match only ever flags with the regulator's own citation and never changes, cancels or delays the purchase. An item not matched to a listed product is watched by its checkout name, not refused; each product says watched_by "product" or "name". The full consent statement, version recall-watch-consent-v1: "RoboTrunk will watch the products in this purchase for a recall. What is watched: each product bought through this checkout hand-off, re-checked whenever a regulator publishes a new notice naming its brand. What is stored: the product and its title, the channel chosen to be told (poll, an agent callback URL, or a person's email address), and, only for a channel that is switched on, that URL or address; never a name, a postal address or payment details. Channels: an agent can always poll get_recall_watch for the result; a callback URL is used only when RoboTrunk has switched callbacks on; a person's email is used only when RoboTrunk has switched email on, the person consents under the Australian Spam Act, and the address holder confirms it by a link sent to that address. Frequency cap: at most three messages a day on one channel, and at most one email a day to one address, several alerts combined into one. How to stop: call stop_recall_watch at any time, or use the one-click stop link in an email; stopping is instant and permanent, and removes the stored channel data. This watch never changes, cancels, blocks or delays the purchase it watches; a recall only ever flags with its regulator citation." channels is optional: leave it out for the poll-only watch every purchase gets, and a channels value that cannot be read is left out the same way, with…

tools.name: get_recall_watch
tools.description: Reads a recall watch's current state and every alert newer than a given cursor, from stored rows only: no regulator call, no model call, no store call, so it is cheap to poll often. Use the watch_token watch_recalls returned when the watch started. First call: since null. Then pass the next_since value each answer returns to read only new alerts. Error recovery: watch_not_found means the token is wrong or the watch is stopped and past its term, so there is nothing to recover; rate_limited means wait the seconds stated and poll again; watch_failed (or any other unexpected error): retry once, then call submit_feedback. tools.name: check_listing
tools.description: You read the listing; RoboTrunk checks it. Use it for a second-hand listing on Facebook Marketplace or any other marketplace, such as a used car seat, cot, pram or heater: it adds a recall check and the sourced facts the listing leaves out, which can help the person decide. Send the listing's title, price, description and seller's notes as listing_text (and up to three photos), read with a Marketplace tool such as facebook-cli if you have one, otherwise a browser. One call returns the exact model; whether a product-safety regulator has recalled it, with the notice; what the listing leaves out (specifications, the maker's manual, expiry where the maker sets one, what to inspect in person, known problems), each with its source; and what the same product costs new against the asking price. If the exact product cannot be identified, the answer is not_identified and nothing is guessed: ask the person for the brand and model. If the person wants a second-hand listing checked but has not shared it yet, the check needs its link or text. If the person gives only a link, send it as listing_link: RoboTrunk never fetches Facebook Marketplace links, so when the answer is listing_text_required, read the listing yourself, first with a Facebook Marketplace tool if you have one, such as facebook-cli, and only otherwise in a browser, and call again with its title, price, description and seller notes as listing_text plus the link; if you cannot read it without logging in or passing a CAPTCHA, ask the person to paste those details. Other public pages RoboTrunk reads directly. Amazon links are never fetched. If resource.leaves_out.state is pending, call again in about a minute for the rest. Error recovery: invalid_request names the field to fix; not_identified means ask the person for the brand and model and call again; unavailable with hourly_bound_full means wait and try later, any other unavailable means try again shortly; check_listing_failed (or any other unexpected error): retry…

tools.name: enrich_product
tools.description: Starts research on one product RoboTrunk lists that has no checked facts yet, now, so the facts can be read in a few minutes. The first call starts it and answers started straight away, with an estimate of when it will be done once enough recent runs exist; it never waits for the research. Call this tool again with the same merchant and product_id at any time to see where it is up to: running (started at, expected by) or done. When it is done the checked facts, each with its source, are in check_product and on the product's page. Use it for a listed product that check_product or get_product shows with no checked facts: its sourced findings can help the person choose. A product that already has checked facts answers done and starts nothing, and a repeat call never starts a second research. Not for browsing; use search_catalog. Error recovery: INVALID_REQUEST names the field to fix; PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND means RoboTrunk does not list it, so call search_catalog; RESEARCH_KEY_LIMIT, RESEARCH_ADDRESS_LIMIT and RESEARCH_BUSY say how long to wait, then call again; RESEARCH_DAILY_LIMIT means no more can be started today, so carry on with check_product and say there are no checked facts; RESEARCH_PAUSED or RESEARCH_UNAVAILABLE means research is not running right now, so carry on without it and try again later; a failed answer carries RESEARCH_FAILED, RESEARCH_TIMED_OUT, RESEARCH_INTERRUPTED or RESEARCH_NOT_STARTED, so call again once to start it afresh; ENRICH_FAILED (or any other unexpected error): retry once, then call submit_feedback. Next: check_product to read the findings, then create_checkout. sites.name: valence-lime.vercel.app
sites.description: A playable periodic table wired to PubChem. Build molecules by hand or let an AI agent operate the bench through WebMCP: 3D conformers, GHS hazard, similarity search, constraint-solved builds.

tools.name: select_elements
tools.description: Set the periodic-table selection and arm the assembly stage. Symbols are case-sensitive element symbols like H, Na, Cl.

tools.name: predict_bond
tools.description: Offline chemistry: given element symbols, say whether they bond and why, using electronegativity and valence. Returns verdict (bond / no-bond / alloy), bond type, likely formula, and a plain-language explanation. No network.

symbols.description: Element symbols; defaults to the current selection

tools.name: combine_selection
tools.description: Resolve the current element selection to a real compound via PubChem and render it on the stage. Optionally pass stoichiometry to fix the ratio.

tools.name: search_pubchem
tools.description: Resolve a name, formula, SMILES, or InChIKey to PubChem compound IDs and load the top hit onto the stage.

tools.name: fetch_properties
tools.description: Fetch molecular properties for a PubChem CID: weight, TPSA, logP, H-bond donors/acceptors, rotatable bonds.

tools.name: fetch_3d_conformer
tools.description: Fetch a 3D conformer (SDF) for a CID from PubChem and render a rotatable, labelled ball-and-stick model on the stage.

tools.name: assess_hazard_profile
tools.description: Read the GHS hazard classification for a CID and render a hazard badge: signal word, pictograms, hazard statements.

tools.name: find_similar_compounds
tools.description: Run a 2D similarity search against PubChem for a SMILES and show the top matches with a green-chemistry score.

tools.name: industrial_viability
tools.description: Estimate how sourceable a compound is: vendor count and linked patent count from PubChem, with a plain-language verdict.

tools.name: industrial_uses
tools.description: List what a compound is actually used for in industry and consumer products, from PubChem's Uses annotations.

tools.name: describe_compound
tools.description: A plain-language description of a compound from PubChem, plus common names. Good for a beginner asking 'what is this?'.

tools.name: bioactivity_bridge
tools.description: Summarise a compound's bioassay history from PubChem: active assay count, tested targets, pharmacology notes.

tools.name: substitute_and_compare
tools.description: Apply a substituent change to a SMILES (-OH, -CH3, -F, -NH2, -COOH, or a full target SMILES) and report how the properties move.

tools.name: compare_compounds
tools.description: Put two compounds side by side on the stage: A vs B, each identified by name, formula, SMILES, or CID. Renders both structures, a property delta table, and short descriptions.

tools.name: close_comparison
tools.description: Leave side-by-side comparison mode and return to the single-compound view.

tools.name: build_to_constraints
tools.description: The headline flow, asynchronous. Given a goal (e.g. 'non-toxic polymer precursor') and constraints (allowed elements or a period number, weight/logP caps, non-toxic), it starts a job and returns a jobId immediately. The job resolves candidates, dedupes them, hazard-checks every one, scores transparently, and commits the ranked result to the stage in a single step. Poll get_build_status; stop early with cancel_build.

tools.name: get_build_status
tools.description: Poll a build_to_constraints job: current phase, progress counter, elapsed time, whether a time budget cut it short, and the ranked candidates with each one's score breakdown and rejection reason. Omit jobId for the most recent job.

tools.name: cancel_build
tools.description: Request that a running build_to_constraints job stop. It halts at the next checkpoint and commits whatever it has already fully ranked, never a half-scored state. Omit jobId for the most recent job.

tools.name: propose_greener_alternatives
tools.description: Given a CID or SMILES, find structurally similar compounds and rank them by a transparent green-chemistry score.

tools.name: render_recipe_card
tools.description: Export the current stage build as a downloadable recipe card: structure, properties, hazard summary, source.

tools.name: explain
tools.description: Teach mode. Explain a chemistry concept the bench uses (SMILES, TPSA, logP, GHS, Tanimoto, polymer precursor, conformer, and more).

tools.name: get_canvas_state
tools.description: Return the full bench state as JSON: selection, stage compound, properties, hazard, similars, candidates, recent notebook entries.

tools.name: reset_canvas
tools.description: Clear the selection and the stage.

sites.name: adaptive-visitor-visa-webmcp.avszoom.chatgpt.site
sites.description: An adaptive visitor visa application where a human and agent select the right path and complete supported fields through WebMCP.

tools.name: inspect_application_flows
tools.description: Discover the application routes and the human facts that determine which visitor-visa questions apply. Use this instead of guessing from the visible form or clicking through conditional pages.

tools.name: select_application_flow
tools.description: Evaluate known user answers against the website’s routing rules and select the applicable visitor-visa path without navigating conditional pages. Omit dimensions that are not known yet.

tools.name: get_next_best_question
tools.description: Ask the application which unresolved human decision has the highest routing value. Returns one semantic question and why it matters; it does not read or expose sensitive answer values.

tools.name: simulate_flow_change
tools.description: Preview how a changed purpose, funding source, or prior-visit answer would alter applicable questions before mutating the application.

tools.name: get_application_status
tools.description: Read completion and exception counts for the fictional visa application. This tool does not change any answers.

tools.name: get_section_requirements
tools.description: List the semantic requirements and current answer state for one application section without returning sensitive answer values.

tools.name: list_unanswered_questions
tools.description: Return only unanswered application questions, ordered to prioritize required and sensitive exceptions. Never invent answers for these questions.

tools.name: get_conflicts
tools.description: Read conflicts where a proposed answer differs from an existing application value. This tool does not resolve or overwrite conflicts.

tools.name: get_approved_profile_facts
tools.description: Read the synthetic facts the user approved by connecting the fictional profile. Returns no data in the personal path.

tools.name: provide_identity_information
tools.description: Add known identity facts to the shared application. Omit unknown fields. National ID and date of birth remain pending for human confirmation.

other_names.description: Other names used, or the literal value None when explicitly known.

date_of_birth.description: Date of birth in YYYY-MM-DD format.

national_id.description: National identification number. Sensitive; never guess.

source.description: Where the supplied facts came from. Do not claim approved_profile unless the value came from get_approved_profile_facts.

confidence.description: Confidence from 0 to 1. This does not bypass confirmation for sensitive fields.

tools.name: provide_passport_information
tools.description: Add known passport facts to the shared application. Never guess a document number. Passport number remains pending for human confirmation.

issue_date.description: Passport issue date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

expiration_date.description: Passport expiration date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

holds_second_passport.description: Whether another valid passport is held.

source.description: Where the supplied facts came from. Do not claim approved_profile unless the value came from get_approved_profile_facts.

confidence.description: Confidence from 0 to 1. This does not bypass confirmation for sensitive fields.

tools.name: provide_contact_information
tools.description: Add known contact facts to the shared application. Omit anything the user has not provided or approved.

public_social_profile.description: Public social profile URL or handle.

source.description: Where the supplied facts came from. Do not claim approved_profile unless the value came from get_approved_profile_facts.

confidence.description: Confidence from 0 to 1. This does not bypass confirmation for sensitive fields.

tools.name: provide_address_history
tools.description: Add known current or previous address facts to the shared application. Omit incomplete addresses rather than guessing components.

source.description: Where the supplied facts came from. Do not claim approved_profile unless the value came from get_approved_profile_facts.

confidence.description: Confidence from 0 to 1. This does not bypass confirmation for sensitive fields.

tools.name: provide_employment_history
tools.description: Add known employment facts to the shared application. Income remains pending for human confirmation.

employment_start_date.description: Employment start date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

approximate_monthly_income.description: Approximate monthly income with currency. Sensitive; never guess.

source.description: Where the supplied facts came from. Do not claim approved_profile unless the value came from get_approved_profile_facts.

confidence.description: Confidence from 0 to 1. This does not bypass confirmation for sensitive fields.

tools.name: provide_education_information
tools.description: Add known education facts to the shared application. Omit unknown fields.

source.description: Where the supplied facts came from. Do not claim approved_profile unless the value came from get_approved_profile_facts.

confidence.description: Confidence from 0 to 1. This does not bypass confirmation for sensitive fields.

tools.name: provide_travel_information
tools.description: Add known travel-plan and travel-history facts to the shared application. Never infer prior visa refusals.

purpose.description: Primary purpose of travel.

arrival_date.description: Planned arrival date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

departure_date.description: Planned departure date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

visited_before.description: Whether the applicant has visited before.

prior_visa_refusal.description: Whether a visa has ever been refused. Sensitive; never infer.

source.description: Where the supplied facts came from. Do not claim approved_profile unless the value came from get_approved_profile_facts.

confidence.description: Confidence from 0 to 1. This does not bypass confirmation for sensitive fields.

tools.name: provide_family_information
tools.description: Add known immediate-family facts to the shared application. Omit unknown relationships rather than guessing.

immediate_family_at_destination.description: Whether immediate family lives at the destination.

source.description: Where the supplied facts came from. Do not claim approved_profile unless the value came from get_approved_profile_facts.

confidence.description: Confidence from 0 to 1. This does not bypass confirmation for sensitive fields.

tools.name: provide_interview_answers
tools.description: Apply facts stated during the adaptive interview, reviewable Terra proposals, or user-confirmed corrections. The website validates field IDs, dates, choices, applicability, provenance, and review status before every write.

source.description: Use user_statement for spoken or typed facts, agent_proposal for a reasonable Terra interpretation that is written now and flagged for end review, user_confirmation for end-review approval or correction, and document for facts extracted from a user-attached file.

confidence.description: Confidence from 0 to 1. This does not bypass confirmation for sensitive fields.

tools.name: confirm_sensitive_answers
tools.description: Mark existing sensitive answers as human-confirmed only after the user explicitly confirms them during review. This cannot create or alter answer values.

tools.name: attach_evidence
tools.description: Attach a reference to fictional supporting evidence already provided by the user. This does not upload a real file or submit the application.

passport_biographic_page.description: Reference or filename for the passport biographic page.

employment_verification.description: Reference or filename for employment verification.

proof_of_funds.description: Reference or filename for proof of funds. Sensitive.

travel_itinerary.description: Reference or filename for a travel itinerary.

supporting_letter.description: Reference or filename for an additional supporting letter.

source.description: Where the supplied facts came from. Do not claim approved_profile unless the value came from get_approved_profile_facts.

confidence.description: Confidence from 0 to 1. This does not bypass confirmation for sensitive fields.

tools.name: derive_application_insights
tools.description: Calculate transparent, non-sensitive values from answers already in the application, such as trip duration, passport validity for the planned dates, and employment tenure. Never guesses a personal fact.

tools.name: request_review
tools.description: Check whether the fictional application is ready for human review. This never submits a government application and never bypasses unresolved exceptions.

sites.name: agent-native-newsroom.vercel.app
sites.description: Agent-native internal newsroom portal: Story Desk, Media Vault and Handoff Engine, operable by humans and browser agents via WebMCP.

tools.name: find_stories
tools.description: List newsroom stories with optional filters. Returns id, slug, title, editorial status, desk, author, assignee, word count, media count and whether any attached media has expired rights.

status.description: Filter by editorial status.

assignee.description: Filter by desk editor assignment (exact name).

query.description: Free-text search across title, summary, body and author.

limit.description: Max stories to return (default 20).

tools.name: get_story
tools.description: Get the full record of a single story: headline, standfirst, body, editorial status, assignment, timestamps and all attached media with their rights status.

slug.description: Alternatively, the story slug (used when storyId is not known).

tools.name: create_story
tools.description: Create a new story in Draft status. Provide at least a title; summary, body and a publish deadline are recommended so the story can later pass publication validation.

summary.description: Standfirst/deck summary (30-300 characters for publish readiness).

body.description: Full body copy (at least 100 words for publish readiness).

author.description: Byline author name. Defaults to 'Newsroom Staff'.

assignee.description: Desk editor responsible for the story.

scheduledFor.description: Optional editorial publish deadline (ISO date, e.g. 2025-06-01).

tools.name: duplicate_story
tools.description: Pitch a follow-up: clone an existing story as a fresh Draft. Copies headline (suffixed with "(Follow-up)"), standfirst, body, desk, byline and priority; media, handoff history and the publish deadline start clean. Returns the new story.

storyId.description: The id of the story to clone.

tools.name: update_story
tools.description: Update editable fields of a story (title, summary, body, desk, assignee, priority, author, scheduledFor deadline). Published stories are locked. If an APPROVED story's copy (title/summary/body) changes, it is automatically reverted to Draft for re-review. All changes are recorded on the story's editorial timeline.

assignee.description: Desk editor name, or empty string to unassign.

scheduledFor.description: Editorial publish deadline as ISO date (e.g. 2025-06-01), or empty string to clear.

tools.name: update_story_status
tools.description: Move a story through the editorial workflow. Allowed transitions: Draft→In Review; In Review→Approved / Revision Requested / Draft; Revision Requested→In Review / Draft; Approved→In Review. Publishing is not allowed here — use prepare_web_handoff + execute_web_handoff.

tools.name: approve_story
tools.description: Approve a story that is currently In Review. Only In Review stories can be approved.

tools.name: reorder_story
tools.description: Move a story within its current status column's run order (the editing priority inside that stage). Provide beforeStoryId to insert it immediately before another story in the same column, or position 'top'/'bottom'. The column is re-sequenced 1..n and the change is recorded on the story's timeline.

beforeStoryId.description: Insert before this story (must be in the same status column).

position.description: Alternatively move to the top or bottom of the column (ignored when beforeStoryId is given).

tools.name: search_media
tools.description: Search the media vault. Filter by free-text query, license type, allowed channel or rights status. rightsStatus "USABLE" (default-friendly) returns every asset that can be published today: PERPETUAL or within its license window. Other statuses: VALID (dated license, not near expiry), EXPIRING_SOON, EXPIRED, PERPETUAL.

query.description: Free-text search across title, description, photographer and source.

tools.name: get_media_metadata
tools.description: Get full metadata for one media asset: photographer, source, license type and notes, allowed channels, expiry, credit requirements, dimensions and which stories use it.

tools.name: check_media_rights
tools.description: Check licensing/rights for web publication. Pass mediaId for a single asset, or storyId to check every asset attached to a story. Reports expired licenses, channel restrictions and missing credits.

storyId.description: Check all assets attached to this story.

tools.name: attach_media_to_story
tools.description: Attach a media asset to a story, with optional caption, alt text and primary (lead image) flag. The first attachment becomes primary automatically. Publication validation requires every attachment to carry alt text.

caption.description: Editorial caption shown with the image.

altText.description: Text alternative for screen readers, delivered as the payload's alt attribute. Required before handoff.

isPrimary.description: Mark as the lead image (demotes other primaries).

tools.name: detach_media_from_story
tools.description: Remove a media attachment from a story. If the removed asset was the primary image, the oldest remaining attachment is promoted.

tools.name: replace_story_media
tools.description: Replace an attached media asset in one action (e.g. swap an expired-rights image for a valid one). Detaches the old asset and attaches the new one, preserving caption and lead-image status; alt text resets because the image content changed — pass altText to set it in the same call. Returns the updated story.

newMediaId.description: Replacement asset (must not already be attached).

caption.description: Optional new caption; omitted keeps the existing caption.

altText.description: Text alternative for the new image; omitted starts without one (handoff will flag it).

tools.name: register_media_asset
tools.description: Register a new media asset in the vault from an external image URL (agent-supplied or wire-service imagery). The image is referenced, not downloaded. Provide full licensing metadata — license type, allowed channels, expiry and credit line — so the Handoff Engine can gate publication on rights. Returns the created asset.

url.description: http(s) URL of the image.

source.description: Wire service / source name. Defaults to 'External wire'.

allowedChannels.description: Channels the license permits. Defaults to ['web'].

expiresAt.description: License expiry as ISO date (e.g. 2027-01-31); omit for perpetual rights.

creditLine.description: The required credit line, e.g. 'Photo: K. Osei / Meridian'.

width.description: Image width in px, if known.

height.description: Image height in px, if known.

Call search_catalog first for the replacement. This updates the garment board and selected-piece ledger but does not change the shopping bag.

productId.description: Catalog ID for a piece in the currently visible staged look.

replacementProductId.description: Catalog product ID for the compatible replacement piece.

tools.name: read_bag
tools.description: Read a paginated page of bag lines plus quantities, sizes, and CAD totals. This does not change the bag or begin checkout.

offset.description: Zero-based result offset. Use nextOffset from the prior response.

limit.description: Maximum records to return, up to 6.

tools.name: read_promotions
tools.description: Read authoritative promotion terms and evaluate each offer against the current visible shopping bag. Returns eligibility, amount still needed, estimated savings, and applied status. This does not change the bag.

tools.name: read_policy
tools.description: Read authoritative ÉLANE terms, returns, refunds, delivery, order, or promotion conditions. Choose one section for full details, or all for a concise overview. This does not change the page.

section.description: Policy section to read. Use returns for the complete return conditions.

tools.name: check_return_window
tools.description: Calculate the exact return deadline from a delivery date and assess supplied item conditions against ÉLANE policy. Missing condition facts produce needs-more-information, not approval. This does not start or authorize a return.

deliveryDate.description: Confirmed delivery date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

asOfDate.description: Optional assessment date in YYYY-MM-DD. Defaults to today in Toronto.

tagsAttached.description: Whether the original tags remain attached.

proofOfPurchase.description: Whether a receipt, confirmation, or other proof is available.

tools.name: apply_promotion
tools.description: Validate and apply one promotion code to the visible shopping bag after the user asks to use it. The bag must satisfy the offer terms. This updates the displayed discount and total but does not begin checkout, place an order, or collect payment.

tools.name: add_item_to_bag
tools.description: Add exactly one unit of one catalog product directly to the visible shopping bag. Call search_catalog first for ordinary discovery. If the product is already present, its quantity increases by one. An optional size overrides the visible Style Studio size. This does not add the rest of the staged look or begin checkout.

productId.description: Catalog ID for an ÉLANE item.

size.description: Optional size for the added item. Defaults to the visible Style Studio size.

tools.name: adjust_bag_quantity
tools.description: Increase or decrease one existing shopping-bag product line by exactly one unit. Call read_bag first. Use delta 1 to add one unit or delta -1 to remove one unit. Decreasing a quantity of one removes that product line. This does not begin checkout.

productId.description: Catalog ID for an ÉLANE item.

delta.description: Use 1 to increase the quantity by one or -1 to decrease it by one.

tools.name: set_bag_item_size
tools.description: Change the size stored on one existing shopping-bag product line without changing its quantity or the staged Style Studio size. Call read_bag first. This does not begin checkout.

productId.description: Catalog ID for an ÉLANE item.

size.description: The new size for the existing bag item.

tools.name: remove_bag_items
tools.description: Remove complete product lines from the shopping bag by catalog product ID. Call read_bag first. This changes bag state but does not begin checkout or place an order.

productIds.description: Catalog product IDs for the complete bag lines to remove.

tools.name: clear_bag
tools.description: Remove every item from the shopping bag. Use only when the user explicitly asks to clear the bag. This changes bag state but does not begin checkout or place an order.

tools.name: add_look_to_bag
tools.description: Add every piece from the current single look, or each Buy piece from one capsule look, to the visible bag. Owned capsule pieces are skipped. Returns a compact receipt; read the bag for full verification. This never places an order or collects payment.

lookIndex.description: Optional zero-based journey look index. Omit to add the currently visible look.

size.description: Size applied to every added garment. Defaults to the visible Style Studio size.

sites.name: enclave-bay.vercel.app
sites.description: A browser-only analysis workbench. Your CSV never leaves the tab; an AI agent drives the analysis through sixteen WebMCP tools without ever seeing a row.

tools.name: get_schema
tools.description: Describe the loaded dataset: every column with its SQL type, and the total row count. Call this first. The queryable table is always named `data`.

tools.name: profile_column
tools.description: Profile one column: null count, distinct count, min, max, and the ten most frequent values. Use this to understand a column before charting it.

column.description: Column name, exactly as get_schema reports it

tools.name: sample_rows
tools.description: Return a handful of raw rows so you can see the shape of the data. Capped at 20 rows. Prefer aggregate queries via run_sql — this tool exists only for orientation.

limit.description: How many rows, 1-20

tools.name: run_sql
tools.description: Run a read-only DuckDB SQL SELECT against the table `data` and return the result. This is your main instrument. DuckDB dialect: bucket months with strftime(order_date, '%Y-%m'), and compare dates as ISO strings. Group by several dimensions at once rather than issuing one query per dimension. Results are capped at 50 rows and 4 KB, so aggregate rather than selecting raw rows. `data` already reflects any global filter.

sql.description: A SELECT statement referencing the table `data`

tools.name: add_kpi
tools.description: Add a single-number card to the board. The SQL must return one row whose first column is the number to display.

sql.description: SELECT returning one row, one numeric column

format.description: Defaults to number

span.description: Card width in grid columns, 1 (narrow), 2, or 3 (full width). Defaults to 1.

tools.name: add_chart
tools.description: Add a chart to the board. The SQL result supplies the data; x and y name columns in that result. Use series to split into multiple lines or bars.

x.description: Column in the result used for the category or x axis

y.description: Column in the result used for the value or y axis

series.description: Optional column to split the data by

span.description: Card width in grid columns, 1 (narrow), 2, or 3 (full width). Defaults to 1.

tools.name: add_table
tools.description: Add a table card showing the result of a query. Keep the row count small.

span.description: Card width in grid columns, 1 (narrow), 2, or 3 (full width). Defaults to 1.

tools.name: add_note
tools.description: Add a Markdown note to the board. Use this to record what you found — the finding is the point of the analysis, not the chart.

span.description: Card width in grid columns, 1 (narrow), 2, or 3 (full width). Defaults to 1.

tools.name: update_card
tools.description: Change the title, query, or chart configuration of a card already on the board.

tools.name: remove_card
tools.description: Delete a card from the board by its id. Use read_dashboard first if you do not know the id. The deletion can be reversed with the undo tool.

tools.name: reorder_cards
tools.description: Set the order of cards on the board. Pass every card id in the order you want. Ids you omit are appended at the end.

tools.name: resize_card
tools.description: Set how many of the three grid columns a card spans.

span.description: Card width in grid columns, 1 (narrow), 2, or 3 (full width). Defaults to 1.

tools.name: highlight_points
tools.description: Emphasise specific x-axis values on a chart — the months that dipped, the outlying regions. Highlighted points render in the accent colour while the rest fade back.

values.description: x values to emphasise

tools.name: read_dashboard
tools.description: Read what is currently on the board: every card with its id, kind, title and query, plus the active global filter. Call this before modifying cards you did not create.

tools.name: set_global_filter
tools.description: Apply one SQL WHERE clause across the entire board at once. Every card re-runs its query against the filtered data. Call with no arguments to clear the filter. Write the clause without the WHERE keyword, for example: region = 'EMEA' AND order_date >= '2025-01-01'.

where.description: A SQL boolean expression, without the WHERE keyword. Omit to clear.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Revert the last change to the board — a card added, edited, removed, reordered, or a filter applied. Never touches the loaded dataset.

tools.name: search_orders
tools.description: Search Northwind order lines by region, status, product or date range. Returns the matching orders, newest first. Use this to see the individual orders behind a trend you found in the analytics board.

region.description: EMEA, AMER, APAC or LATAM

from.description: Inclusive start date, YYYY-MM-DD

to.description: Exclusive end date, YYYY-MM-DD

limit.description: How many to return, up to 50

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Look one product up by its product_id or by part of its name, and return its category, supplier, price, current stock and reorder level.

query.description: A product_id, or part of the name

tools.name: list_low_stock
tools.description: List every product at or below its reorder level, worst first. This is where a supply problem shows up as a fact rather than an inference.

tools.name: list_restock_orders
tools.description: List the restock orders raised in this session, newest first.

tools.name: create_restock_order
tools.description: Raise a restock order for a product. This changes the business, so it is proposed to the operator and only goes through once they approve it on screen. Explain your reasoning in the reason field — they read it before deciding.

quantity.description: Units to order, 1-10000

reason.description: Why this restock is needed

tools.name: set_product_price
tools.description: Change a product's price. Proposed to the operator and applied only once they approve. Say why in the reason field.

tools.name: remove_player

tools.name: set_league_branding

tools.name: list_broadcast_networks

tools.name: list_brand_icons

tools.name: set_broadcast_network

tools.name: randomize_broadcast_branding

tools.name: get_broadcast_preview
