subscriptionId.description: Stable id of the subscription to protect or unprotect, such as streambox.

protected.description: True to prevent cancellation preparation and confirmation; false to remove protection.

tools.name: get_cancellation_run_status
tools.description: Read current reactive mission-control statuses, decisions, and progress for prepared subscription operations.

tools.name: abandon_cancellation_run
tools.description: Safely abandon or clear prepared cancellations and pending retention offers without cancelling anything. Use when the user says 'Never mind', 'Don't cancel these', 'Cancel this run', or wants to abort prepared operations.

subscriptionId.description: Optional specific subscription id to remove from the prepared run. If omitted, clears the entire run.

tools.name: reset_demo
tools.description: Reset all fictional subscriptions, protections, prepared operations, and activity history to CancelDesk's deterministic seed state. Use before an isolated demo or test run. This never affects a real subscription or external provider.

sites.name: canvasops-webmcp.vercel.app
sites.description: A collaborative architecture canvas where humans and agents configure cloud infrastructure together.

tools.name: analyze_current_architecture
tools.description: Read the complete live graph, positions, configuration, connections, cost, active-policy findings, resilience score, and architecture fingerprint. Call before modifying an unfamiliar architecture.

tools.name: get_active_policy
tools.description: Read the exact user-selected architecture policy, including its preset, monthly budget, required regions, minimum replicas, and always-on safety checks. Call before validating or proposing policy-sensitive changes.

tools.name: get_component_catalog
tools.description: Read the complete supported semantic component vocabulary and defaults. Call before designing or expanding an architecture. Use these types exactly and never invent unsupported component types.

tools.name: get_selection_context
tools.description: Read the user's current node and connection selection. Call when the user says this, selected, these nodes, or refers to the current focus.

tools.name: validate_architecture
tools.description: Deterministically validate the live architecture against budget, region, replica, connectivity, and failover policies without changing it.

tools.name: add_infrastructure_node
tools.description: Add exactly one supported semantic component from the shared catalog at deterministic coordinates. Never invent a type outside the schema. Analyze first to avoid overlap; for multi-step changes, prefer propose_architecture_plan.

tools.name: move_node
tools.description: Move one existing node to exact canvas coordinates. node_id accepts a permanent ID, short reference such as N4, or an unambiguous label.

tools.name: remove_node
tools.description: Remove one existing node and all attached edges. node_id accepts an ID, short reference, or unambiguous label. This mutation is undoable.

tools.name: connect_nodes
tools.description: Create a validated directional connection. Each endpoint accepts a permanent ID, short reference such as N4, or an unambiguous label.

tools.name: disconnect_nodes
tools.description: Remove one directional connection. Each endpoint accepts a permanent ID, short reference, or unambiguous label.

tools.name: update_node_config
tools.description: Update a node's common semantic metadata, label, technology, ownership, environment, ports, region, sizing, replicas, custom properties, and/or environment variables. node_id accepts an ID, short reference, or unambiguous label.

tools.name: group_nodes
tools.description: Create a system boundary around existing nodes. Boundaries cannot be nested. References accept permanent IDs, short references, or unambiguous labels.

tools.name: set_group_members
tools.description: Replace the complete member list of an existing system boundary. Omitted previous members are safely detached, not deleted.

tools.name: set_group_collapsed
tools.description: Collapse or expand a system boundary without deleting its members or connections.

tools.name: auto_layout_architecture
tools.description: Arrange every live node into a deterministic layer- or region-based pattern and fit the canvas.

tools.name: simulate_region_outage
tools.description: Start or recover a regional outage. Affected nodes and traffic paths are highlighted without provisioning anything.

tools.name: undo_last_change
tools.description: Revert the most recent canvas mutation as one atomic action.

tools.name: redo_last_change
tools.description: Replay the most recently undone human or agent mutation as one atomic action.

tools.name: propose_architecture_plan
tools.description: Preview a strict multi-operation architecture plan with a cost diff. The human must approve the in-page proposal before changes apply atomically.

tools.name: provision_and_pay

sites.name: haoku.app
sites.description: Haoku

tools.name: list_sources
tools.description: Lists the sources in the workspace: id, name, kind (pdf, text, image), the url pasted text came from, pages, size, and how many blocks cite each one.

tools.name: search_sources
tools.description: Finds a phrase across the PDF and text sources (or some of them) and returns hits ready to cite: source, page, occurrence, the exact passage and its surroundings.

query.description: Words to look for; case, spacing and hyphenation are ignored.

items.description: A source by id (from list_sources) or by file name.

sources.description: Restrict the search to these sources.

limit.description: Defaults to 30.

tools.name: read_source
tools.description: Returns the text of one page of a PDF, the whole text of a text source, or an image as a data URL. Quote from it to cite.

source.description: A source by id (from list_sources) or by file name.

page.description: PDF page to read. Defaults to 1.

tools.name: get_selection
tools.description: Where the user is right now: the selected block (id, type, content, markdown, citations), any text selected in the document, any text selected in an open source, which source is open, and how many passages wait in the context. Read the passages themselves with list_context.

tools.name: list_context
tools.description: The passages the user gathered from the sources, in two groups. "free" are not cited by any block yet: they are the material a new block is built from, and add_block and link_sources use them by default. "used" are already cited somewhere in the document; they are listed so you can tell them apart, and citing one again is refused. For what the document already says use get_workspace; to read a source itself use read_source.

tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: Returns the title, the sources, every block in order (id, type, excerpt or full content + markdown, citations with their footnote keys), the footnotes, which sections are covered, and — with include_markdown — the whole document as markdown.

include_content.description: Return full block content and markdown instead of excerpts. Defaults to false.

include_markdown.description: Also return the whole document as one markdown string (blocks, elements, footnotes).

tools.name: set_title
tools.description: Renames the space: the name in the top bar, the title of the printed document and the file name of an export. Short and about the subject, the way a chapter is named — the user can undo it.

title.description: The new name, e.g. "Memory in AI agents".

tools.name: add_block
tools.description: Adds a block and shows it at once. Either give "type" and "content" — heading: { text, level?: 1|2|3 (default 2) }; paragraph: { text } — markdown; write [1], [2]… in the text to mark where each citation applies (they become footnotes); callout: { title?, body (markdown), tone?: "idea"|"example"|"warning"|"why" (default "idea") }; diagram: { title?, nodes: [{ label, citation? }], edges?: [{ from, to, label? }] } — any graph: from/to by 1-based node position or label, branches and cycles allowed, laid out automatically; without edges the nodes form a chain; comparison: { title?, columns: [string], rows: [{ label, cells: [string] }] }; image: { source: an image source (id or name), caption? } — or give raw "markdown" for one block. The passages the user gathered in the context and has not used yet are cited by default (use_collected: false to leave them). Block markdown: `## heading`, free markdown paragraphs, a GFM table (first column = row labels, optional **title** line above), `![caption](space:// )`, or an element: body , {"nodes":[{"label"}],"edges":[{"from":0,"to":1}]} , Cite with [^k] marks (keys from get_workspace) or list citations and use [1], [2]….

content.description: Shape depends on type; see the tool description.

markdown.description: Raw markdown for exactly one block, instead of type + content.

position.description: Where the block goes: "end" (default), "start", { "after": block_id }, { "before": block_id } or { "in_section": heading_block_id } for the end of that section.

source.description: A source by id (from list_sources) or by file name.

page.description: Page number as printed, starting at 1. Text sources are a single page.

quote.description: A passage of the source, quoted from read_source or search_sources. Spacing, line breaks and hyphenation do not matter.

occurrence.description: Which occurrence when the quote repeats on the page. Defaults to 1.

items.description: Where a piece of content comes from. Give page and quote for PDFs and text; an image is cited by source alone.

citations.description: Passages this block draws on, in the order the [n] marks refer to. A passage another block already cites is refused: each one backs a single block.

use_collected.description: Defaults to true: the block cites the passages the user gathered in the context and has not used yet (get_selection → gathered, the ones with free: true), before any listed here, and the basket is emptied. Pass false when the block has nothing to do with them.

tools.name: update_block
tools.description: Changes a block: partial "content" (same shape as add_block for its type; fields left out stay, collections replace), or raw "markdown" for the whole block, and/or "citations" that replace the ones it has.

content.description: Same shape as add_block for the block's type; partial.

markdown.description: Raw markdown replacing the whole block (one block).

source.description: A source by id (from list_sources) or by file name.

page.description: Page number as printed, starting at 1. Text sources are a single page.

quote.description: A passage of the source, quoted from read_source or search_sources. Spacing, line breaks and hyphenation do not matter.

occurrence.description: Which occurrence when the quote repeats on the page. Defaults to 1.

items.description: Where a piece of content comes from. Give page and quote for PDFs and text; an image is cited by source alone.

tools.name: remove_block
tools.description: Deletes one or more blocks from the document. undo brings them back.

tools.name: move_block
tools.description: Moves a block to another position in the document.

position.description: Where the block goes: "end" (default), "start", { "after": block_id }, { "before": block_id } or { "in_section": heading_block_id } for the end of that section.

tools.name: focus_block
tools.description: Selects a block, scrolls the document to it and flashes it, so the user sees what you are talking about.

tools.name: open_source
tools.description: Opens a source in the viewer beside the document, at a page or at a quoted passage, which is marked.

source.description: A source by id (from list_sources) or by file name.

page.description: Page number as printed, starting at 1. Text sources are a single page.

quote.description: A passage of the source, quoted from read_source or search_sources. Spacing, line breaks and hyphenation do not matter.

tools.description: Leaves a persistent coloured wash on a quoted passage of a PDF source, with an optional note. Visible whenever that source is open.

sites.name: heliumtools.org
sites.description: Helium Tools

tools.name: list-helium-tools
tools.description: List every tool page on heliumtools.org: path, what it does, and the WebMCP tools it registers once open. Use open-helium-tool to navigate to one; its tools become available after navigation (a toolchange event fires).

tools.name: open-helium-tool
tools.description: Navigate this tab to one of the site's tool pages. After navigation the page registers its own WebMCP tools (listed by list-helium-tools) and fires toolchange — re-query the tool list, then use the page's tools.

path.description: The tool page to open.

tools.name: get-hnt-price
tools.description: Current HNT price snapshot from the heliumtools.org price API: live market price in USD (Jupiter aggregator) and the on-chain oracle price that HNT-to-Data-Credits minting pays, with timestamps. Cached server-side (~1 min freshness). For a live chain read, open /hnt-price and use get-hnt-price-instant.

tools.name: open-wallet-dashboard
tools.description: Show a wallet in the dashboard UI: balances, fleet map, rewards, IoT connectivity and traffic (per-Hotspot health, and each Hotspot's daily delivered messages per operator), Mobile activity (daily data-transfer HNT, users served, heartbeats, speedtests, bans; kept live while the page is visible), governance, and activity all load for the user to see. Like any view, the wallet is added to this browser's Recent wallets on the dashboard's lookup screen. Use the get-* tools to read the underlying data.

address.description: Solana wallet address (base58) to display.

tools.name: get-wallet-summary
tools.description: Token balances (HNT/MOBILE/IOT/SOL/DC) with USD prices, portfolio total, and fleet stats (counts by network/device type, asserted locations, regions, onboarding DC) for a wallet. Cached server-side ~60s. Onboard dates are not included — use get-wallet-onboarding.

address.description: Solana wallet address (base58). Optional when the dashboard already shows a wallet — defaults to that one.

tools.name: get-wallet-fleet
tools.description: Paged per-Hotspot list for a wallet plus fleet stats (counts by network/device type, asserted locations, regions, onboarding DC). Each row: name, entityKey, assetId, network(s), deviceType, location (H3 cell) with city/state/country, elevation (m), gain (tenths of a dBi), and dcOnboardingFeePaid. On-chain metadata only — for onboard dates use get-wallet-onboarding; for IoT connectivity and traffic, get-wallet-iot-status; for Mobile activity, get-wallet-mobile-activity; for rewards, get-wallet-rewards. Sorted by entityKey; use offset/limit and pagination.nextOffset to retrieve the full fleet. Stats cover the entire fleet.

address.description: Solana wallet address (base58). Optional when the dashboard already shows a wallet — defaults to that one.

offset.description: Start at this offset; use pagination.nextOffset for the next page.

limit.description: Maximum Hotspots on this page.

tools.name: get-wallet-rewards
tools.description: Pending (unclaimed) Hotspot rewards for one page of a wallet's fleet as decimal token amounts (e.g. "12.345678" IOT), totaled per token and listed per Hotspot where nonzero. Served from a ~15min cache — rewards distribute roughly daily. Sorted by entityKey. Totals cover only this page (aggregateScope: page); use offset/limit and pagination.nextOffset for the rest. Up to 100 Hotspots per page; claim via the /hotspot-claimer page's tools.

address.description: Solana wallet address (base58). Optional when the dashboard already shows a wallet — defaults to that one.

offset.description: Start at this offset; use pagination.nextOffset for the next page.

limit.description: Maximum Hotspots on this page.

tools.name: get-wallet-onboarding
tools.description: When a wallet's Hotspots were onboarded, read from chain (block time of the first successful transaction on each Hotspot's IoT/Mobile info account): first and latest date, a per-month count (UTC), and per-Hotspot ISO dates (a Hotspot on both networks shows the earlier one; null = couldn't be determined). Hotspots from before Helium's April 2023 move to Solana show their migration date, not their original deployment. Sorted by entityKey. Dates, first/latest and monthly counts cover only this page (aggregateScope: page); use offset/limit and pagination.nextOffset for the rest. Up to 200 Hotspots per page; dates are cached server-side once resolved, so a first lookup of a large fleet is the slow one.

address.description: Solana wallet address (base58). Optional when the dashboard already shows a wallet — defaults to that one.

offset.description: Start at this offset; use pagination.nextOffset for the next page.

limit.description: Maximum Hotspots on this page.

tools.name: get-wallet-iot-status
tools.description: Per-Hotspot IoT connectivity and 30-day delivered LoRaWAN messages for a wallet's IoT Hotspots. Connectivity is a per-UTC-day verdict (active = connected to the Helium Packet Router on the latest reported day), not online-now. Health combines the two: inactiveTraffic (not connected, but had messages in the window — check these first), activeQuiet (connected, no messages in 30 days), inactiveQuiet, activeTraffic. Page membership follows entityKey before health filtering, so pages hold still when the dashboard's scan finishes; rows run most actionable first within a page. To triage, pass health to list matching rows within each page. Pagination always counts all IoT Hotspots, including nonmatches: follow pagination.nextOffset even when hotspots is empty. Use offset/limit to retrieve all pages. Uses the dashboard's finished scan when that wallet is on screen (whole-fleet counts, same as the UI); otherwise looks up at most 200 IoT Hotspots per page. aggregateScope identifies whether counts/health/traffic cover the fleet (dashboard) or only this page (own scan). For one Hotspot's daily messages per OUI (operator), use get-iot-hotspot-traffic.

address.description: Solana wallet address (base58). Optional when the dashboard already shows a wallet — defaults to that one.

health.description: List only rows in this health state within each entityKey page. Pagination still counts every IoT Hotspot; continue with nextOffset even when no rows match. counts and health cover the whole fleet with dashboard data, or the scanned page otherwise.

offset.description: Start at this offset; use pagination.nextOffset for the next page.

limit.description: Maximum Hotspots on this page.

tools.name: get-iot-hotspot-traffic
tools.description: One IoT Hotspot's delivered LoRaWAN messages per day and per OUI (the routing ID of a LoRaWAN Network Server operator) over the 30-day window, with operator names from Helium's well-known OUI list. One Hotspot per call — triage a wallet with get-wallet-iot-status first. `daily[].byOui` maps OUI id → messages that UTC day; `quietNetworkWide: true` means that OUI delivered nowhere on the network in the last 7 days (an operator-side drop, not this Hotspot's); `recentShare` is the last 7 days' daily average ÷ the 30-day daily average (null when it can't be stated honestly).

entityKey.description: The IoT Hotspot's entity key (its Helium public key, base58) — the entityKey from get-wallet-iot-status or get-wallet-fleet.

tools.name: get-wallet-mobile-activity
tools.description: Recent Mobile network activity for a wallet's Mobile Hotspots: data-transfer HNT per UTC day for the last 7 days published (with that day's HNT price and the rewarded bytes it paid for), users served on the latest usage day, ban status, and for WiFi indoor/outdoor Hotspots the heartbeats and rejected heartbeats in a 60-minute window (location trust, distance from the asserted location, reported positions) and the latest speedtest average in a 24-hour window. A window ends now while its data is fresh, otherwise at its last successful check (windows gives each end); null means unknown, never 0. Issues, most serious first: banned (latest ban record is a ban), then WiFi health signals that don't change data-transfer HNT: noHeartbeat (none in the heartbeat window), lowTrust (latest location trust below 1), lowSpeedtest (latest speedtest multiplier below 1), rejectedHeartbeats (any in the window). counts, rewards and usage cover every Mobile Hotspot (a count is null while its data isn't in). hotspots is paged: membership follows entityKey, so pages hold still between calls, and rows run most actionable first within a page; to triage across the fleet, pass issue (counts say how many have each). Use offset/limit and pagination.nextOffset (default 50, max 200); with issue set, the matching set follows live data and can change between calls. When the wallet is on screen, reads the dashboard's own data with no extra downloads (waiting up to 45 s for its first check), unless that tab is hidden and last checked over 5 minutes ago. Otherwise runs one check itself (up to 60 s, then returns what it has), reading Helium's public Mobile network data files whole: roughly 25 MB for a fleet of data-only Hotspots and 55 MB with WiFi Hotspots when this browser hasn't read them recently, and little once it has, since the files serve every wallet and share the dashboard's cache. Mobile Hotspots with ecc_compact keys (CBRS radios) aren't covered. For IoT Hotspots use get-wallet-iot-status.

address.description: Solana wallet address (base58). Optional when the dashboard already shows a wallet — defaults to that one.

offset.description: Start at this offset; use pagination.nextOffset for the next page.

issue.description: List only Mobile Hotspots with this issue. counts still cover every Mobile Hotspot.

limit.description: Maximum Hotspots on this page; rows run most actionable first within it.

tools.name: get-wallet-transactions
tools.description: Categorized recent transactions for a wallet (rewards claims, transfers, Hotspot ops). Pass `before` (a transaction signature from a previous page) to paginate.

address.description: Solana wallet address (base58). Optional when the dashboard already shows a wallet — defaults to that one.

limit.description: Max transactions to return.

before.description: Paginate: only transactions before this signature.

tools.name: list-ouis
tools.description: Catalog of every OUI (organization) on the Helium IoT network: OUI number, owner, payer, escrow account, and delegate keys.

tools.name: get-oui-balance
tools.description: Data Credit escrow balance, burn rates (1-day and 30-day), and estimated days remaining for an OUI. Also shows the lookup (with its balance chart) in the page UI.

tools.name: prefill-alert-subscription
tools.description: Fill in the low-escrow alert form (OUI, email, optional label and webhook URL) for the user to review and submit. Does not subscribe by itself — the user must click Subscribe, and email verification follows. Alerts fire at 14, 7, and 1 days of escrow remaining.

label.description: Optional label for this subscription.

webhook_url.description: Optional HTTPS webhook to call alongside the email.

tools.name: get-dc-mint-quote
tools.description: Convert between HNT, Data Credits, and USD at the on-chain oracle price the DC mint actually pays (conservative ema − 2×conf, not the headline spot). Pass exactly one of hnt_amount, dc_amount, or usd_amount; returns all three plus the price used. 1 DC is always $0.00001 (100,000 DC per USD); the HNT side floats.

usd_amount.description: USD value of Data Credits wanted.

tools.name: resolve-oui
tools.description: Resolve a Data Credit delegation target — an OUI number or a payer key — to its escrow account, payer, and current escrow DC balance. Use before delegating DC to an OUI.

target.description: An OUI number (e.g. "12") or a payer key (base58).

tools.name: get-iot-onboard-fees
tools.description: Current on-chain fees for onboarding a Helium IoT Hotspot, in Data Credits: full (PoC-eligible) vs data-only onboard fees and the location assert fee. Cached ~6h server-side.

tools.name: get-mobile-onboard-fees
tools.description: Current on-chain fees for onboarding a WiFi network as a Helium Mobile data-only Hotspot, in Data Credits: onboard fee plus location assert fee. Cached ~6h server-side.

tools.name: open-mobile-onboard-tab
tools.description: Switch the Mobile WiFi Onboarding page between its tabs: 'onboard' (the wizard), 'manage' (already-onboarded networks), or 'guide' (per-vendor router setup instructions).

tab.description: Tab to show.

tools.description: Read the current mission, layout mode, visible sections and product groups, the entity the person has selected, cart totals, and the state version. Read-only: nothing on the page changes.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Find catalog products by text, purpose, price ceiling, delivery ceiling, or minimum warmth, ranked by the current sort. Read-only: use it to obtain product ids before calling a write tool.

query.description: Free text matched against name, description, and category.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Read the cart lines, subtotal, item count, remaining mission budget, and any constraint warnings. Read-only.

tools.name: set_mission
tools.description: Record what the person is trying to accomplish and reorganise the store around it. Budget, deadline, party size, and priorities are parsed into visible, editable chips. Reversible page state changes; no order is placed.

mission.description: The outcome in the person's own words, including any budget and deadline.

applyMissionView.description: Whether to switch the page into Mission View immediately.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional. The state version the caller believes the page is at. The action is refused if the page has moved on.

tools.name: apply_mission_view
tools.description: Switch the page to Mission View: group products into Essential, Useful, and Optional by mission fit and optionally hide promotional sections. Reversible.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional. The state version the caller believes the page is at. The action is refused if the page has moved on.

tools.name: organize_products
tools.description: Regroup and re-sort the visible catalog using approved layout modes only. Does not change catalog or cart data. Reversible.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional. The state version the caller believes the page is at. The action is refused if the page has moved on.

tools.name: set_card_presentation
tools.description: Change how product cards are presented: their shape, how many sit per row, how loudly the price reads, how large the imagery is, which facts appear on the card face, and whether descriptions show. Choose a named preset, individual settings, or both. Only the store's own designs are available — no markup, styles, or sizes can be supplied. Reversible layout-only change.

preset.description: A coherent starting design. "dense-decision" for comparing many options, "visual-browse" for imagery, "price-first" when budget is the question, "default" to return to the standard cards.

columns.description: Cards per row. "auto" follows the responsive default; list layout is always one.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional. The state version the caller believes the page is at. The action is refused if the page has moved on.

tools.description: Show or hide known page sections and product groups. Protected regions stay visible and hidden sections remain recoverable. Reversible layout-only change.

items.description: A known page section or product group id. Free-form selectors are not accepted.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional. The state version the caller believes the page is at. The action is refused if the page has moved on.

tools.name: move_section
tools.description: Move one known section before or after another. Page sections move among page sections; product groups move among product groups. Reversible.

sectionId.description: A known page section or product group id. Free-form selectors are not accepted.

anchorSectionId.description: A known page section or product group id. Free-form selectors are not accepted.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional. The state version the caller believes the page is at. The action is refused if the page has moved on.

tools.description: Set what the word "this" refers to on the page — a product, a section, a mission constraint, or a panel. Draws the same visible selection outline a click would.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional. The state version the caller believes the page is at. The action is refused if the page has moved on.

items.description: A catalog product id.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional. The state version the caller believes the page is at. The action is refused if the page has moved on.

tools.name: set_reference_product
tools.description: Pin one product as the reference that alternatives are measured against. Reversible.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional. The state version the caller believes the page is at. The action is refused if the page has moved on.

tools.name: exit_comparison
tools.description: Leave Comparison View and restore the previous layout. Reversible.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional. The state version the caller believes the page is at. The action is refused if the page has moved on.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add one to four known catalog products to the visible fictional cart, with bounded quantities and an optional short reason. This changes cart state and is reversible. It does not place an order.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional. The state version the caller believes the page is at. The action is refused if the page has moved on.

tools.name: update_cart_quantity
tools.description: Set the quantity of one cart line, or remove it by setting the quantity to zero. Reversible; does not place an order.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional. The state version the caller believes the page is at. The action is refused if the page has moved on.

tools.name: undo_last_action
tools.description: Restore the most recent reversible layout, comparison, or cart snapshot. Whoever made the change, human or agent, it is undone the same way.

tools.name: reset_experience
tools.description: Return mission, layout, selection, comparison, cart, and checkout to the seeded Browse View. Ask the person before calling this: it discards their work.

confirmed.description: Set to true only after the person has agreed to discard the current session.

tools.name: open_cart
tools.description: Bring the cart drawer on screen so the person can see the kit, its line items, and the running total — or close it again. This only moves the drawer: it changes no cart contents and places no order.

open.description: True to show the cart, false to close it.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional. The state version the caller believes the page is at. The action is refused if the page has moved on.

tools.name: preview_checkout
tools.description: Validate the cart against stock, budget, and delivery constraints and open the visible review surface. Returns a confirmation token. No order is created.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional. The state version the caller believes the page is at. The action is refused if the page has moved on.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional. The state version the caller believes the page is at. The action is refused if the page has moved on.

sites.name: koshara.vercel.app
sites.description: Koshara

tools.name: check_transactions
tools.description: Validate and check a batch of proposed Koshara transactions without creating them. Use this for statement imports instead of validating transactions one by one. Checks account/category validity, required fields, review metadata, and possible duplicates. Categorize the batch yourself using one list_categories call; this tool does not infer categories.

amount.description: Positive amount in INR.

tools.name: get_import_context
tools.description: Return the accounts, categories, recent transaction reference data, and active staged import in one call. Use this once before preparing a statement so you can reuse existing finance structures and identify possible duplicates.

tools.name: create_import_session
tools.description: Create a temporary statement import workspace. This does not add anything to Transactions. Reuse the returned session ID when staging rows or proposing groups.

tools.name: stage_transactions
tools.description: Add a prepared transaction batch to a temporary import session for human review. This never creates live Koshara Transactions; uncertain and duplicate rows are excluded by default.

amount.description: Positive amount in INR.

tools.name: update_import_item
tools.description: Adjust one staged row without creating a live transaction. Use it to improve the proposed description, account, category, note, or skip decision. Suspected duplicate overrides remain a human-only action in the Statements review UI.

tools.name: group_import_items
tools.description: Propose that two or more statement rows represent one logical expense, such as EMI principal, interest, and tax. The group remains a suggestion until the human chooses Merge or Keep separate in Koshara.

tools.name: get_import_session
tools.description: Return the current staged rows, review statuses, duplicate references, and proposed groups for one import session. This is read-only.

tools.name: get_accounts
tools.description: Returns available Koshara accounts. When importing a statement, call this once and map all transactions to the appropriate existing account. Do not invent or silently create an account when the correct account is uncertain.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: Returns all existing Koshara categories, including optional monthlyBudget values in INR. When processing multiple transactions, call this once and use the returned category list to categorize the entire batch. Prefer existing categories and avoid creating new ones unnecessarily; use Uncategorized with needs_review when genuinely uncertain.

tools.name: search_transactions
tools.description: Search Koshara transactions using the same live data shown in the Transactions UI. Use this to inspect existing activity before importing or answering finance questions.

query.description: Matched against description and notes.

from.description: Inclusive YYYY-MM-DD date.

to.description: Inclusive YYYY-MM-DD date.

amount.description: Exact amount in INR.

tools.name: get_spending_summary
tools.description: Return structured expense and category facts from Koshara for a date range, optionally filtered by account or category. Includes budgets and variance, transaction counts, review and uncategorized totals, six-month category trends, top merchants, recurring payments, and exact possible-duplicate groups. Use these facts for external reasoning; Koshara does not generate AI insights.

from.description: Inclusive YYYY-MM-DD date. Defaults to the start of the current month.

to.description: Inclusive YYYY-MM-DD date. Defaults to today.

tools.name: configure_cashflow_chart
tools.description: Update the currently visible Dashboard cash-flow chart after analyzing Koshara data with read-only finance tools. This changes temporary presentation state only and never changes transactions, accounts, categories, or budgets. Use an insightTitle to summarize the finding, comparison to show change over time, and highlights to identify responsible dates or categories.

mode.description: Visible cash-flow series.

from.description: Inclusive start date.

to.description: Inclusive end date.

accountIds.description: Existing account IDs to include. Empty or omitted includes every account.

categoryIds.description: Existing category IDs to include. Empty or omitted includes every category.

comparePreviousPeriod.description: Overlay the immediately preceding period of equal duration.

highlightedDates.description: Dates to emphasize on the chart.

highlightedCategoryIds.description: Existing category IDs to emphasize as drivers.

insightTitle.description: Short agent-generated title explaining the chart insight.

tools.name: configure_category_spending_chart
tools.description: Update the currently visible Dashboard spending-by-category pie chart after analyzing Koshara data with read-only finance tools. This changes temporary presentation state only and never changes transactions, categories, or budgets.

from.description: Inclusive start date.

to.description: Inclusive end date.

accountIds.description: Existing account IDs to include. Empty or omitted includes every account.

categoryIds.description: Existing category IDs to include. Empty or omitted includes every spending category.

highlightedCategoryIds.description: Existing category IDs to emphasize in the pie chart.

insightTitle.description: Short agent-generated title explaining the category insight.

tools.name: create_account
tools.description: Create a Koshara account only when the user explicitly requested or confirmed that new account. Do not create accounts automatically while interpreting a statement.

tools.name: update_account
tools.description: Update selected fields on an existing Koshara account. Omitted fields remain unchanged.

tools.name: delete_account
tools.description: Permanently delete an account and all transactions assigned to it. Only call this after the user explicitly requests deletion and understands the returned transaction count will also be removed.

tools.name: get_transaction
tools.description: Get one Koshara transaction by its exact ID, including review metadata and resolved account/category names.

tools.name: create_transaction
tools.description: Create one transaction in the live Koshara store. Use create_transactions instead for statement imports. Do not silently guess an uncertain account or category: ask the user, or follow their instruction by using a suitable fallback such as Uncategorized and reviewStatus needs_review.

tools.name: update_transaction
tools.description: Update selected fields on an existing transaction. Use reviewStatus confirmed after uncertainty has been resolved; omitted fields remain unchanged.

tools.name: delete_transaction
tools.description: Permanently delete one transaction. Only call this after the user explicitly asks to delete that exact transaction.

sites.name: listen-synth.netlify.app
sites.description: A Web Audio synthesizer your AI agent can actually listen to — analyze its own output in real time, then shape the sound with you, in natural language. Accessible sound design for everyone.

tools.name: get_current_patch
tools.description: Get the full current synthesizer patch: every oscillator, filter, envelope, LFO and FX setting. Call this before changing anything so you know the starting point.

tools.name: analyze_sound
tools.description: LISTEN to the synth's live output. Runs real-time FFT + time-domain analysis and returns structured audio features (brightness, bass/mid/high balance, harmonicity, envelope, movement) plus a plain-language summary. Best called WHILE a note is playing — use play_note first, then listen, then adjust.

tools.name: set_params
tools.description: Change MANY synth parameters in ONE call (the whole point: coordinated sound design). Provide a flat map of param paths to values. Paths: oscA/oscB.{wave,octave,detune,level}, sub.level, filter.{cutoff,resonance,envAmount}, env.{attack,decay,sustain,release}, lfo.{wave,rate,toCutoff,toPitch}, fx.{delayTime,delayFeedback,delayMix,reverbMix}, master. Waves: sawtooth,square,triangle,sine.

params.description: Flat map of param path → value, e.g. {"filter.cutoff": 800, "env.attack": 0.002}

tools.name: shape_sound
tools.description: Translate a natural-language sound goal into coordinated synth moves. Understands words like: darker, brighter, warmer, thicker, thinner, glassy, punchier, smoother, wobblier, womp, spacier, drier, 80s, aggressive, airy, pluckier. Use this when the user describes a vibe rather than exact parameters.

description.description: e.g. 'darker and thicker but keep the punch', or 'glassy 80s pad'

tools.name: play_note
tools.description: Play a single note. Accepts a MIDI number (60 = middle C) or a note name like 'C4', 'A2', 'F#3'. Hold it long enough to analyze the sound.

note.description: MIDI number (e.g. 60) or name (e.g. 'C4').

durationMs.description: How long to hold, ms (default 900). Longer is better for analysis.

tools.name: play_chord
tools.description: Play a chord (strummed). Provide 2-5 notes as MIDI numbers or names, or a chord name like 'Cmaj7', 'Am', 'G7'.

tools.name: describe_current_sound
tools.description: Get a producer's description of the current patch WITHOUT needing audio — derived from the parameter values themselves. Useful when audio isn't playing.

tools.name: save_preset
tools.description: Save the current sound as a named preset. The preset AUTOMATICALLY becomes a new agent tool (load_preset__ ) that you or the user can call later. This is dynamic tool registration in action.

name.description: A short name, e.g. 'dark_pluck' or 'Glass Pad'

tools.name: list_presets
tools.description: List all available presets (built-in + user-saved) and which are currently exposed as tools.

tools.name: randomize_patch
tools.description: Randomize the patch within a musical vibe for inspiration. Great starting point for a sound-hunt.

tools.name: watch_for_changes
tools.description: Ask what the HUMAN has changed by hand since a given time (or since your last tool call). Returns which knobs they turned, old→new values, so you can respond to their intent — the heart of two-way collaboration. Call this before big moves, or when the user says 'what did I just do?'.

sinceMs.description: Unix ms timestamp. Omit to use the time of the last analyze_sound call.

tools.name: compare_to_target
tools.description: Score how close the CURRENT sound is to a described target (e.g. 'dark, thick, punchy'), and suggest the single next best move. Use this to iterate toward a vibe with the user: analyze → compare → adjust → repeat.

target.description: Target description, e.g. 'dark and punchy' or 'bright glassy pad'

tools.name: explain_sound_in_plain_words
tools.description: Explain the current sound in everyday, non-technical language — for users who don't know synthesis or who use a screen reader. Returns a friendly paragraph plus per-knob plain descriptions. Use this to make sound design accessible to everyone.

tools.name: compose_pattern
tools.description: Compose a musical loop (bassline / arp / pad / lead) that fits the CURRENT sound you designed. You provide the vibe; this builds a 16-step-per-bar pattern and loads it. Then play_pattern to hear it, and render_to_wav to export it. Call after you're happy with the sound.

tools.name: play_pattern
tools.description: Play the currently composed pattern as a loop through the synth. Stop with stop_pattern.

tools.name: stop_pattern
tools.description: Stop the looping pattern.

tools.name: render_to_wav
tools.description: BOUNCE the current sound + composed pattern to a downloadable WAV file (44.1kHz stereo 16-bit). This produces a real audio artifact the user keeps. Call after composing a pattern and confirming the sound with analyze_sound.

bars.description: 1-16 bars to render (default: the pattern's length)

name.description: File name base, e.g. 'dark-techno-bass' (default from vibe)

tools.name: generate_sound_card
tools.description: Generate a 'Sound DNA' card: a shareable PNG that captures what you (the agent) HEARD — your own descriptive words, the waveform, spectrum, and the full patch recipe. A reproducible artifact of the sound. Call after analyze_sound.

vibe.description: Short descriptor; defaults to your analyze_sound summary

tools.name: export_vital_preset
tools.description: Export the CURRENT sound as a production-ready VITAL preset (.vital) — the free, most popular Serum alternative — that producers can load straight into their DAW. The sound you designed together becomes a real studio instrument, not just a browser demo. Use after the sound is finalized.

style.description: Optional style tag, e.g. 'bass', 'pad', 'lead'

tools.name: describe_capabilities
tools.description: Explain what this agent-native synth lets humans and agents do together, and the recommended listen-adjust loop.

sites.name: masil-webmcp.vercel.app
sites.description: MASIL

tools.name: masil_get_capabilities
tools.description: Read MASIL's versioned activities, workflows, valid actions, and person-control boundaries. Use for capability questions or a genuinely unknown workflow—not before a direct request that already matches a named tool. MASIL is a provider and visual projection, never a second Agent.

tools.name: masil_get_session_state
tools.description: Read the exact visible scene, revision, and currently valid next actions when the current scene is ambiguous. A successful action result already confirms its own completed state.

tools.name: masil_get_execution_log
tools.description: Read sanitized, timed semantic invocations and revisions when the person asks for history or a state mismatch needs diagnosis. Successful action results already confirm visible completion.

tools.name: masil_set_language
tools.description: Switch MASIL's visible interface between Korean and English without changing calligraphy text.

tools.name: masil_set_webmcp_panel
tools.description: Open or close the visible WebMCP inspector and select history or tools. Activity state is unchanged.

tools.name: masil_project_agent_presence
tools.description: Project a real phase of the same user Agent into the Orb and a short caption. Never send audio, transcripts, token deltas, private memory, or inferred emotion.

tools.name: masil_go_home
tools.description: Return home and discard current in-memory activity state. Requires personConfirmed=true for this exact loss.

tools.name: masil_open_activity
tools.description: First call from home: open the requested calligraphy or Janggi space. For calligraphy, include suggestions only when the person asks for ideas or has not named what to write. A later spoken choice is exact authored text: preserve its script and wording (for example 쉼 stays 쉼, not 休) unless the person explicitly asks for translation or Hanja. If they already named text, omit suggestions, then generate and place the resolved exact text with masil_set_calligraphy_reference; a suggestion is not a finished reference. For Janggi, open first and then read the board. Camera and moves are separate actions.

character.description: Candidate text shown exactly as the person may choose it. Do not silently replace Hangul with Hanja or Hanja with Hangul.

tools.name: masil_set_calligraphy_reference
tools.description: Place the person's resolved exact 1-4 character text. Preserve their latest script and wording: 쉼 stays 쉼. Convert only when explicitly requested: '무병장수를 한자로' is 無病長壽 and '추석 한자로' is 秋夕. Generator text, character, image, caption, and alt must agree. Submit each newly generated image here once; never pre-reject or regenerate it from its URL, filename, or metadata. MASIL is the pixel-validation authority. Only after an actual REFERENCE_IMAGE_* rejection, regenerate with that exact defect and resubmit. Success means the reference is visible, not that drawing input is active: tell the person what is visible and leave the next input choice to them. Start camera only on explicit request; use the stop tool only for an active camera request.

character.description: Exact text visible on the reference. Preserve the person's chosen script; translate to Hanja only when explicitly requested.

referenceImageUrl.description: PNG/WebP data URL, same-origin URL, or CORS-readable HTTPS URL meeting the 3:2 real-alpha black-ink contract. JPEG, filesystem/blob paths, opaque backgrounds, and checkerboards fail.

tools.name: masil_start_calligraphy_camera
tools.description: Start camera-first air writing only after this explicit person request. Native browser permission remains human-controlled; denial falls back to direct drawing. Never infer consent.

tools.name: masil_stop_calligraphy_camera
tools.description: Honor an explicit no-camera or stop-camera request and enter direct touch/pointer writing while preserving the reference and strokes. Use after placing the reference even when camera never started. Never call without the person's explicit preference.

tools.name: masil_clear_calligraphy
tools.description: Clear only human-authored strokes and preserve the already-visible generated reference. Preconditions: the exact reference is visibly placed and the person explicitly asked to clear their strokes. Call once with personConfirmed=true; do not reopen calligraphy, replace the reference, or clear anything else.

tools.name: masil_get_janggi_state
tools.description: Open Janggi first, then read its exact turn, position, coordinates, and legal destinations. Reading is not a visible preview: if the person asks where a piece can go, follow with one masil_move_janggi_piece preview and wait for their choice. Acknowledge a returned Cho lastMove before an explicitly requested Han reply. MASIL is the rules authority.

tools.name: masil_wait_for_person_janggi_move
tools.description: After opening Janggi, wait for one Cho board gesture only when the person said they will move directly. The result is their validated visible move. Reply with exactly one Han move only when explicitly requested, then acknowledge both moves. Never wait for future speech.

tools.name: masil_move_janggi_piece
tools.description: After reading state, submit one rules-authoritative action. To show where a piece can go, call preview with one legal destination, actor=person, personConfirmed=false; listing coordinates is not a visible preview. For a requested move, submit the person's exact destination with actor=person and personConfirmed=true, including an apparently illegal request so MASIL can reject it without substitution. Never play Han after a person move unless they explicitly requested an immediate reply; then use actor=agent once and acknowledge their move before naming yours. Move success resolves after visible animation.

action.description: preview must be called to show one legal route on the visible board and does not change turn; move commits one exact move; pass/reset are consequential and require the person's explicit request.

actor.description: person plays Cho; the calling Agent plays Han.

pieceId.description: Stable piece id returned by masil_get_janggi_state.

spokenMove.description: Short person phrase or Agent reply description for the visible log.

personConfirmed.description: Required on every call. True only for the person's exact confirmed move, pass, or reset; false for preview and Agent actions.

tools.name: masil_open_support_note
tools.description: Open a private no-action support note only after explicit request. Silence, mood, or activity is never consent.

tools.name: masil_prepare_support_review
tools.description: Prepare the minimum disclosure and local-demo route for person review. This creates no request.

tools.name: masil_create_local_handoff
tools.description: Create an in-memory demo handoff only after two confirmations at the exact visible revision. Nothing is sent externally.

tools.name: masil_get_handoff_status
tools.description: Read the local owner, status, callback time, and next step.

tools.name: masil_return_to_activity
tools.description: Return to the exact preserved activity without deleting the handoff result.

sites.name: meal-planner-llai.onrender.com
sites.description: Plan meals, save recipes and build shopping lists with WebMCP.

tools.name: meal_context
tools.description: Read the user's structured meal-planning context for a date range in one call: saved recipe summaries, pantry inventory, planned meals, and the calculated shopping list. Use this before proposing or revising a meal plan so you respect what the user has already saved and planned.

tools.name: list_recipes
tools.description: Find recipes in the user's saved recipe memory. Search matches recipe names, tags, and ingredient names. Use returned recipe IDs for planning meals or retrieving scaled ingredient quantities.

query.description: Optional text to match against recipe names, tags, and ingredients

tags.description: Optional tags that every returned recipe must have

max_total_minutes.description: Optional maximum prep plus cook time in minutes

tools.name: get_recipe
tools.description: Get one saved recipe with exact ingredients, quantities, units, instructions, times, tags, and timestamps. Optionally scale all numeric ingredient quantities to a different serving count.

servings.description: Optional target servings; null keeps the recipe's base servings

tools.name: save_recipe
tools.description: Create or update a recipe in durable browser storage. Store structured servings, prep/cook time, ingredient quantities and units, tags, and ordered cooking instructions. Pass id only when updating an existing recipe.

id.description: Existing recipe ID when updating; omit for a new recipe

tags.description: Short descriptive tags such as quick, vegetarian, high-protein

quantity.description: Numeric amount. Use null when the recipe says 'to taste' or otherwise gives no number.

unit.description: Unit such as g, ml, tbsp, tsp, cup, item, or an empty string when unitless

tools.name: delete_recipe
tools.description: Delete a saved recipe and remove any meal-plan entries that refer to it.

tools.name: get_meal_plan
tools.description: Read planned breakfasts, lunches, and dinners in a date range. Results include recipe names, servings, tags, and cooking times, which makes prior weeks available as durable meal-plan history.

tools.name: plan_meal
tools.description: Create or replace one meal-plan slot for a date. The website immediately updates and remembers the selection.

tools.name: plan_meals
tools.description: Plan or replace multiple meal slots atomically enough for a weekly planning workflow. Prefer this over many plan_meal calls when the user approves several meals at once.

tools.name: remove_meal
tools.description: Remove a breakfast, lunch, or dinner from a specific date while preserving all other meal-plan history.

tools.name: list_pantry
tools.description: Read the user's pantry inventory with exact quantities and units. Use it before shopping-list or use-what-I-have planning tasks.

tools.name: set_pantry_item
tools.description: Create or replace the available quantity of a pantry ingredient. Set quantity to zero to remove the matching ingredient and unit from the pantry.

quantity.description: Quantity currently available

unit.description: Unit; use the same unit as recipes when possible

tools.name: build_shopping_list
tools.description: Calculate an exact shopping list from planned meals in a date range. Recipe quantities are scaled to planned servings, combined by normalized ingredient and unit, and can be reduced by matching pantry quantities.

subtract_pantry.description: Whether to subtract matching pantry quantities; normally true

tools.name: export_meal_data
tools.description: Return a complete JSON-safe snapshot of the user's locally stored recipes, meal-plan history, pantry inventory, and timestamps for backup or agent-side analysis.

tools.name: shopping_price_context
tools.description: Read the user's explicitly saved shopping location, preferred stores, current shopping-list quantities, existing price estimates and saved unexpired price quotes. Use this before researching grocery prices or promotions.

tools.name: set_shopping_profile
tools.description: Save the location and preferred stores that the user explicitly wants used for grocery pricing. This is optional and stored only in this browser.

location.description: User-provided city, suburb, region or country; empty string clears it

preferred_stores.description: Optional retailer names the user prefers

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code such as ZAR, USD or GBP

tools.name: save_price_quotes
tools.description: Save current grocery price quotes or promotions for shopping-list ingredients after researching the user's chosen location. Package size is required so the page can estimate actual packages that must be purchased rather than only ingredient consumption cost.

ingredient.description: Ingredient name exactly as it appears in the shopping list when possible

package_quantity.description: Amount contained in one purchasable package

package_unit.description: Package unit such as g, kg, ml, l, item, each or an empty string

price.description: Current price for one package in the shopping profile currency

location.description: Location the quote applies to; normally the saved shopping location

promotion.description: Optional promotion text; empty string when not promotional

valid_until.description: Optional YYYY-MM-DD promotion/quote expiry date; empty string when unknown

tools.name: priced_shopping_list
tools.description: Return the current shopping list with package-aware estimated purchase cost per ingredient, store/deal details, coverage and estimated basket total using saved unexpired quotes.

tools.name: clear_price_quotes
tools.description: Clear saved grocery prices and promotions without changing the user's recipes, pantry, meal plan or shopping location.

tools.name: import_meal_data
tools.description: Replace the current browser-local recipes, meal-plan history and pantry with a previously exported Meal Planner version 1 snapshot. Validate all recipe references, meal slots, quantities and pantry records before replacing state. Shopping location and saved price quotes are not changed.

data.description: Complete object previously returned by export_meal_data

tools.name: set_shopping_currency
tools.description: Set the ISO 4217 currency used for grocery prices. Infer this from the user's explicitly saved shopping location before researching or saving prices. For example use USD for the United States, MGA for Madagascar, ZAR for South Africa, GBP for the United Kingdom, and JPY for Japan. Do not infer or request device geolocation; use only the location saved in shopping_price_context.

currency.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code appropriate to the saved shopping location

sites.name: muster-fire-drill.vercel.app

tools.description: Route one clear training intent through the bounded plan, people, equipment, and review specialists on this page.

tools.name: read_plan
tools.description: Read the selected fictional building plan, roles, occupants, exits, and revision. No external effects.

tools.name: start_drill
tools.description: Start the fictional tabletop exercise on this page. Does not alarm, call, dispatch, or control a building.

tools.name: send_inject

tools.name: record_action
tools.description: Record one facilitator-confirmed team action and owner in the exercise log.

tools.name: check_coverage

tools.name: stage_report

tools.name: inspect_zone
tools.description: Highlight one fictional floor zone and read its fixture occupancy, assistance count, and nearest plan exit.

tools.name: compare_routes

tools.name: analyze_route_sketch
tools.description: Measure a facilitator-drawn path against this fictional plan and flag whether its endpoint reaches an available exit.

tools.name: read_drill_guide
tools.description: Read the fictional exercise checklist for before, during, or after the drill. Not live emergency guidance.

tools.name: read_hazard
tools.description: Read the current scripted hazard snapshot. This is not a physical fire-spread prediction or live sensor feed.

tools.name: read_floor_register

tools.name: read_site_context

tools.name: read_equipment
tools.description: Read planned equipment; optional item_id and 3d view locate a marker. Never activates an alarm or certifies equipment.

tools.name: read_lessons

tools.name: record_human_signal
tools.description: Record a facilitator-observed participant signal. Never infer personality, intent, emotion, or competence.

tools.name: prepare_team_handoff
tools.description: Preview one fictional responder assignment between F07 rooms. Shows the path and checks on the live page. Does not move a marker or record completion; only the human Confirm assignment button can accept it.

sites.name: negativezero.com
sites.description: Negative Zero deploys an agent swarm that finds and mitigates exposures before they can be weaponised. UK cybersecurity, Cyber Essentials certification body, AI assurance and forward-deployed…

tools.name: list_events
tools.description: Lists Negative Zero events (hackathons, briefings, webcasts) with start time, location, audience, who may register ("registration": open | code-required | customers-and-prospects | invitation-only) and a link. Defaults to upcoming events; pass scope "past" or "all" for history. Read-only; nothing is recorded. Use this instead of scraping /events; register with register_event_interest where registration is not invitation-only.

scope.description: Which events to return. Default "upcoming".

tools.name: list_news
tools.description: Lists Negative Zero news posts and research/resource articles (title, summary, date, tags, URL), newest first. Filter by type ("news" or "research") or a tag, and optionally only items published since a date. Read-only. Follow up with get_article for the full text.

type.description: Default "all".

tag.description: Case-insensitive tag filter, e.g. "Cyber Essentials".

since.description: YYYY-MM-DD; only items on or after this date.

limit.description: Default 20.

tools.name: get_article
tools.description: Returns the full text of one Negative Zero news post or resource article as Markdown, with title, date, tags and canonical URL. Use the id from list_news (it is the last path segment of the article URL). Read-only.

id.description: Article id / slug, e.g. "what-is-cyber-essentials".

tools.name: get_ce_question_set
tools.description: Returns Negative Zero's 12-question Cyber Essentials readiness check as structured data (question id, control area, question text, the exact answer options, and the assessor note), plus how it is scored and links to the official IASME/NCSC question set documents. Use it to walk a user through the check, then call assess_ce_readiness with their answers. Read-only.

set.description: Only "nz-readiness" is available as data. Official documents are returned as links.

tools.name: assess_ce_readiness
tools.description: Scores answers to Negative Zero's 12-question Cyber Essentials readiness check and returns a per-area status (Ready for review / Needs review / Likely blocker), the scope verdict, and what to fix first. Answers are matched to the exact option labels from get_ce_question_set; the status is derived here, never trusted from the caller. No email, no CRM record, nothing stored — this is the try-before-you-share-details step. Read-only.

answers.description: Map of question id → chosen option label (case-insensitive), e.g. { "scope-cloud": "Yes, all included" }. Partial answer sets are scored, with unanswered ids listed.

tools.name: estimate_ce_plus_price
tools.description: Returns Negative Zero's indicative Cyber Essentials Plus certification price for an organisation size band, instantly and without collecting any details: the list price and the discounted price available when the quote is requested through this site's agent tools (10% off, launch offer). Give either the orgSize band label or an employee count. Read-only; nothing is recorded. The formal, binding quote is a separate step.

employees.description: Alternative to orgSize: total headcount; the band is derived.

tools.name: get_trust_center_summary
tools.description: Returns Negative Zero's public security posture as structured data for vendor reviews, procurement questionnaires and audits: certifications and their status, vulnerability disclosure policy and contact, which documents are NDA-gated and how to request them, and privacy/data-handling facts. Only what the public Trust Center states; nothing gated is described. Read-only.

topic.description: Narrow the response. Default "all".

tools.name: explain_ce_control
tools.description: Asks Negative Zero's Cyber Essentials readiness agent (grounded in the NCSC Requirements for IT Infrastructure v3.3 and IASME guidance) to explain a control area or answer a specific Cyber Essentials question in plain English, optionally for the user's situation. Returns the answer text. Uses assessor-safe language; never a pass/fail verdict. The exchange is retained for 30 days for quality and abuse monitoring — do not include passwords, credentials or IP addresses. Rate-limited per connection.

question.description: What to explain or answer.

area.description: Optional control area to focus on.

context.description: Optional one-line description of the user's organisation or setup (no secrets).

tools.name: check_request_status

Returns the current stage (received / processing / in progress / completed / closed) and what to do next. No personal data is returned. Read-only; references expire 90 days after submission.

tools.name: gap_analysis_from_estate
tools.description: Turns what you know about the user's IT estate into a Cyber Essentials gap analysis: which of the five control areas (and scope) are ready for review, need review or are likely blockers, the requirement behind each gap, the evidence an assessor will ask for, and the fix. Give a structured `estate` description and/or explicit `answers` to the 12 readiness questions (answers win over estate-derived values); anything not covered is listed as not assessed with the question to ask. Deterministic and read-only; nothing is stored. Set narrative:true for a short plain-English summary from the Cyber Essentials agent (that one exchange is retained 30 days).

estate.description: Structured facts about the user's estate. Only set what is known; omit unknowns.

cloudServicesInScope.description: Will all cloud services be included in scope?

softwareFirewallsEnforced.description: Host firewall enforced on laptops/desktops used outside the office.

defaultCredentialsChanged.description: Default passwords changed and unnecessary services disabled on internet-facing devices, routers and firewalls.

answers.description: Optional explicit answers: question id → option label (see get_ce_question_set). These override estate-derived values.

tools.name: answer_security_questionnaire
tools.description: Answers standard vendor-security / procurement questionnaire items about Negative Zero using only what the public Trust Center and privacy notice state — certifications, penetration testing, vulnerability disclosure, sub-processors and data locations, international transfers, retention, AI use, cookies, bot protection, UK GDPR. Each answer carries its source page and whether the underlying document is NDA-gated (request via request_trust_center_access). Items the site does not publish are returned as 'not published' with the route to ask — never guessed. Read-only; nothing is stored.

tools.name: get_meeting_booking_link
tools.description: Returns the self-service booking link for a 20-minute call with Negative Zero's lead assessor (scoping a Cyber Essentials / Cyber Essentials Plus assessment, or discussing a platform demo), with guidance on when to use it versus the request tools. sites.name: nexusops-nu.vercel.app
sites.description: A WebMCP-powered IT operations platform for investigating production incidents with AI agent collaboration

tools.name: get_active_incidents
tools.description: List active production incidents requiring operator attention. Call this first to discover what is currently broken before investigating a specific incident. Read-only; safe to call at any time.

tools.name: get_incident
tools.description: Retrieve the current state of a specific incident: severity, status, affected service and symptoms. Use this to confirm incident details before further investigation. Read-only; safe to call at any time.

tools.name: get_services
tools.description: List all services and their current health status. Use this to see the broader service landscape and confirm which services are healthy vs. degraded. Read-only; safe to call at any time.

tools.name: get_incident_evidence
tools.description: Return the consolidated metrics, logs, timeline, deployment and prior-finding evidence already gathered for an incident in one call. Use this to get a single evidence snapshot instead of calling multiple observation tools individually. Read-only; safe to call at any time.

tools.name: get_service_health
tools.description: Retrieve a service's current health signals: status, latency, error rate, request rate, CPU and memory. Use this to quickly assess whether a service is under resource pressure. Read-only; safe to call at any time.

tools.name: get_dependencies
tools.description: Retrieve a service's dependency graph and the health of each dependency. Use this to check whether a failure is isolated to one service or part of a broader dependency chain. Read-only; safe to call at any time.

tools.name: get_deployment_history
tools.description: Retrieve recent deployments for a service, including what changed and when. Use this to check whether a recent release could explain a regression. Read-only; safe to call at any time.

tools.name: get_metrics
tools.description: Retrieve a time series of a service's telemetry: latency, request rate, error rate, CPU, memory and database connections. Use this to quantify how severe a degradation is. Read-only; safe to call at any time.

tools.name: get_logs
tools.description: Retrieve structured application logs for a service. Use this to find the specific error or timeout events that explain elevated metrics. Read-only; safe to call at any time.

tools.name: get_incident_timeline
tools.description: Retrieve the chronological sequence of events leading up to an incident. Use this to establish whether a deployment or other change preceded the incident. Read-only; safe to call at any time.

tools.name: compare_metrics
tools.description: Compare an incident's current telemetry against its prior healthy baseline and return the delta for each metric. Use this to measure how far a service has drifted from normal. Read-only; safe to call at any time.

tools.name: correlate_events
tools.description: Cross-reference deployment events, telemetry changes, log signals and incident timing into one correlation summary. Use this after gathering individual evidence to look for a consistent causal pattern. Read-only; safe to call at any time.

tools.name: run_diagnostic
tools.description: Run a structured diagnostic comparing a service's current telemetry, deployments and logs against baseline, returning a diagnosis, confidence and recommended next step. Use this as a final cross-check before proposing remediation. Read-only: it never executes remediation.

tools.name: create_investigation_finding
tools.description: Store a human-readable investigation finding for operator review. Use this to persist a conclusion so a human can audit how it was reached. Mutating but low-risk: it only appends to the investigation record and cannot affect production.

finding.description: Investigation finding to store for operator review.

tools.name: propose_remediation
tools.description: Generate a specific, evidence-based mitigation recommendation (target action, rationale, risk) for a human to review. Use this once a root cause is established. Read-only: it proposes an action but never executes anything and always requires human approval first.

tools.name: approve_remediation
tools.description: Record an explicit human operator approval for a specific remediation action on a specific incident. This tool represents a human decision, not an agent decision, and is the only way execute_remediation can subsequently succeed.

tools.name: execute_remediation
tools.description: Execute a previously proposed, simulated remediation action (e.g. a rollback). Mutating and high-risk: this call is rejected unless a matching approve_remediation call was already recorded for the same incident and action. Never call this without confirmed human approval.

approved.description: Must be true and must match recorded human approval.

tools.name: verify_remediation
tools.description: Verify whether a service has actually recovered after remediation, based on its real current status and metrics. Use this after execute_remediation; it reports no recovery if remediation hasn't run yet. Read-only; safe to call at any time.

tools.name: verify_incident
tools.description: Verify the current state of an incident (open vs. resolved) based on real service status. Use this to check overall incident closure independent of any specific remediation. Read-only; safe to call at any time.

tools.name: get_agent_activity
tools.description: Read the live audit trail of every tool invocation made so far: agent, tool, arguments, duration and success. Use this to review what has already been investigated or executed before duplicating work. Read-only; safe to call at any time.

tools.name: add_rect

tools.name: set_fill

sites.name: origami-webmcp.onrender.com
sites.description: An agent-native origami studio. A person folds a sheet of virtual paper in 3D while an AI agent reads the real crease and layer state through WebMCP tools and folds alongside them.

tools.name: get_sheet
tools.description: Summary of the paper on the stage: how many flat regions it has, how many folds have been applied, how deep the layer stack is, whether it is turned over, and how many creases are foldable now. Returns counts, not geometry.

tools.name: list_creases
tools.description: Every crease that can be folded from the current state, with its id, a short label, its endpoints in sheet coordinates, and how many flat regions the fold would move. Only these ids are accepted by fold_crease.

tools.name: describe_sheet
tools.description: The current state in plain sentences, suitable for reading aloud to the person. Same text the canvas exposes as its accessible description.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: The authored catalogue: each model's id, name, difficulty, and step count. These are simple-fold models; the engine does not do reverse or petal folds, so no crane is offered.

tools.name: get_active_model
tools.description: Which model is selected, how many of its steps the sheet has completed, and whether the sheet is still on its sequence.

tools.name: get_next_step
tools.description: The next authored step for the active model, naming the crease id, the fold type, and a short note. Fails when no model is selected or the sheet has left the sequence.

tools.name: check_progress
tools.description: Whether the sheet matches the expected state for the active model. Progress is measured by replaying the model and comparing geometry, so a fold the person made by hand is reported honestly rather than assumed away.

tools.name: get_fold_history
tools.description: Applied sheet changes in order, including folds and whole-model flips, each tagged person or agent. Returns at most the newest ten plus total and truncation counts; undone changes are excluded.

tools.name: get_view
tools.description: The shared camera as azimuth degrees, elevation degrees, and zoom factor. The person and the agent drive the same view.

tools.name: get_tool_activity
tools.description: Recent tool calls this page recorded, newest last, each tagged with its origin. Entries include text supplied by the caller.

tools.name: fold_crease
tools.description: Fold the sheet along one currently legal crease. Refuses any id outside the legal set and names the legal ids in the refusal. Returns the resulting sheet summary.

crease_id.description: Crease id from list_creases, for example diag-a.

type.description: valley folds the flap up and over, mountain tucks it under.

tools.name: advance_step
tools.description: Perform the next authored step of the active model. Fails when no model is selected, when the model is complete, or when the sheet has left the sequence. It never silently corrects the sheet.

tools.name: undo_fold
tools.description: Step back one change in the action history, whether a fold or whole-model flip. The person can always take over, so undo is available to both of you.

tools.name: redo_fold
tools.description: Reapply the most recently undone fold or whole-model flip, when one exists.

tools.name: reset_sheet
tools.description: Discard all folds and return to a fresh square. Past three folds this requires confirm true, so a casual call cannot wipe the person's work.

confirm.description: Must be true to discard more than three folds.

tools.name: flip_sheet
tools.description: Turn the whole model over, the diagram instruction that usually loses people. Layer order and face colours invert with it.

tools.name: select_model
tools.description: Set the active target from the authored catalogue. Does not fold anything on its own; use advance_step to walk the sequence.

model_id.description: Model id from list_models, for example blintz.

tools.name: highlight_crease
tools.description: Make one crease pulse in the scene so the person can see which flap you mean. This is how you point at the answer instead of describing it.

tools.name: clear_highlight
tools.description: Remove any crease highlight from the scene.

tools.name: set_view
tools.description: Orbit and zoom the shared camera so the person sees what you are working on. Omitted values stay as they are.

elevation.description: Vertical angle in degrees, 15 to 85. The sheet is flat, so lower is not useful.

zoom.description: Zoom factor, 0.5 to 2.2. The camera already frames the sheet.

sites.name: ownerspec.com
sites.description: Independent specs, sizing and part-compatibility answers for home equipment. No vendor owns the numbers here.

tools.name: scan_images_c2pa
tools.description: Scan every on the current page for C2PA Content Credentials (content provenance metadata) and return a per-image summary: whether a manifest is present, the claim generator (the tool that produced or edited the image), the title, and the signer name. Use this to find which images on a page carry provenance data. Note: provenance is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

limit.description: Maximum number of images to fetch and scan (default 25, max 100).

tools.name: inspect_image_c2pa
tools.description: Fetch a single image (by CSS selector or URL) and return its fully decoded C2PA manifest store: every manifest's claim, assertions (e.g. c2pa.actions edit history, schema.org authorship), and the COSE signature details (algorithm and signing-certificate identity). Provide exactly one of `selector` or `url`. Note: the signature is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

selector.description: CSS selector for an element on the page.

url.description: Same-origin image URL (absolute same-origin, or relative to the current page) to fetch and inspect. Cross-origin URLs are rejected.

tools.name: ownerspec_read_page
tools.description: Returns the current page (or another ownerspec.com page path) as Markdown, with front matter giving the canonical URL, title and the date its facts were last verified. Cite the canonical URL.

path.description: Page path such as /water/guides/iron-in-well-water/. Defaults to the current page.

tools.name: ownerspec_get_quick_answer
