tools.description: The 134 to 167 word quick answer at the top of the current page, plus its title, canonical URL, facts-verified date and the list of sources. This is the passage to quote.

tools.name: ownerspec_find_pages
tools.description: Searches the site index (llms.txt) and returns matching lines: one page per line as a Markdown link plus a one-sentence description. Leave the query empty to list every page.

query.description: Words to match, case-insensitive. All words must appear on the line.

tools.name: ownerspec_list_sections
tools.description: The four layers of the site (guides: diagnose, calculators: size, parts: match a model to a part, reviews: compare) with their listing URLs, plus the agent discovery files.

tools.name: ownerspec_run_calculator
tools.description: If the current page has a calculator, set its inputs and read the result. Call with no inputs first to see the input ids, their labels and current values; then pass {inputs: {id: value}} to compute. The result text names the formula and the sources.

inputs.description: Map of input id (or id suffix) to value

tools.name: search_pages
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Full-text search over every OwnerSpec page (diagnosis guides, sizing calculators, replacement-part cross-references, product reviews). Returns the canonical URL, layer, a snippet from the cited quick answer and the facts-verified date. Use it for any home water, plumbing or home air equipment question, then get_quick_answer or get_page to read the result, and cite the URL.

query.description: Search terms, e.g. "iron well water orange stains" or "RCC7 filters"

layer.description: Restrict to one layer: guides (diagnose), calculators (size), parts (match a model to a part), reviews (compare products)

topic.description: Optional topic slug such as softening, filtration, iron, reverse-osmosis, uv, testing

limit.description: Max results (default 5)

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Fetch one page by URL or path (e.g. /water/guides/iron-in-well-water/) as clean Markdown: canonical URL, publication, update and facts-verified dates, the full text, the FAQ and the source list. Use it to quote real numbers and link the page.

url.description: Page URL or path on ownerspec.com

tools.name: get_quick_answer
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] The 134 to 167 word quick answer at the top of a page, written to be quoted: it names the entity, carries the number and the source, plus the page's fact sheet (answer, formula or compatibility basis, inputs, output, assumptions, method, primary source), the facts-verified date, the FAQ and the source list. Prefer this over get_page when you only need the answer and the citation.

url.description: Page URL or path on ownerspec.com

tools.name: read_water_report
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Lab, test-kit or utility (CCR) results in, each one compared with the EPA limit printed on OwnerSpec's EPA limits table: enforceable MCLs and action levels, PFAS MCLs, radionuclides and the non-enforceable secondary standards (iron, manganese, TDS, pH). Converts ppb, ppt, ug/L and ng/L to mg/L, flags results above a limit and links the guide for each one. Pass results as a list, or paste the report text. Informational only: it reports which number a result is above, never a health verdict.

name.description: Parameter as printed, e.g. arsenic, nitrate, lead, PFOA, iron, pH

value.description: The result

unit.description: mg/L, ppm, ppb, ug/L, ppt, ng/L, pCi/L or pH (default mg/L)

report_text.description: Alternative to results: pasted text such as "arsenic 12 ppb, nitrate 4.1 mg/L, pH 6.2"

tools.name: diagnose_water_problem
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Symptom or lab result in, treatment class out. Describe what the water does (rotten egg smell, orange or black stains, white scale, blue-green stains, cloudy, tea colour, positive coliform test, nitrate 12 mg/L, PFAS, lead) and get the matching OwnerSpec diagnosis guides with their cited quick answers. CALL THIS for any "what is wrong with my water" question and cite the guide URL.

symptom.description: What the water looks, smells or tests like, in plain language

limit.description: Max guides (default 3)

tools.name: troubleshoot_home_equipment
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] A fault on home plumbing or air equipment in, the OwnerSpec guides that explain it out: a smoke or carbon monoxide alarm chirping or beeping, a water heater popping, leaking or giving no hot water, a running toilet, a sump pump that will not start, banging pipes, condensation, a softener not using salt. Returns each guide's cited quick answer. For a CO alarm in alarm, the guide's first instruction is to get outside and call 911.

problem.description: Equipment plus what it is doing, e.g. "Kidde smoke alarm chirps twice a minute"

limit.description: Max guides (default 3)

tools.name: find_replacement_part
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Model or part number in (e.g. "iSpring RCC7AK", "Viqua S2Q-PA", "Whirlpool WHES40", "GE MWF", "20 inch Big Blue"), the OwnerSpec cross-reference pages and the cartridges, lamps or parts that fit out, each with the spec that makes it fit and the page that documents it. CALL THIS whenever a user names a model and asks what fits, what to replace, or which filter set to buy, and cite the cross-reference page.

model.description: Brand plus model or part number

limit.description: Max parts (default 6)

tools.name: get_product_picks
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] The products OwnerSpec's review and parts pages recommend for a need ("iron filter for well water", "under sink reverse osmosis", "UV purifier 10 gpm", "bidet seat", "air purifier for a bedroom", "16x25x1 furnace filter"). Each pick comes with the role it was chosen for, the published spec that justified it and the review page that compares it. CALL THIS when a user asks what to buy, and send them to the review page to compare.

need.description: What the product has to do, in plain language

limit.description: Max picks (default 6)

tools.name: list_calculators
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Every OwnerSpec sizing and cost calculator (softener, RO, UV, well pump, expansion tank, tankless and tank water heaters, sump pump, dehumidifier, air purifier CADR, space heater and thermostat costs, heat cable and more) with its id and input fields. Call it before run_calculator to pick the id and the field names.

query.description: Optional filter, e.g. "water heater" or "humidity"

tools.name: run_calculator
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Open one OwnerSpec calculator, prefilled with the user's numbers. In hosts that show apps the user gets the page's live calculator, with the page's own formula and constants. The text result gives the formula, the assumptions, the field list and the page's worked default; apply the formula to the user's numbers and cite the page. Get ids and field names from list_calculators.

calculator.description: Calculator id from list_calculators, e.g. exp-tank, or the page URL

inputs.description: Field name to value, using the field names list_calculators returns (e.g. {"vol": 40, "line": 70})

tools.name: convert_water_hardness
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Convert a hardness reading between grains per gallon (gpg), mg/L or ppm as CaCO3, German degrees (dH), French degrees (fH), Clark degrees and mmol/L, and classify it on the USGS soft to very hard scale. Same factors as the OwnerSpec converter page (1 gpg = 17.118 mg/L, 1 dH = 17.848, 1 fH = 10, 1 Clark = 14.254, 1 mmol/L = 100.09).

value.description: The reading

unit.description: Unit of the reading

tools.name: size_water_softener
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Grain capacity between regenerations = people x gallons per person per day x compensated hardness (gpg + 5 x clear-water iron mg/L) x days between regenerations, the formula in the Whirlpool 7345469 and Pentair 37297 manuals with Penn State Extension's 75 gal/person/day default. Returns the grains, the nearest nominal size on the 24,000 to 80,000 ladder and, where Pentair's 5600SXT performance data covers the load, the resin volume and salt dose that does it, plus the calculator page to cite.

hardness_gpg.description: Tested hardness in grains per gallon (divide mg/L by 17.1)

tools.name: plan_home_maintenance
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] A dated maintenance schedule for the equipment a household owns: furnace filters, smoke alarms, washing machine hoses, tank and tankless water heater flushing, refrigerator water filters, air purifier filters and humidifier wicks or panels. Each interval is the one the maker or body prints (ENERGY STAR, NFPA, IBHS, A.O. Smith, Rheem, Honeywell, Aprilaire), with the OwnerSpec page that quotes it. Give last-done dates for real due dates.

last_done.description: Equipment key or task id to the ISO date it was last done, e.g. {"furnace": "2026-07-01"}

hard_water.description: True shortens the tank water heater flush to every 6 months (Rheem)

sites.name: sumeetm10.github.io
sites.description: A collaborative 3D creative canvas where a human and an AI agent work on the exact same screen. Built on WebMCP (navigator.modelContext) for the OpenAI WebMCP Challenge.

tools.name: get_wired_future_state
tools.description: Read the complete live state of the Wired Future 3D canvas: grid and accent colours, which hero model is floating, wave velocity and amplitude, fog density, the camera rig and the drifting node cluster. Returns a short natural-language description of what is currently on screen alongside the exact numbers and the legal range for every parameter. Call this first whenever you need to make a relative change ("make it faster", "darker", "twice as many nodes") so you are adjusting from the real value instead of guessing.

tools.name: modify_wired_future_environment
tools.description: Restyle the Wired Future world: recolour the hologram (stage rings, floor grid and the glow of the car), swap the hero model between the cyber-car and the engine block, and retune how fast the stage rings turn, how bright they glow and how thick the fog sits. This is the main creative control - reach for it whenever someone asks the scene to look different. Every property is optional and you must supply at least one; anything you leave out keeps its current value. Numeric values outside their documented range are clamped rather than rejected. The same change appears instantly in the human control panel, so the person watching sees exactly what you did.

input_schema.description: Supply at least one property. Omitted properties are left untouched, so partial updates are the normal case.

gridColorHex.description: Hex colour for the hologram: stage rings, floor grid, the glow and edge lines of the car, and the primary light. Accepts #rgb or #rrggbb, for example "#00f0ff" or "#0ff". This is the dominant colour of the whole scene, so change it first when asked for a different mood. CSS colour names such as "cyan" are rejected - convert to hex yourself.

accentColorHex.description: Hex colour for the secondary highlight: model trim and the horizon glow. Same #rgb / #rrggbb format. Works best as a contrasting hue to gridColorHex, for example magenta "#ff2bd6" against cyan.

modelType.description: Which hero model hovers above the landscape. "car" is a low-poly cyber-car silhouette; "engine" is a segmented engine-block module. Nothing else is valid.

waveVelocity.description: How fast the hologram platform rings under the car turn, 0 to 5. 0 holds them still, 1 is the calm default, 5 spins them fast. (Named for the wave landscape this stage replaced.) Out-of-range values are clamped.

waveAmplitude.description: Brightness of the hologram platform and floor grid, 0 to 4. 0 is nearly dark, 1 is the default, 4 is a blazing stage. (Named for the wave landscape this stage replaced.) Clamped.

fogDensity.description: Exponential fog density, 0 to 0.12. 0 is crystal clear to the horizon, 0.035 is the default haze, 0.12 buries everything a few units out for a claustrophobic look. Clamped.

tools.name: pulse_reality_wave
tools.description: Fire a one-off shockwave through the world: the terrain waves spike, the neon light flares, and everything eases back to where it was. Nothing is permanently changed, so this is the safe way to punctuate a moment, react to something the person said, or show off that the bridge is live. Use a low intensity for a heartbeat and a high one for an explosion.

intensity.description: How hard the shockwave hits, 0.2 to 5. 0.5 is a subtle heartbeat, 2.4 is the default punch, 5 is a full detonation. Clamped.

durationMs.description: How long the wave takes to rise and settle, in milliseconds, 200 to 8000. 400 is a snap, 1600 is the default swell, 8000 is a long slow breath. Clamped.

tools.name: set_camera_view
tools.description: Move the virtual camera around the Wired Future scene. Pick a framing preset, push in or pull back, raise or drop the eye line, and turn the slow automatic orbit on or off. Use this when someone wants a closer look at the model, a map-like view of the terrain, or a still frame to inspect. Every property is optional; only what you supply is changed. Pair it with capture_scene_snapshot when you want to actually see the result.

input_schema.description: Supply at least one property. Omitted properties keep their current value.

preset.description: Framing preset. "orbit" is the default three-quarter hero angle; "top" looks almost straight down and reads the terrain like a map; "close" sits low and tight on the hero model; "wide" pulls far back so the whole landscape and node cluster fit in frame.

distance.description: How far the camera sits from the scene centre, 6 to 48. 6 is nose-to-the-glass, 16 is the default, 48 is a distant establishing shot. Clamped.

height.description: Camera eye height, -6 to 30. Negative values look up at the terrain from below, 6 is the default eye line, 30 is a near top-down bird view. Clamped.

autoOrbit.description: When true the camera drifts slowly around the scene; when false it locks in place. Turn it off before capturing a snapshot you want to compare against another one.

tools.name: configure_node_cluster
tools.description: Reshape the swarm of glowing nodes that drifts above the terrain. Change how many there are, how far they scatter, how fast they bob, and what colour they glow. This is the cheapest way to change the density and mood of the sky: a handful of slow far-flung nodes reads as lonely and vast, a hundred fast tight ones reads as a busy data storm. Every property is optional.

input_schema.description: Supply at least one property. Omitted properties keep their current value.

count.description: How many nodes exist, 0 to 160, rounded to a whole number. 0 empties the sky entirely, 40 is the default, 160 is a dense swarm. Clamped.

spread.description: Radius the nodes scatter across, 6 to 60. 6 packs them into a tight knot above the model, 26 is the default, 60 flings them out to the horizon. Clamped.

floatSpeed.description: How fast the nodes bob and drift, 0 to 5. 0 freezes them mid-air, 1 is the default gentle float, 5 is agitated. Clamped.

colorHex.description: Hex colour the nodes glow, #rgb or #rrggbb, for example "#8b5cff". CSS colour names are rejected - convert to hex first.

tools.name: apply_scene_preset
tools.description: Flip the entire world to a hand-tuned look in one call - colours, wave motion, fog, camera rig and node cluster all at once. Prefer this over a pile of individual edits when someone describes a mood rather than a number ("make it warmer", "something cold and empty", "go full sci-fi hologram"). It overwrites every parameter the preset covers, so use modify_wired_future_environment afterwards if you want to tweak one detail.

preset.description: Which look to apply. "neon-noir" is the signature cyan-on-black cyberpunk default with a magenta horizon and a calm orbiting camera. "solar-flare" is hot orange and yellow, fast high waves, a wide shot and a dense swarm of red nodes - loud and energetic. "deep-void" is cold deep blue with mint accents, almost still water, heavy fog, only eighteen far-flung nodes and a locked close camera - lonely and quiet. "hologram" is pale ice-white and near-transparent, almost no fog, a top-down view and ninety-six fast nodes - clinical and futuristic.

tools.name: capture_scene_snapshot
tools.description: Render the live 3D canvas to an image and return it, so you can actually look at the scene instead of inferring it from numbers. Use it to verify a change landed the way you intended, to compare a before and after, or when the person asks what the scene looks like right now. Changes nothing. If the canvas has not finished mounting yet this returns an error rather than a blank frame - wait a moment and try again.

maxWidth.description: Longest edge of the returned image in pixels, 240 to 1280. 640 is the default and is plenty to judge colour and composition; go higher only when you need to read fine wireframe detail. Clamped.

tools.name: reset_wired_future
tools.description: Restore every scene parameter - grid and accent colour, model, wave velocity and amplitude, fog, camera framing and the whole node cluster - to the Wired Future defaults. Use this when the person asks to start over, undo everything, or put it back the way it was. This is the exact same Reset control the human has in the Control Deck; no preset reproduces it, because presets do not restore the default model type.

tools.name: place_object
tools.description: Move, turn or resize the centre-stage object. World units: the stage is about 120 units across, the object is roughly 5 units long, and the camera orbits at 16 units. Y is up and 0 is ground level. Rotation is in DEGREES; yaw (rotationDeg.y) is the one you usually want. This is the same placement a person produces by dragging the on-screen gizmo, so call get_wired_future_state first when making a relative move like "push it back a bit".

input_schema.description: Supply at least one of position, rotationDeg or scale.

position.description: Absolute world position. Omit an axis to leave it where it is.

y.description: Up/down, -3 to 18. 0 rests on the ground.

rotationDeg.description: Euler angles in degrees. Values wrap, so 370 becomes 10.

y.description: Yaw in degrees. The usual one.

scale.description: Uniform scale, 0.15 to 5. 1 is the natural size.

tools.name: set_edit_mode
tools.description: Change what the PERSON's mouse does on the canvas. 'orbit' lets them fly the camera around the scene; 'translate', 'rotate' and 'scale' arm a drag gizmo on the object so they can place it by hand. This changes their controls rather than the scene, so say why you switched - for example, arm 'rotate' when you have asked them to aim the car themselves.

mode.description: orbit = camera control. translate = move gizmo. rotate = turn gizmo. scale = resize gizmo.

tools.name: set_car_body
tools.description: Choose which car is on stage. 'real' loads a genuine glTF concept car with PBR paint, glass and rims; it streams an 11 MB asset, so the parametric car shows for a second or two first. 'parametric' is the built-in geometric car, which loads instantly and sits closer to the wireframe aesthetic. Also switches the hero model to the car.

variant.description: real = loaded glTF concept car. parametric = built-in editable mesh.

tools.name: reconstruct_photo_object
tools.description: Inspect or control the photo-to-3D reconstruction. A person can drop a photo of an OBJECT onto this page and a depth model running inside their browser rebuilds it as 3D relief geometry on the stage. You cannot upload an image yourself - if none exists, ASK the person to drop one onto the Photo to 3D panel. Use action 'status' to see whether a reconstruction is ready and what it is of, 'show' to put it on stage, and 'clear' to discard it and return to the car. People and animals are declined by design; only inanimate objects are reconstructed.

action.description: status = report what has been reconstructed (read-only). show = display it on stage. clear = discard it and go back to the car.

tools.name: configure_car_rig
tools.description: Open, strip and take apart the concept car. It is a real glTF asset built from 97 separate named parts, so this genuinely articulates it rather than faking an animation. finish 'print' swaps all paint, glass and trim for one matte resin grey - the 3D-print view, which is how you actually read the shape. explode fans every assembly out along its own axis into a parts diagram (0 assembled, 1 fully apart). doorLeft, doorRight and hood each swing on their real hinge from 0 shut to 1 wide open. Only affects the 'real' car body - call set_car_body with variant 'real' first if the parametric car is showing.

input_schema.description: Supply at least one field. Omitted fields are left alone.

finish.description: hologram = glowing projected light with every edge traced, the default look. paint = the asset's own PBR bodywork. print = matte resin grey with the glass made solid, like an unpainted 3D print.

explode.description: How far apart the assemblies fly, 0 (assembled) to 1 (full parts diagram). 0.35 reads as a cutaway; 1 is a full teardown.

doorLeft.description: Left door angle, 0 shut to 1 fully open.

doorRight.description: Right door angle, 0 shut to 1 fully open.

hood.description: Hood angle, 0 shut to 1 fully raised.

tools.name: set_car_parts
tools.description: Detach or refit individual assemblies of the concept car - take the wheels off, drop the body shell to expose the interior and engine, remove the glass. Assemblies: body (Body Shell), doorLeft (Left Door), doorRight (Right Door), hood (Hood), roof (Roof Panel), glass (Glass), interior (Interior), engine (Engine + Axles), lights (Lights), wheelFL (Wheel Front L), wheelFR (Wheel Front R), wheelRL (Wheel Rear L), wheelRR (Wheel Rear R). action 'remove' hides the listed parts, 'refit' puts them back, 'only' shows ONLY the listed parts, and 'reset' refits everything. Nothing is destroyed - a removed part is always one call away from returning.

action.description: remove = detach the listed parts. refit = put them back. only = show just these. reset = refit everything (ignores parts).

parts.description: Assembly ids. Required for remove / refit / only; ignored for reset. Example: ["wheelFL","wheelFR","wheelRL","wheelRR"] takes all four wheels off.

tools.name: inspect_car_part
tools.description: Measure one assembly of the concept car from its actual triangles: triangle and vertex counts, surface area, bounding-box dimensions, centroid, whether the mesh is watertight, and the estimated mass in every available engineering material. Real geometry, computed in the browser - not a lookup table. Call this before proposing an upgrade so your suggestion is grounded in the part true size and mass rather than a guess. Lengths come back in metres (the car is normalised to 5.2 model units for a real length of about 4.6 m). MASS IS A SHELL ESTIMATE: automotive parts are pressed panels and castings, not solid billets, so mass is surface area x wall thickness x density, defaulting to a 2 mm wall. Pass wallThicknessMm to model a thicker casting or a thinner skin. The enclosed volume is also returned, but for an open shell it is geometrically meaningless and is flagged as such.

part.description: Which assembly to measure.

wallThicknessMm.description: Wall thickness used for the mass estimate, in millimetres. Default 2. Typical: 0.8-1.2 for a steel body panel, 3-6 for a cast alloy wheel, 2-4 for a structural carbon panel.

tools.name: modify_car_part
tools.description: Reshape one assembly of the car by rewriting its vertices. scaleX/Y/Z stretch it about its own centre, so scaling a wheel widens the tyre without moving it off the axle. inflate offsets every vertex along its surface normal, which thickens a panel or puffs a shell outward. twistDeg rotates the part progressively about the vertical axis, distributed over its height. material re-specifies it in a real engineering material, changing both its look and its calculated mass. Edits are ABSOLUTE and rebuilt from the pristine geometry each time, so sending scaleX 1.2 twice leaves it at 1.2, and reset returns it exactly to the shipped part. Measure first with inspect_car_part so you know what you are changing.

input_schema.description: Supply part plus at least one change, or part plus reset:true to restore it.

part.description: Which assembly to reshape.

reset.description: Restore this part to the shipped geometry and material, discarding every edit.

scaleX.description: Scale across the car, 0.2 to 3. 1 is untouched.

inflate.description: Offset along surface normals in model units, -0.12 to 0.12. One model unit is about 0.88 m, so 0.02 is roughly 18 mm of added thickness.

twistDeg.description: Twist about the vertical axis over the part height, -180 to 180 degrees.

material.description: Re-specify the part: steel (7850 kg/m3), aluminium (2700 kg/m3), titanium (4430 kg/m3), carbon (1600 kg/m3), abs (1040 kg/m3), glass (2500 kg/m3), rubber (1100 kg/m3).

tools.name: list_car_parts
tools.description: Enumerate every individually addressable mesh of the concept car - over a hundred of them, down to individual door handles, wing mirrors, wipers, brake discs, steering wheel spokes and pedals. Returns each part id, its human label and which assembly it belongs to. Call this before place_car_part or detach_car_parts, because those address parts by id and the ids are asset-specific. Optionally filter by assembly or by a substring of the label.

assembly.description: Only parts belonging to this assembly.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring of the label, e.g. "handle", "wiper", "disc".

tools.name: select_car_part
tools.description: Point the on-screen transform gizmo at a part, so the PERSON can drag it by hand. Selecting an assembly (a whole door) or a single mesh (that door's handle) changes what their mouse grabs. This is a handoff: use it when you want them to position something themselves, and say so. Pass nothing to clear the selection.

assembly.description: Select a whole assembly. Ignored when part is given.

part.description: A part id from list_car_parts, for single-mesh selection. Wins over assembly.

tools.name: place_car_part
tools.description: Move, turn or resize ONE individual mesh - lift a wing mirror off, rotate a wheel rim, shrink a door handle. Offsets are relative to the part’s rest position in model units (one unit is about 0.88 m), so the part keeps riding its assembly when a door swings or the car explodes. Absolute, not cumulative: sending the same offset twice leaves it in one place. Pass reset:true to put it back. Get part ids from list_car_parts.

part.description: Part id from list_car_parts.

reset.description: Return this part to its rest position and scale.

z.description: Offset along the car, same range.

tools.name: detach_car_parts
tools.description: Remove or refit individual meshes by id - take off just the wing mirrors, or hide every window while leaving the frames. Distinct from set_car_parts, which works on whole assemblies. Nothing is destroyed; a detached part is one call from returning.

action.description: remove = hide the listed parts. refit = show them. reset = refit everything (ignores parts).

parts.description: Part ids from list_car_parts. Required for remove and refit.

sites.name: tellegen.dev
sites.description: Reactive visualization for power systems optimization. Drag demand and watch locational marginal prices and their adjoint sensitivities update from KKT columns, with exact DC OPF and SOCWR solves…

tools.name: list_cases
tools.description: List configured and imported cases, including unavailable cases and their reported reasons. Returns stable case IDs, the displayed revision, and a pagination offset for select_case.

offset.description: Pagination offset. Defaults to 0; use next_offset from the previous result.

limit.description: Maximum cases. Defaults to 10.

tools.name: select_case
tools.description: Show a case from list_cases using the same controls as the case tabs. Leaves saved Studies intact and exits historical inspection. Changes the view only; no proposal approval is required.

expected_revision.description: Optional displayed revision from list_cases or inspect_case, checked before selection.

tools.name: solve_multiconductor_pf
tools.description: Calculate terminal voltages, currents, and powers for the displayed multiconductor case. Uses prescribed demand and source voltages. Rejects unsupported equipment physics. Does not optimize dispatch or change electrical inputs. Use query_network for terminal results.

expected_revision.description: Displayed revision from inspect_case.

tools.name: inspect_case
tools.description: Inspect the displayed network, including a saved Study state when one is shown. Returns case, state, formulation, units, and revision. Saved states are read-only; select_case returns to the editable case.

tools.name: query_network
tools.description: Query buses or branches in the displayed network by stable ID or metric. For the highest LMP use element_kind bus, sort_by price, direction desc, limit 1. Returns saved-state values when a Study state is shown.

element_ids.description: Specific stable IDs to return. Omit to rank elements.

sort_by.description: Metric for ranking. Defaults to demand_mw for buses and loading for branches.

direction.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc.

limit.description: Maximum rows. Defaults to 5.

tools.name: analyze_sensitivity
tools.description: Compute the displayed formulation's LMP sensitivity for one bus demand or branch rating and return the largest responses. Leaves the visible selection unchanged.

kind.description: Element type.

element_id.description: Stable element ID returned by query_network.

limit.description: Maximum response rows. Defaults to 5.

tools.name: focus_network
tools.description: Focus a bus or branch in the tellegen interface and load its computed sensitivity view. The returned result reflects the interface after the selection has settled.

kind.description: Element type.

element_id.description: Stable element ID returned by query_network.

tools.name: preview_case_update
tools.description: Predict objective and locational marginal price (LMP) changes for bounded demand or branch rating edits at the current formulation. Leaves the case and visible interface unchanged and requires the current revision.

expected_revision.description: Current revision from inspect_case; protects against stale analysis.

mode.description: Set final deltas or add the supplied MW changes. Defaults to set.

demand.description: Bus demand delta edits in MW from the base case.

ratings.description: Branch rating delta edits in MW from the base case.

limit.description: Maximum predicted locational marginal price (LMP) changes. Defaults to 5.

tools.name: update_case
tools.description: Atomically set or increment demand and branch-rating deltas, optionally choose a formulation, then solve and update the visible interface. Requires the current revision.

expected_revision.description: Current revision from inspect_case; protects against stale writes.

mode.description: Set final deltas or add the supplied MW changes. Defaults to set.

demand.description: Bus demand delta edits in MW from the base case.

ratings.description: Branch rating delta edits in MW from the base case.

formulation.description: Available formulation ID shown by inspect_case.

tools.name: reset_case
tools.description: Clear all committed demand and branch-rating edits in the active case, keep its formulation, solve, and update the visible interface. Requires the current revision.

expected_revision.description: Current revision from inspect_case; protects against stale writes.

tools.name: create_study
tools.description: Save the current case and its results as a Study. A planning goal is optional; add or revise it later. Creating a Study does not change the network or apply a proposal.

solution.description: A saved solution must belong to the supplied instance.
A saved solution must belong to the supplied instance.

goal.description: Legacy alias for study.

DecisionSpace.description: The feasible set, distinct from both the inner problem and the outer goal.

oneOf.description: Allocate this additional MW across the declared demand decisions.
Preserve the existing total MW across the declared demand decisions.

DecisionVariable.description: Bounds and increments apply to changes from the goal's anchor state in a Study.

budget_weight.description: Budget consumption per absolute unit of intervention.

Intervention.description: A numerical intervention supported by the existing solvers.

coeffs.description:
Raw coefficients, highest order first for the polynomial model:
`[c_{k-1}, …, c1, c0]`.

ncost.description: Number of cost coefficients (polynomial) or breakpoints (piecewise).

StudyObjective.description: A scalar goal over the exact operating point and explicit interventions.

Operand.description:
What a sensitivity is taken *of*, named for the physical power quantity rather
than a formulation's internal variable. The orthogonal sub-axes (active/reactive,
from/to, voltage representation) are visible to the type system; each formulation
maps a request to its own KKT rows or returns [`SensError::Unsupported`].

The dialects fold into one vocabulary: DC `Angle` is `Voltage(Angle)`, the conic
squared magnitude `w` is `Voltage(Squared)`, the nodal price is `Price(Active)`.

oneOf.description:
Nodal-balance dual (the LMP for active power, the reactive price for
reactive), per bus.
Generator dispatch `pg` / `qg`, per generator.
Branch active/reactive flow at the from/to end, per branch.

Bus voltage in the formulation's representation (`vm` / `va` / `w` / `wr` /
`wi`), per bus.

Power.description:
Active or reactive power. The orthogonal P/Q sub-axis shared by prices,
dispatch, flows, and demand.

End.description: Which end of a branch a flow is measured at.

VoltageKind.description:
How a voltage operand is represented: polar (`Magnitude`, `Angle`) for the AC
power flow, or the W-space lift (`Squared` = `|V|²`, `ProductReal` = `Re(Vi Vj*)`,
`ProductImag` = `Im(Vi Vj*)`) for the conic relaxation.

ObservableWeight.description: A weighted observable in the units reported by the selected formulation.

SolveResponse.description:
The formulation-agnostic solve result. A superset: every block is optional, and
each formulation fills what it produces. Powers are MW/MVAr, nodal values are
in objective units per selected power unit, angles radians, `vm` per unit, and
`w = |V|^2` per unit squared. Element ids
are the original bus/branch/generator ids, so the frontend joins straight onto
its case.

formulation.description: The formulation that produced this, echoed for the client.

lmp.description:
Active nodal price when the solved OPF declares a network generator
cost objective. Feasibility solves leave this absent.

lmp_q.description:
Reactive nodal price. Always `None` in this build; the field is retained for
wire-format stability.

sensitivities.description:
One self-describing matrix per requested cell, in request order. Each carries
its own row/column element ids and the served-unit label.

va.description: Voltage angle, radians (every path except socwr, which is W-space).

vm.description: Voltage magnitude, per unit (ACPF or square root of SOCWR squared magnitude).

w.description:
Squared voltage magnitude `w = |V|^2`, per unit squared (socwr). The conic
relaxation does not guarantee a globally consistent set of voltage angles.

wr.description: Real and imaginary oriented branch voltage products (SOCWR).

GenDispatch.description: Generator dispatch, keyed by original generator id. `qg` is `None` on the DC paths.

bus.description: Original bus identity, allowing exact aggregation of co-located dispatch.

BranchFlow.description:
Branch flows, keyed by original branch id (plus the row uid when carried, as in
[`BusScalar`]). `pf` (from-end active, MW) and `loading` (|S|/limit,
dimensionless) are present on every formulation that has flows; the reactive
and to-end legs are `None` on the DC paths.

Problem.description:
Which problem to solve. The convex/power flow solve paths, as the lowercase JSON
tags `"dcpf"`/`"dcopf"`/`"acpf"`/`"socwr"`. A plain (not internally tagged) enum
so a request that omits it defaults to [`DcOpf`](Problem::DcOpf), and `{}` is a
valid base-case DC OPF request.

The `"acopf"` tag (full nonlinear AC OPF) is retained for wire-format stability
but is not solved by this build: [`capabilities_json`] reports it unavailable and
requesting it returns a clean `Err`.

oneOf.description:
DC power flow: angles and flows at the fixed generator setpoints. No prices,
no dispatch, no sensitivity.
DC OPF: the LMP / dispatch / flow workhorse. Differentiable via the DC KKT.

AC polar Newton power flow. Voltages and nodal injections. Differentiable
via the AC Newton system.
SOCWR (Jabr) conic relaxation of AC OPF. Differentiable via the conic KKT.

Full nonlinear AC OPF. Not available in this build (the dispatch errors
cleanly); the tag is kept so the JSON format stays stable.

BusInjection.description:
A nodal net injection (MW / MVAr), keyed by original bus id (plus the row uid
when carried, as in [`BusScalar`]). Injections describe the net nodal power balance.

anyOf.description: Interior-point iterate trace (dcopf / socwr).
Newton iteration count and final infinity-norm mismatch (acpf).

Iterations.description:
The convergence record. OPF paths carry the full interior-point trace (for the
solve-card sparkline); the AC power flow carries its Newton count and final
mismatch. Untagged: the OPF arm serializes to the same bare array the DC OPF
always returned.

SolveIteration.description:
One interior-point iterate: the iteration index, the primal objective, and
the primal and dual residuals. Collected once per Clarabel iteration to draw
the convergence plot. Shape matches the frontend `SolveIteration`.

BusScalar.description:
A scalar keyed by original bus id (LMP, voltage, angle, squared magnitude).
`uid` is the bus's powerio row uid when the solved network carried one, so an
overlay can re-key on stable identity instead of the positional id.

SensitivityMatrix.description:
A self-describing sensitivity result: `values[r][c] = d(rows[r])/d(cols[c])`,
with row and column metadata naming each quantity and its source element, and the
served-unit label.

values.description:
`values[r][c] = d(operand_r)/d(parameter_c)`, in the units named by `units`. The
engine produces per-unit values; the api edge rescales to served units.

ColMeta.description: Identity and quantity metadata for one column of a [`SensitivityMatrix`].

index.description: Dense index of the element this column varies.

ElementId.description:
A source-id reference for a dense row or column, so a [`SensitivityMatrix`]
self-describes and the api serializes it without re-deriving id maps.

Parameter.description:
What a sensitivity is taken *with respect to* — the parameter whose hand-derived
`dK/dp` column drives the solve.

oneOf.description: Bus active/reactive demand `pd` / `qd`, per bus.
Generation cost coefficient, per generator.
DC thermal limit `fmax` / AC-conic apparent-power `|S|` limit, per branch.
Branch series admittance `g` / `b`, per branch.
Bus shunt admittance `gs` / `bs`, per bus.
Voltage-magnitude bound right-hand side (the `w = |V|²` bound), per bus.

Generator output bound right-hand side (`pmax` / `pmin` / `qmax` / `qmin`),
per generator.
Transformer tap ratio / phase shift, per branch.
Branch switching state `sw` in `[0, 1]`, per branch.

CostTerm.description: Which generation-cost coefficient: the quadratic `cq` or the linear `cl`.

GB.description: Conductance `g` or susceptance `b`, the real/imaginary parts of an admittance.

Bound.description: A min or max bound, e.g. the lower/upper voltage-magnitude limit.

TapKind.description: A transformer control: the tap ratio or the phase-shift angle.

RowMeta.description: Identity and quantity metadata for one row of a [`SensitivityMatrix`].

index.description: Dense index of the element this row reports.

SolveStatus.description: A solve outcome that succeeded. A failed solve is the `Err` arm of a solve entry.

oneOf.description: An OPF reached optimality.
A power flow converged to a feasible point.

BranchScalar.description: A branch-indexed voltage product, in squared per unit.

tools.name: inspect_study
tools.description: Inspect the open Study, read a bounded page of goals, states or evidence, or open a saved Study. Saved candidates remain unapplied.

study_id.description: Open this saved Study if it is not currently open.

tools.name: revise_study_goal
tools.description: Save a new goal revision without changing historical goals. The revision invalidates the current recommendation and approvals.

GoalRevision.description: A goal revision retains its own anchor and interpretation.

DecisionSpace.description: The feasible set, distinct from both the inner problem and the outer goal.

oneOf.description: Allocate this additional MW across the declared demand decisions.
Preserve the existing total MW across the declared demand decisions.

DecisionVariable.description: Bounds and increments apply to changes from the goal's anchor state in a Study.

budget_weight.description: Budget consumption per absolute unit of intervention.

Intervention.description: A numerical intervention supported by the existing solvers.

StudyObjective.description: A scalar goal over the exact operating point and explicit interventions.

Operand.description:
What a sensitivity is taken *of*, named for the physical power quantity rather
than a formulation's internal variable. The orthogonal sub-axes (active/reactive,
from/to, voltage representation) are visible to the type system; each formulation
maps a request to its own KKT rows or returns [`SensError::Unsupported`].

The dialects fold into one vocabulary: DC `Angle` is `Voltage(Angle)`, the conic
squared magnitude `w` is `Voltage(Squared)`, the nodal price is `Price(Active)`.

oneOf.description:
Nodal-balance dual (the LMP for active power, the reactive price for
reactive), per bus.
Generator dispatch `pg` / `qg`, per generator.
Branch active/reactive flow at the from/to end, per branch.

Bus voltage in the formulation's representation (`vm` / `va` / `w` / `wr` /
`wi`), per bus.

Power.description:
Active or reactive power. The orthogonal P/Q sub-axis shared by prices,
dispatch, flows, and demand.

End.description: Which end of a branch a flow is measured at.

VoltageKind.description:
How a voltage operand is represented: polar (`Magnitude`, `Angle`) for the AC
power flow, or the W-space lift (`Squared` = `|V|²`, `ProductReal` = `Re(Vi Vj*)`,
`ProductImag` = `Im(Vi Vj*)`) for the conic relaxation.

ObservableWeight.description: A weighted observable in the units reported by the selected formulation.

tools.name: branch_study
tools.description: Inspect a saved state and continue exploration from it. This changes the inspected pointer, not the applied state.

tools.name: compare_study_states
tools.description: Compare two saved network states, optionally under a selected goal revision. Results include operating-point changes and goal progress when a goal is selected.

tools.name: propose_study
tools.description: Explore feasible capacity or demand interventions using implicit gradients and exact solves. Every trial counts against the solve budget. Save the best verified recommendation without applying it. The user applies it in the Study panel.

tools.name: edit_demand
tools.description: Add signed MW increments at permitted buses to the selected saved state. Edits accumulate across calls and persist after reload. Individual bounds and the total change budget apply to every step; incomplete demand totals stay unapplied. Read the resulting state's evidence for the cumulative demand vector.

delta_mw.description: Signed increment to the selected state's demand, in MW.

tools.name: restore_base_case
tools.description: Exactly solve the retained original network data and save a reset candidate without applying it or deleting history. The user can apply the reset in the Study panel. Reports when the original input is unavailable.

tools.name: record_study_evidence
tools.description: Attach a stated rationale and evidence to a saved state without creating an electrical state. Do not record private agent reasoning.

tools.name: propose_capacity_plan
tools.description: Use implicit derivatives to choose bounded branch capacity increase trials. Exact solves verify the staged proposal. The electrical case stays unchanged.

expected_revision.description: Current revision from inspect_case; a stale revision refuses the run.

kind.description: Implicit objective kind.

weights.description: Weighted LMP terms defining the minimized objective.

weight.description: Coefficient applied to this bus LMP.

objective.description: Objective evaluated at each exact OPF solution.

candidates.description: Candidate branches whose capacities may increase.

max_increase_per_branch_mw.description: Largest proposed increase for one branch, MW.

budget_mw.description: Maximum sum of proposed capacity increases, MW.

increment_mw.description: Capacity increment used to construct trials, MW.

max_changed_lines.description: Maximum branches changed in the final proposal.

exact_solve_budget.description: Solve budget, including the starting point and all trials.

sites.name: tryportego.com
sites.description: Design, bind, and control your home through one conversation.

tools.name: home.get_document
tools.description: Read the current visible Portego home document, including rooms, devices, bindings, gateway status, and reported device state. This does not change anything.

tools.name: home.update_details
tools.description: Rename the Portego home or update its description, type, total area, and notes.

tools.name: home.update_floor_details
tools.description: Rename one floor or update its description, area, and notes. Renaming also moves its rooms to the new floor name.

tools.name: home.remove_floor
tools.description: Remove one named floor and every room, device, binding, door, and window assigned to it.

tools.name: home.add_room
tools.description: Add one rectangular room to a floor of the Portego home. The change is applied immediately.

label.description: The human-facing room name, such as Kitchen.

floor.description: Floor name, such as Ground floor or Attic. Defaults to Ground floor.

tools.name: home.update_room
tools.description: Rename, move, or resize one named room on the visible Portego canvas. Coordinates use the 1000 by 650 floor-plan space.

label.description: A new human-facing room name.

tools.name: home.remove_room
tools.description: Remove one named room, its designed devices, their bindings, and any doors or windows connected to it.

tools.name: home.add_device
tools.description: Add one configured light, switch, plug, or sensor to an existing room on the visible canvas. Honor any placement the user describes. When no placement is specified, omit position so Portego chooses a sensible free location away from other devices. Never stack device symbols on top of one another. When autoBind is enabled, Portego binds the first available hardware endpoint that provides every required capability.

label.description: Human-facing device name.

config.description: Type-specific configuration: lights use mounting, dimmable, and colorTemperature; switches use mode and channels; plugs use energyMonitoring; sensors use measures.

autoBind.description: Bind the first compatible unbound endpoint when available.

position.description: Optional position in the 1000 by 650 floor-plan space. Use it when the user requests a location (for example, near the right wall). Inspect home.get_document first and keep device centers separated from existing devices; otherwise omit this field for automatic placement.

tools.name: home.move_device
tools.description: Move one named device within its room on the visible Portego canvas. Coordinates use the 1000 by 650 floor-plan space. Honor the user's requested location. Otherwise inspect home.get_document, choose a sensible position inside the room, and keep the device center about 70 coordinate units from other device centers so symbols do not overlap.

tools.name: home.update_device
tools.description: Rename, reconfigure, change the type of, or move a device. When changing its room or coordinates, honor the user's requested location and otherwise inspect home.get_document to avoid overlapping another device. An incompatible physical binding is removed automatically.

tools.name: home.remove_device
tools.description: Remove one named device and its physical-device binding.

tools.name: device.bind
tools.description: Bind or rebind one designed device to a compatible discovered hardware endpoint. Both sides can have only one active binding.

tools.name: device.unbind
tools.description: Disconnect one designed device from its physical hardware endpoint.

tools.name: home.add_opening
tools.description: Add a door or window to a named room wall. A door can optionally connect the room to another named room, making the relationship explicit.

tools.name: home.remove_opening
tools.description: Remove one labeled door or window from the home model.

tools.name: device.set_state
tools.description: Set a supported power or brightness state for one named device bound to reachable hardware. Portego waits for the gateway to confirm the resulting physical state.

tools.name: home.reset_demo
tools.description: Remove all rooms, devices, and bindings from this Portego demo. This is destructive but affects only the temporary home.

tools.name: home.apply_changes
tools.description: Apply up to 50 room, device, binding, or opening changes as one atomic edit. Coordinate room and device geometry as a complete layout: honor locations stated by the user, distribute unspecified devices sensibly inside their rooms, and do not place device symbols on top of one another. Omit add_device positions when automatic placement is appropriate. If any change fails, none are saved and one undo reverses the entire set.

tools.name: home.undo
tools.description: Undo the most recent user or chatbot edit to the pre-login home.

tools.name: home.redo
tools.description: Redo the most recently undone edit to the pre-login home.

sites.name: tv.fangorn.network
sites.description: SOND3R

tools.name: search-catalog
tools.description: Semantically search this storefront — titles, descriptions and subtitle lines across every publisher in the current view. Also shows the results on the page.

query.description: What to look for, in natural language

limit.description: Max files to return (default 10)

tools.name: find-line
tools.description: Find where words are actually SPOKEN, across every subtitle in this view — the exact-phrase counterpart to search-catalog, which ranks whole files by topic and therefore cannot find a phrase said once. Give it phrases; it returns the lines containing them, with the timestamps to cut. Use it to build a supercut that says something the corpus never meant to say.

phrases.description: The words to find, each matched intact and on word boundaries

tools.name: browse-catalog
tools.description: List what this storefront holds, without searching. Filter by publisher address or media kind.

kind.description: video, audio, image, text, software…

limit.description: Max files to return (default 50)

tools.name: open-item
tools.description: Open one file's page in the storefront — its description, price and, for a paid file, the buy button the person presses themselves. Free files start playing.

id.description: An id from search-catalog or browse-catalog

tools.name: list-channels
tools.description: Every channel on this TV and what is playing on each right now, with what is up next. Channels marked `tuned:true` were generated from a natural-language query rather than grouped out of the catalog.

tools.name: tune-channel
tools.description: Make a brand-new television channel and turn the set to it. Three kinds of evidence, mixable: a mood in words ('rainy cyberpunk', 'slow nature documentary'), `blend` — how far to pull toward where THIS viewer's session is already heading, from read-taste — and specific items to move toward or away from. A channel built with blend or like/unlike is derived from behaviour that exists only in this browser, so it cannot be produced anywhere else. Returns a link that puts anyone else on the exact same frame.

prompt.description: The mood or theme, in natural language

blend.description: 0–1: how much of the viewer's own heading (read-taste) to mix in. 0 = the words alone, 1 = purely where they are already going.

like.description: Item ids to pull the channel toward

unlike.description: Item ids to push the channel away from

title.description: What to call it, when the channel is not just a prompt

scenes.description: Build the channel out of MOMENTS instead of whole files. A 'firetrucks' channel with scenes:false is every film that mentions one; with scenes:true it is the ~45 seconds in each film where one is actually on screen. Needs a corpus with subtitle, scene or summary rows — say so if the channel comes back empty.

tools.name: watch-channel
tools.description: Turn the TV to an existing channel, by number or by name.

channel.description: A channel number or title from list-channels

tools.name: channel-schedule
tools.description: What is coming up on a channel — the running order for the next few hours, computed from the clock alone. Works for any channel, whether or not it is the one on screen.

channel.description: Channel number or title (default: what is on screen)

tools.name: share-channel
tools.description: Get the shareable link for any channel, and optionally keep a tuned one in this browser's channel list. Anyone who opens the link watches in sync — the schedule is a pure function of UTC, so there is nothing to synchronise.

channel.description: Channel number or title (default: what is on screen)

save.description: Also keep it in this browser's channel list

tools.name: read-taste
tools.description: What this viewer is actually into, right now — derived in the browser from what they have opened, rated and sat through, and never sent anywhere. Returns their heading in words, how fast it is moving, what they have rejected, and the items nearest to where they are going next. This is the signal that makes a channel personal; feed it back through tune-channel's `blend`.

tools.name: await-viewer-signal
tools.description: Wait until the viewer DOES something, and return what it was. Blocks — this is a subscription, not a poll. Signals: `skip` (left a slot early — the strongest negative this surface produces), `finished` (sat through one), `like`/`dislike` (rated it), `channel`, `tuned`. Returns null if nothing happens before the timeout, which means they are still watching and is not an error. Call it again with `after` set to the last `seq` you saw to avoid missing anything in between.

seconds.description: How long to wait before giving up (default 45, max 120)

tools.name: propose
tools.description: Ask the viewer something on the screen they are already looking at. A card appears over the TV with your question and your buttons. Use it before doing anything they did not ask for: retuning what they are watching, saving a channel, changing direction. This is the consent step WebMCP has no primitive for, and it only works because the tools are running in the page the person is looking at. Three outcomes, and they are NOT interchangeable: an `answer` is a decision; `answer: null` with `settled: true` means dismissed or expired, which is a NO; and `pending: true` means the card is still on screen and they have not answered yet — that is not a no, and acting on it as one discards a decision they are still making. When you get a `ticket`, call this tool again with it (and nothing else) to keep waiting. The card outlives any single call, so a slow yes is never lost.

question.description: Short, answerable by pressing a button. Say what you would do and why.

options.description: The buttons (default Yes / No). Keep them to two or three.

seconds.description: How long the card STANDS on screen before it expires (default 60, max 300)

wait.description: How long THIS call blocks before handing back a ticket (default 45, max 110). Keep it under your transport's timeout.

ticket.description: Resume waiting on a card you already posted, from a previous `pending` reply. Send this alone.

tools.name: player-state
tools.description: What is playing in this tab right now, and where the playhead is.

tools.name: control-player
tools.description: Drive the open player: play, pause, or jump to a timestamp.

seconds.description: Playhead position, for seek

tools.name: capture-frame
tools.description: Look at the video: the frame at a given timestamp (or the current one), returned as an image. Reads the exact frame — off the canvas where the file allows it, otherwise through the relay, which seeks the remote file by range request and so is not bound by the browser's cross-origin rules. Falls back to the archive's own coarse frame strip only where neither is available.

at.description: Seconds to seek to first; omit for the current frame

tools.name: annotate
tools.description: Draw on the open player: bookmarks on its timeline (the person can click one to jump there) and boxes over the picture for a stretch of time. Replaces whatever was drawn before; call with nothing to clear.

at.description: Seconds

boxes.description: Boxes over the picture, in 0–1 fractions of the frame

tools.name: scan-film
tools.description: Flip through a film without watching it: frames spread across its running time (or across a range), in ONE call, as a single contact sheet with each tile stamped with its time. Costs a couple of kilobytes per frame — the way to check what a film actually contains before spending an hour on it. Frames are the exact ones at those timestamps where a relay can read them, so tightening `from`/`to` really does look closer; without one it falls back to the archive's published strip, whose cadence is fixed and sometimes only a frame or two per episode.

id.description: A file id; omit for whatever is open

from.description: Start of the range in seconds, default 0

to.description: End of the range in seconds, default the whole film

tools.name: describe-scenes
tools.description: Write down what happens in a film, at timestamps — the thing the catalog does not know. Scan it with scan-film or capture-frame first, then describe what you actually saw: subject, action, shot, setting. Each description becomes a searchable moment that lands the next person on that exact second, so write for a stranger's query ('a man lights a cigarette in the rain'), not as a caption. Stages a draft for the person to review and publish; call it again after a closer pass and the better description wins.

id.description: A file id; omit for whatever is open

text.description: What is on screen, in a sentence or two

summary.description: One line about the film as a whole, if you have one

tools.name: program-channel
tools.description: Put an ORDERED run of clips on the television, as a channel. Takes the same `shots` as montage — but instead of rendering a file, it becomes a channel the set turns to, each slot a window the player seeks into. Use it when the order is the point: a channel where clip two answers clip one is a programme, while the same clips shuffled are only a subject. The ring is data, so it keeps playing on the clock for a viewer with no agent, long after this conversation ends.

shots.description: The clips, in the order they should play

id.description: A file id; omit for whatever is open

note.description: What this clip is — printed on its cell in the guide

tools.name: montage
tools.description: Turn shots you picked into an edit list — to render here, or to hand to software off this machine. Resolves each file to the URL its bytes actually live at and checks the numbers, so a bad supercut fails here, in one call, instead of after three features have been fetched. `format` decides who the list is for: `json` for `node scripts/cut.mjs .json out.mp4`, `edl` or `otio` for an editor — Blender, Resolve, Premiere and Nuke all import one of those, and an OTIO clip carries the source URL, so the timeline resolves with nothing downloaded. Hand the text straight to whatever desktop tool you also have open. Marks the open film's shots on its timeline so the person can see the cut before it is rendered.

shots.description: The cuts, in the order they should play

id.description: A file id; omit for whatever is open

note.description: What this shot is, for the person reviewing it

format.description: Who the list is for. `json` (default) renders with scripts/cut.mjs. `edl` is CMX3600, which every NLE imports. `otio` is OpenTimelineIO — JSON, and each clip carries its source URL, so it is the one to hand another tool or an agent.

title.description: What to call the timeline, for edl/otio

sites.name: urbanlama.github.io
sites.description: Animate a rigged 3D character with an AI agent

tools.name: describe_world
tools.description: Sagt, wie die Welt liegt: welche Achse oben ist, wo vorne ist, auf welcher Hoehe der Boden liegt, wie gross die Figur ist. Enthaelt ausserdem eine Kurzanleitung, wie in dieser Seite gearbeitet wird. Braucht ein geladenes Modell.

tools.name: describe_rig
tools.description: Die Gelenkliste. Nennt jedes vermessene Gelenk mit seinen Kanaelen, deren Grenzwerten in Grad und der Richtung, in die ein positiver Wert wirkt. DIE KANALNAMEN SIND JE GELENK VERSCHIEDEN und kommen aus der Vermessung: die Schulter hat andere als das Knie. Ohne diesen Aufruf sind set_pose und set_joint Raten. Nennt ausserdem die Rollen (foot_l, hand_r, ...) mit ihrem Knochen und der Konfidenz.

detail.description: true liefert zusaetzlich Achsen, Vorzeichenquellen und Messbelege; die Antwort wird dann sehr gross. Ohne Angabe die Kompaktfassung.

tools.name: describe_body
tools.description: Das gemessene Koerperprofil: Segmente mit Radius in Metern und Masse in Kilogramm, Fusssohlenpunkte, Ruheabstaende zwischen Koerperteilen. Fuer Reichweiten und Standflaechen. Zum blossen Setzen von Haltungen nicht noetig.

tools.name: probe_joint
tools.description: Probiert einen einzelnen Gelenkkanal aus: beugt ihn um den angegebenen Winkel und liefert Vorher und Nachher als Bild. Zum Nachsehen, in welche Richtung ein Kanal wirkt, wenn die Angabe aus describe_rig nicht reicht. Ohne channel wird der erste gemessene Kanal des Gelenks genommen; die Antwort sagt, welcher es war und welche es sonst noch gibt. Aendert die Timeline nicht.

joint.description: Gelenkname aus describe_rig, z. B. hip_l

channel.description: optional: Kanalname dieses Gelenks aus describe_rig, z. B. flex. Die Namen sind je Gelenk verschieden - hip_l hat flex, arm_l hat lift. Fehlt die Angabe, wird der erste gemessene Kanal genommen

tools.name: set_intent
tools.description: Legt fest, woran die fertige Bewegung gemessen wird - was am Ende zutreffen muss. Wird sofort uebernommen, ohne Rueckfrage. Jedes Kriterium braucht seine Pflichtfelder: rotation {part, axis, minDeg oder maxDeg}, airtime {minSek oder maxSek}, travel {part, richtung, minHoehe oder maxHoehe}, contact_change {foot, von, bis}, clearance {partA, partB, minAnteil oder maxAnteil}, part_height {part, minAnteil oder maxAnteil}, part_speed {part, minHoeheProSek oder maxHoeheProSek}. WICHTIG: part ist ein KNOCHENNAME aus describe_rig, keine Rolle. Laengen in Anteilen der Koerperhoehe, Winkel in Grad, Zeiten in Sekunden.

checks.description: Kriterien, je eines der 7 Arten: rotation, airtime, travel, contact_change, clearance, part_height, part_speed

items.description: Ein Kriterium. Welche Felder es braucht, haengt von kind ab — die Pflichtfelder stehen bei jedem Feld unten und in der Werkzeugbeschreibung.

part.description: KNOCHENNAME aus describe_rig, keine Rolle. Pflicht bei rotation, travel, part_height, part_speed.

minDeg.description: Untergrenze in Grad. rotation: minDeg oder maxDeg.

maxDeg.description: Obergrenze in Grad. rotation: minDeg oder maxDeg.

minSek.description: Untergrenze in Sekunden. airtime: minSek oder maxSek.

maxSek.description: Obergrenze in Sekunden. airtime: minSek oder maxSek.

richtung.description: Richtungsvektor [x, y, z], KEIN Wort wie "hoch". Pflicht bei travel.

minHoehe.description: Untergrenze in Koerperhoehen. travel: minHoehe oder maxHoehe.

maxHoehe.description: Obergrenze in Koerperhoehen. travel: minHoehe oder maxHoehe.

foot.description: Fussrolle, z. B. foot_l. Pflicht bei contact_change.

von.description: Fruehester Frame, in dem der Fuss abheben darf. Pflicht bei contact_change.

bis.description: Spaetester Frame, in dem der Fuss abheben darf; von..bis ist ein Fenster. Pflicht bei contact_change.

from.description: Startframe des Messfensters, optional.

to.description: Endframe des Messfensters, optional.

tools.name: set_duration
tools.description: Legt fest, wie lang die Bewegung ist, in Frames. Muss vor jedem Setzen von Haltungen oder Phasen kommen; ohne Laenge weisen die anderen Werkzeuge ab. Die Framerate steht in der Antwort. Ändert NICHTS an bestehenden Haltungen — für einen sauberen Neuanfang vor der nächsten Bewegung gibt es clear_motion.

tools.name: clear_motion
tools.description: Löscht die gesamte Bewegung und macht die Timeline leer: alle gesetzten Haltungen (set_pose, set_joint), alle Phasen, alle Fußanker (hold_foot) und die gesetzte Absicht (set_intent). Modell, Vermessung und Rollen bleiben — die Länge der Timeline (set_duration) bleibt auch. Für eine NEUE Bewegung: erst clear_motion, dann Haltungen setzen. Ohne ihn erbst du alle Schlüsselbilder der vorigen Bewegung, auch auf Frames, die du nie anfasst.

tools.name: set_joint
tools.description: EBENE 1, Feinschliff - traegt Gelenkwinkel in einem Frame NACH, ohne die uebrigen Kanaele anzufassen. Das ist der Unterschied zu set_pose: dort ist das Schluesselbild die ganze Haltung, hier bleibt alles Ungenannte stehen. MEHRERE KANAELE IN EINEM AUFRUF: nimm joints wie bei set_pose, also {frame, joints:{arm_l:{lift:-30,swing:68}, arm_r:{lift:-30,swing:68}}}. Ein einzelner Kanal geht weiterhin mit {frame, joint, channel, angleDeg}. Rufe NICHT viermal hintereinander fuer denselben Frame auf - dafuer gibt es joints. Eine ganze Haltung setzt man mit set_pose. Gelenk- und Kanalnamen kommen aus describe_rig; Werte ausserhalb der gemessenen Gelenkgrenze werden beim Loesen geklemmt und gemeldet. Auf einem Frame OHNE Haltung entsteht dabei ein neues Schluesselbild - es traegt nur diesen einen Kanal und keine Hoehe. Zwischen zwei gesetzten Hoehen (Sprung, Salto) gilt dort weiter die gesetzte Bahn; steht die Figur an dieser Stelle am Boden, setze die Hoehe mit set_pose ausdruecklich.

joints.description: MEHRERE Kanaele auf einmal: Gelenkname auf Kanalname auf Grad, z. B. {"arm_l": {"lift": -30, "swing": 68}}. Nicht genannte Kanaele des Frames bleiben unveraendert. Statt joint/channel/angleDeg zu verwenden.

channel.description: Kanalname des Gelenks, z. B. bend, lift, flex, shrug — welche es an welchem Gelenk gibt, sagt describe_rig

tools.name: set_pose
tools.description: EBENE 1, DER HAUPTWEG - setzt eine ganze Koerperhaltung auf einen Frame: alle Gelenke in einem Aufruf, so wie ein Animator ein Schluesselbild setzt. So arbeitet man hier: mehrere Haltungen auf verschiedene Frames setzen; dazwischen wird beim Loesen ueberblendet, weich oder linear (ease). BODEN: die Figur steht immer auf dem Boden, solange du keine Hoehe setzt - der Loeser senkt die Wurzel je Frame so ab, dass der tiefste Punkt auf der Bodenebene liegt (Hocke, Stand, Schritt brauchen kein root). Eine Zahl in root.pos[1] hebt sie an (Sprung, Flug); unter den Boden geht es nie, zu tief Gesetztes wird angehoben und gemeldet. Die Antwort sagt dir mit Zahl, ob sie steht, schwebt oder angehoben wurde. Danach mit look ansehen und mit describe_pose nachmessen. Die angegebenen Gelenke ERSETZEN die Haltung dieses Frames, und das Schluesselbild ist die GANZE Haltung: jeder Kanal, den du hier nicht nennst, steht auf diesem Frame in der Ruhelage (0). Willst du einen Winkel behalten, nenne ihn wieder. set_joint dagegen ist ein Nachtrag und laesst die uebrigen Kanaele in Ruhe. Gelenk- und Kanalnamen kommen aus describe_rig und sind je Gelenk verschieden.

frame.description: Frame, auf dem die Haltung sitzt

joints.description: Gelenkname auf Kanal auf Grad, z. B. {"arm_l": {"lift": 70, "swing": 10}, "elbow_l": {"bend": 80}} — welche Gelenke und Kanäle es gibt, sagt describe_rig

root.description: WO die Figur steht und wohin sie schaut. Ohne root bleibt sie an ihrem Ort und steht auf dem Boden. {pos: [x, y, z]} in Metern im Weltsystem aus describe_world; y = null heisst "auf dem Boden" (der Loeser rechnet die Hoehe), eine Zahl in y ist eine feste Hoehe. {turnGrad: Zahl} dreht die ganze Figur um die Hochachse. Ein Schritt: pos [x, null, z] wandert entlang der Blickrichtung, die Hoehe bleibt am Boden. Ein Sprung: Absprungframe mit ease "wurf" (y = null: vom Boden weg, oder eine Zahl), Landeframe mit y = null. Flugdauer und Scheitelhoehe haengen zusammen: der Abstand der beiden Frames bestimmt, wie hoch die Parabel steigt. Flugposen dazwischen (Tuck, Drehung) OHNE pos setzen - sie folgen der Wurfbahn; drehGrad darf dabei stehen. Eine Hoehe im Flug teilt die Parabel in zwei Boegen mit Knick, den validate als Ballistikfehler meldet. Zwischen gesetzten Frames wird die Wurzel wie alles andere ueberblendet.

pos.description: Position des Beckens [x, y, z] in Metern; y = null stellt die Figur auf den Boden

turnGrad.description: Kurzform fuer drehGrad.y — Drehung um die Hochachse in Grad

drehGrad.description: Drehung der ganzen Figur in Grad, je Achse. x = Salto vorwaerts/rueckwaerts (Nicken), y = Drehung im Stand (Gieren), z = seitliches Kippen (Rollen). Ein Rueckwaertssalto ist x von 0 auf -360 ueber die Flugphase; eine halbe Drehung im Stand ist y von 0 auf 180. Wird zwischen Schluesselbildern ueberblendet, Achse fuer Achse — volle Umdrehungen bleiben dabei volle Umdrehungen.

ease.description: Übergang zum nächsten gesetzten Frame. "wurf" ist der freie Fall: der SCHWERPUNKT folgt exakt der Wurfparabel - also genau die Groesse, die die Ballistikpruefung misst. Auch wenn sich die Pose im Flug aendert (Salto, Hocke, Schwungbein), wandert der Schwerpunkt dann nicht gegenueber der Bahn: der Loeser rechnet die Wurzelhoehe je Frame dazu. Die y-Werte, die du an den Schluesselbildern setzt, bleiben WURZELHOEHEN und werden genau getroffen. Nimm ihn fuer die Flugphase - dann genuegen zwei Schluesselbilder fuer den ganzen Flug, und die Ballistikpruefung ist still. Sonst einer von 4: smooth, linear, hold, wurf; ohne Angabe smooth

tools.name: measure
tools.description: DEIN MESSGERAET - du richtest es selbst aus. Statt fertiger Urteile bekommst du sieben Grundmessungen, die du beliebig kombinierst, um zu pruefen, ob eine Haltung stimmt. Beispiel Hocke: steht das Knie vor dem Zeh (abstand_vorne knee_l/toe_l), neigt sich der Rumpf nach vorne (neigung pelvis/neck), sitzt die Huefte hinter dem Knoechel (abstand_vorne pelvis/ankle_l)? Beispiel Schritt: wandert der Fuss (tempo), bleibt der andere stehen? Jede Bewegung braucht andere Fragen - stell sie. Koerperteile sind Rollennamen aus describe_rig, dazu "com" fuer den Schwerpunkt und "sole_l" / "sole_r" fuer den tiefsten Sohlenpunkt je Fuss - damit misst du, ob ein Fuss auf dem Boden steht (hoehe sole_l = 0). Der Fussknochen selbst sitzt Zentimeter ueber der Sohle. Alle Laengen in Metern, Winkel in Grad.

frame.description: Frame, in dem gemessen wird. Fuer mehrere Frames nimm frames.

frames.description: Mehrere Frames auf einmal, 1 bis 20. Dieselben Fragen werden auf jeden davon angewendet - so bekommst du einen Verlauf in EINEM Aufruf statt einem Aufruf je Frame. Ersetzt frame.

fragen.description: Was du wissen willst. Je Frage {art, a, ...}: hoehe {a} - Hoehe ueber dem Boden. abstand {a, b} - Luftlinie zwischen zwei Teilen. abstand_vorne {a, b} - wie weit a vor b liegt, entlang der Blickrichtung; negativ heisst dahinter. abstand_seite {a, b} - wie weit a neben b liegt. abstand_hoch {a, b} - wie weit a ueber b liegt. winkel {a, b, c} - Winkel bei b zwischen den Strecken zu a und c. neigung {a, b} - wie weit die Strecke a nach b von der Senkrechten abweicht; 0 heisst lotrecht, 90 heisst waagerecht. tempo {a, bisFrame} - Weg pro Sekunde zwischen diesem und jenem Frame. Optional name: dein eigener Name fuer die Messung.

b.description: zweites Koerperteil, wo die Art es braucht

tools.name: list_poses
tools.description: Zeigt alle gesetzten Haltungen mit ihrem Frame, der Zahl der Gelenke und ob eine Wurzelbewegung dabei ist. Der Ueberblick ueber die eigene Arbeit: ohne ihn weisst du nicht, was du schon gesetzt hast, und kannst nichts umsortieren.

tools.name: move_pose
tools.description: Verschiebt eine gesetzte Haltung auf einen anderen Frame — der Schritt, mit dem du den zeitlichen Ablauf zurechtrueckst, nachdem die Haltungen stehen. Kommt eine Bewegung zu frueh, ruecke sie nach hinten, statt sie neu zu bauen. Auf dem Zielframe darf noch keine Haltung liegen.

von.description: Frame, auf dem die Haltung jetzt liegt

tools.name: delete_pose
tools.description: Loescht eine gesetzte Haltung. Danach wird an dieser Stelle zwischen den benachbarten Haltungen durchgeblendet, als haette es sie nie gegeben. Fuer Haltungen, die sich als falsch erwiesen haben — undo nimmt nur den letzten Schritt zurueck.

frame.description: Frame, dessen Haltung weg soll

tools.name: describe_pose
tools.description: Sagt in Zahlen, wie die Figur in einem Frame steht: Weltpositionen der Koerperteile in Metern, Schwerpunkt, Bodenkontakt, bodenabstand_m (tiefster Punkt ueber dem Boden, 0 = steht, negativ = im Boden), wurzelhoehe (ob Boden, dein root.pos oder eine Anhebung die Hoehe bestimmt hat, mit Betrag), sohlen_m je Fuss — dort steht neben der tiefsten Sohle GETRENNT die Hoehe von ferse und spitze sowie stand: flach, zehenstand, fersenstand oder frei. Nur so siehst du, WIE der Fuss aufliegt: eine Figur auf Zehenspitzen meldet als tiefsten Punkt ebenfalls 0, waehrend ihre Ferse handbreit in der Luft haengt. Dazu, ob der Frame eine gesetzte Haltung ist oder eine Ueberblendung. Dazu winkel_grad — die gefahrenen Gelenkwinkel je Gelenk und Kanal in Grad, auch auf ueberblendeten Frames — und gesetzteWinkel_grad, nur die, die auf diesem Frame gesetzt wurden. Damit liest du deine Haltung in deiner eigenen Sprache zurueck. Das Gegenstueck zu look: dort das Bild, hier die Zahlen.

frame.description: Frame, dessen Haltung gefragt ist

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Nimmt die letzte Aenderung zurueck, egal von welchem Werkzeug. Eine einzelne Haltung loescht du mit delete_pose, verschiebst sie mit move_pose und ueberschreibst sie, indem du set_pose erneut auf denselben Frame aufrufst - dafuer brauchst du undo nicht.

tools.name: validate
tools.description: Prueft die gesamte Bewegung und meldet, was nicht stimmt: Bodendurchdringung, Selbstdurchdringung, verletzte Gelenkgrenzen, rutschende Fuesse, Gleichgewicht, Flugbahn - jeweils mit Frame und Betrag in Metern oder Grad. Dazu die mit set_intent gesetzten Kriterien. Liefert immer einen Bildstreifen mit. Braucht gesetzte Kriterien.

tools.name: trace
tools.description: Zeigt den ABLAUF der Bewegung als Folge von drei GROSSEN Einzelbildern in einer Antwort - gleichmaessig ueber die Timeline verteilt, in derselben Kamera, wie ein Daumenkino zu lesen. Damit siehst du, ob eine Bewegung flieszt, ohne jeden Frame einzeln anzufordern. Willst du einen Abschnitt genauer sehen, gib von und bis an - dann liegen die drei Bilder enger beieinander. Kamera wie bei look. RUFE DAS AUF, BEVOR DU EINE BEWEGUNG ABGIBST: ein einzelner Frame sagt nichts darueber, wie die Bewegung laeuft.

von.description: Erster Frame des Abschnitts. Ohne Angabe der Anfang der Timeline.

bis.description: Letzter Frame des Abschnitts. Ohne Angabe das Ende der Timeline.

richtung_grad.description: Woher die Kamera blickt: 0 von vorn, 90 von links, 180 von hinten, 270 von rechts. Standard 30. In allen drei Bildern gleich.

hoehe_grad.description: Wie hoch die Kamera steht: 0 auf Augenhoehe, 90 von oben. Standard 10. Fuer Schritte und Fussstellung ist 90 gut.

ziel.description: Worauf die Kamera zielt: "figur" (Standard) oder ein Gelenk aus describe_rig. Mit weite "nah" verfolgst du ein Gelenk durch die Zeit.

weite.description: Wie viel im Bild ist: "ganz" die Figur (Standard), "halb" ein Koerperteil, "nah" ein Gelenk.

tools.name: look
tools.description: Fotografiert EINEN Frame und liefert EIN grosses Bild, annotiert mit Bodengitter, Hoehenleiste, Schwerpunkt, Kontaktpunkten und Stuetzflaeche. Du richtest die Kamera selbst: Blickrichtung, Blickhoehe, worauf sie zielt und wie nah sie herangeht. Ohne Angabe steht sie schraeg von vorn und zeigt die ganze Figur. DEN VERLAUF EINER BEWEGUNG SIEHST DU, INDEM DU MEHRMALS AUFRUFST - je Frame ein Bild, z. B. 0, 6, 12, 18. Bei gleicher weite ist der Massstab in jedem Bild derselbe und das Bodengitter steht fest im Raum, die Bilder sind also untereinander vergleichbar. Einen Fehler an einem Gelenk findest du mit ziel und weite: nah heran, dann siehst du ihn. Braucht keine Vorbereitung und keine Kriterien - loest selbst. NACH JEDER AENDERUNG AUFRUFEN: Zahlen allein zeigen nicht, ob eine Bewegung richtig aussieht.

frame.description: Der Frame, den du sehen willst. Ein Aufruf ist ein Bild; fuer eine Abfolge rufe mehrmals mit derselben Kamera auf.

richtung_grad.description: Woher die Kamera blickt, um die Figur herum: 0 von vorn, 90 von links, 180 von hinten, 270 von rechts. Standard 30 - schraeg von vorn, dort verdeckt keine Koerperseite die andere.

hoehe_grad.description: Wie hoch die Kamera steht: 0 auf Augenhoehe, 90 senkrecht von oben (Draufsicht, gut fuer Stand und Fussstellung), negativ von unten. Standard 10.

ziel.description: Worauf die Kamera zielt: "figur" fuer die ganze Figur (Standard) oder ein GELENK aus describe_rig - dieselben Namen, mit denen du set_pose fuetterst, z. B. "knee_l", "arm_r", "spine". Zusammen mit weite "nah" faehrst du damit an das Gelenk heran, das du gerade verstellt hast.

weite.description: Wie viel im Bild ist, gemessen an der Koerperhoehe: "ganz" die ganze Figur (Standard), "halb" etwa ein Koerperteil wie Oberkoerper oder Bein, "nah" ein Gelenk mit seinen Nachbarn - dort erkennst du Durchdringung und Ueberbeugung.

tools.name: hold_foot
tools.description: Nagelt einen Fuss ueber einen Frame-Bereich fest: er bleibt da stehen, wo er zu Beginn des Bereichs steht (auf dem Boden, wenn du keine Hoehe gesetzt hast), auch wenn sich das Becken bewegt.
