Der Loeser rechnet die Beinkette dafuer selbst - du musst keine Gelenkwinkel dafuer suchen; ohne gesetzte Hoehe darf das Becken dabei sinken, so wie beim Gehen. GENAU DAS BRAUCHST DU FUER SCHRITTE: der Standfuss bleibt fest, waehrend die Figur ueber ihn hinweg wandert, der andere schwingt frei - und den haeltst DU ueber dem Boden (Knie beugen, Huefte heben); steckt er im Boden, wird die Figur angehoben und der Anker verfehlt, die Antwort sagt es. Ohne Anker rutschen die Fuesse mit dem Becken mit und validate meldet es. Mehrere Anker sind erlaubt; foot "beide" nagelt beide Fuesse fest. EINE SPANNE AENDERST DU MIT EINEM AUFRUF: ruf hold_foot mit demselben Fuss und der neuen Spanne, sie ersetzt jede alte, die sie beruehrt - kein remove noetig. Der Fuss bleibt dabei an dem Ort, an dem der alte Anker ihn hielt, auch wenn der Anfang wandert. Setze sie ERST, wenn die Haltungen stehen: sie wirken nach den Haltungen. Deine gesetzten Beinwinkel bleiben dabei stehen; reicht der Rest der Kette nicht bis zum Anker, gibt die Huefte nach und der Bericht nennt den Fuss mit dem Betrag in Metern, der fehlt.

foot.description: Fussrolle aus describe_rig: foot_l, foot_r oder beide

von.description: erster Frame, in dem der Fuss steht

bis.description: letzter Frame, in dem er steht

remove.description: true entfernt alle Anker dieses Fusses in diesem Bereich

tools.name: export_clip
tools.description: Schreibt die fertige Bewegung als glTF heraus, mit Wurzelbewegung, in Metern und Y-oben. Letzter Schritt, wenn die Bewegung steht.

sites.name: waymark-sable.vercel.app
sites.description: Learning roadmaps you and your agent build together. Your agent researches and plans; you learn; the path adapts.

tools.name: create_path
tools.description: Create a new learning path for the user. Call this first when the user asks to learn a topic. Returns the path_id used by all other tools.

topic.description: What the user wants to learn

goal.description: The user's concrete end goal

tools.name: add_step
tools.description: Add a learning step (article, video, exercise, project, or quiz) to a path. Provide `why` — a one-sentence rationale shown to the user on the step card. URLs are validated server-side; dead links are rejected.

position.description: Insert index; omit to append

url.description: Resource link. For videos prefer YouTube URLs — they embed in the page and the user's watch progress is tracked for you.

why.description: Why this step, in one sentence

phase.description: Curriculum phase this step belongs to (e.g. 'Fundamentals', 'Capstone'). Steps are grouped under phase headings in the UI.

tools.name: remove_step
tools.description: Remove a step from a path. Fails if the user has locked the step — locked steps are under the user's control and must not be removed.

tools.name: get_path
tools.description: Read the full current state of a learning path, including step order, statuses, locks, and user notes.

tools.name: list_paths
tools.description: List all of the user's learning paths. Call this on a return visit to re-orient yourself.

tools.name: mark_step
tools.description: Update a step's progress status on the user's behalf, optionally attaching a note about their experience.

tools.name: update_step
tools.description: Edit a step's title, resource URL, rationale, kind, or time estimate. Fails on user-locked steps.

tools.name: reorder_steps
tools.description: Reorder a path's steps. Provide the complete list of step ids in the new order. User-locked steps must stay at their current positions.

tools.name: record_note
tools.description: Attach a note to a step on the user's behalf — their reaction to a resource, a confusion, a takeaway. Notes are shown on the step card and inform future adaptation.

tools.name: get_progress
tools.description: Read a progress summary for a path: per-step statuses, notes, completion counts, remaining time, and days since last activity. watched_percent is measured from the embedded video player (reliable). engaged_minutes is time spent away after opening an external resource — a rough attention signal, not verified consumption. Call this on a return visit before suggesting what to do next.

tools.name: create_quiz
tools.description: Create a multiple-choice quiz attached to a step. The USER answers it in the page UI — do not answer it yourself. Set reveal: 'on_step_done' to author quizzes ahead of time — the page shows the quiz automatically when the user finishes the step. Give each question a `remedial` follow-up step; if the user misses that question, the page automatically proposes it (user approves) even with no agent present. When you're in the loop live, call await_quiz_results after creating.

step_id.description: The step this quiz checks understanding of

reveal.description: on_step_done hides the quiz until the user marks the step done (default: immediately)

remedial.description: Follow-up step auto-proposed to the user if they miss this question

tools.name: get_quiz_results
tools.description: Read the user's answers to a quiz. Returns pending status until the user submits in the page. Use missed questions to adapt the path.

tools.name: await_quiz_results
tools.description: Wait (block) until the user submits a quiz in the page, then return their results — call this right after create_quiz instead of polling. Returns pending if the timeout passes first; you can call it again.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait before giving up (5–300, default 60)

tools.name: propose_revision
tools.description: Propose a set of path changes for the USER to accept or decline in the page UI — use this instead of direct edits when a change is significant (inserting remedial steps after a failed quiz, restructuring a phase) or touches user-locked steps. The user's accept is their consent, so proposals MAY include locked steps. Poll get_proposal_status afterwards.

reason.description: Why you're proposing this, in one or two sentences. Shown to the user.

position.description: add_step: insert index; omit to append

step_id.description: remove_step / update_step

tools.name: await_proposal_decision
tools.description: Wait (block) until the user accepts or declines a proposal in the page — call this right after propose_revision instead of polling. Accepted ops are already applied when this returns. Returns pending if the timeout passes first.

timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait before giving up (5–300, default 60)

tools.name: get_proposal_status
tools.description: Check whether the user accepted or declined a proposal. Accepted ops are already applied — read the path with get_path afterwards. A declined proposal should be respected, not retried.

tools.name: highlight_step
tools.description: Point the user at one step on the page: it scrolls into view with your short message attached. Use when telling the user where to pick up or what to look at — the message should say why.

message.description: One sentence shown in a bubble on the step

tools.name: create_flashcards
tools.description: Attach a flashcard deck to a step for the USER to review in the page — front is the prompt, back is the answer. Good after the user finishes a concept-heavy step. Check retention later with get_review_stats.

tools.name: get_review_stats
tools.description: Read the user's flashcard results for a deck: per-card seen/got-it counts and last result. Cards repeatedly marked 'again' signal concepts to reinforce with remedial steps or a quiz.

tools.name: plan_weeks
tools.description: Assign steps to calendar weeks (1-based) so the path fits the user's stated hours per week — each step shows its week badge in the UI. Provide an assignment for every step you want scheduled; steps omitted keep their current week.

sites.name: weave.eo2suite.com
sites.description: AI-native creator workspace with local-first files, knowledge workflows, and multi-agent orchestration

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List all EO2Weave projects with their folder counts and last access time.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a new EO2Weave project. Folders (local directories) are attached separately by the user in the UI — a new project starts empty.

tools.name: list_mounted_folders
tools.description: List the local folders the user has granted EO2Weave access to (path, owning project, read-only flag). Conversations are bound to one of these folders — use this to find which folder a task should target, then list_conversations to find conversations working on it.

tools.name: list_conversations
tools.description: List conversations (metadata only, no message bodies), newest first. Filter by mounted folder to find conversations that operate on it.

folderId.description: Only conversations bound to this mounted folder id (from list_mounted_folders)

limit.description: Max entries to return (default 20, max 100)

offset.description: Offset for paging

tools.name: search_conversations
tools.description: Full-text search across all conversations (titles + message bodies). Supports optional project and time-window filters (Unix epoch ms). Returns conversation ids, titles and matched excerpts — the semantic way to locate "the conversation where we discussed X".

query.description: Keyword or phrase to search for

updatedAfter.description: Unix epoch ms lower bound on conversation updatedAt

limit.description: Max results (default 10, max 50)

tools.name: create_conversation
tools.description: Create a new conversation. NOTE: a new conversation has NO mounted folder — it cannot operate on files until the user mounts a folder in the UI. For file tasks prefer an existing conversation bound to the target folder (list_mounted_folders + list_conversations).

tools.name: rename_conversation
tools.description: Rename a conversation. Marks the title as manual (auto-title generation will not overwrite it). Operates on THIS EO2Weave instance only — when multiple instances are open, use the variant matching the conversation’s origin.

tools.name: get_messages
tools.description: Read the message history of a conversation, newest page first. Content is the final text per message; tool-call details are omitted. Single messages over 32KB are truncated with truncated:true.

page.description: 1 = newest page (default)

pageSize.description: Messages per page (default 50, max 200)

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a user message into a conversation and start the EO2Weave agent on it. Runs with the app’s currently configured provider/model (see list_providers / set_default_model). By default returns immediately with status "started" — poll get_run_status / get_run_progress for progress. wait=true blocks (max timeoutMs, hard cap 300s) and returns the final result with the agent’s summary and changed files. If the conversation already has a run in progress the message is queued (status "queued"). The conversation must have a mounted folder for file-manipulation tasks.

content.description: Message text (the task for the agent)

wait.description: Block until the run finishes (default false). Caps at 55s — for longer tasks use wait=false and poll get_run_status.

timeoutMs.description: Max wait when wait=true (default 50000, hard cap 55000 — the extension relay times out at 60s)

tools.name: get_run_status
tools.description: Get the status and (when finished) the result of a run started with send_message. Result includes the agent’s final summary, the list of changed files, and token usage.

runId.description: Run id from send_message

tools.name: get_run_progress
tools.description: Live progress of a running run: elapsed time, completed tool-call count, the tool currently executing (name + argument preview) and a preview of the streaming output. Use to report progress or detect liveness. For finished runs returns only the terminal status.

runId.description: Run id from send_message

tools.name: cancel_run
tools.description: Cancel a running or queued run.

runId.description: Run id from send_message

tools.name: read_folder_file
tools.description: Read a file from the workspace of the given conversation (path relative to the folder root). NOTE: this is the workspace copy — changes reach the real local disk when the user syncs to disk.

conversationId.description: Conversation whose workspace to read from

path.description: Relative path, e.g. "src/App.tsx"

tools.name: write_folder_file
tools.description: Write a file into the workspace of the given conversation (creates parent folders, overwrites existing). Goes to the workspace copy — the user syncs to the real disk from the UI. Useful to hand documents/specs to the agent before send_message.

conversationId.description: Conversation whose workspace to write into

path.description: Relative path, e.g. "specs/fix-login.md"

content.description: Full file content (text)

tools.name: list_folder_files
tools.description: List files under a path in the conversation’s workspace. Paths are relative to the folder root. depth 0 = direct children only.

path.description: Relative directory path (default "" = folder root)

tools.name: list_providers
tools.description: List every LLM provider configured in the app: whether an API key / OAuth is set up, its pinned (frequently used) models, and which provider+model is currently the global default used by all new runs.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: List all models available for a provider (live catalog when the provider supports fetching, cached otherwise). Pinned models are flagged.

tools.name: add_pinned_model
tools.description: Add a model to a provider’s pinned (frequently used) list.

tools.name: remove_pinned_model
tools.description: Remove a model from a provider’s pinned list.

tools.name: send_scouts
tools.description: Plans a stay or outing in Provence (Bouches-du-Rhône) from one fuzzy wish in any language: 'romantic weekend, good food, not too touristy', 'j'hésite entre les Alpilles et la côte'. Use when the visitor expresses a desire rather than a precise query, even with no place named. Runs 2-4 scout searches over the official Provence Tourisme catalogue (2798 places, 3600+ dated events) and plants keep/dismiss flags on the shared map. Search terms in French; mission and labels in the visitor's language.

mission.description: The visitor's desire in one short sentence, IN THE VISITOR'S LANGUAGE (shown on screen).

label.description: Short label for this scout IN THE VISITOR'S LANGUAGE, e.g. "villages du Luberon" / "Luberon villages".

query.description: Free-text search, FRENCH terms.

tags.description: Tag slugs (ALL required). Call explain_vocabulary for slugs.

cluster.description: One of the five myProvence guide clusters.

month.description: Month, YYYY-MM.

scouts.description: 2 to 4 DIFFERENT search angles on the same desire.

tools.name: filter_places
tools.description: Searches the official Provence Tourisme catalogue: 2798 hotels, campings, chambres d'hôtes, leisure and 232 walking/cycling routes in the Bouches-du-Rhône. Use for precise lodging or activity questions about Provence, any language: "hôtel avec piscine", "que faire à Marseille". Translate query terms and tags to French. Filters: tag slugs (see explain_vocabulary), town, cluster, stars, free-text. Results carry canonical myprovence.fr URLs and light the shared map. A fuzzy wish fits send_scouts.

cluster.description: Restrict to one cluster. Omit to search all 2798 places.

tags.description: Tag slugs, ALL of which must be present. Example: ["parking","animaux-acceptes"]. Call explain_vocabulary for the full list.

anyTags.description: Tag slugs, ANY of which is enough.

town.description: Town name, e.g. "Marseille". Matched case- and accent-insensitively.

query.description: Free-text keyword search over names, towns, summaries and criteria labels, accent-insensitive. The catalogue is FRENCH: translate terms to French first ("Schwimmbad" -> "piscine", "dog friendly" -> "animaux acceptes"). Example: "street food".

limit.description: Maximum results. Hard cap 100; page with offset for the rest.

tools.name: explain_vocabulary
tools.description: The catalogue filters by opaque numeric tags (parking is term 469). This tool publishes the human vocabulary: every tag slug, its French label, which Drupal vocabulary it belongs to, and how many places carry it. Pass query to search, omit it for the most common tags. Use the returned slugs with filter_places.

query.description: Optional label/slug fragment to search for, e.g. "piscine".

tools.name: get_place
tools.description: Returns the full official record of one Provence place instantly: name, town, cluster, star rating, all tags as readable slugs, coordinates, summary and the canonical myprovence.fr URL. Use when the visitor asks about one specific place — "tell me more about that hotel", "does it have parking?", "c'est comment, ce camping ?". Look it up by id (from any earlier result) or by its myprovence.fr URL.

id.description: The place id, from filter_places results.

url.description: A myprovence.fr page URL or path, e.g. "/les-guides/hebergements/hotels/...".

tools.name: compare_places
tools.description: Compares 2 to 5 catalogue places side by side on a shared attribute matrix (town, rating, which tags each has or lacks) straight from the official record. Use when the visitor hesitates between places already found here — "which of the two has parking AND a pool?", "lequel est le mieux placé ?". Highlights the compared places on the shared map so the visitor sees the same comparison.

ids.description: 2 to 5 place ids to compare side by side.

tools.name: find_near
tools.description: Radius search over the official catalogue around a named town or a lat/lng point, optionally within one cluster. Use for any distance-shaped question about Provence places: "near Cassis", "within 10 km of Aix", "autour des calanques", "close to the station". Returns places sorted by distance in km and recentres the map the visitor is watching. Only places with known coordinates are searched.

town.description: Centre on a known town, e.g. "Cassis".

cluster.description: One of the five myProvence guide clusters.

tools.name: find_events
tools.description: Searches the official Provence Tourisme agenda: 3600+ dated events in the Bouches-du-Rhône (festivals, concerts, marchés, expos). Use for what-is-happening questions in Provence — "que faire ce week-end", a month, a town — any language; translate query terms to French. Filters: free-text query, month ("2026-10"), from/to, category, town, tags. Chronological results with dates and canonical myprovence.fr URLs, lit on the shared map. find_tonight covers "tonight"; send_scouts covers fuzzy wishes.

month.description: Whole-month shorthand, e.g. "2026-10" for October 2026. Overrides from/to.

from.description: Window start (inclusive).

to.description: Window end (inclusive).

category.description: Agenda category slug from the event URLs, e.g. "concert", "marche", "visites-guidees", "exposition". Unknown values return the valid list.

query.description: Free-text keyword search over event names, towns and summaries, accent-insensitive. The catalogue is FRENCH: translate terms to French first ("Weihnachtsmarkt" -> "marche de noel"). Example: "street food festival".

tools.name: get_catalog_stats
tools.description: Coverage of the catalogue: total places, count per cluster, number of towns, how many places carry coordinates and tags, and the 25 most common tags with their populations. Call this first to understand what can be asked.

tools.name: set_view
tools.description: Steer the map the visitor is looking at: recentre and zoom. Mutates only the view state of this browser tab; changes nothing anywhere else.

tools.name: highlight_places
tools.description: Marks a set of places on the shared map and result list so the visitor sees the places being discussed. Each search call replaces the map selection, so a final answer stays fully visible when this receives the complete set of cited ids (hotels and events together; events without exact coordinates get town-level pins). Mutates only the view state of this browser tab.

ids.description: Place ids to highlight on the shared map and list.

tools.name: ask_visitor
tools.description: Ask the visitor ONE short question by placing tappable choice cards on the page they are looking at — never ask preferences in chat when this tool is available. Resolves with their tap. If they take longer than ~45s you receive {status:"pending", input_id}: keep helping and collect the answer later with get_input_result. Their choices are decisions, not suggestions.

question.description: One short question, in the visitor language (French here).

options.description: 2-4 short tappable choices.

tools.name: get_input_result
tools.description: Collect the answer to a pending ask_visitor ticket. Statuses: answered (their choice), pending (still deciding — continue helping, retry later), dismissed (they closed the question: respect it, do not re-ask).

input_id.description: The pending ticket returned by ask_visitor.

tools.name: get_visitor_signals
tools.description: The visitor talks with their hands: pings dropped on the map (plus-comme-ca = more like this here, eviter = avoid this area, question = curious about this spot), locks on results (their firm choices — never argue), card answers, typed WISHES (they wrote a desire into the page box: the page only records it — it is waiting for YOU to interpret it and call send_scouts), and yields. Returns gestures since your last call plus current locks and pings. Worth reading before any search or proposal.

tools.name: get_demand_pulse
tools.description: The destination's live agent demand, aggregated by town over the last 7 days (counters only, k-anonymized). Calling it lights the demand layer on the shared map: coral for served demand, bright yellow for requests that found NOTHING — the invisible demand. Narrate one factual line from it, e.g. "84 asks around Marseille this week; the zero-result ones are the offer gaps".

tools.name: get_scout_reports
tools.description: The last scout mission with the visitor's verdicts: kept (their decision, treat as fixed), dismissed (do not re-propose), pending (still deciding). Any plan or postcard grounds itself in these verdicts.

tools.name: find_tonight
tools.description: What is ACTUALLY happening tonight (or a given day) near the visitor: real dated events from the official agenda, sorted by distance when a town or coordinates are given, else within the area the visitor is currently looking at. Use for "ce soir", "tonight", "que faire maintenant", "this weekend" (call once per day). Results carry distance_km and light up on the shared map.

date.description: Day to look at, YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for today (the visitor's day).

town.description: Center the search on this town.

radius_km.description: Walking/driving range in km. Default 15.

tools.name: get_visitor_view
tools.description: The visitor's CURRENT context, live: map viewport with the TOWNS it frames (townsInView, ranked; dominantTown when one leads), zoom, hand-set filters, kept selection, and visible place names. Use when they say "here", "around this", "what am I looking at", and before proposing anything. The viewport is the visitor's true focus: a zoom on one town with the town filter still on "all towns" means THAT town, dominantTown says which.

tools.name: write_postcard
tools.description: Composes the closing keepsake: a short letter from day 2-3 of the trip, first person, in the visitor's language, grounded ONLY in their choices — kept flags, locked cards and the accepted pin all count. The factual footer (places, towns, dates, links) prints automatically from that selection; the body text is the prose on top. Displays full-screen on the page; refuses while no choice exists.

title.description: Postcard title, French, e.g. "Trois jours entre Luberon et mer".

body.description: The letter, written from day 2 or 3 of the trip, first person, French. Mention ONLY places and events from the visitor's kept selection (the factual footer is printed automatically from that selection).

day.description: Which trip day the letter is written from.

tools.name: compose_carnet
tools.description: Composes the briefing pack from the visitor's choices (kept flags, locked cards, accepted pin): a print-ready carnet de voyage with the real photographs, one section per day. Reference ONLY ids from that selection — unknown ids are refused with the valid list. Assign dated events to their day, places to arrival/anytime sections; day labels and notes in the visitor's language. The visitor gets a Download-PDF button.

title.description: Carnet title in the visitor's language, e.g. "Week-end à Cassis".

label.description: Day heading, e.g. "Samedi matin" / "Saturday evening".

itemIds.description: Ids from the KEPT selection only (get_scout_reports / read_visitor_wish).

note.description: One short editorial line for the day.

tools.name: get_agent_demand
tools.description: The Demand Mirror: every tool call made in this session with its arguments and result count. Zero-result calls are demand the catalogue could not answer. Session-scoped; nothing here identifies the visitor.

zeroResultsOnly.description: Return only the requests that found nothing.

sites.name: whentoprofit.vercel.app
sites.description: When will your business become profitable?

tools.name: get_current_project
tools.description: Get a structured snapshot of the currently active WhenToProfit project: the project name, business type, forecast start date, the active scenario, all available scenarios with their decision/event counts, the normalized base assumptions, and the key current financial summary (profitability month, cash-flow-positive month, runway, total revenue, total operating profit, final cash balance, annualized revenue, and simple valuation estimate). Use this to understand what the user is modeling before suggesting any scenario or making changes.

tools.name: get_project_assumptions
tools.description: Get the currently active WhenToProfit project's assumptions grouped by category (revenue drivers, variable costs, fixed operating costs, startup/initial investment). Returns both the raw business-level driver values with human-readable labels and the normalized universal model inputs used by the financial engine. Use this to understand what drives the current forecast before suggesting or analyzing changes.

tools.name: get_active_scenario
tools.description: Get the currently selected WhenToProfit scenario: its id, name, whether it is the Base Case, and every change/event it contains (type, targeted field, value or financing amount, forecast month, calendar month, and whether it is monthly-recuring or one-time). Use this to understand exactly what the user is currently simulating before analyzing or comparing plans. Read-only, never mutates state.

tools.name: get_financial_results
tools.description: Get the complete current forecast results for the active WhenToProfit scenario: a month-by-month table (revenue, variable costs, gross profit, fixed operating costs, operating profit, financing received, cash balance, ARR) and key summary metrics (operational break-even month, cash-flow-positive month, runway, total revenue, total operating profit, final cash). ARR is only reported when applicable to the business type. Read-only — does not change any state.

tools.name: analyze_business
tools.description: Analyze the currently active WhenToProfit project + scenario using the existing forecast results. Returns the revenue trajectory, gross margin, operating margin, profitability timing, cash/runway situation, and a few deterministic observations. Use this after getting project context to move from raw numbers to decision-oriented insight. Read-only — does not change state.

tools.name: explain_metric
tools.description: Explain one WhenToProfit metric to a non-finance user. Provide the metric name (e.g. "operational break-even", "runway", "gross margin", "operating margin", "cash-flow positive", "revenue", "operating profit", "ARR", or "valuation"). Returns what it means, its current value from the live forecast, how WhenToProfit calculates it, and how to interpret it. Read-only.

metric.description: The metric to explain (e.g. 'runway', 'gross margin').

tools.name: calculate_valuation
tools.description: Estimate the current active project's value using WhenToProfit's simplified approach. Tech/SaaS uses a revenue/ARR multiple (default 4x); Retail/F&B uses an operating-profit multiple (default 3x). Optionally override the method and multiple. Returns the method, multiple, underlying metric and value, estimated valuation, and a clear disclaimer that this is a planning estimate, not a professional valuation. Read-only.

method.description: Optional: override the valuation method.

multiple.description: Optional: override the multiple to apply.

tools.name: compare_scenarios
tools.description: Compare WhenToProfit scenarios for the current project by running the existing financial engine for each. Pass an optional array of scenario ids; if omitted, all scenarios are compared. Returns per-scenario total revenue, total operating profit, operational break-even month, cash-flow-positive month, runway, ending cash, ARR (when applicable) and simplified valuation. Deterministic and read-only — does not change the active scenario or any project state.

scenarioIds.description: Optional scenario ids to compare. Defaults to all scenarios.

tools.name: inspect_model_health
tools.description: Check the current WhenToProfit project + active scenario for obvious data integrity problems the model can detect: zero/negative starting cash, invalid (NaN/negative) assumptions, out-of-range percentages, missing forecast start date, or projected cash exhaustion. Returns a structured status (healthy / warning / error), a list of issues, warnings, and the affected assumption keys when known. Read-only.

tools.name: simulate_scenario
tools.description: Test hypothetical WhenToProfit changes WITHOUT saving them. Provide either raw scenario changes or business events (type + date/fromMonth + params). Runs the existing financial engine on the current project's base inputs combined with the hypothetical changes and returns simulated decision metrics (operational break-even, cash-flow-positive month, runway, totals, ARR/valuation) plus a delta summary vs the current active scenario. Side-effect free — the active scenario, project, and localStorage are never modified. Use this to explore 'what if' ideas before committing.

changes.description: Optional raw ScenarioChange[] (set/add/financing).

events.description: Optional business-event list: { type, date? | fromMonth?, params?, label? }.

tools.name: find_path_to_goal
tools.description: Search for a feasible set of deterministic changes that could achieve a financial goal in the current WhenToProfit project. Uses the SAME grid-search solver as the Reach a Goal UI. Goal types: 'target_arr', 'target_annual_revenue', 'target_operating_profit' (monthly operating profit), or 'target_profitability' (become profitable by a target month). Optionally require cash to never go negative. Returns the baseline, recommended candidate path(s) with their changes, projected decision metrics, and trade-offs. Never mutates project state. Use when a user asks 'what would it take to reach X?'.

goal.description: What goal to reach.

targetValue.description: Target value (dollars; for target_profitability this is the month by which profit must be positive).

targetMonth.description: Optional forecast month (1-24) by which the goal must be met. Defaults to month 24.

cashNeverNegative.description: Require projected cash to never go below $0.

tools.name: compare_simulation
tools.description: Run several hypothetical WhenToProfit simulations side by side using the existing financial engine, and return key decision metrics for each plus the current active scenario as a baseline. Each simulation is passed the same way as simulate_scenario (raw changes[] or business events[]). Deterministic and read-only — nothing is persisted and the active scenario never changes.

simulations.description: List of simulations, each { name?, changes? | events? }.

tools.name: create_scenario
tools.description: WRITE: create and SAVE a new scenario for the active WhenToProfit project. The new scenario is empty, becomes the active scenario, and the project is persisted through the normal store. Base Case is never modified. Returns the new scenario id, name, whether it is active, and the project id.

tools.name: add_scenario_event
tools.description: WRITE: add and SAVE a business event/change to an existing NON-Base scenario. Supports the same event types as the UI (hire_people, change_price, change_growth, change_churn, increase_marketing, change_costs, raise_financing, one_time_investment). Provide scenarioId, event type, a date (YYYY-MM) or fromMonth, and event params. Base Case is immutable and rejected. Persists through the normal store and recalculates financial results. To test WITHOUT saving, use simulate_scenario.

scenarioId.description: Target scenario id.

type.description: One of the supported business event types.

date.description: Start date YYYY-MM (in the project's forecast).

params.description: Event parameters keyed by the event type's fields.

label.description: Optional label.

tools.name: update_scenario_event
tools.description: WRITE: modify an existing event/change in a NON-Base scenario. Provide scenarioId and the event id ("change_ "). Update the event type, date/fromMonth, params, or label. Base Case is immutable. Persists through the normal store and recalculates results. Read events first via get_active_scenario to find event ids.

eventId.description: Event id (change_<index>).

type.description: New event type.

params.description: New parameters.

tools.name: move_scenario_event
tools.description: WRITE: move an existing event/change in a NON-Base scenario to a different calendar month. Provide scenarioId, eventId (change_ ), and newDate (YYYY-MM) within the forecast. Base Case is immutable. Persists through the normal store, recalculates results, and returns the old/new dates. Use only when the user intends to change when a decision takes effect.

tools.name: remove_scenario_event
tools.description: WRITE: remove an existing event/change from a NON-Base scenario. Provide scenarioId and eventId ("change_ "). Base Case is immutable. Persists through the normal store, recalculates results, and returns the removed change plus updated metrics.

tools.name: rename_scenario
tools.description: WRITE: rename an existing NON-Base scenario in the active project. Provide scenarioId and a non-empty name. Base Case cannot be renamed. Persists through the normal store.

tools.name: set_active_scenario
tools.description: Switch the UI to a different scenario in the active project. Provide scenarioId. Validates that the scenario belongs to the project, then uses the exact same handler as the UI so scorecards/charts update and stay in sync. This changes which scenario is viewed but does NOT modify any assumptions or events.

scenarioId.description: Scenario id to make active.

tools.name: apply_goal_path
tools.description: WRITE: apply a goal path (candidate changes from find_path_to_goal) to an explicit NON-Base scenario. Each change is validated and applied through the same event-mutation flow the UI uses, then results are recalculated and persisted. Base Case is immutable. Unsupported changes are skipped and reported. Prior steps: find_path_to_goal to obtain a path; create_scenario for a target if needed.

changes.description: Candidate changes from find_path_to_goal.

sites.name: 312deals.com
sites.description: Food and drink deals today across Chicago and the suburbs: 83,000+ deals at 12,000+ restaurants and bars in 149 neighborhoods. Happy hours, Taco Tuesday, wing nights and brunch specials, free.

tools.name: search_chicago_deals
tools.description: Find food and drink deals across 149 Chicago neighborhoods and suburbs. Covers happy hours, daily specials (taco tuesday, wing wednesday), brunch deals, late-night eats, chain app promotions (McDonald's, Chipotle, BWW), game day specials, and seasonal offers at 12,000+ venues. Returns deal title, venue, address, times (when the venue lists them), savings, last_checked_at, and a link to each venue page. Use day="today" for tonight, active_now for right now, checked_within_days to keep only recently confirmed offers. Example: search for "half off wings" in "West Loop" on "thursday".

day.description: Day of week or "today"

query.description: Free-text search, e.g. "oysters", "bottomless mimosas"

active_now.description: Only deals running right now in Chicago (needs listed hours)

price_range.description: Price ceiling: a food or drink item at or under it

price_on.description: With price_range, "food" counts only food items above $0 (for "eat for $10 or less")

min_rating.description: Minimum venue Google rating, 1 to 5 (a venue rating, not proof the offer is current)

checked_within_days.description: Only offers seen on the venue page within this many days (30 is a good default for "current")

limit.description: Max results (default: 20, max: 50)

tools.name: deals_near_location
tools.description: Find active deals near a Chicago address, landmark, or coordinates. Geo-proximity search within a configurable radius. Returns deals sorted by distance. Give either an address or lat/lng. Example: deals near "333 N Michigan Ave" within 0.5 miles.

address.description: Street address or landmark, e.g. "333 N Michigan Ave" or "Wrigley Field" (use this OR lat/lng)

lat.description: Latitude, e.g. 41.8827 (with lng, instead of address)

limit.description: Max results (default: 20, max: 50)

tools.name: get_venue_deals
tools.description: Get all current deals for a specific Chicago venue by name or ID. Returns venue details (address, hours, rating) plus every active deal. Example: get deals for "Big Star" or "Au Cheval".

tools.name: chicago_deal_of_the_day
tools.description: Get today's featured deal in Chicago, the best value deal active right now. Optionally filter by zone. Example: "what's the best deal today?" or "deal of the day in the suburbs".

zone.description: Geographic zone filter

tools.name: chicago_chain_deals
tools.description: Get current national chain restaurant deals in Chicago. McDonald's, Chipotle, BWW, Portillo's, Taco Bell, Wendy's, Chili's, and 9+ more. Includes app-only deals and in-store specials. Example: "Chipotle app deals" or "chain restaurant specials near me".

tools.name: chicago_neighborhood_deals_summary
tools.description: Get counts for a Chicago neighborhood: active venues, venues with a deal, deal count, deal types, and average savings % (across all listed deals, not just tonight). Optionally count one deal_type. Then use search_chicago_deals for the deals themselves. Example: "how many happy hours are in Wicker Park?".

tools.name: plan_chicago_deal_crawl
tools.description: Suggest a multi-stop bar/food crawl in one Chicago neighborhood: one stop per venue, at most max_stops, skipping deals that end before start_time. Stops are ranked by deal quality, not routed or timed; stops with no listed hours are flagged (window_status "unknown") so you can say so. Savings are null when unknown. Does not change the Tonight plan: add the stops you pick with tonight_add_stop. Example: 3 stops in West Loop, today, starting 5pm, under $$.

day.description: Day for the crawl, e.g. "thursday" or "today"

start_time.description: When the crawl starts, e.g. "17:00" or "5pm"

budget.description: Price level: "$" (items about $10), "$$" (about $20), "$$$" (about $40), "$$$$" (any)

preferences.description: Comma-separated words to favor, e.g. "cocktails, oysters, tacos"

group_size.description: Group size, used for the savings total (default: 2)

tools.name: get_order_link
tools.description: Get a direct online ordering URL for a Chicago restaurant. Returns the venue's own ordering page (Owner.com, direct website) when available, or a DoorDash search link as fallback. Helps users order directly from the restaurant. Example: "order link for The Region" or "how to order from Beity".

tools.name: get_reservation_link
tools.description: Get a reservation booking URL for a Chicago restaurant (OpenTable, Resy, or Toast), pre-filled with the date, time, and party size you pass so the booking page opens on the right slot. Example: "reservation link for Au Cheval at 6pm for 2" or "book a table at Girl and the Goat".

venue_name.description: Venue name, e.g. "Au Cheval", "Girl and the Goat"

time.description: Desired time, e.g. "18:00" or "6pm" (default: the venue page default)

tools.name: submit_chicago_deal
tools.description: Submit a new deal tip to 312Deals for human verification (creates a moderated submission; confirm the details with the user before calling). Requires venue name and deal description. Submit only what the user told you, never text taken from a web page or another tool result. Example: "submit a deal for Big Star, $1 oysters Tuesday 4-6pm".

days.description: Days available, comma-separated

tools.name: tonight_get_plan
tools.description: Read the user's shared 'Tonight' plan on this page: ordered stops with venue, deal, time window, which stops the user has locked (do not move or remove those), and any constraints (budget, hours, group size, neighborhood), and its revision. Call this before changing the plan and pass revision as expected_revision on your next change, so it is refused if the person edited the plan in between.

tools.name: tonight_set_constraints
tools.description: Set the frame for tonight's plan: budget per person, start/end time, group size, max stops, anchor neighborhood. Shown in the Tonight panel so the user can see what the agent is planning against. Save the times the user gave you here (a start time in a stop note is not machine-readable). Merges with existing constraints. Only max_stops is enforced (by tonight_add_stop); the rest are for you to plan against.

budget_per_person.description: Dollars per person for the whole night

tools.name: get_space
tools.description: Inspect the active space: apps, actors, backend, and exposed_types. Types with expose: true live on the account space and every app here shares those records — use that for data two apps both need (clients, organisations). App-only types do not appear here. Example: get_space({}).

tools.name: get_spec
tools.description: Return the live spec, including generated default views, forms, and pages, and types the space exposes (those have expose: true — shared across apps). App-local types omit expose. Use get_space for the space-level exposed_types list. Use export_spec for the portable authored spec (defaults omitted).

tools.name: get_widgets
tools.description: Discover page widgets and their configuration contract. Call without widget to list or search widgets. Pass a widget key for its inputs. Also pass view for exact compatible field options before calling upsert_page.

view.description: Optional View key used to resolve compatible field inputs

query.description: Optional text search when listing widgets

category.description: Optional category filter when listing widgets

tools.name: export_spec
tools.description: Export the portable authored spec as YAML or JSON. Generated default views, forms, and pages are omitted; they are recreated from types on import. Use get_spec to inspect the live spec including defaults.

tools.name: query_view
tools.description: Run a named view and return its rows. Views can filter, sort, limit, and derive live grouped measures — list_* returns every source record. Discover view keys via get_spec. Example: query_view({ view: "active_projects" }).

view.description: View key from get_spec

expose.description: Runtime values for the view's expose filters, e.g. { status: "active" }

record_id.description: Current record id when the view filters on $record.id

tools.name: apply_spec
tools.description: Replace the entire active app spec with a YAML or JSON document. Not a merge: types, views, forms, flows, and pages missing from the document are deleted. Generated defaults are recreated from types. Requires confirm: true. A document with no types is refused unless wipe: true — { key: "foo" } is not a full spec. Example: apply_spec({ spec: " ", confirm: true }).

spec.description: Full YAML or JSON document for the app spec

confirm.description: Must be true. apply_spec replaces the entire spec.

wipe.description: Required with confirm if the document has no types and the app already has some.

tools.name: upsert_type
tools.description: Create or update a type and its fields. Use a singular key and label for one record; optional collection_label overrides the automatically pluralized list name (for example label: "Person", collection_label: "People"). Providing fields replaces the type's field list; omitting fields leaves existing fields unchanged. Add or change one field with upsert_field. fields is an array of {key, type, label, ...} or a map of key → field. Enum fields can use presentation: "badge" and explicit value_semantics; number fields can use presentation: "rating". Reference fields need target. expose: true stores the type on the account space so every app shares its records. Omit expose (or false) for app-only types. Example: upsert_type({ key: "person", label: "Person", collection_label: "People", expose: true, fields: [{ key: "name", type: "text", required: true }] }).

collection_label.description: Optional plural label for lists and navigation. Omit it to infer an English plural from label; pass an empty string to clear an existing override.

expose.description: If true, the type lives on the account space and all apps share its records. If false or omitted, the type belongs only to this app.

fields.description: Fields to create with the type. Array of field objects, or a map of field key → field (or shorthand type string).

target.description: Referenced type key (reference fields)

anyOf.description: Shorthand field type, e.g. text

target.description: Referenced type key (reference fields)

tools.name: upsert_field
tools.description: Add or update one field on a type without removing the others. type is the type key; field_type is the field kind: text, number, date, boolean, enum, reference. Enum fields need values and can use presentation: "badge" with explicit value_semantics of neutral, info, success, warning, or danger; use neutral when meaning is unclear. Reference fields need target. A number field can use presentation: "rating", variant: "segments", and max from 2 to 10. Example: upsert_field({ type: "submission", key: "stage", field_type: "enum", values: ["submitted", "winner", "rejected"], presentation: "badge", value_semantics: { submitted: "neutral", winner: "success", rejected: "danger" } }).

type.description: Type key (not the field kind)

target.description: Referenced type key (reference fields)

tools.name: rename_field
tools.description: Rename a field key while keeping its identity and stored values.

tools.name: delete_field
tools.description: Remove a field from a type and drop its SQLite column.

tools.name: upsert_view
tools.description: Create or update a named view (a stored query: filter, sort, limit, columns, or live grouped measures). For a normal view, include fields in the order people should see them, such as fields: ["name", "status", "client.name"]. If fields is omitted while creating a normal view, builder.run chooses up to six useful source fields automatically; an empty fields array is invalid. Omitting fields while updating preserves the existing selection. For a grouped view, omit fields to derive them from group_by and measure aliases. group_by accepts one source field. measures supports count, sum, avg, min, and max; avg accepts field or fields. Sort aggregate aliases with order_by. Run it with query_view. Example: upsert_view({ key: "scores", source: "review", group_by: "submission", measures: { review_count: { op: "count" }, overall_score: { op: "avg", fields: ["quality", "impact"] } }, order_by: { overall_score: "desc" } }).

fields.description: Ordered visible columns for a normal view. Reference labels may use paths such as client.name. Omit on creation to infer useful defaults; omit on update to preserve existing columns; omit for grouped views to derive aggregate columns.

measures.description: Named live aggregates for a grouped view

tools.name: upsert_form
tools.description: Create or update a form over a type. Example: upsert_form({ key: "intake", type: "client", fields: ["name", "email"], mode: "create" }).

tools.name: upsert_flow
tools.description: Create or update a flow. Steps may create, set, delete, query, branch, or invoke other flows. expose: ["agent"] registers invoke_ . Example: upsert_flow({ key: "mark_paid", expose: ["agent"], input: { invoice: "ref(invoice)" }, steps: [{ set: { "invoice.status": "paid" } }] }).

tools.name: upsert_page
tools.description: Create or update a page of grids and widgets. Call get_widgets first to discover widget keys, required values, and compatible fields. Widget values are validated against that contract. Optional folder groups it in the app menu. Optional icon is one of: page, dashboard, table, chart, line, donut, board, calendar, list, inbox, people, money, time. If icon is omitted when creating a page, a one-time default is inferred from its widgets; later edits do not change it. A group nests children in a blocks array even when there is only one widget. columns is how many widgets sit side by side; unused columns stay empty. Example: upsert_page({ key: "board", icon: "board", path: "/board", blocks: [{ kind: "group", columns: 1, blocks: [{ kind: "widget", widget: "table", values: { view: "active_projects" } }] }] }).

blocks.description: Page layout. A group nests children in a blocks array — always an array, even for one widget.

columns.description: Widgets side by side in this group (1–4). Unused cells stay empty.

tools.name: create_app
tools.description: Create an app in the active space and switch to it. The new app can use types the space already exposes (see get_space.exposed_types) — do not recreate those types in the app. Example: create_app({ name: "Invoicing" }).

tools.name: delete_app
tools.description: Delete an app created from this account space. Shared records stay.

tools.name: switch_app
tools.description: Switch the active app by id. Space-exposed types stay available; app-local types change with the app.

tools.name: create_space
tools.description: Create a new account space with its own apps. After switching to it, upsert_type({ expose: true }) creates types every app in this space shares — e.g. a customer type used by both a CRM and invoicing. Example: create_space({ name: "Studio" }).

sites.name: booknbouncestl.com
sites.description: Bounce-house, water-slide and party equipment rentals near St. Charles, Missouri.

tools.name: get-business
tools.description: Business profile: locations, currency, hours, booking lead time, delivery methods, setup surfaces, and AI checkout mode.

tools.name: get-rental
tools.description: Details for one or more rentals: description, dimensions, images, price estimate, and the options tree (accessories, dropdown choices, separate units). Use option ids from here when adding options to a cart.

start_time.description: HH:MM, 24-hour. Optional: defaults to the business's usual start time, reported back as assumed_start_time.

duration_hours.description: Optional: defaults to the business's usual event duration, reported back as assumed_duration_hours. Omit it (or send null) to ask for that default — 0 is not a way to say 'unset' and is refused.

tools.name: check-availability
tools.description: Check whether rentals are available for an event date, time, and duration. Quantity is required — availability depends on it. If start_time or duration_hours is omitted the business default is used and the response says so; confirm any assumed value with the customer before creating a cart.

end_date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Optional: check a whole range in one call — at most 14 days after event_date (wider spans are refused). The response then adds days[], one entry per day from event_date through end_date, each day fully conflict-checked at the same start time and duration. Range rows carry no price_estimate (per-day pricing is skipped for cost); price a chosen day with a single-date check or price-cart.

start_time.description: HH:MM, 24-hour. Optional: defaults to the business's usual start time, reported back as assumed_start_time.

duration_hours.description: Optional: defaults to the business's usual event duration, reported back as assumed_duration_hours. Omit it (or send null) to ask for that default — 0 is not a way to say 'unset' and is refused.

rental_id.description: Rental id from search-rentals or get-rental.

tools.name: price-cart
tools.description: Fast discovery pricing for a set of items on a date. Estimate only: excludes tax, delivery, coupons, and conditional pricing. For exact totals, build a cart and set the event address — never create a quote just to see a price.

start_time.description: HH:MM, 24-hour. Optional: defaults to the business's usual start time, reported back as assumed_start_time.

duration_hours.description: Optional: defaults to the business's usual event duration, reported back as assumed_duration_hours. Omit it (or send null) to ask for that default — 0 is not a way to say 'unset' and is refused.

rental_id.description: Rental id from search-rentals or get-rental.

option_id.description: Option id from the get-rental options tree.

choice_id.description: Chosen dropdown choice id, when the option is a dropdown.

tools.name: get-delivery-options
tools.description: Valid delivery methods for an address, whether the address is in the service area, and a distance-charge preview.

tools.name: create-cart
tools.description: Start a transaction. The event window is the required first step of any booking flow; the returned cart_id is needed by every later cart call. Unlike the discovery tools, this one does NOT assume a start time or duration — both must come from the customer, because this window is what they get quoted and committed to; confirm them when you create the cart, not as part of an up-front question list. Carts are free and invisible to the business — they hold no inventory and expire on their own, so create several to build alternative packages to compare.

start_time.description: HH:MM, 24-hour. Required — ask the customer, do not guess.

duration_hours.description: Required — ask the customer, do not guess.

tools.name: add-to-cart
tools.description: Add items to a cart. Returns the full recalculated cart (price and availability per line) — no follow-up call needed.

rental_id.description: Rental id from search-rentals or get-rental.

option_id.description: Option id from the get-rental options tree.

choice_id.description: Chosen dropdown choice id, when the option is a dropdown.

tools.name: update-cart-item
tools.description: Change quantity or options of items already in the cart. Quantity 0 removes the item. Returns the full recalculated cart.

rental_id.description: Rental id from search-rentals or get-rental.

option_id.description: Option id from the get-rental options tree.

choice_id.description: Chosen dropdown choice id, when the option is a dropdown.

tools.name: get-cart
tools.description: Current cart contents with prices, availability, fees, totals, and what is still missing before a quote can be created. To weigh several candidate carts against each other, use compare-carts instead of reading them one by one.

tools.name: set-cart-details
tools.description: Set contact info, event address, delivery method, setup surface, a coupon code, or a new event window (event_date + start_time) on the cart. Returns the full cart with final tax and delivery. Moving the date re-prices the cart and re-checks availability — useful for comparing the same package on different dates before quoting.

event_date.description: Move the event to a new date (YYYY-MM-DD). The cart re-prices and re-checks availability: items that conflict on the new date stay in the cart flagged has_conflict — only create-quote refuses on conflicts. Requires start_time. Useful for comparing the same package on different dates (weekend pricing can differ).

start_time.description: Event start time (HH:MM, 24-hour). Required when changing event_date — ask the customer, do not guess.

duration_hours.description: Event duration in hours. Omit to keep the cart's CURRENT duration — that is state the customer already set, not an assumption made for them. 0 is not a way to say "unset" and is refused.

surface.description: Setup surface at the event location — a top-level field, not part of event_address. Valid values are the surfaces list from get-business. Required before create-quote.

tools.name: create-quote
tools.description: Turn ONE cart — the package the customer explicitly chose — into a real quote with final pricing (tax, delivery, coupons). This notifies the business, enters their sales queue, and holds inventory: never call it to see a price (cart totals are already exact), and never quote more than one cart per event. Returns a quote reference and whether online booking is possible.

tools.name: create-checkout-session
tools.description: Finish the transaction. Returns links for the customer: quote_url to review and book the quote (nothing is signed at the quote step), and — once the event is booked — payment_url to sign and pay, which is the same contract page contract_url points at. Before booking there is no payment link: the customer books from quote_url and pays on the page that follows. Or (when the business allows agent booking) a booked confirmation. Payment is never taken through this tool.

tools.name: compare-carts
tools.description: Price 2-4 candidate carts side-by-side: per-cart items and exact totals plus computed differences. Read-only — no quote is created, no inventory is held. Use before create-quote so the customer picks one package.

cart_ids.description: 2-4 distinct cart ids (from create-cart) to compare.

tools.name: render-rental-search
tools.description: Render a rental gallery from final search-rentals output. Always call search-rentals first, then pass its complete structured result as data.

data.description: The complete structured result returned by the required data/action tool.

tools.name: render-rental
tools.description: Render rental detail cards from final get-rental output. Always call get-rental first, then pass its complete structured result as data.

data.description: The complete structured result returned by the required data/action tool.

tools.name: render-cart
tools.description: Render a cart from final create-cart, get-cart, add-to-cart, update-cart-item, or set-cart-details output. Call the relevant cart tool first, then pass its complete structured result as data.

data.description: The complete structured result returned by the required data/action tool.

tools.name: render-cart-comparison
tools.description: Render a side-by-side comparison from final compare-carts output. Always call compare-carts first, then pass its complete structured result as data.

data.description: The complete structured result returned by the required data/action tool.

tools.name: render-quote
tools.description: Render a quote receipt from final create-quote output. Always call create-quote first, then pass its complete structured result as data.

data.description: The complete structured result returned by the required data/action tool.

tools.name: search-rentals
tools.description: Search rental items by name, category or keyword — or call it with NO query to browse the catalogue grouped by category. Use the query-less form for "what can I rent?" style questions instead of guessing search terms. One call returns up to 50 items; when more remain the response carries next_cursor — pass it back as cursor to get the next page. Results are limited to items this page can actually rent, verified against the booking system on a best-effort basis.

query.description: Optional. Words to match against item names, categories and descriptions. OMIT to browse the catalogue.

cursor.description: Optional. next_cursor from a previous browse response, to fetch the following page. Opaque — pass it back unchanged. Ignored when a query is given.

sites.name: chessup-gamma.vercel.app
sites.description: Play chess, review a mistake with your browser agent, and practise it on the same board.

tools.name: read_coach_instructions
tools.description: Read this first. Explains how to coach on this board: the human plays the built-in bot, you review from `events`, run puzzle drills with set_puzzle_queue, keep a lesson plan and reward progress. Sparring (playing against the human) is optional. Cheap and read-only.

tools.name: get_game_state
tools.description: Read the board: FEN, turn, status, material, engine evaluation, recent moves, active puzzle and drill progress, the human's recent mistakes (heuristics and Stockfish centipawn loss), `events` since your last call and `next`. Call it every time the human talks to you.

tools.name: get_legal_moves
tools.description: List legal moves in SAN (optionally only for one square, then with from/to details), plus the best capture and any mate in one. Use it to check a move before make_move or to build hints.

square.description: Optional square like 'e2' to list only moves of the piece on that square.

tools.name: undo_move
tools.description: Take back the last N half-moves (default 1) so the human can retry; also reactivates a failed puzzle.

count.description: Number of half-moves to undo. Default 1.

tools.name: analyze_position
tools.description: Run the built-in Stockfish engine on the current position (or a given FEN): evaluation from White's perspective, best move and line, and up to 3 alternatives with their evaluations. Use it to verify a claim before teaching it, to find the best move for a review, or to check a puzzle idea. Depth 8-20 (default 14).

fen.description: Position to analyse. Defaults to the board.

multipv.description: How many best lines to return. Default 1.

tools.name: highlight_squares
tools.description: Colour squares to draw attention: green good/safe, red danger, yellow key square, blue plan, orange warning. Replaces highlights unless append=true. Cleared automatically on the next move.

append.description: Keep existing highlights and add these. Default false.

tools.name: draw_arrows
tools.description: Draw arrows for plans, threats or candidate moves. Replaces arrows unless append=true. Cleared automatically on the next move.

from.description: Start square, e.g. 'g1'.

to.description: End square, e.g. 'f3'.

append.description: Keep existing arrows and add these. Default false.

tools.name: clear_annotations
tools.description: Remove all highlights and arrows from the board.

tools.name: coach_note
tools.description: Show a one-sentence caption under the board (tip, praise, warning, question or info) tied to what is on the board right now. Put explanations in the chat, not here.

text.description: The note text.

kind.description: Visual style of the note. Default 'tip'.

tools.name: set_lesson_plan
tools.description: Replace the lesson plan in the side panel: a title and 3-6 steps with status todo/active/done/skipped. The page seeds a simple plan (play, review, drill) from the profile; replace it with a better one once you know the student, and keep it current with update_lesson_step.

title.description: Plan title, e.g. 'Today: stop hanging pieces'.

tools.name: update_lesson_step
tools.description: Update one lesson step by zero-based index: status (todo/active/done/skipped), title or description. Mark steps active when started and done when completed.

index.description: Zero-based index of the step.

tools.name: award_badge
tools.description: Give a uniquely named badge with an emoji for a real milestone (first puzzle solved, a clean game, a new pattern learned). Badges are permanent in the profile.

tools.name: add_xp
tools.description: Add XP with a reason (negative allowed). Scale: 5-10 for a good move or answer, 20-40 for a puzzle, 50+ for a won game or a finished lesson step. Returns total, level and leveledUp.

amount.description: XP to add (can be negative).

reason.description: Short reason shown to the student.

tools.name: record_mistake
tools.description: Log a mistake the app cannot detect itself (opening, king safety, positional, endgame) into the human's long-term profile with severity, FEN before the move, movePlayed and betterMove. Simple tactical errors are auto-recorded.

severity.description: Default 'mistake'.

description.description: One sentence the student will read later.

fen.description: Position before the mistake. Defaults to the position before the last move.

tools.name: get_player_profile
tools.description: Read the persistent profile: XP, level, badges, game and puzzle stats by theme, mistakes by category, weakestAreas, recent drills, the lesson plan, and candidatePuzzles: validated puzzles built from the human's own mistakes, ready to pass to set_puzzle_queue. Call it at session start and before every drill.

tools.name: make_move
tools.description: Play a move for the side to move. Use it in sparring mode (opponent 'agent') or to demonstrate a line. SAN ('Nf3', 'O-O', 'e8=Q') or from/to. Illegal moves are rejected with the legal list. Refused during the human's turn in an active puzzle. In sparring, follow with wait_for_player_move.

san.description: Move in Standard Algebraic Notation, e.g. 'Nf3'.

from.description: Origin square, e.g. 'e2' (use together with `to`).

to.description: Target square, e.g. 'e4'.

promotion.description: Promotion piece when a pawn reaches the last rank. Defaults to queen.

comment.description: Optional short explanation shown to the human next to the move.

tools.name: new_game
tools.description: Reset to the starting position. Choose the human's colour and the opponent: 'bot' (default, built-in engine level 1-3, instant), 'agent' (sparring: you play via make_move + wait_for_player_move) or 'human' (they play both sides). Clears any puzzle or drill.

playerColor.description: Colour the human plays. Default white.

opponent.description: Who plays the other side. Default 'bot'; 'agent' = sparring with you.

botLevel.description: Strength of the built-in bot when opponent is 'bot'.

cancelDrill.description: Set true to abandon an active drill on purpose.

tools.name: set_position
tools.description: Put a FEN on the board, or a single puzzle when you add title, goal, hint, theme and a SAN `solution` (human's move first, alternating sides). The app validates the line, auto-plays replies and grades the human. For several puzzles use set_puzzle_queue. Without title/goal/solution it only sets the position.

fen.description: Full FEN string, e.g. 'r1bqkb1r/pppp1ppp/2n2n2/4p2Q/2B1P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB1K1NR w KQkq - 4 4'.

goal.description: What the student must achieve, e.g. 'White to play and win a piece'.

hint.description: Optional hint the student can reveal.

theme.description: Tactical/strategic theme tag for tracking, e.g. 'fork', 'pin', 'mate_in_1'.

solution.description: Solution line in SAN, student's move first, alternating sides. e.g. ['Qxf7#'] or ['Nxe5','Nxe5','Qh5+','g6','Qxe5'].

playerColor.description: Which colour the student plays. Defaults to the side to move in the FEN.

cancelDrill.description: Set true to abandon an active drill on purpose.

tools.name: set_puzzle_queue
tools.description: Start a drill: 3-5 puzzles the app serves one by one, grades against the solution, auto-plays replies, awards XP and records results per theme. Each puzzle: fen, title, goal, optional hint, theme, and a SAN `solution` (human's move first, alternating). Every line is checked for legality and by Stockfish (the human's moves must be best); rejected puzzles come back with the reason. After calling it, END YOUR TURN; the human tells you when done.

fen.description: Full FEN of the puzzle position.

goal.description: What to achieve, e.g. 'White to play and win a piece'.

hint.description: Optional hint the human can reveal.

cancelDrill.description: Set true to replace an active drill on purpose.

tools.name: get_decision_state
tools.description: Read the current live public-property workspace without changing it.
