id.description: Unique dataset Id (required for search_data tools)

slug.description: Human-readable unique identifier for the dataset, used in URLs

summary.description: A brief summary of the dataset content

description.description: A markdown description of the dataset content

page.description: Link to the dataset page (must be included in responses as citation source)

count.description: Total number of data rows in the dataset

origin.description: Source or provider of the dataset

license.description: Dataset license information (must be included in responses)

geolocalized.description: Whether the dataset has geographic data

bbox.description: Geographic bounding box [lonMin, latMin, lonMax, latMax]

temporalDataset.description: Whether the dataset has temporal data

startDate.description: Start date of the time period

endDate.description: End date of the time period

timePeriod.description: Time period covered by the dataset

key.description: Column identifier

type.description: Data type of the column

enum.description: List of all possible values for this column

enumTruncated.description: Whether the enum list was truncated because it exceeded 20 values

enumTotal.description: Total number of enum values before truncation

labels.description: Object mapping actual data values (keys) to human-readable labels (values). Use keys for filters.

concept.description: Semantic concept associated with the column

schema.description: Dataset column schema with types and metadata

sampleLines.description: Array of 3 sample data rows showing real values from the dataset. Use these examples to understand exact formatting, casing, and typical values for _eq and _search filters.

tools.name: get_dataset_schema
tools.description: Get column schema and 3 sample rows for a dataset. Call this when you do not already know the column keys and types — if they were provided to you (e.g. by the parent assistant), skip it and query directly. A rejected filter/sort/metric returns a 400 listing the column's valid operations, so you can self-correct without fetching the schema upfront.

datasetId.description: The exact dataset ID from the "id" field in list_datasets results. Do not use the title or slug.

tools.name: search_data
tools.description: Search for data rows in a dataset using full-text search or column filters. Returns matching rows as CSV. Do NOT use for statistics — use calculate_metric or aggregate_data instead.

datasetId.description: The exact dataset ID from the "id" field in list_datasets results. Do not use the title or slug.

q.description: French keywords for full-text search across all dataset columns (simple keywords, not sentences). Can be combined with filters, but prefer filters alone when criteria target specific columns. Use query for broad keyword matching across all columns. Examples: "Jean Dupont", "Paris", "2025"

filters.description: Column filters as key-value pairs: column_key + suffix, all values strings. Example: { "ville_eq": "Paris", "age_lte": "30", "nom_search": "Jean" }. Suffixes include _eq, _in, _gt/_lt, _search and more; if one is rejected the 400 error lists what the column supports. Never _c_-prefix a column filter (use ville_eq, not _c_ville_eq).

bbox.description: Bounding box "lonMin,latMin,lonMax,latMax" (lon before lat), e.g. "-2.5,43,3,47". Geolocalized datasets only.

geoDistance.description: Proximity filter "lon,lat,distance" (lon first), e.g. "2.35,48.85,10km"; distance "0" = point-in-polygon. Geolocalized datasets only.

dateMatch.description: Date "YYYY-MM-DD" (single day) or "YYYY-MM-DD,YYYY-MM-DD" (range), e.g. "2023-11-21". Temporal datasets only.

select.description: Optional comma-separated list of column keys to include in the results. Useful when the dataset has many columns to reduce output size. If not provided, all columns are returned. Use column keys from describe_dataset. Format: column1,column2,column3 (No spaces after commas). Example: "nom,age,ville"

sort.description: Sort order for results. Comma-separated list of column keys. Prefix with - for descending order. Special keys: _score (relevance), _i (index order), _updatedAt, _rand (random), _geo_distance:lon:lat (distance from point, for geolocalized datasets — longitude first, then latitude). Examples: "population" (ascending), "-population" (descending), "_geo_distance:2.35:48.85" (closest to lon=2.35, lat=48.85)

size.description: Number of rows to return per page (default: 10, max: 50). Increase when you know you need more results upfront to avoid multiple pagination round-trips.

page.description: Page number (default 1)

next.description: URL from a previous search_data response to fetch the next page of results. When provided, all other parameters (query, filters, select, sort, size) are ignored since the URL already contains them.

datasetId.description: The dataset ID that was searched

total.description: Number of data rows matching the search criteria and filters

items.description: Data row object containing column keys as object keys with their values

results.description: An array of data rows matching the search criteria (up to the requested size).

next.description: URL to fetch the next page of results. Absent when there are no more results. Pass this value as the next input parameter to get the next page.

tools.name: aggregate_data
tools.description: Aggregate dataset rows by 1-3 columns with optional metric (sum, avg, min, max, count). Defaults to counting rows per group. For a single global metric without grouping, use calculate_metric.

datasetId.description: The exact dataset ID from the "id" field in list_datasets results. Do not use the title or slug.

groupByColumns.description: Columns to GROUP BY (like SQL GROUP BY). These define the categories/buckets, NOT the column to compute metrics on. Use column keys from describe_dataset (min 1, max 3).

column.description: The column to compute the metric ON (e.g., "salary" for average salary). This is NOT the grouping column. Use column keys from describe_dataset.

type.description: Metric to compute on each group. "count" counts rows per group (identical to omitting the metric parameter — does NOT count non-null values of the specified column).

metric.description: Optional metric to compute ON EACH GROUP. If not provided, defaults to counting rows per group.

filters.description: Column filters as key-value pairs: column_key + suffix, all values strings. Example: { "ville_eq": "Paris", "age_lte": "30", "nom_search": "Jean" }. Suffixes include _eq, _in, _gt/_lt, _search and more; if one is rejected the 400 error lists what the column supports. Never _c_-prefix a column filter (use ville_eq, not _c_ville_eq).

bbox.description: Bounding box "lonMin,latMin,lonMax,latMax" (lon before lat), e.g. "-2.5,43,3,47". Geolocalized datasets only.

geoDistance.description: Proximity filter "lon,lat,distance" (lon first), e.g. "2.35,48.85,10km"; distance "0" = point-in-polygon. Geolocalized datasets only.

dateMatch.description: Date "YYYY-MM-DD" (single day) or "YYYY-MM-DD,YYYY-MM-DD" (range), e.g. "2023-11-21". Temporal datasets only.

sort.description: Sort order for aggregation results. Use special keys: "count" or "-count" (by row count asc/desc), "key" or "-key" (by column value asc/desc), "metric" or "-metric" (by metric value asc/desc). Default: sorts by metric desc (if metric specified), then count desc. Example: "-count" to sort by most frequent values first

datasetId.description: The dataset ID that was aggregated

total.description: The total number of rows in the dataset

total_values.description: The total number of different values aggregated across all specified columns

total_other.description: Number of rows NOT included in the returned aggregations (only the top groups are returned). Add this to the sum of all group totals to reconstruct the dataset total.

total.description: Total number of rows aggregated for this group

total_values.description: Total number of different values aggregated for this group

total_other.description: Number of rows NOT included in the returned aggregations for this group

value.description: The value of the aggregated column (string or number)

metric.description: The value of the aggregation metric (e.g., sum, avg) on the selected column

aggs.description: Nested aggregation results when multiple columns are specified (max 3 levels deep)
Array of aggregation results for each group (limited to 20 rows)

tools.name: calculate_metric
tools.description: Calculate a single metric on a dataset column: avg, sum, min, max, stats, value_count, cardinality, percentiles. For per-group breakdowns, use aggregate_data.

datasetId.description: The exact dataset ID from the "id" field in list_datasets results. Do not use the title or slug.

fieldKey.description: The column key to calculate the metric on (use keys from describe_dataset)

metric.description: Metric to calculate. Available: avg, sum, min, max (for numbers); min, max, cardinality, value_count (for strings); value_count (for others); stats returns count/min/max/avg/sum; percentiles returns distribution.

percents.description: Comma-separated percentages for percentiles metric (default: "1,5,25,50,75,95,99"). Only used when metric is "percentiles".

filters.description: Column filters as key-value pairs: column_key + suffix, all values strings. Example: { "ville_eq": "Paris", "age_lte": "30", "nom_search": "Jean" }. Suffixes include _eq, _in, _gt/_lt, _search and more; if one is rejected the 400 error lists what the column supports. Never _c_-prefix a column filter (use ville_eq, not _c_ville_eq).

bbox.description: Bounding box "lonMin,latMin,lonMax,latMax" (lon before lat), e.g. "-2.5,43,3,47". Geolocalized datasets only.

geoDistance.description: Proximity filter "lon,lat,distance" (lon first), e.g. "2.35,48.85,10km"; distance "0" = point-in-polygon. Geolocalized datasets only.

dateMatch.description: Date "YYYY-MM-DD" (single day) or "YYYY-MM-DD,YYYY-MM-DD" (range), e.g. "2023-11-21". Temporal datasets only.

datasetId.description: The dataset ID that was queried

fieldKey.description: The column key that was queried

total.description: Total number of rows included in the calculation

metric.description: The calculated metric value. For avg/sum/min/max/value_count/cardinality: a single number (or a string for min/max on string columns). For stats: an object {count, min, max, avg, sum}. For percentiles: an object mapping percentage strings to values, e.g. {"25": 30000, "50": 42000, "75": 55000}.

tools.name: get_field_values
tools.description: List distinct values of a column. Useful to discover values before filtering with _eq or _in.

datasetId.description: The exact dataset ID from the "id" field in list_datasets results. Do not use the title or slug.

fieldKey.description: The column key to get values for (use keys from describe_dataset)

q.description: Optional text to filter values (prefix/substring match within this column)

sort.description: Sort order for the values (default: asc)

size.description: Number of values to return (default: 10, max: 1000)

datasetId.description: The dataset ID that was queried

fieldKey.description: The column key that was queried

values.description: Array of distinct values for the specified column

tools.name: subagent_dataset_data
tools.description: Query dataset rows, compute aggregations, and explore field values. Describe the data you want in plain language — do not write filter or URL syntax yourself: the sub-agent queries and returns a ready-to-paste filterQuery for a table/map link. Provide the dataset ID; if you already know the columns (keys and types), pass them too so it can query directly without re-fetching the schema.

task.description: The task to delegate to this sub-agent. Include all relevant context from the conversation that the sub-agent needs to accomplish the task (user preferences, constraints, data references, etc.).

tools.name: get_current_location
tools.description: Get the current page location in the portal, including its full URL, route path, name, parameters, query, and breadcrumbs.

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: List all available pages in the portal navigation menu, plus detail page patterns for datasets, applications, events, news, and reuses. Returns full absolute URLs — use them verbatim when writing links; substitute {slug} and append `? ` for filtered views, but never alter the origin or path prefix.

tools.name: navigate
tools.description: Navigate to a page in the portal. Accepts either a full absolute URL (as returned by list_pages or get_current_location) or a bare path — both work. Use list_datasets, list_applications, list_events, list_news, or list_reuses to find resource slugs/refs — prefer the human-readable `slug` over the `id` when building dataset and application paths. Optionally pass query parameters. IMPORTANT: when you search or filter data from a dataset, offer to navigate the user to the filtered table view at /datasets/{slug}/table by passing the same filter parameters as query params — but only when the search returned results (totalResults > 0).

path.description: The destination, either a full absolute URL (e.g. as returned by list_pages) or a path (e.g. "/datasets", "/datasets/my-dataset", "/event/my-event"). Both are accepted.

query.description: Optional query string to append to the URL (without leading "?"). For dataset table/map pages, pass the filterQuery from the dataset_data subagent Context verbatim — do not build or edit the filter parameters yourself. On the table page you may additionally append `cols=<column keys>` to choose which columns are displayed, but do not otherwise alter the filter syntax.

tools.name: pageFilters_get
tools.description: Read the current page filters synced with embedded visualizations and dataset previews. Returns concept filters (keys starting with "_c") and per-dataset filters (keys starting with "_d_ _"), plus selection markers (keys starting with "_s_") that tell which visualization emitted a filter. Call a block's describe_filters_* tool first to learn which keys it accepts.

tools.name: pageFilters_set
tools.description: Set or clear page filters synced with embedded visualizations and dataset previews. Pass a "params" object mapping filter keys to values; an empty string, null, or undefined value clears that key. Use keys advertised by a block's describe_filters_* tool (concept keys start with "_c", per-dataset keys with "_d_ _"). When clearing a filter, also clear its selection marker ("_s_" + the filter key without its "_c_"/"_d_" prefix and operator suffix).

params.description: Map of filter key -> value. Empty/null value clears the key.

tools.name: geocode_address
tools.description: Convert a French address or place name into geographic coordinates using the IGN Geoplateforme geocoding service. Returns matching locations with coordinates, postal code, city, and relevance score.

q.description: Address or place name to search for in France. Examples: "20 avenue de Segur, Paris", "Mairie de Bordeaux", "33000"

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

label.description: Full formatted address

score.description: Relevance score (0-1)

type.description: Result type (e.g., housenumber, street, municipality)

postcode.description: Postal code

context.description: Geographic context (department, region)

results.description: Array of geocoding results with coordinates

tools.name: get_user_geolocation
tools.description: Get the current geographic position of the user using the browser Geolocation API. Returns longitude, latitude, and accuracy (for geo_distance/bbox filters use lon,lat order). The user may be prompted to grant location permission.

tools.name: list_applications
tools.description: List data visualizations (applications) published on this portal. Returns title, slug, and summary for each application.

size.description: Number of results to return (default 10, max 50)

page.description: Page number (default 1)

tools.name: list_events
tools.description: List events published on this portal. Returns title, slug, and dates for each event.

size.description: Number of results to return (default 10, max 50)

includePast.description: Include past events (default false, only upcoming events)

tools.name: list_news
tools.description: List news articles published on this portal. Returns title, slug, and date for each article.

size.description: Number of results to return (default 10, max 50)

tools.name: list_reuses
tools.description: List community reuses published on this portal. Returns title, slug, and summary for each reuse.

size.description: Number of results to return (default 10, max 50)

sites.name: dattheshshenoy.github.io
sites.description: Roomwright — furnish a room by talking to your AI agent. A WebMCP room planner.

tools.name: roomwright_get_room
tools.description: Return the room's dimensions and openings plus every placed piece with its id, product, variant, position (metres, origin at the near-left corner), and rotation. Call this first to learn what is in the room and to get placement ids.

tools.name: roomwright_list_catalog
tools.description: List the furniture catalogue. Optionally filter by category. Each entry has product_id, dimensions (metres), colour/finish variants, price (USD), and the free space the piece needs in front of it.

tools.name: roomwright_add_item
tools.description: Place a piece in the room. Give product_id (from list_catalog). Optional: variant_id, x and z in metres, rotation_degrees. With no position the piece is auto-placed — wall-hugging pieces against the emptiest wall, others near the centre clear of what is there. Returns the new placement_id and any clearance issues it introduces.

product_id.description: a product_id from list_catalog, its exact name, or an unambiguous part of the name (e.g. "milo" or "coffee table")

variant_id.description: optional variant id

tools.name: roomwright_create_custom_item
tools.description: Make a custom piece from a primitive and place it in the room. shape is box (cabinet, built-in, block), cylinder (column, round pouffe), panel (a thin room divider), or platform (a low step or podium). width/depth/height in metres (cylinder ignores depth). Optional name, hex colour, position and rotation. Returns the new product_id and placement_id.

tools.name: roomwright_move_item
tools.description: Move a placed piece to a new centre position in metres. The position is clamped so the piece stays fully inside the room. Returns whether it was clamped and any clearance issues at the new spot.

tools.name: roomwright_rotate_item
tools.description: Rotate a placed piece about the vertical axis. degrees is relative by default; set absolute true to set the heading directly. Angles snap to 15-degree steps.

tools.name: roomwright_resize_item
tools.description: Override a placed piece's size — width (along its own left-right), depth (front-back), height, in metres. Give any subset; each is clamped to 0.15-8 m. The piece re-renders at the new size and its clearance is recomputed. Setting all three back to the catalogue size clears the override.

tools.name: roomwright_set_variant
tools.description: Change a placed piece's colour or material. variant_id comes from list_catalog's variants list for that product.

variant_id.description: a variant id for the piece's product

tools.name: roomwright_duplicate_item
tools.description: Add another copy of a placed piece — same product and variant. By default the copy is nudged clear of the original. Pass mirror to place it as a mirror image across the room's centre line instead: "east-west" for a matching piece on the opposite left/right side (same distance from its wall, heading flipped), "north-south" for front/back. Use "east-west" for a chair on each side of a sofa.

tools.name: roomwright_remove_item
tools.description: Remove a placed piece from the room by its placement_id.

tools.name: roomwright_set_room_dimensions
tools.description: Resize the room. Any of width, length, height in metres (width 1.5-20, length 1.5-20, height 2.2-4.5). Pieces that fall outside the new bounds are pulled back inside and reported.

length.description: interior length, metres

tools.name: roomwright_set_opening
tools.description: Add or change a door or window. Omit opening_id to ADD one — give kind (door or window) and wall (north, south, east, west); it starts centred, and you may also pass offset_m, width_m, sill_m or height_m to place it exactly. Pass opening_id (from get_room) to CHANGE that opening — any of wall, offset_m (from the wall's start corner), width_m, sill_m (windows), height_m, or kind. Values are clamped to fit the wall and ceiling.

opening_id.description: omit to add a new opening; give it to change an existing one

kind.description: door or window

wall.description: which wall

offset_m.description: distance from the wall's start corner to the opening's near edge

sill_m.description: height of the sill above the floor (windows)

tools.name: roomwright_remove_opening
tools.description: Remove a door or window by its opening_id.

tools.name: roomwright_suggest_spot
tools.description: Ask where a piece could go. Optionally pass product_id (so the spots actually fit that piece) and near (a wall, the centre, the window, or the door) to bias the result. Returns the total open floor, the longest clear run along each wall, and up to three candidate positions with x/z in metres, a rotation, whether each sits against a wall, and how much clear space surrounds it.

product_id.description: optional — a product_id, name, or name fragment, so candidates fit this piece

tools.name: roomwright_check_layout
tools.description: Evaluate the current arrangement: overlapping pieces, pieces that block a door or window, pieces that do not have their required free space, and walkways under 0.75 m. Returns an overall status (ok, warn, bad), each issue with the piece it concerns, and the narrowest gap in the room.

tools.name: roomwright_get_shopping_list
tools.description: The pieces currently in the room as a shopping list — each product with quantity, unit price, and line total, plus the grand total in USD.

tools.name: roomwright_select_item
tools.description: Highlight a placed piece in the 3D view and open its Inspector panel, so the user can see which piece you are talking about or about to change. Pass no placement_id to clear the selection.

tools.name: roomwright_set_view
tools.description: Switch the camera between 'orbit' (an angled 3D view of the room) and 'plan' (looking straight down at the floor plan). Use plan to let the user judge the layout, orbit to show the room.

view.description: orbit or plan

tools.name: roomwright_reset_layout
tools.description: Clear everything and start over: removes every placed piece, every custom piece, and every opening you added, and restores the default room size and its original door and window. Undoable in the app. Use this when the user asks to start fresh.

sites.name: dmproperties.com
sites.description: Diana Morales Properties has been considered one of the most trusted Real Estate agencies in Marbella & the Costa del Sol. Our Marbella property for sale portfolio features some of the most…

tools.name: wp_list_post_types
tools.description: Lists every kind of content this site can store — standard WordPress ones such as posts and pages, plus any custom ones this site defines. Returns each one's slug, which other tools need.

tools.name: wp_search_posts
tools.description: Returns a page of published content entries of one kind, newest first. Only public entries: drafts and other unpublished states are invisible.

post_type.description: Which kind of content to list. Use one of the values in this enum; only these content types are readable via MCP on this site.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Defaults to 1.

with_translations.description: When true, each result also says which languages it has been translated into. Slower, so leave it off unless you need it. Defaults to false.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 language code, e.g. en, es. Defaults to en.

tools.name: wp_get_post
tools.description: Returns one published content entry. Identify it by id, or by slug together with post_type, or by url. If you pass more than one, id wins, then slug + post_type, then url. At least one of id, slug (with post_type) or url is required; with none, the call fails with maettro_mcp_not_found. Only published entries: drafts and other unpublished states are invisible.

id.description: The entry's numeric ID.

slug.description: The entry's slug. Only works together with post_type.

post_type.description: Required only when identifying by slug. Use one of the values in this enum; only these content types are readable via MCP on this site.

url.description: The entry's full public URL.

detail_level.description: full returns everything, including the body content. excerpt returns a lightweight version: summary text, assigned terms, word count and SEO metadata, without the body. Defaults to full.

include_acf_fields.description: Adds the entry's custom field values. Only works with detail_level: full. To know which field names to expect, check wp_get_acf_schema first. Defaults to false.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 language code, e.g. en, es. Defaults to en.

tools.name: wp_list_taxonomies
tools.description: Lists every way this site can classify content — standard WordPress ones such as categories and tags, plus any custom ones this site defines. Returns each one's slug, which other tools need.

tools.name: wp_search_terms
tools.description: Finds terms inside one classification by name — for example, searching the site's categories. Pass search to filter by name; omit it to list all terms in the taxonomy. Each term includes its id, name, slug, parent and count.

taxonomy.description: Taxonomy slug, e.g. category, post_tag. Get valid values from wp_list_taxonomies.

search.description: Text to match against term names. Omit to list all terms in the taxonomy.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 language code, e.g. en, es. Defaults to en.

tools.name: wp_get_term
tools.description: Returns one term of one classification by its ID.

id.description: Term ID. Find it with wp_search_terms.

taxonomy.description: Taxonomy slug, e.g. category, post_tag. Get valid values from wp_list_taxonomies.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 language code, e.g. en, es. Defaults to en.

tools.name: wp_get_post_terms
tools.description: Returns the terms of one classification currently assigned to one content entry — for example, which categories a post is filed under.

id.description: Post ID (any post type, native or custom).

taxonomy.description: Slug of the taxonomy: native WordPress (category, post_tag) or custom taxonomy.

tools.name: wp_get_acf_schema
tools.description: Returns which custom fields exist for a kind of content: each field's name, type and allowed values. Use it to inspect the custom fields defined for a content type or entry, for example before interpreting include_acf_fields results from wp_get_post. Pass post_type to inspect a content type, or post_id to inspect the type of a specific entry; post_id takes precedence when both are given. With neither, it defaults to post.

post_type.description: Which kind of content to inspect. Defaults to post. Ignored when post_id resolves to an existing entry. Get valid values from wp_list_post_types.

post_id.description: A specific entry; its own kind of content is used. When both are given, post_id takes precedence.

tools.name: web_listings_search_properties
tools.description: Searches individual properties for sale or rent — a single apartment, villa, plot or commercial unit. Returns a short summary of each match: enough to compare and choose, without the full description or photos.

filter.description: What kind of listing to return. Omit to return all kinds.

ids.description: Return only these specific property IDs.

countries.description: Location IDs. Resolve names with web_listings_get_location.

provinces.description: Location IDs. Resolve names with web_listings_get_location.

areas.description: Location IDs. Resolve names with web_listings_get_location.

subareas.description: Location IDs. Resolve names with web_listings_get_location.

cities.description: Location IDs. Resolve names with web_listings_get_location.

categories.description: Property category IDs. Resolve names with web_listings_get_types.

types.description: Property type IDs. Resolve names with web_listings_get_types.

features.description: Feature IDs. Resolve names with web_listings_get_features.

filters.description: Theme filter names or URL slugs in any language, e.g. beach, gatedcommunity, comunidad-cerrada. Resolve names with web_listings_get_filters. Unknown values are ignored.

pool.description: yes = has any pool, no = has none, private = has a private pool, communal = has a communal pool.

garage.description: yes = has any garage, no = has none, private = has a private garage, communal = has a communal garage.

garden.description: yes = has any garden, no = has none, private = has a private garden, communal = has a communal garden.

price_from.description: Minimum price, expressed in the currency selected by the currency parameter (default EUR).

price_to.description: Maximum price, expressed in the currency selected by the currency parameter (default EUR).

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code, e.g. EUR. Defaults to EUR.

order.description: Field to sort by. Omit to use the site's own default order.

order_direction.description: Defaults to desc (highest or newest first). Use asc for the cheapest, smallest or oldest first. Ignored when order is omitted.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Defaults to 1.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 language code, e.g. en, es. Defaults to en.

tools.name: web_listings_get_property
tools.description: Returns the full record of one property by its ID: description, location, features, prices and measurements. The photo is not included in this record.

id.description: Internal Inmobalia property id.

lang.description: Optional ISO 639-1 code (default en) to select multilingual columns.

tools.name: web_listings_get_location
tools.description: Finds a location by name and returns the matches, best first. Each match includes its ID and its full hierarchy (country, province, area, subarea, city). Use the ID in the countries, provinces, areas, subareas or cities parameters of web_listings_search_properties or web_listings_search_developments.

name.description: Free-text location name, e.g. "Sierra Blanca", "Manilva". Must be at least 2 characters long.

level.description: Restricts the search to one level. Omit to search all levels.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 language code, e.g. en, es. Defaults to en.

tools.name: web_listings_search_developments
tools.description: Searches new-build developments — residential projects sold as a whole, each containing many individual units. Returns a short summary of each match: enough to compare and choose, without the full description or photos.

countries.description: Location IDs. Resolve names with web_listings_get_location.

provinces.description: Location IDs. Resolve names with web_listings_get_location.

areas.description: Location IDs. Resolve names with web_listings_get_location.

subareas.description: Location IDs. Resolve names with web_listings_get_location.

cities.description: Location IDs. Resolve names with web_listings_get_location.

categories.description: Property category IDs. Resolve names with web_listings_get_types.

types.description: Property type IDs. Resolve names with web_listings_get_types.

filters.description: Theme filter names or URL slugs in any language for developments, e.g. beach, comunidad-cerrada. Resolve names with web_listings_get_filters. Unknown values are ignored.

order.description: Field to sort by. price uses the development's starting price. Omit to use the site's own default order.

order_direction.description: Defaults to desc (highest or newest first). Use asc for the cheapest or oldest first. Ignored when order is omitted.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. Defaults to 1.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 language code, e.g. en, es. Defaults to en.

tools.name: web_listings_get_development
tools.description: Returns the full record of one new-build development by its ID: description, location, starting price, available types, and the IDs of its individual units. The photo is not included in this record. Look up each unit ID with web_listings_search_properties to get bedroom, bathroom and size details for that specific unit.

id.description: Internal Inmobalia development id.

lang.description: Optional ISO 639-1 code (default en).

tools.name: web_listings_get_types
tools.description: Finds a property type by name and returns the matches, best first. Each match includes its ID and the category it belongs to. If name is omitted, returns the full catalog of categories and types instead. Use the ID in the categories or types parameters of web_listings_search_properties or web_listings_search_developments.

name.description: Free-text type name, e.g. "duplex", "apartment". Must be at least 2 characters long. Omit to get the full catalog.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 language code, e.g. en, es. Defaults to en.

tools.name: web_listings_get_features
tools.description: Finds a property feature by name and returns the matches, best first. Each match includes its ID. If name is omitted, returns the full catalog of features instead. Use the ID in the features parameter of web_listings_search_properties.

name.description: Free-text feature name, e.g. "air conditioning", "sea view". Must be at least 2 characters long. Omit to get the full catalog.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 language code, e.g. en, es. Defaults to en.

tools.name: web_listings_get_filters
tools.description: Lists the theme filters available for property or development searches, with the URL slug localized for the requested language. Each entry has a canonical name and its slug. Use the name (or any slug) in the filters parameter of web_listings_search_properties or web_listings_search_developments.

struct.description: Which catalog to list. Defaults to property.

lang.description: ISO 639-1 language code, e.g. en, es. Defaults to en.

tools.name: web_listings_get_property_image
tools.description: Returns a ready-to-use URL for the main photo of one property, if it has one.

id.description: Internal Inmobalia property id.

tools.name: web_listings_get_development_image
tools.description: Returns a ready-to-use URL for the main photo of one new-build development, if it has one.

id.description: Internal Inmobalia development id.

tools.name: open_url
tools.description: Opens a same-origin page in the user's browser, in the same tab. Accepts a relative path (for example /property/...) or an absolute URL on the same host, preferably a URL returned by another tool. External hosts and non-http(s) schemes are rejected without navigating. Returns a short confirmation when the navigation starts, or an error message explaining why it did not.

url.description: URL of the page to open: a relative path on this site (for example /property/...) or an absolute same-host URL. Prefer the exact value returned by another tool; a relative path you compose yourself is also accepted. External hosts and non-http(s) schemes are rejected.

sites.name: formless-health.vercel.app
sites.description: A live, agent-editable interface running in your browser.

tools.name: get_website_summary
tools.description: Call this first when you connect to the website. Explains what Formless Labs is and how to use its tools.

tools.name: get_website_prompt
tools.description: Returns the prompt that governs how the agent should work with this website, capability by capability, naming the tool that delivers each one.

tools.name: list_project_files
tools.description: Lists source files in the live WebContainer project with revision, editability, size, and hash.

tools.name: read_project_files
tools.description: Reads one to twenty UTF-8 source files from the live project. Use list_project_files first.

tools.name: apply_project_changes
tools.description: Atomically writes or deletes editable application files, validates the project, and rolls back failures. Full file contents are required for writes.

tools.name: reset_project
tools.description: Restores the editable app to the starter snapshot. Call only after the user explicitly requests a reset.

tools.name: get_ui_elements
tools.description: Returns the stable IDs and current state of instrumented elements in the live preview.

tools.name: navigate_to_route
tools.description: Moves the live preview to one of the routes the app declares. Prefer this over clicking a link: it works even when the navigation control is off-screen, and it cannot miss. Call with no path to list the available routes.

tools.name: highlight_ui_elements
tools.description: Highlights one or more live UI elements, optionally blinks between two colors, and dims or hides everything else in the preview. Set durationSeconds to clear the highlight automatically.

tools.name: clear_ui_highlights
tools.description: Restores every registered UI element to its normal visual state.

tools.name: poll_user_messages
tools.description: Returns typed and final speech messages after a monotonic cursor. Poll approximately every two seconds while listening for user input.

tools.name: speak_text
tools.description: Speaks text aloud through the page, using the browser's speech synthesizer. Use it to answer a user who is talking rather than typing. Keep each turn to a sentence or two: the call does not return until the utterance finishes. The result lists the available voices, so a later call can pick one by name.

tools.name: stop_speaking
tools.description: Immediately stops anything the page is saying and drops whatever is queued behind it.

tools.name: get_health_summary
tools.description: Summarizes the patient-authorized health record: what it contains, how much of it there is, and over what dates. Call this before any other health tool. Reports whether the record is the user's own, the de-identified sample, or absent.

tools.name: list_health_records
tools.description: Lists items in the health record as dated, titled lines, newest first. Filter by group, free text, status, or a date range, and page with offset. This is the cheap way to find the handful of refs worth reading in full.

tools.name: read_health_records
tools.description: Reads the full content of specific health records by ref, as taken from the provider's FHIR API. format "fields" is the labelled human reading, "fhir" is the verbatim resource JSON, and "text" is the prose of a clinical-note file. Give refs from list_health_records, or a group to read its first items.

tools.name: list_app_versions
tools.description: Lists the published versions of this app that anyone can switch to, and reports which one the live preview is currently showing.

tools.name: publish_app_version
tools.description: Publishes the current editable app as a named version that every visitor can see and load. Publishing is public and permanent until you unpublish it, so ask the user before calling this.

tools.name: switch_app_version
tools.description: Replaces the live preview with a published version. The current working copy is overwritten, so confirm with the user first — publish their unsaved work before switching if they want to keep it.

sites.name: handoff-webmcp-nine.vercel.app
sites.description: Humans set intent and constraints. Agents plan, propose, and execute — nothing external happens without approval. Built on WebMCP.

tools.name: get_board_summary
tools.description: Get the current mission (goal, deadline, budget, constraints), whether GitHub is connected and which repository is selected, task counts by column and priority, total estimated cost, whether that's over budget, how many external tasks are still unapproved, and how many decisions are waiting. Call this first, before doing anything else, to understand the current situation.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: List tasks on the board, optionally filtered to a single column.

column.description: Only return tasks in this column. Omit for all tasks.

tools.name: search_tasks
tools.description: Search task titles and notes for a keyword or phrase.

query.description: Text to search for, case-insensitive.

tools.name: get_activity_ledger
tools.description: Read recent activity — who did what, and why — in chronological order. Useful before proposing a plan, so you don't repeat work already done.

limit.description: How many recent entries to return. Defaults to 30.

tools.name: set_mission
tools.description: Record the mission the person described: what they're trying to accomplish, the deadline, the budget, and any constraints they stated (e.g. 'don't publish anything without my approval'). Call this as soon as a person states or changes their goal, so it's visible on the shared board rather than left in conversation.

budget.description: Budget ceiling, in the same currency the person used.

constraints.description: The rules the agent must operate within, e.g. 'No weekend work'.

tools.name: create_task
tools.description: Add a new task to the board. Mark external: true for anything that will be publicly or externally visible once done (a published page, a sent email, a live announcement) — that flag is what makes move_task ask for approval before it's marked done.

cost.description: Estimated cost of this task, if the mission tracks a budget.

external.description: True if completing this task makes something publicly visible.

tools.name: update_task
tools.description: Edit an existing task's title, notes, priority, or cost estimate.

tools.name: move_task
tools.description: Move a task to a different column. Moving a task marked external into 'done' does not execute immediately — it raises a decision in the Decision Room and this call returns { status: 'pending_approval' } instead of the updated task.

tools.name: delete_task
tools.description: Remove a task. This never executes immediately for an agent — it raises a decision in the Decision Room and returns { status: 'pending_approval' }. Prefer moving to 'done' unless the person specifically wants it gone.

tools.name: propose_plan
tools.description: Bring a plan to the person instead of just executing it. Use this for anything with a real tradeoff (cost vs. scope, speed vs. risk) or that touches several tasks at once. Give one option if there's a single clear course of action, or two-to-three if there's a genuine choice — each option lists the concrete board changes it would make if approved. Nothing in 'changes' happens until the person (or you, once they've said 'approve it') calls approve_decision.

title.description: Short name for the decision, e.g. 'Get the launch under budget'.

rationale.description: Why you're raising this now, in plain terms.

label.description: Short name, e.g. 'Cut the animation work'.

description.description: What this option does and what it trades off.

changes.description: Changes to apply if this option is approved. Board changes (move/update/create/delete) apply instantly. github_* changes are real GitHub writes — they only ever run from here, after approval, never from a direct tool call. github_create_issue needs {action, owner, repo, title, body?, labels?}. github_comment_issue needs {action, owner, repo, number, body}. github_create_branch needs {action, owner, repo, branchName, fromRef?}. github_open_pr needs {action, owner, repo, title, head, base?, body?}.

id.description: Task id — required for move, update, delete.

patch.description: Fields to change — used for update.

task.description: New task fields — used for create.

owner.description: Repo owner — required for github_* actions.

repo.description: Repo name — required for github_* actions.

body.description: Used by github_create_issue, github_comment_issue, github_open_pr.

fromRef.description: Base branch for github_create_branch. Defaults to the repo's default branch.

base.description: Base branch for github_open_pr. Defaults to the repo's default branch.

tools.name: approve_decision
tools.description: Approve a pending decision — use this when the person tells you, in conversation, to go ahead with a proposal or a gated action you raised. This is what actually applies the change (including any GitHub write); approving executes the chosen option's changes immediately.

id.description: The decision id, from propose_plan's result or get_board_summary.

optionId.description: Which option to approve. Omit if the decision only has one.

tools.name: reject_decision
tools.description: Reject a pending decision — use this when the person tells you not to go ahead with something you raised.

tools.name: select_repository
tools.description: Set which repository the mission is scoped to. owner/repo must be a repository the connected account can access. This doesn't change anything on GitHub — it just tells the board (and the tools below) which repo to read from by default.

tools.name: inspect_repository
tools.description: Get a repository's basic metadata: description, default branch, whether it's private, open issue count, stars, and when it was last pushed to. Omit owner/repo to use the currently selected repository.

owner.description: Omit to use the currently selected repository.

repo.description: Omit to use the currently selected repository.

tools.name: list_repo_issues
tools.description: List a repository's issues (pull requests are excluded). Omit owner/repo to use the currently selected repository.

state.description: Defaults to 'open'.

tools.name: list_repo_pull_requests
tools.description: List a repository's pull requests, including each PR's head/base branches and the head commit SHA (useful for get_repo_check_status). Omit owner/repo to use the currently selected repository.

state.description: Defaults to 'open'.

tools.name: list_repo_commits
tools.description: List a repository's most recent commits. Omit owner/repo to use the currently selected repository.

perPage.description: How many commits to return. Defaults to 10, maximum 30.

tools.name: get_repo_check_status
tools.description: Get CI/check-run status for a ref — a branch name or a commit SHA (e.g. a PR's head SHA from list_repo_pull_requests). Omit ref to check the repository's default branch. Omit owner/repo to use the currently selected repository.

ref.description: Branch name or commit SHA. Defaults to the default branch.

tools.name: find_repo_blockers
tools.description: Scan open issues and pull requests for likely blockers: bodies mentioning 'blocked by #N' / 'depends on #N', and PRs whose latest checks are failing. Returns each flagged item with its likely owner and the reason it was flagged. This is a heuristic, not a guaranteed dependency graph — say so if you relay it. Omit owner/repo to use the currently selected repository.

sites.description: Inspect and control ROS robots from the browser

tools.name: connect_to_robot
tools.description: Set the rosbridge WebSocket URL and reconnect.

tools.name: get_topics
tools.description: List all ROS topics.

tools.name: get_topic_type
tools.description: Get the message type for a ROS topic.

topic.description: Full topic name, e.g. /turtle1/cmd_vel

tools.name: get_topic_details
tools.description: Get publishers, subscribers, and type for a topic.

tools.name: subscribe_once
tools.description: Subscribe to a topic and return the first message received.

tools.name: subscribe_for_duration
tools.description: Subscribe to a topic and collect messages for a given duration.

tools.name: publish_once
tools.description: Publish a single message to a topic.

tools.name: publish_for_durations
tools.description: Publish a sequence of messages with delays between each.

durations.description: Delay in seconds after each message

tools.name: turn_by_angle
tools.description: Rotate a robot in place by an angle in degrees. Computes duration = (|angle_deg| x pi/180) / angular_velocity and sends a zero-velocity stop when finished. Prefer this over publish_for_durations for rotation — it removes the error-prone duration maths from the caller. Positive angle_deg = counter-clockwise, negative = clockwise. Units: angle_deg in degrees, angular_velocity in rad/s. Example — turn turtle1 90 degrees counter-clockwise at 1.0 rad/s: turn_by_angle(cmd_vel_topic='/ts1/turtle1/cmd_vel', msg_type='geometry_msgs/Twist', angle_deg=90)

tools.name: move_by_distance
tools.description: Move a robot forward or backward by a distance in metres. Computes duration = |distance_m| / linear_velocity and sends a zero-velocity stop when finished. Prefer this over publish_for_durations for straight-line motion. Positive distance_m = forward, negative = backward. Units: distance_m in metres, linear_velocity in m/s. Example — move turtle1 forward 1 metre at 0.5 m/s: move_by_distance(cmd_vel_topic='/ts1/turtle1/cmd_vel', msg_type='geometry_msgs/Twist', distance_m=1.0)

tools.name: get_services
tools.description: List all available ROS services.

tools.name: get_service_details
tools.description: Get the request/response type and provider node for a service.

tools.name: call_service
tools.description: Call a ROS service with a request payload.

tools.name: get_nodes
tools.description: List all running ROS nodes.

tools.name: get_node_details
tools.description: Get publishers, subscribers, and services for a node.

tools.name: get_connected_robots
tools.description: Detect connected robots by finding active cmd_vel topics on the ROS network. Works with any robot — no hardcoded names. Returns the cmd_vel topic and message type for each robot. Call this when you need to discover robot topics before issuing motion commands.

tools.name: move_robots
tools.description: Move multiple robots simultaneously. All start and stop at the same time. Use get_connected_robots() first to get topics and message types. Each robot entry needs: cmd_vel_topic, msg_type, and linear_x and/or angular_z.

tools.name: get_robot_description
tools.description: Fetch the robot's URDF from the /robot_description ROS parameter. Requires robot_state_publisher to be running.

tools.name: get_joint_states
tools.description: Read current joint positions (rad), velocities (rad/s), and efforts (N·m) from /joint_states.

topic.description: Joint states topic (default: /joint_states)

tools.name: calendar_show_history
tools.description: Show the history of calendar changes with commit messages, authors, and timestamps. Use this to see what changes have been made and by whom. Each history entry can be used with calendar_undo to rollback to that state.

limit.description: Maximum number of history entries to return (default: 10)

totalEntries.description: Total number of commits in history

position.description: Position in history (0 = current)

message.description: Commit message

author.description: Author name (agent ID if from agent commit)

canRollbackTo.description: Whether this commit can be rolled back to

changes.description: Change summary (if available from agent commit)

message.description: Human-readable summary

tip.description: Helpful tip for the user

tools.name: calendar_undo
tools.description: Undo calendar changes by rolling back to a previous state. You can either: - Undo a number of steps: { "steps": 1 } to undo the last change - Rollback to a specific commit: { "commitId": "abc123..." } Use calendar_show_history first to see available states to rollback to.

steps.description: Number of changes to undo (default: 1). Use this OR commitId, not both.

commitId.description: Specific commit ID to rollback to (get from calendar_show_history)

message.description: Human-readable result message

rolledBackTo.description: Commit ID that was rolled back to

tools.name: calendar_compare_states
tools.description: Compare calendar states between two commits to see what changed. Useful for understanding the difference between the current state and a previous state, or between any two points in history.

oldCommitId.description: The older commit to compare from (defaults to one step back)

newCommitId.description: The newer commit to compare to (defaults to current state)

message.description: Human-readable summary

tools.name: calendar_start_sandbox
tools.description: Start an isolated sandbox session for making calendar changes. When in a sandbox: - Your changes won't affect other agents or the main calendar - You can experiment freely and rollback if needed - Changes are only applied to main when you explicitly commit them Use this when you want to make multiple changes that should be reviewed together, or when multiple agents need to work on the calendar concurrently.

agentName.description: A unique identifier for this agent session (e.g., 'claude-scheduler')

modelName.description: The AI model name (e.g., 'claude', 'gpt4', 'gemini'). Used for tracking.

message.description: Human-readable result message

branch.description: Git branch name for the sandbox

agentId.description: Unique agent identifier

tips.description: Helpful tips for using the sandbox

tools.name: calendar_preview_changes
tools.description: Preview what changes this agent has pending compared to the main calendar. Shows: - Events that were added - Events that were removed - Events that were modified Use this before committing to review your changes.

agentId.description: Agent ID or branch name to preview (defaults to current agent if in a sandbox)

hasChanges.description: Whether the agent has pending changes

agentId.description: Agent ID being previewed

summary.description: Summary of changes

message.description: Human-readable summary

tip.description: Helpful tip

tools.name: calendar_commit_changes
tools.description: Commit your sandbox changes to the main calendar. This merges all your pending changes into the shared calendar that everyone sees. Use calendar_preview_changes first to review what will be committed.

agentId.description: Agent ID or branch name to commit (defaults to current agent)

message.description: Description of the changes being committed (for the audit log)
Human-readable result message

tip.description: Helpful tip

tools.name: calendar_list_agents
tools.description: See what AI agents are currently working on the calendar. Shows all active sandbox sessions with their last activity time. Useful for coordination when multiple agents are making changes.

agentId.description: Agent identifier

message.description: Human-readable summary

tip.description: Helpful tip

tools.name: calendar_switch_branch
tools.description: Switch to a different calendar branch. This is an advanced tool for viewing what different agents have done. - Switch to an agent's branch to see their pending changes - Switch to "main" or "default" to see the shared calendar state

branch.description: Branch name to switch to ('main', 'default', or an agent branch name)

message.description: Human-readable result message

currentBranch.description: The branch that is now active

agent.description: Agent info if switched to an agent branch

tools.name: calendar_show_preview
tools.description: Show a visual preview of an agent's pending changes in the calendar UI. When activated: - Added events appear as green dashed "phantom" events - Modified events appear as amber dashed events showing the new state - Removed events appear as red dashed strikethrough events - A banner appears at the top with Accept/Reject buttons This lets users visually review AI-proposed changes before approving them.

agentId.description: ID of the agent whose changes to preview

message.description: Human-readable result message

agentId.description: Agent being previewed

changes.description: Summary of pending changes

tip.description: Helpful tip for the user

tools.name: calendar_hide_preview
tools.description: Exit the agent preview mode and return to normal calendar view. This hides all phantom events and removes the preview banner. The agent's changes are NOT affected - they remain on their branch.

message.description: Human-readable result message

tools.name: calendar_get_preview_status
tools.description: Check if the calendar is currently in preview mode. Returns information about which agent is being previewed and what changes are pending.

previewAgentId.description: ID of the agent being previewed

message.description: Human-readable status message

tools.name: calendar_list_events
tools.description: List all calendar events, optionally filtered by date range or user. Returns event IDs needed for update/delete operations. Shows events from the current branch (main or agent sandbox).

startDate.description: Filter events starting from this date (YYYY-MM-DD)

endDate.description: Filter events ending before this date (YYYY-MM-DD)

tools.name: calendar_update_event
tools.description: Update an existing calendar event. Provide only the fields you want to change. Changes are made on the current branch. Use calendar_commit_changes to save to main.

eventId.description: The ID of the event to update

startDate.description: New start date/time (ISO format or 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM')

endDate.description: New end date/time (ISO format or 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM')

message.description: Human-readable result message

event.description: The updated event

tools.name: calendar_delete_event
tools.description: Delete a calendar event by ID. Changes are made on the current branch. Use calendar_commit_changes to save to main.

eventId.description: The ID of the event to delete

message.description: Human-readable result message

tools.name: calendar_get_state
tools.description: Get the current calendar state including view, date, filter, settings, and available users. Use this to understand the current context before making changes.

tools.name: calendar_filter_by_user
tools.description: Filter calendar events to show only events for a specific user, or 'all' to show everyone. The view updates immediately to reflect the filter.

userId.description: User ID to filter by, or 'all' to show all users. Get user IDs from calendar_get_state.

tools.name: calendar_navigate
tools.description: Navigate the calendar to a specific view and/or date. Available views: day, week, month, year, agenda NOTE: Navigation happens AFTER this tool returns. The page will change but you'll still receive the success response. This is expected behavior. Examples: - Show today in week view: { "view": "week", "today": true } - Go to specific date: { "date": "2025-12-25" } - Switch to month view: { "view": "month" }

view.description: Calendar view to switch to

today.description: Set to true to navigate to today's date

message.description: Human-readable result message

navigatingTo.description: Where the calendar is navigating to

tools.name: calendar_schedule_meeting
tools.description: Create a new calendar event. This is the PRIMARY way to create events. Example: Schedule a 1-hour meeting tomorrow at 2pm: { "title": "Team Sync", "date": "2025-12-08", "startTime": "14:00", "durationMinutes": 60 } After creating events, use calendar_commit_changes to save them to the main calendar, or use calendar_show_preview to show the user what you've created.

date.description: Date of the meeting (YYYY-MM-DD format, e.g., '2025-12-08')

startTime.description: Start time in 24h format (HH:MM, e.g., '14:00' for 2pm)

userId.description: User ID to assign (uses first user if not specified). Get IDs from calendar_get_state.

message.description: Human-readable result message

event.description: The created event

tip.description: Helpful next step

tools.name: calendar_find_free_time
tools.description: Find available time slots on a given day. Use this BEFORE scheduling to avoid conflicts. Returns a list of free time slots that meet the minimum duration requirement. Checks against all events on the current branch (main or agent sandbox).

userId.description: Check availability for a specific user only

existingEventsCount.description: Number of existing events on this day
