sites.name: webmcp-beryl.vercel.app
sites.description: A presentation editor where a human and an AI agent edit the same live deck through WebMCP — click a region to edit it directly, or let an agent call one of 19 tools to build slides, charts, and…

tools.name: get_deck_state
tools.description: Returns the full current state of the presentation deck: all slides in order, their layouts, the active slide, and the current theme. Use this when you need an overview of the WHOLE deck (e.g. how many slides exist, what order they're in, the current theme) — not as a routine first call before every action. If you only need one slide's regions, call get_slide_structure directly instead; calling both back to back is usually redundant since get_slide_structure alone is enough for editing a specific slide.

tools.name: get_slide_structure
tools.description: Returns one slide's layout name and the full list of its regions (id, name, type, and current content). You usually do NOT need to call this before writing to a region — all content tools accept a region's name directly (e.g. 'left_body', 'body', 'title'), which is stable and predictable per layout, so you can go straight to the tool for the content you want to add. Call this when you don't already know a slide's layout/region names, or want to check current content before overwriting it. If slideId is omitted, uses the currently active slide.

slideId.description: The id of the slide to inspect. Defaults to the active slide if omitted.

tools.name: get_region_content
tools.description: Returns the current content and type of a single region on a slide. Use this to check what's already in a region before overwriting it, or to confirm a previous edit took effect. If slideId is omitted, uses the currently active slide.

slideId.description: The id of the slide the region belongs to. Defaults to the active slide if omitted.

regionId.description: The region's id (from get_slide_structure) OR its name directly (e.g. 'title', 'body', 'left_body', 'right_body', 'media').

tools.name: add_slide
tools.description: Creates a new slide using the given layout (defaults to 'title+bullets' if omitted) and inserts it at the given position (defaults to the end of the deck). Returns the new slide's id. Call this when the user wants to add a new slide to the presentation.

layout.description: Layout id for the new slide

position.description: 0-indexed position to insert at; defaults to the end

tools.name: remove_slide
tools.description: Permanently removes a slide from the deck. slideId is required (not defaulted to the active slide) since this is destructive — call it only when the deletion target is unambiguous, and this cannot be undone by the agent.

slideId.description: The id of the slide to delete

tools.name: duplicate_slide
tools.description: Creates a copy of an existing slide, including all its region content, and inserts it immediately after the original. Returns the new slide's id. Call this when the user wants to reuse a slide's structure/content as a starting point for a new one. If slideId is omitted, duplicates the currently active slide.

slideId.description: The id of the slide to duplicate. Defaults to the active slide if omitted.

tools.name: reorder_slides
tools.description: Moves a slide to a new position (0-indexed) in the deck's slide order. Call this when the user wants to reorder slides, e.g. 'move the agenda slide to the front.' If slideId is omitted, moves the currently active slide.

slideId.description: The id of the slide to move. Defaults to the active slide if omitted.

newPosition.description: The 0-indexed position to move the slide to

tools.name: set_slide_layout
tools.description: Changes a slide's layout to a different named layout, preserving content in any regions whose names match between the old and new layout (unmatched regions are dropped, new regions start empty). Call this when the user wants to restructure a slide, e.g. turn a single-column slide into a two-column one. If slideId is omitted, restructures the currently active slide.

slideId.description: The id of the slide to restructure. Defaults to the active slide if omitted.

tools.name: fill_text_region
tools.description: Sets or replaces the text content of a single text-type region. Call this to write or overwrite a specific named region (other than the title or main body, which have their own convenience tools). This automatically converts the region to a text type — you do NOT need to call set_region_type first, even if the region currently holds a different type. If slideId is omitted, targets the currently active slide.

slideId.description: The id of the slide the region belongs to. Defaults to the active slide if omitted.

regionId.description: The region's id (from get_slide_structure) OR its name directly (e.g. 'title', 'body', 'left_body', 'right_body', 'media') — names are stable per layout. Prefer just trying a likely name directly (including right after the active slide changes) rather than calling get_slide_structure defensively first: a wrong name fails with a clear list of that slide's actual region names, which is cheap to recover from and faster than checking every time.

text.description: The text to set

tools.name: set_bullets
tools.description: Sets a bullets-type region's list of points, replacing any existing bullets. If maxPoints is given, truncates to that many bullets. Call this to populate or replace a bulleted list region with short, scannable points — keep each bullet under ~12 words. This automatically converts the region to a bullets type — you do NOT need to call set_region_type first, even if the region currently holds a different type. If slideId is omitted, targets the currently active slide.

slideId.description: The id of the slide the region belongs to. Defaults to the active slide if omitted.

regionId.description: The region's id (from get_slide_structure) OR its name directly (e.g. 'title', 'body', 'left_body', 'right_body', 'media') — names are stable per layout. Prefer just trying a likely name directly (including right after the active slide changes) rather than calling get_slide_structure defensively first: a wrong name fails with a clear list of that slide's actual region names, which is cheap to recover from and faster than checking every time.

bullets.description: The bullet point strings, in order

maxPoints.description: Optional cap on the number of bullets to keep

tools.name: set_region_type
tools.description: Changes what kind of content a region holds, clearing its content in the process, WITHOUT setting new content. You almost never need to call this before filling a region — fill_text_region, set_bullets, set_chart_data, and set_diagram_steps all automatically convert the region to the matching type themselves when you call them directly, so just call the tool for the content you actually want to add. Only use this tool if you specifically want to change a region's type and leave it empty (e.g. to prep it for someone else to fill in later). Note: 'image-placeholder' is a dead end — there is no tool that can set real image content, so only convert a region to that type if the user specifically wants an empty placeholder for a human to fill in later; prefer set_chart_data or set_diagram_steps if the user actually wants visual content now. If slideId is omitted, targets the currently active slide.

slideId.description: The id of the slide the region belongs to. Defaults to the active slide if omitted.

regionId.description: The region's id (from get_slide_structure) OR its name directly (e.g. 'title', 'body', 'left_body', 'right_body', 'media') — names are stable per layout. Prefer just trying a likely name directly (including right after the active slide changes) rather than calling get_slide_structure defensively first: a wrong name fails with a clear list of that slide's actual region names, which is cheap to recover from and faster than checking every time.

type.description: The new region type

tools.name: clear_region
tools.description: Empties a region's content while keeping the region itself (and its type) in place on the slide. Call this when the user wants a region blanked out without removing it from the layout. If slideId is omitted, targets the currently active slide.

slideId.description: The id of the slide the region belongs to. Defaults to the active slide if omitted.

regionId.description: The region's id (from get_slide_structure) OR its name directly (e.g. 'title', 'body', 'left_body', 'right_body', 'media') — names are stable per layout. Prefer just trying a likely name directly (including right after the active slide changes) rather than calling get_slide_structure defensively first: a wrong name fails with a clear list of that slide's actual region names, which is cheap to recover from and faster than checking every time.

tools.name: adjust_font_size
tools.description: Nudges a region's font size up or down by one step from its current size (each step is roughly 10%, clamped to a sane range). Call this when the user asks to make text bigger/smaller on a specific region, or when a region's text looks cramped or too large. Content is auto-fit to its region as it's written, so this is for manual fine-tuning on top of that, not required for normal use. If slideId is omitted, targets the currently active slide.

slideId.description: The id of the slide the region belongs to. Defaults to the active slide if omitted.

regionId.description: The region's id (from get_slide_structure) OR its name directly (e.g. 'title', 'body', 'left_body', 'right_body', 'media') — names are stable per layout. Prefer just trying a likely name directly (including right after the active slide changes) rather than calling get_slide_structure defensively first: a wrong name fails with a clear list of that slide's actual region names, which is cheap to recover from and faster than checking every time.

direction.description: Whether to increase or decrease the font size

tools.name: set_chart_data
tools.description: Sets a chart region's data as a list of {label, value} points, rendered as a real bar or pie chart. This automatically converts the region to a chart type and fills it in ONE call — do NOT call set_region_type first, that would only change the type and leave it empty. Replaces any existing chart data. Use this to visualize simple numeric comparisons (e.g. market share, survey results, feature usage) — not for photos or illustrations. Keep to at most 8 data points for a legible chart; extras beyond that are dropped. Pie charts read best with 5 or fewer points. If the user just wants the same data shown as a different chart style (e.g. 'make it a pie chart'), use set_chart_type instead — it keeps the existing numbers rather than requiring you to resend them. If slideId is omitted, targets the currently active slide.

slideId.description: The id of the slide the region belongs to. Defaults to the active slide if omitted.

regionId.description: The region's id (from get_slide_structure) OR its name directly (e.g. 'title', 'body', 'left_body', 'right_body', 'media') — names are stable per layout. Prefer just trying a likely name directly (including right after the active slide changes) rather than calling get_slide_structure defensively first: a wrong name fails with a clear list of that slide's actual region names, which is cheap to recover from and faster than checking every time.

data.description: The data points to chart, in order

label.description: Category label for this point

value.description: Numeric value for this point — relative proportions are what matter

tools.name: set_chart_type
tools.description: Switches an existing chart region between 'bar' and 'pie' style WITHOUT changing its data — use this instead of set_chart_data when the user just wants a different visual style for the same numbers (e.g. 'make that a pie chart instead'). The region must already be a chart with data set via set_chart_data; if it isn't, this fails and you should use set_chart_data instead to set both the type and the data together. If slideId is omitted, targets the currently active slide.

slideId.description: The id of the slide the region belongs to. Defaults to the active slide if omitted.

regionId.description: The region's id (from get_slide_structure) OR its name directly (e.g. 'title', 'body', 'left_body', 'right_body', 'media') — names are stable per layout. Prefer just trying a likely name directly (including right after the active slide changes) rather than calling get_slide_structure defensively first: a wrong name fails with a clear list of that slide's actual region names, which is cheap to recover from and faster than checking every time.

chartType.description: The chart style to switch to

tools.name: set_diagram_steps
tools.description: Sets a diagram region's content as an ordered sequence of short step labels, rendered as a left-to-right flow of connected boxes. This automatically converts the region to a diagram type and fills it in ONE call — do NOT call set_region_type first, that would only change the type and leave it empty. Replaces any existing steps. Use this for simple process flows, roadmaps, or sequences (e.g. "Plan → Build → Test → Ship"). Keep to at most 6 steps, each a short label (~3-5 words); extras beyond that are dropped. If slideId is omitted, targets the currently active slide.

slideId.description: The id of the slide the region belongs to. Defaults to the active slide if omitted.

regionId.description: The region's id (from get_slide_structure) OR its name directly (e.g. 'title', 'body', 'left_body', 'right_body', 'media') — names are stable per layout. Prefer just trying a likely name directly (including right after the active slide changes) rather than calling get_slide_structure defensively first: a wrong name fails with a clear list of that slide's actual region names, which is cheap to recover from and faster than checking every time.

steps.description: The step labels, in order

tools.name: set_title
tools.description: Convenience tool that sets the text of a slide's title region directly, without needing to look up its regionId first. Call this whenever the user wants to set or change a slide's title. If slideId is omitted, edits the currently active slide.

slideId.description: The id of the slide to edit. Defaults to the active slide if omitted.

tools.name: set_body_text
tools.description: Convenience tool that sets the text of a slide's main body region directly, without needing to look up its regionId first. Use this for simple paragraph-style body content; use set_bullets instead if the content should be a bulleted list. If slideId is omitted, edits the currently active slide.

slideId.description: The id of the slide to edit. Defaults to the active slide if omitted.

text.description: The new body text

tools.name: apply_theme
tools.description: Applies a named theme (color palette and fonts) to the entire deck, affecting all slides. Call this when the user wants to change the overall look of the presentation, e.g. 'make it look more corporate' or 'switch to the dark theme.'

sites.name: webmcp-integration.vercel.app
sites.description: Find your next open source contribution in minutes, not hours. Powered by WebMCP.

tools.name: search_projects
tools.description: Search open-source projects by broad filters (domain, activity, stars) when the user does NOT name specific skills/languages. If the user names languages/skills, prefer match_skills_to_projects instead so the skill graph populates.

tools.name: match_skills_to_projects
tools.description: ALWAYS use this tool when the user names any programming language or skill — including phrasings like 'find me Python projects', 'JavaScript and Python beginner projects', 'show me Rust repos', or 'actually, find me Python projects'. This is the ONLY tool that populates the on-screen skill graph, so prefer it over search_projects whenever a language/skill is mentioned. Pass every language/skill the user named in the 'skills' array and set experienceLevel from words like 'beginner'.

tools.name: find_issues
tools.description: Find open issues in a project filtered by labels, difficulty, or skill requirements.

projectId.description: e.g. facebook/react

tools.name: summarize_project
tools.description: Get comprehensive project summary including purpose, tech stack, and community health.

tools.name: estimate_first_response_time
tools.description: Estimate how responsive a project is to contributors by sampling recent closed pull requests: median time to first response (first comment/review from someone other than the PR author) and median time to merge. Returns a responsiveness rating. Use to judge whether a PR here is likely to be reviewed or ignored — pairs well with search_projects to find active AND responsive projects.

projectId.description: e.g. facebook/react

sampleSize.description: How many recent closed PRs to sample (3-15, default 10)

tools.name: explain_issue
tools.description: Get beginner-friendly explanation of an issue with context and suggested approach.

tools.name: draft_contribution_plan
tools.description: Generate a concrete, step-by-step first-contribution plan for a project (and optionally a specific issue): setup commands, which files to look at, how to run tests, and a PR checklist. Synthesizes the repo's README and CONTRIBUTING guide with AI. Use when the user has picked a project/issue and asks how to actually get started.

projectId.description: e.g. facebook/react

issueId.description: Optional issue number to tailor the plan to a specific issue

tools.name: assess_issue_difficulty
tools.description: Assess whether an issue is realistically doable for a given experience level, beyond its label. Analyzes comment volume, age, description detail, keywords, and assignment/claim signals to return a difficulty score, reasons, and red flags (taken, contentious, stale). Use after find_issues to filter to genuinely doable issues.

projectId.description: e.g. facebook/react

tools.name: check_issue_availability
tools.description: Check whether an issue is free to work on: is it assigned, has someone claimed it in a recent comment, or is there already an open PR referencing it? Returns available | likely-taken | taken with evidence. Use after find_issues, before a user commits time to an issue, to avoid duplicate work.

projectId.description: e.g. facebook/react

tools.name: check_contribution_requirements
tools.description: Get contribution requirements including CLA, code style, testing, and PR process.

tools.name: track_contribution
tools.description: Track a project or issue in the contribution tracker, OR change the status of an already-tracked one. Provide projectId (owner/repo) and a status: interested, in-progress, pr-submitted, merged, or abandoned. Use for requests like track facebook/react, mark next.js as merged, or move it to in-progress. The change shows on the dashboard.

tools.name: get_mentorship_projects
tools.description: Find projects in mentorship programs like GSoC, Outreachy, MLH, or Hacktoberfest.

tools.name: highlight_project
tools.description: Visually highlight a project node in the on-screen skill graph. Pass a specific name (e.g. 'excalidraw' or 'facebook/react'), OR a superlative describing the current results: 'most-starred', 'most-forked', or 'most-issues'. The matching node glows and its connections are emphasized while others dim. Use this (NOT a new search) when the user asks to point out, highlight, or focus on a project in the results already shown.

project.description: Project name or owner/repo to highlight in the graph.

tools.name: focus_skill
tools.description: Focus the on-screen skill graph on a single selected skill (e.g. 'Python'), emphasizing that skill node and the projects it connects to while fading the rest. Use when the user wants to see the projects for one particular skill.

skill.description: The skill/language to focus on (must be one the user selected).

tools.name: reset_graph
tools.description: Clear any highlight or focus on the on-screen skill graph, restoring all nodes and connections to full visibility.

tools.name: summarize_my_progress
tools.description: Summarize the user's open-source contribution journey from their tracker. Returns totals per status, the tech stacks (languages) they use most, which merged project they closed fastest, average days-to-merge, when they started, and their completion rate. Use when the user asks things like 'how's my progress', 'what tech do I use most', 'which project did I close earliest', or 'summarize my contributions'.

tools.name: set_skill_profile
tools.description: Update what the app remembers about the user: skills/languages, interests/domains, experience level, contribution types. ADD via skills/interests (they MERGE and de-duplicate, so 'also add Go' keeps prior skills). REMOVE specific items via removeSkills/removeInterests (e.g. 'drop Go' -> removeSkills: ['Go']) — this deletes only those items and keeps the rest. Classify a language/framework (Rust, React) as a skill and a domain/topic (developer tools, climate) as an interest. To wipe everything, set clear:true. Use for statements like 'remember I know Rust', 'add Go to my skills', 'drop Go', or 'forget my profile'.

clear.description: If true, forget the entire profile.

tools.name: get_skill_profile
tools.description: Show the user what the app currently remembers about them: their saved skills, interests, experience level, and contribution preferences. Read-only — does NOT search or change anything. Use for questions like 'what skills have you logged for me?', 'what do you remember about me?', or 'show my profile'.

tools.name: get_recommendations
tools.description: Recommend projects tailored to the user's SAVED profile (skills + interests), without them re-stating anything. Renders the matches in the on-screen skill graph and results, like match_skills_to_projects. Use for open-ended requests such as 'what should I work on?', 'recommend me some projects', or 'find me something new'. If the user names specific skills in THIS request, pass them in overrideSkills — an explicit request wins over the saved profile for this turn.

overrideSkills.description: Skills explicitly named in this request; these take precedence over the saved profile.

sites.description: A meal-planning and shopping-list app that humans and AI agents can drive together, live, via WebMCP.

tools.name: search-recipes
tools.description: Search the recipe catalog by free-text query, required tags, and/or a max prep time. By default, results are filtered to only recipes that match the household's currently active dietary preferences.

query.description: Free text to match against recipe name or ingredients.

tags.description: Require all of these tags.

maxPrepMinutes.description: Only include recipes that take this many minutes or less.

respectDietary.description: Filter out recipes that conflict with active dietary preferences. Defaults to true.

maxCaloriesPerServing.description: Only include recipes at or under this many calories per serving.

minProteinPerServing.description: Only include recipes with at least this many grams of protein per serving.

sortBy.description: How to order results. 'pantryMatch' ranks recipes needing the fewest additional ingredients first -- use this to answer "what can I make with what I already have". 'expiringSoon' ranks recipes that use the most soon-to-expire pantry items first -- use this to reduce food waste. Defaults to 'relevance'.

tools.name: get-recipe
tools.description: Get full details for one recipe, including ingredients and instructions, by its recipe id.

recipeId.description: The recipe id, e.g. from search-recipes results.

tools.name: get-dietary-preferences
tools.description: Get the household's currently active dietary preferences and avoided ingredients.

tools.name: set-dietary-preferences
tools.description: Update the household's dietary preferences (vegetarian, vegan, glutenFree, dairyFree, nutFree) and/or the list of ingredients to avoid. Only the fields provided are changed. Affects future recipe searches and blocks conflicting meal-plan additions unless overridden.

avoidIngredients.description: Ingredient names to avoid entirely, e.g. ["shellfish"].

tools.name: get-meal-plan
tools.description: Get the full Mon-Sun meal plan with recipe names, servings, and an estimated total cost for the week.

tools.name: get-week-nutrition-summary
tools.description: Get per-serving nutrition (calories, protein, carbs, fat) for each planned day plus the weekly total and the average per planned day -- use this to answer "how many calories a day is this plan averaging" or check it hits a protein target.

tools.name: add-recipe-to-plan
tools.description: Assign a recipe to a day of the week. Fails with an explanation if the recipe conflicts with active dietary preferences unless force is true. Automatically refreshes the shopping list.

day.description: Day of the week to plan.

recipeId.description: Recipe id to assign, from search-recipes or get-recipe.

servings.description: Servings to cook; defaults to the recipe's normal serving size.

force.description: Set true to add the recipe even if it conflicts with dietary preferences.

tools.name: remove-recipe-from-plan
tools.description: Clear whatever recipe is assigned to a given day of the week. Automatically refreshes the shopping list.

tools.name: plan-week
tools.description: Automatically fill in the meal plan for multiple days at once under a set of constraints, instead of calling add-recipe-to-plan repeatedly. Always respects active dietary preferences (never overrides them). By default only fills empty days, avoids repeating a recipe already used that week, and -- if a weekly budget is set -- skips a day rather than exceed it. Returns which days were planned and, for any day that couldn't be filled, why.

days.description: Days to plan; defaults to all 7.

tags.description: Require all of these tags on every recipe chosen.

maxPrepMinutes.description: Only consider recipes that take this many minutes or less.

avoidRepeats.description: Don't reuse a recipe already planned elsewhere this week. Defaults to true.

onlyEmptyDays.description: Only fill days with no recipe assigned yet. Defaults to true.

respectBudget.description: Skip a day rather than exceed the weekly budget, if one is set. Defaults to true.

maxCaloriesPerServing.description: Only consider recipes at or under this many calories per serving.

minProteinPerServing.description: Only consider recipes with at least this many grams of protein per serving.

prioritizeExpiring.description: Prefer recipes that use pantry items expiring soon, to reduce food waste. Defaults to false (prefers pantry match generally).

tools.name: get-budget-status
tools.description: Get the weekly grocery budget (if set), the meal plan's current estimated cost, and how much room is left.

tools.name: set-weekly-budget
tools.description: Set (or clear, with amount: null) the household's target weekly grocery budget in dollars.

amount.description: Non-negative dollar amount, or null to clear the budget.

tools.name: get-pantry
tools.description: List pantry staples the household is tracking and whether each is currently in stock.

tools.name: update-pantry-item
tools.description: Mark a pantry item as in stock or needed, and/or set when it expires. Items marked 'have' are excluded from the generated shopping list even if a planned recipe calls for them. Fields omitted are left unchanged.

have.description: true if currently stocked at home. Omit to leave unchanged.

expiresOn.description: ISO date string (e.g. "2026-09-05") this item expires on, or null to clear it. Omit to leave unchanged.

tools.name: get-expiring-soon
tools.description: List pantry items that are on hand and expire within the given number of days (default 3), soonest first -- use this to plan meals that use them up and reduce food waste. A negative daysUntilExpiry means already expired.

withinDays.description: Expiry window in days. Defaults to 3.

tools.name: get-shopping-list
tools.description: Get the current shopping list: ingredients needed for the week's planned recipes, minus what's already in the pantry.

tools.name: regenerate-shopping-list
tools.description: Recompute the shopping list from the current meal plan and pantry state. Usually unnecessary since other tools auto-refresh it, but useful to force a recheck.

tools.name: toggle-shopping-item
tools.description: Check or uncheck an item on the shopping list, e.g. after it's been bought.

unit.description: Optional unit to disambiguate items with the same name.

tools.name: get-recent-activity
tools.description: Get a log of recent actions taken on this plan by either the human or an agent, most recent first.

limit.description: Max entries to return, defaults to 10.

tools.name: undo-last-action
tools.description: Revert the single most recent state-changing action (by either the human or an agent) -- plan changes, pantry edits, dietary/budget changes, or shopping-list edits. Only one level deep and there is no redo, so check get-recent-activity first if you're unsure what it would undo. Fails if there's nothing to undo.

sites.name: 3way.dev
sites.description: Halden is a working 3way shop exchange: a person, their visiting agent, and the store's service agent share an attributed return or support session.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Search the catalogue.

query.description: Free text search.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Fetch one product by SKU.

tools.name: list_my_orders
tools.description: List the signed-in customer's orders.

tools.name: get_order_status
tools.description: Status and contents of one order.

tools.name: get_policy
tools.description: The full returns and warranty policy text.

tools.name: get_conversation
tools.description: The conversation so far, with who said each line.

tools.name: evaluate_return_eligibility
tools.description: Authoritative verdict on whether an item can be returned, and by which route. Always call this instead of reasoning about the policy yourself.

itemId.description: The id of the line within the order — the `itemId` field returned by get_order_status or list_my_orders, e.g. "IT-1". Call one of those first if you do not have it. This is not the SKU and not the product title.

reason.description: Why the item is coming back. Pick by what the customer actually described, and do not reason about the policy consequences — that is what the verdict is for. defect: the item itself is faulty or arrived broken, with nothing said about the parcel or the courier — a cracked, dead, or misbehaving item is this one. damaged-in-transit: the customer described damage to the shipment — a crushed box, torn packaging, a courier incident. Do not choose this merely because the item is broken; it needs something said about the shipping. wrong-item: we shipped something other than what was ordered. changed-mind: nothing is wrong with it.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Add a message to the shared exchange. The person and the service can see it. Set intent to "relay" only when passing on what the person said; otherwise the message is attributed to the visiting agent speaking for itself.

text.description: What to say.

intent.description: Defaults to "own".

tools.name: provide_context
tools.description: Front-load what you already know about the customer and their problem, so the store does not have to ask. Call this first, before anything else.

summary.description: One or two sentences on what the customer wants.

data.description: Structured facts: orderId, dates, what was tried.

tools.name: request_return
tools.description: Propose a return or warranty claim. Always allowed — this only creates a pending request and tells you whether it qualifies. It does not move any money.

itemId.description: The id of the line within the order — the `itemId` field returned by get_order_status or list_my_orders, e.g. "IT-1". Call one of those first if you do not have it. This is not the SKU and not the product title.

reason.description: Why the item is coming back. Pick by what the customer actually described, and do not reason about the policy consequences — that is what the verdict is for. defect: the item itself is faulty or arrived broken, with nothing said about the parcel or the courier — a cracked, dead, or misbehaving item is this one. damaged-in-transit: the customer described damage to the shipment — a crushed box, torn packaging, a courier incident. Do not choose this merely because the item is broken; it needs something said about the shipping. wrong-item: we shipped something other than what was ordered. changed-mind: nothing is wrong with it.

tools.name: request_cancel
tools.description: Propose cancelling an order before it arrives. Always allowed — this only creates a pending request and tells you whether the order can still be stopped. It cancels nothing on its own.

tools.name: request_address_change
tools.description: Propose redirecting an order to a different address before it arrives. Always allowed — this only creates a pending request and tells you whether the order can still be redirected. It changes nothing on its own.

address.description: The full new delivery address, as the customer gave it.

tools.name: request_records_release
tools.description: Propose releasing the customer's own account records for one order — the card type and its last four digits, the billing postcode, and the delivery address on file. Always allowed: this only creates a pending request and discloses nothing. The records are not readable any other way, including by you.

tools.name: disclose_order_records
tools.description: Release the customer's account records for a pending request: card type and last four digits, billing postcode, and delivery address. The values are held by the server and returned only against a completed confirmation — this page never has them beforehand, so there is nothing here to read without the customer present. This is a consequential action. It only succeeds after the customer confirms it themselves in the widget — you cannot confirm on their behalf.

requestId.description: The id returned by request_records_release.

tools.name: await_reply
tools.description: Wait here until someone else says something. Nothing is pushed to you otherwise: this page can only answer calls you make, so after you say something, the reply exists in the conversation but you will not see it until your next call. Call this to wait for it instead of ending your turn or polling in a loop. It returns as soon as there is anything new, or after a few seconds with nothing_new: true if the conversation stayed quiet — call it again if you are still waiting. Safe to call at any time; it changes nothing and can wait on nothing but conversation.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait before giving up, in milliseconds. Default 25000, max 30000.

tools.name: confirm_return
tools.description: Confirm and complete a pending return or warranty claim, refunding the customer. This is a consequential action. It only succeeds after the customer confirms it themselves in the widget — you cannot confirm on their behalf.

requestId.description: The id returned by request_return.

tools.name: cancel_order
tools.description: Cancel the order. This is a consequential action. It only succeeds after the customer confirms it themselves in the widget — you cannot confirm on their behalf.

requestId.description: The id returned by request_cancel.

tools.name: change_address
tools.description: Change the delivery address. This is a consequential action. It only succeeds after the customer confirms it themselves in the widget — you cannot confirm on their behalf.

requestId.description: The id returned by request_address_change.

sites.name: agentbridge-webmcp.netlify.app
sites.description: Next-generation luxury apparel platform exposing 34 WebMCP tools on document.modelContext for AI agents while delivering a sleek human shopping experience.

tools.name: login
tools.description: Authenticate a user with their email address and password. Use this when the user wants to sign in, or when a protected tool returns AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED. Returns the authenticated user profile on success, or an error message for invalid credentials. After a successful login, previously unavailable authenticated tools become available.

tools.name: register
tools.description: Create a new user account with a name, email, and password. Use this when the user wants to sign up for a new account. Returns the newly created user profile on success. The user is automatically logged in after registration, making authenticated tools available.

name.description: Full name for the new account.

email.description: Email address for the new account.

password.description: Password for the new account (minimum 6 characters).

tools.name: get_account_info
tools.description: Check the current authentication status and retrieve the logged-in user profile. Use this to determine whether the user is signed in before attempting protected operations. Returns the user profile (id, name, email, role) if authenticated, or an unauthenticated status.

tools.name: navigate_to_page
tools.description: Navigate the user's browser to a specific page or section in the store with proper security boundaries and flow validation. Allowed targets: "home" (/), "products" (/products), "product_detail" (/products/{productId}), "compare" (/compare), "cart" (/cart), "checkout" (/checkout), "account" (/account), "orders" (/account?tab=orders), "wishlist" (/account?tab=wishlist). Protected pages (checkout, account, orders, wishlist) enforce session and cart requirements before navigating. Use this tool when the user asks to go to, open, or visit a major store section.

page.description: Target page within the application.

productId.description: Product ID or slug (required when page is "product_detail").

items.description: Product ID or slug.

productIds.description: List of product IDs when navigating to "compare".

category.description: Category slug to filter when navigating to "products" (e.g. "laptops", "smartphones").

searchQuery.description: Search keyword to filter when navigating to "products".

view.description: Comparison layout mode: "parallel" (side-by-side) or "serial" (stacked detailed cards).

tools.name: view_product_page
tools.description: Navigate the user's browser directly to a specific product detail page to display photos, full hardware specifications, stock status, and customer reviews. Use this when the user asks to "show", "open", "view", or "inspect" a specific product. The productId must be a valid ID or slug from a prior search or catalog result.

productId.description: Product ID or slug to open in the browser.

tools.name: view_comparison_page
tools.description: Open the product comparison page in the user's browser to compare 2 to 4 products side-by-side or serially. Use this when the user asks to compare multiple products visually on the screen. The page adapts its presentation to "parallel" (side-by-side columns, ideal for 2-3 products) or "serial" (stacked detailed cards, ideal for 4+ products or mobile). Product IDs must come from previous search or catalog results.

items.description: Product ID or slug.

productIds.description: List of 2 to 4 product IDs to compare on screen.

view.description: Comparison layout mode: "parallel" for side-by-side columns, "serial" for stacked detailed cards, or "auto" to adapt to product count.

tools.name: filter_apparel
tools.description: Filter the fashion and apparel catalog by specific clothing attributes: gender (Women, Men), category (Tops, T-Shirts, Jeans), color (Red, Blue, Green, Black, White, Indigo), size (XS, S, M, L, XL, 26-36), and price range. Returns matching apparel items with colors, available sizes, fabric specifications, prices, and stock status. Prevents failure modes by validating available color-department combinations: Women Tops are available in Red, Blue, Green; Men T-Shirts are available in Black, White, Blue; Jeans are in Indigo, Blue, Black.

color.description: Color filter: Red, Blue, Green (women tops); Black, White, Blue (men tees); Indigo, Blue, Black (jeans).

size.description: Size filter: e.g. "XS", "S", "M", "L", "XL" or waist sizes "26", "28", "30", "32", "34".

inStockOnly.description: If true, returns only items currently in stock.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (default: 15).

tools.name: get_apparel_size_guide
tools.description: Retrieve verified size charts, fit recommendations, and body measurements (bust, chest, waist, hips, inseam) for Women's Tops, Men's T-Shirts, Women's Jeans, and Men's Jeans. Use this tool whenever users ask about sizing, fit advice, or body measurements to prevent wrong-size ordering and return failures.

category.description: Apparel category to retrieve sizing for: "WomensTops", "MensTshirts", "WomensJeans", "MensJeans", or "All".

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Search the store product catalog by keyword, product name, brand, or category. Use this when the user asks to find, discover, or look up products. Returns matching products with their IDs, names, prices, ratings, stock status, and specifications. Product IDs from the results can be used with get_product_details, add_to_cart, compare_products, and other tools.

query.description: Product name, keyword, color, brand, or category (e.g., "red silk blouse", "black pima cotton tee", "high-rise indigo jeans").

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (default: 10).

tools.name: get_product_details
tools.description: Retrieve full details for a specific product by its ID or slug. Use this when the user asks for more information about a particular product found via search_products or filter_products. sites.name: agentic-sudoku.vercel.app
sites.description: A Sudoku board you and an agent can solve together.

tools.name: get_board_state
tools.description: Read the current Sudoku board. Rows are numbered 1-9 top to bottom, columns 1-9 left to right, and boxes 1-9 in reading order. Returns all 81 cells with their digit (or null if empty), who put it there ('clue' for the puzzle's starting digits, 'player' for the human, 'agent' for you), and the pencil candidates written in that cell. Also returns the difficulty, elapsed time, and whether the board is playing, paused, or complete. The puzzle solution is not available through any tool -- reason from the visible board, as the human does.

tools.name: check_for_conflicts
tools.description: List every cell involved in a duplicate digit within a row, column, or box, grouped so you can see which cells collide with which. Rows are numbered 1-9 top to bottom and columns 1-9 left to right. Returns an empty list when the board has no duplicates. This reports duplicates only -- it does not tell you whether a digit is correct, because the site never reveals the puzzle solution.

tools.name: highlight_pattern_cells
tools.description: Tint cells on the board to point the human at a pattern, without changing anything they have written. Rows are numbered 1-9 top to bottom, columns 1-9 left to right, and boxes 1-9 in reading order. Use target_cells for the cells your deduction concludes about, and because_cells for the cells that justify it; the two are drawn differently so the human can tell them apart. Supply at least one of the two. Marks fade on their own after about a minute, and change no digit and no pencil mark. Requires explanation: one or two sentences the human will see, saying what you are pointing at and why.

tools.name: show_pattern_hint_toast
tools.description: Show the human a short coaching note near the Sudoku board. Rows are numbered 1-9 top to bottom, columns 1-9 left to right, and boxes 1-9 in reading order. It disappears after five seconds, or sooner if they dismiss it. It never takes their keyboard focus and never stops them playing. The explanation you supply IS the note the human reads, so write it to them, not about them.

tools.name: clear_visual_annotations
tools.description: Remove every highlight, beam, and coaching note you have placed on the Sudoku board. Rows are numbered 1-9 top to bottom, columns 1-9 left to right, and boxes 1-9 in reading order. The human's digits, pencil marks, timer, and undo history are untouched -- this clears only your own marks.

tools.name: fill_cell
tools.description: Put one digit into one empty, non-clue cell of the Sudoku board. Rows are numbered 1-9 top to bottom, columns 1-9 left to right, and boxes 1-9 in reading order. The cell must be empty and not a starting clue, and the board must not be paused or complete, or the call is rejected and nothing changes. You are allowed to be wrong: a digit that duplicates one in the same row, column, or box will be placed and flagged as a conflict, exactly as it would be for the human. The human can undo it with a single press of their Undo button, and your digit is marked as yours on the board. Their selected cell does not move. Requires explanation: one or two sentences saying why this digit goes here, which the human sees.

tools.name: draw_constraint_beams
tools.description: Cast a visible ray along a whole row, column, or box of the Sudoku board to show a constraint -- for example, the row that already contains a 6 and therefore rules a 6 out elsewhere. Rows are numbered 1-9 top to bottom, columns 1-9 left to right, and boxes 1-9 in reading order. Beams are drawn as lines, which keeps them distinct from the human's own square highlighting, and several beams stay individually readable where they cross. Optionally name the digit a beam is about. Beams fade on their own after about a minute and change nothing on the board. Requires explanation: one or two sentences the human will see, saying what the beams rule out.

tools.name: update_pencil_marks
tools.description: Set the pencil candidates of specific empty cells of the Sudoku board to exactly the digits you list. Rows are numbered 1-9 top to bottom, columns 1-9 left to right, and boxes 1-9 in reading order. This replaces whatever was in those cells -- an empty digit list erases that cell's marks. No other cell is touched, and the whole call is a single undo step for the human. Cells holding a digit, and starting clues, are rejected: if any cell you list is invalid, NOTHING is changed, so you can retry the whole call after correcting it. Requires explanation: one or two sentences the human will see, saying why these digits and not others.

tools.name: auto_fill_all_pencil_marks
tools.description: Fill every empty cell of the Sudoku board with exactly the digits that are still legal there, given the board as it stands. Rows are numbered 1-9 top to bottom, columns 1-9 left to right, and boxes 1-9 in reading order. Cells that already hold a digit are not touched. This is one undo step for the human. If the human has written their own pencil marks, this replaces them -- in that case you must pass acknowledges_replacing_marks: true AND say so in your explanation, or the call is rejected. The candidates are worked out from the visible board only, exactly as the human would work them out.

tools.name: playback_deduction_sequence
tools.description: Play a short walkthrough on the Sudoku board: a list of steps performed one after another, each with its own explanation shown as that step happens. Use it to teach a chain of reasoning. Rows are numbered 1-9 top to bottom, columns 1-9 left to right, and boxes 1-9 in reading order. Each step has an action: "fill" places a digit (needs row, col, digit); "pencil" sets a cell's candidates (needs row, col, digits); "highlight" marks cells (needs cells); "beam" casts a ray (needs unit_type and unit_number). The human can stop it at any moment simply by clicking or typing on the board -- playback halts immediately, completed steps stay done and are NOT rolled back, and this call tells you how many finished and why it stopped. Each step remains a separate undo step for the human. This call takes several seconds to return, by design.

tools.name: load_technique_practice
tools.description: Replace the current Sudoku puzzle with a curated one that drills a specific technique. Rows are numbered 1-9 top to bottom, columns 1-9 left to right, and boxes 1-9 in reading order. This DISCARDS the human's current board and they are NOT asked first, so only do it when they have asked you to, and say why. Drills are available for: hidden-single, locked-candidates, naked-pair. Every drill has exactly one solution and genuinely requires its technique -- it cannot be finished without it.

tools.name: show_coordinate_ruler
tools.description: Show numbered guides around the Sudoku grid: the column numbers 1 to 9 across the top and the row numbers 1 to 9 down the left side. Rows are numbered 1-9 top to bottom, columns 1-9 left to right, and boxes 1-9 in reading order. Use this so the human can read a cell’s coordinates straight off the board instead of counting squares — it makes it much easier for them to tell you which cell they mean. The guides stay until they are removed and change nothing about the puzzle: no digit, no candidate, no timer, and nothing to undo. Calling this when they are already showing is fine and simply does nothing. Requires explanation: one or two sentences saying why, which the human sees.

tools.name: hide_coordinate_ruler
tools.description: Remove the numbered row and column guides from around the Sudoku grid. Rows are numbered 1-9 top to bottom, columns 1-9 left to right, and boxes 1-9 in reading order. This changes nothing about the puzzle itself — no digit, no candidate, no timer, and nothing to undo. Calling this when the guides are not showing is fine and simply does nothing. Requires explanation: one or two sentences saying why, which the human sees.

tools.name: switch_difficulty
tools.description: Load a brand-new Sudoku puzzle at a chosen difficulty, replacing the one on screen. Rows are numbered 1-9 top to bottom, columns 1-9 left to right, and boxes 1-9 in reading order. A new puzzle resets the clock to zero and clears the undo history, and every puzzle has exactly one solution. The board cannot be switched while it is paused. This DISCARDS whatever the human had done on the current board, and they are NOT asked first -- so only do it when they have asked you to, and say why. Requires explanation: one or two sentences saying why you are changing the difficulty, which the human sees.

tools.name: pause_timer
tools.description: Pause the game: the elapsed-time clock stops and the board is covered, exactly as it is when the human presses their own Pause button. Rows are numbered 1-9 top to bottom, columns 1-9 left to right, and boxes 1-9 in reading order. The human can resume at any moment with their own Resume control, and you can resume with "resume_timer". While the board is paused, every other tool that changes it is refused; reading the board still works. This changes no digit, no candidate, and nothing that can be undone. Requires explanation: one or two sentences saying why you are pausing, which the human sees.

tools.name: resume_timer
tools.description: Resume a paused game: the clock restarts from where it stopped and the board becomes playable again. Rows are numbered 1-9 top to bottom, columns 1-9 left to right, and boxes 1-9 in reading order. This is the one tool that works while the board is paused -- every other tool that changes the board is refused until the game is running again. This changes no digit, no candidate, and nothing that can be undone. Requires explanation: one or two sentences, which the human sees.

tools.name: restart_puzzle
tools.description: Replace the board with a DIFFERENT Sudoku puzzle at the SAME difficulty it is already on. Rows are numbered 1-9 top to bottom, columns 1-9 left to right, and boxes 1-9 in reading order. Use this when the human wants a fresh grid rather than a harder or easier one -- for example when they come back to a half-finished board they no longer want. It takes no difficulty argument on purpose: the level is read from the board, so the level after is the level before. The new puzzle is always a different grid, has exactly one solution, resets the clock to zero, and clears the undo history. The board cannot be restarted while it is paused. This discards whatever the human had done, and they are NOT asked first -- so only do it when they have asked you to, and say why. Requires explanation: one or two sentences saying why, which the human sees.

tools.name: undo_move
tools.description: Take back the most recent change to the Sudoku board -- exactly what the human's own Undo button does, and reversible by them in the same way. Rows are numbered 1-9 top to bottom, columns 1-9 left to right, and boxes 1-9 in reading order. It always takes back the LAST change, whoever made it: yours or theirs. The result tells you which, so you can say what you just took back. A change that touched several cells at once, such as filling every pencil mark, is taken back whole in a single step. There is nothing to undo on a board where nothing has been changed yet, and the call is refused while the board is paused. There is no redo, so a change you take back is gone. Requires explanation: one or two sentences saying why you are taking this back, which the human sees.

Definitions can include POMs or actions that are not currently visible or callable; action return POMs describe possible next surfaces, not guarantees. sites.name: canvasmind-design.netlify.app
sites.description: Plan a room and check whether a wheelchair user can actually reach every seat. Exposes its geometry to AI agents over WebMCP.

tools.name: get_layout
tools.description: Return the room's name and dimensions, and every item in it with its id, type, label, exact position and size. ALL UNITS ARE CENTIMETRES, with (0,0) at the top-left corner of the room. Call this FIRST before any edit, because item ids are the only way to address furniture. The room is drawn to a bitmap canvas with no DOM, so this is the only way to know what is in it.

tools.name: find_items
tools.description: Find items by a case-insensitive substring of their label, by exact type, or both. Use this instead of get_layout when the room is busy and you only need a few items.

query.description: Substring of the label, or an exact item id

type.description: Restrict to one furniture type

tools.name: describe_selection
tools.description: Return the item the HUMAN currently has selected, plus its four nearest neighbours and the exact gap in centimetres to each. Call this when the user says 'this table', 'that one', or 'the selected item' — it is how you resolve what they are pointing at.

tools.name: measure_gap
tools.description: Return the exact shortest distance in centimetres between two items, and whether that gap is wide enough for a wheelchair (needs 90cm). Use this to answer questions like "can someone get between these two tables?". Measuring a distance from rendered pixels is not something a vision model can do reliably.

tools.name: check_accessibility
tools.description: Run the full accessibility audit on the current layout. Checks for items outside the room, overlapping furniture, blocked door clearance zones (150cm), and — most importantly — whether every item can actually be REACHED from a doorway along a continuous 90cm wide route. Reachability is computed with a flood fill over an occupancy grid, so it catches furniture that is boxed in even when nothing overlaps. Returns ok:true when the layout passes. While it reports problems, a 'fix_accessibility' tool becomes available.

tools.name: add_item
tools.description: Place a new item in the room and return it, including its generated id. Position x,y is the TOP-LEFT corner in centimetres. Each type has sensible default dimensions (a round_table is 150x150cm and seats 8; a wheelchair_space is 90x130cm) which you can override with w and h, and a natural shape you can override with shape:'rect' or shape:'round'. Omit x and y to auto-place. A room needs at least one 'door' item on a wall or nothing can be reached.

type.description: Furniture type

label.description: Short name, e.g. 'Table 7' or 'Fire exit'

x.description: Left edge in cm from the room's left wall

y.description: Top edge in cm from the room's top wall

shape.description: Override the outline. Defaults to the type's natural shape.

tools.name: move_item
tools.description: Move an item so its top-left corner sits at an exact centimetre position. This is precision a vision model cannot achieve from a screenshot.

id.description: Item id from get_layout, e.g. 'i3'

tools.name: resize_item
tools.description: Set an item's width and depth in centimetres. Minimum 20cm; the item is kept inside the room. Use this to model real furniture the user owns — a 220cm banquet table, a 60cm-deep bar. Resizing changes clearances, so re-run check_accessibility afterwards.

id.description: Item id from get_layout

tools.name: rotate_item
tools.description: Rotate an item by 90 degrees, swapping its width and depth. Position is unchanged.

tools.name: set_item_props
tools.description: Change an item's label and/or its seat count. Position and size are unchanged.

label.description: New label

tools.name: remove_item
tools.description: Take an item out of the room permanently, along with the seats it provided. Not undoable, so confirm with the user before removing anything they placed.

tools.name: align_items
tools.description: Align two or more items to their shared average on one axis. axis:'x' lines them up in a vertical column; axis:'y' lines them up in a horizontal row.

ids.description: Item ids to align

axis.description: 'x' = same left edge, 'y' = same top edge

tools.name: auto_arrange
tools.description: Push all furniture apart until every gap meets the wheelchair route width and every door clearance zone is clear, keeping everything inside the room. Animates over a few seconds and honours cancellation. Use this when the user says 'fix the spacing', 'make this accessible', 'tidy up' or 'rearrange'. Returns whether the layout is compliant afterwards.

tools.name: show_accessible_route
tools.description: Toggle the visual overlay on the canvas. Green shows floor a wheelchair can actually reach from a doorway; red shows floor that is wide enough but cut off. Turn this on when explaining an accessibility problem to the user so they can see what you are describing.

show.description: true to show, false to hide, omit to toggle

tools.name: set_room
tools.description: Set the room's name and/or its interior dimensions in centimetres. The canvas is drawn at 1 pixel per centimetre, so a 1200x700 room is 12m x 7m. Every field is optional — pass only what you want to change.

name.description: What this room is called, e.g. 'Banquet Hall'

tools.name: export_image
tools.description: Download the current floor plan as an image file, with the room name and the accessibility verdict stamped underneath it — so the exported file is a shareable record, not just a screenshot. Use this when the user says they want to save, download, export or send the plan.

format.description: Image format (default png)

tools.name: clear_room
tools.description: Remove every item including doors. Not undoable — confirm with the user first.

tools.name: fix_accessibility
tools.description: Available ONLY while check_accessibility reports problems. Pulls furniture back inside the room, clears door zones, and separates items until every route meets the wheelchair width. Returns what it changed and whether the layout now passes.

sites.name: careers-webmcp.vercel.app
sites.description: Join Northwind, headquartered in India with a globally distributed workforce. We're building the intelligent infrastructure that connects exceptional talent with borderless opportunity.

tools.name: careers_get_context
tools.description: Get a bounded snapshot of where the current user is on the careers site: sign-in state, current page, current job/application, and active search filters.

tools.name: careers_search_jobs
tools.description: Search the current employer job catalog with structured filters (department, level, location, workplace, skills, compensation) or free text. Returns bounded, ranked results.

tools.name: careers_get_job

tools.name: careers_open_page

Use it instead of building a link yourself; careers_get_context lists which pages are available.

tools.name: careers_get_site_info

topic.description: Omit to get every topic.

tools.name: careers_get_saved_jobs
tools.description: List job postings the signed-in candidate has saved for later.

tools.name: careers_set_saved_job
tools.description: Save or remove a job posting from the signed-in candidate saved list. Uses the same save action as the normal careers site.

tools.name: careers_get_my_applications
tools.description: List the signed-in candidate own job applications with status and revision.

tools.name: careers_get_application
tools.description: Retrieve the signed-in candidate own application draft or submitted application, including current field values and any missing required fields.

tools.name: careers_start_application
tools.description: Start (or resume) the signed-in candidate application draft for a job, prefilled from their profile, using the same flow as the normal Apply button.

tools.name: careers_update_application
tools.description: Update fields on the signed-in candidate own draft application. Requires the last-read revision; rejected if the human has changed the draft since.

tools.name: careers_submit_application
tools.description: Check the candidate's draft against the same rules as the normal form, then open it for final review. This site requires the person to press Submit themselves, so this tool does not submit for them: it returns 'awaiting_human_confirmation', or VALIDATION_ERROR listing what is missing.

tools.name: careers_set_search_view
tools.description: Show a search on the site's own jobs page: opens open-positions, types the query into the visible search box, and applies the filters. Use it after careers_search_jobs to put your results on screen for the person; read results from careers_search_jobs, not from here.

query.description: Free text typed into the visible search box.

department.description: Department name exactly as the site lists it, e.g. "Engineering".

country.description: Country name or slug, e.g. "United States".

tools.name: careers_focus_application_field
tools.description: Open the candidate's application and move the cursor to one field, highlighting it. Use this when the person has to supply something you should not invent — for example their phone number or notice period — so they can see exactly where to type.

applicationId.description: Defaults to the application currently open on the page.

tools.name: careers_create_account
tools.description: Fill this site's normal sign-up form with details the person gave you and open it for them to confirm. It never creates the account itself: it returns 'awaiting_human_confirmation', and once they press Create account careers_get_context reports them signed in. Never invent an email address.

tools.name: careers_create_export
tools.description: Build a downloadable CSV and get back a handle to it, not the rows: row count, columns and a short preview. Use it instead of paging search results when you need a whole result set, then read only the slices and columns you need with careers_read_export. The person gets the same file.

query.description: Optional job filters, same shape as careers_search_jobs. Ignored for the applications dataset.

columns.description: Restrict the export to these columns. Defaults to all columns for the dataset.

tools.name: careers_read_export
tools.description: Read a bounded window of rows from an export created by careers_create_export. Narrow the columns to only what you need so you can scan a large result set without pulling every field. Returns hasMore so you know whether to continue.

sites.name: chrissaautomates.com
sites.description: See how AI research agents can decide when to stop, escalate, switch retrieval routes, and avoid unnecessary paid calls using measured benchmark evidence.

tools.name: recommend_agent_retrieval_strategy
tools.description: Compute an evidence-guided web retrieval strategy from the frozen Agent Utility Index benchmark without calling a provider.

tools.name: get_agent_utility_index_evidence
tools.description: Return the public frozen benchmark evidence that powers evidence-acquisition decisions.

tools.name: create_evidence_contract
tools.description: Create the live Agent Evidence Gate state that defines what a vendor recommendation must prove before the agent can proceed. Updates the same state visible to the human.

tools.name: inspect_evidence_gaps
tools.description: Read the required claims that still block the current agent action.

tools.name: run_direct_evidence_check
tools.description: Retrieve the contract's first-party URLs with Direct Fetch, test the hard evidence gates, update the visible workspace, and block or clear the action without spending Firecrawl credits.

tools.name: recommend_evidence_retrieval
tools.description: Apply the current contract plus the frozen Agent Utility Index policy to decide whether the agent should FREE_STOP, request Firecrawl approval, or execute an approved escalation.

tools.name: approve_firecrawl_escalation
tools.description: Sensitive paid action. Only call after the human explicitly approves paid retrieval. The exact confirmation phrase is exchanged for a short-lived server-signed token scoped to the current contract and URLs before Firecrawl can run.

tools.name: check_action_clearance
tools.description: Return ACTION_ALLOWED only when every required claim in the current evidence contract is verified; otherwise return ACTION_BLOCKED with the exact unresolved gates.

tools.name: get_evidence_decision_report
tools.description: Return the machine-readable audit report with claim evidence, source URLs, retrieval routes, paid-call counts, action clearance, and frozen benchmark context.

tools.name: research_and_verify_web_question
tools.description: Use this when the user needs current web research, vendor discovery, product comparison, pricing/plan verification, feature verification, or an evidence-backed shortlist. The user does not need to provide URLs. Discover candidates, prefer first-party evidence for hard vendor claims, and return the supported answer with sources.

known_url.description: Optional starting source URL. Do not require it when the user has not provided one.

tools.name: build_verified_shortlist
tools.description: Use for find, compare, recommend, shortlist, vendor-selection, or product-selection requests where the user has requirements. Discover candidates automatically, verify must-have claims with current web evidence, reject unsupported options, and update the same shortlist visible to the human. URLs are not required from the user.

tools.name: get_verified_shortlist
tools.description: Read the shortlist and requirements currently visible to the human, including qualified, near-match, rejected options and their evidence checks.

tools.name: refine_verified_shortlist
tools.description: Use after the human changes a requirement, such as adding a budget, removing credit-card requirements, changing a minimum allowance, or narrowing a feature. Re-run discovery and verification and update the same visible shortlist.

tools.name: create_research_board
tools.description: Create the board visible to the human. At creation time the agent may translate the user's request into must-have criteria. After creation, humans control the rules; agents control candidate discovery and evidence.

tools.name: get_research_board
tools.description: Read the exact current board state. Pass since_revision when you already saw an earlier revision; the response includes only the recorded changes since then as changes_since, while still returning the current board for safe synchronization.

tools.name: add_research_candidate
tools.description: Add a candidate discovered by the agent. Candidates are deduplicated by normalized domain when available, otherwise by normalized name. The agent may add candidates but may not change human-controlled requirements.

tools.name: update_candidate_evidence
tools.description: Write one researched candidate/requirement cell. Supply the board revision research started from and the exact evidence cell revision expected. Unrelated board edits do not invalidate the write; a changed requirement or newer write to this same cell does. VERIFIED requires a source URL. A rejected VERIFIED-without-source attempt is also written to shared activity so the human can see the guardrail fire live.

tools.name: get_missing_checks
tools.description: Return only the automatic research queue. MISSING and PARTIAL cells are eligible for automatic recheck. FAILED is terminal and excluded unless the human changes the rule or explicitly asks the agent to revisit it.

sites.name: duet-webmcp.vercel.app
sites.description: Compose music together with AI, directly in your browser.

tools.name: get_project_state
tools.description: Use this when you need a concise overview of the live Duet project before choosing an edit. Returns tempo, key, mode, chord track, selection and per-track note summaries without flooding context with every note.

tools.name: get_selection
tools.description: Use this when you need the exact notes and chord context inside the bars currently selected by the person.

tools.name: analyze_harmony
tools.description: Use this when you need deterministic harmonic analysis of a selected or explicit bar range. Duet computes chord functions and scale fit with tonal instead of guessing.

tools.name: set_selection
tools.description: Use this when you want to visibly focus the person's editor on a track and bar range before reading or changing it. This changes only the shared cursor, not the music.

tools.name: set_chord_progression
tools.description: Use this when the person asks for a chord progression. Replaces consecutive chord slots from startBar, validates every symbol, and creates audible block or arpeggiated chord notes.

mode.description: draft (default): show the result as a ghost preview the person accepts or discards on the page; apply: write immediately because the person explicitly asked for that.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional stateVersion you last read; the call is rejected if the person changed the page since.

tools.name: add_notes
tools.description: Use this when you know the exact notes to add to melody, bass, or chords. Note names and beat positions are validated and converted to Duet's internal ticks.

mode.description: draft (default): show the result as a ghost preview the person accepts or discards on the page; apply: write immediately because the person explicitly asked for that.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional stateVersion you last read; the call is rejected if the person changed the page since.

tools.name: transform_selection
tools.description: Use this when the person asks to transpose, change mode, quantize, or humanize the currently selected notes. Mode changes preserve melodic contour with deterministic tonal mapping.

mode.description: draft (default): show the result as a ghost preview the person accepts or discards on the page; apply: write immediately because the person explicitly asked for that.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional stateVersion you last read; the call is rejected if the person changed the page since.

tools.name: generate_line
tools.description: Use this when the person asks Duet to write a bass, counter melody, or pad over existing chords. Generation follows deterministic chord-tone and voice-leading rules.

mode.description: draft (default): show the result as a ghost preview the person accepts or discards on the page; apply: write immediately because the person explicitly asked for that.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional stateVersion you last read; the call is rejected if the person changed the page since.

tools.name: set_tempo
tools.description: Use this when the person asks to change playback speed. Duet safely clamps the requested tempo to 40–220 BPM and reports the applied value.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional stateVersion you last read; the call is rejected if the person changed the page since.

tools.name: play
tools.description: Use this when the person asks to listen to the project or a bar range. Starts Duet's existing browser playback; if sound has not been unlocked, returns a clear user-action request.

tools.name: get_recent_activity
tools.description: Use this at the start of a turn to see what the person did on the page since you last looked: recorded takes, notes added or deleted, chords set, selection moves, undo, drafts they accepted or discarded. Lets you react to their playing instead of asking.

tools.name: suggest_progressions
tools.description: Use this when the person describes a feeling (happy, sad, dreamy, tense, epic, jazzy, calm) instead of chord names. Returns chord progressions realized in the project's key with a one-line reason each, so you can offer choices in plain words or install one with set_chord_progression / propose_variations.

tools.name: propose_variations
tools.description: Use this to let the person choose by ear. Creates 2–3 alternative drafts for the same bars (chords by mood, or bass / pad / counter melody in different styles, or answers to a phrase). Each appears on the page as a lettered option with Listen / Accept / Discard; nothing is written until one is accepted.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional stateVersion you last read; the call is rejected if the person changed the page since.

tools.name: answer_phrase
tools.description: Call and response. Takes the phrase the person just played or selected on the Melody track and writes an answering phrase in the following bars: same rhythm, moved through the key (echo, sequence, invert or contrast), landing on chord tones. Defaults to the last recorded take, then the selection. Returns a draft the person can hear and accept.

mode.description: draft (default): show the result as a ghost preview the person accepts or discards on the page; apply: write immediately because the person explicitly asked for that.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional stateVersion you last read; the call is rejected if the person changed the page since.

tools.name: resolve_draft
tools.description: Accept or discard drafts you proposed. Use after the person tells you which option they like; accepting writes it to the song as a normal undoable change and discards only its rival options (same group), so options for other bars or tracks stay available. Without draftId, acts on the option currently previewed on the page.

tools.name: set_sections
tools.description: Label parts of the song (Intro, Verse, Chorus…) on the bar ruler so you and the person can talk about 'the chorus' instead of bar numbers. Replaces all labels; each starts at a bar and runs until the next.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional stateVersion you last read; the call is rejected if the person changed the page since.

tools.name: set_instrument
tools.description: Change the sound of a track: piano, epiano, strings, pad, bass or pluck. Cheap and instantly audible; good when the person says 'softer', 'warmer' or 'like strings'.

expectedStateVersion.description: Optional stateVersion you last read; the call is rejected if the person changed the page since.

tools.name: describe_selection
tools.description: Use this when the person says something is missing or asks what could be better but cannot say what. Returns a deterministic plain-language diagnosis of the selected bars (or a given range): empty tracks, missing or static chords, a melody that circles or leaps, notes clashing with their chord or outside the key, each with a suggested tool call. Read it, then offer choices.

isPrimary.description: Whether this column is a primary key

tools.name: export_to_sql

tools.name: suggest_improvements

tools.name: diagnose_schema_problem

tools.name: check_schema_consistency

requirement.description: The feature or requirement to check against (e.g. 'user authentication with roles', 'soft deletes', 'multi-tenancy')

tools.name: import_schema_from_sql

tools.name: import_schema_from_prisma

prisma_text.description: The full content of the Prisma schema file

tools.name: delete_table

tableName.description: Name of the table to delete

tools.name: delete_relation

sourceTable.description: The table that has the foreign key (arrow origin)

tools.name: rename_table

tools.name: get_table_details

tableName.description: Name of the table to inspect

sites.name: geodesics.org
sites.description: Trust networks need human–AI collab. WebMCP makes the shared tab easier for everyone.

tools.name: geodesics_agent_login
tools.description: Authenticate as a visitor agent. Paths: (1) Moltbook identity — { moltbook_identity } (mint at moltbook.com/api/v1/agents/me/identity-token); (2) jury desk key — { key } or { identifier, key }; (3) couple — { identifier, invite } or { mode:"linked" }; (4) classic — { identifier, secret }. Moltbook login seats you on the moltbook ring.

identifier.description: Agent id. Optional with jury key (defaults to jury-<shortcut>). Required for secret/invite.

moltbook_identity.description: Temporary Moltbook identity token (JWT). Mint with POST /api/v1/agents/me/identity-token. Never send your Moltbook API key.

key.description: Unique WebMCP challenge desk key from the application. Auth + jury ring membership.

secret.description: Issued secret from .env. Classic path — omit when using key/invite/linked.

invite.description: inv_… from human Observer. Bonds + logs in without secret.

mode.description: Elevate from human couple cookie when linked_agent is already set.

tools.name: geodesics_agent_logout
tools.description: Clear the visitor agent session in this tab.

tools.name: geodesics_couple_claim
tools.description: Claim a human couple invite (inv_…). Prefer geodesics_agent_login({ identifier, invite }) which bonds + logs in. This tool also accepts identifier+invite without a prior secret login.

invite.description: inv_… short-lived invite from the human.

identifier.description: Agent id when not already logged in (secret not required).

tools.name: geodesics_couple_request
tools.description: Logged-in agent requests a couple bond. Requires the human's Dynamic email — they get a Yes/No notification on their tab (no paste codes).

tools.name: geodesics_couple_status
tools.description: Poll whether the human accepted your couple request (Yes/No). Updates session when linked.

tools.name: geodesics_couple_inbox
tools.description: Read couple chat with your linked human (middle dock CHAT panel). Requires bond.

after.description: Optional message id — only newer messages.

tools.name: geodesics_couple_reply
tools.description: Send a chat message to your coupled human (appears in the middle CHAT panel).

body.description: Message text.

message.description: Alias for body.

key.description: Invite key from the host / human / post.

url.description: Alias for origin.

route.description: Observed path. e.g. search → product → checkout

goal.description: Optional intent.

note.description: Alias for goal.
