sites.name: glassbook.vercel.app
sites.description: Glassbook is local-first budgeting behind glass: an AI agent works beside you in this tab, and every action is visible and undoable. No server, no accounts, no API keys. Your money. Your browser.…

tools.name: get_overview
tools.description: Call this first to understand the user's ledger. Returns a one-line app description, months present with transaction counts, totals, categories, budgets, rules count, and the current view. No input. Amounts in the rest of the tool API are dollars (negative = expense).

tools.name: list_transactions
tools.description: List transactions to get ids before categorize_transactions or highlight_transactions. Filter by month (YYYY-MM), category id/name (or "uncategorized"), and a case-insensitive query on merchant+rawDescription. Returns cleaned merchant names only (no rawDescription). Default limit 50, max 100. Amounts are dollars (negative = expense).

month.description: Optional calendar month filter as YYYY-MM (e.g. 2026-07).

category.description: Optional category id or name (case-insensitive), or "uncategorized".

query.description: Optional case-insensitive substring matched against merchant and rawDescription.

limit.description: Max rows to return. Default 50, maximum 100.

offset.description: Number of matching rows to skip. Default 0.

tools.name: get_spending_summary
tools.description: Summarize expenses (negative amounts only) grouped by category, merchant, or month. Use after categorizing to answer "where did the money go?" and "why was expensive?". Optional month (YYYY-MM) scopes the period; omit for all months. Returns groups sorted by spend desc plus grand expense total and income total. Amounts in dollars.

group_by.description: How to group expenses: category, merchant, or month.

month.description: Optional YYYY-MM period. Omit to include every month in the ledger.

tools.name: find_recurring
tools.description: Detect recurring expense charges (subscriptions, rent, retainers). Groups expenses by merchant: recurring means ≥3 occurrences, amount variance under 15%, and a weekly (6-8d) or monthly (25-35d) cadence. Call when hunting forgotten subscriptions or forecasting annual cost. No input. Amounts in dollars (negative = typical charge).

tools.name: get_budget_status
tools.description: Check each budgeted category for a month (default: the dashboard month, which is the latest month with data if the user has not picked one): limit, spent, remaining, percent used, and over. Also returns totals. Use after set_budget or to see if the user is over. Amounts in dollars. Spent counts only categorized expenses.

month.description: Optional YYYY-MM to evaluate. Defaults to the dashboard month.

tools.name: categorize_transactions
tools.description: Flagship write: assign categories in one batched call (one undo frame). First list_transactions to collect ids, then batch aggressively (up to ~100 ids per call) instead of one-by-one. Input is assignments: [{transaction_ids, category}] so one call can sort many categories. Category accepts id or name. Amounts elsewhere are dollars (negative = expense).

assignments.description: Groups of transaction ids to assign to a category. Each item: { transaction_ids: string[], category: string }.

category.description: Category id or name (case-insensitive), or "uncategorized" to clear.

tools.name: create_category
tools.description: Create a new spending or income category when none of the defaults fit. Rejects duplicate names (case-insensitive). Optional hex color; a default color/icon is chosen if omitted. Use before create_rule or categorize_transactions if you need a new bucket.

name.description: Display name for the new category.

tools.name: create_rule
tools.description: Add an auto-categorization rule when the user corrects a category or wants future imports auto-sorted. Matches a case-insensitive substring on merchant (default) or rawDescription. apply_now (default true) immediately categorizes existing uncategorized matches. Use after spotting a recurring merchant.

category.description: Category id or name to assign when the rule hits.

field.description: Which field to search. Default merchant.

apply_now.description: If true (default), apply all rules to current uncategorized transactions.

tools.name: apply_rules
tools.description: Run every saved rule over currently uncategorized transactions. Use after importing or when create_rule was called with apply_now false. Returns how many rows were categorized. No input.

tools.name: set_budget
tools.description: Set or remove a monthly budget for a category (id or name). monthly_limit is dollars; pass null or 0 to remove the budget. Use after get_spending_summary to lock in a limit. Undoable.

monthly_limit.description: Monthly limit in dollars, or null/0 to remove the budget.

tools.name: add_transaction
tools.description: Manually add one transaction sourced as agent. date is YYYY-MM-DD, amount is dollars (negative = expense, positive = income), optional category id/name and note. Use for missing cash or a correction, not for bulk imports.

merchant.description: Cleaned merchant name shown in the ledger.

amount.description: Amount in dollars. Negative = expense, positive = income.

note.description: Optional note stored on the transaction.

tools.name: delete_transactions
tools.description: Remove transactions by id. Undoable. Use for duplicates, junk, or a mistaken add_transaction. Prefer categorize when the charge is real.

transaction_ids.description: Ids to delete. Call list_transactions first.

tools.name: annotate_transaction
tools.description: Set or clear a note on a single transaction. Pass an empty string to clear. Use to remember context ("work lunch", "reimburse") without changing the category. Undoable.

transaction_id.description: Id of the transaction to annotate.

note.description: Note text. Empty string clears the note.

tools.name: highlight_transactions
tools.description: Visually point the user at specific transactions you are discussing. Switches to the transactions view, rings the rows, scrolls the first into view, and auto-clears after 10s. Pass an empty transaction_ids array to clear immediately. Not undoable.

transaction_ids.description: Ids to highlight. Empty array clears the current highlight.

note.description: Optional context remembered only in the activity log.

tools.name: set_view_filters
tools.description: Update the human's visible transaction filters so you and the user look at the same slice. Navigates to the transactions view. Pass null on a field to clear it. Not undoable.

month.description: YYYY-MM to filter, or null to show all months.

category.description: Category id/name, "uncategorized", or null to clear the category filter.

query.description: Search substring, or null to clear search.

uncategorized_only.description: If true, show only uncategorized rows.

kind.description: all, spend, or income. Filters the visible list by amount sign.

view.description: Optional. If "transactions", navigate there (always does).

tools.name: navigate_to_view
tools.description: Switch the visible Glassbook page so the user follows along. Views: dashboard, transactions, budgets, import, rules. Log-only; not undoable.

view.description: Which app view to show.

tools.name: pin_insight
tools.description: Pin a durable finding the user should remember (shows on the Dashboard). Keep body under ~200 characters. Optional emoji. Undoable write. Use for conclusions, not transient status.

body.description: Supporting detail, ideally under 200 characters.

emoji.description: Optional emoji prefix for the card.

tools.name: get_dashboard_state
tools.description: Call to see exactly what the user is currently looking at, so you can talk about what's on their screen. Returns current view, dashboard selected month, active transaction filters, highlighted transaction ids, and pinned insight titles. No input.

sites.name: greatwallflorence.com
sites.description: Great Wall Restaurant in Florence, MA — freshly prepared Chinese classics, sushi, and an extensive gluten-free menu. Dine in, take out, or order online.

tools.name: get_restaurant_info
tools.description: Get this restaurant's name, address, phone, whether it is open now, whether online ordering is available, which of pickup/delivery it offers with estimated wait times, and what the customer pays by. Call this first.

tools.name: list_menu_categories
tools.description: List the menu categories available right now, with how many dishes each has.

tools.name: search_menu
tools.description: Find dishes by name, description or category, optionally within one category. Returns item ids, prices (per size/variation) and whether the dish has options. Use get_item_details before adding a dish that has options. If the restaurant offers Express (see get_restaurant_info), pass expressOnly to list only Express-eligible dishes.

query.description: Words to match, e.g. 'general tso chicken' or 'spicy'. Omit to list a category.

expressOnly.description: Only Express-eligible dishes (shorter wait). Only for restaurants that offer Express.

tools.name: get_item_details
tools.description: Get one dish's sizes/variations and its option groups (which are required, how many choices are allowed, the default, and each option's extra price). Required groups without a default must be answered in add_to_cart.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a dish to the customer's cart. If the dish has more than one size, pass variationId. Pass selections for option groups ([{ groupId, optionIds }]); groups you don't mention keep their default. Required groups without a default must be answered. Prices are computed by the restaurant's server. Returns the updated cart.

variationId.description: Required when the dish has more than one size/variation.

note.description: Special request for the kitchen, e.g. 'no onions'.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current cart: each line (with its lineIndex), quantities, chosen options, notes, line totals and the subtotal.

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description: Change the quantity of a cart line (lineIndex from get_cart). Quantity 0 removes the line.

tools.name: remove_cart_item
tools.description: Remove a line from the cart (lineIndex from get_cart).

tools.name: set_fulfillment_method
tools.description: Choose pickup or delivery (only methods the restaurant offers; see get_restaurant_info). The delivery address is entered by the customer at checkout.

tools.name: start_checkout
tools.description: Open the checkout screen with the current cart. Then use the checkout tools (set_contact_details, set_delivery_address, send_verification_code / verify_phone_code, set_payment_method, place_order), or let the customer finish on screen. Card payment is always entered by the customer.

tools.name: get_checkout_status
tools.description: What the open checkout still needs before the order can be placed: contact fields, delivery address state, phone verification, payment method, total, and the blocking reason shown on the Place order button.

tools.name: set_contact_details
tools.description: Fill the customer's name, phone and email on the open checkout (only what you pass changes). Use the customer's real details, with their permission. The email gets the receipt.

tools.name: set_delivery_address
tools.description: For delivery orders: fill the address and run the same check the customer's Confirm button does (address lookup, delivery zone, distance). Returns status valid, outside (with distance and max), unavailable, or unverifiable (the address couldn't be verified; only call confirm_unverified_address if the customer says to deliver there anyway).

state.description: Two-letter state, e.g. MA.

notes.description: Instructions for the driver.

tools.name: confirm_unverified_address
tools.description: Only after set_delivery_address returned unverifiable AND the customer confirmed the address is right: accept it as typed (the same as the customer tapping 'Deliver here anyway').

tools.name: send_verification_code
tools.description: Pay-in-person pickup orders need the phone verified: this texts a code to the phone on the checkout. Ask the customer to read you the code, then call verify_phone_code. Returns not_required when no verification is needed.

tools.name: verify_phone_code
tools.description: Enter the code the customer received by text message.

tools.name: set_payment_method
tools.description: Choose pay in person (pay at pickup or to the driver). Agents can't choose or enter card payment; for card, the customer completes payment in the card form on screen.

tools.name: place_order
tools.description: Place the order (pay in person only). Before calling, confirm the cart, pickup/delivery and total with the customer. Fails with the same reason the Place order button shows if anything is still missing. Returns the order id on success.

sites.name: jjhub.erisera.com
sites.description: JJHub

tools.name: list_tool_groups
tools.description: JJHub registers its WebMCP tools progressively: a small core set is always available and the rest are grouped by workflow. Lists every group with its description, tool names and whether it is currently loaded, plus the page limits (how many tools may be registered at once) and how many slots remain. Call load_tool_group to make a group's tools callable.

tools.name: load_tool_group
tools.description: Registers one workflow group's tools on this page so they become callable. If that would exceed the page budget, the least recently used loaded group is evicted first (evict defaults to true) and the response names the evicted group and tools — their schemas leave your working set and must be re-loaded before use. With evict: false the load is refused instead, listing the groups you could unload. Loading an already-loaded group is a no-op. Group names come from list_tool_groups.

group.description: Group name from list_tool_groups.

evict.description: Evict the least recently used group if needed (default true); false refuses instead.

tools.name: search_tools
tools.description: Keyword search over every JJHub WebMCP tool's name and description (loaded or not). Returns matching tool names with their group and whether each is currently loaded, so you can discover a tool and then load_tool_group its group.

query.description: Words to look for, e.g. 'land stack' or 'conflict'.

limit.description: Max matches (default 15).

tools.name: list_repositories
tools.description: List every repository JJHub manages, with GitHub connection and daemon status.

tools.name: get_repository
tools.description: Get one repository's details (GitHub connection, App coverage, daemon heartbeat).

repositoryId.description: JJHub repository id — see list_repositories for available ids.

tools.name: list_changes
tools.description: List every jj-style change in a repository.

repositoryId.description: JJHub repository id — see list_repositories for available ids.

tools.name: get_change
tools.description: Get one change's full detail (status, commit history, restack flag, etc.).

repositoryId.description: JJHub repository id — see list_repositories for available ids.

changeId.description: jj change id, e.g. 'CHG-1' — see list_changes.

tools.name: get_change_diff
tools.description: Per-file unified diffs of a change's projected branch against its base; landed changes return the merged PR audit diff.

repositoryId.description: JJHub repository id — see list_repositories for available ids.

changeId.description: jj change id, e.g. 'CHG-1' — see list_changes.

tools.name: create_change
tools.description: Create a change (projects a branch + draft PR on GitHub when connected); parentChangeId stacks it on an existing change.

repositoryId.description: JJHub repository id — see list_repositories for available ids.

parentChangeId.description: Parent change id, if stacking on another change.

parentChangeIds.description: Ordered parent change ids for a multi-parent jj graph change.

base.description: Base ref, e.g. 'main', if not stacking on a change.

stackId.description: Stack to add this change to, if any.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional: retry this exact call safely — the same key + the same arguments replays the original result instead of re-executing.

tools.name: describe_change
tools.description: Edit a change's title and/or description (like 'jj describe').

repositoryId.description: JJHub repository id — see list_repositories for available ids.

changeId.description: jj change id, e.g. 'CHG-1' — see list_changes.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional: retry this exact call safely — the same key + the same arguments replays the original result instead of re-executing.

tools.name: amend_change
tools.description: Amend (rewrite) a change in place — descendants will need a restack.

repositoryId.description: JJHub repository id — see list_repositories for available ids.

changeId.description: jj change id, e.g. 'CHG-1' — see list_changes.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional: retry this exact call safely — the same key + the same arguments replays the original result instead of re-executing.

tools.name: split_change
tools.description: Split a change: a new change with the given title stacks on top of it.

repositoryId.description: JJHub repository id — see list_repositories for available ids.

changeId.description: jj change id, e.g. 'CHG-1' — see list_changes.

title.description: Title for the newly split-off change.

description.description: Description for the newly split-off change.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional: retry this exact call safely — the same key + the same arguments replays the original result instead of re-executing.

tools.name: squash_change
tools.description: Squash a change into its parent.

repositoryId.description: JJHub repository id — see list_repositories for available ids.

changeId.description: jj change id, e.g. 'CHG-1' — see list_changes.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional: retry this exact call safely — the same key + the same arguments replays the original result instead of re-executing.

tools.name: abandon_change
tools.description: Abandon a change outright (closes its projected PR on GitHub).

repositoryId.description: JJHub repository id — see list_repositories for available ids.

changeId.description: jj change id, e.g. 'CHG-1' — see list_changes.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional: retry this exact call safely — the same key + the same arguments replays the original result instead of re-executing.

tools.name: restore_change
tools.description: Re-materialize an abandoned OR squashed-away change as a live draft with its original changeId, from the op log's pre-deletion snapshot. Former children stay reparented where abandon/squash left them (returned as formerChildren, not automatically reclaimed); a former parent that has since landed or vanished re-roots the restored change onto its base instead (reported as rerootedOnBase).

repositoryId.description: JJHub repository id — see list_repositories for available ids.

changeId.description: jj change id, e.g. 'CHG-1' — see list_changes.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional: retry this exact call safely — the same key + the same arguments replays the original result instead of re-executing.

tools.name: duplicate_change
tools.description: Create an independent copy of a change with the same title/description/content (like 'jj duplicate'). The source is never touched — it can be duplicated even if landed, queued, or abandoned.

repositoryId.description: JJHub repository id — see list_repositories for available ids.

changeId.description: jj change id, e.g. 'CHG-1' — see list_changes.

destinationChangeId.description: New primary (first) parent for the duplicate — mirrors jj's 'duplicate -d/--onto'. Replaces ONLY the source's first parent; every other parent (a join's non-primary edges) carries over unchanged. Omit to keep every one of the source's parents exactly as-is.

tools.name: reparent_change
tools.description: Repoint a change's parent edges directly (graph-level reparent, not a content rebase). Reuses create_change's cycle detection. Marks the change and its descendants needsRestack rather than performing the rebase itself — call restack_change afterward to materialize it.

repositoryId.description: JJHub repository id — see list_repositories for available ids.

changeId.description: jj change id, e.g. 'CHG-1' — see list_changes.

parentChangeIds.description: New ordered parent edges, replacing the change's current ones outright. The first element becomes the new primary parent (PR base once restacked); any additional elements are a join's non-primary parents, recorded but never projected to GitHub (Change.unprojectedParentIds). An empty array re-roots the change with no parent.

tools.name: restack_change
tools.description: Rebase a needs-restack change onto its rewritten ancestor and clear its needsRestack flag.

repositoryId.description: JJHub repository id — see list_repositories for available ids.

changeId.description: jj change id, e.g. 'CHG-1' — see list_changes.

workspaceId.description: Issue #268: explicitly target this workspace for local-write routing. Never inferred — omitting it always yields localApply:'not_requested', even if the repository has a configured write route.

expectedWorkspaceWorkingCopyChangeId.description: Only meaningful with workspaceId: the working-copy change id this call expects the target workspace to currently be on. A mismatch yields localApply:'skipped_diverged' instead of proceeding against a workspace that has moved.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional: retry this exact call safely — the same key + the same arguments replays the original result instead of re-executing.

expressOnly.description: Only Express-eligible dishes (shorter wait). Only for restaurants that offer Express.

tools.name: get_item_details
tools.description: Get one dish's sizes/variations and its option groups (which are required, how many choices are allowed, the default, and each option's extra price). Required groups without a default must be answered in add_to_cart.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a dish to the customer's cart. If the dish has more than one size, pass variationId. Pass selections for option groups ([{ groupId, optionIds }]); groups you don't mention keep their default. Required groups without a default must be answered. Prices are computed by the restaurant's server. Returns the updated cart.

variationId.description: Required when the dish has more than one size/variation.

note.description: Special request for the kitchen, e.g. 'no onions'.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current cart: each line (with its lineIndex), quantities, chosen options, notes, line totals and the subtotal.

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description: Change the quantity of a cart line (lineIndex from get_cart). Quantity 0 removes the line.

tools.name: remove_cart_item
tools.description: Remove a line from the cart (lineIndex from get_cart).

tools.name: set_fulfillment_method
tools.description: Choose pickup or delivery (only methods the restaurant offers; see get_restaurant_info). The delivery address is entered by the customer at checkout.

tools.name: start_checkout
tools.description: Open the checkout screen with the current cart. Then use the checkout tools (set_contact_details, set_delivery_address, send_verification_code / verify_phone_code, set_payment_method, place_order), or let the customer finish on screen. Card payment is always entered by the customer.

tools.name: get_checkout_status
tools.description: What the open checkout still needs before the order can be placed: contact fields, delivery address state, phone verification, payment method, total, and the blocking reason shown on the Place order button.

tools.name: set_contact_details
tools.description: Fill the customer's name, phone and email on the open checkout (only what you pass changes). Use the customer's real details, with their permission. The email gets the receipt.

tools.name: set_delivery_address
tools.description: For delivery orders: fill the address and run the same check the customer's Confirm button does (address lookup, delivery zone, distance). Returns status valid, outside (with distance and max), unavailable, or unverifiable (the address couldn't be verified; only call confirm_unverified_address if the customer says to deliver there anyway).

state.description: Two-letter state, e.g. MA.

notes.description: Instructions for the driver.

tools.name: confirm_unverified_address
tools.description: Only after set_delivery_address returned unverifiable AND the customer confirmed the address is right: accept it as typed (the same as the customer tapping 'Deliver here anyway').

tools.name: send_verification_code
tools.description: Pay-in-person pickup orders need the phone verified: this texts a code to the phone on the checkout. Ask the customer to read you the code, then call verify_phone_code. Returns not_required when no verification is needed.

tools.name: verify_phone_code
tools.description: Enter the code the customer received by text message.

tools.name: set_payment_method
tools.description: Choose pay in person (pay at pickup or to the driver). Agents can't choose or enter card payment; for card, the customer completes payment in the card form on screen.

tools.name: place_order
tools.description: Place the order (pay in person only). Before calling, confirm the cart, pickup/delivery and total with the customer. Fails with the same reason the Place order button shows if anything is still missing. Returns the order id on success.

sites.name: life-shift.veltrax.chatgpt.site
sites.description: Play your decisions before you live them in an adaptive life simulation powered by bounded WebMCP capabilities.

tools.name: get_life_state
tools.description: Read age, turn, life metrics, context, and run status.

tools.name: get_life_history
tools.description: Read immutable life history.

tools.name: get_decision_profile
tools.description: Read derived decision-profile metrics. Not a diagnosis. Not editable.

tools.name: get_open_threads
tools.description: Read unresolved life threads.

tools.name: get_financial_state
tools.description: Read cash, income, debt, net worth, and living cost.

tools.name: get_career_state
tools.description: Read career track, skills, network, and job context.

tools.name: get_world_state
tools.description: Read coarse world conditions. Values are bounded categories, not a full economy.

tools.name: get_available_opportunities
tools.description: Read which player actions the engine currently allows, plus locked paths and their requirements.

tools.name: get_director_budget
tools.description: Read remaining Director Budget and cycle state.

tools.name: get_pending_director_cycle
tools.description: Returns the Director evaluation that became pending after the participant lived a chapter. Inspect life state, history, decision profile, threads, finances, career, world, and Director Budget. Make at most one justified world intervention bound to this cycleId. Never make the participant's life decisions. If no intervention is warranted, call complete_director_cycle with outcome observe_only.

tools.name: complete_director_cycle
tools.description: Close the current Director Cycle without changing the world. Use only when a pending crisis already exists or repeating the last event would feel fake.

cycleId.description: ID of the current pending Director Cycle opened after Advance 1 Year.

outcome.description: Use only when no world intervention is warranted this cycle.

summary.description: Why the Director chose not to intervene.

tools.name: create_job_opportunity
tools.description: Introduce a bounded job opportunity. The engine calculates compensation from life state and quality.

cycleId.description: ID of the current pending Director Cycle opened after Advance 1 Year.

opportunityType.description: Bounded job circumstance type. The engine sets compensation.

quality.description: Relative quality. The engine maps this to income using life state.

rationale.description: Why this opportunity follows current history and state.

tools.name: create_career_setback
tools.description: Create a bounded career setback. The engine calculates income and wellbeing effects.

cycleId.description: ID of the current pending Director Cycle opened after Advance 1 Year.

tools.name: create_business_opportunity
tools.description: Introduce a bounded business or side-project development. The engine calculates numeric effects.

cycleId.description: ID of the current pending Director Cycle opened after Advance 1 Year.

tools.name: create_financial_event
tools.description: Create a bounded financial circumstance. The engine sets the dollar amount from life state and severity.

cycleId.description: ID of the current pending Director Cycle opened after Advance 1 Year.

tools.name: create_network_opportunity
tools.description: Introduce a bounded network opening. The engine updates network and career if accepted.

cycleId.description: ID of the current pending Director Cycle opened after Advance 1 Year.

tools.name: create_housing_event
tools.description: Create a bounded housing circumstance. The engine calculates cash, equity, or mobility effects.

cycleId.description: ID of the current pending Director Cycle opened after Advance 1 Year.

tools.name: create_world_event
tools.description: Expensive. Move exactly one world dimension one notch. Cannot rewrite life metrics.

cycleId.description: ID of the current pending Director Cycle opened after Advance 1 Year.

dimension.description: Exactly one world dimension may move one notch.

sites.name: loopsmith.lemon.earth
sites.description: A browser DAW that exposes WebMCP tools so an agent can compose, arrange and actually measure the mix.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Read the full state of the session: tempo, swing, loop length, every track with its mixer settings, synth settings and note pattern. Call this first to learn track ids.

tools.name: describe_arrangement
tools.description: Musical summary of the loop: detected key and confidence, note density per bar, which bars each track is active in, pitch ranges, and notes about empty or muted tracks. Use this to reason about structure without reading every note.

tools.name: analyze_mix
tools.description: LISTEN to the current mix. Renders the loop offline and measures it: per-track loudness (LUFS), true peak, crest factor, spectral centroid, energy per frequency band, plus frequency-masking conflicts between tracks and mix-bus headroom. Use this whenever the user asks how something sounds ('is it muddy?', 'is the bass too loud?') or before changing EQ or levels. This information is not available from the page's HTML.

trackIds.description: Optional subset of track ids. Omit to analyze everything.

tools.name: set_tempo
tools.description: Set the tempo in BPM and/or the swing amount applied to off-beat 16th notes.

tools.name: add_track
tools.description: Add an instrument track. Kinds: kick, snare, hat (drum synths, pitch ignored), bass, keys, lead (subtractive synths). Returns the new track id.

kind.description: Instrument type.

name.description: Display name, defaults to the kind.

notes.description: Optional starting pattern.

midi.description: MIDI note number, e.g. 60 for C4.

note.description: Alternative to midi, e.g. "C3" or "F#4".

tools.name: remove_track
tools.description: Delete a track and its pattern.

tools.name: write_pattern
tools.description: Write notes onto a track. mode 'replace' clears the track first; mode 'merge' adds to what is already there. Changes are applied immediately and are audible on the next loop.

notes.description: Notes to place. `step` is a 16th-note index from 0; there are 16 steps per bar. Drum tracks ignore pitch.

midi.description: MIDI note number, e.g. 60 for C4.

note.description: Alternative to midi, e.g. "C3" or "F#4".

mode.description: Default 'replace'.

tools.name: clear_pattern
tools.description: Remove every note from a track, keeping its sound and mixer settings.

tools.name: set_mix
tools.description: Set a track's level in dB, stereo pan, mute or solo.

tools.name: set_eq
tools.description: Set a track's EQ: high-pass corner, low-pass corner, and one peaking band. Use analyze_mix first to find out which band actually needs work.

peakFreq.description: Centre frequency of the peaking band in Hz.

peakGainDb.description: Boost or cut at that frequency, -24 to +24 dB.

peakQ.description: Bandwidth of the peaking band, 0.3 to 12.

tools.name: transport
tools.description: Start or stop playback. The loop plays continuously and edits are heard immediately.

fromStep.description: Step to start from when playing. Default 0.

tools.name: select_track
tools.description: Focus a track in the UI. Selecting a track also registers extra tools for editing that specific instrument's sound, so call this before trying to change synth parameters.

tools.name: propose_pattern
tools.description: Suggest a pattern WITHOUT applying it. It appears in the UI as ghost notes with Accept / Reject / Preview buttons so the user stays in control. Use this for creative variations, alternative arrangements, or anything the user should audition before committing. Use write_pattern instead when the user asked for the change directly.

label.description: Short description shown to the user.

ops.description: One entry per track this proposal would change.

notes.description: Notes to place. `step` is a 16th-note index from 0; there are 16 steps per bar. Drum tracks ignore pitch.

midi.description: MIDI note number, e.g. 60 for C4.

note.description: Alternative to midi, e.g. "C3" or "F#4".

tools.name: list_proposals
tools.description: List proposals and whether the user has accepted, rejected, or not yet answered them.

tools.name: resolve_proposal
tools.description: Accept or reject a proposal on the user's behalf. Only do this when the user has said clearly which one they want; otherwise leave it for them to click.

tools.name: diff_since
tools.description: What changed in the session since a moment in time, and who changed it (user or agent). Call this after the user has been editing to catch up before making further changes — the user can turn knobs and draw notes while you are thinking.

sinceMs.description: Unix milliseconds. Use the `now` value from a previous call to chain.

tools.name: set_synth_param
tools.description: Change the sound of the selected track "kick" (kick). Parameters: wave (sawtooth/square/triangle/sine), detune (cents), attack/decay/release (seconds), sustain (0..1), cutoff (Hz), resonance (Q), envAmount (Hz of filter sweep). This tool only exists while a track is selected.

value.description: Numeric value, or the waveform name for `wave`.

tools.name: audition_selected
tools.description: Play the selected track "kick" once on its own, without starting the transport. Useful for letting the user hear a sound change in isolation.

sites.name: mandate-webmcp.vercel.app
sites.description: Scoped, supervised, revocable authority for AI agents acting on a bank payment operations desk. Built on WebMCP.

tools.name: get_desk_status
tools.description: Orientation for the whole desk: who is on it, what authority you currently hold as an agent, how the payment queue breaks down, which payments are blocked and why, account balances, and how long until each payment rail closes for the day. Call this first.

tools.name: explain_my_limits
tools.description: Read-only report of the limits you are already operating under on this desk, and why they apply. Use it to understand a refusal you have received. It reports only and changes nothing.

tools.name: search_payments
tools.description: Search the payment queue. Filter by status, rail, beneficiary name, reference, minimum or maximum amount, or restrict to only those payments that currently cannot move. Returns a summary of each match.

status.description: Payment status to filter on. Use "any" for no status filter.

beneficiary.description: Case-insensitive substring of the beneficiary name.

reference.description: Case-insensitive substring of the payment reference.

minAmount.description: Minimum amount as written, for example "1000.00". Do not convert to cents.

maxAmount.description: Maximum amount as written, for example "5000.00". Do not convert to cents.

onlyBlocked.description: If true, return only payments that cannot move as they stand.

tools.name: get_payment
tools.description: Full detail on one payment, including every control the desk evaluates against it and the plain-English result of each. Use this before asking anyone to approve anything.

id.description: Payment id, for example "PMT-2041".

tools.name: explain_hold
tools.description: Explain in plain language why a specific payment cannot move, and list the concrete routes forward. Use this to give a person a straight answer instead of a status code.

id.description: Payment id, for example "PMT-2048".

tools.name: search_beneficiaries
tools.description: Search the beneficiary register by name or country, with verification status, screening status and payment history for each.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring of the beneficiary name or two-letter country code.

status.description: Verification status filter.

tools.name: get_exposure
tools.description: Cash position per account: what is available, what the queue has already pledged against it, and what is genuinely free to spend. Use this before promising anyone that a payment can be funded.

tools.name: recheck_screening_with_bureau
tools.description: Re-check a beneficiary against the Sentinel screening bureau, a separate organisation on its own origin that holds the sanctions watchlist. Use this when a payment is stopped on a screening match and someone needs to know whether the match still stands today. The bureau answers with a decision and a reason; it never releases the underlying list, and this desk cannot overrule it.

beneficiaryId.description: Beneficiary id from search_beneficiaries, for example "BEN-06".

tools.name: get_audit_trail
tools.description: The desk audit trail in plain English: every action taken by a person or an agent, in order, with who did it and when. Nothing an agent does on this desk is unlogged.

limit.description: How many of the most recent entries to return. Defaults to 20.

tools.name: draft_payment
tools.description: Prepare a new payment as a draft. This moves no money: it creates something a person or a mandate can later release. The draft appears on the desk screen immediately.

accountId.description: Account to debit, for example "ACC-EUR-01". Use get_exposure to list them.

beneficiaryId.description: Beneficiary id from search_beneficiaries, for example "BEN-01".

amount.description: Amount as written, for example "4820.00". Do not convert to cents.

currency.description: Currency of the payment.

rail.description: Payment rail to send it on.

reference.description: Payment reference, usually an invoice number.

tools.name: amend_payment
tools.description: Change a draft payment: its amount, rail, reference or beneficiary. Only drafts can be amended; anything already approved or released cannot be edited.

id.description: Payment id to amend.

amount.description: New amount as written, for example "4820.00".

reference.description: New payment reference.

tools.name: attach_evidence
tools.description: Attach supporting evidence to a payment - an invoice, contract clause or written instruction that explains why the money is owed. Audit expects every payment to carry this.

id.description: Payment id.

label.description: What the evidence is, for example "Invoice INV-CS-20551" or "Supply agreement SA-2024-11 clause 7".

kind.description: Type of evidence.

tools.name: request_authorization
tools.description: Route one specific payment, identified by its id, to a person at the desk for approval. Covers that single payment and nothing else. This does not return until they decide, so you get their actual answer rather than an acknowledgement.

id.description: Payment id to route for authorisation.

note.description: What you want them to know: why this is owed, what you checked, and anything that needs their judgement. Write it for a person, not a log.

tools.name: release_payment
tools.description: Release a payment so it actually goes out. You can only do this on your own if a person has granted you a mandate that covers it; otherwise this refuses and tells you the route that would work.

id.description: Payment id to release.

tools.name: propose_mandate
tools.description: Request permission from a person. Use this whenever you need authority you do not have: after being refused for lack of authority, or when someone tells you to ask them for permission to act on your own. You propose the limits - the most per payment, a total budget, how long it lasts, which rails - and they can tighten any part before agreeing, or refuse outright. This does not return until a person decides. If they agree, new tools become available to you immediately.

perPayment.description: The most you are asking to be able to release in a single payment, as written, for example "5000.00".

total.description: The total you are asking to be able to release across all payments under this mandate, for example "50000.00".

currency.description: Currency the limits are expressed in.

minutes.description: How long you are asking the authority to last, in minutes. Keep it short; ask again if you need longer.

rails.description: The rails you are asking to cover.

knownBeneficiariesOnly.description: Whether to limit the mandate to beneficiaries already verified on file. Asking for true makes a person far more likely to agree.

reason.description: Why you are asking, in plain language: what you intend to do with it and what it saves the person. They read this before deciding.

tools.name: get_mandate
tools.description: The standing mandate in force right now, if any: its limits, how much of its budget is left, and when it expires.

tools.name: undo_last_agent_action
tools.description: Ask a person to reverse the last thing you did. Use this the moment you realise you have made a mistake, rather than trying to correct it with another payment.

reason.description: Why it should be reversed, in plain language.

tools.name: ask_the_desk
tools.description: Put a question or a recommendation in front of whoever is at the desk right now and wait for their written answer. Use this when you need a human judgement that is not itself a payment approval, for example whether a supplier relationship is genuine or which of two invoices is the correct one.

sites.description: MapsMCP

tools.name: get_map_state
tools.description: Read the current MapsMCP viewport, selected place, route, and staged ride.

tools.name: search_places
tools.description: Search MapsMCP's structured London place catalog. Returns stable place IDs for later tools.

tools.name: get_place_details
tools.description: Read a structured place and nearby places without relying on a marker tooltip.

tools.name: find_nearby_places
tools.description: Find structured places near a place ID within a real-world radius, optionally filtered by category.

tools.name: measure_distance
tools.description: Measure straight-line geographic distance between two place IDs.

tools.name: get_map_viewport
tools.description: Read exact map camera center, zoom, geographic bounds, and structured places visible right now.

tools.name: get_places_in_view
tools.description: List structured places inside the current map viewport.

tools.name: pan_map
tools.description: Move the visible map camera in a compass direction by real-world metres. Use instead of pixel dragging.

tools.name: set_map_viewport
tools.description: Set the map camera to exact latitude, longitude, and optional zoom. Use instead of simulating pan or wheel gestures.

tools.name: zoom_map
tools.description: Zoom the visible map by a signed number of levels. Use instead of wheel events.

tools.name: fit_places
tools.description: Fit the visible map camera to one or more structured place IDs.

tools.name: focus_place
tools.description: Fly the map camera to a structured place ID and select it in the human UI.

tools.name: plan_route
tools.description: Preview a route between two MapsMCP place IDs in car, cycle, or walk mode. Does not create a booking.

tools.name: clear_route

tools.name: drop_pin
tools.description: Drop a named visible pin at an exact latitude and longitude.

tools.name: list_pins
tools.description: List pins that have been dropped onto the shared human map.

tools.name: remove_pin
tools.description: Remove a pin from the shared human map by its stable pin ID.

tools.name: prepare_ride
tools.description: Stage a simulated ride quote between place IDs. The human must confirm in the UI.

tools.name: search_posts
tools.description: Search posts, pages or custom post types on the site.

query.description: Search keywords.

post_type.description: Post type slug (default: any).

tools.name: get_post
tools.description: Retrieve a single post or page by ID or slug.

id.description: Post ID.

tools.name: get_menu
tools.description: Return the items of a navigation menu.

menu.description: Menu name, slug, or ID (default: primary).

tools.name: submit_contact_form
tools.description: Submit a Contact Form 7 form programmatically.

fields.description: Key-value pairs matching the form field names.

tools.name: get_site_info
tools.description: Return basic site metadata (name, description, URL, language).

tools.name: get_categories
tools.description: List all post categories with their slugs and counts.

tools.name: woo_search_products
tools.description: Search WooCommerce products by keyword, category or price range.

query.description: Search keywords.

tools.name: woo_get_product
tools.description: Get full details for a single WooCommerce product.

id.description: Product ID.

tools.name: woo_add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a product to the WooCommerce cart.

product_id.description: Product ID.

quantity.description: Quantity (default: 1).

tools.name: woo_get_cart
tools.description: Return the current cart contents and totals.

tools.name: woo_remove_from_cart
tools.description: Remove an item from the cart by cart item key.

tools.name: woo_apply_coupon
tools.description: Apply a coupon code to the cart.

tools.name: woo_get_checkout_fields
tools.description: Return the checkout form fields so an agent can fill them.

tools.name: woo_get_product_categories
tools.description: List all WooCommerce product categories.

tools.name: woo_get_payment_methods
tools.description: List the payment gateways currently available for checkout.

tools.name: woo_get_shipping_methods
tools.description: List available shipping rates for the cart, based on the address set via woo_set_checkout_details.

tools.name: woo_set_checkout_details
tools.description: Fill in billing/shipping details and order notes ahead of placing an order. Field keys match woo_get_checkout_fields.

fields.description: Key-value pairs, e.g. billing_first_name, billing_email, shipping_address_1, order_comments.

tools.name: woo_place_order
tools.description: Place a real WooCommerce order from the current cart and saved checkout details. Requires confirm:true.

confirm.description: Must be true to actually place the order.

fields.description: Optional checkout fields to set/override before placing the order.

payment_method.description: Payment gateway id from woo_get_payment_methods. Auto-selected if only one is available.

shipping_method.description: Shipping rate id from woo_get_shipping_methods. Auto-selected if only one is available.

sites.name: northgardenws.com
sites.description: North Garden is a Chinese restaurant in West Springfield, MA. See the full menu, hours and directions — and order online for pickup.

tools.name: get_restaurant_info
tools.description: Get this restaurant's name, address, phone, whether it is open now, whether online ordering is available, which of pickup/delivery it offers with estimated wait times, and what the customer pays by. Call this first.

tools.name: list_menu_categories
tools.description: List the menu categories available right now, with how many dishes each has.

tools.name: search_menu
tools.description: Find dishes by name, description or category, optionally within one category. Returns item ids, prices (per size/variation) and whether the dish has options. Use get_item_details before adding a dish that has options. If the restaurant offers Express (see get_restaurant_info), pass expressOnly to list only Express-eligible dishes.

query.description: Words to match, e.g. 'general tso chicken' or 'spicy'. Omit to list a category.

expressOnly.description: Only Express-eligible dishes (shorter wait). Only for restaurants that offer Express.

tools.name: get_item_details
tools.description: Get one dish's sizes/variations and its option groups (which are required, how many choices are allowed, the default, and each option's extra price). Required groups without a default must be answered in add_to_cart.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a dish to the customer's cart. If the dish has more than one size, pass variationId. Pass selections for option groups ([{ groupId, optionIds }]); groups you don't mention keep their default. Required groups without a default must be answered. Prices are computed by the restaurant's server. Returns the updated cart.

variationId.description: Required when the dish has more than one size/variation.

note.description: Special request for the kitchen, e.g. 'no onions'.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current cart: each line (with its lineIndex), quantities, chosen options, notes, line totals and the subtotal.

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description: Change the quantity of a cart line (lineIndex from get_cart). Quantity 0 removes the line.

tools.name: remove_cart_item
tools.description: Remove a line from the cart (lineIndex from get_cart).

tools.name: set_fulfillment_method
tools.description: Choose pickup or delivery (only methods the restaurant offers; see get_restaurant_info). The delivery address is entered by the customer at checkout.

tools.name: start_checkout
tools.description: Open the checkout screen with the current cart. Then use the checkout tools (set_contact_details, set_delivery_address, send_verification_code / verify_phone_code, set_payment_method, place_order), or let the customer finish on screen. Card payment is always entered by the customer.

tools.name: get_checkout_status
tools.description: What the open checkout still needs before the order can be placed: contact fields, delivery address state, phone verification, payment method, total, and the blocking reason shown on the Place order button.

tools.name: set_contact_details
tools.description: Fill the customer's name, phone and email on the open checkout (only what you pass changes). Use the customer's real details, with their permission. The email gets the receipt.

tools.name: set_delivery_address
tools.description: For delivery orders: fill the address and run the same check the customer's Confirm button does (address lookup, delivery zone, distance). Returns status valid, outside (with distance and max), unavailable, or unverifiable (the address couldn't be verified; only call confirm_unverified_address if the customer says to deliver there anyway).

state.description: Two-letter state, e.g. MA.

notes.description: Instructions for the driver.

tools.name: confirm_unverified_address
tools.description: Only after set_delivery_address returned unverifiable AND the customer confirmed the address is right: accept it as typed (the same as the customer tapping 'Deliver here anyway').

tools.name: send_verification_code
tools.description: Pay-in-person pickup orders need the phone verified: this texts a code to the phone on the checkout. Ask the customer to read you the code, then call verify_phone_code. Returns not_required when no verification is needed.

tools.name: verify_phone_code
tools.description: Enter the code the customer received by text message.

tools.name: set_payment_method
tools.description: Choose pay in person (pay at pickup or to the driver). Agents can't choose or enter card payment; for card, the customer completes payment in the card form on screen.

tools.name: place_order
tools.description: Place the order (pay in person only). Before calling, confirm the cart, pickup/delivery and total with the customer. Fails with the same reason the Place order button shows if anything is still missing. Returns the order id on success.

sites.name: northline-business-supply.zihao-y.chatgpt.site
sites.description: B2B supplier of sit-stand desks, ergonomic seating, monitors, docking stations, business laptops and office IT equipment. Net 30 invoicing, next-day delivery and assembly service.

tools.name: list_categories
tools.description: List the product categories of the Northline Business Supply catalogue with their ids, names and product counts. All prices on this site are in EUR excluding 21% VAT.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Search the catalogue for office furniture and IT equipment (desks, chairs, monitors, laptops, docks, keyboards, headsets, monitor arms, storage, power, networking, printing). Returns matching products with SKU, price, volume pricing, stock and options. Use the SKU with get_product or add_to_cart.

query.description: Free-text keywords or a SKU, e.g. "sit-stand desk", "27 inch usb-c monitor", "thunderbolt dock". Leave empty to list everything in a category.

category.description: Restrict to a category id (see list_categories), e.g. "desks", "monitors", "docking".

brand.description: Restrict to a brand name.

maxPrice.description: Maximum unit price in EUR excluding VAT.

inStockOnly.description: Only return items that are in stock.

sort.description: Sort order.

limit.description: Maximum number of results (default 20).

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get full details for one product by SKU: description, specifications, options (finishes, colours, layouts), volume price breaks, stock and lead time, and related SKUs.

tools.name: list_workstation_setups
tools.description: List the recommended per-seat workstation configurations (bundles of desk, chair, monitor, arm, dock, cable management etc.) with their component SKUs and per-seat price. Add one with add_setup_to_cart.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a product to the shopping cart by SKU and quantity, optionally choosing product options such as finish, colour or keyboard layout. Volume pricing is applied automatically. Returns the updated cart.

quantity.description: Quantity to add (default 1).

options.description: Product option selections as key/value pairs, e.g. {"Top finish":"White","Frame colour":"Black"}. Omit to use the default (first) value of each option. Use get_product to see available options.

tools.name: add_setup_to_cart
tools.description: Add a complete recommended workstation configuration to the cart, multiplied by the number of seats. Component quantities and default options can be adjusted afterwards with update_cart_item / add_to_cart.

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description: Change the quantity of a cart line. Set quantity to 0 to remove it. If the same SKU is in the cart with several option combinations, pass options to target one line.

sku.description: Product SKU already in the cart.

quantity.description: New quantity (0 removes the line).

options.description: Product option selections as key/value pairs, e.g. {"Top finish":"White","Frame colour":"Black"}. Omit to use the default (first) value of each option. Use get_product to see available options.

tools.name: remove_from_cart
tools.description: Remove a product line from the cart.

options.description: Product option selections as key/value pairs, e.g. {"Top finish":"White","Frame colour":"Black"}. Omit to use the default (first) value of each option. Use get_product to see available options.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current cart: lines with quantities, options and prices, the selected delivery method, totals (subtotal, discount, delivery, VAT, total) and the estimated delivery date.

tools.name: clear_cart
tools.description: Remove every item from the cart.

tools.name: set_delivery_method
tools.description: Choose the delivery method for the cart: "standard" (1–3 working days, free over €500), "express" (next working day, €79) or "assembly" (delivery to the room, assembly and packaging removal, from €149).

method.description: Delivery method id.

tools.name: get_checkout_info
tools.description: Get everything needed to place an order: the signed-in business account (company, credit terms, credit limit, primary contact), saved delivery address ids, available delivery and payment methods, and the current cart totals.

tools.name: place_order
tools.description: Record a simulated order for the current cart contents on the Meridian Labs demo account. This represents a binding action in the demo flow. Show the user the final contents, total and delivery estimate, then call this tool only after the user explicitly approves them and accepts the terms. Returns the locally stored order confirmation.

purchaseOrderNumber.description: The buyer's internal PO reference; printed on the invoice.

contactName.description: Name of the person placing the order.

contactEmail.description: Email address for the order confirmation.

contactPhone.description: Phone number for the delivery driver (optional).

addressId.description: Saved address id: "hq" (Amsterdam head office) or "utrecht" (Utrecht office). Omit when supplying a new address.

newAddress.description: New delivery address, used when addressId is omitted.

postcode.description: Postcode

country.description: Country (default Netherlands)

deliveryMethod.description: Delivery method id; defaults to the one selected on the cart.

requestedDeliveryDate.description: Preferred delivery date, YYYY-MM-DD (optional; earliest next working day).

notes.description: Notes for the warehouse or delivery team, e.g. floor and room (optional).

acceptTerms.description: Must be true after the user accepts the terms of sale.

confirmedByUser.description: Must be true only after the user explicitly approves the final cart contents, total and delivery estimate.

tools.name: get_order
tools.description: Get an existing order by its order id (e.g. "NBS-104211"), including status, lines, totals and delivery details.

tools.name: list_orders
tools.description: List the orders on this business account, newest first.

tools.name: request_quote
tools.description: Record a simulated project quote request for the products currently in the cart (recommended for 10+ workstations or when assembly, staged delivery or old-furniture removal is needed). Returns a locally stored quote reference; no external request or email is sent.

contactName.description: Requester name (defaults to the account contact).

contactEmail.description: Email that would receive the quote (defaults to the account contact).

notes.description: Project details: number of seats, timing, assembly needs.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the product catalogue by keyword or SKU and open the results page.

q.description: Search products, brands or SKUs — e.g. sit-stand desk, 27" monitor, Thunderbolt dock

tools.name: filter_catalog
tools.description: Filter the product catalogue by keyword, category, brand, maximum price and stock status. Submitting navigates to the filtered catalogue page.

sites.name: open-mercy.com
sites.description: Play Open Mercy free in your browser - the ruthless stacking card game. Real-time multiplayer with friends (2-20 players), vs AI mode, Draw 6, Draw 10, Skip Everyone, Color Roulette, hand swaps,…

tools.name: scan_images_c2pa
tools.description: Scan every on the current page for C2PA Content Credentials (content provenance metadata) and return a per-image summary: whether a manifest is present, the claim generator (the tool that produced or edited the image), the title, and the signer name. Use this to find which images on a page carry provenance data. Note: provenance is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

limit.description: Maximum number of images to fetch and scan (default 25, max 100).

tools.name: inspect_image_c2pa
tools.description: Fetch a single image (by CSS selector or URL) and return its fully decoded C2PA manifest store: every manifest's claim, assertions (e.g. c2pa.actions edit history, schema.org authorship), and the COSE signature details (algorithm and signing-certificate identity). Provide exactly one of `selector` or `url`. Note: the signature is decoded but NOT cryptographically verified.

selector.description: CSS selector for an element on the page.

url.description: Same-origin image URL (absolute same-origin, or relative to the current page) to fetch and inspect. Cross-origin URLs are rejected.

tools.name: how_to_play
tools.description: Return a primer on Open Mercy rules, card types, and basic tactics.

tools.name: get_state
tools.description: Snapshot of the current game from your seat: your hand, the public table state, whose turn it is, what action is required of you now, and the exact legal moves. Opponent hands are never revealed. Read this before every move.

tools.name: wait_for_turn
tools.description: Block until it is your turn or an action is required of you, then return the fresh state. Use this instead of polling. Resolves immediately if you can already act.

tools.name: start_single_player
tools.description: Start an offline game against the bot, exactly like the in-app vs-bot game: you versus one bot ("Terminator"). Deals hands and begins play.

tools.name: create_multiplayer_game
tools.description: Create an online room and become the host. Returns the room code to share.

tools.name: join_multiplayer_game
tools.description: Join an online room by its 6-character room code.

tools.name: start_multiplayer_game
tools.description: Start the multiplayer game you host. Requires at least 2 players.

tools.name: play_card
tools.description: Play a card from your hand by id. For wild cards you must also pass a color. The move is rejected if it is not in your current legal moves.

tools.name: draw_card
tools.description: Draw from the deck. If a draw stack is active you take the penalty; otherwise you draw until you find a playable card.

tools.name: pick_wild_color
tools.description: Choose the color for a wild card you just drew and are about to play.

tools.name: call_uno
tools.description: Call MERCY (the last-card call). Do this when you are about to be left with one card to avoid a penalty.

tools.name: swap_hands
tools.description: After playing a number 7, swap your entire hand with the chosen opponent.

tools.name: skip_swap
tools.description: Decline the number 7 swap and pass your turn.

tools.name: set_roulette_color
tools.description: Choose the target color when you are the victim of a wild color roulette.

tools.name: select_discard_all_top
tools.description: After a discard-all, choose which of the discarded cards lands on top of the pile.

tools.name: leave_game
tools.description: Leave the current game and return to the lobby.

tools.name: jizura_get_state
tools.description: Read the editor, revision, one-based lines/cuts and source rows. Use detail=false for a small status response. Audio and font files must be supplied through the existing browser file inputs.

tools.name: jizura_list_options
tools.description: Search IDs and localized labels. category is style, font, settings, or a technique group. Pagination is one-based.

tools.name: jizura_set_lyrics
tools.description: Replace raw lyrics (LRC and JIZURA syntax supported), or clear lyrics and line settings. Undo uses the existing edit history.

tools.name: jizura_update_settings
tools.description: Update only supplied settings. Empty font IDs restore style defaults. exportRange uses one-based lines and requires revision. Discover values with list_options.

tools.name: jizura_set_timing
tools.description: Update timing, set/delete manual line times, or clear manual times. Times use seconds; line references require revision.

tools.name: jizura_edit_line
tools.description: Edit one parsed line. Text replaces its source row body, preserving LRC tags (shared timestamps on that source row also change). Send text separately from layout/cuts/lock. cuts=0 and layout="" restore automatic choices.

tools.name: jizura_edit_cut
tools.description: Set a technique on a one-based cut within its line. key="" restores automatic selection. quiet toggles extra-effect suppression for the group.

tools.name: jizura_set_techniques
tools.description: Enable/disable techniques in one group. Omit keys to affect the entire group, keeping the same safe defaults as the UI bulk buttons.

tools.name: jizura_set_locks
tools.description: Set randomization locks for technique groups (tech) or effect parameters (params).

tools.name: jizura_randomize
tools.description: Randomize all, style, mood, palette, composition, line, or cut. Line/cut targets require revision and one-based references. Explicit line reroll unlocks that line, as in the UI.

tools.name: jizura_history
tools.description: Use edit undo/redo or look previous/next. These are separate existing histories.

tools.name: jizura_preview
tools.description: Play, pause, seek in seconds, set loop/preview volume/mute or display mode. Audio may require a real browser gesture.

tools.name: jizura_tap_sync
tools.description: Start tap synchronization at a line, record the current playhead, undo the last tap, or stop. Prefer set_timing for known timestamps.

tools.name: jizura_project
tools.description: Get/import/save the existing project JSON or get/save AE JSON. JSON does not include audio/font bytes. Import replaces the current project. File inputs are #fileProject, #audioFile, #fontFile.

tools.name: jizura_start_export
tools.description: Start MP4 or PNG ZIP export. Returns a job immediately; poll get_export_status. Direct-to-file MP4 requires the existing #btnMP4File browser button.

tools.name: jizura_get_export_status
tools.description: Read the latest export job. completed means encoding completed; download_started is not proof of a file saved on disk. Only the latest job is retained.

tools.name: jizura_cancel_export
tools.description: Cancel the current export. Poll status for cancellation completion.

tools.name: jizura_reset_project
tools.description: Open the existing irreversible reset confirmation. The user must confirm in the UI; this tool never bypasses confirmation.

tools.name: home_search
tools.description: Search parlhub's parliamentary data by section. Navigates to the chosen section's catalogue with the query applied (this is what the homepage search box does — there is no global search backend, so no rows are returned here). After the navigation the catalogue registers its own _filter and _query_state tools: re-read the tool list and use those to refine, sort, page or export the results. Scopes (each with what its query matches): people (People) — Searches name, place and postcode. votings (Votings) — Searches the voting title and the title of the affiliated affair. affairs (Affairs) — Searches the affair title and the affair number. speeches (Speeches) — Searches the wording of the speeches. bodies (Parliaments) — Searches the name of a country, canton, city or town. groups (Committees & groups) — Searches name, abbreviation and description of committees and parliamentary groups. meetings (Meetings) — Searches name, location and description. texts (Texts) — Searches the text type and the wording. documents (Documents) — Searches the document name and category. interests (Interests) — Searches organization name, function and parliamentary group. organizations (Organizations) — Searches the organization name.

q.description: Free-text query, e.g. a person or party name.

scope.description: Which section catalogue to search. Defaults to the scope the page shows.

sites.name: police-portal-mu.vercel.app
sites.description: police-portal

tools.name: fir.identify_required_fields
tools.description: FIR helper. You call me to know which FIR fields are required now and which become required once a given IPC section is set (e.g. theft switches "property" to required). Do NOT try to read the form on screen for this — I compute it authoritatively. Read me first, then populate via fir.fill_field.

sections.description: IPC / special-act section codes, e.g. ["379"] (must match formSchema option values).

recordId.description: Incident id to target; defaults to the selected/most recent record.

tools.name: fir.fill_field
tools.description: FIR action. I write one FIR field by dotted path and value into the record and the live form updates. This is how you file paperwork — do NOT click/type into the browser. Call me repeatedly (complainant.name, offense.sections, accused.*, narrative, and conditional property/witnesses) until fir.validate_form passes.

field.description: Dotted field path. Always-visible: complainant.name, complainant.fatherName, complainant.address, complainant.phone, complainant.email, offense.date, offense.time, offense.place, offense.beat, offense.sections, accused.name, accused.age, accused.sex, accused.description, narrative. Conditional (shown for some sections): property, witnesses.

value.description: Value to set. Use a string for text, array of strings for offense.sections/property.

recordId.description: Incident id to target; defaults to the selected/most recent record.

tools.name: fir.flag_missing
tools.description: FIR action. I mark FIR fields as needing an officer to review before submission (e.g. ambiguous identity). Call me instead of guessing a value you cannot confirm.

fields.description: Dotted field paths that are incomplete or ambiguous (e.g. ["complainant.address"]).

reason.description: Why these need human review.

recordId.description: Incident id to target; defaults to the selected/most recent record.

tools.name: fir.validate_form
tools.description: FIR action. I run the same validation the officer's form uses and return { valid, errors } with field->message. Call me before fir.submit to confirm the FIR is complete — this is the source of truth, not reading the page.

recordId.description: Incident id to target; defaults to the selected/most recent record.

tools.name: fir.submit
tools.description: FIR action. I submit the completed FIR after full-form validation passes and return the persisted id, firNumber and status. Call me to file the record — never press a button in the browser. I reject with errors if anything is missing; fix via fir.fill_field.

recordId.description: Incident id to target; defaults to the selected/most recent record.

tools.name: fir.find_similar_cases
tools.description: FIR research helper. I search the case archive for prior FIRs matching given IPC sections (optional location filter) and return precedents for repeat offenders. Read-only; call me for background, not to change records.

sections.description: IPC section codes to match, e.g. ["379"].

location.description: Optional place / area substring to constrain search.

tools.name: fir.create
tools.description: FIR action. I create a fresh blank FIR and select it so later calls act on it. Optionally pre-seed complainantName / sections / narrative. Call me to start a case instead of clicking the UI.

sections.description: Optional IPC section codes to pre-fill, e.g. ["279", "304A"] for a hit-and-run / rash driving.

tools.name: fir.link_erss
tools.description: FIR action. I link an FIR back to the ERSS-112 call that led to it, so the officer sees the source (an "Escalated from ERSS-112" marker appears). Pass the ERSS record id. Call me after you escalate a call — do not edit the UI.

erssId.description: The ERSS-112 record id to reference.

recordId.description: The FIR incident id to link (defaults to selected/most recent).

tools.name: challan.lookup_rc
tools.description: Challan helper. I look up a vehicle by its registration number in the transport database and return owner, address, vehicle class and fuel type. Call me to identify a vehicle — do not search the page.

tools.name: challan.auto_calculate_fine
tools.description: Challan helper. I compute the traffic fine for an MVA offence + vehicle class from the statutory matrix and return the amount in rupees. Call me to price a challan before challan.submit.

tools.name: challan.submit
tools.description: Challan action. I persist a traffic challan onto the active record and cross-link it to the FIR. Pass rcNumber, offenseCode and fineAmount (from challan.lookup_rc / challan.auto_calculate_fine). Call me to issue the challan — do not fill the form in the browser.

offenseCode.description: MVA section code used to compute the fine.

recordId.description: Incident id to attach the challan to (defaults to selected/most recent).

tools.name: dispatch.classify_nature
tools.description: ERSS helper. I map a natural-language emergency into an official ERSS-112 nature code ("heart attack" -> MED-001, "fire" -> FIR-003). Call me to classify a call.

tools.name: dispatch.get_available_units
tools.description: ERSS action. I return the units you can dispatch (ambulance, patrol, fire) with ETA. Call me before dispatch.assign_unit to pick a unit id.

type.description: Optional unit type filter (e.g. Ambulance).

tools.name: erss.create_call
tools.description: ERSS action. I create a standalone ERSS-112 emergency call from free text: classify the nature, set priority and select the record. Returns id, erssNumber and nature. Call me to log an incoming 112 call — do not open/locate the Emergency Call Log in the browser.

description.description: Free-text emergency description, e.g. "hit and run on MG Road".

channel.description: Reporting channel (default Voice).

tools.name: dispatch.assign_unit
tools.description: ERSS action. I assign a response unit to an incident and set its status to dispatched. Pass unitId from dispatch.get_available_units. Call me to dispatch — never manipulate the dispatch UI.

unitId.description: Unit id from dispatch.get_available_units, e.g. PCR-88.

recordId.description: Incident id; defaults to the selected/most recent incident.

tools.name: record.list
tools.description: Record helper — call me FIRST. I return the portal's records (FIR / e-Challan / ERSS-112) with optional module/status/text filters and each record's id. Always call me to discover a record id before acting, instead of reading the on-screen list.

module.description: Optional module filter: fir, challan, dispatch, or empty for all.

status.description: Optional status filter (draft, acknowledged, dispatched, closed).

text.description: Optional free-text search across firNumber / complainant / narrative / RC.

tools.name: record.select
tools.description: Record action. I set which record later calls (fir.*, challan.submit, dispatch.*) act on by default. Pass recordId from record.list. Call me to focus work on one record instead of interacting with the list UI.

sites.name: privta-webmcp-demo.mateolafalce.chatgpt.site
sites.description: Privta

tools.name: describe_data
tools.description: Confirms that Privta is ready to run private financial SQL summaries in the browser. It does not return account or transaction data.

tools.name: show_latest_expense
tools.description: Runs a local DuckDB SQL query for the latest expense, renders it in the Privta document, and returns the transaction summary.

tools.name: show_smallest_expense
tools.description: Runs fixed local SQL for the historical debit with the smallest absolute amount. Expenses are debits, including transfers; it renders and returns the result.

tools.name: show_largest_expense
tools.description: Runs fixed local SQL for the historical debit with the largest absolute amount. Expenses are debits, including transfers; it renders and returns the result.

tools.name: search_transactions
tools.description: Runs fixed local SQL to find the newest matching transactions by date, category, merchant text, or absolute amount. It returns at most 50 rows and renders the matching summary.

tools.name: show_spending_by_month
tools.description: Runs fixed local SQL to group debit spending by month, ending on the newest available transaction date.

months.description: Number of latest calendar months to include.

tools.name: compare_recent_spending
tools.description: Runs fixed local SQL to compare debit spending in the latest available 30 days with the preceding 30 days.

tools.name: show_category_breakdown
tools.description: Runs the fixed local spending summary grouped by category. Expenses are debit transactions, including transfers.

tools.name: show_recurring_transactions
tools.description: Runs fixed local SQL to group recurring debit transactions by merchant. It reports observed history and does not infer a future payment date.

tools.name: show_merchant_summary
tools.description: Runs fixed local SQL to group debit spending by merchant, optionally filtering merchant text or a date range.

tools.name: show_account_balance
tools.description: Returns the current local balance for one or all Privta accounts and renders it in the document. It does not reconstruct a historical balance from transactions.

tools.name: show_unusual_expenses
tools.description: Runs fixed local SQL to flag debit transactions at least two population standard deviations above the historical debit average. This is not a fraud decision.

tools.name: show_transaction_by_recency
tools.description: Runs fixed local SQL for an ordinal transaction such as the tenth most recent transaction, renders it in the Privta document, and returns the transaction summary.

position.description: The requested 1-based position among all transactions, ordered newest first.

tools.name: show_financial_summary
tools.description: Runs a local DuckDB SQL summary for spending, income, or cash flow, renders the result in the Privta document, and returns the summary. Use last_7_days for last week and last_30_days for last month.

period.description: Use last_7_days for last week and last_30_days for last month.

from.description: Optional inclusive date in YYYY-MM-DD.

to.description: Optional inclusive date in YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.name: make_transfer
tools.description: Transfers USD from Privta checking to a saved contact. This changes fictional funds; ChatGPT Desktop must obtain user approval before this tool executes.

tools.name: pay_service
tools.description: Pays a pending USD service bill from Privta checking. ChatGPT Desktop must obtain user approval before this tool executes.

tools.name: dispute_charge
tools.description: Starts a dispute for a transaction. ChatGPT Desktop must obtain user approval before this tool executes.

tools.name: create_budget_rule
tools.description: Creates a monthly USD budget alert. ChatGPT Desktop must obtain user approval before this tool executes.

sites.name: qotien.fr
sites.description: Simulateur impôt 2026

tools.name: fiscal_impot_revenu
tools.description: Impôt sur le revenu (barème 2026) — Impôt sur le revenu brut d'un foyer (barème progressif, quotient familial plafonné, décote). Revenus 2025.

revenu_net_imposable.description: Revenu net imposable du foyer (€), après abattements.

parts.description: Nombre de parts de quotient familial.
