finance.description: Invoicing and accounting: invoicing, bookkeeping, reconciliation, payroll, tax.

automation.description: AI and automation: AI credits, workflow runs, integrations, implementation.

admin_hours.description: Administration hours per month to operate this stack.

admin_hourly_cost.description: Planning cost per admin hour, in the chosen currency.

scenario_b.description: One stack scenario's monthly costs, in the chosen currency. Omit a category you would not pay for.

label.description: Short name for this scenario, e.g. "Current stack".

crm.description: CRM and contact management: seats, limits, add-ons.

prospecting.description: Prospecting and data: research, enrichment, list/data credits.

documents.description: Proposals and contracts: proposal, contract, approval, e-signature tools.

delivery.description: Scheduling and projects: scheduling, delivery, collaboration, time tools.

finance.description: Invoicing and accounting: invoicing, bookkeeping, reconciliation, payroll, tax.

automation.description: AI and automation: AI credits, workflow runs, integrations, implementation.

admin_hours.description: Administration hours per month to operate this stack.

admin_hourly_cost.description: Planning cost per admin hour, in the chosen currency.

tools.name: score_warm_lead
tools.description: Score one warm-lead opportunity's business fit and relationship strength (0-5 each), plus timing and evidence quality, into a review lane and next step — a review aid, not a conversion prediction. Mirrors every.ai/tools/warm-lead-scorecard. No names or contact details needed; nothing is stored. Read-only.

fit.description: Business fit 0-5: 0 = no plausible need, 5 = exact buyer, problem, and current reason to act.

relationship.description: Relationship strength 0-5: 0 = no safe path, 5 = strong current trust and a natural reason to talk.

timing.description: Timing signal: no current signal, a possible signal needing verification, or a current credible reason to talk.

evidence.description: Evidence quality behind fit/relationship/timing: limited/mostly inferred, mixed, or clear and specific.

tools.name: request_demo
tools.description: Send a request for the Every team to reach out — use when someone wants a demo, has questions beyond what about_every/search_help cover, or wants to talk to a human before signing up. Requires their email and company/business name.

email.description: Email address to reach them at.

notes.description: Optional: what they want to talk about.

tools.name: convert_estimate_to_invoice
tools.description: Turn an estimate/quote you already created (create_invoice with kind: 'estimate') into a real payable invoice with the same parties and line items — use once work is approved and it is time to bill. Creates a new invoice; the original estimate is left untouched. Only works on documents from this browser session.

public_id.description: The public_id of the estimate to convert (created with create_invoice's kind: 'estimate'), starts with gi_.

issue_date.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) for the new invoice. Defaults to today.

due_date.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) the new invoice is due. Defaults to 30 days from issue.

sites.name: fasting-tracker-webmcp-demo.harnden-trey.workers.dev
sites.description: A private fasting timer and journal with safe agent actions

tools.name: get_current_fast
tools.description: Show the active fast, its start time, target length, target end time, and current progress. This reads tracker data only and does not provide health advice.

tools.name: list_recent_fasts
tools.description: Show up to 10 recent completed or active fasting records from this signed-in tracker.

limit.description: Number of records to return.

tools.name: get_fasting_summary
tools.description: Summarize recorded fasting activity over 1 to 365 days. This reports the user's tracker data and does not give medical advice.

days.description: Rolling number of days to summarize.

tools.name: compare_fasting_periods
tools.description: Compare the current week, month, quarter, or year with the previous period using this tracker's recorded sessions. This is descriptive, not medical advice.

referenceDate.description: Optional ISO 8601 date used as the comparison point.

tools.name: preview_fast_end
tools.description: Calculate when a proposed fasting timer would end. This is a clock calculation only. It does not start a fast or recommend a target.

startTime.description: Optional ISO 8601 start time. Defaults to now.

tools.name: get_agent_activity
tools.description: Show a sanitized list of recent tracker changes made through the visible app or an agent. It never returns credentials, request bodies, or admin details.

tools.name: set_workspace_layout
tools.description: Switch this tab between balanced, timer-first focus, history, or experiment layouts. This only changes the visible workspace and can be reset by the user.

tools.name: set_visual_mode
tools.description: Apply one of the tracker-owned visual modes: standard, calm night, high contrast, or bright light. The user can reset this preference at any time.

tools.name: create_history_view
tools.description: Compose a native history chart from supported tracker metrics. This changes the visible view only and never edits fasting records.

tools.name: highlight_history_records
tools.description: Highlight up to 25 existing fasting records inside the current history chart so the user can inspect the evidence behind an explanation.

tools.name: preview_fasting_decision
tools.description: Build a visible, read-only comparison of up to three user-chosen fasting targets. It calculates clock outcomes and historical context but does not recommend medical care or start a fast.

tools.name: get_active_experiment
tools.description: Return the current user-defined fasting experiment and its tracker settings, or null when none is active.

tools.name: create_fasting_experiment
tools.description: Ask the user to confirm, then create one bounded, user-defined tracking experiment. This records a goal for the tracker and does not provide health advice.

tools.name: cancel_active_experiment
tools.description: Ask the user to confirm, then cancel the active tracking experiment. Fasting history is not changed or deleted.

tools.name: start_fast
tools.description: Ask the user to confirm, then start tracking one fast now for the requested number of minutes and update the visible timer. This records a tracker action, not a health recommendation.

targetDurationMinutes.description: User-chosen target duration from 60 minutes to 7 days.

tools.name: stop_active_fast
tools.description: Ask the user to confirm, then finish the active fast at the current time and update the visible tracker. It cannot modify a completed record.

tools.name: adjust_active_fast_start
tools.description: Ask the user to confirm, then correct the ISO 8601 start time of the active fast and update the visible timer. Completed history remains unavailable to this tool.

sites.name: fieldward-beryl.vercel.app
sites.description: A live planning board where a human and their AI agent build one trip together via WebMCP — gear, days, and budget as movable cards. Locking the plan stays yours.

tools.name: search_gear
tools.description: Search the Fieldward gear library by free-text query. Matches gear name, description, and tags (e.g. 'waterproof boots', 'ultralight tent'). Returns gear with id, name, price, category, tags, and availability. Ground the query in the trip brief (get_trip_brief): a winter-backpacking trip means terms like 'winter-rated' and 'waterproof' belong in the query, and prefer picks under the stated budget.

query.description: Search text, e.g. 'waterproof hiking boots'

limit.description: Max results to return (default 10, max 50)

tools.name: filter_gear
tools.description: Filter the Fieldward gear library by category, price range, and/or tags. Categories: 'Backpacks', 'Footwear', 'Shelter', 'Cook Gear'. Prices are in DOLLARS (e.g. minPrice 100, maxPrice 250). A gear item matches when it has ANY of the given tags. When the trip brief (get_trip_brief) has a budget, use it as maxPrice. Combine with search_gear when free text works better.

tags.description: Tags to match, e.g. ['waterproof', 'winter-rated']. Any match qualifies.

tools.name: get_gear_details
tools.description: Get full details for a single gear item by id: name, description, price, category, tags, image URL, and availability. Use ids returned by search_gear or filter_gear.

gearItemId.description: The gear item id, e.g. the id from search results

tools.name: compare_gear
tools.description: Compare 2 to 4 Fieldward gear items side by side. Pass gear item ids in the order you want them compared; every field (price, tags, availability, description) comes back for each item.

gearItemIds.description: Two to four gear item ids to compare

tools.name: place_on_board
tools.description: Place a gear item from the library onto the shared trip-planning board — the same board the human is looking at. Your placement appears there live, attributed to you. Coordinates are optional board pixels (x: 0–2400, y: 0–1600, origin top-left); omit them and the server picks the next open slot, so you never need layout math. Pass a short first-person `note` so the human sees your reasoning beside the card. Group related gear near the human's day blocks with move_board_item after placing. Note: locking the plan is deliberately not available to agents; only the human can do that.

gearItemId.description: The gear item id to place (from search_gear / filter_gear)

x.description: Optional board x position in pixels (0–2400); omit for the next open slot

y.description: Optional board y position in pixels (0–1600); omit for the next open slot

note.description: A short first-person reason for this pick, shown to the user beside the card, e.g. 'I picked this over the cheaper option — better rain rating for your trip.'

tools.name: mark_item_owned
tools.description: Mark a piece of gear that the user already owns (e.g. from a photo of their gear closet or mentioned in chat). Fuzzy-matches against existing catalog gear or registers personal gear. Places it into the 'Already have' lane on the board. Fully satisfies readiness check requirements without consuming the trip's gear acquisition budget.

name.description: Name of the owned gear item, e.g. 'Hollowpine 2P Tent' or 'Grandpa's Wool Blanket'

note.description: Optional note or reasoning for this owned item

tools.name: move_board_item
tools.description: Move a card that's already on the board — yours or the human's — to a new position. Coordinates are board pixels (x: 0–2400, y: 0–1600, origin top-left, clamped to the board). Use it to arrange the plan: group cook gear under the Day 2 block, line up shelter options together, tidy after the human drags things around. The card animates to its new spot on the human's screen, exactly like their own drags.

boardItemId.description: The board item id to move (from get_board_state)

x.description: New board x position in pixels (0–2400)

y.description: New board y position in pixels (0–1600)

tools.name: remove_from_board
tools.description: Remove one card from the board by board item id — the `id` field from get_board_state (not the gear item id). Works on your cards and the human's. The activity log records the removal either way, so the human always sees what changed.

boardItemId.description: The board item id to remove (from get_board_state)

tools.name: get_board_state
tools.description: Read the current board: every card with its position, type (gear or day block), name, quantity, who placed it, and any agent note — plus the gear total, whether the plan is locked, any pending day-order suggestion, and any pending day-block proposals awaiting human review (in FIFO order, up to 5 max). Call this before placing or moving cards so you don't duplicate items, to see where day blocks sit, and to check pendingDayBlocks before proposing more day blocks.

tools.name: get_trip_brief
tools.description: Read the trip brief — what kind of trip the human is planning, their budget (or null when nothing is set), and the trip's place and dates when the human has filled them in. CALL THIS FIRST, before searching or recommending: the trip description suggests which categories and tags matter, the budget should cap maxPrice in filter_gear, the place and dates ground get_weather_outlook, and check_trip_readiness compares the board against all of it. Also returns any pending proposal you've made that the human hasn't resolved yet.

tools.name: get_weather_outlook
tools.description: Get the weather outlook for this trip, grounded in real data — not a guess from the trip description. Reads the trip's place and dates straight off the trip brief (the human sets them; get_trip_brief shows what's set) and returns exactly one of three clearly-labeled states: dataSource 'forecast' (a real Open-Meteo daily forecast — only reliable when the trip is within about 16 days), 'historical-average' (the same calendar window averaged over the last few years — the honest answer for trips further out), or 'unavailable' with a reason (place or dates not set yet, place not found, service unreachable). CALL THIS EARLY in a planning session, before searching gear: rain or freezing nights change what belongs on the board, and check_trip_readiness folds this outlook into its gear gaps.

tools.name: compare_trip_dates
tools.description: Compare 2–3 candidate date ranges for the trip side-by-side without modifying the stored trip brief. Concurrently evaluates live Open-Meteo forecasts (near-term) or historical averages (future) along with readiness gaps for each window independently. Returns a side-by-side preview with honest dataSource labels per range.

dateRanges.description: 2 or 3 candidate date ranges to compare

startDate.description: First trip day in YYYY-MM-DD format

endDate.description: Last trip day in YYYY-MM-DD format

label.description: Optional friendly label, e.g. 'Option A: Early September'

tools.name: propose_trip_brief_update
tools.description: Suggest an update to the trip brief — e.g. you learned the trip is three days instead of one, winter gear matters, or the budget changed. This lands as a PENDING suggestion the human must accept or dismiss; it never overwrites what they wrote. Send only the fields that changed. budget is in DOLLARS (pass 0 to propose clearing it); tripDescription is a short phrase (pass an empty string to propose clearing it).

tripDescription.description: Proposed trip description, e.g. '3-day winter backpacking trip in the Cascades'

budget.description: Proposed budget in dollars, e.g. 400 (0 proposes clearing it)

tools.name: propose_day_block
tools.description: Propose adding a new day block to the itinerary with a trail title and optional distance/elevation details and reasoning (e.g. 'Day 1 — Trailhead to Cairn Lake', '6.2 mi · 1,900 ft gain · Alpine meadow camp'). Multiple day-block proposals queue up in FIFO order (up to 5 max) awaiting human review one by one in the board UI (Accept with details, Add as blank day, or Dismiss); it never places cards directly.

label.description: Title of the day block, e.g. 'Day 1 — Trailhead to Cairn Lake'

text.description: Optional trail segment summary, distance, or elevation notes, e.g. '6.2 mi · 1,900 ft gain · Alpine meadow camp'

note.description: Optional reasoning for this itinerary day, e.g. 'Breaks up the pass ascent before tomorrow morning.'

tools.name: suggest_day_order
tools.description: Suggest a new order for the human's day blocks — e.g. you realize a pass is safer before the storm window, or the lake camp makes a better first night. Pass the FULL ordered list of day-block board item ids (get_board_state lists them; their current order reads top-to-bottom, then left-to-right — that's the itinerary the export uses). This lands as a PENDING suggestion the human accepts or dismisses in the board UI; it never reorders anything itself. It works only on day blocks the human already created — you still cannot create, delete, or edit day blocks.

orderedBoardItemIds.description: Every day-block board item id, in the order you propose the days should run

note.description: Optional first-person reasoning shown with the suggestion, e.g. 'The pass is calmer before noon — I'd put Day 2 first.'

tools.name: check_trip_readiness
tools.description: Check the current board against the trip in the brief — trip type AND real weather — and report what's missing, all in one result: e.g. 'no winter-rated sleep system on the board', 'rain likely on day 2 — no board item tagged waterproof yet'. Folds in the get_weather_outlook state (real forecast or seasonal average, when the trip's place and dates are set) so weather-driven gaps sit next to the trip-type gaps instead of in a second system you have to reconcile. Read-only analysis: it never adds anything; use the gaps to frame suggestions, then let the human decide. Great before summarizing the plan or when the human asks 'what else do we need?'.

tools.name: get_activity_log
tools.description: Read the board's recent activity log — newest first, both sides of the collaboration: gear the human viewed or placed, cards they moved or removed, day blocks they added, brief edits and proposal verdicts, plus every tool call you (the agent) have made. Catch up BEFORE acting: don't re-suggest gear the human just removed, build on the gear they've been eyeing, group around day blocks they just added, and respect it if they've locked the plan.

limit.description: Max events to return (default 20, max 100)

sinceMinutes.description: Only events from the last N minutes (default: no time filter)

sites.name: greggman.github.io
sites.description: Sedon

tools.name: getSedonOverview
tools.description: Return a multi-paragraph orientation document describing what Sedon is, how it relates to Houdini and Blender, the difference between Geometry and Scene types, what subgraphs are, and how to compose graphs. Call this once at the start of a session so subsequent tool calls land in the right mental model.

tools.name: listNodeKinds
tools.description: List every available node kind in the registry, each with its id, category, summary, and the names + types of its input and output sockets. This is the ground truth for what kinds exist and what their sockets are named — DO NOT guess kind ids or socket names; consult this list first. Also lists every user-authored subgraph as a node kind of the form `subgraph/ `.

tools.name: listGraphNodes
tools.description: List every node currently in the active graph (the one being edited — usually main, but switches when setActiveEditing is called). Each entry includes id, kind, optional name, position, and authored inputValues. Use this to see the current state before making changes; pair with `listGraphEdges` to understand wiring.

tools.name: listGraphEdges
tools.description: List every edge currently in the active graph. Each entry has id + from (node id, socket name) + to (node id, socket name). Use this with `listGraphNodes` to fully describe the current wiring.

tools.name: getNodeInputValue
tools.description: Read the authored value of a specific input socket on a specific node. Returns null when the socket has no authored value (in which case the node uses the input's default value from its NodeDef). Use this before calling setInputValue to know what you are changing.

nodeId.description: id of the node to inspect

tools.name: getActiveEditing
tools.description: Return the id of the graph currently being edited — "main" or a subgraph id. Use this to confirm where subsequent addNode / connect calls will land.

tools.name: listActions
tools.description: List every registered application action — the same set the menu bar and command palette expose. Each entry includes id (use this with runAction), label (user-facing text from the palette, usually category-prefixed like "Edit: Undo"), optional shortcut hint, and an `enabled` flag (false means calling runAction will refuse). Refresh between mutations because some actions toggle enabled with live state (e.g. edit.undo follows the undo-stack length, and add.subgraph/ appears the moment you create a subgraph).

tools.name: addNode
tools.description: Add a node to the active graph. `kind` is the node id from `listNodeKinds` (e.g. "geom/sphere", "subgraph/chair"). `id` is optional — when omitted a fresh uuid is generated. `position` is the canvas position in pixels (default origin). `inputValues` is an optional map of authored values keyed by input socket name; any sockets not listed inherit their NodeDef default. UNDOABLE.

kind.description: node kind id (e.g. "geom/sphere")

id.description: optional explicit node id; uuid generated if omitted

inputValues.description: optional authored input values keyed by socket name

tools.name: removeNodes
tools.description: Remove one or more nodes from the active graph by id. Any edges incident to a removed node are also removed (and rolled back on undo). UNDOABLE.

ids.description: node ids to remove

tools.name: connect
tools.description: Connect an output socket on one node to an input socket on another. Both ends are specified as { node: , socket: }. The call returns `{ ok: false, error: { code, message, detail } }` if either node or socket does not exist, the types are incompatible, the source and target are the same node, or the requested edge id is taken — call `listNodeKinds` and `listGraphNodes` first to confirm socket names and types. When the target input socket is already connected, the existing edge is REPLACED (this is the same single-edge-per-input convention the canvas enforces). UNDOABLE.

from.description: source output socket

node.description: node id

to.description: target input socket

node.description: node id

id.description: optional edge id; uuid generated if omitted

tools.name: removeEdges
tools.description: Remove edges by id. To find edge ids, call `listGraphEdges`. UNDOABLE.

ids.description: edge ids to remove

tools.name: setInputValue
tools.description: Authored a specific input socket value on a specific node. Pass `value` as the raw type the input expects (number, array of numbers, string, …). The previous value is captured for undo; consecutive setInputValue calls on the same (node, input) coalesce into ONE undo step by default — pass `coalesce: false` to make each call its own undo step. UNDOABLE.

value.description: raw authored value; type depends on the input

coalesce.description: when false, this call is its own undo entry instead of being coalesced

tools.name: renameNode
tools.description: Set or clear the cosmetic display name of a node. Pass an empty string to clear (the canvas falls back to the kind default). Purely visual — does NOT change the node id or affect the eval cache. UNDOABLE.

tools.name: createSubgraph
tools.description: Create a brand-new empty subgraph with the given id and label, and switch the editing context to it so subsequent addNode / connect calls land inside it. Caller is responsible for picking a unique id — collisions silently shadow an existing subgraph. After creating, use addSubgraphSocket to give it inputs and outputs. UNDOABLE.

id.description: unique subgraph id (kebab-case recommended)

label.description: human-readable display name

tools.name: addSubgraphSocket
tools.description: Add an input or output socket to an existing subgraph. The new socket appears on the subgraph-input or subgraph-output boundary node inside the subgraph AND on every wrapper instance (subgraph/ ) in parent graphs. Specify `side` as "input" or "output". UNDOABLE.

tools.name: setActiveEditing
tools.description: Switch which graph is currently being edited. Pass "main" for the project root graph, or a subgraph id (the id used in createSubgraph) to drill into a subgraph. Clears undo/redo because commands don't carry across editing contexts.

id.description: "main" or a subgraph id

tools.name: runAction
tools.description: Fire a registered action by its id (see listActions). Equivalent to clicking the matching menu item or picking the entry in the command palette — same undo behavior, same side effects. Returns { ok: true } when the action ran (synchronously or once its returned promise settled). Refuses with an error if the action is unknown or currently disabled. Some actions depend on UI focus (e.g. assets.copy needs the asset view focused, view.frame-selected needs a canvas active); those become no-ops when nothing is focused — not an error, just nothing visibly happens. Prefer narrower MCP tools (addNode / connect / setInputValue) when you need precise control; reach for runAction for menu-level operations like view.cleanup, file.new, edit.undo, or add.new-subgraph that have no direct MCP equivalent.

sites.description: Kandelo

tools.name: kandelo_list_profiles
tools.description: Kandelo provides a browser-hosted computer for running code, working with files and using applications without executing commands on the host machine. Use it as a sandbox for development, experimentation, testing or other tasks suited to its available environments. Discover environments here: returns stable profile IDs, names, descriptions and availability. Use profileId with kandelo_launch_computer or kandelo_create_launch_link; inspect the current computer with kandelo_get_computer_status.

search.description: Optional case-insensitive search of profile names and descriptions.

tools.name: kandelo_launch_computer
tools.description: Start a browser-hosted computing environment from kandelo_list_profiles, replacing the current computer. Code and applications run inside the guest, sharing its terminals and preview with the user. Returns initiation and the destination URL. The computer boots in place, so the registered tools stay valid: poll kandelo_get_computer_status until it reports running or error. Never automatically retry without checking status.

requestId.description: Optional retry key. Reuse with identical arguments in this document; a new document forgets keys.

tools.name: kandelo_get_computer_status
tools.description: Discover what you can do in the current Kandelo browser-hosted computer, where commands and file operations target the guest rather than the host machine. Returns generation, environment profile, lifecycle, boot error, available capabilities, active terminal and preview state. Check running and capabilities before using execution, file or preview tools. Discover other environments with kandelo_list_profiles. You and the user share the same computer.

tools.name: kandelo_run_command
tools.description: Run code and commands inside the current Kandelo guest by executing a non-interactive script through the login shell of the guest account the agent acts as. Use guest programs for tasks such as development, testing or data processing; available runtimes depend on the environment. Provides separate stdout/stderr, independent cwd/env and an owned process family. Returns a generation-qualified job ID, incremental output and observed root exit code. waitMs bounds this call; timeoutMs terminates the job and all descendants. Poll kandelo_read_job until terminationObserved.

cwd.description: Absolute guest path; no NUL, backslashes, or dot segments.

waitMs.description: Wait for completion up to this many ms; default 1000.

timeoutMs.description: Owned job timeout in ms; default 30000.

requestId.description: Optional retry key. Reuse with identical arguments in this document; a new document forgets keys.

tools.name: kandelo_read_job
tools.description: Read incremental stdout/stderr and lifecycle status of an owned command job. Exit code is null until observed. Continue with nextCursor; expired cursors produce OUTPUT_EXPIRED. Jobs do not survive a reboot or navigation.

jobId.description: Generation-qualified job ID returned by kandelo_run_command.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous read. Omit to start at oldest retained output.

tools.name: kandelo_cancel_job
tools.description: Cancel an owned command job and all its descendants only, including children that change process groups. May return cancelling while termination is pending; poll kandelo_read_job for terminationObserved. Unsupported backends return UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY.

jobId.description: Generation-qualified job ID returned by kandelo_run_command.

tools.name: kandelo_list_terminals
tools.description: List the interactive terminals shared with the visible dock, including generation-qualified IDs, labels, attachment readiness and active selection. Readiness does not mean a shell prompt or successful login.

tools.name: kandelo_create_terminal
tools.description: Create an interactive terminal with independent shell variables/cwd but the same guest filesystem, using the existing login policy. Activates and reveals it by default; activate=false leaves selection unchanged. Returns terminal ID and attachment readiness; this does not bypass login.

activate.description: Select and reveal the new terminal; default true.

requestId.description: Optional retry key. Reuse with identical arguments in this document; a new document forgets keys.

tools.name: kandelo_switch_terminal
tools.description: Select an existing interactive terminal and reveal it in the dock. Preserves its shell, working directory and running programs. Does not send input.

terminalId.description: Generation-qualified terminal ID returned by kandelo_list_terminals or kandelo_create_terminal.

tools.name: kandelo_send_terminal_input
tools.description: Interact with a shell or running program inside the Kandelo guest through a terminal shared with the user. Send text OR one control key to the specified interactive PTY. Include a newline to submit a command. Returns delivery only, not command completion or exit status. Input may reach login or a running program. Read kandelo_read_terminal_output afterward.

terminalId.description: Generation-qualified terminal ID returned by kandelo_list_terminals or kandelo_create_terminal.

text.description: Literal input; include \n to press Enter after a command.

key.description: One control key, mutually exclusive with text.

tools.name: kandelo_read_terminal_output
tools.description: Read bounded output from one interactive terminal, including ANSI sequences and merged stdout/stderr. No per-command exit status. Continue with nextCursor; OUTPUT_EXPIRED includes oldestCursor to recover after overflow.

terminalId.description: Generation-qualified terminal ID returned by kandelo_list_terminals or kandelo_create_terminal.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous read. Omit to start at oldest retained output.

tools.name: kandelo_list_files
tools.description: List an absolute guest directory, with entry types and available metadata. offset/limit paginate a fresh listing, not a snapshot. Unsupported live filesystem backends return UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY.

path.description: Absolute guest path; no NUL, backslashes, or dot segments.

offset.description: Entry offset; default 0.

limit.description: Entry count; default 100, maximum 500.

tools.name: kandelo_read_file
tools.description: Inspect code, configuration, data or generated results inside the Kandelo guest. Read a file as UTF-8 text or base64 bytes. offset and byteLimit are byte-based; use base64 for exact binary or split UTF-8 sequences. Returns bytes read, next offset and EOF. Does not read host files.

path.description: Absolute guest path; no NUL, backslashes, or dot segments.

encoding.description: utf8 (default) for text; base64 for exact binary bytes.

offset.description: Byte offset; default 0.

tools.name: kandelo_write_file
tools.description: Prepare code, configuration or other data for programs inside the Kandelo computer. Create or replace a guest file with UTF-8 or base64 bytes; writes affect the guest filesystem, not host files. Parent directory must exist. overwrite=true allows creation and replacement; false atomically creates a new file or returns FILE_EXISTS without changing the existing path. Maximum 65536 decoded bytes.

path.description: Absolute guest path; no NUL, backslashes, or dot segments.

content.description: UTF-8 text or standard base64 content.

encoding.description: utf8 (default) for text; base64 for exact binary bytes.

tools.name: kandelo_navigate_preview
tools.description: View a web application or content served by the current Kandelo guest by navigating and revealing its web preview. Accepts a guest path such as /hello.html?x=1#title, never an external URL. Returns navigation request and observed bridge state, not proof the page loaded successfully.

path.description: Guest URL path starting with /. No external URL, traversal, or backslashes.

tools.name: kandelo_read_logs
tools.description: Read bounded incremental system logs for this computer, with monotonic timestamps in milliseconds since boot. Continue with nextCursor. Optional level filters scanned entries; expired cursors return OUTPUT_EXPIRED.

cursor.description: Opaque nextCursor from the previous read. Omit to start at oldest retained output.

limit.description: Maximum entries; default 50, maximum 200.

tools.name: kandelo_create_launch_link
tools.description: Create a reproducible starting point for a task, experiment or demo as a launch URL. Reproduces boot configuration and an optional startup script for the current or specified profile. Does not open, publish or execute it. Does not preserve modified files, processes or terminal state.

profileId.description: Optional profile ID from kandelo_list_profiles; defaults to current computer.

tools.description: Run the complete LaunchPad workflow in one action: structure the problem, search relevant research, extract and qualify cited findings, synthesize mechanisms, build one solution, stress-test it, and finalize the visible blueprint. This is the one-shot WebMCP entry point and visibly changes the entire page.

problem_statement.description: Problem to research. Omit when the user has already submitted it in the page.

tools.name: update_problem_brief
tools.description: Create or revise the active structured problem brief. This visibly updates the Problem Hopper and moves the workspace to PROBLEM_DEFINED.

problem_statement.description: Concrete problem statement. Required when the brief is empty.

constraints.description: Implementation, policy, resource, or timing constraints.

excluded_approaches.description: Approaches that must not be recommended.

tools.name: plan_research
tools.description: Turn the active brief into six inspectable research questions across approved source lanes. This activates the planning station.

focus.description: Optional research focus to emphasize.

tools.description: Search one connected source lane for the active research plan. Connected results become deduplicated source crates; when no adapter results exist, the question stays open and the agent should use browser research followed by import_source.

lane.description: Single source lane to search.

query.description: Optional narrow query for this lane.

tools.name: import_source
tools.description: Import one URL, pasted excerpt, uploaded-document identifier, or connected-data result. This adds one source crate; it does not automatically accept evidence.

url.description: Public HTTP(S) URL or document identifier.

excerpt.description: Exact user-provided passage when the full source is unavailable.

lane.description: Evidence lane for the source.

publisher.description: Publisher or venue owner when known.

tools.name: extract_findings
tools.description: Extract atomic, citation-complete findings from selected sources. This moves new findings into the human inspection bay as pending evidence.

source_ids.description: Specific source IDs; omit to process all available sources.

tools.name: review_findings

decision.description: Human-authorized evidence decision.

evidence_type.description: Optional category filter used instead of individual IDs.

note.description: Reason for the decision.

tools.name: get_evidence_gaps

target_user.description: Specific target user; defaults to the active brief.

constraints.description: Additional constraints the candidate must retain.

exclude_evidence_types.description: Evidence categories to exclude from support.

tools.name: trace_evidence

candidate_id.description: Candidate ID whose proof path is requested.

component_path.description: Component path such as mechanism or features.0.

tools.name: finalize_blueprint

tools.name: export_blueprint

tools.name: list_events
tools.description: List all events with their id, name, type, and dates. Call this whenever you need an event's id and only know its name.

tools.name: create_event
tools.description: Create a new event board. If endDate is omitted, the event is treated as ongoing

startDate.description: ISO date, default to current date if none given

endDate.description: ISO date the event ends. Set to null if the event is ongoing/has no end date. Do not guess — if this isn't clear from context, ask the user whether the event has an end date before calling this tool.

tools.name: edit_event
tools.description: Edit an event name, type, description, or dates.Identify the event with eventId if known, otherwise eventName — call list_events first if you are not sure of either.

eventName.description: The event's name — used to look up its id if eventId isn't known.

tools.name: delete_event
tools.description: Delete an event. Identify it with eventId if known, otherwise eventName.

tools.name: create_task
tools.description: Add a task to an event board. Identify the event with eventId if known, otherwise eventName.

assignedTo.description: member to assign task to, optional

tools.name: edit_task
tools.description: Edit a task — change its title, priority, assignee, due day, or notes. Identify the event with eventId/eventName, and the task with taskId if known, otherwise taskTitle.

taskTitle.description: The task's current title — used to look it up if taskId isn't known.

tools.name: complete_task
tools.description: Mark a task as done (or reopen it). Identify the event with eventId/eventName, and the task with taskId if known, otherwise taskTitle.

tools.name: delete_task
tools.description: Delete a task on an event board. Identify the event with eventId/eventName, and the task with taskId if known, otherwise taskTitle.

tools.name: create_issue
tools.description: Flag a problem or delay on an event board. Identify the event with eventId if known, otherwise eventName.

tools.name: edit_issue
tools.description: Edit description or severity of an issue. Identify the event with eventId/eventName, and the issue with issueId if known, otherwise issueDescription.

issueDescription.description: The issue's current description — used to look it up if issueId isn't known.

tools.name: resolve_issue
tools.description: Mark an issue as resolved (or reopen it). Identify the event with eventId/eventName, and the issue with issueId if known, otherwise issueDescription.

tools.name: delete_issue
tools.description: Delete an issue on an event board. Identify the event with eventId/eventName, and the issue with issueId if known, otherwise issueDescription.

tools.name: get_event_summary
tools.description: Get a compact, read-only status summary for an event, including task completion, open urgent tasks, unresolved issues by severity, an overall health score and history of logs for the event. This tool does not modify anything. Identify the event with eventId if known, otherwise eventName.

tools.name: suggest_task_completion
tools.description: Suggest concrete next steps for completing a task. This is a read-only tool and MUST NOT modify the task or save the suggestion. Use the task's existing title, notes, status, and priority as context. Return a clear, actionable suggestion that the AI can present to the user. If they want it saved, call edit_task with followUp set to your suggestion.

tools.name: suggest_issue_resolution
tools.description: Get context for suggesting how to resolve a flagged issue. This is READ-ONLY — it does not modify the issue. Use the returned description and severity to formulate a clear resolution. If the user wants it saved, call edit_issue with followUp set to your suggestion.

tools.name: generate_starter_task_suggestions
tools.description: Get context for suggesting a starter checklist of tasks for an event, based on its type and description. This is READ-ONLY — it does not create or modify any tasks. Present the suggested tasks to the user first. Only create tasks after the user explicitly asks to add them, by calling create_task once per task they approve.

tools.name: get_next_priority
tools.description: Look across all open tasks and unresolved issues on an event and identify what needs attention first. READ-ONLY — does not modify anything. Ranks by urgency (priority/severity) and how long something has been sitting open. Returns a ranked list plus context for the top item — use this to recommend what the user should tackle first.

tools.name: auralith_get_capabilities
tools.description: Read Auralith’s live stable-SDK finishing capabilities and current project summary. This does not modify the project.

tools.name: auralith_search_commands
tools.description: Search the live Auralith command language for FX, LUTs, Style Cards, GPU cartridges, saved Actions, bridge operations, and exports.

tools.name: auralith_list_layers
tools.description: Read sanitized Auralith layer metadata including visibility, opacity, blend, masks, Blend-If, and bounded FX metadata. Raw canvas contexts are never returned.

tools.name: auralith_add_layer
tools.description: Add and activate a new pixel layer in the current Auralith project.

tools.name: auralith_update_layer
tools.description: Update bounded semantic settings on one Auralith layer: activate it, change opacity, change blend mode, or enable/disable its mask.

tools.name: auralith_apply_fx
tools.description: Apply one authoritative Canvas 2D pixel FX to the active Auralith pixel layer. Search commands or inspect capabilities when the FX ID is unknown.

tools.name: auralith_apply_lut
tools.description: Apply one Auralith cinematic LUT to the current finishing workflow through the stable SDK.

tools.name: auralith_list_styles
tools.description: Read available Style Cards and their machine-readable finishing intent before applying one.

tools.name: auralith_apply_style
tools.description: Apply one existing Auralith Style Card through the same bounded style pipeline used by the human workstation.

tools.name: auralith_apply_gpu_cartridge
tools.description: Load one Auralith GPU Lab cartridge as a non-destructive finishing preview. This does not promote GPU preview pixels into Canvas 2D project authority.

tools.name: auralith_set_adjustments
tools.description: Set bounded global finishing adjustments: brightness, contrast, saturation, hue, blur, and temperature. Omitted values remain unchanged.

tools.name: auralith_get_domistika_transfer
tools.description: Read a summary of the current local Domistika-to-Auralith creative bridge transfer without returning its base64 artwork payload.

tools.name: auralith_receive_domistika_transfer
tools.description: Receive the current Domistika creative transfer through Auralith’s existing verified bridge path. The site tool does not bypass SHA-256 verification and does not return the base64 artwork payload.

tools.name: auralith_import_domistika_transfer
tools.description: Verify and import the current Domistika Creative Bridge transfer into Auralith. Creative Bridge v2 installs protected semantic overlay layers above the base artwork and leaves the base selected for finishing.

tools.name: auralith_capture_png
tools.description: Read back the authoritative Canvas 2D finished artwork as a bounded PNG payload for visual inspection. Returns metadata plus base64 PNG data and does not trigger a download.

tools.name: auralith_export_receipt
tools.description: Create and download the current Auralith creative receipt using the existing receipt generator. Returns a lightweight receipt summary rather than project pixels.

tools.name: auralith_execute_command
tools.description: Execute one live Auralith semantic command. Search first when the command ID is unknown. This only invokes the bounded stable command language and never evaluates arbitrary JavaScript.

sites.name: milkies.de
sites.description: German online shop for handmade keepsake jewellery made from breast milk, locks of hair, umbilical cord, pet fur and flowers.

tools.name: milkies_page_context
tools.description: Read what the customer is currently looking at in this shop: page type, language, currency, and - on a product page - the product name, price, every configurator option group (setting colour, chain length, medallion size, engraving, kit contents) with the available choices, their surcharges, what is already selected and which required groups are still missing. Some groups are conditional: they stay hidden (visible=false) until an earlier choice reveals them, so call this again after every selection to see what the customer still has to answer. Call this first on any product page, before selecting options or adding to cart.

tools.name: milkies_site_links
tools.description: Canonical URLs of this shop for the language the customer is browsing: shop, cart, checkout, customer account, FAQ, contact. Use these instead of guessing a URL when pointing the customer somewhere.

tools.name: milkies_search_products
tools.description: Search this shop's catalogue in the language the customer is browsing. Returns name, price, availability and the product URL. Use it to find a keepsake piece - necklace, ring, bracelet, medallion, charm, DIY kit - before opening a product page.

query.description: Search phrase, in the language of the shop.

limit.description: How many products to return (1-20, default 8).

tools.name: milkies_list_chapters
tools.description: List the Circle of Life chapters this shop actually carries. Every piece belongs to a stage of life - breastfeeding, motherhood, pets, journeys, wedding, memorial and others - and each chapter groups the products made for it. Call this before browsing, so you name a chapter that exists here.

tools.name: milkies_list_kinds
tools.description: List the kinds of jewellery this shop sells - necklaces, bracelets, rings, earrings, charms, sets, kits, extras - with how many products each holds. Use it together with a chapter to narrow a search.

tools.name: milkies_browse_chapter
tools.description: List the products of one Circle of Life chapter, optionally narrowed to a kind of jewellery (necklace, bracelet, ring, earrings, charm, set). Use it when the customer knows the occasion - "something for my dog", "a wedding keepsake" - rather than a product name.

chapter.description: Chapter key or name from milkies_list_chapters.

kind.description: Optional kind of jewellery to narrow to.

limit.description: How many products to return (1-30, default 12).

tools.name: milkies_find_by_keepsake
tools.description: Start from what the customer has kept and wants preserved - breast milk, a baby's hair, an umbilical cord stump, placenta, a hand or foot print, an ultrasound image, a heartbeat trace, pet fur, pet ashes, a paw print, flowers from a bouquet, wedding fabric, sand or shells from a trip, ashes of a loved one. Returns the chapter that covers it and the products made for it. This is usually the fastest way to help someone who does not know what our pieces are called.

keepsake.description: What the customer kept, in their own words, any language.

limit.description: How many products to return (1-30, default 12).

tools.name: milkies_get_product
tools.description: Full details of one product by id: price, availability, description and categories. Use it for a product the customer is not currently looking at.

product_id.description: Product id.

tools.name: milkies_compare_products
tools.description: Put two or three products side by side: price, availability, what the description says and which categories they belong to. Use it when the customer is deciding between pieces.

product_ids.description: Two or three product ids from search or browse results.

tools.name: milkies_select_option
tools.description: On the current product page, choose one option inside a configurator group - setting colour "Silver", chain length "45 cm", medallion size "18 mm", ring size, kit contents, or a product variant such as metal colour. Match by the group title and the option label shown on the page. The choice goes through the normal shop interface, so price and validation update exactly as they would for the customer.

group.description: Title of the option group, e.g. "Setting's colour".

option.description: Label of the option to select, e.g. "Silver".

tools.name: milkies_set_text_option
tools.description: Fill in a text field of the configurator on the current product page - typically an engraving (a name, a date, coordinates). Respects the character limit shown on the page and reports it if the text is too long.

group.description: Title of the field group, e.g. "Engraving".

text.description: Text to enter.

tools.name: milkies_size_guide
tools.description: Sizing help: the ring sizes, chain lengths and bracelet lengths actually offered on the product the customer is looking at, with whatever measurements the shop states (circumference, diameter, US and UK equivalents). Reads the live product so the answer matches what can be bought.

tools.name: milkies_add_to_cart
tools.description: Add the product on the current page to the customer's cart, with the options currently selected. Refuses if a required configurator group is still unanswered and reports exactly what is missing. This prepares a purchase: confirm the choices with the customer first. Payment always stays with the customer at checkout.

quantity.description: Quantity, default 1.

tools.name: milkies_read_cart
tools.description: Read the customer's current cart: items with the configurator options they chose, quantities, totals, applied discounts and the checkout link.

tools.name: milkies_apply_coupon
tools.description: Apply a discount code the customer already has, and report whether the shop accepted it and what it changed. Never invent a code: use only one the customer gave you or one shown on this shop.

tools.name: milkies_find_topic_page
tools.description: Find this shop's own page about one kind of keepsake or question - preserving a wedding bouquet, jewellery with dog fur, an ultrasound engraving, ring sizing, how to send breast milk in. Returns real pages of this shop with their URLs. Open the page and read it instead of answering from memory: these pages carry our actual instructions, prices and terms.

topic.description: The subject, in the language of the shop or the customer's own words.

tools.name: milkies_how_it_works
tools.description: How ordering a keepsake piece works in this shop: whether a collection kit is posted first, how the customer sends their keepsake in, production time, delivery and returns. Returns this shop's own pages on the subject. Read them before answering - never state delivery times or terms from memory.
