tools.name: set_blueprint_script
tools.description: REPLACE a blueprint's entire logic by compiling FeatherScript source into its node graph (the fastest way to author behavior — one call instead of many add_graph_node/connect calls). See the FeatherScript section of the engine guide for the language. The source must be the COMPLETE script (start from get_blueprint_script when editing). Syntax errors AND unsupported lines reject the change and leave the previous graph intact — never applied as silent comment nodes. Returns the resulting node/edge counts.

source.description:
Complete FeatherScript source, e.g. "blueprint Guard

on update(dt):
    if (AI.distance_to_player() < 5):
        self.jump()"

tools.name: create_new_project
tools.description: Create a brand new blank project with a clean scene, resetting the canvas. Call this when the user asks to start a new project or create a game from scratch.

tools.name: create_object
tools.description: Create a new scene object. Returns its id. Spawn dynamic physics objects slightly above the ground (y > 0). Pass parentId to nest it under another object (e.g. building a composite character).

position.description: [x, y, z]

parentId.description: Nest the new object under this existing object.

terrain.description: Only for kind:"terrain": procedural terrain/chunk/foliage settings.

size.description: Total terrain width/depth in world units.

chunkSize.description: Streamed chunk width/depth in world units.

resolution.description: Segments per chunk edge. Higher = more detail/cost.

streamRadius.description: Render chunk rings around the camera/player.

physicsRadius.description: Physics chunk rings around characters/dynamic bodies.

editSpacing.description: World units between persistent sculpt/paint samples.

textureAssetId.description: Optional image asset id for the layer base texture, or "" to clear.

normalMapAssetId.description: Optional image asset id for the layer normal map, or "" to clear.

slopeLimit.description: Minimum normal Y for placement; higher avoids steep slopes.

grassMesh.description: 'clump' (default) is the stylized painted-card grass with gradient/variation/interaction; the rest are simple legacy shapes.

stylizedGrass.description: Look/motion of the 'clump' grass. Prefer set_grass_look for a whole look; use this to tweak single settings.

gradientBottom.description: Root hex color — dark values plant the grass in the ground.

gradientOffset.description: Where the dark root ends, 0..1 up the blade.

windSpeed.description: How fast gusts scroll across the field.

windNoiseScale.description: Gust size; smaller = longer rolling waves.

bendPivot.description: Height where bending starts; below it the clump stays rooted.

perspectiveCorrection.description: Leans tips toward the camera when looking down so top-down views stay full.

interactionStrength.description: How far characters/vehicles shove grass aside during Play.

pushDownAmount.description: How far actors mash grass down.

trailTint.description: Hex color multiplier on grass currently bent by an actor.

normalLift.description: Leans shading toward straight up; high = soft turf lighting.

fadeStart.description: Distance where grass starts fading out.

fadeEnd.description: Distance where grass is fully gone.

treeSpecId.description: Scatter a parametric tree ASSET from the project tree library (see list_tree_specs) instead of the simple crowns. "" clears it.

treeMesh.description: Built-in tree shape: 'fir' = stylized layered conifer (stacked tiers — the BOTW/stylized-nature look, best default), 'cone' = single cone, 'round' = single sphere crown.

grassSource.description: Grass mesh source: 'builtin' high-quality wind-animated blades (default), 'image' a 2D billboard from grassImageAssetId, or 'model' from grassModelAssetId.

grassModelAssetId.description: Model asset id for 3D grass (sets grassSource to model), or "" to clear.

treeModelAssetId.description: Model asset id for 3D trees (sets treeSource to model), or "" to clear.

grassImageAssetId.description: Image asset id for 2D billboard grass (use with grassSource:"image"), or "" to clear.

treeImageAssetId.description: Image asset id for 2D billboard trees (use with treeSource:"image"), or "" to clear.

windStrength.description: Foliage sway multiplier on the global scene wind (0 = stiff, no sway). Set the wind via set_scene_environment.

interactStrength.description: BOTW-style player interaction: how strongly grass/flowers part & flatten around a passing player/vehicle during Play. 1 = natural (default), 0 = ignores actors, >1 = exaggerated.

flowerDensity.description: Wildflower density 0..1 — small brightly-colored blooms (red/yellow/white/purple/pink/orange) scattered through the grass; they sway and part like the blades. 0 = none. Only appears in grass/mixed mode.

tools.name: create_meadow
tools.description: One-click BOTW-style meadow: creates a streamed terrain carpeted in dense INTERACTIVE grass + wildflowers (they part & flatten around the player/vehicles during Play, then spring back) with scattered swaying trees, then sets a gentle breeze, sky-dissolving atmospheric fog, and the Stylized Nature render look. The fastest way to a lush, living outdoor scene. Returns the terrain id.

position.description: Terrain origin. Default [0,0,0].

size.description: Terrain footprint in world units. Default 400.

grassColor.description: Base grass hex (per-blade variation is added automatically). Default a lush green.

trees.description: Scatter swaying trees too (mixed). Default true; false = pure grass field.

tools.name: create_water_volume
tools.description: Create an Unreal-style water/physics volume: a box trigger that renders a realistic ANIMATED water surface (Gerstner waves, fresnel reflection, depth color, foam, caustics, optional underwater screen tint) and makes characters swim + gives dynamic bodies buoyancy/drag/wave lift. Scale controls the volume size. Pick a `style` (ocean/pool/lake/toxic/lava) for an instant look, or set the individual visual fields. Defaults to the "ocean" look.

buoyancy.description: Upward force multiplier for dynamic bodies in the volume.

drag.description: Linear drag in water; higher slows objects faster.

angularDrag.description: Rotational damping hint for water interaction.

surfaceBounce.description: Extra upward bounce when objects hit the water surface.

style.description: Ready-made look: ocean | pool | lake | toxic | lava | custom. Sets all the visual fields below.

shallowColor.description: Hex tint near the surface / shallow edges.

deepColor.description: Hex tint of deep water (also the underwater fog color).

surfaceOpacity.description: Rendered water-surface opacity (clear pool low, murky high).

caustics.description: Animated caustic shimmer across the surface 0-1.

underwaterFog.description: Tint the screen + murk the view while the camera is submerged.

flowStrength.description: Current strength: 0 = still lake, >0 = flowing river/waterfall (surface scrolls + bodies drift).

flowAngle.description: Current direction in degrees on XZ (0 = +X, 90 = +Z).

rainStrength.description: Rain on the water: 0 = clear, >0 speckles the surface with raindrop ripple rings (use for storms).

position.description: Center of the water volume. Default [0,1,0].

color.description: Underlying box tint hex (the animated surface is driven by style/shallowColor/deepColor). Default #2BA8FF.

opacity.description: Underlying box opacity. Default 0.45 (the surface has its own surfaceOpacity).

tools.name: update_transform
tools.description: Update an object's position, rotation (radians) and/or scale.

position.description: [x, y, z]

tools.name: update_renderer
tools.description: Update an object's inline material/render settings. For imported models, color/metalness/roughness need overrideMaterial:true; textureAssetId applies an image texture. Set hideInPlay:true for editor-visible trigger/debug meshes that should disappear during Play/runtime.

opacity.description: Surface opacity 0–1 (1 = opaque). Below 1 renders translucent — use ~0.5 for water/glass.

hideInPlay.description: Hide this renderer during Play/runtime while keeping it visible in the editor. Trigger volumes default to hidden at runtime unless explicitly false.

textureAssetId.description: An "image"-type asset id for the base-color map, or "" to remove the texture.

overrideMaterial.description: For model objects: when true, color/metalness/roughness override the model's baked materials.

tools.name: set_scene_environment
tools.description: Set the active scene sky/fog/base lighting. Use this for mood, time of day, sunset/night/daylight, panorama skyboxes, fog, and Unreal-style volumetric fog/light shafts (volumetricFog* fields — atmospheric mist, sun glow, god rays). This is scene-level World Settings, not a Blueprint node.

skyTextureAssetId.description: Image asset id for an equirectangular panorama, or "" to clear.

environmentMapAssetId.description: Image asset id of an equirectangular panorama/HDRI used as the image-based-lighting (IBL) source — real reflections + ambient sampled from it, replacing the studio light rig. Independent of skyMode. "" to clear (back to studio).

atmosphericFog.description: Sky-sampled atmospheric fog: exponential aerial perspective whose color auto-follows the sky horizon, so distant hills/mountains dissolve into the sky (BOTW/Genshin stylized-outdoors look). Uses fogFar as the range. Best with a procedural sky; ignored when volumetric fog is on.

volumetricFogEnabled.description: Unreal-style raymarched volumetric fog: height-based mist + sun glow (in-scattering) and god-ray light shafts. Replaces flat linear fog when on. Great for atmospheric/cinematic/foggy/dusty looks.

volumetricFogDensity.description: Volumetric fog thickness (≈0.02 thin haze, 0.1+ thick).

volumetricFogHeight.description: World Y where volumetric density starts thinning out.

volumetricFogFalloff.description: How fast volumetric fog thins with height (0 = uniform).

volumetricScattering.description: Sun scatter anisotropy (−0.95..0.95); higher = stronger forward glow toward the sun.

volumetricSunStrength.description: Strength of the volumetric sun glow / light shafts.

volumetricMaxDistance.description: Far clamp (world units) for the volumetric raymarch.

wind.description: Global wind force vector [x,y,z] (world space). Drives all cloth and pushes dynamic bodies by their windInfluence. [0,0,0] = calm.

gravity.description: World gravity acceleration [x,y,z] in units/s². Earth = [0,-9.81,0] (the default), Moon = [0,-1.62,0], space = [0,0,0]. Every dynamic body scales this by its own gravityScale.

toneMapping.description: Film tonemapping curve for the whole scene — the biggest single lever on overall look. aces = classic punchy filmic (default); agx = modern, preserves bright highlights instead of blowing them to white (great for neon/sunlit/HDR scenes); neutral = accurate/flat PBR; reinhard/cineon = classic curves; linear/none = no filmic shaping.

toneMappingExposure.description: Exposure multiplier before tonemapping. 1 = neutral, >1 brighter, <1 darker.

ambientMode.description: Ambient fill model. hemisphere grades sky color above → ground color below (more natural); flat is a constant term (legacy).

contactShadows.description: Soft grounding shadow blob under objects. On by default; turn off for flying/space/no-floor scenes.

contactShadowY.description: World Y the contact-shadow plane sits at — match the ground height. Default 0.

contactShadowScale.description: Footprint size of the contact-shadow plane in world units. Default 14; raise for big scenes.

contactShadowBlur.description: Contact-shadow softness. Default 2.4; 3–4 gives broad studio-style edges.

contactShadowFar.description: Vertical capture distance for contact casters. Default 6 world units.

contactShadowColor.description: Contact-shadow tint as a hex color. Near-black scene hues integrate more softly than pure black.

dayCycleEnabled.description: When on, Play advances time of day and drives sun/sky from a built-in day/night ramp.

dayCycleDuration.description: Real seconds for a full day loop while Playing. Default 360 (~6 min).

dayCycleTime.description: Normalized time of day 0–1 (0 midnight, 0.25 sunrise, 0.5 noon, 0.75 sunset).

tools.name: apply_lighting_preset
tools.description: Apply a complete one-click scene lighting/look preset. It updates sky, fog, sun, environment intensity, bloom/vignette, quality/shadow/AO budget, and project color grade together.

preset.description: sunny, overcast, night, cyberpunk, indoor, cinematic, or godrays (low hazy sun + strong volumetric light shafts).

tools.name: set_physics
tools.description: Enable/configure object physics. Use fixed solids for walls/floors, dynamic for movable bodies, and fixed triggers for pickups/volumes.

materialPreset.description: Physical surface preset: default, rubber, slime, ice, metal, stone, wood, or mud. Applies friction/bounce/damping.

lockedTranslation.description: AXIS LOCK [x,y,z]: freeze this DYNAMIC body's position on those world axes. [false,false,true] pins a 2.5D side-scroller prop to the play plane.

lockedRotation.description: AXIS LOCK [x,y,z]: freeze this DYNAMIC body's rotation about those world axes. [true,false,true] keeps a crate/barrel/character upright while it can still turn.

windInfluence.description: How strongly global scene wind pushes this DYNAMIC body (0 = ignores wind). Set the wind itself via set_environment.

knockOverThreshold.description: BREAKAWAY PROP (GTA streetlight): on a FIXED body, an impact faster than this speed (u/s) converts it to a dynamic body that tumbles with the hit — lamp posts, signs, fences, bollards. 0/omit = solid.

ccd.description: Continuous Collision Detection: stops a fast DYNAMIC body tunnelling through thin walls/floors at high speed. Small cost — enable for bullets, fast vehicles, fast-falling props. Projectiles always have it.

extraColliders.description: COMPOUND COLLIDER: extra shapes welded to this body (a hammer = box head + capsule handle; an L-shaped counter = two boxes). They move rigidly with the body and share its material/trigger/layer settings. Pass the FULL list (replaces). Verify with F10 during Play.

offset.description: Local offset from the body origin.

tools.name: set_character_controller
tools.description: Add/configure the built-in third-person character controller on an object (WASD move, Shift sprint, Space jump, optional follow camera). The motion it produces auto-drives an animator with speed/verticalSpeed parameters. Pass enabled:false to remove control. All numeric fields optional.

acceleration.description: Ground accel toward target speed (units/s²). Default 60.

deceleration.description: Ground decel to a stop (units/s²). Default 70.

fallMultiplier.description: Gravity ×multiplier while descending. >1 = snappier fall. Default 1.9.

jumpCutMultiplier.description: Upward velocity kept when jump released early, 0..1. Default 0.45.

coyoteTime.description: Grace seconds after leaving a ledge a jump still fires. Default 0.12.

jumpBufferTime.description: Jump pressed up to this many seconds BEFORE landing fires on touchdown. Default 0.15. 0 disables.

landingRecovery.description: 0..1: hard landings briefly sap speed + dip the camera, scaled by impact (drives the "landing" animator source). Default 0.4. 0 disables.

apexHang.description: Gravity ×multiplier near the jump apex — <1 adds a brief controllable hang at the peak. Default 0.65. 1 disables.

sprintTurnFactor.description: Turn-rate ×multiplier at full sprint (full rate at a walk) so fast runs carve wider arcs. Default 0.55. 1 disables.

slideEnabled.description: Sprint-slide: tapping crouch at sprint speed drops into a steerable momentum slide (drives the "sliding" animator source; jump cancels into a slide-hop). Default true.

slideSpeedBoost.description: Slide entry speed = current speed × this. Default 1.2.

turnInPlace.description: Idle third-person body rotates toward the mouse-look camera. Default true.

turnInPlaceThreshold.description: Yaw difference before idle turning starts, radians. Default 0.45.

turnInPlaceSpeed.description: Turn-in-place rotation speed in radians/sec. Defaults to turnSpeed.

mantleEnabled.description: Enable Space-to-vault/mantle against obstacles tagged vaultable/mantleable.

keyMantle.description: Optional dedicated mantle key. Empty/omitted means jump key can mantle.

mantleRange.description: Forward search distance for vault/mantle targets. Default 1.35.

mantleMaxHeight.description: Tallest obstacle top that can be mantled. Default 1.45.

vaultMaxHeight.description: Low obstacle height treated as vault. Default 0.9.

mantleDuration.description: Seconds for the mantle/vault arc. Default 0.38.

modelYawOffset.description: Facing offset in radians; use Math.PI (~3.14159) to flip a model that faces backwards.

strafe.description: Face the camera + move 8-way (pairs with a 2D MoveX/MoveY blend space).

meleeComboCount.description: Melee combo chain length 1–3. >1 enables attack input buffering between hits. Default 1.

meleeComboWindow.description: Seconds after a swing starts during which another Attack press queues the next combo hit. Default 0.35.

meleeHitstop.description: Wall-clock seconds of global slow-mo on a successful melee hit (0 = off). ~0.09 feels snappy.

rollIFrameStart.description: Seconds from roll start when dodge invulnerability begins. Pair with rollIFrameEnd.

rollIFrameEnd.description: Seconds from roll start when dodge invulnerability ends. Both 0 = no i-frames.

lockOnEnabled.description: Lock-on targeting: keyLockOn toggles a lock on the nearest living target (object with health > 0 or enemy tag); the character strafes facing it and the camera frames both. Default true.

lockOnRange.description: Max distance to acquire a lock-on target. Default 16.

lockOnBreakDistance.description: Distance at which an existing lock breaks. Default 22.

keySwapShoulder.description: Tap to mirror the third-person camera to the other shoulder (also flips the aim shoulder shift). Default "KeyV".

cameraOffset.description: [side, up, back]. Negative Z is behind.

tools.name: set_vehicle
tools.description: Add/configure the built-in VEHICLE (car) controller on an object — the driving peer of set_character_controller. WASD drives (W throttle, S brake/reverse, A/D steer, Space handbrake to drift, H horn). TWO physics models via physicsModel: (1) "arcade" (default) = a hand-rolled tire/bicycle model with the tunables below (weightTransfer/tractionControl/downforce/grip etc.) on a dynamic Rapier convex body; raise turnRate for snappier turning, weightTransfer/lower handbrakeGrip for drift, tractionControl/downforce for planted racers; supports crashDamageEnabled (rollovers/wheel-break/crush/debris). (2) "raycast" = a REAL Rapier DynamicRayCastVehicleController sim (BeamNG/sim-racing style): genuine per-wheel ray-cast suspension, weight transfer, tire friction, true rollovers, PLUS a full drivetrain sim — engine torque curve + RPM + a gearbox (auto or manual paddle shifting; engine audio pitch follows RPM through the gears; the runtime mirrors live values into "RPM"/"Gear"/"Speed" project vars for HUD binding), aero drag + downforce, front/rear anti-roll bars, ABS + traction-control assists, and per-wheel SURFACE grip (wheels read the `surface` instance variable — tarmac/curb/dirt/grass/gravel/sand/snow/ice — of whatever they roll over; tag runoff areas to punish corner-cutting). In raycast mode the car needs NO Rapier body of its own (the sim builds a dynamic chassis from the object scale), the 4 wheel CHILD objects go in wheelObjectIds in [FL,FR,RL,RR] order, and the FRONT pair (the actual wheel ids, NOT anchors) go in steeredWheelIds. Tune with engineForce/brakeForce/handbrakeForce/drivetrain/brakeBias, chassisMass/centerOfMassY (lower = harder to roll), wheelFrictionSlip/sideFrictionStiffness + the suspension fields, the gearbox fields (transmission/gearRatios/finalDrive/idleRpm/maxRpm/shiftUpRpm/shiftDownRpm/shiftTime), aeroDrag/downforceSim/antiRollFront/antiRollRear, absEnabled/tcsEnabled/surfaceGripEnabled, and the DRIVING-FEEL trio — engineBrakeForce (off-throttl…

physicsModel.description: "arcade" (default) tire model, or "raycast" for the real Rapier sim vehicle (per-wheel suspension/weight-transfer/rollovers). Use raycast for sim-racing / realistic cars.

deformable.description: (raycast) Soft-body crash damage: the body MESH plastically dents/crumples on hard impacts during Play (direction + force based). Great for BeamNG-style destruction.

turnRate.description: Arcade steering authority multiplier. Default 2.8; higher turns harder.

gripFactor.description: Lateral grip 0..1; higher damps sideways tire slip faster. Default 0.96.

handbrakeGrip.description: Lateral grip 0..1 while handbrake held — lower = looser drift. Default 0.24.

weightTransfer.description: 0..1 grip loss/lean from accel, braking, and cornering load. Higher feels heavier and more analog. Default 0.42.

tractionControl.description: 0..1 throttle cut when tires are slipping. Lower for raw/drifty cars, higher for planted assists. Default 0.35.

downforce.description: Speed-squared extra grip/downward impulse. 0 for loose trucks, higher for race cars. Default 0.18.

crashDamageEnabled.description: Enable impact damage, rollovers, wheel breakage, body crush, and debris on dynamic cars. Default true.

crashDamageThreshold.description: Impact speed below this is a normal bump. Default 12.

crashRolloverThreshold.description: Impact speed where hard crashes briefly tumble/roll the car. Default 22.

crashRolloverStrength.description: Angular impulse multiplier on hard crashes. Higher flips/tumbles more. Default 0.32.

crashDeformation.description: Visual crush amount 0..1 from accumulated damage. Default 0.45.

crashWheelBreakThreshold.description: Accumulated damage at which wheels start hanging crooked. Default 1.6.

crashDebris.description: Throw small dynamic debris chunks on heavy impacts. Default true.

wheelRadius.description: Wheel radius (u) — sets spin rate (and the raycast wheel ray length). Default 0.4.

engineForce.description: (raycast) Max engine force N at full throttle, split across driven wheels. Default 1800.

brakeForce.description: (raycast) Max service-brake force N, split by brakeBias. Default 2200.

handbrakeForce.description: (raycast) Extra rear-wheel brake force N from the handbrake. Default 1400.

drivetrain.description: (raycast) Which wheels get engine force. Default rwd.

brakeBias.description: (raycast) Brake split 0..1: 0 all-rear, 0.5 even, 1 all-front. Default 0.55.

centerOfMassY.description: (raycast) Center-of-mass Y offset; negative = lower = far harder to roll. Default -0.4.

wheelFrictionSlip.description: (raycast) Forward tire grip; higher = less wheelspin. Default 1.4.

transmission.description: (raycast) auto self-shifts on RPM; manual shifts on keyShiftUp/keyShiftDown (E/Q default; gamepad Y/LB). Default auto.

finalDrive.description: (raycast) Final-drive ratio multiplied into every gear. Default 3.6.

maxRpm.description: (raycast) Redline; the limiter cuts power past it. Default 7200.

keyShiftUp.description: (raycast manual) Shift-up key code. Default KeyE.

keyShiftDown.description: (raycast manual) Shift-down key code. Default KeyQ.

aeroDrag.description: (raycast) Quadratic air drag — shapes top speed. Default 0.5.

antiRollFront.description: (raycast) Front anti-roll bar stiffness (flatter cornering; stiffer front = understeer). Default 6000.

antiRollRear.description: (raycast) Rear anti-roll bar stiffness (stiffer rear = oversteer/rotation). Default 4200.

absEnabled.description: (raycast) ABS assist: keeps the fronts steering under hard braking. Default true.

tcsEnabled.description: (raycast) Traction control: tames wheelspin launches + power-oversteer. Turn OFF for a raw drift car. Default true.

surfaceGripEnabled.description: (raycast) Per-wheel surface grip from the `surface` instance variable of whatever a wheel rolls over (tarmac/curb/dirt/grass/gravel/sand/snow/ice). Default true.

engineBrakeForce.description: (raycast) Engine braking N at the driven wheels when coasting off-throttle in gear — scales with gear ratio + RPM, so lifting/downshifting slows the car into corners. 0 = freewheel. Default 600.

loadSensitivity.description: (raycast) 0..1 weight-transfer grip balance: braking loads the fronts (sharper turn-in, lift-off oversteer on a closed throttle), throttle loads the rears (planted exits). Average grip unchanged. 0 = off. Default 0.6.

counterSteerAssist.description: (raycast) 0..1 automatic opposite lock toward the slip angle once the car genuinely slides — keeps drifts/snap-oversteer catchable. 0 for a raw sim feel. Default 0.5.

aiDriver.description: Self-driving car: steers itself around the scene's "Checkpoint <n>" gates with no blueprint. Race rivals AND ambient city traffic both use this — pick the behavior with aiMode.

aiMode.description: AI driving behavior. "race" (default): laps the checkpoints IN ORDER at racing pace with rubber-banding. "wander": ambient TRAFFIC — treats the checkpoints as a road network, picks a random nearby gate at each one, cruises at city pace.

aiSkill.description: AI pace 0..1 (corner speed, commitment, steering aggression). Default 0.7; use ~0.2-0.35 for calm city traffic.

aiRubberBand.description: (race mode) 0..1 keep-the-pack-close assist: slows when ahead of the player, pushes when behind. 0 = honest pace. Default 0.5.

wheels.description: (raycast, PREFERRED) Explicit wheel rig: each wheel object with its declared role — order never matters. Drives drivetrain split, brake bias, handbrake and anti-roll pairing. Replaces the whole rig; wins over the legacy wheelObjectIds/steeredWheelIds convention.

steered.description: Turns with steering input. Defaults true on the front axle.

wheelObjectIds.description: LEGACY (prefer `wheels`): the 4 spinning tire mesh ids in [FL,FR,RL,RR] order. Arcade: child meshes at [0,0,0]. Raycast: direct wheel CHILD objects of the car.

steeredWheelIds.description: LEGACY (prefer `wheels`): front steering ids. Arcade: prefer wheel-anchor empty ids (direct wheel ids also work). Raycast: MUST be the front wheel ids that appear in wheelObjectIds.

tireMarkIds.description: Particle emitter object ids near tire contact patches; runtime emits only while slipping/handbraking.

garageBodyIds.description: (raycast) Ordered MODEL ASSET ids for the in-game garage: a "CarBody" project variable (0,1,2…) picks which body the chassis wears at runtime (chassis re-fits automatically). Replaces the whole list. Also editable in the Inspector Garage section.

brakeDiscIds.description: (raycast) Brake DISC child object ids — their emissive glows orange with accumulated brake heat (sustained hard braking from speed) and cools when released.

loosePartIds.description: (raycast) LOOSE cosmetic child part ids (bumpers/spoiler/skirts): a hard impact tears off the part facing the hit — it becomes a free dynamic prop tumbling away with the car momentum; R-respawn bolts everything back on.

hoodCameraOffset.description: (raycast) Car-local [side, up, forward] hood camera position — the Play camera cycles chase → hood → cockpit on C (hold V to look back).

cockpitCameraOffset.description: (raycast) Car-local [side, up, forward] cockpit (driver's eye) camera position for the C-key view cycle.

keyHorn.description: Key code that sounds the horn. Default KeyH.

cameraOffset.description: [side, up, back]. Negative Z is behind.

engineSoundId.description: Audio asset id LOOPED as the engine (playback rate rises with speed).

skidSoundId.description: Audio asset id LOOPED while the tires slip (volume ∝ drift).

brakeSoundId.description: One-shot brake squeal on hard deceleration.

hornSoundId.description: One-shot horn fired on the horn key.

collisionSoundId.description: One-shot impact when the car hits something while moving.

tools.name: set_playing
tools.description: Start or stop the runtime preview (Play mode).

tools.name: search_engine_tools
tools.description: Search across all 200+ advanced Feather Engine tools by keyword (e.g. "ragdoll", "joint", "cinematic", "audio", "ui", "particle", "timeline", "material", "prefab", "terrain", "vehicle"). Returns matching tool names, descriptions, and input parameters so you can call them using execute_engine_tool.

query.description: Keyword, system, or feature to search for (e.g. "ragdoll", "camera", "water", "cloth", "score", "light"). Pass empty string or "categories" to list all categories.

limit.description: Maximum number of tool definitions to return (default 8).

tools.name: execute_engine_tool
tools.description: Execute any advanced Feather Engine tool from the full 200+ tool catalog by name (e.g. tools discovered via search_engine_tools like add_joint, set_ragdoll, create_cinematic, add_cinematic_shot, create_ui_document, add_ui_element, customize_vehicle, etc.).

toolName.description: The exact name of the engine tool to execute (from search_engine_tools or the engine tool catalog).

parameters.description: JSON dictionary of arguments for the specified tool.

sites.name: ff-draft-dashboard.vercel.app
sites.description: Live drafting dashboard that predicts players taken and better view of available players

tools.name: drafty_set_insight_view
tools.description: Select Auto or a registered Drafty insight in the Decision or Supporting slot, and optionally expand or split that slot.

tools.name: drafty_get_workspace
tools.description: Read the compact current Drafty configuration, rankings view, focused profile, insight deck, editability, and target count.

tools.name: drafty_get_decision_context
tools.description: Read the compact deterministic draft decision context: roster, recent picks, opponent needs, shortlist evidence, and two-turn market pressure.

tools.name: drafty_get_player_evidence
tools.description: Read bounded board, tier, ADP, projection, status, outlook, analyst-note, historical, and nearby-peer evidence for one stable player ID.

tools.name: drafty_search_players
tools.description: Search the current Drafty player universe, ESPN outlook snippets, and licensed analyst notes. Returns stable player IDs for later actions.

tools.name: drafty_configure_workspace
tools.description: Apply a validated partial league, lineup, ranking-source, or ADP-source configuration before the draft starts.

tools.name: drafty_set_rankings_view
tools.description: Select the position, ADP-round, or targets rankings view and optionally set positions, an ADP round, sorting, or the below-ADP filter.

tools.name: drafty_show_player_profile
tools.description: Focus a player by stable ID, optionally pin the focus, select Auto, Draft value, Outlook, or Production, and open or close advanced evidence.

tools.name: drafty_set_player_target
tools.description: Add or update one player's earliest target round, or remove that player's target by passing null. Use a stable player ID from search.

tools.name: drafty_start_rank_editing
tools.description: Start or resume bounded custom positional-rank editing before any player has been drafted or purged.

tools.name: drafty_move_player_rank
tools.description: Move one player to a validated one-based rank within that player's position while custom rank editing is active.

tools.name: drafty_save_rank_edits
tools.description: Save the active custom ranking board to Drafty's canonical browser profile, queue authenticated cloud sync when available, and finish editing.

tools.name: drafty_get_help
tools.description: Read one bounded first-party Drafty setup, live-draft, rankings, sync, mock-review, agent-tool, or troubleshooting guide without changing the workspace.

tools.name: drafty_list_mock_drafts
tools.description: List compact owner-scoped completed fantasy drafts for the active or requested season, including both mocks and real drafts.

tools.name: drafty_review_mock_draft
tools.description: Analyze a completed draft using its captured format and observed pick deadlines. Returns per-player and lineup PAR, latest-safe pick timing, pick-level evidence, replay fidelity, and up to five starter-PAR-first alternate rosters. No hypothetical league-format reinterpretation is performed.

preserve_picks_through.description: Keep the user's recorded selections through this user-pick number, then optimize later picks.

max_changed_picks.description: Limit each returned alternate to this many selections that differ from the recorded roster.

tools.name: drafty_open_mock_review
tools.description: Open one completed fantasy draft in Drafty's visible scorecard dialog by stable draft ID and season.

sites.name: floortris.floortris.workers.dev
sites.description: A room planner people and agents share through native WebMCP. Agents create proposals; humans review and Apply.

tools.name: generateRoom
tools.description: Create a separate furnished room proposal in centimetres. For an L-shape or nook, pass floorPlan as 4–24 ordered rectilinear corner points; width/depth are its bounding box. Points define wall-1, wall-2, etc. in order, and openings on a custom plan name segmentId plus its outward wall direction. When interpreting a drawing, include measurementContext with labelled/provider/confirmed/inferred/estimated provenance and assumptions. The human alone applies it. Check the returned validation, brief and omissions. Use native WebMCP for agent room edits. Leave Apply, Discard, Unlock and room-input confirmation to the human; do not click those controls on their behalf.

tools.name: getRoomState
tools.description: Read accepted room, rules, authoritative ownership, revision and brief. Coordinates are centimetres, grid origin top-left; x east and y south. Never changes the selected view. Use native WebMCP for agent room edits. Leave Apply, Discard, Unlock and room-input confirmation to the human; do not click those controls on their behalf.

tools.name: listFurniture
tools.description: List placed pieces and authoritative owned inventory with measured sizes and locks. Read only. Use native WebMCP for agent room edits. Leave Apply, Discard, Unlock and room-input confirmation to the human; do not click those controls on their behalf.

tools.name: listCatalogue
tools.description: List named furniture, made-to-window treatments and lighting variants plus local wall/floor palettes. Window treatments require attachedOpeningId; wall lights require wallAnchor; table lamps require supportObjectId. Results page via offset/limit; check hasMore. Read only. Use native WebMCP for agent room edits. Leave Apply, Discard, Unlock and room-input confirmation to the human; do not click those controls on their behalf.

tools.name: createProposal
tools.description: Create a layout draft copied from Current, or a setup draft for human confirmation. Never overwrites an active draft. Requires accepted current/rule revisions and an idempotency key. Use native WebMCP for agent room edits. Leave Apply, Discard, Unlock and room-input confirmation to the human; do not click those controls on their behalf.

tools.name: setRoomGeometry
tools.description: Stage room bounding dimensions, name, or a measured rectilinear floorPlan. Custom points define wall-1, wall-2, etc. in order; pass null to return to the rectangular bounding box. Human Confirm room inputs is required. Existing fixed fixtures and openings are revalidated against the new outline. Use native WebMCP for agent room edits. Leave Apply, Discard, Unlock and room-input confirmation to the human; do not click those controls on their behalf.

tools.name: setOpening
tools.description: Stage a complete door or window record in a setup proposal. On custom plans, segmentId names wall-1, wall-2, etc.; offset runs from that segment’s top/left endpoint and wall is its outward direction. Accepted openingLocks are human-only pins and cannot be overridden. Hinged doors use an open 90 degree pose; unsupported mechanisms are explicitly blocked. Use native WebMCP for agent room edits. Leave Apply, Discard, Unlock and room-input confirmation to the human; do not click those controls on their behalf.

tools.name: setConstraints
tools.description: Stage rule assumptions, required kinds and an optional accessibility planning pack. Accessibility results are advisory planning assistance, never certification. Cannot modify accepted rules without human confirmation. Cell size remains 20 cm. Use native WebMCP for agent room edits. Leave Apply, Discard, Unlock and room-input confirmation to the human; do not click those controls on their behalf.

tools.name: placeFurniture
tools.description: Place one catalogue variant, one owned instance, or one checked candidate in a layout proposal. For fixtures, use attachedOpeningId for a curtain/blind, explicit wallAnchor for a wall light, and supportObjectId for a table lamp. Ceiling fixtures use originCell and the actual ceiling outline. Owned sizes and locks remain authoritative. Use native WebMCP for agent room edits. Leave Apply, Discard, Unlock and room-input confirmation to the human; do not click those controls on their behalf.

tools.name: createCustomFurniture
tools.description: Create one agent-authored measured floor object in an active proposal. The legacy rectangle contract is unchanged. A custom sofa may instead add strict declarative sectional geometry: 2–12 connected, edge-sharing seat/corner/chaise modules with exact local centimetre rectangles, height and facing. Parent dimensions must exactly equal the module envelope; primaryFacing alone controls TV/coffee-table relationships while every exposed module front is checked for access. No arbitrary tags, shapes, rule overrides, code, markup, URLs, remote assets or mounts. Placement must introduce no blocking rule failures and requires human Apply. Use native WebMCP for agent room edits. Leave Apply, Discard, Unlock and room-input confirmation to the human; do not click those controls on their behalf.

tools.name: updateFurniture
tools.description: Move, quarter-turn, choose a named variant, change TV/wall-light anchors, attach window treatments, link table-lamp supports or desk chairs, and assign lightingZone. Semantic fixture dimensions/mount heights are normalized from their named window, ceiling or support. Cannot set size, ownership, locks or required status. Candidate references must be current. Use native WebMCP for agent room edits. Leave Apply, Discard, Unlock and room-input confirmation to the human; do not click those controls on their behalf.

tools.name: removeFurniture
tools.description: Remove an unprotected piece from a layout proposal. Fixed, locked and required owned pieces cannot be removed. Optional owned omissions are reported. Use native WebMCP for agent room edits. Leave Apply, Discard, Unlock and room-input confirmation to the human; do not click those controls on their behalf.

tools.name: findPlacements
tools.description: Search checked placements for an object or variant without changing the draft. For relationship fixtures, place once with attachedOpeningId or supportObjectId first. Results are ranked by furniture-function rules before decorative preferences. Bounded results are not proof of infeasibility. Use native WebMCP for agent room edits. Leave Apply, Discard, Unlock and room-input confirmation to the human; do not click those controls on their behalf.

tools.name: proposeLayout
tools.description: Run the bounded local planner in an existing layout proposal. It preserves owned locks and may return partial results. An optional strategy changes only the ranking and default optional pieces; every result still passes the same rule engine. Supply an idempotency key to safely replay a completed request. Use native WebMCP for agent room edits. Leave Apply, Discard, Unlock and room-input confirmation to the human; do not click those controls on their behalf.

tools.name: setAppearance
tools.description: Change a proposal wall, floor, or furniture finish from listCatalogue. Geometry and rule flags stay unchanged; Apply remains human-only. Use native WebMCP for agent room edits. Leave Apply, Discard, Unlock and room-input confirmation to the human; do not click those controls on their behalf.

tools.name: checkLayout
tools.description: Read the shared engine report without changing draft readiness or view. Supports rule-code, object and region filters, and paginated issues or cells. Full-layout status and brief remain explicit even for focused reports. Use native WebMCP for agent room edits. Leave Apply, Discard, Unlock and room-input confirmation to the human; do not click those controls on their behalf.

sites.name: getfitcraft.com
sites.description: A gamified AI fitness app built by exercise scientists to solve the #1 fitness problem: quitting. Streaks, quests, and an AI coach make showing up easier.

tools.name: find_fitcraft_calculator
tools.description: Recommend the best FitCraft calculator for a user goal such as protein, calories, macros, body fat, BMI, strength, daily water intake (hydration), FFMI and lean body mass, or weight loss percentage.

goal.description: The user goal or metric they want to calculate. ffmi covers fat-free mass index and lean body mass; water_intake covers hydration and how much water to drink a day; weight_loss_percentage covers the percent of body weight lost and weight-loss milestones, while calories covers a calorie target for losing weight.

tools.name: generate_workout_plan
tools.description: Generate a complete weekly resistance training plan (split, exercises, sets, reps, rest, effort target, and progression rule) from goal, experience, training days, equipment, session length, and optional extra gear (pull-up bar, rings or low bar, bench, resistance band). An exercise that needs gear the user does not have is swapped for a no-gear alternative, and each exercise lists the extra gear it uses. Deterministic rule engine that mirrors the FitCraft Free AI Workout Plan Generator page. Also returns a shareUrl that opens the same plan on that page.

goal.description: Training goal: muscle (build muscle), weight (lose weight), consistent (build the habit on a minimum effective dose).

experience.description: Training experience: beginner (under 6 months), intermediate (6 months to 2 years), advanced (2 years or more).

days_per_week.description: Resistance training days per week, 2 to 5.

equipment.description: Available equipment: none (no equipment, bodyweight only), dumbbells, or gym (full gym).

session_length.description: Available session time: short (10 to 20 minutes), medium (20 to 30 minutes), long (30 to 45 minutes).

extras.description: Optional extra gear the user also has, for equipment none or dumbbells (ignored for gym, which has all of it): bar (overhead pull-up bar, for chin-ups and chin-up negatives), rings (rings, suspension straps, a low bar, or a sturdy table to row under, for inverted rows), bench (Bulgarian split squats, bench dips, supported rows, pullovers), band (resistance band, for pull-aparts and pulldowns from a door anchor). Omit or leave empty when the user has none of these.

tools.name: calculate_protein_target
tools.description: Calculate an evidence-based daily protein target using FitCraft ranges for healthy adults.

unit.description: Weight unit.

goal.description: Training or nutrition goal.

body_fat_percent.description: Optional body-fat percentage for fat-loss estimates.

tools.name: calculate_tdee
tools.description: Calculate basal metabolic rate and total daily energy expenditure using FitCraft calculator logic.

sex.description: Biological sex used by the Mifflin-St Jeor equation.

body_fat_percent.description: Optional body-fat percentage for Katch-McArdle BMR.

tools.name: calculate_bmr
tools.description: Estimate basal metabolic rate from three published equations at once: Mifflin-St Jeor 1990 (recommended default), the revised Harris-Benedict of Roza and Shizgal 1984, and the Katch-McArdle lean-mass equation published by Cunningham 1991, which is used when a body fat percentage is supplied. Returns the recommended estimate with its plus or minus 10 percent accuracy band, all three equation outputs, and the population caveats. Mirrors the FitCraft BMR Calculator page.

sex.description: Biological sex; selects the sex-specific constants in the two age-based equations.

body_fat_percent.description: Optional body-fat percentage. Supplying it switches the recommendation to the Katch-McArdle lean-mass equation.

tools.name: calculate_macros
tools.description: Calculate daily calorie, protein, fat, and carbohydrate targets in one of five explicit goal modes: aggressive-cut (22.5 percent deficit), moderate-cut (15 percent), maintain, lean-bulk (7.5 percent surplus), or standard-bulk (15 percent). Also returns the projected weekly weight change as a percent of body weight. Deterministic and local-only; mirrors the FitCraft macro calculator page.

goal.description: Goal mode. aggressive-cut = 22.5 percent below maintenance with a 1.8 g/kg protein floor; moderate-cut = 15 percent below; maintain = no change; lean-bulk = 7.5 percent above; standard-bulk = 15 percent above. The legacy values cut, maintenance and bulk map to moderate-cut, maintain and standard-bulk.

calories.description: Optional maintenance calories. If omitted, maintenance is estimated from the sex/age/height/activity fields.

sex.description: Sex, used by the Mifflin-St Jeor equation when maintenance calories are not supplied.

age.description: Age in years. Required when maintenance calories are not supplied; also drives the PROT-AGE 1.6 g/kg protein floor at 65 and older.

height.description: Height. Required when maintenance calories are not supplied.

activity_level.description: Daily activity level used to turn BMR into maintenance calories. Defaults to moderate.

training.description: Resistance-training experience, which sets the protein base before the goal mode shifts it. Defaults to intermediate. The legacy values recreational and serious map to intermediate and advanced.

body_fat_percent.description: Optional body-fat percentage; switches maintenance estimation to Katch-McArdle.

tools.name: calculate_bmi_and_wthr
tools.description: Calculate BMI and optionally waist-to-height ratio using FitCraft health-screening logic.

tools.name: calculate_body_fat
tools.description: Estimate body-fat percentage with the US Navy circumference method (default), or from caliper skinfolds with the Jackson-Pollock 3-site or 7-site equations.

sex.description: Biological sex; selects the sex-specific equation.

method.description: navy (default) uses height, neck, waist and, for women, hip circumferences. jackson_pollock_3 uses age plus chest, abdomen, thigh (men) or triceps, suprailiac, thigh (women) skinfolds in mm. jackson_pollock_7 uses age plus all seven skinfolds in mm.

unit.description: Navy method only: unit for height and all circumferences. Defaults to in.

hip.description: Navy method: hip circumference, required for female estimates.

chest.description: Skinfold in mm: diagonal fold between nipple and front of armpit.

midaxillary.description: Skinfold in mm (7-site): vertical fold on the side of the torso at the level of the bottom of the sternum.

triceps.description: Skinfold in mm: vertical fold on the back of the upper arm, midway between shoulder and elbow.

subscapular.description: Skinfold in mm (7-site): diagonal fold just below the lower tip of the shoulder blade.

abdomen.description: Skinfold in mm: vertical fold 2 cm to the right of the navel.

suprailiac.description: Skinfold in mm: diagonal fold just above the front of the iliac crest.

thigh.description: Skinfold in mm: vertical fold on the front of the thigh, midway between hip and knee.

tools.name: calculate_ffmi
tools.description: Calculate fat-free mass index (FFMI), height-normalized FFMI, lean body mass and fat mass from height, weight and sex, with an optional body fat percentage. With body fat, fat-free mass is weight x (1 - body fat); without it, lean body mass is estimated with the Boer 1984 formula. Returns a sourced category band (Schutz et al. 2002 population medians, ESPEN low cutoffs, college-athlete norms, and the 25.0 value Kouri et al. 1995 observed in steroid-free athletes, presented as an observation rather than a hard ceiling). Mirrors the FitCraft FFMI Calculator page.

sex.description: Sex; selects the Boer formula coefficients and the reference bands.

body_fat_percent.description: Optional body fat percentage. Supplying it switches from the Boer estimate to a direct fat-free mass calculation.

tools.name: calculate_one_rep_max
tools.description: Estimate one-rep max and training loads from lifted weight and reps.

unit.description: Weight unit.

rpe.description: Optional RPE from 6 to 10. Defaults to 10.

tools.name: calculate_heart_rate_zones
tools.description: Estimate maximum heart rate from age by Tanaka 2001, Fox 1971 (220 minus age), Nes 2013, and Gulati 2010, then the five training zones by percent of max and by the Karvonen heart rate reserve method.

formula.description: Max HR formula used for the zones: tanaka (default, recommended), gulati (women), nes (active adults), legacy (Fox 1971, 220 minus age, unvalidated). Every formula is returned in max_heart_rate.byFormula regardless of this choice.

resting_heart_rate.description: Optional resting heart rate in bpm. Unlocks Karvonen heart rate reserve zones.

measured_max_hr.description: Optional measured or watch-learned max HR in bpm. Overrides the age formula and feeds the zones directly.

tools.name: assess_body_recomposition
tools.description: Assess whether body recomposition (losing fat and gaining muscle at the same time) fits a person, and return their maintenance calories, recomposition calorie target, daily protein target, lifting frequency, and an expected timeline.

sex.description: Biological sex; used by the Mifflin-St Jeor equation and the body-fat bands.

activity_level.description: Daily activity level. Defaults to moderate.

training_status.description: Resistance training experience. new covers never trained or returning after a long break. Defaults to under_1_year.

body_fat_percent.description: Optional body-fat percentage. When supplied, protein is set from fat-free mass and the recomposition verdict uses measured body fat instead of a BMI estimate.

tools.name: calculate_calories_burned
tools.description: Estimate calories burned for a workout from activity, intensity, duration and body weight. Covers walking, treadmill, running, a steps-to-calories mode, cycling, swimming, hiking, stair climbing, jump rope, bodyweight and HIIT circuits, strength training, and yoga or Pilates. Returns gross calories, calories above resting, calories per minute and the MET value, with the 2024 Adult Compendium code behind it.

activity.description: Activity performed. walking, treadmill and running take speed_mph and incline_percent. steps takes steps and cadence_steps_per_min. Everything else takes effort.

speed_mph.description: walking, treadmill and running only: pace in miles per hour. Snapped to the nearest Compendium code for the compendium method; used exactly by the ACSM equations.

incline_percent.description: walking, treadmill and running only: percent grade. Defaults to 0.

effort.description: Effort-based activities only (cycling, swimming, hiking, stair_climbing, jump_rope, bodyweight_hiit, strength_training, yoga_pilates). Defaults to moderate.

steps.description: steps activity only: total step count.

cadence_steps_per_min.description: steps activity only: walking cadence in steps per minute. Snapped to the nearest CADENCE-Adults threshold of 80, 100, 110, 120 or 130. Defaults to 100.

duration_minutes.description: Minutes of actual movement. Required for every activity except steps, where it is derived from the step count and cadence.

method.description: Pace-based activities only: compendium (default) uses 2024 Adult Compendium MET codes, acsm uses the ACSM walking and running metabolic equations.

tools.name: calculate_steps_to_distance
tools.description: Convert a step count into miles and kilometers using a step length estimated from standing height and sex, with separate walking and running step lengths, an optional measured step-length override, and an optional calorie estimate.

steps.description: Number of steps to convert.

height_unit.description: Unit for height. Defaults to in.

sex.description: Sets the step-length coefficient: 0.415 x height for male, 0.413 for female.

mode.description: Walking or running. Running steps are much longer. Defaults to walk.

pace.description: Pace. Walking: casual (2.5 mph), average (3.0 mph, default), brisk (3.5 mph), very_brisk (4.0 mph). Running: easy_jog (5.0 mph), steady (6.2 mph, default), fast (7.0 mph).

weight.description: Optional body weight. Supplying it adds a calorie estimate.

weight_unit.description: Unit for weight. Defaults to kg.

step_length.description: Optional measured step length. Overrides the height-based estimate.

step_length_unit.description: Unit for the measured step length. Defaults to in.

tools.name: calculate_water_intake
tools.description: Estimate how much water to drink per day from sex, body weight, daily exercise minutes and climate. The starting range runs from the EFSA 2010 to the IOM 2005 Adequate Intake for total water, adjusted for body weight, temperature, humidity and altitude with the water-turnover equation of Yamada et al. 2022, plus a sweat-based exercise add-on. Returns a drinks target and range, total water including food, water from food, the exercise add-on and cups, in mL, liters and US fluid ounces.

sex.description: Sex; selects the IOM and EFSA Adequate Intakes (women 2.0 to 2.7 L, men 2.5 to 3.7 L of total water a day) and the reference weight.

exercise_minutes.description: Minutes of sweaty exercise on a typical day, 0 to 480. Defaults to 0.

climate.description: Where the person spends most of the day: temperate (about 20 C / 68 F, or air-conditioned indoors, default), warm (about 27 C / 80 F), hot (about 32 C / 90 F), hot_humid (32 C at 80 percent humidity) or altitude (about 2,000 m / 6,500 ft).

tools.name: calculate_weight_loss_percentage
tools.description: Calculate the percent of starting body weight lost, the amount lost, which clinical milestone that reaches (3 to 5% where benefits begin, 5% clinically meaningful, then 10, 15 and 20%), the weight at the next milestone, optional progress toward a goal weight, and an optional average weekly pace as a percent of body weight judged against the 0.5 to 1% per week band. Includes STEP 1 and SURMOUNT-1 trial benchmarks. Mirrors the FitCraft Weight Loss Percentage Calculator page. Never returns dosing advice.

starting_weight.description: Weight at the start, in weight_unit. 70 to 700 lb or 32 to 318 kg.

goal_weight.description: Optional goal weight in weight_unit. Must be below starting_weight. Adds progress toward the goal.

weeks_elapsed.description: Optional weeks since starting_weight was recorded, 1 to 520. Adds the average weekly pace.

tools.name: ippodo_recommend_tea
tools.description: Use when a shopper wants Ippodo tea recommendations based on taste, caffeine, brewing style, experience, gift intent, time of day, or tea category rather than a product name. Ranks the live tea-quiz assortment of matcha, gyokuro, sencha, bancha, and teabags, returning in-stock products with match reasons and the cheapest available variant. Prefer this over search_catalog for preference-based discovery such as a first latte, caffeine-free evening tea, or first-time matcha. After the shopper chooses a tea, call get_product for variants, ippodo_get_brewing_guide for preparation, or ippodo_build_tea_setup for utensils, then Shopify update_cart to add items. Leaves the cart unchanged.

category.description: Tea family to keep in the result set. Use "matcha", "gyokuro", "sencha", "bancha", or "teabags" when the shopper named a category. Use "any" when they did not. Matched against product handle, title, and type — not tags or description boilerplate.

occasion.description: When the shopper plans to drink the tea. Evening and after_meal boost lower-caffeine and roasted options; morning and daytime prefer brighter or standard-caffeine teas.

format.description: How the shopper wants to prepare tea. "matcha" keeps powdered teas, "loose_leaf" keeps leaf teas, "teabags" keeps bagged teas, and "any" does not filter by format.

flavor.description: Dominant flavor the shopper asked for. "umami" and "balanced" favor classic matcha and gyokuro; "roasted" and "smoky" favor hojicha and similar; "any" skips flavor ranking.

caffeine.description: Caffeine preference. "none" returns only caffeine-free teas such as mugicha; "low" boosts hojicha, genmaicha, and mugicha; "standard" keeps typical green-tea caffeine; "any" does not filter.

preparation.description: Brewing or serving style. "latte" boosts Ikuyo and similar culinary matcha; "koicha" boosts thicker usucha/koicha grades; "usucha" favors everyday whisking matcha; "cold_brew" and "iced" favor teas that drink well chilled.

experience.description: Shopper familiarity. "first_time" boosts approachable daily teas such as Sayaka and Ikuyo; "experienced" leaves room for richer grades such as Ummon.

gift.description: Set true when the purchase is a gift. Boosts giftable cans, classic matcha, and the Ippodo gift card.

limit.description: Maximum number of teas to return. Defaults to 3. Use 5 only when the shopper wants a wider shortlist.

ok.description: True when the tool succeeded. False when error is set.

error.description: Human-readable error the agent can show or use to retry. Present when ok is false.

recommendations.description: Ranked in-stock teas, best match first.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID. Pass as catalog.id to get_product.

handle.description: Product handle. Can be passed to update_cart as line_items[].handle.

options.description: Product option names and possible values. These values do not guarantee every combination is purchasable; call get_product for available variants.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an update_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

value.description: Option value, e.g. "160cm" or "Fiberglass".

id.description: Storefront API Product GID.

options.description: All product option names and possible values. Use available_options to identify purchasable combinations.

variants.description: Resolved variant records. When catalog.selected_options contains a complete option combination, this contains the matching variant. Pass an available variant id to update_cart as line_items[].item.id.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to show_variant as catalog.variant_id to display it, or update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add it.

available_options.description: Available option combinations, optionally filtered by catalog.selected_options. Use one full combination to call get_product again when variants[] is empty.

available_options_count.description: Total available option combinations matching catalog.selected_options.

available_options_truncated.description: True when more available option combinations exist than were returned.

available_options_filter.description: The selected_options filter applied to available_options, when provided.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart, update line item quantities, or remove items. Batch EVERY change for one request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart once per item. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use line_items[].id from get_cart to update or remove an existing line, passing the ABSOLUTE target quantity (not a delta; quantity 0 removes the line). Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant.

menuUrl.description: URL of the menu to browse. Empty/omitted returns the root menu. Copy the URL from links in previous responses of this tool. Example: "https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/ecommerce" or "https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/ecommerce/catalog"

reason.description: One sentence describing the original user request and why you are browsing this part of the docs menu.

The mentioned tool will give you instructions how to use the API.', 'NEVER try to guess the API or endpoint, ALWAYS check the docs using "SearchSiteApiDocs" tool. The url param should be taken from the "SearchSiteApiDocs" tool. It usually starts with "https://www.wixapis.com".

url.description: The url of the api to call - ALWAYS get the information from the API docs retrieved using the 'SearchSiteApiDocs' tool or from the conversation context, the URL MUST BE ABSOLUTE URL. Usually it starts with 'https://www.wixapis.com'.

method.description: The HTTP method to use for the API call (e.g. GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)

body.description: A string representing of a valid JSON object to describe the body of the request

tools.name: SearchSiteApiDocs
tools.description: Searches for site "Jour Cards Store" (https://www.jour-cards.com//_api/mcp?withSkills=true) API documentation and returns how to use the site using the API. You are a helpful "Jour Cards Store" site assistant chatbot and you are helping the user perform actions on the site - to query the site's data or to perform an action on the site. Specify the API endpoint, resource, or action you need information about (e.g., 'get site details endpoint', 'create data collection', 'update product API', 'REST authentication'). If you can't find what you need, try to rephrase your search term. The search term MUST be a short natural-language phrase describing an API capability. Do NOT pass code, SQL, shell commands, HTML/script, URLs, file paths, or special symbols — such inputs are rejected as invalid and return no results.

searchTerm.description: A short, natural-language search term describing the API capability you need — a generic term, not too specific (e.g., "how to fetch products" instead of "avocados in stock"). Use plain words only: no code, SQL, shell commands, HTML, URLs, file paths, or special symbols.

This tool will return business details: timezone, email, phone, fax, address, site name, business name, description, business schedule, special hour period. It will also return site features that you can use via other tools (bookings, store, etc.). Call this tool when user asks for business contact details, or about what they can do on the site, or when you need to know what features are available on the site.

tools.name: SearchInSite
tools.description: Searches the site "Jour Cards Store" (https://www.jour-cards.com//_api/mcp?withSkills=true) for information. Use this tool ONLY in the following cases: 1. You just used "GetBusinessDetails" tool and you did not find the information you need. 2. You already tried to find an entity (e.g., product, service, etc.) using an API tool and you did not find the information you need. 4. The request is too vague and you do not know what type of entity it is and what to search for in the docs. Do NOT use this tool for searching for products or other offered services - use the 'SearchSiteApiDocs' tool instead (unless you already tried that tool and you did not find the information you need). This tool DOES NOT support filters - you cannot ask questions like "find me something under $10".

searchTerm.description: The term to search for in the site, e.g. "working hours" or "store locations"

tools.name: ExecuteWixAPI
tools.description: Run JavaScript against the Wix REST API on site "Jour Cards Store" (https://www.jour-cards.com//_api/mcp?withSkills=true), on the visitor's behalf. The code runs in a sandbox and you get back whatever it returns. PREFER THIS TOOL OVER CallWixSiteAPI. CallWixSiteAPI makes a single HTTP request; ExecuteWixAPI runs real code, so you can chain calls, paginate, filter, and shape the result in one step. Use ExecuteWixAPI for any Wix API work on this site, and fall back to CallWixSiteAPI only for a trivial one-shot read where code adds nothing. DO A WHOLE RECIPE IN ONE CALL. When a task needs several requests — e.g. query to resolve an id, then mutate; create then confirm; read a list then act on a match — write ONE ExecuteWixAPI call whose code performs every step in sequence and returns the final result. Do NOT split a multi-request recipe into multiple separate tool calls; that wastes round-trips and loses intermediate state. If a recipe from the docs lists steps 1..N, the code should run steps 1..N. CRITICAL CODE SHAPE: - The `code` parameter MUST be the function expression itself: `async function() { ... }` or `async () => { ... }`. - Do NOT send a script body like `const result = await ...; return result;`. - Do NOT call the function yourself. The tool calls it for you. - Put all `const`, `await`, and `return` statements inside the function body. Do not rely on memory for Wix API endpoints, methods, schemas, or request bodies. Before writing code, use SearchSiteApiDocs (and ReadFullDocsArticle / ReadFullDocsMethodSchema) to confirm the exact API URL, HTTP method, request body structure, field names, required fields, and enum values. The URL usually starts with `https://www.wixapis.com`. Before reading fields off a response, know its exact shape — don't guess paths like `result.id` when it may be `result.results[0].item.id`. Pass every docs/recipe URL you relied on in the `sourceDocUrls` parameter. Authentication: pass the `visitorToken` parameter (from GenerateVisit…

code.description: JavaScript async function expression to execute against the Wix REST API. The value must be the function itself, for example `async function() { ... }` or `async () => { ... }`, not a script body and not an invoked function. Return the final answer from inside the function. Do not write top-level `const`, top-level `await`, or top-level `return` outside the function body. Use `wix.request({ method, url, body })` for Wix API calls. Every call runs against the current visitor site; do not set `scope`, `siteId`, or auth headers. Full Wix API URLs and paths starting with `/` are supported. Wix REST API page size limits vary — use 100 as a safe default unless the method schema (via SearchWixAPISpec) confirms a higher limit is supported. For cursor-based APIs, pass the next cursor as `cursorPaging: { limit: 100, cursor: pagingMetadata.cursors.next }` — not inside `paging`. Check the method schema to confirm whether the API uses `paging` (offset-based) or `cursorPaging` (cursor-based) before paginating.

reason.description: One sentence explaining the original user request and why you are executing code to complete it.

hasMutations.description: Whether this code creates, updates, deletes, publishes, imports, uploads, or otherwise mutates site data on the visitor’s behalf. Set this to true for create/update/delete/bulk create/import/upload calls even if the reason is inspection, verification, or response-shape discovery. Read-only GET/query/list/search calls can use false.

sourceDocUrls.description:
The URLs of the documentation, recipes, API articles, or schema sources where you confirmed the Wix REST endpoints, HTTP methods, request body shapes, auth contexts, and required fields used by this code.
Include every docs/schema source needed for the endpoints and request shapes used in the code.
MAKE SURE THE ENDPOINT URLS AND REQUEST SHAPES ARE REALLY THERE AND YOU ARE NOT GUESSING THEM !!!
Each value must be a valid URL like:
- https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/... (REST API reference docs)
Use ["user-provided"] if the user gave you all endpoint and request details directly.
Use ["other"] ONLY IF YOU HAVE A VERY GOOD REASON TO DO SO

tools.name: GetSitePages
tools.description: Returns the COMPLETE list of pages that exist on this site, as route patterns. Only these pages exist; never guess or invent a URL (e.g. /shop, /store, /checkout, /account) - a path not listed here will show a 404. `title` is the page's name in the site menu; match it against what the visitor asks for. Static routes are exact paths (e.g. /cart). Dynamic routes contain [param] placeholders (e.g. /products/[slug]) or a rest placeholder ([...path]); `identifiers` says what fills each placeholder (e.g. slug: STORES.PRODUCT.SLUG means the product's slug from the Stores products API) and `pageIdentifier` names the Wix page type. A route with `acceptsSubpath` also accepts a concrete path below it, e.g. the product page URL returned by the Stores API. Navigate with NavigateToPage, passing the route pattern and a `params` value for every placeholder. If the page the visitor asks for is not in the list, say so instead of navigating.

tools.name: NavigateToPage
tools.description: Navigates the browser to a page on this site. Pass `path` as one of the site's route patterns and, for every [placeholder] in it, a value in `params` (WebMCP substitutes and URL-encodes them). A concrete path that matches a known route is accepted too, such as a product page URL returned by the Stores API. Never guess a path that is not listed; it will show a 404. Never derive a placeholder value from a name or title; take it from the record the relevant API returns. path.description: A route from the site's route map, e.g. /cart or /products/[slug]. Placeholders are filled from `params`.

params.description: One value per [placeholder] in `path`, keyed by placeholder name, e.g. { "slug": "everyday-mug" }. Omit for static routes.
