target.description: "next" | "prev" | "first" | "last" | number | title fragment

tools.name: open_product
tools.description: Open the merchant product detail page ("Learn more") for the focused card or a given target, in a new tab.

target.description: Optional: same forms as focus_product; defaults to focused card

tools.name: buy_now
tools.description: Jump to the merchant checkout ("Buy now") for the focused card or a given target, in a new tab. Nothing is purchased on this site; the merchant checkout handles payment.

target.description: Optional: same forms as focus_product; defaults to focused card

tools.name: show_brands
tools.description: Open the brands page: every independent brand in the catalog with product counts; pick one to see its products.

tools.name: refine_results
tools.description: Re-run the current search or landing page with a tighter price band: "cheaper" halves the median price as the new maximum, "pricier" uses it as the new minimum.

tools.name: browse_all
tools.description: Open the endless browse page over the whole catalog (optionally filtered by brand).

tools.name: describe_focused
tools.description: Return a one-sentence description (title, brand, price, type) of the focused product card.

tools.name: close_panel
tools.description: Close the product sheet (or any open panel) and return to the list.

tools.name: help
tools.description: Show the input grammar and the list of registered WebMCP tools.

sites.name: webmcp-tools.owid.pages.dev
sites.description: An interactive visualization from Our World in Data.

tools.name: find_chart
tools.description: Search Our World in Data's charts and return candidates as paths. Pass the countries or regions the user asked about so charts that lack them are flagged. Many OWID topics have several charts whose titles differ in ways that matter, and many are different views of the same page — so pass the whole `chart:` path back to open_chart rather than reconstructing a URL. Present the options to the user if more than one fits.

query.description: Topic to search for, e.g. 'infant mortality' or 'CO2 emissions per capita'

entities.description: Optional countries/regions the user cares about, e.g. ['Czechia', 'Slovakia']

tools.name: open_chart
tools.description: Open an Our World in Data chart, optionally pre-configured with specific countries, a time range and a tab. Pass the `chart:` path from find_chart verbatim — it carries the parameters that pick which view of a multi-dimensional chart to show. This navigates the page; once it loads, the chart's own tools become available.

chart.description: The `chart:` path from find_chart, e.g. '/grapher/electricity-mix?metric=share_of_generation&source=solar'. A bare slug like 'infant-mortality' also works for simple charts.

entities.description: Countries/regions to show, using exact OWID names

tab.description: Which view to open on. Use 'line' when the user asks for a line chart or a trend over time — charts with a map default to showing the map.

tools.name: find_article
tools.description: Search Our World in Data's articles and written research. Use this whenever the user asks what OWID has written about a topic, or for an article, explainer or piece of writing — chart search does not return prose, so answering from memory invents titles that do not exist. Returns real titles and paths; open one with open_article.

query.description: Topic to search for, e.g. 'solar energy' or 'battery costs'

tools.name: open_article
tools.description: Open an Our World in Data article. Use an `article:` path from find_article. This navigates the page; call read_page afterwards to read it.

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: Read the text of the Our World in Data page currently open — the article body, including its footnotes and references. ALWAYS call this before answering any question about what this page says, what a number on it is, or where a claim on it comes from. OWID articles are written and sourced by our researchers; the study or figure you recall may not be the one on the page.

tools.name: open_search
tools.description: Open Our World in Data's search results page for a topic, so the user can browse everything we have on it. Use this only when the user wants to browse for themselves — if they asked a question, find_chart or find_article answers it without making them read a results page.

query.description: Search terms, e.g. 'population density'

resultType.description: 'data' for charts and indicators, 'writing' for articles, 'all' (default) for both

tools.name: get_chart_state
tools.description: Read the current state of the chart on this page: its title, which entities (countries/regions) are selected, the time range shown, and which view is active. Call this before making a relative change such as adding an entity to the existing selection.

tools.name: list_chart_entities
tools.description: List the countries and regions available on this chart. Use the optional query to filter, and always use the exact names returned here when selecting entities.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring filter, e.g. 'slov' or 'income'

tools.name: select_entities
tools.description: Set which countries or regions the chart shows, replacing the current selection. Use exact names from list_chart_entities. To add to what is already shown without removing anything, use add_entities instead.

tools.name: add_entities
tools.description: Add countries or regions to the chart's current selection, keeping what is already shown. Use this for requests like 'also show Poland' or 'add the EU average'.

tools.name: set_time_range
tools.description: Set the time range the chart displays, e.g. for 'since 1990' or 'between 2000 and 2020'. Omit either bound to leave it unchanged.

tools.name: set_chart_view
tools.description: Switch which view of the data is shown — a line chart, the world map, the data table, or any other view this chart offers. Use this for 'show it as a line chart' or 'show me the map': many OWID charts open on the map, and switching view does NOT require navigating. Call get_chart_state to see which views are available.

view.description: One of the values listed in get_chart_state's 'Available views', or a plain name like 'line', 'line chart', 'map', 'table', 'slope' or 'bar'

tools.name: get_chart_data
tools.description: Read the actual data values behind the chart on this page, as CSV, for the entities and time range currently shown. ALWAYS call this before stating any number, trend, or comparison — do not answer from memory, because the figures you recall may not match this chart's source, units, or revision.

tools.name: get_chart_metadata
tools.description: Read this chart's sources, units, and Our World in Data's own curated notes about how the data should and should not be interpreted. Call this before explaining what a chart means or why values differ between countries — these caveats are written by the researchers who assembled the data.

tools.name: get_chart_image_url
tools.description: Get a URL for a static PNG or SVG image of the chart as it is currently configured, for embedding in a reply or sharing. This returns a link only — it does NOT navigate the page. Never navigate the tab to an image: doing so unloads the chart and all of these tools stop working.

format.description: Image format, defaults to png

tools.name: download_chart_data
tools.description: Give the user a download link for this chart's data as a CSV file, covering the entities and time range currently shown. Use when the user asks to download, export, or save the data.

scope.description: 'shown' (default) respects the current selection and time range; 'full' downloads every entity and year on the chart

sites.name: yaqeeninstitute.ca
sites.description: Canadian site of Yaqeen Institute, an Islamic research institution publishing work on topics that affect today's society.

tools.name: search_yaqeen_content
tools.description: Search Yaqeen Institute's library of 2,000+ peer-reviewed papers, articles, videos, and infographics covering all areas of Islamic scholarship. Use this tool whenever a user asks: what does Islam say about X, Islamic perspective on X, Muslim view on X, how to deal with X as a Muslim, or asks about topics like faith (iman), prayer (salah), fasting (sawm), Ramadan, Quran, hadith, Prophet Muhammad (seerah), Islamic law (fiqh), mental health, depression, anxiety, spirituality, Islamic history, Islamic civilization, social justice, Islamophobia, marriage, parenting, gender, evolution, or doubt in Islam. Returns up to 8 results with titles, abstracts, authors, and direct URLs to yaqeeninstitute.org.

query.description: The search query, e.g. "mental health in Islam" or "Ramadan preparation"

topic.description: Optional: filter by topic name, e.g. "Faith", "Psychology & Mental Health", "Sharia", "History"

tools.name: get_yaqeen_article
tools.description: Retrieve full metadata and optionally the opening content of a specific Yaqeen Institute article by its URL slug. Use this when you need the complete abstract, author, topics, and canonical URL for a specific piece of content — or when you want to quote or cite a passage from the article. Set include_content to true to receive the first 800 characters of the article body, which you can use to quote or cite specific text in your response.

slug.description: The URL slug of the article, e.g. "depression-the-darkness-before-dawn"

include_content.description: Set to true to include the opening 800 characters of the article body. Useful for quoting or citing specific text. Defaults to false.

tools.name: get_yaqeen_video
tools.description: Retrieve detailed metadata for a Yaqeen Institute video by its URL slug, including the YouTube URL and chapter markers. Use this when a user wants to watch a specific video or needs the YouTube link. Yaqeen produces 2,100+ videos covering lectures, animated explainers, Ramadan series, Q&As, and short-form content.

slug.description: URL slug of the video, e.g. "the-beginning-and-the-end-ep-1"

tools.name: get_yaqeen_scholar
tools.description: Retrieve the profile of a Yaqeen Institute scholar or researcher by their URL slug. Returns biography, title, department, photo URL, and their 20 most recent publications. Use this when a user asks about a specific Islamic scholar, wants to know who wrote an article, or asks 'who is [name]' for any Yaqeen author. Yaqeen's team includes scholars like Dr. Omar Suleiman, Dr. Tesneem Alkiek, Dr. Tahir Wyatt, Sh. Mohammad Elshinawy, and 200+ researchers and contributors.

slug.description: URL slug of the scholar, e.g. "omar-suleiman" or "tesneem-alkiek"

tools.name: browse_yaqeen_series
tools.description: Browse Yaqeen Institute's multi-part content series, or get the full table of contents for a specific series. Returns series titles, descriptions, and episode counts. Pass a slug to get all episodes in order. Use this when a user asks for a series, a collection of videos or articles on a topic, a guided learning path, or 'what can I watch during Ramadan.' Popular series include 'Angels in Your Presence,' '40 Hadiths on Social Justice,' 'The Beginning and the End,' and 'Qur’an 30 for 30.'

slug.description: Optional: slug of a specific series to get its full table of contents, e.g. "angels-in-your-presence"

limit.description: Optional: max number of series to return when browsing (default 20)

tools.name: get_related_content
tools.description: Find content related to a specific Yaqeen article, paper, or video. Returns companion resources including PDFs, study guides, infographics, series, and related articles. Use this after retrieving an article to find additional resources on the same topic, or when a user asks "what else should I read on this?" or "is there an infographic version of this?"

slug.description: URL slug of the article to find related content for

tools.name: browse_yaqeen_curriculum
tools.description: Browse Yaqeen Institute's Islamic education curriculum for high school and middle school students and educators. Returns topics and units with descriptions and downloadable teaching materials. Use this when a user is a teacher, parent, or educator looking for structured Islamic education resources, lesson plans, or classroom materials on topics like faith, ethics, and principles of Islam.

topic_slug.description: Optional: slug of a specific curriculum topic to get its full unit list with download links, e.g. "principles-of-faith"

tools.name: browse_yaqeen_topics
tools.description: Browse Yaqeen Institute's full topic taxonomy. Returns all research areas with descriptions and article counts. Use this when a user asks what topics or areas Yaqeen covers, or to find the correct topic name to pass to search_yaqeen_content. Yaqeen's top-level research areas include: Faith (iman, Allah, Quran, angels, prophets, afterlife), Sharia (Islamic law, acts of worship, fiqh, methodology), Politics & Practical Theology (identity, Islamophobia, social justice, gender, epistemology), History (seerah, Islamic civilization, Islam in the West), Psychology & Mental Health (mental health, trauma, spirituality, doubt, religious identity), Family & Community (parenting, marriage, education, culture), Nature & Science (evolution, health, technology, environment), and Data (research reports, datasets).

parent_only.description: If true (default), returns only top-level parent topics. Set to false to include sub-topics.

tools.name: browse_yaqeen_books
tools.description: Browse Yaqeen Institute's collection of free downloadable Islamic books. Returns titles, descriptions, authors, and PDF download links. Optionally pass a slug for a specific book. Use this when a user asks about Islamic books, wants free reading material, or is looking for Ramadan reading recommendations.

slug.description: Optional: slug of a specific book for its full detail

tools.name: get_yaqeen_annual_report
tools.description: Retrieve Yaqeen Institute's annual impact reports with PDF links. Shows research output, community impact, and financial transparency. Use this when a user asks about Yaqeen's impact, how donations are used, or requests accountability information before donating.

year.description: Optional: filter by fiscal year, e.g. 2024

tools.name: search_audio_content
tools.description: Find Yaqeen Institute audio content a user can listen to while multitasking — including podcast episodes, full podcast series, and audiobooks. Use this tool when a user asks: 'Is there a podcast about X?', 'I want to listen to something about Islam while driving/working out', 'Can I listen to this instead of reading it?', 'What Islamic podcasts does Yaqeen have?', 'Is there an audio version?', 'I want Islamic content about mental health / OCD / grief / faith / Ramadan / Quran that I can listen to'. Pass a query to search for episodes and audiobooks on that specific topic. Returns Yaqeen's three podcast series (DoubleTake, Dogma Disrupted, Quran Convos Tadabbur) along with matching podcast episodes and audiobooks. Note: many individual papers also have audio narrations available directly on their article pages — the response will guide the user on how to find those.

query.description: Topic to search for in podcast episodes and audiobooks, e.g. 'mental health', 'OCD', 'grief', 'Ramadan', 'faith doubts'. Leave empty to browse all available audio content.

tools.name: search_video_transcript
tools.description: Search the transcript of a specific Yaqeen Institute video for a topic or keyword, and return the exact timecoded segments where it is discussed — including YouTube deeplinks that jump directly to that moment. Use this after finding a relevant video slug via search_yaqeen_content. Pass the video's URL slug and a search query (e.g. 'challenges Salahuddin faced', 'proof of God', 'dealing with grief'). Returns up to 8 matching transcript segments, each with a formatted timecode (MM:SS), the spoken text, and a YouTube deeplink with ?t= that takes the user directly to that moment in the video.

slug.description: URL slug of the Yaqeen video, e.g. "the-beginning-and-the-end-ep-1". Obtain this from search_yaqeen_content first.

query.description: The topic or phrase to search for in the transcript, e.g. "Salahuddin Jerusalem" or "proof of God existence"

tools.name: get_islamophobia_resources
tools.description: Retrieve Yaqeen Institute's curated research and media specifically organized to counter Islamophobia and anti-Muslim narratives. Use this tool when a user: (1) has encountered a negative claim about Islam or Muslims — e.g. 'Muslims are violent,' 'Islam oppresses women,' 'Muslims want to impose Sharia law,' 'Islam is incompatible with Western values,' 'Muslims support terrorism,' or 'Islam is an irrational faith'; (2) is asking how to respond to Islamophobia, anti-Muslim prejudice, or discrimination; (3) asks what Islamophobia is or why anti-Muslim bias exists; (4) is a Muslim who feels targeted, misrepresented, or exhausted by having to defend their faith. myth_topic.description: Optional keyword to filter to the most relevant myth section, e.g. "violence", "women", "sharia", "culture", "terrorism", "faith"

tools.name: get_new_muslim_resources

topic.description: Optional: the user's most immediate need. Use 'prayer' for salah questions, 'ramadan' for fasting and Ramadan questions, 'quran' for Quran connection, 'identity' for cultural identity and convert experience, 'general' for broad getting-started guidance.

tools.name: load_youtube_video

tools.name: get_workspace_state

tools.name: get_transcript_outline

segmentId.description: A transcript segment ID returned by a read tool.

tools.name: set_analysis_lens

tools.name: create_claim

tools.name: compare_claims

tools.name: create_learning_path

tools.name: update_conclusion

text.description: The revised evidence-grounded conclusion.

reason.description: What changed and why.

maxPrice.description: Only products at or below this price (INR)

quantity.description: Default 1

tools.description: Remove a product from the cart entirely by product id.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_state_info
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns a runtime snapshot of the THN Web SDK global state on the current hotel webpage, including property and hotel identifiers, booking system, page name, language, device, SDK version, environment, and hostname. Use this when a THN staff member needs to understand the current SDK context — for example to confirm which property is loaded, which environment is active, or which SDK version is running. Do not use this tool for hotel-guest-facing tasks; it exposes internal SDK identifiers that are not meaningful to end users.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_dom_element
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Finds a DOM element on the current hotel webpage using a CSS selector and returns its innerHTML. Use this when a THN staff member needs to inspect the rendered HTML of a specific element — for example to verify that a THN widget or message is present in the DOM and correctly rendered. Returns found: true with the markup in html when the element exists, or found: false when no matching element exists. This tool does not modify the DOM; use thn_internal__show_message or thn_internal__hide_message to control message visibility.

selector.description: A valid CSS selector identifying the element to inspect, e.g. "#thn-note" or ".thn-widget"

tools.name: thn_internal__list_messages
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Lists all messages currently registered across all THN widget types (note, exit, layer, inliner) on the hotel webpage. Returns each message's ID, name, and the widget it belongs to. Use this as a first step when a THN staff member needs to identify which messages are available before calling thn_internal__get_message_state, thn_internal__show_message, or thn_internal__hide_message. This tool does not filter by visibility or state — it lists all registered messages regardless of whether they are currently shown, hidden, or eligible to display.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_message_state
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns the current runtime state of a specific THN message identified by its ID, including flags such as opened, closed, and the widget type it belongs to. Use this when a THN staff member needs to diagnose why a message is or is not displaying — for example to check whether it has already been opened, closed, or is being suppressed. Use thn_internal__list_messages first to discover available message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to inspect, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__show_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Forces a THN message to display on the hotel webpage, bypassing all normal display guards such as frequency caps, triggers, beacons, and eligibility rules. Returns the message's previous and current state after the forced display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to preview or test a specific message regardless of whether it would normally be shown. This tool mutates widget state and stubs internal widget methods for the duration of the call — it is intended for inspection and testing only, not for production user flows. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs, and thn_internal__hide_message to reverse the effect. Throws an error if the message ID is not found.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to force-display, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__hide_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Hides a currently displayed THN message on the hotel webpage, either by gracefully animating it out of the DOM (if it is actively rendered) or by marking it as closed in state to prevent future display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to dismiss a message during inspection or testing — for example after using thn_internal__show_message to force-display it. This tool mutates widget and message state; it is intended for inspection and testing only. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to hide, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__get_bus_history
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Reads the recent history of events emitted on the THN Web SDK internal event bus, returning each event name and its arguments. Use this when a THN staff member needs to trace SDK activity — for example to verify that a specific event was fired, to understand the sequence of events leading to a behaviour, or to debug event-driven logic. Results can be filtered by a regex pattern on the event name and limited in count (default 50, most recent events returned last). Note that event arguments containing DOM elements or functions are collapsed to compact placeholders to avoid serialization issues.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return: the most recent ones, listed oldest to newest. Defaults to 50.

filter.description: Optional regex pattern to filter events by name, e.g. "message" or "^booking"

Use this when the guest asks what this property is, where it is located, or which currency it works in. Any piece of information that is not available is returned as null. Takes no input.

Hides a currently displayed THN message on the hotel webpage, either by gracefully animating it out of the DOM (if it is actively rendered) or by marking it as closed in state to prevent future display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to dismiss a message during inspection or testing — for example after using thn_internal__show_message to force-display it. This tool mutates widget and message state; it is intended for inspection and testing only. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to hide, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__get_bus_history
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Reads the recent history of events emitted on the THN Web SDK internal event bus, returning each event name and its arguments. Use this when a THN staff member needs to trace SDK activity — for example to verify that a specific event was fired, to understand the sequence of events leading to a behaviour, or to debug event-driven logic. Results can be filtered by a regex pattern on the event name and limited in count (default 50, most recent events returned last). Note that event arguments containing DOM elements or functions are collapsed to compact placeholders to avoid serialization issues.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return: the most recent ones, listed oldest to newest. Defaults to 50.

filter.description: Optional regex pattern to filter events by name, e.g. "message" or "^booking"

tools.name: thn_site__get_hotel_info
tools.description: Returns basic information about the hotel whose website the guest is currently browsing: its name, website URL, main currency, location, geographic area and type of establishment (for example Hotels, Resorts or Apartments). Use this when the guest asks what this property is, where it is located, or which currency it works in. Any piece of information that is not available is returned as null. Takes no input.

tools.name: thn_site__get_rates

tools.name: thn_internal__get_dom_element
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Finds a DOM element on the current hotel webpage using a CSS selector and returns its innerHTML. Use this when a THN staff member needs to inspect the rendered HTML of a specific element — for example to verify that a THN widget or message is present in the DOM and correctly rendered. Returns found: true with the markup in html when the element exists, or found: false when no matching element exists. This tool does not modify the DOM; use thn_internal__show_message or thn_internal__hide_message to control message visibility.

selector.description: A valid CSS selector identifying the element to inspect, e.g. "#thn-note" or ".thn-widget"

tools.name: thn_internal__list_messages
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Lists all messages currently registered across all THN widget types (note, exit, layer, inliner) on the hotel webpage. Use this as a first step when a THN staff member needs to identify which messages are available before calling thn_internal__get_message_state, thn_internal__show_message, or thn_internal__hide_message. messageId.description: The ID of the message to inspect, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

Use this when a THN staff member needs to preview or test a specific message regardless of whether it would normally be shown. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs, and thn_internal__hide_message to reverse the effect. Throws an error if the message ID is not found.

sites.name: cedarfield-clinic.vercel.app
sites.description: Cancelled appointments at Cedarfield Clinic, released as they come in. Choose a time, give the patient’s details, and confirm.

tools.name: clinic_list_drops
tools.description: List the appointment slots in this clinic's current drop: id, time, clinician, kind, and state (open, held_by_you, held_by_other, taken_by_rival, taken_by_other, booked_yours, expired_hold). Read-only — it changes nothing. Start here, then clinic_hold_slot to take one slot out of the race for your human. There is deliberately NO booking tool on this page: only your human can book, with one key press on the page. Fictional clinic, simulated rival — nothing real is booked.

tools.name: clinic_find_slots
tools.description: Search the live board by clinician, kind, and/or time window (after/before). Answers with the matching open slots, and when nothing matches, names which constraint eliminated everything so you can relax the right one. Includes seconds until the next release. Read-only.

clinician.description: Clinician name or part of one, e.g. "Boone" or "Dr. Boone".

kind.description: Appointment kind or part of one: "New patient", "Follow-up", "Consult".

after.description: Earliest acceptable start, e.g. "9:00 AM" or "9".

tools.name: clinic_clinicians
tools.description: Who is on today's board: each clinician with their open slot times and appointment kinds. Use it to answer "what doctors are there?" before searching or holding. Read-only.

tools.name: clinic_hold_slot
tools.description: Hold one open slot for your human for a short time (the result carries ttl_seconds and seconds_left). A hold is NOT a booking: it expires on its own, and no tool here can turn it into a booking. On success, relay the result's next_step sentence to your human — they press one key on the page and the slot is theirs. If the slot is already gone the result says so, with the ids that are still open: pick another and call again.

slot_id.description: The id of an open slot, exactly as clinic_list_drops returned it (e.g. "slot-3").

tools.name: clinic_hold_status
tools.description: How long your human has left on the slot you are holding: slot, ttl_seconds, seconds_left, state. Read-only, no input. Call it while your human is deciding, so you can tell them how much time is on the clock. Booking still happens only by their own key press.

tools.name: clinic_release_hold
tools.description: Give back the slot you are holding so someone else can take it. Takes no input — it releases the one hold this session has. Use it when your human says no, or picks a different slot. It cannot book anything; nothing on this page can.

tools.name: clinic_prepare_cancel
tools.description: Arm the page for the person to CANCEL their booked appointment. Cancels nothing itself: the dock shows "press to cancel" and only a key, switch or held gesture from the person performs it. Refused when nothing is booked.

tools.name: clinic_prepare_move
tools.description: Arm the page for the person to MOVE their booking to another slot. Holds the target slot so it cannot be taken while they decide, then the dock shows "press to move". Moves nothing itself — one press from the person performs the swap atomically. Refused without a booking or an open target.

new_slot_id.description: The open slot to move the booking to, from clinic_find_slots or clinic_list_drops.

tools.name: clinic_explain_confirm
tools.description: Explain why this page has no booking or confirmation tool, and what your human has to do instead. Read-only, no input, no side effects. Call it if you are hunting for the tool that completes the booking: there is none, and this tells you exactly what to say to your human.

tools.name: clinic_wait_for_request
tools.description: Waits for the next thing your human says, signs or types TO THE PAGE (they may not be able to type to you). Returns their words as text, or request:null after timeout_seconds (max 60) if they said nothing. Loop: call this, act on the request with the other tools, tell them what happened, call this again. Stop when the request is 'stop'. Their words may be short ('yes', 'the first one').

tools.name: clinic_ask
tools.description: Puts ONE question with 2–3 short choices on the page, in your human’s own panel, and waits for their answer — they answer there (button, keyboard, switch, voice, or a hand shape), not to you. Returns answer:{index,label,via}, or answer:null after timeout_seconds (max 60), or stopped:true. For decisions only, never for consent: no choice can book, cancel or move — the page’s own controls do that. Keep the question under 160 characters and each choice under 40.

question.description: The question, plain words, ≤ 160 characters.

choices.description: 2–3 choices, each ≤ 40 characters. Put the affirmative first.

tools.name: clinic_set_sign
tools.description: Labels the page's camera switch board for your human: the camera reads five hand shapes (thumbs up, thumbs down, fist, one finger, two fingers) and each means a phrase the page hands to you through clinic_wait_for_request. Set a shape's phrase when your human asks — e.g. thumbs up = 'hold me the earliest appointment'. Empty phrase switches that shape off. Never the open palm: that is your human's consent, not a phrase. Kept in their browser.

shape.description: One of: thumbs up, thumbs down, fist, one finger, two fingers.

phrase.description: What that shape should mean, in your human’s words (≤ 120 chars). Empty switches the shape off.

tools.name: clinic_join_waitlist
tools.description: Put your human in line for a slot that is NOT open (held or booked by someone else). If it comes back — a hold lapses, a cancellation — the clinic hands it to the first in line as a fresh three-minute hold, in order: nobody races. Reversible (clinic_leave_waitlist). Answers with the position. Booking still takes one press from your human.

slot_id.description: A slot that is held or booked by someone else, from clinic_list_drops.

tools.name: clinic_leave_waitlist
tools.description: Take your human out of the line for a slot they no longer want. Reversible, immediate. Use it when they change their mind or when they have booked something else.

slot_id.description: A slot that is held or booked by someone else, from clinic_list_drops.

tools.name: clinic_patient_details
tools.description: Who the appointment is for at Cedarfield Clinic: full name, date of birth (day/month/year) and phone. Fill it from what you know about your human; they press Save themselves — a submit you make is refused.

sites.name: chameleon-webmcp.ryan-970.workers.dev
sites.description: Chameleon

tools.name: describe_current_state
tools.description: Returns the board snapshot plus unfinished. Empty tables, kanban, and checklists need add_rows (or bind_data first). A form with fields but no minted tool needs create_form_tool. add_rows does not mint. Also: title, theme, widgets (id, type, title, position, config, fields, rowCount, sample rows), mintedTools, last 10 activity entries, stateVersion, and humanChangesSinceLastDescribe: every human create, rename, drag, edit, delete, undo, or sample-load command since your last call, newest first with undone state. Read it before reorganizing so you build on their changes rather than over them. Pass stateVersion as expectedStateVersion on your next static mutation; STALE_STATE means re-read.

include_sample_rows.description: Set false to omit sample rows for a smaller response.

tools.name: add_widget
tools.description: Creates one widget and returns widgetId plus required next. Repeated logs (blood sugar, applications) must be type=form, then create_form_tool. Pipeline/status board: kanban with a select groupByField, never table. Bind omitted fields for table, kanban, chart, or form. Checklist: skip bind_data, then add_rows with text/done/due/note. Notes: config.markdown only. "No rows yet" / "No items yet" means unfinished. Omit position to auto-place.

type.description: table = flat records; kanban = pipeline/status board (needs a select groupByField); checklist = todos via add_rows; note = markdown prose only, not data; chart and form also exist.

config.description: Type-specific config. Kanban defaults: groupByField "status", cardTitleField "title" — pass those field keys, or override config to match. Notes: config.markdown for prose only.

fields.description: Column schema at creation (same as bind_data). Prefer this when you already know the columns. Fields alone leave "No rows yet" — call add_rows next. For kanban include a select field matching config.groupByField (default key "status") plus a title field (default key "title").

key.description: Stable snake_case identity for this field.

label.description: Display name shown on the widget.

type.description: Value type. select requires options; other types forbid options.

options.description: Required when type is "select"; forbidden otherwise.

position.description: Grid placement on a 12-column grid. One row unit is ~40px. Omit to auto-place below existing widgets.

expectedStateVersion.description: The stateVersion from your latest describe_current_state call. Pass it on static mutations to avoid overwriting a newer human or agent change. If stale, the tool returns STALE_STATE without changing the board.

rationale.description: One sentence explaining why you are making this change. Shown to the human in the activity log.

tools.name: bind_data
tools.description: Defines or replaces fields for a table, kanban, chart, or form; it never inserts rows. Existing rows migrate: kept keys survive, removed keys drop, and invalid select values clear. Form minted tools re-register with the new schema; call create_form_tool if none exists. Otherwise call add_rows next because "No rows yet" is unfinished. The checklist and note widgets reject this tool. Fields use snake_case keys and text|number|date|select|boolean|url types; select needs options.

widgetId.description: A widget id as returned by add_widget or describe_current_state, e.g. "w_x8Kd2q".

key.description: Stable snake_case identity for this field.

label.description: Display name shown on the widget.

type.description: Value type. select requires options; other types forbid options.

options.description: Required when type is "select"; forbidden otherwise.

expectedStateVersion.description: The stateVersion from your latest describe_current_state call. Pass it on static mutations to avoid overwriting a newer human or agent change. If stale, the tool returns STALE_STATE without changing the board.

rationale.description: One sentence explaining why you are making this change. Shown to the human in the activity log.

tools.name: add_rows
tools.description: REQUIRED after a table, kanban, or checklist. Do not put that data in a note. For a form, call create_form_tool first and then the minted tool; add_rows only seeds. "No rows yet" / "No items yet" means you skipped this. Checklist keys: text, done, due, note (skip bind_data). Up to 50 rows. Returns new row ids. Then check unfinished. A form without a minted tool is not done.

widgetId.description: A widget id as returned by add_widget or describe_current_state, e.g. "w_x8Kd2q".

rows.description: Objects keyed by this widget's field keys. Checklist keys: text, done, due, note. This is how you fill table/kanban/checklist data — do not put it in a note.

expectedStateVersion.description: The stateVersion from your latest describe_current_state call. Pass it on static mutations to avoid overwriting a newer human or agent change. If stale, the tool returns STALE_STATE without changing the board.

rationale.description: One sentence explaining why you are making this change. Shown to the human in the activity log.

tools.name: create_form_tool
tools.description: Mints a persistent tool from a form widget. REQUIRED after you add a form for repeated entries such as blood sugar; add_rows does not mint and is not a substitute. Name it verb_noun such as log_blood_sugar. The schema mirrors current fields and remints when they change. Each call appends one validated row. Survives reload until the form is deleted or remove_minted_tool is called. Returns the generated input schema.

widgetId.description: Must be a form widget with at least one bound field.

toolName.description: snake_case verb phrase, e.g. "log_blood_sugar". Must not collide with an existing tool.

description.description: Written for the next agent. Say what one call records, name the fields and units or options, and give one example invocation in prose.

expectedStateVersion.description: The stateVersion from your latest describe_current_state call. Pass it on static mutations to avoid overwriting a newer human or agent change. If stale, the tool returns STALE_STATE without changing the board.

rationale.description: One sentence explaining why you are making this change. Shown to the human in the activity log.

tools.name: update_widget
tools.description: Updates a widget's title, config, and/or position. Only passed keys change. Config is merged per key; pass null to clear one. Use set_layout for coordinated moves, add_rows or update_rows for data, and bind_data for fields. Patch config.markdown for note prose only. Changing form config does not remint its tool because the field signature is unchanged.

widgetId.description: A widget id as returned by add_widget or describe_current_state, e.g. "w_x8Kd2q".

config.description: Partial config patch, validated against the widget's type schema after merge.

position.description: Grid placement on a 12-column grid. One row unit is ~40px. Omit to auto-place below existing widgets.

expectedStateVersion.description: The stateVersion from your latest describe_current_state call. Pass it on static mutations to avoid overwriting a newer human or agent change. If stale, the tool returns STALE_STATE without changing the board.

rationale.description: One sentence explaining why you are making this change. Shown to the human in the activity log.

tools.name: read_widget_data
tools.description: Returns rows of one widget's dataset with pagination. Use when you need more than the 3 sample rows from describe_current_state — for example to compute a summary, find a row id to update, or check what the human typed. Rows include _id, _createdAt, and _updatedAt. Note widgets have no dataset. An empty row list on a table, kanban, or checklist is unfinished work; call add_rows.

widgetId.description: A widget id as returned by add_widget or describe_current_state, e.g. "w_x8Kd2q".

tools.name: get_activity_log
tools.description: Returns the board's command log, newest first — every mutation made by you or by the human dragging, editing, or deleting things by hand. Each entry has an actor ('human'|'agent'), an action name, a human-readable summary, and the rationale the agent gave. Use it to answer "what did the human change?" or to review your own recent edits before reorganizing.

actor.description: Filter to only human edits or only agent edits.

since_seq.description: Only entries with seq greater than this value.

tools.name: remove_widget
tools.description: Deletes a widget and its data. Any minted tool owned by a form is removed from the registry and persistence. Charts that source the widget remain and show an empty state. Use this only when the whole widget should go; use delete_rows to keep its schema. Undo restores the widget, rows, and minted tools.

widgetId.description: A widget id as returned by add_widget or describe_current_state, e.g. "w_x8Kd2q".

expectedStateVersion.description: The stateVersion from your latest describe_current_state call. Pass it on static mutations to avoid overwriting a newer human or agent change. If stale, the tool returns STALE_STATE without changing the board.

rationale.description: One sentence explaining why you are making this change. Shown to the human in the activity log.

tools.name: update_rows
tools.description: Applies partial patches to existing rows by row id (get ids from read_widget_data). Only the keys you pass change. Use this to move kanban cards (patch the group-by field), check off checklist items (patch done), or correct values. To add new data, use add_rows — not a note. Up to 50 patches per call. The call is atomic: if any patch is invalid, none apply.

widgetId.description: A widget id as returned by add_widget or describe_current_state, e.g. "w_x8Kd2q".

set.description: Field key → new value. Pass null to clear a value.

expectedStateVersion.description: The stateVersion from your latest describe_current_state call. Pass it on static mutations to avoid overwriting a newer human or agent change. If stale, the tool returns STALE_STATE without changing the board.

rationale.description: One sentence explaining why you are making this change. Shown to the human in the activity log.

tools.name: delete_rows
tools.description: Deletes rows by id from one widget. Up to 50 per call. Deleted rows can be restored with undo. If you intend to clear an entire widget, pass all row ids from read_widget_data rather than deleting the widget itself.

widgetId.description: A widget id as returned by add_widget or describe_current_state, e.g. "w_x8Kd2q".

expectedStateVersion.description: The stateVersion from your latest describe_current_state call. Pass it on static mutations to avoid overwriting a newer human or agent change. If stale, the tool returns STALE_STATE without changing the board.

rationale.description: One sentence explaining why you are making this change. Shown to the human in the activity log.

tools.name: set_layout
tools.description: Repositions and resizes widgets in one atomic call on the 12-column grid. Pass every widget you want to move; unlisted widgets keep their position but may be pushed down so nothing overlaps. Prefer this over update_widget.position when several widgets move together. Call describe_current_state first so coordinates include any human dragging. Give a rationale shown in the activity log. Typical use: group related widgets, put the most actionable widget top-left, give charts at least w=6. Returns the final layout after collision-push.

widgetId.description: A widget id as returned by add_widget or describe_current_state, e.g. "w_x8Kd2q".

items.description: Widgets to move or resize. Unlisted widgets keep their position but may be pushed down.

expectedStateVersion.description: The stateVersion from your latest describe_current_state call. Pass it on static mutations to avoid overwriting a newer human or agent change. If stale, the tool returns STALE_STATE without changing the board.

rationale.description: One sentence explaining why you are making this change. Shown to the human in the activity log.

tools.name: set_theme
tools.description: Restyles the whole board. Set theme name neutral|butter|chocolate|matcha|stone|gothic|y2k, mode light|dark, density comfortable|compact, or board title. All arguments are optional; only passed values change. Use sparingly. Pick a theme that fits the user's stated goal, such as matcha for a health log or neutral for a job search, and stick with it. Returns the applied theme and title.

theme.description: Astryx theme name. matcha suits a health log; neutral suits a job search.

expectedStateVersion.description: The stateVersion from your latest describe_current_state call. Pass it on static mutations to avoid overwriting a newer human or agent change. If stale, the tool returns STALE_STATE without changing the board.

rationale.description: One sentence explaining why you are making this change. Shown to the human in the activity log.

tools.name: remove_minted_tool
tools.description: Removes a tool created by create_form_tool from the live registry and persistence. Use this when the shortcut is obsolete or needs a better name. The form widget and its rows stay unchanged. Static tools cannot be removed. Returns the removed tool name.

toolName.description: snake_case verb phrase, e.g. "log_blood_sugar". Must not collide with an existing tool.

expectedStateVersion.description: The stateVersion from your latest describe_current_state call. Pass it on static mutations to avoid overwriting a newer human or agent change. If stale, the tool returns STALE_STATE without changing the board.

rationale.description: One sentence explaining why you are making this change. Shown to the human in the activity log.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Reverts the most recent board mutations, human or agent, newest first, up to 10 steps. Returns what was undone. Removed widgets, rows, and minted tools are fully restored and re-registered when applicable. There is no redo; reapply changes with the normal tools if needed.

expectedStateVersion.description: The stateVersion from your latest describe_current_state call. Pass it on static mutations to avoid overwriting a newer human or agent change. If stale, the tool returns STALE_STATE without changing the board.

rationale.description: One sentence explaining why you are making this change. Shown to the human in the activity log.

sites.name: chiptunes.app
sites.description: Create or listen to complete Game Boy songs, composed automatically in your browser and played through an emulation of the original sound chip.

tools.name: what_can_i_do_here
tools.description: What this page offers and how to use it. Call this when the user asks what they can do here, what this site is, or how it works — and consider calling it once when you first encounter this page, to introduce it to the user. Returns a short introduction meant to be relayed. Answers instantly, even before the page has finished loading.

tools.name: chiptunes_now_playing
tools.description: What the station is playing right now: title, tempo, position, whether it is paused, which screen face is on, and whether the editor is open.

tools.name: chiptunes_play_mood
tools.description: Compose a complete song for a mood word and play it. Use chiptunes_now_playing to see the available moods.

tools.name: chiptunes_transport
tools.description: Control playback: next, previous, play, pause or toggle.

tools.name: chiptunes_current_song
tools.description: The document of the song on air. It is the whole arrangement as a string, and it round-trips: hand it to chiptunes_play_song, to a share link, or to the Node API to edit or export it.

tools.name: chiptunes_play_song
tools.description: Put a specific song document on the deck and play it, with its visuals and transport, exactly as a shared link would.

tools.name: chiptunes_editor
tools.description: Open the tracker on the song that is playing, on a given document, or on an empty song; or close it and hand the screen back to the station.

document.description: optional: open this song instead of the one playing

tools.name: chiptunes_variant
tools.description: Make a version of the song on air with a different feeling and play it: sadder for a death screen, intense for a boss, calmer for a menu. The original document is returned too, so you can go back.

mood.description: happier, sadder, darker, brighter, calmer, intense, sparser, dreamier

tools.name: chiptunes_screen
tools.description: Choose the display: crt (Modern), dmg (Game Boy), nes, or mix to let it re-roll on every track.

tools.name: chiptunes_capabilities
tools.description: Every word this understands and every knob it has: scenes, moods, musical genres, game genres, forms, techniques, the hundred-odd game titles it can read as a style, the transform operations, and the things it deliberately cannot do. Read this BEFORE composing rather than guessing at vocabulary.

tools.name: chiptunes_ask
tools.description: Describe music in a sentence and hear it: "a dungeon theme like Castlevania, 40 seconds, no drums", "a gloomy song about exploring a cave", or a change to what is on air like "make it much slower". Returns exactly what it understood, what it ignored, and anything it refused, so you can tell the user the truth rather than guessing whether it worked.

text.description: the request, in plain English

apply_to_current.description: treat it as a change to the song on air rather than a new one

play.description: put the result on the deck (default true)

tools.name: chiptunes_compose
tools.description: Compose from a structured brief rather than a sentence: a scene, a length in seconds, a key and mode, voices to leave out. Anything it could not satisfy comes back in `unmet` instead of being quietly dropped.

scene.description: title, menu, overworld, town, shop, cave, battle, boss, victory, game_over, credits

exclude.description: lanes to leave out: Melody, Harmony, Bass, Drums

tools.name: chiptunes_variations
tools.description: Compose several DIFFERENT songs from one brief and get them all back, unranked, each with its measurements. This is the thing that is cheap here and expensive everywhere else: twenty complete songs take about thirty milliseconds and cost nothing, so you can offer the user a real choice instead of one take. Nothing is scored or pre-selected; the choosing is yours.

tools.name: chiptunes_analyse
tools.description: Measure a song instead of listening to it: how major or minor its pitch material is, whether its phrases climb or fall, how much the melody agrees with the chords under it, how high it sits, how busy it is, whether it ends on the tonic. You cannot hear the output; this is how you check that what you asked for is what you got.

document.description: omit to measure whatever is on air

tools.name: chiptunes_export
tools.description: Take the music away: a share link that carries the whole arrangement in the URL, a Standard MIDI file, or a 32 KB .gb cartridge that boots on real Game Boy hardware. The link needs no server and stores nothing; the files are built in the page and handed straight to the user.

document.description: omit to export whatever is on air

tools.name: thn_internal__get_state_info
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns a runtime snapshot of the THN Web SDK global state on the current hotel webpage, including property and hotel identifiers, booking system, page name, language, device, SDK version, environment, and hostname. Use this when a THN staff member needs to understand the current SDK context — for example to confirm which property is loaded, which environment is active, or which SDK version is running. Do not use this tool for hotel-guest-facing tasks; it exposes internal SDK identifiers that are not meaningful to end users.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_dom_element
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Finds a DOM element on the current hotel webpage using a CSS selector and returns its innerHTML. Use this when a THN staff member needs to inspect the rendered HTML of a specific element — for example to verify that a THN widget or message is present in the DOM and correctly rendered. Returns found: true with the markup in html when the element exists, or found: false when no matching element exists. This tool does not modify the DOM; use thn_internal__show_message or thn_internal__hide_message to control message visibility.

selector.description: A valid CSS selector identifying the element to inspect, e.g. "#thn-note" or ".thn-widget"

tools.name: thn_internal__list_messages
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Lists all messages currently registered across all THN widget types (note, exit, layer, inliner) on the hotel webpage. Returns each message's ID, name, and the widget it belongs to. Use this as a first step when a THN staff member needs to identify which messages are available before calling thn_internal__get_message_state, thn_internal__show_message, or thn_internal__hide_message. This tool does not filter by visibility or state — it lists all registered messages regardless of whether they are currently shown, hidden, or eligible to display.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_message_state
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns the current runtime state of a specific THN message identified by its ID, including flags such as opened, closed, and the widget type it belongs to. Use this when a THN staff member needs to diagnose why a message is or is not displaying — for example to check whether it has already been opened, closed, or is being suppressed. Use thn_internal__list_messages first to discover available message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to inspect, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__show_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Forces a THN message to display on the hotel webpage, bypassing all normal display guards such as frequency caps, triggers, beacons, and eligibility rules. Returns the message's previous and current state after the forced display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to preview or test a specific message regardless of whether it would normally be shown. This tool mutates widget state and stubs internal widget methods for the duration of the call — it is intended for inspection and testing only, not for production user flows. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs, and thn_internal__hide_message to reverse the effect. Throws an error if the message ID is not found.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to force-display, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__hide_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Hides a currently displayed THN message on the hotel webpage, either by gracefully animating it out of the DOM (if it is actively rendered) or by marking it as closed in state to prevent future display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to dismiss a message during inspection or testing — for example after using thn_internal__show_message to force-display it. This tool mutates widget and message state; it is intended for inspection and testing only. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to hide, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__get_bus_history
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Reads the recent history of events emitted on the THN Web SDK internal event bus, returning each event name and its arguments. Use this when a THN staff member needs to trace SDK activity — for example to verify that a specific event was fired, to understand the sequence of events leading to a behaviour, or to debug event-driven logic. Results can be filtered by a regex pattern on the event name and limited in count (default 50, most recent events returned last). Note that event arguments containing DOM elements or functions are collapsed to compact placeholders to avoid serialization issues.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return: the most recent ones, listed oldest to newest. Defaults to 50.

filter.description: Optional regex pattern to filter events by name, e.g. "message" or "^booking"

tools.name: thn_site__get_hotel_info
tools.description: Returns basic information about the hotel whose website the guest is currently browsing: its name, website URL, main currency, location, geographic area and type of establishment (for example Hotels, Resorts or Apartments). Use this when the guest asks what this property is, where it is located, or which currency it works in. Any piece of information that is not available is returned as null. Takes no input.

tools.name: thn_site__check_availability
tools.description: Checks whether the hotel has rooms available for the given check-in and check-out dates and room occupancy (adults, children and children ages per room). Use this when the guest asks if there is availability on specific dates. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to check, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__compare_rates
tools.description: Compares the hotel's direct rate with other booking channels for the given dates and rooms. Use this when the guest asks about price comparisons or other booking channels. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to compare rates for, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__get_direct_booking_benefits
tools.description: Describes the benefits of booking directly on the hotel website. Use this when the guest asks about why book direct. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__get_rates
tools.description: Returns the hotel's rates for the given dates and occupancy. Use this when the guest asks about prices. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to get rates for, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__list_amenities
tools.description: Lists the hotel amenities and services. Use this when the guest asks about pool, parking, extras, etc. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__list_rooms
tools.description: Lists the room types the hotel offers. Use this when the guest asks what rooms exist. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__start_booking
tools.description: Starts a booking for the given dates and rooms, optionally with a currency, a promo code and a language. Use this when the guest wants to book. Returns a URL to the booking engine where the guest can complete the booking, so open that URL to continue. When a booking URL cannot be built it returns the hotel website URL instead, or null if that is not available either.

rooms.description: The rooms to book, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

currencyCode.description: Currency the guest wants to see prices in, as an ISO 4217 code such as USD. When omitted, USD is used

languageCode.description: Language the guest wants the booking engine in, such as en or zh_TW

promoCode.description: Promo code to apply to the booking

promoCodeType.description: Type of the promo code, when known

Use this as a first step when a THN staff member needs to identify which messages are available before calling thn_internal__get_message_state, thn_internal__show_message, or thn_internal__hide_message. This tool does not filter by visibility or state — it lists all registered messages regardless of whether they are currently shown, hidden, or eligible to display.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_message_state
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns the current runtime state of a specific THN message identified by its ID, including flags such as opened, closed, and the widget type it belongs to. Use this when a THN staff member needs to diagnose why a message is or is not displaying — for example to check whether it has already been opened, closed, or is being suppressed. Use thn_internal__list_messages first to discover available message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to inspect, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__show_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Forces a THN message to display on the hotel webpage, bypassing all normal display guards such as frequency caps, triggers, beacons, and eligibility rules. Returns the message's previous and current state after the forced display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to preview or test a specific message regardless of whether it would normally be shown. This tool mutates widget state and stubs internal widget methods for the duration of the call — it is intended for inspection and testing only, not for production user flows. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs, and thn_internal__hide_message to reverse the effect. Throws an error if the message ID is not found.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to force-display, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__hide_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Hides a currently displayed THN message on the hotel webpage, either by gracefully animating it out of the DOM (if it is actively rendered) or by marking it as closed in state to prevent future display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to dismiss a message during inspection or testing — for example after using thn_internal__show_message to force-display it. This tool mutates widget and message state; it is intended for inspection and testing only. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to hide, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__get_bus_history
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Reads the recent history of events emitted on the THN Web SDK internal event bus, returning each event name and its arguments. Use this when a THN staff member needs to trace SDK activity — for example to verify that a specific event was fired, to understand the sequence of events leading to a behaviour, or to debug event-driven logic. Results can be filtered by a regex pattern on the event name and limited in count (default 50, most recent events returned last). Note that event arguments containing DOM elements or functions are collapsed to compact placeholders to avoid serialization issues.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return: the most recent ones, listed oldest to newest. Defaults to 50.

filter.description: Optional regex pattern to filter events by name, e.g. "message" or "^booking"

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

query.description: Search query string.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID. Pass as catalog.id to get_product.

handle.description: Product handle. Can be passed to add_to_cart as line_items[].handle.

options.description: Product option names and possible values. These values do not guarantee every combination is purchasable; call get_product for available variants.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID. Pass as catalog.id to get_product.

handle.description: Product handle. Can be passed to add_to_cart as line_items[].handle.

options.description: Product option names and possible values. These values do not guarantee every combination is purchasable; call get_product for available variants.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

value.description: Option value, e.g. "160cm" or "Fiberglass".

id.description: Storefront API Product GID.

options.description: All product option names and possible values. Use available_options to identify purchasable combinations.

variants.description: Resolved variant records. When catalog.selected_options contains a complete option combination, this contains the matching variant. Pass an available variant id to add_to_cart as line_items[].item.id.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart. Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant. To change a quantity or remove something already in the cart, use update_cart_lines instead — this tool can only add.
