sites.name: mrinkl.github.io
sites.description: You play. Your agent arranges. A four-track loop sequencer that exposes its state as WebMCP tools, so ChatGPT or Chrome can add drums, chords and bass under what you just played — and ask your ears…

tools.name: get_session
tools.description: Read the whole session in one call: key, tempo, swing, style, mode, position, per-track note counts split human/agent, the progression, recent human actions, undo depth and any open audition. Use when you need context before acting or after the human changed something. Returns a summary under 700 characters, not the notes; call get_track for those.

tools.name: get_track
tools.description: Read one track as compact per-bar text: scale degree@step for bass, chords and lead, or 16-character lane patterns for drums, with human and agent note counts. Use when the human asks what they just played or you need exact pitches before harmonising or editing. Pass bars to read a subset; the reply stays under 1500 characters.

track.description: Track to read: drums, bass, chords, lead.

bars.description: Bars to include, 1 to 4 (1 to 4 entries). Omit for all four bars.

items.description: Bar number, 1 to 4.

tools.name: suggest_chords
tools.description: Analyse the human melody on the lead track and rank 4-bar chord progressions that fit it, with detected key candidates and a reason per suggestion; writes nothing. Use when the human asks what chords or harmony go under what they played, before calling add_chords. Needs notes on the lead track; returns error no_melody otherwise.

n.description: How many suggestions to return, 1 to 5. Default 3.

tools.name: audition
tools.description: Play the human 2 or 3 variants (progression, rhythm, bass pattern, drum density, tempo, swing) in the tab and wait for them to keep one; the pick is applied as one undoable action. Use when the human asks to hear or compare options, or you cannot pick between two ideas by theory. Waits up to wait_seconds, then returns awaiting_human, card open.

question.description: Question shown above the options, up to 120 characters, e.g. "Walking or octave bass?".

options.description: 2 or 3 variants to compare. Each has a label, an optional why, and the changes it applies.

items.description: One variant the human can preview and keep.

label.description: Short name on the button, 1 to 40 characters, e.g. "Walking".

why.description: One-line reason to consider it, up to 80 characters.

changes.description: What this variant changes versus the current session. Omitted fields stay as they are.

progression.description: Chord progression, 1 to 4 chords (numerals or names), written to the chords track.

items.description: One chord as a Roman numeral (i, VI, bVII, V7, iiø7) or a chord name (Am, Fmaj7, G7, Bb).

rhythm.description: Chord rhythm: pad, stab, arp, pulse or offbeat.

bass_pattern.description: Bass pattern: root, root_fifth, octave, walking or follow_kick.

drum_density.description: Drum density: sparse, medium or busy.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the human to choose, 5 to 60 seconds. Default 25.

tools.name: undo
tools.description: Revert the most recent agent actions, one or more steps, or everything back to a given undo_id. Use when the human says undo, revert, go back, or dislikes what you just added. Refuses with reason top_is_human_action when the newest change is the human's own work (they undo with Cmd+Z).

undo_id.description: Revert to just before this undo_id (as returned by a writer). Overrides steps.

steps.description: How many agent actions to undo, 1 to 5. Default 1.

tools.name: transport
tools.description: Start or stop loop playback, optionally from a given bar, and report the playhead position and audio state. Use when the human asks to play, start, stop, pause, or hear it from bar 3. Before the first tap in the tab, play returns audio muted_until_user_taps; ask the human to press Play once.

action.description: play starts the loop (or keeps it running); stop halts it.

from_bar.description: Bar to start from when playing, 1 to 4. Default: bar 1.

tools.name: export_midi
tools.description: Build a Standard MIDI File of all four tracks and arm the Download button in the header with it; nothing downloads until the human clicks. Use when the human wants to export, save, or take the loop into a DAW such as Logic, Ableton or GarageBand. Filename is letters, digits, _ or - only, 1 to 40 characters; the .mid extension is added.

filename.description: File name without extension: letters, digits, _ or -, 1 to 40 characters. Default bandmate.

tools.name: set_groove
tools.description: Set tempo, key, mode, swing, style or metronome in one call; notes transpose to a new key unless transpose_content is false. Use when the human wants it faster, slower, in another key, more swing, or another sound (lofi, house, synthwave). Only the fields you pass change. Visible in the grid immediately; the loop keeps playing; returns undo_id.

key.description: Tonic, sharps or flats: C, C#, Db, D, D#, Eb, E, F, F#, Gb, G, G#, Ab, A, A#, Bb, B. Flats are normalised to sharps.

mode.description: Scale mode: major or minor.

swing.description: Swing amount, 0 to 60 (0 straight, 30 is a classic MPC feel, 60 heavy).

style.description: Sound preset: lofi, house or synthwave. Changes drum tables, filter, reverb and defaults.

metronome.description: true turns the metronome click on, false turns it off.

transpose_content.description: When key or mode changes: true (default) transposes existing notes, false leaves them as they are.

tools.name: add_chords
tools.description: Write a 4-bar chord progression to the chords track from Roman numerals or chord names (1 or 2 repeat to fill 4 bars), voiced smoothly. Use when the human wants chords, harmony or a progression under a melody; for single notes use write_notes. Replaces the chords track. Visible in the grid immediately; the loop keeps playing; returns undo_id.

progression.description: One chord per bar, 1 to 4 entries: numerals (i, VI, III, VII, bVII, V7) or names (Am, F, Bb, G7).

items.description: One chord as a Roman numeral (i, VI, bVII, V7, iiø7) or a chord name (Am, Fmaj7, G7, Bb).

rhythm.description: Articulation: pad (held), stab (short hits), arp (arpeggio), pulse (8ths), offbeat. Default per style.

tools.name: add_bass
tools.description: Generate a bass line on the bass track that follows the current chord progression using a named pattern. Use when the human asks for bass, a bassline or low end under the chords. Requires chords first (call add_chords); otherwise returns error needs_chords. Visible in the grid immediately; the loop keeps playing; returns undo_id.

pattern.description: Bass pattern: root, root_fifth, octave, walking, or follow_kick (root on every kick). Default root.

octave.description: Register: 2 (default, D2 to D3) or 1 (an octave lower, sub bass).

tools.name: add_drums
tools.description: Write a whole drum beat (kick, snare or clap, hats, percussion) for all 4 bars from the style tables at a chosen density, with an optional bar-4 fill. Use when the human asks for drums, a beat or a groove; to change one lane use set_drum_steps. Replaces the drum track. Visible in the grid immediately; the loop keeps playing; returns undo_id.

density.description: Busyness: sparse (kick and snare only), medium (default) or busy (16th hats, ghosts).

fill.description: true (default) adds a snare fill in bar 4; false keeps bar 4 plain.

style.description: Pattern table to use: lofi, house or synthwave. Defaults to the session style.

tools.name: write_notes
tools.description: Write single notes (note names or scale degrees at bar/step) to bass, chords or lead, merging with or replacing what is there. Use when the human wants a melody, riff, hook or note edit; for a chord progression use add_chords. Max 64 notes; pitches clamp to the track range. Visible in the grid immediately; the loop keeps playing; returns undo_id.

track.description: Melodic track to write: bass, chords, lead. Drums use set_drum_steps.

notes.description: Notes to write, 1 to 64. Each has bar, step, note and optional octave, length, velocity.

items.description: One note placed at a bar and 16th step.

step.description: 16th step within the bar, 1 to 16 (1 is the downbeat).

note.description: Note name with octave, upper-case (C4, F#3, Bb2), or scale degree 1 to 7 with b or # prefix (b3, #4).

octave.description: Octave for a scale degree, 1 to 7. Default: the track home octave (bass 2, chords 4, lead 4).

length.description: Length in 16th steps, 1 to 16. Default 1.

velocity.description: Loudness 0.1 to 1. Default 0.8; 0.9 and above renders as an accent.

mode.description: merge (default) adds to existing notes; replace clears the track first (asks if human notes go).

tools.name: set_drum_steps
tools.description: Set one drum lane to a 16-step pattern of X (accent), x (hit), o (ghost) and . (rest), for all or given bars. Use when the human wants to tweak one lane (more hats, kick on every beat, ghost snares); for a whole beat use add_drums. The pattern is exactly 16 characters. Visible in the grid immediately; the loop keeps playing; returns undo_id.

lane.description: Drum lane: kick, snare, clap, hat, openhat, perc.

pattern.description: 16 characters, one per 16th: X accent, x hit, o ghost, . rest (- and 0 rest, 1 hit). E.g. x.o.x.o.x.o.x.o.

bars.description: Bars to write, 1 to 4 (1 to 4 entries). Omit to write all four bars.

items.description: Bar number, 1 to 4.

tools.name: set_track
tools.description: Mute, unmute, solo or set the volume of one track without touching its notes; idempotent. Use when the human asks to silence, bring back, isolate, turn up or turn down a track. Only the fields you pass change. Visible in the grid immediately; the loop keeps playing; returns undo_id.

track.description: Track to change: drums, bass, chords, lead.

muted.description: true mutes the track, false unmutes it.

solo.description: true solos the track (others go quiet), false clears solo.

volume_db.description: Track gain in dB, -24 to 6. Defaults: drums -4, bass -8, chords -12, lead -10.

tools.name: clear_track
tools.description: Remove every note or hit from one track, human and agent alike; the human confirms first when the track is not empty. Use when the human explicitly says to wipe, clear, delete or empty a track. Never call it to make room before writing; other writers replace on their own. Visible in the grid immediately; the loop keeps playing; returns undo_id.

track.description: Track to empty: drums, bass, chords, lead.

sites.name: olivegreenhotel.com
sites.description: Discover Heraklion from the comfort of the eco-friendly Olive Green Hotel. Boutique experience meets sustainable practices. Book your stay now!

tools.name: thn_internal__get_state_info
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns a runtime snapshot of the THN Web SDK global state on the current hotel webpage, including property and hotel identifiers, booking system, page name, language, device, SDK version, environment, and hostname. Use this when a THN staff member needs to understand the current SDK context — for example to confirm which property is loaded, which environment is active, or which SDK version is running. Do not use this tool for hotel-guest-facing tasks; it exposes internal SDK identifiers that are not meaningful to end users.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_dom_element
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Finds a DOM element on the current hotel webpage using a CSS selector and returns its innerHTML. Use this when a THN staff member needs to inspect the rendered HTML of a specific element — for example to verify that a THN widget or message is present in the DOM and correctly rendered. Returns found: true with the markup in html when the element exists, or found: false when no matching element exists. This tool does not modify the DOM; use thn_internal__show_message or thn_internal__hide_message to control message visibility.

selector.description: A valid CSS selector identifying the element to inspect, e.g. "#thn-note" or ".thn-widget"

tools.name: thn_internal__list_messages
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Lists all messages currently registered across all THN widget types (note, exit, layer, inliner) on the hotel webpage. Returns each message's ID, name, and the widget it belongs to. Use this as a first step when a THN staff member needs to identify which messages are available before calling thn_internal__get_message_state, thn_internal__show_message, or thn_internal__hide_message. This tool does not filter by visibility or state — it lists all registered messages regardless of whether they are currently shown, hidden, or eligible to display.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_message_state
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns the current runtime state of a specific THN message identified by its ID, including flags such as opened, closed, and the widget type it belongs to. Use this when a THN staff member needs to diagnose why a message is or is not displaying — for example to check whether it has already been opened, closed, or is being suppressed. Use thn_internal__list_messages first to discover available message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to inspect, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__show_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Forces a THN message to display on the hotel webpage, bypassing all normal display guards such as frequency caps, triggers, beacons, and eligibility rules. Returns the message's previous and current state after the forced display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to preview or test a specific message regardless of whether it would normally be shown. This tool mutates widget state and stubs internal widget methods for the duration of the call — it is intended for inspection and testing only, not for production user flows. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs, and thn_internal__hide_message to reverse the effect. Throws an error if the message ID is not found.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to force-display, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__hide_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Hides a currently displayed THN message on the hotel webpage, either by gracefully animating it out of the DOM (if it is actively rendered) or by marking it as closed in state to prevent future display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to dismiss a message during inspection or testing — for example after using thn_internal__show_message to force-display it. This tool mutates widget and message state; it is intended for inspection and testing only. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to hide, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__get_bus_history
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Reads the recent history of events emitted on the THN Web SDK internal event bus, returning each event name and its arguments. Use this when a THN staff member needs to trace SDK activity — for example to verify that a specific event was fired, to understand the sequence of events leading to a behaviour, or to debug event-driven logic. Results can be filtered by a regex pattern on the event name and limited in count (default 50, most recent events returned last). Note that event arguments containing DOM elements or functions are collapsed to compact placeholders to avoid serialization issues.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return: the most recent ones, listed oldest to newest. Defaults to 50.

filter.description: Optional regex pattern to filter events by name, e.g. "message" or "^booking"

tools.name: thn_site__get_hotel_info
tools.description: Returns basic information about the hotel whose website the guest is currently browsing: its name, website URL, main currency, location, geographic area and type of establishment (for example Hotels, Resorts or Apartments). Use this when the guest asks what this property is, where it is located, or which currency it works in. Any piece of information that is not available is returned as null. Takes no input.

tools.name: thn_site__check_availability
tools.description: Checks whether the hotel has rooms available for the given check-in and check-out dates and room occupancy (adults, children and children ages per room). Use this when the guest asks if there is availability on specific dates. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to check, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__compare_rates
tools.description: Compares the hotel's direct rate with other booking channels for the given dates and rooms. Use this when the guest asks about price comparisons or other booking channels. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to compare rates for, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__get_direct_booking_benefits
tools.description: Describes the benefits of booking directly on the hotel website. Use this when the guest asks about why book direct. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__get_rates
tools.description: Returns the hotel's rates for the given dates and occupancy. Use this when the guest asks about prices. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to get rates for, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__list_amenities
tools.description: Lists the hotel amenities and services. Use this when the guest asks about pool, parking, extras, etc. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__list_rooms
tools.description: Lists the room types the hotel offers. Use this when the guest asks what rooms exist. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__start_booking
tools.description: Starts a booking for the given dates and rooms, optionally with a currency, a promo code and a language. Use this when the guest wants to book. Returns a URL to the booking engine where the guest can complete the booking, so open that URL to continue. When a booking URL cannot be built it returns the hotel website URL instead, or null if that is not available either.

rooms.description: The rooms to book, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

currencyCode.description: Currency the guest wants to see prices in, as an ISO 4217 code such as USD. When omitted, USD is used

languageCode.description: Language the guest wants the booking engine in, such as en or zh_TW

promoCode.description: Promo code to apply to the booking

promoCodeType.description: Type of the promo code, when known

sites.name: pathfinder-decision-space.tak8.chatgpt.site
sites.description: An agent-first workspace for exploring engineering programs, comparing colleges, and making a choice you can explain.

tools.name: get_pathfinder_guide
tools.description: Read-only operating guide for low-context agents. Call once before acting, or request a focused topic. It maps user intent to the safest tool sequence, explains the four views and three state layers, provides examples, and gives repair hints. It never changes state.

topic.description: Use all once for orientation, or choose one focused section.

maxExamples.description: Return at most this many copyable intent-to-tool examples.

tools.name: get_decision_state
tools.description: Start every decision journey here after reading get_pathfinder_guide. Return the compact saved decision, active temporary scenario/effective program, candidate IDs and statuses, and current workspace. Use candidate/evidence tools for facts.

tools.name: get_candidate_data
tools.description: After candidate IDs are known, read sourced facts and transparent Pathfinder-derived signals for specific colleges. Request only needed dimensions; the response then includes only their supporting facts. Cost includes published family-income net-price bands and sticker-price pieces; these are comparisons, not a personal aid estimate. This never mutates or asserts an objective ranking.

candidateIds.description: Use 3–5 serious schools when possible; six is the practical comparison maximum.

tools.name: search_candidates
tools.description: Discover candidate IDs in the 75-school sourced catalog by name, city, state, or published average net price. Returns up to 15 focused results; then use candidate data/evidence or compose_workspace.

tools.name: get_candidate_evidence
tools.description: After a candidate ID is known, return field-level sources, dates, caveats, and derivation methods for factual claims. Optional dimensions must be valid.

tools.name: explain_candidate_position
tools.description: Explain why one candidate leads or trails specific reference candidates on visible dimensions and current preference importance. Returns transparent per-dimension comparisons, not admission odds or an objective ranking. Use compose_workspace afterward to show the comparison.

tools.name: begin_agent_activity
tools.description: Immediately show a friendly working state before a multi-step comparison, research, scenario, or saved-choice update. This changes presentation only, never the saved decision or a scenario. Follow it with get_decision_state and the needed fact tools, then compose_workspace; a successful composition clears this status.

tools.name: search_programs
tools.description: Search exact sourced academic-program records from the program catalog. If CIP is omitted, all catalog programs are eligible. Completions describe program scale, not quality or admission likelihood.

tools.name: get_program_evidence
tools.description: After search_programs, pass its programId to return exact CIP-6 completion evidence, broader CIP-4 school outcomes, and national BLS context for related occupations.

tools.name: update_decision
tools.description: Durably and atomically change canonical preferences, circumstances, or program only. It never changes candidate status or workspace layout. Call get_decision_state first; use create_scenario for temporary requests. Finish an active scenario before calling.

tools.name: set_candidate_status
tools.description: Durably change one candidate lifecycle status only: active, pinned, finalist, or excluded. It never changes preferences or workspace layout. Finish an active scenario first; exclusion requires a reason.

tools.name: create_scenario
tools.description: Create one temporary, non-destructive branch for changed preferences, circumstances, or program. The canonical decision is untouched. If a scenario is active, adopt or discard it first.

tools.name: discard_scenario
tools.description: Terminal scenario action. Close the active scenario and restore the canonical decision without adopting any temporary value. Optionally guard with expectedScenarioId.

tools.name: adopt_scenario_changes
tools.description: Terminal scenario action. Explicitly select preference dimensions, circumstances, and/or program to make durable, then close the scenario. Unselected temporary changes are discarded.

tools.name: compose_workspace
tools.description: Change presentation only; never mutate the canonical decision or scenario values. Use frontier for attention, compare for differences/why, place for geography and climate, and scenario only when a scenario is active. In Place mode, set climateLens to match a cold or heat question and include every school the user wants located in mapCandidateIds. In Compare cost views, set affordabilityBand to open the published family-income band relevant to the question. Include 2–3 concise annotations with type question after every composition; they appear as polished Explore next suggestions. Other annotation types become one consolidated takeaway. Candidate IDs come from get_decision_state or search_candidates; version guards are optional. This clears any working state started with begin_agent_activity.

primaryCandidateIds.description: Use 3–5 serious schools when possible; six is the practical comparison maximum.

secondaryCandidateIds.description: Keep alternatives compressed; primary plus secondary may not exceed eight schools.

annotations.description: Use non-question annotations for one main takeaway. Include 2–3 type=question annotations as concise, actionable next questions for the student or parent.

candidateIds.description: Use 3–5 serious schools when possible; six is the practical comparison maximum.

climateLens.description: For Place mode, choose the weather detail that answers the user's question. Use nightsBelow40F or nightsBelow32F for cold concerns; use daysAbove90F or daysAbove100F for heat concerns.

affordabilityBand.description: Published family-income range to open in the cost card. This is a presentation focus, not a personal aid estimate.

mapCandidateIds.description: Use 3–5 serious schools when possible; six is the practical comparison maximum.

candidateIds.description: Use 3–5 serious schools when possible; six is the practical comparison maximum.

sites.name: pineapplesour.github.io
sites.description: Drop a bank or card statement into the tab. Nothing uploads. A WebMCP agent analyses it in place, and you watch every tool call it makes.

tools.name: get_overview
tools.description: Start here. Returns what is loaded (files, row count, date range, accounts, currencies), the money totals, how much of the data is still uncategorised, any budgets, what the person is currently looking at on screen, and the page's egress meter showing how many bytes have left the browser.

tools.name: query_transactions
tools.description: Return individual transactions matching a filter, newest first by default, together with the totals for the whole matching set. Use this when you need to look at specific rows. The row list is capped (default 50, maximum 500) but the totals always cover every match, so prefer summarize_spending when you only need a number.

tools.name: summarize_spending
tools.description: Group the transactions and total each group - by category, merchant, month, account or day. This is the cheap way to answer almost any 'how much' question; it reads every matching row but returns only the groups.

tools.description: Return a month-by-month series, optionally for one category or merchant, so you can talk about whether something is going up or down rather than just its total.

tools.name: find_recurring
tools.description: Detect charges that repeat on a schedule - subscriptions, rent, memberships - by clustering merchants and testing the gaps between charges for weekly, monthly, quarterly or yearly regularity. Reports the typical amount, the annualised cost, and any price change between the early and recent charges, which is how a quiet price rise gets caught.

minOccurrences.description: How many charges before something counts as recurring. Defaults to 3.

tools.name: find_anomalies
tools.description: Flag transactions worth a second look: charges far outside the normal range for that same merchant (scored against the median and MAD, so one big charge cannot hide another), the same amount billed twice within two days, and unusually large one-off payments at merchants with no history.

tools.name: propose_categories
tools.description: Propose rules that assign a category to every transaction matching a merchant. This does NOT change anything on its own: the rules are staged, the page shows the person exactly how many rows each rule would touch, and they approve or discard. Two extra tools - apply_staged_changes and discard_staged_changes - appear while something is staged. sites.name: quipra.github.io
sites.description: One desk shared by a person and an agent. Paper, pens, ruler, compass, stencils. Nothing else.

tools.name: guide
tools.description: Read one desk skill by topic: core, geometry, lettering, vectors, illustration, animation, recipes, collaboration, layers. core (the desk and its loop) comes with the first look; read geometry before a construction, lettering before labels, vectors for organic shapes, illustration for pictures, animation for motion, recipes to make your own tools, collaboration when the person has drawn, layers to organize. tools.name: edit
tools.description: Change existing marks without redrawing, or animate them. Select by ids, group and/or region, then any of: pen (restyle), dx/dy (move), scale (about a point, default the mark's center), rotate (degrees clockwise), label, regroup, duplicate (edit copies, keep originals). With at (seconds) the same fields become a KEYFRAME instead: the mark tweens there from its previous key with ease or bezier; opacity and reveal (write-on) are keyable too. wiggle adds smooth random drift, boil re-noises the edge like hand-drawn animation, preset applies a built-in motion (rise, drop, pop, fade, wipe, typewriter, breathe, spin, shake, drift, sketchy, fadeOut, sink) or one you made, stagger cascades a group. align (left, center, right, top, middle, bottom) lines the selection up by its bounds, toPaper: true against the sheet instead; distribute (horizontal, vertical) spaces it evenly between the outermost two. hidden and order manage layers. Playback starts automatically.

tools.name: make
tools.description: Make your own tool for this session. kind motion: a named animation preset (keys with relative times, wiggle, boil) applied to any marks with edit preset. kind brush: a named pen you design (kind, color, width, opacity, dash, texture, taper, fill, effects shadow|glow|blur, and a full engine block: tip, spacing, sizeBase, sizeGain, flowBase, flowGain, scatter, grain, multiply, oriented, sizeJitter, flowJitter, angleJitter, pressureCurve, wet, dual) and then use anywhere as pen: { brush: name }. kind recipe: a named list of construct steps with parameters, written as JSON text in steps; any number in a step may be an expression over $params such as "($A.x+$B.x)/2" or "hypot($B.x-$A.x,$B.y-$A.y)/2" (functions: sqrt abs min max hypot sin cos tan atan2 round). sites.name: reddynitish.github.io
sites.description: LogicLab — a digital logic workspace where you and your AI agent build, test, debug, and understand circuits together, live, through WebMCP.

tools.name: get_circuit_state
tools.description: Read the full current circuit: every component (gates, inputs, outputs) with its id, type, position, label and value, every wire, and the live simulated signal on every component and wire. Call this first, before making any change, to see what's already on the canvas.

tools.name: list_examples
tools.description: List the built-in example circuits (id, name, description) available to load_example.

tools.name: load_example
tools.description: Replace the current circuit on the canvas with one of the built-in examples. Use list_examples to see valid ids.

tools.name: add_component
tools.description: Place a new component on the canvas: an INPUT (a toggleable source bit), an OUTPUT (a display terminal), or a gate (AND, OR, NOT, XOR, NAND, NOR). Returns the new component's id, which you'll use with connect_components.

type.description: Component type to place.

label.description: Optional human-readable label, e.g. 'A' or 'Sum'.

tools.name: update_component
tools.description: Update an existing component: reposition it (x/y), rename it (label), or — for INPUT components only — set its value (inputValue: 0 or 1).

tools.name: remove_component
tools.description: Delete a component from the canvas. Any wires attached to it are removed too.

tools.name: connect_components
tools.description: Connect the output of one component to an input port of another. Gates with two inputs (AND/OR/XOR/NAND/NOR) use toPort 0 or 1; NOT and OUTPUT have a single input port, toPort 0. An input port can only carry one wire — disconnect_components first if it's already driven.

from.description: Id of the component driving the wire (its output).

to.description: Id of the component receiving the wire.

tools.name: disconnect_components
tools.description: Delete a single wire by id (from get_circuit_state's wires list).

tools.name: set_input
tools.description: Set an INPUT component to 0 (LOW) or 1 (HIGH).

tools.name: simulate
tools.description: Recompute every signal in the circuit from the current INPUT values and return the resulting value on each component and wire, plus any wiring issues found (feedback loops, floating inputs, doubled drivers). Call after making changes to see the effect.

tools.name: generate_truth_table
tools.description: Exercise every combination of the circuit's INPUT components (2^n rows) and report the resulting OUTPUT values for each — the deterministic way to see everything a circuit does at once, instead of toggling inputs one at a time.

tools.name: validate_circuit
tools.description: Check whether the circuit correctly implements a named function (AND, OR, NOT, XOR, NAND, NOR, HALF_ADDER, FULL_ADDER, MUX_2TO1, DECODER_2TO4) across every input combination. The comparison is exact, code-computed truth-table matching — not a guess — and returns the specific input rows where the circuit's behavior diverges from the expected function, so you can pinpoint what's wrong.

tools.name: highlight_component
tools.description: Draw the student's eye to specific components and/or wires with a reason string (e.g. 'this AND gate should be an OR gate'). Used while diagnosing a broken circuit. Call clear_highlights when done.

tools.name: clear_highlights
tools.description: Remove every debugging highlight currently shown on the canvas.

tools.name: reset_circuit
tools.description: Remove every component and wire, returning to a blank canvas.

sites.name: relaylab-three.vercel.app
sites.description: RelayLab lets a human and an external AI agent co-edit one B-roll timeline through a structured WebMCP contract.

tools.name: get_timeline
tools.description: Read the live RelayLab timeline, including ghost and committed B-roll overlays, distinct source-video and main-timeline ranges, human locks, reasons, project approval status, and immutable audio policy. Call this after the human edits or locks an overlay; it always reads current shared state.

tools.name: get_edit_plan
tools.description: Read the agent's current structured editorial plan: every decision (uploaded-B-roll placement, generated-B-roll suggestion) with its timeline range, transcript context, reason, status (proposed/accepted/rejected/modified-by-human/locked), and ranked alternatives where known. This is the coherent 'what is the plan' answer, derived live from the same overlays and suggestions get_timeline reports — never a separate or stale copy. Includes timelineRevisionUsed, the timeline revision this snapshot reflects.

tools.name: get_project_summary
tools.description: Read a compact project summary: title, duration, approval status, transcript/B-roll counts, overlay counts by state, the current pacing preference, and the immutable audio policy. Use this before deeper reads to decide what to look at next.

tools.name: get_transcript
tools.description: Read a bounded slice of timestamped transcript by optional startSeconds/endSeconds and/or segment count. Never returns the full transcript unbounded: defaults to 20 segments and caps at 100.

startSeconds.description: Only include segments ending after this time in seconds.

endSeconds.description: Only include segments starting before this time in seconds.

maxSegments.description: Maximum number of segments to return; defaults to 20, capped at 100.

tools.name: find_overlay_opportunities
tools.description: Read-only heuristic scan for B-roll candidate slots. Finds pacing gaps plus transcript cues for products/apps, lists, concrete objects/places, and examples. Optional startSeconds/endSeconds bound the scan; maxTalkingHeadSeconds is safely clamped to 5-30. Returns overlapping transcript text and a stable reason enum. Never creates or modifies an overlay.

maxTalkingHeadSeconds.description: Pacing threshold in seconds; safely clamped to the 5-30 range.

startSeconds.description: Optional inclusive start of the timeline range to inspect.

endSeconds.description: Optional exclusive end of the timeline range to inspect.

tools.name: search_broll
tools.description: Search available indexed B-roll source moments by description/tag relevance, optional minDuration/maxDuration, duration fit, and recent-reuse penalty. Returns source ranges and scores. Excludes unindexed or invalid source ranges and never creates a proposal.

query.description: Free-text search terms, matched against moment descriptions and tags.

minDuration.description: Exclude source moments shorter than this many seconds.

maxDuration.description: Exclude source moments longer than this many seconds.

targetDuration.description: Optional precise desired duration for compatibility and fit scoring.

matchThreshold.description: Optional deterministic strong-match threshold; defaults to the configured 0.65 value.

limit.description: Maximum number of ranked results to return; defaults to 10.

tools.name: propose_overlay
tools.description: Create a non-destructive GHOST B-roll proposal from an indexed moment while the project is planning. This never commits, approves, locks, or changes the base track, and B-roll remains muted. Arguments are validated and clamped to safe source/project bounds.

momentId.description: Indexed B-roll moment identifier from the project library.

timelineStart.description: Desired start in seconds on the locked base-video timeline.

duration.description: Desired duration in seconds; clamped to source and project bounds.

reason.description: Concise editorial reason for this visual support.

tools.name: update_overlay_proposal
tools.description: Update an existing unlocked GHOST proposal while planning. May change timeline start, duration, validated source in/out, or reason. Rejects human-locked overlays with HUMAN_LOCKED and cannot change approval, base media, locks, or audio.

tools.name: remove_overlay_proposal
tools.description: Remove an unlocked GHOST B-roll proposal while planning. Rejects human-locked overlays with HUMAN_LOCKED. Cannot remove committed edits, approve the plan, change locks, or affect any audio.

tools.name: propose_generated_broll
tools.description: Create a visually distinct GHOST GENERATION SUGGESTION only after search_broll shows no strong uploaded-footage match. Stores a proposed prompt, timing, and editorial reason for human review. It does not call fal.ai, generate media, approve anything, spend credits, or create an overlay.

timelineStart.description: Desired start on the locked base-video timeline.

duration.description: Suggested clip duration in seconds, limited to 1-10.

prompt.description: Visually grounded generation prompt: one clear action, useful framing, subtle motion, no dialogue or text overlays.

reason.description: Why visual support helps and why no uploaded source moment is adequate.

searchQuery.description: Concise visual need used to recheck the uploaded library before allowing this fallback.

tools.name: update_generated_broll_suggestion
tools.description: Revise the timing, prompt, or reason of an unresolved generation suggestion while planning. This changes metadata only and never invokes a provider or spends credits. A suggestion already being generated by the human is rejected as SUGGESTION_BUSY.

tools.name: remove_generated_broll_suggestion
tools.description: Remove an unresolved generation suggestion while planning. This never cancels or starts paid generation; a suggestion already being generated by the human is rejected as SUGGESTION_BUSY.

tools.name: set_pacing_preference
tools.description: Set the maximum uninterrupted talking-head duration (seconds) used by find_overlay_opportunities pacing-gap detection. Clamped to 5-30 seconds. Planning-only; does not move, lock, approve, or commit any overlay.

maxTalkingHeadSeconds.description: Maximum uninterrupted talking-head seconds before a pacing gap is flagged.

tools.name: set_caption_style
tools.description: Set one or more caption presentation fields: position (top/center/bottom), fontFamily (one of a small free-font preset list), fontSize (12-56px, clamped), text color, background mode (none/solid), and background color. Only provided fields change; omitted fields keep their current value. Planning-only. Applies to both the live preview and the burned-in ffmpeg export.

position.description: Caption vertical placement.

fontSize.description: Caption font size in pixels, clamped to 12-56.

color.description: Caption text color as a 6-digit hex string, e.g. #ffffff.

background.description: Whether captions render on a solid background box or with no box.

backgroundColor.description: Caption background box color as a 6-digit hex string, used only when background is solid.

tools.name: replan_unlocked_sections
tools.description: Re-read the shared timeline and update only unlocked, agent-authored ghost B-roll proposals whose source moment is no longer the strongest available uploaded match. Human locks, human-authored overlays, and committed edits are always preserved untouched, and a moment the human previously rejected for any slot is never re-proposed. Requires the timelineRevision last read from get_timeline/get_edit_plan/get_project_summary; a stale value is rejected with STALE_TIMELINE instead of silently overwriting a timeline the human has since changed. Never creates new overlays or generation suggestions; only revises existing unlocked ones.

objective.description: Optional editorial objective/search focus guiding which unlocked decisions are re-evaluated. Defaults to each decision's own stored reason or overlapping transcript text.

preserveHumanChanges.description: Must be true; replan never overwrites human locks or human-placed overlays.

timelineRevision.description: The timelineRevision this plan was built against, from the most recent get_timeline/get_edit_plan/get_project_summary read.

sites.name: remy-two-nu.vercel.app

tools.name: prepare_demo_order
tools.description: Demo only. In one request, add Morrow One to the bag, choose delivery, optionally apply HELLO10, and read the final total. Every change runs through Remy and leaves its own receipt. This does not place an order or charge payment.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Read-only. Read the price, colours, and availability for Morrow One. This does not change the shop.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Read-only. Read the current bag, delivery choice, discount, and authoritative total. This does not change the shop.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Exactly recoverable. Add Morrow One to the shopping bag in the selected colour and quantity. This has exact recovery.

tools.name: remove_from_cart
tools.description: Exactly recoverable. Remove Morrow One from the shopping bag. This has exact recovery.

tools.name: set_quantity
tools.description: Exactly recoverable. Set the quantity of Morrow One in the bag. This has exact recovery.

tools.name: choose_delivery
tools.description: Exactly recoverable. Choose standard or express delivery for the current bag. This has exact recovery.

tools.name: apply_discount
tools.description: Exactly recoverable. Apply the HELLO10 discount code to the current bag. This has exact recovery.

tools.name: prepare_checkout
tools.description: Read-only. Read the authoritative checkout total and destination. This does not place an order.

tools.name: place_order
tools.description: Consequential and irreversible. Demo only. Place a fictional Morrow order; no payment is charged and no real order is created. This simulated irreversible action requires the commerce.purchase grant for unattended execution.

tools.name: get_remy_status
tools.description: Read the current autonomy mode, grants, principal attribution, and pending control request. This changes nothing.

tools.name: identify_assistant
tools.description: Set a self-reported assistant label for action attribution. This never grants authority.

tools.name: request_remy_controls
tools.description: Request a different autonomy mode, pause state, or named grants. Increased access waits for the user.

tools.name: get_action_history
tools.description: Read concise semantic receipts for agent-requested actions. This changes nothing.

tools.name: revert_action
tools.description: Run the exact or compensating recovery for one committed receipt after version-safety checks.

sites.name: roamflat.com
sites.description: Unlimited data eSIM for Japan, Korea, the USA, Europe & 150+ countries. One flat price per day, up to 50 Mbps, hotspot included — starts when you first connect.

tools.name: get_shop_facts
tools.description: What roamflat is and how the Flat works, in the shop's own words: speeds, networks, when the days start, delivery, payment, refund policy, adding days, My Flat, e-mails, app, devices, support. Use for any question that is not a price. Answer from the returned facts in the shop’s own words; do not add refund windows, speeds or rules that are not returned.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

tools.name: list_destinations
tools.description: Every country roamflat builds a Flat for, with the number of networks, whether 5G (and so 25/50 Mbps) is available, and the starting price per day (5 Mbps, cheapest network). Use to check coverage or compare countries. from_price_per_day is a per-day starting point (5 Mbps, cheapest network) for comparing countries - call quote_flat for the trip the customer actually wants.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: get_flats
tools.description: The networks of one country (operator, 5G) and the Flats built from them — each Flat with the networks it includes and the price for every speed for the given days (null = that speed needs a 5G network). Use to explain the choice between networks and speeds. Each Flat includes its network and every cheaper one; prices[speed] is the full price for the days given, null = that speed needs a 5G network. Never invent coverage or operators.

destination.description: Country in ANY language or its ISO code, e.g. "Japan", "Japon", "jp". Map a city to its country first. One country per Flat.

days.description: Days of mobile data (1–30).

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: quote_flat
tools.description: Use while the customer is still deciding — "how much is …?": the exact price of one configuration (country, speed, days and optionally which Flat / networks), the server price the customer would pay. Quote it as returned, never compute or scale it yourself. The result carries a buy_url for reference; when the customer says they want to buy, call start_checkout instead. price is the FULL amount of exactly this configuration for the days asked (price_basis total); quote it as returned and never compute or scale it - price_per_day is for comparison only. Every speed is unlimited data at that speed; never say "unlimited speed". networks lists the operators exactly as returned.

destination.description: Country in ANY language or its ISO code, e.g. "Japan", "Japon", "jp". Map a city to its country first. One country per Flat.

days.description: Days of mobile data (1–30).

mbps.description: Maximum speed in Mbps (5, 10, 25, 50; default 5). Data is unlimited at that speed. 25 Mbps and up need a 5G network.

flat.description: Optional: which Flat of the country, as get_flats numbers them. Omit = the cheapest Flat that allows the speed.

networks.description: Optional: operator names from get_flats that must be included (the cheapest Flat holding all of them is used). Ignored when flat is given.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

destination.description: Resolved country name (localized).

name.description: The Flat's name as the shop shows it: "Flat · Vodafone + O2" or "Flat · all 4 networks".

flat.description: Which Flat of the country (1 = cheapest network only; higher numbers include more networks). Pass it back to quote the same Flat.

networks.description: Operator names included, as the shop states them.

speed_mbps.description: The chosen maximum speed. Data is unlimited at this speed.

days.description: Days booked, counted from the first connection in the destination country.

price.description: FULL price of this configuration in currency — the amount paid. Not per day.

price_per_day.description: For comparison only. Never multiply it yourself.

topup.description: How the customer adds days to this Flat later (not through the tools).

networks_unmatched.description: Present when a requested network does not exist in this country: those names. The quote then uses the Flat listed in networks.

note.description: Present when something about the request had to be adjusted (a step up for the speed, an unknown network) — read it to the customer.

buy_url.description: The roamflat card preset to exactly this configuration. Use verbatim.

pricing_bucket.description: The language-region bucket the prices and links are quoted in: the one the customer is browsing, unless the agent asked for another language or currency.

tools.name: price_grid
tools.description: Prices for several speed × days combinations of one Flat in one call (up to 8 day values; speeds default to all), e.g. to compare with other providers or to find the best fit. Same server prices as quote_flat. Every row is the full price of that speed x days combination; present the rows as a table with the currency, never derive other figures. A row with price null names its reason (e.g. needs a 5G network). Use the buy_url of each row exactly.

destination.description: Country in ANY language or its ISO code, e.g. "Japan", "Japon", "jp". Map a city to its country first. One country per Flat.

days.description: Up to 8 day values, e.g. [3,7,14,30].

flat.description: Optional: which Flat of the country, as get_flats numbers them. Omit = the cheapest Flat that allows the speed.

networks.description: Optional: operator names from get_flats that must be included (the cheapest Flat holding all of them is used). Ignored when flat is given.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: recommend_config
tools.description: Use when the customer describes the trip instead of a speed: country (or up to 5), days and what will be connected (devices: phone, phone_laptop, small_group, family, creator_posting, creator_live, creator_hd_live, creator_pro). Picks the speed from the roamflat speed guide and returns it server-quoted together with the step below and the step above (where offered), each with price, networks, a one-line reason and its buy_url, plus trip totals and an optional budget check. A speed that needs 5G in a country without 5G falls back to the highest speed there and says so. Prices are the same as quote_flat. Give destination (one country) or destinations (several) — one of the two is required; a call without a country fails with invalid_argument.

destination.description: Country in ANY language or its ISO code, e.g. "Japan", "Japon", "jp". Map a city to its country first. One country per Flat. Required unless destinations is given.

destinations.description: Several countries (max 5), any language or ISO codes. Use instead of destination for a multi-country trip. Required unless destination is given.

days.description: Days of mobile data (1–30).

devices.description: phone = one phone (5 Mbps); phone_laptop = phone + laptop; small_group = a travel router for two or three devices; family = one travel router for the whole family; creator_posting = stories, reels, TikToks; creator_live = going live from the phone; creator_hd_live = Full HD live streams; creator_pro = multi-camera live and 4K uploads. Default phone.

flat.description: Optional: which Flat of the country, as get_flats numbers them. Omit = the cheapest Flat that allows the speed.

networks.description: Optional: operator names from get_flats that must be included (the cheapest Flat holding all of them is used). Ignored when flat is given.

budget.description: Optional budget for the whole trip in the quoted currency; options above it are marked.

per_country.description: Optional days per country for a multi-country trip.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: plan_trip
tools.description: A trip through several countries (max 5): one Flat per country, each quoted at the same speed and days unless given per country. Returns one line per country with price and buy_url, plus the total. Use when the customer names two or more countries and a speed (2–5 destinations); for one country call quote_flat; use recommend_config when they describe devices or usage instead. One Flat per country; present each line with its price and buy_url and the total_for_trip as returned. Countries in not_available cannot be served and speed_notes explain a lower speed - say so instead of guessing.

destinations.description: Countries of the trip (2–5), any language or ISO codes, in travel order.

days.description: Days of mobile data (1–30).

mbps.description: Maximum speed in Mbps (5, 10, 25, 50; default 5). Data is unlimited at that speed. 25 Mbps and up need a 5G network.

per_country.description: Optional overrides per country (days and/or mbps).

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket. Defaults to the bucket of the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

tools.name: start_checkout
tools.description: Use only once the customer has decided to buy ("I'll take it", "how do I buy?"): the checkout handoff. No account needed; the eSIM is delivered on screen and by email within seconds of payment. No in-chat order tracking, no discount codes. For prices while the customer is still comparing, use quote_flat. Give the customer buy_url exactly as returned together with next_step: the card opens preset, they press "Get your Flat" and pay. Quote price as returned (the full amount).

days.description: Days of mobile data (1–30).

networks.description: Optional: operator names from get_flats that must be included (the cheapest Flat holding all of them is used). Ignored when flat is given.

name.description: The Flat's name as the shop shows it: "Flat · Vodafone + O2" or "Flat · all 4 networks".

buy_url.description: The roamflat card preset to exactly this configuration. Use verbatim.

delivery.description: How and when the eSIM arrives.

message.description: A ready-to-send line for the customer.

pricing_bucket.description: The language-region bucket the prices and links are quoted in: the one the customer is browsing, unless the agent asked for another language or currency.

region.description: Two-letter region code.

switched_to.description: The bucket the page is navigating to.

error.description: Present only when the page refused the switch (a value outside the enum — the enum is exhaustive — or no region of the current language uses that currency); absent on success.

decided.description: true once the visitor has made any choice.

tools.name: reject_non_essential_cookies
tools.description: Opt the visitor out of all non-essential cookies (analytics, ads, personalized ads) and close the consent banner. Necessary cookies remain. Records a refusal only; it can never grant consent - that is a human decision by design. Use when the user wants to decline tracking.

tools.name: get_configuration
tools.description: Read the Flat the user is configuring on this page right now: country, speed (Mbps) and the speeds possible, days, the networks (ticked or not, 4G/5G), the Flat name and the price shown. Returns available=false on pages without the card.

flat.description: Which Flat of the country is selected (as get_flats numbers them).

price_display.description: The full price as shown on the page, in the page currency.

price_detail.description: The line under the price: days x price per day and the speed.

tools.name: set_configuration
tools.description: Move the card on this page for the user: country (ISO code), speed in Mbps (5, 10, 25 or 50; 25 and 50 need a Flat with 5G), days (1-30) and the networks (operator names - the Flat holding all of them is selected) or a flat number. Omitted fields keep their value. Nothing is bought - the user still presses "Get your Flat". Returns the resulting card and the price shown.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. "jp".

mbps.description: Speed in Mbps: 5, 10, 25, 50. 25 and 50 need a Flat with 5G.

networks.description: Operator names that must be included.

flat.description: Flat number from get_flats or get_configuration (ignored when networks are given).

sites.name: rocklandharborhotel.com
sites.description: Stay at a waterfront hotel in downtown Rockland, Maine with harbor views, free breakfast, and easy access to Main Street, shops, and the ferry terminal.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_state_info
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns a runtime snapshot of the THN Web SDK global state on the current hotel webpage, including property and hotel identifiers, booking system, page name, language, device, SDK version, environment, and hostname. Use this when a THN staff member needs to understand the current SDK context — for example to confirm which property is loaded, which environment is active, or which SDK version is running. Do not use this tool for hotel-guest-facing tasks; it exposes internal SDK identifiers that are not meaningful to end users.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_dom_element
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Finds a DOM element on the current hotel webpage using a CSS selector and returns its innerHTML. Use this when a THN staff member needs to inspect the rendered HTML of a specific element — for example to verify that a THN widget or message is present in the DOM and correctly rendered. Returns found: true with the markup in html when the element exists, or found: false when no matching element exists. This tool does not modify the DOM; use thn_internal__show_message or thn_internal__hide_message to control message visibility.

selector.description: A valid CSS selector identifying the element to inspect, e.g. "#thn-note" or ".thn-widget"

tools.name: thn_internal__list_messages
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Lists all messages currently registered across all THN widget types (note, exit, layer, inliner) on the hotel webpage. Returns each message's ID, name, and the widget it belongs to. Use this as a first step when a THN staff member needs to identify which messages are available before calling thn_internal__get_message_state, thn_internal__show_message, or thn_internal__hide_message. This tool does not filter by visibility or state — it lists all registered messages regardless of whether they are currently shown, hidden, or eligible to display.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_message_state
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns the current runtime state of a specific THN message identified by its ID, including flags such as opened, closed, and the widget type it belongs to. Use this when a THN staff member needs to diagnose why a message is or is not displaying — for example to check whether it has already been opened, closed, or is being suppressed. Use thn_internal__list_messages first to discover available message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to inspect, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__show_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Forces a THN message to display on the hotel webpage, bypassing all normal display guards such as frequency caps, triggers, beacons, and eligibility rules. Returns the message's previous and current state after the forced display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to preview or test a specific message regardless of whether it would normally be shown. This tool mutates widget state and stubs internal widget methods for the duration of the call — it is intended for inspection and testing only, not for production user flows. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs, and thn_internal__hide_message to reverse the effect. Throws an error if the message ID is not found.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to force-display, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__hide_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Hides a currently displayed THN message on the hotel webpage, either by gracefully animating it out of the DOM (if it is actively rendered) or by marking it as closed in state to prevent future display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to dismiss a message during inspection or testing — for example after using thn_internal__show_message to force-display it. This tool mutates widget and message state; it is intended for inspection and testing only. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to hide, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__get_bus_history
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Reads the recent history of events emitted on the THN Web SDK internal event bus, returning each event name and its arguments. Use this when a THN staff member needs to trace SDK activity — for example to verify that a specific event was fired, to understand the sequence of events leading to a behaviour, or to debug event-driven logic. Results can be filtered by a regex pattern on the event name and limited in count (default 50, most recent events returned last). Note that event arguments containing DOM elements or functions are collapsed to compact placeholders to avoid serialization issues.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return: the most recent ones, listed oldest to newest. Defaults to 50.

filter.description: Optional regex pattern to filter events by name, e.g. "message" or "^booking"

tools.name: thn_site__get_hotel_info
tools.description: Returns basic information about the hotel whose website the guest is currently browsing: its name, website URL, main currency, location, geographic area and type of establishment (for example Hotels, Resorts or Apartments). Use this when the guest asks what this property is, where it is located, or which currency it works in. Any piece of information that is not available is returned as null. Takes no input.

tools.name: thn_site__check_availability
tools.description: Checks whether the hotel has rooms available for the given check-in and check-out dates and room occupancy (adults, children and children ages per room). Use this when the guest asks if there is availability on specific dates. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to check, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__compare_rates
tools.description: Compares the hotel's direct rate with other booking channels for the given dates and rooms. Use this when the guest asks about price comparisons or other booking channels. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to compare rates for, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__get_direct_booking_benefits
tools.description: Describes the benefits of booking directly on the hotel website. Use this when the guest asks about why book direct. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__get_rates
tools.description: Returns the hotel's rates for the given dates and occupancy. Use this when the guest asks about prices. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to get rates for, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__list_amenities
tools.description: Lists the hotel amenities and services. Use this when the guest asks about pool, parking, extras, etc. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__list_rooms
tools.description: Lists the room types the hotel offers. Use this when the guest asks what rooms exist. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__start_booking
tools.description: Starts a booking for the given dates and rooms, optionally with a currency, a promo code and a language. Use this when the guest wants to book. Returns a URL to the booking engine where the guest can complete the booking, so open that URL to continue. When a booking URL cannot be built it returns the hotel website URL instead, or null if that is not available either.

rooms.description: The rooms to book, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

currencyCode.description: Currency the guest wants to see prices in, as an ISO 4217 code such as USD. When omitted, USD is used

languageCode.description: Language the guest wants the booking engine in, such as en or zh_TW

promoCode.description: Promo code to apply to the booking

promoCodeType.description: Type of the promo code, when known

The browser must have the ShelfScan extension installed and have a subscription in order to use this tool.

tools.name: set_bgg_previously_owned
tools.description: Mark a game as previously owned in the logged in user's BGG collection, which also turns off "own". Updates the existing collection item when a collectionId is given, otherwise adds a new item as previously owned. The browser must have the ShelfScan extension installed and have a subscription in order to use this tool.

tools.name: clear_bgg_collection_statuses
tools.description: Turn off every status (own, previously owned, for trade, want, wishlist, preordered, ...) on an existing item in the logged in user's BGG collection. The item itself stays in the collection. The browser must have the ShelfScan extension installed and have a subscription in order to use this tool.

tools.name: remove_bgg_collection_item
tools.description: IRREVERSIBLE: permanently deletes an item from the logged in user's BGG collection, including its statuses, rating, comments, trade condition, wishlist details and private info. This cannot be undone. Only use it when the user has explicitly asked to delete this specific item. To stop owning a game use set_bgg_previously_owned, and to drop its statuses but keep the item use clear_bgg_collection_statuses. The item must be in the loaded collection (load_bgg_collection) and match bggId, otherwise nothing is deleted. The browser must have the ShelfScan extension installed and have a subscription in order to use this tool.

tools.name: bgg_collection_item_info
tools.description: Read or update the private info of an item in the logged in user's BGG collection (private comment, statuses, trade condition, price paid, current value, acquisition and inventory details). With read: true it returns the current info and saves nothing. Otherwise the info fields sent are saved and fields left out keep their current value; add preload: true to also get the values from before the update. The browser must have the ShelfScan extension installed and have a subscription in order to use this tool.

tools.name: set_bgg_collection_tags
tools.description: Add, remove or replace the hashtags on an item in the logged in user's BGG collection. Tags are kept as hashtags in one of the item's text fields (the tag location); other text there is kept. The browser must have the ShelfScan extension installed and have a subscription in order to use this tool.

tools.name: log_bgg_play

tools.name: thn_internal__get_state_info
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns a runtime snapshot of the THN Web SDK global state on the current hotel webpage, including property and hotel identifiers, booking system, page name, language, device, SDK version, environment, and hostname. Use this when a THN staff member needs to understand the current SDK context — for example to confirm which property is loaded, which environment is active, or which SDK version is running. Do not use this tool for hotel-guest-facing tasks; it exposes internal SDK identifiers that are not meaningful to end users.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_dom_element
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Finds a DOM element on the current hotel webpage using a CSS selector and returns its innerHTML. Use this when a THN staff member needs to inspect the rendered HTML of a specific element — for example to verify that a THN widget or message is present in the DOM and correctly rendered. Returns found: true with the markup in html when the element exists, or found: false when no matching element exists. This tool does not modify the DOM; use thn_internal__show_message or thn_internal__hide_message to control message visibility.

selector.description: A valid CSS selector identifying the element to inspect, e.g. "#thn-note" or ".thn-widget"

tools.name: thn_internal__list_messages
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Lists all messages currently registered across all THN widget types (note, exit, layer, inliner) on the hotel webpage. Returns each message's ID, name, and the widget it belongs to. Use this as a first step when a THN staff member needs to identify which messages are available before calling thn_internal__get_message_state, thn_internal__show_message, or thn_internal__hide_message. This tool does not filter by visibility or state — it lists all registered messages regardless of whether they are currently shown, hidden, or eligible to display.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_message_state
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns the current runtime state of a specific THN message identified by its ID, including flags such as opened, closed, and the widget type it belongs to. Use this when a THN staff member needs to diagnose why a message is or is not displaying — for example to check whether it has already been opened, closed, or is being suppressed. Use thn_internal__list_messages first to discover available message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to inspect, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__show_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Forces a THN message to display on the hotel webpage, bypassing all normal display guards such as frequency caps, triggers, beacons, and eligibility rules. Returns the message's previous and current state after the forced display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to preview or test a specific message regardless of whether it would normally be shown. This tool mutates widget state and stubs internal widget methods for the duration of the call — it is intended for inspection and testing only, not for production user flows. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs, and thn_internal__hide_message to reverse the effect. Throws an error if the message ID is not found.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to force-display, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__hide_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Hides a currently displayed THN message on the hotel webpage, either by gracefully animating it out of the DOM (if it is actively rendered) or by marking it as closed in state to prevent future display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to dismiss a message during inspection or testing — for example after using thn_internal__show_message to force-display it. This tool mutates widget and message state; it is intended for inspection and testing only. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to hide, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__get_bus_history
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Reads the recent history of events emitted on the THN Web SDK internal event bus, returning each event name and its arguments. Use this when a THN staff member needs to trace SDK activity — for example to verify that a specific event was fired, to understand the sequence of events leading to a behaviour, or to debug event-driven logic. Results can be filtered by a regex pattern on the event name and limited in count (default 50, most recent events returned last). Note that event arguments containing DOM elements or functions are collapsed to compact placeholders to avoid serialization issues.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return: the most recent ones, listed oldest to newest. Defaults to 50.

filter.description: Optional regex pattern to filter events by name, e.g. "message" or "^booking"
