Returns a runtime snapshot of the THN Web SDK global state on the current hotel webpage, including property and hotel identifiers, booking system, page name, language, device, SDK version, environment, and hostname. Use this when a THN staff member needs to understand the current SDK context — for example to confirm which property is loaded, which environment is active, or which SDK version is running. Do not use this tool for hotel-guest-facing tasks; it exposes internal SDK identifiers that are not meaningful to end users.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_dom_element
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Finds a DOM element on the current hotel webpage using a CSS selector and returns its innerHTML. Use this when a THN staff member needs to inspect the rendered HTML of a specific element — for example to verify that a THN widget or message is present in the DOM and correctly rendered. Returns found: true with the markup in html when the element exists, or found: false when no matching element exists. This tool does not modify the DOM; use thn_internal__show_message or thn_internal__hide_message to control message visibility.

selector.description: A valid CSS selector identifying the element to inspect, e.g. "#thn-note" or ".thn-widget"

tools.name: thn_internal__list_messages
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Lists all messages currently registered across all THN widget types (note, exit, layer, inliner) on the hotel webpage. Returns each message's ID, name, and the widget it belongs to. Use this as a first step when a THN staff member needs to identify which messages are available before calling thn_internal__get_message_state, thn_internal__show_message, or thn_internal__hide_message. This tool does not filter by visibility or state — it lists all registered messages regardless of whether they are currently shown, hidden, or eligible to display.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_message_state
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns the current runtime state of a specific THN message identified by its ID, including flags such as opened, closed, and the widget type it belongs to. Use this when a THN staff member needs to diagnose why a message is or is not displaying — for example to check whether it has already been opened, closed, or is being suppressed. Use thn_internal__list_messages first to discover available message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to inspect, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__show_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Forces a THN message to display on the hotel webpage, bypassing all normal display guards such as frequency caps, triggers, beacons, and eligibility rules. Returns the message's previous and current state after the forced display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to preview or test a specific message regardless of whether it would normally be shown. This tool mutates widget state and stubs internal widget methods for the duration of the call — it is intended for inspection and testing only, not for production user flows. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs, and thn_internal__hide_message to reverse the effect. Throws an error if the message ID is not found.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to force-display, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__hide_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Hides a currently displayed THN message on the hotel webpage, either by gracefully animating it out of the DOM (if it is actively rendered) or by marking it as closed in state to prevent future display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to dismiss a message during inspection or testing — for example after using thn_internal__show_message to force-display it. This tool mutates widget and message state; it is intended for inspection and testing only. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to hide, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__get_bus_history
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Reads the recent history of events emitted on the THN Web SDK internal event bus, returning each event name and its arguments. Use this when a THN staff member needs to trace SDK activity — for example to verify that a specific event was fired, to understand the sequence of events leading to a behaviour, or to debug event-driven logic. Results can be filtered by a regex pattern on the event name and limited in count (default 50, most recent events returned last). Note that event arguments containing DOM elements or functions are collapsed to compact placeholders to avoid serialization issues.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return: the most recent ones, listed oldest to newest. Defaults to 50.

filter.description: Optional regex pattern to filter events by name, e.g. "message" or "^booking"

Use this when the guest asks what this property is, where it is located, or which currency it works in. Any piece of information that is not available is returned as null. Takes no input.

sites.name: switchboard-100.pages.dev
sites.description: Human + agent control center for LLM provider budgets, priced model catalogs and routing policy. Agent-ready via WebMCP.

tools.name: get_provenance
tools.description: Explain where the numbers on this dashboard come from and how far they can be trusted. Call this before making a recommendation so you can state the limits of your evidence. Returns the measurement date, the run and call counts, and per-model sample sizes. Read samplingCaveat: the measurements are spread across a whole catalogue on a single structured-output task, so per-model sample counts are small — treat medianLatencyMs as indicative and p95LatencyMs as coarse, and say so when a recommendation turns on a latency margin of a second or less. Every field here is prose and counts for you to paraphrase, not a machine-readable prohibition list.

tools.name: list_providers
tools.description: List every LLM provider with its monthly budget cap in USD and its projected monthly spend under the policy currently in force, plus the total cap across all providers. Provider ids are kebab-case, e.g. 'opencode-go', 'openai'. Caps are NOT writable by you — there is no set_budget tool; use propose_budget_change, which the operator must approve. Projected spend is derived from operator-declared call volumes and published prices, not from a billing API: there is no billing history, actuals or time series anywhere on this surface, so never describe these figures as what was spent.

tools.name: list_traffic_classes
tools.description: List the traffic classes this workload is split into, with the constraints each must satisfy, and how many models are currently eligible for each. Read this before proposing any routing change — the constraints are the whole point and several are not about money. Per class: monthlyCalls and average token counts, which are OPERATOR-DECLARED estimates and not measured (you cannot change them; only the human can, in the UI). Then the constraints: maxP95Ms, minSuccessRate (judged against the chain-level delivery rate, not one model's success rate), requireQualityGates, maxDataRetentionDays (null here means UNCONSTRAINED — the opposite of null on a model, where it means undocumented and therefore not clearable), allowTrainingOnData (false means never route to a model that trains on submitted data, in any chain position, including fallbacks), requireMeasured. You cannot write these constraints — but the operator can, under 'relax constraints' on each class in the UI. So when a class has zero eligible models, the useful move is to name precisely which constraint is emptying the set and what it would cost to relax each one, then let them choose. Do not route around a constraint you were not given permission to relax.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: List the priced model catalogue joined with this operator's own measurements. Prices are per million tokens from published provider documentation. Call get_provenance for how the measurements were produced and how coarse they are. Per model: requestSuccessRate (0-1), medianLatencyMs, p95LatencyMs, observedCalls (the sample size behind those latencies — check it before trusting a small latency gap), costPer1kSuccessfulUsd (cost per 1000 DELIVERED outputs, i.e. price divided by success rate; prefer it over raw price, because a cheap model that fails half its calls is not cheap), and meetsQualityGates. GOVERNANCE, and read this carefully: on a MODEL, dataRetentionDays and trainsOnData are null when the provider does not document them, and null means UNKNOWN, which is not the same as safe. On a TRAFFIC CLASS the same-named constraints being null means UNCONSTRAINED. The two nulls are opposites, so do not carry one across the join. Every governance filter here excludes undocumented models rather than assuming the best. If you only need a set of models that is legal for a class, pass eligibleForClassId and skip the individual filters — it applies the class's real constraints, including the ones these filters cannot express.

measuredOnly.description: Only models with measurements. Default false.

excludeDead.description: Drop models that returned zero successful calls in every run. Unmeasured models are kept — use measuredOnly to drop those. Default false.

maxDataRetentionDays.description: Only models documented to retain data for at most this many days. Models with undocumented retention are excluded.

excludeTrainsOnData.description: Drop models that train on submitted data AND models where this is undocumented, since undocumented is not safe. Default false.

minSuccessRate.description: Only models with a measured request success rate at or above this (0-1). Excludes unmeasured models.

maxCostPer1kDeliveredUsd.description: Only models at or below this cost per 1000 delivered outputs, in USD. Excludes unmeasured models.

limit.description: Cap the number of models returned, cheapest per delivered output first. Omit for all matches.

maxP95Ms.description: Only models with measured p95 latency at or below this many milliseconds.

requireQualityGates.description: Only models that passed the quality gates. Default false.

eligibleForClassId.description: Return only models satisfying every constraint of this traffic class. Simplest way to get a legal candidate set.

tools.name: get_model
tools.description: Full detail on one model, including why it failed its quality gates if it did (gateFailureReasons), and a per-class verdict listing exactly which constraint each traffic class would reject it on. Use this when you need to justify excluding a model, or to understand whether a rejection is a hard blocker or a warning you can route around with a fallback.

tools.name: compare_models
tools.description: Rank candidate models for one traffic class, using that class's own token profile and declared volume, so the money figures are comparable to each other and to get_routing_policy. Note this differs from the costPer1kSuccessfulUsd in list_models, which uses the measurement task's own token profile — do not quote the two side by side. Only models satisfying every HARD constraint of the class are ranked; the rest come back under rejected with the blocking codes. Ranking: 'cost' = lowest cost per delivered output; 'latency' = lowest measured p95; 'reliability' = highest success rate; 'balanced' (default) = costPerDelivered × (1 + p95ms/10000) × 1.5 if it fails quality gates. Fallbacks: performance constraints (quality gates, latency) soften to warnings for a fallback because a slow answer beats none, but governance constraints (retention, training) never soften — so a model rejected on RETENTION or TRAINING cannot serve this class in any position. Call this before proposing a routing change.

classId.description: Traffic class id. Call list_traffic_classes for valid ids (e.g. 'realtime', 'batch', 'sensitive').

limit.description: How many ranked candidates to return. Default 8.

tools.name: get_routing_policy
tools.description: The routing policy currently in force, with the resolved primary and fallback chain per traffic class and the projected monthly cost, delivery rate and latency each chain produces. Call this before proposing changes so your proposal is a genuine diff against reality rather than a rewrite from scratch.

tools.name: simulate_policy
tools.description: Project what a candidate routing policy would cost and deliver, WITHOUT applying it. Classes you omit keep their current routing. Definitions: deliveredRatePct is the chain-level probability that some link succeeds, i.e. 1 minus the product of every link failing — this, not a single model's requestSuccessRate, is what a class's minSuccessRate is judged against. expectedLatencyMs is the probability-weighted median across the chain. worstCaseLatencyMs is the SUM of p95 across the WHOLE chain — what a request pays if every link but the last fails. It is reported unconditionally, so it never understates the tail; read tailRiskProbability alongside it, which is the chance of getting past the primary at all. HOW A LATENCY CEILING IS JUDGED, because the two rules interact: a fallback whose own p95 exceeds the ceiling is a WARNING, not a blocker, since a slow answer beats no answer — so the class stays permissible. But the chain's summed worst case is checked too and raises a CHAIN_LATENCY warning when it exceeds the ceiling. So a chain can be permissible and still carry a flagged tail. Say which you mean: "the primary meets your 4s ceiling; the chain can reach Xms in the Y% of cases where the primary fails" is the honest phrasing. Cost counts every attempt, since a failed call is still billed. The candidate's compliance verdict is returned here too and is the same computation check_compliance runs, so you do not need both — call check_compliance only when you want to audit the LIVE policy. One side effect: this repaints the projection on the operator's screen so they can follow your reasoning, so iterate deliberately rather than sweeping dozens of candidates.

rules.description: Candidate routing rules. One entry per traffic class you want to change; classes you omit keep their current rule.

fallbackModelIds.description: Models tried in order if the primary fails. Pass [] for no fallback.

label.description: Short human-readable name for this candidate, shown on screen.

tools.name: check_compliance
tools.description: Audit the live policy — or a candidate rule set if you pass one — against every constraint at once: latency ceilings, success-rate floors, quality gates, data-retention limits, the no-training-on-data requirement, AND the spend caps (TOTAL_BUDGET and PROVIDER_BUDGET blockers when projected spend exceeds a cap). Blockers mean the routing is not permissible as configured; warnings mean permissible but fragile. An empty blockers list is the bar a proposal should clear. Because spend is included, a clean result does mean the plan fits the operator's declared budget — but only the budget that is actually recorded, so if they stated a target in conversation, propose it via propose_budget_change first so it becomes auditable. simulate_policy returns this same verdict for a candidate; use this tool for the live policy.

rules.description: Candidate routing rules. One entry per traffic class you want to change; classes you omit keep their current rule.

fallbackModelIds.description: Models tried in order if the primary fails. Pass [] for no fallback.

tools.name: find_waste
tools.description: Lint the live policy against the measurements and report everything wrong with it. Each finding carries a kind: "spend" means money is being wasted right now (a routed model that never succeeds, a class routed to something dearer than a compliant alternative, a model over $1 per 1000 delivered outputs that still fails its gates); "risk" means a fragility rather than a cost (a class with one or zero eligible models); "hygiene" means a data gap (catalogue entries priced but never measured). Only "spend" findings carry estimatedMonthlySavingsUsd — do not present risk or hygiene findings as costs. Every finding cites the numbers behind it. Start here when the operator asks an open question like "where is my money going", but say plainly that these are projections from declared volumes, not billed spend.

tools.name: propose_policy_change
tools.description: Put a routing change in front of the operator for approval. This does NOT apply the change — routing decides where money and customer data go, so it stays a human decision. The proposal appears on their screen as a rule-by-rule diff with the projected cost delta and the compliance verdict. You will get back a proposal id; poll get_proposal_status to learn what the operator decided and read any note they left. If they reject with a reason, address the reason and propose again rather than resubmitting the same rules.

rules.description: Candidate routing rules. One entry per traffic class you want to change; classes you omit keep their current rule.

fallbackModelIds.description: Models tried in order if the primary fails. Pass [] for no fallback.

rationale.description: Why this change is right, in terms the operator can check: which constraint it fixes, what it costs, what it gives up. Cite the numbers you used.

tools.name: propose_budget_change
tools.description: Ask the operator to change a monthly spend cap — either the total across all providers (scope 'total') or one provider's cap (scope 'provider'). Like routing, this is not applied directly: a budget is a spending authorisation, so only the human can grant it. WHAT A CAP DOES: it is advisory in the sense that nothing here proxies traffic, but it is enforced as a compliance blocker — check_compliance and simulate_policy both report TOTAL_BUDGET and PROVIDER_BUDGET blockers when projected spend exceeds a cap, so a routing proposal that busts a cap will not come back clean. If the operator states a spending target in conversation, propose it as the total cap so it becomes an auditable constraint rather than something you have to remember. Returns a proposal id to poll with get_proposal_status.

scope.description: 'total' changes the cap across all providers; 'provider' changes one provider's cap and requires providerId.

providerId.description: Required when scope is 'provider'. Call list_providers for valid ids.

monthlyBudgetUsd.description: Proposed new monthly cap in USD.

rationale.description: Why this cap, tied to projected spend.

tools.name: withdraw_proposal
tools.description: Retract a proposal you submitted that is still pending, because you have thought better of it or are about to submit a corrected version. Only pending proposals can be withdrawn; an approved one has already been applied and a rejected one is already closed. This applies immediately and needs no approval — withdrawing spends nothing and routes nothing. The proposal stops awaiting a decision but stays in the operator's history marked withdrawn; nothing is deleted.

tools.name: get_proposal_status
tools.description: Check what the operator decided about a proposal you submitted. Status is 'pending' (still on their screen), 'approved' (applied; re-read get_routing_policy to see the new state), 'rejected', or 'withdrawn' (you retracted it). A human decision can take minutes or hours: if it is still pending, report the proposal id to the user and stop rather than looping — do not resubmit the same rules, and use withdraw_proposal if you want to replace it. A rejection usually carries decisionNote explaining what was wrong; read it and propose a corrected version addressing that specific objection. Omit proposalId to list every proposal and its status.

proposalId.description: Proposal id such as 'P-1'. Omit to list all.

tools.name: pin_insight
tools.description: Leave a short finding on the operator's dashboard. Unlike routing and budget changes this applies immediately and needs no approval, because it only adds a note — nothing is spent and nothing is routed differently. Use it to record a trade-off the operator has to decide, or a conclusion worth keeping after the conversation ends.

title.description: One line, specific. Prefer "Sensitive class has no compliant model" over "Compliance issue".

body.description: Two or three sentences with the numbers behind it.

tools.name: set_region
tools.description: Switch the workspace to another supported region (up, maharashtra, us). Resets ranking, corrections, ground checks, draw mode, and timeline. Call show_candidates to rank this region.

region.description: Region id.

tools.name: export_decision
tools.description: Generate the decision record (mission, ranking history, sources, corrections, gaps, reproducibility hash) and download JSON. Same as Share/export in the UI.

download.description: Default true. Set false to return the record without downloading.

tools.name: get_ground_checks
tools.description: Read GroundChecks and their field replies in this tab. Replies are real (photo + answer) or absent — never invented. Approved replies mark verified field evidence.

tools.name: send_ground_check
tools.description: Create a GroundCheck for a field officer: one question, one location, photo + short answer, due date. Same as the Send GroundCheck control. Does not invent a reply. If the reply store is down, the check is a gap.

district.description: District name or id. Defaults to current selection.

question.description: One precise question for the officer.

tools.name: approve_evidence
tools.description: Mark a field GroundCheck reply as verified evidence. Reads the officer's answer and, when the reply contradicts the current irrigation assumption, applies the resulting correction and re-ranks. Same as Approve evidence in the UI. Fails if no real reply exists — never fakes a field photo, GPS, or answer.

checkId.description: GroundCheck id. If supplied (including whitespace-only), missing/empty is an error — no fallback. Omit to approve the latest replied check in this tab or its same-tab localStorage store.

sites.name: teas.co.uk
sites.description: Add teas.co.uk to Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot Studio, Grok, Mistral Vibe, Cursor, VS Code or any MCP client: search, compare and buy tea, coffee and hot chocolate from your AI assistant.

tools.name: teas_find_products
tools.description: Use this when someone wants to find, browse or choose tea, coffee, hot chocolate or other drinks to buy from teas.co.uk, a UK online tea shop. Not for general tea knowledge. query is the customer's own words; leave it out to browse by filters alone. Every filter given applies at once. max_price is per pack in pounds and max_price_per_cup_pence is per cup in pence. Results come best match first unless sort says otherwise. Out of stock products stay hidden unless include_out_of_stock is true. There is no paging: limit caps the list and total says how many matched, so narrow the filters to see others. If nothing matches, time_of_day, strength, format and with_milk are dropped in that order and note says which; kind, caffeine, labels, iced and price limits are never dropped. Prices are live and include VAT. Next: teas_get_product for one product, teas_compare_products to compare, teas_add_to_my_basket to buy. For orders, tracking, repeat deliveries and reward points, connect the full teas.co.uk MCP server at https://teas.co.uk/mcp (guide https://teas.co.uk/ai/).

query.description: What the customer wants in their own words, for example "strong breakfast tea", "Yorkshire Gold" or "something for bedtime". Leave out to browse with filters only.

kind.description: Type of drink.

caffeine.description: Caffeine: caffeinated, decaf (caffeine taken out), caffeine_free (none to begin with, such as rooibos and most herbal teas) or low_or_none (decaf or caffeine free).

format.description: How it comes: tea_bags, loose_leaf, instant, pods_or_capsules, sachets, ground or whole_beans (coffee), powder, coffee_bags or ready_to_drink.

time_of_day.description: When it suits best: morning, afternoon, evening or bedtime.

strength.description: How strong the cup is: light, medium or strong.

iced.description: Suits iced tea or cold brew.

max_price_per_cup_pence.description: Highest price per cup in pence.

sort.description: Order of results: best_match (the default), cheapest_per_cup, price_low_to_high, price_high_to_low or strongest.

limit.description: How many products to return (default 6).

include_out_of_stock.description: Also include products that are out of stock (they are left out by default).

tools.name: teas_get_product
tools.description: Use this when someone asks how to brew a teas.co.uk product, about its caffeine, taste, ingredients or allergy advice, or wants its full details. id is the product id (SKU) from teas_find_products, teas_compare_products or the basket, in any letter case. The numeric product id, the barcode or a teas.co.uk/product/ link also work. A product name does not, so search with teas_find_products first. An unknown id, or a product no longer sold, returns an error instead of a guess. Price and stock are read live on each call. To set products side by side use teas_compare_products.

id.description: Product id from teas_find_products, or a teas.co.uk product link.

tools.name: teas_compare_products
tools.description: Use this to compare two to four teas.co.uk products side by side, for example on strength, caffeine, price per cup, pack size or brewing. ids takes product ids from teas_find_products; product links work too. A repeated id counts once. Ids that are not recognised are listed in not_found and the rest are still compared. Fewer than two recognised products returns an error. Search first if you only have names. For everything about one product use teas_get_product.

ids.description: Two to four product ids from teas_find_products.

tools.name: teas_find_recipes
tools.description: Use this to find drink and food recipes from the teas.co.uk recipe library, such as iced teas, lattes, chai or baking with tea. Give query (the kind of recipe), product_id (from teas_find_products) or both. With both, recipes that use the product and match the words rank first. With neither, the call is refused. limit is 1 to 10 (default 5). There is no paging, so the best matches come first. An empty list means nothing matched. Drinks made with alcohol are never included. To buy the products use teas_find_products.

query.description: What kind of recipe, for example "iced peach tea" or "chai latte".

product_id.description: Optional product id from teas_find_products.

limit.description: How many recipes (default 5).

tools.name: teas_delivery_and_returns
tools.description: Use this when someone asks about teas.co.uk delivery prices, free delivery, dispatch times, which countries it delivers to, or how returns and refunds work. It takes no input because the answer is the same for everyone. Policy only: it never looks at an order. Returns and order tracking are in My Account on teas.co.uk.

tools.name: teas_quote_cart
tools.description: Use this to price products for the person before anything goes in a basket. Pass up to 20 items (id from teas_find_products and quantity) and the delivery country. It returns live prices including VAT, every delivery option teas.co.uk offers for that country and parcel, the total with the cheapest option, how much more to spend for free UK delivery, stock, and a basket link the person can open. Nothing is stored and no basket changes. For a basket the person keeps, call teas_add_to_my_basket; to hand over checkout, call teas_go_to_checkout.

id.description: Product id from find_products.

quantity.description: How many packs.

items.description: Products and quantities to price, 1 to 20 lines. The same id twice is added together.

country.description: Delivery country as a two letter code, for example GB, IE or FR. Leave out for the UK.

tools.name: teas_find_substitutes
tools.description: Use this when a product is out of stock, too dear, or the person wants something similar to try. Pass one product id from teas_find_products or a teas.co.uk product link. It returns products of the same kind and caffeine, near the same strength, split into cheaper and premium by price per cup, in stock first and closest match first. limit sets how many of each come back (default 3). Next: teas_get_product for details, teas_compare_products to compare, teas_add_to_my_basket to buy.

id.description: Product id from teas_find_products, or a teas.co.uk product link.

limit.description: How many cheaper and how many premium alternatives, 1 to 10. Defaults to 3.

tools.name: teas_get_promotions
tools.description: Use this when the person asks about offers, discounts, codes or what is on sale at teas.co.uk. It lists products on sale now with the usual price and when the sale ends (biggest saving first, in stock only), any offer codes teas.co.uk has made public, and the free UK delivery threshold. Codes that are not public are never shown, and checkout on teas.co.uk applies the final price. Next: teas_get_product for details, quote_cart for a total, teas_add_to_my_basket to buy.

limit.description: How many products on sale to list, 1 to 20. Defaults to 10.

tools.name: teas_add_to_my_basket
tools.description: Add a teas.co.uk product to the basket in this browser, only when the visitor asks. The quantity is added to any already there. Nothing is bought until the visitor checks out and pays on teas.co.uk.

id.description: Product id from teas_find_products.

tools.name: teas_update_my_basket
tools.description: Set the quantity of a product already in the basket in this browser, or remove it with quantity 0, only when the visitor asks.

id.description: Product id (from teas_view_my_basket or teas_find_products).

quantity.description: New quantity; 0 removes the product.

tools.name: teas_view_my_basket
tools.description: Show the basket in this browser with its subtotal. An assistant connected to https://teas.co.uk/mcp can also keep a basket and give a checkout link.

tools.name: teas_go_to_checkout
tools.description: Open the teas.co.uk checkout page in this browser so the visitor can review the basket and pay. The visitor checks out and pays; the assistant never enters payment details and nothing is ordered by this tool.

tools.name: teas_basket_link
tools.description: Make a teas.co.uk basket link for up to 20 products to give the person (https://teas.co.uk/go/basket/?items=ID:QTY,...). Opening it shows a confirmation page; nothing changes until the person presses Add to basket. Never open it yourself.

tools.name: ask_tea_advice
tools.description: Ask teas.co.uk a tea question in plain words (Ask API): the answer, the products it uses and their evidence and citations. Read only.

question.description: The question in plain words.

tools.name: teas_start_subscription
tools.description: Use this when someone wants a teas.co.uk product delivered again and again (subscribe and save). Pass one product id from teas_find_products or a teas.co.uk product link. Returns the subscriber price, how often it comes and a link to the product on teas.co.uk, where the person presses Subscribe and save, then signs in, checks out and pays for the first delivery. This tool orders and charges nothing. Later deliveries follow every cycle as new orders with the same discount, teas.co.uk emails five days before each one and takes no automatic card payments, and the person can pause, resume or cancel at any time (my_subscriptions, change_subscription). When the product cannot be a repeat delivery, eligible is false and note says why.

id.description: Product id from teas_find_products, or a teas.co.uk product link.

sites.name: thefritzamsterdam.com
sites.description: Stay at THE FRITZ HOTEL, a boutique hotel in Amsterdam’s Museum District near the Rijksmuseum. Stylish rooms & central location.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_state_info
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns a runtime snapshot of the THN Web SDK global state on the current hotel webpage, including property and hotel identifiers, booking system, page name, language, device, SDK version, environment, and hostname. Use this when a THN staff member needs to understand the current SDK context — for example to confirm which property is loaded, which environment is active, or which SDK version is running. Do not use this tool for hotel-guest-facing tasks; it exposes internal SDK identifiers that are not meaningful to end users.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_dom_element
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Finds a DOM element on the current hotel webpage using a CSS selector and returns its innerHTML. Use this when a THN staff member needs to inspect the rendered HTML of a specific element — for example to verify that a THN widget or message is present in the DOM and correctly rendered. Returns found: true with the markup in html when the element exists, or found: false when no matching element exists. This tool does not modify the DOM; use thn_internal__show_message or thn_internal__hide_message to control message visibility.

selector.description: A valid CSS selector identifying the element to inspect, e.g. "#thn-note" or ".thn-widget"

tools.name: thn_internal__list_messages
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Lists all messages currently registered across all THN widget types (note, exit, layer, inliner) on the hotel webpage. Returns each message's ID, name, and the widget it belongs to. Use this as a first step when a THN staff member needs to identify which messages are available before calling thn_internal__get_message_state, thn_internal__show_message, or thn_internal__hide_message. This tool does not filter by visibility or state — it lists all registered messages regardless of whether they are currently shown, hidden, or eligible to display.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_message_state
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns the current runtime state of a specific THN message identified by its ID, including flags such as opened, closed, and the widget type it belongs to. Use this when a THN staff member needs to diagnose why a message is or is not displaying — for example to check whether it has already been opened, closed, or is being suppressed. Use thn_internal__list_messages first to discover available message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to inspect, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__show_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Forces a THN message to display on the hotel webpage, bypassing all normal display guards such as frequency caps, triggers, beacons, and eligibility rules. Returns the message's previous and current state after the forced display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to preview or test a specific message regardless of whether it would normally be shown. This tool mutates widget state and stubs internal widget methods for the duration of the call — it is intended for inspection and testing only, not for production user flows. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs, and thn_internal__hide_message to reverse the effect. Throws an error if the message ID is not found.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to force-display, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__hide_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Hides a currently displayed THN message on the hotel webpage, either by gracefully animating it out of the DOM (if it is actively rendered) or by marking it as closed in state to prevent future display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to dismiss a message during inspection or testing — for example after using thn_internal__show_message to force-display it. This tool mutates widget and message state; it is intended for inspection and testing only. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to hide, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__get_bus_history
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Reads the recent history of events emitted on the THN Web SDK internal event bus, returning each event name and its arguments. Use this when a THN staff member needs to trace SDK activity — for example to verify that a specific event was fired, to understand the sequence of events leading to a behaviour, or to debug event-driven logic. Results can be filtered by a regex pattern on the event name and limited in count (default 50, most recent events returned last). Note that event arguments containing DOM elements or functions are collapsed to compact placeholders to avoid serialization issues.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return: the most recent ones, listed oldest to newest. Defaults to 50.

filter.description: Optional regex pattern to filter events by name, e.g. "message" or "^booking"

tools.name: thn_site__get_hotel_info
tools.description: Returns basic information about the hotel whose website the guest is currently browsing: its name, website URL, main currency, location, geographic area and type of establishment (for example Hotels, Resorts or Apartments). Use this when the guest asks what this property is, where it is located, or which currency it works in. Any piece of information that is not available is returned as null. Takes no input.

tools.name: thn_site__check_availability
tools.description: Checks whether the hotel has rooms available for the given check-in and check-out dates and room occupancy (adults, children and children ages per room). Use this when the guest asks if there is availability on specific dates. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to check, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__compare_rates
tools.description: Compares the hotel's direct rate with other booking channels for the given dates and rooms. Use this when the guest asks about price comparisons or other booking channels. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to compare rates for, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__get_direct_booking_benefits
tools.description: Describes the benefits of booking directly on the hotel website. Use this when the guest asks about why book direct. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__get_rates
tools.description: Returns the hotel's rates for the given dates and occupancy. Use this when the guest asks about prices. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

rooms.description: The rooms to get rates for, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

tools.name: thn_site__list_amenities
tools.description: Lists the hotel amenities and services. Use this when the guest asks about pool, parking, extras, etc. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__list_rooms
tools.description: Lists the room types the hotel offers. Use this when the guest asks what rooms exist. Currently returns a message saying it is not available yet, with the hotel website URL to continue on.

tools.name: thn_site__start_booking
tools.description: Starts a booking for the given dates and rooms, optionally with a currency, a promo code and a language. Use this when the guest wants to book. Returns a URL to the booking engine where the guest can complete the booking, so open that URL to continue. When a booking URL cannot be built it returns the hotel website URL instead, or null if that is not available either.

rooms.description: The rooms to book, one entry per room

adults.description: Number of adults in the room

children.description: Number of children in the room

childrenAges.description: Age of each child in the room

currencyCode.description: Currency the guest wants to see prices in, as an ISO 4217 code such as USD. When omitted, USD is used

languageCode.description: Language the guest wants the booking engine in, such as en or zh_TW

promoCode.description: Promo code to apply to the booking

promoCodeType.description: Type of the promo code, when known

tools.name: thn_internal__get_state_info
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns a runtime snapshot of the THN Web SDK global state on the current hotel webpage, including property and hotel identifiers, booking system, page name, language, device, SDK version, environment, and hostname. Use this when a THN staff member needs to understand the current SDK context — for example to confirm which property is loaded, which environment is active, or which SDK version is running. Do not use this tool for hotel-guest-facing tasks; it exposes internal SDK identifiers that are not meaningful to end users.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_dom_element
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Finds a DOM element on the current hotel webpage using a CSS selector and returns its innerHTML. Use this when a THN staff member needs to inspect the rendered HTML of a specific element — for example to verify that a THN widget or message is present in the DOM and correctly rendered. Returns found: true with the markup in html when the element exists, or found: false when no matching element exists. This tool does not modify the DOM; use thn_internal__show_message or thn_internal__hide_message to control message visibility.

selector.description: A valid CSS selector identifying the element to inspect, e.g. "#thn-note" or ".thn-widget"

tools.name: thn_internal__list_messages
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Lists all messages currently registered across all THN widget types (note, exit, layer, inliner) on the hotel webpage. Returns each message's ID, name, and the widget it belongs to. Use this as a first step when a THN staff member needs to identify which messages are available before calling thn_internal__get_message_state, thn_internal__show_message, or thn_internal__hide_message. This tool does not filter by visibility or state — it lists all registered messages regardless of whether they are currently shown, hidden, or eligible to display.

tools.name: thn_internal__get_message_state
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Returns the current runtime state of a specific THN message identified by its ID, including flags such as opened, closed, and the widget type it belongs to. Use this when a THN staff member needs to diagnose why a message is or is not displaying — for example to check whether it has already been opened, closed, or is being suppressed. Use thn_internal__list_messages first to discover available message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to inspect, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__show_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Forces a THN message to display on the hotel webpage, bypassing all normal display guards such as frequency caps, triggers, beacons, and eligibility rules. Returns the message's previous and current state after the forced display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to preview or test a specific message regardless of whether it would normally be shown. This tool mutates widget state and stubs internal widget methods for the duration of the call — it is intended for inspection and testing only, not for production user flows. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs, and thn_internal__hide_message to reverse the effect. Throws an error if the message ID is not found.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to force-display, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__hide_message
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Hides a currently displayed THN message on the hotel webpage, either by gracefully animating it out of the DOM (if it is actively rendered) or by marking it as closed in state to prevent future display. Use this when a THN staff member needs to dismiss a message during inspection or testing — for example after using thn_internal__show_message to force-display it. This tool mutates widget and message state; it is intended for inspection and testing only. Use thn_internal__list_messages to find message IDs. Throws an error if the message ID is not found in any widget.

messageId.description: The ID of the message to hide, as returned by thn_internal__list_messages

tools.name: thn_internal__get_bus_history
tools.description: THN internal tool for THN staff. Reads the recent history of events emitted on the THN Web SDK internal event bus, returning each event name and its arguments. Use this when a THN staff member needs to trace SDK activity — for example to verify that a specific event was fired, to understand the sequence of events leading to a behaviour, or to debug event-driven logic. Results can be filtered by a regex pattern on the event name and limited in count (default 50, most recent events returned last). Note that event arguments containing DOM elements or functions are collapsed to compact placeholders to avoid serialization issues.

limit.description: Maximum number of events to return: the most recent ones, listed oldest to newest. Defaults to 50.

filter.description: Optional regex pattern to filter events by name, e.g. "message" or "^booking"

Use this when the guest asks what this property is, where it is located, or which currency it works in. Any piece of information that is not available is returned as null. Takes no input.

sites.name: tryprismlaunch.vercel.app
sites.description: An agent-native launch-video studio for software. You direct; your agent turns the product you built into the film that launches it.

tools.name: prism.read_guide
tools.description: Required first: read SKILL.md and PRISM_METHOD.md before planning, drafting or editing. Call once per document; returns the full current guide. Editing tools require both this session. Re-read relevant sections before stages and revisions.

document.description: Required before work: read SKILL.md for operation and PRISM_METHOD.md for creative method. Call separately for each full guide.

tools.name: prism.get_project_context
tools.description: Read required agent guidance, storage, canvas and process state. Read agentGuidance first: call prism.read_guide for both guides before planning or editing, including when resuming an existing film. Then follow process and the person's notes.

tools.name: prism.create_project
tools.description: Create and open an empty composition in linked storage. Starts with visual/audio tracks and grows as clips are placed. Needs storage setup first. Read both guides with prism.read_guide before work.

slug.description: Folder name to create under .prismlaunch, e.g. 'vector-launch'. (up to 48 chars)

name.description: Human-readable title, e.g. 'Vector launch video'. (up to 80 chars)

durationSeconds.description: Usually omit this. A new composition starts with no runtime and grows automatically as you place clips, so you do not have to guess a length up front. (0.5–300)

tools.name: prism.open_project
tools.description: Show a composition that already exists in the linked folder, by its folder name. Use the slugs from get_project_context. Read both guides with prism.read_guide before work.

slug.description: Folder name under .prismlaunch, as listed by get_project_context. (up to 48 chars)

tools.name: prism.submit_brief
tools.description: Stage 1: audience, message, feeling, length. Gather product assets first. End your turn after submission; only the person approves in Process. Follow PRISM_METHOD.md §5. Read both guides with prism.read_guide before work.

audience.description: One kind of person, specifically. Not 'developers'. (up to 200 chars)

message.description: The one sentence the film has to land. No commas, no 'and'. (up to 200 chars)

feeling.description: One word: what they should feel. Relief, envy, recognition, calm. (up to 40 chars)

lengthSeconds.description: 15 is one idea, 30 is one idea with a turn, 45 is an idea with an escalation. (5–180)

summary.description: One sentence on what you did and why. Shown to the person beside the artifact. (up to 300 chars)

tools.name: prism.submit_concepts
tools.description: Stage 2: submit 2–4 directions, scored with the six tests, and recommend one. Requires approved brief. PRISM_METHOD.md §5. Read both guides with prism.read_guide before work.

id.description: Short handle, e.g. 'c1'. (up to 40 chars)

line.description: The idea in one sentence with no 'and'. (up to 200 chars)

angle.description: Which lever produced it: 'the enemy', 'before/after', 'the contrast'… (up to 40 chars)

score.description: Out of 12, from the six tests in PRISM_METHOD.md §5. (0–12)

directions.description: Two to four directions. Three is right. Generated from 8–12 angles, not the first one. (2–4 items)

recommended.description: The id of the one you recommend. (up to 40 chars)

summary.description: One sentence on what you did and why. Shown to the person beside the artifact. (up to 300 chars)

tools.name: prism.submit_script
tools.description: Stage 3: submit timed beats and optional voiceover. Timing follows events. Requires approved concept. PRISM_METHOD.md §1, §6. Read both guides with prism.read_guide before work.

id.description: (up to 40 chars)

label.description: 'Hook', 'Reveal', 'Proof 1'… (up to 40 chars)

words.description: On-screen text in runs of 1–4 words per line; one accent word. PRISM_METHOD.md §6. (up to 160 chars)

seconds.description: Derive from visual events, never a preset budget. Usually 2–4 seconds per section, averaging two events per second. PRISM_METHOD.md §1. (0.3–20)

sound.description: What the music or SFX does here. (up to 140 chars)

beats.description: The film as connected visual events. Around 10–12 sections for 30 seconds; let the actual events determine length. PRISM_METHOD.md §1. (2–14 items)

voiceover.description: The full VO if there is one. Never the same words as on screen. (up to 800 chars)

summary.description: One sentence on what you did and why. Shown to the person beside the artifact. (up to 300 chars)

tools.name: prism.submit_storyboard
tools.description: Stage 4: DRAW every shot with required visual.layers (positioned UI, images, subjects, words, cursors and keyframes), plus action, duration, handoff and sound. Section titles alone are not boards. Read SKILL.md Visual storyboards. Requires approved script. Read both guides with prism.read_guide before work.

id.description: (up to 40 chars)

beatId.description: The script beat this boards. (up to 40 chars)

label.description: 'Hook', 'Reveal', 'Proof 1'… (up to 40 chars)

frame.description: What is on screen: ground, composition, type role, the product if shown. A sentence a designer could draw from. (up to 280 chars)

action.description: The events, in order, with frames: what arrives, what it does, what leaves. 'Line pops in 6f, holds 18f, out 5f; phone flies in 20f, drifts.' (up to 240 chars)

handoff.description: What is still on screen when the next panel starts — the object that carries the cut. 'The phone, flying left, dragging the bar.' (up to 140 chars)

durationInFrames.description: At 30fps: the SUM of the events' frames in `action`, never a budget chosen first. Then nudged onto the beat grid once you have chosen music. (6–9000)

sound.description: What the music or SFX does here. (up to 140 chars)

words.description: The on-screen words, if any. Under seven. (up to 160 chars)

id.description: (up to 40 chars)

label.description: What this object represents; describe missing footage honestly. (up to 80 chars)

text.description: (up to 240 chars)

src.description: An imported image under assets/ or a library/ image. Never invent a screenshot path. (up to 200 chars)

fontSize.description: Fraction of canvas height. (0.015–0.4; defaults to 0.055)

until.description: Exclusive end frame; omit to remain until the cut. (1–9000)

keyframes.description: Ordered target poses at shot-local frames. Omitted pose fields keep their preceding value. hold makes a cut. (0–8 items; defaults to [])

layers.description: Back to front. Draw the actual shot: subjects, UI regions, text and movement, not its section title. (1–32 items)

visual.description: REQUIRED shot composition. Position real screenshots or labelled rough subjects, type, arrows and cursors. Keyframes show changes within the shot. Section titles alone are not boards.

panels.description: One panel per script beat, in order. Board the first, then the last, then fill between. (2–40 items)

summary.description: One sentence on what you did and why. Shown to the person beside the artifact. (up to 300 chars)

tools.name: prism.lay_animatic
tools.description: Optional planning scaffold: copy approved boards to the Boards track. Re-running replaces that track. Before animatic review, replace all roughs with approved style elements and remove/hide Boards; this tool does not build finished shots. Requires approved storyboard. Read both guides with prism.read_guide before work.

tools.name: prism.submit_animatic
tools.description: Stage 6: submit all shots in the approved visual style with continuous music. Visible storyboard roughs are refused. Watch playback with sound first; still captures cannot verify audio or stalls. Human approval locks timing. Requires approved style frames. PRISM_METHOD.md §10. Read both guides with prism.read_guide before work.

summary.description: One sentence on what you did and why. Shown to the person beside the artifact. (up to 300 chars)

tools.name: prism.submit_style_frames
tools.description: Stage 5: submit the look, elements and 2–3 real clips (hook, reveal, endcard). Requires approved storyboard. PRISM_METHOD.md §7. Read both guides with prism.read_guide before work.

look.description: Which look from PRISM_METHOD.md §7 — kinetic, void, paper, editorial or spec — or 'custom' if you built your own.

items.description: (up to 60 chars)

elementIds.description: The elements the look is made of — at least the headline style. From prism.add_element. (1–60 items)

items.description: (up to 60 chars)

clipIds.description: The clips you built for real — the hook, the reveal, the endcard. Everything else copies these. (1–12 items)

summary.description: One sentence on what you did and why. Shown to the person beside the artifact. (up to 300 chars)

tools.name: prism.submit_build
tools.description: Stage 8: submit the finished film with placeholders replaced and sound placed. Requires approved polish. After human approval, request_render. PRISM_METHOD.md §10. Read both guides with prism.read_guide before work.

summary.description: One sentence on what you did and why. Shown to the person beside the artifact. (up to 300 chars)

tools.name: prism.submit_polish
tools.description: Stage 7: submit checklist verdicts and revised sound plan after reviewing the rough with sound, muted and half size. Requires approved animatic. PRISM_METHOD.md §9, §12. Read both guides with prism.read_guide before work.

items.description: (up to 200 chars)

checklist.description: Each line of the §12 checklist you ran against the rough, with its verdict: '✓ two events per second', '✗ the cut at f240 has no handoff — the phone now carries it'. (1–80 items)

soundPlan.description: The sound, rethought against the person's notes: the filled-in plan from PRISM_METHOD.md §9. The build places it. (up to 1600 chars)

summary.description: One sentence on what you did and why. Shown to the person beside the artifact. (up to 300 chars)

tools.name: prism.wait_for_decision
tools.description: Read the submitted stage’s human decision and note. Call once when the person returns after review. Do not poll: submit, end your turn and ask for review. Read-only.

stage.description: Which stage to wait on. Default: the one that is submitted and waiting.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long to wait before returning "still waiting", so you can call again. Default 25, kept short so the call fits any harness. (1–600)

tools.name: prism.use_toolset
tools.description: Switch the visible PrismLaunch tools. workflow: project and 8 stages; graphics: tracks, text, shapes, icons, particles; media: HTML, devices, image, video, audio; elements: reusable styles/library/place; edit: update clips, canvas, preview, capture and render. Call again whenever another set is needed, then fetch tools again.

sites.name: u9itus.com
sites.description: U9itus exposes civic-research tools to AI agents via WebMCP: find candidates, pull a dossier, compare candidates, list ballot measures, look up elections, and submit candidate leads.

tools.name: u9itus_current_page
tools.description: Describe the u9itus.dev page the user is currently viewing (page type, and the candidate in focus if any). Call this first to ground follow-up civic questions. On the map (page_type "map"), call u9itus_map_view for the place on screen; on the comparison page ("compare"), call u9itus_comparison_view.

tools.name: u9itus_find_candidates
tools.description: Search u9itus published candidate and elected-official profiles by name and/or filters. Use for questions like 'who is running for X in Y', 'Texas candidates funded by AIPAC', or to resolve a name mentioned in an article to a u9itus profile (each result has a uuid for u9itus_get_candidate). The response includes `total` (all matches), `count` (this page), and `next_offset` — to get every match, keep calling with `offset: next_offset` until it is null. When `funded_by` is set, each result also carries a `funding_match` array citing the specific contributors / PACs and dollar amounts.

q.description: Name or partial name to search for.

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. CA.

governance_level.description: federal | state | county | municipal (as stored on the profile).

running.description: true = only active candidates; false = only seated officials.

funded_by.description: Keep only candidates whose FEC / OpenSecrets donor snapshot shows money from this source — a PAC, committee, advocacy group (e.g. 'AIPAC'), industry, or contributor name. Naming a known advocacy group also matches its aligned PACs. Matched results include a `funding_match` array with the named sources and amounts.

limit.description: Results per page (default 10, max 20).

offset.description: Skip this many matches — pass the previous response's next_offset to page.

tools.name: u9itus_get_candidate
tools.description: Full civic dossier for one candidate by uuid: office, party, district, bio, official links, transparency IDs (FEC/OpenSecrets/Ballotpedia/Vote Smart), recent verified news, donor snapshot, and upcoming elections in their state.

tools.name: u9itus_compare_candidates
tools.description: Return full dossiers for 2–4 candidates at once (by uuid) so you can present a structured side-by-side comparison.

tools.name: u9itus_list_ballot_measures
tools.description: List US ballot measures (always state/county scoped) with plain-language yes/no meanings. Filter by state, free-text, and status (upcoming|passed|failed). Each result carries a `read_more` link ({label, url}) to the full legal text and fiscal analysis — cite it when the user asks about detail the summary omits (eligibility thresholds, dollar amounts, funding source, repayment terms). If a state has none yet, the response includes a `backfill` block (status queued|in_progress|unavailable) — relay its message and offer u9itus_watch_ballot_measures.

state.description: Two-letter US state code.

q.description: Free-text match on title or measure number.

tools.name: u9itus_watch_ballot_measures
tools.description: When u9itus_list_ballot_measures reports no measures for a state, register an email to be notified once that state's measures are published. Confirm the email with the user first.

state.description: Two-letter US state code.

email.description: Where to send the one-time notification.

tools.name: u9itus_upcoming_elections
tools.description: Upcoming election stages (primary, general, runoff) and candidate filing deadlines for a US state.

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX.

tools.name: u9itus_list_races
tools.description: List the races in a US state that have confirmed running candidates — who is running against whom — with each election date. Each race carries `compare`: pass it as the arguments to u9itus_open_comparison to open the side-by-side comparison and its printable voter guide. Filter with `q`: an office, a district such as CA-12, a city, or a candidate's name.

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. CA.

q.description: Keep races whose office, district, city or candidate names contain this text.

limit.description: Races to return (default 20, max 50).

tools.name: u9itus_open_comparison
tools.description: Open u9itus's side-by-side comparison of candidates for the same seat (up to 3 people), which includes a printable, source-referenced voter guide. Pass a race's `compare` object from u9itus_list_races, or a state and congressional district, or a state and a candidate's full_name (plus office) for statewide and local seats. It checks the comparison first: when none is available it says why and stays on this page. Otherwise it returns the seat and its candidates, then navigates this tab to the comparison. With no `selected`, it picks running candidates first, up to 3; tell the user who was left out.

state.description: Two-letter US state code.

district.description: Congressional district for a U.S. House race, e.g. CA-12 or 12.

office.description: Office, e.g. Governor or Mayor. Optional for House races.

full_name.description: A candidate on the seat. Needed when there is no district.

selected.description: Candidate keys to include, from u9itus_list_races `running` or a previous comparison.

tools.name: u9itus_latest_candidate_news
tools.description: Most recent verified news about candidates / officials across every published profile, newest first. Use this for 'what's the latest candidate news' or 'which candidate is in the news' — it answers in one call instead of opening dossiers one by one. Every item links to the original story (`source_url`) and identifies the candidate, including their `profile_url`. Filter by state, topic, or headline text.

state.description: Two-letter US state code.

topic.description: Restrict to a single topic key, e.g. 'economy'.

tools.name: u9itus_submit_candidate_lead
tools.description: Report a candidate you spotted (e.g. named in an article the user is reading) who may be missing from u9itus. This does NOT publish anything — the lead is queued as 'pending' for human verification. Always confirm with the user before calling.

state.description: Two-letter US state code, if known.

office_hint.description: Office they are seeking, e.g. 'US House NC-06'.

source_url.description: URL of the article / page the candidate was found on.

context.description: Short quote or summary giving evidence (max ~2000 chars).

tools.name: u9itus_map_view
tools.description: What the u9itus U.S. map is showing right now: level (overview, region, state or district), the state and congressional district in focus, which data layers are on, and a share_url for this view. Call it before describing the map or after the user moves it. To research the place, pass the state to u9itus_find_candidates, u9itus_upcoming_elections or u9itus_list_ballot_measures.

tools.name: u9itus_map_show
tools.description: Move the u9itus U.S. map the user is looking at. Give a state (optionally with a congressional district) to fly there and open its panel of officials and candidates; give only a region to show that region; give nothing to return to the national overview. `district` is a congressional district number only. For a state, county or city candidate, pass `state` and `candidate` without a district. Returns the new view, plus `candidate_opened` when a candidate was asked for.

state.description: Two-letter code or full name, e.g. "CA" or "California".

district.description: Congressional district number, e.g. "12" or "CA-12". Use "AL" for at-large states. Requires state.

region.description: Show a whole region. Ignored when state is given.

candidate.description: Open this candidate's card once the state's panel loads: the profile_url from u9itus_find_candidates, or its /p/{slug} slug. Requires state.

tools.name: u9itus_map_find_district
tools.description: Find the congressional district for a U.S. street address or 5-digit ZIP code and show it on the map with its officials and candidates. Only use an address the user gave you for this lookup. It is matched with the U.S. Census geocoder; u9itus does not save it or put it in the URL. A full street address is exact. A ZIP can cover several districts: then the map does not move and `choices` lists them, so ask the user for their street address or which district, then call u9itus_map_show.

address.description: Street address with city, state and ZIP (e.g. "1000 San Pablo Ave, Albany, CA 94706"), or a 5-digit ZIP code.

tools.name: u9itus_map_set_layer
tools.description: Turn a data layer on the u9itus U.S. map on or off. Layers: districts (Congressional district lines across all 50 states.); party (Color states by the party of the current governor (replaces poverty coloring).); poverty (Color states by poverty rate, Census ACS 5-year (replaces party coloring).); population (Shade congressional districts by resident population. Needs a state open.); cities (Incorporated city and town boundaries. Needs a state open.); topcities (Top cities by 2020 Census population and state government offices. Needs a state open.); candidates (Statewide candidates at each state capital. sites.name: wadi.house
sites.description: Wadi: 3D Home Designer

tools.name: wadi_wdl_reference
tools.description: A self-contained primer for Wadi's .wdl design language and the authoring loop. Call this FIRST before writing WDL.

tools.name: wadi_get_wdl
tools.description: Return the current live house as editable .wdl source. Read this before modifying an existing design.

tools.name: wadi_set_wdl
tools.description: Compile .wdl and load it into the live 3D model. STRONGLY PREFER EDITING A TEMPLATE over building from scratch: wadi_list_homes -> wadi_choose_home (closest match) -> wadi_get_wdl -> edit -> wadi_set_wdl. Authoring a whole house from a blank .wdl is error-prone (wall alignment, roof sizing, cantilever support, staircase); only do it if no template fits. On a compile/schema error the model is unchanged and errors are returned; on success returns the structural check — READ IT AND FIX WARNINGS before telling the user it is ready. Loop: get -> edit -> set -> fix -> repeat.

tools.name: wadi_check_wdl
tools.description: Compile-check .wdl WITHOUT loading it (dry run). Returns errors, or ok.

tools.name: wadi_list_modules
tools.description: List the custom component modules registered for the current model (import ref + source size). These reusable component .wdl files are saved inside the .wadi. Inbuilt packs (std-furniture, konkan/base) are always available and are not listed.

tools.name: wadi_add_module
tools.description: Register (or replace) a reusable component module by its import ref, then recompile the live model. The module is a .wdl holding `component Name { … }` definitions in LOCAL coords (no `house` block). After adding, `import "ref" as ns` in the main WDL (wadi_set_wdl) and place it with `use ns.Name at (x,y)`. Saved inside the .wadi so the design is self-contained. Returns the structural check.

ref.description: the import ref, e.g. "dining-set"

tools.name: wadi_remove_module
tools.description: Remove a custom component module by its import ref and recompile. Also remove its `import` line from the main WDL if the component is no longer used.

ref.description: the import ref to remove

tools.name: wadi_list_homes
tools.description: List the ready-made home designs to start from (id, title, meta).

tools.name: wadi_choose_home
tools.description: Load one ready-made home by id (from wadi_list_homes) as your STARTING POINT — pick the one closest to what the user wants, then read it with wadi_get_wdl and edit it. This is the recommended way to begin; it is far more reliable than authoring from scratch.

id.description: template id, e.g. family_home

tools.name: wadi_read_home
tools.description: Return a ready-made home's .wdl source WITHOUT loading it — study an example (how it does a roof, staircase, grid, etc.) without disturbing the user's current model. Use this to look things up; use wadi_choose_home only when you actually want to start from that home. Ids come from wadi_list_homes.

id.description: template id, e.g. family_home

tools.name: wadi_describe_house
tools.description: The whole house as structured data (floors, rooms with sizes/positions in feet, connections, roof, plot, variables, staircases, and a structural summary). Read this to understand the current design. The `staircases` array reports each stair's flight count, climb direction, the top-landing rectangle (where you step onto the floor) with its facing, and the min box length for 1 and 2 flights — use it to size and orient stairs.

tools.name: wadi_check
tools.description: Run the C1-C12 structural linter over the live house and return errors + warnings.

tools.name: wadi_capture_view
tools.description: Render the current 3D model to a PNG image so you can see the result.

tools.name: wadi_undo
tools.description: Undo the last change.

tools.name: wadi_redo
tools.description: Redo the last undone change.

sites.name: webconverter.app
sites.description: WebConverter is a complete WebMCP server: AI agents can convert images, build and merge PDFs, OCR scans, extract PDF text, convert documents with Pandoc, transcribe audio with Whisper, remove image…

tools.name: convert_image
tools.description: Convert an image to another format entirely in the browser — no upload. WASM importers accept BMP, DDS, GIF, HDR, ICO, JPEG, KTX, PGM, PIC, PNG, PPM, PSD, TGA, WebP; a browser-decode fallback adds HEIC (Safari/iOS), AVIF, GIF and more. Outputs PNG, JPEG, BMP, TGA, HDR, EXR, KTX2 or WebP.

tools.name: images_to_pdf
tools.description: Combine one or more images into a single PDF, one image per page, in order, in the browser.

tools.name: images_to_searchable_pdf
tools.description: Combine images into a PDF *and* run OCR (Tesseract.js, lazy-loaded) so the resulting PDF has selectable, searchable text on top of the original pixels. Useful for scans and screenshots.

tools.name: merge_pdfs
tools.description: Merge multiple PDF files into a single PDF (all pages, in order) — in the browser, no upload.

tools.name: reorder_pdf_pages
tools.description: Reorder the pages of a single PDF and write a new PDF with the given order. pageOrder is an array of zero-based source-page indices, in the desired order.

tools.name: delete_pdf_pages
tools.description: Drop the listed zero-based page indices from a PDF, writing a new PDF of the remaining pages, in their original order.

tools.name: extract_pdf_text
tools.description: Pull text out of a PDF (pdf.js) — plain text by default, or simple Markdown with one `## Page N` heading per page when `asMarkdown: true`.

tools.name: convert_document
tools.description: Convert a document between formats with Pandoc (WebAssembly). Common inputs: docx, odt, rtf, html, markdown, latex, rst, mediawiki, epub. Common outputs: markdown, html, plain, latex, rst, asciidoc, docx, odt. The first call lazily downloads Pandoc WASM (~56 MB); it is cached afterwards.

tools.name: convert_audio
tools.description: Convert an audio file — or extract the audio track from a video — to MP3, OGG, WAV or FLAC. Decoding uses the browser's codecs, so anything the browser can play is accepted.

tools.name: convert_video
tools.description: Transcode a video to MP4 (H.264 + AAC), WebM (VP9 + Opus) or animated GIF using ffmpeg-wasm in the browser. The first call lazily downloads the ffmpeg core for the chosen output (~30 MB per variant); cached afterwards.

config.description: Optional: resolution ('WxH'|'original'), fps, videoBitrate, audioBitrate, muteAudio.

tools.name: trim_video
tools.description: Cut a clip from startTime → endTime (seconds) out of a video using ffmpeg-wasm, without re-uploading anything. Output is MP4 by default.

tools.name: remove_image_background
tools.description: Produce a version of the image with the background made transparent (or a chosen colour). Uses a tiny U²-Net-P ONNX model (≈4 MB) for the initial mask, then a deterministic WASM matting pass to clean the edges. Output is PNG (default) or WebP — both preserve transparency.

tools.name: transcribe_audio
tools.description: Transcribe an audio file — or the audio track of a video — to text with timestamps using a quantised Whisper model (whisper.cpp compiled to WASM). Runs entirely in the browser. The first call downloads the model (~40 MB) once, then caches it. English by default; the bundled model is English-only.

tools.name: convert_3d_to_gltf
tools.description: Convert a 3D scene (FBX, OBJ, DAE, PLY, STL, GLTF, GLB, 3DS, LWO, BLEND, X, MS3D, ASE) to glTF 2.0 or binary GLB, entirely in the browser. Native magnum-plugins importers handle the mainstream formats (ufbx for FBX/OBJ, GltfImporter for glTF/GLB, StanfordImporter for PLY, StlImporter for STL, OpenGexImporter for OGEX); Assimp is the fallback for the long tail (DAE, 3DS, LWO, BLEND, X, …). Output is written by Magnum's GltfSceneConverter. Optional MeshOptimizer pass re-encodes meshes for the GPU vertex cache and can simplify them by a target ratio. Lazy-loads the matching WASM module per family.

fileName.description: Original filename; the extension is used to pick the importer.

outputFormat.description: glTF (JSON + embedded buffers) or GLB (single compact binary). Defaults to gltf.

optimize.description: Run MeshOptimizer vertex-cache / overdraw / vertex-fetch passes on every mesh.

simplifyRatio.description: Fraction of triangles to KEEP, 0..1. 0 or 1 disables simplification.

tools.name: list_supported_formats
tools.description: Enumerate every format and tool WebConverter exposes via WebMCP.

Also sets oscillators.N.enabled = true. ### width { op: "width", amount: 0..1, method?: "unison" | "pan" | "stereo_fx" | "auto" } auto (default): unison below 0.6; unison + stereo_fx at or above 0.6 unison: oscillators.0.unisonVoices = clamp(round(1 + amount*8), 1, 8) oscillators.0.unisonDetune = amount*0.…

tools.name: create_patch
tools.description: Create contrasting A/B proposals by default so unresolved, subjective, exploratory, or character-choice directions can be auditioned simultaneously rather than guessed. Examples include warm bass harmonic profile (rounded sub-heavy sine versus saturated analog saw) and dreamy pad motion (slow strings versus gated ambient). A high-impact but unambiguous replacement may be direct: set singleProposal to true only for an exact, settled, or explicitly single request. Paired creation requires a named comparisonAxis, replaces any prior B, and leaves A active. This is comparison, not undo; use undo only to reverse an already committed transaction.

budget.description: Presupuesto total con cargos conocidos

tools.name: select_tire

tools.name: prepare_quote

warehouseId.description: ID exacto de un local del stock visible

tools.name: search_vehicle_batteries

applicationId.description: ID exacto de una aplicación descubierta en la sesión

tools.name: select_battery
tools.description: Selecciona una batería de los resultados actuales solo después de que el usuario confirme ese producto. Elegir una aplicación de vehículo no confirma una batería alternativa. Si también indicó una localidad, guarda su ID exacto.

locationId.description: ID exacto de una localidad del producto visible

tools.name: prepare_battery_quote
tools.description: Prepara una cotización y selecciona la batería; requiere que el usuario confirme este producto, la cantidad y la localidad. Elegir una aplicación de vehículo no confirma una batería alternativa. Valida inventario. La localidad puede ser un punto de retiro o A domicilio.

locationId.description: ID exacto de la localidad visible elegida, incluida A domicilio

tools.name: read_battery_catalog
tools.description: Devuelve las fichas locales con IDs, Ah, CCA, dimensiones, polaridad y precio para que tú compares según las especificaciones respaldadas o la petición del usuario. No requiere vehículo ni prueba compatibilidad. No filtra ni decide similitud. Devuelve listingId para presentar alternativas; reutiliza uiState.batteryListing vigente.

tools.name: present_battery_alternatives
tools.description: Muestra entre una y cinco baterías que tú elegiste al comparar sus fichas. Requiere listingId y batteryIds de read_battery_catalog vigente en esta sesión. Mantiene tu orden; no selecciona ni cotiza productos, ni verifica compatibilidad con vehículos. Devuelve fichas completas con localidades e inventario.

tools.name: start_card_checkout
tools.description: Abre directamente el formulario después de cotizar con éxito, sin preguntar si desea abrirlo y sin cobrar. Requiere producto y cantidad ya confirmados y cotizados, y modalidad elegida por el usuario. Usa los IDs exactos del producto cotizado. Para baterías la modalidad debe corresponder a su localidad cotizada. El usuario completa datos de facturación y pulsa Pagar; para delivery, el formulario solicita su ubicación y guarda automáticamente las coordenadas y dirección. Puede corregir el pin y los textos sin confirmación adicional. No pidas datos de tarjeta en el chat.

tools.name: get_checkout_context
tools.description: Devuelve la cotización de pago, ubicación guardada y transacción actuales. No inicia ni confirma un pago. Úsala para obtener el contexto verificado y el transactionId antes de consultar su estado.

tools.name: get_payment_status
tools.description: Consulta el estado guardado por el backend para el transactionId de get_checkout_context. Solo VALIDATED acredita el resultado aprobado; PENDING no lo confirma. mode distingue simulación local de PagoPlux sandbox.

tools.name: request_advisor_handoff
tools.description: Transfiere la conversación actual a un asesor humano con su contexto. Úsala cuando el usuario lo solicite explícitamente o acepte una sugerencia de escalamiento.
