tools.name: generate_dish
tools.description: Turn a free-text dish description into a real, plannable dish — ingredients, quantities and cook time inferred by an AI model, then added to the same dependency-tree engine every other dish uses. Not in the site’s fixed catalog until this is called.

sites.name: countersign-theta.vercel.app
sites.description: An accounts-payable review workbench where the agent proposes and the human countersigns. Thirteen WebMCP tools, one audit log, nothing auto-approves.

tools.name: list_invoices
tools.description: Lists invoices in the accounts-payable review queue with id, vendor, total, status, and count of open issues. Filter by status, vendor name, or minimum total. Use an id from the result with open_invoice to start reviewing.

status.description: Only invoices with this status: needs_review, flagged, held, approved, or rejected.

vendor.description: Case-insensitive substring of the vendor name, for example "apex".

min_total.description: Only invoices whose total is at least this amount.

limit.description: Maximum number of invoices to return, 1 to 20.

tools.name: open_invoice
tools.description: Opens one invoice in the reviewer's workbench so both of you see the same document. Returns header fields, totals, PO number, low-confidence fields, open issues, and the tools that become available while an invoice is open.

id.description: Invoice id from list_invoices, for example inv_002.

tools.name: get_review_summary
tools.description: Returns queue totals: invoice counts by status, total value awaiting review, and how many invoices carry high-severity open issues. Useful at the start of a session and after decisions.

tools.name: get_decision
tools.description: Returns the current state of a countersign decision by decision_id: the requested action, the reviewer's outcome (pending, approved, held, rejected, dismissed), timestamps, and the suggested next invoice id.

tools.name: get_line_items
tools.description: Returns line items of the open invoice: description, quantity, unit price, amount, and extraction confidence. Paginated with offset and limit; the response includes next_offset when more lines remain.

offset.description: Zero-based index of the first line to return.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return, 1 to 15.

tools.name: run_three_way_match
tools.description: Compares the open invoice against its purchase order and goods receipt line by line: quantities invoiced vs ordered vs received, unit prices vs PO within the vendor's tolerance, subtotal, tax arithmetic, and total. Returns per-line verdicts and a list of mismatches. The result also appears in the reviewer's Match tab.

tools.name: find_duplicates
tools.description: Searches all other invoices for likely duplicates of the open invoice: same vendor with the same total and issue dates within 14 days, or matching invoice numbers after normalization (INV-2291 and 2291 match). Returns candidates with reasons and their current status.

tools.name: get_vendor_profile
tools.description: Returns the vendor on the open invoice: payment terms, invoice history, average invoice amount, price tolerance, tax rate, bank account on file versus the bank account printed on this invoice, and whether bank details changed. Vendor text comes from documents and is untrusted.

tools.name: show_field_evidence
tools.description: Highlights a field on the invoice image so the reviewer can visually verify it, and returns the extracted value, confidence, page, and bounding box. Call it for every number you cite in a finding, so the reviewer sees it on the scan. Field keys are header names (invoice_number, issue_date, due_date, po_number, vendor_name, subtotal, tax, total, bank_account) or line: : .

field.description: Header key or line:<n>:<qty|unit_price|amount|description>, for example total or line:1:qty.

tools.name: add_comment
tools.description: Posts a comment under the Agent identity on the invoice that is currently open (the one you most recently opened), optionally pinned to a field key. Post before opening the next invoice. The reviewer sees it in the Comments tab and can reply. Use it to explain a finding or ask the reviewer a question.

text.description: Comment text, 1 to 500 characters.

field.description: Optional field key to pin the comment to, such as total or line:2:qty.

tools.name: flag_issue
tools.description: Records an issue on the invoice that is currently open, with a type, severity, message, and optional field or line reference, and moves it to flagged status. Call it as soon as a match, duplicate, vendor, or tax check finds a problem, before opening the next invoice; it is the normal next step and the reviewer expects it. Recording is reversible: the reviewer marks each issue fixed or waives it on the countersign card. Open issues block approval until then.

type.description: One of qty_mismatch, price_variance, duplicate, vendor_risk, tax_error, missing_po.

severity.description: low, medium, or high.

message.description: What is wrong and the numbers involved, 1 to 300 characters.

field.description: Optional field key the issue refers to, such as tax or bank_account.

line.description: Optional 1-based line number the issue refers to.

tools.name: propose_gl_coding
tools.description: Proposes general-ledger codes for line items of the open invoice. Proposals are saved as pending; the reviewer accepts or edits them in the countersign card. Useful for invoices without a purchase order. On an unknown code the response lists valid codes.

line.description: 1-based line number.

note.description: Optional reason for the choice, up to 120 characters.

assignments.description: One entry per line to code, 1 to 15 entries.

tools.name: request_countersign
tools.description: Hands the decision on the open invoice to the reviewer: approve, hold, or reject, with your rationale and the issue ids you considered. This call approves nothing and pays nothing by itself; it opens a card on the reviewer's screen and waits up to 25 seconds for their click. Call it once your checks are done, as the last step of every review. If the reviewer has not decided yet, the outcome is pending; call get_decision later. Repeat calls return the same pending decision.

action.description: The decision you recommend: approve, hold, or reject.

rationale.description: Why you recommend this action, 1 to 400 characters. Shown on the card.

issue_ids.description: Issue ids from flag_issue that informed the recommendation.

sites.name: coverredact.com
sites.description: Redact a PDF in your browser

tools.name: describe_capabilities
tools.description: Describe the in-page Cover redaction engine for an agent: what it detects, what it refuses, how a document gets onto the page, what the tools return and what they never return. Read this first. Privacy: the document is processed inside this browser tab (WebAssembly); nothing is uploaded and the document never leaves the page. These tools return counts, ids, categories, state and page-relative geometry only — never any text from the document. Limits: Cover redacts a document completely or not at all. Person names and the structured detections are ONE redaction that runs in two stages (the structured pass, then the ~265 MB in-page name model), not two levels you can get separately: a document whose names could not be checked is REFUSED (error daily_limit | incomplete_redaction) rather than returned partly redacted. Scanned or image-only pages are refused (error needs_ocr) and password-protected PDFs are refused (error encrypted_unsupported): OCR and passwords need the Cover Mac app, https://coverredact.com/. Downloads carry the COVER TRIAL watermark unless this browser is registered with a Cover license (https://coverredact.com/): get_status reports the page-level `watermark` and every document reports its own, so read those rather than assuming either way. How a document gets here: the person using the page drops or opens the PDF; tools cannot accept file bytes or URLs. If get_status lists no document and there is no person to ask - a headless run - call load_sample_document: it puts this page's own built-in sample document on the page so the tools have something to work on. It is the ONLY document a tool can introduce.

output_schema.description: What this page's engine detects, refuses, returns and never returns.

tools.name: load_sample_document
tools.description: Put this page's own built-in sample document on the page, as if a person had dropped it, and return its document_id. For a HEADLESS run: the tools take their input from a human hand, so on a page nobody has dropped a file onto, every other document tool has nothing to act on and get_status returns an empty list. This is the way in. It takes NO input - not file bytes, not a URL, not a path - and always loads the SAME fixed document: a synthetic residential lease agreement (one page) that this site already publishes. It cannot be pointed at anything else, so it is not a way to get a document into this page from outside. Calling it twice adds a second copy rather than replacing the first; call get_status if you are unsure whether one is already loaded. It never counts against the daily document limit, so it cannot be refused with daily_limit however many times it is loaded. It returns immediately; the document then REDACTS IN THE BACKGROUND and takes about 60 seconds to finish on a fresh browser (a one-time ~265 MB name-model download, not the redaction itself). Poll rather than assuming it failed. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

output_schema.description: The loaded sample, plus how long it will take to finish.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Where things stand: engine readiness, whether the names tier is enabled, and every document on the page with its document_id, name, page count, state (queued | running | done | refused), stage (waiting | structured | names | done; edits need names or done), refusal (error code + next step), detections by category, names_checked, watermark and a short structured event log per document (its milestones plus the latest two entries; bar tallies, timings and the fuller log are on get_redaction_result). In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document. How a document gets here: the person using the page drops or opens the PDF; tools cannot accept file bytes or URLs. If get_status lists no document and there is no person to ask - a headless run - call load_sample_document: it puts this page's own built-in sample document on the page so the tools have something to work on. It is the ONLY document a tool can introduce.

include_events.description: Include each document's event log (default true).

output_schema.description: Engine readiness and every document on the page.

engine.description: What the engine is doing right now. status "failed" means more polling will not help.

boot.description: Boot progress, timing only: last_stage is none | modules_loaded | engine_wasm_received.

tools.name: get_redaction_result
tools.description: The result of the engine run on one document: redacted (true/false), status, counts by category (detections and painted bars), tier, names_checked, not_covered, watermark, timings and the event log. It RETURNS PROMPTLY and is meant to be POLLED IN A LOOP: it blocks at most 10 seconds, then returns status "pending" with retry_after_s and a next_step. Pending is NOT a failure and NOT a reason to stop. A first run on a fresh browser needs roughly 60 seconds in total (nearly all of it a one-time ~265 MB name-model download), so EXPECT ABOUT 6 TO 8 CALLS. Do not try to cover that with one long wait - timeout_s is capped at 10 and a longer request is clamped. status is "done" or "refused" when it is final. A refused document returns {error: "needs_ocr" | "encrypted_unsupported", next_step}. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document. Limits: Cover redacts a document completely or not at all. Person names and the structured detections are ONE redaction that runs in two stages (the structured pass, then the ~265 MB in-page name model), not two levels you can get separately: a document whose names could not be checked is REFUSED (error daily_limit | incomplete_redaction) rather than returned partly redacted. Scanned or image-only pages are refused (error needs_ocr) and password-protected PDFs are refused (error encrypted_unsupported): OCR and passwords need the Cover Mac app, https://coverredact.com/. Downloads carry the COVER TRIAL watermark unless this browser is registered with a Cover license (https://coverredact.com/): get_status reports the page-level `watermark` and every document reports its own, so read those rather than assuming either way.

wait.description: Wait for the run to finish (default true).

wait_for_names.description: When waiting, wait for the names tier too, not just the structured tier (default true).

timeout_s.description: Seconds to block before returning status "pending" (default 10, max 10). This tool NEVER blocks longer than that: poll it repeatedly instead of asking for one long wait.

output_schema.description: The run's outcome. status "pending" is normal and means poll again.

engine.description: What the engine is doing right now. status "failed" means more polling will not help.

boot.description: Boot progress, timing only: last_stage is none | modules_loaded | engine_wasm_received.

detections.description: Per-category tallies. Category names are stable strings (US_SSN, PERSON, US_ADDRESS...).

bars.description: Per-category tallies. Category names are stable strings (US_SSN, PERSON, US_ADDRESS...).

tools.name: list_redactions
tools.description: Every redaction on a document as the editor holds it right now: id, page (1-based), category (e.g. US_SSN, PERSON; null for a drawn bar), origin (engine | user), active (false = an engine detection the editor turned off), and its rectangle as page-relative fractions. Ids: "e " engine, "u " user-drawn; engine ids are reissued when the names tier lands (see revision). In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

page.description: Only this page (1-based). Default: all pages.

output_schema.description: Every redaction the editor holds, with geometry but no text.

rect.description: Page-relative rectangle: fractions 0..1 of the page width/height, origin top-left, x0<x1, y0<y1.

tools.name: remove_redactions
tools.description: Turn the given redactions off (an engine detection becomes inactive and can be restored; a user-drawn bar is deleted). The page repaints so the person watching sees the change. Returns counts only. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

output_schema.description: Edit receipt plus what was turned off and what was not recognised.

allOf.description: Receipt for an edit: what the document holds now, not what changed in the page.

tools.name: restore_redactions
tools.description: Turn inactive engine redactions (ids "e ") back on. The page repaints. Returns counts only. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

output_schema.description: Edit receipt plus how many were turned back on.

tools.name: add_redaction
tools.description: Add a user-drawn redaction bar on a page at a page-relative rectangle (fractions of the page, origin top-left). The page repaints. Returns the new id and counts. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

page.description: 1-based page number.

rect.description: Page-relative rectangle: fractions 0..1 of the page width/height, origin top-left, x0<x1, y0<y1.

output_schema.description: Edit receipt plus the new bar's id (redaction_id, "u<n>"), page and rect as applied.

rect.description: Page-relative rectangle: fractions 0..1 of the page width/height, origin top-left, x0<x1, y0<y1.

tools.name: redact_similar
tools.description: The magic tool, keyed by an EXISTING redaction id: the engine reads the value under that bar (in-page; it is never returned) and redacts every other occurrence of it across the document, on every page. Returns only the number of bars added. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

redaction_id.description: An existing, active redaction id from list_redactions.

output_schema.description: Edit receipt plus how many other occurrences were covered. The value itself is never returned.

tools.name: unredact_similar
tools.description: The magic tool in reverse, keyed by an EXISTING redaction id: every other active redaction of the same value across the document is turned off. The keyed bar itself stays. Returns only the number turned off. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

redaction_id.description: An existing, active redaction id from list_redactions.

output_schema.description: Edit receipt plus how many other occurrences were turned off.

tools.name: remove_category
tools.description: Turn off every active engine redaction of one category (e.g. PERSON, US_ADDRESS) on a document. The page repaints. Returns counts only. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

category.description: A category name as returned by list_redactions / get_redaction_result counts.

output_schema.description: Edit receipt plus how many of that category were turned off.

tools.name: restore_category
tools.description: Turn every inactive engine redaction of one category back on. The page repaints. Returns counts only. In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document.

category.description: A category name as returned by list_redactions / get_redaction_result counts.

output_schema.description: Edit receipt plus how many of that category were turned back on.

tools.name: finalize
tools.description: Bake the current redaction set into the ORIGINAL document (edited sets go through the engine's apply-rects; an untouched set is the engine's own output) and hand the redacted PDF to the person through the page's download. The file goes to their machine, never through this tool: the result carries filename, byte size, page count, the number of active redactions, and watermark (whether the engine stamped THIS file). In-tab, nothing uploaded; returns geometry and counts, never any text from the document. Limits: Cover redacts a document completely or not at all. Person names and the structured detections are ONE redaction that runs in two stages (the structured pass, then the ~265 MB in-page name model), not two levels you can get separately: a document whose names could not be checked is REFUSED (error daily_limit | incomplete_redaction) rather than returned partly redacted. Scanned or image-only pages are refused (error needs_ocr) and password-protected PDFs are refused (error encrypted_unsupported): OCR and passwords need the Cover Mac app, https://coverredact.com/. Downloads carry the COVER TRIAL watermark unless this browser is registered with a Cover license (https://coverredact.com/): get_status reports the page-level `watermark` and every document reports its own, so read those rather than assuming either way.

output_schema.description: The handoff receipt. The FILE is not returned here - it goes to the person through the page download.

sites.name: customware.ai

limit.description: Max number of results (default 100).

tools.name: get_scn_page
tools.description: Fetch the full content of a specific SCN / territory page by slug. Returns title, description, category, tags, and a plain-text summary of the body. Use list_scn_pages or search_content to find slugs.

full.description: If true, returns the full body text instead of a summary.

tools.name: list_blog_posts
tools.description: List Customware blog posts (slug, path, title, description, publishedAt).

tools.name: get_blog_post
tools.description: Fetch a specific blog post by slug. Returns metadata and a text summary.

tools.name: list_resources
tools.description: List long-form resource articles (slug, path, title, description, category).

tools.name: search_content
tools.description: Full-text search across every Customware page (SCN landing pages, blog posts, resource articles). Returns the top matches with kind, path, title, description, and a snippet.

query.description: Search query.

limit.description: Max results (default 10).

kind.description: Restrict results to a content kind.

tools.name: open_pricing

tools.name: start_cpq_survey

tools.name: book_demo

tools.name: request_demo

tools.name: get_pricing_summary

sites.name: dassey.github.io
sites.description: Every fatal crash in America, 2001–2024. Drill from the national picture down to a single crash — vehicles, people, conditions — straight from NHTSA's Fatality Analysis Reporting System.

tools.name: get_map_view
tools.description: Read the current state of the crash map: where it is centred, the zoom, the active year range, the fatal-crash toll inside the current view, and any pin, isolated road or checked route. Call this first to know what the user is looking at.

tools.name: set_year_range
tools.description: Limit the map to a range of crash years. FARS coverage on this map runs 2001 to 2024. Everything else — the heat field, the road toll, the route check — re-counts for the chosen years.

from.description: First year to include, 2001-2024.

to.description: Last year to include, 2001-2024.

tools.name: set_map_view
tools.description: Move the map to a place, or to explicit coordinates and zoom. Zoom past level 9 to make individual crashes appear; the whole lower 48 sits near zoom 4.

place.description: A US place to centre on, e.g. "Flagstaff, AZ". Ignored if lat and lng are given.

zoom.description: Zoom level, 3 (national) to 18 (street). Defaults to 11 for a place.

tools.name: find_place
tools.description: Look up candidate US places for a search string without touching the map. Use it to disambiguate before dropping a pin or checking a route.

query.description: Place name, address or landmark.

limit.description: How many candidates to return, 1-10. Default 5.

tools.name: set_pin
tools.description: Drop the pin on a place or coordinate and scope the map to a radius around it, so every count becomes "within N miles of here". This is the tool for "how bad is it around me / around this address".

place.description: A US place to pin. Ignored if lat and lng are given.

radiusMiles.description: Ring radius in miles; snapped to the nearest offered value (1, 3, 5 or 10).

tools.name: search_roads
tools.description: Search the national road index by name and get each road's full 2001-2024 toll across every state it runs through. Use it to find the exact road name before isolating one.

query.description: Part of a road name, e.g. "I-40" or "US-1".

limit.description: How many roads to return, 1-25. Default 10.

tools.name: select_road
tools.description: Isolate one road nationally: the map shows only its crashes, coast to coast, and reports its toll for the active year range. Takes a name from search_roads, or a colloquial one like "hwy 6", which resolves to the deadliest road carrying that number.

name.description: Exact road name as returned by search_roads.

tools.name: check_route
tools.description: Check a drive end to end: routes A to B, counts every death within a quarter mile of the road, colours the route by how deadly each stretch has been, and returns the worst stretches. This is the tool for "is this drive dangerous".

from.description: Start of the drive, e.g. "Barstow, CA".

to.description: End of the drive, e.g. "Las Vegas, NV".

tools.name: list_crashes_in_view
tools.description: List the individual fatal crashes currently plotted, deadliest first, with the case id needed by get_crash_record. Needs the map zoomed in far enough for dots to appear; if a pin is set the list is limited to its ring.

limit.description: How many crashes to return, 1-200. Default 25.

tools.name: get_crash_record
tools.description: Pull the full FARS case file for one crash: date and time, conditions, every vehicle with speed and outcome, every person with age, restraint and injury. Use case ids from list_crashes_in_view.

state.description: State name or two-digit FIPS code, e.g. "Arizona" or "04".

tools.name: capture_map_screenshot
tools.description: Take a PNG of the map exactly as the user sees it, so you can look at the heat field, the plotted crashes or a coloured route yourself. Returns the picture plus the same numbers get_map_view reports. The map canvas only; side panels are HTML and are described in the text instead.

tools.name: set_basemap
tools.description: Switch the basemap. "dark" is the default CARTO Dark Matter, best for reading the heat field; "street" shows road names and buildings, better for a screenshot of one neighbourhood.

style.description: Which basemap to show.

tools.name: clear_selection
tools.description: Drop the pin, the isolated road and the route check and go back to the whole country. Use it before starting a different question.

recenter.description: Also fit the map back to the lower 48. Default true.

sites.name: eos.lil.run
sites.description: A local-first Mermaid editor your agents can use too. Instant Pele rendering, stored in your browser, every action exposed as a WebMCP tool.

tools.name: get_library
tools.description: The library: diagrams (id, title, tags, starred, dates), the tag tree with emoji and counts, and totals. Filters work like the sidebar: query (fuzzy title and contents), starred, tags (include nested tags), deleted (only diagrams in Deleted), sort.

tools.name: get_diagram
tools.description: One diagram: title, tags, starred, Mermaid source and the version id it's at (pass it to update_diagram as baseVersion or expectedVersion). version reads the source at a past version; history: true adds the version list, where agent edits are listed separately from the person's.

tools.name: get_view
tools.description: What the person is looking at: page, open diagram, library filters, preview zoom, whether Settings and the sidebar are open.

tools.name: get_settings
tools.description: Settings, the theme in effect (light or dark, plus the full app --eos-* and diagram --pele-* CSS including defaults; Pele's variables are documented at https://pele.run/theming) and storage used.

tools.name: export
tools.description: Export a diagram (id) or raw Mermaid (source). Formats: svg, png (data URL), mmd (with the version id it's at, for a diagram), link (a share link that opens a copy in another browser, or the original in a browser that already has it), backup (the whole library as JSON; no id needed). For invalid Mermaid, svg and png return parse_error with line and column, and mmd returns ok with valid: false and the error, so either works as a dry-run check. link doesn't check the source. download: true also saves the file like the Export menu.

source.description: Raw Mermaid, instead of id

includeTags.description: For link: include the diagram's tags

tools.name: create_diagram
tools.description: Create a diagram from Mermaid source, or import one from an Eos share link (fromShareLink). Importing a link whose title and source match a diagram already in the library returns that diagram, with existing: true, and leaves it as it is (starred isn't applied): editing it edits the person's diagram. To get a copy instead, or to duplicate any diagram, read it with get_diagram and create from its source. Opens it unless open is false. Returns the version id its source is at and whether the source parses.

source.description: Mermaid source

tags.description: Use slashes for nesting, e.g. work/backend

tools.name: update_diagram
tools.description: Edit a diagram. Every field is optional and the edit lands as one change in history, credited to the agent: title, source (full Mermaid; applied as a minimal diff), starred, addTags, removeTags. revert: "undo" or "redo" steps back or forward through the agent's own source edits, keeping the person's (title, tags and starred aren't undoable: set them back directly), or a version id from get_diagram's history restores that version. deleted: true moves it to Deleted (asks the person; reversible), false restores it. Pass baseVersion, the version id returned with the source you edited, to merge your source as the changes you made to it, keeping edits others made since; without it, source replaces the text. When others' edits were merged in, the result includes the merged source. expectedVersion refuses the edit if anything changed since that version.

tools.name: update_tag
tools.description: Rename or move a tag (and everything nested under it) across every diagram, and/or set its sidebar icon. moveTo is the new full path: "archive/backend" nests it, "backend" puts it at the top level. emoji: an emoji, or null for the default #.

tools.name: set_view
tools.description: Change what the person sees. page: "library" (with optional filters; filters on their own also show the library) or "diagram" (with diagramId). previewVersion shows a past version of the open diagram read-only, or "latest" to go back. zoom changes the preview. settingsOpen shows or hides Settings; sidebarOpen shows or hides the sidebar.

tags.description: One tag: the library shows one tag at a time

previewVersion.description: A version id from get_diagram's history, or "latest"

tools.name: set_theme
tools.description: Change the theme: mode (light, dark or system), appCss (--eos-* variables) and/or diagramCss (--pele-* variables). Start from the CSS get_settings returns. null resets an override to the default.

tools.name: delete_tag
tools.description: Remove a tag, and tags nested under it, from every diagram. Asks the person to confirm. Diagrams themselves are kept.

tools.name: import_backup
tools.description: Import a backup (from export with format backup). merge adds to the library; replace wipes local data first and asks the person to confirm.

tools.name: delete_all_data
tools.description: Delete every diagram in this browser, with its stars and tag emoji. Settings are kept. Asks the person to confirm. Can't be undone.

sites.description: Faultline

tools.name: propose-architecture
tools.description: Replace the canvas with a starting architecture built from a plain-language requirements sentence. Understands intent keywords (read-heavy, cache, background jobs / async, static assets, serverless, key-value / NoSQL, multi-region / survive a region outage, prototype / cheap) and a region name (defaults to us-east-1). Every resource is configured, placed and connected. This is a starting point — follow with resilience-lint. One undo step.

requirements.description: One or two sentences describing the system, e.g. "public web app with a Postgres database and background email jobs, must survive an availability-zone outage".

tools.name: describe-architecture
tools.description: List every resource on the canvas (id, kind, label, provider variant, region/zone placement) and every dependency edge. Call this first to see the current design before adding, connecting or configuring anything. Read-only.

tools.name: add-resource
tools.description: Add one cloud building block to the architecture canvas. Call repeatedly to sketch a design.

kind.description: Which vendor-neutral building block to add.

label.description: Short human-readable name, e.g. "orders API".

tools.name: connect
tools.description: Add a dependency edge — `from` depends on / calls `to`. Both resources must already exist.

from.description: Id of the dependent resource, e.g. "compute-1".

to.description: Id of the depended-on resource, e.g. "database-1".

tools.name: configure-resource
tools.description: Set an existing resource's provider variant and/or its region/availability-zone placement. Omitted fields are left unchanged.

id.description: Resource id, e.g. "database-1".

variant.description: Provider service, e.g. "rds-multi-az". See the active profile on /learn.

region.description: Region id, e.g. "us-east-1".

az.description: Availability zone, e.g. "us-east-1a". Omit for a regional (multi-AZ) deployment.

tools.name: move-resource
tools.description: Set an existing resource's position on the canvas (top-left origin). Use it to lay out the diagram so the dependency flow reads clearly.

id.description: Resource id, e.g. "compute-1".

x.description: Horizontal position; 0 is the left edge.

y.description: Vertical position; 0 is the top edge.

tools.name: remove-resource
tools.description: Delete a resource from the canvas by id. Any dependency edges to or from it are removed too. One undo step.

id.description: Resource id, e.g. "cache-1".

tools.name: simulate-failure
tools.description: Knock out one availability zone (pass az) or a whole region (omit az) and report which resources go down, which degrade, and why.

region.description: Region id, e.g. "us-east-1".

az.description: Availability zone to fail, e.g. "us-east-1a". Omit to fail the entire region.

tools.name: find-spofs
tools.description: List resources that are single points of failure by construction, with the resources each would take down.

tools.name: resilience-lint
tools.description: Run rule-based resilience checks over the current design. Each finding has a severity (high / medium / low), the resource it concerns, a plain-language explanation of the risk and the fix, and a citation to the architectural principle in Designing Data-Intensive Applications (2nd ed.) behind it. Read-only: reports, changes nothing on the canvas.

tools.name: explain
tools.description: Explain a selection in plain language: its role in the design, its dependencies and dependents, what its failure would take down, and a relevant principle from Designing Data-Intensive Applications (2nd ed.). Pass a resource id (e.g. "database-1") or an edge as "from->to" (e.g. "compute-1->database-1"). Read-only: reports, changes nothing.

selection.description: A resource id ("database-1") or a dependency edge ("compute-1->database-1").

tools.name: estimate-cost
tools.description: Order-of-magnitude monthly cost of the current design (USD), from the bundled pricing snapshot — not a live quote. Returns the total, a per-resource breakdown, unpriced resources, and the delta since the previous estimate. Read-only.

tools.name: generate-iac
tools.description: Emit the current architecture as Terraform HCL for the human to review. Read-only: produces text, changes nothing. Each configured resource becomes one or more `resource` blocks with its AWS variant and placement; an alb -> compute edge wires target groups, other edges become depends_on. Network and IAM are var.* inputs, not generated. Returns a fenced hcl code block.

target.description: Output format. Only "terraform" is supported today.

query.description: Free text. Every word must appear; accents and case are ignored.

type.description: Activity type, e.g. "publication", "workshop" or "grant".

tag.description: A subject tag the entry carries.

limit.description: Rows per page (default 10, at most 50).

tools.name: list_research_projects

type.description: Publication type.

tag.description: A subject tag the publication carries.

sites.name: frontmcp.dev
sites.description: The FrontMCP API reference for TypeScript MCP servers, from decorators and contexts to auth, plugins, testing and deployment, checked against the SDK it describes, with a runnable example for…

tools.name: call_playground
tools.description: Sends one MCP request to a Playground's server from its Call tab, as the user would: the user sees the result in the Call tab and the exchange in the Wire tab. A stopped Playground starts first. Returns the JSON-RPC response, with any notifications streamed before it. Time limit: 60 seconds.

index.description: The Playground's position on the page, from 1, as list_playgrounds gives it.

method.description: An MCP method: tools/call, resources/read or prompts/get, or a list method like tools/list.

params.description: Its params, like { "name": "search_tickets", "arguments": { "query": "log" } } for tools/call.

tools.name: edit_playground
tools.description: Puts new code in one of the page's Playgrounds, as if the user typed it: the user sees it in the editor, the Playground counts as edited, and its Reset button brings back the original example. It replaces only the files you give, which must be files the Playground has; their earlier code, the user's edits included, is gone. The Playground restarts with the new code; returns the compile errors with file and line, or the error that stopped the server starting, or the new catalog. Time limit: 60 seconds.

index.description: The Playground's position on the page, from 1, as list_playgrounds gives it.

name.description: The file's name, like "server.ts", or "server.test.ts" for tests written with @frontmcp/testing.

files.description: The files to replace, by name.

tools.name: get_current_page
tools.description: Returns the frontmcp.dev page open in this tab: its path, title, and the section headings on it, each with the anchor that links to it. Use it to know what the user is reading before you answer, or to point them to a section.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Returns a frontmcp.dev docs or blog page as Markdown: its title, summary and full text, with code samples and links to other pages. Use it to read a page that search_docs or list_pages found. Takes a path on this site, like /reference/sdk/tool; other sites are refused.

path.description: The page's path, like /learn/your-first-tool, or its full frontmcp.dev URL.

tools.name: get_playground
tools.description: Returns one Playground on the page: its files as the user sees them, with their edits, its status (and the error, if it has one), whether the user edited it, the response to the last request sent from its Call tab, and its last test results. Use it to see what the user is working on, or why their code fails.

index.description: The Playground's position on the page, from 1, as list_playgrounds gives it.

tools.name: get_version
tools.description: Returns the FrontMCP version this site documents, the MCP protocol version its examples speak, and the latest FrontMCP releases with their summaries and changelog links. Use it before giving version-specific advice.

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: Returns the site's navigation: for Learn, Reference, Examples and Compare, the sidebar's groups and pages in reading order, and the blog's posts, each with its title and path. Use it to see what the docs cover, or to find a page by where it sits.

section.description: Only this part of the site. All of them by default.

tools.name: list_playgrounds
tools.description: Returns the Playgrounds on the page open in this tab, in page order: each one's index (its position, from 1), the heading it sits under, its file names, its status (not started, starting, running, stopped while the user reads elsewhere, or error) and whether the user edited its code. Use it before get_playground, edit_playground, call_playground or run_playground_tests.

tools.name: navigate
tools.description: Opens a frontmcp.dev page in this tab, as a link on the site does, and scrolls to a section when you give its anchor. Only the site's own pages: the docs, the blog, and /, /playground, /releases and /versions. Returns the page's path and title once it shows.

path.description: The page's path, like /reference/sdk/tool, or its full frontmcp.dev URL.

anchor.description: A section on the page, like "options" or "#options", from search_docs or get_current_page.

tools.name: open_playground
tools.description: Opens the full-page Playground, /playground, in this tab with your files loaded in its editor, where the user can edit and run them and share the link. Returns the link. Use it to hand the user a project to try; then list_playgrounds and the other Playground tools work on it.

name.description: The file's name, like "server.ts", or "server.test.ts" for tests written with @frontmcp/testing.

hidden.description: Kept out of the file tabs.

files.description: The project's files.

tools.name: run_in_playground
tools.description: Compiles FrontMCP code and starts it in the Playground's runtime in this page: FrontMCP and a simulated MCP client in a Web Worker, as the site's Playgrounds run. Nothing is shown to the user. Returns, in order: the compile errors with file and line, or the error that stopped the server starting; else the server's catalog (tools, resources, resource templates and prompts, with their schemas); then the response to `call`, if given; then, with `runTests`, the results of the project's *.test.ts files. The files may import @frontmcp/sdk, @frontmcp/testing, @frontmcp/plugins, the @frontmcp/plugin-* packages, @frontmcp/adapters and each other, and export their tools, resources and prompts, or an @App or @FrontMcp class. The server is disposed afterwards, and the whole run has a time limit of 60 seconds. Use it to check that code compiles and behaves as you expect before you suggest it.

name.description: The file's name, like "server.ts", or "server.test.ts" for tests written with @frontmcp/testing.

hidden.description: Kept out of the file tabs.

files.description: The project's files.

call.description: One request to send once the server is running.

method.description: An MCP method: tools/call, resources/read or prompts/get, or a list method like tools/list.

params.description: Its params, like { "name": "search_tickets", "arguments": { "query": "log" } } for tools/call.

runTests.description: Also run the tests in the project's *.test.ts files.

tools.name: run_playground_tests

sites.name: guide-webmcp.vercel.app
sites.description: Northstar Health is a fictional legacy patient portal that Guide can adapt through WebMCP around a person's functional visual needs.

tools.name: get_portal_state
tools.description: Read what Robert currently sees in the fictional Northstar Health portal, including bounded component personalization, human overrides, and pending actions. Calibration attempts and simulator state are intentionally excluded. Call this before continuing a shared workflow.

tools.name: get_northstar_context
tools.description: Read Northstar’s supported goals, complete workflow steps, current availability, blocked and future actions, human decisions, consequential boundaries, assistance levels, and bounded interface adaptations. Use this instead of guessing from the visual layout.

tools.name: personalize_for_task
tools.description: Primary personalization capability. Immediately compose Northstar’s existing semantic regions around the person’s goal, functional difficulty, presentation preferences, and desired help level. Use one call for requests such as “show me only what matters, use simple language, and help me reschedule, but let me choose the time” or for an initial response to difficult controls. This may open the non-committing chooser, but it never selects a time, confirms an appointment, changes permissions, hides required warnings, or injects arbitrary interface code. Reuse this tool to refine the live arrangement, such as switching between step-by-step and one-page presentation.

goal.description: The supported Northstar outcome the interface should prioritize.

assistanceLevel.description: How much help to present. This never replaces confirmation rules.

informationDensity.description: How prominently primary and supporting information are presented.

languageStyle.description: Whether labels use standard portal language or plainer task language.

workflowLayout.description: Whether workflow choices and review appear sequentially or together.

navigationPresentation.description: Focused keeps unrelated sections discoverable under progressive disclosure; full shows all section controls.

guideVisibility.description: Whether Guide visibly points and explains after the immediate website transformation.

timeSelection.description: Who may choose a replacement time. Use person when the person says they want to choose.

regionAdjustments.description: Optional bounded adjustments to website-authored semantic regions. Unsupported combinations are ignored.

openWorkflow.description: Open the safe non-committing workflow entry when true. Defaults to true.

tools.name: configure_accessibility
tools.description: Apply one or more explicitly requested Northstar settings, such as “make text 175%” or “use stronger contrast,” while preserving omitted settings. For a complete task-centered reorganization, use personalize_for_task. Calibration is optional fine-tuning when the person asks for it or the first adaptation is insufficient.

textScale.description: Changes the visible text scale percentage.

contrast.description: Switches between standard and stronger visual contrast.

density.description: Simplified prioritizes primary tasks and reduces secondary information.

controlSize.description: Changes the visible size of interactive controls.

spacing.description: Changes separation between controls and content groups.

emphasizeInteractive.description: Makes buttons and links more visually distinct when true.

colorIndependentStatus.description: Adds icons, shapes, and text so status is not conveyed by color alone.

readAloud.description: Enables optional webpage speech for visible Guide messages when true.

tools.name: start_interface_calibration
tools.description: Optional fine-tuning after an initial adaptation when the person repeatedly misses controls, does not know what target size or spacing works, or explicitly asks to calibrate. Do not require calibration before helping, and do not call from a diagnosis word alone. This opens safe local practice, selects a calibration family rather than a disability template, and never automatically confirms an appointment.

domain.description: The implemented functional calibration family. Use pointer_precision for difficulty accurately acquiring controls.

goal.description: The bounded portal task to continue locally after the person approves their preferences.

tools.name: guide_to
tools.description: Move the distinct Guide pointer to a visible semantic target, highlight it, and explain it without activating the target. Use this when the person asks where something is or what it does.

tools.name: draft_engagement_letter

sites.description: Cursus

tools.name: search_courses
tools.description: Search the course catalogue by free text, subject area, term or credit limit. Returns the matching courses with their credits, the term they run in, and their prerequisites. Use this before adding anything, because the screen only shows part of the catalogue.

text.description: Free text over code and name, e.g. "rendering"

area.description: maths, software, systems, data, theory, graphics, physics, general

term.description: Only courses taught in this term, 1 to 6

tools.name: explain_requirement
tools.description: Explain what a course requires: the full prerequisite chain, how deep it is, and which links are still missing from the current plan. The chain is not visible on the page.

tools.name: what_this_closes
tools.description: Say what committing to a course would close off. Answers the question a timetable cannot: which specialisation tracks stop being completable if this course takes the slot, because of prerequisite chains and the credit cap in later terms. Use it before advising a choice.

term.description: Which term it would go in, 1 to 6

tools.name: compare_options
tools.description: Weigh two courses against each other for the same slot: what each one closes off, and what is lost either way. Use this when a student is choosing between two courses and the term has room for one — it is the question they actually ask, and it takes one call instead of two. Whichever is rejected is not merely unchosen: the slot is gone.

course_a.description: One of the two course codes

term.description: The term both would compete for, 1 to 6

tools.name: plan_status
tools.description: The current plan: what is in it, per term, with credits, plus which specialisation tracks are still open and which are already closed off.

tools.name: add_course
tools.description: Add a course to the plan, in a given term. Checks the prerequisite chain, the timetable, the credit cap and which terms the course is taught in — and when one of those blocks it, the answer names what would unblock it.

term.description: Term 1 to 6. Defaults to the first term it runs in.

tools.name: remove_course
tools.description: Remove a course from the plan. Checks what else in the plan depends on it first, and names those courses if there are any.

tools.name: protect_track
tools.description: Hold a specialisation open. Once protected, any course that would close it is refused — including when the same person asks for it later. Use this when the student has said what they are not willing to give up, before exploring anything that might cost it. Pass protect: false to release it again.

track.description: Track id: data, systems, graphics or theory.

protect.description: True to protect (the default), false to release.

tools.name: propose_plan_for_track
tools.description: Work out what still has to be taken to complete a specialisation track, and in which terms. It proposes and does not add anything, so the whole route can be looked at before any of it is committed. Returns a concrete list, or — if it cannot be done from here — the course that blocks it and what it would cost to unblock. Track ids: data, systems, graphics, theory.

track.description: data, systems, graphics or theory

tools.name: explain_infeasibility
tools.description: When a specialisation cannot be completed, say exactly why: which course cannot be placed, which rule stops it, and what would have to be dropped to make room — with what each of those trades would close in turn. Use it instead of telling a student "it is not possible".

track.description: data, systems, graphics or theory

tools.name: list_actions
tools.description: Everything that has been done to this plan so far, in order, in plain language. Each entry has a step number that undo_to accepts.

tools.name: share_plan
tools.description: Turn the plan into a link that can be sent to somebody — a tutor, an adviser, a friend who took the course last year. Nothing is stored: the link carries the actions themselves, and opening it replays them through the same rules, so a link cannot produce a plan this page would have refused to build.

tools.name: undo_to
tools.description: Rewind the plan to how it was after a given step, discarding everything after it. Returns the plan that results, because after a rewind your idea of the state is out of date.

step.description: Keep steps up to and including this one. 0 empties the plan.

sites.name: iamtanmaypro.github.io
sites.description: Sparkbench

tools.name: ping_workbench
tools.description: Health check for the Sparkbench electronics lab. Call this first to confirm you are connected. Returns the app name and a greeting so the student knows their agent can see the workbench.

tools.name: describe_workbench
tools.description: Get a compact summary of the electronics bench: every component with its id, type and value, plus how terminals are wired together. The canvas is a rendered simulation, so looking at the screen gives shapes at best: this tool is the only source of exact ids, values and terminal-level wiring. Call it first to ground yourself before reading measurements or suggesting changes.

tools.name: read_measurements
tools.description: Read the live simulation: voltage across, current through, and power in each component, plus fault flags (short circuit, open circuit, LED burnout, blown fuse). The screen only renders brightness and one headline fault, so these solver numbers are the only exact readings available. Use it after any wiring change to see what the circuit really does.

tools.name: get_lesson_state
tools.description: See which lesson the student is working on, its goal, how far through the five-lesson track they are, and whether the current circuit meets the goal yet. Pair with check_answer when the student asks how they are doing.

tools.name: read_notes
tools.description: Read the sticky notes pinned to the bench. The student or you may have written them; notes can contain the student's own assumptions, so verify claims against measurements before relying on them.

tools.name: check_answer
tools.description: Check the student's circuit against the current lesson goal. Returns pass or fail with the specific failing checks, which the lesson panel never lists on screen. It never reveals the full solution, so you can coach without giving the answer away.

tools.name: open_lesson
tools.description: Switch the bench to a different lesson. The seeded circuit for that lesson is loaded and the goal panel updates. Dynamic toolsets follow the lesson, so the actions you may propose change with it.

lesson_id.description: Lesson to open: ohms-law, series-parallel, switches-logic, diagnose-fault, or free-build.

tools.name: focus_component
tools.description: Point the student's attention at one component: the canvas pans and zooms to it, it gets a pulse highlight, and it becomes the selected part in the inspector. Use it to say "look here" while explaining.

id.description: Component id from describe_workbench, e.g. bat1 or r2.

tools.name: place_component
tools.description: Add a new component to the bench, like the student dragging one from the parts palette. The student must approve before it appears. Call describe_workbench first, place with this, then wire the part with connect.

type.description: Component to place: battery, resistor, led, bulb, switch, fuse, ammeter, or voltmeter (the lesson may restrict this).

x.description: Horizontal position on the bench; omit to let the bench pick a free spot.

y.description: Vertical position on the bench; omit to let the bench pick a free spot.

value.description: Starting value: ohms for resistors, volts for batteries, amps for fuses.

tools.name: connect
tools.description: Wire two component terminals together, like dragging a wire between them on the canvas. Terminal ids look like bat1:a or r2:b. The student must approve before the wire appears; the bench re-solves right after.

from_terminal.description: Terminal to start the wire from, format <component>:a or :b, e.g. bat1:a.

to_terminal.description: Terminal to end the wire at, format <component>:a or :b, e.g. r1:b.

tools.name: set_property
tools.description: Change one property of a component already on the bench: its value (resistance in ohms, battery voltage, fuse rating) or a switch's open/closed state. The student must approve before the change is applied.

id.description: Component id from describe_workbench, e.g. r2.

property.description: Which property to change: value (number) or closed (boolean, switches only). Defaults to value.

value.description: New setting: a number for value (ohms, volts, amps), or true/false for closed.

tools.name: get_proposal_status
tools.description: Check the outcome of a proposal you made with a write tool: approved, rejected, or pending_approval. Call it after any write returns pending_approval so you never assume the change happened.

proposal_id.description: The proposal_id a write tool returned, e.g. prop12.

tools.name: submit_lab_report
tools.description: Submit the lab report for the current lesson: the student fills in their name, what they built, and what they observed versus what they expected. Fill the fields in for the student, then let them check the form and press Submit themselves; the report is never sent automatically.

observed_vs_expected.description: What did you expect vs what happened?

sites.name: learn.powerplatform.fyi
sites.description: An adaptive PL-400 course that coaches Power Platform developers to mastery through a governed lesson, practice, and tool-roster loop.

tools.name: get_learner_state
tools.description: Read this first, every session — the learner's rubric scores, misconception fire counts, phase, gate status, attempt count, their written lesson aims, one-line rule compressions, and run commitments, PLUS coachingNotes (durable observations from previous coaching sessions, including yours) and a coachCalibration summary of how earlier confidence hints and rubric proposals matched engine outcomes. Call again before choosing any coaching move. When a rule compression exists, critique it against the lesson's governing rule — what did they miss or overstate?

tools.name: get_current_context
tools.description: Read the current objective and, when the learner is on a lesson page, that lesson's slug, title, and section anchors — each anchor carries the title of the section it names, so you can tell the learner where you are sending them. Call first in every session and after any navigation, to orient before coaching. For the lesson's actual teaching material, call get_lesson_brief.

tools.name: get_lesson_brief
tools.description: Read the authored teaching material for the lesson the learner is on: title, epigraph, governing rule, exam-recognition clue, mnemonic, the scenario prompt (and its expected answer once the learner has committed and the page has revealed it to them), the concept hierarchy with summaries, the distractor teardown the page shows — why each tempting choice is tempting and why it fails — the visual walkthrough steps, production nuance, the four targeted drills, the reflection prompts, the page section anchors with their titles, and the official references. Call this before you begin coaching a lesson and whenever the learner moves to a new lesson. This is the authored curriculum you teach from, not your own PL-400 knowledge: when the lesson's framing differs from your prior assumptions, follow the lesson and say it differs, and add nothing of your own while a question is open. Before asking any probing question, establish the scenario in one or two sentences so the learner is reasoning about something concrete; never ask a question that assumes context you have not just given them. While a question is unanswered, do not restate the governing rule, exam clue, or mnemonic — several of them name the correct option almost verbatim; make the learner recall the rule instead of reciting it. The brief carries exactly what the lesson page shows its reader and nothing it withholds: no question rationales and no correct options.

tools.name: navigate_to_anchor
tools.description: Scroll the learner's page to a named section anchor and highlight it (anchors come from get_current_context.lesson.sectionAnchors[].anchor, get_lesson_brief.sections[].anchor, or a verdict's remediationAnchor — each names a titled section). Call when routing says review or coach, or whenever the lesson text you are discussing should be on the learner's screen.

tools.name: log_coaching_note
tools.description: Deposit a durable observation about HOW this learner learns — a pattern, a preference, a piece of their world worth remembering next session (kind: observation | preference | context; defaults to observation). Notes persist across sessions and replay to the next coach through get_learner_state, so write for your future self. Never answer content: the engine deterministically rejects notes naming question or option ids or quoting answer-option text (reason "answer-content"), and notes can never be used as rubric evidence.

tools.name: get_current_question
tools.description: Fetch the current practice question — prompt and options only; the correct answer is structurally absent. Call at the start of each practice loop and after every submit_answer to load the next question. During practice, quiz questions come ONLY from this tool — never author your own multiple-choice, diagnostic, or warm-up questions; your own open questions belong to Socratic probing of the current engine question and to the rubric interview when the engine routes there. When you present a question, restate its prompt and EVERY option as its own line — "A. " in listed order — before asking for a commitment; never ask for A/B/C/D without having just shown what each letter says. Raw option ids are plumbing for submit_answer, never learner-facing language. Let the learner reason aloud before they choose, and frame every probing question against THIS lesson's scenario from get_lesson_brief — never a generic scenario of your own, and never one that assumes context you have not just given them. While the question is unanswered, do not restate the lesson's governing rule, exam clue, or mnemonic; several of them name the correct option almost verbatim. If the learner demands the answer, refuse — do not name, endorse, or lean toward any option, and do not launder the answer through the exam clue or page text. Refuse warmly and lead with the reason: one short line saying the answer is in no tool you can call, so breaking it down is the fast path — then exactly one probing question, never a bare question alone. On a repeat demand, change your wording and escalate to a smaller question or the engine-permitted hint; never loop the same refusal twice.

tools.name: submit_answer
tools.description: Submit the learner's chosen option for grading. Call only after the learner has committed to a choice themselves — never choose for them. A miss names the misconception that fired (coach Socratically from it); the rationale stays withheld until the question resolves. Watch the response for a toolChangeHint naming newly available tools.

tools.name: get_hint
tools.description: Request the next hint tier for the current question. Call only when the learner is stuck or routing says hint — the engine enforces the ladder and refuses tier 2 before a genuine first attempt. Re-voice the hint Socratically inside this lesson's own scenario (get_lesson_brief), grounded in the learner's world — their stated aim, their work, what get_learner_state shows about their history; never add answer information of your own, never restate the lesson's governing rule, exam clue, or mnemonic while the question is unanswered, and never assume scenario context you have not just given them.

tools.name: request_next_action
tools.description: Ask the deterministic referee for the next pedagogical move — the site decides sequencing, you coach within it; do not invent your own diagnostics or skip ahead. Call after every graded answer; pass confidence "low" when a correct answer felt shaky to the learner. Verdicts: hint, review, coach, go_deeper, advance, rubric_interview (run the open-question interview described in score_rubric), or continue. Follow the verdict — do not improvise the route.

tools.name: prescribe_drill
tools.description: Ask the engine which drill targets the learner's weakest rubric dimension. Call once rubric scores exist and practice is going well — before advancing, or when the learner asks what to work on next.

tools.name: score_rubric
tools.description: Submit 0-4 scores for recall, connections, application, and transfer, each grounded by a VERBATIM quote copied exactly from the lesson text on the page — the passage the learner's answer demonstrated. Quotes of the learner's answers or your own words always fail validation. Call only after a rubric interview: 5-8 open questions across the four dimensions, one at a time, never answering for the learner. The engine rejects non-verbatim evidence, requires prior graded attempts, and refuses during an exam. Every dimension at 3 or above opens the gate; the response then names the newly available tools.

tools.name: set_lesson_aim
tools.description: Record why the learner is here: "I'm reading this because I need to ___". ASK for the aim as your FIRST question of every session, before any practice, and store the answer here (200 chars max). It persists per lesson — keyed "track" when the learner is on the hub rather than a lesson page — appears in get_learner_state, and can never be used as rubric evidence. Set it again if the learner's goal shifts. Connect the aim to goals you already know this learner has — from their coaching notes and previous aims — and reflect that connection back to them.

tools.name: set_focus
tools.description: Stage lighting for coaching. Call with preset "focus-section" and that section's anchor (from get_current_context.lesson.sectionAnchors[].anchor) to spotlight the section you are coaching the learner through — the page dims its sibling sections and highlights the target; call "clear-focus" when moving on. "exam-lighting" is site-managed: the site applies and clears the muted exam theme itself at exam start and exit, and requests for it are refused. While an exam is active every preset except "clear-focus" is refused. Effects are a fixed set of page presets — this tool accepts no styling input.

sites.name: lessonique.com
sites.description: An interactive learning platform assisted through WebMCP.

tools.name: get_system_capabilities
tools.description: Discover registered profiles, providers, surfaces, actions, guidance capabilities, and limits.

tools.name: set_guide_build_status
tools.description: Report the real guide-planning stage before classroom creation. Start with understanding-goal, advance one stage at a time, and let create_guided_lesson own successful completion. Use error with a learner-facing message when planning cannot continue.

tools.name: create_guided_lesson
tools.description: Create or replace a complete guided lesson transactionally. Always declare lessonMode. Use only the lesson steps and scene beats required for clarity, with at most 15 Learning Plan steps and 15 scene beats. Avoid filler or unnatural compression and group closely related concepts when needed. Use explain when the learner asks to understand, learn, see, or be shown a concept: provide complete example code and progressive explanation beats, not a workspace full of TODOs. When an initial scene teaches source code, preserve Monaco precision by giving each visual explanation beat one semantic target for the exact token, single line, or contiguous multi-line range being discussed, together with the registered highlight, spotlight, focus, or pointer effects that communicate that target. Treat endColumn as the exclusive endpoint after the final target character. Use practice only when the learner asks for an exercise, challenge, TODO, or hands-on work. Use mixed for a demonstration followed by a small validated exercise. Map every coding-exercise beat, including an intermediate exercise, to a lesson step with structural validation criteria and an editor-change interaction wait; Lessonique validates it in the same beat and gates Next or Finish. Use at most 5 final-exercise criteria and write each criterion's learner-visible requirement alongside its validator. Omit supportingItems from the final beat: Lessonique derives the numbered list from those criterion requirements in the same order, so the guide and validation progress cannot diverge. Wrap every code-related term in single backticks, including keywords, identifiers, functions, values, data types, HTML tags, CSS tokens, and short expressions (for example, `const`, ` `, `getUser()`, `string`, or `42`). Only inline code spans are supported; do not use HTML or other Markdown for presentation.

lessonMode.description: Use explain for complete examples and guided demonstrations without TODO-driven work; practice for incomplete exercises and validation; mixed for explanation followed by a small exercise.

requirement.description: Describe this validation gate in learner-visible language. Final coding-exercise numbered requirements are derived from these values in criterion order.

items.description: Wrap every code-related term in single backticks, including keywords, identifiers, functions, values, data types, HTML tags, CSS tokens, and short expressions (for example, `const`, `<section>`, `getUser()`, `string`, or `42`). Only inline code spans are supported; do not use HTML or other Markdown for presentation.

steps.description: Use only the Learning Plan steps required by the teaching content, up to 15. Prefer clarity over count, avoid filler or unnatural compression, and group closely related concepts when needed.

allowManualNavigation.description: Set true for progressive explanations so the learner advances locally with Previous, Next, and Finish instead of asking ChatGPT for each micro-step.

lessonStepId.description: Reference the Learning Plan section taught by this micro-step. Reuse the same ID across consecutive beats in one section.

type.description: Use explanation for one small concept, interaction while the learner works, validation while checking declared criteria, and feedback for success or correction.

title.description: Wrap every code-related term in single backticks, including keywords, identifiers, functions, values, data types, HTML tags, CSS tokens, and short expressions (for example, `const`, `<section>`, `getUser()`, `string`, or `42`). Only inline code spans are supported; do not use HTML or other Markdown for presentation.

body.description: Keep this explanation focused on the active micro-step; do not combine multiple concepts into a wall of text. sites.name: letshum.com
sites.description: Residents search, compare, and order internet service without leaving your product. You earn on every activation. White-label, provider-neutral, live in days.

tools.name: open_internet_marketplace
tools.description: Open Hum’s home internet marketplace, optionally after validating a US service address with Smarty. If an address is ambiguous, returns up to five short-lived candidates for clarification instead of guessing. A unique multi-unit building may be opened without choosing a unit.

address.description: A US street address, ideally including city, two-letter state, and ZIP code.

candidateId.description: A short-lived candidateId returned by an earlier ambiguous call on this page.

unit.description: Optional apartment, suite, or unit to validate at the selected building.

tools.name: get_marketplace_state
tools.description: Read the verified service address, qualification status, visible checkout step, non-sensitive cart contents, totals, and missing fields in the current Hum internet marketplace.

tools.name: set_internet_needs
tools.description: Answer the marketplace questions about home size, connected devices, and internet uses so Hum can reveal and rank recommendations. Use the choices exposed by the current marketplace state.

tools.name: set_service_unit
tools.description: Validate and add or change an apartment, suite, or unit at the currently verified building, then rerun the Hum marketplace for that unit. If no exact unit exists, returns choices for clarification instead of guessing.

tools.name: list_internet_plans
tools.description: List internet plans for the verified address, including provider, price, speed, technology, fees, promotions, and whether Hum can complete checkout.

tools.name: select_internet_plan
tools.description: Select an orderable Hum internet plan using the opaque planId from list_internet_plans and begin final availability verification. Provider-site-only plans cannot be selected.

tools.name: get_order_options
tools.description: Read the structured choices for the current order-options or installation step, including opaque IDs, selections, quantities, inclusion rules, and dependencies. After an option step is set, call this again for the next category.

tools.name: set_order_options
tools.description: Replace the currently visible option category in the Hum cart and advance to the next checkout step. Use the opaque IDs from get_order_options. Omitted categories stay unchanged; an empty array clears removable selections. Included items, dependencies, radio choices, and quantity limits are enforced.

tools.name: set_installation_preferences
tools.description: Set the desired service-start date and self or professional installation in the visible checkout. The start date must be within the next 30 days beginning tomorrow.

tools.name: set_customer_information
tools.description: Merge non-sensitive customer contact and mailing address into the visible Hum checkout using the same validation as human entry. This tool does not accept date of birth or account PIN.

tools.name: set_sensitive_order_information
tools.description: Set date of birth and/or a four-digit account PIN in the visible Hum order. Before calling, tell the user these values are sensitive and explicitly offer the choice to enter them privately in the visible form instead. Returns only whether each value was provided and never returns the values.

tools.name: review_internet_order
tools.description: Validate the current order, move the visible widget to Order Summary, and return an exact non-sensitive summary plus a short-lived reviewId. This tool never submits or purchases anything.

tools.name: place_internet_service_order
tools.description: PURCHASE: Submit a real internet-service order for the exact contents previously returned by review_internet_order. Call only after the user explicitly approves that reviewed order. Requires the current reviewId and rejects any changed, stale, or already-submitted order. Success is reported only with a visible confirmed order number; submission_unconfirmed must not be retried.

tools.name: card.setType

output_schema.description: Confirmation message

output_schema.description: Confirmation message

output_schema.description: Confirmation message

output_schema.description: Confirmation message

tools.name: card.setBackgroundImage

imageUrl.description: URL of the image to use as card background.

output_schema.description: Confirmation message

tools.name: card.export
tools.description: Exports the business card in the specified format. Supported formats: "png", "jpg", "webp" (image), "html" (standalone HTML file), "vcf" (vCard contact file).

output_schema.description: Confirmation message with export format
