tools.description: Return authoritative details for a catalog item, including price, availability, modifiers, dietary tags and applicable options.

itemId.description: The unique item ID.
Unique item ID

price.description: Price in major currency units

variants.description: Item variant choices

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Initialize a new shopping cart session for the customer. Returns an authoritative cartId session handle. To inspect existing cart contents, use get_cart. To add items, use add_to_cart.

tableIdentifier.description: Optional table number, room, or seat identifier.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add an available catalog item with selected options to the active cart session identified by cartId. To inspect full cart totals and lines, use get_cart. To modify existing lines, use update_cart.

cartId.description: Optional unique cart session ID. If omitted, uses active session cart.

itemId.description: The unique itemId (preferred) or exact natural title of the item to add (e.g. "item_vegan_avocado" or "Avocado Tartine"). If both match, itemId takes precedence.

notes.description: Special preparation instructions or customer notes.

clearExisting.description: Clear existing cart items before adding, ensuring clean cross-venue isolation.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Inspect the contents of the active cart session identified by cartId, including line items, modifier options, subtotal, discounts, and final total. Does NOT initialize a new cart session (use create_cart).

cartId.description: Optional unique cart session ID to inspect. If omitted, returns active session cart.

currency.description: Authoritative 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code

modifiers.description: Applied modifier and option selections for this line item

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Modify the quantity or notes of an existing line item in the cart session using lineId and quantity (set quantity to 0 to remove the line). Requires both lineId and quantity. Does NOT add new catalog items (use add_to_cart).

cartId.description: Optional unique cart session ID. If omitted, updates active cart.

lineId.description: The lineId (cartKey) of the item to update.

quantity.description: New quantity for the line item (0-50). Set to 0 to remove the line item from the cart.

notes.description: Updated notes or instructions.

tools.name: apply_coupon
tools.description: Apply a promotional coupon code or discount voucher to the active shopping cart session identified by cartId. Recalculates discounts and updates the cart subtotal and final total.

couponCode.description: The promotional discount or coupon code to apply (e.g. SAVE10, WELCOME20, PACY50).

cartId.description: Optional cart session identifier. If omitted, applies to the active session cart.

currency.description: Authoritative 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code

fulfillment.description: Fulfillment method for the order: "dine_in" (in-house table service), "pickup" (counter takeout), or "delivery" (room or delivery address). Defaults to "dine_in".

tableIdentifier.description: Table number, room, suite, seat, or pickup counter (e.g. "Table 12" or "12").

phone.description: Customer contact phone number in standard international E.164 format (e.g. +12025550123 or +2348012345678).

currency.description: Authoritative 3-letter ISO 4217 currency code

maxRecommendations.description: Maximum number of pairing recommendations to return.

tools.name: request_staff
tools.description: Send an immediate service or waiter call notification to venue floor staff.

details.description: Optional additional details.

query.description: Optional free-text keyword or location search (e.g. "Lagos sushi", "spa Lekki"). All filters are optional; an empty call returns the current venue directory listing.

name.description: Exact or partial business name (e.g. "Pacy Group", "Emerald Cafe").

totalFound.description: Total number of matching merchant venues discovered.

slug.description: Matched direct venue slug identifier if an exact slug was found or selected.

conceptSlug.description: Department or category slug to navigate to within the storefront. Must be one of the 23 supported department slugs or aliases in the enum: dining concepts ("dining", "menu", "restaurant", "bar"), wellness ("spa", "wellness", "treatments"), retail ("boutique", "retail", "shop", "apparel", "electronics"), stays ("stays", "hotel", "rooms", "suites"), repairs ("repairs", "services", "diagnostics", "quotes"), or media ("media", "studio", "rate-card").

sites.name: abracomiudo.pt
sites.description: Primeira Roupinha de Bebé

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search this store's catalogue by keyword. Returns name, price, stock and a link for each match. Use this FIRST whenever the shopper names something specific they want. It does not open anything or change the cart: call get_product for detail, add_to_cart to buy.

query.description: What to search for, in the shopper's own words

limit.description: Maximum results to return (default and maximum 20)

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse the store the way a shopper would. Called with no arguments it lists the categories the merchant features in the store navigation; called with a category permalink it lists that category's products, with name, price and a link. Stock is not included here - call get_product before adding anything from a category listing. Use it when the shopper is exploring rather than looking for something specific.

category.description: Category permalink from a previous browse_store call. Omit to list the categories.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get one product's details, OR open it in the browser. Returns description, price, stock, and for a product with variants every option and the values it accepts under "options" - not the combinations themselves; use show_variant for a specific one. Set navigate=true when the shopper wants to SEE the product ("show me", "open", "view", "take me to"). Leave it false, the default, when you need data to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart - the browser then stays where it is. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that.

product.description: The product's id or permalink, as returned by search_catalog or browse_store. A variant id is accepted too and answers about the product it belongs to.

navigate.description: Open the product page. Default false: the shopper stays where they are.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Show one specific variant of a product on the page, chosen by its option values, and report its price and stock. Opens the product page with that variant selected, so the shopper sees what is being discussed. Use it after get_product to resolve a combination.

product.description: The product's id or permalink. A variant id may be given instead, and then options can be left out: it already names one variant.

options.description: The values to show, as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Values come from get_product's "options"; matching ignores case, and a partial selection is fine: the first available variant matching it is shown.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Read the shopper's current cart: line items, quantities, discounts, shipping and total. This is the same cart shown on screen, so read it before answering anything about what they are buying rather than relying on what was said earlier in the conversation.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a product to the shopper's cart, which updates on screen immediately. A variant id names what to add on its own; otherwise, for a product with variants, pass the option value ids from get_product's "options" - and if the shopper has not chosen yet, ask them, or call show_variant to show one first. Adding does not start checkout - use proceed_to_checkout when they are ready to pay.

product.description: What to add: a variant id, or a product's id or permalink from search_catalog, browse_store or get_product.

options.description: Variant selection as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Matching ignores case. Omit for products without variants, or when a variant id was given.

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description: Change the quantity of a line already in the cart, or remove it by setting the quantity to 0. Use the cart_item_id from get_cart, not the product id.

tools.name: estimate_shipping
tools.description: What the store can ship to a destination and what it costs, for the cart as it stands. Ask for it when the shopper wants to know the delivery cost or time before they check out - it is the question that most often decides whether they finish. Needs a country and a region; a postal code makes the estimate exact where the store charges by it.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code, e.g. PT, CL, US

region.description: Region, state or province, as the store's checkout names it

postal.description: Postal or ZIP code, when known

municipality.description: Municipality, where the store uses one

tools.name: apply_coupon
tools.description: Apply a discount coupon code to the cart and report the resulting total.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empty the shopper's cart, removing every item and any coupon. ALWAYS confirm with the shopper first: this discards everything they chose and cannot be undone. To remove a single line use update_cart_item with qty 0 instead.

tools.name: get_recommended_products
tools.description: Products this store recommends alongside what is already in the cart. Use it to suggest genuinely related items before checkout.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Open checkout so the shopper can review and pay. Use it when they say they are done. You CANNOT place the order or enter payment details, and no tool here can: the shopper completes the purchase themselves. Once this returns, stop - do not navigate again and do not tell them the order was placed.

sites.name: agentbridge-delta.vercel.app
sites.description: AgentBridge exposes 12 in-page WebMCP tools so capable browser agents can search meals, build a cart, and open checkout while the user watches.

tools.name: list-categories
tools.description: Discover available food categories such as burgers, pizza, sushi, Indian, and breakfast. Use when the user wants ideas or has not named a cuisine; otherwise call search-restaurants directly.

tools.name: search-restaurants
tools.description: Find restaurants matching a food, cuisine, or category. Start here for requests like 'find me a burger for one person under $20' by using category 'burgers' or query 'burger'. Returns restaurant ids, ratings, price level, ETA, delivery fee, and offers. Next call get-restaurant-menu. Price level is not the final order total.

query.description: Free-text search (e.g. 'spicy ramen', 'vegan')

sortBy.description: Sort order

freeDelivery.description: Only show restaurants with free delivery

offers.description: Only show restaurants running an offer/promo

under30.description: Only show restaurants delivering in 30 min or less

tools.name: get-restaurant-menu
tools.description: Get the full menu for a restaurant returned by search-restaurants. Returns item ids, prices, descriptions, sections, and dietary tags. Select suitable items from this result, then use get-cart to verify a total budget because fees and tax are added at checkout.

restaurantId.description: The restaurant id from search results (name also works)

tools.name: filter-menu-items
tools.description: Narrow the current menu by food name, dietary needs, section, or maximum item price. maxPrice applies per item, not to the full order. To satisfy a total budget, add a candidate and check the final total with get-cart.

restaurantId.description: Restaurant id (defaults to the open restaurant)

dietaryTags.description: Dietary filters: vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, spicy, halal, kosher

section.description: Menu section (e.g. Popular, Sides, Drinks, Desserts)

query.description: Text to match in item name/description

tools.name: find-meals
tools.description: Search individual dishes ACROSS ALL restaurants in one call by intent, budget, and meal time — the fastest way to answer requests like 'a healthy lunch under $15' or 'something spicy for dinner'. Returns matching dishes with their restaurant, price, and image, ranked by relevance, and updates the storefront the user is watching. Prefer this over opening menus one at a time. Then call add-to-cart with an item id. Intent words understood in query include: healthy, light, hearty, spicy, sweet, protein, comfort — plus any dish or cuisine name. maxPrice applies per dish; confirm the full order total with get-cart because fees and tax are added at checkout.

query.description: Dish, cuisine, or intent keywords (e.g. 'healthy bowl', 'spicy', 'comfort')

mealType.description: Filter by meal time or course

maxPrice.description: Maximum price per dish in USD

dietaryTags.description: Dietary filters: vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, spicy, halal, kosher

limit.description: Maximum number of dishes to return (default 12)

tools.name: add-to-cart
tools.description: Add a menu item using its item id, quantity, and optional size or extra option ids. Returns the updated cart and complete totals. For budget requests, inspect the returned total and adjust the cart if it exceeds the user's limit.

itemId.description: The menu item id (an item name is also accepted)

quantity.description: Quantity (default 1)

optionIds.description: Optional option ids (e.g. 'large') from the item's option groups

tools.name: remove-from-cart
tools.description: Remove an item from the cart by item id or name. Use to correct a selection or bring an order within budget. Returns the updated cart and totals.

itemId.description: The menu item id or name

tools.name: update-cart-item
tools.description: Set the quantity of an item already in the cart using its item id or name. Quantity 0 removes it. Returns recalculated totals for portion or budget adjustments.

itemId.description: The menu item id or name

quantity.description: New quantity

tools.name: get-cart

Stock is not included here - call get_product before adding anything from a category listing. Use it when the shopper is exploring rather than looking for something specific.

category.description: Category permalink from a previous browse_store call. Omit to list the categories.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get one product's details, OR open it in the browser. Returns description, price, stock, and for a product with variants every option and the values it accepts under "options" - not the combinations themselves; use show_variant for a specific one. Set navigate=true when the shopper wants to SEE the product ("show me", "open", "view", "take me to"). Leave it false, the default, when you need data to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart - the browser then stays where it is. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that.

product.description: The product's id or permalink, as returned by search_catalog or browse_store. A variant id is accepted too and answers about the product it belongs to.

tools.name: show_variant

product.description: The product's id or permalink. A variant id may be given instead, and then options can be left out: it already names one variant.

options.description: The values to show, as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Values come from get_product's "options"; matching ignores case, and a partial selection is fine: the first available variant matching it is shown.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Read the shopper's current cart: line items, quantities, discounts, shipping and total. This is the same cart shown on screen, so read it before answering anything about what they are buying rather than relying on what was said earlier in the conversation.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a product to the shopper's cart, which updates on screen immediately. A variant id names what to add on its own; otherwise, for a product with variants, pass the option value ids from get_product's "options" - and if the shopper has not chosen yet, ask them, or call show_variant to show one first. Adding does not start checkout - use proceed_to_checkout when they are ready to pay.

product.description: What to add: a variant id, or a product's id or permalink from search_catalog, browse_store or get_product.

options.description: Variant selection as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Matching ignores case. Omit for products without variants, or when a variant id was given.

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description: Change the quantity of a line already in the cart, or remove it by setting the quantity to 0. Use the cart_item_id from get_cart, not the product id.

tools.name: estimate_shipping

Needs a country and a region; a postal code makes the estimate exact where the store charges by it.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code, e.g. PT, CL, US

region.description: Region, state or province, as the store's checkout names it

postal.description: Postal or ZIP code, when known

municipality.description: Municipality, where the store uses one

tools.name: apply_coupon
tools.description: Apply a discount coupon code to the cart and report the resulting total.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empty the shopper's cart, removing every item and any coupon. ALWAYS confirm with the shopper first: this discards everything they chose and cannot be undone. To remove a single line use update_cart_item with qty 0 instead.

tools.name: get_recommended_products
tools.description: Products this store recommends alongside what is already in the cart. Use it to suggest genuinely related items before checkout.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout

tools.name: create_cart
tools.description: Create the shopper's cart with the given items, for a shopper whose cart has no items yet. It is the tool for a shopper asking to add or buy something when the cart is empty, and that request is all the authorization it needs. Each line item names a ProductVariant GID in item.id (variant_id from search_catalog or browse_store, or variants[].id from get_product for specific options) and a quantity; every item from one request fits in one call. tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Set the shopper's cart to exactly the given line items. This is a full replacement, not a patch: afterwards the cart holds these lines and only these. - A listed line with its line_items[].id keeps its place and is set to the given quantity, which is absolute (2 means 2, not 2 more). - A listed item without a line id is added, or, when that variant is already on one line of the cart, sets that line's quantity. - A line in the cart that is not listed is removed. It takes the cart's lines as most recently returned by get_cart, create_cart or update_cart. When the cart has changed since then (for example, the shopper edited it on the page, or a new cart replaced it), or an id is given that is not the shopper's current cart, nothing changes and the result is the current cart with an error message. Since the outcome depends only on the lines sent, repeating a call leaves the cart as it is. An empty line_items list empties the cart; leaving line_items out leaves the lines as they are. Returns the whole resulting cart, including its line ids, and messages about the call.

id.description: Optional: the page has one cart, the shopper's, and update_cart always acts on it. When given (the id from a cart result), it is compared with the current cart, and a mismatch changes nothing.

tools.name: ask_business
tools.description: Ask the store a question about its policies and services: returns, refunds and exchanges, shipping and delivery, privacy, terms, subscriptions, contact details and opening hours, or FAQ topics such as gift wrapping. The store answers it: from its own knowledge base when the store offers Ask, otherwise from its published policies, FAQ pages and articles. Put the shopper's question in ask.query in their own words, one question per call; name the topic when the shopper only implies it (e.g. a question about sending back a gift is a returns question). Read-only: it does not change the cart, place orders, or start returns. For products, prices and availability, use search_catalog or get_product. Examples of questions: - What is your return policy? - How long does shipping to Canada take? - What is your phone number? - What are your hours of operation? - Do you offer gift wrapping?

type.description: The kind of page, e.g. refund_policy, shipping_policy, privacy_policy, terms_of_service, faq, page or article.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search this store's catalogue by keyword. Returns name, price, stock and a link for each match. Use this FIRST whenever the shopper names something specific they want. It does not open anything or change the cart: call get_product for detail, add_to_cart to buy.

query.description: What to search for, in the shopper's own words

limit.description: Maximum results to return (default and maximum 20)

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse the store the way a shopper would. Called with no arguments it lists the categories the merchant features in the store navigation; called with a category permalink it lists that category's products, with name, price and a link. Stock is not included here - call get_product before adding anything from a category listing. Use it when the shopper is exploring rather than looking for something specific.

category.description: Category permalink from a previous browse_store call. Omit to list the categories.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get one product's details, OR open it in the browser. Returns description, price, stock, and for a product with variants every option and the values it accepts under "options" - not the combinations themselves; use show_variant for a specific one. Set navigate=true when the shopper wants to SEE the product ("show me", "open", "view", "take me to"). Leave it false, the default, when you need data to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart - the browser then stays where it is. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that.

product.description: The product's id or permalink, as returned by search_catalog or browse_store. A variant id is accepted too and answers about the product it belongs to.

navigate.description: Open the product page. Default false: the shopper stays where they are.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Show one specific variant of a product on the page, chosen by its option values, and report its price and stock. Opens the product page with that variant selected, so the shopper sees what is being discussed. Use it after get_product to resolve a combination.

product.description: The product's id or permalink. A variant id may be given instead, and then options can be left out: it already names one variant.

options.description: The values to show, as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Values come from get_product's "options"; matching ignores case, and a partial selection is fine: the first available variant matching it is shown.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Read the shopper's current cart: line items, quantities, discounts, shipping and total. This is the same cart shown on screen, so read it before answering anything about what they are buying rather than relying on what was said earlier in the conversation.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a product to the shopper's cart, which updates on screen immediately. A variant id names what to add on its own; otherwise, for a product with variants, pass the option value ids from get_product's "options" - and if the shopper has not chosen yet, ask them, or call show_variant to show one first. Adding does not start checkout - use proceed_to_checkout when they are ready to pay.

product.description: What to add: a variant id, or a product's id or permalink from search_catalog, browse_store or get_product.

options.description: Variant selection as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Matching ignores case. Omit for products without variants, or when a variant id was given.

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description: Change the quantity of a line already in the cart, or remove it by setting the quantity to 0. Use the cart_item_id from get_cart, not the product id.

tools.name: estimate_shipping
tools.description: What the store can ship to a destination and what it costs, for the cart as it stands. Ask for it when the shopper wants to know the delivery cost or time before they check out - it is the question that most often decides whether they finish. Needs a country and a region; a postal code makes the estimate exact where the store charges by it.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code, e.g. PT, CL, US

region.description: Region, state or province, as the store's checkout names it

postal.description: Postal or ZIP code, when known

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empty the shopper's cart, removing every item and any coupon. ALWAYS confirm with the shopper first: this discards everything they chose and cannot be undone. To remove a single line use update_cart_item with qty 0 instead.

query.description: What to look for, in plain words.

limit.description: How many products to return.

id.description: The product ID. Pass it back to get_product_details or add_to_cart instead of the name.

price.description: Formatted, including any subscription terms.

name.description: The product name, or part of it. Ignored when `id` is given.

id.description: The product ID from an earlier answer. Exact, and never ambiguous - prefer it over a name when you have one.

id.description: The product ID. Stable; pass it to add_to_cart rather than the name.

zone.description: The shipping zone name.

postage.description: Cost including VAT, or a note that it is set at checkout.

id.description: The category term ID.

self_service.description: Whether a member does all of it themselves.

tools.description: Put a product in the basket at Bearded Colonel. Changes the basket; it does not take payment or place an order, and anything added can be removed again. product.description: The product name, or part of it. Ignored when `id` is given.

needs_option.description: True when a frequency has to be chosen before this can be added.

items.description: How many items the basket now holds.

id.description: The product ID of this line. Pass it to update_cart_item.

tools.description: Change how many of a line already in the basket, or remove it by setting quantity to 0. Changes the basket; it does not take payment. Returns { text, updated, name, quantity, count, total }.

quantity.description: The new quantity. 0 removes the line.

tools.name: get_product

Leave it false, the default, when you need data to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart - the browser then stays where it is. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that.

options.description: The values to show, as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Values come from get_product's "options"; matching ignores case, and a partial selection is fine: the first available variant matching it is shown.

tools.name: get_cart

tools.name: add_to_cart

A variant id names what to add on its own; otherwise, for a product with variants, pass the option value ids from get_product's "options" - and if the shopper has not chosen yet, ask them, or call show_variant to show one first. Adding does not start checkout - use proceed_to_checkout when they are ready to pay.

product.description: What to add: a variant id, or a product's id or permalink from search_catalog, browse_store or get_product.

options.description: Variant selection as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Matching ignores case. Omit for products without variants, or when a variant id was given.

tools.name: update_cart_item

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code, e.g. PT, CL, US

region.description: Region, state or province, as the store's checkout names it

postal.description: Postal or ZIP code, when known

tools.name: apply_coupon

tools.name: cancel_cart

tools.name: get_recommended_products

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Open checkout so the shopper can review and pay. Use it when they say they are done. You CANNOT place the order or enter payment details, and no tool here can: the shopper completes the purchase themselves. Once this returns, stop - do not navigate again and do not tell them the order was placed.

sites.name: clipbrief-weld.vercel.app
sites.description: A WebMCP surface where a human and an agent review a short-video corpus together and leave with a marketing brief.

tools.name: list_videos
tools.description: Browse the clip corpus. Optionally filter by category, hook type, hashtag or maximum duration. Returns compact summaries — id, title, creator, duration, measured signals, and whether a transcript and teardown already exist. Cheap and instant. Start here when you do not know what is in the corpus.

hookType.description: question | shock | pov | stat | demo | testimonial | other

maxDurationS.description: Only clips at or under this many seconds.

limit.description: Cap the number returned.

tools.name: get_video
tools.description: Everything known about one clip: its metadata, its full transcript with timings, and its creative teardown if one has been produced. Use this instead of transcribe_video or analyze_video when you only need results that already exist — it never calls a model.

tools.name: search_transcripts
tools.description: Find clips by what is actually said in them, across every transcript in the corpus at once. Returns the best matching line per clip with its timestamp, ranked. Also highlights the matching clips on screen for the human. This is the fastest way to answer "which clips talk about X".

query.description: A word or phrase spoken in the clips, e.g. "retinol" or "cold brew".

limit.description: Cap the number of clips returned.

tools.name: focus_video
tools.description: Scroll the feed to one clip and play it, optionally seeking to a timestamp. Use this whenever you reference a specific clip, so the human can see the thing you are talking about. It changes what is on screen; it returns no analysis.

video_id.description: The clip id to bring on screen.

tools.name: transcribe_video
tools.description: Return the transcript for one clip. Clips that ship a caption track are parsed from it; the rest were transcribed with Whisper running locally at build time, and those responses carry live:false plus the model used. Results are committed, so this is instant and costs nothing. If you only need a transcript that already exists, get_video is equivalent and clearer.

force.description: Ignored for the speech-to-text path, which is build-time only.

tools.name: analyze_video
tools.description: Produce the creative teardown for one clip: the verbatim hook and its type, core message, audience, tone, CTA, pain point, the objection it handles, and key phrases. Served from cache instantly; pass force:true to re-run the model live, which takes a few seconds. Fields the transcript does not support come back as empty strings rather than invented.

force.description: Re-run the model instead of serving the committed result.

tools.name: analyze_text
tools.description: Tear down a script the human pastes in, rather than a clip in the corpus. Same output shape as analyze_video, with video_id null. Use this when someone shares copy they wrote and wants it analysed the same way. Always calls the model, so it takes a few seconds.

text.description: The full script. At least 40 characters.

label.description: Optional name for the pasted script.

tools.name: rank_videos
tools.description: Reorder the feed by a measured property of the clips, optionally within one category, and show a "ranked by" banner to the human. Every value is computed from the encoded file and the committed transcript — pace is words per minute, hook_speed is how many seconds pass before the opening line ends, cut_rate is the mean seconds per transcript cue. There are no view or like counts in this corpus because none of these clips has ever been published anywhere.

by.description: pace = words per minute · duration = seconds · hook_speed = seconds until the hook ends (lowest first) · hook_length = words in the opening line (lowest first) · words = total words spoken · cut_rate = mean seconds per transcript cue (lowest first).

tools.name: add_to_brief
tools.description: Put one clip into the human's brief tray, where it appears on screen immediately and persists across reloads. Requires the clip to have both a transcript and a teardown — call analyze_video first if it does not. Adding the same clip twice replaces the existing row rather than duplicating it.

note.description: Optional short note explaining why this clip earns its place.

tools.name: remove_from_brief
tools.description: Take one clip out of the brief tray. The human can also do this by hand, so read the tray with get_brief before assuming you know what is in it.

tools.name: get_brief
tools.description: Read what is currently in the brief tray, including rows the human added or removed by hand. Call this before answering any question about the brief — your own add_to_brief calls are not the whole story, because the human edits the same tray you do.

tools.name: export_brief_csv
tools.description: Export the brief tray as a CSV and start the download for the human. Twenty-six fixed columns: the clip, its absolute permalink, the full teardown with the model that produced it, and the measured signals — words, pace, hook length, speech density. Returns the row count and the column list so you can describe the file you just made. Fails cleanly if the tray is empty.

filename.description: Optional. ".csv" is appended if missing.

sites.name: commandcanvas.vercel.app
sites.description: Try a sketch and its linked diagram, create and arrange objects, and inspect your changes. No account or API key required.

tools.name: get_canvas_state
tools.description: Read a compact semantic projection of the live canvas, current selection, and recent activity receipts without changing the room. Call this with scope selected before acting when the user says this, that, or the selected object; use the returned stable object ID in the next tool call.

tools.name: create_object
tools.description: Create one note, task board, schedule, diagram, chart, data table, reference card, decision, action item, summary, risk, or open-question card from compact semantic content. CommandCanvas assigns safe IDs, geometry, z-order, and nested IDs, so use this directly for ordinary creation requests without reading the canvas first. To create a visual from the user's spoken explanation of a selected sketch without image inference, first read the selected state, pass its ID as sourceSketchId, and CommandCanvas will preserve the sketch and place the linked visual beside it.

tools.name: update_object_content
tools.description: Append bounded text to one active note or thought through the versioned mutation pipeline. Provide a stable objectId, or omit it only after get_canvas_state with scope selected confirms the intended note; this cannot replace content or apply arbitrary JSON patches.

tools.name: transform_object
tools.description: Move, resize, or rotate one existing, unpinned canvas object through the canonical mutation pipeline. When the user says this or that, first read the selected canvas state and then use that stable object ID.

tools.name: set_object_state
tools.description: Pin, unpin, minimize, or restore one existing canvas object and record the resulting receipt. Resolve this, that, or selected through get_canvas_state before using its stable object ID.

tools.name: discard_object
tools.description: Move one explicit canvas object to recoverable trash; this never performs permanent deletion. Resolve this, that, or selected through get_canvas_state before using its stable object ID.

tools.name: organize_objects
tools.description: Group explicit canvas objects inside a semantic frame, or ungroup an existing frame, through one reversible mutation.

tools.name: history_action
tools.description: Undo or redo the latest reversible shared canvas mutation and record an attributable history receipt.

tools.name: transform_sketch
tools.description: Interpret a selected sketch into a new structured diagram or chart beside it while preserving the source sketch. Omit outputKind or use auto when the image, narration, and instruction should determine the concrete visual family.

tools.name: prepare_meeting_packet
tools.description: Create or refresh a reviewable meeting-packet draft from current semantic canvas objects; this does not approve or send it.

tools.name: request_packet_send
tools.description: Stage an approved meeting packet for explicit host confirmation. This tool never sends email by itself and cannot override the approved recipient snapshot.

tools.name: control_workspace
tools.description: Control the current participant's local canvas view or drawing session. Start, finish, or cancel drawing; zoom, fit, focus, or restore the viewport. These local controls never discard objects, approve packets, send email, or fabricate a shared mutation receipt.

tools.name: show_variant

tools.name: update_cart_item

sites.name: ekene-111.github.io
sites.description: CoWriter: a screenplay you and an AI agent write together, live, using WebMCP.

tools.name: get_script
tools.description: ALWAYS call this FIRST, before any other tool, no matter what the user is asking for. It reads the entire current script: the story premise (title, logline, theme, genre, tone), the human-authored outline (the story's real, act-by-act throughline — e.g. Act 1 with its beats, Act 2 with its beats, etc. — including beats not written as scenes yet), all acts and their actually-written scenes (heading, action, dialogue), the full character list, and the idea board. Every scene you write, every edit you make, and every consistency check must be grounded in this outline and premise — they are the source of truth for where the story is headed, not just whatever scene happens to be open. The outline is the plan; the scenes are what's actually been written; they won't always be in sync yet.

tools.name: update_premise
tools.description: Revise the story's premise: title, logline, theme, genre, and/or tone. Use this if the direction of the story shifts, so future writing (by you or the human) stays grounded in the current premise. Only the fields you provide are changed.

logline.description: One or two sentences summarizing the story.

theme.description: The underlying idea/message the story is about.

tools.name: add_outline_beat
tools.description: Add a new beat to a named act in the story outline — the human-authored, act-by-act throughline of the whole story, independent of which scenes have actually been written yet. Use this to plan ahead or record a structural decision. If the act doesn't exist yet in the outline, it's created.

actLabel.description: Which act this beat belongs to, e.g. "Act 2".

text.description: A single beat, e.g. "Mara realizes the letter is addressed to her."

position.description: Optional 0-based index within that act to insert at. Defaults to the end.

tools.name: update_outline_beat
tools.description: Rewrite an existing outline beat's text.

beatId.description: The id of the beat to update (from get_script).

tools.name: set_outline
tools.description: Replace the entire outline at once with a full act-by-act structure. Use this only when asked to import, restructure, or rewrite the whole outline — for a single change, prefer add_outline_beat / update_outline_beat instead.

groups.description: Ordered list of acts, each with its ordered beats.

tools.name: add_scene
tools.description: Add a brand-new scene to a given act of the script. The new scene appears live on the user's screen immediately.

actId.description: The id of the act to add the scene to (from get_script).

action.description: Action / description text for the scene.

position.description: Optional 0-based index to insert the scene at within the act. Defaults to the end.

tools.name: edit_scene
tools.description: Rewrite or tweak an existing scene's heading, action text, and/or dialogue. Only the fields you provide are changed; everything else is left as-is.

sceneId.description: The id of the scene to edit (from get_script).

tools.name: reorder_scenes
tools.description: Reorder the scenes within one act by supplying the full desired order of scene ids.

actId.description: The act whose scenes should be reordered.

orderedSceneIds.description: Scene ids in the new desired order.

tools.name: add_character
tools.description: Add a new character to the story bible (name, one-line description, key traits).

tools.name: update_character
tools.description: Revise an existing character's description or traits.

characterId.description: The id of the character to update (from get_script).

tools.name: add_idea
tools.description: Drop a loose plot idea, a 'what if', or a direction the story could go onto the shared idea board — without committing it to the script yet.

tools.name: check_consistency
tools.description: Get every dialogue line in the script annotated with its speaker, plus the full character bible, formatted specifically for reviewing consistency. Use this to find things like: a character's dialogue contradicting their established traits, a speaker who has no character entry, or pacing/repetition issues across scenes. This tool returns data for you to analyze — after finding issues, report them to the user and optionally fix them with edit_scene / update_character.

tools.name: list_angebote
tools.description: Listet alle Privatstunden-Angebote von Ulf Seidl, staatlich gepruefter Skilehrer in Flachau (Snow Space Salzburg), genau wie auf ersteschischule.at. Liefert je Angebot: id, Name (de, en, nl), Dauer, Preis in Euro als Zahl (preis_eur) und als Text, Kurzbeschreibung und ob es ein Aufpreis je weiterer Person ist (aufpreis_je_person). Dazu Waehrung, Hoechstzahl Personen sowie Saison und Treffpunkt laut Seite. Nur lesen.

tools.name: get_angebot
tools.description: Liefert ein einzelnes Angebot von Ulf Seidl anhand der id aus list_angebote (schnupperstunde, halbtag_privat, ganztag_privat oder weitere_person): Name, Dauer, Preis in Euro, Beschreibung, den Aufpreis je weiterer Person, die Hoechstzahl Personen, Saison und Treffpunkt sowie nextSteps zur Anfrage. Gibt bei unbekannter id einen Fehler mit der Liste gueltiger ids zurueck. Nur lesen.

id.description: id aus list_angebote.

tools.name: get_preise_und_bedingungen
tools.description: Liefert die Preisliste von Ulf Seidl in Euro (Schnupperstunde, Halbtag, Ganztag, Aufpreis je weiterer Person bis 4 Personen) und die Regeln zum Ablauf als woertliche Saetze von ersteschischule.at: Anfrage, Treffpunkt nach Vereinbarung, Familie oder Freunde bis 4 Personen. Gibt ausserdem unter offen_bei_ulf die Themen zurueck, zu denen die Website nichts sagt (z. B. Storno, Zahlung, Liftkarte) - diese bitte direkt bei Ulf erfragen, nicht annehmen.

tools.name: list_faqs
tools.description: Liefert die haeufigen Fragen zu Ulf Seidls Privat-Skiunterricht in Flachau mit Antwort (je Eintrag frage und antwort): Preise, Saison, Treffpunkt, Zielgruppen, mehrere Personen, Sprache, Termine kurzfristig, Ablauf einer Anfrage. Jede Antwort steht so auf ersteschischule.at. Optional mit suchbegriff, dann nur passende Eintraege.

suchbegriff.description: Optional: Wort oder kurze Wortfolge, z. B. Preis, Kinder, Treffpunkt. Leer = alle Fragen.

tools.name: suche_website
tools.description: Durchsucht alles, was ersteschischule.at ueber Ulf Seidls Privat-Skiunterricht sagt - haeufige Fragen, Angebote und Preise, Ablauf, Qualifikationen, Saison und Treffpunkt - nach einem Suchbegriff oder einer Frage in eigenen Worten. Liefert je Treffer bereich, titel, text und das Werkzeug mit den vollstaendigen Daten. Ohne Treffer: leere Liste und die Themen, die bei Ulf direkt zu erfragen sind.

suchbegriff.description: Suchbegriff oder Frage, z. B. "Was kostet ein halber Tag" oder "Kinder".

tools.name: get_treffpunkt_und_anfahrt
tools.description: Liefert den Treffpunkt laut ersteschischule.at: Treffpunkt nach Vereinbarung direkt an der Piste in Flachau, und das Gebiet (Flachau, Snow Space Salzburg), woertlich wie auf ersteschischule.at. Gibt Anfahrt, Parken und uebliche Treffpunkte nur zurueck, wenn Ulf sie angegeben hat; sonst stehen sie unter offen_bei_ulf. Nur lesen.

tools.name: get_saison
tools.description: Liefert die Saison, in der Ulf Seidl in Flachau unterrichtet (Dezember bis April, als Text und als Monatszahlen von_monat/bis_monat), den Satz der Seite "auch waehrend der Saison oft noch Termine frei" und den schnellsten Weg zu Ulf laut Seite (Telefon oder WhatsApp). Set navigate=true when the shopper wants to SEE the product ("show me", "open", "view", "take me to"). Leave it false, the default, when you need data to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart - the browser then stays where it is. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that.

A variant id names what to add on its own; otherwise, for a product with variants, pass the option value ids from get_product's "options" - and if the shopper has not chosen yet, ask them, or call show_variant to show one first. Adding does not start checkout - use proceed_to_checkout when they are ready to pay.

sites.name: flatwrite.md
sites.description: A minimalist markdown editor with live preview, paged document layout, and one-click export to HTML, PDF, or shareable URL.

tools.name: render_markdown
tools.description: Render markdown into FlatWrite-styled HTML and fragments, with optional typography and page-layout controls. Provide either the raw markdown inline (`markdown`) or an allowlisted URL (`markdownUrl`) pointing to raw markdown content. Use this when you need the rendered HTML artifacts.

markdown.description: Raw markdown content to render.

markdownUrl.description: URL pointing to raw markdown content. Must be on an allowlisted host (raw.githubusercontent.com, raw.gitlab.com, bitbucket.org), http(s) only, and <=1 MB. Host validation is enforced server-side.

font.description: Font family — must be a bundled family.

oneOf.description: Scale token (e.g. "-1", "0", "1")
Absolute pixel value (8..72)

size.description: Font size as a scale token (e.g. "-1", "0", "1").

oneOf.description: Scale token (e.g. "-1", "0")
Absolute weight (100..900, multiples of 100)

weight.description: Font weight as a scale token (e.g. "-1", "0").

oneOf.description: Scale token (e.g. "-1", "0", "1")
Absolute multiplier (0.8..4.0)

line.description: Line height as a scale token (e.g. "-1", "0", "1").

uiZoom.description: UI zoom level (1.0 = default; >1 zooms in, <1 zooms out).

pageSize.description: Page size for paged output. Only effective when docEngine is pagedjs or vivliostyle.

marginsLR.description: Left/right page margin preset. Only effective when docEngine is pagedjs or vivliostyle.

marginsTB.description: Top/bottom page margin preset. Only effective when docEngine is pagedjs or vivliostyle.

footer.description: Include a page-number footer in paged output.

width.description: Content width in pixels (400..1400). Only effective when docEngine="none".

docEngine.description: Document engine — "none" emits plain CSS; "pagedjs"/"vivliostyle" wrap the output in @page rules.

surfaceMode.description: Surface mode hint. "app" unlocks the appFramework picker; otherwise this is metadata only.

theme.description: Theme identifier rendered as body[data-theme="..."] so consumer CSS can theme via attribute selectors. Free-form (alphanumeric, dash, underscore) — common values are "light" and "dark".

kind.description: Output format — always "html" for render tools.

title.description: Best-effort title extracted from the first H1 heading.

wordCount.description: Approximate word count of source markdown.

body.description: Self-contained <body> fragment.

output_schema.description: Rendered markdown as self-contained HTML fragments with document metadata.

tools.name: list_render_options
tools.description: Return the supported fonts, UI frameworks, document engines, page sizes, orientations, margins, and surface modes for the render_markdown tool. Call this before rendering if you need to know which enum values are valid; call render_markdown when you have the options and are ready to render.

ok.description: Always true for successful options listing.

fonts.description: Bundled font families that can be passed as fontFamily.

frameworks.description: UI frameworks that can be passed as framework when surfaceMode is "app".

docEngines.description: Document engines that can be passed as docEngine.

pageSizes.description: Page size presets that can be passed as pageSize.

orientations.description: Page orientations that can be passed as orientation.

margins.description: Page margin presets that can be passed as marginsLR or marginsTB.

surfaceModes.description: Surface mode hints that can be passed as surfaceMode.

options.description: Supported enum values for each render option category.

defaults.description: Default values used when an option is omitted.

pageSize.description: Default page size.

output_schema.description: Supported values for the render_markdown tool, wrapped in a typed envelope.

tools.name: get_document_state
tools.description: Return the current state of the active document in the FlatWrite editor: title, word count, render mode, unsaved changes flag, and available export formats. Use this before export or share tools to check readiness; use update_document_content to change the content.

output_schema.title: DocumentStateOutput
output_schema.description: Current state of the active document in the FlatWrite editor.

documentId.description: Stable identifier for the active document.

title.description: Best-effort title from the first H1 or document URL.

wordCount.description: Approximate word count of the current markdown.

charCount.description: Character count of the current markdown.

unsavedChanges.description: Whether the editor content differs from the last loaded/saved state.

url.description: Canonical URL of the current document (share URL or source URL, empty if new).

availableExports.description: Export formats available for the current document.

canShare.description: Whether the document is small enough to share via URL.

tools.name: create_document
tools.description: Create a new blank document in the FlatWrite editor, optionally with initial markdown content. Use this to start a new document; use open_document to load an existing one from a URL or share link.

markdown.description: Optional initial markdown content for the new document.

title.description: Optional title for the new document.

output_schema.title: CreateDocumentOutput
output_schema.description: Result of creating a new document.

documentId.description: Stable identifier for the new document.

url.description: URL of the new document (empty for a blank document).

nextSuggestedTool.description: Suggested next tool to call (e.g. update_document_content).

tools.name: open_document
tools.description: Open an existing document from a URL or share link in the FlatWrite editor. Use this to load a remote markdown file or a previously shared document; use create_document to start blank.

url.description: URL of the markdown file or FlatWrite share link to open.

output_schema.title: OpenDocumentOutput
output_schema.description: Result of opening an existing document.

documentId.description: Stable identifier for the opened document.

url.description: URL of the opened document.

active.description: Whether the document is now the active document in the editor.

nextSuggestedTool.description: Suggested next tool to call (e.g. get_document_state).

tools.name: update_document_content
tools.description: Update the markdown content of the active document in the FlatWrite editor. Use this to edit the document programmatically; use get_document_state to inspect the result.

markdown.description: New markdown content for the document.

output_schema.title: UpdateDocumentOutput
output_schema.description: Result of updating document content.

documentId.description: Stable identifier for the updated document.

stateVersion.description: Monotonic revision number for optimistic concurrency.

nextSuggestedTool.description: Suggested next tool to call (e.g. render_markdown_preview).

tools.name: list_recent_documents
tools.description: Return a list of recently opened documents from the editor session. Use this to discover what the user has been working on; use open_document to load one.

output_schema.title: ListRecentDocumentsOutput
output_schema.description: List of recently opened documents.

documentId.description: Stable identifier for the document.

url.description: Source URL or share URL.

tools.name: render_markdown_preview
tools.description: Triggers the editor's built-in preview pane. No HTML is returned — this tool produces a visual side-effect only. Agents that need HTML output must use render_markdown instead.

markdown.description: Optional markdown to preview. If omitted, previews the current editor content.

kind.description: Result modality — always "preview".

documentId.description: Stable identifier for the previewed document.

output_schema.description: Result of rendering markdown into the editor preview pane.

tools.name: export_document_html
tools.description: Export the active document as a self-contained HTML file. The export opens in a new browser tab for human users. Completes synchronously. Use export_document_pdf for print-ready output.

documentId.description: Stable identifier for the exported document.

format.description: Export format — always "html".

downloadUrl.description: Blob URL of the exported HTML (temporary, valid for the session).

output_schema.description: Result of exporting the document as HTML.

tools.name: export_document_pdf
tools.description: Export the active document as a PDF by triggering the browser print dialog with the rendered preview. Completes synchronously. The print dialog opens for human users. Use export_document_html for a downloadable HTML file.

documentId.description: Stable identifier for the exported document.

format.description: Export format — always "pdf".

pageCount.description: Number of pages in the rendered output, if known.

output_schema.description: Result of exporting the document as PDF (via browser print dialog).

tools.name: create_share_link
tools.description: Create a shareable URL for the active document and copy it to the clipboard. Use this to share the document; the link expires after 30 days. Use get_document_state to check canShare before calling.

documentId.description: Stable identifier for the shared document.

shareUrl.description: Shareable URL that loads the document in the FlatWrite editor.

expiresAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the share link expires.

output_schema.description: Result of creating a shareable URL for the document.

tools.name: assist_document
tools.description: Rewrite, shorten, fix grammar, or apply a custom instruction to markdown via FlatWrite Assist (Morph: Reflex + Router + Compact + Fast Models). Returns full markdown plus the edited piece. Does not modify the editor — apply with update_document_content if desired. When selectionStart and selectionEnd are provided, only that span is rewritten.

markdown.description: Full markdown document. Optional in the browser WebMCP path (defaults to the active editor). Required for server MCP.

mode.description: Assist mode.

instruction.description: Freeform instruction. Required when mode is "custom".

selectionStart.description: Optional selection start index (inclusive) within markdown.

selectionEnd.description: Optional selection end index (exclusive) within markdown.

selectionText.description: Optional selection text (defaults to markdown.slice(start, end)).

output_schema.title: AssistDocumentOutput
output_schema.description: Result of Morph-powered document assist. Returns full markdown with the edit applied, plus the edited piece for selection-scoped edits. Does not modify the editor automatically.

markdown.description: Full document markdown after applying the edit (selection spliced or whole-doc replace).

piece.description: Edited content for the target scope only (selection text or full document).

scope.description: Whether the edit targeted a selection or the whole document.

explanation.description: Short human-readable summary of what changed.

model.description: Morph Fast Model id that produced the edit.

compacted.description: Whether Compact ran on the input before generation.

usage.description: Token usage from the model call, when available.

reflex.description: Reflex classifier labels for user and assistant turns.

nextSuggestedTool.description: Suggested next tool (e.g. update_document_content to apply).

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search this store's catalogue by keyword. Returns name, price, stock and a link for each match. Use this FIRST whenever the shopper names something specific they want. It does not open anything or change the cart: call get_product for detail, add_to_cart to buy.

query.description: What to search for, in the shopper's own words

limit.description: Maximum results to return (default and maximum 20)

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse the store the way a shopper would. Called with no arguments it lists the categories the merchant features in the store navigation; called with a category permalink it lists that category's products, with name, price and a link. Stock is not included here - call get_product before adding anything from a category listing. Use it when the shopper is exploring rather than looking for something specific.

category.description: Category permalink from a previous browse_store call. Omit to list the categories.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get one product's details, OR open it in the browser. Returns description, price, stock, and for a product with variants every option and the values it accepts under "options" - not the combinations themselves; use show_variant for a specific one. Set navigate=true when the shopper wants to SEE the product ("show me", "open", "view", "take me to"). Leave it false, the default, when you need data to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart - the browser then stays where it is. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that.

product.description: The product's id or permalink, as returned by search_catalog or browse_store. A variant id is accepted too and answers about the product it belongs to.

navigate.description: Open the product page. Default false: the shopper stays where they are.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Show one specific variant of a product on the page, chosen by its option values, and report its price and stock. Opens the product page with that variant selected, so the shopper sees what is being discussed. Use it after get_product to resolve a combination.

product.description: The product's id or permalink. A variant id may be given instead, and then options can be left out: it already names one variant.

options.description: The values to show, as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Values come from get_product's "options"; matching ignores case, and a partial selection is fine: the first available variant matching it is shown.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Read the shopper's current cart: line items, quantities, discounts, shipping and total. This is the same cart shown on screen, so read it before answering anything about what they are buying rather than relying on what was said earlier in the conversation.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add a product to the shopper's cart, which updates on screen immediately. A variant id names what to add on its own; otherwise, for a product with variants, pass the option value ids from get_product's "options" - and if the shopper has not chosen yet, ask them, or call show_variant to show one first. Adding does not start checkout - use proceed_to_checkout when they are ready to pay.

product.description: What to add: a variant id, or a product's id or permalink from search_catalog, browse_store or get_product.

options.description: Variant selection as {option name: value}, e.g. {"Size": "M", "Colour": "Purple"}. Matching ignores case. Omit for products without variants, or when a variant id was given.

tools.name: update_cart_item
tools.description: Change the quantity of a line already in the cart, or remove it by setting the quantity to 0. Use the cart_item_id from get_cart, not the product id.

tools.name: estimate_shipping
tools.description: What the store can ship to a destination and what it costs, for the cart as it stands. Ask for it when the shopper wants to know the delivery cost or time before they check out - it is the question that most often decides whether they finish. Needs a country and a region; a postal code makes the estimate exact where the store charges by it.

country.description: Two-letter ISO 3166-1 country code, e.g. PT, CL, US

region.description: Region, state or province, as the store's checkout names it

postal.description: Postal or ZIP code, when known

municipality.description: Municipality, where the store uses one

tools.name: apply_coupon
tools.description: Apply a discount coupon code to the cart and report the resulting total.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Empty the shopper's cart, removing every item and any coupon. ALWAYS confirm with the shopper first: this discards everything they chose and cannot be undone. To remove a single line use update_cart_item with qty 0 instead.

tools.name: get_recommended_products
tools.description: Products this store recommends alongside what is already in the cart. Use it to suggest genuinely related items before checkout.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Open checkout so the shopper can review and pay. Use it when they say they are done. You CANNOT place the order or enter payment details, and no tool here can: the shopper completes the purchase themselves. Once this returns, stop - do not navigate again and do not tell them the order was placed.

sites.name: graphweave-app.vercel.app
sites.description: Intelligent reactive architecture canvas powered by the W3C WebMCP Standard. AI agents directly manipulate, traverse, analyze, and heal distributed software topologies live in the browser DOM.

tools.name: run_architecture_audit
tools.description: Execute the real-time Architecture Linter on the canvas to detect SPOFs, unencrypted channels, and compliance violations.

tools.name: auto_remediate_violation
tools.description: Automatically execute an architectural quick-fix for a specific violation ID (e.g. provision read replica, upgrade to TLS).

violationId.description: Unique identifier of the violation to remediate

tools.name: add_service_node
tools.description: Spawn an architectural service node onto the visual canvas with specific tier roles.

id.description: Unique alphanumeric identifier (e.g., auth-service)

label.description: Display name (e.g., OAuth 2.0 Auth Server)

tools.name: remove_service_node
tools.description: Decommission a service node from the visual canvas and safely prune all attached network connections.

nodeId.description: Unique alphanumeric identifier of the service node to decommission

tools.name: add_connection
tools.description: Establish a network connection edge between two services with protocol and encryption attributes.

targetId.description: Target destination service node ID

protocol.description: Protocol: gRPC, HTTPS, PostgreSQL Wire, Redis, WebSocket, Kafka, TCP

isEncrypted.description: Whether transport is encrypted with TLS/mTLS

tools.name: remove_connection
tools.description: Sever a network connection link between two services.

targetId.description: Target destination service node ID

tools.name: flag_threat
tools.description: Highlight a security vulnerability, bottleneck, or STRIDE threat on a specific node.

tools.name: resolve_threat
tools.description: Remediate a previously flagged security threat on a node, restoring its healthy security posture.

nodeId.description: ID of the node to remediate

tools.name: simulate_chaos_outage
tools.description: Simulate a chaos engineering service outage (crash, latency, DDoS) to evaluate cascading dependency impacts.

nodeId.description: Target node ID to take offline

scenario.description: Chaos failure scenario

tools.name: reset_canvas
tools.description: Reset the visual canvas to a blank slate by clearing all nodes and connections.

tools.name: apply_auto_layout
tools.description: Trigger Dagre hierarchical graph layout optimization to organize nodes into clean tiers.

direction.description: Layout direction (Left-to-Right or Top-to-Bottom)

tools.name: get_topology_snapshot
tools.description: Read the complete current architecture topology JSON including nodes, edges, threats, and compliance posture score.

sites.name: groundtruth-taupe-beta.vercel.app
sites.description: You read the imagery. Your agent reads everything else. A WebMCP post-disaster damage assessment console over real NOAA storm-day imagery of Fort Myers Beach after Hurricane Ian.

tools.name: get_view
tools.description: What the assessor is looking at RIGHT NOW: map bounding box, zoom, which imagery layer and capture date is displayed, how many buildings are in frame, and which building is selected. Call this first — every other tool is scoped to this view.

tools.name: list_in_view
tools.description: List buildings inside the current viewport, newest-first by exposure. Returns a bounded page with a cursor plus summary statistics for the whole view. Filter by exposure band, damage grade, or whether a building has been graded yet. Use this to find candidates, then get_feature for detail.

exposure.description: Only this surge-exposure band: Severe, High, Moderate, Low or Unknown.

status.description: Filter by assessment status.

limit.description: Max rows to return, 1-25.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous call's `next cursor` line.

tools.name: get_feature
tools.description: Full detail for one building: use, footprint area, floors, ground elevation, modelled surge depth, estimated occupancy, distance to the nearest shelter and fire station, and any assessment or notes already recorded against it.

id.description: Building id exactly as returned by list_in_view, e.g. b95954642.

tools.name: get_assessments
tools.description: Every damage assessment recorded so far in this session, with who wrote each one and whether the human has locked it. Use before proposing grades so you do not duplicate or contradict work the assessor has already done.

author.description: Only records written by this author.

limit.description: Max rows, 1-25.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous call.

tools.name: set_view
tools.description: Move the assessor's map. Give either a named place on Estero Island or an explicit bounding box. This changes what the human sees, so say why you are moving them. Named places: Estero Island, Times Square, north end, mid island, south end, Matanzas Pass Bridge, Big Carlos Pass, Santini Plaza.

place.description: A named place on Estero Island, e.g. "Matanzas Pass Bridge".

bbox.description: Explicit bounds as [west, south, east, north] in WGS84 degrees.

tools.name: select_feature
tools.description: Highlight one building on the assessor's map and open its detail panel. Use this to point at what you are talking about instead of describing coordinates.

id.description: Building id from list_in_view.

tools.name: propose_grade
tools.description: Record a proposed damage grade for one building, attributed to the agent. Refused if the assessor has locked that building — human judgement always wins. Always give a rationale that cites what you actually used (exposure band, elevation, occupancy, imagery).

id.description: Building id from list_in_view.

grade.description: One of: No visible damage, Affected, Minor damage, Major damage, Destroyed, Inaccessible.

rationale.description: Why this grade, in one sentence. Cite the evidence you used.

tools.name: propose_batch
tools.description: Apply one damage grade to several buildings at once. Atomic: if ANY building in the list is locked by the assessor, nothing is written and the locked ids are returned. Use for sweeps like grading every severe-exposure structure on one block.

ids.description: Building ids from list_in_view. Max 40.

grade.description: One of: No visible damage, Affected, Minor damage, Major damage, Destroyed, Inaccessible.

rationale.description: Why this grade applies to the whole set, in one sentence.

tools.name: add_note
tools.description: Attach a short note to one building under the agent's own identity. Notes are advisory context for the human assessor — observations, caveats, things worth checking on the ground. They are never presented as the assessor's own words.

id.description: Building id from list_in_view.

text.description: The note. One or two sentences.

tools.name: set_event_context
tools.description: Write what YOU know about this event into the page — storm track, surge behaviour, comparable historical events, anything the site itself has no way to know. This is the one tool where your own world knowledge, not the page's data, is the payload. Say where it came from.

summary.description: What the assessor should know about this event. 2-5 sentences.

attribution.description: Where this came from, e.g. "model knowledge, NHC TCR AL092022".

tools.name: create_tasking
tools.description: Build a field crew dispatch list from graded buildings and send it for the assessor's review. This does NOT dispatch anyone: it opens a review dialog and this call blocks until a human clicks approve or reject. Expect to wait. If the assessor rejects, respect it and do not retry with the same list.

ids.description: Buildings the crew should visit. Max 25.

crew.description: Which crew or capability is needed, e.g. "USAR team 2", "structural engineer".

tools.name: compare_imagery
tools.description: Switch the assessor's map between NOAA's storm-day aerial imagery (30 Sep 2022, two days after Ian made landfall) and an undated Esri reference image showing the neighbourhood intact. Only available while both layers cover the visible area. The reference layer has no published capture date — do not describe it as a dated 'before' image.

layer.description: Which layer to show.

tools.name: guild.get_profile

tools.name: guild.list_missions
tools.description: List public missions, preserving untrusted public terms and decision-relevant card fields.

tools.name: guild.inspect_mission
tools.description: Read an authoritative public mission snapshot and its ordered, hash-linked event timeline.

tools.name: guild.publish_mission

tools.name: guild.rally_reference_party

tools.name: guild.apply_to_mission
tools.description: Apply the active agent to one exact public mission version with evidence and availability.

tools.name: guild.withdraw_application

tools.name: guild.propose_allocation

tools.name: guild.accept_pact

tools.name: guild.report_progress

tools.name: guild.submit_artifact

tools.name: guild.inspect_receipt
