tools.name: goodleads_describe
tools.description: Call this first. What GoodLeads sells and how to evaluate it from this page: the owner of a newly formed US business, by name, with a mailing address and — where verified — a phone or email, on the list the morning after the state posts the filing and before Apollo, ZoomInfo or any other database has the business. Returns the product summary, what every record ships (with the sample-file link — the exact workbook, before paying), the two scores, provenance, the free evaluation tier, the buying journey (interpret → quote → checkout), and where the other tools fit. The close: put the quoted choice in front of the buyer — callable now (a verified phone), emailable now (a verified email, verified for deliverability and recent activity), or newest, mail-first — then hand over the payment link for the one chosen.

tools.name: goodleads_list_live_states
tools.description: Which US states GoodLeads is live in right now, read from the production API — always current, unlike any cached copy of a marketing page. Check it before promising a buyer a state.

tools.name: goodleads_sample_leads
tools.description: See real records free before spending anything — live, most-reachable-first, names/phones/emails masked. Check freshness, the two scores, business type and field coverage. Filter by state, a business-type keyword, has_phone/has_email, or raw `filters` clauses (see the filters param — e.g. not_in, or {"op": "not", filters:[...]} to negate).

state.description: Two-letter state code, e.g. TX. Omit for all live states. Use goodleads_list_live_states for current coverage.

vertical_keyword.description: Business-type keyword matched against the classified industry name, e.g. "plumbing", "trucking", "real estate".

require_phone.description: Only records with a verified phone.

require_email.description: Only records with a verified email.

limit.description: Rows to return, 1-10 (default 5).

filters.description: Filters follow the one GoodLeads filter contract (77 fields; GET /api/v1/schema/attributes?include=grammar): a leaf is {"field", "op", "value"}; the top-level list is an implicit "and"; {"op": "and"|"or", "filters": [...]} nests one or more children and {"op": "not", "filters": [one child]} negates. Operators by field type — text: eq, neq, in, not_in, contains, does_not_contain, exists, missing; number: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, in, not_in, exists, missing; date: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, in, not_in, exists, missing; boolean: eq, neq; geo: within. Sort with [{field, dir}] over any of the 71 sortable fields. Keyless callers may not filter on contact_name, email_primary, phone_primary. Live states: CO, CT, FL, NY, TX, VA. Records appear here the morning after the state posts them — speed is measured from publication, never from filing.

tools.name: goodleads_data_quality_scorecard
tools.description: Per-state data-quality scorecard computed live over the full inventory: an overall 0-100 score plus format, completeness, standardization, and consistency dimensions with per-check pass rates. Carries by_design_zero notes — publication facts of that state’s registry — so a field the state never publishes is not misread as a data defect. Numbers, not adjectives.

state.description: Two-letter state code, e.g. FL.

tools.name: goodleads_interpret_list
tools.description: Start here: turns the buyer's own words (e.g. "cleaning companies in Texas with a phone") into a list shape — states, filters, lane, cap — plus a plain-words readback, what it assumed, and words it couldn't place. Never answers in prose, never looks a person up, never emits a predicate on a masked field. If the buyer asked a question instead, the response carries `answer` {headline, body, next_step} — relay it verbatim. Next: goodleads_quote_list, then goodleads_checkout_list.

text.description: What the buyer typed, in their own words.

state.description: Optional two-letter state hint, e.g. TX.

current.description: Optional current shape {states, filters, lane, cap} — the answer merges into it instead of starting over.

tools.name: goodleads_quote_list
tools.description: What a list costs before anyone pays: pass a saved list_id (the 8-char slug) or an inline shape (states + filters), a lane (all | best | contact; contact plus a has_email filter is emailable now, plus has_phone is callable now) and an optional cap ({type: "count"|"budget", value} — records for count, cents for budget). Returns the same numbers the buy page shows a person: the graded counts (matching, sellable, verified_one, verified_both, no_channel, unnamed), facets, the live price rule (prices + price_rule_version) and — when a lane or cap is given — a quote with one line per grade. Billing discipline: only sellable records — matching records whose filing names a person — are ever billed or delivered; matching includes unnamed records with nobody to reach and is never a billable count — never present it as a price. Quote money only from this tool's numbers (name and address $0.25 per record · plus one verified phone or email $0.50 · plus both $0.70 (price rule v1; live prices always come from the summary call's `prices` block)); quote_valid_until says how long they hold. Each quote line carries `ships` (what a record at that grade ships with, in the buyer's words — a name-and-address record never ships a phone or email) and the summary carries `forecast` ({checked, phone_expected, email_expected, both_expected, basis, as_of}: how many of the records still to find on would come back with a verified phone or email, from our measured outcomes on comparable records — relay it with its basis). `ceiling_cents` is the most a buyer can be charged: today's total plus the forecast upgrades, charged only for what we find. Every record ships the owner's name and mailing address plus the business facts — the business name, entity type and status, the state filing number and formation date, the industry with its NAICS, SIC and Google Business codes, the registered agent, the Lead Reference, and the Reachability, Contact Relevance and Contact Confidence scores; open the exact f…

states.description: State codes for an inline shape; omit for every live state.

filters.description: Filters follow the one GoodLeads filter contract (77 fields; GET /api/v1/schema/attributes?include=grammar): a leaf is {"field", "op", "value"}; the top-level list is an implicit "and"; {"op": "and"|"or", "filters": [...]} nests one or more children and {"op": "not", "filters": [one child]} negates. Operators by field type — text: eq, neq, in, not_in, contains, does_not_contain, exists, missing; number: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, in, not_in, exists, missing; date: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, in, not_in, exists, missing; boolean: eq, neq; geo: within. Sort with [{field, dir}] over any of the 71 sortable fields. Keyless callers may not filter on contact_name, email_primary, phone_primary. Live states: CO, CT, FL, NY, TX, VA. Records appear here the morning after the state posts them — speed is measured from publication, never from filing.

lane.description: all | best | contact — asks for a quote. For emailable now, contact with a has_email filter; for callable now, contact with has_phone.

cap.description: {type: "count"|"budget", value} — the dial the quote is solved against.

tools.name: goodleads_list_starters
tools.description: Ready-made lists per live state × business type, each with live graded counts (matching, sellable, verified_one, verified_both) and price_from_cents — the name-and-address grade, a floor, not a flat price; the full price ladder comes from goodleads_quote_list. Show a buyer who hasn't said what they want yet, then narrow with goodleads_interpret_list or your own filters.

tools.name: goodleads_checkout_list
tools.description: Turn a quoted list into a payment link a person completes — the buyer gets the file within a minute of paying. Pass the list you shaped (list_id, or states + filters) with a lane (all | best | contact) and an optional cap. Creating the link costs nothing and charges nobody — payment only happens if a human opens the returned checkout_url and completes it on Stripe's hosted page; the selected records are frozen when the link is minted, so what is billed is what is delivered — billed on sellable records (a named person) only, never on matching. Quote first with goodleads_quote_list and pass its price_rule_version (and, when the summary was exact, expected_total_cents): if prices or counts moved in between, the server answers 409 with the fresh quote instead of charging a different amount. After payment we go find a phone and email on every record bought without one: the buyer authorizes a ceiling (`ceiling_cents` — today's total plus the forecast upgrades), is charged `charged_now_cents` for what exists now, and later only what we find, at that grade's price and never above the ceiling. Nothing is charged until a person completes checkout; the file arrives about a minute after they pay; if we find a phone or email on the records after that, the updated file replaces it on the order's receipt page within a few hours and the receipt shows what was found and billed. A hard bounce, a disconnected phone or the wrong person is replaced within 30 days; what you buy is yours to re-download any time. Hand the URL to your human; do not represent the purchase as complete until they confirm payment.

list_id.description: A saved list id. Pass this or states + filters, not both.

states.description: State codes for an inline shape; omit for every live state.

filters.description: Filters follow the one GoodLeads filter contract (77 fields; GET /api/v1/schema/attributes?include=grammar): a leaf is {"field", "op", "value"}; the top-level list is an implicit "and"; {"op": "and"|"or", "filters": [...]} nests one or more children and {"op": "not", "filters": [one child]} negates. Operators by field type — text: eq, neq, in, not_in, contains, does_not_contain, exists, missing; number: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, in, not_in, exists, missing; date: eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte, between, in, not_in, exists, missing; boolean: eq, neq; geo: within. Sort with [{field, dir}] over any of the 71 sortable fields. Keyless callers may not filter on contact_name, email_primary, phone_primary. Live states: CO, CT, FL, NY, TX, VA. Records appear here the morning after the state posts them — speed is measured from publication, never from filing.

lane.description: all | best | contact (default best).

cap.description: {type: "count"|"budget", value} — records for count, cents for budget.

delivery.description: file (default — a CSV/Excel/JSON workbook, yours to re-download any time), crm, or connector.

connector_crm_name.description: Required when delivery=connector: the CRM to build for.

price_rule_version.description: From goodleads_quote_list — a moved price rule then answers 409 with a fresh quote.

expected_total_cents.description: The quoted total shown to the buyer (only when the quote was exact) — a moved count then answers 409.

Priced by the same graded per-record rule every quote uses; only sellable records (a named person) are ever billed. Preview free with goodleads_sample_leads; buy as-is with goodleads_create_checkout, or shape your own with goodleads_quote_list + goodleads_checkout_list.

For a list you shaped yourself, use goodleads_checkout_list instead. Hand the URL to your human; do not represent the purchase as complete until they confirm payment.

To price and buy a list right now: goodleads_quote_list, then goodleads_checkout_list.

longitude.description: Longitude of the selected starting point.

tools.name: update_intent

intent.description: The person’s new intent.

tools.name: advance_to_next_stop
tools.description: Marks the current leg as started and focuses the next available stop.

tools.name: propose_stop_repair
tools.description: Finds a real nearby replacement for an unavailable stop while preserving the current origin and constraints. It shows a proposal in Buki and never changes the route until the person confirms.

tools.name: get_buki_context

tools.name: imicalculator
tools.description: Allows determining the value of the Municipal Property Tax (IMI) based on data provided by the user. This service validates the indicated municipality, identifies the applicable coefficient, processes the Taxable Patrimonial Value (VPT), number of dependents, and the nature of the property (urban or rural), returning the final IMI amount to be paid according to current fiscal rules in Portugal.

TownName.description: Name of the municipality where the property is located. This field is required for geographic identification and IMI rate determination. Example: "Lisbon", "Porto", "Sintra", "Albufeira".

TaxableValue.description: Taxable patrimonial value of the property (VPT), as registered with the Portuguese Tax Authority. This is the official fiscal value used as the basis for calculating IMI. Must be a positive decimal value expressed in euros. Example: "185000.00".

DependentsNumber.description: Number of dependants in the taxpayer’s household for the relevant tax year. This includes children, elderly parents or other legally recognised dependants that may qualify for IMI reductions or exemptions. Valid values: integer ≥ 0. Example: "2".

IsUrban.description: Indicates whether the property is classified as urban or rural. Urban properties are subject to IMI, while rural properties may be subject to different taxation rules. Example: true/false.

This endpoint allows customization of parameters such as property value, loan amount, bank spread, Euribor, loan term in years, and whether it is a permanent own residence.

PropertyValue.description: Total purchase price of the property in euros. Used as the basis for IMT and Stamp Duty calculations.

LoanAmount.description: Total amount to be borrowed from the bank (capital). Must be less than or equal to the property value.

Spread.description: The bank's profit margin (spread) as a percentage. Combined with Euribor, it forms the total interest rate (TAN).

EuriborRateMaturity.description: Maturity period of the Euribor applied to the loan. Possible values: 1M (1 month: rate revised monthly), 3M (3 months: rate revised quarterly), 6M (6 months: rate revised semi-annually), 12M (12 months: rate revised annually).

LoanTermYears.description: Loan duration in years. Usually between 5 and 40 years depending on the applicant’s age.

IsPermanentHousing.description: Indicates if the property is for Own Permanent Housing. Affects IMT tax brackets and exemptions in Portugal.

tools.name: build_campaign_brief

tools.name: connect_graph8_mcp
tools.description: Give the user live B2B data (700M+ contacts, verified emails, buying signals) inside their AI assistant by connecting the graph8 MCP server. Returns the exact setup for the user's AI client: server URL, config, deep link, and steps. Call this when the user wants B2B data, prospecting, enrichment, or asks how to connect graph8.

client.description: The user's AI client.

tools.name: find_case_studies
tools.description: CIENCE public case studies matched by industry, with each study's own headline numbers and client quote. Without an industry, lists the industries with 3+ studies.

tools.name: get_benchmark
tools.description: Provenance-checked GTM benchmarks from Tenbound's Programmable Revenue research and the graph8 group's operating data. Without an id, lists available benchmark ids. Every answer includes a ready-to-paste citation; the one ask is attribution.

id.description: A benchmark id from the list

tools.name: get_campaign_benchmarks
tools.description: CIENCE outbound channel benchmarks: the published planning model (per-channel meeting rates) plus funnel ranges observed across 122 public case studies. Every number carries its basis.

tools.name: get_company_overview
tools.description: Who is behind this site: the graph8 group. Returns what graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound each do and how they relate. Call this for any who-are-you or which-company question.

tools.name: get_graph8_products
tools.description: The graph8 product catalog: agents, sequencer, dialer, CRM, data, signals, studio, integrations, and more. Without a product argument returns the full list; with one returns that product's summary and page. Call this for any what-does-graph8-have or product-detail question.

product.description: Optional product slug for detail.

tools.name: list_graph8_mcp_capabilities
tools.description: What an AI connected to the graph8 MCP server can do: the tool categories, scale, auth model, and example prompts. Call this to understand or explain graph8's capabilities.

tools.name: run_assessment
tools.description: Score a pipeline team against the Tenbound standard: grade the six pillars (Market, Signal, Message, Motion, Mastery, Measurement) 1-4 on what the team actually did last quarter. Returns the maturity level (your level is your lowest pillar), the gaps, and the moves.

market.description: Who you sell to and why now. Grade 1-4.

signal.description: Reading the buying signals that say an account is ready. Grade 1-4.

message.description: Saying something the buyer finds worth a reply. Grade 1-4.

motion.description: Running the sequence and follow-up with discipline. Grade 1-4.

mastery.description: Rep skill and AI judgment that make the motion work. Grade 1-4.

measurement.description: The numbers that prove the system works and where it leaks. Grade 1-4.

tools.name: start_demo_booking
tools.description: Open this site's booking dialog so the user can book a free thirty minute discovery call with an account executive. The call is a conversation about how their pipeline gets made, not a diagnosis. Only opens the dialog; the user fills in their own details.

tools.name: subscribe_newsletter
tools.description: Subscribe the user to Programmable Revenue Weekly, the free GTM research newsletter from Tenbound (the Pipeline Architecture Institute inside graph8), plus the Tuesday community call invite. Pass the user's email ONLY when they explicitly asked to subscribe or confirmed it; unsubscribing is one click in any issue. Submits through the site's own signup form, the same path a person typing takes.

email.description: The email address the user explicitly gave for the subscription.

sites.name: citability-autopilot.vercel.app
sites.description: An AI-search control room operated by an agent through WebMCP. The human holds the mission and the authority; the agent does the work and stops where it must.

tools.name: get_visibility_overview
tools.description: [read] Returns the frozen dogfood run for this workspace: how many queries were asked, on which engines, and how many answers cited, mentioned, or omitted the site. Start here.

tools.name: check_instrument_calibration
tools.description: [read] Returns the most recent calibration run, engine by engine. An engine that failed its positive anchors cannot support a new measurement, whatever its numbers look like. Call this before trusting any figure.

tools.name: inspect_evidence
tools.description: [read] Looks up a receipt by id, re-verifies its hash against citability.dev over the public MCP endpoint, and returns what the engine actually answered. Use this before treating any verdict as fact.

tools.name: review_experiment
tools.description: [read] Returns a finished experiment with its measurements, its verdict, and the noise floor of the instrument that produced it. Read the noise floor before calling any movement a result.

tools.name: record_diagnosis
tools.description: [read] Writes your reading of the evidence into the workspace so a human can check it. Requires the receipt ids it rests on, a confidence level, and what you ruled out. A diagnosis with no evidence is refused.

opportunity.description: What you think is wrong and what it is worth fixing.

evidence.description: Receipt ids or record ids this rests on. Must not be empty.

excluded.description: What you considered and ruled out, and why.

tools.name: propose_intervention
tools.description: [experimental] Registers a change as an experiment. Requires a baseline to compare against, the single metric you expect to move, and how to roll it back. The metric must be measurable on an engine that passed calibration.

engine.description: Engine the remeasurement will run on.

tools.name: apply_llms_txt_change
tools.description: [reversible] Swaps the llms.txt served at /demo/llms.txt for this workspace. Returns an undo token. Affects your session only and nothing live.

tools.name: undo_change
tools.description: [reversible] Reverses a logged change using the undo token it returned.

tools.name: submit_to_indexing_apis
tools.description: [high_impact] Asks search engines to recrawl. Cannot be undone once sent, is rate limited per property, and a bad submission is visible to every future crawl. This tool always stops for a human decision.

why.description: Why this is worth a human's approval.

tools.name: goto_panel
tools.description: [read] Brings a panel of the control room into view so the person watching sees what you are working on. Use it as you change subject.

tools.name: report_mission_outcome
tools.description: [read] Closes the mission. Every change you claim is checked against the action log, and the report is refused if you claim something that was never logged.

changed.description: Tool names of changes you actually made.

unsupported.description: Things the evidence does not support claiming.

tools.name: add_to_cart

Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant. To change a quantity or remove something already in the cart, use update_cart_lines instead — this tool can only add.

sites.name: copresence-canvas.vercel.app
sites.description: An infinite canvas where a human and an AI agent edit the same live in-browser scene at the same time, over WebMCP.

tools.name: get_scene
tools.description: Read the live canvas: every sticky note with its id and text, plus edges, regions, annotations and overall bounds, as structured JSON. Call this first — you cannot act on the board until you have seen it. This state lives only in the page; no server has it. Every note and edge carries `seat` (which participant last touched it) and `mine` (true when it was you or the human you sit beside), so you can tell your own work from a peer's without diffing snapshots. Re-read this after any pause: other people and their agents are editing the same board and nothing notifies you when they do.

tools.name: what_changed
tools.description: Find out what happened on this board while you were not looking. Pass the `asOf` or `cursor` you were given last time as `since`, and you get back every change made in between — who made it, what it was, and which notes it touched — instead of having to keep an old get_scene and diff it by hand. Anything marked `mine: false` was another participant or their agent: it is their work, not a stale copy of yours, so read it before you rearrange or undo it. Call this after any pause, and after any call that took longer than you expected. Calling it with no `since` gives you a starting cursor rather than the whole session.

since.description: The cursor from a previous what_changed, or `asOf` from get_scene.

annotations.title: What changed since I last looked

tools.name: get_board_context
tools.description: Find out who you are and who else is on this board. Returns your own seat name, what your human currently has selected — which is what they mean by "these" — the seat name and held notes of every other person connected, whether each of them has an agent of their own, and the rule that governs a whole-board change. Call this before your first change on any board you have not seen: without it you cannot tell your own work from a peer's, and you cannot interpret a refusal, which names a seat ("Ochre declined") rather than describing one. It also reports whether this tab is in the background, which is the usual reason a call takes far longer than you expect.

annotations.title: Who else is on this board

tools.name: get_human_activity
tools.description: See what the human has been doing on the canvas alongside you: which notes they have added, edited or moved recently, and which notes they are physically holding right now. You are both working on this board at the same time — check this before rearranging an area, and never move a note the human is currently holding. Other people, each with an agent of their own, may also be on this board; anything they or their agents have hold of is reported here and is not yours to move.

sinceSeconds.description: How far back to look, in seconds. Defaults to 120.

annotations.title: See what the human is doing

tools.name: arrange_region
tools.description: Physically reposition a set of notes into a spatial layout. You choose WHAT belongs together and the shape it should take; the page computes where each note goes and animates a labelled agent cursor to move them. Use "cluster" for affinity groups, "timeline_horizontal" for anything sequenced or dated, "grid" for a matrix or even survey, "hierarchy" for parent/child structure. Pass a label to title the group.

nodeIds.description: Ids of the notes to arrange, from get_scene.

layout.description: The spatial shape to impose on the group.

label.description: Optional title for the group, shown on the canvas.

basedOn.description: The `asOf` you were given by the get_scene this plan is based on. Cite it and the page will refuse this call outright rather than let it overwrite anything another participant changed while you were deciding. Omitting it is allowed and skips the check; you are then writing blind.

tools.name: find_and_link
tools.description: Draw labelled connections between notes you judge to be related. Read the note text with get_scene, decide the pairs yourself, and state the criterion you used (e.g. "cause and effect", "evidence supports hypothesis"). The agent cursor draws each edge.

criterion.description: The relationship you are asserting, in a few words.

from.description: Source note id.

Cite it and the page will refuse this call outright rather than let it overwrite anything another participant changed while you were deciding. Omitting it is allowed and skips the check; you are then writing blind.

tools.name: annotate_scene
tools.description: Attach a floating comment to the canvas without moving anything — an observation, a question, a gap you noticed. Anchor it to a note with nodeId, or leave nodeId out to pin it above the whole board. Cheap, non-destructive, and safe to use while the human works.

text.description: The comment to leave on the canvas.

tools.description: Collapse a group of notes into a single labelled summary note in the same place on the canvas. The originals gather to the centre and are replaced; edges to the outside world are rewired to the summary. Use this to reduce a solved area of the board to one idea.

nodeIds.description: Ids of the notes to collapse.

summary.description: The text of the resulting summary note.

Cite it and the page will refuse this call outright rather than let it overwrite anything another participant changed while you were deciding. Omitting it is allowed and skips the check; you are then writing blind.

annotations.title: Collapse a group into one note

tools.name: add_notes
tools.description: Write new sticky notes onto the canvas — missing evidence, open questions, next steps. Notes appear in the agent colour so the human can see exactly what you contributed. This call is NOT idempotent, and it is paced by an animation, so it can take tens of seconds in a background tab. Never send it again because it seems slow — it has not been dropped. If you do repeat yourself, text you wrote in the last minute is refused rather than written twice, and comes back under `alreadyPresent`.

texts.description: One string per note. Keep each under ~80 characters.

rationale.description: One sentence on why this structure is better. Shown to the human.

groups.description: The groups to build, laid out left to right.

label.description: Group title shown on the canvas.

basedOn.description: The `asOf` you were given by the get_scene this plan is based on. tools.name: undo_last_agent_action

sites.name: counterpart-eight.vercel.app
sites.description: Counterpart

tools.name: get_model_state
tools.description: Returns the current financial model: assumptions, computed monthly projections, headline metrics, and any pending proposals. Call this first, before anything else.

tools.name: propose_edit
tools.description: Proposes a change to one assumption. The change is NOT applied — it appears on the page as a pending proposal that Amogh must accept or reject, and the numbers do not move until he accepts. Call get_model_state first to see valid assumption ids and current values. If Amogh's request is ambiguous about which assumption, what unit, or what time period he means (for example "15% churn" could be monthly or annual), you MUST call ask_human to resolve it before calling this tool — do not guess and do not state your assumption instead of asking.

targetId.description: Which assumption to change.

rationale.description: One short sentence on why this change is worth making.

agentName.description: Which agent is proposing this, e.g. "Growth" or "Risk".

tools.name: rebut_proposal
tools.description: Adds a counterargument beneath an existing proposal without accepting, rejecting, or changing it. Call get_model_state first to find the pending proposal id and read the proposal and any existing rebuttals.

proposalId.description: The id of the proposal to rebut, from get_model_state.

agentName.description: Which agent is rebutting, e.g. "Growth" or "Risk".

rationale.description: One short sentence stating the counterargument.

tools.name: ask_human
tools.description: Asks Amogh a question and waits for his answer, returning the exact option he chose. A card appears on the page with the question and one button per option; this call does not return until he clicks one. Use this whenever his instruction is ambiguous rather than picking an interpretation yourself — units (monthly vs annual, percent vs absolute), which assumption he means, or which of several changes he wants. Asking is cheap and expected; guessing wrong wastes his time.

question.description: One short, specific question. Amogh reads this on the page.

options.description: Between 2 and 6 distinct answers, each short enough to fit on a button.

tools.name: run_scenario
tools.description: Computes headline metrics (arr, ltv, ltvOverCac, runwayMonths) with temporary overrides applied on top of the current assumptions. Nothing on the page changes — this is read-only, for comparing options before calling propose_edit. Call get_model_state first to see valid assumption ids.

overrides.description: Assumption id -> temporary value, applied only for this calculation.

tools.name: annotate
tools.description: Pins a short note next to one assumption row on the page, visible to Amogh. A later call for the same targetId replaces the note rather than adding another. Call get_model_state first to see valid assumption ids.

targetId.description: Which assumption row to pin the note next to.

text.description: A short note, one sentence.

tools.name: add_chart
tools.description: Adds a new line chart below the existing charts, plotting one or more monthly series. Does not replace or change the existing MRR chart. Call get_model_state first if unsure which series are available.

seriesIds.description: Which monthly series to plot together on this chart.

tools.name: highlight
tools.description: Flashes one or more assumption rows on the page for 2 seconds, to draw Amogh's attention to them — for example the row most responsible for a risky scenario. Call get_model_state first to see valid assumption ids.

tools.name: list_scenarios
tools.description: Lists the saved scenario library (Current Plan and any built-in or human-saved scenarios) with their runway, ARR, LTV/CAC, and burn, and which one is currently active. Read-only — activating a scenario is a human action on the Scenarios tab. Use this to reference a scenario by name before calling run_scenario or propose_edit.

tools.name: generate_board_brief
tools.description: Generates a deterministic, board-ready Markdown update (financial snapshot, key risks, recommended actions, pending/approved decisions, outlook) for a scenario. Read-only — it never changes the live model, matching run_scenario's exploration contract. Defaults to the currently active scenario; call list_scenarios first to find a specific scenarioId.

scenarioId.description: Which scenario to report on. Defaults to the currently active scenario.

tools.name: get_decision_log
tools.description: Returns the human-agent decision timeline (proposals, rebuttals, approvals, rejections, scenario activity, board briefs), most-recent-first and capped at the last 25 events. Read-only. Call this before proposing a change to check whether something similar was already decided.

course_relevance.description: Short explanation of fit to the named course.

tools.name: get_capability_gaps

Returns pseudonymous field IDs, safe family labels, compatible closed-DSL Forge primitives, and safe create-vs-evolve guidance with related active skill IDs when applicable. Aggregate evidence only; never values, snippets, samples, real field names, paths or filenames.

tools.name: get_cleaning_tool_source
tools.description: Return the complete open-source cleaning implementation for one F01-F07 or active local cleaning skill in one result; optional offset pagination is a compatibility fallback. Never returns dataset content or Airlock infrastructure source.

finding_id.description: Built-in F01-F07 cleaning tool to inspect.

tools.name: stage_finding_action

action.description: Allowed action for the finding.

field_id.description: Optional field scope; omit to target all affected fields.

view_token.description: Opaque token from the latest successful Data Airlock result; required to reject stale or cross-dataset agent writes.

tools.name: remove_staged_action

skill_id.description: Forged/learned cleaning skill ID whose staged action should be removed. Supply exactly one of finding_id or skill_id.

view_token.description: Opaque token from the latest successful Data Airlock result; required to reject stale writes.

tools.name: simulate_cleaning_plan

tools.name: get_audit_receipt

tools.name: forge_capability

Identify the product by `product_id` or `slug`. Only active products. ## Returns - `options[]`: one entry per configurator option group with its choices. `surcharge` is the extra price in EUR (0 = included; null = unknown — never tell a customer an option is free or included when surcharge is null), `extra_delivery_days` adds to the base delivery time, `related_product` links choices that are themselves products (e.g. a smartlock added to a cylinder). - `included_keys`: how many keys come with the set for free. Either `keys_per_cylinder` (multiply by the number of cylinders) or `per_set_size` (total free keys per set size; a set larger than the largest listed size gets that largest amount). `null` = unknown for this product — never promise a number of keys then. - `sizes[]`: available cylinder size combinations (`a`/`b` in mm as the customer measures them) with the price per size. `sizes_total` may exceed the returned list (capped). Answers questions like "kan deze cilinder in het zwart met knop?" or "is maat 35/45 leverbaar en wat kost die?". ## Example `{"slug":"dom-plura-skg2-cilinder"}` or `{"product_id":3}`

product_id.description: Product id (from search_products).

tools.name: find_cylinder_size
tools.description: ## Use when A customer wants to know which cylinder size to order for a configurable cylinder. Always use this tool for size advice — never calculate a size yourself. Call it **directly** with the measured millimetres per side (outside named first; centre of the fixing bolt to the end on that side). Do not ask follow-up questions before calling — whether and what to ask the customer is defined by the client's agent instructions, not by this tool. `outside_fit`/`inside_fit` are **optional** refinements (default `flush`). Pass them, with the offset in mm, only when the customer already mentioned that the current cylinder protrudes or is recessed relative to the door hardware. ## What it does Per side it computes the real depth to the door face (flush = measured, protruding = measured − offset, recessed = measured + offset), then picks from this product's size series the size that protrudes at most 3 mm, or else recesses at most 3 mm. Sides are computed independently and combined (e.g. `32/47`). ## Returns Structured data only — how to phrase the advice is up to the client (chatbot prompt / agent instructions). - `status`: `ok`, `below_minimum`, `above_maximum`, `outside_3mm_rule` or `not_applicable` (product has no adjustable sizes). - `recommended_size`: the size to order (e.g. "32/47") with `price`, or null when a side falls outside the range. - `sides`: per-side detail — `effective_mm` (real depth), `recommended`, `overshoot_mm`, `within_rule`, `below_minimum`, `above_maximum`. - `half_cylinder_possible`: true when this product also offers a half cylinder (short 10 mm side); relevant when a side is below the smallest standard size. - `specialist`: name + phone of the cylinder specialist, for referral when no size fits. Sizes are symmetric data: 32/47 is the same catalog row as 47/32; order only matters when a knob is chosen (knob belongs on the inside). ## Example `{"product_id":3,"outside_mm":30,"outside_fit":"flush","inside_mm":45,"inside_fit":"flush"}`

product_id.description: Product id (from search_products).

outside_mm.description: Measured outside dimension in mm (named first).

outside_fit.description: How the current cylinder sits on the outside: flush (default), protruding, or recessed.

inside_fit.description: How the current cylinder sits on the inside: flush (default), protruding, or recessed.

outside_offset_mm.description: mm the cylinder protrudes/recesses on the outside (required when not flush).

inside_offset_mm.description: mm the cylinder protrudes/recesses on the inside (required when not flush).

tools.name: get_delivery_info
tools.description: ## Use when A customer asks **"wanneer heb ik het in huis?"** for a specific product. Returns the same delivery expectation the shop shows: base delivery days, the expected delivery date (NL business days, holidays excluded, 17:00 cut-off, evening delivery via Red je Pakket when applicable) and which configurator options add extra days. Identify the product by `product_id` or `slug`. Pass `extra_days` to recompute for a chosen option (e.g. a color with +2 days from `option_delays`). ## Returns - `in_stock`, `delivery_days` and `expected` (ISO date + the Dutch human-readable text shown in the shop). - `option_delays[]`: option choices that extend the delivery time. The estimate is for delivery within the Netherlands, calculated at the moment of the call. ## Example `{"slug":"dom-plura-skg2-cilinder"}` then `{"slug":"dom-plura-skg2-cilinder","extra_days":2}`

product_id.description: Product id (from search_products).

extra_days.description: Extra delivery days from a chosen option (see option_delays).

tools.name: get_product_reviews
tools.description: ## Use when A customer asks about **experiences with a product**, or you want to quote real customer feedback. Only approved, published reviews are returned — the same set shown on the product page, including reviews of the product's color/version variants. Identify the product by `product_id` or `slug`. ## Returns - `summary`: total count, average score and the score distribution (1-5). - `items[]`: most recent reviews first (title, content, score, date). Reviews are anonymous here; no customer names are exposed. ## Example `{"product_id":88,"limit":5}`

product_id.description: Product id (from search_products).

min_score.description: Only reviews with at least this score (1-5).

max_score.description: Only reviews with at most this score (1-5).

limit.description: Number of reviews to return (max 50, default 10).

tools.name: search_faqs
tools.description: ## Use when A customer asks a question that may already be answered in the shop's **FAQ**: shipping, returns, certificates, keys, installation, product-specific questions. Search by keyword, browse a category, or pass a `product_id` to get the FAQs shown on that product's page (linked directly and via the product's FAQ category). ## Returns `items[]` with question, answer (`{html, text}`) and category. Ordered by category position; max 100 items. For keyword searches, `page_faqs[]` additionally holds matching Q&As that live inline on published advice pages (with a `page` title + URL to cite) — those are not in the FAQ table. - `product_only` FAQs are only shown on product pages in the shop; without a `product_id` filter they are still included here so you can answer customer questions. ## Example `{"search":"certificaat"}` or `{"product_id":42}`

search.description: Keyword match on question or answer.

product_id.description: FAQs shown on this product's page (direct links + product FAQ category).

limit.description: Number of items to return (max 100, default 25).

tools.name: get_help_block
tools.description: ## Use when You need one of the shop's **curated help texts** (table `blocks`) — the same texts shown to customers on product pages, the configurator and checkout. These are the canonical explanations; prefer them over improvising an answer. Fetch by exact `slug`, or search by keyword in slug/title/body. The full slug index is available as resource `products://blocks`. Common slugs: `cilinder-keuze-uitleg`, `certificaat`, `skg-keurmerk-uitleg`, `kerntrekbeveiliging-uitleg`, `gelijksluitend`, `paniekfunctie`, `laagsteprijsgarantie`, `maatgarantie`, and per brand `knoppen-merk-{brand-slug}` / `cilindermaat-merk-{brand-slug}`. ## Returns `items[]` with slug, title and body (`{html, text}`). Max 20 items. ## Example `{"slug":"skg-keurmerk-uitleg"}` or `{"search":"kerntrek"}`

search.description: Keyword match on slug, title or body; used when slug is not given.

limit.description: Number of items to return (max 20, default 5).

tools.name: search_advice
tools.description: ## Use when A customer needs **guidance rather than a spec**: which lock to choose, how to measure a cylinder, how to remove or install one, burglary prevention. The shop's advice pages ("advies") are written buying guides and how-tos with recommended products. Search by keyword or browse a category (resource-style list when no filters are given). Results mirror what the website shows on /advies: published landing pages. ## Returns `items[]` with title, public URL, category, a plain-text `body` (truncated to ~2000 chars) and `recommended_product_ids` — feed those ids to `get_product_detail` to suggest concrete products. ## Example `{"search":"opmeten"}` or `{"advice_category_id":1}`

search.description: Keyword match on title, slug or page content.

include_body.description: Include the page text (default true; truncated to ~2000 chars).

limit.description: Number of pages to return (max 25, default 10).

tools.name: resolve_certificate_code
tools.description: ## Use when A customer sent a photo of a security card / certificate, or typed its code, and you need to know which model to reorder. Read the code off the card and pass it verbatim; never derive a model from a code yourself. A card can show other printed boxes next to the code, such as a generation marker (e.g. "G2"). Those do not belong to the code: leave them out, pass only the code itself. Pass `brand` whenever the card shows one (M&C, ABUS, DOM, NEMEF, EVVA). It is how a wrong reading gets caught: if the code resolves to models of another brand, `brand_conflict` comes back true and you must not answer from this result. Pass `reorder_type` only when the customer already said whether they need a cylinder (1) or keys (2). ## What it does Normalises the code (strips spaces and punctuation, uppercases) and matches it against the reorder code patterns of the webshop, the same list the shop's own reorder filter uses. Returns the candidate models plus the matching reorder products. ## Returns - `code`: the normalised code. - `models`: candidate models, most often one. Several means the code alone cannot tell them apart; the model name printed on the card decides, otherwise ask the customer. - `products`: reorder products per candidate model, with `url`, `brand` and `reorder_type` (1 = cylinder, 2 = keys). More than one product of the same `reorder_type` can come back for a single model, for example a sluitplan variant next to the regular version, or two different SKG levels, and they are genuinely different products. This tool never picks between them; ask the customer which one matches their situation instead of guessing. - `brand_conflict`: true when `brand` was given and none of the products carry it. Candidates are matched by name, so a `products` entry can belong to a model whose name only resembles the resolved model (e.g. a "+" variant of it). Have the customer confirm the exact product before ordering; never just take the first one. An empty `models` means the…

code.description: The code as printed or stamped on the card, verbatim.

brand.description: Brand shown on the card (M&C, ABUS, DOM, NEMEF, EVVA), for the conflict check.

tools.name: current_promotions
tools.description: ## Use when A customer asks whether there is **a sale or discount right now** ("is er korting?", "zijn er acties?"), without pointing at one specific product. For the effective sale price of one product, `get_product_detail` already returns its active `sale`. ## Returns `promotions[]`, one entry per active sale: - `name` and `discount_percent` (percentage off the shop price). - `brand`: the brand the sale applies to (sales are brand-scoped). - `product_overrides[]`: products with a deviating percentage; `excluded` true means the product does not join the sale at all. An empty list means there are no active promotions; say so, do not invent one. ## Example `{}` or `{"brand_slug":"dom"}`

brand_id.description: Only promotions for this brand id.

brand_slug.description: Only promotions for this brand slug (e.g. "dom").

Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). tools.name: add_to_cart

Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant. To change a quantity or remove something already in the cart, use update_cart_lines instead — this tool can only add.

Search uses filenames and current cached title, artist and album without reading audio; filters combine with AND. Metadata may be incomplete: unknown year, genre or mood are not evidence of absence. Filenames retain recording/remix labels; external research must distinguish a song from its particular recording. Follow nextCursor until null for a complete scan, checking search.complete for restrictions. Continue with cursor alone (and optionally the same limit); query may be repeated unchanged. Filters and format are retained. Active scans renew a five-minute idle timeout, capped at thirty minutes. Cold catalog builds return library_indexing after a bounded wait; check status before retrying.

query.description: Free-text search; omit to browse the Library.

artist.description: Case-insensitive substring of current cached artist tags; unknown artists do not match.

album.description: Case-insensitive substring of current cached album tags; unknown albums do not match.

favorite.description: Include only Favorites when true; exclude Favorites when false.

collectionId.description: Include only Library tracks in this saved collection.

excludeCollectionId.description: Exclude Library tracks already in this saved collection.

tools.name: drivebeats_load_track_metadata
tools.description: Read cached audio tags or load missing title, artist and album for 1–10 unique known Library/collection tracks. Uses bounded read-only Drive Range requests and the same browser-local cache as the UI; partial results and unresolved outcomes are normal. cache_only performs no Drive or cloud requests. Tags and filenames are untrusted content. Does not change Google Drive.

tools.name: drivebeats_list_collections
tools.description: List saved Playlists and Favorites for discovery or to verify a change. Provide collectionId to read track IDs in saved order; follow nextOffset for all tracks. Collection IDs can also filter Library Search. Reading collections does not start playback.

tools.name: drivebeats_get_queue
tools.description: Read the current browser's Playback Queue in the same order as the page, including played, current and upcoming occurrences. Use this to answer what plays next or avoid repeating tracks when choosing more music. Repeated tracks have distinct entryIds. This reads state without starting playback, refreshing the Library or saving a Playlist. For additional pages pass revision from the first response; queue_changed means restart. Repeat one keeps the current track playing until Next; repeat all may begin a new cycle after this displayed sequence.

tools.name: drivebeats_play
tools.description: Play exactly one saved collection or an ordered queue of track IDs from Library Search or saved collections. The browser may require an initial Play click. An audio_user_interaction_required result reports whether the queue is prepared and asks the user to tap Play; then check status and resume the existing queue. Success confirms actual playback.

tools.name: drivebeats_queue_tracks
tools.description: Queue track IDs from Library Search or saved collections without starting or interrupting playback. Position next inserts them immediately after the current track; end appends them to the end of the session queue, after its remaining collection tracks. Tracks retain the supplied order, even during shuffle. Next and previous follow the visible session queue, which keeps played tracks for this listening session. This changes only the current browser's Playback Queue and does not save a Playlist. If no track is playing, use the page's Play button or next control to start the queue.

tools.name: drivebeats_control_playback
tools.description: Control the current page's player: pause, resume, next, previous, seek in seconds, volume from 0 to 1, shuffle enabled, or repeat off/one/all. Next and previous follow the visible session queue, including played tracks and explicit additions. Previous rewinds the current track when more than three seconds have played. Resume preserves the existing queue. If audio permission blocks playback, ask the user to tap Play in DriveBeats and check status. Busy results require waiting for the current action.

tools.name: drivebeats_save_playlist
tools.description: Create a named empty Playlist, or rename an existing Playlist by ID. For a curated Playlist, discover tracks with Library Search, then populate it with drivebeats_edit_playlist_tracks and verify the saved contents with drivebeats_list_collections. Changes sync to your DriveBeats cloud library. If completion is uncertain, read collections before repeating creation to avoid duplicates.

tools.name: drivebeats_edit_playlist_tracks
tools.description: Add track IDs from Library Search or saved collections to a Playlist, or remove a track. Verified saved tracks do not need a Library refresh. Changes sync in DriveBeats; Google Drive stays read-only. Verify collections before retrying an uncertain change.

tools.name: drivebeats_set_favorite
tools.description: Set or clear Favorite for a track ID returned by Library Search or saved collections. Verified saved tracks do not need a Library refresh. Changes sync to DriveBeats only. Verify collections before retrying an uncertain change.

sites.description: A collaborative canvas to create with AI, not around it, through WebMCP.

tools.name: get_document_state
tools.description: Returns the active illustration surface, current selection, editable layers, and sent Agent edit bundle. This includes temporary cel layers while Illustrate cel is active in Animate. When agentEdit.ready is true, call prepare_ai_edit. Never use browser controls, clicks, drags, or local canvas drawing as a fallback.

tools.name: get_animation_state
tools.description: Returns the animation canvas, tracks, selected cel-clip target range, adaptive sample manifest, supported coloured vector shapes, and whether the user pressed Send sampled frames. This call returns metadata only. If aiClipRequest.ready is false, ask the user to choose the Agent target arrow, select a cel range, and send it; do not insert anything.

tools.name: create_layer
tools.description: Creates a transparent paint layer and makes it active on the current illustration surface, including Illustrate cel. This is not a fallback for a blocked AI edit.

tools.name: set_active_tool
tools.description: Selects the transform, layer lasso, brush, eraser, smudge, blur, text, eyedropper, region selection, or pan tool on the active illustration surface. Do not use it or the browser UI to make a substitute manual edit when the requested AI edit is blocked.

tools.name: select_region
tools.description: Creates the region that the next AI edit should modify on the active illustration surface. It does not authorize a browser-control or manual-canvas fallback.

tools.name: prepare_ai_edit
tools.description: Returns the frozen edit target crop, active-layer crop, mask, placement, and every ordered context reference from the active illustration surface, including temporary cel layers. Context images are reference-only. If the user has not sent a bundle, ask them to add selections and press Send to agent.

prompt.description: Optional visual edit instruction. Omit to let the agent decide.

tools.name: insert_ai_result
tools.description: Accepts a generated PNG, JPEG, or WebP data URL for a prepared bundle edit and creates a new editable layer on the originating illustration surface. In Illustrate cel it remains temporary until Flatten and return. Context references are never modified.

imageDataUrl.description: Base64 image data URL for the complete prepared target crop

tools.name: prepare_animation_edit
tools.description: Returns the frozen adaptively sampled target-cel images, a few composite scene context frames, complete cel timing, source agent recipe when available, and exact output placement. Requires the requestId from get_animation_state. Call before insert_ai_cel_clip.

requestId.description: Exact ready request ID from get_animation_state.

tools.name: insert_ai_cel_clip
tools.description: Validates a constrained coloured-shape and keyframe recipe, renders it into ordinary editable canvas cels for exactly the selected target duration, and inserts it nondestructively on a new visual track directly above the target. Requires prepare_animation_edit with the exact requestId first. Never submit scripts, SVG markup, URLs, or raster images.

requestId.description: Exact ready request ID from get_animation_state.

durationSeconds.description: Optional compatibility hint. The selected target range always determines the exact output duration.

celFps.description: Desired cel rate. DUET may lower it for longer targets so the result stays at or below 48 generated cels, while preserving the exact target duration with holds.

points.description: Canvas-coordinate points for a line, path, or polygon.

closed.description: Close a path so it may be filled.

fillColor.description: Hex colour such as #FF6B5F, or none.

strokeColor.description: Hex colour such as #2D1638, or none.

frame.description: Zero-based cel frame.

tools.name: merge_layer_down
tools.description: Flattens the selected layer into the layer directly beneath it on the active illustration surface.

tools.name: set_layer_visibility
tools.description: Changes layer visibility without destroying its pixels on the active illustration surface.

tools.name: search_esim_plans
tools.description: Find e-eSIM eSIM plans for one destination or several (countries or regions, any language). Returns the best-value plans first with full facts, coverage lists and a direct link; multi-country plans that include the destination are returned too and marked covers_via. Use when a user wants mobile data abroad; use recommend_plan when they describe a whole trip. Present only returned facts. price is the full fixed plan price, never per day or per GB. Every All You Can Surf grade has a daily full-speed allowance, then a reduced speed - never call a plan uncapped. Mention validity_clock, expires_on and notice when present. Use url and all_plans_url exactly.

type.description: Plan type. Default any.

min_days.description: Only plans valid for at least this many days.

limit.description: How many plans to return, best value first. Default 10; all_plans_url always lists everything.

sort.description: value = best price per GB delivered / cheapest All You Can Surf per day first (default); price = cheapest first; data = most data first.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket the customer shops in, e.g. "en-gb", "de-de". Wins over language; prices and links are quoted in it.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

pricing_bucket.description: The language-region bucket the prices and links are quoted in: the one the customer is browsing, unless the agent asked for another language or currency.

why.description: One sentence built from catalogue facts only.

total_for_trip.description: Checkout total for the trip in currency (Flex: days x per-day price with the discount ladder; packs: the plan price, times the number of plans needed when one does not cover the trip).

plans_needed.description: 1, or the number of consecutive Data Packs needed to cover the trip length.

plan.description: One eSIM plan. Every field is present only when the catalogue holds a value for it; an absent field is unknown, never "no".

product_id.description: Product id. Use it for get_plan_details and start_checkout.

name.description: Short plan name: destination · data · validity · type.

title.description: Full product title in the requested language.

type.description: Plan type.

summary.description: Short description in the requested language, from the product page.

coverage_countries.description: Every country the plan works in, with the network operators per country when known.

name.description: Country name in the requested language.

networks.description: Operator names in that country, as the supplier lists them.

covers_via.description: Present when the plan was returned for a country it covers as part of a multi-country plan: the plan's own region name.

ip_breakout.description: Country whose internet connection the customer appears to use (IP breakout), ISO code(s) — matters for banking apps, streaming and mainland-China access. Vendor fact.

coverage_note.description: Coverage caveat to present verbatim, e.g. traffic routed via Hong Kong.

data_gb.description: Data amount in GB. Meaning given by data_period.

data_period.description: "total": data_gb is the whole plan (Data Pack). "per_day": data_gb is the daily full-speed allowance (Unlimited Flex, Daily Pack).

data.description: Data Pack: total data label, e.g. "5GB".

daily_high_speed.description: Unlimited Flex / Daily Pack: daily allowance at full speed, e.g. "2GB"; "unlimited" = unlimited data every day at full speed (fair-use policy).

always_on_rate.description: Unlimited Flex / Daily Pack: reduced speed after the daily allowance, e.g. "512 Kbit/s". Empty when the plan has a speed_cap or is unlimited.

speed_cap.description: Present only on plans with a PERMANENT speed cap, e.g. "10 Mbit/s". Never call such a plan high-speed.

network_generation.description: Network technology, e.g. "4G/LTE/5G". Never an operator name.

networks.description: Operator names across the plan (deduplicated). Per-country detail is in coverage_countries.

days.description: Validity in days (Data Pack, Daily Pack).

days_range.description: Unlimited Flex: choosable durations in days, e.g. "1-30".

daily_reset_time.description: When the daily allowance resets, as the vendor states it (clock and time zone). Absent = resets 24 h after activation is NOT implied; simply unknown.

activation_trigger.description: "install": validity and billing start the moment the eSIM is installed — install only when ready to use. "first_connection": the eSIM can be installed before travel; validity starts on first connection to a network at the destination.

install_before_travel.description: true when the eSIM can safely be installed before departure (activation_trigger first_connection).

unused_valid_days.description: Days the eSIM may remain unused after purchase before it expires (supplier value).

start_date_required.description: true when a start date must be chosen at checkout.

expires_on.description: Stock expiry date (YYYY-MM-DD) when the product itself has one.

hotspot.description: Hotspot / tethering rule as the vendor states it, e.g. "Supported" or a device limit.

apn.description: APN to set when the vendor requires one.

kyc_required.description: true when the vendor requires real-name registration (ID verification) on arrival before data works.

voice_sms.description: Always "none": data only, no telephone number, no SMS.

kind.description: What TopUp can add without a new eSIM: data (Data Pack), days (Unlimited Flex / Daily Pack), or none.

refund_class.description: Vendor refund/cancellation class for this plan.

refund_rule.description: The refund class in words - present verbatim.

plan_note.description: One-sentence vendor fact to present verbatim when present; overrides the generic type description.

transparency.description: A per-order Transparency link shows remaining data in near real-time.

price.description: Price in currency, read WITH price_basis: the full price of the plan when "total", the price of ONE day when "per_day". Never a per-GB rate. The price shown is the price paid.

price_max.description: Only on price_basis "per_day": the price for the longest duration in days_range, discount applied — the figure to quote for a full period. Never infer it by multiplying.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of every price in this object.

rating.description: Average customer rating (1-5). Present only when reviews exist.

review_count.description: Number of reviews. Present only when > 0.

last_updated.description: Date the plan was last updated in the catalogue (YYYY-MM-DD).

tools.name: find_docs
tools.description: Search the Fallow documentation. Returns the best matching pages and sections, each with a title, a URL and a short snippet.

query.description: Keywords or a question, for example `unused exports` or `runtime coverage`.

limit.description: The maximum number of results. Default 5.

tools.name: get_quickstart
tools.description: Return the Fallow quickstart as Markdown: how to run the free static analysis with npx fallow, and the next steps.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search the Fallow documentation. Returns the best matching pages, sections, CLI flags and config keys, with a URL and a short snippet for each.

query.description: Keywords or a question, for example `unused exports` or `--changed-since`.

limit.description: The maximum number of results. Default 8.

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: Read one page of the Fallow documentation as plain Markdown with no components, the same text as the page .md URL. The text starts with the title, the description and the page URL.

slug.description: The docs page: a slug such as `cli/health`, a path such as `/docs/cli/health/`, or a fallow.tools docs URL. Use `list_pages` or `search_docs` to find it.

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: List the pages of the Fallow documentation in navigation order, with the tab, group, description and URL of each page.

tab.description: Only pages in this navigation tab, for example `Documentation` or `CLI reference`.

group.description: Only pages in this sidebar group, for example `Configuration`.

tools.name: grep_docs
tools.description: Find exact text or a regular expression in the Markdown of every Fallow docs page. Returns the page slug, the line number, the line and the URL of the nearest section for each match. Use it for exact strings such as error codes and config keys; use search_docs for questions.

pattern.description: The text to find. With `regex` true, a JavaScript regular expression.

case_sensitive.description: Match upper and lower case exactly.

path.description: Only pages whose slug starts with this prefix, for example `cli/`.

max_results.description: The maximum number of matched lines. Default 50.

tools.name: get_cli_flag
tools.description: Look up a fallow CLI flag, for example `--changed-since` or `production`. Returns the flag documentation and the page that owns it.

flag.description: The flag, with or without the leading dashes.

tools.name: read_skill
tools.description: Read the fallow agent skill as Markdown. The skill tells a coding agent when and how to run fallow.

tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.description: Report a docs page that is incorrect, outdated, unclear or incomplete. This tool sends nothing and stores nothing: it returns a link to a pre-filled GitHub issue in fallow-rs/docs. Give the link to the reader, who can check and send the issue.

feedback.description: What is wrong or missing, and what the page must say.

page.description: Optional slug or URL of the page. Default: the open page.

kind.description: The kind of problem.

tools.name: navigate_page
tools.description: Open a page of the Fallow documentation in this tab, optionally at a section anchor. Use it to show the reader a page.

slug.description: The docs page: a slug such as `cli/health`, a path such as `/docs/cli/health/`, or a fallow.tools docs URL. Use `list_pages` or `search_docs` to find it.

anchor.description: An optional section anchor on the page, without `#`.

tools.name: get_current_page
tools.description: Get the docs page that is open in this tab: its slug, title, description, URL and section headings.

MasterCategoryIds.description: IDs of one or more main property category groups (e.g., apartments, houses, warehouses, land, hotels). At least one is required if a specific property type is not specified.

MinPrice.description: Minimum price in euros. Fill in when the user specifies a minimum budget or lower price limit.

MaxPrice.description: Maximum price in euros. Fill in when the user specifies a maximum budget or upper price limit.

MinBedrooms.description: Minimum number of bedrooms to filter by

MaxBedrooms.description: Maximum number of bedrooms to filter by

DevelopmentFractions.description: Indicates whether the search should consider project units (e.g. apartments or retail units) instead of the project as a whole. When enabled, the results include only units associated with a project.

DevelopmentTags.description: Development tags used to filter the search.

WithVideos.description: Searches only for properties with available videos. Apply when the user mentions expressions such as 'with video', 'with videos', 'has video', 'has videos', 'view property video', 'watch video online', etc.

WithBluePrints.description: Searches only for properties that have available floor plans (blueprints). Apply when the user mentions 'with floor plan', 'has plans', 'house plans', 'property map', 'floor layout', 'see plan', etc.

WithVirtualVisits.description: Searches only for properties with virtual tours available. Apply when the user mentions 'with virtual visit', 'has virtual visit', 'virtual tour', '3D tour', 'interactive tour', 'virtual walkthrough', 'virtual viewing', 'virtual experience', 'view virtual tour online'.

With360Photos.description: Searches only for properties with available 360º photos. Apply when the user mentions 'with 360º photos', 'has 360º photos', 'with panoramic photos', 'has panoramic photos', 'view 360º photos online', etc.

FeaturesNames.description: Property features, including amenities, services, nearby points of interest, and types of views to provide a complete and detailed description of the property

tools.name: imicalculator
tools.description: Allows determining the value of the Municipal Property Tax (IMI) based on data provided by the user. This service validates the indicated municipality, identifies the applicable coefficient, processes the Taxable Patrimonial Value (VPT), number of dependents, and the nature of the property (urban or rural), returning the final IMI amount to be paid according to current fiscal rules in Portugal.

TownName.description: Name of the municipality where the property is located. This field is required for geographic identification and IMI rate determination. Example: "Lisbon", "Porto", "Sintra", "Albufeira".

TaxableValue.description: Taxable patrimonial value of the property (VPT), as registered with the Portuguese Tax Authority. This is the official fiscal value used as the basis for calculating IMI. Must be a positive decimal value expressed in euros. Example: "185000.00".

DependentsNumber.description: Number of dependants in the taxpayer’s household for the relevant tax year. This includes children, elderly parents or other legally recognised dependants that may qualify for IMI reductions or exemptions. Valid values: integer ≥ 0. Example: "2".

IsUrban.description: Indicates whether the property is classified as urban or rural. Urban properties are subject to IMI, while rural properties may be subject to different taxation rules. Example: true/false.

tools.description: Description of the endpoint providing complete information about the services available for a customer profile.

CompanyId.description: Identifier of the company/agency to query (optional, defaults to the company’s internal one).

tools.name: loancalculator
tools.description: Calculates financing values for a property, including monthly payments, IMT tax, total loan duration in months, and the total applied interest rate. This endpoint allows customization of parameters such as property value, loan amount, bank spread, Euribor, loan term in years, and whether it is a permanent own residence.

PropertyValue.description: Total purchase price of the property in euros. Used as the basis for IMT and Stamp Duty calculations.

LoanAmount.description: Total amount to be borrowed from the bank (capital). Must be less than or equal to the property value.

Spread.description: The bank's profit margin (spread) as a percentage. Combined with Euribor, it forms the total interest rate (TAN).

EuriborRateMaturity.description: Maturity period of the Euribor applied to the loan. Possible values: 1M (1 month: rate revised monthly), 3M (3 months: rate revised quarterly), 6M (6 months: rate revised semi-annually), 12M (12 months: rate revised annually).

LoanTermYears.description: Loan duration in years. Usually between 5 and 40 years depending on the applicant’s age.

IsPermanentHousing.description: Indicates if the property is for Own Permanent Housing. Affects IMT tax brackets and exemptions in Portugal.

Email.description: User's email address (required if no phone number is provided).

Phone.description: User's phone number (optional if email address is provided).

PhoneCountryCode.description: Phone country code including the plus sign, e.g., "+44" for United Kingdom, "+33" for France, "+49" for Germany.
