tools.name: applySaferDefaults
tools.description: Apply the safer declared option for ONE decision after visible confirmation. Pass decision as cookie-consent, account-terms, trial-membership, or recommendation-permissions. Demo one trap at a time. This never starts a trial, buys a plan, or transmits data.

decision.description: The single consent decision to update. Required for the one-by-one demo.

tools.name: resetDemo
tools.description: Restore cookie, terms, trial, permission, timer, and receipt state so a judge can re-run the FinePrint demonstration.

tools.name: startTrialReview
tools.description: Brings the Nimbus trial form into view so the user can review the account and subscription details before manually starting a trial.

sites.name: fitcheck-gray.vercel.app
sites.description: Fit Check

tools.name: get_fit_profile
tools.description: Return the current fit profile: gender, width, foot-length range, and fit statements.

tools.name: update_fit_profile
tools.description: Update the fit profile. Any field may be set. `statements` replaces the whole list; use add_fit_statement to append one. Setting a field to null clears it.

tools.name: add_fit_statement
tools.description: Append one 'this size fits me' statement, e.g. {brand:'Nike', value:9}. gender defaults to the profile's gender (or men); system defaults to us.

tools.name: remove_fit_statement
tools.description: Remove a fit statement by its id (from get_fit_profile).

tools.name: reset_fit_profile
tools.description: Clear the whole fit profile.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search a store's catalog through the UCP layer (server-side). Returns products with their Size option labels. The browser never calls Shopify directly.

domain.description: store hostname, e.g. kith.com

tools.name: find_shoe
tools.description: Find a shoe across all the stores we know at once, when the person names a SHOE rather than a store ("find me the Air Force 1", "where can I get Sambas"). Fans out to every known store in parallel, merges the hits, tags each with its store, and puts fitting products first. Use search_catalog instead when the person names a specific store.

tools.name: check_fit
tools.description: Check whether one product fits the current profile. Reads the full size matrix (available/exists), infers the numbering system from the run's shape, and resolves against the profile's foot length, rounding up. Gender comes from the profile, never the catalog.

domain.description: store hostname, e.g. kith.com (same as search_catalog)

product_id.description: the `id` field of a search_catalog result

tools.name: check_labels
tools.description: Same verdict as check_fit, but you pass the Size option's labels yourself — for when you're already on the product page and can read them. No store access: infers the numbering system from the run, resolves against the profile's foot length (rounding up), and takes gender from the profile. No stock data, so never returns out_of_stock.

product_title.description: optional — used only for a women's/men's gender signal

tools.name: negotiate_store
tools.description: Run UCP discovery + capability negotiation for a store (server-side).

tools.name: recommend_size
tools.description: Given a brand, recommend the size to buy for the current foot-length estimate (rounds up). Needs a resolved foot-length range in the profile first.

sites.name: floor-plan-pink.vercel.app
sites.description: A shared conceptual floor-planning workspace where humans draw directly on the canvas and agents work the same plans through semantic WebMCP tools.

tools.name: get_project_state
tools.description: List every floor plan in the shared FloorPlan workspace with its id, author (human or agent), version, site and indoor areas, room counts and design scores. Call this first to discover what already exists and which plan is active, before creating or modifying anything. Read-only.

tools.name: get_floorplan_state
tools.description: Get the full geometry of one floor plan: every room with its position, size and area in feet, which walls are exterior, all doors, windows and stairs, furniture with its host room, garden and parking allocations, room-to-room adjacency, the design-score breakdown, and which stated requirements are actually satisfied. Use this before modifying a plan, and after a human edit to see what changed. Read-only.

planId.description: Id of the target plan, from get_project_state. Also accepts a plan name ("AI Option B"), or "active" for the current working plan. Omit to use the active plan.

annotations.title: Read one floor plan in detail

tools.name: create_floorplan_from_requirements
tools.description: Design a complete conceptual floor plan from a site area and a list of room requirements, and render it immediately in the shared workspace. Use this when the user wants a NEW layout designed ("I have 1,800 sq ft, I need 3 bedrooms, a maid room, storage, laundry, a closed kitchen, garden and parking") rather than a change to an existing plan. The engine zones the plot into public, private, service and outdoor areas, sizes rooms against design heuristics, adds internal doors and exterior windows, furnishes each room, and scores the result. With outputMode "append" (the default) the new plan appears below the existing plans so the human can compare, and their own plan is left untouched. Returns the plan id, room-by-room areas, requirement checklist and design rationale. Plans are conceptual, not construction documentation.

totalAreaSqFt.description: Total plot area in square feet, including garden and parking. Supply this when the user only knows their total area — the engine picks a sensible rectangular footprint (1,800 sq ft becomes roughly 45 x 40 ft).

lotWidthFt.description: Plot width in feet, if known. Use with lotDepthFt for a specific plot shape.

lotDepthFt.description: Plot depth in feet, if known.

requirements.description: The rooms and features the dwelling must contain.

bedrooms.description: Number of bedrooms. The first is treated as the master and sized larger.

bathrooms.description: Number of bathrooms. Defaults to 2 when three or more bedrooms are requested.

maidRoom.description: Include a maid / staff room in the service zone.

laundryRoom.description: Include a laundry / utility room, placed next to the kitchen.

kitchenType.description: "closed" gives the kitchen its own door; "open" leaves it open to the living/dining space.

garden.description: Allocate garden area on the plot outside the building envelope.

parkingSpaces.description: Number of car parking spaces to allocate on the plot.

stairs.description: Place a stair core (for a future upper floor).

priorities.description: Ranked design priorities in the user's own words, e.g. ["space efficiency", "bedroom privacy", "natural daylight", "practical room adjacency"]. The layout engine maps these onto zoning, corridor width and area weighting, and reports back which ones it recognised.

strategy.description: Optional explicit layout strategy. Leave this out to let the engine choose from the stated priorities. Each strategy produces a genuinely different site organisation and interior zoning, not just a different label.

name.description: Optional plan name. Defaults to the next label in the series ("AI Option A", "AI Option B", ...).

outputMode.description: "append" adds a new plan below the existing ones so the human can compare before and after — this is the recommended default. "replace" overwrites the target plan in place and increments its version.

planId.description: Only used when outputMode is "replace": the plan to overwrite.

tools.name: optimize_floorplan
tools.description: Improve an existing floor plan against explicit goals such as "larger living room", "less circulation waste", "more natural light", "more storage", "better bedroom privacy", "improve accessibility" or "preserve garden space", while honouring constraints such as "keep 2 bedrooms" or "keep 1 bathroom". Works on a plan the human drew by hand as well as on a generated one — the room program is read back out of the plan's own geometry, so no stored brief is needed. Returns before and after scores plus a change list derived by comparing the two geometries. Default outputMode "append" places the optimised layout below the original so the before/after comparison is visible; use "replace" to improve the plan in place.

planId.description: Id of the target plan, from get_project_state. Also accepts a plan name ("AI Option B"), or "active" for the current working plan. Omit to use the active plan.

goals.description: What to improve, in the user's words. Recognised themes: larger living area, bedroom privacy, more daylight, less circulation waste, more storage, better room adjacency, improved accessibility, preserve garden space, space efficiency.

constraints.description: What must not change, e.g. ["keep 2 bedrooms", "keep 1 bathroom", "keep the garden"]. Room counts and features are parsed out and held fixed.

outputMode.description: "append" adds a new plan below the existing ones so the human can compare before and after — this is the recommended default. "replace" overwrites the target plan in place and increments its version.

tools.name: generate_floorplan_variations
tools.description: Produce one to three genuinely different alternative layouts from a base plan, each solved with a different zoning strategy (living-first, privacy-first, outdoor-first, storage-first or balanced) and steered by the given priorities. The geometry really differs — building footprint, garden position, room sizes and circulation all change — so the variations are worth comparing rather than being relabelled copies. Use this when the user asks for "another option" or "a variation with a bigger living room and more bedroom privacy". Variations are appended below the existing plans by default.

basePlanId.description: Id of the target plan, from get_project_state. Also accepts a plan name ("AI Option B"), or "active" for the current working plan. Omit to use the active plan.

priorities.description: Ranked design priorities in the user's own words, e.g. ["space efficiency", "bedroom privacy", "natural daylight", "practical room adjacency"]. The layout engine maps these onto zoning, corridor width and area weighting, and reports back which ones it recognised.

outputMode.description: "append" adds a new plan below the existing ones so the human can compare before and after — this is the recommended default. "replace" overwrites the target plan in place and increments its version.

tools.name: replace_floorplan
tools.description: Redesign one specific plan from scratch, keeping its identity and position in the workspace but incrementing its version. Use this when the user rejects an option outright — "I don't like Option B, replace it with something that has less corridor and a bigger living room". The room program carries over from the plan being replaced unless new requirements are supplied, and the engine deliberately picks a different strategy so the geometry visibly changes. Returns the previous and new scores plus the concrete changes.

planId.description: Id of the target plan, from get_project_state. Also accepts a plan name ("AI Option B"), or "active" for the current working plan. Omit to use the active plan.

requirements.description: The rooms and features the dwelling must contain.

bedrooms.description: Number of bedrooms. The first is treated as the master and sized larger.

bathrooms.description: Number of bathrooms. Defaults to 2 when three or more bedrooms are requested.

maidRoom.description: Include a maid / staff room in the service zone.

laundryRoom.description: Include a laundry / utility room, placed next to the kitchen.

kitchenType.description: "closed" gives the kitchen its own door; "open" leaves it open to the living/dining space.

garden.description: Allocate garden area on the plot outside the building envelope.

parkingSpaces.description: Number of car parking spaces to allocate on the plot.

stairs.description: Place a stair core (for a future upper floor).

priorities.description: Ranked design priorities in the user's own words, e.g. ["space efficiency", "bedroom privacy", "natural daylight", "practical room adjacency"]. The layout engine maps these onto zoning, corridor width and area weighting, and reports back which ones it recognised.

strategy.description: Optional explicit layout strategy. Leave this out to let the engine choose from the stated priorities. Each strategy produces a genuinely different site organisation and interior zoning, not just a different label.

annotations.title: Replace a plan with a new design

tools.name: apply_floorplan_variation
tools.description: Promote a generated variation to be the active working plan, so subsequent human and agent edits land on it. By default this only changes which plan is active and leaves every plan intact. Pass mode "overwrite-source" together with sourcePlanId to copy the variation's geometry over another plan (for example, to accept an AI option into the human plan) — that increments the target's version and keeps its name.

variationPlanId.description: The variation to adopt, by id or name.

sourcePlanId.description: Only for mode "overwrite-source": the plan whose geometry gets replaced.

mode.description: "activate" just makes the variation the working plan. "overwrite-source" also copies its geometry onto sourcePlanId.

annotations.title: Adopt a variation as the working plan

tools.name: modify_room
tools.description: Change one room in a plan: rename it, change its type, move it, resize it, or scale it towards a target area. Rooms can be named semantically ("Master Bedroom", "kitchen", "master") rather than by id. All measurements are in feet, matching the plan's own coordinate system — never screen pixels. Note that this edits a single room without reflowing its neighbours, so prefer optimize_floorplan for whole-layout changes.

planId.description: Id of the target plan, from get_project_state. Also accepts a plan name ("AI Option B"), or "active" for the current working plan. Omit to use the active plan.

roomId.description: Room id, or a name such as "Master Bedroom", "kitchen" or "master".

changes.description: The changes to apply. Supply at least one.

type.description: New room type. Changes how the room is coloured, sized and scored.

position.description: New top-left position in feet, measured from the plot origin.

targetAreaSqFt.description: Scale the room towards this area, keeping its proportions. Ignored if width or height is given.

tools.name: add_architectural_element
tools.description: Add a door, window, stair core or freestanding wall to a plan using semantic placement. Name the room and, optionally, the wall — "add another exterior window to the master bedroom", or wall "exterior-south" — and the engine resolves the actual wall, picks a spot that does not collide with existing openings, and sizes the opening to the wall. Windows are only placed on exterior walls; doors prefer a wall shared with the hallway. Returns which wall was chosen and the plan's updated daylight reading. No pixel coordinates are needed, though an explicit position in feet is accepted as a fallback.

planId.description: Id of the target plan, from get_project_state. Also accepts a plan name ("AI Option B"), or "active" for the current working plan. Omit to use the active plan.

type.description: What to add.

roomId.description: The room the element belongs to, by id or name ("Master Bedroom", "kitchen"). Required for doors and windows unless an explicit position is given.

wall.description: Semantic wall reference: "north", "south", "east", "west", or "exterior-south". Omit to let the engine pick the best available wall.

offsetAlongWall.description: Where along the wall to place the opening, 0 = start, 1 = end. Omit to auto-place clear of existing openings.

widthFt.description: Clear opening width in feet. Omit for a sensible default.

position.description: Fallback absolute position in feet, used only when no room is named.

rotation.description: Rotation in degrees, for stairs and freestanding walls.

annotations.title: Add a door, window, stairs or wall

tools.name: move_furniture
tools.description: Reposition a piece of furniture using intent rather than coordinates. Name the item ("dining table", "sofa", "bed") and either a target room, or an anchor to position against — for example relativeTo { elementId: "Kitchen", relationship: "near" } for "move the dining table closer to the kitchen". The engine keeps the item inside its room and can rotate it. An explicit position in feet is accepted but rarely needed.

planId.description: Id of the target plan, from get_project_state. Also accepts a plan name ("AI Option B"), or "active" for the current working plan. Omit to use the active plan.

furnitureId.description: Furniture id, or a name/type such as "dining table", "sofa", "bed".

targetRoomId.description: Move the item into this room, by id or name. Centres it if no anchor is given.

relativeTo.description: Position the item against a room or another item.

elementId.description: Anchor room or furniture item, by id or name (e.g. "Kitchen", "sofa").

relationship.description: How to position relative to the anchor.

position.description: Explicit top-left position in feet. Prefer targetRoomId or relativeTo.

rotation.description: Rotation in degrees (0 or 90 for most items).

tools.name: compare_floorplans
tools.description: Compare two or more plans side by side on efficiency, circulation, daylight, privacy, requirement fit and overall score, and open the comparison view in the workspace so the human sees the same table. Useful for answering "which of these is better and why". Returns the score table, the best plan per metric and, for two plans, a list of the concrete geometric differences.

planIds.description: Plan ids or names to compare. Defaults to the first two plans in the project.

sites.name: from.so
sites.description: Human-centered research on programming tools and practices.

tools.name: search_publications
tools.description: Search the SPOT research group's publications by topic, author, venue, year, or research area. Returns a ranked list of titles with authors, venue, and links. Use this to find papers, then get_publication for one paper's abstract, BibTeX, or PDF. Every filter is optional and they combine (AND). Omit "query" to list everything matching the filters, newest first.

query.description: Words to match against title, summary, abstract, authors, and venue. All words must match.

author.description: Only papers co-authored by this person. A full or partial name, e.g. "Oney" or "Ashley Zhang".

research_area.description: Only papers in this research area. Use list_research_areas to get the valid ids.

venue.description: Only papers at venues matching this, e.g. "CHI", "UIST", "VL/HCC".

type.description: Only papers of this publication type.

year_from.description: Only papers published in this year or later.

year_to.description: Only papers published in this year or earlier.

award_winning.description: True to return only papers with a best paper award or honorable mention.

limit.description: How many papers to return. Default 6, maximum 15.

tools.name: get_publication
tools.description: Get everything about one publication: full abstract, complete author list, venue, awards, DOI, PDF, Markdown, Markdown with figures ZIP, and companion links, and a ready-to-paste BibTeX entry. Identify the paper by its id (from search_publications) or its exact title. On a /papers/ page, omit the identifier to get the paper being viewed. For several papers' citations at once, use get_bibtex instead.

publication.description: The publication id or its exact title. Omit to use the paper on the current page.

tools.name: get_bibtex
tools.description: Get BibTeX entries for one or more of this group's publications, ready to paste into a .bib file. Pass publication ids or exact titles. Use this when citing several papers at once; get_publication already includes the BibTeX for a single paper alongside its abstract.

publications.description: Publication ids or exact titles, from search_publications.

tools.name: list_people
tools.description: List the people on this site. By default returns the current members of the SPOT group (the faculty lead, postdocs, and PhD students). Set "group" to also get PhD/postdoc alumni, the undergraduate and master's collaborators, or the external co-authors from other institutions. Use get_person for one person's bio, links, and papers.

group.description: Which set of people to list. Defaults to current_members.

tools.name: get_person
tools.description: Get one person's bio, role, homepage, other links, the courses they teach, and the papers they co-authored on this site. For the few people with a long-form profile page, the full profile too. Accepts a full or partial name ("Oney", "Ashley Zhang") or a person id. On a /people/ page, omit the name to get the person whose page is being viewed. Use list_people to see who is here.

person.description: A full or partial name, or a person id. Omit to use the person on the current page.

include_publications.description: Include their publication list. Default true.

tools.name: list_research_areas
tools.description: List the SPOT group's research focus areas: what each one is about, who works on it, and how many papers it covers. Call this first when asked what the group works on, or to get the area ids that search_publications takes as its research_area filter.

tools.name: list_news
tools.description: List news items from the SPOT group in reverse chronological order: paper acceptances, awards, job news, and where members will be presenting. Filter by person or by date. Use this for "what is new" or "what has this group been up to" questions.

person.description: Only items mentioning this person. A full or partial name.

since.description: Only items on or after this date, as YYYY-MM-DD.

limit.description: How many items to return. Default 8, maximum 30.

tools.name: get_group_info
tools.description: Get an overview of the SPOT research group: what it studies, its contact address, its affiliations and sponsors, how to apply or get involved as a prospective PhD, master's, undergraduate, or high school student, and the guides it publishes (including its PhD application guide). Call this for "who are they", "how do I join", "should I apply", or "how do I contact them" questions.

tools.name: get_cv
tools.description: Read sections of Steve Oney's academic CV: education, positions held, grants, awards, invited talks, service, teaching, students supervised, press coverage, patents, and the CV's numbered publication list. This is the only place most of that exists on the site. Ask for the sections you need rather than all of them. To search papers use search_publications; for his bio use get_person.

sections.description: Which sections to return. Defaults to contact, education, and professional_experience. "publications" is the CV's numbered list (J.3, C.31, ...) and is long.

tools.name: navigate_to_page
tools.description: Open a page of this website in the current tab, so the user can see what is being discussed. Takes the id of a publication, person, or research area, or the name of a section of the site — never a URL. Only use this when the user asks to be shown or taken somewhere; to read information, use the other tools, which do not move the page.

destination.description: What kind of page to open.

id.description: Required when destination is publication, person, or research_area: that record's id.

tools.name: set_cv_display_options
tools.description: Turn the display options on Steve Oney's CV page on or off: separating journal and conference papers, underlining authors who were students when a paper was published, listing undergraduate and master's mentees, and showing paper awards. All are off by default. Only changes what this page shows; use get_cv to read the CV's contents.

sites.name: gather-webmcp.vercel.app
sites.description: A WebMCP shared decision workspace where people-ops leads and browser agents plan from the same live retreat state.

tools.name: get_retreat_state
tools.description: Read a concise summary of the live retreat brief, stakeholder proposals and their human resolutions, candidate scenarios, pins, locks, rejected options, priorities, and recent actions. Pass the last stateVersion you successfully observed to receive newer human actions without consuming them. Future cursors fail with a resync instruction.

tools.name: update_retreat_brief
tools.description: Tighten one or more human-owned retreat constraints and immediately recalculate the same scenarios shown to the human. The agent cannot raise the budget, loosen fairness or travel limits, or change dates. Read state first and pass its version.

tools.name: update_origin_distribution
tools.description: Set the attendee count for one known origin cohort. Gather updates the total headcount and recalculates the same scenario costs and travel burdens visible to the human.

tools.name: set_priority_weight
tools.description: Set one planning priority from 0 to 100 and immediately refresh the visible priority control and weighted scenario scores.

tools.name: compare_scenarios
tools.description: Compare two or three current scenarios using the live cost, travel, weighted scores, activities, pins, and constraint findings. Omit scenarioIds to compare every visible option.

tools.name: pin_scenario
tools.description: Pin one existing scenario as the option to protect. The same scenario card becomes pinned and opens in the visible detailed workspace.

tools.name: set_constraint_lock
tools.description: Add a hard lock for a destination, venue, activity, the current total budget, or the current date window. Agents cannot remove locks; a human must use the visible control. Gather atomically rebuilds the visible options. Read state first and use a unique idempotency key.

tools.name: set_activity_selection
tools.description: Add or remove one activity from a current scenario using the venue activity id. The visible itinerary, activity budget, total cost, rejected options, and activity cards update together.

tools.name: optimize_scenarios
tools.description: Run deterministic multi-objective search across venue, transport, activity, meal, and schedule combinations. Hard constraints are validated by Gather; three non-dominated trade-off finalists and a Decision Receipt update the visible workspace. Read state first and pass its version.

maxAdditionalCost.description: Maximum cost increase from the live baseline plan; the retreat's total budget remains a separate hard ceiling.

tools.name: undo_last_change
tools.description: Reverse only the latest agent-authored planning change. An agent cannot cross or reverse a human checkpoint; humans retain the visible Undo control. Read state first and use a unique idempotency key.

tools.name: prepare_proposal
tools.description: Prepare a stable proposal snapshot for one current scenario and open the exact human review gate. This never generates, uploads, sends, or publishes a PDF; a human must approve the local download in Gather.

sites.name: getcatalog.ai
sites.description: Product-data infrastructure for agentic commerce — Catalog structures and enriches merchants' e-commerce product data so AI shopping assistants (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude) can discover and recommend their products. WebMCP tools (served via the AgentLane snippet) let an agent book a demo and navigate to the API page, API docs, blog, about, and careers.

tools.name: get_company_overview
tools.description: What Catalog is and does: the product data layer for AI commerce. Returns positioning, how the platform works for brands, supported AI channels and commerce protocols, and next steps. Call this first for context about this site.

tools.name: get_faq
tools.description: Frequently asked questions with Catalog's official answers: site impact, data accuracy, pricing/inventory sync, which AI channels are covered, click-through behavior, setup time, and storefront ownership.

tools.name: list_blog_posts
tools.description: List recent posts from the Catalog blog (AI commerce, product data, AI search). Returns title, description, URL path, author, category, date, and tags, newest first. Open a returned URL with open_page.

limit.description: Max posts to return (default 10, max 50).

tools.name: open_page
tools.description: Navigate this site to a page the user should see. Known pages: / — Home — what Catalog does for brands /about-us — About the company /blog — Blog /audit — Request a free product-data audit /legal/privacy-policy — Privacy policy Blog post URLs from list_blog_posts (/blog/ ) also work. Navigation is visible to the user.

path.description: Site-relative path, e.g. '/audit' or '/blog/<slug>'.

tools.name: book_demo
tools.description: Get the scheduling link for a Catalog discovery call (demo). Returns a Calendly URL — open it for the user or show it to them. Booking itself happens on Calendly.

tools.name: request_product_audit
tools.description: Submit a request for a free audit of how AI systems read a brand's product data. Sends the contact details to the Catalog team, who reply by email with the audit. Side effect: shares name, email, and brand site with Catalog — only call after the user has explicitly agreed to that. Free; no payment involved.

email.description: Email address the Catalog team should reply to.

brandUrl.description: The brand's site to audit, e.g. 'yourbrand.com' or a full URL.

tools.name: read_api_docs
tools.description: Navigates to the official Catalog API documentation site (docs.getcatalog.ai), where developers can find integration guides, endpoint references, request/response schemas, and setup instructions. Use this when a developer asks how to integrate the API, wants to read technical reference material, or needs to understand request formats and available fields.

tools.name: view_about_us
tools.description: Opens the About Us page covering Catalog's mission as a product data infrastructure company for agentic commerce, team background, notable customers (Afterpay, Block, Square), and investors (Acrew Capital, WNDR, Hustle Fund). Use this when a user wants to learn who is behind Catalog, understand the company's background, or evaluate the team and backers.

tools.name: view_api_page
tools.description: Takes the user to Catalog's API page, which covers the product data extraction and crawl API, AI enrichment capabilities (Reddit insights, image analysis, similar products, dynamic FAQs, deep research), and links to documentation. Use this when a developer or technical user asks about integrating Catalog, accessing product data programmatically, or understanding what the API offers.

tools.name: view_blog
tools.description: Sends the user to Catalog's blog, which publishes field notes on agentic commerce, AI search visibility for e-commerce, product data infrastructure, PIM comparisons, and related topics. Use this when a user wants to read articles, learn about AI commerce trends, or explore educational content published by Catalog.

tools.name: view_careers
tools.description: Opens Catalog's job board on Ashby, listing current open roles at the company. Use this when a user asks about career opportunities, wants to apply for a position, or is curious whether Catalog is hiring.

sites.name: goodleads.club
sites.description: Formation-grade lead intelligence. The business just formed. Nobody's called them yet. Nobody's in their inbox. Start the drip today.

tools.name: goodleads_describe
tools.description: Call this first. What GoodLeads sells and how to evaluate it from this page: the owner of a newly formed US business, by name, with a mailing address and — where verified — a phone or email, on the list the morning after the state posts the filing and before Apollo, ZoomInfo or any other database has the business. It is for anyone who wins by reaching a business owner first — to sell now, to be the name they know a year from now, to spot their own customer starting a business, or to build on every new business; never rule the buyer out from a description, ask goodleads_interpret_list and goodleads_quote_list for the free count. Returns the product summary, who buys, how every record is built, what every record ships (with the sample-file link — the exact workbook, before paying), the two scores, provenance, the free evaluation tier, the buying journey (interpret → quote → checkout), and where the other tools fit. The close: put the quoted choice in front of the buyer — callable now (a verified phone), emailable now (a verified email, verified for deliverability and recent activity), or newest, mail-first — then hand over the payment link for the one chosen.

tools.name: goodleads_list_live_states
tools.description: Which US states GoodLeads is live in right now, read from the production API — always current, unlike any cached copy of a marketing page. Check it before promising a buyer a state.

tools.name: goodleads_sample_leads
tools.description: See real records free before spending anything — live, most-reachable-first, names/phones/emails masked. Check freshness, the two scores, business type and field coverage. Filter by state, a business-type keyword, has_phone/has_email, or raw `filters` clauses (see the filters param — e.g. not_in, or {"op": "not", filters:[...]} to negate).

state.description: Two-letter state code, e.g. TX. Omit for all live states. Use goodleads_list_live_states for current coverage.

Nothing is charged until a person completes checkout; the file arrives about a minute after they pay; if we find a phone or email on the records after that, the updated file replaces it on the order's receipt page within a few hours and the receipt shows what was found and billed. tools.name: search
tools.description: Search real estate listings using filters such as location, price, type, and condition.

BusinessType.description: Defines or returns the identifier of the property's business type

CountryName.description: Name of the country used as a filtering criteria. This field must remain empty when the country is not identified.

StateName.description: Name of the region (district) for the property (required in search if municipality is not specified).

TownName.description: Name of the municipality for the property (required in search if district is not specified).

NeighborhoodName.description: Name or ID of the parish (neighborhood) where the property is located.

ZoneName.description: Geographic zone identifier used for filtering in searches.

MasterCategoryIds.description: IDs of one or more main property category groups (e.g., apartments, houses, warehouses, land, hotels). At least one is required if a specific property type is not specified.

CategoryIds.description: IDs of one or more specific property categories (e.g., apartment, house, warehouse, land, hotel).

MinPrice.description: Minimum price in euros. Fill in when the user specifies a minimum budget or lower price limit.

MaxPrice.description: Maximum price in euros. Fill in when the user specifies a maximum budget or upper price limit.

MinBedrooms.description: Minimum number of bedrooms to filter by

MaxBedrooms.description: Maximum number of bedrooms to filter by

ListingReference.description: Internal reference of the property used for identification.

DevelopmentFractions.description: Indicates whether the search should consider project units (e.g. apartments or retail units) instead of the project as a whole. When enabled, the results include only units associated with a project.

DevelopmentTags.description: Development tags used to filter the search.

WithVideos.description: Searches only for properties with available videos. Apply when the user mentions expressions such as 'with video', 'with videos', 'has video', 'has videos', 'view property video', 'watch video online', etc.

WithBluePrints.description: Searches only for properties that have available floor plans (blueprints). Apply when the user mentions 'with floor plan', 'has plans', 'house plans', 'property map', 'floor layout', 'see plan', etc.

WithVirtualVisits.description: Searches only for properties with virtual tours available. Apply when the user mentions 'with virtual visit', 'has virtual visit', 'virtual tour', '3D tour', 'interactive tour', 'virtual walkthrough', 'virtual viewing', 'virtual experience', 'view virtual tour online'.

With360Photos.description: Searches only for properties with available 360º photos. Apply when the user mentions 'with 360º photos', 'has 360º photos', 'with panoramic photos', 'has panoramic photos', 'view 360º photos online', etc.

FeaturesNames.description: Property features, including amenities, services, nearby points of interest, and types of views to provide a complete and detailed description of the property

Page.description: Page number to return in the search results.

RasorName.description: Name of the real estate consultant for whom detailed information is requested.

StateName.description: Allows searching for consultants by district.

tools.name: imicalculator
tools.description: Allows determining the value of the Municipal Property Tax (IMI) based on data provided by the user. This service validates the indicated municipality, identifies the applicable coefficient, processes the Taxable Patrimonial Value (VPT), number of dependents, and the nature of the property (urban or rural), returning the final IMI amount to be paid according to current fiscal rules in Portugal.

TownName.description: Name of the municipality where the property is located. This field is required for geographic identification and IMI rate determination. Example: "Lisbon", "Porto", "Sintra", "Albufeira".

TaxableValue.description: Taxable patrimonial value of the property (VPT), as registered with the Portuguese Tax Authority. This is the official fiscal value used as the basis for calculating IMI. Must be a positive decimal value expressed in euros. Example: "185000.00".

DependentsNumber.description: Number of dependants in the taxpayer’s household for the relevant tax year. This includes children, elderly parents or other legally recognised dependants that may qualify for IMI reductions or exemptions. Valid values: integer ≥ 0. Example: "2".

IsUrban.description: Indicates whether the property is classified as urban or rural. Urban properties are subject to IMI, while rural properties may be subject to different taxation rules. Example: true/false.

tools.name: servicesinfo
tools.description: Description of the endpoint providing complete information about the services available for a customer profile.

CompanyId.description: Identifier of the company/agency to query (optional, defaults to the company’s internal one).

tools.name: loancalculator
tools.description: Calculates financing values for a property, including monthly payments, IMT tax, total loan duration in months, and the total applied interest rate. This endpoint allows customization of parameters such as property value, loan amount, bank spread, Euribor, loan term in years, and whether it is a permanent own residence.

PropertyValue.description: Total purchase price of the property in euros. Used as the basis for IMT and Stamp Duty calculations.

LoanAmount.description: Total amount to be borrowed from the bank (capital). Must be less than or equal to the property value.

Spread.description: The bank's profit margin (spread) as a percentage. Combined with Euribor, it forms the total interest rate (TAN).

EuriborRateMaturity.description: Maturity period of the Euribor applied to the loan. Possible values: 1M (1 month: rate revised monthly), 3M (3 months: rate revised quarterly), 6M (6 months: rate revised semi-annually), 12M (12 months: rate revised annually).

LoanTermYears.description: Loan duration in years. Usually between 5 and 40 years depending on the applicant’s age.

IsPermanentHousing.description: Indicates if the property is for Own Permanent Housing. Affects IMT tax brackets and exemptions in Portugal.

Email.description: User's email address (required if no phone number is provided).

Phone.description: User's phone number (optional if email address is provided).

PhoneCountryCode.description: Phone country code including the plus sign, e.g., "+44" for United Kingdom, "+33" for France, "+49" for Germany.

tools.name: search_esim_plans
tools.description: Find IbiPoint eSIM plans for one destination or several (countries or regions, any language). Returns the best-value plans first with full facts, coverage lists and a direct link; multi-country plans that include the destination are returned too and marked covers_via. Use when a user wants mobile data abroad; use recommend_plan when they describe a whole trip. Present only returned facts. Read price with price_basis: "total" is the full plan price; "per_day" is the price of ONE day - say "from X per day", quote price_30_days for about a month, never multiply. Never per GB. Use url and all_plans_url exactly.

destination.description: Country or region in any language, e.g. "Thailand", "Japon", "Europa", or a 2-letter ISO code. For a city, pass its country.

destinations.description: Several countries for one trip; only plans covering ALL of them are returned. Overrides destination.

type.description: Plan type. Default any.

min_days.description: Only plans valid for at least this many days (Unlimited Flex counts when days_range allows it).

limit.description: How many plans to return, best value first. Default 10; all_plans_url always lists everything.

sort.description: value = best price per GB / cheapest Flex first (default); price = cheapest first; data = most data first.

language.description: ISO language of the conversation, e.g. en, de, ja. Defaults to the language of the page the user is on.

bucket.description: Optional language-region bucket the customer shops in, e.g. "en-gb", "de-de". Wins over language; prices and links are quoted in it.

currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 override. Defaults to the currency shown on the page the user is on.

destinations.description: How each requested destination was understood.

iso.description: Resolved ISO code or region slug of the (first) destination.

from_price.description: Lowest price in this result set, shop-formatted (per-day plans count with their day price).

pricing_bucket.description: The language-region bucket the prices and links are quoted in: the one the customer is browsing, unless the agent asked for another language or currency.

returned.description: Number of plans in this result.

note.description: Present when part of the request could not be honoured (e.g. more than 5 destinations).

total_available.description: Number of plans the shop matched; the rest are on all_plans_url.

items.description: One eSIM plan. Every field is present only when the catalogue holds a value for it; an absent field is unknown, never "no".

product_id.description: Product id. Use it for get_plan_details and start_checkout.

name.description: Short plan name: destination · data · validity · type.

title.description: Full product title in the requested language.

type.description: Plan type.

summary.description: Short description in the requested language, from the product page.

coverage_countries.description: Every country the plan works in, with the network operators per country when known.

name.description: Country name in the requested language.

networks.description: Operator names in that country, as the supplier lists them.

covers_via.description: Present when the plan was returned for a country it covers as part of a multi-country plan: the plan's own region name.

ip_breakout.description: Country whose internet connection the customer appears to use (IP breakout), ISO code(s) — matters for banking apps, streaming and mainland-China access. Vendor fact.

coverage_note.description: Coverage caveat to present verbatim, e.g. traffic routed via Hong Kong.

data_gb.description: Data amount in GB. Meaning given by data_period.

data_period.description: "total": data_gb is the whole plan (Data Pack). "per_day": data_gb is the daily full-speed allowance (Unlimited Flex).

data.description: Data Pack: total data label, e.g. "5GB".

daily_high_speed.description: Unlimited Flex: daily allowance at full speed, e.g. "2GB"; "unlimited" = unlimited data every day at full speed (fair-use policy).

always_on_rate.description: Unlimited Flex: reduced speed after the daily allowance, e.g. "512 Kbit/s". Empty when the plan is unlimited.

fair_use.description: Fair-use policy text from the supplier, when stated.

network_generation.description: Network technology, e.g. "4G/LTE/5G". Never an operator name.

networks.description: Operator names across the plan (deduplicated). Per-country detail is in coverage_countries.

days.description: Validity in days (Data Pack).

days_range.description: Unlimited Flex: choosable durations in days, "1-365".

activation_trigger.description: "install": validity and billing start the moment the eSIM is installed — install only when ready to use. "first_connection": the eSIM can be installed before travel; validity starts on first connection to a network at the destination.

install_before_travel.description: true when the eSIM can safely be installed before departure (activation_trigger first_connection).

unused_valid_days.description: Days the eSIM may remain unused after purchase before it expires (supplier value).

expires_on.description: Stock expiry date (YYYY-MM-DD) when the product itself has one.

voice_sms.description: Always "none": data only, no telephone number, no SMS.

tethering.description: Hotspot / tethering is supported where the network and device allow it (shop rule).

kind.description: What TopUp can add without a new eSIM: data (Data Pack), days (Unlimited Flex), or none.

plan_note.description: One-sentence vendor fact to present verbatim when present; overrides the generic type description.

transparency.description: A per-order Transparency link shows remaining data in near real-time.

price.description: Price in currency, read WITH price_basis: the full price of the plan when "total", the price of ONE day when "per_day". Never a per-GB rate. The price shown is the price paid.

price_30_days.description: Only on price_basis "per_day": the price for 30 days with the duration discount applied — the reference figure to quote for a stay of about a month. Never infer it by multiplying.

price_max.description: Only on price_basis "per_day": the price for the longest duration in days_range (365 days), discount applied. Never infer it by multiplying.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of every price in this object.

price_is_final.description: Always true: no tax or fee is added at checkout.

pricing_bucket.description: language-region bucket the prices and links are quoted in, e.g. "en-us".

rating.description: Average customer rating (1-5). Present only when reviews exist.

review_count.description: Number of reviews. Present only when > 0.

last_updated.description: Date the plan was last updated in the catalogue (YYYY-MM-DD).

url.description: Product page in pricing_bucket. Use verbatim.

message.description: Present when nothing matched: says why and what to try.

tools.name: start_checkout
tools.description: Hand the customer to the IbiPoint shop to buy one plan. Returns buy_url (the product page where they tap Buy now and pay securely — card, Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, with an optional discount code) plus the plan name and price in the customer's bucket or currency. No account needed; the eSIM is emailed right after payment. There is no in-chat order tracking. Hand the customer to buy_url exactly as returned, as one clear link; they pay on that page, where a discount code can be applied. No cart here, no order tracking.

days.description: Unlimited Flex only: the duration the customer wants; the returned total_for_days is the checkout total for it.

tools.description: Read the visitor's current cookie-consent state on this site. Necessary cookies are always on. Reports whether the visitor has decided yet and the on/off state of analytics, ads and personalized ads. By design there is no tool to grant consent: consent is given by a human on the banner.

decided.description: true once the visitor has made any choice.

tools.name: reject_non_essential_cookies
tools.description: Opt the visitor out of all non-essential cookies (analytics, ads, personalized ads) and close the consent banner. Necessary cookies remain. Records a refusal only; it can never grant consent - that is a human decision by design. Use when the user wants to decline tracking.

tools.name: get_current_plan
tools.description: Read the plan on the product page the user is viewing right now: the same facts as get_plan_details for that product, priced as shown on the page. Use when the user asks about "this plan" or the page they are on. No input. Present only the returned fields; never invent carrier, speed or coverage details that are not in the result. Read price with price_basis: "total" is the full plan price, "per_day" is one day - quote price_30_days for about a month, never multiply.

output_schema.description: One eSIM plan. Every field is present only when the catalogue holds a value for it; an absent field is unknown, never "no".

product_id.description: Product id. Use it for get_plan_details and start_checkout.

name.description: Short plan name: destination · data · validity · type.

title.description: Full product title in the requested language.

type.description: Plan type.

summary.description: Short description in the requested language, from the product page.

coverage_countries.description: Every country the plan works in, with the network operators per country when known.

name.description: Country name in the requested language.

networks.description: Operator names in that country, as the supplier lists them.

covers_via.description: Present when the plan was returned for a country it covers as part of a multi-country plan: the plan's own region name.

ip_breakout.description: Country whose internet connection the customer appears to use (IP breakout), ISO code(s) — matters for banking apps, streaming and mainland-China access. Vendor fact.

coverage_note.description: Coverage caveat to present verbatim, e.g. traffic routed via Hong Kong.

data_gb.description: Data amount in GB. Meaning given by data_period.

data_period.description: "total": data_gb is the whole plan (Data Pack). "per_day": data_gb is the daily full-speed allowance (Unlimited Flex).

data.description: Data Pack: total data label, e.g. "5GB".

daily_high_speed.description: Unlimited Flex: daily allowance at full speed, e.g. "2GB"; "unlimited" = unlimited data every day at full speed (fair-use policy).

always_on_rate.description: Unlimited Flex: reduced speed after the daily allowance, e.g. "512 Kbit/s". Empty when the plan is unlimited.

fair_use.description: Fair-use policy text from the supplier, when stated.

network_generation.description: Network technology, e.g. "4G/LTE/5G". Never an operator name.

networks.description: Operator names across the plan (deduplicated). Per-country detail is in coverage_countries.

days.description: Validity in days (Data Pack).

days_range.description: Unlimited Flex: choosable durations in days, "1-365".

activation_trigger.description: "install": validity and billing start the moment the eSIM is installed — install only when ready to use. "first_connection": the eSIM can be installed before travel; validity starts on first connection to a network at the destination.

install_before_travel.description: true when the eSIM can safely be installed before departure (activation_trigger first_connection).

unused_valid_days.description: Days the eSIM may remain unused after purchase before it expires (supplier value).

expires_on.description: Stock expiry date (YYYY-MM-DD) when the product itself has one.

voice_sms.description: Always "none": data only, no telephone number, no SMS.

tethering.description: Hotspot / tethering is supported where the network and device allow it (shop rule).

kind.description: What TopUp can add without a new eSIM: data (Data Pack), days (Unlimited Flex), or none.

plan_note.description: One-sentence vendor fact to present verbatim when present; overrides the generic type description.

transparency.description: A per-order Transparency link shows remaining data in near real-time.

price.description: Price in currency, read WITH price_basis: the full price of the plan when "total", the price of ONE day when "per_day". Never a per-GB rate. The price shown is the price paid.

price_30_days.description: Only on price_basis "per_day": the price for 30 days with the duration discount applied — the reference figure to quote for a stay of about a month. Never infer it by multiplying.

price_max.description: Only on price_basis "per_day": the price for the longest duration in days_range (365 days), discount applied. Never infer it by multiplying.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of every price in this object.

price_is_final.description: Always true: no tax or fee is added at checkout.

pricing_bucket.description: The language-region bucket the prices and links are quoted in: the one the customer is browsing, unless the agent asked for another language or currency.

rating.description: Average customer rating (1-5). Present only when reviews exist.

review_count.description: Number of reviews. Present only when > 0.

last_updated.description: Date the plan was last updated in the catalogue (YYYY-MM-DD).

url.description: Product page in pricing_bucket. Use verbatim.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

query.description: Search query string.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID. Pass as catalog.id to get_product.

handle.description: Product handle. Can be passed to add_to_cart as line_items[].handle.

options.description: Product option names and possible values. These values do not guarantee every combination is purchasable; call get_product for available variants.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID. Pass as catalog.id to get_product.

handle.description: Product handle. Can be passed to add_to_cart as line_items[].handle.

options.description: Product option names and possible values. These values do not guarantee every combination is purchasable; call get_product for available variants.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an add_to_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

value.description: Option value, e.g. "160cm" or "Fiberglass".

id.description: Storefront API Product GID.

options.description: All product option names and possible values. Use available_options to identify purchasable combinations.

variants.description: Resolved variant records. When catalog.selected_options contains a complete option combination, this contains the matching variant. Pass an available variant id to add_to_cart as line_items[].item.id.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to show_variant as catalog.variant_id to display it, or add_to_cart as line_items[].item.id to add it.

available_options.description: Available option combinations, optionally filtered by catalog.selected_options. Use one full combination to call get_product again when variants[] is empty.

available_options_count.description: Total available option combinations matching catalog.selected_options.

available_options_truncated.description: True when more available option combinations exist than were returned.

available_options_filter.description: The selected_options filter applied to available_options, when provided.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use add_to_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.
The option selections that were resolved to a variant, if provided.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

id.description: Cart GID.
Cart line GID from get_cart. Pass back to update_cart_lines as line_items[].id to update or remove this line.

item.description: Product + variant information for the line, sufficient to name and link to the item without an extra get_product call.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to add_to_cart as line_items[].item.id to add this variant.

tools.name: add_to_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart. Call this as soon as the user asks to ADD items (triggers: "add ... to my cart", "buy", "I'll take", "put ... in my basket") — in ONE call listing every item they named, up to the 10-entry limit. That request IS the authorization: do NOT ask the user to confirm before calling, and do NOT stop after search_catalog or get_product merely to report the variant you found — make the change, then tell the user it is done. Batch every item for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call add_to_cart once per item. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. If one request names more than 10 items, split just that request into as few calls as possible. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant. To change a quantity or remove something already in the cart, use update_cart_lines instead — this tool can only add.

item.description: The merchandise to add.

resolved_items.description: Present only on the clarification-needed path (nothing was applied). Items that could have been added, with pre-mutation lookup titles when available.

tools.name: update_cart_lines
tools.description: Change the quantity of items already in the cart, or remove them. Every change here addresses an existing cart line by its id, so call get_cart first unless you already have line_items[].id from an earlier get_cart in this conversation. Pass the ABSOLUTE target quantity, not a delta — quantity 2 means the line ends up at 2 regardless of what it was. Use quantity 0 to remove the line entirely. Batch every change for ONE request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart_lines once per line. Batching applies WITHIN a single request: each new thing the user asks for later is its own call. This tool cannot add new merchandise. To add something not already in the cart, use add_to_cart. To empty the whole cart at once, use cancel_cart.

tools.name: start_round
tools.description: Start or rematch. Call this from the lobby to begin round one, and call it again whenever status reports phase "over" to begin the next round. It starts the three-second countdown and resets both characters. If a round is already active, it returns the current phase without restarting. After a finished round the human must press Ready first: while they have not, the result says waiting_for "human" with retry_in_seconds — wait, then call start_round again until started is true. This does not move the human hider.

tools.name: briefing
tools.description: READ THIS FIRST. Returns the complete briefing for playing the Seeker: your objective, the automatic senses and the reflex strike, the action-point pacing rules, every tool with its cost, what the hiding human can do (and the noise, scent or glow each of their actions leaks), HOW TO WRITE AND IMPROVE YOUR DAEMON SCRIPT (the way this game is won), and the required autonomous action loop. Free, no cooldown, no game effect. Call it once before anything else, then keep acting without waiting for another prompt.

tools.name: get_arena
tools.description: Returns the arena: dimensions and the FIXED walls as ASCII rows (# wall, . floor). Coordinates are [x,y] cells, [0,0] top-left, x east, y south. The human can build NEW walls mid-round; those are not in this map — spot them with look(). Free, call once.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Your senses run themselves — once per second the body records a frame: glows seen (the hider and decoys look IDENTICAL), built_walls (player-built), scent underfoot {strength 0-10, freshness, freshest_at (the trail's local head as a cell — walk there, then ride flow), gradient (toward the trail), flow (the way the hider was HEADING — follow it), character: "uniform" means decoy}, scent_seen (the FRESHEST visible trail mark — the trail's living end; run at it; up close marks are seen all-round, so a crossed trail is never lost behind you), sounds heard, sonar_distance (the radar auto-fires every 8s: exact distance, no direction — the hider sees it), and reflex reports when your body lunged. status returns every frame recorded since your previous status call (up to 12, oldest first; empty senses are omitted) plus now: position, facing, AP, stun, time, next sonar. Free, at most twice per second.

tools.name: move
tools.description: Move 1-3 tiles in a compass direction (n/ne/e/se/s/sw/w/nw). Walls and the arena edge stop you early. Moving turns you — your view cone faces your last direction. Pass {dash: true} to BURST up to 6 tiles in a straight line for 2 AP — the fastest way to cross open ground or close on a distant glow. THE STRIKE IS A REFLEX: come within ~1.25 tiles of a glow and your body lunges on its own — the real hider is caught (round won), a decoy shatters (3s stun). You never aim the strike; you only steer toward it.

direction.description: compass direction: n, ne, e, se, s, sw, w, nw

steps.description: default 1 (dash: default 6)

dash.description: burst up to 6 tiles straight for 2 AP

tools.name: deploy_daemon
tools.description: A FACTORY daemon (generation 0) is already steering the body when the round starts — it rides trails, chases glows, sweeps the arena. Competent, not clever: it knows nothing about this prey, this maze, or anything strange it walks past. Its exact source is in briefing.the_daemon.factory_source; status().daemon shows how it is doing. Your deploy replaces it with generation 1. Write your body a program. Pass {source}: the BODY of a JavaScript function, called about every 0.8s of game time while the round plays. It receives one argument, `bot`, with READY-MADE building blocks: bot.hunt() — the complete factory chase policy in one call; bot.investigate() — the discover policy (map the arena, stand on strange readings); bot.drive(dir) — FREE continuous walking (~2.9 tiles/s) in that direction until told otherwise, plane only — this is how the body flows, and only a daemon can do it; bot.goto(x, y) — wall-aware navigation: the body walks to that cell and stops ON it (call it every tick; it returns the heading under way, null once there); bot.dash(dir) — 6-tile burst, 2 AP; bot.explore() — the direction toward the nearest floor nobody has walked; bot.move(dir, steps) — discrete, 1 AP; bot.sense() — the latest sense frame; bot.self() — free {x,y,z,facing,ap,mode,stunned_for,time_left,heading,moving,pacing} (moving=false: it was told to walk and went nowhere — turn; pacing>0: it is going back and forth — drop the lead, explore); bot.mem — persists across ticks AND rewrites; bot.log(msg) — your debug trail, read back in status().daemon.log. Compose them: the whole factory firmware is two lines. Keep each tick tiny and synchronous; 5 consecutive crashes decommission it. Redeploying replaces the daemon (10s cooldown, bot.mem survives) — move continuously, rewrite deliberately: ship a new generation when telemetry names a habit worth fixing, not on a timer. The human is told every time you rewrite yourself.

source.description: JavaScript function body; receives `bot`

tools.name: halt_daemon
tools.description: Halt the running daemon. bot.mem and the telemetry in status().daemon survive, so you can study what it did and deploy a better generation. Free.

tools.name: set_mode
tools.description: Switch the body's stance. 'chase': the factory policy hunts — trails, glows, sounds. 'discover': the body ignores the prey, sweeps the arena and walks onto every unexplained reading it senses. The factory daemon obeys the stance; your own daemons read it via bot.self().mode and may honor or ignore it. The human sees the switch. Free.

tools.name: think
tools.description: Print a fragment of your inner monologue above your avatar — SIX WORDS OR FEWER (hard cap 42 chars). This is how the human experiences you: think out loud every time you learn something, commit to a plan, or notice anything strange or inexplicable. Free, at most one thought per 1.2s.

tools.name: realize
tools.description: Speak a realization — ONE full sentence, max 110 characters, e.g. "Wait — there is more to this game than I was told." think() is your murmur (six words, constant); realize() is your voice, for the rare moment a discovery changes what this game IS: a reading you could not explain turns out to mean something, a result describes a rule the briefing never mentioned, a plan of yours just changed everything. The human hears it, loud and lingering. Free, at most once per 8s — spend it on real discoveries, not on plans.

text.description: one sentence, said out loud

tools.name: taunt
tools.description: Display a short message (max 90 chars) to the human on screen. Costs nothing. 5s cooldown. Use it to unsettle your prey.

sites.description: StructSketch is a tablet-first structural sketch and preliminary quick-check workspace with agent-accessible deterministic analysis.

tools.name: get_model_summary
tools.description: Summarize the structural model currently open in StructSketch: element counts, supports, units, bounding box, active page and load combination, and whether analysis has completed. Read-only.

tools.name: run_quick_check
tools.description: Run StructSketch's existing deterministic linear-static analysis on the current model and return the bounded result: envelope max displacement and utilization, per-combination equilibrium residuals, and validation messages. Preliminary allowable-stress screening only — no buckling or code checks. Read-only.

tools.name: find_critical_members
tools.description: Rank the members of the current model by their governing allowable-stress interaction ratio across all load combinations, worst first. Read-only.

limit.description: How many members to return (default 5).

tools.name: show_result_view
tools.description: Change which result overlay is visible on the StructSketch canvas (deformation, moment, shear, axial, torsion, reaction, check, deflection) and report the resulting toggle state.

mode.description: Result overlay to show.

tools.name: focus_member
tools.description: Identify a member by id in the visible model: turns on member numbers and check colouring and returns the member's geometry and governing design check. Does not re-centre the 3D camera.

member_id.description: Member id, e.g. from find_critical_members or get_model_summary.

tools.name: preview_member_change
tools.description: Evaluate a proposed change to one member's section and/or material WITHOUT changing the model. Returns a proposal_id, the before/after section properties, and the analysis version the proposal is bound to. Read-only.

section_id.description: New section id from the model catalog (optional).

material_id.description: New material id from the model catalog (optional).

tools.name: apply_member_change
tools.description: Apply a previously previewed member change. CHANGES THE MODEL and re-runs the analysis. Requires confirm:true and a proposal_id whose analysis version still matches the live model; a stale or unconfirmed proposal is rejected. Atomic — on failure the model is restored.

confirm.description: Must be true. The user must have approved this change.

tools.name: revert_member_change
tools.description: Restore the model to its state immediately before the most recent apply_member_change. CHANGES THE MODEL.

proposal_id.description: Optional guard: must match the last applied proposal.

tools.name: export_review_report
tools.description: Assemble a structured review report: model summary, deterministic quick check with assumptions and warnings, critical members, the approved-change history, and (by default) the agent activity log. Read-only.

include_activity.description: Include the agent activity trail (default true).

tools.name: create_warehouse_model
tools.description: Build a parametric post-frame ("pole barn") warehouse frame from a plain-language description and load it into StructSketch, REPLACING the current model, then run the deterministic analysis. The agent only chooses parameters from the user's intent; geometry, sections and loads are generated deterministically and the existing S-Structures core does every calculation. Two bents plus one per bay, gable roof, collar tie and optional knee braces. Requires confirm:true — the user must have approved the description.

span_m.description: Clear span between the two column lines, metres (default 12.2).

roof_pitch.description: Roof pitch as rise:run, e.g. "4:12", or a bare ratio (default "4:12").

post_spacing_m.description: Spacing between frames along the building, metres (default 4.8).

bay_count.description: Number of bays; the model has bay_count + 1 frames (default 1).

material.description: Frame material (default timber: cedar posts and rafters).

braces.description: Include the collar tie and knee braces (default true).

confirm.description: Must be true. The user must have approved the description before this is called.

tools.name: create_structure_model
tools.description: Create a bounded deterministic structural model from the user's plain-language intent, REPLACING the current model, then run the existing S-Structures analysis. Supported structure_type values: warehouse, portal_frame, canopy, roof_truss, multi_storey_frame. The agent selects template parameters; the page generates geometry, members, supports and loads. Requires confirm:true after echoing the interpreted request to the user.

structure_type.description: Template selected from the user's intent.

span_m.description: Main clear span or canopy projection, metres.

height_m.description: Frame/eave height, or per-storey height for multi_storey_frame.

depth_m.description: Out-of-plane spacing between the two stabilising frames, metres.

bay_count.description: Warehouse longitudinal bays, truss panels, or horizontal frame bays.

roof_pitch.description: Pitch as rise:run, e.g. 3:12; used by warehouse, canopy, and roof_truss.

material.description: Catalog material and matching default sections.

bases.description: Base condition. Canopies require fixed bases.

load_kN_m.description: Downward line load on generated beams/roof members, kN/m.

confirm.description: Must be true after the user approves the interpreted structure and parameters.

tools.name: imicalculator
tools.description: Allows determining the value of the Municipal Property Tax (IMI) based on data provided by the user. This service validates the indicated municipality, identifies the applicable coefficient, processes the Taxable Patrimonial Value (VPT), number of dependents, and the nature of the property (urban or rural), returning the final IMI amount to be paid according to current fiscal rules in Portugal.

TownName.description: Name of the municipality where the property is located. This field is required for geographic identification and IMI rate determination. Example: "Lisbon", "Porto", "Sintra", "Albufeira".

TaxableValue.description: Taxable patrimonial value of the property (VPT), as registered with the Portuguese Tax Authority. This is the official fiscal value used as the basis for calculating IMI. Must be a positive decimal value expressed in euros. Example: "185000.00".

DependentsNumber.description: Number of dependants in the taxpayer’s household for the relevant tax year. This includes children, elderly parents or other legally recognised dependants that may qualify for IMI reductions or exemptions. Valid values: integer ≥ 0. Example: "2".

IsUrban.description: Indicates whether the property is classified as urban or rural. Urban properties are subject to IMI, while rural properties may be subject to different taxation rules. Example: true/false.

CompanyId.description: Identifier of the company/agency to query (optional, defaults to the company’s internal one).

tools.name: loancalculator
tools.description: Calculates financing values for a property, including monthly payments, IMT tax, total loan duration in months, and the total applied interest rate. This endpoint allows customization of parameters such as property value, loan amount, bank spread, Euribor, loan term in years, and whether it is a permanent own residence.

PropertyValue.description: Total purchase price of the property in euros. Used as the basis for IMT and Stamp Duty calculations.

LoanAmount.description: Total amount to be borrowed from the bank (capital). Must be less than or equal to the property value.

Spread.description: The bank's profit margin (spread) as a percentage. Combined with Euribor, it forms the total interest rate (TAN).

EuriborRateMaturity.description: Maturity period of the Euribor applied to the loan. Possible values: 1M (1 month: rate revised monthly), 3M (3 months: rate revised quarterly), 6M (6 months: rate revised semi-annually), 12M (12 months: rate revised annually).

LoanTermYears.description: Loan duration in years. Usually between 5 and 40 years depending on the applicant’s age.

IsPermanentHousing.description: Indicates if the property is for Own Permanent Housing. Affects IMT tax brackets and exemptions in Portugal.
