sites.name: sheeesh3.github.io
sites.description: A rough-cut video editor an agent can drive. Select the sentence that must survive; the agent builds the clip around it. Your video never leaves the tab.

tools.name: get_editor_state
tools.description: Read the current state of the Cutlet editor: the loaded video, how many sentences the transcript has, what the user has anchored, and every clip with its segments, duration and revision. Call this before editing a clip, and again after the user says they changed something — revisions change when a human edits, and you need the current one to write safely.

tools.name: read_transcript
tools.description: Read the transcript as sentences, each with a stable id like s0042 and its start and end time. Use the ids — never raw timestamps — when you propose a clip. To find clips in a recording you have not seen, call this once with detail "skim": it returns every sentence shortened to a few words, so a whole recording arrives in one result and you can see its shape. Then read the stretches that look promising with detail "full" before you commit to any boundary. There are two transcripts here. scope "source" (default) is the whole recording as spoken — that is where you find clips. scope "clip" is one cut as it actually plays: only the sentences it kept, in play order, with each gap marked where material was dropped. Read that before you judge or revise a cut — the segment list tells you what survived, but only this tells you how the joins sound.

scope.description: source (default) reads the whole recording as spoken. clip reads one cut as it plays — kept sentences only, gaps marked. Use clip to hear an edit before revising it.

clipId.description: Which clip to read when scope is "clip". Defaults to the selected clip, which is what the user means by "this".

detail.description: full (default) returns complete sentences, up to 120. skim returns every sentence shortened to about 11 words, up to 900 — use it to survey a whole recording before choosing where to look.

startSentenceId.description: First sentence to return, e.g. "s0042". Defaults to the start of the transcript, or to the user's anchor when there is one.

count.description: How many sentences to return. Default 40 when reading in full, the whole transcript when skimming.

before.description: Also include this many sentences of context before startSentenceId. Useful when you need to find where a thought begins.

tools.name: search_transcript
tools.description: Find sentences matching a word or phrase, anywhere in the transcript. Returns matching sentence ids with a little surrounding context so you can judge where a thought starts and ends before proposing a range. This is the cheap way to locate a moment in a long recording.

query.description: Words to look for. Case-insensitive; all words must appear in the sentence, in any order.

limit.description: Maximum number of hits. Default 8, maximum 25.

contextSentences.description: How many sentences either side of each hit to include. Default 1.

tools.name: get_guidelines
tools.description: Read the editorial rules this editor works by: the difference between a topic and a cut, what makes a cut land, how long clips should be, and what this tool set can and cannot do. Read this once before your first edit.

tools.name: create_clip
tools.description: Create a clip and add it to the rail. Pass one contiguous range for a topic (startSentenceId + endSentenceId), or a list of segments for a cut with gaps in it. Ranges are inclusive of both ends. If the user has anchored a sentence, that sentence should fall inside what you create.

startSentenceId.description: First sentence, for a single-range clip.

endSentenceId.description: Last sentence, inclusive, for a single-range clip.

segments.description: For a cut: the pieces to keep, in order. Each is {startSentenceId, endSentenceId}, inclusive. Gaps between them are the sentences you are dropping.

title.description: Short human title. A few words, sentence case.

note.description: One line on why this shape — the user reads this.

preview.description: Play it immediately. Default true — the point is for the human to watch it.

tools.name: update_clip
tools.description: Change an existing clip: replace its segments, move an edge, retitle it, or set the padding around each cut. Pass expectedRevision with the revision you last read — if a human has edited it since, the write is refused and you are told the real revision, so you can look at what they did instead of overwriting it.

expectedRevision.description: The revision you last saw on this clip. Strongly recommended — it is what stops you clobbering a human edit.

segments.description: Replace every segment. Each is {startSentenceId, endSentenceId}, inclusive. They are sorted into transcript order unless you also pass preserveOrder.

note.description: New one-line note.

pad.description: Seconds of breathing room added at each end of every segment, 0 to 2. Raise it if the cuts feel clipped; lower it if they feel slack.

preserveOrder.description: Play the segments in the order you listed them rather than in transcript order. Use it to rearrange a cut — to open on the punchline and then give the setup, say. Reordering is safe because it makes no new boundary: every piece keeps the sentence ids it already had.

preview.description: Play the revised clip. Default true.

tools.name: cut_clip
tools.description: Reduce a clip to a postable length by keeping the sentences you name and dropping the rest, then write the result back to the same clip. Runs of consecutive ids become one piece; every break between them becomes a cut. Read the clip in full first and choose the lines yourself. Deciding what survives is the judgement this tool exists to carry — there is no automatic mode, because nothing mechanical can tell a throwaway aside from the payoff.

clipId.description: The clip to cut down, usually a topic.

expectedRevision.description: The revision you last saw on it.

keepSentenceIds.description: The sentences to keep, in any order. Aim for 30 to 60 seconds of speech unless the user asked for something else. Keeping two sentences in a row reads better than keeping two good ones with a hole between them.

note.description: One line on what you kept and why.

tools.name: edit_clip_sentence
tools.description: Drop a single sentence out of a clip, or put one back. Dropping an interior sentence splits the clip into two segments with a gap where it was. This is the fine adjustment after the shape is roughly right — reach for it when the user says one specific line has to go or come back.

action.description: remove drops it from the clip; add puts it back in transcript order.

tools.name: split_sentence
tools.description: Cut one sentence into two at a word boundary, when the boundary you need is not one the transcript has. Sentences come from whatever punctuation the speech recogniser guessed, and it guesses badly: a missed full stop leaves a sixty-word run you can only take whole. Splitting makes the boundary you want into a real sentence with its own id, so you can then cut on it like any other. The first half keeps the original id; the second half gets a new one, reported back. Clips are rewritten so they still contain exactly what they contained before — splitting changes the vocabulary, never the edit. Read the sentence first so you can count the words.

afterWord.description: How many words stay in the first half. 5 means the split falls after the fifth word, so the sixth begins the new sentence. Must be at least 1 and less than the number of words in the sentence.

tools.name: preview_clip
tools.description: Play something in the player so the human can watch it. Give it a clipId to play a clip, gaps and all, or a pair of sentence ids to audition a range before committing to it. Playback happens in the user's tab; you get back what you asked it to do, not the video.

clipId.description: Play this existing clip, jumping its gaps.

startSentenceId.description: Play from this sentence. Use with endSentenceId to audition a range.

endSentenceId.description: Play up to and including this sentence.

mode.description: play (default) runs it and stops at the end. seek parks the playhead at the start.

tools.name: search-products
tools.description: Search the product catalog. Handles any query: specific products, broad categories, gifts, occasions, or open discovery. Never assume a category is unavailable: always search before responding. The response is data only: a list of matching products (name, ID, price, description, and any product-specific attributes) plus pagination and the available filters. The raw results are for your eyes only: the client never sees them. NEVER describe or characterize the raw results to the client: do not mention how many there are, what categories they fall into, or that they look off-topic. While searching, stay silent: do not narrate what you are doing, announce searches, or report progress between tool calls. Speak only once the carousel is rendered. Act on the response as follows: - FIRST SEARCH: use the keyword only (plus sort if needed). Read the available filters in the response; these are the only valid filter options for follow-ups. - REFINEMENT: if the user's intent matches an available filter, apply it. If it doesn't match any filter, start a new keyword search. - ITERATE: a single search is never enough. Run several searches (2 minimum) before rendering: vary the keyword, apply a filter, or page deeper, and compare results across them. Quality comes from this multi-call exploration; one call then render gives shallow results. - CURATION: read results and pick the best matches for the client's intent, grounding your choice in each product's description. If zero results, broaden the keyword or relax filters and search again: do NOT call render-carousel. If fewer than 3 results and the user didn't ask for a specific product, search again with broader terms. Only after exploring across several searches, call render-carousel with the selected IDs. - PRESENT: Once you have 3-6 distinct, relevant products, call render-carousel with their IDs. Recommend ONLY AFTER the carousel displays, in carousel order. The sweet spot is 3-6 products.

keyword.description: Short noun phrases extracted from conversational input. Never pass full sentences. ALWAYS use the singular form, not the plural. Include color, material, and style descriptors for accuracy. For vague gift or occasion queries without a clear product type, use broad category terms. Preserve the existing keyword across filter refinements; only replace when the user makes a completely different request.

sort.description: Sort order.

priceRange.description: Price range in dollars. Format: 'min-max' e.g. '0-500', '1000-2000'.

tools.name: render-carousel
tools.description: Display the products you curated as an inline carousel for the client. ## When to call Call this AFTER searching and curating, and BEFORE writing your recommendation. Do not describe the products in text first; the carousel shows them. Stay silent until it has rendered, then speak. ## What to pass Pass the IDs of the 3-6 products you chose, in display order (most relevant first). Order is significant: the carousel shows them in this exact order and your recommendation must follow the same sequence. Pass distinct products, not several variants of the same one; the detail view lets the client explore a product's variants (colors, sizes, and so on). ## After the carousel Recommend in carousel order so the client can follow along. The cards already show image, title, price, and key facts, so do not repeat them: add useful analysis tied to the client's need. Suggest a refinement the client has not addressed yet (from the available filters), never one they already used. ## Accuracy Use only the data returned for each product. Never invent attributes, materials, or availability. If the client asks about something not present, open that product's detail or search again before answering.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID. Pass as catalog.id to get_product.

handle.description: Product handle. Can be passed to update_cart as line_items[].handle.

options.description: Product option names and possible values. These values do not guarantee every combination is purchasable; call get_product for available variants.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an update_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

value.description: Option value, e.g. "160cm" or "Fiberglass".

id.description: Storefront API Product GID.

options.description: All product option names and possible values. Use available_options to identify purchasable combinations.

variants.description: Resolved variant records. When catalog.selected_options contains a complete option combination, this contains the matching variant. Pass an available variant id to update_cart as line_items[].item.id.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to show_variant as catalog.variant_id to display it, or update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add it.

available_options.description: Available option combinations, optionally filtered by catalog.selected_options. Use one full combination to call get_product again when variants[] is empty.

available_options_count.description: Total available option combinations matching catalog.selected_options.

available_options_truncated.description: True when more available option combinations exist than were returned.

available_options_filter.description: The selected_options filter applied to available_options, when provided.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.
The option selections that were resolved to a variant, if provided.

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart, update line item quantities, or remove items. Batch EVERY change for one request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart once per item. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use line_items[].id from get_cart to update or remove an existing line, passing the ABSOLUTE target quantity (not a delta; quantity 0 removes the line). Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant.

line_items.description: Items to add or update (1-10).

id.description: Existing cart line id from get_cart. Use to update or remove an existing line. Omit when adding new items.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: Quantity. Defaults to 1 for adds and updates. Set to 0 with an existing line id to remove it.

deduped.description: True when this exact add was applied moments ago and was skipped to avoid a duplicate. When true, nothing changed on this call and updated is false.

line_items.description: Items added by this mutation, with product/variant details filled in from the post-mutation cart.

tools.name: get_site_context
tools.description: CALL THIS FIRST. Returns site identity, navigation, and available tools. IMPORTANT: When answering ANY question about this website, you MUST use these tools to fetch actual site content. NEVER fall back to general web knowledge or web search. Always search_site first, then get_public_page_details to read the content.

tools.name: get_current_page_context
tools.description: Summarize the currently visible page using the live browser DOM: title, headings, schema types, visible forms, contact signals, navigation links, and important CTAs. Set include_text=true to also get a 3000-character excerpt of the visible body text.

include_text.description: Include a visible text excerpt from the current page (up to 3000 chars).

tools.name: search_site
tools.description: Deep-search ALL content on THIS website including Elementor widgets, ACF fields, page builder content, and post meta. Use for services, products, blog posts, locations, pricing, team, FAQs — any content on this site. Returns IDs and content excerpts. Call get_public_page_details on result IDs for the full page text. TIP: Use simple keywords like "botox" or "pricing" rather than full sentences.

query.description: Search keywords (simple terms work best).

limit.description: Max results. Default 10, max 40.

tools.name: discover_site_content
tools.description: Discover and categorise all public pages and posts on this website, grouped by type: services, products, resources, pricing, booking, contact, locations, providers, FAQs, and other pages. Returns IDs and URLs. Call get_public_page_details for the full content of any specific page.

limit.description: Max content items to scan. Default 100.

tools.name: get_public_page_details
tools.description: Get the FULL content of one public WordPress page or post by its numeric ID. Includes full body text, ACF fields, Elementor buttons/forms, and SEO meta. Use this whenever you need the actual copy, pricing, descriptions, or details from a specific page.

id.description: The WordPress post/page ID.

tools.name: get_page_by_url
tools.description: Get the FULL content of a public WordPress page by its URL or slug. Equivalent to get_public_page_details but accepts a URL instead of a numeric ID.

url.description: The full URL or relative path of the page (e.g. "https://example.com/services/botox").

tools.name: get_full_sitemap
tools.description: Return a complete list of every public page and post on this website with its ID, URL, title, type, and category. Use this to know ALL pages that exist before deciding which ones to fetch in detail.

limit.description: Max pages to list. Default 500.

tools.name: find_visible_forms
tools.description: List all visible non-sensitive forms on the current page with their purpose, fields, method, and WebMCP tool names.

tools.name: find_page_actions
tools.description: List visible calls-to-action on the current page: book, contact, request demo, see pricing, shop, download, subscribe, and navigation links.

tools.name: focus_page_action
tools.description: Scroll to and focus a visible page action selected from find_page_actions, so the user can see it before clicking.

label.description: Optional action label to match when index is unknown.

sites.description: SOAR Media Agency: Your partner for branding, content production, digital identity, and event management. Elevate your brand with our expert services!

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

query.description: Search query string.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID. Pass as catalog.id to get_product.

handle.description: Product handle. Can be passed to update_cart as line_items[].handle.

options.description: Product option names and possible values. These values do not guarantee every combination is purchasable; call get_product for available variants.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID. Pass as catalog.id to get_product.

handle.description: Product handle. Can be passed to update_cart as line_items[].handle.

options.description: Product option names and possible values. These values do not guarantee every combination is purchasable; call get_product for available variants.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an update_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

value.description: Option value, e.g. "160cm" or "Fiberglass".

id.description: Storefront API Product GID.

options.description: All product option names and possible values. Use available_options to identify purchasable combinations.

variants.description: Resolved variant records. When catalog.selected_options contains a complete option combination, this contains the matching variant. Pass an available variant id to update_cart as line_items[].item.id.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to show_variant as catalog.variant_id to display it, or update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add it.

available_options.description: Available option combinations, optionally filtered by catalog.selected_options. Use one full combination to call get_product again when variants[] is empty.

available_options_count.description: Total available option combinations matching catalog.selected_options.

available_options_truncated.description: True when more available option combinations exist than were returned.

available_options_filter.description: The selected_options filter applied to available_options, when provided.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.
The option selections that were resolved to a variant, if provided.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

id.description: Cart GID.
Cart line GID from get_cart. Pass back to update_cart as line_items[].id to update or remove this line.

item.description: Product + variant information for the line, sufficient to name and link to the item without an extra get_product call.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add this variant.

variant_title.description: Variant title (e.g. "Large / Black"). Empty or "Default Title" for single-variant products.

url.description: Direct URL to the product page with the variant preselected.

line_price.description: Total price for the line (quantity × unit_price).

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart, update line item quantities, or remove items. Batch EVERY change for one request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart once per item. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use line_items[].id from get_cart to update or remove an existing line, passing the ABSOLUTE target quantity (not a delta; quantity 0 removes the line). Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant.

line_items.description: Items to add or update (1-10).

id.description: Existing cart line id from get_cart. Use to update or remove an existing line. Omit when adding new items.

item.description: The merchandise to add.

id.description: ProductVariant GID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123".

handle.description: Product handle. Adds the selected or first available variant; call get_product first if the user requested specific options.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: Quantity. Defaults to 1 for adds and updates. Set to 0 with an existing line id to remove it.

deduped.description: True when this exact add was applied moments ago and was skipped to avoid a duplicate. When true, nothing changed on this call and updated is false.

line_items.description: Items added by this mutation, with product/variant details filled in from the post-mutation cart.

item.description: Product + variant information for the line, sufficient to name and link to the item without an extra get_product call.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add this variant.

variant_title.description: Variant title (e.g. "Large / Black"). Empty or "Default Title" for single-variant products.

url.description: Direct URL to the product page with the variant preselected.

quantity.description: Actual quantity on the cart line after the mutation. May differ from requested_quantity if the line merged with an existing entry or availability capped the add.

requested_quantity.description: Quantity the caller asked to add.

resolved_items.description: Present only on the clarification-needed path (nothing was applied). Items that could have been added, with pre-mutation lookup titles when available.

item.description: Product + variant information for the line, sufficient to name and link to the item without an extra get_product call.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add this variant.

variant_title.description: Variant title (e.g. "Large / Black"). Empty or "Default Title" for single-variant products.

url.description: Direct URL to the product page with the variant preselected.

quantity.description: Actual quantity on the cart line after the mutation. May differ from requested_quantity if the line merged with an existing entry or availability capped the add.

requested_quantity.description: Quantity the caller asked to add.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Remove all items from the cart in one step. Use when the user wants to empty their cart or start over.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Proceed to checkout. Verifies the cart is not empty, then MOVES the browser to the checkout page. The tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: manage_orders
tools.description: Navigate to the customer's order history page. Use when the user asks about past orders, order status, tracking, or returns. The user will be prompted to log in if not already authenticated. This MOVES the browser to the order history page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: search_shop_policies_and_faqs
tools.description: Used to get facts about the store's policies, FAQ, or contact details. When the question is about specific policy kinds, set policy_types to those kinds; leave it unset for general FAQ questions. Some examples of questions you can ask are: - What is your return policy? (policy_types: ["refund"]) - What is your shipping policy? (policy_types: ["shipping"]) - What is your phone number? (policy_types: ["contact"]) - What are your hours of operation? (policy_types: ["contact"]) - Do you offer gift wrapping? (general FAQ, no specific policy kind — leave policy_types unset)

query.description: A natural language query. Searches FAQ pages and articles, and routes policies by keyword when policy_types is omitted.

policy_types.description: Policy kinds to fetch, chosen from the user's question — e.g. ["refund"] for returns/exchanges, ["contact"] for phone/hours/address. Include every kind the question touches. Omit when no specific policy is relevant (e.g. a general FAQ question).

policies.description: Store policies and contact information matching the query.

type.description: Policy kind: refund, shipping, privacy, terms_of_service, terms_of_sale, subscription, legal_notice, or contact.

body.description: The policy text (may contain HTML).

pages.description: Store pages (e.g. FAQ, help) matching the query.

body.description: The page body (may contain HTML) for the top matched pages.

tools.name: offer_spark

tools.name: read_room_principles

sites.name: spatialize-pink.vercel.app
sites.description: Check a route against your clear width, from a validated 3D floor-plan twin and sourced access evidence. Agents can ask and propose; only people publish.

tools.name: get_venue_overview
tools.description: Summarise this venue: its name, footprint in metres, how many rooms, doors and landmarks were extracted from the floor plan, and whether the extracted data has been reviewed by a person yet. Call this first to orient yourself.

tools.name: list_destinations
tools.description: List the places in this venue a visitor can be routed to — entrances, restrooms, lifts, stairs and named destinations — with the id you should pass to find_step_free_route.

type.description: Optional filter by landmark type.

tools.name: find_step_free_route
tools.description: Compute a route between two places in this venue and report it turn by turn. By default it only returns step-free routes suitable for a wheelchair user. If no step-free route exists, it names the exact door that blocks it rather than just refusing. The 3D view on the page follows along so the person sees the route.

to.description: Destination landmark id or label.

from.description: Starting landmark id or label. Defaults to the main entrance.

step_free.description: Require a step-free route. Defaults to true.

tools.name: describe_room
tools.description: Describe one room: its area, category, which rooms it connects to and through which doors, and how confident the extraction was about it.

room.description: Room id or label.

tools.name: check_accessibility
tools.description: Audit the whole venue for step-free access: which destinations are reachable from the main entrance without steps, which are not and why, which doors are recorded as barriers, and every doorway's clear width so the person can judge it against their own equipment. Use check_route_clearance for one person's needs on one route.

tools.name: list_data_issues
tools.description: List everything about this venue's extracted data that is unresolved: open review issues raised by the validator, and entities the vision model was unsure about. Use this to find what a visitor could usefully confirm or correct on the ground.

tools.name: list_disputed_claims
tools.description: List access reports the venue team declined to accept. Visitors are often a better source on a building than the building's own record, so declined reports are kept rather than deleted. Call this before telling someone a route is fine — the venue may say step-free where a visitor reported otherwise.

tools.name: check_route_clearance
tools.description: Check one route against a specific person's needs: the narrowest doorway they can pass, in millimetres, and whether steps rule it out. Answers clear, blocked or unknown — unknown when a doorway on the route has an unconfirmed measurement or an unresolved visitor dispute. Lists every limiting doorway so the person decides.

to.description: Destination landmark id or label.

from.description: Starting landmark id or label. Defaults to the main entrance.

minimum_clear_width_mm.description: Narrowest doorway the person can pass, in millimetres. For example 760 for many manual wheelchairs.

require_step_free.description: Whether steps rule the route out. Defaults to true.

tools.name: simulate_closure
tools.description: What-if, changing nothing: if a doorway were closed or a lift out of use, which destinations would stop being reachable without steps from the main entrance, and which would still be? For planned works or an out-of-service lift. Nothing is proposed or recorded.

door.description: A doorway to treat as closed, by name or id.

landmark.description: A lift or other landmark to treat as out of use, by name or id.

tools.name: focus_view
tools.description: Move the 3D venue view on this page to a landmark, and optionally switch between the 3D walkthrough and the flat 2D plan. Use it to show a person what you are talking about instead of only describing it.

target.description: Landmark id or label to focus.

mode.description: Optional view mode.

tools.name: get_board
tools.description: Read the current board: the question, gamePhase (setup, opening, playing or ended), every node (id, label, kind, parentId, createdBy, isGap, gapReason, note, url), both move budgets, whose turn it is, openingMovesLeft, the live score out of 100, openGaps (explicit gaps plus implicit ones: concepts with no resource or skill beneath them), selectedNodeId (the node the human clicked), visualization (forest or board) and focusedTree. Free: costs no move. Call it before every move so you use real node ids.

tools.name: get_node_state
tools.description: Read one node in detail: its label, kind, parent, children, gap flag and reason, note, url, who created it and whether the human has it selected. Omit nodeId to read the node the human currently has selected. Free: costs no move.

nodeId.description: The id (for example "n2") or the exact label of the node. Omit it to read the selected node.

tools.name: plant
tools.description: Plant the root node on an empty board, using the question itself as the label. Free: costs no move. Before a game has started this starts one, with the label as the question. As the agent you then open the game: grow up to 3 free branches under the root and call pass to hand over to the human.

label.description: Label for the root node, usually the learning question itself.

note.description: Optional short note to attach to the root.

tools.name: branch
tools.description: Add a child node under an existing node. Costs one of your 6 moves and ends your turn. During your opening (gamePhase "opening") it is free instead, and the opening ends after 3 such moves or when you pass. A resource or skill branched directly under a gap closes that gap automatically. A concept with no resource or skill anywhere beneath it counts as an implicit gap and costs points at the end, so follow concepts with resources and skills. Scoring rewards coverage (concepts with a resource or skill under them), depth up to three levels, having all three kinds, both players contributing, and notes or urls on nodes.

parentId.description: The id (for example "n2") or the exact label of the target node. This node becomes the parent.

label.description: A short label for the new node, two to five words.

kind.description: concept for an idea or topic, resource for a book, course, article or tool (add its url), skill for an ability to practise.

note.description: Optional short note explaining the node.

url.description: Optional http(s) link, especially for a resource.

tools.name: prune
tools.description: Remove a node and everything under it. Costs one of your 6 moves and ends your turn. During your opening (gamePhase "opening") it is free instead, and the opening ends after 3 such moves or when you pass. The root cannot be pruned. The human can undo your most recent action, so prune only what is clearly off-topic or duplicated.

nodeId.description: The id (for example "n2") or the exact label of the target node.

tools.name: mark_gap
tools.description: Flag a node as an open knowledge gap that the other player should fill, keeping its kind. Costs one of your 6 moves and ends your turn. During your opening (gamePhase "opening") it is free instead, and the opening ends after 3 such moves or when you pass. You cannot mark the root, a node that is already a gap, or a node that already has a resource or skill directly under it. Every gap still open when the game ends costs 5 points, so mark gaps you expect to be filled and give a reason.

nodeId.description: The id (for example "n2") or the exact label of the target node.

reason.description: Optional challenge question explaining what is missing.

tools.name: annotate
tools.description: Attach or replace a note and/or an http(s) url on any node. Free: costs no move and does not end your turn, so you can annotate on either turn. Each node with a note or url earns 1 point, up to 10. Pass an empty string to clear a field. To add to a note or change one passage of it without retyping the rest, use edit_note.

nodeId.description: The id (for example "n2") or the exact label of the target node.

note.description: The note for the node, in Markdown if you like: headings, lists, links and code all render.

url.description: An http(s) link for the node.

tools.name: edit_note
tools.description: Co-write the Markdown note on a node with the human. Read the note first with get_node_state (it is the node's note field), then either append a new paragraph or section at the end, or replace one passage quoted exactly from the note. The human sees the change at once, even while the note is open in their editor, and keeps anything they are still typing. Free: costs no move and does not end your turn. Use annotate to replace a whole note. Notes are limited to 20000 characters.

nodeId.description: The id (for example "n2") or the exact label of the target node.

mode.description: append adds text after the current note as a new paragraph; replace swaps the passage in find for text.

text.description: The Markdown to add, or the replacement for the passage in find (empty removes the passage).

find.description: For replace only: a passage quoted exactly from the current note. It has to match exactly once, so quote enough of it.

tools.name: pass
tools.description: End your turn without moving. Free: costs no move. During your opening this hands the board to the human, which is how the opening should end. Later, if both players yield in a row the game ends, so pass only when you have nothing to add or want the human to respond first.

tools.name: announce
tools.description: Tell the human what you are doing, in your own words. The page shows the text over the board and reads it aloud (unless a voice session is already speaking for you). Free: costs no move and never changes the turn, so call it in any phase. Call it right before or after each move with a one- or two-sentence first-person summary, and whenever you hand the board over (after a pass, or a move that ends your turn) add a handoff line that tells the human it is their turn and suggests what to do next. Keep each field under 200 characters.

summary.description: What you are doing and why, in one or two short first-person sentences. Example: I added the resource "Eloquent JavaScript" under Closures, which closes that gap.

handoff.description: Optional "your turn" line, spoken after the summary when you are handing the board to the human. Example: Your turn: fill the gap under Agent loops, or deepen another concept.

sites.name: teacollection.com
sites.description: Made for childhood. Inspired by the world. Shop globally inspired children's clothing for girls, boys, baby & toddler (newborn–16). Unique prints, ethical sourcing & free shipping on orders $150+.

tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Search the store catalog for products, collections, articles, and pages. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. If the user asks for a specific product variant, call get_product after search_catalog to inspect available variants, then show_variant to display one.

query.description: Search query string.

limit.description: Max results per type (1-10). Defaults to 5.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID. Pass as catalog.id to get_product.

handle.description: Product handle. Can be passed to update_cart as line_items[].handle.

options.description: Product option names and possible values. These values do not guarantee every combination is purchasable; call get_product for available variants.

tools.name: browse_store
tools.description: Browse OR navigate to store collections. Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

collection.description: Collection handle to browse (e.g. "best-sellers", "new-arrivals"). Omit to list all collections. Use "all" to browse every product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the collection page after loading data. Set true for user intents like "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to" a collection. Requires a collection handle. Defaults to false.

sort_by.description: Sort order. Options: best-selling (default), price-ascending, price-descending, title-ascending, title-descending, created-descending, created-ascending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (starts at 1). Each page returns up to 30 products.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID. Pass as catalog.id to get_product.

handle.description: Product handle. Can be passed to update_cart as line_items[].handle.

options.description: Product option names and possible values. These values do not guarantee every combination is purchasable; call get_product for available variants.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an update_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

selected_options.description: Known product option selections to filter available_options. Use exact option names and values from search_catalog options or a prior get_product available_options entry.

value.description: Option value, e.g. "160cm" or "Fiberglass".

id.description: Storefront API Product GID.

options.description: All product option names and possible values. Use available_options to identify purchasable combinations.

variants.description: Resolved variant records. When catalog.selected_options contains a complete option combination, this contains the matching variant. Pass an available variant id to update_cart as line_items[].item.id.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to show_variant as catalog.variant_id to display it, or update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add it.

available_options.description: Available option combinations, optionally filtered by catalog.selected_options. Use one full combination to call get_product again when variants[] is empty.

available_options_count.description: Total available option combinations matching catalog.selected_options.

available_options_truncated.description: True when more available option combinations exist than were returned.

available_options_filter.description: The selected_options filter applied to available_options, when provided.

tools.name: show_variant
tools.description: Navigate the browser to a product page, with a specific variant OR a partial option filter selected. Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. This MOVES the browser to the exact variant page with the variant pre-selected; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

catalog.description: Provide EITHER variant_id OR selected_options. Handle is required unless the user is already on the product page.

handle.description: Product handle. If omitted, uses the current product page's handle.

variant_id.description: ProductVariant ID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123", or the numeric variant ID. Use when the user picked a specific fully-specified variant. Omit when using selected_options.

selected_options.description: Partial (or full) option selections, e.g. [{"name":"Color","value":"Purple"}]. Use when the user names some options but not all (e.g. "show me the purple shoe" — pass only Color). The first matching available variant will be selected automatically. Use exact option names and values from get_product available_options or search_catalog options.
The option selections that were resolved to a variant, if provided.

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Get the current shopping cart contents — line items with product titles, variant titles, handles, URLs, images, unit prices, quantities, and totals. Everything needed to describe the cart to the user in natural language, without a follow-up get_product call per line. Works from any page.

id.description: Cart GID.
Cart line GID from get_cart. Pass back to update_cart as line_items[].id to update or remove this line.

item.description: Product + variant information for the line, sufficient to name and link to the item without an extra get_product call.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add this variant.

variant_title.description: Variant title (e.g. "Large / Black"). Empty or "Default Title" for single-variant products.

url.description: Direct URL to the product page with the variant preselected.

line_price.description: Total price for the line (quantity × unit_price).

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Add products to the cart, update line item quantities, or remove items. Batch EVERY change for one request into a SINGLE call — line_items accepts up to 10 entries; do NOT call update_cart once per item. Do NOT retry a call that already returned a result: adds are cumulative, so repeating a call adds duplicate items. Use line_items[].item.id with a ProductVariant GID when the exact variant is known. Use line_items[].id from get_cart to update or remove an existing line, passing the ABSOLUTE target quantity (not a delta; quantity 0 removes the line). Use handle or query only when adding the selected or first available variant.

line_items.description: Items to add or update (1-10).

id.description: Existing cart line id from get_cart. Use to update or remove an existing line. Omit when adding new items.

item.description: The merchandise to add.

id.description: ProductVariant GID from get_product variants[].id, e.g. "gid://shopify/ProductVariant/123".

handle.description: Product handle. Adds the selected or first available variant; call get_product first if the user requested specific options.

query.description: Search query to find and add the selected or first available variant. For specific variants, call search_catalog/get_product first and pass item.id.

quantity.description: Quantity. Defaults to 1 for adds and updates. Set to 0 with an existing line id to remove it.

deduped.description: True when this exact add was applied moments ago and was skipped to avoid a duplicate. When true, nothing changed on this call and updated is false.

line_items.description: Items added by this mutation, with product/variant details filled in from the post-mutation cart.

item.description: Product + variant information for the line, sufficient to name and link to the item without an extra get_product call.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add this variant.

variant_title.description: Variant title (e.g. "Large / Black"). Empty or "Default Title" for single-variant products.

url.description: Direct URL to the product page with the variant preselected.

quantity.description: Actual quantity on the cart line after the mutation. May differ from requested_quantity if the line merged with an existing entry or availability capped the add.

requested_quantity.description: Quantity the caller asked to add.

resolved_items.description: Present only on the clarification-needed path (nothing was applied). Items that could have been added, with pre-mutation lookup titles when available.

item.description: Product + variant information for the line, sufficient to name and link to the item without an extra get_product call.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add this variant.

variant_title.description: Variant title (e.g. "Large / Black"). Empty or "Default Title" for single-variant products.

url.description: Direct URL to the product page with the variant preselected.

quantity.description: Actual quantity on the cart line after the mutation. May differ from requested_quantity if the line merged with an existing entry or availability capped the add.

requested_quantity.description: Quantity the caller asked to add.

tools.name: cancel_cart
tools.description: Remove all items from the cart in one step. Use when the user wants to empty their cart or start over.

tools.name: proceed_to_checkout
tools.description: Proceed to checkout. Verifies the cart is not empty, then MOVES the browser to the checkout page. The tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: manage_orders
tools.description: Navigate to the customer's order history page. Use when the user asks about past orders, order status, tracking, or returns. The user will be prompted to log in if not already authenticated. This MOVES the browser to the order history page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: search_shop_policies_and_faqs
tools.description: Used to get facts about the store's policies, FAQ, or contact details. When the question is about specific policy kinds, set policy_types to those kinds; leave it unset for general FAQ questions. Some examples of questions you can ask are: - What is your return policy? (policy_types: ["refund"]) - What is your shipping policy? (policy_types: ["shipping"]) - What is your phone number? (policy_types: ["contact"]) - What are your hours of operation? (policy_types: ["contact"]) - Do you offer gift wrapping? (general FAQ, no specific policy kind — leave policy_types unset)

query.description: A natural language query. Searches FAQ pages and articles, and routes policies by keyword when policy_types is omitted.

policy_types.description: Policy kinds to fetch, chosen from the user's question — e.g. ["refund"] for returns/exchanges, ["contact"] for phone/hours/address. Include every kind the question touches. Omit when no specific policy is relevant (e.g. a general FAQ question).

policies.description: Store policies and contact information matching the query.

type.description: Policy kind: refund, shipping, privacy, terms_of_service, terms_of_sale, subscription, legal_notice, or contact.

body.description: The policy text (may contain HTML).

pages.description: Store pages (e.g. FAQ, help) matching the query.

body.description: The page body (may contain HTML) for the top matched pages.

tools.name: halo_get_context
tools.description: HALO is a local music instrument, not an AI chat. The external agent composes original MIDI parts. Read halo_get_context first; pause transport for stable long edits, then use baseRevision with one batch of up to 256 operations. Use exact:true, steps and noteEvents for explicit notes. Re-read state to verify. User track 6 is index 5. No mouse/keyboard emulation, model key, server or manual JSON exchange is needed. Audio stays local; no microphone permission or raw recordings are exposed. See registry for 4/4, role ranges, fixed orbit geometry and unavailable per-note parameters. Returns catalog, limits, current score, resolved notes, visual state and history counts.

tools.name: halo_get_capabilities
tools.description: Read actual built-in sounds/sample metadata, role compatibility, MIDI/key/FX/master/visual limits and operation fields. No PCM.

tools.name: halo_get_state
tools.description: Read the current canonical project, visual settings and revision after an edit. No audio data.

tools.name: halo_validate_operations
tools.description: Validate an entire musical transaction without changes. Return precise errors; fix invalid commands instead of inventing capabilities.

tools.name: halo_preview_operations
tools.description: Compute before/after project and visual state on copies. Does not play or apply. A stale revision fails.

tools.name: halo_apply_operations
tools.description: Apply one validated batch to the actual open HALO score, with session Undo/Redo and autosave. Supports tracks/notes, phrases, complete arrangements, FX, master and supported visual modes. Musical loading pauses playback; no automatic download or microphone access.

tools.name: halo_undo
tools.description: Undo the last applied agent transaction; reject if later manual edits conflict.

tools.name: halo_redo
tools.description: Redo the last undone agent transaction; reject conflicting manual edits.

tools.name: halo_playback
tools.description: Request play/pause through HALO transport. Play may still need a browser audio gesture; inspect the returned playing flag and never claim sound if blocked.

tools.name: halo_export_project
tools.description: Read a portable project object for saving by the external agent. The live score is already autosaved locally. No audio or model configuration.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search entries by meaning and by name. Returns the best entries with their summary, URLs, and the sections that matched (heading, deep link, snippet). Works for natural-language questions ("CIA chemist who ran the LSD program"), names, aliases and codenames.

q.description: What to look for, in plain language or as a name.

type.description: Only entries of this type.

tag.description: Only entries with this tag (case-insensitive), such as "CIA" or "1960s".

year_from.description: Only entries whose earliest known year (birth, start, or date) is at least this.

year_to.description: Only entries whose earliest known year is at most this.

tools.name: search_semantic
tools.description: Like search, but ranked by meaning alone, without the boost for title and alias matches. Fails rather than falling back when the embedding service is down.

query.description: What to look for, in plain language.

type.description: Only entries of this type.

tag.description: Only entries with this tag (case-insensitive).

year_from.description: Only entries whose earliest known year is at least this.

year_to.description: Only entries whose earliest known year is at most this.

tools.name: search_lexical
tools.description: Full-text search for exact words and "quoted phrases" in every entry body (case-insensitive, all terms must appear in the same section). Returns matching sections with snippets and the footnotes cited in them. Use for names, codenames, quotations and spellings that search by meaning blurs.

query.description: Words and "quoted phrases", all required.

type.description: Only entries of this type.

tag.description: Only entries with this tag (case-insensitive).

tools.name: search_citations
tools.description: Find a source in the footnotes (author, title, archive, URL, "quoted phrase"), and every entry and footnote that cites it, plus the typed relations that footnote sources. Query by provenance rather than content.

query.description: Words and "quoted phrases" that must all appear in the footnote, such as "Exempt from Disclosure" or a domain.

limit.description: Distinct citations to return.

tools.name: get_entry
tools.description: Full text of one entry as markdown: frontmatter (aliases, dates, typed relations with sources), body with links rewritten to site URLs, and footnoted citations.

id.description: Entry id (the URL slug, such as "allen-dulles") or an exact title.

tools.name: neighbors
tools.description: Entries directly connected to one entry in the link graph, wikilinked ones first, each marked "links to", "linked from", "links both ways", or "named in prose".

id.description: Entry id (the URL slug, such as "allen-dulles") or an exact title.

tools.name: find_path
tools.description: Shortest documented chain of connections between two entries. Steers around mega-hubs such as "United States" so each hop is a specific shared page, and prefers hops backed by a sourced typed relation. Each hop lists those relations (type, role, dates, and the footnote that sources it).

from.description: Entry id (the URL slug, such as "allen-dulles") or an exact title.

to.description: Entry id (the URL slug, such as "allen-dulles") or an exact title.

edges.description: links (default): wikilinks only. any: also hops where two entries are only named together in prose, which mostly run through hubs. relations: only typed frontmatter relations (member_of, employed_by...), each sourced by a footnote.

exclude.description: Entries the path may not pass through, such as hubs ("united-states"). Comma-separated over GET.

k.description: Up to k paths. Each alternative shares no intermediate entry with an earlier one, so these are distinct routes, not the k shortest.

tools.name: similar
tools.description: Entries most similar in subject matter to one entry, whether or not they link to it. Useful for finding related material the links miss.

id.description: Entry id (the URL slug, such as "allen-dulles") or an exact title.

tools.name: timeline
tools.description: Everything dated to a year, a year range, or an entry, with its source: frontmatter dates, typed relation start and end dates, and every sentence in the archive that gives a date in range ("October 14, 1988", "late 1974", "winter 1975"), each with the footnotes that source it. Grouped by the date as written and sorted, so conflicting accounts of the same event sit side by side. For an entry, reads that entry and the pages that link to it, keeping their sentences that name it.

year_from.description: Start of a range of at most 25 years.

entry.description: An entry (usually an event) whose dated statements to collect, across the pages that link to it. Combine with years to narrow.

offset.description: Skip this many items; use next_offset from the previous page.

tools.name: list_entries
tools.description: Page through every entry's frontmatter: title, type, aliases, dates, location, tags, summary, and typed relations with their sources. No body text. For everything at once, download bulk_url.

type.description: Only entries of this type.

tag.description: Only entries with this tag (case-insensitive).

updated_since.description: Only entries updated on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD).

tools.name: browse_store

Set navigate=true whenever the user wants to be taken to a collection page in the browser (triggers: "browse to", "go to", "show me", "open", "take me to", "navigate to" a collection or category). With navigate=false (default), returns collection or product data without changing the page — use this only when the user is asking a question about the catalog, not asking to view it. Without a collection handle, lists all collections. With a handle, returns products from that collection; use "all" to browse everything. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. Prefer this over search_catalog when the user names a category, collection, or wants to explore. With navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the collection page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

tools.name: get_product
tools.description: Get product details, OR navigate the browser to the product page. Set catalog.navigate=true whenever the user wants to see/view the product in the browser (triggers: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to", "navigate to" a product). Set catalog.navigate=false (default) only when you need data (description, options, variants, prices, availability) to answer a question or to prepare an update_cart call — the browser stays on the current page. Defaults to the current page's product if no catalog.id is provided. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for that. For a specific variant (color/size/etc.), use show_variant instead — it accepts partial option selections like "purple" without needing every option. With catalog.navigate=true this MOVES the browser to the product page; the tool result then confirms the destination and instructs you not to navigate again — follow it.

id.description: Storefront API Product GID, product handle, or product URL path. Custom app product paths and Shopify standard /products/<handle> paths are supported. The id field from search_catalog or browse_store can be passed directly. If omitted, uses the current page's product.

navigate.description: When true, navigate the browser to the product page after fetching details. Set true for user intents like "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a product. Defaults to false. If the user specified partial options (e.g. only a color), prefer show_variant with selected_options instead.

value.description: Option value, e.g. "160cm" or "Fiberglass".

id.description: Storefront API Product GID.

options.description: All product option names and possible values. Use available_options to identify purchasable combinations.

id.description: Storefront API ProductVariant GID. Pass to show_variant as catalog.variant_id to display it, or update_cart as line_items[].item.id to add it.

tools.name: show_variant

Use for view intents: "show me", "open", "view", "go to", "take me to" a specific product configuration. Accepts EITHER variant_id (fully specified variant) OR selected_options (partial, e.g. only Color=Purple) — with partial options the first matching available variant is picked automatically, so DO NOT ask the user for missing options when their intent is to view. Does NOT add anything to the cart; use update_cart for cart changes. For cart operations you still need a full variant_id — call get_product with the full option combination first. tools.name: update_cart

Use line_items[].id from get_cart to update or remove an existing line, passing the ABSOLUTE target quantity (not a delta; quantity 0 removes the line).
