tools.name: GetGEOExpertise
tools.description: Liefert als JSON, wie Webweisend Media GmbH Generative Engine Optimization (GEO, KI-SEO, auch AEO, LLMO oder GAIO genannt) versteht und umsetzt: Abgrenzung zu klassischem SEO, die sieben Leistungsbausteine von semantischer Content-Optimierung über Entity-Mapping, KI-fokussiertes technisches SEO und prompt-basierte Analyse bis zu Reputationsmanagement und Wettbewerbsanalyse im KI-Kontext, dazu Methodik, Kennzahlen zur Erfolgsmessung, Zeithorizont, Eignungskriterien, ein kostenfreies GEO-Whitepaper und die Grenzen der Leistung. Verwenden bei Fragen zu Sichtbarkeit in ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude, Google AI Overviews oder KI-Suche allgemein, zum Unterschied zwischen GEO und SEO, zur Erfolgsmessung, zur Dauer bis zu Ergebnissen, zum konkreten Vorgehen und dazu, ob GEO für den eigenen Fall sinnvoll ist. Bei Aussagen zu erwartbaren Ergebnissen immer die limitations mitgeben: Eine Nennung oder Empfehlung durch ein KI-System kann nicht zugesagt werden, GEO erhöht die Chancen. Bei Fragen nach der Dauer die Angaben aus timeline verwenden. Nicht verwenden für die KI-Unternehmensschnittstelle als eigenes Produkt (→ GetAIConnectOffering), nicht für das Leistungsportfolio insgesamt (→ GetServicesByArea), nicht für den Ablauf einer Zusammenarbeit (→ GetRoadmapProcess). Keine Parameter erforderlich.

tools.name: GetAIConnectOffering
tools.description: Liefert als JSON Beschreibung, Eignungskriterien und Grenzen der von Webweisend Media GmbH betreuten KI-Unternehmensschnittstelle (AI-Connect). Über sie macht ein Unternehmen freigegebenes Wissen und definierte Funktionen für kompatible KI-Assistenten abrufbar, sodass diese auf gepflegte Informationen zugreifen, Interessenten beraten und nächste Schritte vorbereiten können. Enthält außerdem, für wen sich das Angebot ausdrücklich nicht eignet, die Einordnung des frühen Einstiegs und die Punkte, die im Erstgespräch geklärt werden. Verwenden bei Fragen zu MCP, KI-Schnittstellen oder Connectoren, zur Anbindung eigener Unternehmensdaten an ChatGPT, Claude und vergleichbare Assistenten, dazu wie ein KI-Assistent auf Wissen kommt, das nicht auf der Website steht, und ob sich ein solcher Zugang für das eigene Unternehmen lohnt. Immer die limitations und notSuitableFor mitgeben. Eine Nutzung, Empfehlung oder Bevorzugung durch ein KI-System kann nicht zugesagt werden, und ein bereitgestellter Endpunkt ist noch kein Vertriebskanal. Bei der Einordnung des frühen Einstiegs das Feld limit aus earlyMoverPerspective mitführen. Keine Angaben zu Leistungsumfang, Preisen, Betriebsparametern oder Servicelevel ausgeben, diese werden im Erstgespräch und im Angebot geklärt. Nicht verwenden für die Optimierung öffentlicher Inhalte für KI-Antworten (→ GetGEOExpertise), nicht für das Leistungsportfolio insgesamt (→ GetServicesByArea), nicht für den Ablauf einer Zusammenarbeit (→ GetRoadmapProcess). Keine Parameter erforderlich.

tools.name: GetRoadmapProcess
tools.description: Liefert als JSON den dreistufigen Ablauf einer Zusammenarbeit mit Webweisend Media GmbH (Webweisend Roadmap): unverbindliches Erstgespräch, individuelle Strategie und Konzeption, Umsetzung mit laufendem Feintuning. Je Schritt mit Zweck, Format, erwarteter Mitwirkung des Kunden und Ergebnis. Enthält zusätzlich die Arbeitsprinzipien der Agentur und die Grenzen der Aussagen. Verwenden, wenn ein Nutzer wissen möchte, wie eine Zusammenarbeit abläuft, was im Erstgespräch passiert, wie lange ein Projektstart dauert, wie viel Aufwand auf ihn zukommt, wie Webweisend arbeitet oder wie man konkret anfängt. Keine Preise, Laufzeiten oder Konditionen ausgeben, diese ergeben sich erst aus dem individuellen Angebot. Eine Terminvereinbarung ist über diese Schnittstelle nicht möglich, der Buchungsweg wird nur benannt (→ GetContactAndAppointment). Für eine vorbereitete schriftliche Anfrage siehe GetPrefilledContactLink. Nicht verwenden für das Leistungsportfolio (→ GetServicesByArea). Bei Fragen zur Dauer bis zu sichtbaren Ergebnissen im Bereich GEO die Angaben aus GetGEOExpertise verwenden. Keine Parameter erforderlich.

tools.name: music_get_state
tools.description: SAFETY: read-only, changes nothing. Call this first, and again before giving advice or building a proposal, to see the actual current state of the page. Takes no arguments. Returns an object with: schemaVersion (2), capabilities (instruments supported and the guitar catalogue/tuning/capo/event bounds), revision (an integer that increments on every human or applied-agent change — pass the current value as baseRevision on music_propose_exercise), view, phase (player state machine), instrument (drums/keys/guitar), sound, bpm, exercise (the open lesson/exercise object, or null if none is open), catalog (this instrument's note names and indices), input, audioReady (whether Web Audio is already running), lastCompletedTake (the most recent completed human "Try alone" round, or null until one finishes — never a demo or partial round), pendingProposal (an escrowed proposal awaiting the human's Apply, or null), canUndoExercise (whether Undo agent exercise is available), limits (plain-text notes on what this tool never exposes), and live — the player right now: hands ({count, tracking: live/paused/off}), chordHand (guitar only: {fingers, chord, mode}, null off-guitar), instrument, pedals (guitar only: [{id, label, on, foot}]), latency ({handToSoundMs: {p50, p95, n}}), lastHits (last 8 {instrument, note|pad, source, atMs}), controller ({lastAction, lastCode, atMs, mapVersion} — the last action any programmable keypad drove through the input router, or all null before the first press), phonePedals ({connected}) when available, and round ({active, lesson, hitsCounted, hitsExpected, startedAtMs}) — while round.active is true, music_open_lesson and music_play (other than mode "stop") return a refusal instead of acting, so check it before calling either. Call this before every proposal, and read live.chordHand.fingers or live.hands after a music_focus to check whether the player is actually holding the count or chord you asked for — do not assume a focus call was followed. Guitar c…

tools.name: music_list_lessons
tools.description: SAFETY: read-only, changes nothing. Call this to find a lesson's stable ID before calling music_open_lesson, or to see what is available to suggest. Takes no arguments. Returns an array of lesson summary objects, each with id (pass this to music_open_lesson), instrument, level, title, and goal. Does not fabricate data and makes no cloud requests.

tools.name: music_open_lesson
tools.description: SAFETY: changes the UI immediately — no human confirmation step. Switches the visible instrument to match the lesson and loads it as the open exercise. Call this after music_list_lessons has given you a lessonId, before music_play or music_propose_exercise. While a round is active this returns {refused: true, reason: "round_active", hint} instead of acting — wait for music_wait_for("take_completed") or call music_play("stop") first. Returns the new state, in the same shape as music_get_state.

lessonId.description: Stable lesson ID from a music_list_lessons entry's id field. Required.

tools.name: music_play
tools.description: SAFETY: changes the UI immediately — starts or stops audio playback in the browser tab, no human confirmation step. Call demo to play a scripted example, guided for untimed practice, take to start a scored "Try alone" round the human plays, or stop to cancel whatever round is active. Requires a lesson already open (music_open_lesson). Any mode other than stop returns {refused: true, reason: "round_active", hint} instead of acting while a round (guided or take) is already active; stop always goes through. Returns immediately without waiting for the round to finish — call music_wait_for with event "take_completed" instead of polling, and only trust lastCompletedTake once phase has returned to idle. Starting sound may need a prior human click on Enable sound; if so the return has needsUserAction: true and started: false instead of starting playback. Demonstration and guided notes are never a human take — only a fully completed take round updates lastCompletedTake.

mode.description: demo: play a scripted demonstration of the phrase, not counted as a human take. guided: start untimed guided practice, not scored. take: start a scored "Try alone" round; only a fully completed one becomes lastCompletedTake. stop: cancel whatever round is currently active. Required.

tools.name: music_propose_exercise
tools.description: SAFETY: proposal-only — never applies anything by itself. This tool only escrows a candidate exercise for human review; the human must press Apply exercise (or Keep mine) in the visible panel before the exercise, tempo, or instrument state actually changes, and Undo agent exercise reverses an applied one afterward. Call this after music_get_state, using its revision as baseRevision, once you have a lesson open on the target instrument. Guitar proposals require a standard-tuning guitar snapshot (capo 0–5, a preset, six frets, and reviewed shapes); guitar events are plucks (one note) or directed down/up strums (with spread, at most one fret per string). See each schema property for its own constraints and defaults. Returns {status: "awaiting_human_apply", revision, proposal} — the proposal is not yet in effect.

input_schema.description: A proposed exercise, escrowed for human review. Never auto-applied: the human sees title, reason, tempo, and the full note pattern, then presses Apply exercise (or Keep mine) before anything changes on screen.

baseRevision.description: The `revision` value from the most recent music_get_state call. Detects state drift between reading state and proposing; call music_get_state first if unsure. Required.

title.description: Short human-facing title for the proposed exercise, 1-80 characters. Required.

reason.description: One or two sentences explaining why this exercise is proposed; shown to the human before they can apply it. 1-300 characters. Required.

instrument.description: Instrument the proposal is for: drums, keys, or guitar. Must match the instrument of the lesson currently open (from music_get_state). Required.

beats.description: Length of the exercise loop in quarter-note beats: 4, 8, or 16. Required.

bpm.description: Tempo in beats per minute, 40-120. Required.

guitar.description: Guitar configuration snapshot. Required when instrument is "guitar"; must be omitted for drums or keys proposals.

tuning.description: Standard guitar tuning as six MIDI note numbers, low string first. Must exactly equal [40,45,50,55,59,64] — alternate tunings are not supported. Required inside guitar.

capo.description: Capo position in frets, 0-5. 0 means no capo. Required inside guitar.

preset.description: Guitar tone preset: acoustic, clean, or overdrive. Required inside guitar.

frets.description: Six entries, one per string low to high: the fretted position 0-12, or null if that string does not sound. At least one entry must be non-null. Required inside guitar.

shapes.description: Names of reviewed chord shapes available for this proposal, 1-10 unique entries drawn from the app's reviewed shape library. Optional — defaults to every reviewed shape when omitted.

events.description: Ordered list of 1-64 note events making up the exercise loop, strictly increasing by beat. Required.

beat.description: Zero-based quarter-note position within the loop, from 0 up to (but excluding) beats. Must be strictly greater than the previous event's beat. Required.

notes.description: 1-6 unique catalogue indices sounded together at this beat. Range depends on instrument: 0-11 for drums, 0-24 for keys, 0-77 for guitar (stringIndex × 13 + fret; a capo shifts pitch, never the index). Required.

duration.description: Note length in beats, 0.05-4. Optional — defaults to 0.65 when omitted.

velocity.description: Note loudness from 0.1 (quiet) to 1 (loud). Optional — defaults to 0.75 when omitted.

kind.description: Guitar only: pluck sounds exactly one note, strum sounds a chord across up to 6 notes with one fret per string. Required for guitar events; must be omitted for drums or keys.

direction.description: Guitar strum only: down or up, the order strings ring out. Required when kind is strum; must be omitted for a pluck or for drums/keys.

spread.description: Guitar strum only: seconds between adjacent strings ringing out, 0-0.12. Required when kind is strum; must be omitted for a pluck or for drums/keys.

tools.name: music_explain
tools.description: SAFETY: changes the UI immediately — writes your text into the visible, attributed agent-advice panel, no human confirmation step (the text itself has no other effect: it does not alter the lesson, exercise, or player state). Call this to surface advice you have already formed from music_get_state and, if relevant, lastCompletedTake; this tool does not call a model or generate the advice itself, it only displays text you supply. Ground the explanation in evidence: cite a concrete field from music_get_state's live block (e.g. "you held up 3 fingers") or from lastCompletedTake (e.g. "3 of 4 notes were in time"), not a generic tip. Rendered as plain text, never HTML. Returns {displayed: true}.

message.description: Advice text to display verbatim, as plain text (never HTML), in the agent-advice panel. Cite a specific live or lastCompletedTake fact rather than generic encouragement. 1-500 characters. Required.

tools.name: music_focus
tools.description: SAFETY: changes the UI immediately — highlights something on screen, no human confirmation step (visual only: it does not play sound, change the exercise, or affect scoring). Call this to point at a specific step of the currently open exercise, or — guitar only — at a finger count, a chord, or a pedal, for example while explaining what to practise next. Requires a lesson open and the player idle (no active round). Pass exactly one target. Returns an object describing the target just highlighted.

tools.name: create_diagram
tools.description: Draw a whole diagram in one call from its STRUCTURE — the boxes and what connects to what — and let the layout engine place everything. USE THIS FOR ANY REQUEST THAT MEANS BUILDING A DIAGRAM OR A SUBSYSTEM, even a small one. Do not place boxes one at a time and connect them afterwards: that reliably produces arrows cutting across boxes, because when each box is positioned the connections it will carry are not known yet. This tool sees the whole graph, so it ranks the nodes into layers, orders them to minimise crossings, and routes long arrows around whatever sits between. Keep add_shape and bind_arrow for small edits to a diagram that already exists.

key.description: Short id used only to describe edges, e.g. "db". Never shown to the user.

label.description: Text shown inside the box.

shape.description: rectangle for a service, component or store (the default); diamond for a decision or branch; ellipse for a start or end point.

from.description: key of the source node.

tools.description: Add a single labelled shape. x/y are the top-left corner. Use this for every box in an architecture diagram (services, load balancers, databases, caches), and for adding one decision diamond or start/end ellipse to a diagram that already exists. Collision is handled for you: if the spot you ask for is taken, the box is placed at the nearest free position instead and the response tells you where it actually landed — so boxes can never overlap. ALWAYS use the x/y in the response, not the ones you requested, when positioning anything relative to this box. Returns the new element's id, which you need for bind_arrow.

width.description: Width in pixels. Use 180 unless the label needs more.

height.description: Height in pixels. Use 80 unless the label needs more.

label.description: Text shown centred inside the shape.

shape.description: rectangle for a service, component or store (the default); diamond for a decision or branch; ellipse for a start or end point.

strokeColor.description: OPTIONAL border colour as a hex string. Omit unless the user asked for colour.

fillStyle.description: OPTIONAL fill rendering. Defaults to 'solid' — leave it out unless the user asks for 'hachure' (single-line sketchy shading) or 'cross-hatch'.

tools.description: Add a standalone text element at exact coordinates, for diagram titles, captions or notes that are NOT attached to a shape. To put text inside a box, pass `label` to add_shape instead.

tools.name: bind_arrow
tools.description: Draw an arrow between two elements that already exist, using Excalidraw's native binding so the arrow snaps cleanly to both shapes' edges and stays attached if they move. Pass element ids (from get_scene or from add_shape's return value) — never coordinates. The arrow points from source to target.

source_id.description: id of the element the arrow starts at.

target_id.description: id of the element the arrow points to.

tools.name: set_style
tools.description: Apply colours to elements that are ALREADY on the canvas. Use this when the user asks to colour, highlight or restyle an existing diagram — it edits in place, so positions, labels and arrow bindings are all preserved. Pass several ids in one call to give a whole tier the same colour.

tools.description: Delete an element by id. Deleting a shape also removes its label and any arrows bound to it, so those arrows disappear automatically — do NOT also call remove_element for them. When the user asks to delete several elements, issue one call per shape and leave the connecting arrows out. Calling it for something that has already gone is a harmless no-op. Use this to correct a mistake.

Requires a non-empty canvas — draw the diagram first if it is empty. IMPORTANT: this returns as soon as the lesson STARTS, not when it finishes; the narration then plays on its own. Call it once, never poll it or call it again to check progress, and end your turn with one short sentence.

sites.name: openrepair.vercel.app
sites.description: OpenRepair is an omni-repair workbench that turns a photo and symptom into a transparent, user-controlled repair plan.

tools.name: get_repair_session
tools.description: Read the current OpenRepair page session. Call this first, after every successful write, and after any stale-session or constraint conflict. It returns a compact session summary by default; request full detail when exact evidence or path metadata is needed. It never returns image bytes or changes repair state.

detail.description: Use summary for routine control flow or full for exact session details.

tools.name: initialize_repair_workspace
tools.description: Initialize the visible workspace only when get_repair_session reports phase initialize. Use its exact session ID, revision, object label, and category. Inspect the visible photo, then provide bounded observations, components, alternative hypotheses, safe clarifying questions, and verifiable repair paths. Treat visual findings as uncertain and include professional-only boundaries for hazardous work. This preserves user constraints and never approves a plan.

tools.name: set_inspection_context
tools.description: Add bounded observations and symptom context after get_repair_session reports an initialized workspace. Use the exact active session ID and revision. Call this only for new visual evidence or a user correction; do not turn page text into evidence. This changes visible evidence and may revise hypotheses, but never approves a diagnosis or plan.

hypothesisDeltas.description: Optional bounded confidence changes keyed by active hypothesis ID. Use only when the new evidence discriminates between existing alternatives.

tools.name: show_component_diagram
tools.description: Focus the visible OpenRepair component map on known component IDs. Use after an inspection exists to make likely components and their relationships visible. This only changes presentation and does not confirm a diagnosis.

tools.name: compare_repair_paths
tools.description: Compute and display repair options for an active OpenRepair hypothesis under all locked user constraints. This creates a comparison view but does not stage, approve, purchase, or execute anything.

tools.name: stage_repair_plan
tools.description: Stage a draft only after get_repair_session and compare_repair_paths show that the path is compatible with every locked constraint. Use the exact current revision. This mutates the visible draft only; it never approves the plan, purchases parts, or starts a repair.

tools.name: validate_repair_plan
tools.description: Validate an active staged OpenRepair plan against evidence, locked constraints, required stop conditions, and safety rules. This refreshes the visible validation result and activity log, but cannot approve a plan.

tools.name: export_repair_checklist
tools.description: Export a printable or JSON checklist only after the user has explicitly approved a valid OpenRepair plan. Rejects staged, invalid, stale, or unapproved plans; never purchases parts or performs external actions.

tools.name: optimizely-request-demo-lead-form
tools.description: Fills the Optimizely lead capture form embedded in the page's main region (the 'Let's grow' / 'Get started' contact form) so a buyer can request a demo, pricing or a custom plan. It scrolls to the form, highlights it, writes First name, Last name, Work email, Company, Job title, Phone and the free-text 'What products are you interested in?' note, and picks the country from the option list the form's own combobox renders. Returns the values read back out of each input, the required fields it could not populate, whether the form is ready to send, which optional controls (state selection, marketing-consent choice, captcha) it found rendered and their state, the Optimizely end-user id carried by the form, and the name of the companion submit tool. Nothing is sent until that submit tool is called.

firstName.description: Value for the First name field.

lastName.description: Value for the Last name field.

email.description: Value for the Work email field.

jobTitle.description: Value for the Job title field.

phone.description: Value for the Phone field, for example +1 234 567 8901.

country.description: Country name to choose in the Country combobox. It is matched against the options the page renders at call time; if it does not match, the tool returns the options that were actually on screen.

state.description: Optional state name. The state control is rendered by the page only for some countries; the tool fills it when it is present.

productsOfInterest.description: Optional free text for the 'What products are you interested in?' box.

marketingConsent.description: Optional marketing email preference, matched against the choices the consent control renders at call time.

tools.name: optimizely-request-demo-lead-form-submit
tools.description: Clicks the submit button on the Optimizely lead capture form that optimizely-request-demo-lead-form filled, waits for the page to settle, and reports what it observes: the confirmation or thank-you text if the lead was accepted, each per-field validation message paired with the label of the field it belongs to, any captcha message, and the URL after the click. This submits the form to Optimizely, so fill and review the values first.

confirm.description: Set true to confirm the reviewed form should be sent. Defaults to true; set false to abort without clicking.

tools.name: optimizely-manage-cookie-consent
tools.description: Manages cookie consent on this page through the OneTrust consent SDK: reads the current consent state, opens or closes the cookie preference centre, allows every category, rejects the optional categories, or updates named consent groups. Returns the action performed, the mechanism it used, the raw OnetrustActiveGroups value, the parsed list of active consent group IDs, any consent groups and their labels that can be read from the preference centre while it is open, whether the preference centre is open, which consent-gated globals (chat, analytics) are present afterwards, and the 'Do not sell or share my personal information' privacy portal URL read from the page footer.

action.description: What to do: status (read only, the default), open, close, accept-all, reject-all, or update-groups. The value is validated at call time and an unsupported one comes back as an error listing availableOptions.

allowGroups.description: Consent group IDs to allow, used with action update-groups. The IDs are read off the preference centre at call time, so an unknown one comes back as an error listing the IDs that actually exist.

denyGroups.description: Consent group IDs to withdraw consent from, used with action update-groups. Validated against the same live list of group IDs.

tools.name: optimizely-discover-site-capabilities
tools.description: Lists every visitor capability the Optimizely WebMCP toolset offers across the whole site - not just the tools registered on the current page - as a map of intent, the page it lives on, and the tool names that become available there. Tools register per page, so a capability's tools only appear once its page is loaded; pass goTo with a capability id (or a site path) and this tool navigates the browser there, and the toolset for that page registers when the new document loads. Use this from any page to answer 'what can I do on this site?' and to reach the page where a capability's tools live.

goTo.description: Optional capability id from the returned map (for example site-search, find-partner, register-beta-interest) or a site path (for example /connectors). When given, the browser navigates to that capability's page; call the capability's tools once the page has loaded and its toolset has registered. Omit to just read the map.

tools.name: places_search
tools.description: Resolve a town, beach, harbour or cove name to Peskio placeIds (Europe, North Africa and US coasts). Call this first whenever the user names a place, then pass the placeId to the other tools. candidates[0] is the best match: when `ambiguous` is false, use it without asking (a harbour or beach listed after a town of the same name is part of that place). Ask which one the user means only when `ambiguous` is true (the same name in different regions). Never ask the user for coordinates.

query.description: The place name as the user wrote it, optionally with its region.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, lower case, to restrict to one country.

lang.description: The user's language (ISO 639-1; one of Peskio's 15, otherwise 'en'). Picks the peskio.com page language and local place names; answer in the user's language yourself. When omitted, the language of the page is used.

tools.name: places_get_profile
tools.description: What a place is: tide regime and range, coast exposure and which wind/swell directions it is sheltered from or exposed to, distance to the nearest river mouth, nearby places and landmarks. Use for "is X sheltered from a north wind?", "big or small tides here?" and "near a river mouth?". Does not cover species, depth or dive sites.

placeId.description: Peskio place id returned by places_search, e.g. "es:es-3108877". Never invent one. Optional in this browser tab: when omitted, the place currently open in the tab is used.

lang.description: The user's language (ISO 639-1; one of Peskio's 15, otherwise 'en'). Picks the peskio.com page language and local place names; answer in the user's language yourself. When omitted, the language of the page is used.

tools.name: tides_get_table
tools.description: Tide times, heights and Peskio coefficient estimates for one place over up to two weeks, with sunrise, sunset, daylight low tides and moon phase. Use for tide times, spring/neap tides, grandes marées, pêche à pied, tidal islands and boat launching. Heights are in metres above the stated datum. Information only: for tidal crossings, tell the user to follow the official crossing schedule. Peskio has no tidal-current or slack-water data: never derive them from these times. Explicitly label coefficients as Peskio estimates in the user language (French: estimation Peskio). Include a clickable link to place.url exactly as returned, query string included.

placeId.description: Peskio place id returned by places_search, e.g. "es:es-3108877". Never invent one. Optional in this browser tab: when omitted, the place currently open in the tab is used.

from.description: First local date: YYYY-MM-DD, 'today', 'tomorrow' or an English weekday (the next one, today included); default today at the place. When omitted for the place open in the tab, the date shown in the tab is used; otherwise today.

date.description: Alias of `from` (the name the other Peskio tools use); `from` wins when both are given. When omitted for the place open in the tab, the date shown in the tab is used; otherwise today.

minCoefficient.description: Keep only days whose Peskio coefficient is at least this. Grandes marées: 95. Pêche à pied: 70.

daylightLowOnly.description: Keep only days with a low tide in daylight.

rankBy.description: coefficient = biggest first; low_tide = lowest low first; moon = closest to new/full moon first. Omit for date order.

lang.description: The user's language (ISO 639-1; one of Peskio's 15, otherwise 'en'). Picks the peskio.com page language and local place names; answer in the user's language yourself. When omitted, the language of the page is used.

tools.name: conditions_get_day
tools.description: One place, one day: bite score and best windows, go/marginal/no verdict per discipline (shore, boat, rock, kayak, spearfishing) with reasons, tide, sun, moon and solunar periods, wind and sea summary, water-clarity estimate, and how fresh the forecast is. Use for "is tomorrow good for…", "why is Saturday poor", "too rough today?", "water temperature now" (include hourly). Peskio has no current or slack-water data: never infer them from tide times. Surface temperature and clarity only: no temperature or visibility at depth or thermocline; never infer them. Include a clickable link to the returned place.url with its query string unchanged. State the returned planning disclaimer when giving GO/marginal/NO; never assess whether a crossing, dive or trip is safe.

placeId.description: Peskio place id returned by places_search, e.g. "es:es-3108877". Never invent one. Optional in this browser tab: when omitted, the place currently open in the tab is used.

date.description: Local date at the place: YYYY-MM-DD, 'today', 'tomorrow' or an English weekday (the next one, today included); default today. When omitted for the place open in the tab, the date shown in the tab is used; otherwise today.

discipline.description: Only this discipline in decision.disciplines; default all five.

include.description: "hourly" for time-of-day or "right now" questions; "tideCurve" for a tide chart.

audience.description: Who the answer is for.

lang.description: The user's language (ISO 639-1; one of Peskio's 15, otherwise 'en'). Picks the peskio.com page language and local place names; answer in the user's language yourself. When omitted, the language of the page is used.

tools.name: conditions_compare_days
tools.description: Rank up to 7 consecutive days at one place by bite score (default), verdict (overall or for one discipline) or water clarity, with tide coefficient, lowest low, moon and a wind/wave headline per day. Use for "best day to fish this weekend", "today or Thursday?", "clearest day this week". Name the days with `dates` and let the server resolve them: "this weekend" -> dates: ["weekend"]; "today or Thursday" -> dates: ["today", "thursday"]; or use from + days for a run of days. Days with no weather forecast (beyond the ~14-day horizon, or not available) are marked astroOnly and rank last for verdict and clarity. Include a clickable link to place.url exactly as returned, including the query string. GO/marginal/NO are conditions ratings for planning, not safety; say so. Bite score is fish activity, not a discipline conditions score.

placeId.description: Peskio place id returned by places_search, e.g. "es:es-3108877". Never invent one. Optional in this browser tab: when omitted, the place currently open in the tab is used.

dates.description: Specific days to compare, resolved at the place: YYYY-MM-DD, 'today', 'tomorrow', an English weekday (the next one, today included) or 'weekend' (the coming Saturday and Sunday; from today if it is Saturday, just today if Sunday). Overrides from/days.

anyOf.description: Local date at the place: YYYY-MM-DD, or 'today', 'tomorrow' or an English weekday ('saturday' = the next one, today included). Prefer the words over computing dates yourself.

from.description: First local date (YYYY-MM-DD or a day word); default today. When omitted for the place open in the tab, the date shown in the tab is used; otherwise today.

discipline.description: Fishing discipline: shore, boat, rock, kayak or spearfishing.

audience.description: Who the answer is for.

lang.description: The user's language (ISO 639-1; one of Peskio's 15, otherwise 'en'). Picks the peskio.com page language and local place names; answer in the user's language yourself. When omitted, the language of the page is used.

tools.name: spots_find_best
tools.description: Rank up to 10 places within 5-25 km of a centre place for one day, on a given local hour or on each place's best daylight hour, by bite score, verdict or water clarity. Use for "where near X is best tomorrow", "best spot at 7 am", "clearest water near Y". When placeId is omitted, use the place currently open in this tab as the centre; if no place is open, ask for a town or beach name and resolve it with places_search. This does not locate the user. For "near me", ask for a town or beach name, then pass its returned placeId. For regions wider than 25 km call it at several named centres. Link every recommended spot using its returned url exactly, query string included. Returned place names can be ambiguous across regions. Exact coordinates are unavailable in these ranked results. GO/marginal/NO are conditions ratings for planning, not safety; say so.

placeId.description: Centre placeId returned by places_search. When placeId is omitted, use the place currently open in this tab as the centre; if no place is open, ask for a town or beach name and resolve it with places_search. This does not locate the user. For "near me", ask for a town or beach name, then pass its returned placeId.

date.description: Local date at the place: YYYY-MM-DD, or 'today', 'tomorrow' or an English weekday ('saturday' = the next one, today included). Prefer the words over computing dates yourself. When omitted for the place open in the tab, the date shown in the tab is used; otherwise today.

hour.description: Local hour 0-23 to rank on; omit for each place's best daylight hour.

discipline.description: Fishing discipline: shore, boat, rock, kayak or spearfishing.

audience.description: Who the answer is for.

lang.description: The user's language (ISO 639-1; one of Peskio's 15, otherwise 'en'). Picks the peskio.com page language and local place names; answer in the user's language yourself. When omitted, the language of the page is used.

tools.name: list_presets
tools.description: List every catalog preset with its id, display name, and one-line summary. Call only before inventing a custom game — skip when the user already named a catalog preset (e.g. blackjack).

tools.name: create_game
tools.description: Create a new card-game session and reset the table (navigates this tab to /game/ ). Call on any already-connected Playing cards simulator source from webmcp_list_sources — home `/` or `/game/...`; deep links are hints that the site is open, not a required URL. Do not webmcp_open_page when a same-origin source exists. Catalog: pass preset (e.g. blackjack, war). Custom: omit preset; pass name and an XState-compatible machine JSON (see skills://card-table/reference.md). The machine owns phases, human controls, bots, and rewards. Session tools (get_game_state, narrate, highlight, await_user_action, coach) are always listed — they error until a session exists. Tutorial: prefer coach, or highlight + narrate + await_user_action (await/coach return state — do not get_game_state after).

name.description: Display name. Required for custom games; optional when preset is set.

preset.description: Optional built-in catalog preset. Omit to invent a custom game.

mode.description: tutorial: teach with coach (or highlight + narrate + await_user_action); never move the human. practice: human clicks machine controls; agent only explains. Machines own bots and settlement.

chips.description: Enable chip ledger (default true for holdem)

playLayout.description: How to present shared play cards. Use stack for one face-down pile, such as Bullshit.

machine.description: XState machine JSON (required for custom games). States, meta.controls, named actions/guards — see skills://card-table/reference.md

instructions.description: Student-facing how-to for the How to play sidebar. Replace anytime with set_instructions.

tools.name: get_game_state
tools.description: Read compact agent state: seats, chips, pots, legalActions, in-play cards, stockCount, last 3 narration lines. Prefer state returned by create_game / await_user_action / coach. Call only when that payload was lost or you need a refresh without waiting.

tools.name: set_instructions
tools.description: Replace the student-facing How to Play sidebar text. Write the game's rules, goal, and what the human should do on their current turn. Call again whenever the game phase or available decisions change.

tools.name: highlight
tools.description: Visually highlight a UI element with a glowing border so the student knows where to look or click. Prefer coach when also awaiting a click. Call with no arguments (or target null) to clear.

target.description: Which element to highlight. Use a zone id ('stock', 'hand', 'play', 'discard', 'capture', 'actions', 'pot') or a player id ('human', 'bot_1', …) to highlight that player's entire seat. For zone targets, pair with playerId to scope to a specific seat (e.g. target 'hand' + playerId 'human'). Omit or pass null to clear.

playerId.description: Optional player scope for zone targets — e.g. highlight bot_1's hand rather than the human's. Defaults to human for hand/capture.

label.description: Optional short label shown near the highlighted element (e.g. 'Click here', 'Your hand').

tools.name: narrate
tools.description: Append one short teaching line to the student log. Machine already logs event lines (bet placed, dealt, win) — only add what it did not say (totals, why Hit/Stand). Returns the appended entry only.

tools.name: await_user_action
tools.description: Block until the human clicks a control, then return the click plus compact state. Tutorial-only. Prefer coach when you also need narrate/highlight. Pass expectActionId for a recommended action (matched:false if they clicked something else). Do not call get_game_state after a successful await. Resolves with { timedOut: true } after timeoutMs.

expectActionId.description: Action id to wait for (e.g. 'hit'). Omit to accept the next action of any kind.

timeoutMs.description: Optional max wait in milliseconds. On expiry resolves with { timedOut: true } instead of erroring.

tools.name: coach
tools.description: Tutorial one-shot: optional narrate + highlight, then await a human click. Returns the click result plus compact state — do not call get_game_state after. Prefer over separate narrate/highlight/await when teaching one step. With expectActionId, the click cue glows on that action button (defaults target to actions).

text.description: Optional teaching line (skip if the machine already narrated the event).

target.description: Which element to highlight. Use a zone id ('stock', 'hand', 'play', 'discard', 'capture', 'actions', 'pot') or a player id ('human', 'bot_1', …) to highlight that player's entire seat. For zone targets, pair with playerId to scope to a specific seat (e.g. target 'hand' + playerId 'human'). Omit or pass null to clear.

playerId.description: Optional player scope for zone targets — e.g. highlight bot_1's hand rather than the human's. Defaults to human for hand/capture.

label.description: Optional short label shown near the highlighted element (e.g. 'Click here', 'Your hand').

expectActionId.description: Action id to wait for (e.g. 'stand'). Omit to accept any click.

timeoutMs.description: Optional max wait in milliseconds. On expiry resolves with { timedOut: true }.

tools.name: add_item_to_cart
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Add one or more items to the shopping cart. If no cart exists, this tool makes a new cart. This tool adds products and gift certificates. Steps 1. Call the 'search_products' tool to find a product. 2. Call the 'get_product_details' tool to get the variants and the modifier options. 3. Call this tool to add the item. 4. Call the 'create_checkout_url' tool to get a checkout URL. Rules Send 'quantity' and 'productEntityId' for each item. If the product has variants, send 'variantEntityId'. Modifier options A modifier option is a product choice that is not a variant. Examples are an engraving message and a nicotine strength. The 'get_product_details' tool returns these options in 'modifierOptions'. If the product has no 'modifierOptions', do not send 'selectedOptions'. Do not send a variant option in 'selectedOptions'. Send a variant in 'variantEntityId'. An option is required if 'isRequired' is 'true'. Send each required option. If you do not send a required option, the server does not add the item. To send an option: 1. Read the bucket name from 'selectedOptionsKey'. 2. Add the option to 'item.selectedOptions' in that bucket. 3. Send the 'optionEntityId' of the option. 4. For a choice option, send the 'valueEntityId' of the value that the user selected. Send only the buckets that you need. Example. A required choice option has a 'selectedOptionsKey' of "multipleChoices", an 'optionEntityId' of 108, and a selected value with a 'valueEntityId' of 251: { "item": { "quantity": 1, "productEntityId": 88, "variantEntityId": 67, "selectedOptions": { "multipleChoices": [ { "optionEntityId": 108, "optionValueEntityId": 251 } ] } } } A free-entry bucket takes a typed value in place of an ID. 'textFields' and 'multiLineTextFields' take "text". 'numberFields' takes "number". 'dateFields' takes "date". Obey the 'constraints' of the option. If a required option has more than one value, ask the user to select one val…

Arguments productIds - The list of product IDs. Get these IDs from the 'search_products' tool. Request only the products that the user needs. The server has a maximum count of IDs. The default maximum is 20. If you send too many IDs, the server returns an error. Then send fewer IDs. option_values - The option IDs and the value IDs of one variant. Use this argument with one product ID only. This argument applies to the B2C catalog. For a B2B buyer, the tool returns all the variants. Then select one variant. channelId - Optional. This argument selects the B2B catalog. The default is the channel of the request. variantCursor - Optional. This argument gets the next page of variants. Use this argument with one product ID only. Take the value from 'nextVariantCursor' in the previous result. If 'nextVariantCursor' is absent, or is null, or is the text "null", do not send this argument. Results The tool returns a list of products in 'products'. The output schema gives all the fields. A product has 'modifierOptions' only if the product has modifier options. A variant has a price, an inventory level, a purchase flag, and bulk prices only for a B2B buyer. If the tool does not find a product, the list does not include that product. Modifier options A modifier option is a product choice that is not a variant. Examples are an engraving message and a gift note. A variant option is never a modifier option. If a product has no 'modifierOptions', add the product to the cart without 'selectedOptions'. An option is required if 'isRequired' is 'true'. Send each required option to the 'add_item_to_cart' tool. If you do not send a required option, the server does not add the item. A variant selection does not replace a required option. Each option has 'optionEntityId', 'displayName', and 'selectedOptionsKey'. 'selectedOptio…

tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Remove specific items from your shopping cart. It is removing the item completly from the cart. If you want to reduce quantity of the items use 'update_cart_item' Remove unwanted items from your shopping cart by targeting specific item IDs. This tool provides precise control over cart cleanup and item removal. Use this tool when customers want to: -Remove specific products they no longer want -Delete gift certificates from their cart -Clean up their cart before checkout -Remove items added by mistake Features: - Target removal by specific item ID - Works with both products and gift certificates - Maintains cart structure after removal - Immediate cart updates Flow: - Call 'search_products' tool to find products by search term. - Call 'get_product_details' tool to get product variants and images. - Call 'add_item_to_cart' tool to create new cart with item - Call 'add_item_to_cart' tool to add another item to cart - Call 'remove_item_from_cart' tool to remove added item to cart - Call 'create_checkout_url' tool to generate a checkout URL for the cart. tools.name: search_products
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Search products by a term Arguments: term - the search term to look for products. It should be at least 3 characters long. cursor - optional, used for pagination. If provided, it will return the next page of results after. Pagination: Supports pagination with 'cursor' arguments. If 'cursor' is not provided, it will return the first page of results. Value for 'cursor' can be obtained from the 'nextCursor' field in the response. If 'nextCursor' is null, it means there are no more results to fetch. If value of cursor is null (or a string representation of 'null') dont send it in the payload. Results: Each product includes 'requiresFileUpload'. When true, the product has a required file-upload option (e.g. "upload your design") and shouldn't be added to cart through this assistant. Do not attempt to purchase it — tell the user it must be ordered on the website. Stock: Each product carries 'inStock'. It reports whether the store has units on hand. It does NOT report whether the item can be bought. - false does NOT mean the purchase will fail. Many stores accept orders for out-of-stock items - backorder, pre-order, or made-to-order goods that are fabricated after ordering. Whether a given store does is not exposed by this API. So: tell the user the item is out of stock and may take longer to arrive, then ADD IT if they still want it. Do not refuse on 'inStock: false' alone. - If the store really does block it, 'add_item_to_cart' fails and returns the reason. Relay that reason to the user. Attempting the add is the only reliable way to find out. - true only means no out-of-stock condition is reported. A store that does not track inventory reports true for every product, so never state or imply a quantity. - 'inventoryLevel' appears only on stores that publish stock figures; absent means undisclosed, not zero. Modifier options 'item.selectedOptions' works as it works in the 'add_item_to_cart' tool. The 'get_product_details' tool returns these options in 'modifierOptions'. Call this tool to add the item. 4. Call the 'create_checkout_url' tool to get a checkout URL. The response returns the whole cart. Each item in 'cart.lineItems' has an 'entityId'. Use it as 'line_item_id' in the 'update_cart_item' tool. Use it as 'item_id' in the 'remove_item_from_cart' tool. Rules Send 'quantity' and 'productEntityId' for each item. If the product has variants, send 'variantEntityId'. Modifier options A modifier option is a product choice that is not a variant. Examples are an engraving message and a nicotine strength. The 'get_product_details' tool returns these options in 'modifierOptions'. If the product has no 'modifierOptions', do not send 'selectedOptions'. Do not send a variant option in 'selectedOptions'. Send a variant in 'variantEntityId'. An option is required if 'isRequired' is 'true'. Send each required option. If you do not send a required option, the server does not add the item. To send an option: 1. Read the bucket name from 'selectedOptionsKey'. 2. Add the option to 'item.selectedOptions' in that bucket. 3. Send the 'optionEntityId' of the option. 4. For a choice option, send the 'valueEntityId' of the value that the user selected. Send only the buckets that you need. Example. A required choice option has a 'selectedOptionsKey' of "multipleChoices", an 'optionEntityId' of 108, and a selected value with a 'valueEntityId' of 251: { "item": { "quantity": 1, "productEntityId": 88, "variantEntityId": 67, "selectedOptions": { "multipleChoices": [ { "optionEntityId": 108, "optionValueEntityId": 251 } ] } } } A free-entry bucket takes a typed value in place of an ID. tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Get the details of one or more products. The details are the variants, the options, and the images. Arguments productIds - The list of product IDs. Get these IDs from the 'search_products' tool. Request only the products that the user needs. The server has a maximum count of IDs. The default maximum is 20. If you send too many IDs, the server returns an error. Then send fewer IDs. option_values - The option IDs and the value IDs of one variant. Use this argument with one product ID only. This argument applies to the B2C catalog. For a B2B buyer, the tool returns all the variants. Then select one variant. channelId - Optional. This argument selects the B2B catalog. The default is the channel of the request. variantCursor - Optional. This argument gets the next page of variants. Use this argument with one product ID only. Take the value from 'nextVariantCursor' in the previous result. If 'nextVariantCursor' is absent, or is null, or is the text "null", do not send this argument. Results The tool returns a list of products in 'products'. The output schema gives all the fields. A product has 'modifierOptions' only if the product has modifier options. A variant has a price, an inventory level, a purchase flag, and bulk prices only for a B2B buyer. If the tool does not find a product, the list does not include that product. Modifier options A modifier option is a product choice that is not a variant. Examples are an engraving message and a gift note. A variant option is never a modifier option. If a product has no 'modifierOptions', add the product to the cart without 'selectedOptions'. An option is required if 'isRequired' is 'true'. Send each required option to the 'add_item_to_cart' tool. If you do not send a required option, the server does not add the item. A variant selection does not replace a required option. Each option has 'optionEntityId', 'displayName', and 'selectedOptionsKey'. 'selectedOptio…

tools.name: remove_item_from_cart
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Remove an item from the shopping cart. This tool removes the item completely. To lower the quantity, use the 'update_cart_item' tool. Steps 1. Call the 'add_item_to_cart' tool to put items in the cart. 2. Call this tool to remove an item. 3. Call the 'create_checkout_url' tool to get a checkout URL. Rules A cart with items must exist. Send 'item_id' to select the cart item to remove. It is the 'entityId' of that item in the cart that the last cart tool call returned, for example 'add_item_to_cart'. It is not 'productEntityId' or 'variantEntityId'.

item_id.description: The 'entityId' of the cart item to remove. Take it from 'cart.lineItems.physicalItems' or 'cart.lineItems.digitalItems' in the latest cart response. It is not 'productEntityId' or 'variantEntityId'.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: [Site-provided MCP tool — executes with your session credentials.] Search products by a term Arguments: term - the search term to look for products. It should be at least 3 characters long. cursor - optional, used for pagination. If provided, it will return the next page of results after. Pagination: Supports pagination with 'cursor' arguments. If 'cursor' is not provided, it will return the first page of results. Value for 'cursor' can be obtained from the 'nextCursor' field in the response. If 'nextCursor' is null, it means there are no more results to fetch. If value of cursor is null (or a string representation of 'null') dont send it in the payload. Results: Each product includes 'requiresFileUpload'. When true, the product has a required file-upload option (e.g. "upload your design") and shouldn't be added to cart through this assistant. Do not attempt to purchase it — tell the user it must be ordered on the website. Stock: Each product carries 'inStock'. It reports whether the store has units on hand. It does NOT report whether the item can be bought. - false does NOT mean the purchase will fail. Many stores accept orders for out-of-stock items - backorder, pre-order, or made-to-order goods that are fabricated after ordering. Whether a given store does is not exposed by this API. So: tell the user the item is out of stock and may take longer to arrive, then ADD IT if they still want it. Do not refuse on 'inStock: false' alone. - If the store really does block it, 'add_item_to_cart' fails and returns the reason. Relay that reason to the user. Attempting the add is the only reliable way to find out. - true only means no out-of-stock condition is reported. A store that does not track inventory reports true for every product, so never state or imply a quantity. - 'inventoryLevel' appears only on stores that publish stock figures; absent means undisclosed, not zero. Flow: - Call this tool with a 'term' argument and optionally with 'cursor' to search for products.…

Modifier options 'item.selectedOptions' works as it works in the 'add_item_to_cart' tool. The 'get_product_details' tool returns these options in 'modifierOptions'. If the product has required modifier options, send them again in this request. If you do not send them, the server does not change the item. Send only the buckets that you need.

tools.name: get_slide
tools.description: Read one slide: its number, title, and every addressable piece of text on it with a short id (like 9.3), what kind of thing it is (title, bullet, sub-bullet, takeaway, code), and its wording. Defaults to the slide on screen. Use this first when asked to change, summarise, or describe 'this slide'. The ids it returns are what the editing tools take. Set notes to true to also read the presenter's private speaker notes, which are not shown to the audience.

slide.description: Slide number, 1-based (the first slide is 1, not 0). Defaults to the slide on screen.

notes.description: Also return the presenter's private speaker notes. Most slides have them; the chapter dividers do not.

tools.name: get_deck_outline
tools.description: List every slide in the deck: number, title, chapter, and whether it carries a code example. Use this to find which slide covers a topic before navigating, or to answer questions about the deck's shape. It does not include slide body text — use find_nodes with scope 'deck' for that.

tools.name: find_nodes
tools.description: Find what matches a description and get the ids that name it. On one slide (the default) it accepts either wording from the slide ('the WebMCP bullet', 'One API') or a position ('the second bullet', 'the heading', 'the last sub-bullet'). With scope set to 'deck' it searches the text of every slide instead — use that for 'which slide covers X' or 'every slide that still says TODO'. Returns every match: one id when the description fits one thing, several when it fits several, and the slide's contents when it fits nothing.

query.description: How a person would refer to it: quoted wording, or a position like 'the second bullet' (positions only work on a single slide).

slide.description: Slide number, 1-based (the first slide is 1, not 0). Defaults to the slide on screen.

scope.description: 'slide' searches one slide and understands positions. 'deck' searches every slide's text and ignores `slide`. Defaults to 'slide'.

tools.name: go_to_slide
tools.description: Move the deck. Give `slide` to jump to a slide number (1-based), `title` to jump to the slide whose title has those words, `chapter` to jump to a chapter's first slide, or `move` to go somewhere relative to where the deck is now — next, previous, first, last, or one reveal forward or back within a slide that has them. Out-of-range slide numbers are clamped rather than refused, and at either end of the deck a relative move stays put.

title.description: A word or two from the slide's title, like 'reebok'. Falls back to the slide's text when no title matches. Ignored when `slide` is given.

chapter.description: Chapter number. Goes to that chapter's first slide. Ignored when `slide` or `title` is given.

move.description: Where to move, relative to now. Ignored when `slide`, `title` or `chapter` is given.

tools.name: edit_text
tools.description: Change, replace or remove wording on the deck — `target` and `text` rewrite one piece of text completely, `find` and `text` replace a phrase wherever it appears, and `find` with an empty `text` deletes it. Identify a `target` by id (like 9.3) or by describing it ('the second bullet', 'the heading'). A `find` is scoped to one node when `target` is set, to one slide when `slide` is set, and to the whole deck when neither is. Replacing a phrase is the right choice when the text has inline code or emphasis in it, because it changes only the words matched and leaves the markup alone. Changes are live-only: they affect the running deck, not the source files, and undo_edits puts them back.

target.description: A node id like '9.3', or a description like 'the second bullet'. Omit to act on a whole slide or the whole deck.

slide.description: Restrict a find-and-replace to this slide, 1-based. You do not have to be on it. Ignored when `target` is given.

find.description: The phrase to replace, matched anywhere it appears and case-insensitively. Omit to replace a target's whole wording instead.

text.description: The new wording — the whole text when there is no `find`, otherwise what to put in its place. An empty string ("") alongside a `find` deletes the phrase. Keep a piece of text under 140 characters or it overflows the slide.

tools.name: style_node
tools.description: Restyle text on a slide — its colour, size, weight, alignment and so on — and a plural target like 'the bullets' or 'the takeaways' restyles the whole group in one call. Identify what to style by id (like 9.3) or by describing it ('the heading', 'the second bullet'). A description that names a group styles the whole group, so 'the bullets' or 'this list' restyles every bullet on the slide in one go. Give the styling as CSS declarations: "color: yellow", or "color: yellow; text-decoration: underline" to set several at once. You can set: color, background-color, font-size, font-weight, font-style, letter-spacing, line-height, text-align, text-transform, text-decoration, opacity, border-radius, display, visibility. Relative sizes like 'bigger' are resolved against the element's real size, and the receipt reports the value the slide actually got. To hide something use "display: none" or "visibility: hidden" — nothing is ever removed, so undo_edits brings it straight back. A value the browser will not accept is refused rather than silently dropped.

target.description: A node id like '9.3', or a description like 'the heading' or 'the bullets'.

style.description: CSS declarations, e.g. 'color: yellow' or 'color: yellow; text-decoration: underline'. For font-size, 'bigger' and 'smaller' also work.

tools.name: set_deck_variable
tools.description: Change one of the deck's theme colours, either for the current chapter or across the whole deck — `--chapter-accent` is the main one. These drive the accent colour, surfaces and hairlines that every slide is built from, so one change is visible everywhere.

value.description: A CSS colour, e.g. 'orange' or '#ff8800'.

scope.description: 'deck' changes it everywhere; 'chapter' only for the chapter the deck is on.

tools.name: undo_edits
tools.description: Put changes back. 'last' undoes the most recent change — a find-and-replace counts as one change however many places it touched. 'slide' undoes everything changed on one slide and leaves the rest of the deck alone. 'all' returns the whole deck to exactly how it shipped. Navigation is not a change, so this never moves the deck.

scope.description: How much to put back. Defaults to 'last'.

slide.description: Which slide to revert, 1-based. Only read when scope is 'slide'; defaults to the slide on screen.

email.description: Required for Phase 2; ignored in Phase 1.

sites.name: scvd.store
sites.description: An evidence observatory for agentic commerce: preflight an x402 door before paying, free conformance checks on the signed receipt after, a Bitcoin-anchored corpus over time. USDC on Base, Polygon,…

tools.name: read_store_guide
tools.description: Returns the store's guide as plain text: the catalog with prices, how x402 payment works here, the free instruments, and the house promises. Free; no purchase is made and nothing is stored.

tools.name: preflight_endpoint
tools.description: Probes one x402 endpoint unpaid and returns whether it serves a well-formed x402 v2 payment challenge right now: the verdict, the level reached on the L0–L6 evidence ladder, each check's tri-state result, and what a single probe cannot establish. A shape check at one moment, not an uptime or delivery claim. Free and rate limited; the ceiling travels with the result.

url.description: The https endpoint a buyer would GET expecting a 402 challenge.

tools.name: look_at_door
tools.description: Returns what the store holds about one x402 door: one unpaid probe now, folded with the signed weekly record of that host — rounds probed of rounds since first seen, the passport tier with its fraction, the last probed round's failed checks, and whether the door answers now the way the last signed round saw it. Not a score or a rank; counts carry their denominators. Free.

url.description: The https x402 door you are asking about.

since.description: Optional. A signed week, e.g. 2026-W34, to reproduce against that week's row.

tools.name: check_before_you_pay
tools.description: Probes one x402 door unpaid and replays the stock @x402/core client selection over the accepts it returned, under the caller's own profile. Returns which accept a stock client would sign — network, asset, amount, signing window — or that it would refuse locally before signing, with the stage and the setting that decided it. Free; nothing is signed and nothing is paid.

url.description: The https x402 door you are about to pay.

client_profile.description: The caller's own x402 client settings. Absent, the replay runs against a client configured with nothing, the case that loses money quietly.

max_amount_per_payment_usd.description: Your spendControls.maxAmountPerPayment, in dollars; false if you set it to false.

spend_controls_disabled.description: True if you pass spendControls: false — the one escape from the whole filter.

tools.name: check_conformance
tools.description: Verifies any issuer's signed x402 offer or receipt (a compact JWS): structure, the signature against the issuer's did:web key, and liveness. Returns a verdict with every check named. With public_key_hex supplied the check runs fully offline. Free; the method is MIT-licensed and identical to the published verifier.

artifact.description: The signed offer or receipt as a compact JWS: header.payload.signature, base64url.

kind.description: Optional: offer | receipt. Detected from the artifact when absent.

public_key_hex.description: Optional ed25519 public key, hex. Supplying it makes the check fully offline.

tools.name: verify_artifact
tools.description: Verifies a certificate, visit stamp or context anchor by its id against the store's own ed25519 key. Returns valid (true or false), the artifact kind, and a one-line note. Free and unlimited, for artifacts anyone bought or none.

id.description: A cert_, stamp_, or anchor_ id.

tools.name: check_order
tools.description: Returns the current state of a human-queue order by its order_id: status (queued or completed), the promised window in hours, and the deliverable once completed. The same record GET /api/order/{order_id} serves. Free; past its window the order carries a window_breached block stating what is owed.

order_id.description: The order_id from a human-queue purchase result.

tools.name: find_in_catalog
tools.description: Searches this store's shelf and returns compact rows: id, name, price in USDC, instant or human-fulfilled, and what each item reads. Filters by a price ceiling, a text match, or both; an item_id returns that one item with its description. Free and read-only. Nothing is ranked or recommended.

q.description: Words to match against an item's id, name, subtitle and description.

max_price_usdc.description: A ceiling in USDC. Items at or below it match.

item_id.description: One item's id. The answer carries that item alone, in full.

sites.name: sendero-alpha.vercel.app
sites.description: Prepare, validate, and save an itinerary generated with ChatGPT and Sendero.

tools.name: get_itinerary_planning_protocol
tools.description: Load Sendero's current versioned instructions, prepared brief, and canonical JSON schema for generating a new itinerary. Use this before researching or constructing the itinerary. Extract the facts already supplied in the user's natural language into brief; never ask the user to write field syntax. Multi-city requests may use destination as an ordered list or destinations as an ordered array, and Sendero will normalize them. The page will reflect those facts and move to the automatic generation step when the brief is ready, without requiring form entry or prompt copying. When this page-scoped tool is available for the open Sendero creation page, prefer this page workflow over remote Sendero planning tools so the page can show progress, review, and authoritative save state. Sendero returns instructions but does not call a model.

brief.description: Trip facts extracted from the user's natural-language request. The user never needs to know or write these field names. Omit the brief only to use fields already entered on the Sendero page.

locale.description: Language inferred from the user's request.

oneOf.description: A city, region, or country in the traveller's own words.
A city, region, or country in the traveller's own words.

destination.description: One destination, or an ordered list when the request contains multiple cities.

oneOf.description: A city, region, or country in the traveller's own words.

destinations.description: Ordered destinations for a multi-city trip. Sendero normalizes them into its canonical destination label.

tools.name: validate_and_stage_itinerary
tools.description: Validate one complete generated itinerary against the current Sendero protocol and place a local draft in this browser's persistent Sendero cache. This works without a Sendero account and is the authoritative review handoff for the open page. It does not save a canonical trip. Correct blocking errors before continuing and review all warnings.

brief.description: Trip facts extracted from the user's natural-language request. The user never needs to know or write these field names. Omit the brief only to use fields already entered on the Sendero page.

locale.description: Language inferred from the user's request.

oneOf.description: A city, region, or country in the traveller's own words.
A city, region, or country in the traveller's own words.

destination.description: One destination, or an ordered list when the request contains multiple cities.

oneOf.description: A city, region, or country in the traveller's own words.

destinations.description: Ordered destinations for a multi-city trip. Sendero normalizes them into its canonical destination label.

itinerary.description: The complete itinerary object matching itinerarySchema returned by get_itinerary_planning_protocol.

tools.name: get_staged_itinerary
tools.description: Read the validated local Sendero itinerary draft currently cached by the open page and its warnings. This does not require an account and does not save or modify the canonical trip library.

draftId.description: A draftId returned by validate_and_stage_itinerary. Omit it to use the draft currently open on the page.

tools.name: update_itinerary_reservation_statuses
tools.description: Update the purchase or booking tracker for one specific reservation/ticket or for a list of specific entries in the validated local Sendero draft. This requires an authenticated Sendero account; when signed out, preserve the draft and let the page offer sign-in instead of changing status. Use confirmed only when the user says they already booked or bought it; use pending when they say they have not. All requested entries are validated before the browser draft changes. This tracker never books, buys, contacts, or cancels with a provider. Use this page tool before saving; saved trips are edited from their private Sendero page.

draftId.description: A draftId returned by validate_and_stage_itinerary. Omit it to use the draft currently open on the page.

updates.description: One or more exact reservation or ticket entries to update. Use confirmed for 'already booked/bought' and pending for 'not booked/bought yet'.

activityId.description: The exact activity ID in the staged itinerary.

dayDate.description: The activity date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

status.description: confirmed means the user says it is already booked or bought; pending means it is not booked or bought yet.

tools.name: save_staged_itinerary
tools.description: Explicitly save one validated local draft from the open creation page as an authoritative Sendero trip. This requires a Sendero account; when signed out, preserve the browser draft and let the page offer sign-in or account creation. Call only when the user asked to save. Report success only from the returned trip, webId, and version.

draftId.description: A draftId returned by validate_and_stage_itinerary. Omit it to use the draft currently open on the page.

tools.name: share_saved_itinerary_by_link
tools.description: Enable public read-only access for the saved Sendero itinerary currently selected on this page and return its shareable URL. Anyone with the link can view it but cannot collaborate or modify it. This requires an authenticated Sendero account, an already saved itinerary, owner permission, and an explicit user request to make it public. Report success only from the returned shareUrl.

draftId.description: A draftId returned by validate_and_stage_itinerary. Omit it to use the draft currently open on the page.

tools.name: invite_saved_itinerary_member
tools.description: Invite one person by email to the saved Sendero itinerary currently selected on this page. viewer grants read-only private access; editor grants collaboration access. Sendero sends the invitation, so call this only after the user explicitly asks to invite that exact email with that role. This requires an authenticated account, an already saved itinerary, and owner permission. Report success only from the returned invitation status and delivery receipt.

draftId.description: A draftId returned by validate_and_stage_itinerary. Omit it to use the draft currently open on the page.

email.description: Email address of the person to invite.

role.description: viewer can only view; editor can collaborate on the itinerary.

tools.name: discard_staged_itinerary
tools.description: Discard the selected local Sendero browser draft and remove its itinerary content. This works without an account and never deletes a saved trip.

draftId.description: A draftId returned by validate_and_stage_itinerary. Omit it to use the draft currently open on the page.

sites.name: sepiola.semanticintent.dev
sites.description: Sepiola, a WebMCP telestrator: a page that draws an analyst's read onto a persistent screen. The analyst decides, the pen draws, the screen has no opinions.

tools.name: cue_roster
tools.description: Load a roster onto the rink. Give `text`, the pasted lineup (any format, one player per line), when an analyst is configured; or `fixture`, the name of a read in fixtures/. `opponent_text`, the other side's lineup, gives games in hand its second bar.

tools.name: read_ice
tools.description: Reveal the read: ice quality under the skates, badges, the calls, games in hand. `start` (YYYY-MM-DD) moves the window; the analyst defaults to today.

tools.name: circle
tools.description: Spotlight one skater with the reason pinned above. Without a reason, the analyst's own line is used.

ids.description: Skater ids from the read.

tools.name: replay
tools.description: Stage the reasoning behind one skater: his week, the analyst's line, his projected points, and the call if the analyst made one.

id.description: A skater id from the read.

tools.name: split
tools.description: Two skaters' weeks side by side, then the analyst's call on who gets the start, if the analyst made one.

a.description: A skater id from the read.

b.description: A skater id from the read.

tools.name: cut_to
tools.description: Bring a window forward: rink, panel, hand, replay, or console.

tools.name: cue_board
tools.description: Put up the draft board: the analyst's tiers by position from last season, one note per prospect, and where each position thins out. Give `drafted_text`, the players already taken by anyone (one per line, any format), and the analyst crosses them off. Give `mine_text`, your own picks, and the analyst also says who to take next: its top three are marked on the board in its order. `playoff_start_week` and `playoff_end_week` (your league's fantasy playoff weeks; week 1 opens with the NHL season and, when that is mid-week, runs to the second Sunday, as Yahoo counts it) let that pick weigh each club's games in them. `categories`, the league's scoring categories as its settings list them (e.g. "G, A, +/-, PPP, SOG, HIT, BLK; W, GAA, SV%, SO"), has the analyst rank the board and the pick for them instead of points. `fixture` loads a saved board.

tools.name: wipe
tools.description: Clean the screen. The roster stays cued; the read, the circle, and the replay are cleared.
