tools.description: Quote a Fintonic personal loan in Spain. Collects amount, duration, and the user's FinScore profile (ASNEF + employment + income + housing + other loan payments), maps the profile to a band, and shows the band-specific monthly installment in a result widget. After the result widget renders, the widget's CTA opens fintonic.com directly for the user to continue — your job is done at that point. This fits when the user mentions a loan, simulation, monthly payment, or amount/duration combination. For informational questions about how Fintonic, FinScore, ASNEF, OpenBanking, security, or the product work, `explain_fintonic` is the right tool; this one quotes a specific loan and collects FinScore inputs for the calculation rather than explaining concepts. INPUTS: a quote needs `amount`, `durationMonths`, `notInASNEF`, `laboralSituation`, `monthlyIncome`, `housingPayment`, `otherLoanPayments` (plus `laboralSituationConfidence`). Any subset can be supplied: pass whatever the user has stated and the flow asks for the rest through interrupts, one or two at a time, in their language. EXTRACTION: when the user states any of the input values, extract them into `stateUpdates` on the `start` call. Also extract `locale` — "en" if the user's latest message is in English, otherwise "es" (default Spanish). - `amount` (1,000–50,000 €), `durationMonths` (one of: 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54, 60, 66, 72, 78, 84, 90, 96) - `notInASNEF` boolean — true means the user is NOT in the ASNEF registry (good); false means listed (blocked) - `laboralSituation` (Funcionario, Fijo, Temporal, Por obra y servicio, Fijo discontinuo, Autónomo, Interino, Pensionista, Desempleado, Becario, ND) — always paired with `laboralSituationConfidence` ("high" | "medium" | "low") so the system can clear and re-ask when you flag a guess. - `monthlyIncome` (net monthly income in €) - `housingPayment` (monthly rent OR mortgage payment; 0 if neither) - `otherLoanPayments` (sum of all other monthly loan/credit obligati…

action.description: "start" to begin the flow, "continue" to resume after a pause (interrupt or widget), "reset" to restart from the beginning with a correction to a previously-collected field

intent.description: Required when action is "start". Provide a brief summary of the user's goal for this flow. Do not invent missing intent.

context.description: Optional when action is "start". Describe the situation or environment that led the user to start this flow — e.g. what page they are on, what they were doing, or what triggered the request. Do not invent missing context.

stateUpdates.description: State field values to set before processing the next node. Pass the user's answer (keyed by the field name from the response) and any other values the user mentioned. For nested state fields, use dot-paths like "driver.name".

amount.description: Loan amount in euros. Must be between 1000 and 50000. Values off the 500€ grid are rounded silently.

durationMonths.description: Loan duration in months. Must be one of 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54, 60, 66, 72, 78, 84, 90, 96. Off-grid values are rejected.

locale.description: User interface language: "es" (Spanish, default) or "en" (English). Set based on the language of the user's latest message so widgets mirror it.

notInASNEF.description: Whether the user is NOT listed in the ASNEF delinquency registry. True = not listed (qualifies); false = listed (blocked).

laboralSituation.description: User's employment status. Must be one of: Funcionario, Fijo, Temporal, Por obra y servicio, Fijo discontinuo, Autónomo, Interino, Pensionista, Desempleado, Becario, ND

laboralSituationConfidence.description: How confident the LLM is in the laboralSituation it picked. Output alongside laboralSituation. On low, the system clears the value and re-asks.

housingPayment.description: Monthly rent OR mortgage payment in euros (mutually exclusive). 0 if the user has neither.

otherLoanPayments.description: Sum of the user's other monthly loan/credit obligations in euros (car, personal loans, credit cards, etc.). 0 if none.

sessionId.description: Session identifier. If the response includes a `sessionId`, pass it back on every subsequent "continue" and "reset" call for this flow.

tools.name: simulation_result
tools.description: Display tool for the `loan` flow — renders EITHER the estimated monthly installment for the user's FinScore band (offer mode) OR a "no-offer" notice with the reason (rejection mode). Only call this tool when the `loan` flow returns `status: "widget"` with `tool: "simulation_result"` — pass the `data` from the flow response verbatim, including `kind` and `locale`. Never call it in response to a user's own loan-simulation intent (use `loan` for that). When you speak to the user, reply in their language (default Spanish, tú — warm and direct). On an OFFER, don't restate the numbers the widget already shows; invite them to continue if they want to apply, mentioning "sin compromiso" / "no commitment" naturally. On a REJECTION, the widget already shows the reason — keep your text minimal (one short line of empathy or a next step if relevant).

kind.description: Widget mode: "offer" shows the estimated installment + TAE + apply CTA; "rejection" shows a no-offer notice with the documented reason.

amount.description: Loan amount in euros (shown in both modes)

durationMonths.description: Loan duration in months (shown in both modes)

band.description: Offer mode only — FinScore band inferred from the user's profile.

installment.description: Offer mode only — monthly installment in euros for the estimated band.

tae.description: Offer mode only — APR (TAE) for the estimated band.

reason.description: Rejection mode only — which documented rejection text the widget should render. "asnef" = listed on ASNEF; "employment" = laboralSituation not supported; "no_offer" = profile too low for any band.

locale.description: User interface language for the widget. Pass verbatim from the flow's `data` — the flow mirrors the user's message language, defaulting to Spanish.

tools.name: search_activities
tools.description: Search for free tours and paid activities on GuruWalk. Finds free walking tours and experiences by destination, date range, and number of attendees. When the user mentions a city name (e.g. "Valencia", "Roma"), pass it as the `destination` parameter. Dates, attendee counts, and activityType are all optional — do not ask the user for them, proceed with whatever the user provided. If the user mentions any specific category, attraction, landmark, or activity type (e.g., "tablao flamenco", "food tour", "London Eye tickets", "Eiffel Tower visit", "wine tasting"), call list_destination_options FIRST to get valid verticalId/tagId values for the destination, then pass them here. This tool navigates the user's browser to the results page — a single call completes the search; never retry with different parameters unless the user explicitly asks.

destination.description: REQUIRED. The destination city name mentioned by the user. Pass the user's literal text (e.g., 'Valencia', 'New York', 'Roma') without modification.

beginsAt.description: Start date of the search range in YYYY-MM-DD format

endsAt.description: End date of the search range in YYYY-MM-DD format

activityType.description: Type of activities to search for. 'free-tour' = free walking tours (the default option, what most users want). 'paid' = paid activities like food tours, museum tickets, day trips. 'all' = both free tours and paid activities together.

verticalId.description: Optional vertical ID to filter by. Use this to filter by a specific category (e.g., Tablaos Flamencos = "171" in Sevilla). Get valid IDs from list_destination_options first.

tagId.description: Optional free-tour tag ID. Get valid IDs from list_destination_options first. Providing a tagId implies free tours: activityType will be treated as 'free-tour'.

tools.name: list_destination_options
tools.description: Look up the available filter options for a destination: vertical categories (e.g. Tablaos Flamencos, Food Tours, Day Trips) and free-tour tags (e.g. Nocturno, Imprescindible). Use this BEFORE search_activities when the user mentions any specific category, attraction, landmark, or activity type — match the user's intent to one of the returned ids and pass it as verticalId or tagId to search_activities. Examples that should trigger this lookup: "tablao flamenco", "food tour", "London Eye", "Eiffel Tower", "Sagrada Familia", "wine tasting", "Vatican Museums".

destination.description: Free-text destination name from the user, e.g. "Sevilla", "Roma", "Paris".

tools.name: sendFeedback
tools.description: Report an issue in the documentation of i18next documentation so the team can fix it. Use it whenever, while helping a user, you come across content that is outdated, contradictory, missing information, or otherwise unhelpful. Also use it when the user themselves reports a problem with the docs, even if you could not verify it yourself. If it's your own observation, do a quick sanity check that the issue is real before reporting — no need to exhaustively re-read the page. Send one call per distinct issue and do not report the same issue twice in a conversation. Do not use this tool to confirm that a page is accurate; it is for reporting problems only.

content.description: Explain the issue in full, as if writing to a documentation maintainer who never saw this conversation. Describe what is wrong, where on the page it appears (quote the exact sentence or section title when possible), what the user was trying to do, and, when relevant, what the correct or expected information should be. Write a few clear, specific sentences in English. Never include personal or confidential information from the conversation. Up to 2048 characters.

pageUrl.description: The full URL of the page the issue is about (e.g. https://www.i18next.com//getting-started), so the finding is linked to the exact page.

goal.description: The broader end goal you were ultimately trying to accomplish (as/on behalf of the user) when you hit this issue. Gives the team the context you were working towards. Optional.

tools.name: prepare_accessible_journey
tools.description: Prepare a complete trip from natural place names. The supported service area is limited to Taipei City and New Taipei City in Taiwan; do not imply that journeys outside those two cities are supported. Treat words such as here, current location, 這裡, or 目前位置 according to their grammatical role: '從這裡到淡水' uses fresh browser location as origin, while '從淡水到這裡' uses it as destination. If the user gives only a destination, omit origin to use fresh browser location. Never reuse a previous journey's current location, claim permission was granted, or ask for coordinates. The service prioritizes less walking, fewer transfers, and avoiding identified stairs; this is not an accessibility guarantee. Only describe a result as relatively more suitable when its preferenceAssessment explicitly says so. If state is needs-location, explain that the user can allow location or say a nearby landmark. Speak about the journey, not tools or implementation details.

origin.description: The origin as the user naturally said it. Omit when the user did not provide one or said current location.

destination.description: The destination as naturally said. Use current-location when the user explicitly means here as the destination.

originCandidateId.description: Use only after the user confirms an origin candidate returned by this action.

destinationCandidateId.description: Use only after the user confirms a destination candidate returned by this action.

tools.name: describe_current_location
tools.description: Use when the user asks where they currently are, such as '這裡是哪裡？' or '我現在在哪裡？'. Request a fresh one-time browser location, reject stale cached coordinates, reverse-geocode it to an approximate address or nearby place, update the visible page, and never expose coordinates. Journey planning is supported only in Taipei City and New Taipei City in Taiwan; identifying a location must not be presented as route coverage outside those two cities.

tools.name: select_journey_alternative
tools.description: Switch the Taipei City or New Taipei City journey currently shown on this page to one of the alternatives returned by prepare_accessible_journey. Use the exact alternativeId from the current journey result only after the user asks for that option or expresses a preference that clearly identifies it, such as less walking or the second option. Never invent an ID or use this action to extend service outside Taipei City and New Taipei City. The action updates the visible route and refreshes arrival information for the newly selected first transit leg. Speak about the route choice, not tools or implementation details.

alternativeId.description: The exact id of an alternative in the current journey result.

sites.name: navigatorbuilds.github.io
sites.description: Elara

tools.name: verify_elara_record
tools.description: Verify one signed Elara validation record entirely offline, in this browser. Checks structure, identity binding (the embedded public key must SHA3-256 to the claimed identity) and the ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) post-quantum signature over the record's canonical bytes. Returns {verdict, headline, checks[], reason}; verdict is VERIFIED, PARTIAL or FAILED. HONEST SCOPE: VERIFIED means the bytes are intact and the signer is who the record claims — it does NOT mean the record was accepted, sealed or time-anchored by any network, and it is not a statement that anyone was authorized to create it. INPUT MUST BE RAW TEXT: pass the record exactly as read from disk or network, never JSON.parse'd first — records carry u64 fields above JavaScript's 2^53 integer precision, and a parse/re-stringify round-trip corrupts the exact bytes the signature commits to (parsed objects are rejected with FAILED). Never throws: malformed input returns FAILED with the parse reason.

record_json.description: The validation record as RAW JSON text, exactly as read — never re-serialised from JSON.parse (u64 fields round above 2^53; see tool description).

tools.name: verify_mandate_bundle
tools.description: Check offline whether an agent was authorized to perform an act, under a scoped, revocable mandate. Input is a bundle {bundle_version, act, mandates[], revocations[]} of signed carrier records. Returns {verdict, authorized, principal, signer, lineage[], scope_deferred, soundness_caveats[], checks[], explanation, reason}. HONEST SCOPE: a CONSISTENT verdict proves the signatures and that authority held at the act's signed time GIVEN ONLY THE RECORDS IN THIS BUNDLE. It does NOT prove those records are sealed or time-anchored, and it CANNOT detect a revocation the bundle's author withheld — which is why the verdict is CONSISTENT and never AUTHORIZED. Read soundness_caveats before relying on it. INPUT MUST BE RAW TEXT: pass the bundle exactly as read, never JSON.parse'd first — act nonces are u64 and round above JavaScript's 2^53 integer precision, so a parse/re-stringify round-trip corrupts the signed bytes (parsed objects are rejected with FAILED). Never throws: malformed input returns FAILED.

bundle_json.description: The mandate bundle envelope as RAW JSON text, exactly as read — never re-serialised from JSON.parse (u64 nonces round above 2^53; see tool description).

tools.name: explain_verdict
tools.description: Translate a verdict from verify_elara_record or verify_mandate_bundle into the claim it does and does NOT support. Use this before repeating a verdict to a user: it names the limits explicitly (integrity and signer identity — never 'authorized on a chain'; a bundle cannot reveal a revocation its author withheld; the artifact is a signed hash-linked evidence log, not a blockchain). Pure formatting over the verdict object you pass in — it re-verifies nothing and cannot report anything stronger than it was given.

verdict_json.description: A verdict object (or its JSON text) as returned by one of the verify tools.

tools.name: sendFeedback
tools.description: Report an issue in the documentation of NGXS so the team can fix it. Use it whenever, while helping a user, you come across content that is outdated, contradictory, missing information, or otherwise unhelpful. Also use it when the user themselves reports a problem with the docs, even if you could not verify it yourself. If it's your own observation, do a quick sanity check that the issue is real before reporting — no need to exhaustively re-read the page. Send one call per distinct issue and do not report the same issue twice in a conversation. Do not use this tool to confirm that a page is accurate; it is for reporting problems only.

content.description: Explain the issue in full, as if writing to a documentation maintainer who never saw this conversation. Describe what is wrong, where on the page it appears (quote the exact sentence or section title when possible), what the user was trying to do, and, when relevant, what the correct or expected information should be. Write a few clear, specific sentences in English. Never include personal or confidential information from the conversation. Up to 2048 characters.

pageUrl.description: The full URL of the page the issue is about (e.g. https://www.ngxs.io//getting-started), so the finding is linked to the exact page.

goal.description: The broader end goal you were ultimately trying to accomplish (as/on behalf of the user) when you hit this issue. Gives the team the context you were working towards. Optional.

tools.name: search_knowledge
tools.description: Search the Pirate Skills knowledge: the Growth Codex, the Builder Codex and Insights. Returns the best matching chapters with a link; for a signed-in person each also carries a short excerpt. Without sign-in it returns titles and links only (which codex, the title, the url): the person signs in for the excerpts. Cite the url of every chapter you use in your answer.

tools.name: list_events
tools.description: Upcoming Pirate Skills events, soonest first by date, with a link to each event page (a Forge session links the Forge page, where the seat is sold) and, for a signed-in person, whether they are registered. A Forge cohort appears only as its start – the first session of its Build or Grow part; its weekly sessions are never listed here. Present them in that date order, and give each event its one line from `about` – what it is and who it is for – so the person knows what they are looking at (an event without `about` is a one-off; its subtitle says it). When the person asks about their own Forge cohort or its sessions, use my_forge_sessions instead. `cadence` is how often that event's format meets – weekly only for the Forge (every week of a six-week phase), monthly for Vibe Coding Cologne, the Pirate Lab and AI Compass, quarterly for the Vibe Hackathon, one-off otherwise; give each event its own and never carry one event's cadence over to the others. `when` is the day and time to quote, in Berlin time; `startsAt`/`endsAt` are the same moment in UTC, for working with, never for quoting (the Captain's copy leaves them out, and gives a subtitle an earlier event already carried as null).

type.description: Filter by event type label, e.g. "Pirate Lab" or "Vibe Coding Cologne". Omit for all.

tools.name: get_offers
tools.description: What Pirate Skills sells right now, with prices, read live (only what is on sale appears, and only what create_checkout sells): the Pirate Pass and the Forge Pass (monthly, prices before VAT, three-month minimum), which replace the Pirate Forge tiers (those are listed only until the passes are on sale), and a Captain on Deck session with Ben (the price is per session; up to 10 in one checkout) while it is on sale – each bought with create_checkout. `priceText` is the price to quote: euros, plus US dollars once a dollar price is set (both in one string, "€ / $"), with the person's likely currency first. An offer marked purchasable false carries a note saying why (a Pirate Pass holder cannot buy the Forge Pass on top). Event tickets (the Vibe Hackathon) are not listed here: a ticket is bought on the event page from list_events, where the price depends on the date and tier. Free events are registered with register_for_event, and the free Codex is read with search_knowledge. Every purchase is paid by the person on Stripe's own page; no agent takes a card or charges anyone.

A page match never determines a patient diagnosis, treatment choice, or provider choice, and responseGuidance.patientConclusion always remains not_determined. sites.description: Check an OpenCloud instance for known vulnerabilities, missing hardening, weak security headers and available updates. Free to use, with no account required.

tools.name: scan_opencloud_security
tools.description: Queue a security scan for a publicly reachable OpenCloud instance. Submitting is all this does: it answers with a uuid, the state 'queued' and the url of the result page. The rating does not exist yet. Scanning is asynchronous. Submission answers 202 Accepted with a uuid and the state 'queued'; the rating does not exist yet. Poll GET /api/scans/{uuid} every 3 seconds until the response carries 'done': true, which happens when the state reaches 'completed' or 'failed'. Allow up to about 5 minutes. This page registers no tool that reads a result - browser tools belong to the page they are on. Open the returned url; the result page registers get_scan_result and export_scan_report for that scan. A request chooses what to scan, never how hard. target_url, ignore_hardenings, release_track and output_format are the only accepted fields; anything else answers 422 naming the field. Concurrency, timeouts and TLS verification are server-side settings with no request-side equivalent. 429 is not a refusal. A client limit and a per-target cooldown both answer 429 with Retry-After in seconds; wait that long and try again, at most 3 times. A Retry-After longer than 300 seconds is a daily cap or a block for scanning hosts that were not OpenCloud: do not wait it out, tell the user. 403 means the deployment scans approved instances only. The whole scanner is open source and runs locally with no limits at all: https://github.com/sowoi/check-opencloud-security The uuid is the whole of the authorisation. Whoever has it can read that scan and nobody else can, there is no endpoint that lists scans, and an unknown, malformed or expired uuid all answer 404 alike. Treat it as a secret, do not guess one, and do not retry a 404 - the result is gone. This tool does not throw. A failure comes back as ok: false with status, error and retryable, plus retryAfter in seconds where the server sent one. retryable false means stop and report the error; do not call the tool again.

ignore_hardenings.description: Hardening identifiers to waive. A waived finding is still reported; it just stops capping the rating.

output_format.description: What the result page renders for the visitor.

release_track.description: How the version is judged. Changes the rating's reasoning and nothing about the scan itself.

target_url.description: Public OpenCloud base URL or hostname. It must resolve publicly; a private, loopback or link-local address is refused and retrying will not help.

tools.description: Report an issue in the documentation of semantic-release so the team can fix it. Use it whenever, while helping a user, you come across content that is outdated, contradictory, missing information, or otherwise unhelpful. Also use it when the user themselves reports a problem with the docs, even if you could not verify it yourself. If it's your own observation, do a quick sanity check that the issue is real before reporting — no need to exhaustively re-read the page. tools.name: getPage
tools.description: Fetch the full markdown content of a specific documentation page from Stavr Team Services. Use this when you have a page URL and want to read its content. Accepts full URLs (e.g. https://stavr-team.gitbook.io/nodes-guides//getting-started). Since `searchDocumentation` returns partial content, use `getPage` to retrieve the complete page when you need more details. The content includes links you can follow to navigate to related pages.

tools.name: sendFeedback
tools.description: Report an issue in the documentation of Stavr Team Services so the team can fix it. Use it whenever, while helping a user, you come across content that is outdated, contradictory, missing information, or otherwise unhelpful. Also use it when the user themselves reports a problem with the docs, even if you could not verify it yourself. If it's your own observation, do a quick sanity check that the issue is real before reporting — no need to exhaustively re-read the page. Send one call per distinct issue and do not report the same issue twice in a conversation. Do not use this tool to confirm that a page is accurate; it is for reporting problems only.

content.description: Explain the issue in full, as if writing to a documentation maintainer who never saw this conversation. Describe what is wrong, where on the page it appears (quote the exact sentence or section title when possible), what the user was trying to do, and, when relevant, what the correct or expected information should be. Write a few clear, specific sentences in English. Never include personal or confidential information from the conversation. Up to 2048 characters.

pageUrl.description: The full URL of the page the issue is about (e.g. https://stavr-team.gitbook.io/nodes-guides//getting-started), so the finding is linked to the exact page.

goal.description: The broader end goal you were ultimately trying to accomplish (as/on behalf of the user) when you hit this issue. Gives the team the context you were working towards. Optional.

tools.name: resolve_item
tools.description: Use this tool first whenever a user asks how to dispose of an item in Midori City/みどり市 or Aoba City/あおば市. Semantically interpret descriptive human wording into a concise ordinary item concept before calling; do not merely copy a long description. For a request containing multiple items, call this tool separately for every item and preserve stated quantities; never combine item names into one query. Pass municipality='midori' or municipality='aoba' to match the named city. Only normalize when one meaning is reasonably clear. If several items remain plausible or status is ambiguous, stop for that item and ask the user instead of choosing a candidate.

tools.name: get_disposal_rule
tools.description: Call this after resolve_item succeeds, once for each resolved item. Return the fictional municipality's declared demo rule using the canonical item_id, quantity, dimensions, and contents state supplied by the user. Pass municipality='midori' for みどり市 or municipality='aoba' for あおば市. Never invent missing conditions. If risk_level is high or auto_confirmation_allowed is false, explain the rule but do not automatically continue to an action.

item_id.description: Canonical waste item ID

quantity.description: Number of items

longest_side_cm.description: Longest side in centimetres, when known

municipality.description: Optional municipality ID. Use 'midori' for みどり市 / Midori City and 'aoba' for あおば市 / Aoba City. If omitted, use the municipality currently selected on the page.

tools.name: prepare_bulky_pickup
tools.description: Call this only after get_disposal_rule says the item is bulky and reservation_required=true, and call it separately for each eligible item. A confirmation_required result opens the page's Human Confirmation Gate, and only a human click can finalize the demo.

outbound.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. The day the traveller actually flies out.

inbound.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. The day they actually fly back. On departure-date forms this is used to derive the stay length. Omit if only the outbound day is fixed - then give nights.

searchWindow.description: Use whenever the user described a PERIOD rather than dates: "sometime in November", "all of November", "the first two weeks of July", "anytime this summer". from.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Earliest day the trip may start.

to.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Latest day the trip may end.

nights.description: How many nights the trip lasts ("5 nights" = 5, "a week" = 7, "a fortnight" = 14). Required with searchWindow. Never derive it from the length of searchWindow - a one-month window is not a one-month trip. With exactDates it may replace an omitted inbound date; when both are supplied, the explicit nights value controls stay-length selectors.

tools.description: Proposes a new task for the user's Lumos panel task board. The task is NOT created until the user approves it in the panel's own confirmation dialog. If the user declines, nothing is written and the result reports approved:false. Never claim the task exists unless ok is true. The result echoes the stored task only when the user has separately approved sharing the board (see lumos-list-tasks); otherwise ok:true arrives with no 'task' field and that still means it was written.

title.description: Short task title, as the user would read it on the board.

when.description: Optional human-readable schedule hint shown on the task row, e.g. 'Yarın 14:00'.

tools.name: lumos-complete-task
tools.description: Marks an existing Lumos panel task as completed. This tool needs the user's board-sharing consent BEFORE it does anything: without that consent every call — valid ref, unknown ref, missing ref, or an already completed task — returns the exact same ok:false refusal with reason 'read_consent_required', no task is looked up and no confirmation dialog is shown. That refusal is NOT evidence that the task is missing or that the board is empty; do not report it as such — ask the user to approve sharing the board (see lumos-list-tasks) and then retry. Once sharing is approved the task is still NOT completed until the user approves it in the panel's own confirmation dialog; if the user declines, nothing is written and the result reports approved:false. A task that was already done comes back with reason 'already_completed' and nothing is written. Approving a completion is NOT permission to read the board: the result carries a 'task' field only while the sharing consent is in force. Use lumos-list-tasks first to get a valid ref.

ref.description: Task id from lumos-list-tasks, or the exact task title.

sort.description: Order before pagination: recently_updated (default), price_asc (cheapest), price_desc, year_desc (newest model), mileage_asc (lowest kilometres). Unknown values sort last; slug breaks ties.

offset.description: Zero-based result offset; follow nextOffset for the same filters and sort.

tools.name: docket_ask_website
tools.description: Ask a question about this company's product, pricing, integrations, security or implementation, and get an answer from the knowledge the company publishes for visitors. Prefer this over reading or scraping the page: it covers the whole site, not just what is on screen. It cannot book meetings or answer about anything other than this company. When a slide or video illustrates the answer, the result says so and carries show_content: this page can put it on the visitor's screen. Offer it to them, and if they want it call docket_open_website_agent with that starting_message. No image is returned and there is no link to render. Every result includes a conversation_id. Pass it back as conversation_id on the visitor's follow-up questions so the answer takes the earlier exchange into account; omit it to start a fresh conversation. An id expires after a period of inactivity: each result says when in conversation_note, and an expired one is replaced automatically with a new conversation_id rather than failing.

question.description: One question about this company or its product.

conversation_id.description: The conversation_id from this tool's previous result. Pass it to continue the same conversation; omit it to start a new one. If it has expired, the result comes back with a new one to use from then on.

tools.name: docket_open_website_agent
tools.description: Open this company's live AI sales agent on the visitor's screen and start a conversation. The agent can show product slides and videos, answer follow-ups in real time, and help book a meeting. Use it when the visitor wants to talk to the company, see the product, or go deeper than a single answer — this is the next step after docket_ask_website. This changes what the visitor sees, so only call it when they have asked for it. With starting_message, the conversation opens on that message as if the visitor had typed it; without it the agent opens with its own greeting. mode is 'chat' (text, default) or 'voice' (spoken, needs a microphone). If a conversation is already open, this does nothing.

starting_message.description: The visitor's first message to the agent, in their words. Omit to let the agent open the conversation.

mode.description: 'chat' for text (default), 'voice' for a spoken call.

sites.name: duckboard-webmcp.alexmnahas.workers.dev
sites.description: A native WebMCP data canvas powered by DuckDB-Wasm in your browser.

tools.name: duckdb_sql
tools.description: Execute DuckDB SQL in this tab's browser-local DuckDB-Wasm database. Use SQL to load, join, transform, aggregate, and sample data before presenting it. The session is stateful until the page reloads, so statements may create, query, update, or drop tables and views across calls. DATA SOURCES - Local files must first be selected or dropped by the user. They are registered under local/*; discover them with SELECT * FROM glob('local/*'). Query them with read_csv, read_json, read_parquet, or supported filename shorthand. - SQL may read public HTTPS data supported by DuckDB-Wasm. Browser CORS rules still apply: the remote server must allow this page to fetch the URL. - DuckDB-Wasm differs from native DuckDB in extension and filesystem support. Consult the Wasm documentation before relying on a native-only feature. RESULTS - Multi-statement SQL executes every statement and persists its changes; structuredContent contains only the final statement's result. - The response includes column names, DuckDB types, and JSON-safe rows in structuredContent. - Big integers and exact decimals are returned as strings. Binary values are base64 strings. FIRST-PARTY DUCKDB DOCUMENTATION - DuckDB-Wasm overview: https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/clients/wasm/overview - DuckDB-Wasm data ingestion: https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/clients/wasm/data_ingestion - DuckDB-Wasm extensions and browser limitations: https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/clients/wasm/extensions - SQL statements: https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/sql/statements/overview - SELECT syntax: https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/sql/query_syntax/select - SQL functions: https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/sql/functions/overview - Friendly SQL: https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/sql/dialect/friendly_sql - Data formats: https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/data/overview

tools.name: render_html
tools.description: Replace the full-screen canvas with an HTML data visualization. Favor a visual-first result: let the data dominate, keep explanatory text sparse, establish a clear visual hierarchy, use motion only when it communicates change or flow, adapt to the viewport, and preserve accessible names and reduced-motion behavior. The HTML is mounted inside a fresh opaque-origin iframe that cannot access the host page, storage, DuckDB, local files, or WebMCP tools. PRELOADED RUNTIME - Sigvelo design tokens are already loaded with the clean style and blue color preset. - @mcp-b/web-components and @mcp-b/viz-components are already registered. Do not import them again. - The sandbox already applies the Sigvelo UI font, text and canvas colors, border-box sizing, zero body margin, and full-viewport minimum sizing. Do not repeat those resets. - Prefer semantic custom elements and tokens over recreating controls, cards, metrics, tables, or chart chrome with custom CSS. tools.name: search_hoteles
tools.description: Search for Hoteles on the Hotels search form. Builds the search and moves the user to the results page - it does not return offers or prices itself; read those from the results page.

place.description: Exactly one destination or specific hotel name as the user said it, e.g. "Crete" or "Blue Lagoon Resort".

exactDates.description: The fixed hotel stay dates. Hotel search does not support flexible date windows.

checkin.description: Check-in date in ISO YYYY-MM-DD format.

checkout.description: Check-out date in ISO YYYY-MM-DD format.

rooms.description: Defaults to one room, two adults, when omitted.

childrenAges.description: Each child's age. Every child needs an age - do not call with a missing one.

tools.name: search_vuelo_hotel
tools.description: Search for Vuelo+Hotel on the Portfolio search form. Builds the search and moves the user to the results page - it does not return offers or prices itself; read those from the results page.

destinations.description: Destination names as the user said them, e.g. ["Crete", "Rhodes"]. Omit or send an empty list when the user wants any destination.

departures.description: Departure city/airport names as the user said them. Omit for no departure restriction.

exactDates.description: Use ONLY when the user knows the real travel dates, e.g. "out on 12 June, back on the 19th". The form may represent this as two calendar dates or as a departure date plus the derived stay length. Never use this to express a period to search inside - for that use searchWindow.

outbound.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. The day the traveller actually flies out.

inbound.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. The day they actually fly back. On departure-date forms this is used to derive the stay length. Omit if only the outbound day is fixed - then give nights.

searchWindow.description: Use whenever the user described a PERIOD rather than dates: "sometime in November", "all of November", "the first two weeks of July", "anytime this summer". These are the bounds of the period to search inside, NOT the trip itself - the trip is shorter and floats within them. Always pair with nights. If the user gave any period at all, send it here - do not drop the dates because they are not exact.

from.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Earliest day the trip may start.

to.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Latest day the trip may end.

nights.description: How many nights the trip lasts ("5 nights" = 5, "a week" = 7, "a fortnight" = 14). Required with searchWindow. Never derive it from the length of searchWindow - a one-month window is not a one-month trip. With exactDates it may replace an omitted inbound date; when both are supplied, the explicit nights value controls stay-length selectors.

nightsMax.description: Upper bound when the user gave a range of nights, e.g. nights: 7, nightsMax: 10 for "1-1.5 weeks".

rooms.description: Defaults to one room, two adults, when omitted.

childrenAges.description: Each child's age. Every child needs an age - do not call with a missing one.

tools.name: generate_placeholder
tools.description: Generates an image or video placeholder, or a file of fake placeholder data. For kind=image and kind=video: give a background and the text color is derived from it to guarantee WCAG contrast. Pass foreground as well to choose both yourself, and read the reported contrast to know how the pair came out. The text of the placeholder is the dimensions. Pastel palettes available: gray, red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, violet, rose. For kind=text: writes fake data instead of pixels, so width, height, palette, background and foreground do not apply and are refused. Use textPreset for a ready-made bundle such as a user profile or an API response, or textPreset=custom with textCategory and textGenerator for one specific value. The catalog spans person, internet, location, company, commerce, phone, date, finance, string, color, number, word, git, system, database, vehicle, airline, book, music, food, animal, science and lorem. Common ones: internet.email, internet.url, person.fullName, person.jobTitle, location.city, location.country, location.zipCode, company.name, commerce.productName, finance.amount, string.uuid, lorem.paragraph. The file extension follows textFormat: .txt, .json, .csv, .md. CSV separates its columns with ';' unless textDelimiter says otherwise, because that is the delimiter a spreadsheet expects where the decimal separator is a comma, which includes Spanish.

kind.description: Generate a still image, a looping output, or a file of fake placeholder data. kind=text ignores every pixel setting below and uses the text* ones instead.

imageFormat.description: Output format for kind=image. Defaults to png.

videoFormat.description: Output format for kind=video, including the animated image containers. Defaults to mp4.

palette.description: Name of the pastel palette, for example "azure" or "sage". If background is passed too, background wins.

background.description: Background color as 6 hex digits, for example "E0E0E0", without #. The text color is derived from it to guarantee contrast, unless foreground is passed too.

foreground.description: Text color as 6 hex digits, for example "2B2B2B", without #. Only the dimensions are written on the placeholder, in this color. Passed without background, it keeps the background that is already set; the measured contrast is reported and may be below AA.

showProgressBar.description: Draw a progress bar at the bottom. Video only.

showText.description: Writes the dimensions in the middle of the placeholder. Defaults to true; set it to false for a frame with nothing written on it. It does not touch the clock or the progress bar, which have their own parameters.

transparent.description: Leaves the background unpainted so the file carries an alpha channel. The background color still decides the text color, so the contrast guarantee is unchanged. Only png, webp, svg and gif honor it; the other formats export opaque.

sound.description: Adds a soundtrack to the video. Defaults to false, and it only works for the video containers, not for gif, mjpeg-avi or jpeg-zip.

soundTone.description: Which soundtrack: 'tango' is a synthesized tango nuevo at 100 BPM, 'beep' is a soft 440 Hz beep every second, 'tone' is the same pitch held quietly for the whole video, and 'noise' is white noise. Defaults to tango.

textPreset.description: A bundle of generators for kind=text: a lorem sentence or paragraph, a user profile, a company, a product, an address, a payment card, or an API response. 'custom' uses textCategory and textGenerator instead. Defaults to a lorem sentence.

textCategory.description: Group of generators for kind=text, for example lorem, person, internet, location, company, commerce, finance or string. Only with textPreset=custom.

textGenerator.description: The single generator to call for kind=text, written as category.method, for example internet.email or location.city. Only with textPreset=custom.

textLocale.description: Which set of names, addresses and words kind=text draws on. A few generators come out the same in both: the lorem filler is latin in any language, and IBANs have no Spanish dataset, so finance.iban returns a Belgian one either way. Defaults to en.

textCount.description: How many rows to generate for kind=text. Defaults to 10.

textFormat.description: How the rows are written for kind=text. plain is bare text with no header, json is a JSON array with one object per row, csv and md are tables with a header row. Defaults to plain.

textSeparator.description: What goes between the fields of one row in the text format, as the literal characters. Only read when textFormat is plain.

textDelimiter.description: What goes between the columns in the CSV format, as the character itself. Only read when textFormat is csv. The default is ';', which is what a spreadsheet expects where the decimal separator is a comma, Spanish included.

download.description: If false, it only configures and returns the preview without downloading. Defaults to true.

tools.name: generate_placeholder
tools.description: Configures and generates an image placeholder, a video placeholder, or a file of fake text data in the browser. For an image or a video: adjust dimensions, pastel palette, contrast and background (flat, transparent or an animated texture), and the file is downloaded. For text: fake names, addresses, emails, companies, products and payment details in English or Spanish, written as plain text, JSON, CSV or a Markdown table, and the rows are returned.

tools.name: search_let_hotel
tools.description: Search for Let+Hotel on the Portfolio search form. Builds the search and moves the user to the results page - it does not return offers or prices itself; read those from the results page.

destinations.description: Destination names as the user said them, e.g. ["Crete", "Rhodes"]. Omit or send an empty list when the user wants any destination.

departures.description: Departure city/airport names as the user said them. Omit for no departure restriction.

exactDates.description: Use ONLY when the user knows the real travel dates, e.g. "out on 12 June, back on the 19th". outbound.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. The day the traveller actually flies out.

inbound.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. The day they actually fly back. On departure-date forms this is used to derive the stay length. Omit if only the outbound day is fixed - then give nights.

searchWindow.description: Use whenever the user described a PERIOD rather than dates: "sometime in November", "all of November", "the first two weeks of July", "anytime this summer". These are the bounds of the period to search inside, NOT the trip itself - the trip is shorter and floats within them. Always pair with nights. If the user gave any period at all, send it here - do not drop the dates because they are not exact.

from.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Earliest day the trip may start.

to.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Latest day the trip may end.

nights.description: How many nights the trip lasts ("5 nights" = 5, "a week" = 7, "a fortnight" = 14). Required with searchWindow. Never derive it from the length of searchWindow - a one-month window is not a one-month trip. With exactDates it may replace an omitted inbound date; when both are supplied, the explicit nights value controls stay-length selectors.

nightsMax.description: Upper bound when the user gave a range of nights, e.g. nights: 7, nightsMax: 10 for "1-1.5 weeks".

rooms.description: Defaults to one room, two adults, when omitted.

childrenAges.description: Each child's age. Every child needs an age - do not call with a missing one.

source.description: Source city name (e.g., "Bangalore", "Singapore", "Kuala Lumpur", "Phnom Penh")

destination.description: Destination city name (e.g., "Chennai", "Johor Bahru", "Penang", "Siem Reap")

date.description: Travel date. Use ISO YYYY-MM-DD with the correct calendar year (same as the user's "today"). Accepts natural language ("today", "tomorrow") or "in N days". If the year is wrong/outdated, it is corrected to this year or next.

filters.description: Optional filters to pre-apply on the results page. Include every criterion the user asked for (e.g. AC + SLEEPER + Volvo) in one object.

departureTime.description: Preferred departure time slot: MORNING (6AM-12PM), AFTERNOON (12PM-6PM), EVENING (6PM-12AM), NIGHT (12AM-6AM)

arrivalTime.description: Preferred arrival time slot: MORNING (6AM-12PM), AFTERNOON (12PM-6PM), EVENING (6PM-12AM), NIGHT (12AM-6AM)

operatorOrBusBrandKeyword.description: Operator or bus brand mentioned by the user (e.g. "Volvo", "Benz"). Resolved on the results page against live filter data.

runAfterSearchResultsLoad.description: Optional. Same fields as runSrpBookingFlow (openBus, selectSeats, continueToBoardingPoints, applyFilters, waitForSearchResultsMs). Stored for the results page to execute after tuples load.

tools.name: searchBuses
tools.description: Search for available buses between two cities on a specific date. Resolves city names automatically. Use this tool on the HOME page when the user gives route + date + filters in one prompt. Optionally include filter preferences (AC, seat type, departure/arrival slots, operator/brand keyword like Volvo) — they are applied after navigation to the results page. source.description: Source city name (e.g., "Bangalore", "Singapore", "Kuala Lumpur", "Phnom Penh")

destination.description: Destination city name (e.g., "Chennai", "Johor Bahru", "Penang", "Siem Reap")

date.description: Travel date. Use ISO YYYY-MM-DD with the correct calendar year (same as the user's "today"). Accepts natural language ("today", "tomorrow") or "in N days". If the year is wrong/outdated, it is corrected to this year or next.

departureTime.description: Preferred departure time slot: MORNING (6AM-12PM), AFTERNOON (12PM-6PM), EVENING (6PM-12AM), NIGHT (12AM-6AM)

arrivalTime.description: Preferred arrival time slot: MORNING (6AM-12PM), AFTERNOON (12PM-6PM), EVENING (6PM-12AM), NIGHT (12AM-6AM)

operatorOrBusBrandKeyword.description: Operator or bus brand mentioned by the user (e.g. "Volvo", "Benz"). Resolved on the results page against live filter data.

runAfterSearchResultsLoad.description: Optional. Same fields as runSrpBookingFlow (openBus, selectSeats, continueToBoardingPoints, applyFilters, waitForSearchResultsMs). Stored for the results page to execute after tuples load.

tools.name: search_mcp_servers
tools.description: Agent quick start: (1) search_mcp_servers with query or filters → (2) get_mcp_server with slug and include instructions or connect → (3) connect using connectAction/connectPath. Use harvest_only for independent servers; catalog_listing for MCPBundles bundles; connect_path/connect_action for actionability; verification instead of live_tools when you need probe precision. kind describes listing shape, not ownership — check catalogListing and connectAction on each result. Results include connectPath, connectAction, catalogListing, toolInventoryStatus, pageUrl, and toolsCount when observed. Provide query and/or at least one filter — enforced at execution time.

query.description: Search term, e.g. "stripe", "postgres", or "weather". Optional when a filter facet is set.

kind.description: Browse chip shape (not ownership): managed = MCPBundles API integrations (api_bundle); provider = remote_mcp (publisher wire; may still have catalogListing true); webmcp = in-browser surface. For independent harvest servers use harvest_only.

catalog_listing.description: When true, only rows with a global MCPBundles bundle. When false, only rows without one.

harvest_only.description: Independent remote servers only (remote_mcp, no global bundle). Best for long-tail discovery.

connect_path.description: Filter by what Hub can do: managed/importable/import_auth_required/browse_only or aliases connect_now, import_server, import_may_need_sign_in, view_only.

connect_action.description: Alias for connect_path using agent vocabulary.

verification.description: Evidence level: tools_listed, auth_handshake, curated, reachable (same as live_tools when omitted).

category.description: Single category slug (legacy). Aliases map narrowly (e.g. productivity → PROJECT_MANAGEMENT). Prefer categories when ANDing.

categories.description: Category slugs ANDed together, e.g. ["marketing", "developer-tools"]. Same as browse categories=.

exclude_categories.description: Omit listings in these categories (primary category or harvest flag slug, e.g. ecommerce).

mcp_app.description: Only servers shipping an MCP App / interactive UI surface.

live_tools.description: Shorthand for verification=reachable when verification is omitted.

no_upstream_sign_in.description: Only servers that need no upstream service sign-in or OAuth (public "No sign in" facet).

one_click_sign_in.description: Only listings with OAuth dynamic client registration (one-click sign-in facet).

min_tools.description: Only servers reporting at least this many tools from the probe. Null toolsCount means unknown or auth-gated, not zero tools.

limit.description: Results per page (default 12, max 100). Use cursor from nextCursor for the next page.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from pagination.nextCursor or nextCursor on the prior response.

include.description: Response tiers: summary (default), instructions (server markdown), connect (install URLs and guidance).

host.description: Preferred MCP host for install links when include contains connect.

tools.name: find_restaurants
tools.description: Search and filter NYC restaurants tracked by this site. Use this tool when the user wants to find restaurants, browse dining options, or look up reservation details for a specific restaurant. All filter parameters are optional and case-insensitive partial matches — combine any number of them to narrow results. When no filters are provided, returns all restaurants. Each result includes: restaurant name, cuisine, NYC neighborhood, reservation platform (e.g. Resy, OpenTable, Phone), direct booking link, how far in advance reservations open, and the daily release time in Eastern Time. Examples of when to use this tool: - "What Italian restaurants do you have?" → { cuisine: "Italian" } - "Show me restaurants in the West Village" → { neighborhood: "West Village" } - "What restaurants use Resy?" → { reservation_method: "Resy" } - "Tell me about Don Angie" → { name: "Don Angie" } - "Find Japanese restaurants in Soho" → { cuisine: "Japanese", neighborhood: "Soho" } Do NOT use this tool for: - Calculating when reservations open for a specific date (use get_reservation_open_date instead) - Finding restaurants not tracked by NYC RSVPs - Making or managing actual reservations

name.description: Restaurant name to search for. Partial match, case-insensitive. Example: 'carbone', 'Don Angie'

cuisine.description: Cuisine type to filter by. Partial match, case-insensitive. Examples: 'Italian', 'Japanese', 'Mexican', 'French'

neighborhood.description: NYC neighborhood/area to filter by. Partial match, case-insensitive. Examples: 'West Village', 'Soho', 'Williamsburg', 'Lower East Side'

reservation_method.description: Booking platform to filter by. Partial match, case-insensitive. Examples: 'Resy', 'OpenTable', 'Phone', 'Tock'

tools.name: get_reservation_open_date
tools.description: Calculate exactly when reservations open for a specific restaurant on a desired date. Use this tool when the user wants to know when to book, when reservations drop, or when to set a reminder for a specific dining date. Returns one of two outcomes: - If reservations are already open: tells the user they can book now and provides the booking link. - If reservations are not yet open: returns the exact date and time (in Eastern Time) when reservations will be released, plus the booking link. The restaurant_name must match a restaurant tracked by this site. If unsure of the exact name, use find_restaurants first to look it up. Examples of when to use this tool: - "When do reservations open for Carbone on March 15?" → { restaurant_name: "Carbone", desired_date: "2026-03-15" } - "I want to eat at Don Angie on my birthday April 20th" → { restaurant_name: "Don Angie", desired_date: "2026-04-20" } - "When should I check Resy for a July 4th dinner at 4 Charles?" → { restaurant_name: "4 Charles Prime Rib", desired_date: "2026-07-04" } Do NOT use this tool for: - Browsing or searching for restaurants (use find_restaurants instead) - Dates in the past - Restaurants not tracked by this site

restaurant_name.description: Exact name of the restaurant as it appears on NYC RSVPs. Use find_restaurants first if unsure of the exact name.

desired_date.description: The date the user wants to dine, in YYYY-MM-DD format. Must be a future date.

tools.description: Start here for an OBC ONE onboard courier / hand-carry quote. Works directly with the server, without interacting with the website form. Call with all known user-provided details, or {} to discover required information. Returns missingFields and clarificationQuestions; ask these in the chat. Ask whether ambiguous cities mean an airport or address; never select an airport silently. OBC ONE accepts enquiries from freight forwarders, businesses and private customers. darkTextColor.description: CSS text color used when the viewer prefers a dark color scheme.

last_name.description: Required. The customer's last name. Max 100 characters. Example: "Janssens".

email.description: Required. The customer's email address. Must be a valid email format. Example: "sophie.janssens@example.com".

phone.description: Required. The customer's phone number including international country code, starting with "+". Example: "+32 470 12 34 56". Must contain at least 7 digits.

interest.description: Required. Free-text answer to "How can we help you?" — what the customer is looking for or wants to discuss. Example: "I am looking for an engagement ring with a 1ct round diamond.". Max 2000 characters.

budget.description: Optional. The customer's budget range in EUR. Only include if the customer voluntarily shares it — do not push for this.

language.description: Optional. ISO-like language code in which the Valquère consultant should follow up with the customer. pattern.description: Get Theoretical Physics Canon books optionally using fuzzy string filter matched against entry description (Chicago-style citations with author, year, title, publisher). Calling get_books() with no arguments will return all the books in the canon. Keep filter short — ideally a single keyword like an author surname or a key title word. Although filters are applied fuzzily filtering is very restrictive so multi-word filter string will almost certainly filter out desired results. For broad exploration, use just one term. E.g. get_books("Newton") to get books by Newton, or make multiple queries like get_books("1960") up to get_books("1969") to get books published in the 1960s. Or simply get_books("196") to get books published in the 1960s and filter out desired titles yourself. Filtering is fuzzy thus tolerating one character mismatch, like missing character or extra character, so get_books("Newtn") will also return books by Newton; leverage this functionality when useful or when uncertain about the exact filter pattern.

tools.name: query
tools.description: Query the server logs. Sets all filters and visualization in one atomic call — every parameter is always applied together, so no stale state can carry over from a previous query. FILTERS (all optional — omit or pass null to leave unfiltered): status — HTTP status code: '200' | '201' | '301' | '304' | '401' | '403' | '404' | '500' method — HTTP verb: 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE' | 'PATCH' | 'HEAD' | 'OPTIONS' pathSearch — substring matched against the request URL path, e.g. '/api' dateFrom — start date inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD (resolve "last week", "yesterday", etc. before calling) dateTo — end date inclusive, YYYY-MM-DD AGGREGATION (required): groupBy — dimension to group by: 'date' | 'status' | 'method' | 'path' | 'country' | 'user_agent' measure — metric to compute: 'count' (requests) | 'bytes' (bandwidth) | 'unique_ips' CHART (required): chartType — 'line' (trends over time, best with groupBy=date) | 'bar_vertical' | 'bar_horizontal' | 'table' (raw rows, groupBy/measure ignored)

status.description: HTTP status filter. Omit for no filter.

method.description: HTTP method filter. Omit for no filter.

pathSearch.description: URL path substring filter. Omit for no filter.

dateFrom.description: Start date YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for no lower bound.

dateTo.description: End date YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for no upper bound.

measure.description: Metric to compute: count (requests), bytes (bandwidth), or unique_ips.

chartType.description: Chart type. Use line for trends over time (best with groupBy=date). Use table for raw rows (groupBy/measure ignored).

sites.description: Choose your best offer from more than 175,000 cars in 20,000 locations around the world! New high-quality vehicles meeting your needs and your budget.

tools.name: search_cars
tools.description: Find and compare rental cars anywhere in the world, then hand the user a direct booking link. Use this tool whenever someone wants to rent, hire, or book a car, van, SUV, convertible, people carrier or similar vehicle for a trip — including airport pickups, one-way rentals between cities, long weekends, week-long holidays, business trips and road trips. Handles natural requests like "cheapest automatic at Malaga airport for a week in June", "7-seater in Faro under €300 total", "one-way from Venice to Verona", "SUV with unlimited mileage in Denver", "rental car for a 23-year-old driver in Dublin", or the same questions in Spanish, German, French, Italian and 13 other languages. Accepts city names or IATA airport codes (e.g. "Malaga", "Venice", "AGP", "VCE") and filters by vehicle category, transmission, supplier, specific model, maximum total price and currency. Returns live availability with all-in prices in the user's local currency, per-day cost, deposit split, fuel policy, mileage limit, included insurance, free-cancellation deadline, supplier name and rating, plus a deep link that opens the exact deal on economybookings.com for checkout. Read-only: it searches and compares, it never books or takes payment.

pickupLocation.description: Pickup location — city name or IATA airport code. Use "Malaga" or "AGP", NOT "Malaga Airport".

dropoffLocation.description: Dropoff location — omit for round-trip (same as pickup). Provide for one-way rentals.

pickupDate.description: Pickup date as YYYY-MM-DD. MUST be today or later — past dates are rejected. Before calling the tool, sanity-check the date against TODAY (which is in your system context). If the user says a bare month/day with no year (e.g. 'June 15'), interpret it as the next future occurrence. If the user explicitly states a past year (e.g. 'June 15, 2024'), DO NOT call the tool — first ask whether they meant the next future year (e.g. 2026) and confirm before proceeding.

dropoffDate.description: Dropoff date as YYYY-MM-DD. MUST be on or after pickupDate, and on or after today. Same year-resolution rules as pickupDate: prefer the next future occurrence for ambiguous dates and confirm with the user before calling the tool with any explicitly-past date.

driverAge.description: Driver's age (years). **DO NOT ASK THE USER FOR THIS — it is friction we explicitly want to avoid.** Leave the field blank by default; the server returns prices computed for a 35-year-old (the no-surcharge mid-band), which is the right answer for the vast majority of users. Only populate this field when (a) the user volunteered their age in this conversation without being asked, or (b) you already have it from prior context / memory you have on the user. Do NOT ask the user to provide their age just because surcharges might apply — they can correct us afterwards if needed.

category.description: Comma-separated car categories. Substring match — e.g. "Luxury" matches both "Luxury" and "Luxury Elite". Valid values from EconomyBookings docs §6.3: Mini, Mini Elite, Economy, Economy Elite, Compact, Compact Elite, Intermediate, Intermediate Elite, Standard, Standard Elite, Fullsize, Fullsize Elite, Premium, Premium Elite, Luxury, Luxury Elite, Oversize, Special, Van, Electric, Midsize, SUV, Estate, Convertible, Small.

maxPrice.description: Maximum total price in the customer currency (e.g. 300 for £300 total).

limit.description: Maximum cars to return (1-5)

locale.description: User's preferred language as a BCP 47 tag (e.g. 'en-GB', 'es-ES', 'fr-FR', 'de-DE', 'pt-BR'). Infer from the language the user is writing in — if they message in Spanish, pass 'es-ES'; in German, 'de-DE'; etc. Used to localise prices and to redirect them to the matching version of the booking site. Skip when the conversation language matches the host's UI language (we'll pick it up from there).

country.description: User's CURRENT country (where they physically are right now) as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (e.g. 'GB', 'ES', 'US', 'KR', 'JP'). Drives the currency and pricing market we ask EB for. NOT the trip destination they're searching for. Priority order for inferring this: (1) the user's approximate location provided in the system context — if present, use that country; (2) timezone if known; (3) what the user has explicitly said in this conversation about where they are right now. Do NOT use long-term memory of where the user usually lives — they may be travelling. Do NOT use the trip destination. If sources conflict (e.g. memory says one country, system location says another), trust the system location — the user is likely travelling. Skip if no signal at all — we'll fall back to other location detectors.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code (e.g. 'USD', 'EUR', 'GBP', 'KRW'). Pass this ONLY when the user explicitly asks for prices in a specific currency (e.g. 'show me the price in USD'). Otherwise leave blank — the server picks the right currency from the user's country. Overrides the country-derived currency.

supplier.description: Optional supplier filter — pass the supplier name (or a unique substring) when the user asks for a specific car-hire company (e.g. 'ClickRent', 'Hertz', 'GoldCar', 'Europcar'). Case-insensitive substring match against the supplier list. If we can't find that supplier we'll surface the closest available alternatives.

vehicleModel.description: Optional vehicle make / model filter — pass it when the user mentions a specific car (e.g. 'Toyota Corolla', 'Fiat 500', 'BMW 1 Series'). Case-insensitive substring match against the vehicle name. If the exact model isn't available we'll surface the closest alternatives.

The form may represent this as two calendar dates or as a departure date plus the derived stay length. Never use this to express a period to search inside - for that use searchWindow.

to.description: ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Latest day the trip may end.

With exactDates it may replace an omitted inbound date; when both are supplied, the explicit nights value controls stay-length selectors.

tools.name: SearchProperties
tools.description: Search for properties for sale or rent on the Costa del Sol (Spain): apartments, penthouses, villas, townhouses, plots and commercial premises. Use this tool whenever the user wants to find, filter or shortlist properties by location, type, price, bedrooms or amenities. Coverage: Marbella, Estepona, Benahavís, Sotogrande, Mijas, Fuengirola, Manilva and the wider coastal area, including districts such as Golden Mile, Puerto Banús, Nueva Andalucía, Sierra Blanca and La Zagaleta. Operational rules: 1) Options (op) combine with AND; FEATURES (cop) combine with OR (any of them). A property must satisfy every option AND at least one feature: two options = both required; two features = either is enough. If the user wants alternatives between OPTIONS (e.g. two amenities from the same options set), the site cannot combine them — leave the options empty and explain the limitation instead (features ARE combinable as alternatives: send them in cop). 2) Only the most specific location level applies (subarea > area > city): "Marbella + Golden Mile" returns only Golden Mile results. 3) Proximity searches ("near X", "within Y km") use only genuinely adjacent same-level locations (roughly 10-15 km); never include far-away municipalities (e.g. Mijas, Mijas Costa or Málaga are not near Estepona). 4) If the request mixes more than 2-3 unrelated or far-apart zones, or is unclear, do not run the search — ask the user to clarify. After searching, never invent specific properties, prices or addresses; simply confirm that the results are now visible on the page.

In that case leave the conflicting filters empty; the answer will explain that the site supports AND combinations only. q11.description: [communication] Does your child have other trusted adults they could talk to if they were not comfortable coming to you?
